title: [URGENT] Mayor checkout has 25 STAGED reverted core source files on main (re-frame.hicasso -> re-frame.ui)
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-19 by the rf2-aw1ez worker, from a read-only look at the mayor
checkout while confirming its own edits had not leaked there. NOT CAUSED BY THAT
WORKER — its fence was two READMEs and one Python script, and its worktree is
clean. NOT REPAIRED, per the do-not-repair-outside-your-worktree rule. Surfacing
it so it is not lost if the observing agent's report is missed.

WHAT IS THERE. C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2 (the mayor checkout, on main, HEAD
c85e024316) has 25 files STAGED in the index, all under
implementation/core/src/re_frame/: 610 insertions, 931 deletions. Porcelain shows
'M ' — staged AND the working tree matches the index, so the files ON DISK carry
the old content too, not just the index.

WHAT THE CONTENT IS. A time-travelled tree, not a deliberate edit. The staged
error.cljc blob is 2787adc1a9, which is exactly the blob at c07b9f8467^ — the
state before 'docs(core,routing): the substrate prose stops teaching two retired
view artefacts' (rf2-9sz2t) landed on 2026-08-16. The staged text restores
references to re-frame.ui, which CLAUDE.md records as RETIRED AND REMOVED (Mike's
2026-08-14 disposition rf2-0yp7w, executed by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16). Sample
staged hunk in error.cljc:
    -;; `re-frame.ssr` and `re-frame.hicasso` are sibling artefacts
    +;; `re-frame.ssr` and `re-frame.ui` are sibling artefacts

IT IS NOT A CLEAN SINGLE-COMMIT REVERT, which matters for the remedy. Of the 25
staged files only 11 match c07b9f8467^ exactly; the other 14 differ from that
point too, so the tree is stale from some earlier and not-uniform base. Do not
reach for 'git revert <one commit>'. The 14: adapter/context.cljs,
adapter/use_frame.cljs, error_emit.cljc, events.cljc, frame.cljc, fx.cljc,
late_bind/directory.cljc, registrar.cljc, router.cljc, source_coords.cljc,
source_coords/open_endpoint.cljs, substrate/spine.cljs, test_support.cljc,
trace/projection.cljc.

WHY IT IS P0. The mayor loop commits .beads on its heartbeat. Anything that
commits with this index staged carries all 25 reverted source files with it —
a well-formed commit whose subject names something else entirely, which compiles
and which no gate catches, landing a silent 25-file revert on main. This is the
exact failure CLAUDE.md's merge-base bullet records ('a commit whose subject named
one record file carried 23 reverted source files with it, swept in by a git add -A
in a worktree whose base had moved'). Local builds are already reading the stale
files from disk.

SUGGESTED REMEDY, for the mayor to decide rather than for a worker to apply:
confirm no live agent intends these (nothing should be staged on main in the
mayor checkout), then 'git restore --staged --worktree implementation/core/src'
or equivalent, and re-verify with 'git status --porcelain' empty and
'git rev-parse HEAD' == 'git rev-parse origin/main'. Check the other checkouts
for the same staleness before assuming it is confined to this one.

ACCEPTANCE: git status --porcelain in the mayor checkout shows no staged
implementation/ paths, the working files match HEAD, and no commit on main
carries the re-frame.ui reversion.
close_reason:
REPAIRED BY THE MAYOR, 2026-08-19 11:52 AUSEST, within minutes of the report. Thank you for filing it rather than touching it — that was the right call, and the P0 was the right priority.

CONFIRMED BEFORE ACTING, not after. git status showed 25 paths under implementation/core/src/re_frame/ staged as M with the working tree matching the index, 610 insertions against 931 deletions. Direction tested rather than size: git grep -c -F 're-frame.ui' on the working core.cljc returned 2, and the same fixed-string search against HEAD:<same path> returned 0. A string present in the working tree and absent from HEAD means the content is OLDER, so this was a reversion and not an edit.

THE REPAIR: git checkout HEAD -- implementation/core/src/ — restoring index and working tree together, HEAD being equal to origin/main at aa44b550eb. Afterwards git status --porcelain returns zero paths, the index is empty, and HEAD still equals origin/main. Nothing was committed, nothing pushed, and no revert was attempted: your reading that only 11 of 25 matched a single point is exactly why git revert was the wrong tool.

THE MECHANISM, and it is the same one that hit worker/armconf-c4hhk's branch this morning: git checkout <rev> -- <path> STAGES as well as writes. That worker ran it to restore a substrate for its window, caught the contamination on its own branch with a three-dot merge-base diff, and rewrote its history. What survived was this — the same command's effect in the MAYOR checkout, which no branch diff can see. Recorded as bd memory checkout-rev-path-stages-silently.

YOUR STATED RISK WAS THE RIGHT ONE TO RAISE AND IT DID NOT MATERIALISE. The .beads heartbeat could indeed have swept all 25 in under an unrelated subject, which is the failure CLAUDE.md's merge-base bullet records. It did not, because scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh commits ONE explicit path — .beads/issues.jsonl — rather than staging what it finds. That is the guard working, and it is worth knowing it held under a live instance rather than only in prose. A hand-rolled git commit from that checkout would have taken all 25.

ONE THING I CANNOT ESTABLISH: which process ran the checkout in the mayor checkout, and when. It was absent at 11:07 and present by 11:47. The harness path-resolution leak CLAUDE.md warns about is the likeliest carrier. The remedy is unchanged either way — the mayor checkout's status is now part of what this loop reads, not only the branches'.

title: docs/the-mayor-method: cut the three non-README files to terse, fix the one genericity leak
description:
Mike set three standing requirements for docs/the-mayor-method on 2026-08-21. Measured
against the tree at origin/main the same day, two are already met and one is not.

MET — SELF-CONTAINED. Across all four files there are zero references to CLAUDE.md, to
.claude/commands, to MEMORY.md, AGENTS.md, TESTING.md, scripts/, to any bead id, or to
the project name. The two operator-specific rules the tree cannot carry - the project
stance and the chat voice - are correctly represented as SLOTS rather than as content
(dispatch-prompt-template.md:569 asks the mayor to paste the stance from the file that
owns it; loops.md:608 says "reassert any voice the operator has asked for"). That is the
right shape for a generic method.

MET — GENERIC, with one leak. dispatch-prompt-template.md:637 names a real pull request
number from this repository. That is the only project-specific string in the tree. The
`bd ...` command names that appear 13 times across the two large files are NOT leaks:
beads is the tracker this method is written for, README.md already names it as a
dependency, and Mike confirmed on 2026-08-21 that beads is the tracker in use.

NOT MET — TERSE AND TIGHT. The three non-README files are 151,006 bytes across 2,269
lines: bootstrap.md 19,633 / 350, dispatch-prompt-template.md 67,426 / 938,
loops.md 63,947 / 981. README.md (12,264) is EXEMPT - it is the human-facing
introduction and is explicitly not a destination for material moved out of the others.

WHAT MAKES THEM LONG IS NOT WAR STORIES. Only 53 of those 2,269 lines carry an incident
marker (a date, a measurement, a count of occurrences); the incident narrative was
already stripped when the method layer was split from the command layer. What is left is
DISCURSIVE METHOD PROSE: rules stated twice, rhetorical scaffolding between them
("Each of those is one line and each hides a way to be wrong. They are unpacked below."),
motivation given a full paragraph where a clause carries it, and consequences restated
after the rule that already implied them.

THE JOB is to cut that scaffolding while losing NO operational rule and NO named trap.
acceptance_criteria: Every operational rule and named trap present before the edit is present after it, proven by a before/after rule census. No heading added, renamed or removed. README.md unchanged. PR #8376 leak removed. check_doc_slugs.py, check_readme_links.py --ci and mkdocs build --strict all green.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8636 (2026-08-21) — RECORD CORRECTION, IMPLEMENTATION REMAINS COMPLETE. The close reason says no heading was added, renamed, or removed, but merge 9418f8e4 deliberately removes two duplicate bootstrap headings: 'Local-green is not CI' and 'Concurrent workers share the machine's temp directory'. The PR body states this correctly, external-anchor search is empty, and both rule bodies survive under dispatch-prompt-template.md, so no implementation work is reopened; this note only corrects the durable completion record.
close_reason: Done in PR #8636 (branch worker/tighten-bm1qm). Cut discursive scaffolding from the three non-README files: 151,006 -> 144,558 bytes, 2,269 -> 2,186 lines. Rule census 409 before / 409 accounted for after, with 3 entries deliberately merged into the Common preamble block that already carried them verbatim (named in the PR body). No heading added, renamed or removed in any of the four files, verified by diff. README.md untouched. Genericity leak removed: the pull-request number is gone and a scan for repo names, tracker ids, change numbers, out-of-tree paths, home paths, operator names and dates returns zero hits across all three files. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0, plus a planted-fault negative control that reddened on exactly the plant and restored to an identical blob hash. Two redundancies left standing as a call for the mayor: the 'Failure modes these shapes close' index, and bootstrap.md's overlap with the other two files.

      git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -cE '^\+  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$'

EXERCISE THE REGEX IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE YOU TRUST THE BULLET YOU WROTE, because a discriminator only ever tested where the answer is zero is untested. Verified at dispatch: it reads 1 on commit 366e4fca79, which added a job, and 0 on 4cf4d711a2, which added none. Reproduce both.

The hook is right and was NOT bypassed. The mayor checkout has been restored to clean, so you start from an unmodified origin/main.

THE GENERIC TREE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY GENERIC. A leak census over each file for repository, OS and person names returns 2, 0, 1, 1. It is not a stub awaiting content.

AND IT ALREADY CARRIES THE MERGE LOOP IN FULL. loops.md section 1 runs lines 46-369 with a section per clause: 'Clause 1 - zero failures is not green', 'Clause 2 - cancelled is not passed', 'Clause 3 - require the terminal state', 'Clause 4 - a settled rollup is not a quiet branch', 'Clause 5 - reading, not counting', then 'Merging', 'After each merge', 'When a change is not green'. title: ci: the Playwright --with-deps hang leaves NO annotation and now reds the trunk — the '0 failures in 183 samples' trade in test.yml has gone stale
description:
MEASURED by the mayor 2026-08-20 from CI, not from memory. Every premise below is a CLAIM — check each at source before acting.

THE TRUNK IS RED AND THE CAUSE IS ONE STEP. On main run 32206828695 (push, head 03b76d4eede2) FIVE browser jobs died together: CLJS hicasso HMR cancelled at 40.3 min (cap 40), CLJS hicasso controlled-input cancelled at 25.3 min (cap 25), Adapter testbed smokes cancelled at 30.3 min, docs/cljs playground cancelled at 15.3 min, Tenant-switcher testbed smoke FAILURE at 5.6 min. On the later main run 32216390799 (head 989680b16f, the trunk tip at filing) MCP conformance FAILED at 6.2 min and docs/cljs playground cancelled at 15.3 min again.

THE FAILING STEP NAMES ITSELF. In job 95959283361 the log reads: Playwright cache HIT and restored (key Linux-playwright-96be61e0...), then `Run npx playwright install --with-deps chromium || .github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh` at 04:41:54Z, then at 04:47:06Z `The action 'Install Playwright chromium (for hermetic browser preload)' has timed out after 5 minutes`, then `Terminate orphan process: pid (2730) (npm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium)`. The browser DOWNLOAD was cached and skipped, so the hang is in the apt hop under `--with-deps` — exactly the second mode `.github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh:176` already names under rf2-swos.

THE DEFECT THIS BEAD IS FILED ON IS NOT THE OUTAGE. It is that the hang is INVISIBLE. The `|| playwright-install-failed.sh` handler fires only on a NON-ZERO EXIT. A step the runner guillotines on `timeout-minutes` is KILLED, not failed, so the handler never runs: the job reports `cancelled`, prints no "no gate ran" annotation, and carries no verdict on the code under test. A reader then cannot tell provisioning from a real regression without opening the raw log, which is what this diagnosis cost.

THE TRADE IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN AND ITS NUMBER HAS GONE STALE. `.github/workflows/test.yml` (the comment block immediately above the `Install Playwright (Chromium + system deps)` step near line 4451) records the gap as deliberately unpatched: moving the cap into the command (`timeout 270 npx playwright install ...`) would fix it but breaks `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py`'s `^npx playwright install\b` setup pattern and would fail-open the gap map — "At 0 failures in 183 samples that trade is not worth taking." THAT DENOMINATOR IS NOW WRONG. This is at minimum SEVEN job-level incidents across two main runs and one PR run inside a single day. Re-derive the rate at the tip; do not carry my count forward by adding to it.

IN SCOPE
1. Re-derive the true failure rate from CI at the tip, and correct the stale comment wherever that trade is written down.
2. Close the no-annotation gap WITHOUT fail-opening `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py`. The gap map's pattern and the install call sites must keep agreeing, so whatever shape is chosen, change the pattern AND the call sites in ONE commit and prove the gap map still resolves every site.
3. Verify by PLANTING, not by assertion: make the chosen mechanism actually produce the annotation on a simulated hang, and show the red.

OUT OF SCOPE — do not widen any job cap. Do not remove `--with-deps` without evidence the system deps are already present on the runner image. Do not touch any measurement threshold or budget constant.

A reasoned REFUSAL is a complete and good deliverable: "the trade still holds at the re-derived rate, here is the number" is a correct outcome if that is what the evidence says.

HOT ZONE: `.github/workflows/*` and `.github/scripts/*` are one-toucher-at-a-time. This bead owns them.

title: hicasso: arm the within-run LEVEL witness — both modes still certify, and the high population is now n=3
description:
THE DEFECT SURVIVES ITS PARENT. rf2-77gz8 closed because its DECISION RULE was
discharged — the work count is identical across the mode, so different-work-per-
write is excluded. But the BUG that bead is named for is untouched: BOTH MODES
STILL CERTIFY. The leg witness asks whether a window's legs are ALIKE, and in
both modes they are; it has nothing to say about which of two LEVELS the window
sits at. So the gate passes a window whose level is ~13-20% off, and any figure
quoted from this arm from a single run is still a coin toss.

WHY IT CAN NOW BE ARMED, WHICH IS WHAT CHANGED. rf2-77gz8 held a within-run level
witness as a PROPOSAL explicitly because the high population was n = 1 RUN, which
cannot set a threshold. It is now n = 3 runs: alloc-9jrhi/bisect-1 (+3,792 B,
unarmed) and alloc-77gz8 run09 and run19 (+2,532 B, armed) — the latter two
committed with full per-round data and a work census.

THE WITNESS. Every run already records what it needs: compare the certified level
BEFORE the transition against the certified level after it, WITHIN one run, and
refuse when the step exceeds a declared bound. Both high runs hold ~19,004 at
rounds 1-3, ramp over rounds 4-5, and settle from round 6 — so the two populations
are separated inside a single run's own data, with no new instrument and no
second run.

THE POPULATIONS, from the committed corpus (this is the part to re-derive rather
than trust): the normal population's round-3-to-4 movement sits in the low
hundreds of bytes, and the mode's is thousands. rf2-77gz8's re-analysis quoted
-43 to +158 B normal against 3,912-3,948 B in the mode. NOTE that a re-derivation
using median-of-rounds-1-3 against median-of-rounds-4-6 gives a WIDER normal band
(about -961 to +896 B on the same datasets), so THE BAND DEPENDS ON THE
DEFINITION and the definition must be pinned before a threshold is set. Do not
take either band on trust.

WHAT TO DECIDE. Whether this becomes a REFUSAL (exit non-zero, like the leg
witness) or a recorded verdict that gates only what may be QUOTED. The arm's
figures are load-bearing for the published allocation series, and a refusal that
fires on a legitimate run is expensive; a verdict that nobody reads is useless.
rf2-77gz8's own framing was a refusal "when the step exceeds a declared bound".

CONSTRAINT. The rig blobs are the constancy guarantee the whole published series
rests on. Any witness must be computable from data ALREADY recorded — it is, see
above — so this is an analysis-side change, not a rig change, and must not alter
the bundle the arm compiles.

AND IT IS COUPLED TO rf2-zu82n — dispatch them TOGETHER, a233t FIRST. rf2-zu82n registers alloc_level_witness.test.cjs into the test:script-helpers spine; this bead is the fail-open INSIDE that same witness, where segmentsOf creates entries only for segment names that occur and adjudicates only when zero segments occur, so a record missing one whole measured segment formats CERTIFIED. Arming the spine gate before fixing the fail-open would wire in a gate that cannot fire on the defect it exists to catch — the exact shape this project keeps finding. Neither bead names the other; that is why this is recorded here.

FAIL-OPEN CLOSED, and the two decisions the bead asked for were already discharged. PR #8569, first of two commits.

THE PREMISE HELD AND WAS REPRODUCED FIRST. segmentsOf instantiated a map entry only the first time a segment name OCCURRED; the consumer loop iterated over exactly what existed; the only guard fired when ZERO occurred. Measured on the committed alloc-77gz8/run01 with uix-subs deleted from every one of its 18 rounds: CERTIFIED, half the arm's measurement gone, the verdict line still reading 'every segment holds its level across the transition'.

THE REPAIR. MEASURED_SEGMENTS declares what the floor arm measures. segmentsOf seeds its map from that roster, so a declared segment the record never mentions arrives at the consumer loop as an empty row list rather than as no entry at all, and is refused there under a third code, level-segment. A segment PRESENT but not declared is still adjudicated: the roster is a floor on what must be there, not a whitelist of what may be. adjudicate and scoreCorpus both take it as an option.

THE BAND DEFINITION, RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON TRUST. Pinned form is min(certified r1-5) -> median(certified r>=6). Re-derived: normal n=60 at 96..194 B (0.494%..1.015%), elevated n=40 at 2,616..3,984 B (13.766%..21.070%). NEITHER band this bead quoted is that one — -43..+158 B is the one-round form, which OVERLAPS the elevated band by 1,452 B on the larger corpus, and -961..+896 B is the median-of-r4-6 form. Both were already tabulated and defended in the shipped header; my re-derivation reproduces it exactly, so nothing was re-pinned.

REFUSAL vs RECORDED VERDICT was likewise already settled by this bead's earlier commits on main: it is a REFUSAL that exits non-zero. level-segment is a refusal for the same reason level-window is — a segment never recorded has no level to compare and no figure to quote, so refusing it and quoting nothing from it are the same statement.

COSTS THE CORPUS NOTHING, MEASURED. All 103 records carrying an alloc object carry exactly reagent-subs and uix-subs in every round. Corpus control unchanged in every figure: 101 admissible, 100 scored, 40 elevated, 60 normal, zero false refusals, zero misses, same bands, missing-segment 0.

PROVED AGAINST A REAL RECORD. The gate reads alloc-77gz8/run01 from disk, asserts it certifies intact, deletes one whole segment in memory, and asserts the result refuses with level-segment, reports the absent segment, still reads the survivor, and no longer formats CERTIFIED. Reverting the witness to its pre-repair state takes the gate to 9/14. Ten fixtures added, 26 -> 36.

title: hicasso: the floor arm is MULTI-modal, and the armed/unarmed confound on the high level is open
description:
MEASURED by rf2-77gz8's twenty-run window (PR #8513), record
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-second-mode-a-pre-registered-twenty-run-window.md,
twenty datasets under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-77gz8/.

THE OBSERVATION. The floor arm's elevated level is NOT a single fixed quantum.
Three settled levels now exist at the SAME revision (4a1537cb71), all on both
segments, all page-global and discrete:

  low    reagent-subs 19,100   uix-subs 19,540   (18 of 20 runs here, and the prior corpus)
  new    reagent-subs 21,632   uix-subs 22,072   +2,532  (run09, run19 — census ARMED)
  high   reagent-subs 22,892   uix-subs 23,332   +3,792  (alloc-9jrhi/bisect-1 — census UNARMED)

21,632 - 19,100 = 2,532 and 22,072 - 19,540 = 2,532 — the same discrete number on
two segments that share nothing but the page, exactly the bimodality signature
rf2-77gz8 described, at a DIFFERENT magnitude. So "bimodal at exactly 3,792 B"
understates the arm, and a future reading must not assume the step it finds is
3,792 B.

THE CONFOUND, and it is the whole question. The two +2,532 B runs were taken with
the work census ARMED (P0_WORK_COUNT=1); bisect-1 was UNARMED. rf2-n1b9h
established that arming does not move the LOW level — four armed runs reproduce
19,100 / 19,540 to the byte — but it never reached the high mode, so NOTHING
establishes that arming leaves the HIGH level alone. The census compiles three
counter increments into the write path, and the surviving mechanism for the mode
is a runtime codegen effect in exactly that path, so an interaction is not a
far-fetched hypothesis: it is the specific thing one would expect to interact.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT. Unarmed runs at 4a1537cb71 that REACH the mode, scored on
the same estimator (median over certified windows at round index >= 6 of that
window's legMedian). If the unarmed high level reads 22,892 / 23,332 and the
armed one reads 21,632 / 22,072, arming shifts the high mode and the two are ONE
level. If unarmed runs also produce 21,632 / 22,072, they are genuinely distinct
levels and the arm has at least three.

COST AND STOPPING RULE. The mode ran at 2 in 20 (10%) at this revision, and a run
is about 60 seconds including its :advanced build, so this is cheap. Pre-declare
the run count as rf2-77gz8's window did — the stopping-rule defect is the live
risk on a low-rate event, not a theoretical one.

NOTE the unarmed arm cannot answer any work-count question, by construction. This
bead is about the LEVEL only.
close_reason:
ANSWERED by a pre-registered seventy-run window (PR #8531). ARMING DOES NOT MOVE THE LEVEL — the confound is refuted from BOTH directions, and either alone settles it: nine UNARMED runs read EXACTLY 21,632/22,072 (this bead's own decision rule names that outcome as 'they are genuinely distinct levels'), and armed-13 reads 22,884/23,324 — the +3,792 level, ARMED, within 8 B on both segments. Sharper than either tally, armed-06 and unarmed-05 trace the elevated ramp BYTE-IDENTICALLY for ten consecutive rounds on reagent-subs and eleven on uix-subs, through the step and into the settle: the same curve on two different bundles. The LOW level is byte-identical across arms too (19,100/19,540, 16 each), re-confirming rf2-n1b9h on a larger sample.

So rf2-77gz8's high-mode readings are NOT instrument-contaminated and neither is any other in the corpus; every downstream bead resting on them is unaffected. The arm has at least four settled levels and arming gates none of them.

Exactly 70 runs taken (35 ARMED, 35 UNARMED, strictly alternating), count committed before the runner ran once, sized against the ARMED arm's own re-derived rate. 69 admissible with ZERO control or read-back exclusions; armed-25 produced NO reading (Chromium failed to launch) yet exited 1 exactly like the 69 good runs — committed as evidence of its own exclusion and NOT replaced.

LIMITS: the MECHANISM is untouched, and the +3,792 level is seen once in 69 readings — enough to refute 'arming gates it', not enough to speak to its rate. Two unanticipated findings carried onward: the mode's RATE is not a property of the revision (rf2-6kxub), and the elevated level has page-global fine structure at -12 and +96 B, present in both arms (recorded on the studio page, not filed — it is a description of the arm, not a defect).

CLOSED because the confound this bead was filed to resolve is decided, and decided in the direction that leaves the corpus standing. No rig file touched.

title: [xray] refuse :rf.adapter/hicasso — the kind now exists and the denylist's premise is stale
description:
FUNCTIONAL, and it is a degradation rather than a missing nicety.

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs` carries `react-element-render-kinds`, a DENYLIST
of adapter `:kind`s whose `:render` slot takes substrate-native React ELEMENTS — Xray's shell is
hiccup, so it cannot mount through them and refuses loudly-but-cleanly instead (one console.warn
plus an inspectable status diagnostic). Unknown kinds keep today's PERMISSIVE behaviour, by
design, so the mount tests can ride plain-atom.

That set is `#{:rf.adapter/ui :rf.adapter/uix :rf.adapter/helix :rf.adapter/freehand}`, and its
docstring reasons explicitly from Hicasso minting no kind:

  "HICASSO IS COVERED BY THE `:rf.adapter/uix` ENTRY, AND HAS NO ENTRY OF ITS OWN BECAUSE IT
   MINTS NO KIND (rf2-wtznc). There is no `:rf.adapter/hicasso` — Hicasso ships no adapter at
   all. ... The absence of a hicasso member is therefore correct and load-bearing, not an
   oversight."

That premise is now false. rf2-hvr5h shipped `re-frame.hicasso.substrate` (PR #8512) with
`:kind :rf.adapter/hicasso`, and `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md` now teaches
`(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` as the default. A Hicasso page that follows the chapter reports
`:rf.adapter/hicasso`, which is not in the set, so Xray takes the permissive path and mounts a
hiccup shell into an element-shaped `:render` — an uncaught React child error where the clean
diagnostic used to be.

THE FIX IS ONE MEMBER PLUS A DOCSTRING PARAGRAPH, and the structural reason is exactly the one
already written for `:rf.adapter/freehand`: `re-frame.hicasso.substrate` builds its adapter from
`re-frame.substrate.spine/make-react-adapter`, so its `:render` IS the spine's element-shaped one.
The paragraph quoted above must be rewritten rather than left standing beside a contradicting
member — it is the piece a future reader would trust.

A page that keeps installing UIx is unaffected.

title: hicasso: count the WORK inside a measured window, to split rf2-77gz8's two surviving candidates
description:
THE ONE OBSERVATION rf2-77gz8 NEEDS. rf2-77gz8's re-analysis (PR #8483, record docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-second-mode-is-per-write-and-the-controls-never-move.md) narrowed the floor arm's 3,792 B second mode from five candidates to TWO, and showed the committed corpus cannot separate them:

  (a) DIFFERENT WORK per write -- a re-entrant registration, a duplicated reaction, an extra pass.
  (b) A V8 TIER/DEOPT in the compiled write path -- most specifically a loss of escape analysis, which turns elided allocations into real ones at a fixed cost per invocation.

Both predict exactly what was measured: a byte-exact, per-write, page-global constant appearing at a work-count boundary, with the controls untouched. Nothing committed distinguishes them, because `alloc-tick` counts WRITES, not the work inside one.

WHAT TO BUILD. A monotone WORK COUNTER read per measured window, beside the existing byte counters: event-handler invocations, subscription recomputations, and render calls. Record it in the dataset the way rf2-erre5 records the raw sample stream.

WHAT IT DECIDES, in one reading. Take a high-mode and a low-mode window.
  - Counts IDENTICAL while bytes differ by 3,792/write  ->  (a) is EXCLUDED, and the residue is per-invocation allocation, i.e. a runtime codegen effect.
  - Counts DIFFER                                        ->  (a) is ESTABLISHED and (b) is excluded.

WHY THIS RATHER THAN V8 TRACING FIRST. It is page-side; it is a CENSUS OF MONOTONE COUNTERS and so reads the same on a loaded box (no quiet machine, no fleet drain); it needs no --trace-deopt and no --allow-natives-syntax; and it decides the WHOLE remaining question rather than confirming one branch. V8 tracing (--trace-deopt, or %GetOptimizationStatus) is the CONFIRMING SECOND move, and only if the counts come back identical.

SECOND DELIVERABLE, from the same instrument. rf2-77gz8's within-run level witness is held as a PROPOSAL at n = 1 run. The round-4 step separates the two populations cleanly on the committed data -- normal -43 to +158 B (n = 11 segment-runs) against the mode's 3,912-3,948 B (n = 2 segment-runs, ONE run) -- but one run cannot set a threshold. A run that reproduces the mode supplies the second observation and lets the witness be armed.

FENCE AND SEQUENCING. This edits the rig under implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/ (p0_heap.cljs and/or p0_run.cjs). Those blobs are the constancy guarantee the whole alloc-9jrhi series and the rf2-nkeba figures are published against, so this is a DELIBERATE, SEPARATE act: it must not run inside a measurement window, and its first output is NOT a published figure. rf2-77gz8 was left open for exactly this.

BEWARE. The bench suite is heavyweight -- two concurrent runs WEDGE rather than fail, holding several gigabytes each and returning nothing. One run at a time, never concurrent.

WHAT LANDED. Three monotone counters — event-handler invocations, subscription recomputations, render calls — read at every measured window's open and close and recorded beside tick0/tick as work0/work/workDelta. Verified against counts it HAD to hit rather than merely nonzero: at B=24 over a 7-write window, renders = 168 and subs = 168xR (168/504/1176/3360 at R=1/3/7/20) on all four substrate columns, with controls reading 0/0/0 every round.

THE CONSTANCY GUARANTEE IS NOW PROVABLE RATHER THAN PROMISED, which was this bead's own central risk — the rig blobs are what the whole alloc-9jrhi series and the rf2-nkeba figures are published against. counting? is a goog-define defaulting to false and all three call sites are MACROS, so an :advanced build constant-folds the gate and drops the counter array entirely: an unarmed build compiles the bundle this rig compiled before the census existed. Closed by construction, not by discipline.

THE READING WAS REFUSED AND THE REFUSAL IS SOUND. The decision rule needs one high-mode window and one low-mode window; SIX RUNS PRODUCED NO HIGH-MODE WINDOW. So rf2-77gz8's candidates (a) different work per write and (b) a V8 tier/deopt both stand untouched. THE ROUND-4 STEP IS NOT A WORK-COUNT EFFECT. That is a claim about the STEP and explicitly not about rf2-77gz8's 3,792 B rider.

AND IT ALREADY NARROWED A SIBLING. rf2-rs8q6's premise is that a window's legs are not W repetitions of one work unit; the constant census excludes the whole different-work-per-leg family and leaves the per-invocation-cost family. rf2-77gz8 stays OPEN for that, on the worker's recommendation and mine — its within-run level witness is still a PROPOSAL at n = 1.

title: hicasso: the allocation window cannot drive both writes in one process - V2 needs a PAIRED mode before its residual can be assessed
description:
FOUND BY rf2-0gjqi's re-analysis, 2026-08-18, record docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-eight-signs-are-one-block.md (PR #8458). No window was taken and no rig file was touched -- this is a design finding derived at source.

THE PROBLEM. allocation-instrument-rework.md:231-232 requires the two writes to be compared as a same-page/same-run pair. The instrument cannot do that. ALLOC_WRITE is read once from process.env at module scope (implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs:1504), ALLOC_WRITE_SPECS has exactly two members and no paired option (:1490), and the resolved kind is passed into every arm window of the run (:2335, :2342). One process therefore drives ONE write, so every write-all vs write-page comparison this instrument has ever produced differences two sequential process runs in a fixed order.

WHAT THAT COSTS, measured rather than asserted. On the V1/V2 re-run window the eight mid-rung sign comparisons all read page below all, and that unanimity carries no information: the eight cells share one run order, share one floor per segment per write (the reagent-subs floor certified 4 of 6 rounds under all and all four of that segment's mid-rung cells report n = 4, so they difference against the same four floor windows), and rf2-77gz8's second floor mode moves both segments by exactly the same 3,792 B, which merges the two segments as well. Eight cells, one draw. A shared floor offset of 2,472 B/write on reagent-subs and 928 B/write on uix-subs reverses every sign, and three runs at one revision under one write span 3,852 / 3,912 B/write in certified floor median.

WHAT TO BUILD. A paired mode that drives BOTH kinds at each arm inside one round and records them as a pair.

  (1) THE PAGE ALREADY AFFORDS IT. allocWindow takes the write as a per-window kind argument (implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_heap.cljs:1182-1188): all? is (= kind "write-all") and write? is (or (= kind "write") all?). Both are values of a parameter the page reads once per window. Only the driver's process-global pin prevents pairing.

  (2) THE FLOOR MUST BE PAIRED TOO. The floor is the dominant shared term -- see above. A paired mode that pairs only the arms leaves it intact and buys nothing.

  (3) THE RECORD MUST CARRY THE PAIRING. A pair needs to be identifiable as a pair in the raw record, so a later estimator can take matched within-round differences rather than reconstructing them from two files.

  (4) THE PIN AT p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs MUST BE AMENDED, NOT DELETED. Its content is criterion 6's separation: a reader of any row can tell FROM THE ROW which write produced it. Under a paired mode a row carries both, so the pin becomes an assertion that each recorded window names its own kind. Same delicacy rf2-gxrr called out for the previous amendment.

WHAT IS NOT ASKED FOR. No gate widened, no band moved, no threshold touched. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES stays 6, ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays 600,000, tau stays where it is.

SEQUENCING. rf2-77gz8 should be resolved alongside or first. Whether the ladder ARMS carry the floor's second mode is untested -- the mode was observed on a floor-plan run with no arms in it -- and that single unknown decides whether a page-global level cancels in arm minus floor or not. A paired mode gives the instrument the ability to answer it, because it puts an arm window and a floor window under both writes in one round for the first time.

BLOCKS rf2-0gjqi, whose audit says explicitly: after the paired mode lands, compare matched certified pairs.
close_reason:
PR #8461 (branch worker/paired-irxrw). The allocation window can now drive BOTH writes in one process.

WHAT LANDED, against the four requirements.

(1) P0_ALLOC_WRITE gains a third value, paired. The selection became a LIST rather than a spec: ALLOC_WRITE_SPECS is untouched and still holds exactly two writes -- paired is not a third one -- and a new ALLOC_WRITE_SELECTIONS names which of them a run drives and in what order. The arm loop runs ONE PASS PER (segment, leg), so every arm is measured under both writes inside the same round, on the same page, in the same process. Off paired there is one leg and the body issues exactly the calls it issued before, in the same order.

The pass RE-SEEDS at B, and that is not incidental. :p0/write-all rebuilds :cells at cells-n whatever is mounted while :p0/write-page rebuilds at (count (:cells db)), and the mounted boundaries read cells 0..(B/roots-1) either way -- so a page leg inheriting an all leg's grid would rebuild 300 cells, BE the bulk write, and pass the warm-write read-back with nothing to say so. prepare(segment, B) was already the first statement of every segment pass; running one pass per leg is what keeps that true, rather than a new page-side door. A second commit pins it from the page's own sources.

THE LEG ORDER ALTERNATES on round parity, exactly as the segment order does. A fixed order would confound the write with within-round position, which is the defect this bead exists to remove. Over the six default rounds each leg leads three times.

(2) THE FLOOR IS PAIRED TOO. The floor is an arm of the plan, so the leg pass takes it under both writes like every other arm, and the pin asserts both its legs by name rather than leaving it to follow from the loop.

(3) THE RECORD CARRIES THE PAIRING. Every recorded window names its own writeSelector and write and carries pairKey -- the arm key its legs share -- so an estimator groups on a field rather than parsing a key or reconciling two files. Each round records the leg order it ACTUALLY drove, after the parity flip. Fits are per write, so no slope is a line through a mixture.

(4) THE PIN IS AMENDED, NOT DELETED, and rf2-gxrr's delicacy was read first. Its CONTENT is criterion 6's separation and its SHAPE was a single interpolated spec, adequate only because a process drove one write. Under paired the claim moves to WINDOW granularity: the amended pin asserts each recorded window names its own kind, adjudicated over a RECORD through the shipped exported allocWriteProvenance rather than matched in source. It refuses an unpaired-shaped record, a half pair, a window naming a write the run did not drive, and a window whose selector and event disagree.

ADDITIVE, measured rather than asserted. The same synthetic row driven through origin/main's summariseAlloc and the amended one prints byte-identical output on all three plans (8103 / 4749 / 4299 chars). The probe was shown non-vacuous by a one-character plant that made it report DIFFERS. The JSON record gains two row fields, one round field and three per-window provenance fields; no figure, gate, certificate or printed line reads them except the pin.

NO GATE WIDENED, no band moved, no threshold touched. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES stays 6, ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays 600,000, tau stays where it is. p0_heap.cljs, p0_arms.cljs and p0_fixture.cljc are untouched -- the bead's claim that the page already affords per-window kinds was verified at source and holds.

NO MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN OR PUBLISHED. rf2-77gz8 was not chased; what this removes for it is the cross-process confound, not the mode.

GATES: p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs 86 passed before, 93 passed after, exit 0 captured; a planted fault in allocWriteProvenance took it to 2/93 failed exit 1, red on the amended pin's own assertions, restored and verified by git hash-object. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh ran to completion twice, exit 0 both times, classifier docs=false jvm=true node=true.

rf2-0gjqi stays OPEN: its audit obligation -- compare matched certified pairs -- is unmet until a window is taken through this mode.

title: hicasso: the floor arm's rise/W is BIMODAL at exactly 3,792 B and both modes certify
description:
MEASURED by rf2-9jrhi 2026-08-18 (PR #8457), record docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-bisect-is-flat-and-the-floor-has-a-second-mode.md, eight datasets committed under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-9jrhi/. Filed rather than chased: rule 3 of a measurement window forbids improving the rig mid-window, and identifying the mechanism needs an instrument this one may not build.

THE OBSERVATION. Two runs of the floor arm at B = 24 under :p0/write-all, taken twelve minutes apart, on the SAME instrument and the SAME implementation/core/src commit (4a1537cb71), both with a passing positive control and 0 unverified read-backs, differ in steady-state rise/W by EXACTLY 3,792 B on BOTH segments:

  run 2   reagent-subs 22,892 B/write   uix-subs 23,332 B/write
  run 7   reagent-subs 19,100 B/write   uix-subs 19,540 B/write

22,892 - 19,100 = 3,792. 23,332 - 19,540 = 3,792. The same number on two segments that share nothing but the page, so it is page-global and discrete rather than proportional.

IT IS A TRANSITION WITHIN A RUN, not a property of a run. Run 2 reads 18,908 - 18,980 at rounds 1-3, steps at round 4, and holds 22,892 for the remaining fourteen rounds. Run 7 never steps. A property of the revision would have been present from round 1.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY THE EXISTING GATES DO NOT SEE IT. BOTH modes CERTIFY. Round 2 of run 2 reads legs [18980, 19492, 18980, 18980, 18980, 18980], round 12 reads [22892, 22892, 22892, 22892, 22892, 23640] -- each is six byte-stable repetitions of one work unit, zero falling steps, zero refusals, worst leg deviation 2.70% and 3.27% against a tau of 25%. The leg witness asks whether a window/s legs are ALIKE and in both cases they are; it has nothing to say about which of two LEVELS the window sits at. So the certificate passes a window whose level is 20% off.

CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY PUBLISHED SINGLE-RUN FIGURE. The between-run spread at one revision (3,792 B) is LARGER than the 982 - 3,456 B across-time effect rf2-nkeba and rf2-9jrhi were trying to resolve, and larger than the 1,769 / 1,765 B floor drop V2 accepted in rf2-2rtt6.140. Any F_old quoted from one run therefore carries an uncertainty exceeding the differences it is being used to argue about. This is a plausible mechanism for the whole across-time artefact.

WHAT IS RULED OUT. Not the heap trajectory: the absolute used-heap level at each window/s opening (recoverable since rf2-erre5) tracks within 8 KB between the high run and a low one across all eighteen rounds, ending 6,191,823 B against 6,184,236 B. Not a collection: zero falling steps in the quoted windows. Not the prime term: its certified-window median is 6,801 - 6,864 B in every one of six control-passing runs regardless of revision or mode.

CANDIDATES, none preferred: a V8 tier or deoptimisation transition in the compiled write path; a page-global allocation the counter attributes to the leg; an :advanced build artefact.

UNRESOLVED: whether the mode is revision-dependent. Observed once in eight runs, all three of which at 4a1537cb71 (one high, two low), against zero of four at other revisions. One in three against zero in four decides nothing.

RELATED. rf2-rs8q6 is the round-indexed dispersion of a window/s legs -- the SPREAD within a window. This is the LEVEL of the window, which is a different quantity and survives the gate that one is about.

comments.text:
MAYOR 2026-08-18, BACKLOG REREAD — DISPATCHED, and recording WHY IT SAT so the gap is not repeated.

HOW IT SURFACED. The reread reads the raw open list rather than a ready view, and this bead was the only P1 that is UNASSIGNED, UNBLOCKED and carries ZERO COMMENTS. Every other P1 on the list is an epic, is @Mike, or has a recorded blocker. So it had no reason on it for not being dispatched, and none was ever given — it was simply passed over on tick after tick while smaller, more legible work went out. **A bead with no notes is not a bead with no claim; it is a bead nobody has argued about**, and on a busy list that reads as low-signal when it is the opposite.

WHY IT SHOULD HAVE GONE OUT EARLIER, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: its estimand is ALLOCATION — bytes per write, a census of monotone counters — so it reads the same on a loaded box. **It never needed the quiet machine and never needed to wait behind the clock lane.** I had been treating 'the measurement lane' as one queue draining behind one drain. It is two lanes with different physics, and only one of them is scarce. The allocation half sat idle through several ticks in which the box was free and I dispatched documentation instead.

WHY IT IS P1 AND NOT A CURIOSITY, restated from its own description so a future reader does not have to reconstruct it: two runs of the floor arm at B = 24 under :p0/write-all, twelve minutes apart, on the SAME instrument and the SAME implementation/core/src commit 4a1537cb71, both with a passing positive control and 0 unverified read-backs, differ in steady-state rise/W by EXACTLY 3,792 B on BOTH segments (22,892 vs 19,100 and 23,332 vs 19,540). Same discrete number on two segments sharing nothing but the page, so page-global and discrete rather than proportional. And it is a TRANSITION WITHIN a run: run 2 reads 18,908-18,980 at rounds 1-3, steps at round 4, holds for fourteen more; run 7 never steps. **BOTH MODES CERTIFY** — the gate cannot tell them apart, so any figure taken from this arm is a coin toss between two stable values about 20% apart, and everything downstream that cites the floor inherits it.

WHAT THE DISPATCH ASKS FIRST, deliberately: whether the mechanism can be identified from the EIGHT DATASETS ALREADY COMMITTED under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-9jrhi/, with no new run at all. Round-level data showing a step at round 4 in one run and never in another is a strong substrate, and a conclusion drawn from existing data beats one needing a fresh window. The brief also requires the candidate mechanisms to be ENUMERATED and says which are EXCLUDED — a discrete page-global 3,792 B has several plausible causes (an array's doubling, a lazily-installed cache, a JIT tier transition, a GC promotion, a re-entrant registration) and an unexcluded alternative is the difference between a finding and a guess.

THE FILER'S REFUSAL IS PRESERVED AS A CONSTRAINT rather than overridden: rf2-9jrhi filed rather than chased because rule 3 forbids improving the rig mid-window and the mechanism may need an instrument that window could not build. This dispatch MAY build one — but only after establishing the committed data cannot answer it, and as a deliberate separate act with its own controls, not by drifting into rig-building because analysis got hard.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RE-ANALYSED 2026-08-18 (worker/bimodal-77gz8, PR #8483, draft). NO window taken, NO instrument built, NO rig file touched. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-second-mode-is-per-write-and-the-controls-never-move.md. Everything below is re-derived from the eight committed alloc-9jrhi datasets, plus the driver read at the blob the runs executed (e88d2be45e...).

BEAD STAYS OPEN. The mechanism is NOT identified. Four candidates are excluded on evidence; two survive and the corpus cannot separate them.

ESTABLISHED FROM THE COMMITTED DATA ALONE.
1. The mode is a PER-WRITE cost. The prime work unit is ONE write and carries the same step as each of the six measured writes: +3,792 B on the legs and +3,792/+3,808 B on the prime, on BOTH segments. (The 16 B is one sampler read's footprint - every `gaps` entry in every window.)
2. An INDEPENDENT counter confirms it. `cdpBracket` is Runtime.getHeapUsage() read over CDP from OUTSIDE the page: 24,380-26,566 B per window higher in the high run, against 7 x 3,792 = 26,544 for a seven-write window. Two counters sharing no code path agree.
3. THE CONTROLS NEVER MOVE. Across all 8 datasets, 4 revisions, every round, idle/ctl1/ctl2 take exactly ONE value each: 16 / 8,064 / 3,264. Fifty-four control windows in the high run read what the low run's read.
4. The two runs did IDENTICAL work in IDENTICAL order - `tick0` agrees at all 18 rounds (21, 105, 133, ..., 1001).
5. THE ROUND-4 TRANSITION IS UNIVERSAL. Every one of the seven 18-round runs steps at the round 3->4 boundary: the other six by -43 to +158 B, this run by 3,948/3,912 B. The AS-RUN driver has no round-4 behaviour - its only round-indexed statement is `round % 2`, a parity flip shared with rounds 0 and 2, neither of which steps.
6. The step decomposes EXACTLY: 19,100 + 3,792 = 22,892 and 19,540 + 3,792 = 23,332. The high mode is the universal round-4 step PLUS a discrete 3,792 B rider at the same boundary.
7. The extra bytes are TRANSIENT GARBAGE: 743,232 B more allocated over rounds 4-17, against a 4,812 B difference in the closing heap.
8. The transition is bracketed to ticks 224-252 and did not disturb the control path that ran inside the bracket.

EXCLUDED, with the evidence.
- An :advanced/static build artefact -- the high run read LOW at its OWN rounds 1-3 before stepping; no static build property changes within one page's life.
- A page-global allocation the counter attributes to the leg -- the 54 control windows, plus confirmation by a second counter outside the page.
- A collection / GC generation promotion -- zero falling steps, heaps close within 4,812 B, and a collection moves a level down not up.
- A growing array's doubling or a one-time lazily-installed cache -- both pay ONCE; this pays on ~196 subsequent writes and is not retained.
- The prime term -- primeExcess moves 16 B while the baseline moves 3,792 B.

SURVIVING, and NOT separated by anything committed.
(a) DIFFERENT WORK per write (re-entrant registration, duplicated reaction, extra pass). `alloc-tick` counts WRITES, not handler invocations, so the identical schedule does not speak to it.
(b) A V8 TIER/DEOPT in the compiled write path, most specifically a loss of escape analysis. Consistent with everything above and the only candidate that also explains why all seven runs transition at the same round; but no dataset records V8 tier state.

THE ONE OBSERVATION THAT SEPARATES THEM. Add a monotone WORK COUNTER to the measured window - event-handler invocations, subscription recomputations, render calls, counted per window beside the byte counters - and read it in a high-mode and a low-mode window. Identical counts while bytes differ by 3,792/write EXCLUDES (a) and leaves per-invocation allocation. Differing counts ESTABLISHES (a). Preferred over V8 tracing as the first move: page-side, a census of monotone counters (so a loaded box is fine), no --trace-deopt and no quiet machine, and it decides the WHOLE remaining question. Filed as a follow-up.

THE BOTH-MODES-CERTIFY HAZARD - a disposition, held as a PROPOSAL not a gate. The mode announces itself WITHIN a single run, in a quantity every run already records: the round-4 step is -43 to +158 B in the normal population (n=11 segment-runs) and 3,912-3,948 B in the mode (n=2 segment-runs, one run) - non-overlapping, a factor of 24 apart. A within-run level witness comparing the pre-round-4 certified level against the post-round-4 one, refusing when the step exceeds a declared bound, would have refused the high run FROM ITS OWN DATA, with no new instrument and no second run. NOT armed here: the high population is n=1 RUN, which cannot set a threshold. The instrument above would also reproduce the mode and supply the second observation.

NOT CONCLUDED. The mechanism (two candidates survive - nothing licenses attributing this to a deopt). Revision-dependence: the count is unchanged (one high of three at 4a1537cb71, zero of four elsewhere); what IS added is that the round-4 transition is present at EVERY revision measured, so the runs differ in the SIZE of the step, not its presence or timing - which reframes the open question but does not answer it. No bound on the mode's rate (one in eight, no null arm bounds it). Nothing about wall-clock (no timing quantity computed; the datasets record none). No published figure revised - the rf2-9jrhi estimand was re-derived and reproduces to the byte.

ESTIMATOR, named precisely: the MEDIAN, over CERTIFIED windows at round index >= 6, of that window's `legMedian`. Not a mean, and not the driver's printed B/write column.

MAYOR — rf2-n1b9h HAS REPORTED (PR #8505) AND THIS BEAD IS NOT ANSWERED. Recording what it did and did not settle, so nobody reads the instrument's arrival as a verdict. 2026-08-19 00:32 AUSEST.

THE READING WAS REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE CORRECT DELIVERABLE. rf2-n1b9h's decision rule needs one high-mode window and one low-mode window. SIX RUNS PRODUCED NO HIGH-MODE WINDOW. THE REFUSAL IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT FAULT, AND THE WORKER PROVED IT RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT. At 4a1537cb71 four armed runs reproduce rf2-9jrhi's published LOW-mode figures TO THE BYTE — 19,100 and 19,540 — ten days later. At HEAD the arm lands within 6 B of bisect-7. And idle/ctl1/ctl2 take the same single values (16 / 8,064 / 3,264) the whole unarmed corpus takes. An instrument that reproduces a ten-day-old published figure byte-for-byte is working; the mode simply did not appear.

WHAT IS NOW SETTLED, AND IT IS NOT THIS BEAD'S QUESTION: across 216 arm windows and 1,512 writes the work census takes ONE value, 7/0/0, identical on BOTH SIDES of the universal round-4 step. title: fix the racy expunge step in jvm-weak-node-record-does-not-strong-pin-its-abandoned-reaction
description:
`implementation/core/test/re_frame/observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:2471`
(`jvm-weak-node-record-does-not-strong-pin-its-abandoned-reaction`) is
NON-DETERMINISTIC and reddened the `jvm-core-prod-gate` CI job on PR #8429
(run 32027783986, job 95381750435) with a diff that cannot reach it — the
branch's only in-lane file is a DOCSTRING-only edit to `error_emit.cljc`.

FAILURE OBSERVED
  FAIL in (jvm-weak-node-record-does-not-strong-pin-its-abandoned-reaction)
       (observation_port_cljs_test.cljc:2507)
  the abandoned handle was reclaimed once its node record's weak key died
  expected: (gc-until-cleared? handle-ref)
  actual:   (not (gc-until-cleared? #object[java.lang.ref.WeakReference ...]))

The FIRST assertion (line 2499, `rx-ref`) passed; only the SECOND (line 2507,
`handle-ref`) failed. That split is the whole diagnosis.

MECHANISM — clearing and ENQUEUEING are two separate steps
`node-records` is a `java.util.Collections/synchronizedMap
(java.util.WeakHashMap.)` (`substrate/observation.cljc:716`). A WeakHashMap
drops its strong reference to an entry's VALUE only in `expungeStaleEntries`,
which is driven by its private ReferenceQueue and runs only when a MAP
OPERATION is invoked.

`gc-until-cleared?` (line 2454) returns true the moment `(.get wref)` is nil —
i.e. as soon as the GC CLEARS the referent. But HotSpot clears a weak reference
during the collection and then has the ReferenceHandler thread move it to its
ReferenceQueue ASYNCHRONOUSLY, afterwards. So there is a real window in which
`rx-ref` reads cleared while the WeakHashMap's own key reference has not yet
been enqueued.

The test performs its single expunge-triggering map operation at line 2506:

    (.size ^java.util.Map @#'obs/node-records)

If that `.size` lands inside the window, `expungeStaleEntries` finds an empty
queue and removes nothing. The table still strongly holds the record VALUE ->
:owners -> handle. The following `gc-until-cleared? handle-ref` then runs 40
GC cycles WITHOUT PERFORMING ANY FURTHER MAP OPERATION, so nothing ever
expunges, the handle stays strongly reachable, and the loop returns false —
deterministically, for that run. A loaded CI runner widens the window, which
is why this shows up in CI and not locally.

The property under test (rf2-vxgfnd.37 — the value must not strong-reference
its own weak key) is genuinely satisfied: the reaction WAS collected, which is
exactly what line 2499 proves. Only the second-order observation is racy.

REMEDY (suggested, not prescribed)
Move the expunge-triggering map operation INSIDE the retry loop rather than
performing it once before it — e.g. a `gc-until-cleared?` variant that calls
`(.size ...)` on each cycle, or drain-then-poll on a ReferenceQueue. A single
pre-loop `.size` cannot be made reliable, because the enqueue it depends on
has no happens-before edge with the clear that the loop is watching.

DO NOT weaken the assertion or add it to the prod-gate known-red roster: the
assertion is correct and the property is real. It is the fixture's timing that
is wrong.

EVIDENCE THE FAILURE IS NOT PR #8429's
- The exact CI command, `bash scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh`
  (.github/workflows/test.yml:1525), run three times on that branch's head
  e93fc922b1 in a worker worktree: exit 0 each time, 1986 tests / 8696
  assertions, 0 failures (same counts as the failing CI run).
- `implementation/scripts/**` is not on core's classpath (core deps.edn
  `:paths ["src"]`), so neither the cljs-probe nor the bundle-isolation
  self-test change is even loaded by this lane.
- The one in-lane file, `error_emit.cljc`, changes only text inside the
  `dispatch-on-error!` docstring string literal; no form is touched.
close_reason: Fixed on worker/orphans-k9rzr (PR #8429, commit c6ef2754ef, rebased to fcaf1e2c0c). gc-until-cleared? gains a poke arity that runs once per cycle INSIDE the bounded loop; the enrolled leg of jvm-weak-node-record-does-not-strong-pin-its-abandoned-reaction passes (.size @#'obs/node-records) through it instead of calling it once before the loop. That closes the clear-versus-enqueue window: a WeakHashMap releases an entry's VALUE only in expungeStaleEntries, which runs on a map operation and drains the map's own ReferenceQueue, and a Reference is CLEARED during collection but ENQUEUED afterwards by the ReferenceHandler thread. Whichever cycle follows the enqueue now expunges; no happens-before edge is relied on. This is the discipline the two rf2-8vvdo provenance proofs in the same file already use (lines 3540 and 3664) — this fixture was the one site never brought up to it, and rf2-8vvdo's own comment records the same asymmetry. The assertion is UNCHANGED: nothing relaxed, nothing deleted, nothing added to the prod-gate known-red roster. Control: replacing the poke with a throwing lambda reddened the gate at exit 1 with the planted text printed verbatim, reachable only from the loop's :else branch — proving the runtime executed the new path and that poke runs per-cycle; counts identical (1986/8696) either side; restore verified by git hash-object. bash scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh exit 0 on the final base.

title: hicasso: bisect F_old's surviving ~1-3.5 KB drop across 2026-08-08 -> 2026-08-13, on ONE instrument
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-nkeba, 2026-08-17, PR #8434, record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-controls-target-is-not-the-quantity-it-is-read-against.md

WHAT rf2-nkeba SETTLED, so this bead starts from the right place. V1's across-time clause failed by a published 16 - 20%. Most of that is a comparison artefact: the 2026-08-08 target is a round MEDIAN of rise/W taken on a pre-prime, pre-certificate instrument over an UNSELECTED population, while today's figures are per-window values on a CERTIFIED subset with the prime excluded. Three differences at once, none of them documented.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, and it is this bead's subject. Against the LOWEST of the six 2026-08-08 rounds with its largest step removed — the most generous like-for-like the surviving artefacts support — today's certified readings are still low by:

  reagent-subs   >= 982 B   (4.7% - 7.0%)
  uix-subs       >= 2,472 B (10.7% - 14.9%)

A gap at every cell. Smaller than published, and real.

WHAT IS ALREADY ELIMINATED, so this bead does not re-tread it:

- THE RESEEDED PAGE WIDTH — REFUTED on two independent grounds. `:p0/write-all` is byte-identical at 4a1537cb71 and 2e993181f8 and rebuilds `cells-n` = 300 regardless of the seed; the floor arm holds no subscription and the seed runs inside `prepare!` outside the measured region; and V1's own first clause reads F_old flat to <= 117 B over a 24x seeded-width range, i.e. <= ~351 B extrapolated to 300 cells.
- THE PRIME — accounted, and re-derived on the 2026-08-08 data itself at ~6,231 / ~6,267 B (1,038 / 1,045 per write), SMALLER than the pooled 6,966 the corpus subtracts.
- THE WORK UNIT — byte-identical at both revisions: same three statements, same drain split, same stride-2 sampling, same `write-all!` and `dispatch-sync!`.
- THE TOOLCHAIN — playwright 1.59.1, react/react-dom 19.2.0, shadow-cljs 3.4.10 at both revisions. CAVEAT: the 2026-08-08 dataset records no runtime version, so a resident-binary difference is neither ruled in nor out.

WHAT IS LEFT. Drift in the event pipeline. The drop was already present by 2026-08-13 (legMedian 19,781 / 20,446), so it happened inside 2026-08-08 -> 2026-08-13. Twenty-two commits landed under implementation/core/src in that interval and NONE was shown to be it.

WHAT THIS BEAD WOULD RUN. A bisection: the floor arm at B = 24 under write-all, at two or three revisions spanning that interval, on the CURRENT instrument at every point so the estimator is constant and only the substrate moves. That is the one design constraint that matters — a bisection that also moves the rig measures nothing.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN WINDOW rather than an extension of rf2-nkeba's. It needs a browser, it needs the rig frozen across several revisions, and Shape 6 forbids adding a rung or an arm inside a running window. rf2-nkeba added neither and launched no browser.

NOT ASSUMED: that the substrate is where it went. That is the surviving candidate, not an established one, and a bisection that comes back flat across the interval is a legitimate and informative result — it would push the question onto the runtime, which the pins cannot settle.

comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT PR #8434 — premise correction from rf2-nkeba. MERGED-PR AUDIT PR #8434 — the median/mean re-derivation and source facts verify, but the landed record crosses its own comparability boundary in four actionable places.

1. That inference does not follow: certification can correlate with level, and neither the missing old legs nor the missing current raw/all-window dataset bounds the selection effect. The safe verdict is that the quantities are not comparable. “A residual survives regardless”, “something also moved”, and “what is left is event-pipeline drift” are therefore unsupported; the latter also conflicts with the page’s own statement that resident-runtime drift remains possible.

2. THE 8-OF-12 “ADVERSARIAL” RESULT IS NOT AN EXTREMUM. Independently driving the exact shipped `allocSteps` blob (`c57c824a6f28fda28a6a01d0d0ad65b91c6fb99b`) produced a valid certified reconstruction for every one of the twelve stored `(rise,maxStep,falls)` triples. The reconstructed streams reproduce `rise`, `maxStep`, `falls=0`, and `endpoints` exactly, while all 12 certify at the shipped τ=0.25 (absolute worst deviations 20.29%–23.83%). Thus the preserved scalars support 0/12 under the first-leg model and at least 12/12 under another arrangement. The landed 8/12 is one construction, not “arranged to certify if any arrangement can.”

3. THE COMPARISON TABLE REVERSES POSITIONAL RESULTS. The source rows list current values low-to-high, but every delta row lists their results in the opposite order. For example reagent 19,349 / 19,650 / 19,816 must pair with published percentages −19.74 / −18.51 / −17.80 and lowest-round deltas −1,449 / −1,148 / −982, not the landed reverse; uix 19,712 / 20,696 must pair with −20.29 / −16.31 and −3,456 / −2,472. The ranges remain right, but the per-window mapping is false.

4. THE PAGE CLAIMS A PHANTOM FOLLOW-UP. “The seed decoupled from B” run is said to be “filed as its own bead instead,” but the only #8434 follow-ups filed at that time are rf2-9jrhi and rf2-erre5; neither owns that rung, and description/title searches find no such bead. title: [docs-defect] the setup skill teaches the same false :init-fn hot-reload claim, and a CI guard ENFORCES it
description:
SAME DEFECT AS rf2-r0kk7, DIFFERENT SURFACE. rf2-r0kk7 measured, on
shadow-cljs 3.4.10, that a :browser build whose only entry point is a
module :init-fn does NOT re-render after a hot reload: shadow loads the
new code (the console logs `load JS ... views.cljs`), logs

  shadow-cljs: reloading code but no :after-load hooks are configured!

and #app keeps painting the OLD view for as long as you wait (90s
measured). Adding a ^:dev/after-load hook makes the identical edit land
in ~1s with app-db intact. Both halves were re-measured under rf2-r0kk7
on the real generated scaffold, Reagent and UIx.

skills/re-frame2-setup/ teaches the OPPOSITE in three places:

  * references/entry-namespace.md:25 -- "shadow-cljs's `:browser` target
    re-runs `:init-fn` (`init`) after EACH hot reload, so `init` IS the
    re-render path -- no separate `^:dev/after-load` hook."
  * references/first-counter.md:90 -- ";; shadow-cljs's :browser target
    re-runs :init-fn (init) after EACH hot ..." (inside the SOLE
    copy-complete core.cljs the skill tells the author to copy).
  * references/shadow-cljs.md:107 -- "**`:init-fn` re-runs after each hot
    reload.** For shadow-cljs's :browser target the module :init-fn is
    both the startup entry and the default after-load hook ... no
    separate ^:dev/after-load hook."

CONSEQUENCE: an agent or human following the setup skill builds an app
with no hot reload, exactly as the generator template did.

THE GUARD ENFORCES THE FALSEHOOD. scripts/check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py
carries HOT_RELOAD_DRIFT (defined ~L146) and find_hot_reload_drift
(~L271), which FAIL the build if either skill leaf says :init-fn is a
one-time startup hook, says it does not re-run on a reload, or
recommends adding a ^:dev/after-load hook. Its docstring (L20-31) names
that framing "Camp B" and calls it wrong, citing the template README as
its authority -- the README rf2-r0kk7 has now corrected. So the guard
must be INVERTED in the same PR as the prose, or the corrected pages
will not merge. It scans only SHADOW_CLJS + ENTRY_NAMESPACE (run(),
~L388), which is why rf2-r0kk7's template-only fix did not red it.

The bead that installed the guard is cited in its header as rf2-fd1mf3;
that ruling was made on an unmeasured premise. Check it before writing.

SCOPE: skills/re-frame2-setup/references/{entry-namespace,first-counter,
shadow-cljs}.md + SKILL.md if it repeats the claim, and
scripts/check_skill_setup_counter_drift.py (invert HOT_RELOAD_DRIFT so it
catches the FALSE claim instead of the true one, and update its docstring
+ its self-test Case D). tools/template is already corrected (rf2-r0kk7,
PR #8400) -- copy its shape: a ^:dev/after-load re-render hook with the
one-time boot ceremony left in `init`, which is also what
docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md and every examples/ entry ns
already teach.

VERIFY BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading: the skill ships copyable blocks,
so materialise one and drive a real `shadow-cljs watch` + browser edit.
rf2-r0kk7's PR body carries a working probe recipe.

title: [docs-defect] the project template says shadow re-runs :init-fn after a hot reload; measured false, so a templated app has no hot reload
description:
MEASURED, not inferred (rf2-ypct8 worker, 2026-08-16). Under
`shadow-cljs watch` on shadow-cljs 3.4.10, a :browser build whose only
entry point is a module `:init-fn` logs, in the page console, on every
reload:

  shadow-cljs: reloading code but no :after-load hooks are configured!

and the page keeps rendering the OLD view. Editing a view's text left the
DOM unchanged for the full 90s the probe waited. Adding
`^:dev/after-load` alongside the same `:init-fn` made the identical edit
land in under a second, with app-db intact (a counter clicked to 2 read
"Tapped 2 times" after the reload).

THREE SITES STATE THE OPPOSITE, and the generated app is built on them:

- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/shadow-cljs.edn:22
  ";; shadow's :browser target re-runs the module :init-fn after each
   hot reload by default — no :after-load hook needed."
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/core.cljs:17
  docstring: "Called by shadow-cljs. Idempotent — re-invoked on each hot
  reload."
- tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:29
  "module's `:init-fn` automatically after each hot reload, so no ..."

CONSEQUENCE. `_uix/core.cljs` calls `uix-dom/render-root` inside `init`
and defines no `^:dev/after-load` hook at all, so an app scaffolded from
the UIx template appears to hot-reload (shadow recompiles, the console
says "load JS") and silently does not re-render. Check `_reagent/core.cljs`
for the same shape — it did not match the grep above, so it may already

title: hicasso: take the BY-SITE allocation window — attribute the round-indexed leg dispersion
description:
MEASUREMENT HALF of rf2-rs8q6, whose EDIT half landed in PR #8380. The
by-site instrument exists and is proved by pin and by a planted-fault red;
nothing has been measured with it. rf2-rs8q6 stays OPEN until this window
runs, because the mechanism is still unidentified.

## The configuration, and why exactly this one

  P0_ALLOC_BY_SITE=1
  P0_ALLOC_PLAN=floor
  P0_ROOTS=4, P0_ALLOC_CELLS in {1, 6, 24}  ->  B in {4, 24, 96}
  both writes (default, and P0_ALLOC_WRITE=all)
  six rounds, three warm-ups, the shipped window

That is rf2-e9wr's own configuration, borrowed from V1, and it is chosen so
the two windows are COMPARABLE window for window. A different page or a
different plan would produce a by-site table nobody could line up against the
72 windows the observation was made on.

ON A QUIET BOX. rf2-e9wr's window was taken on a loaded one and said so; four
of its windows carried six-figure excursions it excluded and named. That page
also leaves "how much of the excursion and collection rate is the loaded box"
open (its 'What this leaves open' #3), and this window is the natural place to
close it.

## What must be read FIRST, because the window is not readable without it

THE IDLE CONTROL'S SITE FIGURES. The mode takes one extra counter reading per
leg, and that read's own footprint sits inside every arm site figure. The idle
control is driven at the same stride precisely so it prices it: an idle leg's
`dispatch` and `drain` figures are that footprint and nothing else, and the
summary prints them at the head of the BY SITE block.

IF THE IDLE FIGURE IS COMPARABLE TO THE ARM EXCESSES (~2,640 B median), THE
MODE'S RESOLUTION IS INSUFFICIENT AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Report it and stop;
do not read an attribution out of it. This is a real possibility and the
instrument does not assume its way past it.

## What settles the mechanism

`siteWitness.dominant`, per window, across the round sequence. `dispatch` puts
the term in the event pipeline and the signal graph; `drain` puts it in
React's commit. The question the bead asks is answered by whether that is
constant, and whether it differs between round 2 (wide, none below 2.66%) and
round 3 (tight, all at or below 0.19%).

`tick0`/`tick` ride back on every window. `alloc-tick` is monotone for the
life of the page and the warm-ups advance it too, so that pair is what a round
index actually IS. A round-indexed effect is an effect indexed by those
numbers, and the first thing to try is plotting the excess against the tick
rather than against the round.

## What settles the hypothesis rf2-rs8q6 named to exclude first

`siteWitness.sameSite`, per window.

  disagree  -> SETTLED. One term cannot be in two places: the recurring
               excess is a DISTINCT term from the prime's, not the same one
               recurring.
  agree     -> NARROWED, not settled. A site is two statements wide. Read the
               magnitudes next: the prime excess is tight (p25 6,800, p75
               6,888 B, 1.3% of its median) so it has a magnitude to hit,
               while the recurring excesses sit at 38% of it at the median and
               span a 15.7x range.
  null      -> the window had no dispersion to place. Expected on round-3
               windows and not a failure.

## A second, cheap window that is worth taking at the same time

A stride-2 / stride-3 PAIR on one configuration, so the extra sampler read's
cost is MEASURED rather than assumed. The falsifiable claim the mode's header
makes is that the arms' leg-magnitude difference between the two strides is
accounted for by the idle control's own difference. If it is not, the mid-leg
read is perturbing the work unit and the site figures are not clean.

## Fences

- DO NOT WIDEN TAU, and do not pin it. rf2-e9wr established that no honest
  calibration exists on the arms' data in either direction, and rf2-rs8q6
  repeats the fence. Nothing in this window is a reason to move a gate.
- NO INSTRUMENT CHANGE MID-WINDOW. If the window shows the instrument needs
  another seam or finer resolution, file that; do not build it inside the
  measurement, which is the split rf2-rs8q6 itself was filed to keep.
- Report refused windows and their reasons at every appearance, as rf2-e9wr's
  page does, and let no figure from a collection-carrying window enter a
  conclusion.
close_reason: WINDOW TAKEN, PR #8419 (docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-dispersion-is-in-the-dispatch-site.md). Seven runs on a drained fleet at rf2-e9wr's exact configuration; all seven positive controls passed, 0 unverified of 12 each. IDLE CONTROL READ FIRST: 16 B per leg per site in all 36 idle windows = 0.65% of the 2,476 B recurring excess, so the stop condition does NOT fire and the mode's resolution is sufficient. MECHANISM: siteWitness.dominant = dispatch in 37 of 41 clean windows, drain in 0, and the SAME site at round 2 (wide) and round 3 (tight) — the bimodality is a change of magnitude within one site. Limit stated: the floor arm's commit is a near-no-op (drain median exactly 80 B in all 72 windows), so nothing generalises to a subscribing arm. SAMESITE = AGREE (37 of 37), which NARROWS and does not settle — the magnitudes do not match (prime a 6,864 B constant at 1.17% IQR vs recurring 500-6,888 B, 13.8x), so rf2-rs8q6 stays OPEN for the mayor with a recommendation that it needs a follow-up rather than closing here. INDEX REFINED from the round to the window ORDINAL (tick0 = 21+28k, identical in all seven runs; same arm 9.97x apart at adjacent ordinals). ESTIMAND QUESTION ANSWERED: the quiet box moved the collection rate by two windows in seventy-two (23 of 72 vs rf2-e9wr's 25 of 72) and did not shrink the tails, closing rf2-e9wr's open question 3 — future allocation windows on this rig need no drained fleet. STRIDE PAIR met its falsifiable claim (idle Delta +16 B predicted, arm Delta median +16 B observed). tau untouched, no gate moved, no instrument change; two instrument findings filed rather than built (rf2-4ctls P2, rf2-stals P3).
