MAYOR 2026-08-16 13:54 AUSEST — THE WINDOW QUEUE, recorded here because this is the P1 that leads it and whoever takes the first quiet box needs the list.

Six beads are now window-only or about to be, and NOT ONE of them can run while any worker is dispatched:

  rf2-ojehu   P1  OPEN         by-site allocation window (this bead) — rig landed via rf2-rs8q6
  rf2-6zc2q   P2  OPEN         direct-return clock S8 re-take — rig landed via rf2-h904p
  rf2-lo7uy   P2  IN_PROGRESS  read_profile slot-distance nulls — rig landing now
  rf2-v5oto   P3  OPEN         author-share split — rig landed, PR #8383
  rf2-w01c    P3  IN_PROGRESS  topo 4x4 clock table — driver landing now
  rf2-85og2   P3  DEFERRED     three budget gates — waits on rf2-w01c's driver, then window-only

THIS IS THE SPLIT WORKING, NOT A BACKLOG PROBLEM. Mike's 2026-08-14 ruling (on rf2-2rtt6.140) said to build every instrument in parallel on a loaded box and 'then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle', so that the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers. Applying it across the lane this session converted five beads from blocked-on-quietness to rig-landed, which is exactly the intended outcome — and it has moved the whole cost onto the second half.

THE CONSEQUENCE THE RULING DOES NOT COVER, and it is a scheduling call rather than a measurement one: the operator's standing instruction is to keep six workers saturated, and a valid window needs ZERO. Those cannot both hold. The queue therefore does not drain by itself — it drains only when somebody deliberately stops refilling. Six live workers today each finished inside roughly forty minutes, so a drain is cheap in wall-clock and expensive only in the dispatches not made during it.

FOR WHOEVER RUNS THE DRAIN: take them back to back in one quiet period rather than one per idle gap, because each re-entry pays the same box-quieting cost. Read rf2-v5oto's newest note first — it records that FOUR queued windows will each want to append to docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md, so that file is a conflict magnet and the appends must be serialised behind the windows rather than raced. rf2-e9wr's configuration is the one rf2-ojehu and rf2-rs8q6 are written against, so those two line up window for window.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
WINDOW TAKEN 2026-08-16 22:05-22:12 AUSEST on a drained fleet. PR #8419. The verdict is self-contained below; the record is docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-dispersion-is-in-the-dispatch-site.md.

CONFIGURATION AS SPECIFIED, unvaried: P0_ALLOC_BY_SITE=1, P0_ALLOC_PLAN=floor, P0_ROOTS=4 (default), P0_ALLOC_CELLS in {1,6,24} -> B in {4,24,96}, both writes, six rounds, three warm-ups, the shipped window. Six by-site runs (72 arm windows) plus a seventh at the shipped stride 2 on one configuration, as the cheap pair the bead names. Chromium 147.0.7727.15, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, branch worker/bysite-ojehu off 63a3d44086.

CONTROLS. All seven positive controls PASSED: direct 8.10 B/double at stride 3 and 8.08 at stride 2, differential 8.0044 at BOTH strides against a predicted 8. 0 unverified of 12 in every run. All seven runs exited 1 on the driver's own alloc refusals -- 23 of 72 arm windows carried an observed collection, 33 of 72 carry a leg past tau, so 39 of 72 certify against rf2-e9wr's 41 of 72.

1. THE IDLE CONTROL, READ FIRST. dispatch 16 B per leg, drain 16 B per leg, range [16-16] in ALL 36 idle windows. That is 0.65% of this window's own 2,476 B recurring excess and 0.61% of rf2-rs8q6's published 2,640 B median. THE STOP CONDITION DOES NOT FIRE -- the mode's resolution is sufficient and an attribution may be read out of it. Corroborated three further ways: every leg of ctl1 moves 8,064 -> 8,080 and of ctl2 3,264 -> 3,280, each exactly +16 B, and the direct control reading moves 8.0827 -> 8.0987 B/double, which is 0.016 x 1,000 doubles x 6 writes = 96 B = 6 legs x 16 B exactly.

2. THE MECHANISM. siteWitness.dominant = dispatch in 37 of 41 clean windows, drain in 0, null in 4 (byte-identical legs, no dispersion to place). It is CONSTANT across the round sequence and, answering the bead's exact question, it is the SAME SITE at round 2 (7 of 7 dispatch, none below 2.59%) and round 3 (10 of 12 dispatch + 2 null). THE BIMODALITY IS A CHANGE OF MAGNITUDE WITHIN ONE SITE, NOT A CHANGE OF SITE. drain's median is exactly 80 B in all 72 windows at every page size, both writes, both substrates -- 0.42% of a leg.

   THE HONEST LIMIT, stated on the page: the floor arm mounts no subscription, so its flushSync commit is a near-no-op by construction, and a null result at drain on this arm is weaker than the counts look. What stands without that caveat is that the arm's ENTIRE per-write allocation and all of its dispersion is in the framework's write rather than the substrate's commit. Nothing generalises to a subscribing arm; one was not measured.

3. THE HYPOTHESIS rf2-rs8q6 NAMED TO EXCLUDE FIRST -- FOR THE MAYOR'S DECISION. siteWitness.sameSite reads AGREE: 37 of 37 clean windows, 44 of 49 collection-free, 63 of 72 overall, and primeSite reads dispatch in 41 of 41 clean windows. Every one of the five disagreements anywhere in the measurement is a collection-carrying or six-figure-excursion window. On the bead's own asymmetry this is NARROWED, NOT SETTLED, so rs8q6 does NOT close on a disagree.

   The magnitudes the bead sends the reader to next do NOT match: the prime excess is a near-constant 6,864 B (p25 6,800, p75 6,880 -- IQR 1.17% of median; whole range 6,526-6,940 B) while the recurring excesses span 500-6,888 B, a 13.8x range, median 2,476 B = 36.1% of the prime's. Both replicate their published counterparts (6,864 B median exactly; rs8q6's +476..+7,456 B / 15.7x / 38%). So the same-term reading survives only as "the prime's term recurs at a POSITION-DEPENDENT FRACTION of itself", which is strictly stronger than what rs8q6 put up and is not established here. RECOMMENDATION: rs8q6 needs a follow-up rather than closing on this window -- the site is settled, the term's identity is not.

4. THE INDEX IS THE WINDOW ORDINAL, NOT THE ROUND. tick0 reads 21, 49, ..., 329 -- step 28, IDENTICAL in all seven runs -- so on this configuration it is an exact affine function of the ordinal k (tick0 = 21 + 28k) and carries no axis the ordinal does not. But the ordinal is FINER than the round and that is where the effect is: within round 2 the two windows read 512 B and 2,502 B at the median (4.89x apart), and the SAME ARM reads 5,106 B at k=3 and 512 B at k=4 -- 9.97x apart at adjacent ordinals -- so the arm is not the carrier. At k=9 the six readings separate PERFECTLY by the write (page -12/-12/-36 B; all 3,464/2,696/2,708 B), which narrows rs8q6's "not of the page, the write or the substrate" at that ordinal, on n=6.

5. THE EXCURSIONS ARE INDEXED TOO, AND THEY ARE NOT THE BOX. Counting |worst leg deviation| >= 70,000 B: ordinals 0, 2 and 8 are excursive in 6 of 6 stride-3 runs and in the stride-2 run; ordinal 1 in 5 of 6 plus stride-2; ordinals 6, 7, 9, 10 and 11 in NONE. Machine load does not align to a window ordinal across seven separate processes, and neither does the mode.

6. THE ESTIMAND QUESTION, WHICH THE BRIEF ASKS ANSWERED EXPLICITLY -- rf2-e9wr's open question 3 CLOSES. Quiet box against its loaded one: 23 of 72 arm windows collection-carrying against 25 of 72; 6 of 49 six-figure excursions against 5 of 47; prime-excess tails -42,124/+492,500 B against -51,684/+360,500 B. DRAINING THE FLEET MOVED THE COLLECTION RATE BY TWO WINDOWS IN SEVENTY-TWO AND DID NOT SHRINK THE TAILS AT ALL. The classification rule holds: an allocation census reads the same on a loaded box, and the excursions rf2-e9wr flagged as a reason to doubt it are real heap traffic indexed by window position, not competing processes. CONSEQUENCE FOR SCHEDULING: a future allocation window on this rig does NOT need the fleet drained. The comparison is not perfectly like for like (rf2-e9wr ran seven stride-2 runs; this ran six stride-3 plus one stride-2), but the stride pair prices that difference at 16 B per leg and 3-vs-4 collection-carrying windows in twelve, far too small to explain 23-vs-25.

7. THE STRIDE PAIR (the cheap second window). Taken on P0_ALLOC_CELLS=6, write=page, back to back. The mode's falsifiable claim is MET: idle Delta(3-2) = +16 B is the prediction, and the arms read a median +16 B, range +10 to +16 B, over the 7 windows collection-free on both sides. ctl1 and ctl2 also move +16 B. The mid-leg read is NOT perturbing the work unit and the site figures are clean. Collection rate unmoved (3 of 12 at stride 2, 4 of 12 at stride 3); prime excess median 6,812 vs 6,864 B, a 52 B difference inside its own 80 B IQR and nothing read from its sign.

FENCES HELD. tau NOT moved in either direction and its uncalibrated marker intact; ALLOC_MIN_WRITES, ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B, ALLOC_CONTROL_SLACK untouched. NO INSTRUMENT CHANGE was made or attempted mid-window. Refused windows are reported at every appearance and no figure from a collection-carrying window enters a conclusion; the headline population additionally excludes six-figure excursions and two windows carrying an intra-leg reclamation.

TWO INSTRUMENT FINDINGS FILED RATHER THAN BUILT:
  rf2-4ctls (P2, BUG) -- a collection INSIDE a leg passes BOTH gates. 24 of 72 windows carry a negative site step; three have falls===0 so the falls gate saw nothing, and TWO of those also certified at tau, one carrying dispatch +305,392 B against drain -285,292 B in a single leg whose net (+2,008 B) is inside tau.
  rf2-stals (P3) -- the BY SITE summary's "worst-dev site" column prints siteWitness.dominant, which is the site with the larger TOTAL absolute deviation across the legs, not the worst leg's site. They agree on this data; the next window that quotes the heading will name the wrong estimator.

WHAT WAS NOT CONCLUDED. The same-term hypothesis is neither excluded nor confirmed. No mechanism INSIDE dispatch is identified (there is no third seam that does not mean instrumenting re-frame from inside the arm). React's commit is not exonerated in general -- only on an arm whose commit does almost nothing. The ordinal indexing is measured, not explained. The write is not claimed to govern the dispersion (k=9 is one ordinal, n=6). Nothing is claimed about within-run machine quietness: Processor Queue Length was read ONLY between runs, never inside one, in eight brackets totalling 37 one-second samples of which 34 read 0 and three read 1 on a 24-core box, with CPU 4.0-25.5%.

title: hicasso: the allocation arms' leg dispersion is round-indexed — 6/6 runs, mechanism unidentified
description:
MEASURED by rf2-e9wr's window on 2026-08-16 (PR #8377), on the instrument
rf2-oiy1 primed at ecd4f6e7f3. Filed rather than chased: identifying the
mechanism needs an instrument a measurement window may not build mid-window.

THE OBSERVATION. Over 72 floor-arm windows (P0_ALLOC_PLAN=floor, B in {4,24,96},
both writes, six rounds each), the relative dispersion of a window's MEASURED
work legs is a function of the ROUND INDEX, not of the page, the write or the
substrate. Restricting to windows with no observed collection (the falls gate,
which is independent of tau):

  round 0   n=5    16.67% - 1,407.95%
  round 1   n=6     0.07% - 1,835.79%
  round 2   n=11    2.66% -    20.37%   <- NONE below 2.66%
  round 3   n=11    0.00% -     0.19%   <- ALL at or below 0.19%
  round 4   n=7     0.06% - 1,505.41%
  round 5   n=7     0.00% -    13.29%

Rounds 2 and 3 are the clean statement and THEY HOLD IN EACH OF THE SIX RUNS
SEPARATELY -- six independent browser launches, each with both round-2 windows
wide and both round-3 windows tight. Machine load does not align to a round
index across six separate processes, so this is a property of the arm work unit
and its round schedule rather than of the box.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not cosmetic. The leg witness rests on the premise
that a window's legs are W repetitions of ONE work unit. On the controls that
premise holds exactly (17 of 18 windows byte-identical). On the arms it does
not, and rf2-oiy1's prime did not fix it -- the prime removes the FIRST leg,
and this is a term that recurs in later legs. Consequence for rf2-e9wr: tau
calibrated on the arms' own clean windows lands at ~0.004 read at round 3 and
~0.41 read at round 2, two orders of magnitude apart, so tau is NOT IDENTIFIED
by the arms' data. That is why rf2-e9wr refused to pin it.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Instrument the arm work unit's allocation by site across
the round sequence -- the excesses are positive legs against a byte-identical
cohort with ZERO falling steps, so they are allocation by the page's own heap,
not a collector artefact and not another process. A candidate worth excluding
first: the excess magnitudes (+476 to +7,456 B, median 2,640 B over 20 windows)
overlap the prime excess's own scale (median 6,864 B), which would suggest the
same term recurring rather than a distinct one -- but that is a HYPOTHESIS this
window did not test, and the byte values do not fall into clean quanta.

DO NOT DISCHARGE THIS BY WIDENING tau. rf2-e9wr established that no honest
calibration exists in either direction; widening runs against that and against
Shape 6.

EVIDENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-arms-spread-does-not-collapse.md
(PR #8377), sections 'The bimodality is round-indexed, in all six runs' and
'Why no tau follows, on either calibration population'.

EDIT HALF DELIVERED — PR #8380. THE BEAD STAYS OPEN: it is about the
mechanism, and an instrument is not a mechanism. No window was taken.

WHAT THE INSTRUMENT IS. `P0_ALLOC_BY_SITE=1` drives the allocation window at a
stride of 3 instead of 2, taking one extra counter reading at the work unit's
ONE seam — between the `dispatch-sync` through the event pipeline and signal
graph, and the `flushSync` commit that follows it. A leg then decomposes as
`dispatch + drain`, exactly, over the same outer pair of readings the shipped
window takes.

THERE IS NO THIRD SEAM that does not change what the arm measures. A finer
split means instrumenting re-frame's own pipeline from a bench fixture, and an
arm carrying instrumentation is not the arm whose figures are published. Two
sites is what the work unit affords, and it is the split that separates the
framework's write from the substrate's commit.

FENCES HELD. Off by default; the collapse is the identity on a stride-2
stream, so every published row is byte-identical and every `allocSteps` /
`allocPrimeSplit` pin stands unedited. The certificate is read off the
COLLAPSED stream, so `allocSteps` never sees a by-site stream and `rise`,
`falls` and `maxStep` cannot move. TAU IS UNTOUCHED in either direction, and a
pin drives every certificate constant in fresh processes with the mode armed
and without it, requiring them equal.

THE HYPOTHESIS THIS BEAD NAMED TO EXCLUDE FIRST IS NOT EXCLUDED, and this
dispatch could not exclude it — that needs a window. What changed is that it is
now DECIDABLE, and asymmetrically: sites DISAGREEING settles it (one term
cannot be in two places), sites AGREEING only narrows it (a site is two
statements wide), and a window with no dispersion reports `null` rather than
`false`.

A PRELIMINARY LEAN, from published data only and offered as a lean: the prime
excess is extraordinarily tight (p25 6,800, p75 6,888 — 1.3% of its median,
constant in absolute bytes across B in {4,24,96} and identical under both
writes), so it has a MAGNITUDE to hit; the recurring excesses sit at 38% of it
at the median and span a 15.7x range, and this bead already notes they fall
into no clean quanta. But magnitude cannot separate "a different term" from
"the same term partially recurring", and the two populations were never paired
window by window. Site is the strong discriminator and site needs the window.

WHAT COULD STILL DEFEAT THE INSTRUMENT, stated rather than assumed: the mode's
extra `mem` read has its own footprint, and the idle control is driven at the
same stride precisely to price it. If that idle figure turns out comparable to
the arm excesses (~2,640 B), the resolution is insufficient and THAT IS THE
FINDING — rf2-ojehu says to report it and stop rather than read an attribution
out of it.

NEXT: rf2-ojehu (P1) carries the measurement window — the configuration
(rf2-e9wr's own, so the two windows line up window for window), the quiet box,
what to read first, and what each outcome settles.

This bead measured a rider and a floor one window deep and read them as a distribution. rf2-ojehu already found the index finer than the round; this is what the finer index is.

THE RIDER IS IN THE ARM'S PATH — over 4,284 control legs, which run the same window machinery, sampler, schedule and positions, the count in the 700-800 B band is ZERO, against 112 of 2,322 arm legs. A term that recurs cannot be flat in the very index its recurrence tracks. 'The recurring excess is the prime's term recurring' is refuted, not merely unsupported.

On the FLOOR arm subs and renders are STRUCTURAL zeros — the arm mounts no subscription, so nothing recomputes and the commit has no update to flush. The census's whole discriminating power on this arm is the one counter that moves, events, and it reads 7 = windowWrites. title: [method] the bottom-up rule is refuted — position does not order tracker text by recency, DATE does
description:
MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. The method tells every worker and every mayor loop to read a tracker item BOTTOM-UP on the reasoning that the description is the oldest text and corrections accrete below it. The FIRST HALF IS RIGHT. The inference from it is wrong, and it fails in two distinct ways that were both hit in one session on 2026-08-15/16.

FAILURE 1 — RENDERED POSITION DOES NOT ORDER BY DATE. Measured on rf2-hic-047: 127 rendered lines. The NEWEST material (a 2026-08-15 audit note) sat at line 79, INSIDE the description block, because audit notes append into the description. An OLDER dated comment (2026-08-12) rendered afterwards at line 111. So the bottom of the output was 3 days STALER than the middle. 'bd show | tail' was used roughly 20 times as a read-the-newest method before this was measured; it is not one.

FAILURE 2 — THE NEWEST MATERIAL MAY NOT BE ON THE ITEM AT ALL. On 2026-08-16 the operator said rf2-0yp7w had a ruling. It was searched bottom-up, and searched again by grep across the epic and all five children then known. Nothing. The ruling had in fact landed at 03:44 as TWO NEW CHILD BEADS, rf2-0yp7w.11 and rf2-0yp7w.12, whose titles carry it ('pre-cut'). A live fix worker was meanwhile executing the instruction the ruling had just superseded, and had to be stopped by hand. Reading position on one item cannot see a decision recorded as a new item.

THE REPAIR, and it is a REPLACEMENT of the mechanism rather than a deletion of the rule:

Keep: the description is the OLDEST text; corrections accrete below it; a top-down read gets superseded instructions.
Replace: 'so read bottom-up' -> 'so find the newest by DATE, not by position'. The concrete method that works:
    bd show <id> | grep -n "AUDIT\|202[0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]"
then read around the latest date. State it generically for other trackers (this tree is published for other repos) with the bd form as the worked example.
Add: when an item is an EPIC or has children, re-enumerate the children before concluding a decision is absent — a ruling may be recorded as a new child rather than a note.

NINE SITES, THREE FILES, ALL MUST MOVE TOGETHER (measured 2026-08-16 03:55; RE-TAKE the list rather than trusting it):
  docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:35, :63, :69, :479, :769

TWO FURTHER TEMPLATE GAPS, same PR, both rules currently ENFORCED IN EVERY LIVE BRIEF but written nowhere:
1. THE GREP FALSE ZERO. A backslash-bearing literal in single quotes returns a FALSE ZERO — a path pattern matched 0 files that demonstrably contained it. Use -F, or a dot wildcard. This is dangerous precisely because zero reads as 'clean'.
2. A MISSING EXIT-CODE FILE IS NO VERDICT, NOT A PASS. The template already forbids piping a gate through a filter (line 637). It does not say what an ABSENT .exit means. Two incidents on 2026-08-16: one worker's harness killed the shell at a 10-minute cap inside the final step with every prior gate green and no .exit written; another's harness reported a backgrounded red run as 'exit code 0' — the SHELL's status — while the .exit file written on the same command line said 1. SCOPE FENCE: method and command files only. Do NOT change gate scripts, workflows or any implementation file. This is a documentation change with no code effect.

title: [hicasso] A boundary CROSSED INTO from a Reagent parent paints once and is then DEAF to writes — both doors, controlled against h/mount!
description:
MEASURED, WITH A LIVE CONTROL, while landing rf2-2dbpd (Story's :hicasso substrate render-fn). Browser lane, real Chromium, real DOM. This is the Hicasso finding rf2-2dbpd's standing instruction asks for; it does NOT block that bead (the crossing paints, so the registration is correct and landed), and it DOES block rf2-kttom, whose worked hicasso testbed cannot have an interactive story until this is fixed.

THE CLAIM, in one line: a minted Hicasso boundary crossed into from a REAGENT parent renders correctly once and then never re-renders again on a write into its own frame — while the SAME boundary under h/mount! repaints.

THE EXPERIMENT. One boundary, one subscription, one adapter, one drain; only the mounting route varies.

  (h/defview hicasso-card [props]
    (swap! !card-runs inc)
    [:article {:data-test "hicasso-card"} (str (:label props) "/" (h/sub [::counter]))])

  adapter : re-frame.adapter.reagent/adapter  (rf/init!) — the adapter a Story host installs, since Story's shell is Reagent
  frame   : rf/make-frame, seeded to 1, then rf/dispatch-sync [..42..] {:frame f}
  drain   : (r/flush) then (react-dom/flushSync (fn [] nil))  — the pair
            re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.ratom-activation-dom-cljs-test spells out
            (reagent reactions recompute, then the sync-lane onStoreChange commits)

  ROUTE 1 — CONTROL, GREEN:
    (h/mount! container {:frame f} [hicasso-card {:label "ctl"}])
    paints "ctl/1"; after the write, body re-runs and DOM reads "ctl/42".

  ROUTE 2 — h/as-element from a Reagent parent, DEAF:
    (rdc/render root [rf/frame-provider {:frame f}
                      [:div (h/as-element [hicasso-card {:label "alpha"}])]])
    paints "alpha/1" — correct, and it is the VARIANT frame's value, so frame
    resolution across the crossing works — then after the write the body run
    count is UNCHANGED (1 -> 1) and the DOM still reads "alpha/1".

  ROUTE 3 — h/as-component (memoized on the head) from the same Reagent parent, ALSO DEAF:
    (react/createElement (memoized (h/as-component hicasso-card)) #js {"label" "brg"})
    paints "brg/1"; after the write, body runs 1 -> 1, DOM still "brg/1".

WHAT IS THEREFORE RULED OUT, and this is why the control matters: the adapter (route 1 uses the same one), the subscription, the drain, the frame provider object (impl.mount/provider and rf/frame-provider create a Provider over the SAME re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context), frame resolution across the crossing (routes 2 and 3 both read the variant frame's seeded value on their first paint), and React reconciliation (a separate green row proves a crossed boundary re-renders WITHOUT remounting when its Reagent parent re-renders — same DOM node across three renders). It is also not the outward-bridge DOOR, since both doors behave identically.

BODY RUNS ARE THE DIAGNOSTIC, not the DOM text. The body run counter says the boundary was never re-invoked, so this is a missing NOTIFICATION and not a stale read: nothing asked the boundary to render again.

WHY IT PROBABLY SURVIVED UNTIL NOW. Every shipped Hicasso DOM suite installs the UIx adapter and mounts through h/mount!. The one mounted witness under a ratom host (arm1 ratom-activation) drives the BENCH arm's runtime (rt/sub), not the shipped impl.collector. So "shipped collector + ratom adapter + foreign root" appears to be an untested combination, which is exactly the shape rf2-2kshh had before it was found (that bead's words: "the arm painted once at mount and was deaf thereafter").

WHERE TO START READING, offered as hypotheses and NOT as findings — I did not verify any of them, and implementation/** was outside my fence:
  - impl.collector wire-cell! / acquire-cell! — cell acquisition is COMMIT-owned; is the commit-time acquire reached at all when the root is not Hicasso's?
  - the difference between impl.mount/tree's codec/root-element (which binds intent/*frame*) and a bare h/as-element / as-component crossing (which bind neither, deliberately — as-component's docstring says so explicitly, citing root-element's reason). If cell wiring depends transitively on that binding, that is the whole difference between route 1 and routes 2/3.
  - whether the useSyncExternalStore subscribe registration is ever performed for these fibers, vs the cold-read path being taken on every render (which would explain correct values at every render AND no self-triggered re-render).

REPRODUCTION IS IN THE REPO, half of it live. tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs carries route 1 as a GREEN row (a-write-repaints-a-boundary-under-hicassos-own-root) plus the §KNOWN GAP section of its ns docstring. Routes 2 and 3 were run red in that file and removed before merge rather than shipped red; re-adding them is a copy of the code above.

IMPACT. A Hicasso view rendered inside any React-shaped host that is not a Hicasso root is non-reactive. Story is the immediate case (its canvas is a Reagent tree and its substrate render-fn splices the boundary in), but the outward bridge is documented for "n/defcomponent, UIx, or plain JavaScript" parents generally, so a consumer embedding a Hicasso view in a UIx or plain-React page is in the same position — worth checking whether a UIx parent is deaf too, since that would widen this considerably.
close_reason:

Controlled properly in real Chromium — one boundary, one subscription, one Reagent adapter, one drain (r/flush plus an empty flushSync) — varying only the root and the parent:

  route                                        paints     repaints on a write
  h/mount! (control)                           ctl/1      YES  ctl/42
  Reagent root + h/as-element                  alpha/1    YES  alpha/42
  Reagent root + memoized h/as-component       brg/1      YES  brg/42
  plain createRoot + h/as-element              plain/1    YES  plain/42

So the sentence a Hicasso view rendered inside any React-shaped host that is not a Hicasso root is non-reactive is WRONG, and it had been shaping dispatch priority for hours.

title: [method] the stranded sweep starts from the worktrees — the in-progress list is empty while workers run
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-15 22:52. The mayor wrote this fix, the mayor-checkout pre-commit hook refused it for touching worker-tracked surfaces, and that hook was right — so it is filed here with the fix written out, exactly as docs/the-mayor-method/README.md instructs.

THE DRIFT. Both copies of the stranded-sweep rule tell the reader to start from the tracker's in-progress list. On this repo that list is routinely EMPTY WHILE WORKERS ARE RUNNING, because dispatches do not claim their beads.

MEASURED, 2026-08-15 22:14. `bd list --status in_progress --limit 0` returned nothing at a moment when worker/retire-final was demonstrably alive: 80 files touched in 15 minutes and a JVM gate started 3 seconds before the read. The three beads it held — rf2-0yp7w.4, rf2-0yp7w.6, rf2-0yp7w.10 — all read `open`.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSED STRAND. The loop's nominal input is empty by construction rather than by health, so a "0 in progress, sweep clean" report is not evidence of anything, and the handoff's "15 consecutive clean stranded sweeps" may be 15 reads of an empty set. Worse: when a worker does die, its beads sit `open`, look dispatchable, and the next dispatch tick is free to send a SECOND WORKER AT THE SAME BRANCH — the collision the method spends a section forbidding. The blindness converts a strand into a collision. This is not hypothetical: retire-final died on a session limit at 22:26 and its three beads read `open` throughout.

TWO FILES, BOTH IN ONE PR, because two copies of one rule disagree within days and the method-reread loop names exactly that failure.

=== FILE 1: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, section 4, the stranded sweep ===
AFTER the existing line "Look for items marked in-progress. If no live worker holds one, it may be stranded." INSERT two paragraphs. Keep this file GENERIC — no bd commands, no repo paths, no PowerShell:

**But start from the worktrees, because that set is routinely empty while workers are running.** Unless your dispatches explicitly claim their items, a worker holds items that still read *open*, and this loop's nominal input is empty by construction rather than by health. Measured here: the in-progress list returned nothing while a worker was provably alive — files being written seconds earlier, a gate process burning CPU — and the three items it held all read open. A *"nothing in progress, sweep clean"* report is then not evidence of anything, and a streak of them is a streak of reads of an empty set.

The failure is worse than a missed strand. A dead worker's items sit open, look dispatchable, and the next dispatch tick sends a **second worker to the same branch** — the collision this method spends a section forbidding. So enumerate the worktrees first, sweep each for recent file activity, and map trees to items; where an item *is* marked in-progress, read it too. It is a real signal, just never the complete one.

=== FILE 2: .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md, after the line beginning "Read the in-progress beads:" ===
INSERT two paragraphs. This file pins CONCRETE commands, so name them:

**START FROM THE WORKTREES, NOT FROM THAT LIST — the in-progress set is routinely EMPTY while workers are running, because dispatches do not claim their beads.** Measured 2026-08-15 22:14: `bd list --status in_progress` returned nothing at a moment when `worker/retire-final` was demonstrably alive — 80 files touched in 15 minutes, a JVM gate started 3 seconds earlier — and the three beads it held (`rf2-0yp7w.4`, `.6`, `.10`) all read `open`. So this loop's nominal input is empty by construction rather than by health, and a "0 in progress, sweep clean" report is **not evidence of anything**. Do not quote a streak of clean sweeps as assurance; a streak of reads of an empty set is what it may be. The failure is worse than a missed strand: the dead worker's beads sit `open`, look dispatchable, and the next dispatch tick is free to send a **second worker at the same branch** — the collision the method spends a section forbidding.

So enumerate `git worktree list` first and sweep each worker worktree for activity, then map trees to beads. One command settles a tree: count files touched recently, excluding `node_modules` and `.git`, and **read the newest filenames** — paths under `.cpcache`, `.scratch` or `implementation/out` mean a gate is running, a tracked source or doc file means the worker is editing, near-zero means a strand. Cross-check against processes started recently (`java`, `node`). That test is keyed to the worktree, which is where the truth is, rather than to a tracker field nobody sets. Where a bead IS marked in-progress, read it too — it is a real signal, just not the only one, and never the complete one.

=== SCOPE FENCE ===
Those two files only. Do NOT add a claim step to dispatch briefs — that is the operator's open call between (a) briefs claim their beads and (b) the sweep reads worktrees; this bead implements (b) while leaving (a) available, and the two are not exclusive. Do NOT touch mayor-dispatch.md, mayor-hygiene.md, or the dispatch-prompt-template.

=== GATE ===
`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers docs/the-mayor-method/ link targets and heading anchors, and runs unconditionally in test.yml's verify-readme-links job. `mkdocs build --strict` also covers docs/the-mayor-method/ (it is NOT under the exclude_docs block that hides docs/design/). Run both. No fenced code blocks are added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched — say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.
notes:

COMPLETENESS — all five scope amendments landed in the four intended method/command files, but the concrete stranded-sweep copy does not fully implement its own new exclusion. `.claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:26` says recent-file activity must exclude both `node_modules` and `.git`; line 32's executable example is still `find <worktree> -newermt '20 minutes ago' -type f | grep -v '/\.git/' | wc -l`, which excludes only `.git`. Preserve the later message/process corroboration and soften “one command settles a tree” / “near-zero means a strand”: neither file mtimes nor one quiet interval is authoritative by itself.

comments.text:
MAYOR, METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-15 23:44 — SCOPE AMENDED. Two further drifts found, both in mayor-hygiene.md, and they ride THIS bead rather than a sibling because they are the same surface and two workers on the method files would conflict. The original two-file scope in the description is SUPERSEDED by this note: the fence is now THREE files.

=== DRIFT 2: TWO COMMAND FILES DIRECTLY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND THE READER IS SENT TO THE STALE ONE ===

`.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md:8` says the liveness discriminator is:
    "The discriminator is `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/worker/<name>` against the SHA you recorded last tick"

`.claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:26` says the OPPOSITE, and says so as an explicit correction:
    "Read the LOCAL ref, not `git ls-remote` — this line said 'ask the REMOTE' until 2026-08-14 and it produced a false strand signal on three workers at once."

posture carries the measurement: on 2026-08-14 05:15 `ls-remote` reported all three live workers unchanged since the previous tick, while their local refs showed `ciretire-cluster` at `b26de366d4` committed 04:59 and `walkctl-1huc` at `73508c1339` committed 05:08. Every worker worktree here is a LINKED worktree sharing one `.git`, so a commit moves the local ref instantly while `origin` moves only when the worker chooses to push — the remote lags, and it lags in the direction that reads as death.

*** AND IT IS WORSE THAN A PLAIN DISAGREEMENT. *** mayor-posture.md:24 tells the reader that "`mayor-hygiene.md` carries why each misleads and IS THE ONE PLACE THAT REASONING LIVES". So posture DEFERS to hygiene for the reasoning while contradicting its conclusion. A reader following that pointer lands on the superseded rule with nothing to warn them.

FIX: correct mayor-hygiene.md:8 to name the LOCAL ref (`git rev-parse worker/<name>`), keep its ahead-count and two-clocks reasoning, which is correct and is genuinely the one place it lives, and fold in posture's measured false-strand evidence so the correction carries its own warrant. Do not delete the `ls-remote` discussion — record it as the superseded rule with the date and the reason, the way this project treats every other superseded record.

=== DRIFT 3: THE CONTAINMENT TEST IS ENFORCED BUT NOWHERE WRITTEN ===

Neither `mayor-hygiene.md` nor `loops.md` §5 contains the words cherry, patch-id or patch-equivalent. Both files answer "is this worker ALIVE?" and neither answers "is this branch's work ALREADY ON MAIN, so may I delete it?"

That second question is the one branch and worktree cleanup actually turns on, and THE OBVIOUS TEST IS WRONG HERE. This repository merges by REBASE, so a merged branch's commits get new SHAs and never become ancestors of main. Measured tonight over 63 worktrees: 60 branches read "ahead of main by 1 to 3 commits" and 58 of them were fully merged. Reading the ahead count would have kept all 58 forever; ignoring it would have deleted the 3 genuinely unmerged spike commits on `worker/receipts-hic081`. `git cherry origin/main <branch>` settled both directions in one command — `-` means an equivalent patch is already upstream, `+` means genuinely new. It returned `-` for all 58 and `+` for receipts-hic081.

FIX: add the containment test to mayor-hygiene.md's branch/worktree cleanup guidance, stating (a) that ancestry and the ahead count are both useless under rebase-merge, (b) that `git cherry origin/main <branch>` is the test, (c) that it protects in BOTH directions, and (d) the measured 58-versus-1 result as its warrant. Note the existing ahead-count paragraph already explains WHY the count misleads for liveness — this is the same trap on a different question, so cross-reference rather than restate.

=== WHY ALL THREE RIDE ONE PR ===
loops.md §4 (drift 1), mayor-posture.md (drift 1), mayor-hygiene.md (drifts 2 and 3). Method and command files are one surface and a hot zone; splitting them across two workers guarantees a conflict. Keep the same gate: `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` plus `mkdocs build --strict` (which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/, unlike docs/design/). Still no fenced code blocks added, so the guide-samples digest gate stays untouched — say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.

comments.text:
MAYOR, METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-16 00:52 — SCOPE AMENDED AGAIN. Two more drifts, both in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md's Shape 6. The fence is now FOUR files. Both were verified absent by grep before filing.

These are rules I ENFORCED in live briefs tonight and which the template does not carry, so the next mayor writing a Shape 6 brief will not include them.

=== DRIFT 4: SHAPE 6 GOVERNS THE RUN AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THE WRITE-UP ===

Every measurement PR merged on 2026-08-15/16 was audited, and EVERY ONE had its published claim stated slightly stronger than its evidence. Three for three, three different workers, all exemplary on the run itself:

  #8326 / rf2-pqyxz — the page calls three values "run-medians" and their spans "effect medians" and "null medians". lane/ratio-between computes no median; it stores the ARITHMETIC MEAN of five per-round ratios in :mean. The effect-versus-null separation is the whole stated basis for "outside instrument resolution", so the conclusion rests on the estimator being what it says it is.
  #8327 / rf2-d360z — a 0.058 spread is said to "loosely bracket" 0.9718, but the three measured ratios are 0.8864 / 0.9444 / 0.9189 and 0.9718 is ABOVE their maximum. It brackets nothing. Separately, the whole 0.100 ms spread is attributed to "the instrument's own run-to-run noise" with "nothing changing between runs", while the SAME paragraph records queue readings of 1, 1 and 2 and concedes two cannot be proven outside a measurement phase.
  #8328 / rf2-3l6hf — see drift 5 below; the write-up asserted a bound its data could not support.

THE SHAPE, AND IT IS NOT CARELESSNESS: what slipped every time is the prose ONE LAYER ABOVE the number. A worker that has just spent an hour being rigorous writes its summary in ordinary confident English, and ordinary confident English overclaims. Not one audit overturned a measurement or a refusal — what they corrected is the sentence a future reader will quote, and readers quote the sentence, not the log. That is how a measured result becomes a false premise in someone else's brief three weeks later, which is exactly what premises-are-claims catches on the INPUT side. This is the same defect on the OUTPUT side and nothing was checking it.

ADD TO SHAPE 6, wording as enforced tonight:

  "Your published sentences are claims too, and they are audited. For every summarising
   statement you write, name the exact evidence that licenses it and check the arithmetic
   of any comparison in it. Do not attribute an observed spread to a single cause unless
   your own data excludes the others — if your queue samples include a non-zero inside a
   measurement phase, you may not call the dispersion the instrument's alone. Name the
   estimator you actually computed, not the one the surrounding prose habitually says.
   A hedged sentence that survives audit is worth more than a confident one that does not."

=== DRIFT 5: NOTHING SAYS AN IMPOSSIBLE READING CANNOT BOUND THE QUANTITY ===

rf2-3l6hf reported reader membership as "bounded: < 0.006 ms/commit", derived from its own most-negative reading. I believed it, wrote it into rf2-07rnj's brief AS GUIDANCE, and reported it to the operator. The merged-PR audit of #8328 refuted it, and rf2-07rnj's own run 2 then read -0.0141 — more than twice the claimed floor — refuting it a second time on independent arithmetic.

THE RULE: let an observed delta y equal an unknown positive true cost t plus estimator error e. A reading of y = -0.0062 proves only that the negative error excursion exceeded 0.0062 + t. It does NOT make +/-0.0062 a calibrated symmetric floor and it CANNOT upper-bound t. A most-negative observation is a statement about the ERROR TERM, not about the quantity. Comparing most-negative readings from DIFFERENT positive-cost arms at two window widths likewise cannot establish a floor-scaling factor.

ADD TO SHAPE 6:

  "An impossible reading tells you the instrument's error reached at least that far. It does
   not calibrate the error and it does not bound the thing you are measuring. If you report a
   bound, name the NULL OR CONTROL ARM that produced it. A bound derived from the impossible
   readings themselves is not a bound — report the term as UNRESOLVED instead."

AND ONE LINE FOR THE MAYOR'S SIDE, because the process failure was mine and premises-are-claims did not catch it: a NUMBER THE BRIEF ASSERTS IS A LEAN TOO. Workers read guidance as instruction and premises as claims, so anything phrased as guidance bypasses the check entirely. Before writing a predecessor's figure into a brief, ask what produced it. Here one question would have caught it: what null arm produced that bound?

=== FENCE, UPDATED ===
Four files, ONE PR, one agent: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md, .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md. Gate unchanged: check_doc_slugs.py plus mkdocs build --strict (which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/). No fenced code blocks added, so the guide-samples digest gate stays untouched — say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.

title: [story] RULING NEEDED: how does a story NAME a hicasso view? :component is a keyword into re-frame's view registry and hicasso mints no entry
description:
FROM rf2-5czki's phase-1 survey (2026-08-15 15:46 AUSEST). THIS IS A RULING FOR MIKE, NOT A DISPATCH. Do not send a worker at it. Everything else in the rf2-5czki programme waits on the answer, because it decides whether Story changes, Hicasso changes, or neither.

THE QUESTION IN ONE LINE: a Story variant names its subject with `:component <keyword>`, and a Hicasso boundary has no keyword to name.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, both halves:
 - tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc:436 and :915 — `[:component {:optional true} :keyword]`, documented at :407 as "keyword id of a registered `:view`". Resolution is `rf/view` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:768-774) against the framework registrar.
 - implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:218-241 — `h/defview` computes `view-name` = "<ns>/<sym>" AND a source coord, then hands both to `collector/mint-view!`. It registers NOTHING with re-frame's registrar. `rf/view` cannot see a Hicasso boundary.

THE `:component` KEYWORD BUYS STORY THREE THINGS, not one, and they cost differently:
 1. the render fn (cheap to replace);
 2. the view's `reg-view` metadata `[:rf/props :schema]`, which is where Story AUTO-DERIVES argtypes — the Controls panel (schemas.cljc:441-448, re-frame.story.malli-schema/view-args-schema-keys). `h/defview` carries no props-schema slot at all;
 3. source coords for open-in-editor. `defview` DOES compute these (hicasso.cljc:225) — they are simply not where Story looks.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE REFUSAL ALREADY ON RECORD. rf2-jkdy / rf2-l86mm / rf2-2og6s refused re-pointing Xray's and Story's tool-tier READS at Hicasso, because a MOUNTED boundary is keyed by its read set and mints no identity (re-frame.hicasso.tool:36-50, 244-263). That refusal is correct and stands. It answers "which view is this mounted boundary?" — a question asked BACKWARDS from the runtime. This bead asks the FORWARD question: the author already knows which view they mean and is naming it in source. `defview` already computes a stable name for it. The two questions are not the same one and the earlier refusal does not settle this.

THE THREE HONEST OPTIONS, ascending in blast radius:

(a) STORY-SIDE — `:component` accepts a var/component as well as a keyword.
    Contained entirely in tools/story. Zero Hicasso change, zero new public surface.
    COST: argtypes auto-derivation degrades to hand-authored `:argtypes` for Hicasso stories; source coords degrade; the `:keyword` schema at schemas.cljc:436/:915 widens and every `view-lookup` consumer in re-frame.story.plan must take the second shape. Snapshot identity hashes a var rather than a keyword — check identity.cljc:293-328 survives that.

(b) HICASSO-SIDE — `h/defview` ALSO registers under a derived id with re-frame's registrar, alongside `mint-view!`.
    Story then needs no change at all beyond the render-fn (rf2-3afns + the phase-C bead). Argtypes and source coords both work, because `defview` already has the name and the coord in hand at hicasso.cljc:224-225.
    COST: new public behaviour in `implementation/hicasso` — the standing facade-export classification duty applies, `scripts/check_facade_inventory.py` and `check_naming_census.py` both police that surface, and it collides with live Hicasso workers. It also needs a clear statement that registering an AUTHORING-TIME name is not minting MOUNTED boundary identity, or it will be read as overturning rf2-jkdy when it does not.

(c) REFUSE — Hicasso components are not storyable, recorded as a deliberate loss.
    Legitimate, and cheap. But it leaves the native substrate the only one a programmer cannot story, which is the inversion rf2-5czki was filed about.

A PRIOR QUESTION MIKE MAY WANT TO SETTLE FIRST, because it may dissolve the whole thing: IS `:hicasso` A "SUBSTRATE" IN STORY'S SENSE AT ALL? Hicasso ships NO adapter — `rg ':kind :rf.adapter' implementation/hicasso` is empty, there is no `:rf.adapter/hicasso` anywhere in the repo, and both Hicasso testbeds boot with `(rf/init! uix-adapter/adapter)` (implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:880). The canonical adapter enum is spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §CLJS reference scope (:2718 inventory, :2800-2809 `:kind` list) and Hicasso is absent from it — correctly, since it rides UIx. So Story's `:substrates` axis (WHICH AUTHORING LAYER WROTE THIS COMPONENT) and core's adapter axis (WHICH RENDERER IS INSTALLED) are DIFFERENT AXES that Story's schema docstring currently conflates: schemas.cljc:282-283 says "The framework supplies the closed set", and the set it points at does not and should not contain `:hicasso`. Widening `SubstrateSet` to `#{:reagent :uix :hicasso}` therefore INVENTS a parallel enum rather than mirroring one. That is either a naming correction Story should take, or evidence that Hicasso stories should ride `:uix` and be distinguished some other way.

RECOMMENDATION FROM THE SURVEY: (b) is the smallest total change and the only one that keeps Controls working, but it spends Hicasso's public surface, so it is Mike's to spend. (a) is the safe fallback and needs no ruling from anyone but Mike on losing auto-Controls. Answer the axis question above first — it may change which of (a)/(b) is even coherent.

NO FENCE — nothing is dispatched from this bead until it is answered.
close_reason: RULED: option (b) minimal-shape hicasso-side registration — keyword id + coords + head slot, no :handler-fn, debug-gated, replace-on-reload, authoring-time-alias wording; axis sub-ruling: :substrates is Story's own authoring-layer enum, widen with :hicasso + fix the docstring. Full ruling in comments. Implementation carrier: rf2-5qaf4 (new, blocks rf2-2dbpd). Delegated ruling, operator-reversible — reopen if Mike overrules.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULING (2026-08-15, delegated to a worker agent by Mike; operator-reversible — reopen if Mike overrules): **OPTION (b)** — h/defview also registers its already-computed name with the framework :view registrar, in the MINIMAL shape:

- Registered id: (keyword (str ns) (str sym)) — byte-identical to reg-view's auto-derived convention. The name is not new: defview already computes it (hicasso.cljc:224) and publishes it as DevTools displayName, the rf:render:<name> User-Timing id, and error attribution. Registration adds RESOLVABILITY, not identity.
- Entry payload: source coord (stored exactly as reg-view stores it) + the minted head under a namespaced slot (e.g. :hicasso/component). NO :handler-fn — rf/view's "returns the registered render fn" contract stays honest: it answers nil for a hicasso entry, and the :reagent substrate degrades to its existing inline diagnostic if mis-pointed.
- DEBUG-GATED with the same mechanism defview already uses for its error extents, so :advanced production bundles fold the registration away entirely — nothing in a production hicasso app renders through the registrar; the entry serves tools only. Hicasso's "no registry at runtime" stance holds in production.
- HOT RELOAD: re-evaluating defview REPLACES the entry behind the same id (registrar's existing replacement behaviour; no accumulation, no aliasing, no naming subsystem). The Story renderer resolves LATE, per render, so HMR late binding is preserved — the story picks up the new head with no story change.
- WORDING DUTY: the defview docstring (and rf2-2dbpd's spec note) states this is an AUTHORING-TIME ALIAS FOR FORWARD RESOLUTION ONLY — mounted boundary identity stays read-set-keyed and unnamed; the tool tier is unchanged; rf2-jkdy / rf2-l86mm / rf2-2og6s stand untouched (they answer the backward question "which view is this runtime boundary?"; storying asks the forward one — the author names the view in source).

WHY (all EIGHT opinions across the four dossiers weighed — the four original analyses and the four Codex reviews; every one converged on (b), differing only in shape details, resolved below and on the downstream beads): Story's keyword is load-bearing in four verified subsystems — render resolution, plan-time validation/Controls, snapshot/watch identity, the substrate render contract — plus HMR late binding. Option (a) would smear a keyword-or-fn union across all of them; decisively, fingerprint.cljc:469-477 canonicalises EVERY function to the :rf/opaque-fn sentinel, so two distinct component values would be INDISTINGUISHABLE to snapshot identity (the operative fact, per Codex — not fn-hash instability), and a value captured at reg-story time renders the STALE head after an HMR reload of the view's ns: a daily-life regression. Option (c) leaves the native substrate the only one a programmer cannot story — the exact inversion rf2-5czki was filed about. Hicasso's "mints no registry" pride is already softened at exactly this point: the name is minted and published today; only lookup is missing.

AXIS SUB-RULING: :substrates is Story's OWN authoring-layer render-strategy enum (which registered render-fn embeds the subject in the canvas), NOT a mirror of the framework adapter enum. Widen it with :hicasso AND correct the false SubstrateSet docstring (schemas.cljc:281-288, "The framework supplies the closed set") in the SAME edit (owned by rf2-2dbpd). No :rf.adapter/hicasso is created anywhere; no second marker. Hicasso still rides the UIx runtime adapter — this is an authoring distinction, not a third adapter.

HONEST LIMITS carried forward (both reviewers' corrections preserved):
- Argtypes auto-derivation is NOT free under ANY option — Hicasso has no props-schema notion. Hicasso stories hand-author :argtypes. An optional ^{:rf/props Schema} slot on defview is DEFERRED until a real user asks for auto-Controls; if Hicasso grows a props-schema story for other reasons, fold it in there rather than adding one for Story alone.
- Stored coords enable lookup but do NOT give element-click source navigation (hicasso does not stamp Story's coord attribute into DOM). Not claimed.
- The one material uncertainty is the Reagent-parent crossing (unwitnessed in-repo). rf2-2dbpd's mandated spike proves it. If the crossing fails entirely, that is a Hicasso finding and the render plan reroutes — the registration remains useful to any Story shell, but this ruling should be re-read in that light.

CASCADE: implementation carrier for the Hicasso-side registration is rf2-5qaf4 (NEW — 2dbpd's fence excludes implementation/**; adapter-timing caveat from the Codex reviews carried there). rf2-2dbpd: render-fn ruled as direct (h/as-element [resolved-view eff-args]) primary with memoized as-component as narrow spike-triggered fallback, host-registered like :uix, enum widen + docstring rewrite. rf2-kttom: lean Option A — dedicated testbed on port 8045, roster-generalised runner, classifier .html gap fixed. Full cascades on those beads.

The Codex recommendation on this dossier was weighed: it AGREED with (b) and sharpened it (the opaque-fn sentinel basis; no :handler-fn; late resolution keeping the bridge stable per head; the acceptance-evidence list) — all folded into this ruling and the downstream beads.

title: [story] Story's single-pane render BYPASSES the substrate registry — a :substrates #{:uix} variant renders under Reagent
description:
FOUND BY rf2-5czki's phase-1 survey (2026-08-15 15:46 AUSEST). This is a LIVE DEFECT FOR UIx TODAY, not a hicasso feature, and it is the reason no third substrate can be added until it lands.

THE CLAIM, VERIFIED AT SOURCE (not inherited from the survey brief):

Story has a substrate registry — `substrate->render-fn`, an open runtime atom with a public `register-substrate!` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:90-126). It is REAL and it is BYPASSED on the path almost every story takes.

1. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:498
     multi? (and variant-id (> (count substrates) 1))
   The declared substrate set is used ONLY as a COUNT. One substrate -> the `:else` branch.

2. canvas.cljs:609-644, the `:else` branch:
     (let [resolved-view (rf/view view-id)]  ... [resolved-view eff-args] ...)
   Straight to the framework view registry, then embedded as a REAGENT hiccup vector. `substrate->render-fn` is never consulted. The `:reagent` registry entry (multi_substrate.cljs:130-145) is DEAD CODE on this path.

3. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/canonical.cljc:126-127, the `render-variant` host-render hook:
     (ui-multi-substrate/render-decorated-view :reagent frame view effective-args decorators)
   `:reagent` is a LITERAL. `render-decorated-view` (multi_substrate.cljs:229-247) does route through the registry, so this path is registry-based but PINNED.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is a bug with a user today: a variant declaring `:substrates #{:uix}` — a set of size one, which is what a single-substrate UIx story looks like — takes the `:else` branch and RENDERS UNDER REAGENT. The canvas and `render-variant` agree with each other only because both are wrong the same way. Nothing in the gate matrix exercises a non-Reagent substrate end to end (the only live-render PR gate is `npm run test:story-play-scripts`), so no gate can catch it.

WHAT TO DO — and keep it to this, it is not an invitation to rework the registry:
 - Route canvas.cljs's `:else` branch through `multi-substrate/render-decorated-view` with the single declared substrate (`(first substrates)`), so the one-substrate case and the many-substrate case resolve the renderer the same way.
 - Make canonical.cljc:126-127 read the active/declared substrate instead of the literal.
 - Keep the two-level miss behaviour the multi_substrate.cljs:155-174 docstring defends (fragment-level inline diagnostic vs cell-level error cell). Do not fold them.
 - Note the ordering dependency the current code relies on: `install-reagent-substrate!` must run before the host-render install (canonical.cljc:167-168).

WATCH FOR: `safe-decorated-view` currently wraps the canvas result and `render-decorated-view` wraps its own; do not decorate twice. The a11y anchor `data-rf-story-variant-root` is stamped by the canvas path (canvas.cljs:634) and NOT by the grid cells (multi_substrate.cljs:296-299) — do not lose it in the reroute; if the grid should stamp it too, that is a separate bead, not this one.

FENCE (uncontended — no open PR and no live worker touches tools/story, checked 2026-08-15 15:46 AUSEST):
  tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs
  tools/story/src/re_frame/story/canonical.cljc
  tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs
  tools/story/test/**
NOT hot zone. Do NOT touch spec/*, implementation/**, or implementation/shadow-cljs.edn.

GATES: `clojure -M:test` from tools/story (JVM; CI job `jvm-tools-story`), and `npm run test:cljs` from implementation/ (tools/story/src + test are on the node-test build's source paths, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:363-364). Add a CLJS arm that registers a STUB substrate and asserts the single-pane path dispatches to its render-fn — that is the arm rf2-nfwbt recovered for `render-view` and it does not exist for the canvas path.

STORY SPEC: tools/story/spec/ is the per-tool spec tree, NOT the repo-root hot zone. Story carries no same-PR spec-sync obligation (rf2-5gka established this); the weaker tools/README.md convention applies. Update tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md if the shipped behaviour changes, or say plainly why not.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #8306 (worker/storyreg-3afns), commit e2557d5584. Both cited sites verified at source before changing anything, and both claims held: canvas.cljs:498 used the substrate set only as a COUNT, with the :else branch at :609-644 calling (rf/view view-id) directly and embedding a Reagent hiccup vector; canonical.cljc:126-127 passed a literal :reagent into render-decorated-view.

Both now resolve the renderer through substrate->render-fn — the same lookup the grid already used. The canvas :else branch calls multi-substrate/render-view with (first substrates); canonical reads the declared set off the compiled plan's [:world :substrates], which already rides render-inputs' :plan (so render.cljc needed no change). Added single-render-substrate to reduce a declared set to one substrate under the rule 'never paint under a substrate the variant did not declare' — multi-substrate variants declaring :reagent are behaviour-unchanged.

The bead's three watch-fors were all honoured: decoration happens exactly ONCE (the canvas consumes render-view and keeps its own safe-decorated-view wrap, because render-decorated-view resolves decorator refs WITHOUT the mode/cell-override run-opts the canvas threads in); the two-level miss behaviour is kept unfolded; data-rf-story-variant-root is preserved on the canvas path. The install-reagent-substrate!-before-host-install ordering is untouched.

WITNESS: tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/canvas_substrate_routing_cljs_test.cljs — 5 deftests that DISTINGUISH which substrate rendered (uix stub marker present AND reagent marker absent), driving the private canvas-inner via @#'. This is the arm the bead asked for and it did not exist. Proven to fail without the fix: reverting the two sources to origin/main (keeping helper + test so the failure is behavioural) gave captured EXIT=1, 7 failures / 2 errors, ALL in the witness ns, test count identical at 13930 so the revert was scoped. The failure text quotes the defect verbatim: the canvas rendered 'rendered under reagent' for a variant declaring :substrates #{:uix}.

GATES (captured exits, not harness-reported — they disagreed twice): fast-PR spine EXIT=0; npm run test:cljs EXIT=0 (13930 tests / 70350 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors); clojure -M:test in tools/story EXIT=0 (1835 / 6747, 0 failures 0 errors); check_doc_slugs.py EXIT=0. JVM gate's tree-identity proved by a hash-verified planted fault in plan.cljc's :substrates fold — EXIT=1, 1 failure, with test/assertion counts identical to the green control.

SCOPE HELD: the one closed substrate enum (schemas.cljc:288) is unchanged and schemas.cljc is not in the diff; zero hicasso references added (rf2-2dbpd remains blocked behind the rf2-1gy4e ruling). Story's own Reagent chrome untouched.

SPEC: tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md gains a 'One declared substrate — the single pane' subsection; shipped behaviour changed, so it was updated rather than waived.

FILED: rf2-r4coe (P2) — workspace.cljc's variant-cell-inner carries the SAME (rf/view view-id) shape, deliberately NOT fixed here because the workspace has no substrate axis at all (never reads :substrates; its docstring pins it as single-substrate), so making it substrate-aware is new behaviour needing a ruling, not a bypass removal.

title: [story] Story has NO hicasso support — it stories Reagent and UIx, and hicasso is the native substrate
description:
MIKE'S DIRECTION 2026-08-15: 'Get story right', alongside 'complete hicasso'. This is the largest concrete gap between those two.

MEASURED AT TRUNK TIP, 2026-08-15 15:40 AUSEST — re-take rather than trust:

  tools/story/src   138 clj/cljs/cljc files
  tools/story/test  182
  tools/story/spec   32
  files mentioning hicasso: ZERO

Story's substrate awareness is REAGENT and UIX only. rg over tools/story/src returns reagent in ~50 files and uix in ~8 (story.cljc, lifecycle.cljc, runtime.cljc, schemas.cljc, share.cljc, url_state.cljc, ui/multi_substrate.cljs). Not one hicasso hit anywhere.

THE CONTRAST THAT MAKES THIS URGENT: XRAY ALREADY DID THIS WORK. tools/xray/src carries 8 hicasso-aware files including FIVE DEDICATED PANELS — panels/hicasso.cljs, hicasso_advisor.cljc, hicasso_causal.cljc, hicasso_helpers.cljc, hicasso_reads.cljs — plus focus.cljc, registry.cljs and panels/epoch/format.cljc. So the Tool-Pair contract demonstrably CAN carry hicasso; Story simply has not taken it.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING MERELY INCOMPLETE. Story is this project's Storybook analogue: the surface where a programmer authors a component in isolation, exercises its states and records expectations. Hicasso is re-frame2 NATIVE. So today a programmer choosing the native substrate cannot story their components at all, while a programmer on the Reagent adapter can. That inverts the intended message about which substrate is first-class, and it is exactly the kind of friction the stance's 'high productivity, low friction' clause exists to prevent.

ui/multi_substrate.cljs is the file that names the supported set, and it is the honest place to start reading.

A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING worth checking while in there: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs names helix, reagent and uix but NOT hicasso, even though xray has hicasso PANELS. So xray may render hicasso data while being unable to MOUNT into a hicasso host. Verify at source; it may be deliberate (xray's own chrome need not be native) or it may be a real gap. Do not assume.

THIS BEAD IS THE PARENT. It is not a single dispatch — 138 source files and a substrate abstraction is a programme, not a task. The first dispatch is a SURVEY that reads how Story abstracts a substrate today, establishes what hicasso support would actually require, and files the phased beads. Nobody should start editing Story before that survey lands.

DO NOT let the survey turn into a rewrite proposal. Story works for two substrates already; the question is what the third costs, not whether Story's design is ideal. Reject a remedy that re-architects Story to add hicasso — that is the gold-plating the stance rejects.
notes:
PHASE-1 SURVEY LANDED, 2026-08-15 15:46 AUSEST (worker/story-survey). No code changed, no PR opened — the output is beads. This bead stays OPEN as the parent.

CENSUS RE-TAKEN, three independent means agreeing (rg --files, find, git ls-files):
  tools/story/src 138, tools/story/test 182, tools/story/spec 33 (this bead said 32; it is 31 top-level + 2 under spec/findings/).
  reagent-mentioning src files 72 (rg -il and grep -rli agree; this bead's "~50" was low).
  uix-mentioning src files 10 (this bead's "~8" was low).
  hicasso-mentioning files in tools/story: ONE, not zero — tools/story/deps.edn:92-108, a comment block, and it matters (below).

THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THIS BEAD EXPECTED. Story's substrate abstraction is an OPEN runtime registry with a public register-substrate! (ui/multi_substrate.cljs:90-126) — and THE DEFAULT RENDER PATH DOES NOT USE IT. canvas.cljs:498 uses the declared substrate set only as a COUNT; a set of size one falls to the :else branch at :609-644, which goes straight to rf/view and embeds the result as a Reagent hiccup vector. canonical.cljc:126-127 passes a LITERAL :reagent to the render-variant host hook. So a variant declaring :substrates #{:uix} renders under Reagent TODAY. That is a live defect with a user, not a hicasso feature request, and it is the true blocker: no third substrate can work until the registry is actually consulted. Filed as rf2-3afns (P1).

ONE BEAD OR FIFTEEN? Neither — FOUR phases, and none of them re-architects anything. There is exactly ONE closed substrate enum in the whole repository (schemas.cljc:288, [:set [:enum :reagent :uix]], verified with rg -n 'enum :reagent' over the tree); everything else is docstring prose or an open registry. Of the 39 src files that actually :require reagent, 37 are under story/ui/ — Story's OWN CHROME, not an assumption about the subject. Story's core is substrate-neutral.

THE CHEAPEST FINDING, and it is the good news: HICASSO NEEDS NO NEW PLUMBING TO PAINT IN STORY'S CANVAS. h/as-component (hicasso.cljc:581-596) is the purpose-built outward bridge — it "mounts a minted Hicasso view under the frame it is already in ... the frame comes from React context, and no second root, state owner or props ABI appears anywhere". Story's canvas already wraps the subject in [rf/frame-provider {:frame variant-id}] (canvas.cljs:606,632), and impl/mount.cljs:32-37 confirms that provider is the same re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context every React-shaped adapter reads. h/mount! is not needed and would be wrong here — it creates a root, and the canvas is already inside one.

THE ONE THING THAT GENUINELY BLOCKS, AND IT IS A RULING FOR MIKE: a story names its subject with :component <keyword>, resolved through re-frame's view registrar (schemas.cljc:436,915; core.cljc:768-774). h/defview computes a view-name AND a source coord (hicasso.cljc:224-225) but registers neither with the registrar. The keyword also buys Story its argtypes auto-derivation off reg-view metadata, which defview has no slot for. Three costed options on rf2-1gy4e (P1) — Story-side widen, Hicasso-side registration, or refuse.

AND A PRIOR QUESTION THAT MAY DISSOLVE IT: Hicasso ships NO adapter (rg for ':kind :rf.adapter' under implementation/hicasso is empty; there is no :rf.adapter/hicasso anywhere in the repo; both Hicasso testbeds boot (rf/init! uix-adapter/adapter)). The canonical adapter enum is spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md :2718 and :2800-2809, and hicasso is correctly absent from it. So Story's :substrates axis and core's adapter axis are DIFFERENT AXES, and schemas.cljc:282-283's claim to mirror "the framework's closed set" is already false. That is on rf2-1gy4e too.

THE EARLIER REFUSALS DO NOT SETTLE THIS, and I checked rather than assumed. rf2-jkdy, rf2-l86mm and rf2-2og6s refused re-pointing TOOL-TIER READS at Hicasso, because a mounted boundary is keyed by its read set and mints no identity. That is correct and it stands. But it answers "which view is this mounted boundary?" — asked backwards from the runtime. Storying asks the forward question, where the author names the view in source. Different question, and the deps.edn comment that cites those beads is about the retired view-tool donor tier, not about rendering.

WHAT XRAY HAD TO DO, AND HOW MUCH TRANSFERS. Xray's hicasso work was roughly 99% NEW SURFACE and 1% wiring: 5 dedicated panel files (2,779 LOC) plus 7 test files (3,228 LOC) and 2 spec docs, against FIVE lines of wiring — one require and two (hicasso/install!) calls in registry.cljs (:81, :340, :1317), one keyword in focus.cljc:126's valid-panels set, and one deps coordinate. It consumes ONE namespace (re-frame.hicasso.tool) in ONE file (panels/hicasso_reads.cljs), four fns, every call try/nil-guarded, zero ownership plane. The transferable lesson is the SHAPE, not the volume: Xray was cheap to wire because it had a per-panel install! sequence designed for exactly that, and Story has the same thing in register-substrate!. Story's problem is that its equivalent seam is bypassed, which Xray's was not. The 2,779 LOC of panels do NOT transfer — Story renders a component, it does not build a new inspector.

SPEC RISK: NONE ON Tool-Pair. spec/Tool-Pair.md has zero hicasso mentions and is militantly substrate-NEUTRAL by construction (:69, :76 — "a tool that names reagent.core/flush! is non-conforming and breaks under UIx"). spec/007-Stories.md names no view substrate at all (its one matching line, :584, is a path inside a relocation note). So no repo-root hot-zone spec bead is needed for this programme. The only hot-zone touch in the whole plan is implementation/shadow-cljs.edn plus .github/workflows in the testbed phase, isolated to rf2-kttom with a sole-toucher fence.

PHASES FILED (all discovered-from this bead):
  rf2-3afns  P1  route the single-pane path + render-variant through the registry (no hicasso; fixes UIx today) — DISPATCHABLE NOW
  rf2-1gy4e  P1  RULING: how does a story name a hicasso view? — HOLD FOR MIKE
  rf2-2dbpd  P2  register the :hicasso render-fn over h/as-component; widen SubstrateSet — blocked-by 3afns + 1gy4e
  rf2-kttom  P2  worked hicasso testbed + gate (HOT ZONE, sole toucher) — blocked-by 2dbpd

SEPARATE FINDINGS, not phases:
  rf2-ek9qb  P2  nothing installs :settled-boundary-hooks; the live shell plays at :provides :headless and settles on setTimeout 0
  rf2-f0ajt  P3  xray mount.cljs's refusal roster is stale — the secondary finding this bead asked to be verified. VERIFIED, and it is a roster/docs gap rather than a correctness gap: hicasso rides :rf.adapter/uix, which is already in the refusal set at mount.cljs:203-220, so a Hicasso host refuses the inline mount correctly today. Nothing says so.
  rf2-48rk3  P3  tools/template scaffolds only :reagent and :uix

HONEST COST: SMALL, and smaller than this bead feared. Not one bead, not fifteen — four, of which one is a ruling and one is a pre-existing bug that is not about hicasso at all. The 138 source files are not the cost centre; 37 of the 39 reagent-requiring files are Story's own chrome and are irrelevant to the subject's substrate. Once the ruling lands: rf2-3afns is a focused two-file reroute plus a stub-substrate test arm; rf2-2dbpd is a render-fn, a memoization decision and a one-line enum; rf2-kttom is a testbed and a build-id. NOTHING IN THE PLAN RE-ARCHITECTS STORY'S SUBSTRATE LAYER, and the survey found no evidence that it needs to.

WHAT REMAINS TO BE BROKEN DOWN: rf2-kttom's testbed content (which component, which states) is unspecified and should be shaped once rf2-2dbpd proves a boundary paints. Nothing else is deferred.

ONE THING TO PROVE BEFORE TRUSTING THE CHEAP PATH, flagged on rf2-2dbpd as a required spike: nothing in the repo renders a Hicasso boundary inside a REAGENT tree today. Every h/as-component call site is a Hicasso test or a UIx/native parent, and listing the .cljs files under implementation, testbeds and examples that require re-frame.hicasso and then filtering for reagent.core returns EMPTY. The crossing is designed and documented, but Reagent is not among its witnessed parents.

FENCE CHECK AT SURVEY TIME (2026-08-15 15:46 AUSEST): tools/story/** is UNCONTENDED. One open PR repo-wide (#8296/#8297 already merged; #8298 on skills/reagent-migration), and none of the four named live workers (overlay-1ppe0, seam-t32wg, epochroster-t7qh8, retire-survey) has a committed or uncommitted tools/story path.

title: hicasso SSR guide hydrates an absent client frame, so the payload seed is a no-op
description:

title: Confirm or overturn: the three 'surviving arm' figures in rf2-m4rpa's ruling were the retiring figure measured three ways
description:

sentence of it.

Measured at source: UIx 1.139-1.217, Reagent 1.154-1.272, slim 1.078-1.306 --
the same band. The claim that hicasso's codec is competitive survives on THREE
independent comparators instead of four.' It also said to RE-VERIFY THOSE THREE

THE RE-VERIFICATION REFUTES THE PREMISE. In
docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-freehand-codec-donor-arm.md, lines 260, 264 and
268, all three figures are the SAME comparison -- 'donor-fh / donor-r1 -- THE
CODEC' -- on the SAME row (mount-M), under three ADAPTER RUNS. In that
instrument uix/reagent/slim are adapter installs (one adapter per process, Spec
006), not arms. The arms are floor / reagent / reagent-slim / uix / donor-r1 /
donor-r2 / donor-fh.

CONSEQUENCE: those three numbers are the RETIRING figure measured three ways.
They do not survive the arm's retirement and cannot carry the codec claim in its
place. Writing 'survives on three independent comparators' would have been the
exact failure mode the ruling exists to prevent -- the retired figure
re-presented on a different arm count.

WHAT THE PR DID INSTEAD: stated that the codec axis does not survive the arm,
that no surviving figure is re-labelled to stand in for it, and that the
remaining donor ratios measure the shell (donor-r2/donor-r1), the substrate
(donor-r*/reagent*) and the frontier (donor-r*/uix). The figure itself is frozen
as a dated historical record, as ruled.

WHAT THIS BEAD DECIDES: whether Mike accepts that reading. If he does, this
closes as confirmed and nothing changes -- PR #8235 already reflects it. If he
does not, the specific sentence he wants written needs naming, because the
worker could find no surviving comparison that prices one runtime hiccup codec
against another.

Nothing is blocked either way. PR #8235 does not depend on the answer.

A worker cannot resolve this because resolving it means contradicting a stated ruling of yours, which is exactly the thing a worker should escalate rather than decide - and the rf2-m4rpa worker was right to execute the parts it could and decline to write the one sentence it could not.

THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS ONE-SIDED. The arms in that instrument are floor, reagent, reagent-slim, uix, donor-r1, donor-r2 and donor-fh. So UIx 1.139-1.217, Reagent 1.154-1.272 and slim 1.078-1.306 are one comparison measured three ways, not three independent comparators.

THE MAYOR RECOMMENDS ACCEPTING THE REFUTATION. Three reasons.

First, the reading is checkable and narrow: it turns on whether an adapter install is an arm, which Spec 006 settles, not on judgement about the numbers.

Second, the failure mode it avoids is the one this project keeps meeting. Writing survives on three independent comparators would have re-presented a RETIRING figure under a different arm count - the same defect as a mean restated as an upper bound, a non-comparability turned into a residual magnitude, and zero call sites called a vacuous law when it was an unmet one. Third, the band agreement that made the three figures look mutually corroborating is exactly what you would expect if they are the same quantity - it is evidence FOR the refutation, not against it.
