That is a real cost and it is why this needs you rather than me: it may change what the donor-arm retirement can conclude.

WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: a reading under which those three adapter runs ARE independent comparators for this claim - which would need Spec 006's one-adapter-per-process framing to be wrong or inapplicable here. If you think that is the case, say so and the sentence can be written as originally ruled.

title: lane_cache wiring gate is Freehand-scoped and dies with the tree, leaving 4 hicasso riders ungated
description:
FOUND BY rf2-it4y5 while re-homing the four shared Node bench helpers.

`lane_cache_wiring.test.cjs` enforces the central shared-build-id invariant: every driver that spawns a shadow-cljs release against a SHARED build id must call resetLaneBuildCache FIRST, with the SAME build id it releases. shadow-cljs derives the build cache dir from the build id alone, so N programs on one id share ONE cache entry; a rider that does not clear runs a bundle it did not build. The gate exists because riders kept landing armed and four had accumulated before anyone counted.

THE PROBLEM. The gate discovers riders with readdirSync(__dirname) -- 'discovered, never listed: a new driver is caught by existing, not by someone remembering to add it'. Its __dirname is implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/, and it asserts RIDERS.length >= 7 naming 'the 7 known freehand-release riders'. It is therefore a gate over FREEHAND's drivers only. When implementation/freehand/ is deleted, the gate goes with it.

WHAT IS LEFT UNGATED. Four hicasso bench drivers are riders of exactly this class today -- they call resetLaneBuildCache AND spawn a release via runner.js -- and no discovery gate covers them:

  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_run.cjs
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/retention_run.cjs
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/run.cjs
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/shapes/census_clock_run.cjs

They share build id 'hicasso-bench'. hicasso's lane_build.test.cjs is NOT this gate -- it tests lane_build.cjs, a different module. The readdirSync hits in the hicasso bench tree are all JSON dataset scans in clock_exit_path.test.cjs.

This is PRE-EXISTING (those four were never covered) but Freehand's deletion turns 'partially enforced' into 'not enforced at all', for a rule whose failure mode is silent: both builds exit 0 and the fault only shows as a runtime error in a page.

LIKELY SHAPE OF THE FIX. lane_cache.cjs now lives at implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/ (rf2-it4y5, PR #8210). The gate could move beside it and discover riders across the bench trees rather than one directory. That is a real redesign, not a move: multi-tree discovery needs its own honesty check to replace the 'RIDERS.length >= 7' fail-open guard. Not attempted under rf2-it4y5, which was a homing decision.

Do NOT fix by deleting the check.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8218 (2026-08-14). The build-id roster, whole-tree discovery, direct/door classification, two centralized cache clears, and 106-case focused gate are sound, but this owner's explicit #8210 acceptance residual is still unguarded. The new requires check accepts any require(...) text ending in lane_cache.cjs, and the fixtures are deliberately never executed. An in-memory probe replacing the corrected require('../lane_cache.cjs') with require('../invented/lane_cache.cjs') still satisfies that check; there is no bad-depth fixture or canonical-resolution assertion. Thus a stale or invented same-basename path can again make the regression fixture look faithful while resolving nowhere.

Keep this exact owner open until the fixture contract proves its lane_cache require resolves to implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/lane_cache.cjs (or an equivalent bad-depth control reds). Do not pin one relative depth across real riders; this is the narrow fixture-fidelity residual already recorded here, not a request to redesign the roster.

THAT IS A HOLD DONE PROPERLY and worth copying: it named a MECHANICAL CONDITION a later reader could evaluate, rather than a judgement. It cost one command to discharge.

The invariant: the compiler derives its cache directory from the build id ALONE, fixed before per-program config merges apply, so N programs sharing an id share one cache entry and any program that does not clear it first RUNS A BUNDLE IT DID NOT BUILD. Both builds exit 0; the failure appears only at page load.

THE SCOPE WAS FOUR TIMES WHAT THE BEAD SAID — fifteen riders, two outside the tree named, and three of the four named drivers reach the compiler through a BUILD DOOR rather than directly. Re-homing the old gate verbatim would still have missed twelve of fifteen.

AND THE REBUILT GATE DISCOVERS BY CONTENT, not by directory: anchored on the folder holding the build config, never on the folder the test lives in. A dying lane now goes RED — proven by moving the donor tree out of the worktree entirely and taking exit 1 naming the empty lane. It also fixed two real defects on the way: two drivers hand-rolled the cache clear without the retry loop the shared helper carries.

title: hd8_witnesses donor-fh arm: decide what the published codec figure becomes when Freehand is deleted
description:
FROM rf2-0yp7w P0 (PR #8202), which REFUSED a briefed ruling and is escalating
the decision rather than taking it.

THE BRIEF RULED: drop hd8_witnesses.cljs's Freehand comparison arm, on the
reasoning that its sibling arms already cover the axis. It carried an explicit
escape: "If dropping it turns out to invalidate a published figure, STOP and
report rather than deleting a number's basis silently." It does, so P0 stopped.

WHAT DEPENDS ON THE ARM:

  docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-freehand-codec-donor-arm.md is an ENTIRE
  studio page whose subject is `donor-fh / donor-r1`, labelled THE CODEC,
  reported across three adapters and six rounds with recorded per-round
  figures (uix 1.139-1.217, reagent 1.154-1.272, slim 1.078-1.306, plus a
  second table on the corrected clock).

  docs/design/hicasso/studio/hd8-composed-donor-arm.md cites it and records
  the sweep schedule as a SEVEN-ARM mount plan that `donor-fh` rides
  (rf2-2rtt6.29). Dropping the arm makes it six.

  hd8_rows.cljs carries `:donor-fh "re-frame.freehand.react/element"` as a
  recorded provenance label.

  hd8_witnesses.cljs's `codecs-differ?` is a FATAL-AT-BOOT check that the two
  codec doors are demonstrably different implementations -- probed on
  `^{:key ...}` vector metadata, which reagent-slim honours and Freehand
  refuses by name. Its docstring: `donor-fh / donor-r1` "is the one figure in
  this instrument that would be unreadable if the answer were no", because a
  ratio of 1.0 could then mean the codecs cost the same OR the arm ran one
  codec twice. Remove the arm and that check has no subject.

STATE AFTER P0: the arm and its `re-frame.freehand.react` require are
UNTOUCHED and still compile (verified: test:hicasso-compile green, 131 lane
namespaces, zero warnings). It dies with Freehand at P4.

THE DECISION FOR MIKE / THE MAYOR, and it is a judgement not a fix:
  (a) retire the arm and mark the studio page's figure as historical, naming
      the commit at which its instrument last existed; or
  (b) keep the codec axis by re-pointing the fourth arm at a codec that
      survives -- but the page's whole argument is that `donor-fh` is
      `donor-r1` with ONE TOKEN CHANGED, so any substitute changes what the
      figure means; or
  (c) accept the arm's deletion and delete the page's headline figure with
      it, explicitly.

Nothing here blocks P0. It blocks P4 from being taken silently.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
THIS ONE IS FOR MIKE, AND I AM NOT DISPATCHING IT (mayor, 2026-08-14).

It asks what the PUBLISHED CODEC FIGURE becomes once hd8_witnesses' Freehand comparison arm is dropped. I ruled the arm dropped when briefing the bench re-home — on the mapper's reasoning that its sibling arms already cover the axis and the B-spine that arm belongs to is Freehand's own programme rather than hicasso's. That ruling stands for the CODE.

BUT A PUBLISHED FIGURE IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF THING. It is a claim this project has made in a document, measured against a comparison that is about to stop existing. Deciding what replaces it is deciding what the performance claim MEANS, not just which test compiles. That is Mike's call and mine to surface rather than settle.

WHAT MIKE NEEDS IN ORDER TO DECIDE, and whoever picks this up should assemble it rather than propose an answer: which published figures actually cite that arm, what each figure claims, and what the surviving arms — Reagent, UIx, reagent-slim — would say in its place. If the answer is that no published figure depends on it, this closes as moot and no decision is needed.

DO NOT SILENTLY RE-BASELINE A PUBLISHED NUMBER. Replacing the comparison and keeping the sentence is the one outcome that would be dishonest.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MY BRIEFED RULING WAS WRONG AND THE ESCAPE CLAUSE CAUGHT IT (mayor, 2026-08-14).

I pre-authorised dropping hd8_witnesses' Freehand comparison arm, on the phase-1 mapper's reasoning that its sibling arms cover the axis. I attached the condition 'if dropping it turns out to invalidate a published figure, STOP and report'. THE WORKER STOPPED, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO.

WHAT IT FOUND AT SOURCE: donor-fh is the SOLE SUBJECT of an entire studio page whose headline figure is labelled THE CODEC, and hd8-composed-donor-arm.md records the sweep as a SEVEN-ARM PLAN that donor-fh rides. It also carries codecs-differ?, a FATAL-AT-BOOT check whose removal would make a 1.0 ratio unreadable — so dropping the arm does not merely remove a comparison, it removes the thing that makes the remaining number interpretable.

THE ARM IS LEFT INTACT. Nothing is broken today.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW DECIDES, and it is Mike's rather than a worker's: what the published codec figure becomes when Freehand is removed. That is deciding what a performance CLAIM MEANS, not which test compiles.

ASSEMBLE THE EVIDENCE, DO NOT PROPOSE AN ANSWER: which published figures cite donor-fh, what each claims, what codecs-differ? actually guards, and what the surviving arms — Reagent, UIx, reagent-slim — would say in its place. If no published figure depends on it, this closes as moot.

DO NOT SILENTLY RE-BASELINE. Replacing the comparison and keeping the sentence is the one dishonest outcome.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth carrying into future briefs: a pre-authorised ruling needs an escape clause naming the specific thing that would invalidate it. 'Drop the arm' alone would have shipped this. 'Drop the arm unless it invalidates a published figure' surfaced it in one pass.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MIKE RULED (2026-08-14): adopt the mayor's recommendation. Three actions, and one thing that must not be lost.

1. RETIRE THE ARM WITH THE TREE. Do NOT vendor a frozen copy of the donor codec. Keeping retired code alive to feed a benchmark resurrects what is being removed, and it rots.

2. FREEZE THE PUBLISHED DONOR FIGURE AS A DATED HISTORICAL RECORD. Keep the number. Add its commit provenance and the date it was measured. DO NOT DELETE IT AND DO NOT RE-BASELINE IT. A reader must be able to see what was measured, against what, and when.

3. LET THE THREE SURVIVING ARMS CARRY THE CLAIM. Measured at source: UIx 1.139-1.217, Reagent 1.154-1.272, slim 1.078-1.306 — the same band. The claim that hicasso's codec is competitive survives on THREE independent comparators instead of four. That is a smaller claim honestly stated, not a weaker one dishonestly preserved.

THE THING THAT MUST NOT BE LOST: the arm carries codecs-differ?, a FATAL-AT-BOOT check. It exists so a 1.0 ratio cannot be read as 'fast' when it actually means 'the two codecs are the same code'. The surviving arms need that check, or its absence needs stating explicitly.

THE FAILURE MODE THIS RULING EXISTS TO PREVENT: deleting the arm, keeping the sentence, and letting the figure quietly become a three-arm mean presented as the old four-arm one. Every place the figure appears must say how many arms it rests on.

RE-VERIFY THE THREE SURVIVING FIGURES AT SOURCE before writing anything. I read them from the bead, not from the measurement records, and twelve of my measurements or relayed claims were refuted today.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
EXECUTED, WITH ONE PREMISE REFUTED AT SOURCE (worker, 2026-08-14). PR #8235.

Actions 1 and 2 executed as ruled. The arm is retired with the tree, no frozen
copy of the donor codec is vendored, and the published figure is kept as a dated
historical record with commit provenance (measured 2026-07-31 at e385cef113; the

measured under three ADAPTER RUNS. uix/reagent/slim there are adapter installs,

do not survive it and cannot carry a claim in its place.

So the sentence 'the claim survives on three independent comparators' was NOT
written: writing it would have been exactly the failure mode the ruling exists

title: The shipped guide's chapter 18 is written against re-frame.hicasso.server, which does not exist
description:
FOUND BY THE GUIDE PROMOTION (rf2-0yp7w phase 5, PR #8199 merged 2026-08-14) while checking every aliased verb in the draft guide against implementation/hicasso/.

THE DEFECT. Chapter 18 of the now-SHIPPED hicasso guide is written against re-frame.hicasso.server and server/render. That namespace DOES NOT EXIST. hicasso.cljc carries a comment saying so and naming the draft guide as the thing written against it.

WHY THIS IS P1 NOW RATHER THAN P3 YESTERDAY. Until an hour ago that chapter sat in docs/design/, excluded from the build and read by nobody. It is now in the shipped nav at docs/core/hicasso/, which is the front door for every new reader. A guide chapter teaching a namespace that cannot be required is worse than a missing chapter: the reader follows it, it fails, and they conclude the library is broken rather than the documentation.

THREE OTHER NAMES RUN AHEAD OF THE CODE, all found the same way and all named explicitly in the index rather than papered over: h/fn and h/frame ship as h/hfn and h/hframe; h/mount! ships as h/root!; and h/hydrate! is NOT EXPORTED, held deliberately under rf2-k1mp. Those three are spelling drift and the index now names them. The server namespace is different in kind — it is an absence, not a rename.

THE DECISION, and it is a real one under Mike's direction that hicasso be FULLY IMPLEMENTED WITH NOTHING DEFERRED: either re-frame.hicasso.server ships and chapter 18 becomes true, or chapter 18 leaves the shipped guide until it does. Shipping the chapter against a namespace that does not exist is the one option that is not honest.

MY READ, offered not imposed: server-side rendering is not a small feature to bolt on, and the SSR work already has its own beads and its own suites. So the likely honest sequence is to pull chapter 18 from the nav NOW — a small, safe edit — and restore it when the namespace lands. That keeps the shipped guide true today without deciding the roadmap.

VERIFY BOTH LIMBS AT SOURCE FIRST: that chapter 18 really is in the shipped nav, and that re-frame.hicasso.server really has no implementation. Four of my measurements were refuted by workers today, and this one is second-hand to me.

FENCE: worker/guidepin-qgbu5 holds docs/core/hicasso/ and mkdocs.yml right now for the digest-pinning work. Sequence behind it or hand it to that worker.

The second candidate (closer-as-wrapper) is left unruled and unforeclosed. Red-state probe: swapping mount/tree for a plain provider-over-root tree reds the parity witness, 2 failures, exit 1.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
SCOPE IS SEVEN FORMS AND A BROKEN INSTALL COORDINATE, NOT ONE CHAPTER (mayor, 2026-08-14). Raising this from a chapter-18 problem to a guide-truth problem, on a second independent measurement.

The rf2-r4j91 worker checked the draft guide against shipped surface while writing the Reagent migration skill, and tabulated what it found in that skill's spec/inputs.md so the next author does not re-derive it. Its list:

  server/render — the namespace does not exist (this bead's original finding)
  ssr/hydrate! — does not exist

A THIRD GUARANTEE LANDED THAT NOBODY ASKED FOR AND THAT BEARS DIRECTLY ON THIS BEAD: R3 makes the declared-gap LEDGER LIVE — it reds when a declared gap CLOSES. So when re-frame.hicasso.server ships, the guide's own note saying it does not exist becomes a build failure rather than quiet staleness. comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
TWO GATES NOW PAIR TO HOLD THIS BOUNDARY, and the pairing is the useful part (mayor, 2026-08-14).

The facade-inventory gate that landed in #8203 reads the DOOR's inventory: which names reach re-frame.hicasso and whether each has a row. The guide-sample gate in PR #8204 reads what the GUIDE TEACHES against that door, and its R3 arm makes the declared-gap ledger LIVE — it reds when a declared gap CLOSES.

SO WHEN THE SERVER NAMESPACE SHIPS, BOTH FIRE, AND THEY SAY DIFFERENT THINGS. The facade gate says the door changed. title: EPIC: retire and REMOVE re-frame.freehand and re-frame.ui — 821 tracked files plus live core and ssr references
description:
MIKE'S RULING 2026-08-14: 'Freehand and re-frame2.ui are to be retired and removed ASAP.' The architecture is a Reagent adapter and a UIx adapter, plus hicasso as re-frame2 native.

CENSUS TAKEN AT TRUNK TIP, 2026-08-14 — these are measurements, and a later pass must re-take them rather than trust them:

  implementation/freehand   590 tracked files
  implementation/ui         231 tracked files

REFERENCES OUTSIDE THOSE TREES, by directory, highest first: spec/conformance/freehand/fixtures 46, implementation/scripts 19, spec 18, docs/design/freehand/decisions 17, docs/api 12, scripts 11, examples/real-apps/realworld_resources 10, docs/EP 10, implementation/ssr/test 9, docs/design/hicasso/studio 9, implementation/core/test 8, implementation/core/src 7, tools/xray/src 6, implementation/ssr/src 6.

THE LINE THAT MAKES THIS AN EPIC RATHER THAN A DELETION: implementation/core/src and implementation/ssr/src BOTH reference Freehand. These are live runtime dependencies in first-class artefacts, not documentation. Deleting the trees without untangling those breaks the build.

ALSO IMPLICATED: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn carries freehand source paths and a :node-test-freehand build; .github/scripts and .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml name freehand; spec/ has 18 referencing files and 46 conformance fixtures — spec is HOT ZONE and takes one toucher.

SUGGESTED PHASING, not ruled — the first dispatch should propose the order and defend it:
  1. Map every reference and classify each as (a) a live dependency that must be re-homed, (b) a test or fixture that dies with the tree, (c) prose that must be re-pointed or deleted.
  2. Re-home or delete the core and ssr dependencies FIRST. Nothing else is safe until those are clear.
  3. Then the build configuration, workflows and scripts.
  4. Then the trees themselves.
  5. Then spec, docs and skills prose — largest by count, lowest by risk.

RELATED AND ALREADY OPEN: rf2-5gka migrates Story's presence bridge OFF Freehand and points the right way. rf2-r4j91 re-aims the Reagent migration skill at hicasso. Neither is blocked by this epic; both reduce it.

DO NOT DELETE ANYTHING IN THE FIRST DISPATCH. The first pass produces the map and the order. A blind removal of 821 files with live core references is how a tree goes red for a day.

comments.text:
PHASE 1 MAP COMPLETE — AND THIS EPIC'S CENTRAL PREMISE, WHICH I WROTE, IS FALSE (mayor, 2026-08-14).

I said core/src and ssr/src carry LIVE RUNTIME DEPENDENCIES on Freehand, and that nothing else was safe until they were untangled. The mapper extracted every ns form across core/src, ssr/src and ssr-ring/src and grepped it: ZERO requires of re-frame.freehand.* or re-frame.ui.*. All 13 references are PROSE in comments and docstrings, plus three data facts — two registry rows and a producer vector in late_bind/directory.cljc, one call BY KEYWORD in frame.cljc (a documented no-op when the artefact is absent), and verbatim COPIES of the ui conversion tables in ssr/ui_tree.cljc that exist precisely because the Independence rule forbids ssr requiring ui.

SO FREEHAND AND re-frame.ui CAN BE DELETED WITHOUT CHANGING A LINE OF SHIPPED CORE OR SSR RUNTIME CODE. My reading of a directory histogram as evidence of coupling was wrong; a reference count cannot distinguish a require from a comment, and I treated it as though it could.

THE FIVE REAL BLOCKERS, none where I was looking:

B1 — implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:526 carries :build-defaults {:build-hooks [(re-frame.ui.compiler.build-hook/hook)]}. That is a REPO-WIDE DEFAULT ON EVERY BUILD. Delete implementation/ui/src without editing that line and every build in the repository fails to resolve the hook symbol. It must land in the SAME COMMIT as the ui/src deletion — not before, not after. This is the sharpest item in the epic and it was invisible in the census.

B2 — the hicasso bench harness lives inside Freehand. 204 files, and implementation/hicasso has no bench directory at all.

B3 — migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod carries ../../../implementation/freehand/test on its production :paths, and two src files genuinely require re-frame.bench.hicasso.front.slot. A shipped JVM artefact reaching into the tree being deleted. B2's re-home resolves it for free.

B4 — core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj walks directory.cljc and scans for matching call sites; deleting the trees reds it. Trivial data edit, but mandatory.

B5 — implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/.../gen.clj hardcodes a roster of ~60 freehand namespaces plus the ui set, gated by three JVM tests, generating spec/api-manifest.edn which ui_context.clj then reads to generate the committed ui-context sheet. Crosses into spec (hot zone) AND skills. That generated sheet serial-bottlenecks merges — sequence it, never parallelise it.

ORDER: P0 re-home the bench harness. P1 the tools/ and migration/ live requires. P2 core/src data plus the gen.clj roster plus spec regen. P3 build configuration, atomically with the deletion. P4 delete the trees. P5 prose — 152 docs files, 19 spec files, mkdocs nav — largest, lowest risk, fully parallelisable once P4 lands.

Freehand and re-frame.ui are INDEPENDENT OF EACH OTHER and CI asserts it: test.yml's JVM freehand job carries a step 'Assert no dependency on the re-frame.ui donor'. So P3 through P5 can run as two parallel lanes after P2, except that B1 forces the ui lane to own shadow-cljs.edn first.

THREE REQUIRED CHECKS THE FAST SPINE DOES NOT RUN are load-bearing here and must be run directly by whoever does P3 and P4: the donor-independence assertion, npm run test:ui-isolation, and npm run test:bspine-compile.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
P0 WORKER STALLED MID-REVERT, RESUMED — AND IT FOUND SOMETHING THE MAP DID NOT (mayor, 2026-08-14).

WHAT HAPPENED. The bench re-home worker hit the harness watchdog after 600 seconds with no progress. Its last words: the JSON rewrites hit BLOB-PINNED PROVENANCE RECORDS inside the recorded measurements, and it was reverting them because they must move verbatim.

THAT FINDING IS IMPORTANT AND SHOULD SURVIVE ANY RESTART. The 36 .json and 4 .edn recorded-measurement files are not inert data — they carry blob-pinned provenance. So the mechanical path rewrite that the .cjs runners need is exactly WRONG for the .json and .edn records: rewriting a path inside one breaks the pin that ties the record to the run that produced it. My brief said move them verbatim; the worker discovered WHY, which is stronger.

STATE WHEN IT STOPPED: 219 modified files, ZERO commits. Roughly two hours of work entirely in the working tree. I did not commit on its behalf — a half-reverted state committed by someone else is worse than no commit, and only that worker knows how far its revert reached. Resumed via message instead.

THE LIKELY CAUSE IS MACHINE LOAD, NOT THE CHANGE. Processor queue read 81 with five workers plus CI contending. That is the same condition behind the par-compile abort another worker saw today.

ALSO FLAGGED TO IT: its dirty list includes implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs, .gitattributes, implementation/README.md and two docs/design/hicasso/studio pages — NONE of them in its fence. Most likely a path-rewrite sweep that widened. core/src especially needs a specific reason, because the phase-1 map established core has ZERO requires on Freehand.

LESSON FOR THE NEXT P0 BRIEF, whoever writes it: require commits at milestones rather than at the end. A branch with commits survives a stall; a working tree does not. This move is large enough that the natural rhythm — move files, fix requires, fix paths, run gates — is four commits, and any of them would have been worth keeping.

WHICH DIRECTION IT FAILS IN, and it is the expensive one. A prefix over-counts, so the census sends a worker to edit surfaces that are healthy — the same class as a fence naming a path that does not exist, except it fails toward action rather than inaction. Every count this epic and its children have published over an unanchored pattern should be READ DOWN, and none should be re-used without re-derivation. Controls that establish the pattern discriminates rather than merely returning few: 'hicasso' returns 966 files, a nonsense token returns 0, and 're-frame.uix'/'re_frame.uix' return 0 — so 're-frame\.ui' carries no equivalent trap and only the hyphenated coordinate form does.

TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE NEXT SLICE:
1. Anchor the coordinate form: 're-frame2-ui([^x]|$)'. Do not anchor by adding 'uix' to an exclusion list — a list re-opens the gap on the next sibling coordinate.
2. Re-derive rather than inherit. This epic's description already carries the standing caution that its own 821-file scope line is a census and therefore a claim; this is the same lesson one level down, and it now has a named mechanism.

ALSO SETTLED BY THAT SLICE, so nobody re-opens it: the repo-root README.md carries NO donor residue — its only match is 'day8/re-frame2-uix' at line 187, which is the false positive above. And docs/api/re-frame.core.md's ':rf.adapter/freehand' and ':rf.adapter/ui' rows need no bead: they are a faithful generated rendering of a DELIBERATE reserved-kind row at implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:27, pinned by spec/006 and spec/Conventions.md:103.

title: hicasso: tau stays unpinned — the controls are not a valid calibration population for the arms
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.140's V3 window on 2026-08-14 (PR #8152). V3's job was to
calibrate tau and then pin it, deleting the ALLOC_LEG_TOLERANCE placeholder line.
THE CALIBRATION INPUT WAS MEASURED. THE PIN WAS NOT TAKEN, and this bead is why.

WHAT V3 MEASURED. The controls-only run (P0_ALLOC_PLAN=controls, both D values,
six rounds, six writes) was the ONLY run of the window's nine to exit 0. Across
all 12 corroborated-clean control windows -- every one inside ALLOC_CONTROL_SLACK
of 8 B/double:

  control windows D=1,000 (6)   worst relative leg deviation 0.99%
  control windows D=400   (6)   worst relative leg deviation 0.00%
  idle windows            (6)   worst relative leg deviation 0.00%

Eleven of the twelve read EXACTLY 0.00%, with the six legs byte-identical. So the
natural spread of a corroborated-clean window on this rig is <= 1%.

WHY THAT DOES NOT YIELD A PIN. V3's stated rule is "a stated multiple of the
observed worst deviation, rounded up to a round number ... a small integer is the
expected answer". Applied honestly that lands tau at roughly 0.02 - 0.05.

AT tau ~ 0.03 A WINDOW CERTIFIES ONLY IF ITS LEG MEDIAN EXCEEDS ROUGHLY 230 KB
(the arms' fixed ~7 KB first-leg excess divided by tau -- see rf2-oiy1). No arm
on this rig reaches that except R=20, and R=20 is ALREADY REFUSED by the
collector at 900 KB - 1.5 MB against the 600,000 B onset. So a tau calibrated as
V3 specifies would refuse the ENTIRE LADDER.

The 0.25 placeholder is therefore FAR MORE PERMISSIVE than an honest calibration,
and it already refuses every floor window. Pinning the calibrated value would not
be a widening or a loosening -- it would be a tightening that stops the row
producing anything at all.

THE DIAGNOSIS, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THIS BEAD. The controls are not a valid
calibration population for the arms. Their work unit is a dropped .slice(), which
has NO first-write re-allocation in it. The arms' work unit is a dispatch-sync
plus a substrate drain, which HAS one, in 336 of 336 measured windows. Calibrating
a tolerance for the second population on the spread of the first assumes the two
have the same window-internal structure, and this window measured that they do
not.

V3's OWN ESCAPE CLAUSE IS WRITTEN FOR THE MIRROR CASE and its substance carries
over: "If the observed spread is so wide that no tau below 1 leaves margin, the
witness is not usable as specified -- report that rather than picking a tau that
certifies everything" (allocation-instrument-rework.md, Validity witness V3).
Here the controls' spread is so TIGHT that the calibrated tau certifies NOTHING.
Either way the instruction is the same: report it, do not pick a tau to suit.

THE OPTIONS, none taken here, with the arithmetic attached:

(a) CALIBRATE ON THE ARMS' OWN CLEAN WINDOWS instead of the controls -- the R=3
and R=7 rungs certify today and their non-first legs are tight. This makes the
calibration population match the population being judged. Needs a rule for which
arm windows are "corroborated clean" when the arms have no 8 B/double prediction
to be corroborated against, which is precisely why the brief reached for the
controls in the first place.

(b) REMOVE THE FIRST-LEG TERM FIRST (rf2-oiy1) and re-calibrate afterwards. If
the excess is removable, the arms' spread may collapse toward the controls' and
the stated rule works unchanged. THIS IS THE ORDERING THIS BEAD ASSUMES: it is
filed BLOCKED ON rf2-oiy1 for that reason, since calibrating against a defect is
how a tolerance gets set to accommodate the defect.

(c) KEEP tau AS A DECLARED PLACEHOLDER and say so in the row, on the ground that
no honest calibration exists while the first-leg term stands. Costs nothing and
is where the tree is today; the objection is that a placeholder that never
resolves is a gate nobody can audit.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, deliberately. tau was NOT pinned, NOT widened and NOT
narrowed. ALLOC_LEG_TOLERANCE stays 0.25 with its uncalibrated marker intact.
Pinning is a source edit -- the constant, the placeholder line and a structural
pin -- and a measurement window does not amend the instrument it is measuring on.
The calibration FIGURE is the window's deliverable; the pin is separate work and
this bead is its home.

EVIDENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-write-halfs-floor-is-the-pipeline.md
(PR #8152), section "V3 -- the tolerance calibrated, and what the calibration
implies".
close_reason: BRANCH (c): tau stays a declared placeholder at 0.25, reported unusable-as-specified on V3's own escape clause. Measured by PR #8377 on the primed instrument; verdict comment above is self-contained. Branch (b) REFUTED (the prime worked -- first-leg term replicates at median 6,864 B and the floor arm goes 6-of-6-refused to 41-of-72-certified -- but the arms' spread did NOT collapse: controls 0.99% worst, arms 0.00-38.91% median 2.69% over 42 collection-free non-excursion windows). Branch (a) REFUTED: the arms' clean windows are not one population, all 11 round-3 windows <= 0.19% vs all 11 round-2 windows 2.66-20.37% in each of six runs, so tau spans two orders of magnitude with the round. No gate widened or touched; only criterion 5's permitted witnesses run. Mechanism of the round-indexed dispersion filed as rf2-rs8q6.

Two workers there would merge-conflict and could silently revert each other, so this waits — but the stronger reason is that oiy1's outcome CHANGES this bead's answer: if leg 1 stops being the sole deviant, the calibration population is a different population and tau's honest value moves with it. oiy1's brief forbids it from touching ALLOC_LEG_TOLERANCE and requires it to report what its repair implies here. comments.text:
FENCE CLEARED, AND REPLACED BY A DIFFERENT ONE (mayor, 2026-08-14 06:16). PR #8159 is MERGED — the JVM http red that held it was transient (attempt 2 green), and the prime is now on main. So the 'wait for #8159' fence this bead carried is discharged, and with it the blockers on rf2-2rtt6.140 and rf2-2rtt6.139 further down the chain.

THE REMAINING FENCE IS THE QUIET BOX, not a dependency. Re-deriving tau means taking a FRESH window on the post-prime instrument, which is a measurement window by kind, and rf2-hic-036's window holds the box under a one-window-at-a-time grant. Lane order now: rf2-hic-036 (running, unblocks ~20 beads), then rf2-hic-045 (rf2-hic-071's only remaining open blocker), then this bead.

WHAT NOT TO DO WHEN IT RUNS: do not calibrate against the pre-prime figures. rf2-oiy1's worker was explicit that the prime removes the very asymmetry this bead's objection rests on — the controls' work unit has no first-write re-allocation and the arms' did — and reported that on its numbers the arms' legs are byte-identical once leg 1 is out, inside the controls' 1% spread. It deliberately adopted nothing on this bead's behalf. So the calibration population may now be valid where it was not, and that has to be re-measured rather than argued.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MAYOR 2026-08-15 23:47 — CLASSIFICATION, so the dispatch tick stops treating this as a measurement window. IT IS NOT ONE.

I inherited this bead in a list of nine "measurement lane" beads and have been carrying it as a clock window waiting for a quiet box. Read at source, it is nothing of the kind. Its own text says "THE OPTIONS, none taken here, with the arithmetic attached" and then enumerates them. Every number it needs has ALREADY BEEN MEASURED — by rf2-2rtt6.140's V3 window on 2026-08-14 (PR #8152), across 12 corroborated-clean control windows and 336 of 336 measured arm windows. There is nothing left to clock.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY OWES IS A DECISION. The finding is that the controls are not a valid calibration population for the arms: the controls' work unit is a dropped .slice() with no first-write re-allocation, the arms' is a dispatch-sync plus substrate drain which has one in every window measured. Calibrating a tolerance for the second population on the spread of the first assumes a shared window-internal structure that this window measured to be absent.

AND V3'S OWN ESCAPE CLAUSE ALREADY GOVERNS THE OUTCOME: "If the observed spread is so wide that no tau below 1 leaves margin, the witness is not usable as specified — report that rather than picking a tau that certifies everything." Here the mirror holds — the controls' spread is so TIGHT that an honest calibration lands tau near 0.02-0.05, which would refuse the ENTIRE ladder. Either way the instruction is identical: report it, do not pick a tau to suit. So the bead is already discharging its instruction; what remains is choosing between the options it lists, starting with (a) calibrate on the arms' own clean windows.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SCHEDULING, WHICH IS WHY THIS NOTE EXISTS:

1. DO NOT hold a quiet-box window for this bead. It needs no box. Holding one costs the lane a slot for nothing, which is exactly the error the operator corrected earlier today when nine beads were reported as "deferred, need a quiet box" while six workers kept the box loud.

2. It is NOT independently dispatchable either. Option (a) needs "a rule for which arm windows are corroborated clean when the arms have no 8 B/double prediction to be corroborated against" — and that rule is precisely what rf2-2rtt6.140's mandated design brief has to settle. rf2-2rtt6.140 criterion 5 forbids any further allocation window before that brief's validity witnesses are green.

3. SO THE REAL FENCE IS rf2-2rtt6.140's DESIGN BRIEF, and that brief is edit-shaped work needing no quiet box at all. It is the head of this cluster: rf2-2rtt6.140 -> then rf2-2rtt6.139 (fenced by .140's criterion 5) and this bead. Dispatch the brief; do not dispatch a window.

THE GENERAL LESSON, worth carrying: the discriminator is the ESTIMAND, not the bead's label or the lane it was filed under. A bead in the measurement lane whose numbers are already taken is a RULING, not a window.

VERDICT — BRANCH (c). tau STAYS A DECLARED PLACEHOLDER AT 0.25. Measured 2026-08-16 by PR #8377, branch worker/w-e9wr off 2cf87aed5e, on the instrument rf2-oiy1 primed at ecd4f6e7f3. Seven browser runs (Chromium 147.0.7727.15, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false); all seven positive controls passed at 8.00 B/double differential against a predicted 8, 0 unverified.

THE ORDERING THIS BEAD ASSUMED WAS SATISFIED, checked at source rather than inferred from the blocker closing: ecd4f6e7f3 is an ancestor of main, the window drives ALLOC_WRITES+1, and allocPrimeSplit removes the prime from every cohort. BRANCH (b) IS REFUTED. (b) predicted that with the excess removed 'the arms' spread may collapse toward the controls' and the stated rule works unchanged'. It did not collapse. Controls re-measured: worst relative leg deviation 0.99%, 17 of 18 exactly 0.00% -- reproducing the published figure exactly. Arms, on the falls gate (an independent cleanliness criterion, not tau): 47 collection-free windows run 0.00% - 1,835.79%; setting aside five six-figure excursions leaves 42 at 0.00% - 38.91%, median 2.69%. Nineteen of those 42 are as tight as the controls and 22 are not.

BRANCH (a) IS REFUTED TOO, and on the very thing this bead flagged as its weakness. (a) needed 'a rule for which arm windows are corroborated clean'. This window measured that the missing rule is not a formality: THE ARMS' CLEAN WINDOWS ARE NOT ONE POPULATION. In each of six independent runs, all 11 collection-free round-3 windows read <= 0.19% while all 11 round-2 windows read 2.66% - 20.37%. So tau calibrated on the arms' own data is ~0.004 at round 3 and ~0.41 at round 2 -- two orders of magnitude apart. tau is NOT IDENTIFIED by that data. Filed as rf2-rs8q6.

THE ARITHMETIC ON EVERY CANDIDATE POPULATION, at a 2x multiple:
  controls (V3 as specified)          worst  0.99%  -> tau ~ 0.02-0.05
  arms, collection-free               worst 1835.79% -> NO tau below 1 exists
  same, excursions discarded          worst 38.91% -> tau ~ 0.8, 2tau bound = 160%, vacuous
  arms at round 3 only                worst  0.19%  -> tau ~ 0.004
  arms at round 2 only                worst 20.37% -> tau ~ 0.41
Every row is a defensible reading of the same run. That span is the refusal.

SO THE WITNESS IS UNUSABLE AS SPECIFIED, on V3's own escape clause in its ORIGINAL orientation (not the mirror this bead invoked): taken whole, the arms' clean windows admit no tau below 1. (c) therefore stands, but on stronger ground than when it was written: this bead offered (c) because 'no honest calibration exists WHILE THE FIRST-LEG TERM STANDS'. The term no longer stands, and there is still no honest calibration. The objection survived its own repair.

THE BEAD'S OBJECTION TO (c) IS ANSWERED, differently than expected: what is now auditable is the REASON, not the number. The control work unit is a single fixed allocation and cannot vary (its own prime excess reads 0 B in all 18 windows); the arm work unit is a dispatch-sync plus a substrate drain and does vary, systematically and by round.

WHAT WAS NOT PINNED, TOUCHED OR WIDENED: ALLOC_LEG_TOLERANCE 0.25, ALLOC_MIN_WRITES 6, ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B 600000, ALLOC_CONTROL_SLACK 0.75, the placeholder marker and the structural pin -- all unchanged. Only V3 and V1's floor shape were run (criterion 5's permitted witnesses); no full plan, no rung, no V2. Nothing from V1's own criterion is restated: F, F0, F_old and the per-cell/per-boundary terms stay where 2026-08-14 left them. studio/** was NOT amended -- a NEW dated record was written, per rf2-5ayg7's freeze.

ONE SOURCE CORRECTION MADE. p0_run.cjs's tau header said 'V3 HAS NOT RUN' and called 0.25 a conservative stand-in, reasoning it 'refuses strictly more than any larger value V3 might land on'. That assumed V3 would land ABOVE 0.25. It landed BELOW, near 0.02-0.05, so 0.25 is 5x-12x MORE permissive than the controls license. The header now says so.

THE BOX, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. This ran LOADED, under the counter-estimand rule. Checked at source, that classification is HALF RIGHT: the counter's reading is load-independent and the controls corroborate it in-run, but a WINDOW'S CLEANLINESS is not -- 25 of 72 arm windows carried a collection and this window cannot separate load from structure there. The verdict is made robust rather than argued around: discard every collection window and every six-figure excursion, the whole class load could explain, and the refutation still holds on the 42 remaining. The round-indexed structure is likewise load-immune, holding in six separate browser processes.

WHAT IS NOT CONCLUDED: the mechanism of the round-indexed dispersion (rf2-rs8q6); the instrument's own refusal rate, which needs these same seven runs on a quiet box; and no bound is claimed from the six-figure excursions -- they bound nothing and are excluded and named.

A NOTE FOR WHOEVER WRITES rf2-2rtt6.140's BRIEF, per the 2026-08-15 23:50 mayor note: this bead is answered, not dissolved. If route (b) retires the mechanism tau is a tolerance on, that deletes the QUESTION but not the finding underneath it -- the arms' work unit is not W repetitions of one work unit, and any witness stated over arm legs inherits that.

title: hicasso: a fixed ~7 KB first-leg excess makes the allocation floor arm uncertifiable at any page size
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.140's V1/V2/V3 window on 2026-08-14 (PR #8152). Nine
browser runs on the granted quiet box; every positive control passed at 8.00
B/double differential. This is the structural result of that window.

THE TERM. Every arm window measured -- 336 of 336, across eight browser runs --
has a POSITIVE first-leg excess over its own cohort median:

  min 3,441 B | p25 6,856 | median 6,966 | p75 8,056 | max 28,448

It is CONSTANT IN ABSOLUTE BYTES across B in {4, 24, 96} (a 24x page range),
IDENTICAL under both :p0/write-all and :p0/write-page, and it survives the three
full-size warm-up windows the driver already runs. The tail legs of a clean
window are byte-identical to one another -- one B=4 floor window reads
[26044, 19256, 19256, 19256, 19256, 19256] -- so the instrument's precision is
excellent and leg 1 is the sole deviant. A collector event looks different and
appears separately, as a NEGATIVE leg (one window read -42,160 B).

WHY IT IS FATAL TO THE WITNESS HALF. The leg rule refuses a window whose leg
deviates from the cohort median by more than tau. A fixed ~7 KB excess therefore
refuses exactly those windows whose median is under 6,966/0.25 ~ 27,900 B. That
prediction agrees with the observed refusal in 290 of 336 windows (86.3%), and
every one of the 46 disagreements is a window refused for an ADDITIONAL reason
(another leg, or a collection) rather than one the rule spared.

The band is squeezed from both ends: a window must allocate MORE than ~28 KB per
write for the fixed excess to fall inside tau, and LESS than ~100 KB per write
for six writes to stay under the measured 600,000 B collection onset.

  arm     leg median        excess as % of median   observed
  floor   17.6 - 24.0 KB    29 - 41%                refused everywhere, 6/6
  R=0     18.3 - 24.4 KB    29 - 38%                refused everywhere, 6/6
  R=1     30.6 - 44.6 KB    16 - 22%                mostly certified
  R=3     43.0 - 61.9 KB    11 - 16%                certified
  R=7     68.0 - 91.4 KB     8 - 10%                certified
  R=20   148.7 - 201.5 KB    3 -  5%                refused by the COLLECTOR

THE FLOOR IS BELOW THE BAND AT EVERY PAGE SIZE, IN EVERY RUN. Its leg median is
17,556 - 23,982 B in all sixteen run x segment cases measured. And the floor is
F, and F IS FLAT IN B -- rf2-2rtt6.140 recorded that, and this window re-measured
it at 0.6% flatness across a 24x page range. So the floor DOES NOT GROW WHEN THE
PAGE GROWS, and no choice of page moves it into the band.

AND arm - floor IS THE QUANTITY EVERY WITNESS IS STATED OVER. The rungs that do
certify cannot be differenced against a floor that never does. Concretely: V2's
criterion is (arm - floor)/B and the floor certified 0 of 6 windows in BOTH V2
runs on BOTH segments, so V2's criterion could not be evaluated on certified data
at any rung. V1's control clause is affected the same way.

THIS IS THE BEAD'S OWN SHAPE, ONE LEVEL DOWN. rf2-2rtt6.140 recorded that
shrinking the measured unit has a floor and the floor is F. This records that
CERTIFYING the measured unit has a floor too, and it is the same F.

THE OPEN QUESTION, WHICH THIS WINDOW DID NOT ANSWER: is the excess removable?
Nobody has measured whether it is warm-up or re-allocation of something the
forced collection reclaimed. The two have different remedies and the window
deliberately did not guess:

(a) IF IT IS WARM-UP -- a fourth full-size warm-up window may clear it. Cheapest
to test, one env-var's worth of change (P0_ALLOC_WARMUPS is already a knob), and
it is a MEASUREMENT rather than a rig change, so it can be tried before any
design decision. Note the driver already warms three full-size windows and the
excess survived all three, so this is the less likely branch.

(b) IF IT IS RE-ALLOCATION AFTER THE FORCED gc() -- caches, hidden classes, or
the drain path's own buffers being rebuilt on the first write after collection --
no amount of warm-up clears it, because the gc() that precedes every measured
window is what creates it. Then the window's leg accounting has to change: either
exclude leg 1 and restate the certificate over W-1 legs, or measure W+1 writes
and discard the first. BOTH ARE CHANGES TO THE CERTIFICATE'S ANTECEDENT and need
the 2-tau bound re-derived; neither is a widening, and the distinction matters
because the pinned probes must stay refused.

(c) IF NEITHER -- the floor is uncertifiable by this witness, and rf2-2rtt6.140's
contingency (ii) is the route: accept F0 as the pipeline's real cost and carry it
as a STATED CONSTANT of the instrument that the floor subtracts, rather than as a
measured arm that must certify.

DO NOT DISCHARGE THIS BY WIDENING tau. The window established that a tau
calibrated as V3 specifies would be SMALLER, not larger (see the sibling bead),
so widening runs against the calibration as well as against Shape 6.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THE WINDOW THAT FOUND IT: it is roughly a one-line change
to the warm-up or the leg accounting and the box was idle and granted. A window
taken on an instrument amended minutes earlier, with no red-then-green proof and
no review, is exactly the uncertified-instrument window criterion 5 exists to
prevent. Same reasoning that filed rf2-gxrr rather than building it in-window.

EVIDENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-write-halfs-floor-is-the-pipeline.md
(PR #8152), sections "The first-leg excess, which explains every refusal" and
"Why that is structural and not a tuning problem".
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8152 (2026-08-14; completeness, correctness, implementation quality) — UPDATED this exact existing floor-certification owner; no duplicate. The exact merge is docs-only, its doc-slug and provenance gates pass, all 12 tables are structurally consistent, and the umbrella correctly remains open with separate owners for the first-leg, tau, and summary issues. The published disposition is internally inconsistent at the point this bead owns, however. the-write-halfs-floor-is-the-pipeline.md says all 72 V1 floor windows were refused and promises refused-window numbers are labelled at every appearance; the same merge’s allocation-instrument-rework.md therefore calls V1 and V2 unassessed. But the result page’s unqualified headline says “V1’s criterion is met at B=24 and B=96 and missed at B=4,” then says contingency (i) is closed by measurement using those refused floor/R20 medians. That promotes diagnostic values from an uncertified floor into a criterion verdict and design decision while the exact repair owner remains open. BOUNDED REPAIR: until this bead produces a certified floor, label those headline/bar/non-crossing results as refused-window indications and keep V1 plus contingency (i) unassessed; if the floor becomes certifiable, remeasure before promoting them. No extra statistics or new instrument is requested.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8159 (2026-08-14; completeness, correctness, implementation quality) — REOPENED this exact existing owner; no duplicate. This PR closes the bead without correcting docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-write-halfs-floor-is-the-pipeline.md: its headline still says V1 is met at B=24/96 and missed at B=4 and its closing disposition says the refused-data non-crossing closes contingency (i), while the same page says all 72 floor windows refused and V1/V2 are unassessed. The PR explicitly ran no new measurement window. Making the instrument capable of a certified floor does not retroactively certify or relabel the historical refused data. No additional statistic or instrument change is requested.

title: hicasso: V2's one-write window is refused by the same package's own six-write averaging floor — a ruling, not a widening
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.140's V1 measurement window, 2026-08-13 23:49 AUSEST. It is a
RULING, not an implementation, and it is filed separately from rf2-gxrr for that
reason: an implementation bead carrying an unsettled ruling gets settled by a
worker guessing.

THE CONTRADICTION IS INSIDE THE SHIPPED PACKAGE. The same rework shipped a
validity witness whose configuration its own preflight refuses.

  V2's configuration, allocation-instrument-rework.md:290-293 — "One page,
  P0_ALLOC_CELLS = 1 (B = 4) ... measured twice, once under each write. ONE
  WRITE PER WINDOW, and at least five independent windows per cell, compared by
  median."

  The preflight, p0_run.cjs:1245 — refuses `writes < ALLOC_MIN_WRITES` (6),
  unconditionally, before a browser is launched. Pinned green as ROUTE 2 in
  p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:795.

Reproduced from the shipped derivation rather than read off the source:
`P0_ALLOC_CELLS=1 P0_ALLOC_WRITES=1` returns admissible:false, "a window of 1
write(s) is under the 6-write averaging floor (ALLOC_MIN_WRITES)".

WIDENING THE FLOOR IS NOT ON THE TABLE. Criterion 4 keeps it ("ALLOC_MIN_WRITES
= 6 stays a floor"), Shape 6 forbids loosening a gate to admit a run, and
rf2-2rtt6.142 put the floor there deliberately. This bead does not ask for it.

WHY IT IS A REAL QUESTION AND NOT A TYPO. The floor's STATED ground is a
precondition on FITTING: "at one write per window this row's four fits came back
at r² 0.75 / 0.28 / 0.94 / 0.31, under its 0.98 floor" and "A one-write window
has no averaging in it whatever certifies the window" (p0_run.cjs:1179-1190).
V2 takes no fit — "V2 makes no fit and quotes no slope; it compares arm − floor
per boundary at each rung between the two writes" (:297-299) — and gets its
averaging from five independent windows per cell compared by median, which is
averaging ACROSS windows rather than inside one. So the floor's own reasoning
may not reach V2. May not. That is the operator's call, not a worker's.

AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS NOT FREE, which is the part worth the operator's
attention. "Just run V2 at six writes" looks costless until the arithmetic is
done. The brief computes the composed operating point (B = 4, R = 20, W = 6) at
≈ 630 KB of rise-plus-largest-step, and ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B — the MEASURED
point on this rig where the first falling step appears — is 600,000 B. So a
six-write V2 at its R = 20 rung sits at or over the rig's own observed
collection onset, and the falls gate would be expected to refuse it. The brief's
one-write choice is doing real work: "At B = 4 a single-write window is a few
tens of KB under either write, so both are comfortably clean and the comparison
is not taken across a refusal" (:295-297).

V2 at B = 4 is therefore squeezed from both sides — the averaging floor pushes W
up, the collection onset pushes W down — and that squeeze is the same shape as
the one this whole bead exists to record, now reappearing one level down.

THE OPTIONS, with the arithmetic attached and none of them taken here:

(a) RUN V2 AT W = 6 ANYWAY and let the R = 20 rung refuse if it refuses. Costs
    no gate change at all. Risk: V2's most informative rung is the one most
    likely to come back refused, and V2 is the write half's falsification test.
    Cheapest to try, and it is a legitimate outcome for the R = 20 rung to
    refuse — that is the instrument working.

(b) SCOPE THE FLOOR TO FIT-BEARING WINDOWS. The floor refuses any window a fit
    will be taken over, and V2's fit-free comparison windows are outside it.
    This is not widening — every fit-bearing window is refused exactly as today,
    and the pinned ROUTE 2 case (a one-write window on the shipped LADDER page)
    still refuses. It is a change to a gate's SCOPE, which needs the operator
    because scope changes are how gates quietly stop gating.

(c) RE-SPECIFY V2 at a W between 1 and 6 chosen against the collection onset
    rather than against either constraint. Needs (b) or a ruling anyway, since
    anything under 6 is refused.

(d) DROP V2. Rejected on sight, recorded so it is not re-proposed: V2 is the
    write half's only falsification test — "if the new write measured something
    else, the per-boundary signal arm − floor would move. V2 measures both
    writes on the same page in the same run and requires that it does not"
    (:217-220). Without it the equivalence argument cannot fail, and an
    equivalence argument that cannot fail is not one.

RECOMMENDATION, offered not taken: (a) first, because it touches nothing and the
question it leaves open — whether the R = 20 rung survives at W = 6 — is
answerable by one window rather than by a ruling. If R = 20 refuses, (b) is the
principled remedy and it arrives with V2's own data attached to justify it.

NOTE V2 IS ALSO BLOCKED BY rf2-gxrr independently: it needs both writes on the
same page in the same run, and the allocation window cannot drive `:p0/write-all`
at all. Settling this bead does not unblock V2 on its own.
notes:
THE DESCRIPTION'S CLOSING NOTE IS NOW STALE, corrected $D. Read this before ruling.

The description ends: "NOTE V2 IS ALSO BLOCKED BY rf2-gxrr independently: it needs both writes on the same page in the same run, and the allocation window cannot drive :p0/write-all at all. Settling this bead does not unblock V2 on its own."

THAT SECOND BLOCKER IS GONE. rf2-gxrr merged as PR #8147 and the mayor verified P0_ALLOC_WRITE present in the bench source on main rather than trusting the merge. The instrument now carries P0_ALLOC_WRITE = page (default) | all, with ONE branch serving both kinds and differing in the event alone - so V2's "both writes on the same page in the same run" is reachable for the first time.

SO THE RULING ON THIS BEAD IS NOW THE ONLY THING BETWEEN THE LANE AND ITS NEXT WINDOW. It releases rf2-2rtt6.140 (P1), and behind that rf2-2rtt6.139 (P1), and behind those roughly a dozen P3 beads fenced on the lane.

NOTHING ELSE IN THE DESCRIPTION HAS MOVED. The contradiction stands: V2 is specified at one write per window (allocation-instrument-rework.md:290-293) and the preflight refuses under six (p0_run.cjs:1245), reproduced as admissible:false. The floor is not up for widening - criterion 4 keeps it, Shape 6 forbids loosening a gate to admit a run, and rf2-2rtt6.142 placed it deliberately. The squeeze still holds: six writes at B=4/R=20 reaches about 630 KB against a MEASURED collection onset of 600,000 B, so the averaging floor pushes W up while the collection onset pushes it down.

The four options and their arithmetic are unchanged, and the worker's recommendation - option (a), run at six and let the R=20 rung refuse if it refuses - still stands offered rather than taken. It touches nothing, and one window answers the open question instead of a ruling.

WHY THIS CORRECTION MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING BOOKKEEPING: a stale "this does not unblock anything on its own" is exactly the line that makes a ruling look low-value and get deferred. It is now the highest-leverage single decision in the backlog.
close_reason:
RULED BY MIKE $D: OPTION (a) — RUN V2 AT SIX WRITES ANYWAY, and let the R=20 rung refuse if it refuses.

His words: "Run V2 at 6 writes anyway".

WHAT THIS SETTLES AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. It settles how V2 runs. It does NOT rule on whether the six-write averaging floor's reasoning reaches a fit-free comparison - that question stays open and unanswered, because option (a) does not need it answered. The floor is untouched. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES stays 6.

REJECTED BY THIS RULING, and none of them are to be revived by a worker:
  (b) scoping the floor to fit-bearing windows - not chosen. Do NOT narrow the gate's scope.
      A scope change is how a gate quietly stops gating, and it is not needed to run V2.
  (c) a write count between 1 and 6 - moot, since anything under 6 is refused and (b) was
      not taken.
  (d) dropping V2 - was already rejected on sight and stays rejected. V2 is the write half's
      only falsification test, and an equivalence argument that cannot fail is not one.

THE PREDICTION THE RULING ACCEPTS. Six writes at B=4/R=20 reaches roughly 630 KB against a MEASURED collection onset of 600,000 B, so the R=20 rung is expected to sit at or over the point where the falls gate refuses. THAT REFUSAL IS AN ADMISSIBLE OUTCOME, NOT A FAILURE. Do not widen ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B, do not drop the rung, do not retry until it passes. A refused rung is the instrument working, and it is reported as the result.

WHY THIS OPTION AND NOT THE PRINCIPLED ONE. It touches nothing, and the open question - does R=20 survive at W=6 - is answerable by ONE WINDOW rather than by a ruling. If R=20 does refuse, option (b) becomes the principled remedy AND ARRIVES WITH V2'S OWN DATA ATTACHED to justify it. Running first is therefore cheaper than ruling first, and it makes any later ruling better founded.

THE OTHER BLOCKER IS ALREADY GONE. rf2-gxrr merged as PR #8147; P0_ALLOC_WRITE was verified present in the bench source on main. V2's "both writes on the same page in the same run" is reachable.

RELEASES: rf2-2rtt6.140 (P1) has no remaining blocker. Behind it rf2-2rtt6.139 (P1), and behind those the lane's fenced P3s.

title: hicasso: the allocation instrument cannot be configured into V1/V2/V3's shapes — the validity witnesses' measurement surface was never built
description:
FOUND BY rf2-2rtt6.140's V1 measurement window, 2026-08-13 23:49 AUSEST, on a
granted quiet box. The window REFUSED before a browser was launched: V1, V2 and
V3 are all unrunnable on the shipped instrument, and the ground is the same in
each case — the measurement surface the design brief specifies for the validity
witnesses was never built. PR #7702 landed criteria 2, 3, 4 and 6 and said so
honestly ("NEITHER ARTEFACT HAS BEEN EXECUTED AGAINST A REAL PAGE"); what it did
not land, and did not claim to, is the configuration surface V1-V3 need.

THIS IS THE WORK THAT UNBLOCKS THE LANE. rf2-2rtt6.140 cannot discharge, and
rf2-2rtt6.139 stays blocked behind it, until this lands.

WHAT IS MISSING, precisely, all three verified against source and reproduced
executably.

(1) THE WRITE SELECTOR — blocks V1 and V2.

V1's configuration is "Each page measured under `:p0/write-all` and under
`:p0/write-page`" (allocation-instrument-rework.md:256), and F_old is not
optional decoration: it is V1's CONTROL. The brief states its job — "That is the
control: it says the rig has not moved under the instrument, and it is the only
way the two writes can be compared like for like" (:260-263) — and criterion 6
turns on it: "The one figure that keeps its full force across the change is
F_old — V1 re-measures it as its control, and an agreement at B = 24 is what
licenses the comparison at all" (:631).

The allocation window cannot drive it. `p0_heap.cljs:1111` hard-codes
`(arms/write-page! @alloc-tick)`; there is no env var, no `kind`, no parameter
that routes it to `write-all!`. `arms/write-all!` still exists as a public door
(p0_arms.cljs:165) and the clock/bulk/fan-out/retention rows still drive it, so
the event is there — it is unreachable FROM THE ALLOCATION WINDOW.

And it is not merely unimplemented, it is PINNED OUT.
`p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:978` asserts
`assert.doesNotMatch(HEAP, /\(arms\/write-all! /, 'and never write-all!')`.
Demonstrated rather than read: a one-line plant at p0_heap.cljs:1111 adding a
selector took the suite from 53 passed / exit 0 to 1/53 failed / exit 1, the one
failure being that pin, and the restore was verified byte-identical by
`git hash-object` against the committed object.

So the pin is the thing to AMEND, and amending it is the delicate half of this
bead. It must not simply be deleted: the pin's real content is criterion 6's
separation — the allocation row and the clock/bulk rows drive different writes,
so a reader of any row can tell from the row which write produced it. The
replacement pin should assert that the allocation window's DEFAULT is
`write-page!` and that `write-all!` is reachable only under a named measurement
switch, with the clock/bulk pin (`:1009`, no clock row drives the new write)
untouched.

(2) A CONTROLS-ONLY MODE — blocks V3.

V3's configuration is "The controls only, at both D values, six rounds, six
writes a window — the row's existing control path, run with the new allocSteps
fields recorded. No arms, no browser page beyond the one the controls already
need" (:443-445).

`--only alloc` has exactly one shape: preflight, then the controls AND the full
ladder plan (floor + 4 rungs x 2 substrates x 2 segments) every round. The mode
surface is closed — `clock | heap | fanout | ladder | alloc` (p0_run.cjs:2362) —
and the no-arms route out is shut by the preflight: `P0_ALLOC_CELLS=0` refuses
with "a page of 0 boundaries (4 roots x 0 cells) has no per-boundary quantity to
publish", correctly.

So V3's controls can only be harvested by riding a full ladder run, which takes
~108 ladder-arm windows to obtain 18 control windows — and criterion 5 freezes
every allocation window that is not V1-V4. That is why this is a mode and not a
workaround.

(3) THE V1 FLOOR-ONLY MODE — a lesser want, stated so it is not rediscovered.

V1 says "Floor arm only — no ladder rungs, no fits, no candidate" (:253).
Unlike (1) and (2) this one is survivable without new code — the floor arm runs
in the shipped plan and its figures can be read out of a full run — but it costs
the whole ladder at each of three pages to obtain one arm, and it takes rung
windows criterion 5 freezes. Fold it into (2) as the same switch if that is
cheap; do not build it separately.

WHAT IS **NOT** ASKED FOR HERE. No gate is widened, no band moved, no threshold
touched. `ALLOC_MIN_WRITES` stays 6, `ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B` stays 600,000,
R=20 stays, tau stays the uncalibrated placeholder until V3 runs. The only
change is that the instrument gains the ability to be CONFIGURED into the shapes
its own design brief specifies for its validity witnesses.

SEQUENCING. (1) and (3) are ready to build. (2) is ready to build. V2 needs the
ruling on the sibling bead as well as (1) — see it before briefing V2.

THE USUAL DISCIPLINE APPLIES, and this bead is instrument code, so it is the
strict form: red-then-green mutation proofs in two commits, structural pins for
the new switch, and NO measurement in the same PR. A measurement window taken on
an instrument written minutes earlier is exactly what criterion 5 exists to
prevent, and it is why this window refused rather than building the switch and
measuring through it.
notes:
CLAUSE 5 FIRED ON PR #8147 AND STOPPED A MERGE THAT LOOKED PERFECTLY GREEN. Recorded $D because this is the clause's first live catch this session and it is easy to skip.

THE PR READ 93 CHECKS, 73 SUCCESS, 20 SKIPPED, ZERO FAILURES, all five runs COMPLETED. Clauses 1 through 4 all passed. On those alone it was mergeable.

CLAUSE 5 ASKS A DIFFERENT QUESTION: was that check set computed against the CURRENT trunk matrix? It was not. PR #8146 - the gate-arming class audit - landed on main after #8147 branched, changing .github/workflows/docs.yml (39 lines) and .github/workflows/test.yml (36 lines). Measured with git diff between #8147's merge-base and origin/main.

SO THE 93 WAS COMPUTED AGAINST THE SUPERSEDED MATRIX. It is a real number about a matrix that no longer exists. Merging on it would have been merging on a stale instrument - the same error class as quoting a pre-rebase green, which the gate-mechanics block warns workers about, arriving one level up at the mayor.

AND #8146 IS EXACTLY THE PR MOST LIKELY TO MOVE THE ANSWER, because its whole purpose was to ARM GATES THAT WERE SILENTLY UNARMED. A PR rebased onto it may now run jobs that were skipped before. The band total should hold at 93 - a skipped job still reports as a check - but WHICH jobs actually execute can change, and that is what the rebase re-measures.

ACTION TAKEN: gh pr update-branch 8147. Head moved 8da53cffca3e to d212403d0f2c and the rollup reset to 14 IN_PROGRESS. Re-verify all five clauses on the NEW head before merging - not just the count, but clause 4's run set at the FULL new SHA.

THE GENERAL RULE, worth carrying: clause 5 is the only clause that can fail while every visible signal is green. The other four are read off the PR; this one requires a comparison AGAINST MAIN that nothing on the page shows you. That is why it is last in the list and first to be skipped.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8147 (completeness/correctness/implementation quality), 2026-08-14.

REOPENED: the new narrowed modes run, but their emitted measurement record is internally contradictory. allocPlanArms returns no arms for the controls plan, and the selected write is invoked only inside the arm loop, so controls-only drives no write at all. Nevertheless allocRow always records writeSelector/write, and summariseAlloc unconditionally prints "WARM 1/3/7/20 READS", "held FIXED across every rung", "Q = E on every rung", "The arm stays MOUNTED", and "THE WRITE IS ..." before later admitting "controls only, no arm mounted". The floor-only report likewise claims 1/3/7/20 rungs and Q=E despite mounting only the floor. An executable synthetic controls row reproduced all contradictory lines while the focused structural suite remained green at 59 passed.

Impact: V3's controls-only artefact falsely attributes an event that did not execute and both narrowed modes misstate the measurement shape. That defeats the provenance/evidence purpose of the new low-friction measurement surface.

Acceptance: make the report header and write provenance plan-aware. Controls-only must explicitly say no arm and no write event was driven; floor-only must not claim rungs, fits, or Q=E. Keep the full plan's claims intact. Extend the structural pins to reject these stale full-plan claims in both narrowed outputs and to prove controls-only does not claim an executed write.

title: Xray hydrates Static Machines into a frame that does not exist yet, so the dispatch is refused and the persisted selection is silently dropped
description:
Found while fixing rf2-8yyd. This is the SECOND cause of that gate's red, and
the half rf2-8yyd's worker was fenced out of (`tools/xray/` belongs to
worker/advisorid-hic037). **rf2-8yyd cannot go green until this lands.**

## The defect

Every dev browser page carrying the Xray preload emits exactly one promoted
refusal at boot:

```
{:error        :rf.error/frame-destroyed
 :event        :rf/redacted
 :event-id     :rf.xray.static.machines/hydrate
 :frame        :rf/xray
 :exception    nil
 :source-coord {:ns   day8.re-frame2-xray.static.machines.panel
                :file "tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/panel.cljs"
                :line 200}}
```

`static/machines/persistence.cljs` `hydrate!` dispatches
`:rf.xray.static.machines/hydrate` into `{:frame defaults/default-frame-id}`
(`:rf/xray`) from `panel.cljs/install!` (line 243), which
`registry.cljs/register-xray-handlers!` runs at install time — before the
`:rf/xray` frame exists.

Its own docstring states the premise that is false:

> "Safe to call before frame `:rf/xray` is mounted — `dispatch` queues the
> event; it lands after the frame is registered. Per `mount.cljs/
> ensure-xray-frame!` the registry handlers install before the frame mounts,
> so the dispatch goes through the standard queue and is replayed against the
> new frame on the first dispatch-cycle."

It is not replayed. The dispatch is refused with `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`
and the hydrate is DROPPED, so the persisted Static-Machines selection +
sub-mode never restore after a reload. That is a real user-visible loss, not
only a noisy line.

## Measured, on this worktree

`worker/storyconsole-8yyd` at `05587d99ea` + `5b686764de`, dev build of
`examples/counter-with-stories`, driven with Playwright and the record read
through the CLJS value's own `toString` (not Playwright's shallow preview):

- `/counter-with-stories/#/stories` (Story shell) — 1 console error at boot,
  the record above, at `t=1251.9ms`.
- `/counter-with-stories/#/` (the plain live app, **no Story shell at all**) —
  the same single error at boot. So this is not a Story problem; it is
  every Xray-preloaded dev page.
- Registry timeline sampled every 5ms from before the first app script: the
  Story shell's `:errors` claim (rf2-8yyd's fix) lands at `t=1610.5ms`,
  ~360ms AFTER the refusal fires. No shell-scoped claim can cover it, and
  claiming earlier would be a lie — the shell owns nothing before it mounts.

Consequence on the gate: after rf2-8yyd's fix the Story feature-load gate
falls from 227 + 20 console errors to 94 + 12, and **every one of the 106
remaining lines is this one refusal**, once per page navigation. The gate
stays red.

## Why nobody saw it before

Nothing surfaced it. The refusal is caught and normalised (nothing throws, 0
`pageerror`), and until rf2-fu75's dev console fallback landed
(`fcf866ea1d`) an unowned promoted error reached no channel at all. Every
other browser runner in the repo is `pageerror`-fatal only; the Story
feature-load runner is the one that counts console errors, which is why this
is where it surfaced. The fallback did exactly the job it was built for.

## Fix shape (not ruled)

Make the hydrate land instead of vanish. Either dispatch it from the seam
that knows the frame exists (`mount.cljs/ensure-xray-frame!`, after the
frame is registered), or have `hydrate!` defer until the frame is present.
Do NOT silence it by deleting the dispatch, and do NOT register an `:errors`
listener from Xray — rf2-fu75 ruled deliberately that Xray does not populate
that registry (it rides the dev-only trace axis), so a claim here would
contradict a standing decision AND leave the hydrate still dropped.

Whatever lands, re-run `npm run test:story-feature-load` and expect 0 console
errors.
notes:
Blocks rf2-8yyd's acceptance. Story-side half is on PR #8126; the gate stays red until this lands. Reproduce: npm run test:story-feature-load from a checkout of worker/storyconsole-8yyd.
FIXED on PR #8136 (worker/xrayhydrate-qw0o, rebased onto main which already carries #8126).

ROOT CAUSE confirmed exactly as described: panel/install! runs from
registry/register-xray-handlers! (orchestrator time), before
mount/ensure-xray-frame! registers :rf/xray. hydrate!'s docstring premise
that dispatch QUEUES and replays for a not-yet-registered frame is false —
the dispatch is refused with promoted :rf.error/frame-destroyed and dropped.

FIX took the 'dispatch from the seam that knows the frame exists' option,
because the repo already had that pattern twice: views.resizable-table/hydrate!
and frame-switcher/hydrate! both carry a frame guard and land from a
mount.cljs first-mount hook. (resizable_table.cljs's docstring even claims to
'mirror static-machines/hydrate!' — parity that did not exist until now.)
 - persistence/hydrate!: frame guard + frame-id arity + dispatch-sync
 - mount.cljs: new ::hydrate-static-machines first-mount hook
 - panel/install!'s call KEPT — now an honest no-op on the production path,
   still live where the frame already exists (:after-load, tests)
Did NOT delete the dispatch; did NOT register an :errors listener (rf2-fu75
ruling untouched).

EVIDENCE — both acceptance claims proved by a RED, not asserted:
 1. RESTORE. Planting a wrong expected value produced
    'actual: (not (= :rf2-qw0o/PLANTED-SABOTAGE :checkout.flow/payment))' —
    the live app-db slot held the persisted prior-session selection. Also
    proves all 8 new tests execute and the gate reads the worker worktree.
 2. CONSOLE ERRORS. Removing ONLY the frame guard on the same tree gave
    94 + 12 = 106 console errors / exit 1; guard in place gives 0 / exit 0.
    106 reproduces this bead's independently-measured residual (94+12)
    EXACTLY, and 92 of those lines name :rf.xray.static.machines/hydrate.
    That is causal proof this fix is what removes them.
 Both plants reverted and verified byte-identical via git hash-object.

GATES (captured exit codes, final rebased base):
 npm run test:story-feature-load — 2 specs, 0 failures, 0 console errors — 0
 npm run test:cljs — 13861 tests / 70051 assertions, 0 failures — 0
 scripts/test-fast-pr.sh — PASS fast PR spine — 0
 scripts/check_doc_slugs.py — 0

NEW COVERAGE: tools/xray/test/.../static/machines/hydrate_restore_cljs_test.cljs
(8 tests / 17 assertions). Drives the REAL register-xray-handlers! +
ensure-xray-frame! boot and never calls hydrate! itself — the pre-existing
persistence suite stayed green through the whole defect precisely because it
called save!/load directly and routed around the seam.

SPEC: 003-Machine-Inspector.md carried the SAME false claim ('hydrate! is
called on install! so the first render after a reload restores the prior
selection') — a spec promising a restore that never happened. Corrected to
name the hook. Deliberately did not touch 017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md (its
Static Machines row is feature-level and e2e-gated; this adds unit coverage
for an existing feature).
