title: the dev console fallback reds the Story/Xray browser gate, and main is green only because that gate is skipped there
description:
BLOCKS EVERY PR THAT ARMS THE STORY/XRAY BROWSER GATE. Found 2026-08-13 by the mayor merge loop while diagnosing PR #8118.

WHAT FAILS. `Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke)` on PR #8118, run 31676770038:

  FAIL Story feature exercise + 20-event load gate: Browser emitted 227 console error(s) and 0 page error(s)
  FAIL Story browser scenarios (rf2-dczqg): Browser emitted 20 console error(s) and 0 page error(s)
  Ran 2 Story feature-load specs. 2 failures.

Then `All required checks passed` blocks the merge: 'needs results' shows exactly one failure among 77.

**NOTE THE SHAPE: 0 PAGE ERRORS, 227 CONSOLE ERRORS.** The gate treats a console error as fatal. Nothing is throwing.

THE CAUSE. PR #8108 (rf2-fu75, commit `fcf866ea1d`) added `report-unowned-error!` to `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc`. In a dev build, on a browser host, when a promoted error reaches an EMPTY `:errors` listener registry, it prints the record to `console.error` prefixed `[re-frame2]`. That is the intended behaviour and the code is correct.

The Story harness DELIBERATELY RUNS FAILING SCENARIOS — the same log shows `failing-event-throws`, `failing-play`, `failing-fx-stub-miss`, `deliberately-failing`, each `expected=fail actual=fail`. Every one of those now produces a framework-captured error with no listener attached, so the fallback prints, and the console-error count explodes. The failing scenarios are the gate working; the console errors are the fallback working; the gate's 'zero console errors' assumption is what is now false.

The matching `[browser:error] [re-frame2] {meta: null, cnt: 8, arr: Array(16), ...}` lines are in the same log.

**WHY NOBODY SAW IT, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** rf2-fu75's worker verified the browser lane carefully and reported 'zero pageerror across all six browser runs'. That was TRUE and it was the wrong measurement — it checked `pageerror`, and this gate is fatal on `console error`. Classic local-green-is-not-CI: the red gate is one the local run did not cover.

**AND MAIN LOOKS GREEN BECAUSE THE GATE IS SKIPPED THERE.** Verified: on main push runs `31675735554` (which IS the `fcf866ea1d` fallback commit) and `31678098717`, the job `Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke)` has conclusion **skipped**. It is surface-armed and most changes do not arm it. #8118 touches `.github/workflows/*` and `TESTING.md`, which does. So a regression has been sitting on main behind a gate that reports green by not running — the exact fail-open shape this project spends its days hunting.

#8118 IS INNOCENT. Its diff is workflow header comments and TESTING.md prose. Do NOT dispatch a fix onto its branch; the defect is on main and the fix belongs there.

## The fix, and it is a judgement call — take route A unless you can show it wrong

ROUTE A (preferred): have the Story harness ATTACH AN `:errors` LISTENER. The contract rf2-fu75 landed states it explicitly: registering ANY `:errors` listener takes CORPUS-WIDE ownership and suppresses the fallback for every category. That is the documented off-switch, and it is honest here — the Story harness genuinely does own these errors, since it runs the failing scenarios on purpose and asserts on their outcomes. Using the mechanism as designed beats working around it.

ROUTE B (only if A fails): exclude `[re-frame2]`-prefixed diagnostics from the gate's console-error count. This WEAKENS a gate, so it needs a reason A does not work. Never widen a gate to admit today's run without one — every gate is there because something once passed that should not have.

DO NOT disable or revert the fallback. It is correct and it was wanted.

## Acceptance

The Story/Xray browser gate passes with the fallback in place AND still reds when a genuine unexpected console error appears. Prove BOTH — a gate that stops counting console errors satisfies half the acceptance and is useless. Plant an unexpected console error and show it red.

Say in the PR body which route you took and why.

## Also file or note

The wider question this exposes — that a required gate skipped on main can hide a regression indefinitely — is worth its own bead if you think it is actionable. Do not fix it here.

title: mayor-merge.md clause 4 compares an uppercase status against a CLI that returns lowercase, so it blocks every settled PR
description:
`.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md` line 17, clause 4 of the merge criterion.

WHAT IS WRONG. The clause says the runs must have `status` all `COMPLETED`. The two gh commands the criterion uses disagree on case:

  gh pr checks --json state   -> UPPERCASE: SUCCESS, SKIPPED, IN_PROGRESS
  gh run list  --json status  -> lowercase: completed, queued, in_progress

So a mayor following clause 4 literally writes `select(.status != "COMPLETED")` and counts every FINISHED run as nonterminal. Measured 2026-08-13 16:20 AUSEST: all six open PRs reported identically as `runs@sha=5 nonterminal=5` while every one of the five runs on each read `completed / success`. Four of those six were green on all five clauses and merged once the comparison was case-folded (#8102, #8103, #8104, #8105).

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPO. Every other trap documented in that file fails OPEN - it admits a merge that should have been refused, and the damage is visible afterwards. This one fails CLOSED. It never ships a bad merge and it never announces itself either. It presents as a CI queue that will not drain, which is the most believable thing in the world, and it can burn ticks indefinitely. The file's own words already cover it: a guard that blocks forever is not safe, it is differently wrong.

WHAT TO CHANGE. Replace line 17 with the text below, verbatim. It is written; do not re-derive it.

---
4. AND `gh run list --branch <headRefName> --commit <headRefOid> --limit 25 --json status,headSha,name` returns runs whose `status` is all `COMPLETED`. `--commit` is what keys this to the current head; the plain table has no `headSha` column at all, so request it in `--json` and compare it rather than eyeballing a listing that cannot show it. **AND CASE-FOLD THAT COMPARISON, because the two commands disagree on case and the mismatch fails CLOSED.** `gh pr checks --json state` returns UPPERCASE (`SUCCESS`, `SKIPPED`, `IN_PROGRESS`); `gh run list --json status` returns lowercase (`completed`, `queued`, `in_progress`). A clause-4 test written `.status != "COMPLETED"` - the spelling this line used until 2026-08-13 - therefore counts every *finished* run as nonterminal, and reported six-for-six PRs as blocked when all six were settled. It cost a tick before the raw JSON was read. Compare `(.status|ascii_upcase) != "COMPLETED"`. Note which direction this error runs: unlike every other trap on this page it blocks rather than admits, so it never ships a bad merge and never announces itself either - it just looks like a CI queue that will not drain. A guard that blocks forever is not safe, it is differently wrong. Also pass the FULL 40-character `headRefOid`: `--commit` with an abbreviated sha matches nothing and returns `[]`, which reads as "no live runs" and passes clause 4 vacuously - the same fail-open shape, one argument away.
---

THE SECOND HALF IS NOT PADDING. The abbreviated-sha case was measured in the same tick: `gh run list --branch worker/ssrrows-bjpe --commit 43b993fc` returns `[]`, while the same query with the full 40-character oid returns the five runs. `[]` reads as 'no live runs at this head' and satisfies clause 4 vacuously. Same clause, one argument away, opposite direction.

SWEEP EVERY CARRIER. `git grep` the clause-4 wording across tracked files and settle each hit in the same PR. Known carriers to check: `.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md`, `docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md` (the hard-won list's 'a settled rollup is not a quiet branch' bullet), `docs/the-mayor-method/README.md`, `ai/findings/the-mayor-method/loops.md` clause 4. THE DISCRIMINATOR: a carrier that states the RULE in prose ('require the terminal state') is correct and stays; only a carrier that gives the literal COMPARISON or a copyable command is wrong. Do not 'fix' the prose ones. List in the PR body what was changed and what was left standing because it was already right.

NOT IN SCOPE: do not restructure the criterion, do not renumber clauses, do not touch clauses 1/2/3/5.

DONE WHEN: line 17 carries the text above; every literal-comparison carrier is settled; the prose carriers are listed as deliberately unchanged.

GATE: `mkdocs build --strict` does NOT cover `.claude/commands/`. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates link targets and heading anchors under `docs/` - run it because `docs/the-mayor-method/` is in scope. No automated gate covers `.claude/commands/`; verify that tree by hand and say so in the PR body.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8109 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/8109), branch worker/clause4-qivw. .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md line 17 replaced verbatim with the bead's ruled text (pasted programmatically from the raw description, byte-for-byte). Both premises re-measured live against PR #8107 head 2816c8c2b4da59134f6459c24b46f1d6618a5034 before writing: gh pr checks --json state -> SUCCESS/SKIPPED (uppercase), gh run list --json status -> completed (lowercase); and --commit 2816c8c2 (abbreviated) -> [] while the full 40-char oid -> 5 runs. End-to-end proof of the fix on that same head: select(.status != "COMPLETED") counts 5, select((.status|ascii_upcase) != "COMPLETED") counts 0. Carrier sweep done by git grep over tracked files: line 17 was the ONLY literal-comparison/copyable-command carrier in the repo. Left standing as correct prose (listed in the PR body): mayor-merge.md line 20 ("require the terminal state"), line 22 (the both-directions paragraph), line 10 (rollup 'status == COMPLETED', genuinely uppercase and clause-2 material), docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md lines 109-127 + 146, docs/the-mayor-method/README.md lines 170-174. ai/findings/the-mayor-method/loops.md is out of scope: git ls-files ai/ is empty, the tree is untracked and mayor-local. Clauses 1/2/3/5 untouched, nothing renumbered. Gate: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, sabotage-verified (planted broken link at bootstrap.md:109 -> exit 1 naming that line; restored, sha256 aa7e9f1c... identical before and after). No automated gate covers .claude/commands/; verified by hand (line count 29, frontmatter parses, backticks/bold balanced, clause numbering 1-5 intact, no trailing whitespace, no bare LF).

title: Surface classifier arms no lane for PROSE surfaces that JVM tests pin — docs/machines, docs/core/freehand, spec/**
description:

THE DEFECT. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh classifies a changed-file list into surface outputs. jvm-machines (test.yml:1915) gates on implementation_jvm == 'true'. A docs-only diff arms NOTHING:

  $ bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh docs/machines/parallel-states.md docs/machines/concepts.md
  implementation_jvm=false        (every other output false too)

docs/machines/** matches NO case arm in the classifier at all. The only docs/* arms in the whole file are the playground bundle (docs/tools/playground/*, docs/cljs/playground.{js,css}) and migration/**. So PR #8068 — the machines-guide rewrite, 13 files, docs-only — skipped the very lane that pins the pages it rewrote, and landed main RED. Nothing surfaced it until an unrelated PR happened to arm implementation_jvm.

IT IS WIDER THAN docs/machines. Measured the same way, every one of these prose surfaces arms NOTHING while a JVM test pins it:

  docs/machines/**                    <- parallel_states_guide_truth_jvm_test.clj, transition_geometry_terminology_jvm_test.clj
  spec/005-StateMachines.md           <- transition_geometry_terminology_jvm_test.clj (4 required pins on §Self-transitions)
  docs/core/freehand/**               <- samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj (digest-pins EVERY fenced block)

  spec/Tool-Pair.md, spec/Security.md <- spec_elision_registry_tense_conformance_test.clj

The general shape: prose-pinning JVM tests are armed by their CODE surface, never by the PROSE surface they pin. A prose-only edit can red them and merge green. spec/** arming nothing is the sharper half — spec is normative and is edited prose-only routinely.

THE FIX is a classifier edit only; test.yml needs no change, because the jobs already gate on the right outputs. Add case arms mapping each pinned prose tree to the lane that pins it:

Consider whether spec/* should arm implementation_jvm wholesale or only the pinned files; wholesale is the conservative choice the file's own comments favour, and the classifier is documented as conservative.

WHY NOT DONE IN rf2-s41i's PR (#8082): .github/ is CI control plane and sequential, and worker/records-cluster was LIVE in .github/scripts/ at the time. The prose+test half shipped alone; this is the arming half.

VERIFY THE FIX by running the classifier directly — it takes explicit paths:
  bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh docs/machines/parallel-states.md
must print implementation_jvm=true. There is also a self-test lane for this script in test.yml; check whether it needs a new expectation row.

title: JVM machines guide-truth tests are RED ON MAIN after the machines-guide rewrite — five deftests across two files
description:

  cd implementation/machines && clojure -M:test -n re-frame.parallel-states-guide-truth-jvm-test

2. Decide per failure whether the TEST or the PROSE is wrong. title: hic: the slice's reset-law row stays GREEN with ::h/revision's trigger deleted — the whole revision story in both authoring reports is unwitnessed
description:
## What was measured (CHECKPOINT 2, rf2-hic-026, `main`@5d54f50d76, 2026-08-13)

The revision bump was deleted from `::discard` in
`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/slice/events.cljs:121`
— i.e. `(update-in [:revision slug] (fnil inc 0))` removed, nothing else
touched — and `npm run test:browser` was re-run from the same worktree.

    [:browser-test] Build completed. (1250 files, 10 compiled, 8 warnings, 57.58s)
    Browser tests: Ran 1474 tests containing 9154 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.
    captured exit 0

Ten files recompiled, so the plant was in the bundle. The baseline immediately
before, on the same worktree, was the identical 1474/9154, captured exit 0.

The row that should have reddened is
`slice/flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs:381` — `discarding-re-baselines-the-field-without-remounting-it` —
whose own failure message names the mechanism:

    "THE RESET LAW (HD-019): the model moved back to a value the field was
     already showing, so React alone sees nothing to do — the changed
     `::h/revision` is what re-baselines it"

It stays green with the changed `::h/revision` removed. The row therefore
witnesses something else — React's ordinary value diff, or the committed echo —
and cannot tell either of them from the revision. That is the hollow-gate
shape: the absence of the symptom has an unrelated cause.

## Why, at source

`::subs/draft` falls back to the article (`slice/subs.cljs:126-129` →
`slice/db.cljs:183-191` `draft-for`), and `::edit` writes every keystroke into
the draft. So React's last rendered `:value` is the typed text, the discard
moves the model to the article's title, and the two differ — React updates the
DOM on its own. The slice's editor is an ACCEPTING field, and an accepting
field cannot witness the revision.

**The corpus already knows this.** `implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:32`
records it against its own `revision` arm, from the #7815 audit: "On the
accepting `revision` field the model has already taken the draft, so an
immediate write and a deferred one put the same string on screen and the row
cannot red on the defect it names." That is why the testbed carries a
`revision-strict` arm — a REJECTING field, where the model can diverge from the
DOM. The slice reproduced the shape the audit had already indicted.

## What this costs beyond the row

Both authoring reports state, as a finding, when `::h/revision` is needed, and
neither statement survives the measurement:

- `authoring-report-slice.md` finding 5: the ordinary Discard button "does not
  work without bookkeeping the application has to add". In the slice it does
  work without it.
- `authoring-report-todo.md` finding 5 (BOUNDED): "`::h/revision` is the reset
  door for a field that OUTLIVES its reset." The slice's field outlives its
  reset and does not need it.

The sharper statement the testbed supports is that `::h/revision` is the reset
door for a field whose model can DIVERGE from the DOM — a rejecting or
normalising field — which is a different population and a different guide row.
Both reports ask for a guide row teaching authors "you will need a counter";
written from either report as it stands, that row teaches a counter to the
population that does not need one.

Consequently the slice's `:revision` app-db key, the `(fnil inc 0)` in two
handlers, `::subs/revision` and the two `::h/revision` props are unexercised
bookkeeping in this application: the L0 row
(`l0_cljs_test.cljs:222` `discarding-restores-the-article-and-bumps-the-revision`)
reds on the plant, but it asserts the counter's own arithmetic, not any
consequence of it.

**The runtime is not indicted.** The reset law itself is witnessed by the
controlled testbed on three engines (`npm run test:hicasso-controlled`,
re-run green by CHECKPOINT 1). This is a defect in the Phase 2 evidence, not
in the shipped mechanism.

## Surface fence

`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/slice/**` and
`docs/design/hicasso/product/authoring-report-slice.md` /
`authoring-report-todo.md`. No runtime code. Not hot-zone. Do NOT run
`npm run test:hicasso-hmr` (binds :dev-http 8061).

## Acceptance

1. Deleting the revision trigger from `::discard` reddens a named row in the
   slice's flow suite — either by giving the editor a rejecting/normalising
   field whose model can diverge from the DOM, or by asserting the DOM value
   directly against a model that did not move.
2. If no ordinary application shape makes the revision load-bearing, the honest
   alternative is taken instead: the bookkeeping comes OUT of the slice and
   finding 5 is withdrawn in both reports with the reason.
3. Both authoring reports' finding 5 states the population `::h/revision` is
   actually for, citing the testbed's `revision`/`revision-strict` pair.
4. The corrective PR quotes the planted re-run: with the trigger deleted the
   browser lane must be RED, with the captured exit code.
close_reason: PR #8086 open. Reproduced the finding (bump deleted from ::discard → 1474/9154, captured exit 0, identical to control). Established the row was NOT salvageable: impl/codec's revision-key says a revision's whole delivery is that its change RE-RUNS THE BODY, and a discard already moves three of the editor's reads, so the bump is inert for every DOM state — measured against an eventless DOM drift too. Took acceptance 2: bookkeeping out of the slice, finding 5 withdrawn and replaced in both reports. New control bites: (update :drafts dissoc slug) deleted → 4 failures, captured EXIT=1, same test/assertion totals as green so no namespace stopped. Second hollow row found in examples/editor and FILED as rf2-5h9k rather than absorbed.

description:

> **Decider**: the operator. The `1,024 B` reading is his ruling and only he can move it.

before the runtime ABI freezes—must name the reason, ceiling, effective revision, reopen conditions,

Phase 1 substrate adjudication" — that is `rf2-hic-018`, which is **closed**, and whose verdict 3 is
precisely the refusal to take it. So the document points at a bead that has already handed the

- `rf2-hic-085` is the only governance-outcome bead and it covers the **K1 amendment and K3

  (`rf2-hic-085`), donor-surface disposition (`rf2-hic-062`). **The shell disposition is not among
  them**, though it is the only one of the four that a *phase exit* is conjoined on.

`rf2-hic-064`'s §1 does name "the byte-exact shell disposition", so the final audit would eventually
trip over it. That is a backstop, not an owner: it surfaces the gap at the last gate rather than
putting it in front of the operator now, and it leaves the Phase 1 exit unadjudicable in the meantime
— which is this checkpoint's own position today.

## What would close it

   owner bead = the bead filed for it; gates = **Phase 1 exit** and *implementation audit complete*;

## The claim, at source

`rf2-hic-016` was **closed by operator ruling on 2026-08-13** with, verbatim in its close reason:

> CLOSED AS ASSUMED, NOT WITNESSED. The bead's remaining deliverable was native IME composition and
> `beforeinput` BEYOND Chromium, with the acceptance that disabling the composition guard turns the
> WebKit IME witness red. That was never run.

> SIX RECORDS CITE THIS BEAD and must not be read as claiming a witness that does not exist … Anyone
> consolidating those pages should carry 'assumed by operator ruling 2026-08-13, not witnessed'
> rather than silently upgrading the row to green.

None of the six carries it. Three of them state a **closure condition that can never be met, against a
bead that is already closed**:

- `docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md:297` — "`rf2-hic-016` closes when those two cells are
  filled from the operator's **manual session** on Firefox and WebKit, with the date and both engine
  builds, **not before**."
- `docs/design/hicasso/native-ime-manual-witness.md:274` — "`rf2-hic-016` closes when **these**
  results — this session's, for **Firefox and WebKit** — are recorded in §2.3 …"
- `docs/design/hicasso/native-ime-scripted-witness.md:238` and `:367` — the same sentence.

And the disposition table that the release reads, `dispositions.md:291-295`, still shows:

| Engine | Native IME |
|---|---|
| Firefox | **Pending the manual session** |
| WebKit | **Pending the manual session** |

`dispositions.md:277-284` compounds it — it narrates the 2026-08-11 change to a scripted witness and
the 2026-08-12 change back to "the **bounded manual session** is reinstated as the acceptance path",

names its deciding witness as "**WebKit/Firefox native composition and `beforeinput`**, range/direction,
autofill, reset, blur, unmount and upgrade matrix". The landed witness says of itself, at

ranges are Chromium-only and the abort signature "cannot be reproduced from page script in any engine,
**so it is not claimed here**". The runner is honest. The records around it are not: they describe the
gap as temporary and owed, when the operator has ruled it permanent and assumed.

This is the fail-open shape one level up — every page true on the day it was written, and the set
misleading now. `rf2-hic-064` reads these pages.

## What would close it

1. Each of the five in-fence records carries, at the point it cites `rf2-hic-016`, the ruling's own

**Do not re-open the IME session.** The operator ruled it will not happen; this bead is about the
records telling the truth about that, and nothing else.

title: ssr-node's absence scan reds the moment the package is wired — reconcile Reading 1 with the schedule it anticipated
description:
BLOCKS PR #8042 (rf2-n8vp), which is complete and correct but cannot go green.

THE COLLISION. implementation/ssr-node/test/absence.test.cjs Reading 1 — 'no client-building tree references this package' — asserts an ABSOLUTE ZERO over tracked files under implementation, examples, tools, scripts and .github. Giving the package a CI lane necessarily writes its path into four of those files, so the act rf2-n8vp exists to perform is the act that reds the suite.

MEASURED, live on PR #8042: job node-ssr-node FAILED in 13s; locally 'npm run test:ssr-node' exits 1 with four hits —
  .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:106
  .github/workflows/test.yml:5171
  implementation/package.json:84
  implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:1058

BLAST RADIUS IS ONE ROW. 6 of 7 suites pass. Inside absence.test.cjs, Reading 2 (no shadow-cljs build, no classpath entry — the one its own header calls 'the strong one') and Reading 3 (no dependency) both still pass with their controls firing. The wiring moves the package no closer to a client bundle; what it violates is a broad proxy, not the claim.

THE PACKAGE PRESCRIBED THE REMEDY. absence.test.cjs:71-88 says an earlier draft carried exactly this test:ssr-node script with a pinned one-string exception, dropped it 'for an unrelated and better reason — it arms eleven expensive CI lanes' (i.e. for rf2-n8vp), and rules: 'If the npm script is wired up later, the answer is one PINNED EXACT STRING deleted from that file before the remainder is scanned — never a broadened pattern and never a skipped file.'

WHY IT NEEDS A RULING RATHER THAN A PATCH. The author foresaw ONE reference. The lane as rf2-n8vp requires it — armed by its own surface and nothing else — needs FOUR, an irreducible ~6-10 reference-bearing lines. The three candidate shapes are not equivalent:
  (a) pinned exact LINES — faithful to the header, but brittle: every future comment edit in those four files reds the suite;
  (b) pinned PATH allowance — the header forbids it ('never a skipped file');
  (c) narrow Reading 1's scope to constructs that can actually put the package in a module graph (require / :source-paths / deps coordinate), leaving Readings 2 and 3 as the strong net.
(c) looks right to me and is the smallest true statement, but it is a contract decision about this artefact and belongs to whoever owns it.

USEFUL FACT FOR THE FIXER: the matcher already separates NAMES from PATHS. /(?<![\w:-])ssr-node(?![\w-])/ refuses a preceding word char, colon or hyphen — so 'test:ssr-node' and 'node-ssr-node' do NOT match, and only path spellings like 'implementation/ssr-node/' do. A narrow reconciliation is well within reach.

FENCE NOTE: rf2-n8vp's brief said 'Do not touch implementation/ssr-node/** itself ... If you find a defect in it, report rather than fix', so the ssr-node worker refused rather than crossed. PR #8028 is MERGED and no open PR touches the package, so the surface is free.

ON MERGE: land the reconciliation, then merge PR #8042 unchanged — its four wiring files need no edit.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8049 (correctness): REOPENED. Reading 1 claims to scan the body of a Clojure/CLJS ns `:require`, but formsAfterKeys calls balancedFormAt immediately after `:require`, which returns only the first libspec vector. A normal `(ns app.core (:require [app.first :as first] [rf.ssr-node.service :as svc]))` therefore yields only `[app.first :as first]` and passes. The permanent control plants the forbidden namespace as the first and only libspec, so it cannot see this fail-open. Scan the whole ns-clause value (likewise multi-form :require-macros/:import/:use/:load as applicable) and add a second-or-later-libspec control. No duplicate found; rf2-6ovv owns Reading 1.

title: hic: PR #7936's witness pairs a fn-form :each fixture with an async row, so cljs.test aborts its whole namespace
description:
THIS, NOT rf2-d3tc, IS WHAT ACTUALLY REDS PR #7936 (branch worker/cbident-hic029).

SITE. implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/retaining_host_callbacks_dom_cljs_test.cljs

    (use-fixtures :each
      (test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture
        {:adapter uix-adapter/adapter :ambient-frame nil :init-fn ...}))

No ':async? true'. Without it make-reset-runtime-fixture returns the FN-FORM
fixture, and cljs.test/execution-strategy maps fn fixtures to :sync, which wraps
every test fn in disable-async. The file's row
'a-delayed-retained-callback-obeys-the-same-law' returns an (async done ...) object
in a browser, so disable-async throws ::async-disabled and test-var-block* rethrows
it as the bare String

    "Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps.  Testing aborted."

That throw aborts the ENTIRE namespace -- every row in the file is lost -- and,
because it is thrown synchronously inside the preceding suite's 'done'
continuation, it also unwinds into whatever chain called that done.

WHY IT ONLY SHOWS IN THE BROWSER. In :node-test (mount/browser?) is false, so the
row returns the skip's (is true ...) rather than an async object, disable-async
never fires, and the node lane is green. Only npm run test:browser reaches it.

FIX. Add ':async? true' to that fixture's option map (the map-form variant --
see make-reset-runtime-fixture's docstring, 'Async map-form variant'). Every other
hicasso -dom-cljs-test suite with async rows already does this.

CAPTURED PROOF (branch worker/donefix-d3tc). A control namespace shaped exactly
like this witness -- fn-form fixture plus one browser-only async row, sorting
between reincarnation-paint and revision -- reproduced #7936's symptom byte for
byte (captured exit 1, no summary). Adding ':async? true' to that SAME control and
changing nothing else took the whole browser lane to captured exit 0, 'Ran 1286
tests containing 7973 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.'

So the position in the run order is innocuous; the fixture form is the fault.
rf2-d3tc's fix stops the failure being MISATTRIBUTED to reincarnation-paint, but it
cannot make #7936 green -- only this one-line change can.
close_reason: Fixed on worker/cbident-hic029 (PR #7936), commit a494e5ca62: ':async? true' on the witness's :each fixture. Premise verified at source — the fixture WAS fn-form and section 6's row IS (async done ...). Reproduced first: captured exit 1, and the symptom is a HANG rather than the predicted literal — the console never carries 'Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps' (0 hits); the run simply produces no cljs.test summary and 'Timed out after 360000ms', with the trail ending at 'Testing re-frame.hicasso.retaining-host-callbacks-dom-cljs-test' plus a FAIL misreported under a-delayed-retained-callback-obeys-the-same-law carrying a neighbouring suite's message. Same site, same one-line cure. After: captured exit 0, 'Ran 1293 tests containing 8008 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.' Node lane also green (13345/67211, 0/0). Inversion proof: one assertion inside the previously-lost async row inverted gave captured exit 1 naming retaining_host_callbacks_dom_cljs_test.cljs:595:19, 'actual: (not (= 4321 1))' — so the row executes; restored and the restore verified byte-identical by SHA-256. No measurement touched. A second commit (68feb58e1f) corrects the verdict doc's third known limit, which named rf2-d3tc for a fault that was this file's own and asserted a lane that is now green.

title: hic-006b — The package-resident heap instrument, and the re-pin it enables
description:
## Why

rf2-hic-006 (PR #7935) could NOT deliver its 'shell/per-read/teardown baselines re-measured on implementation/hicasso' item, and the reason is structural rather than incidental.

1. The pinned heap figures come from `p0_run.cjs --only ladder`, whose candidate arm is `re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.*` in the BENCH tree. That runtime's docstring: 'Residence: the bench/test tree, off every production source path (HD-017). Nothing under implementation/*/src requires this.' implementation/shadow-cljs.edn states the same separation from the other side and names hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py as its enforcer. So implementation/hicasso/src is a deliberately frozen COPY and NO heap instrument points at the package.
2. Independently, the registered instrument has drifted from its own pin. The heap ladder identifies itself by CONTENT HASH, not commit SHA. At 0c0aa22898 not one of its eleven pinned blobs matches, and front/sub_index.cljs no longer exists. A reading taken today could not be compared with the pinned row: the delta would be un-attributable between instrument drift and the package move.

## What to build

A package-pointed heap build id (e.g. :hicasso-heap-bench) whose candidate arm requires re-frame.hicasso instead of re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1, REUSING the existing p0_* driver and fixtures unchanged so the estimator does not move.

## How to run it

Its OWN measurement window, Shape 6, quiet machine, one run at a time. The package arm and BOTH donor arms must be taken IN THE SAME RUN: the two harnesses differ by a measured ~5% common-mode offset and no figure may be scaled from one onto the other.

## Notes

- HOT ZONE: needs a new build id in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. Operator sequences it.
- Coordinate with rf2-hic-018, which already carries implementation/hicasso/test/.../substrate_* (new benches) on its surface line — this may fold into it rather than run separately.
- Until this lands, S1-S5 in docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md are BENCH-TREE figures, not package figures, and the page says so.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-12, operator-overturnable):

RULING — the three coupled choices:
(1) VEHICLE: Option 1 — a dedicated TWO-DISPATCH sequence ahead of rf2-hic-018. First an ordinary PR that makes the existing P0 heap instrument package-pointed; then ONE solo quiet-window Shape 6 run taking the package arm AND both donor arms in the same run, whose PR is the re-pin. Fold-into-hic-018 REJECTED; defer REJECTED (reasons in the WHY section).
(2) RIG RESIDENCE: ride the existing :hicasso-bench build id — ZERO hot-zone edits. The bead's proposed :hicasso-heap-bench id is DEFERRED to rf2-hic-071, reconsidered ONLY if this lane becomes a standing/recurring gate or a second independent workflow needs it (the stopping rule). Verified: hicasso/src is already on the top-level shadow :source-paths (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn ~L158, its comment naming :hicasso-bench), the driver documents the ride as the deliberate house shape ("No shadow-cljs.edn change, deliberately... One id serves N programs", lane cache cleared per build), and it stamps build + initFn into its output — provenance is complete without a named id, and instrument identity in this corpus is carried by content hash regardless.
(3) RIDER: the shell paper-fail line is FROZEN at the literal 1,024 B. Spell it "1,024 B" everywhere; the ambiguous "1 KB" spelling retires. Adjudication rule adopted with it: a confidence band that crosses 1,024 B is UNRESOLVED, not a pass, and no substrate is selected on a point-estimate difference inside that band. Basis: budgets.md section 5's standing recommendation; the row is red under either reading today (1,103 / 1,097 B) but the no-wrapper arm reads 994/992 B, so a remediation landing between 1,000 and 1,024 is a reachable coin-flip between readings. rf2-hic-018's shell disposition consumes this line; it is noted there before dispatch.

VERIFICATION (all re-checked live at HEAD 5f662c4ff2, not taken from the dossier):
- Instrument drift is real: p0_run.cjs live blob 30e16875... vs pin 4718aaea...; arm1/runtime.cljs live 202f7612... vs pin 69bfc6fc...; front/sub_index.cljs ABSENT. budgets.md section 6's pin table matches these live hashes exactly.
- No heap instrument points at the package: every candidate read goes through re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.runtime/sub (bench tree); check_freeze.py live output: "OK: 1 frozen row(s) match the bench tree... no package file imports it".
- CHECKPOINT 1 (rf2-hic-019) returned HELD 2026-08-11 17:28 AUSEST with rf2-hic-018 among the four open discharge deps; hic-018's own deps are all closed and it blocks hic-017 + hic-019.
- Driver overrides documented: P0_BUILD (default hicasso-bench, p0_run.cjs L119), P0_INIT_FN (default re-frame.bench.p0-app/-main, L122), one-line --config-merge of output-dir + :init-fn onto the existing :advanced :browser id.
- budgets.md section 4 carries S1-S5 flagged "not re-pinned on the package"; section 5 (~L258) carries the standing 1,024 B recommendation.

CODEX ADVISORY, adjudicated on the merits:
- ADOPTED — repoint-in-place, not sibling-arm-plus-entry. The dossier's "exactly two new files" sketch is mechanically INCOMPLETE, verified against the code: p0_heap.cljs (1,258 lines) hard-codes the prototype at exactly four candidate seams — mount door L154 (arm1.mount/root!), runtime reset L384 (arm1.runtime/reset-runtime!), live structural census L447 (arm1.runtime/residue), post-unmount residue L1244 (same) — and p0_hicasso.cljs's doors are arm1's (runtime/sub + lang/defview). A sibling view + entry alone would still measure through the prototype's mount/reset/census/residue, and duplicating the heap namespace would be the wrong repair. The package equivalents exist 1:1, verified: re-frame.hicasso.impl.mount/root! (L145), impl.collector/reset-runtime! (L2015), impl.inventory/stats (L126) + residue (L162), facade re-frame.hicasso/defview (macro, hicasso.cljc L97) and /sub (alias of impl.collector/sub, L393). Git history is sufficient residence for the obsolete prototype-pointed instrument (pre-alpha; the package is the product; the freeze header calls divergence expected and permanent).
- ADOPTED — window scope: retained-heap ladder only; no clock/allocation/fan-out/extra-hardware rows unless one could change hic-018's choice; no recurring distributional CI gate (the existing contract keeps noisy heap distributions out of ordinary PR gating).
- REJECTED — single-delivery (instrument commit + evidence commit in one dispatch). Builder and runner stay SEPARATE across two dispatches: the instrument merges and passes CI BEFORE any sample exists, its blob hashes fixed by the merge — pre-registration made mechanical rather than disciplinary — and the window runner cannot "repair" an arm it did not write without ending the window ("the repair is to the ARM, never to the guard"). Codex's own condition ("the rig must be frozen before the first sample") is exactly what the two-dispatch shape enforces structurally. Cost: one extra dispatch. Tracker history: multi-deliverable bundles time out.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
DISPATCH 1 — instrument PR (dispatchable NOW; isolated bench-tree surface implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/; parallel-safe; NOT hot-zone):
- p0_hicasso.cljs: the doors become the package facade — sub from re-frame.hicasso, defview via re-frame.hicasso require-macros; docstring updated to say the arm prices the PACKAGE.
- p0_heap.cljs: ONLY the four seams repoint — requires arm1.mount -> re-frame.hicasso.impl.mount; arm1.runtime -> impl.collector (reset-runtime!) + impl.inventory (residue); call sites L154 / L384 / L447 / L1244. Donors, floor, harness, fixtures, lane collector/fit rules, order-guard, p0_run.cjs and its plans: byte-identical — the estimator does not move.
- Narrow wiring assertions in the existing structural test; run it plus the existing hicasso compile gate, foreground, to completion.
- This PR does NOT touch: budgets.md (its figures do not exist yet), implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, the freehand donor tree, frozen-sources.edn (the one frozen row is front/slot.cljc — untouched). Bench tree requiring re-frame.hicasso is the allowed direction (precedent: :hicasso-release's consumer app); the SEALED fence forbids only package -> re-frame.bench.*.
DISPATCH 2 — the window (only after dispatch 1 MERGES; at the operator-granted quiet):
- Shape 6, SOLO: zero other workers, zero open PRs, dispatch paused; box verified quiet by real counters (Processor Queue Length 0 — the hic-006 method); P-DEV-1 is Mike's machine and only he grants the box.
- ONE invocation of p0_run.cjs --only ladder: package candidate + BOTH donor arms in the same run set (measured ~5% common-mode harness offset — Reagent +5.19%, UIx +5.17% — so no figure may be scaled across runs), the candidate measured in both segments as the arm already provides.
- The rig is frozen at dispatch-1 merge; any rig change invalidates and repeats the window. A refusal (guard exit 2, control not ok, unverified mounts) is a DELIVERABLE: record it on this bead, end the window, re-schedule. NEVER iterate the instrument to force a green. hic-018's heap half holds until an anchor exists.
- Deliverable = the re-pin PR: budgets.md section 4 S1-S5 become package figures with a fresh blob table; section 5 extends to the package readings and records the 1,024 B freeze as RULED (this note is the ruling); section 6's refusal section gets its closure note; the ladder page's provenance re-pins at the fresh blob hashes; publish raw round ranges, all quality verdicts, DOM/Q/structural read-backs, post-unmount residue, and the exact package commit + instrument blobs (the driver already stamps build + initFn).
SEQUENCING / DEPENDENCY DIRECTION: rf2-fe0l now BLOCKS rf2-hic-018 (edge added this session). This sequence feeds hic-018's acceptance: the same-instrument package baseline is taken BEFORE any collector-substrate mutation, which is what makes hic-018's before/after attributable; hic-018 then reuses THIS exact instrument, for viable substrate candidates only. rf2-hic-070 re-pins its K3 citations after hic-018, per its own text ("re-pins, never re-frames"). Context for both workers: the freeze manifest is down to 1 row, the package runtime is 18 owned impl modules (hic-009), and S1-S5 currently describe a diverging prototype — divergence is expected and permanent, which is why the re-pin cannot wait for a "stable" moment.

FENCES:
- NO hot-zone traffic in either dispatch (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/* untouched).
- NO new build id now; :hicasso-heap-bench reconsidered only from rf2-hic-071 under the stopping rule.
- NO instrument iteration to force a green — a window refusal ends the window and is reported.
- Dispatch 1 stays off budgets.md, the freehand donor tree, and frozen-sources.edn.

WHY (options record, preserved from the dossier before its deletion):
- Option 3 (fold into hic-018) rejected: the arm cannot live on hic-018's stated surface (the SEALED fence reds re-frame.bench.* requires under the package, so the fold contaminates a second surface anyway); hic-018 is already Est. L with an amended invariants.md landing slot; one worker holding both rig and verdict has exactly the incentive Shape 6 exists to remove — an adjudicator is built to iterate to green, a measurement worker must not; the baseline would be taken inside the same PR-stream that is about to mutate the collector, re-blurring the attribution this bead exists to fix; and multi-deliverable bundles time out.
- Option 4 (defer) rejected: the window must happen regardless; deferral only moves it onto CHECKPOINT 1's critical path (hic-019 is HELD with hic-018 a discharge bead), while S1-S5 drift further as kernel PRs advance the package. No benefit.
- Option 2 (named id first) rejected today: identity, not capability — a hot-zone sequencing slot and a slower start for zero additional measurement capability; the shadow-cljs.edn "one id, one artefact" argument was written about the package's permanent test gate, not a bench ride whose documented house shape is the merged init-fn.
DISPATCH 2 COMPLETE — the window did NOT refuse. PR #7941 (branch worker/heapmeasure-fe0l).

RUN: one invocation of p0_run.cjs --only ladder, 2026-08-12 06:47-06:51 AUSEST, captured exit 0. Package candidate + BOTH donors in the same run set, as ruled. Tree anchor ce31a30b77 (on origin/main), working tree clean.

RIG VERIFIED AT SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED: module graph read from a cleared cache entry TWICE — pre-window and from the driver's OWN build — identical both times: arm1 namespaces 0, hicasso.impl 16, all four package doors PRESENT. Controlled: the same reader against a sibling init-fn that does require arm1 (clock-app/-main, no rig file touched) reports arm1: 2, hicasso.impl: 0, exit 1. NOTE: dispatch 1 reported 389/32 where I read 130/16 — enumeration method differs (16 is exactly half of 32); the directional facts agree exactly.

PACKAGE FIGURES (S1-S5 now package figures in budgets.md section 4):
  S1 R=0 shell, Reagent seg  1,100 B [1,091-1,107]   (was 1,103, bench tree)
  S2 R=0 shell, UIx seg      1,095 B [1,087-1,101]   (was 1,097)
  S3 per-read vs Reagent     1,417 vs 948 B/read     (was 1,278 vs 947)
  S4 per-read vs UIx         2,115 vs 2,980 B/read   (was 2,115 vs 2,980 — reproduces exactly)
  S5 teardown bytes          indistinguishable from zero; all ten candidate rungs' bands straddle 0; structural witness exactly zero after teardown on every arm of every round.
S6 (cold mount) and S7 (allocation) REMAIN BENCH-TREE — not measured; no package-resident clock instrument exists.

THE ONE RESULT THAT MATTERS FOR hic-018: nine of ten quantities reproduce the prototype's published rows (both donors, both floors, both shells, the UIx-segment slope). EXACTLY ONE moved — the Reagent-segment per-read slope, 1,278 -> 1,417 B/read (+139, +10.9%), bands disjoint by 136 B. So the move is the candidate's, not the instrument's. Governed contrast vs Reagent deepens 1.3492x -> 1.4953x; the UIx win is unchanged to the fourth decimal (0.7099x -> 0.7098x). MECHANISM DELIBERATELY NOT ATTRIBUTED — a package carrying more per-read state should show it in BOTH segments and it shows in one; naming a cause needs ablations a measurement window may not run. That attribution is hic-018's, and it now has the same-instrument package baseline that makes it possible.

SHELL BREACH SURVIVES THE MOVE TO THE PACKAGE — 1,100 / 1,095 B, every one of the twelve readings at or above 1,087 B. Red under the frozen 1,024 B reading AND under the retired 1,000 B one; NOT a band-crossing case, so no UNRESOLVED verdict arises here. It is a property of the design, not of the prototype. The 1,024 B freeze is recorded as RULED in budgets.md section 5; the '1 KB' spelling retires.

CONTROLS (all from this run, none re-derived): positive control 587,500 doubles predicted 4,700,000 B before the run, measured 4,700,284 B [4,699,042-4,700,872], ratio 1.0001 — ok under lane/control-verdict; the R-ladder itself (0->20, all four arms lines, 6 of 6 rounds linear, r2 0.99833-0.99996); segment swap (donor shells differ 291 B across segments, candidate's differ 5 B); floor calibrator 256/255 B; fit self-tests (an absurd 99,999 B R=0 rung moves the fit by zero bits); arm-order guard reportable; 0 unverified of 154 mounts.

STABILITY: nothing refused to measure. Candidate slope bands 1-9 B wide over six rounds. Box occupancy 4.17/3.02% before, 2.15/2.35% after, Processor Queue Length 0 on every sample, zero java, no other worker, no local gate. Higher than the 1.4-3.0% of the 2026-08-04 sections because chrome is 129 processes vs 56 (operator's idle browser) — recorded, not corrected for; this is a retained-heap row and the page has already priced contention on it at ~0.07%.

NO HOT-ZONE FILE WAS NEEDED (rode :hicasso-bench via P0_BUILD/P0_INIT_FN, as ruled).

ONE PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD AT SOURCE: the 'donors/fixtures byte-identical' claim is true of dispatch 1's own diff but NOT against the runs this re-pin compares to. p0_reagent.cljs and p0_uix.cljs moved by docstring only (606bad8445); p0_fixture.cljc moved executably (eb17886c5b) — seed-db gained a grid-width arity defaulting to the published cells-n, and :p0/fan's modulus became (count (:cells db)) where it was that same constant. Measurement-neutral by construction, and settled empirically by both donors and both floors returning on their published anchors. Written into the provenance block rather than glossed.

SCOPE NOTE: besides budgets.md and the ladder studio page, lanes/evidence-baseline.md needed three heap rows updating — budgets.md section 4 names it as the source its rows are carried from, so re-pinning one and not the other would put two figures for one estimand in one corpus.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7941 (2026-08-12 AUSEST; completeness, correctness, implementation quality).

COMPLETENESS: the PR publishes the package S1-S5 rows, retains honest bench-tree labels for S6/S7, records the frozen 1,024 B line, carries the same figures into the evidence baseline, and supplies unusually strong controls, table checks, module-graph evidence, and exact instrument/package blobs. The measurement record is otherwise complete and restrained; no extra bench programme is requested.

CORRECTNESS: the whole-tree identity claim did not survive merge chronology. The one run occurred 2026-08-12 06:47–06:51 AUSEST on `ce31a30b77`. PR #7940 then merged before #7941 and changed `re-frame.events`, `re-frame.fx`, and `re-frame.router`; all three blobs differ between the measured anchor and #7941's landed tree, and they are reachable from the Hicasso benchmark bundle (`impl.state` requires events; core requires router/events/fx). Nevertheless the landed page still says “the measured tree and the published tree are the same tree.” The per-file instrument and Hicasso blobs remain valuable, but they do not establish whole-bundle identity, and neither donors nor the positive control were rerun after the intervening source change. This matters because rf2-hic-018 consumes the row specifically as a before/after attribution anchor.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the two-dispatch frozen-rig design and single quiet window are excellent; the failure is the rebase/merge handoff, not the instrument. Repair minimally: correct the provenance claim and take one governed package+both-donors run on a fully landed anchor before treating the row as the downstream attribution baseline. Re-pin only figures that move. If an equivalent landed rerun already exists, cite it and reconcile the rows instead of creating another campaign. Any moved input must flow to the already named downstream consumers; do not redesign the rig.

This exact owner remains rf2-fe0l: it owns the package-resident heap re-pin and the claim that its landed baseline is attributable. The older rf2-2rtt6.40 provenance bead is page-specific and not a duplicate owner for this run.

I ran git reset --hard origin/main twice while resolving .beads rebase conflicts, which is the same shape. EVIDENCE OF COMPLETION, unchanged: both ruled dispatches landed. Dispatch 1 = PR #7939 repointed the heap rig at the package (four seams; module graph arm1=0, hicasso.impl=32; break-and-restore proved the compile stays GREEN WITH ZERO WARNINGS while four arm1 namespaces leak back, so the compile is not the check, the graph is). Shell breach survives to the package (twelve readings >= 1,087 B, red under both 1,024 and 1,000) so it is NOT a band-crossing case. S6, S7, U1-U4 stay bench-tree.

description:
# Publish CHECKPOINT 1's report and open its five correction-ledger rows

**Filed by rf2-hic-019, which ran read-only with no PR. Severity: coverage (the ledger gate reads these rows).**

rf2-hic-019's Output section requires two tracked artefacts. It ran under a read-only,
no-PR fence and could produce neither, so this bead carries them and their content is
below in full. rf2-hic-064 gates on the ledger, and a finding recorded only in a bead
description is not where the final audit looks.

## 1. `docs/design/hicasso/product/checkpoint-1-kernel.md` does not exist

Verified absent on `main`@`27c5d12754`. It is the pass/miss-per-row report the bead
names.

## 2. `docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md` still reads "*No rows yet — the first checkpoint (rf2-hic-019) has not run.*" (`:61`)

Five rows are owed. Per that file's own rule (`:39`, `:43-48`) the checkpoint that
filed them is the ledger keeper, and corrective PRs never edit the file — so these
rows go in as `open` in a ledger-only commit, and the mayor keeps them from there.

| Checkpoint | Protocol section | Finding | bd id | Severity | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rf2-hic-019 | §3 Quality | `h/boundary` reads `:on-error`/`:reset-key`/`:fallback`/`:children` off a free-form props map with no roster and no shape check; a misspelled key and a non-vector/non-fn `:on-error` each silently report nothing | rf2-czlb | correctness | open |

| rf2-hic-019 | §3 Quality | `::h/mounting` outside a presence tray's direct child is a silent no-op and leaks to the DOM | rf2-34a7 | quality (see that bead's severity note) | open |

## 3. The verdict the report must carry, unsoftened

**HELD — not pass, not fail.** The kernel exit cannot be adjudicated, because four of
this checkpoint's own dependencies were open when it ran (`main`@`27c5d12754`,

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §2 Correctness. Severity: coverage.**

## What is wrong

`docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/adversarial-risks.md:41` (Gate construction):

> Include a sabotage mutation that makes each correctness gate red.

and rf2-hic-019's own protocol §2 requires the checkpoint to *"independently re-run
**one sabotage control per risk family** (all eight)"*. For two of the eight kernel
rows there is nothing to re-run.

### Row 2 — Process-global ownership

Its three witnesses:

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/roots_frames_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
  — **no sabotage in any form.** A case-insensitive search of the whole file for
  `sabotag|mutation|negative.control|redden` returns nothing.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/public_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
  — same: nothing.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/roots_frames_shared_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs:240-252`
  and `:332-335` — two prose notes. The first is genuinely valuable reasoning (it
  records that no single-point mutation reds the row and names the coherent two-point
  one that does) but it is a comment. The second is
  `;; MUTATION (PR body records the red): key the window off the frame in hydrate-root! …`.

### Row 8 — Hydration isolation

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/roots_frames_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs:274-276`
  — `;; SABOTAGE (run by hand, PR body records it): mint ONE window in hydrate-root! …`

  — `;; SABOTAGE (run by hand, PR body records it): point impl.presence-react back at a page-wide window …`

Both are comments. Neither executes.

### The pointer is dangling in every one of them

Every comment says "the PR body records it" and **none names a PR number or a
commit**. A PR body is not in the tree, this repository rebase-merges (so a branch
head is not the commit that landed), and nothing in `docs/design/hicasso/` records
which PR carried which mutation. So a reviewer who is not the author cannot reach the
evidence at all — which is exactly the condition the correction ledger's closure rule
was written to prevent (`docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md:33`:
*"Who re-runs it is never the author of the fix"*).

The same pattern is at
`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/presence_ssr_seam_dom_cljs_test.cljs:140`,
`:323` and `:454`, which is adjacent rather than a kernel row, and worth fixing in the
same pass.

## Why this is not an impossible ask

The package already ships three working executable-sabotage patterns, so this is a
gap rather than a limitation:

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/checkpoint_support.cljs:137-155` —
  `with-macrotask-deferral` restores the pre-fix scheduling *for the width of one
  synchronous form*, with the collector "unmodified and unaware".
- `implementation/hicasso/testbed/hmr_spec.cjs:564-614` — `lostCleanupSabotage` arms,
  asserts the row goes RED, and disarms.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/reincarnation_paint_dom_cljs_test.cljs:266`
  — an in-file sabotage row, recorded in the exercised-population roster at `:317`.

## What should change (sketch)

The mayor picks the tier; either discharges the finding.

**Tier A (preferred).** Give rows 2 and 8 one executing control each, in the shape
`hmr_spec.cjs` already uses: arm the mutation, assert the row reddens, disarm. For row
8's window sabotage this most likely means a seam — a test-only injection point for the
adoption-window mint on `hydrate-root!` — rather than editing `impl/mount.cljs` from a
test. One control per row is enough; the protocol asks for one per family, not one per
assertion.

**Tier B (minimum).** Where a mutation genuinely cannot be armed from a test, the
in-tree comment must name **the PR number and the `main` commit it was run against**,
and the same pair must appear in a tracked record so the audit can find it without the
GitHub UI. `docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md` or a companion table is
the natural home. "The PR body records it", with no PR named, is not a pointer.

Do NOT convert the `:240-252` reasoning note into a test — it is a record of *why* a
single-point mutation is insufficient and is worth more as prose. It needs the PR/commit
pointer, not an executable form.

## Done when

- Kernel risk rows 2 and 8 each have one sabotage control an independent reviewer can run and observe redden, OR each hand-run mutation names its PR number and landed commit in the tree.
- The re-run is recorded where rf2-hic-064 can read it (see the correction ledger's closure rule).
- No existing row's assertions change.

## Tests / checks that matter

- `:browser-test` — these are all `-dom-cljs-test` files, and they degrade to a stated
  skip in the node lane (`roots_frames_support.cljs:85-91`, `impl/mount.cljs:447-451`),
  so the node run proves nothing here. Run the browser lane.
- `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-hicasso && node out/node-test-hicasso.js` for the non-DOM half (553 tests / 2508 assertions green on `main`@`89029ac46d`).

## What NOT to touch

  census-before-release discipline is correct and load-bearing.

title: hic-019 F3 — h/defhost silently discards forms after opts, and never checks opts is a map
description:
# `h/defhost` silently discards every form after `opts`, and never checks that `opts` is a map

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §3 Quality. Severity: correctness.**

## What is wrong

`mint-host!` refuses an unknown option key at the declaration, and its message states
the ruling that motivates the whole guard
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1649-1651`):

> "Reading past an option it does not know is how a policy comes to be set and never applied."

The macro that calls it reads past an entire **form**, silently, one layer above that
guard. `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:309-310`:

    [sym & more]
    (let [doc              (when (string? (first more)) (first more))
          [component opts] (if doc (rest more) more)

`[component opts]` is a fixed two-element sequential destructure over a seq of
arbitrary length. Everything past the second element is dropped with no refusal:

    (h/defhost modal Modal
      {:callbacks {:on-close :event}}
      {:slots #{:title}})          ;; <- mints; the :slots map is GONE

That is the silent-declaration trap the `:slots` reserved-name repair (commit
`5e5c21f5fc`, `codec.cljs:1566`) and the in-flight `:callbacks` sibling exist to
delete, reached one level higher up the same door. A legal-looking declaration mints,
reads back consistent (the head simply has no slots), and the markup written at
`:title` can never arrive.

`h/defview` does NOT have this shape — `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:154`
destructures `[argv & body]`, so its tail is the body and nothing is discarded.
`defhost` is the one door in the family that swallows a tail.

## The second half: `opts` is never checked to be a map

`mint-host!` goes straight from the nil-component check to
`(doseq [k (keys opts)] …)` at `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1643`
with no `map?` guard. `h/reg-state` has exactly that guard —
`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/state.cljc:268-274`,
`:rf.error/hicasso-state-bad-option`, *"reg-state options must be a map"* — and
`mint-host!` does not. So `(h/defhost modal Modal "a docstring in the wrong place"
{:ssr :render})` binds `opts` to the STRING (the docstring probe at
`hicasso.cljc:309` only inspects `(first more)`, which is the symbol `Modal`), drops
the real options map, and hands a non-map to `keys`. Whatever diagnosis the author
then gets, it is not a declaration refusal naming the offending form — which is the
entire point of the declaration extent `defhost`'s docstring argues for at
`hicasso.cljc:289-297`.

## Where

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:309-310` — the fixed two-element destructure that drops the tail
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:320-321` — the splice, which passes only `component` and `opts`
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1643-1653` — the unknown-key refusal it undercuts, with no `map?` check above it
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:154` — `defview`'s `[argv & body]`, the shape that is correct
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/state.cljc:268-274` — the `map?` guard that exists on the comparable surface

## What should change (sketch)

1. **In the macro**: refuse a tail. After binding `doc`, assert that what remains is
   one or two forms, and throw a `clojure.core/ex-info`-shaped compile-time error (or
   `impl.error/fail!` if it can run at expansion) naming the discarded form and the
   two legal arities — `(defhost name component)` and `(defhost name component opts)`,
   each with an optional docstring in second position. A macro-time refusal is right
   here: the fault is in the FORM, not in a value, so it can be caught before anything
   is evaluated.
2. **In `mint-host!`**: add the `map?` guard, ahead of the `doseq`, in `reg-state`'s
   shape and on `:rf.error/hicasso-host-unknown-option` or a sibling id. This also
   catches the non-macro caller.

Keep both messages in the house style: name the offending form, name the recovery.
Do NOT add positional flexibility (a docstring after the component) — refuse it.

## Done when

- `(h/defhost x C {:callbacks {…}} {:slots #{:title}})` fails at compile time naming the discarded form.
- `(h/defhost x C "doc-in-the-wrong-place" {:ssr :render})` fails naming the non-map options value, not from inside `keys`.
- The three legal shapes are unaffected: `(defhost x C)`, `(defhost x C opts)`, `(defhost x "doc" C opts)`.
- New ids (if minted) are rowed in `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md` and Spec 009; `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` passes.

## Tests / checks that matter

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/public_door_macros_cljs_test.cljs` — the door-macro suite is the natural home; a macroexpansion-time refusal may need a `.clj` row or a `try`/`catch` around a `macroexpand`.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/host_slots_dom_cljs_test.cljs` — the sibling suite for `:slots` refusals.
- `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-hicasso && node out/node-test-hicasso.js` (553 tests / 2508 assertions green on `main`@`89029ac46d`).

## What NOT to touch

- `defview`'s `[argv & body]` — correct as it stands.
- The `finally`-closed declaration extent in both macros and its rf2-hic-007 rationale.
- The anonymous-`fn` contract (rf2-jan2) in `defview`.
- `impl/codec.cljs`'s `:slots` / `:callbacks` declaration arms — `cbguard-hic035` is
  live on `implementation/hicasso/src` and `test` for the `:callbacks` reserved-name
  repair. If that lands first, rebase the `map?` guard on top of it; the two touch the
  same function.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7921 (commit 52ecd42ac2). h/defhost's macro now detects a form after opts at MACROEXPANSION (the forms are quoted, so nothing after opts is evaluated) and emits a refusal that fires at namespace load inside the declaration extent, :rf.error/hicasso-host-extra-form; mint-host! gains reg-state's map? guard as :rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-options, nil legal. Raised at load rather than thrown at expansion for two reasons stated in impl.codec/refuse-host-extra-forms!: this package has no JVM test lane (TESTING.md - hicasso is deliberately off implementation_jvm), so a compile-time refusal is witnessed by nothing; and fail!'s ambient :view/:source come from the ledger the EMITTED declaring! writes, so an expansion-time throw would carry less than every sibling defhost refusal. Witnesses: public_door_macros_cljs_test D and E with near-miss controls. node lane 557/2524 green; sabotage removed = 8 failures in exactly those two deftests; tail guard widened to (drop 1) = a legal defhost in error_shape_cljs_test refused at ns load and took the suite down; map? guard widened (nil refused) run alone = the nil near-miss control red.

title: hic-019 F1 — h/boundary reads four props off a free-form map and refuses nothing
description:
# `h/boundary` reads four props off a free-form map and refuses nothing

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §3 Quality / §1 Completeness. Severity: correctness.**

## What is wrong

`h/boundary` is the kernel's error boundary. It consumes exactly four keys out of the
props map an author writes, and there is no roster, no shape check and no refusal
anywhere on the surface. Every other declaration surface in the package refuses an
unknown key at the declaration — `mint-host!` does it explicitly
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1643-1653`, whose own
message says *"Reading past an option it does not know is how a policy comes to be
set and never applied"*), and `h/reg-state` does it at
`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/state.cljc:275-284`. `h/boundary`
is the one surface with no such guard, and it is the surface whose silent failure is
worst: an error boundary that reports nothing.

Two distinct silent failures, both from legal-looking declarations:

1. **A misspelled key is simply dropped.** `props-of`
   (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:124-128`) hands
   the whole `rfProps` map through unfiltered. `:on-error` is consulted at `:143`,
   `:reset-key` at `:163` and `:186`, `:fallback` at `:194`/`:212`, `:children` at
   `:194`/`:213`. `{:on-errors …}`, `{:resetKey …}`, `{:reset_key …}` or
   `{:fall-back …}` mint, cross `rfProps` intact, and are consulted by nothing. The
   author believes they have error reporting; they have none, and nothing says so.

2. **An `:on-error` of the wrong SHAPE is silently ignored.** `report!` at
   `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:143-149` is
   `(cond (vector? on-error) … (fn? on-error) … :else nil)`. So
   `{:on-error :app/boundary-failed}` — a bare intent keyword, which is exactly what
   somebody writes who has not noticed intents are vectors here — swallows every
   caught error and returns nil. So does a string, a map, or a symbol. The `:else nil`
   arm is the whole defect: it is the *silent-declaration trap* the `:slots`
   reserved-name repair (commit `5e5c21f5fc`) exists to delete, one surface over.

This is the same class as `{:slots #{:constructor}}`: legal-looking declaration that
mints, reads back correct, and can never take effect.

## Where

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:124-128` — `props-of`, no filter
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:143-149` — `report!`'s `:else nil`
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:186` — `:reset-key` consult
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:194` — `:fallback`/`:children` consult
- Comparators that DO refuse: `impl/codec.cljs:1643-1653`, `impl/state.cljc:275-284`

## What should change (sketch)

Two guards, both cheap and both at the place the author's stack still points at the
declaration:

1. A roster — `#{:on-error :reset-key :fallback :children}` — checked once per
   render in the boundary's own `render`, refusing an unknown key with the recovery
   naming the four. Reuse `impl.error/fail!` and either the existing
   `:rf.error/hicasso-host-unknown-option` id or a boundary-specific sibling; the
   catalogue checker (`npm run test:hicasso-invariants`) governs which.
2. `report!`'s `:else` arm refuses instead of returning nil, naming the value it was
   given and the two shapes that work (an intent vector, or a 1-arg fn).

Do NOT add a third `:on-error` shape; the two that exist are right. Do NOT convert
this into a render-time nag that fires per commit — one refusal at the offending
declaration, in the `fail!` house style.

## Done when

- `{:on-errors …}` on an `h/boundary` raises at the declaration naming the key and the roster.
- `{:on-error :app/thing}` raises naming the value and the two legal shapes.
- The four legal keys are unaffected; the existing boundary rows stay green.
- The refusal ids appear in `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md` and Spec 009
  if a new id is minted, and `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` passes (the catalogue
  checker enforces the pairing, and it counted 67 live rows at filing time).

## Tests / checks that matter

- New rows in `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
  (or a sibling): one per silent failure above, each asserting the REFUSAL, not the absence of a report.
- `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-hicasso && node out/node-test-hicasso.js` — 553 tests / 2508 assertions green at filing time (`main`@`89029ac46d`).
- `npm run test:hicasso-invariants`.

## What NOT to touch

- `report!`'s vector and fn arms, and the "called from `componentDidCatch` and from
  nowhere else" property.
- The unconditional `intent/with-frame` binding in `render` (`:209`) and its `nil`-frame rationale.
- Anything under `impl/codec.cljs`'s host-declaration arms — `cbguard-hic035` is live
  on `implementation/hicasso/src` and `test` for the sibling `:callbacks` repair.

title: hic test kit: a failed clocked mount leaves the global virtual clock installed
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7861 — correctness and transactional-completeness finding.

`hm/mount!` installs the page-wide virtual clock BEFORE `mint-frame!`, so `:initial-events` timers are correctly captured. But the only pre-handle release in the new code is the later render-refusal branch. If `rf/make-frame` throws while normalising or running `:initial-events` — core deliberately raises `:rf.error/initial-events-step-failed` on that path — control leaves from `mint-frame!` before a handle exists and before `release-clock!` runs.

The failed frame itself is rolled back by core, but `!clock` still owns one holder and global `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, both clearers, and `Date.now` remain replaced. There is no handle to pass to `unmount!` or `residue`, so the rest of the browser run inherits a frozen clock and can hang or false-green. This contradicts both `mount!`'s transactional promise (a throw leaves nothing behind) and the clock's mount-window promise.

BOUNDED REPAIR: keep clock installation before initial events, but make its hold transactional until `handle-for` succeeds. Every escaping pre-handle path must release exactly the hold this call acquired, without double-release on the existing render-refusal path and without restoring globals out from under an already-clocked peer mount. Preserve the original thrown refusal/ex-data; add no public API or new diagnostic.

PROVENANCE: PR #7861 merge c3b64aa4c02c75f15ecca6b424bf7e34437ff037, `implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs`.
acceptance_criteria: Add a real-browser witness that captures the five platform functions, makes a `{:clock true}` mount whose initial event deterministically fails, and proves: the original failure is returned; the provisional frame is absent; all five globals are identity-restored; and a subsequent real timer/plain mount settles. Add the holder-count control: with one clocked peer already live, a second clocked mount's initial-event failure releases only its own hold, leaves the shared clock installed for the peer, and the peer can still advance and cleanly restore it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7883 — mount!'s clock hold is now transactional until handle-for, released once on every escaping pre-handle path. Witnessed by a-failed-clocked-mount-leaves-no-clock-installed (throw inside :initial-events; five platform functions read by identity; leaked-holder arm; real timer settles) and a-failed-clocked-mount-releases-only-its-own-hold (peer control). Confirm-by-revert: 6 + 2 reds without the fix.

title: hic: the test kit's refuse! carries the exact bypass just fixed in the package constructor
description:
Reported by the rf2-hic-007 worker, which correctly did not touch it: the file was fenced to the then-live rf2-hic-020 worker. That fence is now GONE — rf2-hic-020 closed and PR #7805 merged.

THE DEFECT. implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs:177, refuse! does (merge {..shape..} extra) — extra LAST. A test that calls refuse! with a well-formed extra proves nothing. Pass a payload that names :rf.error/id, :recovery and :where and assert the constructor's values win. Mutate the merge order and quote the red.

THE SHARP EDGE WAS NOT THE ONE THE BEAD NAMED, and it is worse: the message is built from the PARAMETERS while the ex-data was built from the PAYLOAD, so the two could name DIFFERENT REFUSALS — the map saying :rf.error/hicasso-true-child while the message said [:rf.error/hicasso-test-not-a-body]. In a kit whose entire deliverable (rf2-hic-020) is that it RAISES THE RUNTIME'S REFUSAL rather than paraphrasing it, a constructor that can disagree with itself defeats the parity outright.

title: hic: h/defview's emitted body fn binds its own name, so a same-named helper recurses forever
description:
Found by the rf2-kjf5 worker (PR #7801) and NOT fixed there — it is a public-door macro bug and a naming decision, so it was correctly left alone.

THE DEFECT

h/defview names its emitted body fn `<sym>-body`. A NAMED fn binds its own name inside its body. So the spelling the kit itself teaches:

    (defn row-body [props] ...)
    (h/defview row [p] (row-body p))

expands to

    (fn row-body [p] (row-body p))

and recurses forever. The programmer's helper is shadowed by the macro's own emitted name.

EVIDENCE, both directions

- Confirmed by macroexpansion.
- Then MEASURED: rendering the suite's existing `greeting` head answers
  {:refused nil, :message "Maximum call stack size exceeded"}.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW

It was unreachable while a minted head ALWAYS refused — the refusal fired before the body could run. PR #7801 (rf2-kjf5) made dev builds retain the body, which is what surfaced it. So this is not a regression introduced by that change; it is a latent defect that change exposed.

IT BITES IN PRODUCTION TOO. The worker states it bites under React exactly as it bites at L2. This is not a test-only artefact.

WHY P1

A programmer following the documented idiom gets infinite recursion with a stack-overflow message that names nothing useful. There is no diagnostic, no refusal id, and nothing points at the macro. That is the opposite of the ergonomics this project is built for.

SHAPE OF THE FIX — A NAMING DECISION, NOT ONLY A CODE ONE

The emitted fn does not need to carry a name a programmer can collide with. Options include gensymming it, or namespacing the emitted name so no ordinary helper can shadow-collide, or emitting an anonymous fn and carrying the display name by another route. Note that the emitted name currently feeds `displayName` and the performance entry id, so whatever is chosen must keep those readable — see the `displayName` stamp in mint-view! and re-frame.hicasso.impl.codec.

CURRENT STATE IN THE TREE

The rf2-kjf5 worker named its NEW fixture `farewell-text` rather than `farewell-body`, with a comment saying exactly why, and deliberately LEFT `greeting` carrying the defect so the reproducer stays in the tree. Do not "tidy" `greeting` away without replacing the reproducer.

ACCEPTANCE

- The documented `<name>-body` helper spelling works rather than recursing.
- A witness pins it, red-first, at L2 AND under React — the worker established it bites in both.
- displayName and the performance entry id remain readable; check the existing witnesses for those before changing the emitted name.
- If the answer is instead to forbid the spelling, it must REFUSE with a named diagnostic rather than overflowing the stack, and the guide must stop teaching it.

Surface: the h/defview macro expansion in implementation/hicasso/, plus whatever carries displayName/entry-id.
notes:
CLOSED VIA PR #7807, and the worker corrected a premise the bead carried: the emitted body fn's name does NOT feed displayName or the performance entry id. Both key on view-name, the '<ns>/<sym>' string the macro computes on its own line and passes to mint-view! as a value; nothing under implementation/hicasso reads a body fn's JS .name (grepped). So the constraint the bead flagged as the hard part cost nothing — which is what made the strongest option affordable.

THE ANSWER CHOSEN: the emitted fn is ANONYMOUS, (fn ~argv ~@body). Not a gensym and not a reserved prefix — those make the collision improbable, anonymity makes it UNREPRESENTABLE. A fn with no name has nothing to shadow with, so there is no reserved spelling to document and nothing a later edit can reintroduce by accident. It also needs no new :rf.error/* id, hence no spec/009 co-edit and no race with rf2-hic-021. Refusing the spelling was the alternative and was declined: the spelling is correct Clojure and the guide teaches helper extraction throughout.

RED-FIRST, both levels: two witnesses written before the macro changed, both RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded — one at L2, one through a real react-dom/server render of a boundary under mount/provider, so the collision is pinned under React too, not at L2 alone. Both controls stayed green either side, isolating the collision.

Also: the rf2-kjf5 reproducer (greeting in test_kit_cljs_test.cljs) is now RENDERED rather than merely declared, so it pins the fixed behaviour instead of sitting inert; and hmr_remount_cljs_test.cljs's namespace docstring, which documented the old expansion, was corrected. Declined to touch the freehand bench donor carrying the same expression — its frozen-sources row is retired and churning the measured tree to fix a package defect costs the one thing that tree provides.
close_reason: PR #7807 merged (8cc6c9fae).
