title: hic: the hydration adoption window is page-global, so a second root's mismatch is never emitted
description:
MEASURED BY THE rf2-hic-012 WORKER (PR #7751), not inferred. It reported rather than fixed because impl/roots.cljs is runtime source and its dispatch fenced that with an explicit STOP.

THE DEFECT. The hydration adoption window is PAGE-GLOBAL, not root-scoped. impl/roots.cljs holds ONE boolean for the whole page and the mismatch emit is gated on it. With two overlapping hydrating roots, root A's closer shuts the window before root B's mismatch reports.

THE MEASUREMENT: two overlapping hydrating roots produce TWO React "Hydration failed" complaints but only ONE :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch. Root B's mismatch is invisible to everything reading the instrumentation stream.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS TONIGHT'S OTHER TWO SILENCED DIAGNOSTICS and should be read alongside them: rf2-x874 (a lowered callback silently writes a successor frame when the memo is cold) and the freeze gate that reported zero failures while comparing nothing. In each case the system is quiet when it should be loud, and quiet reads as healthy.

WHY IT SURVIVED. The worker demonstrated directly that value-level assertions cannot see it: replacing root B's hydrate-root! with root! reddened ONLY the node-identity expando while every text assertion stayed green. A DOM-level or text-level witness will report success on a discarded adoption. Any fix must be witnessed at the instrumentation layer, the way PR #7751 does it.

THE FIX touches impl/roots.cljs and impl/mount.cljs, and probably impl/presence_react.cljs. It is runtime source, so it needs the operator's word before dispatch — this is the second bead tonight blocked on that same fence (see rf2-x874).

ALREADY DONE FOR YOU, so the next worker does not redo it: PR #7751's two affected assertions carry IN-FILE instructions describing exactly what each becomes once root-scoping lands. Read those before designing anything.

NOTE ON PROVENANCE: rf2-hic-012's deliverable 3 offered two branches — root-scope the window, OR justify each remaining global in writing feeding rf2-hic-017. The worker took the second branch and made the justification a MEASUREMENT rather than an assertion, which is why this bead can state a defect instead of a suspicion. Both branches remain available to the operator; scoping is the stronger answer but the written justification is already banked.

GATES for the fix: the browser lane PR #7751 established (9 tests / 71 assertions), the hicasso node suite, the freeze gate, and sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full. Run each gate ALONE and echo $? to its own file — never append a filter to a gate's command line.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): OPTION A — AUTHORIZE ROOT-SCOPING NOW. Make the hydration adoption window (and mismatch emission) root-local; the runtime-source fence on impl/roots.cljs, impl/mount.cljs, impl/presence_react.cljs is lifted for this repair. Option B (keep the banked written justification) rejected: the kernel checkpoint rf2-hic-019 would have to accept a justified global whose MEASURED behavior is a silenced diagnostic, contradicting the trust register hydration-isolation row's own required contract (independent roots cannot suppress one another's complaints) — that signs a known-broken multi-root story into the kernel. Option C (hold) rejected: Wave B would build above a known silent-failure path. WHY: dossier and Codex recommendations independently converged on A; the measurement (PR #7751, MERGED 2026-08-09) removed all doubt — two overlapping hydrating roots produce TWO React "Hydration failed" complaints but only ONE :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch (root A's closer shuts the page-global window; root B's mismatch is silently discarded, so Xray/tests/future SSR witnesses see a healthy root that failed hydration); Codex verified the defect is BROADER than one missing trace — impl/presence_react.cljs is a second reader of the global, so while any root hydrates, a presence component in an UNRELATED ordinary root is also told it is adopting; the global can suppress a legitimate enter transition or let one root end another root's adoption behavior. Correctness currently depends on the relative ordering of commits, passive effects, presence renders, and recoverable-error callbacks across otherwise-independent roots; React's per-root API (onRecoverableError is an option of an individual hydrateRoot; independently configured roots on one page are supported) gives no reason to treat page-wide ordering as an application invariant. Correctness fix, no new application-facing concept; common SPA path pays nothing; keeping the global saves a tiny root-local object at the cost of diagnostics whose silence cannot be trusted.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE: FIX SURFACE: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/roots.cljs (allocates ONE private JS object at module load; its no-argument open/close/read functions all address that singleton), impl/mount.cljs (opens the singleton for every hydrate-root!; every hydrated root mounts a closer that closes the singleton; every root installs the same hydration-reporter consulting the singleton rather than state belonging to its React root), and impl/presence_react.cljs (second reader). IN-FILE INSTRUCTIONS: PR #7751's two affected assertions carry in-file instructions describing exactly what each becomes once root-scoping lands — read those FIRST; the design is half done. PRIOR ART IN-REPO (established local pattern, not a speculative subsystem): the native substrate creates #js {:adopting true} per root and closes over it in the reporter (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs); Freehand does the same while also closing over root-id (implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/root.cljs). REPAIR SHAPE (Codex, adopted): one small mutable adoption ref per hydrate-root! call, kept internal. (1) Mint the ref before constructing the root element and reporter; store it on the opaque root handle so every later render! preserves the same root wrapper. (2) Make hydration-reporter a builder closing over that ref; it emits only while THAT root's ref is open, then always delegates to the existing default reporter — do not weaken fail-open. (3) Pass the same ref to that root's closer; close idempotently after the hydration commit, on explicit unmount, and on synchronous hydration-construction failure. (4) Put the ref in a narrow React context around the hydrated app subtree; presence reads that context and treats a missing value as closed — cost is one provider per hydrated root and one context read only in the optional presence component; ordinary roots and ordinary Hicasso boundaries acquire NO object, provider, hook, registry lookup, or branch. (5) When the server entry is promoted into the product, give each render/request its own ref and provider; do not retain the module flag as a separate server mechanism. (6) Remove the global adoption close from runtime reset — a reset must not change the lifecycle state of a sibling root; root teardown owns root state. REJECTED SHAPES: page-global reference count (keeps B's window open when A commits, but a later recoverable error from already-committed A would then be falsely labelled a hydration mismatch; still leaks adoption semantics into presence components outside both hydrating subtrees — converts one interference bug into another); registry keyed by frame (multiple roots may intentionally share a frame); module registry keyed by container (recreates React context badly, adds cleanup risk). SUPPRESSION vs ATTRIBUTION: suppression is fixable NOW without the final public root API; attribution should close over the stable root identity selected by the root-lifecycle work and include it in the trace (as Freehand does). Do NOT use frame-kw as a substitute for root identity, and do NOT delay the local-state repair to settle the public spelling. WITNESS-LAYER REQUIREMENT: value/DOM-level witnesses provably CANNOT see this — the hic-012 worker showed replacing root B's hydrate-root! with a plain root! reddened ONLY the node-identity expando while every text assertion stayed green; a DOM-level witness reports success on a discarded adoption. The witness must live at the instrumentation layer, as PR #7751's does (9 tests / 71 assertions).

FENCES: touch only implementation/hicasso impl/roots.cljs, impl/mount.cljs, impl/presence_react.cljs plus the PR #7751 browser-lane tests (including the two in-file-instructed assertion updates); no spec/* hot-zone files, no facade export changes, no new public API in this PR. Parallel-safe with rf2-x874 (different files: roots/mount vs frames — no fence collision).

WITNESSES (repair complete when these focused browser witnesses pass AND their sabotage controls red): (1) two overlapping divergent hydrations yield two React complaints AND two framework mismatch events; reusing one ref for both roots must make it red. (2) Root A completes while root B remains adopting; an artificial later recoverable error on A does NOT emit a hydration mismatch while B's genuine mismatch still does — this is the witness that rules out a global counter. (3) Presence isolation: a hydrated root is born present, an ordinary sibling root still gets its enter phase, and closing either root cannot change the other; same row covers teardown-before-passive-effect so no open ref survives its root. (4) Once public root identity lands, each emitted event names the correct root (follow-up wiring, not a blocker for this repair); if a server entry ships, add two independently scoped server renders as the request-isolation witness. GATES: the browser lane PR #7751 established, the hicasso node suite, the freeze gate, and sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full — each gate run ALONE and FOREGROUND to completion, echo $? to its own file, never append a filter to a gate's command line. Payoff: trust register hydration-isolation row closes properly; rf2-hic-046 per-surface SSR witnesses get a truthful stream; React-compat contract (per-root error attribution, identifierPrefix isolation) becomes implementable.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7756 (2026-08-10 AUSEST) — client/runtime root-scoping PASS; exact repair owner complete.

Completeness: the three blocking witnesses land at the instrumentation layer: two genuinely overlapping divergent hydrations yield two React complaints and two framework events; the direct real-door row distinguishes a completed root's later recovery from a sibling's live mismatch and rules out both global boolean and global count; the presence row covers hydrated-born-present, an ordinary sibling's enter phase, independent close, and teardown-before-effect. The explicitly deferred root-id attribution and real server/request matrix already belong to rf2-hic-046 and were never blockers for this repair.

Correctness: independently traced one minted window object from hydrate-root! into the handle, hydration reporter, closer, and subtree context. Nil is closed; ordinary roots allocate/install nothing; one closer and unmount can close only their own window; render! preserves the hydrated root shape; collector reset has no cross-root close. This matches the established substrate pattern and preserves unconditional recoverable-error delegation. No stale zero-arity Hicasso callers remain.

Implementation quality: the six-file diff is coherent and minimal; collector.cljs is necessary because it owned the forbidden global reset call, and the remaining changes are the three runtime surfaces plus focused tests/support. Merged-tree reruns pass: Hicasso Node 46 tests / 188 assertions, browser 1148 / 7099, freeze 7/7, and git diff --check, all exit 0. The two recorded sabotages discriminate the global reporter and page-wide presence reader.

Non-blocking residual transferred to exact owner rf2-hic-046, not duplicated: roots.cljs:54 and presence_react.cljs:130 speak in present tense as if a server request already installs this provider, but the only product-source with-adoption caller is the client hydrate tree. The presence witness obtains its supposed server bytes by settling an ordinary client root rather than react-dom/server, so it does not prove the future per-surface SSR/request contract. That does not invalidate the measured client isolation repair.

Audit traced the per-root reporter/closer/context ownership, verified the required instrumentation and presence witnesses, and reran Node, browser, freeze, and diff gates green. The already-deferred real-server/request matrix remains on exact owner rf2-hic-046.

title: hic: a lowered callback silently writes a same-public-id SUCCESSOR frame whenever the frame-ops memo is cold
description:
FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, not inspection, by the rf2-hic-013 worker (PR #7749, 9 tests / 57 assertions green). It reported rather than fixed because impl/frames.cljs was fenced to a sibling worker. The witnesses that prove it are landing in that PR; this bead is the repair.

THE DEFECT. A lowered callback closes over the frame KEYWORD and resolves its bundle when it FIRES. So where a delayed callback lands depends on the frame-ops memo's warmth at that instant, not on the incarnation the callback was lowered under. After a same-public-id frame is torn down and a successor mounts:

  WARM memo  -> the write is refused. CORRECT BY ACCIDENT: it is the stale memo doing it, not any check.
  COLD memo  -> THE CALLBACK SILENTLY WRITES THE SUCCESSOR'S app-db. No error is emitted.

COLD IS THE ORDINARY CASE — a boundary that rendered but that nobody clicked before the teardown. So the common path is the broken one and the rare path only looks correct.

WHY "EXACT EVICTION ON DESTRUCTION" IS PROVABLY THE WRONG FIX. rf2-hic-013's own deliverable 3 names two candidate remedies: incarnation-keyed bundles, or exact eviction. Eviction was MEASURED and it makes things worse — it converts the single accidentally-correct branch (warm) into the broken one, making the silent successor-write UNIVERSAL. Do not implement it. Note also that forget-frame-ops!, the only eviction door that exists, has exactly ONE caller: reset-runtime!, a test fixture.

THE MEASURED FIX: pin the incarnation into the closure at mint time. The worker measured this repairing BOTH branches. It requires impl/frames.cljs.

WHY THE DOM CANNOT SEE IT, which is why this survived until now. The read path is address-directed and the write path is incarnation-pinned, so after a reincarnation the runtime READS the successor correctly while refusing to WRITE it — perfect markup above dead controls. And commit-basis ties (1 -> 1), so snapshot-of ties and React schedules no re-render; the repair arrives a macrotask later (snapshot 1 -> 2, one notification). A DOM assertion inside that window blames its own timing; after it, it reports green. Any fix must be witnessed at the same layer PR #7749 used, not through rendered output.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE WITNESSES. PR #7749 ships two shipped negative controls and six run controls (NC1 de-memoise frame-ops, NC2 incarnation-sensitive commit-basis, NC3 always-dispose, NC4 never-dispose, NC5 remove the macrotask deferral, NC6 apply the candidate remedy). NC6 in particular predicts exactly which branches a correct fix flips — treat a mismatch against NC6 as evidence your fix is wrong, not that the control is stale.

SECOND, SEPARATE ITEM RECORDED BY THE SAME WORKER, not part of this repair: React law 3 requires a render/commit tear to be "corrected before visible paint". The measured correction here is MACROTASK-DEFERRED, which carries no such ordering guarantee. That is a spec-conformance question about the correction path itself and wants its own ruling; do not silently resolve it inside this fix.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7749 (2026-08-10; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). Independent merged-tree rerun is green, but the witness proves this exact owner remains actionable: a cold or evicted predecessor-era lowered callback silently writes the successor, while a warm stale memo can refuse the live successor current route. The suite encodes the defect as a green test intentionally expected to fail when fixed, so remediation must replace or invert that test. Close only when retained callbacks always refuse, current callbacks route, memo and closure incarnation semantics are repaired together, and the defect test becomes a positive contract.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): APPROVE Option A now — pin the frame incarnation into the lowered callback at mint time. Runtime-source edit AUTHORIZED, scoped to impl/frames.cljs PLUS the smallest corresponding change in impl/collector.cljs. Eviction-on-destruction stays REJECTED (measured worse: converts the accidentally-correct warm branch into the broken one, making the silent successor-write universal). Holding for more design rejected: P1 silent corruption in the kernel with Wave B building on top. WHY THE SCOPE ADDS collector.cljs (verified in source 2026-08-10, correcting the frames.cljs-only framing): the late-binding closure is minted in collector.cljs frame-dispatch — (fn dispatch-for-frame [event] (dispatch! frame-kw event)) memoised into frames/!frame-dispatch under the bare public keyword (collector.cljs ~501) — so frames.cljs alone cannot carry the fix. Fence the rest of the runtime. PR #7749 (witnesses) is MERGED 2026-08-09.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (preserves dossier + Codex analysis; dossier file deleted after this):
(1) MECHANISM — use core's existing capture-frame authority; do NOT invent a new incarnation fence and do NOT add a core late-bind hook. capture-frame called while a frame is LIVE pins that exact incarnation and, after supersession, recovers with :rf.error/frame-destroyed (recover-but-emit, never throw; core.cljc ~1266/1351). A capture made while the id is ABSENT is deliberately address-directed — so Hicasso must acquire the handle during render of the live frame, never at fire time.
(2) CONTRACT — a) at frame-dispatch lookup during render, resolve the currently live incarnation and obtain its rf/capture-frame bundle; b) memoise the ambient closure keyed by that incarnation/bundle identity; the closure calls the CAPTURED bundle's :dispatch-sync inside the existing with-commit window — it must never call dispatch! with the bare frame keyword and resolve again later; c) repeated renders within one incarnation return the identical closure with zero allocation on hit; when the same public id names a new incarnation, the lookup replaces the memo row and returns a fresh closure pinned to the successor; a retained predecessor closure keeps the predecessor bundle and is refused by core; d) treat !frame-ops and !frame-dispatch as ONE logical record — one per-id entry {incarnation, core bundle, batched dispatch closure} is the clearest shape; if two atoms remain, their hit/miss tests must be coupled by exact token/bundle identity so they can never describe different incarnations; e) correctness must NOT depend on a destruction hook — lazy incarnation-mismatch replacement of the one cached row; forget-frame-ops! remains reset/hygiene only (sole runtime caller is the whole-runtime reset, collector.cljs ~1828; other callers are test fixtures).
(3) BOTH HALVES TOGETHER — cold memo: retained predecessor callback silently writes the successor's app-db; warm memo: a freshly minted successor callback is refused by the stale bundle (perfect markup above dead controls). Cache warmth merely chooses between the two failures; safety of retained callbacks and liveness of successor callbacks are one repair, not two.
(4) WHY THE DOM CANNOT WITNESS IT — read path is address-directed (reads successor correctly) while the broken write path refuses; commit-basis ties so React schedules no re-render and the repair arrives one macrotask later, making DOM assertions blame their own timing. Witness at the instrumentation layer PR #7749 used, never through rendered output.
(5) PERF — preserve one shared handler identity per live frame incarnation; the extra live-token comparison lands on the once-per-body cache lookup, not on every event position or event. Run the existing boundary-shell/per-render benchmark; no material regression. Do NOT build a generalized callback-lifecycle subsystem for this bug.

FENCES: do NOT touch the macrotask deferral / read-repair timing — React law 3 "corrected before visible paint" is rf2-2l17's separate ruling; do not silently resolve or alter it inside this fix. Eviction must not be implemented. No public API additions. Runtime edits confined to impl/frames.cljs + impl/collector.cljs. Do not weaken PR #7749's witnesses or its negative controls NC1-NC6.

WITNESSES (the merged-PR audit note above requires the defect-recording green test be replaced/inverted into a positive contract): a) a callback minted under incarnation A refuses after A is destroyed in cold, warm, AND explicitly-reset cache postures; leaves B's app-db untouched; emits exactly one production-surviving :rf.error/frame-destroyed with correct frame and event identity; b) a callback freshly minted under B dispatches successfully in each posture — including the previously broken warm case — with no refusal; c) callback identity is stable across repeated renders of A, changes from A to B, and is stable across repeated renders of B; d) h/fn returning an intent, a plain intent vector, a key-map branch, and a handler minted inside a declared render callback all inherit the same pinned ambient dispatch (one table-driven test — the paths share the mechanism); e) reset still empties the memo inventory; focused Hicasso suite green; f) negative control: restore late keyword resolution and it must reproduce BOTH the cold predecessor-write and the warm successor-refusal (a test proving only stale-callback inertness is incomplete — an all-controls-dead cache would also pass it); g) NC6 rule: PR #7749's NC6 predicts exactly which branches a correct fix flips — treat any mismatch against NC6 as evidence the FIX is wrong, not that the control is stale.

FOLLOW-UP (separate bead, does not gate this repair): bounded seam audit of the two direct collector/dispatch! callers (h/boundary error reporting; the internal mount witness) and of ::h/navigate, which bypasses the ambient dispatcher and delegates an explicitly address-directed frame keyword to routing. Change those only if a retained-operation witness demonstrates the same revival.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7759 (2026-08-10 AUSEST; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). The functional repair is correct: one per-id row now couples the live incarnation token, captured core bundle, and closure over that bundle; same-incarnation hits retain identity, a successor lazily replaces the row, and retained predecessor callbacks are refused by core while fresh successor callbacks route. Independent merged-tree evidence is green: focused Hicasso 50 tests / 236 assertions; browser 1148 / 7100; controlled-input Chromium/Firefox/WebKit 55 checks each; freeze 7/7. The shipped negative control reconstructs both old failures.

KEEP THIS EXACT OWNER OPEN for the small but real completion sweep the PR missed. Runtime/test documentation still describes two memo tables or the old live defect (collector.cljs:23, frozen-sources.edn:55, roots_frames_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs:14, hmr_registry_cljs_test.cljs:332). Also `git diff --check bb38d87..c996347` exits 2 for a new blank line at EOF in reincarnation_routing_cljs_test.cljs. Correct those claims/remove the blank EOF, then this technical owner can close; no duplicate Bead.

description:
# Wire implementation/hicasso into the CI changed-surface classifier

**Found by**: rf2-hic-001, which created the artefact but is fenced out of `.github/`.
**Surface**: `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`
(both HOT ZONE — sequence, do not parallel).

## The hole

TESTING.md §Changed-surface classifier states the rule directly:

> **Adding a new artefact directory needs two matching changes**: a classifier rule (which
> outputs the path lights) and a workflow gate whose `if:` reads them. Either side missing is
> a silent hole — code can land that mutates a surface no PR-time job watches.

`implementation/hicasso/*` is in neither. Observed rather than inferred: on the rf2-hic-001
branch `sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --plan` reports `PLAN docs=false jvm=false node=true`, and
`node=true` only because that diff also touches `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`. A
hicasso-ONLY diff may light nothing at all.

## What to add

- A classifier case for `implementation/hicasso/*`. Today the artefact has no JVM suite (the
  runtime requires React, so every suite is CLJS), so the light that matters is
  `cljs_node_test`. Set only the outputs whose jobs the artefact's tests actually exercise —
  TESTING.md warns that coarse rules clutter the matrix with `skipping` entries.
- Whatever workflow `if:` reads it. The package's suites ride the always-on `:node-test`
  build (`re-frame.hicasso.smoke-cljs-test` matches its `cljs-test$` regexp) and the focused
  `:node-test-hicasso` build rf2-hic-001 added.
- Do NOT add `implementation/hicasso` to `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`'s roster while
  the artefact has no JVM suite: `scripts/check_jvm_lane_rosters.py` fails both ways, so a
  roster entry without a required job is its own red.

## Also decide

`scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py` requires every `test:*` npm script to be reachable from a
workflow or carry a declared disposition. rf2-hic-001 deliberately added NO npm script — the
freeze gate is `python implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py` and is currently run by
hand. Give it a scheduled home: either an npm `test:hicasso` wrapper reached from a workflow,
or a step in the fast-PR spine, or a declared disposition.

## Acceptance

- A hicasso-only diff lights the surfaces whose jobs actually cover it, demonstrated with
  `sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh --plan` on such a diff.
- `python scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py --verbose` and `python scripts/check_jvm_lane_rosters.py`
  stay green.
- `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_freeze.py` runs somewhere on a schedule.

Independent classification gives a representative DOM test exactly cljs_node_test + cljs_browser + hicasso_controlled, and all 315 classifier tests pass. PR #7812 adds 33 lines to implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/error_source_coord_elision_prod_test.cljs. That namespace explicitly matches :browser-test-prod-elision's `-elision-prod-test$` selector and says the ordinary node/browser builds do not reach it. The new hostile-payload witness is load-bearing: the PR's mutation proof records that check_source_coord_elision.cjs still passed under the regression, so only this behavioural production row caught it.

Yet `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` still says Hicasso has no `-elision-prod-test$` namespace and leaves cljs_prod=false; its scope test pins that stale premise. CLOSED AS VERIFIED-DUPLICATE. Both halves the bead asked for now exist on main. Checked by grep before dispatching, not inferred:

CLASSIFIER HALF — .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh has an `implementation/hicasso/*)` case arm (~line 1116) setting cljs_node_test=true, and its own commentary records exactly this bead's finding: "The package landed with no case here at all, so a hicasso-ONLY diff..." It also declares `hicasso_controlled` (line 98) and `hicasso_hmr` (line 104, added by rf2-hic-015), both set for hicasso diffs.

GATE HALF — .github/workflows/test.yml reads both outputs (lines 93-94) and gates two jobs on them: the controlled-input matrix (line 1371, `if: ... hicasso_controlled == 'true'`) and the HMR contract (line 1474, `if: ... hicasso_hmr == 'true'`). The invariants gate runs at line 2871 (`npm run test:hicasso-invariants`, renamed from test:hicasso-freeze by PR #7813).

AND THE HOLE IS NOW CLOSED MORE STRONGLY THAN THE BEAD ASKED. rf2-hic-021's audit found that a predicate-gated job is only correct until the thing it guards grows one more input, and nothing makes anyone revisit the predicate. So PR #7813 added `hicasso-complaint-catalogue` as an UNCONDITIONAL job (line 906, listed in all-required-passed at line 5817) — no `needs:`, no `if:` — which covers every file family it reads by construction. That is a better answer than another classifier arm to the same question.

WHICH BEADS DID IT: rf2-hic-015 (the HMR arm, its classifier edge and the scheduling), rf2-hic-016 (the controlled-input job), rf2-hic-021 / PR #7813 (the unconditional catalogue job and the invariants rename). None of them cited this bead, which is why it stayed open — worth noting as the ordinary way a duplicate survives: the work lands under whichever bead the worker was holding.

If a future artefact directory lands with neither half, TESTING.md's rule still stands and check_gate_scheduling.py is the instrument that would catch it — it currently reports 0 declared holes.

notes:
OPERATOR AUTHORISATION (2026-08-10 ~20:55 AUSEST, Mike, in session) — RUN THIS WHEN THE MACHINE IS QUIET.

Mike's words: "if you get to no dispatchable background agents, then the machine is quiet
and you can run measurement beads."

SO THE GATE IS NO LONGER 'ask the operator'. It is a measurable condition:
  when the dispatchable queue is exhausted and NO background worker is live,
  the machine is quiet and this measurement bead may be dispatched.

WHY THE CONDITION MATTERS, and it is the whole reason this bead was held all session: a
measurement window run against concurrent workers measures the CONTENTION, not the code.
Five or six shadow-cljs spines and a Chromium/Firefox/WebKit browser lane share this one
machine. Shape 6 says it in terms — "one run at a time, never concurrent" — and concurrency
is precisely the interference the window exists to exclude.

DISPATCH IT AS SHAPE 6, NOT SHAPE 1. The inversion is the whole shape:
  - THE CONTROLS ARBITRATE, NOT THE WORKER'S JUDGEMENT ABOUT THE BOX. A worker asked whether
    its machine was quiet enough will always find a reason it was. If a control fails, or the
    arm-order guard exits 2 (a refusal, deliberately not a plain failure), the run REFUSES and
    the worker reports the refusal without weighing it against how the box felt.
  - A REFUSAL IS A DELIVERABLE. Two of three window beads in one day came back as refusals and
    both were correct. If everything refuses, the window succeeded: you now know the rig cannot
    see what you hoped, which is what it was dispatched to find out. Say this in the brief or
    the worker reads its own refusal as failure and hunts for a way to turn it green.
  - NEVER 'fix' a refusal by loosening a gate. Widening a threshold to admit today's run
    retro-admits the failure the gate was built for.
  - DO NOT IMPROVE THE RIG MID-WINDOW. No new instrument, no extra rungs, no third estimator,
    however obvious. File the improvement and run it as its own window.
  - DO NOT RESTATE A PUBLISHED FIGURE ON THIN EVIDENCE. A worker holding four runs all reading
    below both published figures recorded them WITHOUT publishing. That was right.
  - VERIFY THE BOX WITH REAL COUNTERS. `Win32_Processor.LoadPercentage` read 93% while the true
    value was 11%. Use `Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time'` and
    `'\System\Processor Queue Length'` — QUEUE LENGTH IS THE DECISIVE NUMBER, because it says
    whether anything is actually waiting for a core, which is the only thing the window cares
    about.
  - ONE RUN AT A TIME. Two runs the worker believes independent still are not.

AND THE MAYOR'S OWN PRECONDITION: verify quiet before dispatching, do not infer it. `git
worktree list` under the re-frame2-worktrees sibling must show no live worker, and the ready
queue must be exhausted of everything else. If a worker reports mid-window, do NOT dispatch
another — the window owns the machine until it finishes or refuses.

The two measurement beads are rf2-hic-006 (named reference profiles + pinned baselines) and
rf2-hic-029 (retaining-host callback identity: the experiment and the verdict). They are a
SERIAL LANE OF TWO: they must not run concurrently with each other either. rf2-hic-006 first —
it pins the baselines every later gate anchors to.

MAYOR — WORK EXISTS AND IS RECOVERABLE, 2026-08-12 00:34. Read this before dispatching anyone at this bead.

A WITNESS HAS ALREADY BEEN BUILT AND PUSHED. Branch `worker/cbident-hic029`, commit `5adb879e10`, subject "test(hicasso): the retaining-host callback-identity witness (rf2-hic-029)". It adds 620 lines at implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/retaining_host_callbacks_dom_cljs_test.cljs. That commit is ON ORIGIN, so nothing is at risk.

DO NOT READ ITS DIFF AGAINST MAIN AS A DELETION. `git diff origin/main origin/worker/cbident-hic029` reports docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md as -410 lines. That is a STALE BASE, not a deletion: the worker branched before PR #7935 landed that file, and the diff shows main's newer file as absent on the branch side. The worker never touched budgets.md. A rebase merge replays only its own commit, so the file survives. I checked this precisely because a 410-line deletion in a measurement worker's diff must never be waved through.

THE WORKER HAS BEEN SILENT FOR 99 MINUTES and I have not reaped it. Evidence, so the next reader does not have to re-derive it: 1 commit, pushed; worktree clean (no uncommitted WIP); task output file 0 bytes, untouched since 22:55; a status query queued and never delivered, which means it has taken no tool round since; and THIS BEAD IS STILL OPEN AND WAS NEVER MARKED in_progress. So nothing is stranded in the tracker and there is no WIP to recover.

WHY NO REAP: only an agent's own completion report authorises one, and a backgrounded browser-lane gate is indistinguishable from this at 99 minutes. The entire cost of waiting is a stale directory. Do not treat a still commit count or a quiet log as a death certificate.

IF THIS BEAD IS RE-DISPATCHED, START FROM THAT COMMIT rather than from scratch. Check out `worker/cbident-hic029`, rebase onto current main, and READ THE WITNESS BEFORE CHANGING IT — 620 lines is a substantial experiment and re-deriving it wastes the work and risks a different rig. Then finish what it did not: no PR was opened, so the gates were either mid-run or never run.

WHAT THE BRIEF REQUIRED, unchanged and still binding:
  - ONE MEASUREMENT AT A TIME; never background a gate and start another. The rig does not change mid-window.
  - The BROWSER lane decides a DOM measurement; the node lane's DOM assertions degrade to stated skips.
  - A verdict of "no effect" or "not stably measurable" is a COMPLETE deliverable. Do not tune the experiment until it produces a finding.
  - Quote the CAPTURED exit code; the harness misreported a captured 1 as exit 0 thirteen times on 2026-08-11.

DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-12, operator-overturnable):
Recorded 2026-08-12 05:15 AUSEST after full verification of the dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-hic-029.stable-event-verdict.md, now deleted) against tracker, branch, PR and spec.

RULING. Option A stands and its condition is MET, not merely promised: fresh-per-render is SUFFICIENT; NO stable-event primitive is admitted for the interpreted tier. The verdict record docs/design/hicasso/product/callback-identity-verdict.md (commit aa2a7c2705 on worker/cbident-hic029, PR #7936) is RATIFIED as written, and this bead's CLOSED state stands. The mayor's no-reap call is vindicated: the 99-minute silence was a live gate, not a death; reaping would have raced a live worker on its own branch.

MEASURED CONDITION, VERIFIED FROM PR #7936. Every grid row landed exactly as coded: four bail rows read 1 (:absent, :plain-fn, :handler, :native-stable), five churn rows read 6 (:intent-vector, :hfn-inline, :hfn-hoisted, :key-map, :native-churn); safety sections (retention across renders, loud :rf.error/frame-destroyed refusal after teardown, same-public-id reincarnation isolation, delayed fire) and the sabotage control (unpinned rf/capture-frame DOES write the successor) all behaved per contract; ordinary path = 1 boundary body per tick with or without a retaining host. Captured exit codes, not harness summaries.

VOID CONDITION (exact). The ruling is voidable until PR #7936's browser lane lands green. If, on the green re-run after the rf2-d3tc fix, ANY witness grid row or safety/sabotage section lands off the recorded values -- any bail row above 1, any churn row not 6, any safety row off-contract -- the ruling is VOID and the question returns to the operator with the evidence attached. The lane's current red does NOT fire it: three captured-exit-code runs pin the red to a neighbour suite's own defect (reincarnation-paint W1/W2 attach .catch after the .then that calls done, and their cleanup outlives their own test -- rf2-d3tc; witness aside, lane exit 0 with 1284 tests / 7971 assertions / 0 failures; witness present, red with EITHER teardown door, ruling teardown out), not to any witness assertion. A red SAFETY row, if one ever appears, additionally files as a kernel bug against the shipped incarnation-pinning contract and is repaired THERE -- it voids the verdict record until fixed but never by itself argues for a new primitive.

WHY. (1) The safe stable spelling already ships at the native tier: n/use-frame + React's own useCallback -- measured identity-stable AND dispatching (the row that decides), incarnation-pinned by the same mechanism rf2-x874 installed, so safe across abandonment, reincarnation and teardown with zero new surface. The escape for a memo-critical vendor host is a tier drop for that one island, no new API. (2) The ordinary path pays zero: one tick runs one boundary body whether or not a retaining host is on the page; the incarnation pin is a memo row acquired once per incarnation. (3) Materiality: the corpus census found zero foreign components across 85 idiomatic files, and across every application-shaped Hicasso source in-repo the number of callbacks handed to a memoized foreign child is zero. Real but rare, with a shipped answer. (4) :hfn-hoisted = 6 is load-bearing the other way -- hoisting does not help, so the churn is the lowering's, not an authoring mistake; the problem is real, which is why the verdict is a recorded ruling, not a shrug. (5) A new interpreted-tier primitive would be a second mechanism for a solved problem, carrying precisely the retirement/reincarnation hazards the witness's sections 4-6 police, at the tier with the least machinery to police them -- the over-engineering the posture rejects. (6) Spec 4.1's judgment word is now bound: a problem is MATERIAL only when the shipped surface offers no safe spelling for it.

CODEX ADVISORY ADJUDICATION (second-model, weighed on merits). ADOPTED: the sharper reopen boundary -- a two-part conjunction, a real retaining vendor workflow demonstrating material user-visible cost AND the native-island spelling shown materially worse or unusable there; the verdict record's "What would reopen this" clause is that test's operational form. ADOPTED: honest framing -- the grid measures identity behaviour as body-run counts, not latency or heap; a vendor body run's price is a fact about somebody else's code; the record states this verbatim as a known limit. ADOPTED: red-safety-row means repair the existing contract, never new API (with the clarification above that it still voids the record until repaired). ADOPTED (contingency): if reopen evidence ever arrives, the path is an opt-in defhost-edge contract with NO universal per-boundary proxy table, admitted only behind abandonment, reincarnation, delayed-teardown, cleanup and ordinary-path-cost witnesses -- the donor implementation needed candidate/committed callback tables and exact cleanup to provide those laws, which is the cost scale any future proposal must beat. OVERTAKEN, not adopted: "need not wait for the grid's numbers" -- the numbers now exist, and as posture the dossier's conditional discipline was the better form, since spec 4.1's standing rule demands a demonstration. NOTHING REJECTED on the merits.

DOSSIER ANALYSIS PRESERVED (options and consequences, in substance). Option A -- pre-rule conditional on green, no primitive: wins were one dispatch finishes the bead and "material" gets bound to something reusable; cost was ruling before numbers, protected by the void structure. TAKEN, and the condition has since been met. Option B -- hold until measurement lands: honest but bought nothing A's conditional did not already protect, at the price of one more operator round-trip on Checkpoint 1's critical path. NOT NEEDED -- events delivered B's evidence inside A's structure. Option C -- admit the primitive now: rejected; API surface against the standing rule's "only if" and the risk row's "only when required", no demonstrated material need (census zero), and the primitive would carry exactly the hazards the witness polices, at the wrong tier. The sharp fact the witness surfaced, worth keeping: at the interpreted tier no carrier is both identity-stable and dispatching -- the stable ones are inert (:plain-fn unmarked, :handler return-ignored) and the dispatching ones churn, because the per-render wrapper IS the frame pin; the one both-stable-and-dispatching spelling lives at the native tier, assembled from surface that already ships. Hicasso's own boundaries never had the problem (boundary-props= compares with CLJS =, intents are data) -- the question exists only at a foreign React.memo edge.

Unblock = rf2-d3tc (OPEN, P2, critical path for this PR and for Checkpoint 1's row-7 discharge): fix direction already on that bead -- chain reincarnation-paint's W1/W2 cleanup BEFORE done so no promise outlives the test that armed it; that file is rf2-hic-013's lane, hence a separate worker and PR, sequenced first; then rebase #7936, re-run the browser lane, verify the witness rows unchanged (this is the void-condition check), merge. (8) Quiet-window discipline (Shape 6, operator authorisation of 2026-08-10) governed the measurement and governs any re-run: controls arbitrate, one run at a time, refusals are deliverables, never loosen a gate to admit a run.

FENCES. No runtime mutation lands under this verdict. # hic-027 — The L3 mounted test facade

**Phase**: tooling lane · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-020

## Deliverables

## Worker notes

notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7822 (2026-08-10; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). REOPEN EXACT OWNER.

WHAT IS SOUND: frame isolation is structural; the public mounted APIs are compact; authored and landed patch identities match; the untouched browser suite independently passed 1177 tests / 7334 assertions.

CORRECTNESS/ERGONOMICS: a temporary browser witness mounted a valid registered Hicasso view whose body contains a plain function child head, a runtime :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head case. React emitted an uncaught page error, but hm/mount! returned a handle instead of propagating the structured runtime refusal. The call left one extra registered frame and one attached body container. That contradicts the close record's claim that malformed form is surfaced by the runtime and gives the programmer neither the promised error data nor a usable cleanup path.

SAME FAILURE CLASS BY INSPECTION: hydrate! allocates its frame, container, handle, and open/standing counters before settlement. Its timeout branch only rejects; it does not unmount, remove the container, close the adoption window, decrement counters, remove the facade-frame entry, or destroy the frame. A synchronous hydrate-root! failure has the same missing rollback shape.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the two residue sabotage rows call hm/residue and manually repair their induced fault, but never finalize the handle with hm/assert-clean!. Since only assert-clean! records the verdict and releases private open/frame bookkeeping, these tests leave process-global facade state behind and prevent the unread-mount reset gate from reaching zero.

BOUNDED REPAIR: make mount/hydrate construction transactional at one seam. Capture and preserve the original runtime ex-info/id, prevent an uncaught browser pageerror, and restore the exact pre-call frame/container/census state on synchronous render failure or hydration timeout. After sabotage cleanup, finalize the handle and assert clean so the facade's own bookkeeping is exercised. Do not add a new error id, lifecycle framework, or generalized resource tracker.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7822 finding ACCEPTED. QUEUED, NOT DISPATCHED — it must sequence behind worker/kitname-0ckh (rf2-0ckh), which currently holds implementation/hicasso/test_kit/** to rename the L2 entry per naming-ledger row 23. The repair lives in test/mounted.cljs, the same tree. Dispatching now would collide.

WHY THE FINDING IS RIGHT AND WORTH THE FOLLOW-UP, in my reading:

The facade's OWN CLOSE RECORD claimed malformed form is surfaced by the runtime. The audit drove it: a valid registered view whose body contains a plain function CHILD head — a genuine :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head case — and hm/mount! RETURNED A HANDLE. React emitted an uncaught page error, and the call left one extra registered frame and one attached body container. So the programmer gets neither the structured error data nor a usable cleanup path, and the claim in the close record was broader than what the code does. That is the ninth instance this session of a claim exceeding what was driven, and this one was in a close reason I wrote.

Note the id is correct here and is NOT the rf2-z5ji case: hicasso-bad-head is a CHILD-POSITION rule, and this is a child head. rf2-z5ji corrected the guide for the ROOT position, where nothing refuses. The two are consistent.

SAME FAILURE CLASS BY INSPECTION, not driven: hydrate! allocates frame, container, handle and open/standing counters BEFORE settlement, and its timeout branch only rejects — it does not unmount, remove the container, close the adoption window, decrement counters, remove the facade-frame entry, or destroy the frame. A synchronous hydrate-root! failure has the same missing-rollback shape. Whoever takes this should DRIVE that path rather than repairing it by inspection, since inspection is what let the mount! case through.

AND THE FACADE'S OWN TESTS DO NOT EXERCISE ITS BOOKKEEPING: the two residue sabotage rows call hm/residue and manually repair their induced fault but never finalize with hm/assert-clean!. Only assert-clean! records the verdict and releases the private open/frame bookkeeping, so those rows leave process-global facade state behind and prevent the unread-mount reset gate from reaching zero. The tests for the cleanliness instrument are themselves unclean.

BOUNDED REPAIR (from the audit, and it is a fence): make mount/hydrate construction TRANSACTIONAL AT ONE SEAM. Preserve the original runtime ex-info and its id, prevent the uncaught browser pageerror, and restore the exact pre-call frame/container/census state on synchronous render failure or hydration timeout. After sabotage cleanup, finalize the handle and assert clean so the facade's own bookkeeping is exercised. DO NOT add a new error id, a lifecycle framework, or a generalized resource tracker.

DISPATCH NOTE: brief it to drive the hydrate! timeout and the synchronous hydrate-root! failure as separate rows, each able to fail for the reason it names — a row that merely observes rejection would pass against the current missing rollback.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7836 — NORMAL SUCCESSFUL TEARDOWN STILL LEAVES THE FACADE'S OWN DOM CONTAINER BEHIND.

The guide now makes `(hm/mount! form)` followed by `hm/unmount!` + `hm/assert-clean!` the canonical L3 recipe. On that exact path, `mount!` creates and appends a fresh `<div>` when no `:container` is supplied (`mounted.cljs:312` / `impl.mount/fresh-container!`), `unmount!` deliberately leaves every container connected, and `assert-clean!` finalizes counters/frame state without detaching it. The residue census does not count DOM nodes, so it reports clean while each copied test accumulates one empty body child.

This belongs to the exact mounted-facade owner, not a new issue. Bounded repair: record whether the facade created the container; after the post-quiescence residue verdict, detach only a facade-owned container. Preserve a caller-supplied `:container` exactly where it is. Fold the same ownership rule into the already-recorded transactional failure rollback. Witness both arms by body-child identity/count; do not add a page-wide scrubber or generic resource tracker.

The namespace correction and async verdict threading in PR #7836 otherwise match the shipped facade. `hm/rerender!` remains a known deliberate naming divergence already owned by open naming-packet rf2-hic-065; do not duplicate or settle it here.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7840 (merged 2026-08-10T20:17:53Z as 1767f46907) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; no duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: the three driven channels are repaired at one small rollback seam. mount! now returns React render refusals to the caller, synchronous hydrate-root! failures reject, adoption timeouts reject after undoing root/container/frame state, and the two sabotage rows finally release their facade bookkeeping. Authored and landed blobs are identical; the four-commit diff check is clean; all 91 PR checks are non-failing. rf2-cw7p's tombstone prose correction is complete.

RESIDUAL 1 — THE ALREADY-RECORDED #7836 SUCCESS-PATH LEAK WAS RECLOSED WITHOUT BEING FIXED. supplied? is used only by abandon!. A successful default mount still appends a fresh body div, handle-for records no ownership bit, unmount! deliberately leaves every container connected, and assert-clean! reports clean then finalises without detaching it. The canonical mount → unmount! → assert-clean! recipe therefore accumulates one empty facade-owned body node per test. Preserve caller containers, but remove a facade-created one after its residue verdict. This is the existing #7836 note on this owner, not new scope.

RESIDUAL 2 — ASYNC HYDRATION RENDER REFUSALS STILL MISS THE DELIVERY CONTRACT. The new test itself states that a body throwing during adoption reports an uncaught window error through a different channel, but no row drives it. mount! installs onUncaughtError; hydrate! delegates to impl.mount/hydrate-root!, whose options install only onRecoverableError. A valid view whose body raises the same :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head during hydration therefore reports globally, leaves the adoption window open until the budget expires, and rejects later with a generic timeout instead of the runtime's structured refusal. That contradicts this namespace's claim that hydrate! delivers render refusals as data and makes a programmer wait three seconds for the wrong error.

BOUNDED REPAIR: carry one facade-container ownership bit through a successful handle and detach only that node after the cleanliness verdict. Add one hydration row using the existing bad-body witness and capture the root's onUncaughtError so hydrate! rolls back and promptly rejects with the original ex-info, while preserving the existing recoverable-error reporter. No new error id, lifecycle, registry, or generalized tracker.

MAYOR: PR #7838 open with the erasure proof. Recording the worker's stop-point and its two most important findings while the PR is in CI.

IT STOPPED ON THE WIRING, correctly: the bead's "wired into the package's test entry" needs implementation/package.json, which is fenced hot-zone. Its recommendation, which I endorse and will sequence: fold the scan into build:hicasso-release itself —

  "build:hicasso-release": "shadow-cljs release hicasso-release && node hicasso/scripts/check_production_erasure.cjs --self-test && node hicasso/scripts/check_production_erasure.cjs"

Making the scan part of the BUILD'S DEFINITION means the bundle cannot be produced unchecked, and it inherits test.yml's existing cljs-job step with NO NEW PREDICATE — the same reasoning PR #7823 used, and the same reason rf2-hic-021 was reopened for a predicate nobody would revisit. TWO FIRST-PASS SABOTAGES WENT GREEN, and this is the finding that makes the proof trustworthy. Ungating only set-lowering-owner!'s own body left the gate green, because that fn is called only from inside another goog.DEBUG gate and Closure dropped it whole. title: hic-023 — Versioned evidence projection + the four Xray views
description:
# hic-023 — Versioned evidence projection + the four Xray views

**Phase**: tooling lane · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-001
**Surface**: `tools/xray/` (Hicasso producer + views) — **update `tools/xray/spec/*` in the same PR**; `implementation/hicasso/src/` only for the dev-only evidence projection hooks

## Goal
The glass, on the live tier: a versioned, adapter-neutral evidence projection from the Hicasso runtime, and the mounted / read / intent / explain-render views consuming it.

## Deliverables
- The projection: view, frame, source, current reads, known cause, attempt outcome, commit/unmount — projected from state the runtime already retains (no universal accumulator, no second history buffer); envelope carries schema, producer, scope, basis, completeness, loss.
- Honest loss states as first-class: `unknown` / `opaque` / `host-opaque` / `cap` / `uncorrelated` — never an authoritative empty.
- The four views in Xray: mounted boundaries; read attribution (sub → boundary); intent stream; explain-render (which reads changed → why this boundary ran).
- **The privacy projector as a witnessed contract**: query arguments and results pass the existing privacy projection; a witness proves a sensitive value cannot leave unredacted (seeded-value test); Xray and Pair consume the same projected schema byte-for-byte.
- Production: projection returns nil; no evidence/schema sentinels reachable (proof completed by hic-024).

## Acceptance
- Views answer their questions on the tiny consumer app; loss states visibly rendered; Xray/Pair consume one identical schema; `tools/xray/spec/*` updated.

## Worker notes
Read synth-codex §10; `codex/testing-xray.md` evidence contract. Timing proximity never fabricates causality — label uncorrelated links.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7789 (merged 2026-08-10T10:59:03Z as 07ecacf4f847b0dc002fd532ced0667147e7ad6e) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE. COMPLETENESS: the versioned schema, four producer reads, four Xray views, consumer pin, spec, registration, and broad witnesses landed coherently. Actual Pair migration remains separately and exactly owned by open rf2-hic-076; do not duplicate it or call construction alone actual consumption. CORRECTNESS 1 — PRIVACY: projected-query protects the :reads/:edges query field, but entry-rows exports the raw read-key set as :boundary :key, edge-row exports it again under :readers, and explain-render carries it onward. hicasso-helpers then prints raw query vectors in boundary labels and derives DOM testids from them. A sensitive query argument therefore bypasses elide-wire-value, including after frame destruction; the seeded witness covers a secret RETURN VALUE only and its destroyed-frame row asserts only :reads :query. Preserve joinability without carrying raw application arguments, and add a sensitive-query negative control across mounted, attribution, and Why envelopes plus the rendered tree. CORRECTNESS 2 — FRAME ISOLATION: explain-render counts retained runs globally and indexes leads by sub-id alone. A run in frame B can make a frame-A row claim that its window was searched and can appear as an A candidate merely because both frames register the same sub id. Scope window state and candidate matching to the boundary frame, with a two-frame same-sub-id/asymmetric-window witness. The flat Intents roster also concatenates per-frame rings in frame-id order even though it promises dispatch order, and cross-frame bundles can represent fragments of one dispatch; either reconstruct the intended order/identity or state and render per-frame streams honestly. CORRECTNESS 3 — EMPTY SEMANTICS: the shared presence helper classifies every supported empty roster as :idle and renders Hicasso is running and nothing is mounted / clean bill of health. That is true only for the mounted census. Empty Intents is a capped retained window, not proof that nothing dispatched or mounted; empty attribution can coexist with mounted read-free boundaries. Make empties view-specific and keep their loss/remedy visible. ERGONOMICS: Why reports :latest-reads as sub ids only, so [:row 1] and [:row 2] collapse even though their projected query/frame rows are already available; either return the projected read identity or explicitly narrow the claim. IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the algebra and tests are otherwise cohesive and proportionate. Add only bounded witnesses for sensitive query arguments, two frames, per-view empties, and two query variants; no new store or framework is warranted. Full merged-range diff-check passed and all 89 PR checks were non-failing, demonstrating these are missing controls rather than known gate reds.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7792 LIFECYCLE SUPPLEMENT (merged 2026-08-10T10:59:35Z) — UPDATE THIS EXISTING OWNER; NO DUPLICATE. The real React witness establishes facts the #7789 Xray surface does not currently carry: Activity-hidden and unmounted collapse to the same live ownership census until a later 0-to-1 re-subscribe reveals retention retrospectively, while a Suspense-fallback-hidden subtree remains subscribed and therefore looks visible-connected in the tables while absent from the screen. The shipped four views contain no lifecycle view or state. Resolve the normative Xray distinguishes requirement honestly: either add a bounded, justified observable that can distinguish the live states, or render the host-owned distinction as host-opaque and amend the governing promise explicitly. Do not infer hidden-retained from an empty census, and do not label a Suspense-hidden connected row visible. This joins the already-open rf2-hic-023 audit repair; no new history store is presumed.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7802 (2026-08-10): two bounded residuals in the same evidence/Xray owner.

1. THE VERSIONED WIRE SHAPE CHANGED WITHOUT A VERSION BUMP. PR #7802 changes boundary-key elements from `[frame-id query]` to `[frame-id sub-id projected-query]`, intent rows from singular `:frame-id` to plural `:frames`, and `:latest-reads` from bare sub ids to `{:sub-id :query :frame-id}` maps; it also adds host fields. Yet the producer still stamps `:re-frame.hicasso.evidence/v1`, Xray still accepts that same literal, and Spec 027 still calls it v1. This directly defeats the consumer-owned pin whose docs say an evolved shape must mismatch rather than be mis-parsed as exact. Bump producer and consumer to v2 in lockstep (including fixtures/spec); pre-alpha needs no compatibility adapter, but the version must tell the truth.

2. XRAY STILL DROPS PART OF THE PROJECTED IDENTITY WHEN BUILDING ROW KEYS/TESTIDS. `boundary-slug` ignores frame-id, while `attribution-rows` slugs every edge by sub-id alone and the Reads renderer prints neither projected query nor frame. Distinct rows therefore share React keys/testids and can be visually indistinguishable. Direct JVM witness on merge 7c45f3ca9:
  boundary keys `[[:frame/a :row [:row 1]]]` and `[[:frame/b :row [:row 1]]]`
  -> slugs `["row-row-1" "row-row-1"]`;
  attribution rows for `[:row 1]` in frame A and `[:row 2]` in frame B
  -> slugs `["row" "row"]` despite distinct `:frame-id`/`:query`.
Preserve the full projected identity in React keys/testids and render enough of it (especially Reads, and the frame in Why) for a programmer to distinguish rows. Use only projected fields; no raw query data should return.

The producer's redaction, frame-scoped lead search, dispatch ordering/fragment merge, per-view empties, and host-opaque lifecycle wording otherwise review cleanly. Keep the repair within the existing schema/helpers/panel tests; no new store or framework.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7820 (merged 2026-08-10T16:27:25Z as dbbcf05584) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; no duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: producer, Xray consumer and Spec 027 now stamp v2 in lockstep; v1 and future stamps mismatch; no compatibility shim was added. Reads/Why render the projected query and frame, and the data plumbing uses projected fields only. Authored/landed patch ids match. Independent gates passed: tools/xray JVM 1287 tests / 6033 assertions, full implementation CLJS 13024 / 65811, doc slugs, and every edited spec table block has uniform columns.

CORRECTNESS — THE NEW “WHOLE PROJECTED IDENTITY” STRING IS NOT INJECTIVE. read-key-str concatenates each component's pr-str with `-`, then read-slug/boundary-slug pass that string through id-slug, which replaces every non-alphanumeric run with `-`. Namespace separators, hyphens, component boundaries and collection punctuation therefore collapse. Direct JVM reproduction against the landed helper:

  identities:      [:a/b :c :d]   [:a-b :c :d]   [:a :b/c :d]
  read-slugs:      a-b-c-d         a-b-c-d         a-b-c-d
  boundary-slugs:  a-b-c-d         a-b-c-d         a-b-c-d
  distinct counts: 1 and 1

All three are legal, distinct projected identities. The collision again gives distinct rows one React key and one DOM testid — exactly the residual this PR says it closes — and namespaced/hyphenated keyword ids are ordinary programmer inputs, not an adversarial edge.

COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the new witnesses vary frame/query values that remain distinct after lossy slugification, so they prove those fields are present but not that the resulting key preserves identity. The green suites above confirm the collision is unwitnessed.

BOUNDED REPAIR: keep read-key-str as the single projected-identity door and keep raw queries out. Make the React key/testid encoding collision-resistant for the complete projected tuple (for example, a reversible escaped encoding or readable slug plus a stable full-identity suffix), then add the three-way namespace/hyphen/component-boundary control above for both read-slug and boundary-slug. Do not add an ordinal, store, compatibility layer or raw-data escape; rf2-hic-076 remains the separate Pair migration owner.
MAYOR — A CLAIM IN THIS BEAD'S DELIVERABLE IS FALSE, found by the rf2-hic-076 census (PR #7837). Recording it here rather than reopening: the bead's WORK is sound and merged; it is one sentence in the deliverable text that overstates.

THE CLAIM: "Xray and Pair consume the same projected schema byte-for-byte."

THE MEASUREMENT: Xray's Hicasso tab consumes :re-frame.hicasso.evidence/v2. PAIR CONSUMES :re-frame.freehand.evidence/v1. Pair was never moved off the donor at all — and its coupling is not even a require, so nothing in a classpath scan would have shown it.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT DOES NOT: it does not invalidate the v2 bump or the injective slug, which were verified independently and are correct. It does mean the bead's own record asserts a parity that has never held, and rf2-hic-062 or a later reader could take it at face value. If anyone acts on "Xray and Pair consume the same schema" they will be wrong about Pair.

The census now carries the accurate statement, so this note exists so the closed bead does not contradict it.
close_reason:
PR #7826 merged. The AUDIT #7820 residual is closed, and the fix is a proof about the function rather than three passing examples — which is what the previous two attempts on this surface lacked.

REPRODUCED FIRST, on the landed helper: [:a/b :c :d], [:a-b :c :d] and [:a :b/c :d] all slugged to a-b-c-d, distinct counts 1 and 1. Note read-key-str itself was fine; the loss was entirely in id-slug.

THE ENCODING SEPARATES IDENTITY FROM LABEL, which dissolves the tension the earlier attempt fought: #7820 already prints the projected query and frame ON THE ROW, so the key is free to be ugly. identity-slug is the readable id-slug stem (lossy on purpose, keeping testids greppable and every existing includes? assertion true), then "-", then an escaped tail where alphanumerics survive and everything else becomes % plus the UTF-16 code unit in hex. % is itself escaped and u is not a hex digit, so it parses back one way; the escape emits no "-", SO THE LAST "-" IS ALWAYS THE JOIN AND THE TAIL DECODES TO EXACTLY ONE INPUT. No ordinal — the previous worker was right that a number naming nothing is worse than a collision — and no digest, because a 32-bit hash already failed this exact test in rf2-bk2c6.

read-key-str stayed the single door but now spends ONE pr-str over the whole triple instead of three joined by "-", because a separator between printed components is forgeable by a component containing it. Same canonical string the producer sorts its own rows by.

IT FOUND THE IDENTICAL DEFECT ONE LINE AWAY and fixed it: the intent row slug, where :a/b-c and :a-b/c shared a testid.

THE PROPERTY, not examples: 21 component shapes chosen so the three loss mechanisms sit adjacent (namespace separator, in-name hyphen, component boundary; 1 beside 12; [:a :b] beside [[:a] :b]). Generated space 9,261 identities, 10,162 boundary keys, 441 intent rows. A NON-VACUITY assertion pins the pool — the original three-way control must still collide under id-slug alone — so the space cannot silently stop testing anything.

EXCLUSIONS STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: values pr-str cannot print apart — reader-hostile symbols, and two =-equal maps built in different insertion orders. It inherited the producer's canonical form rather than inventing a second one in the consumer, and wrote that into the docstring and Spec 027.

MUTATION RED verified applied before being believed (git diff --stat 10/111, the four landed call sites back in the file): 6 failures naming the colliding rows, including the three-way control at ["a-b-c-d" "a-b-c-d" "a-b-c-d"]. Restored via git checkout --, byte-identical, re-run 16 tests / 126 assertions clean.

Spec duty honoured: tools/xray/spec/027 gains a section on the key being injective and the label being where readability lives, plus the coverage-table row naming the property and its size.

Because the required lane runs with --fail-level error, this blocks correct programmer code.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / ACCEPTANCE: keep the bounded, editor-reliable self-call rule, but distinguish lexical bindings from the enclosing view identity (the hook already centralizes api/resolve). Add parameter/destructuring or let-shadow negative coverage while preserving the recursive self-call positive row. MAYOR 2026-08-10 ~22:10 AUSEST — QUEUED FOR THE NEXT FREE SLOT; NOT DISPATCHED YET
(six workers live). Recording the shape so the next pass does not re-derive it.

THIS IS A STANCE VIOLATION, NOT A NITPICK, WHICH IS WHY IT JUMPS THE P3s. The
project trusts the programmer and rejects nag-diagnostics. check-direct-view-call!
compares TOKEN SPELLING ONLY, it is ERROR level, and the required lane runs with
--fail-level error. So legal code is refused:

  (h/defview card [card] (card) [:div "ok"])
  (h/defview via-let [_] (let [via-let (fn [] :ordinary)] (via-let)) [:div "ok"])

Both report re-frame.hicasso/direct-view-call and exit 3, although each call
resolves to a legal LOCAL BINDING rather than the view Var. A gate that blocks
correct programmer code is worse than no gate.

THE REPAIR IS BOUNDED and the audit says how: keep the self-call rule (it is
editor-reliable, which is why it was chosen over whole-program resolution), but
distinguish a lexical binding from the enclosing view identity — the hook already
centralises api/resolve, so the mechanism is in hand. Add parameter/destructuring
and let-shadow NEGATIVE coverage while preserving the recursive self-call POSITIVE
row. Do not reach for whole-program analysis; that was already declined on this
bead for good reasons (cache-dependent ns-analysis fires in CI and stays silent in
an editor).

NOT A REGRESSION ON MAIN TODAY: main is green and no shipped code trips it. The
exposure is forward — any worker writing a hicasso view whose local binding shares
the view name will be blocked by a false ERROR and will reasonably assume its own
code is wrong.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7804 (merged 2026-08-10T13:50:56Z as 5e33c4eb5) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER AGAIN; no duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: the original false ERROR for a defview parameter, destructuring, ordinary let/for/fn/hfn, single-arity letfn, catch, and as-> is removed; the genuine recursive self-call remains red; the export README now matches the six configured checks. Independent audit runs passed the live lint gate and all four mutation self-tests, the tracked tree stayed clean, and authored/landed patch ids are exact.

COMPLETENESS / CORRECTNESS — MULTI-ARITY letfn PARAMETERS STILL FALSE-RED. locals-bound-by destructures each letfn form as [nm params] and collects params only when that second node is a vector. In a valid multi-arity letfn, the second node is the first arity list, so none of any arity's parameter vectors are recognized. Reproduced against this merge and the pinned :clj-kondo alias:

  (h/defview card [_]
    (letfn [(invoke
              ([card] (card))
              ([card x] (card x)))]
      [:div (invoke (fn [& _] :ok))]))

Both calls to the legal local parameter report re-frame.hicasso/direct-view-call at ERROR and clj-kondo exits 3; a genuine (genuine) self-call in the same probe still reports. This directly contradicts the PR/README claim that letfn parameters are covered and preserves the same build-blocking programmer-friction class #7804 meant to close.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: keep the small syntax-local walker and conservative whole-form silencing. Teach the letfn arm to collect the parameter vector of a single arity OR every parameter vector under its arity lists (the existing fn-locals shape is the nearby model), then add a multi-arity negative fixture and a red mutation witness. No api/resolve, whole-program scope engine, or custom-macro analysis is warranted.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7804 finding ACCEPTED, and this is the FIFTH instance tonight of one specific failure shape — a witness whose STATED SCOPE EXCEEDS THE CASES IT ACTUALLY DRIVES.

Here: locals-bound-by destructures each letfn form as [nm params] and collects params only when that second node is a VECTOR. In a valid MULTI-ARITY letfn the second node is the first arity LIST, so no arity's parameter vector is recognised and every use of a legal local parameter reports direct-view-call at ERROR — clj-kondo exits 3, the build stops. The PR body and the export README both claim letfn parameters are covered. They are covered for single-arity, which is the only shape the witness drove.

THE OTHER FOUR TONIGHT, same shape: rf2-hic-020's parity table covered only the valid raw component while claiming both arms; rf2-hic-007's completeness test claimed all six constructor fields unforgeable while running only where declaring! had already supplied real values; rf2-hic-012's comment recorded the expected result as though measured; rf2-hic-021's completeness check ranged over ids THAT EXIST, so thirteen refusals with no id satisfied it vacuously.

WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING, and it is not carelessness: in each case the witness was written from the FIX, so it drives the shapes the author had in mind while fixing. The shapes that break it are precisely the ones the author did not think of — which is the same set. A test derived from the implementation inherits the implementation's blind spots.

THE COUNTERMEASURE I AM PUTTING IN BRIEFS: derive the witness from the GRAMMAR of the thing, not from the fix. For a letfn arm that means enumerating letfn's actual legal shapes (single-arity vector, multi-arity lists, with and without a docstring/prepost) and driving each, rather than testing the one the fix was written against. State in the PR body which shapes of the grammar you drove and which you did not.

BOUNDED REPAIR (from the audit, and it is a fence): keep the small syntax-local walker and the conservative whole-form silencing. Teach the letfn arm to collect the parameter vector of a single arity OR every parameter vector under its arity lists. Do not reach for resolution — #7804 established by probe that api/resolve returns nil for the cases that matter and never sees locals.

READY TO DISPATCH; held only because six workers are live. Surface is implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/** plus scripts/check_lint_export.py, currently held by nobody.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7818 (merged 2026-08-10T16:16:28Z as 2e2471bc14) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; no duplicate.

COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the new fixtures do not make the stated “every parameter of every arity” property load-bearing. locals-bound-by unions all names for the whole letfn and self-call-nodes then suppresses that entire form as soon as ANY arity binds the view name. Every committed multi-arity negative row binds the same view name in both arities, so recognizing only the later arity is enough to make every row green.

The pinned live gate still exited 0: “OK: 6 checks fire on their fixtures, correct code is silent, and the artefact's own testbeds are quiet.” The source was restored exactly and the worktree verified clean. The current mutation only removes ALL arities, so it does not catch this narrower regression.

BOUNDED REPAIR: add one independent negative case in which the view name is bound only by the FIRST arity and later arities bind different names, plus a self-test mutation that skips the first arity (or an equivalent discriminating mutation). Keep the current small syntax-local walker and whole-form silencing; no resolution or scope engine. rf2-ka4d remains the separate exact owner for the six other binding-form omissions.

It has the bounded repair (one negative case where the view name is bound ONLY by the first arity while later arities bind different names, plus a discriminating self-test mutation) and has been told to sequence this BEFORE rf2-ka4d, since this is a reopened P1 on code already on main.

I also passed on the generalisation, because it corrects an instruction I have been issuing all session: grammar-derivation is necessary and NOT sufficient. Enumerating legal shapes answers 'did I test this form?'; it does not answer 'can this row tell the difference?' The audit settled it by measurement — changing fn-locals' multi-arity source to (rest forms) left the pinned live gate at exit 0. Recorded as bd memory rows-must-be-discriminating-not-merely-shaped.

The PR correctly insists all evidence be measured at clj-kondo 2026.04.15 because the host native binary is 2025.10.23, but check_lint_export.py still searches clj-kondo before clojure and verifies no version. On the audit host the standard documented command selected C:\Users\miket\AppData\Roaming\npm\clj-kondo.cmd v2025.10.23 and exited 0 with the same reassuring OK line; the pinned :clj-kondo alias v2026.04.15 also passed.
