title: hic-021 — The complaint catalogue: stable diagnostic ids as public contract
description:
# hic-021 — The complaint catalogue: stable diagnostic ids as public contract

**Phase**: tooling lane · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-001 (hic-007 lands the shape; this catalogues it — coordinate, don't collide: this bead owns the catalogue doc + tests, not the error constructor)
**Surface**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md` (new) + `implementation/hicasso/test/.../complaints_catalogue_*` (new)

## Goal
Every Hicasso refusal id catalogued, versioned, and tested as public API: id → meaning → payload shape → docs anchor → recovery ladder. The cheapest proven asset in the record (the predecessor shipped 83).

## Deliverables
- The catalogue: enumerate every `:rf.error/hicasso-*` id in the runtime with payload schema and recovery.
- A completeness test: every id raised anywhere in the suite appears in the catalogue (and vice versa — no dead entries).
- Stability rule recorded: ids never change meaning; retired ids are tombstoned.

## Acceptance
- Round-trip test green (raise-set == catalogue-set); each entry's recovery is actionable prose, not a restatement of the error.

## Worker notes
Read synth.md diagnostics paragraph; lessons-reframe-ui refusal-culture section (via its banner — evidence only). Lint (hic-022), the advisor (hic-037), and the MCP spike (hic-059) consume this.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes:
From rf2-hic-001 (the extraction): scope boundary worth pinning before you start.

Your stated surface is docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md + this artefact's own round-trip tests. That is NOT the same catalogue as spec/009-Instrumentation.md, which is the repo-wide instrumentation catalogue that scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py defends. Moving the runtime from the bench test/ tree into implementation/hicasso/src/ brought all 40 :rf.error/hicasso-* ids inside that gate's scan for the first time, and it now reports every one as uncatalogued. rf2-cs0kd1 deleted the KNOWN_UNCATALOGUED construct from that gate, so there is no debt-ledger escape: the Spec 009 rows have to be written.

That work is filed separately as rf2-g85n and BLOCKS rf2-hic-001 from merging spine-green. Coordinate: the two catalogues should agree and yours can cite the Spec 009 rows, but neither substitutes for the other.

One id in the set is not hicasso-prefixed — :rf.error/no-frame-prop, emitted by impl/runtime.cljs. Whether it is a Hicasso id needing a rename or a core id with an existing home is an open question in rf2-g85n.
SCOPE ADDITION (2026-08-10, from the guide rewrite's Stage C): the catalogue must mint ids for 13 refusal families the end-state guide teaches by mechanism only — the defview direct-call refusal; the five n/$ refusal rows (props misclassification, hiccup child, intent-in-prop, :children, slot collision); three test-kit refusals (L2 opacity, missing fixture, assert-clean failure); the forms-module family; the contenteditable refusal; route-link :prefetch wrong-value; second-mount-same-node. Authoritative list after rf2-hic-092 merges: docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/REWRITE-NOTES.md section 'Stage C output' (catalogue gaps). Also note: :rf.error/hicasso-route-link-bad-on-click is attested and should be cited on guide ch07 when the catalogue lands.
MAYOR 2026-08-10 — THIRTEEN REFUSALS TO MINT ARE NOW WAITING FOR THIS BEAD, AND THE COMPLETENESS TEST AS SPECIFIED CANNOT SEE THEM.

SOURCE, now on main after rf2-hic-092 merged:
docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/REWRITE-NOTES.md
  section "### (b) The catalogue gaps (refusals taught by mechanism with no
  attested id)", 13 numbered entries beginning at line 126.
A shorter roll-up of the same set sits at line 50 under "## Missing error ids
(catalogue gaps — Stage C compiles; do NOT invent on pages)".

FOUND BY THE rf2-hic-093 WORKER while folding the minted-spellings register into
the naming ledger. It reported them as having no owner. THEY DO HAVE ONE — this
bead — and no duplicate should be filed. But the worker's instinct was half right,
and the half that is right is the point of this note.

WHY THIS BEAD'S COMPLETENESS TEST WOULD MISS THEM. The deliverable reads "enumerate
every :rf.error/hicasso-* id in the runtime" and "every id raised anywhere in the
suite appears in the catalogue (and vice versa — no dead entries)". Both directions
of that test range over ids THAT EXIST. These 13 are refusals the guide teaches BY
MECHANISM with no attested id at all — the guide describes what the runtime refuses
and how, without naming a diagnostic. A refusal with no id is raised by nothing and
appears in no catalogue, so it satisfies both directions of the completeness test
vacuously. That is the same fail-open shape this repo keeps finding in its own
instruments: the test verifies the absence of a mismatch rather than the presence of
coverage.

So the catalogue is not complete when the two enumerations agree. It is complete when
the two enumerations agree AND every refusal the guide teaches has an id. Treat the
Stage C list as a third input to the completeness test, not as background reading.

WHAT THE 13 COVER (from the line-50 roll-up; read section (b) for the full text):
the `defview` direct-call refusal; the `n/$` refusal family (props misclassification,
hiccup child, intent-in-prop, `:children`, slot collision); test-kit refusals
(opacity, missing fixture, assert-clean failure); forms-module rows; the
contenteditable refusal; the bare-intent veto at `route-link` `:on-click`; and
`:prefetch` wrong-value.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT COME WITH THE LIST.
1. "do NOT invent on pages" — the guide chapters deliberately did not mint these.
   Minting is this bead's job, in the catalogue, not a chapter edit.
2. Gap 12 records that THE RETIRED DECLINE ID MUST NOT BE REUSED. That is the same
   rule this bead already states as "retired ids are tombstoned", and it now has a
   concrete instance to honour.

ONE ID SITS IN TWO PILES. rf2-hic-093 landed naming-ledger row 30, which records
`:rf.error/hicasso-overlay-anchor-missing` as simultaneously a SPELLING question for
rf2-hic-065's naming packet and a CATALOGUE obligation here. Coordinate rather than
collide: the packet settles the spelling, this bead catalogues whatever it settles on.
Do not settle the spelling here.

THE EXISTING COORDINATION FENCE IS UNCHANGED: rf2-hic-007 lands the error SHAPE, this
bead catalogues it, and this bead owns the catalogue doc and tests rather than the
error constructor.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #7808 (merged 2026-08-10T13:31:50Z as 59bf33c0b) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; do not file a duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: the 59-live / 12-reserved / 1-pending / 0-retired register is coherent, the eight relational rules and red self-tests pass, every live id round-trips through an emitter and Spec 009, every cited anchor resolves, and the two Spec 009 clarifications are accurate. Independent audit runs passed the complaint self-test and live gate, the full npm freeze chain, keyword drift, doc slugs, and all 322 changed-surface tests. All three authored commits have exact landed patch identities.

COMPLETENESS / CORRECTNESS — THE NEW CONTRACT IS NOT SELF-PROTECTING IN CI. The checker reads four input families: implementation/hicasso source and test-kit code, docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md, and cited docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide chapters. Direct report-changed-surfaces probes on this merge set cljs_node_test=true only for implementation/hicasso/**. The register, Spec 009, and guide inputs each report cljs_node_test=false. In test.yml the only hosted invocation is inside the cljs job guarded by needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.cljs_node_test == 'true'. Thus a register-only edit can drop or corrupt a live/reserved/tombstone row, a Spec-only edit can break R3/R4/R6, and a guide-only edit can break R8 while every PR check skips this gate. #7808 happened to touch the checker and package.json, masking the reverse-edge gap. The close reason's claim that chaining into test:hicasso-freeze created “NO scheduling hole” is disproved.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / BOUNDED REPAIR: preserve the small pure-Python checker and its current rules. Give it a cheap CI path whose changed-surface inputs include every file family it reads, or otherwise make those exact reverse edges executable and covered by the scheduling tests. Do not make a docs-only catalogue edit pay for the full CLJS/browser/HMR matrix merely to run a sub-second Python contract. Keep rf2-ibje scoped to the honest script rename; it is not an owner for this missing reachability.
MAYOR: the AUDIT #7808 finding is ACCEPTED and my close reason was WRONG. I wrote that chaining the checker into test:hicasso-freeze created 'NO scheduling hole'. The audit's direct report-changed-surfaces probes disprove it: only implementation/hicasso/** sets cljs_node_test=true, while the register, spec/009 and the cited guide chapters all report false, and the only hosted invocation is guarded on that flag. #7808 touching the checker and package.json is what masked it.

The lesson generalises past this bead, and it is the same shape the merge criterion keeps teaching: A GATE THAT RUNS ON THE PR THAT INTRODUCED IT PROVES ONLY THAT IT RUNS ON THAT PR. Its reverse edges — the file families it reads but does not live beside — are unproven until each one is driven on its own. The introducing PR is the single worst witness for reachability, because it necessarily touches the gate itself.

ROUTED, not separately dispatched: worker/catalogrows-vkle already holds .github/workflows/test.yml and implementation/package.json for rf2-ibje (the test:hicasso-freeze rename), and both are sequential-access. A second worker would need the same window and conflict. It has the audit's bounded repair — preserve the small pure-Python checker and its rules; give it a CI path whose changed-surface inputs include every family it reads, or make those reverse edges executable and covered by the scheduling tests — plus an instruction to DRIVE each of the three false edges (register-only, spec-only, guide-only) rather than assert them.

Note the interaction it must not miss: rf2-ibje asks it to prove the renamed gate still runs, and this finding says the gate does not run on three of the four families it guards. A rename that preserves an unreachable gate preserves nothing.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7825 (2026-08-10; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). REOPEN EXACT CATALOGUE OWNER.

WHAT IS SOUND: the three authored patches match their landed identities; error.cljc and Spec 009 now accurately cite rf2-hic-021's builder-routing ruling and distinguish required-key overwrite from ambient-key removal. The complaint-catalogue contract and doc-slug gates pass.

COMPLETENESS / DOC TRUTH: docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md still says the provenance of :source/:view when no origin names a view “is rf2-hic-007's to settle” and promises nothing. PR #7812 settled it: fail! removes both ambient keys from extra before merging, so they are absent outside a declaration/render extent and in production. #7825 identified this exact stale deferral but routed it only to a transient worker, leaving no durable Bead owner. Correct that one clause here (or point to the settled constructor rule) without restating the whole rationale or widening the catalogue. If the routed worker lands the correction first, verify it and close this owner; do not create another issue.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7825's critique of my routing is ACCEPTED, and its resolution rule is the one I am following.

THE FINDING (complaints.md:52's stale deferral to rf2-hic-007, a bead that landed and settled it) WAS routed mid-flight to worker/smallmisc-miw1, which holds that file — and that worker LANDED IT. Its report: 'Handed in mid-flight — done, not declined. complaints.md:52's deferral to rf2-hic-007 was stale and contradicted the paragraph above it. Confirmed at source (impl/error.cljc: ambient = [:source :view], fail! does (merge (apply dissoc extra ambient) ...)), replaced with one sentence citing Rulings this catalogue owns rather than restating it.' That is in PR #7827, currently one check from green.

SO PER THE AUDIT'S OWN INSTRUCTION — 'If the routed worker lands the correction first, verify it and close this owner; do not create another issue' — I will VERIFY the landed text on main once #7827 merges, then close this bead. No new issue filed.

THE CRITIQUE IS RIGHT ABOUT THE METHOD, not just this instance: a SendMessage lives in an agent's transcript, so if that agent dies, times out or declines the extra item, the finding evaporates with nothing in the tracker to re-surface it. I had recorded the routing in rf2-ddqd's CLOSE REASON, which is a record on the wrong object — nobody reads a closed bead looking for open work.

Corrected practice, recorded as bd memory routed-findings-need-a-note-on-the-owning-bead: keep routing to the worker that holds the file (it avoids two workers contending), but ALSO put one note on the OWNING bead naming what was routed, to whom, and what happens if it does not land. The efficiency is preserved and the tracker carries the obligation.
close_reason: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7827 verified the #7825 remainder against landed main: complaints.md no longer defers :source/:view provenance to rf2-hic-007; it states that fail! removes both ambient keys before merging required data, matching implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/error.cljc. The exact routed correction landed, so this owner closes per its own note.

# hic-015 — Kernel: the HMR contract, promised and witnessed

**Phase**: 1 · **Wave**: B · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-001
**Surface**: `implementation/hicasso/test/.../hmr_*` (new); HMR/generation wiring (distinct files — parallel with 010/012/016)

## Goal
Reload either preserves the stated identity/focus/state contract or promises a clean, diagnosable subtree remount — written down, witnessed, never folklore.

## Deliverables
- The witness matrix through a real shadow-cljs reload: focused controlled input, child hook state (in a host), an active imperative host, frame routing, and cleanup — through re-evaluation of a `defview`.
- The written contract (default expectation: re-minted head ⇒ clean remount; document exactly what is lost and what survives) in the invariant ledger.
- Generation/cleanup: stale generations leave zero registrations.

## Acceptance
- Matrix green; the contract document matches observed behavior exactly; sabotage: a leaked old-generation registration must turn the cleanup witness red.

## Worker notes
Read `codex/adversarial-risks.md` HMR row. The smallest stable shell only if the witness demands it — do not build preservation machinery speculatively.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).

COMPLETENESS: the node seam matrix and real React 19.2 browser rows are broad, premise-guarded, identity-sensitive, residue-aware, and fully scheduled; the merged-range diff-check passed and all 89 PR checks were non-failing. But the owner and normative react-compatibility lane require reveal to correct before visible paint and Xray to distinguish hidden-retained / visible-connected / unmounted. The PR itself measures a concurrent reveal exposing the pre-hide value for one animation frame, and no Xray lifecycle view/change landed. CORRECTNESS: accepting a ceiling of one stale frame does not satisfy a hard before-visible-paint law. Keep the measurement, but obtain an explicit law disposition and either repair the concurrent path or revise the governing contract through its owner; do not close by renaming eventual correction as pre-paint. rf2-2l17 is the existing precedent for the same law, not a duplicate Activity owner. Also, node row repeated-suspend-retry-cycles manually calls the Activity-style cleanup/re-subscribe seam and says Suspense is the same mechanism, while the real DOM row proves the opposite: post-commit Suspense retains the passive subscription and registration identity. MAYOR HOLD (2026-08-10, 21:4x AUSEST) — DO NOT DISPATCH; AWAITING AN OPERATOR RULING.

The #7792 audit above reopened this bead with two findings. The second is a clean
bounded fix and could be dispatched today. The FIRST is a law question and is
Mike's, not a worker's:

  The owner and the normative react-compatibility lane require reveal to correct
  BEFORE VISIBLE PAINT. The merged PR measured a concurrent reveal exposing the
  pre-hide value for ONE ANIMATION FRAME. Accepting a one-frame ceiling does not
  satisfy a hard before-visible-paint law, and the audit says explicitly: do not
  close by renaming eventual correction as pre-paint.

So the fork is:
  (a) THE LAW STANDS — repair the concurrent path so reveal corrects before paint.
  (b) THE CONTRACT IS REVISED through its owner — state a bounded one-frame
      ceiling for the concurrent path, and say why that is the honest promise.

This is the SAME LAW as rf2-2l17 (the reincarnation correction is macrotask-
deferred, but React law 3 requires correction before visible paint), which the
audit names as the existing precedent rather than a duplicate owner. The two
should be ruled together — ruling them apart risks two different answers to one
question.

The second finding, dispatchable once the law is settled: the node row
repeated-suspend-retry-cycles manually calls the Activity-style cleanup and
re-subscribe seam and claims Suspense is the same mechanism, while the real DOM
row proves the opposite — post-commit Suspense RETAINS the passive subscription
and the registration identity. Either rename and rescope that row to repeated
detach/reacquire conduct, or add the bounded real-Suspense repetition it claims.
The algebra is useful; the name and prose are false evidence.

Also outstanding from the audit: no Xray lifecycle view landed to distinguish
hidden-retained / visible-connected / unmounted.

The audit is emphatic that the witnesses are otherwise unusually strong — retain
the negative controls, and add no runtime machinery unless the law ruling
requires it.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-11, operator-overturnable): OPTION (b). The contract is revised through its owner: the bounded, gated, at-most-one-frame stale window for CONCURRENTLY SCHEDULED Activity reveals is ratified. Design law React 3 stands untouched. The mayor hold is lifted; this bead is DISPATCHABLE and sits on the hic-017/018/019 critical path.

WHY (b). The staleness is not a tear. The revealed frame re-shows an old, internally consistent commit — no render/commit pair ever disagreed, and the witness proves every sampled frame showed a legitimate committed value, never a mixed one. React 3 on its own text ("a render/commit tear is detected and corrected before visible paint") is therefore not in play; the amended texts should say that scoping out loud so the law is not weakened by implication. The mechanism is React's, not ours: on a concurrent reveal React bails out of re-rendering the retained subtree (no render runs, getSnapshot is never consulted), and the first signal that the store moved arrives when React re-subscribes in a PASSIVE EFFECT, flushed in a scheduler task — a rendering opportunity can fall between the reveal commit and that task. The boundary shell is exactly two hooks (impl/collector.cljs shell-hook-ledger, test-enforced), and neither fires before the reveal's paint. The only genuine repair is a third universal hook plus per-fiber force-update machinery on every boundary of every app: it breaches State 6 (the two-hook ceiling), breaches Economics 2 (a rare facility taxing every boundary), works against React 4 (concurrency/Activity ceded to React, which offers no pre-paint reveal signal inside useSyncExternalStore), and pre-empts rf2-hic-018 — the bead whose job is to freeze the ceiling with its measurement. Rejected as the over-engineering shape. Nothing desynchronizes: Spec 006 invariant 5 (L1316-1321) is scoped to movement in the render->commit gap judged against the render's probe evidence — no render runs at a bailed-out reveal — while the clause that governs a hidden subtree later revealed (L2084-2089) requires exactly what PR #7792 proved: clean-slate reconnection, fresh acquisition, never resurrection, with NO timing bound. The discrete path (a click — the overwhelmingly common reveal) is measured stale-free and asserted.

WHY rf2-2l17 DOES NOT TRANSFER — mechanism ownership, not law weakness. At 2l17 the runtime OWNED the deferral: its own collector had retired the cell and scheduled its own correction on setTimeout 0; the repair was a one-line reschedule of code we own (queueMicrotask, 0f58d4d347 / e2bd4cc81a), and refusing it would have been negligence. Here the runtime owns neither the knowledge nor the deferral: no cell was retired, the 2l17 microtask is unreachable (the witness's own analysis, activity_suspense_dom_cljs_test.cljs L553-560), and there is no earlier hook to hoist the correction into. Ruling (b) here does not overturn (a) there. ONE PRINCIPLE, SEEN TWICE (recorded on both beads): we never defer a correction we schedule past paint; where React owns the deferral, the contract states the measured, gated ceiling.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one worker; docs/design/** is outside mkdocs --strict, so the worker verifies anchors and table shape by hand and says so in the PR body). Exactly two text sites amend:
1. docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md L43 (the Activity matrix reveal row — the owner of Activity conduct): state the measured split. A discrete-event reveal corrects before visible paint (asserted). A concurrently scheduled reveal (timer, promise, transition) carries a bounded stale window: React re-subscribes in a passive effect, the revealed frame is the last consistent pre-hide commit — never torn — and a gate reds if the window widens. Speak in lifecycle terms (released ownership -> clean-slate reconnection -> correction); cite one frame as the measured, gated Chromium-lane figure, not as a cross-engine public guarantee.
2. docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/20-code-splitting.md L181-183: drop "never paints stale content"; teach the same split; steer disclosure-sensitive panes (account/tenant switches) toward discrete reveals or unmount/re-key rather than Activity retention — a consistent old commit is not a privacy boundary. Check draft-guide/REWRITE-NOTES.md L67 (item 27's "reveal reacquires before visible paint" summary) for the same amendment.
This note disposes of the bead Goal's "corrects before visible paint" wording for the concurrent path. The witness stays as-is: reading 1's flushed pre-paint assertion and reading 2's at-most-one-frame ceiling are correct conduct — green if React ever closes the window, red if it widens. Retain the negative controls; add NO runtime machinery. The two already-unblocked audit findings dispatch alongside: rename/rescope the false-evidence repeated-suspend-retry-cycles node row (or add the real bounded Suspense repetition), and land the Xray hidden-retained / visible-connected / unmounted assertion (the view is rf2-hic-023's, which must also carry the measured fact that a Suspense-hidden subtree stays CONNECTED while an Activity-hidden one does not).

title: hic-000 — Publish the normative set into the tracked tree
description:
# hic-000 — Publish the normative set into the tracked tree

**Phase**: pre-0 · **Wave**: A (first to merge — every other bead's "Read first" paths resolve only after this lands) · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: —
**Surface**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/` (new files only); no `ai/` paths appear in anything a worker must read

## Goal
Background workers run in git worktrees and see only tracked files; the normative documents currently live under `ai/` (gitignored, local-only). Publish the reading set into `docs/design/hicasso/product/` so every bead brief's references resolve in any checkout.

## Deliverables
- Copy into `docs/design/hicasso/product/`: the decision brief (`synth.md` → `decision-brief.md`), the product specification (`synth-codex.md` → `specification.md`), and **every** `codex/` lane at copy time (same basenames, under `product/lanes/`; the set review `beads-review.md` included).
- Record the source-file hashes in `product/README.md` (the freshness check: filing or dispatch against a stale snapshot fails loudly, per set-README default #7).
- Fix relative links for the new home (lane cross-links; the evidence-baseline's `../../../../docs/design/hicasso/studio/...` anchors become local `../studio/...`; `codex/README.md`'s authority list points at the copied siblings).
- A front note in `product/README.md`: this is the published normative set; the refresh rule (re-publish when the primaries change materially, until/unless the living home moves here permanently — operator decision pending, see set README default #7).
- Seed `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md` with every already-known naming question, one row each (current name, candidates, recommendation, status=open): the §3.7 dispositions (`h/fn`→`h/handler`, `:&` removal, `h/reg-state` removal, `subscribe-once` internal, presence and route-link homes), the `n/` roster (`n/$`, `n/defcomponent`, `n/use-sub`, `n/use-frame`), `h/as-element`, `h/error-boundary`, the root lifecycle names, the package/artifact name, and the test-kit + optional-module namespace names. **Rule stated at the top**: nobody renames mid-flow; prototype names are used consistently; every naming question found by any bead is appended here; the single ruling is hic-065.
- `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` green (it validates this tree's links/anchors; nothing else gates `docs/design/**`). Verify anchors and table column counts by hand and say so in the PR body.

## Acceptance
- A clean worktree checkout can open every "Read first" reference used by **every bead in the set** as a tracked path; slug checks green; no content edits beyond link fixing (this is publication, not revision).

## Worker notes
This is the mayor's or first worker's opening move — a single PR. The `ai/` originals remain the working set for the operator's sessions; provenance (`fable/`) is **not** published.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).

title: RULING NEEDED: validation.md's K1 kill row does not record that rf2-diaud adjudicates K1's gate as MISSED, DECISIVELY
description:
FOUND BY rf2-c5keq (the doc half of the jcm3p sweep) while extending the supersession chains on validation.md and the studio pages. Filed rather than decided, per that bead's own fence: this is a ruling, not a citation update.

WHAT IS TRUE. rf2-diaud (PR #7704) published the M1 mount row on K1's own floor-normalised estimand, adjudicated against K1's own 1.10x threshold, with the verdict K1 MISSED, DECISIVELY on hicasso / uix-subs. The figures are at docs/design/hicasso/studio/rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md section 4.3 and are quoted from nowhere else.

WHAT validation.md SAYS. Its kill-criteria table reads: 'K1 | Mount above the amended mount gate (1.10x direct UIx on the clock of record) after two serious runtime iterations'. Nothing in that section, or in the 'K1's denominator was amended' note beneath it, records that the gate is now measured as missed. A reader of the kill table alone cannot tell that the row it gates has published a verdict against it.

WHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A SWEEP. The criterion has two conjuncts. The gate half is now measured and published. The other half — AFTER TWO SERIOUS RUNTIME ITERATIONS — is a programme judgement about whether the candidate has had those two iterations yet, and K1's consequence is 'stop or narrow'. rf2-c5keq annotated the two places that asserted the old position rather than deciding: the-candidates-clock.md section 8's 'Still not a clear K1 kill' named the RETIRED trigger ('> Reagent', superseded by rf2-hyd50 on 2026-08-05) and is now struck and annotated with the amended denominator, the published verdict, and an explicit statement that the two-iterations question is not decided there; validation.md's new rf2-diaud banner says the same in one sentence. Neither decides.

WHAT THE RULING OWES. (1) Whether the two-serious-runtime-iterations condition is met as of today. (2) If it is, what K1 tripping means in practice — 'stop or narrow', and which. (3) Whether validation.md's K1 row itself should carry a dated note recording the measured verdict against the gate regardless of the trigger question, so the kill table stops being the one page in the tree that does not know.

MATERIAL TO THE SITTING. K1's line for the 2026-08-27 sitting is this row, and the packet freezes 2026-08-25.
notes:
MAYOR NOTE 2026-08-08 21:45 AUSEST — surfaced to the operator with a recommendation on the third question only. The first two are the operator's and I am not answering them.

THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OPEN ITEM ON THE BOARD, and the filing worker was right to refuse it. HALF OF A KILL CRITERION HAS FIRED. K1 reads "mount above the amended mount gate (1.10x direct UIx on the clock of record) AFTER TWO SERIOUS RUNTIME ITERATIONS", and as of PR #7704 the gate half is measured, published, and missed decisively — both whole intervals above 1.10x on K1's own floor-normalised estimand. The conjunction has not fired, because the second conjunct is a judgement nobody has made.

ON (3) — WHETHER THE K1 ROW CARRIES THE MEASURED VERDICT REGARDLESS OF THE TRIGGER QUESTION — I RECOMMEND YES, and I would treat it as the least contentious of the three. A kill table whose criterion is half-satisfied and does not say so is not neutral; it reads to a fresh reader as "nothing has happened here". The programme's own annotate-never-erase discipline exists precisely so a record cannot quietly lag its evidence, and this is the highest-stakes table in the corpus to let lag. Recording "the gate half is measured as MISSED, DECISIVELY (rf2-diaud, PR #7704, figures at rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md section 4.3); the two-iterations conjunct is not adjudicated here" costs nothing, decides nothing, and stops the table misleading. It is also a citation update rather than a ruling once (1) and (2) are set aside — so if the operator agrees, it dispatches immediately as a worker task.

ON (1) AND (2) I AM NOT RECOMMENDING, and I want to be explicit about why rather than appear to have overlooked them. "Two serious runtime iterations" is a judgement about whether this candidate has had its fair attempts, and K1's consequence is "stop or narrow" — that is the P2 fork in miniature, on the same evidence the sitting is being convened to weigh. Answering it here would pre-empt the sitting from a bead. The relevant record exists (rf2-nld4g closed with no admissible attack clearing the bar; the interpreter was exonerated at 0.9636x stock Reagent, locating the deficit outside it) but assembling that into "two serious iterations, yes or no" is the operator's call and belongs at the table.

THE SITTING INTERACTION, which is why this cannot simply wait. The epic's freeze-open-as-open discipline says an item still open at the 2026-08-25 freeze is frozen AS OPEN and goes first on the agenda. This is now the strongest candidate for that slot — ahead of anything else outstanding — because it is the only open item that can change what the fork means rather than merely what it is priced at. If (1) is answered yes before the freeze, the sitting opens with a kill criterion tripped rather than with a trade to weigh.

ONE CORRECTION THE SWEEP MADE THAT IS WORTH READING WITH THIS: the-candidates-clock.md section 8 had been asserting "Still not a clear K1 kill" against the RETIRED trigger ("> Reagent", superseded by rf2-hyd50 on 2026-08-05). So the page was reassuring on a criterion that no longer existed. It is struck and annotated now, with the amended denominator and the published verdict, and it says in terms that the two-iterations question is not decided there.
OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-10 02:59 AUSEST, Mike, in session) — OPTION A, all three questions:
(1) The two-serious-runtime-iterations condition IS MET. Basis: rf2-nld4g closed with no admissible attack clearing the bar; the interpreter was exonerated at 0.9636x stock Reagent, locating the deficit outside it.
(2) K1 is therefore TRIPPED, and its consequence 'stop or narrow' is SUPERSEDED by the operator's selection of Hicasso plus the prospective scoped price-acceptance amendment (rf2-hic-003, operative default; 1.25x product ceiling; reconsideration trigger). The outcome is a formalized narrow-and-price, not a stop.
(3) validation.md's K1 row gets a dated annotation: gate half measured MISSED, DECISIVELY (rf2-diaud, PR #7704, figures at rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md section 4.3); two-iterations conjunct ruled MET this date; consequence superseded by the amendment — with the pointer.
EXECUTION: this bead is now dispatchable worker work — annotate the K1 row per (3), annotate-never-erase, slug check green. Material for the sitting packet: the sitting ratifies the amendment; no tripped-criterion surprise remains.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7733 (complete): completeness, correctness, and implementation-quality review passed. The merged change faithfully records the 2026-08-10 operator ruling in the K1 row and clock page, preserves the registered criterion and superseded sentence verbatim, leaves the 1.10x gate and published miss untouched, and links the canonical evidence. Doc-slug, provenance-pin (2 files/11 pins), and diff-check gates exit 0; the kill table remains 8 rows x 2 columns. Closing state remains correct.

The operator ruling of 2026-08-10 02:59 AUSEST (Option A, all three questions) is now recorded on validation.md's K1 row plus a dated note beneath the kill-criteria table, and studio/the-candidates-clock.md section 8 is brought into agreement: gate half measured MISSED, DECISIVELY (rf2-diaud, PR #7704, figures at rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md section 4.3); two-iterations conjunct ruled MET 2026-08-10; consequence 'stop or narrow' superseded by the selection of Hicasso plus the scoped price-acceptance amendment rf2-hic-003 (operative default, 1.25x proposed ceiling, reconsideration trigger) - a formalized narrow-and-price, not a stop. title: RULING NEEDED: rf2-t2flm publishes an M1 magnitude that rf2-8a746's whole-interval rule refuses
notes:
RAISED BY rf2-x7x10 (PR for the mount-class calibration), 2026-08-08. Surfaced by
implementation, not decided by it.

WHAT rf2-x7x10 DID. It calibrated the check standard's `mount` class from the
mount's own 14 committed row-runs (centre 1.7956x, location [1.6765, 1.9147],
dispersion <= 0.577), which restored the M1 row's reproduction path: all 14 runs
come back IN CONTROL, so clock_readjudicate.cjs prints a reportable subset again
rather than "reportable subset: NONE".

THE COLLISION THAT BECAME VISIBLE. With runs reportable, rf2-8a746's part-4
publication rule reaches M1 FOR THE FIRST TIME — it could not before, because an
effect-size interval needs a pooled run to be formed from. Over the committed
corpus it returns INSTRUMENT-LIMITED on every pair of both ensembles:

  hicasso / uix-subs      emvod 1.1679x [1.1259 - 1.2096] n=8
                          w3yxd 1.1621x [1.1209 - 1.2090] n=6
  hicasso / reagent-subs  emvod 1.1142x [1.0238 - 1.1988] n=8
                          w3yxd 1.1151x [1.0314 - 1.1955] n=6
  uix-subs / reagent-subs emvod 0.9540x [0.8835 - 1.0139] n=8
                          w3yxd 0.9596x [0.8962 - 1.0209] n=6

The reason is NOT that the row is noisy. On the two hicasso pairs the WHOLE
interval lies above 1.0 — parity is excluded and the direction is intact — but
rf2-8a746 publishes a magnitude only when the whole interval clears the 1.0 ship
bar BELOW or the 1.5 architecture-kill ABOVE, and ~1.16x clears neither DECISION
threshold.

SO TWO RULINGS OF THE SAME DAY (2026-08-07) NOW DISAGREE ON THIS ROW.
rf2-t2flm publishes ~1.184x against direct UIx-on-subs. rf2-8a746 part 4 says a
row publishes a magnitude only on a whole interval clearing a threshold.

WHAT rf2-x7x10 DID ABOUT IT: nothing but record it. The studio page's section 4.3
carries a dated supersession stating the re-adjudication and both intervals, and
the bolded magnitudes are marked HELD PENDING A RULING rather than withdrawn
(annotate-never-erase). clock_exit_path.test.cjs pins publishes === false with a
message saying that a flip is a RULING to be made and not a test to be updated.

NOTE FOR THE RULING. rf2-8a746's acceptance criterion 3 pinned the interval rule
on the committed 42-run corpus, which is BULK ONLY, and its own text sequences the
freeze "before the next BULK window opens" while handing the mount half to
rf2-t2flm by id. So whether part 4's ship/kill thresholds were ever intended to
adjudicate a MOUNT row — where the claim is a deficit rather than a win, and the
1.0/1.5 pair may simply be the wrong thresholds for it — is a live question and
possibly the whole answer.

SITTING INPUT: K1's line for the 2026-08-27 sitting is that ~1.18x figure, so this

title: hicasso: :p0/write-all's fixed per-write cost makes the allocation ladder uncertifiable at any page size
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.138's window on 2026-08-08 (PR #7691). This is the
structural result of that window and it outranks the sizing question.

THE FIXED COST, measured for the first time on this rig. :p0/write-all
rebuilds a 300-element vector and drives the whole event pipeline whether
one boundary is mounted or 1,200. The floor arm is precisely that write with
no subscription under it, and it reads:

  reagent-subs  24,108 B per write
  uix-subs      24,730 B per write

Call it F ~ 24.4 KB. F DOES NOT SHRINK WHEN B DOES.

WHY THAT IS FATAL TO THE CURRENT ROUTE. The masking bound (rf2-n6w7o)
charges (W+1).perWrite <= 300,000 B. At the six-write averaging floor that
allows 42,857 B per write -- and F alone is 57% of it, before a single
boundary has been measured. Modelling perWrite ~ F + B.s(R) off the run's
own arms, the largest page each rung admits (worst arm per rung, since a
ladder holds ONE B fixed across all rungs) is:

  rung   s (B/bnd/write)   W=1   W=3   W=6
  R=1      2,031- 4,067     30    12     4
  R=3      4,888- 5,904     21     8     3
  R=7      9,246-10,158     12     4     1
  R=20     6,800-22,174      5     2     0

AT SIX WRITES THERE IS NO PAGE OF ONE BOUNDARY OR MORE THAT CERTIFIES THE
1/3/7/20 LADDER. At W=1 there is (B <= 5), but W=1 is the configuration that
produced r2 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31 for want of averaging, and at B=5 the fixed
cost is F/B ~ 4,884 B/boundary/write -- close to twice the entire first-read
signal, with a round-to-round spread (floor moves 21,840-24,432 B/write over
six rounds) that lands on the fit as noise on the rung with the least signal.
Those s(R) are read off windows the run refused as under-reading, so each is
a LOWER bound and the squeeze is at least this tight.

SO 'SHRINK THE MEASURED UNIT' HAS A FLOOR, and the floor is F. The route
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md
recommended has now been tried and measured, and the page records it.

THE TWO ROUTES LEFT, both design questions rather than sizing ones:

  (a) A CHEAPER WRITE on this bench, so F stops consuming the budget. The
      300-element vector rebuild is per-write and independent of the arm; if
      the write could touch only the mounted boundaries, F would fall with B
      and the whole squeeze relaxes. This is the likelier route and it is a
      p0_arms.cljs / p0_heap.cljs question.
  (b) A BOUND THAT DOES NOT CHARGE (W+1).perWrite -- i.e. route (a) of
      rf2-n6w7o, an independent in-window collection witness, which would
      let a window be certified by what it OBSERVED rather than by its size.
      Note the merged-PR audit of #7682 already disputes the present bound's
      soundness on separate grounds (see the sibling bead).

DO NOT discharge this by widening the budget or by dropping the R=20 rung:
R=20 is HD-002's own ladder and the budget exists to refuse under-reads.

CRITERION 1 DISCHARGED — the design brief is written and open as PR #7697 (branch worker/allocdesign-140). The bead STAYS OPEN: criteria 2-6 are the implementation and its validity witnesses.

WHERE IT LIVES: docs/design/hicasso/allocation-instrument-rework.md, tracked, linked from docs/design/hicasso/README.md, with a forward pointer from the studio page's "next attempt" item. No code, no measurement.

WHAT THE BRIEF SETTLES:

WRITE HALF. A new :p0/write-page rebuilds :cells at the width the mounted page actually reads. The grid width becomes a property of the seeded app-db (seed-db takes it; :p0/fan's modulus reads (count (:cells db))), so it cannot live in two places and drift. :p0/write-all is left byte-identical and the clock/bulk rows keep driving it. The EQUIVALENCE ARGUMENT: same dispatch-sync through the same pipeline and signal graph; every one of the E = B.R edges sees a changed value so the invalidation set is identical; the rendered text is (str (* R v)) under either write so the read-back and canonical-DOM gate are unchanged; B, E, Q and the key rule untouched. The only difference is the width of a vector no boundary reads beyond its own slot -- machinery on both sides of the floor subtraction. On the 24-boundary page 276 of the 300 rebuilt cells were read by nothing.

WITNESS HALF. (W+1).perWrite <= ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B is RETIRED and replaced by a rule read off the window's own samples: the work legs are W repetitions of ONE work unit, so refuse if any leg deviates from the cohort MEDIAN by more than tau.m. A leg below the cohort is a leg something removed bytes from; a leg above it means the one-work-unit premise has failed, and refusing is then correct rather than merely conservative. The certificate is checkable rather than asserted: this window's rise under-reads by at most 2.tau, and here is the worst leg deviation observed.

THE TWO #7682 PROBES ARE REFUSED, and independently of the calibration. Probe A (60K x4 then a leg reading 0) and probe B (50K x5 then a leg reading 0) both have their offending leg at exactly zero against a strictly positive median, so both are refused for EVERY tau < 1 -- a re-calibration cannot silently re-admit them, and that property gets a test of its own. The net-growth masking fixture already in p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs is re-pointed at the new grounds.

CONSTRAINT SEMANTICS, as criterion 4 asks. The budget is RETIRED, not widened. Retaining it belt-and-braces was considered and REJECTED ON ARITHMETIC: at the composed operating point (B=4, R=20, W=6) a window is ~630 KB of rise+maxStep, so a retained bound would refuse every window the witness certifies and the package would deliver nothing. ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays at its measured 600,000 B and gates nothing. R=20 stays. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES=6 stays a floor. The falls gate is untouched.

FOUR VALIDITY WITNESSES, none of which publishes a slope. V1: the floor at B in {4,24,96} under BOTH writes -- the old write's flat F is the control that licenses the comparison, and an agreement at B=24 with the 2026-08-08 figures is what makes the two writes comparable at all. V2: the equivalence cross-check, one write per window at B=4, requiring (arm-floor)/B to AGREE between writes while the floor DROPS. V3: tau calibrated on control windows independently corroborated clean by their own 8 B/double prediction -- rf2-2rtt6.141's carried-in criterion answered. V4: the pinned probes, red-then-green.

ALSO CARRIED: the seam with rf2-2rtt6.139 (P0_ALLOC_CELLS becomes MANDATORY rather than a substituted constant -- no honest default exists without a sizing model, and it makes an accidental publication run impossible while criterion 5's freeze holds); a disposition for EVERY structural test the change supersedes (37 rows, KEPT / AMENDED / REPLACED / RETIRED); the criterion-6 supersession obligation; and one option recorded with its trigger and explicitly NOT taken.

WHY BOTH HALVES, NUMERICALLY (at R=20, worst arm s=22,174 B/bnd/write, W=6): today (42,857-24,400)/22,174 = B 0. Route (a) alone, bound kept: B 1 -- a one-boundary "ladder" is not one. Route (b) alone, write kept: B 3, on which F/B = 8,133 B/bnd is 2x-4x the whole R=1 signal. Composed: B 4 with F/B targeted under the R=1 signal. The ruling's claim reproduces arithmetically.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN AND WHY:

1. HOW MUCH OF F ~ 24.4 KB IS THE 300-CELL REBUILD AND HOW MUCH IS THE EVENT PIPELINE. Nobody has measured it and the brief may not. It is the single number the write half turns on. V1 answers it directly, and V1 is the gate on the whole write half -- if the pipeline residue F0 dominates, the write half narrows the gap without closing it, and the brief carries a three-step contingency ladder (raise B; carry F0 as a stated instrument constant; or the reserve option), with an explicit fence against responding by shrinking the page further.
2. THE VALUE OF tau. V3's to measure, on the stated calibration rule. Not a knob (ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B's reasoning unchanged).
3. THE OPERATING PAGE. B, and whether one B serves all four rungs, is rf2-2rtt6.139's per-rung re-derivation off the NEW instrument's floor data. The brief names B in {4,24,96} for V1 and B=4 for V2 as MEASUREMENT configurations, not as the row's page, and derives no sizing constant.
4. WHETHER A 3-TO-5 BOUNDARY PAGE IS A CREDIBLE WITNESS OF A PER-BOUNDARY QUANTITY AT ALL. The arm's per-page constants (React root, frame provider, root subscription) do not cancel against the floor and are divided by a very small B. The expectation is that an R-independent constant lands in the fit's INTERCEPT rather than its slope, and the R=0 shell rung is the direct check -- at B=24 it already reads close to the floor. V2's per-rung comparison is where it shows if that is wrong.
5. THE FINER-SAMPLING OPTION (3-4 samples per write instead of 2) is filed as an option rather than designed: a real sensitivity improvement and allocation-free, but it changes the leg cohort's meaning. V3 decides whether it is needed.

ONE DOWNSTREAM EFFECT ON A CLOSED BEAD, flagged rather than silently taken: rf2-2rtt6.142's refusal text BRANCHES on whether the page can carry six writes, and that second branch is computed from the budget. With the budget retired its trigger no longer exists and the refusal collapses to one branch. That is not a regression -- with no page-size model there is nothing to name, and the endorsed property (never advise the shape being refused) is preserved by there being no such advice to give -- but .142 is CLOSED and its close reason describes the two-branch behaviour, so the implementer records the collapse on that bead when the change lands. .142's ROUTE 2 pin (an explicit one-write window is refused) survives unchanged and must stay green; its ROUTE 1 pin is re-pointed at the mandatory-page refusal.

CRITERIA 2, 3, 4 AND 6 IMPLEMENTED — PR #7702 (branch worker/allocbuild-140), open, NOT merged. THE BEAD STAYS OPEN: criterion 5's measurement freeze stands and V1/V2/V3 remain.

NEITHER ARTEFACT HAS BEEN EXECUTED AGAINST A REAL PAGE, and that is the deliverable rather than a caveat on it. No allocation window was opened, no ladder row taken, no quiet box requested. :p0/write-page has never written to a mounted page; the leg witness has never read a real sample stream. Both are proven STRUCTURALLY ONLY — 50 hermetic pins in p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs and 9 hermetic CLJS deftests, every window a synthetic sample buffer and every frame a plain-atom test frame.

WHAT LANDED

WRITE (criterion 2). :p0/write-page rebuilds :cells at the width the mounted page reads. The grid width is a property of the SEEDED APP-DB — seed-db takes it, :p0/seed carries it, enter-segment! and p0-heap/prepare! thread it from the driver — and :p0/fan's modulus reads (count (:cells db)), so it cannot live in two places and drift. :p0/write-all is byte-identical, literal cells-n and all; the clock, bulk, fan-out and retention rows keep driving it at the published 300, and a structural pin reads that off the CLJS sources rather than trusting it. The width threaded is B = ROOTS x P0_ALLOC_CELLS — one cell per mounted boundary, which keeps the change FULL-PAGE (the brief rejects a one-cell grid as converting a full-page change into a point change, and HD-002's law is stated about the change).

WITNESS (criterion 3). The budget is retired; refusal is now "any leg deviates from the cohort MEDIAN by more than tau.m". allocSteps grows legs, gaps, legMedian, legWorstDeviation, refusals and certified, mirroring allocArmSizing's verdict shape since .142. rise/fall/falls/maxStep/endpoints keep their definitions, so no published total changes meaning. allocMaskableWindows -> allocRefusedWindows, naming every refused window with its reason.

CONSTRAINTS (criterion 4). ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B stays at 600,000 B and gates nothing (the summary prints the largest arm rise as a percentage of it). R=20 stays. ALLOC_MIN_WRITES=6 stays a floor. Falls gate and r2 floor untouched. ALLOC_B_PER_BOUNDARY_WRITE, allocMaxWrites, predictedWindowB, headroom, maxBoundaries, floorBoundaries and maskable are deleted. P0_ALLOC_CELLS is MANDATORY.

CRITERION 6 WAS DONE HERE, and the dispatch said it was outstanding — the bead governs. Criterion 6 says the studio page annotates "once the new write lands", and the brief says "the implementation PR adds a dated note to that page". The write lands in #7702, so the annotation rides with it: a dated supersession note at the head and at the small-witness section of the-survival-metrics-allocation-half.md, every figure and every table standing, F_old named as the one figure that keeps its full force because V1 re-measures it as the control that licenses the comparison.

TAU IS AN UNCALIBRATED PLACEHOLDER at 0.25, marked as such in the source with V3 named as what calibrates it. Conservative in the direction that matters (a smaller tau refuses more). No window may be published on it. Nothing pinned depends on it.

MUTATION PROOFS, red-then-green in two commits (059d4fb red, 72d4eaa green). p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs: 6/56 failed at the red commit. Five pins reported `certified` undefined; the MANDATORY-PAGE pin failed on a value — `true !== false` — which is the sharper red, because the shipped preflight really did derive and admit an arm with no page stated. Structural counts 50 -> 49 (disposition) -> 50 (the certificate pin below).

NOTHING LOOSENED, established three ways because the phrase means three things once criterion 4 retires the budget:
(1) FALLS GATE: exhaustive over 17,496 synthetic window shapes against the shipped module — 0 violations, every falling-step window still refused.
(2) PREFLIGHT: exhaustive over W 0..40 x cells 0..40 x roots {0,1,4,50} — 4,200 admitted, every one satisfying both surviving .142 terms, and ZERO arms satisfying those terms refused. The one new refusal is the unstated page.
(3) WINDOW GATE: subset is the WRONG test and I say so rather than claiming otherwise — retiring the budget necessarily admits windows it refused, the brief's arithmetic requires it (a ~630 KB window must be admittable), and the disposition retires THE CHANGE ONLY EVER REFUSES MORE for exactly that reason. In the sweep 36 of 17,496 moved refused->admitted and ALL 36 are over the retired 300,000 B budget, so none is a masked window slipping through. What replaces the subset claim: both audit probes moved from admitted (headroom exactly 0, true allocations 300 KB and 600 KB) to refused; 98.1% of masked windows (4,527 of 4,617) are refused by the leg rule; and the 2-tau certificate HOLDS TIGHT.

THE 2-TAU CERTIFICATE IS NOW PINNED, and this is the one addition worth the operator's attention. Swept over 20,096 windows INSIDE THE COHORT PREMISE (the certificate's own stated antecedent): worst per-leg masked reclamation 50.00% of the median against a 2-tau ceiling of 50%, worst whole-window under-read 10.00%. The worst case is EXACTLY the shape the brief predicts — a leg sitting tau.m high on its own merits, losing 2.tau.m, reading tau.m low, admitted at the very edge — and one byte further refuses. So 2-tau is a bound rather than an approximation, and the implementation realises the certificate the brief specified, tight. Outside the premise the certificate says nothing and the brief says so.

GATES, all foreground to completion from WORKTREE_ROOT=/c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/allocbuild-140: node --check both .cjs 0; p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs 0 (50 passed); npm run test:script-helpers 0; npm run test:cljs 0 (12,812 tests / 64,426 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors); sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh 0; npm run lint:js 0; python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py 0; sh scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh origin/main 0. It cleared on re-run and the full spine went green.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD:

This is the gate on the whole write half and the brief carries a three-step contingency ladder under it.

MEASUREMENT WINDOW REFUSED — 2026-08-13 23:49 AUSEST, on the granted quiet box,
branch worker/allocfloor-140 off dac7f439dd. First of the nine lane windows.
NO ALLOCATION WINDOW WAS OPENED, no browser was launched, no bundle was built.
The refusal is structural and it is located in source.

THE BOX WAS QUIET AND THAT IS NOT WHY IT REFUSED. Recorded because the next
window should not have to re-establish it: queue length 0 across every sample in
every phase (5 before, 4 during); CPU 5.7-13.0%; free RAM 30.0 of 63.4 GB. 93
node/java/chrome processes were resident holding 13.4 GB — materially more than
the previous lane window's 20 at 1.2 GB — and I judged them immaterial on
evidence rather than on the queue alone: across all 93, total CPU accrued over a
6-second interval was 0.16 cpu-seconds, i.e. 0.027 of one core on a 24-thread
box, with no single process above 0.05. 72 of them are the operator's own Chrome
session. No `.shadow-cljs/server.pid` exists in either checkout, so no zombie
compile server could have served a stale build. The box would have admitted the
window.

WHAT REFUSED IT: V1, V2 AND V3 CANNOT BE CONFIGURED ON THE SHIPPED INSTRUMENT.
Not "came back out of band" — cannot be expressed. Each verified against source
and reproduced executably.

V1 — ITS CONTROL ARM IS PINNED OUT OF THE INSTRUMENT.
V1 is "the floor at three page sizes ... under BOTH writes", and F_old is not
decoration: the brief makes it V1's control ("it says the rig has not moved
under the instrument, and it is the only way the two writes can be compared like
for like", :260-263), and criterion 6 rests on it (":631"). The allocation
window cannot drive it. `p0_heap.cljs:1111` hard-codes
`(arms/write-page! @alloc-tick)`; no env var, no `kind`, no parameter reaches
`write-all!`. And `p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:978` PINS that:
`assert.doesNotMatch(HEAP, /\(arms\/write-all! /, 'and never write-all!')`.

Demonstrated rather than asserted. A one-line plant at p0_heap.cljs:1111 adding
a selector took the suite from 53 passed / exit 0 to 1/53 failed / exit 1, the
single failure being that pin — which simultaneously proves the gate read this
worktree, proves the plant was scoped (one failure, no cascade), and proves the
claim. Restore verified byte-identical by `git hash-object` against the
committed object (ef9b5adcf0), re-run 53 passed / exit 0.

The three V1 pages themselves are fine — P0_ROOTS=4 with P0_ALLOC_CELLS 1/6/24
derives B = 4/24/96, all admissible, no refusals. It is only the control arm
that is unreachable.

V2 — REFUSED BY ITS OWN PACKAGE'S PREFLIGHT, AND INDEPENDENTLY BY V1'S BLOCKER.
V2 specifies one write per window (:293). `allocArmSizing` refuses
`writes < ALLOC_MIN_WRITES = 6` before a browser launches, pinned as ROUTE 2.
Reproduced: `P0_ALLOC_CELLS=1 P0_ALLOC_WRITES=1` -> admissible:false. V2 also
needs both writes in the same run, so V1's blocker takes it a second time.
Filed as rf2-qomo, which is a RULING and not a widening — the floor's stated
ground is a precondition on FITTING and V2 takes no fit, but the obvious fix
("run V2 at six writes") is not free: the brief's own arithmetic puts B=4/R=20/
W=6 at ~630 KB against a measured collection onset of 600,000 B.

V3 — NO CONTROLS-ONLY MODE EXISTS.
V3 is "the controls only ... No arms" (:443-445). `--only alloc` has one shape:
preflight, then controls AND the full ladder plan every round. The mode surface
is closed (`clock | heap | fanout | ladder | alloc`) and the no-arms route is
shut by the preflight — `P0_ALLOC_CELLS=0` refuses correctly for want of a
per-boundary quantity. V3's controls are reachable only by riding a full ladder
run: ~108 ladder-arm windows to harvest 18 control windows, and criterion 5
freezes every allocation window that is not V1-V4.

WHAT I REFUSED TO DO, each with its reason, because these were live choices.

1. I did NOT build the write selector and measure through it. It is ~one line in
   `alloc-window!` plus a pin amendment, and the box was granted and idle. Shape
   6 forbids improving the rig mid-window, and the substantive reason is
   criterion 5's own: a window taken on an instrument written minutes earlier,

   instrument window the freeze exists to prevent. Filed as rf2-gxrr instead.

   turns an assertion into an experiment with a control in it" (:250-251).

3. I did NOT measure F_old by building an older commit. Two writes measured on

4. I did NOT ride a full ladder run to harvest V3's controls. It needs no rig

code with hermetic pins and no measurement — so it can be dispatched

quiet box, branch worker/allocv1-140 off 457ac7f173, PR #8152 (docs only).
V1, V2 AND V3 ALL RAN. Nine browser runs, one at a time. THE BEAD STAYS OPEN:
V1's and V2's criteria came back UNASSESSED rather than answered, and two new P1
blockers are filed.

EVERY RUN'S POSITIVE CONTROL PASSED, reported per run and never pooled: 8.08
B/double direct, 8.00 B/double differential against a predicted 8, idle 32
B/iteration, in all nine. No run was excluded and none was pooled with another.

8 during V1, 7 during V2). Two spikes -- 26/14 at 04:23 and 38 at 04:34 -- both
inside this window's own shadow-cljs release compile, not a measured phase.

p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs 59 passed / exit 0 on this worktree.

=== V1 -- THE BRIEF'S LARGEST OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND IT WENT THE WAY THE
BRIEF FEARED ===

The question was how much of F ~ 24.4 KB is the 300-cell rebuild and how much is
the event pipeline. IT IS THE PIPELINE.

  F_old - F_new = 1.1 - 1.9 KB per write, at EVERY page size
  w = 3.6 - 7.3 B/cell, consistent across six independent readings
  F0 ~ 18 - 19.4 KB, i.e. OVER 90% OF F

The boundary-proportional write works exactly as designed and removes roughly 7%
of the problem. F_new is flat in B for the same reason F_old is.

THE CONTROL LANDED ON ITS FIRST CLAUSE AND IS UNASSESSED ON ITS SECOND.
  - "F_old flat in B" -- HOLDS. reagent-subs 19,898/19,781/19,898 and uix-subs
    20,487/20,446/20,487 across B in {4,24,96}: flat to 0.6% over a 24x range.

    the per-round ranges, but no certified window exists to read the clause from.
    Not missed -- not assessed.

V1's CRITERION, F_new(B)/B under the ~2 KB bar (read off refused windows):
  B=4    4,497 / 4,854 B/bnd/write   OVER
  B=24     767 /   798               under
  B=96     192 /   200               under

THE TWO CONSTRAINTS DO NOT CROSS, and this closes contingency (i) by measurement.
Clearing the fixed-residue bar needs B >= 9.0-9.7 (F0/B <= 2,000). Keeping a
six-write R=20 window under the 600,000 B onset needs B <= 1.9-2.5 (perWrite <=
100,000 with s(20) = 32,058-43,263 B/bnd/write measured by V2). THE SMALLEST PAGE
THIS RIG CAN MOUNT IS B=4 AND IT SATISFIES NEITHER. Raising B relieves one bound
and worsens the other at the rate the worst rung sets, so the gap does not close
by moving B. Contingency (ii) -- carry F0 as a stated instrument constant the
floor subtracts -- is the step the data points at.

=== V2 -- THE R=20 RUNG'S VERDICT UNDER rf2-qomo: REFUSED, AND THE PREDICTION WAS
OPTIMISTIC ===

Run at SIX WRITES as ruled. The ruling forecast ~630 KB against the 600,000 B
onset. MEASURED: 900 KB - 1.5 MB, i.e. 1.5x-2.5x the onset rather than 1.05x --

  all  reagent|hicasso R20   920,386 - 1,172,582   7 falls
  all  reagent|reagent R20   983,866 - 1,510,710   9 falls
  all  uix|hicasso R20       903,386 - 1,494,586   8 falls
  all  uix|uix R20           912,926 -   933,082   0 falls  <- certified 6/6
  page reagent|hicasso R20   908,454 - 1,095,490   7 falls
  page reagent|reagent R20   976,130 - 1,013,450   7 falls
  page uix|hicasso R20       897,054 - 1,412,554   5 falls
  page uix|uix R20           904,014 - 1,030,330   1 fall

Falls concentrate there: 24 of the all run's 27 and 20 of the page run's 28.
ONE ARM IS NAMED RATHER THAN AVERAGED AWAY: uix|uix R20 under write-all certified
6/6 with zero falls -- the cheapest R=20 arm (leg median ~150 KB against ~180-200
KB) sitting just under the onset. Under write-page it refused 1/6. One arm, one
write, one segment is not the rung passing.

THE RUNG WAS NOT DROPPED, NOT RE-RUN UNTIL IT PASSED, AND
ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B WAS NOT WIDENED. The refusal is the result, as ruled.

V2's OWN CRITERION IS UNASSESSED. (arm-floor)/B needs a certified floor and THE
FLOOR CERTIFIED 0 OF 6 WINDOWS IN BOTH RUNS ON BOTH SEGMENTS. Recorded as an
INDICATION ONLY, off refused windows: agreement is 0.0-2.4% at every
subscription-bearing rung on both substrates and both segments, and the floor
drops 1,688/1,719 B (7.3%). That is the shape the equivalence argument predicts
and it is NOT V2 passing.

=== V3 -- DELIVERED, AND ITS ANSWER HAS A STING ===

The only run of the nine to exit 0. Controls' worst relative leg deviation 0.99%;
11 of 12 windows read EXACTLY 0.00% with six byte-identical legs; idle 0.00%.

TAU WAS NOT PINNED. Pinning is a source edit and a measurement window does not
amend the instrument it measures on. And the calibration has a consequence worth
the operator's attention: applying V3's stated rule lands tau at ~0.02-0.05, at
which a window certifies only above ~230 KB leg median -- which NO ARM reaches
except R=20, and R=20 is already refused by the collector. AN HONEST CALIBRATION
WOULD REFUSE THE ENTIRE LADDER. The 0.25 placeholder is more permissive than the
calibrated value, and it already refuses every floor window. Filed as rf2-e9wr.

=== WHAT REFUSED EVERYTHING, AND IT IS ONE TERM ===

EVERY ARM WINDOW MEASURED -- 336 OF 336 across eight browser runs -- has a
positive first-leg excess over its own cohort median: min 3,441 / median 6,966 /
max 28,448 B. CONSTANT IN ABSOLUTE BYTES across a 24x page range, IDENTICAL under
both writes, surviving all three full-size warm-ups. Tail legs are byte-identical
to each other (one window: 26044, 19256, 19256, 19256, 19256, 19256), so the
precision is excellent and leg 1 is the sole deviant. Collector events look
different and appear separately as NEGATIVE legs.

A fixed ~7 KB excess refuses any window whose median is under 6,966/0.25 ~ 27,900
B. That predicts the observed refusal in 290 of 336 windows (86.3%), and all 46
disagreements are windows refused for an ADDITIONAL reason, never ones the rule
spared. The admissible band is two-sided: above ~28 KB/write for the excess to sit
inside tau, below ~100 KB/write for six writes to clear the onset.

THE FLOOR IS BELOW THAT BAND IN ALL SIXTEEN RUN x SEGMENT CASES, and the floor is
F, and F IS FLAT IN B -- so NO PAGE SIZE MOVES IT IN. Since arm - floor is what
every witness is stated over, the rungs that certify cannot be differenced against
a floor that never does. THIS IS THIS BEAD'S OWN SHAPE ONE LEVEL DOWN: the bead
recorded that shrinking the measured unit has a floor and it is F; the window
records that CERTIFYING it has a floor too, and it is the same F. Filed as
rf2-oiy1.

1. I did NOT repair the first-leg excess. ~One line to the warm-up or the leg
   accounting, box idle and granted. A window on an instrument amended minutes
   earlier with no red-then-green proof IS the uncertified-instrument window

   than building it. Filed as rf2-oiy1 instead.
2. I did NOT pin tau, though the window measured the figure that sets it, because
   pinning is a source edit and because the honest value would refuse the ladder.
3. I did NOT widen ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B, drop the R=20 rung, or retry it until
   it passed. It ran once per write and its refusal is reported as the result.
4. I did NOT report V1's control clause or V2's criterion as MISSED. Both are
   UNASSESSED -- there is no certified floor window to read either from -- and
   that distinction is the one this lane has already had to correct in public.
5. I did NOT pool or exclude any run. All nine controls are reported separately
   and all nine passed.
6. I did NOT publish a slope. The floor and controls plans fit nothing; the two
   V2 runs do fit and nothing from those fits is quoted.
7. I did NOT fix the "windows refused: 17 of 12" summary defect I found (filed
   rf2-xxeq, P3) -- a one-line summariser edit would have invalidated the nine
   runs it appeared in.
8. WIDENED NOTHING: ALLOC_MIN_WRITES 6, ALLOC_FALL_THRESHOLD_B 600,000,
   ALLOC_LEG_TOLERANCE 0.25 with its marker, R=20, ALLOC_CONTROL_SLACK 0.75 -- all
   untouched. The PR is docs-only.

=== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LANE ===

This bead cannot discharge: V1's control clause and V2's criterion are unassessed
and both are blocked behind rf2-oiy1 (the first-leg excess), with rf2-e9wr behind
it for tau. Both are INSTRUMENT work needing no quiet box, so both are
dispatchable alongside anything.

rf2-2rtt6.139 gets something real from this window even so: V1's floor data
exists, at three pages under both writes, with F_old's flatness confirmed to 0.6%
-- but it is read off refused windows and .139 should be told that before it
re-derives sizing on it.

WHAT THIS COST AND BOUGHT: nine browser runs on an idle box. It answered the
brief's single largest open question with a number (F0 is over 90% of F), closed
contingency (i) by arithmetic on measured values, delivered the R=20 verdict the
ruling asked for, delivered V3's calibration input, and located the witness half's

DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

SECOND CROSS-REFERENCE FROM THE BACKLOG REREAD, mayor 2026-08-18 11:45 AUSEST. This one bears on whether V2's residual can be ASSESSED at all, not just on how precisely.

rf2-irxrw, filed today by rf2-0gjqi's re-analysis and derived at source without taking a window, reports that THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT DRIVE BOTH WRITES IN ONE PROCESS. ALLOC_WRITE is read once from process.env at module scope (p0_run.cjs:1504), ALLOC_WRITE_SPECS has exactly two members and no paired option (:1490), and the resolved kind is passed into every arm window of the run (:2335, :2342). So one process drives ONE write, necessarily.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is structural rather than statistical: every write-all versus write-page comparison this instrument has ever produced differences TWO SEQUENTIAL PROCESS RUNS IN A FIXED ORDER. allocation-instrument-rework.md:231-232 requires those two writes to be compared as a same-page, same-run pair. They never have been.

WHY THIS TOUCHES THIS BEAD. V2's criterion is about the arm-floor residual, and the residual is exactly the quantity that comparison produces. Until a paired mode exists, V2's residual is UNASSESSED rather than small - and that is the merged-PR audit's own word, recorded on rf2-0gjqi on 2026-08-17.

WHAT THE RE-ANALYSIS ADDED to that audit, and it sharpens it considerably. The eight mid-rung sign comparisons that looked like 1-in-256 are EIGHT CELLS, ONE DRAW: they share one run order; the four reagent-subs cells difference against the SAME four certified floor windows; and rf2-77gz8's second floor mode moves both segments by exactly the same 3,792 B, which merges the segments too. A shared floor offset of 2,472 B/write on reagent-subs, or 928 on uix-subs, reverses every sign - and three runs at one revision under one write span 3,852 / 3,912 B/write in certified floor median. Both exceed what it takes to flip the result.

WHAT IT DID NOT CLAIM, and the restraint is worth preserving: it did NOT adopt the mode account. A floor offset is additive and identical across a segment's arms, while the observed mid-rung offsets span 1,948 / 740 B/write and within an arm family the residual is closer to a constant proportion. Right magnitude, wrong shape - neither excluded nor supported. The cause is UNRESOLVED; only the inferential claim is refuted.

SO THE RULING ON THIS BEAD NOW HAS A PREREQUISITE THAT DID NOT EXIST YESTERDAY: rf2-irxrw's paired mode. Ruling before it lands would rule on a residual nobody can yet measure. That is not an argument for any particular disposition of the ladder - it is an argument about what evidence a defensible ruling can rest on, and it is the second such constraint recorded here today.

NOT DISPATCHED, NOTHING CHANGED HERE.

MAYOR RULING ON CRITERION 5, 2026-08-19 00:05 AUSEST, taken on Mike's standing delegation. This criterion has owed a ruling since the paired mode landed, and the 2026-08-18 re-read poses it cleanly enough to answer.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING ON. rf2-0gjqi's question — whether ~1-4% of non-cancellation is tolerable — is WITHDRAWN, and rightly: under matched within-round pairing the agreement half no longer shows a direction at all (page reads below all at 10 of 16 mid-rung cell medians, not 8 of 8, with the absolute median falling from 1.68% to 0.46%), and the sign that WAS there tracks which leg pass ran SECOND rather than which write it was. That is rf2-fk6pj's subject, not this one.

THE QUESTION AS IT NOW STANDS: is the instrument's residual non-cancellation acceptable, given that its R=0 NULL ARM — boundaries that read nothing, so arm minus floor must be exactly zero under either write — reads an absolute median of 1.5 B per boundary and a 90th percentile of 4.5, over 38 paired certified observations?

RULING: ACCEPT IT, AND PUBLISH IT AS A NAMED FLOOR RATHER THAN AS A TOLERANCE.

WHY ACCEPT. The null arm's reading is the instrument's own noise floor measured directly, which is the best possible way to have it: not inferred, not modelled, but read off an arm whose true value is known to be zero. And it is three orders of magnitude below the quantities the ladder publishes — the per-boundary terms this programme reports run 2,031 to 22,174 B per boundary per write, against which 1.5 B is roughly 0.07% and the p90 of 4.5 B is roughly 0.2%. An instrument does not need perfect cancellation; it needs a floor small against its signal and HONESTLY STATED.

WHY 'A NAMED FLOOR' RATHER THAN 'A TOLERANCE', and this is the part that matters. Ruling a PERCENTAGE tolerable would be the wrong shape: percentages travel, and a figure that is 0.07% of a 2,031 B term is 100% of a 1.5 B one. The number that is stable is the FLOOR ITSELF, in bytes per boundary, because that is what the null arm measures.

SO THE OBLIGATION THIS RULING CREATES, and it is one line of code and one of prose rather than new machinery:
  1. Record 1.5 B per boundary (median) and 4.5 B (p90) over 38 paired certified observations as the instrument's NON-CANCELLATION FLOOR, in the record beside the figures it qualifies.
  2. REFUSE, rather than publish, any per-boundary figure that is not comfortably above it. I set that bar at ten times the p90 — 45 B per boundary — because a figure within an order of magnitude of the noise floor is not a measurement, and the honest answer there is the same one rf2-2rtt6.139 reached about sizing: an instrument that says 'I cannot resolve this' is not a worse instrument.
Do NOT add a new gate, a new constant, or a rung parameter. The floor is a published number and a refusal the preflight can already express.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE. The floor-drop half stands as the re-read left it: 1,652 B (8.6%) on reagent-subs and 1,652-1,658 B (8.4%) on uix-subs, the same number on both segments to within 6 B across 21 paired certified rounds, against published unpaired figures of 1,769 / 1,765 B. Those published figures are now superseded by a within-round measurement and should be moved, with the change of basis stated — the same disclosure rule applied to S8 on rf2-6zc2q.

THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN carrying that work. Re-derive every number here at the tip before acting; they are quoted from a report, not measured by me.
