=== APPENDED MEASUREMENT (worker, rf2-a4x1o) — THE P0 CLOCK RED-ZONES, RE-DERIVED ON ONE WITNESS SET. These SUPERSEDE the CLOCK thresholds appended from rf2-2rtt6.4; they supersede NOTHING on the heap axis. Workers append; only the operator amends. ===

Full page: docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md

PRODUCING COMMIT 44900cd4fd35815b3e2462ae7752242efcb296b9
REPRO   node implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/p0_converge_run.cjs
        (run AT that commit on a clean tree; the figures below are that run's)
BUILD   :hicasso-bench — rf2-2rtt6.2's lane reused. NO new build id, NO
        implementation/shadow-cljs.edn change.
RUNTIME HeadlessChrome 147.0.7727.15 (Chromium/Playwright), Windows 11 x64;
        :advanced, goog.DEBUG false, plain :browser module. React 19.2.0,
        Reagent 2.0.1, UIx 1.4.4. BROWSER NUMBERS ONLY.
SCHEDULE 5 rounds x 2 adapter segments x (8 warm-up + 12 samples) per arm;
        three arms per segment interleaved at the sample level, order rotating
        AND reflecting; segment order alternating with the round; ONE ROW PER
        PAGE.

--- WHY THIS ARM EXISTS. rf2-2rtt6.4 measured the frontier on a 1,203-el W1
--- reading [:p0/row i], a 51-el W3 reading [:p0/field i] and a 301-el grid;
--- rf2-2rtt6.2 supplies the BAR'S DENOMINATOR on a 901-el M1 and a 51-el M2,
--- both reading [:p0/cell i]. Each of .4's ratios is sound AS A RATIO. The
--- TABLE was not, because a threshold and the bar row it qualifies were on
--- different pages. Converged onto rf2-2rtt6.2's witnesses: that arm is on
--- main, owns the lane per HD-017, is the denominator HD-012 states the bar
--- against, already carries the in-plan control and the labelled lower bound,
--- and .4's own Open items nominated it.

--- RED-ZONE, CLOCK: UIx-on-subs / Reagent-on-subs, both floor-normalised in
--- the same round and the same segment. 5 rounds, ranges are min-max.

  M1 mount (901 el, 300 boundaries, 1 sub/boundary)      [BAR ROW]
      1.2301x  [1.1099 - 1.3538]   UIx SLOWER, disjoint from 1.0
  M2 mount (51 el, 12 fields, 1 sub/field)               [DIAGNOSTIC ONLY]
      1.0539x  [0.8572 - 1.4286]   STRADDLES 1.0 -> INDISTINGUISHABLE
  BULK BROAD (M1 page, one commit ALL 300 read)          [BAR ROW]
      0.6239x  [0.4701 - 0.7857]   UIx FASTER, disjoint from 1.0
  BULK NARROW (M1 page, one commit exactly ONE reads)    [NOT RESOLVED]
      1.1556x  [1.0417 - 1.2500]   direction UIx-slower, but see STABILITY

  Against the floor: reagent-subs 4.352 / 2.102 / 7.443 / 1.820;
                     uix-subs     5.343 / 2.261 / 4.607 / 2.117.

--- HOW MUCH THE MISMATCH MATTERED: THREE OF FOUR VERDICTS FLIP.

  large-list mount  .4 W1  1.057 [0.907-1.156] INDISTINGUISHABLE
                    ->  M1 1.2301 [1.110-1.354] UIx SLOWER, DISJOINT
  form mount        .4 W3  0.893 [0.843-0.956] UIx faster, DISJOINT, published
                            as a THRESHOLD
                    ->  M2 1.0539 [0.857-1.429] INDISTINGUISHABLE, and graded
                            DIAGNOSTIC to match its bar row
  broad commit      .4 U-broad 0.838 [0.760-0.953] -> 0.6239 [0.470-0.786]
                            same direction, MUCH larger margin
  narrow commit     .4 U-narrow 1.536 [1.226-1.876] DISJOINT
                    ->  1.1556 / 1.0405 depending on the run: direction the
                            same, strength COLLAPSES, does not stably resolve

  MECHANISM. The broad margin widens on the 901-el page because more of the
  window is markup construction, where UIx's compile-time $ beats Reagent's
  runtime hiccup walk; the narrow margin narrows because the floor's top-down
  re-render — the thing a narrow write is compared against — is 3x the work.
  A clock ratio on this axis moves by more than the effects being measured
  when the page changes. That is the whole case for converging.

--- A GRADE MISMATCH THAT IS NOT ABOUT WITNESSES AT ALL. rf2-2rtt6.2 grades its
--- 51-element form row DIAGNOSTIC and says it must not be quoted against the
--- bar (3-6 clock quanta at one mount a sample). rf2-2rtt6.4 batched 8 mounts a
--- sample, lifted the same-sized witness clear of the clamp, and published its
--- form row as a THRESHOLD. So a candidate's form row would have been judged
--- red against a threshold whose bar-row counterpart is unquotable. Resolved
--- here by grading the converged form row diagnostic, like its bar row.

--- ONE ARM RE-RUN, NOT TWO. THE HEAP AXIS WAS ALREADY CONVERGED IN SUBSTANCE.
  .4 list (1,203-el page)     2.262x [2.196-2.335]
  .4 grid (301-el page)       2.254x [2.217-2.288]
  .5 ladder (1,200 bnd, 1 rd) 2.435x  (3,811 B / 1,565 B above a React floor)
  Three shapes differing 4x in markup density and 4x in boundary count agree
  within 8%. Retained bytes per subscribing boundary is a property of the
  BOUNDARY; the clock is not, because element count decides what fraction of
  the window is React's own work. THE HEAP RED-ZONES ON THIS BEAD STAND
  UNCHANGED. (Stated as a claim the operator may reject: the three figures come
  from two instruments and are not a strict replication.)

--- THE DENOMINATOR REPRODUCES rf2-2rtt6.2. The Reagent arm here is a second
--- implementation on the same witnesses, different app ns, different schedule.
--- Its reagent-subs/floor ranges OVERLAP that arm's published ranges on all
--- three shared rows: M1 3.899 [3.447-4.300] vs 4.352 [4.063-4.625];
--- M2 1.874 [1.750-2.050] vs 2.102 [1.625-2.800]; bulk 7.064 [6.200-7.700] vs
--- 7.443 [7.000-8.000]. The convergence moved the FRONTIER arm onto the
--- denominator's pages without moving the denominator.

--- STABILITY, AND THE ONE ROW THAT IS NOT STABLE. The identical instrument was
--- run twice, 5 rounds each. M1 disjoint both times; M2 straddles both times;
--- broad disjoint both times. BULK NARROW: 1.1556 [1.042-1.250] disjoint at the
--- published commit, 1.0405 [0.750-1.333] STRADDLING in the second run. Four
--- estimates (2 runs x 2 estimators) read 1.0405 / 1.1556 / 1.1738 / 1.1972 —
--- direction always UIx-slower, one minimum exactly 1.0000 (the clamp's
--- signature, not a tie). Every leg of that row is 3-5 quanta. PUBLISHED AS
--- CLAMP-LIMITED AND NOT AS A RESOLVED THRESHOLD: read it as "between
--- indistinguishable and ~1.2x slower" and do not judge a candidate red on a
--- finer margin. Lifting it needs k writes to a clock window — an INSTRUMENT
--- change, not a witness change — and rf2-2rtt6.2 has a recorded guard refusal
--- from batching mounts, so it must be re-guarded rather than assumed.

--- TWO ESTIMATORS, PUBLISHED TOGETHER. Every threshold divides one
--- floor-normalised ratio by another, and on the bulk rows a floor sample is
--- only 2-4 quanta. The RAW cross-segment estimator (uix p50 / reagent p50,
--- same round, touching neither floor) agrees on the verdict of every row:
--- M1 1.2028 [1.041-1.354]; M2 0.9989 [0.857-1.143]; broad 0.5582
--- [0.448-0.650]; narrow 1.1972 [1.111-1.250].

--- INSTRUMENT DISCIPLINE
  Arm-order guard REPORTABLE on every arm of every row, both factors; driver
  exit 0. Self-test 8/8 before anything was measured. rf2-ouwh8 ASSERTED AT
  BOOT in both directions — slot-order must degenerate at k=2 and must NOT at
  k=3 — and the run refuses to measure if either fails; three arms per segment
  means this entry never forms a two-arm plan. Canonical-DOM parity clean under
  :advanced inside each segment AND ACROSS THE SEAM, every row, with element
  counts checked against WRITTEN arithmetic (901, 51) so the gate can answer
  false. Every measured mount and write read back out of the DOM inside its own
  window: 0 UNVERIFIED OF 2,460 (600 M1 + 600 M2 + 630 broad + 630 narrow).
  SEGMENT SEAM CONTROL published per row: floor(UIx seg)/floor(Reagent seg)
  straddles 1.0 on ALL FOUR rows (M1 0.979 [0.900-1.056]; M2 0.968
  [0.800-1.167]; broad 0.938 [0.625-1.200]; narrow 1.040 [1.000-1.200]) — a
  materially quieter seam than the one .4 published, which moved up to 1.8x.
  POSITIVE CONTROLS, predicted BEFORE the run, per segment, 8 of 8 PASS at
  +/-25%: M1 predicted 1.9989 -> reagent 1.863 [1.750-2.000], uix 1.979
  [1.895-2.000]; M2 predicted 1.9412 -> 1.803 [1.600-2.000], 1.731
  [1.333-2.000]; broad predicted 1.9989 -> 1.817 [1.667-2.000], 1.923
  [1.667-2.250]; narrow predicted 1.9989 -> 2.013 [1.667-2.400], 1.867
  [1.667-2.000]. Seven of eight sit BELOW prediction, the direction a fixed
  per-root term predicts. (The +/-0.001% standard of this wave is the HEAP
  control's; no clock control can honestly be held to it, and this run measures
  no heap.)

--- THE GUARD REFUSED THIS ARM TWICE AND THE ARM WAS REPAIRED, TOLERANCE
--- UNTOUCHED.
  (1) PHASE. First cut ran all four rows in one page. M1/uix-subs/floor — an
      arm that hand-builds React elements and CANNOT CHANGE — read LAST-THIRD
      2.1739x FIRST-THIRD, ranges DISJOINT; every other arm on the page climbed
      with it (floor 2.09x, ctl-2x 2.07x/1.96x, substrate 1.41x). That is
      rf2-2rtt6.4's unexplained per-segment accumulation, whose repair there was
      one ROUND per page. Repair here: one ROW per page — ~2,460 operations a
      page down to ~600 — which was enough; clean on both factors in both
      subsequent runs, with round-per-page held in reserve.
  (2) PREDECESSOR. narrow/reagent-subs/ctl-2x refused on a TWO-SAMPLE stratum
      labelled with an arm from a DIFFERENT ROW (3.6250x, disjoint).
      lane/collect! advances the :previous pointer only for RECORDED samples,
      so the first recorded sample after a warm-up block carries whatever ran
      twenty operations earlier. rf2-2rtt6.4 met the same class as its <none>
      stratum. Repairs: the warm-up now advances the pointer without banking a
      sample, and one row per page leaves no cross-row adjacency to mislabel.
  Every figure the refused first cut produced looked entirely plausible.

--- WHERE THE TIME GOES (p50 ms, split at the microtask boundary)
  broad  reagent-subs  write 0.0  gap 0.0   drain 2.10
  broad  uix-subs      write 0.40 gap 0.80  drain 0.0
  narrow reagent-subs  write 0.0  gap 0.0   drain 0.40
  narrow uix-subs      write 0.40 gap 0.10  drain 0.0
  The split is total. On Reagent everything is the drain (reagent.core/flush,
  the reaction walk). On UIx NOTHING is the drain: the cost is the write leg

Grounding re-verified: React's Rules of Hooks prohibit hooks in conditions/loops/nested functions (the hoist is a platform constraint, not idiom); React's synthetic keyboard interface omits isComposing while retaining nativeEvent (the collector centralises that seam in intent lowering). Credibility re-verified at the witness level: independent roots, seeded-frame comparator check, canonical-DOM compare, the 17-step script including two composing keystrokes expected to emit nothing, and a separately stated expected-intent vector.

(3) NEW RESERVATION MATERIAL FOR THE VERDICT'S WORDING (Codex, this round): (a) the macro layer deliberately does not inspect view bodies, so there is no compile-time props-validation/linting surface to match UIx's established one; (b) the collector runtime is the larger novel-machinery bet: render scratch state, cached read-set entries, intent lowering, lifecycle fencing, and a useSyncExternalStore shell; (c) a CONCRETE re-subscription hazard worth carrying into any "reservations" sentence: the runtime keys the subscribe function by the boundary's read sequence, and React re-subscribes when that function changes — so a wide, frequently-flipping branch can replace ALL of a boundary's edges at once. Codex's advice, consonant with the no-over-engineering posture: split such boundaries or write them in UIx; do not grow collector machinery to hide them. (d) The dogfood page does not exercise effects, Suspense, local hook state, or most foreign-component crossings — "preferred" scopes to ordinary re-frame screens, never to all React work.

(4) OPTION-B DIVERGENCE, NEW THIS ROUND: Codex now argues the paired "priority field" edit is NOT needed before recording — the current pair already exposes the decisive read/event/controlled-input/conditional-row costs under a non-vacuous equivalence witness, and another small field is unlikely to change the choice. Its closing guidance: record the qualified preference now, keep the surface small, and spend the next ergonomics effort on diagnostics and static/tooling support rather than more syntax. The standing protocol (Option B, one time-boxed session) remains valid if Mike wants the hands-on hour; the evidence no longer requires it.

WHAT REMAINS FOR MIKE: one dated note here with the verdict (reservations named, if any). Option B time-boxed to one session if the hour is available; Option A — the template sentence, ready to sign, amend, or contradict — otherwise: "Preferred, with reservations — Hicasso is the surface I would choose for ordinary re-frame screens; raw UIx remains the escape for React-specific work." A "not preferred" naming the deciding loss is equally valid and weighs toward adapters-as-success.

title: EP-0038: Hicasso — the native view-layer programme
description:
The programme epic for EP-0038 (PR #7257). Hicasso = interpreted Hiccup on a UIx-class React FC host, optimised for re-frame2 (alias h; io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso).

AUTHORITY: docs/EP/EP-0038-the-hicasso-view-layer-programme.md + docs/design/hicasso/ (decisions.md HD-001..HD-021 is normative; then validation.md). Every brief filed under this epic carries the anti-regression fence + banned vocabulary (charter §Constraints) as normative.

WAVES: 0 = standard bead + four fresh like-for-like instruments + draft guide (parallel, off-clock; the old instrument beads rf2-mapni/m7xs7/ssn1o are CLOSED do-not-refile spec donors). 1 = donor-arm stop-gate (off-clock; ruling = delegated advisory vs the published P0 table), then shared front half, then the two tournament arms (six-week clock starts at the first Hicasso-arm commit that mounts the dogfood screen). 2 = P2 fork ruling (DECIDER: Mike; reviews advise) -> graduate one arm into implementation/hicasso/ and build v0, or stop with adapters-as-success (a SUCCESSFUL outcome).

SEQUENCING LAW: before P2 graduation nothing edits spec/*, workflows, or donor src trees; the bench/test measurement lane is carved out (instrument-only merges legal); runtime skeletons stay off main; shadow-cljs.edn build-id touches are hot-zone sequenced. Results -> beads + docs/design/hicasso/studio/. Browser numbers only against the bar; JVM/Node diagnostic-only.
notes:
OPERATOR DIRECTION (Mike, 2026-07-31, recorded by acting mayor): FULL STEAM AHEAD ON HICASSO, WITH ADAPTER OPTIMISATION CONTINUING IN PARALLEL. Two tracks run at once from here:

TRACK 1 — HICASSO (this epic). The programme CONTINUES. Wave-1 proceeds. rf2-2rtt6.8 (the shared front half, which serves BOTH tournament arms) is dispatched NOW on this direction, notwithstanding its 'blocked by the donor gate' line: the operator has directed continuation, .8 is required under either tournament outcome, and .8 does NOT start the six-week clock (per rf2-2rtt6.9/.10, that clock starts at the first commit mounting the dogfood screen). The tournament arms .9 (lean-React) and .10 (PATCH) follow.

TRACK 2 — OPTIMISATION. The adapter/spine optimisation line that produced rf2-2rtt6.13 (-769 B/read) and rf2-2rtt6.25 (double build eliminated; L1 mount red zone closed) continues in parallel rather than being suspended for the programme.

EFFECT ON THE rf2-2rtt6.7 DONOR GATE: the advisory is still to be issued (operator instruction, same message), but the operator's direction is on record BEFORE it, so its question shifts from 'stop or continue' to 'given continue, where does Hicasso have to win, and what is the strongest case against?'. It remains operator-overturnable and is sequenced behind rf2-e3flf so it is issued against gate lines true of the tree it judges.
OPERATOR DIRECTION (Mike, 2026-07-31, recorded by acting mayor): HICASSO PROCEEDS FULL THROTTLE, IN PARALLEL WITH INSTRUMENTING — measurement catches up later. Verbatim: 'I want to do the instrumenting work in parallel with the hicasso work. I don't want to wait for instrumenting to finish and only then start hicasso. I want hicasso to proceed full throttle. Let's do our measuring later (when the instrumenting work is even better).'

WHAT THIS OVERRIDES. The rf2-2rtt6.7 advisory named the clock-gate-line restatement (rf2-b0tz5) a PRECONDITION before any Wave-1 candidate mount row is judged. That precondition is NOT withdrawn — it still governs JUDGING — but it no longer gates BUILDING. Both tournament arms are dispatched now; their candidate rows are scored against the restated bar when the bar is ready, not before.

CONSEQUENCE THE OPERATOR IS ON RECORD AS ACCEPTING: per rf2-2rtt6.9 and rf2-2rtt6.10, THE SIX-WEEK CLOCK (K7) STARTS AT THE FIRST COMMIT THAT MOUNTS THE DOGFOOD SCREEN in either arm. Dispatching both arms therefore starts that clock. K7 is never extended silently (advisory kill signal 9).

BOTH ARMS DISPATCHED IN PARALLEL as a genuine tournament. Fences between them: each owns its own arm namespace and its own witness/instrument files under the bench lane; neither edits the other's; both keep their runtime skeletons OFF MAIN on spike branches per their beads. The shared front half (rf2-2rtt6.8) is landed and is READ-ONLY to both — a change either arm needs there is a new bead, not an edit, so the tournament stays like-for-like.

MEASUREMENT POSTURE for both arms: build and self-witness now; do NOT contend for the box with the instrument workers; publish candidate rows against the restated bar later.
OPERATOR RULING RECORDED (Mike, 2026-07-31): HD-002's fork is decided on its ERGONOMICS half — only Surface B (the ambient collector) is acceptable; Surface A (grouped use-subs) is ergonomically rejected. Full text and the consequences on rf2-2rtt6.1. Both tournament arms notified in flight. The collector's tripwire and survival metric are UNCHANGED and still binding — this ruling decides taste, not correctness, and explicitly cannot waive the ledger tripwire. Key consequence: 'collector loses, grouped stays default' is no longer an acceptable outcome, so a collector failure now means NULL or a new mechanism, not a fallback to A.
K7 HAS STARTED (recorded by acting mayor 2026-07-31). rf2-2rtt6.10 (Arm 2, Hicasso/PATCH) landed dogfood_screen.cljs mounting the dogfood screen on the PATCH runtime — PR #7317, merged, merge commit b27df87f42. Per rf2-2rtt6.9 and rf2-2rtt6.10 the six-week clock starts at the first commit that mounts the dogfood screen in either arm, so the clock is RUNNING FROM 2026-07-31. Advisory kill signal 9: K7 is never extended silently.

ARM 2 MET ITS HARD GATE. The controlled-restore obligation is demonstrated on the 100-cell grid in real Chromium — no act(), no flushSync, no microtask yield, no rAF — with every assertion on the line after dispatchEvent returns. npm run test:browser: 920 tests / 5743 assertions / 0 failures / exit 0. The decisive witness is :unchanged-model-rejection — the model refuses an input the browser has already shown, NOTHING re-renders (dirty-boundaries asserted 0), and the field still converges back to the model with the caret at the position before the refused character. That is the case React gives for free and an own renderer must name; converge-focused! names it at the end of every commit for the cost of one document.activeElement read rather than a walk of the other 99 cells. Invariant 5 is shown by construction (sub cannot read without a bound snapshot; the snapshot is bound in exactly two places; commit! is non-reentrant, observed by a counter) with no fence and no generation counter.

TWO TOURNAMENT-LEVEL FINDINGS, both recorded because they bear on the comparison rather than on one arm:
1. LAZINESS BREAKS THE AMBIENT COLLECTOR, and it is a SURFACE B property, not an Arm 2 one. A for's reads happen when the differ walks the children, NOT when the body returns, so a collector closed at body-return loses every row query. Arm 2 hit it in real Chromium and fixed it; Arm 1 has been told to write a witness and report whether its design already survives it. This matters to the operator's Surface B ruling directly: the surface's whole point is that sub is legal inside a for.
2. HD-002(a)'s OWNERSHIP STATE MACHINE IS NEAR-VACUOUS IN ARM 2's ARCHITECTURE. A body runs only because the commit ran it, and the patch happens in the same synchronous extent, so no read is ever a CANDIDATE — there is no candidate ledger to kill, and reconciliation is two set differences. In Arm 1 React owns the render phase, so that clause is live there and the tripwire is real. This is a structural argument that the two arms do NOT face the same correctness burden under the ruled surface, and it may be decisive.

REMAINDER on rf2-2rtt6.10 (left open, follow-ups filed): rf2-2rtt6.26 islands bridge (defhost) + error boundary — the one unwitnessed roster row; rf2-2rtt6.27 witness rows against the restated bar (the retention TERM LIST is asserted, the bytes are not, so the 0.4-0.5 KB shell target is unverified); rf2-2rtt6.28 SSR/hydration. No candidate bar rows published, per the standing instruction.
OPERATOR RULING — HICASSO IS A REACT ADAPTER; ARM 2 (PATCH) IS DROPPED (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim: 'I want hicasso to be an adaptor for React that is optimised for re-frame2, user ergonomics and performance. I don't want ARM 2 (PATCH).'). Recorded by acting mayor.

THE TOURNAMENT IS OVER. It is decided by PRODUCT DIRECTION, not by measurement, and that distinction must be preserved in the record: Arm 2 did not lose on numbers and did not fail its gates — it MET its hard gate (controlled-restore on the 100-cell grid in real Chromium, 920 tests / 5,743 assertions / 0 failures, no act/flushSync/rAF). It is dropped because the operator does not want an own renderer, not because it could not build one.

WHAT HICASSO IS NOW: a React ADAPTER, optimised for three things in this order as stated — re-frame2 (it is built for this state layer, not a general-purpose view library), USER ERGONOMICS, and PERFORMANCE. rf2-2rtt6.9's lean-React arm is therefore no longer 'tournament arm 1' — it IS the product line. Its brief's competitive fences (own namespace, do not touch the rival, keep the comparison like-for-like) are DISCHARGED; the shared front half is no longer a neutral substrate to be preserved for fairness and may be evolved as the adapter needs, under normal review.

WHAT SURVIVES FROM ARM 2, and must not be thrown away with it:
  - THE LAZINESS FINDING, which is a SURFACE B property and applies to the adapter directly: a for's reads happen when the children are walked, NOT when the body returns, so a collector closed at body-return registers no edges for the rows. Arm 1 has been told to write a witness and report.
  - THE STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION that HD-002(a)'s ownership state machine is near-vacuous when the body runs inside the commit, and LIVE when React owns the render phase. Under this ruling React owns the render phase, so THE CANDIDATE-LEDGER TRIPWIRE IS FULLY IN FORCE for the adapter. That is now the single largest correctness risk in the programme.
  - The controlled-restore witness as EVIDENCE of what correct input behaviour looks like, whether or not the code that produced it is kept.

CONSEQUENT DISPOSITIONS (acting mayor, under the Hicasso authority delegated 2026-07-31): rf2-2rtt6.10 CLOSED as ruled-out; its three follow-ups rf2-2rtt6.26 (islands bridge), rf2-2rtt6.27 (witness rows) and rf2-2rtt6.28 (SSR/hydration) are Arm-2-specific and CLOSED as moot. A separate bead disposes of Arm 2's landed bench code once Arm 1 has mined what transfers.

UNCHANGED: the Surface B ergonomics ruling (only the ambient collector is acceptable; grouped use-subs is below the usability bar, so a collector failure means NULL, not a fallback); the tripwire that overrides the clock; K7, running from 2026-07-31.
OPERATOR DIRECTION — WHAT HICASSO IS, AND WHERE THE EFFORT GOES (Mike, 2026-07-31, two messages, recorded by acting mayor).

(1) VERBATIM: 'I want all the effort to be going into producing an excellent adapter which is a Hiccup interpreter that is highly efficient very data oriented including the mount and unmount capabilities supplied by Replicant and other very data oriented features And I want it to target React.'

(2) VERBATIM: 'I want the effort to go into adversarial design reviews and performance improvement.'

SO HICASSO IS: a HICCUP INTERPRETER, targeting React, highly efficient, VERY DATA-ORIENTED, optimised for re-frame2 + user ergonomics + performance. Not an own renderer (Arm 2 dropped), not a compiler (still a hard fence).

REPLICANT'S FEATURES, VERIFIED FROM PRIMARY SOURCE (replicant.fun, fetched 2026-07-31 — NOT recalled, per the standing rule about library claims):
  - ':replicant/mounting' and ':replicant/unmounting' — DECLARATIVE ATTRIBUTE OVERRIDES applied during mount and unmount. The site: 'you can specify overrides for any attributes during mounting and unmounting. This allows you to declaratively transition elements on mount and unmount, like fading in an element as it is mounted.' This is the capability Mike named. It replaces refs/callbacks/useEffect for enter-and-leave transitions with DATA IN THE HICCUP.
  - CUSTOM ELEMENT ALIASES — user-defined extensions that expand to arbitrary hiccup (their example: i18n without framework coupling).
  - DATA-DRIVEN EVENT HANDLERS — handlers declared as data passed to a global dispatcher, trivially testable.
  - Pure functions and data throughout; Replicant deliberately discourages stateful component abstractions.

WHAT RE-FRAME2 ALREADY HAS OF THAT: the data-driven event handler half is already the shape of Hicasso's intent lowering (event vectors as :on-click, the ::h/value placeholder, submit auto-prevent) and of re-frame's dispatch model generally. So the genuinely NEW capabilities to bring across are the MOUNT/UNMOUNT ATTRIBUTE OVERRIDES and ALIASES — and the harder question is what they mean when the target is React, whose own mount/unmount story is refs and effects. Making a declarative transition work through a React reconciler without leaking a ref or an effect into user code is a real design problem and should be treated as one.

WHERE THE EFFORT GOES, per (2): ADVERSARIAL DESIGN REVIEW and PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT — not feature sprawl, not further instrument bookkeeping. Design decisions on this adapter are to be attacked before they are built on, and the performance work is the point rather than a later phase. The mayor is to bias dispatch accordingly: reviewers whose job is to break a design, and workers whose job is to make it faster.

STILL BINDING: Surface B is the only acceptable read surface (grouped use-subs below the usability bar; a collector failure means NULL, not a fallback). The candidate-ledger tripwire is FULLY LIVE now that React owns the render phase. No compiler, no analyzer, no dual mode, no ViewCell-class object graph. K7 running from 2026-07-31.
OPERATOR CLARIFICATION (Mike, 2026-07-31, verbatim): 'replicant is just an example not an objective.'

CORRECTING THE PREVIOUS NOTE, which read too literally. Replicant is cited as an ILLUSTRATION OF THE SPIRIT — what 'very data-oriented' looks like when someone commits to it — NOT as a feature checklist to match, port, or be measured against. Do not make 'parity with Replicant' a goal, an acceptance criterion, or a comparison row. Its ':replicant/mounting' / ':replicant/unmounting' overrides and its aliases are worth understanding as EXAMPLES of expressing in data what other libraries express in callbacks, refs and effects; they are not a specification.

THE OBJECTIVE, stated without reference to any other library: an EXCELLENT ADAPTER — a hiccup interpreter targeting React, HIGHLY EFFICIENT and VERY DATA-ORIENTED, optimised for re-frame2, user ergonomics, and performance. ARM 1 — THE ADAPTER — HAS LANDED ITS CORE (PR #7321, recorded by acting mayor 2026-07-31). The ruled architecture is now demonstrated rather than proposed, and three of the programme's open correctness risks are closed by evidence.

THE <=2-HOOK SHELL IS HELD, AND MEASURED AT REACT'S DISPATCHER rather than declared: ['useContext' 'useSyncExternalStore'], exactly 2 at 1, 7 AND 20 reads, with no useRef/useState/useMemo/useCallback anywhere in the shell. The mechanism is the interesting part: React gives a function component no per-instance storage except a hook cell, so a shell wanting one has already spent a third hook. Arm 1 gives the shell NO per-instance render-phase state at all — 'subscribe' closes over the read SET and nothing else, so it is a pure function of a value: cached by that value, shared across boundaries, identity-stable exactly while the reads are unchanged, which is precisely React's own re-subscribe condition. getSnapshot returns a monotone epoch sum, so Object.is on one number is a correct change test with no memo. The raw-UIx comparator on the same probe and page RISES with read count. If React's internals slot moves, the witness records UNWITNESSED and FAILS — it cannot silently go green.

THE CANDIDATE-LEDGER TRIPWIRE DID NOT FIRE. Closest approach named honestly: the read-set entry cache is one line from the fence — keyed by read-set CONTENT, never by render or attempt, evicted by a macrotask reaper, and dropping an entry early costs one re-subscribe and no correctness.

THE LAZINESS DEFECT IS REFUTED FOR THIS ARCHITECTURE, STRUCTURALLY: the collector window closes around codec/as-element and the codec is eager everywhere (expand-seq, realize-children, clj->js). No doall, no widened window, no cost, hook budget untouched. Three witnesses, each asserting the SECOND half (a later write re-renders), because a broken implementation passes the first. Further, the four DEFERRED-read escapes (stored handler, invoked handler, delay, stashed lazy seq) now convert into a LOUD ERROR NAMING THE QUERY rather than a silent missing edge — which discharges the substance of rf2-2rtt6.32. One residual is named rather than hidden: a deferred read forced inside another boundary's render is attributed to that boundary.

The collector is the only surface where the read sits at the value's POINT OF USE, so 'what does this boundary depend on?' is answered by reading the body; grouped's declaration and body can DRIFT, and on the collector that drift is not expressible. Raw UIx loses decisively (no conditional read, no helper-donated read, seven hand-written handlers). THE FIX — and this is the part to remember: a key with no cell contributes its frame's commit-basis = @!generation + re-frame.frame/frame-commit-epoch(frame); a cell records the basis it was CREATED at; flush! re-stamps rather than increments. frame-commit-epoch IS THE SUBSTRATE'S OWN observation-port evidence counter, and Spec 006 already uses it verbatim to detect 'the frame's durable state moved in the render->commit gap — without watching anything'. values, so the wrong reader re-renders ONCE, does not re-execute the read, drops the edge on the
next commit, and the value is then frozen for the life of the mount — the exact "correct on
screen, frozen thereafter, attributable to nothing" class the same page calls the worst failure
the ruled surface can have. The structural argument meant to make that class impossible ("a seq at
a prop position goes through `clj->js`") is FALSE at the boundary-prop position: `boundary-element`

exactly one level. Two further real findings: the read-set entry cache degrades to an O(N) scan
selected by read ORDER (an undocumented authoring detail, on the bulk K=100/300 rung), and
`record-reads`'s set difference — the operation HD-002(b) is discharged against — is never
exercised by the wired runtime, because every re-subscribe mints a fresh registration id and
therefore always diffs against the empty set, making a one-key change a full teardown+rebuild.

reaper opens no disagreement window (walked three interleavings). (3) staged-read tear —
SURVIVES, and more strongly than claimed: the epoch sum is term-wise monotone so collision is
impossible, all three `replace-container!` sites bump, and there is no `reg-sub-raw`, so
rf2-2rtt6.44's two axes really are the two (corroboration + one refinement noted there).
(4) "Surface B is preferred, MEASURED" — PARTLY SUPPORTED: DOM parity and the collector<grouped
edge count are real, but the edge count is an efficiency reading against the arm the operator
removed, and nothing is measured against the surviving raw-UIx control; the preference itself is
an argued judgement, which the page is honest about. (5) the loud-error guard — BROKEN, see above.

THE FIVE SOURCES AND WHAT EACH IS GOOD FOR:
  - FREEHAND (implementation/freehand/) — the shipped interpreted substrate this programme is measured against. Its codec question is already settled (Hicasso consumes reagent-slim's), but its DESIGN decisions — the controlled-input door, caller split, declared properties, the roster of callback contracts it needed and Hicasso collapsed — are the map of problems any interpreted view layer must answer. When Hicasso hits a design fork, check what Freehand did and WHY before choosing.
  - RE-FRAME.UI (implementation/ui/) — the EXPERIMENTAL compiled-view substrate. It is the other pole: what a compiler can do that an interpreter cannot (and rf2-2rtt6.41 already used its analyzer's :rf.ui.compile/sub-in-loop refusal as proof a compiler cannot deliver Surface B). Mine it for what compilation bought that the runtime should approximate cheaply, and for the analysis passes whose LESSONS transfer even where their mechanism cannot.
  - REPLICANT — from a DATA-ORIENTED point of view specifically (Mike ruled 2026-07-31 it is 'just an example, not an objective'). Its relevant ideas: pure-data hiccup all the way down, lifecycle as data (mount/unmount hooks in attributes — the ::h/mounting/::h/unmounting presence design is already in this family), event handlers as data. The in-band [::h/prevent ...] head ruling is exactly this school: behaviour carried IN the data where = can see it, not beside it where it cannot.
  - REAGENT — the incumbent. Its default shouldComponentUpdate (value-equality bail-out on props) is DIRECT prior art for the HD-006 memo ruling on rf2-2rtt6.52 — the cascade Hicasso just hit is precisely what Reagent's default stops. Also: ratom deref-capture (the 943 B/read floor nothing beats), cursor/track granularity, and its known losses (the charter's 'Known losses coming from Reagent' section).
  - UIX — the React parent. Its per-hook useSyncExternalStore pattern is what Hicasso's one-hook-plus-index beats on fan-out; its input wrapper (three hooks per input) is what the element-path converge beats; its classpath input-selection defect (rf2-heqwo) is the cautionary tale about implicit selection. Mine it for React-19 integration technique — it is the closest thing to a reference for driving React from CLJS without a legacy adapter.

HOW TO USE THIS IN BRIEFS: when a bead involves a design decision, name which of the five have faced the same decision and what each chose, BEFORE proposing. A choice that contradicts all five needs an argument; a choice one of them already made and regretted needs the regret cited.

title: Configure the beads Dolt remote (operator action)
description:
FOLLOW-UP from the .beads guard work. This is layer 4 of that bead and is OPERATOR ACTION — it cannot be done or verified from a worker worktree, which is why it was carved out rather than attempted.

THE WORK: configure the Dolt remote for the beads database so tracker state has a durable home independent of the git-tracked JSONL export, and confirm bd dolt push / bd dolt pull round-trip.

WHY IT MATTERS: the JSONL export is a mirror, not the source of truth. Today a git-side accident is recoverable only because Dolt still holds the real state locally; without a configured remote there is no off-box copy.

ACCEPTANCE: bd dolt push succeeds; bd dolt pull round-trips on a second checkout; the configuration is recorded somewhere durable rather than living only in one machine's local config.

ASSIGNEE: Mike (operator). Do not dispatch a background worker at this.
notes:
OPERATOR-OWNED DECISION BEAD (Mike, 2026-07-26): one of six to be taken one at a time — rf2-ayq3v, rf2-9sluz, rf2-mhrwq, rf2-o0agl, rf2-4l67v, rf2-2ii52. Do NOT dispatch; do NOT re-surface as a ready-queue candidate.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-27, dossier review): ROUTE = dedicated private GitHub repository as the Dolt origin, over HTTPS — github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads — per the Codex second opinion in the dossier. NOT DoltHub (the dossier's original recommendation), NOT a self/file-based remote, NOT nothing. Pre-authorized fallback: if the initial push trips GitHub's 2 GiB per-push ceiling, switch the same origin to a private DoltHub repo and accept the $50/month — do not build split-push tooling. Timing: before the alpha tag.

WHY (facts re-verified 2026-07-27 against the installed bd 1.0.3 and primary sources):
- DoltHub private storage is free only up to 1 GB/month, then $50/month (dolthub.com/docs/concepts/dolthub/permissions/ — fetched today). The live embedded DB measures ~1.8 GiB, so the DoltHub route costs $50/month from day one. A private GitHub repo is free, the same vendor/trust shape that already holds the code, and this machine's GitHub HTTPS credentials already work (SSH currently fails).
- Git-backed Dolt remotes are first-class in bd 1.0.3, not a trick: the installed `bd bootstrap --help` lists both "If sync.remote is configured: clones from the remote" and "If git origin has Dolt data (refs/dolt/data): clones from git". Dolt stores git-backed data under refs/dolt/data; ordinary source clones never fetch that ref, so a DEDICATED repo keeps ~1.8 GiB out of the code repo entirely.
- Current origin is file://C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/.beads/backup/origin (~3.7 GiB) — same disk, same checkout, gitignored. That is not durability; it is what this ruling replaces.
- The remote must be PRIVATE: the Dolt DB carries ~15K historical event rows including old/new values — more history than the public JSONL mirror exposes.
- Rejected: self/file-based off-box storage (setup + credential overhead matches or exceeds DoltHub with fewer affordances); doing nothing (standing single-disk loss of all tracker + ruling history, and a session-close protocol mandating a push with nowhere to go).

OPERATOR RUNBOOK (~15 min, mayor checkout):
1. Create an empty private repo: `gh repo create day8/re-frame2-beads --private` (no README — Dolt data lives under refs/dolt/data).
2. `bd dolt remote remove origin` then `bd dolt remote add origin https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git`; confirm with `bd dolt show`.
3. `bd dolt push` — the first push uploads ~1.8 GiB, let it run to completion. Verify off-box: `git ls-remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git` must list refs/dolt/data. [acceptance 1]
4. Durable config: check `bd config get sync.remote` and `git diff .beads/config.yaml` — bd should record sync.remote in the tracked config.yaml; if it did not, run `bd config set sync.remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git` and confirm the tracked-file diff. Commit config.yaml via the normal path (it is committable human-authored .beads config; do NOT hand-commit issues.jsonl outside the checkpoint script). [acceptance 3]
5. Round-trip in a genuinely separate fresh clone — NOT a worktree (a worktree can resolve the mayor's database): `git clone https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git <tmpdir>`, then inside it `bd bootstrap --yes` followed by `bd dolt pull`; verify `bd show rf2-4l67v` displays this ruling and `bd dolt show` matches the primary checkout. Delete the tmp clone afterwards. [acceptance 2]
6. FALLBACK if step 3 fails on the 2 GiB per-push ceiling: create a private DoltHub repo, repoint the same origin (`bd dolt remote remove origin` / `bd dolt remote add origin <dolthub-url>`), accept the $50/month, re-run steps 3-5 (recording the DoltHub URL as sync.remote in step 4).
7. Optional cleanup once acceptance passes: delete the old same-disk file remote .beads/backup/origin (~3.7 GiB) to reclaim disk. The JSONL checkpoint remains the cheap human-inspectable recovery floor. Do NOT add a second cloud remote, scheduled backup system, or remote-management abstraction.

Bead stays OPEN, assigned to Mike; close when acceptance 1-3 pass.
DOSSIER REVIEW (2026-07-28): ruling unchanged — route stays a dedicated private GitHub repo (day8/re-frame2-beads) over HTTPS as the Dolt origin, DoltHub fallback, executed before the alpha tag. The dossier's Codex second opinion concurs with the ruled route on every point (GitHub first, one push as the go/no-go, no dual remotes, no split-push tooling) and its mechanics claims all re-verified today against the installed bd 1.0.3 (1b2dd2cb): sync.remote still unset, origin still the same-disk file://.../.beads/backup/origin, embedded DB 1,864,657,504 bytes (~1.74 GiB), file remote ~3.97 GB (step 7's reclaim figure stands).
ONE VERIFIED CORRECTION ADOPTED — DoltHub pricing: DoltHub repriced on 2026-04-24 (primary source fetched today: dolthub.com/blog/2026-04-24-announcing-dolthub-pro-for-5-dollars-per-month/) — private storage over 100 MB is now USD 5/month up to 5 GB, then USD 1/GB/month; the USD 50/month figure in the WHY and runbook step 6 above was the PRIOR pricing (the docs page cited on 2026-07-27 was stale). AMEND step 6 accordingly: the fallback costs ~USD 5/month, not USD 50/month. This changes no part of the route — GitHub remains free, already-authenticated, and first — it just makes the fallback cheap if the ~1.74 GiB initial push trips GitHub's 2 GB per-push ceiling.
URGENCY unchanged: execute before the alpha tag. The tracker's ruling history (including this one) still has no off-box copy.
RUNBOOK AMENDMENTS (dossier review, 2026-07-28 PM): the dossier's Codex second opinion carried TWO required corrections plus refined figures. Both corrections VERIFIED today — pinned upstream sources fetched, plus local checks against the installed bd 1.0.3 (1b2dd2cb) and this checkout's armed pre-commit guard. They SUPERSEDE runbook steps 1, 2 and 4 above; steps 3, 6 (price already corrected to ~USD 5/mo in the note above) and 7 stand, with the order sharpened below (step 5's round-trip now comes AFTER landing config.yaml).

CORRECTION A — SUPERSEDES step 1 (was: create an EMPTY repo, "no README"). Do NOT create a branchless repo: the exact Dolt revision bundled by bd 1.0.3 errors on a git remote with no branches — VERIFIED in the pinned source (dolthub/dolt @ 005921bd, go/libraries/doltcore/dbfactory/git_remote_test.go: test TestGitRemoteFactory_GitFile_RemoteWithNoBranchesFails asserts ErrGitRemoteHasNoBranches). Seed it instead:
  gh repo create day8/re-frame2-beads --private --add-readme
  gh repo view day8/re-frame2-beads --json visibility,defaultBranchRef
Require visibility PRIVATE and a non-null defaultBranchRef before configuring Dolt. The README/branch never mixes with the data — Dolt stores git-backed data under refs/dolt/data, which ordinary clones do not fetch.

CORRECTION B — SUPERSEDES step 2's bare remove/add and step 4's commit guidance. VERIFIED in bd 1.0.3 source (gastownhall/beads @ 1b2dd2cb): `bd dolt remote add origin <url>` writes sync.remote into .beads/config.yaml AND auto-invokes commitBeadsConfig("bd: update sync.remote"), which runs a plain `git commit -m <msg>` with NO pathspec (cmd/bd/dolt.go remote-add handler; cmd/bd/sync_remote.go) — it sweeps EVERYTHING already staged. Also VERIFIED locally: this mayor checkout's guard is armed (.git/mayor-marker present) and the mayor allow-list is exactly .beads/issues.jsonl + MEMORY.md (scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-mayor-commit-boundary.sh), so the auto-commit carrying .beads/config.yaml will be REFUSED here and will leave config.yaml staged. Therefore:
- BEFORE `bd dolt remote remove origin` / `bd dolt remote add origin https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git`: verify `git diff --cached --name-only` prints NOTHING. Never run remote add with .beads/issues.jsonl (or anything else) staged — the no-pathspec auto-commit must never capture it.
- AFTER: confirm `bd dolt show` lists the new origin and `bd config get sync.remote` returns the URL. Expect the auto-commit to warn/fail with config.yaml left staged — that is the guard working, not breakage.
- Land the isolated .beads/config.yaml change through the normal worker/PR path (VERIFIED: workers may carry it — scripts/git-hooks/lib/check-beads-boundary.sh explicitly permits .beads/config.yaml; the mayor checkout cannot commit it), and land+push it BEFORE the fresh-clone round-trip test so bootstrap can find sync.remote.

REFINED FIGURES (re-measured 2026-07-28, drifting upward — the tracker is live): embedded store 1,872,694,753 B (1.744 GiB); old file remote directory 3,977,884,735 B total (~3.98 GB, includes accumulated non-live material — step 7's reclaim figure stands); the remote's LIVE manifest now references 240 table files / 1,842,305,776 B (1.716 GiB) (dossier measured 224 / 1.711 GiB — it grows). Headroom under GitHub's enforced 2 GiB per-push limit is only ~262-291 MiB today and shrinking, so the GitHub-first attempt is a genuine ONE-SHOT go/no-go: on `pack exceeds maximum allowed size` (or equivalent 2 GiB failure) go STRAIGHT to private DoltHub (~USD 5/month after the free 100 MB, through 5 GB; then USD 1/GB/month). No split-push tooling, no second cloud remote. Largest live table file is 1,079,296,714 B (~1.005 GiB) but this is NOT a 100 MB-object-ceiling problem: the bundled Dolt defaults git-backed storage to 50 MiB parts (VERIFIED in pinned source: defaultGitBlobstoreMaxPartSize = 50*1024*1024, dolthub/dolt @ 005921bd go/store/nbs/store.go) — aggregate push size is the only real capacity risk.

PUSH VERIFICATION: `git ls-remote https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git refs/dolt/data` must return the ref. The GitHub web UI shows NOTHING for custom refs — its silence is not evidence either way.

AMENDED ACCEPTANCE SEQUENCE (order is load-bearing): (1) seed + verify the private repo per Correction A -> (2) clean index, repoint origin, confirm sync.remote per Correction B -> (3) one ordinary `bd dolt push` -> (4) ls-remote proof of refs/dolt/data -> (5) land the .beads/config.yaml change via the normal path and push it -> (6) THEN the fresh-clone round-trip (NOT a worktree): `bd bootstrap --yes` + `bd dolt pull`, verify this bead and representative counts -> (7) only after the round-trip passes, delete the old file:// remote (.beads/backup/origin). Per Codex, unverified by this review: the Dolt remotes docs-page wording on the branch requirement (moot — the pinned test at the exact bundled revision is decisive) and the precise line-number citations in the dossier (content of every cited claim verified; some line numbers were a few lines off).
FINAL CONSOLIDATION (dossier review, 2026-07-29): Codex Recommendation CONCURS with the ruled route end-to-end — seeded private repo, refs/dolt/data proof, one-shot GitHub push, DoltHub ~USD 5/mo fallback, sequence — all confirmation of the amended runbook above; not repeated here. TWO DELTAS RECORDED: (1) The clean-index precondition (Correction B) now has a concrete live instance: at dossier-review time .beads/issues.jsonl WAS staged, exactly what bd's pathless auto-commit on remote add would sweep. Re-checked read-only 2026-07-29 11:21:31 AUSEST: git diff --cached --name-only is EMPTY — index clean at this moment — but the mayor checkpoint cycle re-stages the JSONL on its heartbeat, so Mike must let any in-flight tracker checkpoint finish and re-verify an empty index IMMEDIATELY before the remote remove/add, not minutes before. (2) Growth trend, third measurement: live manifest now 262 files / 1,845,969,173 B (1.719 GiB); trend 224 files/1.711 GiB (dossier) -> 240/1.716 GiB (2026-07-28) -> 262/1.719 GiB (2026-07-29 dossier refresh). Headroom under GitHub's 2 GiB per-push limit is ~287.5 MiB and shrinking daily — the one-shot GitHub attempt keeps getting tighter; execute at the next opportunity, before the alpha tag. Runbook otherwise stands as amended. Dossier file deleted after this note.
STATUS (dossier review, 2026-07-31): the before-the-alpha timing hook is gone (release cancelled) but the risk GREW: the Hicasso boot wrote heavily into the tracker (the governance record overflowed a bd column — rf2-0znkn, live evidence of growth), and every EP-0038 ruling/red-zone/audit trail lives on this one disk. Re-measured 2026-07-31 07:44 AUSEST: embedded store 1,955,745,278 B (1.821 GiB; was 1,872,694,753 B on 07-28); old file remote's LIVE manifest 71 table files / 1,864,150,303 B (1.736 GiB) — a Dolt conjoin collapsed the file count (262 -> 71; largest table file unchanged at 1,079,296,714 B) while live bytes keep growing (1.711 -> 1.716 -> 1.719 -> 1.736 GiB); GitHub one-shot headroom now ~270 MiB (was ~287.5 MiB) and shrinking with exactly this growth. ADDENDUM (dossier review, 2026-07-31, Codex Recommendation appended after the STATUS note): Codex CONCURS with the ruled route end-to-end; its independent 07:33 measurements match this review's 07:44 pass exactly (embedded 1,955,745,278 B; live manifest 71 files / 1,864,150,303 B; headroom 283,333,345 B = 270.2 MiB; file remote total now 4,623,052,684 B = 4.306 GiB — up from 3.98 GB, so runbook step 7's reclaim figure is now ~4.3 GiB). THREE REFINEMENTS ADOPTED: (1) URL SCHEME CORRECTION — supersedes the URL in original step 2 / Correction B: the git-backed remote must use the git+https scheme — bd dolt remote add origin git+https://github.com/day8/re-frame2-beads.git — plain https:// is not the git-remote factory's scheme in this build. VERIFIED against the installed bd 1.0.3 binary (embeds the git+https and git+file scheme constants; Codex's pinned cite: dolthub/dolt @ 005921bd go/libraries/doltcore/dbfactory/git_remote.go). (3) Audit the new repo's EFFECTIVE access, not just visibility PRIVATE — day8 is an org, so check org base permissions after gh repo create. Codex also re-confirms keeping the file:// remote until the fresh-clone restore PASSES (already the amended sequence), and it too caught .beads/issues.jsonl staged at research time — a third live instance of the clean-index precondition. COORDINATION (2026-07-31): rf2-0znkn's remedy is being re-ruled toward a bd v1.1.2 DATABASE MIGRATION on this same machine (parallel agent, in flight; the 0znkn bead will carry the coordination). The migration and the first cloud push MUST be explicitly sequenced — sensible order: migrate first, then the one-shot push carries the already-migrated database. Mike should not run this runbook blind to that. Dossier file deleted after this addendum.
FINAL RUNBOOK CONSOLIDATION (dossier review, 2026-07-31 PM): THE note Mike executes from — folds the post-migration verification and the Codex access gate into the amended runbook; earlier notes are history/rationale.

POST-MIGRATION STATE: the bd v1.1.2 migration is DONE (rf2-fwij4 closed; installed bd 1.1.2 build 20e493e5; pre-migration backup at C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-beads-backup-20260731). fwij4's close explicitly parks its deferred acceptance leg on THIS bead — the push + fresh-clone drill below completes it. VERIFICATION GOTCHA (supersedes every earlier "confirm with bd dolt show"): bd dolt show prints "Remotes: (none)" even with a remote configured — it reports the config surface, not persisted database remotes. The remote assertion is bd dolt remote list (plus .beads/embeddeddolt/rf2/.dolt/repo_state.json). bd dolt show is NOT an acceptance instrument.

NEW MANDATORY GATE — EFFECTIVE-ACCESS AUDIT BEFORE ANY BYTES UPLOAD (Codex; ADOPTED): a genuinely new go/no-go, inserted as runbook step 0. It upgrades ADDENDUM refinement (3) from an after-create check into a pre-upload decision gate, makes the owner in original step 1 / Correction A conditional, and must PRECEDE the push (runbook step 4; amended-sequence step 3) — not follow it. Basis: the database is materially richer than the public JSONL (measured: 2,001 issues, 12,786 event rows incl. old_value/new_value long-text + comments). A day8-org repo is readable per org BASE permissions and by org owners — verified: day8 is a 12-member org whose base permission is currently ADMIN, so visibility PRIVATE means all 12 members can deliberately fetch refs/dolt/data ("private" != "only Mike"; the custom ref's absence from ordinary clones and the web UI is not an access control). Do NOT casually change the org-wide base permission as part of this runbook — it affects every day8 repo.

THE RUNBOOK (final; verified against the installed 1.1.2 revisions):

Let the mayor checkpoint finish; require git diff --cached --name-only EMPTY immediately before the next step — bd 1.1.2's remote add STILL stages .beads/config.yaml then runs a pathspec-less git commit (verified at the 1.1.2 source); it sweeps anything staged. 4. One ordinary bd dolt push (no force). Proof: git ls-remote https://github.com/OWNER/re-frame2-beads.git refs/dolt/data returns the ref (plain https is correct HERE — ordinary git; the web UI shows nothing for custom refs). Re-check the stored URL contains no credential.

title: mayor method: no rule says WHICH CLOCK dates a historical commit in prose, and the liveness rule reads as though it does
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-21, step 2 (checking the rules being ENFORCED against what the tree does). It cost a wrong flag to a live worker the same session.

THE GAP. Both layers state the author-versus-committer distinction, and all FOUR mentions are scoped to LIVENESS — is this worker alive? Measured with a grep over .claude/commands/*.md and docs/the-mayor-method/*.md:

  .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md:12   liveness (tip SHA vs ahead count vs %aI/%cI)
  .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:30   liveness (same discriminator, stranded sweep)
  docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md:613-616 liveness (generic form of the same)

NOTHING ANYWHERE SAYS WHICH CLOCK TO READ WHEN **DATING** A COMMIT IN PROSE. That is a different question with the OPPOSITE answer, and the liveness rule actively misleads on it.

WHY THE TWO ANSWERS DIVERGE, and it is not a nuance. This repository rebase-merges, so %aI and %cI differ on essentially every merged commit.
  - For LIVENESS, the committer date is right: a rebase rewrites it, so it moves when the worker moves. The author date is replayed unchanged and reads as death.
  - For DATING A HISTORICAL COMMIT IN PROSE, the AUTHOR date is right: it is when the work was actually written. The committer date is an artefact of when the trunk happened to replay it, which is not a fact about the change at all.

A reader who has only ever met the liveness rule has been taught that %aI is the untrustworthy one, and will 'correct' a correct author date to a committer date.

THE MEASURED INSTANCE. A worker dated a set of deletions 2026-08-15 in a design record. The mayor flagged it against CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-16 and had to retract to the operator. Both dates are right and they are different clocks: commit ef3131f4a2 reads author=2026-08-15T20:07:56, committer=2026-08-16T13:29:40. The worker had used the correct clock; the mayor applied the liveness rule to a dating question.

WHERE THE FIX GOES — TWO LAYERS, KEPT APART.
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, beside the existing liveness passage at 613-616: the GENERIC rule. Which clock answers which question, and why they diverge under rebase. No repository names, bead ids, PR numbers, paths or tool names — that is the method tree's standing constraint.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md and .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md: the EXECUTING layer, where the concrete command may be named. One clause each, pointing at the generic rule rather than restating it, so the two copies cannot drift.

The point is not to add prose. It is that BOTH questions are now answerable from the same passage, so a reader meeting one cannot mistake it for the other.

title: hicasso: the published non-cancellation floor does not describe the corpus the allocation instrument produces now — 23.2% of the null arm sits above the 45 B/boundary bar
description:
MEASURED by rf2-fk6pj's phase-3 window, 2026-08-21, on 164 null-arm cells. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-design-control-comes-before-the-window.md, section D. Datasets: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-passterm/.

THE OBSERVATION. The R = 0 null arm reads nothing, so arm minus floor must be zero under either write; it is the only allocation population whose true value is known in advance, and rf2-2rtt6.140 published it as the instrument's NON-CANCELLATION FLOOR — 1.5 B/boundary median, 4.5 B p90 — setting a REFUSAL BAR of 45 B/boundary at ten times the p90. The fraction of that zero-signal population sitting ABOVE that bar has risen across three windows:

  rf2-0gjqi (parity, 2 x 6 rounds)   2 of 38   =  5.3%   p90  4.5
  phase 2   (seeded, 2 x 6 rounds)   4 of 40   = 10.0%   p90 56.5
  phase 3   (seeded, 4 x 12 rounds) 38 of 164  = 23.2%   p90 61

PHASE 2'S EXPLANATION IS REFUTED, and that is the point of filing this. Phase 2 saw its own p90 jump from 4.5 to 56.5 and wrote that it was AN ARTEFACT OF THE COUNT — four outliers in forty putting one exactly at the 90th-percentile index where two in thirty-eight did not. At n = 164 that no longer holds: a quarter of the population above the bar is a distribution, not an index. The full quantile ladder is p50 = 3, p75 = 19.5, p80 = 54.5, p85 = 59.5, p90 = 61, p95 = 64, max 135.5.

WHAT STILL HOLDS, so it is not over-read. The MEDIAN is 0 in every one of the four runs and the ABSOLUTE MEDIAN holds at 3 B/boundary against the published 1.5. The instrument still cancels in the centre. What has changed is the TAIL, and the tail is what the published bar was derived from.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every allocation window's licence to read its mid-rung figures is the null arm reading flat. The mid-rung figures are thousands of bytes per boundary and are unaffected. What IS affected is any statistic of the same order as the tail — and rf2-fk6pj's phase-3 window is exactly that case: its pre-registered band, built at ten times its own null-arm p90, came out at 610 B/boundary and refused a term whose implied delta was 37.8.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED.
* NO MECHANISM IS PROPOSED and none is excluded. The 12-round runs, the seeded pass order, the session length and the box are all confounded with the corpus date.
* IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED THAT THE PUBLISHED BAR IS WRONG. The bar refuses nothing the ladder publishes and nothing here moves it. What is established is that the DISTRIBUTION it was derived from is not the distribution the instrument produces now.
* THE THREE WINDOWS ARE THREE SESSIONS, not 242 independent observations.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT. A re-derivation of the floor over the whole committed null-arm corpus rather than one window's 38 cells, reporting the quantile ladder per window and per session, and stating whether the published 1.5 / 4.5 / 45 triple should be re-cut or whether the tail is session-carried. THE CONTRADICTION IS IN THE LANDED RECORD ITSELF. `the-window-total-is-the-ceiling.md` says the 884,280 B figure is the highest certified observation, that 168,036 B above it is unsampled, and that this “ceiling is bounded from below by an observation and from above by nothing.” That is the correct evidential status: the largest observed success is a LOWER bound on any real maximum certifiable total, not an upper bound.

The 36 refusals below the figure prove only that it is not sufficient; they do not turn it into a necessary cap.

That conditional projection may be useful, but it cannot reverse the old impossibility claim as a live necessary result.

CHEAPEST CORRECT DISCHARGE: restate B <= 3 everywhere (page, reader output/comments/self-test, README/close record as applicable) as a model-conditioned projection, not a necessary condition. Preserve the empirical B=4 rung result. If a real page-size necessity is wanted, it needs evidence at another B; the page already says that window is unmeasured. title: [bug] check_doc_slugs.py does not validate markdown links inside fenced code blocks — a link gate that fails OPEN
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-zk1xu's worker on 2026-08-21, as a by-product of its planted-fault proof, and it is a fail-open in a gate this project nominates constantly.

THE FINDING, in the worker's own words: its first planted fault broke a markdown link anchor INSIDE a fenced code block it had just added to spec/Spec-Schemas.md, and scripts/check_doc_slugs.py came back GREEN. A second plant in Spec-Schemas PROSE red at exit 1 naming the planted slug, which both proved the gate read that worktree and pinned the blindness as fence-scoped rather than file-scoped or worktree-scoped.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. This is the same shape as every other fail-open hunted in this repo: a search that returns zero reads identically to a check that passed. A broken link inside a fence is invisible, so an edit confined to a fenced block — and spec/Spec-Schemas.md's *Tags schemas all live inside fences — is UNGATED while the PR body truthfully reports check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. The worker hand-verified its own link because it had caught this; the next author will not know to.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST, at origin/main HEAD, and do it in BOTH directions: plant a broken link target inside a fenced block (expect green, which is the defect) and the same target in prose (expect red, which is the control). A one-direction probe cannot tell blindness from a bad plant.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHETHER TO FIX IT OR DOCUMENT IT, and that is a judgement the worker should make and argue rather than assume. Skipping fenced blocks may be DELIBERATE — a fence often carries illustrative or third-party markdown that is not meant to resolve, and validating it would red on examples by design. If that is the reason, the correct deliverable is not a code change: it is one sentence at the top of the checker saying so, plus a line in whatever prose nominates this gate, so the next author knows what the exit 0 does not cover. If there is no such reason, validate inside fences.

DO NOT grow this into a rewrite of the checker. Read what it does, establish which case this is, and land the smaller of the two.

SCOPE: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and its tests. Do NOT edit spec/ pages to work around it.

FENCE: none known at filing. Re-derive at dispatch.

title: ci: a stale SETUP_PATTERNS entry fails check_fast_pr_gap.py OPEN with exit 0 — nothing in CI catches it
description:
MEASURED BY PLANTING under rf2-mul6w (PR #8539). Every premise is reproducible.

WHAT WAS PLANTED. In a worktree carrying the 14 prefixed Playwright call sites (`timeout -k 10 720 npx playwright install ...`), the SETUP_PATTERNS entry was reverted to its pre-fix form `^npx playwright install\b` — i.e. exactly the drift this bead is about: a setup pattern that no longer matches the call sites it covers.

WHAT HAPPENED. `python scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` (the default --check mode) EXITED 0 and printed 'fast-PR gap map clean'. The only visible effect was the headline count moving from 'REQUIRED CHECKS THIS SPINE DOES NOT RUN (96)' to (106), with 10 toolchain-setup steps silently reclassified as unrun GATES — each listed with its own reproduce command telling a reader to run `npx playwright install` locally.

WHY THAT IS THE WRONG DIRECTION. The file's own docstring states the safe direction — 'a new CI job or a new step inside an existing one is reported as UNRUN until somebody teaches this file otherwise' — and that is true for the LANES. It is not true for SETUP_PATTERNS, where the same drift inflates the gap map with false entries and no exit code changes. The header of .github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh calls this 'a fail-open in the very map the merge criterion consults', which is precisely right, and nothing detects it.

THE DRIFT RATCHET DOES NOT COVER THIS. `--check`'s ratchet fires when a SPINE_LANES signature stops matching any required gate step. A SETUP_PATTERNS entry that stops matching has no equivalent: it produces MORE unrun entries, which reads as normal.

SHAPE OF A FIX (not prescriptive). A floor per setup pattern — 'this entry must match at least one required step' — would catch it the same way MIN_REQUIRED_JOBS and MIN_SPINE_CHECKERS catch an empty parse, and in the same spirit. A pattern that matches nothing is either dead or drifted, and both are worth a red.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN #8539. That PR was fenced to closing the annotation gap without fail-opening this map, and it proved by planting that its own pattern-and-call-site change keeps `--list` byte-identical. Adding a new ratchet arm to the gate is a separate change to a hot-zone file.

VERIFICATION ALREADY DONE, reusable here: planting a NON-timeout prefix (`nice -n 5 npx playwright install ...`) at one site moves the count 96 -> 97, so the map does discriminate — it just does not fail.
close_reason: Fixed in this PR. REPRODUCED the fail-open first: reverting the Playwright SETUP_PATTERNS entry to its pre-timeout form took --check's headline 96 -> 106 with exit 0 and 'fast-PR gap map clean'; --self-test also passed. The bead's sketched fix DOES NOT WORK and the measurement says so: 3 of the 13 required Playwright installs are still written bare, so a per-pattern 'matches at least one required step' floor stays GREEN under that exact drift while 10 steps silently become gates. Fix instead watches the CLASSIFICATION: SETUP_CANARIES names a TOOL where SETUP_PATTERNS names a CALL SHAPE, and a required GATE step whose EVERY line is nothing but toolchain installation is a problem. Post-fix the same plant exits 1 with 10 problems naming each drifted call site. The new arm immediately found two LIVE instances of the same class: both 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund' steps were reported as required checks the spine does not run; '^npm install$' widened to long-flag form, and --list loses exactly those two entries (96 -> 94), a narrowing in the correct direction. Self-tests exercise the arm against the known-WRONG answer, the negative control, and the floor that would have passed the failing case.

title: ci: the 300s Playwright step cap is now 1.8x its worst observed success, not 6.1x — a judgement for Mike
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-mul6w (PR #8539), which was fenced OUT of changing any cap. Filing rather than acting.

MEASURED 2026-08-20 over the 140 most recent completed test.yml runs (window 2026-08-18T05:11Z .. 2026-08-20T10:13Z, ALL attempts, every step named 'Install Playwright*'): 377 non-skipped samples, 370 successes.

THE POPULATION THE CAP NOTE DESCRIBES IS GONE. rf2-g3lv's note above the cljs-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation install step recorded 'p50 13s, p90 21s, max 49s. The 300s cap is 6.1x the observed worst case.' Re-derived: p50 14s and p90 34s still, but p95 113s, p99 424s, MAX 621s. FOUR of the 370 successes finished ABOVE 300s (424s, 556s, 589s, 621s).

WHY THAT IS NOT YET AN EMERGENCY. All four sit at jobs with NO step-level cap. Across the three step-capped sites (cljs-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation, tenant-switcher-testbed-smoke, mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair) the worst success is 164s over 80 samples, so the 300s cap is 1.8x its own site's worst case. Clear, but not the comfortable margin the note claims.

WHY IT MIGHT BE ONE. Two of the five install stalls measured on 2026-08-19 were at step-capped sites and died at 312s and 313s (jobs 95959283361, 95932283494) — i.e. AT the cap. Given four uncapped-site successes ran past 300s in the same window, those two are consistent with installs that would have completed given more time, which would make them cap-induced reds rather than genuine outages. Not established either way; distinguishing them needs the raw apt/download timings from those two logs.

THE DECISION IS MIKE'S. rf2-g3lv says DO NOT RAISE THIS NUMBER, and its reasoning still stands on its own terms: the cap exists to bound the rf2-e6enf wedge where four PRs sat 15-75+ min on an apt/dpkg lock. Raising it re-widens exactly that window. So this is a trade between two real costs, not a bug with a fix. rf2-mul6w corrected the stale numbers in the comment and left the cap untouched.

PR #8539 already: re-derived the rate, corrected both stale claims in test.yml's comment block, and closed the no-annotation gap at the 14 job-capped sites.
notes: COST OF THIS HOLD, recorded 2026-08-20 23:50 AUSEST, backlog reread. Checked at source: this bead has NO dependants — nothing blocks on it and nothing stops if it stays. It is a standalone judgement about whether the 300s Playwright step cap should move now that it sits at 1.8x its worst observed success rather than 6.1x. The cost of waiting is that the cap stays where it is; the cost of getting it wrong in either direction is a flaky gate or a slow one. Recorded so it does not read as free and does not get re-triaged every tick.
close_reason:
MIKE'S RULING, 2026-08-21: ACCEPT THE TIGHTER MARGIN. The 300s Playwright step cap STAYS where it is. His stated warrant: it has not been tripped recently. No change to any workflow file; this bead closes on a decision to leave things as they are, which is why there is no PR to cross-reference.

WHAT THIS DECIDES, so a future reader does not re-derive it: the cap sitting at 1.8x its worst observed success rather than the original 6.1x is ACCEPTED as a margin, not treated as a defect. The ratio moving is not by itself grounds to raise the cap.

ONE THING I CHECKED AND AM RECORDING RATHER THAN SUPPRESSING, because it neither overturns the ruling nor deserves to be lost: of the last 40 'tests' workflow runs sampled at close time, 5 succeeded, 2 were still running and 1 was CANCELLED. A cancellation is not a cap trip — the method's own discriminator is elapsed time against the declared cap, where landing ON the cap is a timeout kill and finishing well inside it is a superseding push or a hand cancel, and supersessions are routine under a busy fleet. I did not establish which this was, so it is recorded as unexamined rather than as evidence either way.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: an actual trip — a Playwright step cancelled at or near 300s elapsed. That is the signal, not the ratio.

The pair-mcp CountCheck in scripts/check_readme_inventories.py uses

title: hicasso: the floor arm's mode RATE is not a property of the revision — 0%, 10% and 53% at 4a1537cb71
description:
MEASURED by rf2-c4hhk's seventy-run window (PR #8531), record docs/design/hicasso/studio/does-arming-the-census-move-the-high-level.md, 70 datasets under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-c4hhk/. Filed rather than chased: rf2-c4hhk was sent to answer the armed/unarmed confound and did, and this is a second finding from the same data.

THE OBSERVATION. Three windows at the SAME revision (4a1537cb71), on the SAME instrument (no bench file has changed since 408dfb0aa8), with the SAME plan (floor, write-all, ROOTS=4, CELLS=6, ROUNDS=18) and the SAME estimator, produce three incompatible rates for the elevated mode:

  rf2-n1b9h    6 runs    0 high     0%
  rf2-77gz8   20 runs    2 high    10%
  rf2-c4hhk   69 runs   37 high    53%

WHY IT IS NOT AN ARMING EFFECT, which is the first thing to exclude and the one thing this data can exclude cleanly. rf2-c4hhk alternated armed and unarmed runs strictly, and BOTH ARMS MOVED TOGETHER: 52.9% armed (18 of 34) against 54.3% unarmed (19 of 35). An arming effect would have separated them; an environment effect moves both, and did. rf2-n1b9h's 0% was all-armed and rf2-77gz8's 10% was all-armed, so neither of those is an arming contrast either.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every measurement window on this arm SIZES ITS RUN COUNT against a prior rate, and a pre-declared count is the one thing in these windows that cannot be revised after the fact. rf2-77gz8 sized twenty runs against a re-derived 1-in-7 and got 2 of 20; rf2-c4hhk sized seventy against a re-derived 8.7% on the binding arm and got 53%, i.e. it took roughly four times the runs it needed. The error runs in the expensive direction here, but a window sized against 53% when the box happens to be in the 0% state would produce a null and report a refusal, and the refusal would be an artefact of the sizing rather than a fact about the arm. So this is a live risk to the METHOD, not only an oddity.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is most of it. Nothing here identifies what the rate depends on. The three windows differ in wall-clock date, in what else the box was doing, and in nothing that any dataset records. Candidates worth separating, none of them supported yet: machine load or thermal state at the time of the window; a resident-runtime difference (the Chromium binary is pinned by playwright but the datasets do not record its build); and a within-window ordering effect, since rf2-c4hhk's runs were back-to-back for ninety minutes where earlier corpora were not.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, or at least bound it. The cheap first move is to record what the datasets currently do not: the Chromium build string, the box's load at window open, and the elapsed time since the previous run, all of which ride free on an existing field the way rf2-n1b9h's census does. That converts the next window into evidence about the rate at no extra runner cost. A DELIBERATE variation — the same plan run cold, run hot, and run after an idle gap — is the confirming second move and should not be taken first.

NOTE this bead is about the RATE only. The LEVELS are settled: rf2-c4hhk established that arming moves neither, and the level values themselves reproduce to the byte across all three windows.

  workcount-n1b9h   6 runs   0 high    0.0%
  alloc-77gz8      20 runs   2 high   10.0%   (run09 and run19, both at 21,632 / 22,072)
  alloc-c4hhk      69 runs  37 high   53.6%   (armed 18/34 = 52.9%, unarmed 19/35 = 54.3%)
All three reproduce this bead's figures exactly, including the armed/unarmed non-separation. armed-25 carries no `alloc` block at all, which is the 1 inadmissible of 70.

WHAT THE DATA ALREADY ANSWERS, and it is this bead's own first-named candidate. `generatedAt` is recorded on every run, so the within-window ordering effect is testable NOW without recording anything new:

  session DURATION vs rate      n1b9h  8.2 min -> 0%    77gz8 19.7 min -> 10%    c4hhk 88.3 min -> 53.6%
  c4hhk BY ELAPSED QUARTER      Q1 5/19 = 26.3%   Q2 12/18 = 66.7%   Q3 10/17 = 58.8%   Q4 10/15 = 66.7%

The Q1-vs-rest contrast is a WITHIN-SESSION comparison at ONE revision on ONE box, so it separates elapsed time from wall-clock date and from revision — one-tail hypergeometric P(<=5 high in the first 19 | 37/69 overall) = 0.0054.

And once you condition on the early-session rate the "three incompatible rates" stop being incompatible: at p = 0.263, P(0 high of 6) = 0.16 for n1b9h and P(<=2 of 20) = 0.072 for 77gz8 — neither surprising. Against the POOLED 53.6% they are: 77gz8's 2 of 20 has p = 5.9e-05. So the three rates are consistent with ONE within-session gradient plus sampling, rather than three properties of three revisions.

STATED AT ITS TRUE STRENGTH. This locates the rate on elapsed-time-within-session; it does NOT name a mechanism (thermal, V8 tier accumulation, heap fragmentation over a long session all survive), and across the three corpora duration is confounded with date and time-of-day. The within-c4hhk gradient is the arm that is NOT so confounded.

FILES a worker would touch: none in the rig for the analysis half — read `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/{workcount-n1b9h,alloc-77gz8,alloc-c4hhk}/`, add a reader beside `alloc_heap_trajectory.cjs` (same directory, launches nothing), and publish under `docs/design/hicasso/studio/`. SUBSUMPTION: not a duplicate. rf2-c4hhk settled arming; rf2-77gz8 settled the LEVELS. This is the only owner of the RATE. Not answered by any merged PR I can find.

VERDICT: dispatchable TODAY, beside anything, as an ANALYSIS bead. Do not spend a bench window on it.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE 2026-08-21 03:21 TRIAGE.

(1) THE QUARTILE p IS BOUNDARY-SENSITIVE, and the boundary is a choice rather than a measurement. P(at most 5 high among the first k of 69 | 37 high) reads 0.0210 at k=17, 0.0109 at k=18, 0.0054 at k=19 and 0.0025 at k=20 -- an EIGHTFOLD move across a two-run choice -- and a first-half/second-half split gives 0.093. The triage's p = 0.0054 reproduces exactly at k=19 and should not be the figure a record leads with. The page therefore leads with a test that has NO cut point: Mann-Whitney on each run's position in its session, high against low, U = 763 against a null mean of 592, z = 2.058, ONE-TAIL p = 0.0198. The gradient is real at about p = 0.02, not p = 0.005. The reader's fixtures REQUIRE the sweep to move at least fourfold across the cut and require the boundary-free test to come out weaker than the best cut, so a change that made the quartile figure look robust reds them.

(2) THE BISECT'S HIGH RUN IS THE SECOND OF EIGHT, NOT THE THIRD. The triage's own ordered list shows pilot-rounds6 at +0.0 and bisect-1-a at +3.6; its prose beside that list said third. The direction of the bound is unaffected -- second is if anything earlier.

CONDITIONAL CONSISTENCY, stated as that and not as a test. Against the long session's own early rate (5 of 19 = 26.3%) the two short sessions are unremarkable: P(0 of 6) = 0.160 and P(<=2 of 20) = 0.072. Against its POOLED 53.6% they are 0.0099 and 5.89e-05. All four reproduce the triage exactly. The reference rate is taken from the same data the gradient was found in, so the second row is not an independent confirmation of the first; what it establishes is that ONE within-session gradient plus ordinary sampling accounts for all three observations, where three properties of three revisions is not needed.

THE HONEST BOUND, AND IT SURVIVED INTO THE RECORD IN THREE PLACES -- the page's summary, its body at length, and four reader fixtures that pin it as literals, because it is the half a write-up is most likely to lose. alloc-9jrhi's single high run sits at +3.6 min, SECOND of eight, in a 14.9-minute session. Under the within-c4hhk gradient (27.8% in the first quarter against 52.9-68.8% after) an early run is where a high is LEAST likely. So ELAPSED TIME DOES NOT EXPLAIN THIS RUN, and this bead does NOT discharge rf2-9jrhi's revision-dependence question. It would have, had the high run landed late; it landed early, so the RATE and the mode's REVISION-DEPENDENCE stay separate questions. Nothing here is to be cited as bearing on rf2-9jrhi.

One nuance worth keeping: the bisect's RATE (12.5% at 14.9 min) fits the duration ordering perfectly well. It is its INTERNAL ORDERING that does not fit the within-session gradient. Two different claims about the same eight runs, kept apart on the page.

NOT CONCLUDED: no mechanism (thermal, V8 tier accumulation, heap fragmentation all survive equally); across the three sessions duration is confounded with date and clock time; the whole gradient rests on ONE session; and the LEVELS were not reopened.

THE SECOND MOVE IS CARRIED OUT RATHER THAN DROPPED: filed as rf2-24o2z (record the Chromium build string, the box's load at window open and the inter-run gap). It is hermetic, needs no window, and is a p0_run.cjs change one-toucher with rf2-fk6pj / rf2-csca8 / rf2-onozm -- the mayor's to bundle.
