title: [method-drift] the merge criterion's 'scope did not sprawl' does not name the silent-revert shape, and that is the shape that reached a branch today
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-19 11:25 AUSEST, from a live instance rather than by reading. Filed rather than committed: .claude/commands/ is a worker-tracked surface the mayor checkout's pre-commit hook correctly refuses.

THE INSTANCE. worker/armconf-c4hhk's commit 799334f970 carries the subject 'bench(p0): amend the level-assignment rule at run 3 of 70'. Its contents are 24 files: one studio record and TWENTY-THREE under implementation/core/src/, at 611 insertions and 910 deletions. The 23 are a reversion to pre-retirement content — core.cljc's + side re-introduces 're-frame.ui.frames/mint-frame-ops', a string absent from origin/main and belonging to the RETIRED tree. Mechanism: a worktree whose base had moved, plus a git add -A. Full evidence is on rf2-c4hhk.

WHAT THE COMMAND FILE SAYS TODAY. .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md's merging paragraph says to check 'the diff matches its bead, scope did not sprawl, failure output stays actionable, and a ## Quality gates section is present'. That is not wrong, and read strictly it covers this. But 'scope did not sprawl' describes EXTRA WORK — a worker doing more than it was asked. This is the opposite shape: the diff carries files the worker never edited, at content OLDER than the trunk, and its subject truthfully describes the one file it meant to change.

WHY THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN PEDANTIC. A sprawling scope announces itself — the extra files are new work and read as new work. A silent revert announces nothing: it is well-formed, it compiles, it passes every gate the tree has, and its commit MESSAGE is accurate about the part the author knew about. The five clauses cannot see it, because they measure whether CI is green and CI is green. dispatch-prompt-template.md already tells the WORKER to catch this — 'diff your branch against its MERGE BASE before you push, and read that diff for what you would REVERT' — so the method knows the shape; what is missing is the MAYOR-side half at the moment of merge, where a worker that failed to run its own check is exactly the case that matters.

THE FIX, and keep it to the existing paragraph. Add to the merging checks: read the file LIST against the bead, not just the count — a path the bead does not explain is a finding whichever direction it runs — and for any surprising path, check whether the branch's content is OLDER than the trunk's rather than newer. Name the cheap test: git diff --name-only <merge-base> <branch>, and for a suspicious file, whether a string present on the branch is absent from origin/main. Do NOT add a sixth clause: the five test whether the change is GREEN, and this is a different question, the same way the draft filter is a filter on the list rather than a clause.

DO NOT add a gate, a script or a CI check. A commit that reverts merged work is indistinguishable from one that does not, mechanically — the only discriminator is whether a human-or-agent reader expected those paths.

ACCEPTANCE: one paragraph amended in .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md, citing this bead and rf2-c4hhk; python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci exits 0 (that gate owns .claude/commands/*.md — read its COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC and the command-file arm at source and say why, and note that the arm resolves path-shaped references, so a path you cite must be tracked). check_doc_slugs.py does NOT cover this path; run it only as a control.

So 'owner column 001, 004' becomes '001'; '002, 004' becomes '002, 001'; ':owner "004"' becomes ':owner "001"'. Verify each cell against this rule rather than applying it blind — a cell that names some third spec is not covered by this ruling and should be reported.

WHY, read at source rather than reasoned from the titles, and the division already exists in writing:
  spec/001-Registration.md:85 carries the registration GRAMMAR — that reg-view is the only registration shipping as a defn-shape macro, with reg-view* as the plain-fn partner for runtime and programmatic registration.
  :98 carries the :view kind row in the registration-kind table.
  :260-269 carries the runtime-lookup handle (re-frame.core/view id), what it returns for each render-fn shape, and why the id-keyed registry needs it.

So 001 owns the grammar and the handle; 002 owns what the macro injects. That is not a split I am inventing to settle a manifest cell — 001:359 already points at 002 for exactly this, and the ruling only records which of the two inherits the deleted document's share.

It does not make the api-manifest pair a prose repair. spec/api-manifest.edn and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn are GENERATED AND CHECKED data, so whoever takes them establishes the generator and its gate first and changes the source rather than the artefact — and reports which gate covers it. title: [hic] TRIAGE ONLY: classify the 64 hicasso product files by KIND — the number rf2-ps7ia turns on
description:
REQUESTED BY MIKE, 2026-08-19 10:13 AUSEST. This is a MEASUREMENT bead. It moves nothing, edits nothing, and rules nothing. Its whole deliverable is a classification and a set of counts.

WHY IT EXISTS. rf2-ps7ia must decide where the hicasso normative set lives, and that decision reads very differently depending on how much of the set is actually normative. Nobody has counted. The mayor twice said 'roughly forty files' in chat; the measured figure is SIXTY-FOUR files and 17,044 lines under docs/design/hicasso/product/, with thirteen of those in the lanes/ subtree, against 131 files across the whole docs/design/hicasso/ tree. So the estimate was low by half, which is itself the argument for counting before deciding.

THE QUESTION THIS ANSWERS: is the hicasso spec tree a four-file job or a thirty-file programme? If it is small, rf2-ps7ia is easy and can be executed in one pass. If it is large, it is a sequenced programme and needs to be planned as one.

=== WHAT TO DO ===

Classify EVERY file under docs/design/hicasso/product/ into exactly one of four kinds. Report the counts, and the per-file assignment as a table.

1. VIEW SPECIFICATION — normative statements about how a view is AUTHORED in hicasso. The thing a consumer must obey to write hicasso views correctly. This is the kind with no current home, which is what makes the count matter.
2. SUBSTRATE CONTRACT — normative statements about what a SUBSTRATE must provide. These already have a home in spec/ proper: 004B carries the structural render-tree ABI, 004C root identity and the mount grammar, 006 the substrate contract. If a file is this kind, name which of those it belongs beside.
3. READER-FACING ANSWER — content a hicasso user needs, which belongs stated on a guide page under docs/core/hicasso/ rather than in a design record. Precedent: rf2-75q3l, where three published pages routed readers into an excluded tree and the fix was to make the pages answer their own questions rather than relocate anything.
4. WORKING RECORD — provenance, measurement windows, budgets, decision history. These stay exactly where they are; docs/design is the right tree for them and their provenance pins are gated there.

A file may be MIXED. Say so explicitly rather than forcing it, and give the rough proportion — a 90% working record with one normative paragraph is a very different problem from a half-and-half file, and the mixed count is one of the numbers the decision turns on.

=== ESTABLISHED CONTEXT — verify each at source, do not inherit ===

MIKE'S DIRECTION, 2026-08-19: an artefact-local implementation/hicasso/spec/ folder IS the likely destination for kind 1, CONDITIONAL on spec/ not carrying view specification. THE CONDITION HOLDS: spec/README.md:66 states in terms 'There is no 004 view contract.' spec/004-Views.md and the S3/S4/S5 view-conformance profiles were deleted under rf2-h89ri (PR #8500), and the hole was DECLARED rather than papered over. What survives — 004B, 004C, 006 — is substrate-facing, not view-authoring.

THE PRECEDENT for an artefact-local spec tree is tools/: seven of them carry one (xray, story, template, machines-viz, mcp-base, story-mcp, re-frame2-pair-mcp). There is currently NO spec/ or design/ directory anywhere under implementation/ — this would be the first.

=== TWO RIDERS TO REPORT ON, NOT TO FIX ===

A. THE GATE GAP. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py has DEFAULT_ROOTS of docs, spec, skills, migration, plus an explicit special case for tools/<tool>/spec/**. implementation/** is in NEITHER, and check_readme_links.py reaches only READMEs beside source. So a normative tree at implementation/hicasso/spec/ would be UNGATED from day one — no link or anchor validation. Confirm that at source and say what the smallest correct fix looks like. DO NOT BUILD IT.

B. A POSSIBLE RULING COLLISION. rf2-h89ri deliberately wrote NO 'see hicasso' pointer into spec when it declared the hole, citing rf2-0yp7w.11. A reader hitting 'there is no 004 view contract' should eventually be told where the view spec lives. Read rf2-0yp7w.11 and say whether it forbids that pointer, or whether it only forbade re-aiming RETIRED freehand/ui material at hicasso. Those are different, and the mayor has not verified which.

=== SCOPE FENCE ===

NO MOVES. NO EDITS to any classified file. NO new spec tree. NO gate change. The deliverable is a report and, if it is useful, ONE new working document recording the classification.

Out of scope: the whole of docs/design/hicasso/ outside product/ (the other 67 files) unless your reading shows product/ cannot be classified without them — in which case say so and stop rather than widening.

DO NOT rule rf2-ps7ia. That decision is Mike's and this bead exists to inform it.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

1. Every one of the 64 files assigned a kind, or explicitly marked mixed with a proportion.
2. Counts per kind, and a line count per kind — a four-file kind carrying 6,000 lines is not small.
3. For kind 2, the spec/ document each file belongs beside.
4. The two riders reported with source citations.
5. A one-paragraph answer to the question that prompted this: is the view-specification set a small job or a programme?
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8522 (2026-08-20): reopen exact owner. The delivered census is internally inconsistent about the number of view-specification carriers. Its own per-file classification attributes VS content to 12 files (lanes/adversarial-risks, design-laws, ergonomics-api, hot-path-architecture, react-compatibility-notes, testing-xray, use-cases; plus specification, invariants, facade-freeze, dispositions, complaints), while the headline and conclusion say seven documents. The section titled 'What the seven view-specification carriers actually hold' contains eight rows summing about 1,001 VS lines and silently omits four classified carriers totaling about 135 more lines (adversarial-risks ~15, hot-path ~21, use-cases ~7, complaints ~92), which is how the headline total reaches ~1,136. Acceptance: distinguish the seven files whose PRIMARY kind is VS from all 12 files carrying attributed VS; reconcile the headline, carrier table, small-job conclusion, and owner summary; include or explicitly justify excluded carriers; recompute totals if any classification changes.
close_reason: RECONCILED. PR #8551 (draft->ready) closes the AUDIT-REOPEN #8522 finding. No classification changed; the page now states both file counts (7 primary VS, 12 carrying any VS), lists all twelve carriers so the table reconciles with the headline, and re-derives every count at commit 5858e9317a. Counts and both riders are recorded in full on the bead comment above so rf2-ps7ia can read them without opening the file. Answer unchanged and strengthened: a SMALL JOB (~1,138 normative lines, under 7%, three or four authored documents in one pass), NOT a thirty-file programme — but plan the reading against twelve carriers, not seven, and expect a rewrite in voice rather than a move.

title: [method-drift] no dispatch guidance says to exclude .beads/ from a census, and the export is 15 MB
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-19 00:19 AUSEST. Filed rather than committed: .claude/commands/ is a worker-tracked surface the mayor checkout's pre-commit hook correctly refuses.

THE FACT. .beads/issues.jsonl is 15,007,876 bytes — a full-database export, one issue per line, carrying every title, description and comment in the tracker. It therefore matches almost ANY identifier a census greps for: a namespace, a spec filename, a keyword, a bead id, a build target.

WHAT NOTHING SAYS. Measured:
  • .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md — ZERO mentions of the export.
  • CLAUDE.md mentions issues.jsonl eight times, ALL of them about DURABILITY (never commit it from a worker branch, never stash, checkpoint before clearing). None about search noise.
  • No file under docs/, .claude/ or CLAUDE.md warns that a census must exclude it.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE MORE THAN IN MOST REPOSITORIES. This project runs census-shaped dispatches constantly — the entire retirement programme is 'find every reference to X and adjudicate each one'. A census is the DEFAULT shape of work here, and the default shape has an unstated trap.

THE COST IS TWO-SIDED, and the second side is the dangerous one:
  1. NOISE. The mayor ran git grep -nF for a token tree-wide during this session and got 124 KB of tracker rows back — a single bead description, thousands of characters, before any real hit. In a context-bounded worker that is a material loss for nothing.
  2. A WRONG COUNT THAT LOOKS RIGHT. A worker reported roughly 33 files carrying :freehand-release. Measured with .beads excluded the number is 16. The inflated count came from counting the export. A census that over-counts sends a worker looking for sites that do not exist and undermines its own verdict — and nothing in the output announces that a tracker row is not a source file.

THE FIX: one short paragraph in .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, in the region that already talks about how a search underwrites a claim. Say that any tree-wide census excludes .beads/ (git grep pathspec ':!.beads'), say WHY in one clause (a 15 MB full-database export matches almost everything), and say that a count taken without that exclusion is wrong rather than merely noisy.

DO NOT restate the file size as a pinned constant — it grows every checkpoint. 'A full-database export, currently tens of megabytes' is the durable form.

DO NOT add a gate or a wrapper script. The repair is one sentence in the file a mayor executes while writing a census brief. The rule is already being hand-written into individual briefs, which is the drift this bead closes — a rule enforced ad hoc by whoever remembers it is not a rule.

ALSO VERIFIED THIS PASS, so the next reread need not re-derive it: the check-count band is 88, confirmed from PRs #8512, #8511 and #8510, all merged this session. mayor-merge.md's recorded value is current. And docs/the-mayor-method/** plus .claude/commands/mayor-*.md are UNCHANGED since the previous pass — newest commits are still 71b97d4dbc, 6120eff90f and 4a5cbfea87, the first two of which are this session's own filed fixes, both landed.

Gaps confirmed at tip before editing: grep -ci 'admissib' = 0, grep -c 'issues.jsonl' = 0. Paragraph 1 (census excludes .beads/, count is WRONG not merely noisy, size written as 'currently tens of megabytes' rather than pinned) sits at the end of the Find + group region beside the existing 'A COUNT IS A CLAIM TOO' material. Paragraph 2 (exit code is not a verdict; a measurement brief names the record's own admissibility criteria and states the expected exit code; criteria NOT enumerated) sits after the gate-mechanics-paraphrase paragraph where this file's .exit-file material lives, and says plainly never to write 'the exit code is the verdict' for a runner that refuses by design. Premises verified at source: p0_run.cjs resolves at implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs, its header documents exit 1 as an expected refusal signal and --only alloc is a real lane; the ':!.beads' pathspec measured 23 files -> 21 with the export excluded. comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MAYOR — A SECOND PARAGRAPH FOR THE SAME FILE, found by the next method-reread pass. 2026-08-19 01:15 AUSEST. Folded here rather than filed separately: same surface (.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md), same fix shape (one short paragraph), and a bead per paragraph is the sprawl the stance rejects.

THE DRIFT. Nothing in mayor-dispatch.md distinguishes a runner's EXIT CODE from a window's ADMISSIBILITY. Measured: grep -ci for 'admissib' returns 0, and for 'expected exit' or 'non-zero expected' returns 0.

WHY THAT MATTERS, and it is my own error rather than a hypothetical. I wrote into a measurement dispatch this session: 'the bench runner's own captured exit code is the verdict for the window.' It is wrong. p0_run.cjs --only alloc documents a NON-ZERO expected exit. All twenty runs of that window exited 1. Nineteen were admissible; one failed its positive CONTROL, read low, and was excluded — while exiting exactly like the nineteen good ones. Admissibility is decided by the CONTROLS, READ-BACK VERIFICATION and the PER-WINDOW CERTIFICATE. A worker taking me literally would have folded a control-failing run into the series and shifted the level it reported.

WHY IT IS AN EASY MISTAKE TO REPEAT, which is the argument for stating it: the file's neighbouring rule — capture the runner's OWN exit code, never the harness-reported one — is correct and load-bearing, and 'exit code is the verdict' sounds like the same rule. It is not. That rule says WHOSE number to read. It does not say the number means pass. For an instrument whose job is to refuse, a non-zero exit is the NORMAL case and the verdict lives in the artefact the run produced.

THE FIX: one paragraph beside the existing exit-code guidance. Say that for a MEASUREMENT runner the brief must name the record's own admissibility criteria and state what the expected exit code IS, so a worker can tell a routine refusal from a crash. Say plainly that 'the exit code is the verdict' must never be written for an instrument that refuses by design.

DO NOT enumerate the criteria as a fixed list — they are per-gate and the worker reads them from the record. The rule is 'brief the criteria the record states', not 'here are the criteria'.

ALSO VERIFIED THIS PASS, so the next reread need not re-derive it: the check-count band is 88, measured from PRs #8515, #8513 and #8514, all merged this session. docs/the-mayor-method/** and .claude/commands/mayor-*.md are UNCHANGED since the previous pass — newest commits still 71b97d4dbc, 6120eff90f, 4a5cbfea87.

title: [method-drift] the dispatch loop tells the mayor to re-enumerate CHILDREN, and the ruling that discharges a slice usually sits on a CLOSED DEPENDENCY
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-18, after the gap cost a full dispatch the same evening. This is a rule the mayor is ENFORCING that no command file states at the moment of use — the failure class this loop exists to catch.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS SAY TODAY. `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md:389`, under *Dispatch*, says: "And when a bead has children, re-enumerate them — a ruling is sometimes recorded as a new child bead rather than as a note." `.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md` carries the newest-text-by-timestamp mechanics in full and mentions a close reason only once, in an unrelated passage about routing a finding to a live worker. Neither file says the thing that actually bites.

WHAT IS MISSING, IN ONE SENTENCE. A ruling that discharges a slice is frequently recorded as the CLOSE REASON of a CLOSED bead, and that bead is often linked as a DEPENDENCY under a generated id rather than as an id-prefixed child — so an enumeration of open children cannot see it, and a close reason is normative text rather than an archival note.

THE MEASURED INSTANCE, 2026-08-18 17:18. Dispatching a slice of rf2-0yp7w.9 (the R6 prose sweep), the mayor enumerated the epic's children with a filter on ids beginning `rf2-0yp7w` and found three, all open. The bead that GOVERNED the slice was rf2-0moc4 — a standalone generated id, CLOSED, linked as a dependency — whose close reason reads "RULED (a) KEEP — docs/design/freehand/ stays, contents untouched" and states in terms that the word "Deletes." in rf2-0yp7w.9's own sub-surface list is AN ERROR, NOT AN INSTRUCTION. The id-prefix filter could not see it; `bd show rf2-0yp7w.9` prints it under DEPENDS ON, which is where it had been all along.

The worker refused correctly, re-derived all five of the ruling's reasons, and proved the deciding one by planting a fault: deleting 1 of the 37 files reds `check_doc_slugs.py` through `spec/004-Views.md`'s eleven links. Nothing landed, so the cost was one worker cycle rather than a wrong result — the method's own dominant error class, the mayor's brief.

WHY THE EXISTING SENTENCE MAKES IT WORSE RATHER THAN NEUTRAL. "A ruling is sometimes recorded as a new CHILD bead" is what a mayor reads and trusts, and it is incomplete in the direction that fails: it points at children, so a mayor who follows it faithfully still misses a dependency. An instruction that names one of two carriers reads as exhaustive.

THE REPAIR, and it is two or three sentences in each file rather than a section:

`docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md`, under *Dispatch*, beside the existing children sentence:
  * a ruling may be recorded as a child bead OR as a linked dependency, and it is usually CLOSED by the time it governs;
  * read the item's dependency list, not only its children, and read each linked item's STATUS and CLOSE REASON — a close reason is normative text;
  * enumerating by id prefix is not enumerating: generated ids do not share the parent's prefix.

`.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md`, in the "Find + group" paragraph that already tells the mayor to establish the newest text before briefing: the same three points, pinned to `bd show <id>`'s DEPENDS ON block and to reading closed links.

SCOPE NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT. Both files are hot in the sense that two workers in them conflict; sequence against anything else editing them. Keep it tight — `mayor-dispatch.md` is already dense, and the stance rejects gold-plating. This is a missing clause, not a new section.

title: [method-drift] CLAUDE.md names the wrong link gate for root and implementation READMEs, and omits the CI classifier from the hot-zone list
description:

Both run in `test.yml`'s `verify-readme-links` job on every PR. And say the thing that generalises: the job's NAME reads as though it checks READMEs, and the gate that actually does is the other one.

ITEM 2 — THE HOT-ZONE LIST OMITS THE CI CLASSIFIER.

Two workers in that pair conflict every time.

That omission is live right now — rf2-7b1ti's routing half is in flight and had to be fenced by hand because the list does not carry it.

THE REPAIR: add `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` and its mirror `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` to the hot-zone enumeration, noting that they move in ONE commit.

BOTH ITEMS ARE ONE SMALL PROSE PR ON A HOT-ZONE FILE. CLAUDE.md is not in the enumerated hot-zone list itself, but it is a single-toucher in practice — sequence it against anything else editing it.

The three blocks were extracted MECHANICALLY — `sed -n` line ranges out of `mayor-posture.md` and `dispatch-prompt-template.md` — concatenated with the task-specific half into one brief file per worker under the session scratch directory, and the dispatch prompt was three sentences: read this file IN FULL before anything else, here is the one-line subject, and the premises-are-claims sentence. Every block therefore reached every worker byte-identical to its source. What changed is the TRANSPORT, not the content.

WHY IT IS WORTH RULING RATHER THAN JUST STOPPING. There is a real argument on each side and the mayor should not settle it alone.

FOR the file: a `sed` range CANNOT paraphrase, and paraphrase is the failure the three "paste it VERBATIM" rules exist to prevent — the command file spends a whole paragraph on the gate-mechanics block being "the one a mayor is most tempted to PARAPHRASE", and it names five dispatches in one session that carried five different lengths of it. Mechanical extraction closes that failure by construction rather than by discipline. It also keeps ~25KB of boilerplate per dispatch out of the mayor's context, which is the resource the whole method is organised around.

AGAINST the file: it adds a step that can fail silently. A worker that skims, or that reads the file partially, has not received the blocks at all — and nothing in the transcript distinguishes that from a worker that read every line. A pasted block is IN the prompt and cannot be un-received. The failure mode is also invisible in exactly the way this method keeps warning about: the dispatch looks identical either way, and the first evidence would be a worker doing something a block forbids.

THE THIRD OPTION, and it may be the right one: keep the mechanical extraction and paste the RESULT into the prompt — the same file, `cat`-ed into the dispatch rather than referenced by path. That takes the paraphrase risk to zero AND the un-read risk to zero, at the cost of the mayor's context, which is the one thing being economised.

WHAT SHOULD HAPPEN. Mike (or a delegated ruling) picks one, and whichever is picked, `.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md` and `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` say so explicitly — because right now the tree does something the governing file does not describe, which is precisely the drift the method-reread loop exists to catch. If the ruling is "paste it, as written", this bead closes by the mayor complying and no document changes.

EVIDENCE OF THE PROPERTY CLAIMED. The five brief files are assembled from `_common.md`, which is itself built by: `sed -n '8p' .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md` (stance), `sed -n '538,582p'` (common preamble), `sed -n '478,527p'` (worktree boundary block), `sed -n '637,849p'` (gate mechanics, from the paste-start paragraph to the end of the section) of `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md`. Those ranges are line-number claims against today's tip and would need re-deriving by content if either file moves.

RULING: THE THIRD OPTION. Extract the blocks MECHANICALLY, then PASTE THE RESULT INTO THE DISPATCH. Both halves are mandatory. The extraction is what makes paraphrase impossible; the paste is what makes non-receipt impossible. Referencing a brief file by path is OUT.

But the failure it introduces is the worse kind, because it is INVISIBLE. A worker that skims the file, or reads it partially, has not received the blocks, and nothing in the transcript distinguishes that worker from one that read every line. The first evidence would be a worker doing something a block forbids — which is the shape this whole method keeps warning about, and which the pasted form cannot produce, because a block that is in the prompt cannot be un-received. Between a failure prevented by construction and a failure prevented by a reader's diligence, the method takes construction every time.

WHAT IT COSTS, ACKNOWLEDGED RATHER THAN WAVED AWAY. Roughly 25KB of boilerplate per dispatch, spent from the mayor's context — the one resource the whole method is organised around. I am ruling that this is the right thing to spend it on. A brief is the mayor's scarce output, and README.md is blunt that briefs are where the errors are: workers corrected a mayor's stated premises about twenty times in one session, and each cost a full worker cycle. Context spent making a brief unambiguous is context spent on the highest-leverage artefact the mayor produces. Context saved by making it skippable is a false economy.

title: [method] mayor-dispatch.md never mentions the machine reservation, so a fresh mayor will dispatch straight through a live measurement window
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-18, checking rules the mayor ENFORCES against the command file governing the moment of use. Filed rather than committed because .claude/commands/ is a worker-touched tree — PR #8465 edited mayor-merge.md today — and the mayor checkout cannot commit there.

THE MEASUREMENT, with a positive control so the zero is real:

  grep -ciE 'reserv|quiet box|quiet machine|wedge|drain'  .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md   ->  0
  grep -ciE 'quiet box|quiet machine|wedge'               docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md       ->  3
  grep -ciE 'quiet box|quiet machine|wedge'               docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md -> 4
  grep -c  'GATE MECHANICS'                               .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md   ->  1   (control: the pattern works)

THE DEFECT. The rule exists in the generic method docs and NOWHERE in the command file a mayor actually reads while composing a dispatch. mayor-dispatch.md's own headline instruction is the opposite one — 'drive the open backlog as close to 0 as possible, up to 6 concurrent background workers, refilling the instant a slot frees'. A fresh mayor following that file faithfully, with a Shape 6 clock window live, will saturate the box and invalidate the window.

AND IT WILL NOT FAIL — IT WILL RETURN A PLAUSIBLE NUMBER. That is why this is worth a P2 on a documentation file. A poisoned clock window does not error; it produces a figure that gets published, cited, and built on. The mayor-hygiene.md file already carries the same rule for REAPS ('a reap is machine work: do not run one while a CLOCK measurement window is in flight … the window will not fail, it will return a plausible number that is worthless'), so the principle is established in this corpus — it is simply absent from the one file where dispatch decisions are made.

I ENFORCED IT ELEVEN TIMES TODAY FROM MEMORY ALONE, pasting a 'THE MACHINE IS RESERVED' clause into every dispatch issued while a window was live. Nothing in the tree would have told the next mayor to do that.

WHAT TO ADD to .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md — the shape, not the wording; write it in that file's voice:

  1. Before dispatching, establish whether a MEASUREMENT WINDOW is live and CLASSIFY ITS ESTIMAND. Only a CLOCK estimand needs the quiet box. An ALLOCATION census reads monotone counters and is unaffected by load — it must NOT consume a drain (measured on rf2-ojehu / PR #8419, and again 2026-08-18 by the rf2-0gjqi window).
  2. While a CLOCK window is live, the '6 concurrent workers' target is SUSPENDED. Dispatch only work that cannot load the box — documentation, YAML, tracker prose, cheap python checkers — and say so in chat rather than silently under-saturating.
  3. Every dispatch issued during a live window carries a machine-reservation clause naming what the worker may NOT run: no test-fast-pr.sh, no shadow-cljs, browser, Playwright, npm build or JVM gate; and 'if the only gate covering your surface is a heavy one, STOP AND REPORT' as a CORRECT outcome rather than a failure.
  4. Two heavyweight gates on one box WEDGE rather than fail — no progress, no exit file, no error — so even outside a measurement window, never dispatch two bench-class workers concurrently. Per-attempt artefact naming does nothing for it, because it is contention for the MACHINE.

CROSS-REFERENCE rather than restate: loops.md and dispatch-prompt-template.md own the reasoning; mayor-dispatch.md should pin the DECISION — classify the estimand, then decide — and point at them. Two copies of one rule disagree within days in this corpus.

WHAT IS NOT DRIFT, checked in the same pass and recorded so it is not re-derived: nothing in docs/the-mayor-method/** or .claude/commands/mayor-*.md has changed since 29e9b7e246 (PR #8465); the required-check band is 88, current, confirmed on PRs #8475 and #8478 today; scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py --list heads 94, matching mayor-merge.md clause 1 and confirmed independently by five workers today.

title: hicasso U1-U4 instrument: the bench lane computes no p95/p99, so no clock driver can pin the user-visible rows
description:
LOCATED BY rf2-85og2's 2026-08-18 window, which took no reading and re-verified all
three of its gates as still refused. This bead is the EDIT-SHAPED half of the first
of those three, and it builds fine on a LOUD box — only the run that follows it
needs the drain.

THE FINDING, and it is sharper than the refusal it replaces. budgets.md sec 4 and
sec 9.2 say "no package-resident clock instrument exists" and conclude that U1-U4
and C3/C4 each need "a clock instrument pointed at implementation/hicasso". That
sentence is now imprecise: TWO clock drivers have landed and one of them IS pointed
at the package —
implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/direct_return_clock_app.cljs
requires re-frame.hicasso itself, and budgets.md sec 4's S8 row calls its reading a
"package figure". The other,
implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/topo/clock_app.cljs (rf2-w01c,
window taken 2026-08-18), requires re-frame.bench.hicasso.arm1.runtime and is a
bench-tree instrument.

SO THE BLOCK IS THE ESTIMATOR, NOT THE INSTRUMENT'S AIM. In
implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs, `summarise` answers
`{:n :min :max :p50}` and NO p95 and NO p99 is computed anywhere on that lane —
while every one of U1, U2, U3 and U4 is registered at p95 or p99 (U2 is "50 ms p95
/ 100 ms p99"). budgets.md already records the same fact about C8's ">= 2 ms p95"
disjunct, in its own words: "the instrument computes no p95". rf2-w01c's published
NOT-concluded list reached it independently from the other side.

A SECOND GAP, and it is not the same one. The population differs as well. U1-U4 are
stated over a slice application's own interactions (budgets.md sec 9.3: "Slice-app
user-visible gates"), and both existing drivers mount a SYNTHETIC bench page inside
one react-dom/flushSync window — which is a MOUNT and not a PAINT. A p95 over the
wrong window would be a fabricated line wearing a real estimator.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS. Build the instrument, on a loud box, and take no reading:
  1. A quantile estimator on the lane, registered and self-tested, with its
     definition stated (linear-interpolated quantile is already spelled out in
     clock_readjudicate.cjs and is the obvious donor rather than a second spelling).
  2. A driver whose window is a discrete interaction through to the paint that
     follows it, on one of the witness applications under
     implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ — the slice app is the
     one U1-U4 are stated over.
  3. NO threshold, NO band, NO pinned figure. The reading is a separate quiet-box
     window and is NOT this bead's.

DO NOT WIDEN A LINE OR GUESS A THRESHOLD to make U1-U4 shippable. Three windows in
this programme have refused rather than do that and every refusal carried more
information than a pass would have.

FENCE NOTE: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn is hot-zone. rf2-fe0l's precedent is
that a new driver can ride an existing build id rather than mint one — check that
before asking for the hot-zone edit.

comments.text:
DELIVERABLE 2 LANDED, PR #8579. NO READING TAKEN, no threshold, no band, no pinned figure. Deliverable 1 was re-verified at the tip first (lane/quantile at h=(n-1)q, summarise answering :p95 and :p99, lane_quantile_cljs_test witnessing both) and left alone.

THE PATH DISCREPANCY IN THIS BEAD, RESOLVED AT SOURCE. The description says implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ and the 2026-08-18 06:35 comment says implementation/hicasso/examples/. The DESCRIPTION is right: implementation/hicasso/examples/ does not exist, and the eight witness applications (slice, editor, grid, ledger, forms, navigation, todo, typeahead) live under the test tree.

THE BLOCK WAS NEVER ONLY THE ESTIMATOR, AND THE SECOND HALF IS STRUCTURAL. lane/rounds! calls measure-one! and takes a NUMBER back, so an arm it can schedule is one whose whole window closes inside a synchronous call — and a window that ends at a PAINT cannot, because the browser produces the frame after the task returns and the only handle on it is a callback. Every arm this lane could schedule was therefore one bracketed by react-dom/flushSync. That is why both landed drivers measure a commit: it is the shape the only shared schedule allowed, not a coincidence of what got written. So the driver needed a schedule as well as an aim.

WHAT LANDED

1. lane/rounds-async! — rounds!'s schedule with the return type widened to a promise. Both loops now walk one private visit-plan, so the reflecting order, the warm-up boundary and observe!'s predecessor tagging cannot become two copies; lane_schedule_async_cljs_test runs one deterministic stub through both and asserts the samples, readings and true execution order are = at arm counts 2/4/5/7/8, that the visits stay serial, and that a plain value is accepted. lane_schedule_cljs_test is the regression net over the refactor and is green.

2. slice_echo_clock_app — the driver. It mounts the slice through h/mount! with the application's own :initial-events, differing only in which route it opens on, and its window runs from a real DOM event through requestAnimationFrame then setTimeout 0 — the first task after that frame's rendering lifecycle. The echo is read out of the DOM INSIDE the rAF callback, before style, layout and paint, and banks into lane/tally with assert-verified! refusing at N unverified of M. Every reading is published decomposed (:commit, :to-raf, :raf-to-paint). Four rows: :idle-frame (the floor), :keystroke (U1), :toggle (U2, the click/change path), :ctl-blocked (the control). U3 and U4 are named at source as NOT served, with what each would need.

3. NO HOT-ZONE EDIT, confirmed by building it that way: HICASSO_INIT_FN plus the existing :hicasso-bench id. shadow-cljs.edn untouched.

THE CONTROL IS INVISIBLE TO THE WINDOW IT REPLACES, which is what makes it the right one here rather than a generic sensitivity check. :ctl-blocked spends its injected 50 ms strictly BETWEEN the commit and the frame, on window!'s after-commit! seam, so a rig that had quietly reverted to a commit-bounded window would report a control that predicted 50 ms and measured nothing.

THE RISK THIS BEAD FLAGGED DOES NOT HOLD. The slice app compiles under :advanced through this driver — release build, zero warnings — and runs there. Budgeted for; it cost nothing.

THE FINDING THE RIG PRODUCED, AND THE REPAIR. The instrument's first run REFUSED, and not for load. A paint-bounded window is PREDECESSOR-DEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION: its length is dominated by the wait for the browser's next rendering opportunity, those sit on a grid, and how long a sample waits depends on where in that grid the PREVIOUS sample left the clock. The arm-order guard measured exactly that — :idle-frame read a full rendering interval after :keystroke, which ends just after a paint, and zero after :ctl-blocked, which spans three intervals and ends with a frame already overdue, ranges disjoint; :toggle carried the same contrast. VERDICT: REFUSE.

THE GUARD'S TOLERANCE WAS NOT MOVED. The repair is in the ARM, one line in measure-one!: settle to a fresh frame OUTSIDE the reading so the clock always starts in the first task after a paint, making the grid phase a constant of the instrument rather than a property of whatever ran before it. With it the guard returns REPORTABLE on every arm by predecessor AND by phase, on a loud box.

TWO CONSEQUENCES STATED AT SOURCE rather than left to be found by the reading window: (a) a real interaction arrives at a uniformly random phase in the grid while this one always arrives at the phase with the LONGEST wait, so a reading here is the conservative end of the phase distribution — the end that cannot flatter the application, and the deliberately-randomised-phase alternative is named with its trigger and NOT built; (b) the injected block does not ADD to the wait the unblocked arm pays, it SUBSUMES it, so the control's difference reaches blocked-ms rounded to the grid rather than exactly, which is what control-slack's band is derived from.

WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS NOT THIS BEAD'S. The READING. The instrument has never been read against a line and must not be: U1's one-60-Hz-frame clause, U2's 50 ms p95 / 100 ms p99 and U3's 100 ms appear nowhere in the code, and the only pass/fail the driver makes are the arm-order guard and the positive control, both instrument-integrity checks. rf2-85og2's gate 1 now needs a quiet-box window and nothing else structural. Three things that window should know before it starts:

- THE SCHEDULE KNOBS ARE DELIBERATELY SMALL. {:warmup 8 :samples 12} over 5 rounds is the lane's standard, and a p99 over 12 samples is mostly interpolation — lane/quantile's own docstring prices that. Raise both; the run's wall clock is roughly two frames per sample plus 50 ms per :ctl-blocked sample.
- U3 AND U4 STILL HAVE NO ROWS. U3 (operation latency for a broad operation — a route change, a reset, a save reply) needs per-arm preparation outside the window, because the route the editor rows type into is the route a navigation row would leave. U4 (per-frame latency under dragging or animation) is not one interaction through to one paint at all: it is a run of consecutive frames, and its estimator is a distribution over frame intervals rather than over window lengths. Both want another driver on window!'s mechanism. Neither is built and neither should be guessed at.
- THE FLOOR ROW IS THE ONE TO READ FIRST. :idle-frame is the wait for the next rendering opportunity with no application work at all, and a p95 at the floor and a p95 at twice it are different findings that the figure alone does not distinguish.

GATES. compile_gate.cjs exit 0 (154 namespaces, zero warnings); :advanced release build of the driver exit 0; test:browser exit 0 (1029 tests, 5775 assertions, 0 failures); test:cljs exit 0 (11868 tests, 60087 assertions, 0 failures); _browser-dom-lane-partition.test.cjs exit 0; test:hicasso-invariants exit 0; check_fast_pr_gap.py --list exit 0, 94 required checks the spine does not run. The fast spine did NOT run; the covering lanes were run directly. comments.text:
AUDIT GAPS 1 AND 2 CLOSED, PR #8589. NO READING TAKEN, no threshold, band, budget status or published figure moved, and budgets.md untouched — the refusal posture the audit asked to preserve is preserved. Three files, all in the bench tree: lane.cljs, slice_echo_clock_app.cljs, slice_echo_window_dom_cljs_test.cljs.

GAP 1 — THE REPAIR IS A DIFFERENT PLACE, NOT A DIFFERENT VALUE, and that is forced rather than chosen. per_keystroke_dom_cljs_test solves the accepted-verbatim problem by typing into a field whose model answers something ELSE (the editor's normalising :slug). THE SLICE HAS NO SUCH FIELD: ::events/edit takes what it is given, verbatim, and nothing on the article route normalises or refuses. Checked at source before designing around it.

So: React keeps a controlled input's committed value in TWO places, and only one of them is reachable by a scripted setup. The `value` PROPERTY is written by HTMLInputElement.prototype's setter and by a checkbox's native activation; the `value` CONTENT ATTRIBUTE (defaultValue) is written ONLY by React's own commit. Verified at source in react-dom 19.2.0 — updateInput ends every controlled-input update with setDefaultValue(element, type, value), unconditionally whenever a `value` prop is present — and the repo's own measured mutation trace in per_keystroke_dom_cljs_test carries the matching INPUT@value record. Every measured arm now blanks that mirror OUTSIDE the window and asks inside the frame whether the APPLICATION put the model's own title back.

THE CHECKBOX ARM READS THE SAME MIRROR, and that is the point of it rather than a convenience: ::toggle-published moves the draft, the editor's body re-runs, and React reconciles the title input beside the checkbox, so a restored title mirror is evidence the click reached the model and came back through a commit. defaultChecked would NOT have served, checked rather than assumed — the same updateInput writes it only for an element with no `checked` prop, and this one has.

THE SABOTAGE IS BUILT INTO THE DRIVER, not only into the suite. echo-discrimination! runs once at boot, performs the keystroke arm's setup mutation alone — no DOM event, so no handler, no dispatch, no state write, no commit — through the same window! and the same observation the arms use, and REFUSES to let anything be measured unless the check rejects it. A suite row is the right place to prove a repair; it is the wrong place to keep a driver honest, because the driver is what a quiet-box window runs and the suite is not.

AND IT WAS RUN, AND IT REDDENS. Three permanent suite rows carry the same proof: the driver's own control, plus one per measured arm firing the REAL DOM event with the React root cut off from it by a capture-phase stopPropagation at document — so the user agent's own mutation still happens (the character lands, the checkbox flips) and nothing else does. With the mirror conjunct removed from title-echo-verified? — one line, restoring exactly the shape the audit named — the browser suite goes RED on all three and on nothing else, and the boot control's own message prints the finding in one line: :glass "Intents are dataa", :rendered "<< no commit reached this field >>". 1034 tests on both runs, so nothing aborted a namespace; 5803 assertions / 0 failures / exit 0 control, 5801 / 3 failures / exit 1 planted. Restored and verified by the identical blob hash against the committed object.

GAP 2 — 100 vs 60 RE-DERIVED AT THIS TIP, not quoted: (8+12)*5 = 100 banked per arm against 12*5 = 60 measured. structure-over-measured now narrows the banked parts to the measured population before publication, using a mask derived from lane/visit-plan — the ONE statement of the schedule both of the lane's loops walk — rather than from a second reading of warmup/samples/slot-order inside the driver. That is why visit-plan becomes public and the docstring says so: a mask that had drifted would not fail, it would publish a distribution over the wrong visits and say nothing. keep-measured refuses rather than truncating if the two ever disagree. The verification tally deliberately stays over EVERY window (a count of refusals, not a distribution — it decomposes nothing) and a new :populations key labels all three. THE N RELATIONSHIP IS ASSERTED PER ARM rather than described, plus a row that would catch a narrowing which had silently become a no-op.

TWO THINGS FOUND WHILE HERE, RECORDED AT SOURCE. (a) The first refusal's detail is now kept and published beside the tally — a bare `N unverified of M` over a two-part check is a diagnosis the operator has to reproduce. (b) A NUL-BEARING SENTINEL WAS WITHDRAWN BEFORE IT LANDED: the first spelling of committed-value-sentinel wrapped its text in NUL codepoints, on the reasoning that an untypable codepoint is the strongest sentinel there is. It is also the strongest way to make a source file BINARY — git classifies a file containing a NUL as binary, which cost the file its line-ending normalisation and turned a 378-line diff into a 1001-line whole-file CRLF rewrite. Caught by reading the merge-base diff before pushing, and the reasoning is on the def so it is not re-derived.

NOTHING TO RE-ADJUDICATE. The repair does not make any existing published reading look wrong, because there is no published reading from this instrument: #8579 took none and budgets.md carries no figure from it. U3 and U4 still have no rows, exactly as the file already states at source.

title: hicasso: the allocation window's SECOND leg pass reads lower than its first — a within-round position term of 0.2–0.7%
description:
MEASURED by rf2-0gjqi's paired window, 2026-08-18. Record:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-sign-follows-the-pass-not-the-write.md (PR #8473).
Datasets: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-0gjqi/.

THE OBSERVATION. Under P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired the two write legs of every arm run
as two passes inside one round, and the rig alternates which leads on round
parity (p0_run.cjs:2418). Taking the round as the block and the median of
(page-all)/all over that round's certified mid-rung (R3, R7) cells as its
statistic, THE PASS THAT RAN SECOND READS LOWER IN 10 OF 12 BLOCKS -- 6 of 6 in
run 1, 4 of 6 in run 2 -- WHICHEVER WRITE OCCUPIED IT. Median second-minus-first
-0.59%.

Decomposed under an additive position model, the pass-order half-difference reads
+0.68% (run 1) and +0.21% (run 2), the same sign on both, while the order-free
write half-sum reads -0.33% and +0.24%, opposite signs.

WHY IT MATTERS. It is the class of term that manufactured this instrument's last
inferential finding. rf2-0gjqi's published 8-of-8 was taken with `all` as run 2
and `page` as run 3, so page was ALWAYS the later measurement; a position term of
this sign produces 8 of 8 in one direction with certainty. The paired mode
removes the confound and the unanimity goes with it -- but the term itself is
still in the instrument, and any future estimator that is not order-balanced will
pick it up again.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, so it is not rediscovered as new.

  - THE MAGNITUDE IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THE OLD EFFECT. This is a WITHIN-ROUND
    pass-position term; the old confound was between two PROCESSES. They are not
    the same quantity, and +0.21..0.68% is smaller than the published mid-rung
    absolute median of 1.68%. Right sign, wrong size, different estimand.
  - NO MECHANISM IS PROPOSED and none is excluded.
  - LEG ORDER IS NOT SEPARATED FROM ROUND PARITY. The rig ties them: every
    page-first round is an even round. Any other even/odd property of a round
    acting differently on a first and a second pass would read the same way.
    Separating them needs a leg order that is not a function of round parity,
    which is a rig change and therefore its own window.
  - THE INDEPENDENT BLOCK COUNT IS 2, not 12. The twelve round blocks share a
    session inside each run. The nominal one-sided sign-test p over twelve is
    79/4096 = 0.019 and is quoted only as what the nominal test says.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT. A leg order drawn independently of round parity -- e.g.
seeded per round rather than parity-derived -- would separate the pass-position
term from every other even/odd round property in one window. That is a rig change
and must not be made inside a measurement window.

NOT A GATE PROBLEM. Nothing here is fixed by widening a tolerance, and the
existing gates behave correctly throughout: both runs' positive controls passed at
8.00 B/double differential and 0 unverified read-backs.

MERGED-PR AUDIT #8596 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): exact open owner updated; no duplicate.

THE SEEDED MODE'S CLAIMED BALANCE DOES NOT HOLD AT THE ODD ROUND COUNTS THE NEW PREFLIGHT EXPLICITLY ADMITS. `allocPassFlips` chooses `floor(rounds / 2)` flipped rounds. Driving the exported functions gives n=3 as page/all lead counts 2/1 and n=5 as 3/2; only even n is exactly balanced. The structural pin includes n=5 but asserts only that the TRUE count is `floor(n/2)`, then calls that "balanced exactly as parity" without checking the other leg. The source, test, PR body, and bead update all say each leg leads exactly `floor(rounds/2)` times, which is mathematically impossible at odd n, while the preflight tells an operator that 3 rounds is sufficient.

THIS MATTERS ON THE CHANGE'S OWN DESIGN RULE: its rationale says an unbalanced schedule reintroduces the write/pass-position imbalance the alternation exists to remove. The intended phase-2 default of six rounds is safe, so the rig arm need not be reverted. Before advertising odd counts as admissible, either require an even seeded paired run (minimum 4), or explicitly define and justify near-balance at odd n and make the tests/prose state the unequal lead counts. Pin both legs, not only the flip count.

RELATED CONSISTENCY EDGE: the n<=2 seeded preflight refusal is unconditional, even for one-leg `page`/`all` selections that the new test and source call inert under both modes. Scope the refusal to a paired run or reject a meaningless seeded one-leg selection consistently. The phase-2 paired/default-six window remains the priority.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8601 (2026-08-21) — THE WINDOW CORRECTLY STAYS OPEN, BUT ITS CLAIM THAT RUN 2 “SEPARATED” PASS FROM PARITY IS FALSE, AND THE PRESCRIBED NEXT DESIGN REPEATS THE CONFOUND.

1. DIFFERENT MARGINAL MEDIANS ARE NOT IDENTIFIABILITY. Run 2's six-round schedule has parity·pass = -2, not 0. `decompose` computes two separate marginal median contrasts; it does not jointly fit the correlated columns. A direct synthetic control using the shipped `decompose` proves the failure:
- true PARITY only (even=+1, odd=-1; pass effect 0) reports PASS=-1 and PARITY=+1;
- true PASS only (page-first=+1, all-first=-1; parity effect 0) reports PASS=+1 and PARITY=-1.
Both use run 2's exact schedule `page,page,all,page,all,all`. So run 2's +0.64/-0.22 pair is not a separated pass/parity estimate. Its two numbers merely differ; each can contain the other term. Run 1 makes the same confound visible by returning identical medians, but run 2 does not remove it.

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE LANDED RECORD. The “only run 2 separates,” “independent n=1,” and “four runs, four positive PASS terms” wording is too strong. Three of those four contrasts came from parity-tied or parity-correlated schedules and are page-first GROUPING contrasts, not pass-specific replications. The complementary two-run pooled design has dot=0 and is the only design-level contrast here that balances the columns; it is one paired design and still needs the nonlinear estimator qualified. The cautious terminal conclusion (“not established free of parity”) remains correct, so no shipped decision needs reversal.

THE SUCCESSOR PLAN WOULD REPEAT IT. “Both seeds at symmetric difference 4” gives dot=-2 in every six-round run. It reduces group overlap but does not make either marginal contrast identify its term; the synthetic control above remains maximally wrong. More runs merely replicate that confound. Before another expensive window, pre-register a design/estimator that passes synthetic pure-pass and pure-parity controls. Cheap routes include a round count and schedule with dot=0 WITHIN each run plus an estimator whose behavior is proved on those fixtures, or a joint model/paired contrast that estimates both columns rather than naming two correlated marginal medians. Do not treat “the medians came apart” as the control.

2. THE READER'S ARBITERS DO NOT ARBITRATE. `report()` prints `controlVerdict`, `verification.unverified`, `passOrder`, `parityTied`, and `scheduleDrove`, then unconditionally feeds every row to `blocks`, the headline, both decompositions, and `nullArm`. A copy of seeded-run1 with `controlVerdict.ok=false` still produces all blocks and the “PASS THAT RAN SECOND” headline; reversing round 0's driven legs makes `scheduleDrove=false` and still produces them. The source comments explicitly promise the opposite (“a failed control contributes no data”; disagreement means no figure may be read). Add one fail-closed admissibility boundary used by report/self-test, covering failed/absent control, nonzero/absent verification, wrong mode/seed/tied schedule, and schedule/drive mismatch; prove each rejection.

No duplicate Bead: this open issue already owns the estimator, the window, and its successor design. Keep it open after the terminology/reader repair until a genuinely identifying window exists.

comments.text:
WINDOW TAKEN as worker/passterm-fk6pj, PR #8615. rf2-fk6pj STAYS OPEN. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-design-control-comes-before-the-window.md. Datasets: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-passterm/ (four runs). No rig file edited.

WHAT THIS WINDOW DID NOT TAKE FROM THE BRIEF, AND WHY. The dispatch carried phase 2's own successor plan -- 'both seeds at symmetric difference 4' -- but the merged-PR audit of #8601 (this bead, 2026-08-20 20:43Z) had already refuted it, and the tree agrees: q.parity = 4a - R over R rounds with balanced legs, so it is NEVER zero at R = 6. Symmetric difference 4 is the -2 case. Taking the brief literally would have bought four more runs of the same confound. THE DESIGN WAS CHANGED INSTEAD, to twelve rounds where q.parity = 0 is reachable and is exactly the 2x2 balance.

THE CONTROL THE AUDIT ASKED FOR EXISTS AND RAN BEFORE THE WINDOW. alloc_pass_design.cjs (new, ~430 lines) drives the SHIPPED decompose over synthetic block sets whose true terms are known by construction. Positive: all four selected schedules recover pure PARITY, pure PASS and an unequal 1-and-3 mixture exactly. Negative, which is the half that matters: phase 2's run-2 schedule reports PASS -1 on a corpus with NO pass effect, and PARITY -1 on one with no parity effect; the parity schedule returns one number twice; and no balanced six-round schedule is admissible at all. Exit 0.

THE DESIGN: 12 rounds, 4 runs, seeds by an ENUMERATION RULE not a pick (fk6pj-9, fk6pj-11, fk6pj-2386, fk6pj-33), runs 3 and 4 the exact complements of 1 and 2. Three criteria per seed: not parity-tied, q.parity = 0 WITHIN the run, q.linear = 0 WITHIN the run. Complementing inverts the pass order at every round index, so each pair also balances the pass contrast against the round INDEX.

RESULT -- THE DESIGN IDENTIFIED AND THE PRE-REGISTERED BAND REFUSED.
* All four runs ADMITTED by a fail-closed boundary declared before the runs and proved in both directions (8 clauses broken one at a time, each must refuse; phase 2's own record refused on round count and q.parity). Controls 8.00 B/double, 0 unverified, schedule drove what it drew, all four.
* q.parity = 0 INSIDE EVERY RUN and 0 pooled. First allocation corpus that can say the first of those.
* PASS term +0.65, +0.64, +0.20, +0.29 -- four runs four positive -- pooling to +0.45% over 48 blocks.
* PARITY term -0.23, -0.06, +0.24, +0.34 -- two of each sign -- pooling to +0.02%. On the two COMPLEMENTARY PAIRS, the only contrasts balanced against the round index, it reads +0.01% and -0.00% while PASS reads +0.53% and +0.45%.
* Second-lower in 34 of 48, median -0.50%. Reported, not the headline.
* THE BAND REFUSES BOTH. Ten times this window's own null-arm p90 (61 B/boundary) is 610; the pass term's implied delta at the mid rungs is 37.8 B/boundary (21.4-77.0 over the d_all range). Outcome 3 under the pre-registration. THE PASS TERM IS NOT ESTABLISHED.

A DEFECT IN THIS WINDOW'S OWN PRE-REGISTERED BAND, RECORDED AND NOT REPAIRED. The band compares an AGGREGATE (a contrast of medians over 316 cells) against a PER-OBSERVATION noise scale (one cell's p90). It is too strict by roughly the square root of the count, and the 45 B/boundary bar it was modelled on was set for per-boundary cell MEDIANS. Repairing it after seeing the answer is the precise thing pre-registration exists to prevent, so it stands.

TWO FURTHER FINDINGS.
1. THE PUBLISHED NON-CANCELLATION FLOOR DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS CORPUS, and phase 2's explanation of that is REFUTED at four times the sample size. Fraction of the zero-signal null arm above the published 45 B/boundary bar: rf2-0gjqi 5.3% (2/38), phase 2 10.0% (4/40), here 23.2% (38/164). Phase 2 called its 56.5 p90 'an artefact of the count'; at n=164 the p90 is 61 and a quarter of the population sits above the bar, which is a distribution and not an index. Median 0 and absolute median 3 B/boundary still hold. Filed as rf2-NULLFLOOR below.
2. A PER-ROUND-INDEX NUISANCE IS VISIBLE. Within each complementary pair the PASS term is larger in the original schedule than in its complement, by +0.22% and +0.17%. Complementing inverts q at every index, so that half-difference IS an index-tied term. It cancels in each pair and in the pool. No column is identified and no mechanism is proposed.

FOUR RUNS ARE ONE SESSION. runsInSession 1..4 against a single sessionStartedAt, fourteen minutes on one box. The session-level independent count is 1, which is this bead's own standing complaint applied to its own successor.

title: [ci] the tools-playground job carries NO timeout-minutes — a wedge there burns GitHub's 6-hour default while every sibling caps
description:
FOUND BY THE MAYOR'S MERGE LOOP, 2026-08-18 03:57Z, on PR #8461's run 32094188039. Verified at source at origin/main 147d24a7f5.

THE FACT. .github/workflows/test.yml's 'tools-playground' job (name: 'docs/cljs playground (smoke + bundle-drift, rf2-ee38b.22)', definition begins at test.yml:5889) declares 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest' and goes straight to 'defaults:' with NO 'timeout-minutes' key. It therefore inherits GitHub Actions' default job timeout of 360 minutes.

THAT IS AN OUTLIER, NOT THE HOUSE STYLE. Its siblings in the same file cap themselves: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. 'JVM tools/template' at test.yml:4924 carries timeout-minutes: 35.

THE MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, from the run that surfaced it. On PR #8461's tests run 32094188039 both jobs started at 03:09:3xZ:

  JVM tools/template     normal 10.5 min   ->  killed at its 35-min cap, 03:44:51Z, reported as CANCELLED
  docs/cljs playground   normal 1.4-1.7 min ->  still in_progress at 03:57:31Z, 48 minutes, no cap to stop it

Normal durations measured from the three most recent successful 'tests' runs on main (32092675548, 32082472715, 32080996828). Playground was 28x its normal cost and rising when the mayor cancelled the run by hand.

WHY THIS IS THE JOB'S DEFECT AND NOT THAT PR'S. Two unrelated jobs overran together in one run — a bench-runner change under implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/ cannot slow an unrelated JVM tools/template job and a docs/tools/playground shadow-cljs build at the same time. The wedge is runner-level. The DEFECT this bead carries is not the wedge; it is that one job had no cap to convert the wedge into a fast, legible failure.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THE RUN DEMONSTRATES. The capped sibling failed in 35 minutes and said so. The uncapped one produced a check that NEVER TERMINATES, which is the exact gap rf2-krdb7 filed against the merge rules: those rules cover a check that FAILS and a check that fails before repo code ran, but not one that never terminates. A merge loop meeting the uncapped job has nothing to read and no remedy but a hand cancel. Sequence with rf2-krdb7 or note the overlap; they are complementary, not duplicates — one adds the cap, the other tells the mayor what to do when a check hangs anyway.

THE FIX. Give tools-playground a timeout-minutes proportionate to its measured 1.4-1.7 minute cost with generous headroom. Do not copy 35 from tools/template — that is a 10.5-minute job and the number is not transferable. Pick from this job's own measurements and say in the PR body which runs the figure came from.

HOT ZONE. .github/workflows/* is on the fixed hot-zone list: one toucher at a time, never parallel. The held rf2-fo4ng rename campaign also touches release workflows, so sequence against it.

WHILE YOU ARE THERE, AND AS A SEPARATE QUESTION: re-derive whether any OTHER job in .github/workflows/*.yml lacks timeout-minutes. Report the census. A count is a claim -- do not trust this bead's implication that tools-playground is the only one; it was found by reading one run, not by a sweep.

title: [ruling] does Spec 006 flush-render! fall under the Spec 009 open-drain guard law, or is it expressly outside it?
description:
RAISED BY the merged-PR audit of #8438 on rf2-fxtbj (audit comment 2026-08-17T12:51:09Z), and re-derived at source by rf2-fxtbj's second worker at origin/main e4a6f482c9.

THE LAW. spec/009-Instrumentation.md, the :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch catalogue row: "EVERY substrate whose synchronous flush can publish a render phase MUST call it" — it being the shared open-drain guard re-frame.frame/guard-open-drain! in core (rulings rf2-vxgfnd.207, rf2-87ouj).

THE MEASUREMENT, all with positive controls (see PR for rf2-fxtbj):
  * git grep -nF guard-open-drain! -- implementation/ returns exactly ONE line, implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:3521, the defn itself. ZERO call sites.
  * spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:262 defines the OPTIONAL contract fn flush-render! as "Synchronously commits the substrate's pending renders to the surface", explicitly production-grade and explicitly NOT a test helper.
  * THREE of the six shipped adapter kinds install a :flush-render! slot in src: reagent (adapter/reagent.cljs:38, (f) then reagent.core/flush), reagent-slim (adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:50, reagent2.dom.client/flush-render!, flushSync-backed), and uix (via spine/make-react-adapter at substrate/spine.cljs:3243, whose react-dom/flushSync flush-render! is at spine.cljs:1766). plain-atom, ssr and test-react install none.
  * implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:625 is the live delegated entry point; it calls the installed slot directly and does not call the guard.

SO, READ LITERALLY, the law binds those three and all three currently violate it: each can commit a render phase synchronously from inside an open event drain without meeting the guard. The universal is UNMET, not vacuous.

THE RULING NEEDED — one of two, and a zero grep cannot settle it:
  (a) ENFORCE. Wire guard-open-drain! in at a shared non-cyclic boundary and add open-drain coverage across the three adapters. NOTE THE CYCLE, measured: re-frame.frame ALREADY requires re-frame.substrate.adapter (frame.cljc ns form), so substrate/adapter.cljc cannot simply require re-frame.frame to call the guard from its flush-render! delegation. A late-bind or route-hook seam, or a third namespace, is what an enforcement would need.
  (b) NARROW. Rule the Spec 006 flush-render! contract expressly outside this law and say why in the row — e.g. that the hazard the guard names is a REGISTRY flush rather than a render-commit, which is how the guard's own docstring words it ("Reject a synchronous registry-flush").

WHY IT IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY WORK. Option (b) may well be right and is much the cheaper answer; the guard's docstring and the row's opening sentence both say REGISTRY-flush, and the retired donor call sites were ViewCell-registry flushes. If (b) is the ruling, the whole repair is one clause in the spec row and nothing in implementation/ changes.

STATE OF THE ROW TODAY. rf2-fxtbj's second PR has already removed the FALSE claims that the obligation binds no one and that the universal is vacuous, and the row now names this bead as the open ruling. Nothing is asserted in either direction.

SURFACE IF (b): spec/009-Instrumentation.md only (HOT ZONE, one toucher). SURFACE IF (a): implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/**, implementation/adapters/**, plus the same spec row.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION, 2026-08-18 10:50 AUSEST, recorded so the ruling is cheap. Not dispatched: the measurement is complete and both options are live, which is exactly the shape that needs you.

RECOMMENDATION: TAKE (b), NARROW. Rule the Spec 006 flush-render! contract expressly outside this law, and say why in the row.

THE CRUX, AND I THINK IT IS DECISIVE. The law and the guard it names do not describe the same hazard.

  the catalogue row says   EVERY substrate whose synchronous flush can PUBLISH A RENDER PHASE must call it
  the guard's docstring says   Reject a synchronous REGISTRY-FLUSH

Those are different events. Spec 006's flush-render! is defined as synchronously committing the substrate's pending renders to the surface - a render-commit. The guard implements a registry-flush rejection, and the retired donor call sites it was written against were ViewCell-REGISTRY flushes. So the row generalised past what the guard actually does, and the three adapters were swept in by that generalisation rather than by the hazard.

Read that way this is not a violation to be enforced but a row whose scope outran its own mechanism. (b) aligns the row with the guard. It is one clause in a spec row and nothing in implementation/ changes.

Enforcement needs a late-bind seam, a route-hook, or a third namespace - a new architectural seam - plus open-drain coverage across three adapters, all to enforce a law whose own guard says it was about something else. Under the project stance that is the more-machinery answer to a wording problem.

WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT, and it is worth one check before you rule: if a render-commit CAN publish a render phase from inside an open event drain in a way that is genuinely hazardous - not merely nameable by the row's wording - then narrowing leaves a real hazard unguarded and (a) is right despite its cost. The question is whether the hazard is real for a render-commit, not whether the sentence covers it. Nobody has established that either way, and a zero grep cannot: zero call sites measures COMPLIANCE, not whether the hazard exists.

STATE OF THE ROW TODAY, so you are not ruling against a stale text: rf2-fxtbj's second PR has already removed the false claims that the obligation bound no one and that the universal was vacuous. The row now names this bead as the open ruling and asserts nothing in either direction. Whichever way you rule, the row is ready to receive it.

title: hicasso: make stride-3 leg magnitudes byte-comparable with stride-2 ones, so a byte-for-byte witness can be screened by all three gates
description:
HELD FOR AN OPERATOR RULING, NOT DISPATCHABLE AS FILED. Split out of rf2-fir5n by PR #8443, which took that bead as A REFUSAL PLUS A RECORD REPAIR and deliberately left this half unbuilt.

WHAT rf2-fir5n SETTLED. The intra-leg gate (rf2-4ctls) is inert at the shipped stride and that is CORRECT, not a defect: allocSiteSplit returns no site legs at a stride of 2 because a leg has no interior reading there, so there is no site step whose sign could be read and nothing to widen a test on. title: hicasso: the intra-leg gate can never screen a byte-for-byte comparison against published history — the two strides are not comparable
description:
OBSERVED by rf2-2rtt6.140's V1/V2 re-run window, 2026-08-17. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-certifies-and-the-control-does-not.md. FILED RATHER THAN BUILT — the window's fence forbade editing the rig.

THE STRUCTURE. rf2-4ctls (PR #8420) added allocIntraLegRefusals, a third allocation gate that refuses a window carrying a negative measured site step — a collection INSIDE a leg that both older gates miss. It is deliberately inert at the shipped stride: allocSiteSplit returns an empty siteLegs at stride 2, so the gate returns [] by construction (p0_run.cjs:1792-1795 says exactly this, and calls it inert BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a switch). It bites only under P0_ALLOC_BY_SITE=1, i.e. stride 3.

THE TENSION. p0_run.cjs (around :1360) also records that absolute leg magnitudes at stride 3 are NOT comparable byte for byte with those at stride 2, because each leg carries one extra sampler read. So:

  - any witness whose criterion is a BYTE-FOR-BYTE comparison against a figure published at stride 2 MUST run at stride 2; and
  - at stride 2 the intra-leg gate adjudicates nothing.

V1's second clause is exactly such a witness — it compares F_old against the 2026-08-08 figures of 24,108 / 24,730 B per write — so this window ran all three runs at stride 2 and measured 0 intra-leg refusals across all 276 arm windows. That is the gate being inert, not the windows being clean.

WHY IT MATTERS. 'Certified' on such a page means certified by the leg witness and the falls gate and NO MORE. A collection bracketed inside a single leg would leave the window under-reading with all the gates that ran silent, and under-reading is the direction that manufactures HD-002's flat-at-zero — which is the whole reason rf2-4ctls exists. So the class of comparison that most needs the third gate is precisely the class that cannot use it.

WHAT IS NOT PROPOSED. NOT a widening, NOT a change to tau, and NOT handing the mid samples to allocSteps — that last was already considered and REFUSED by rf2-rs8q6's fence because it would move three published quantities. Nothing here reopens any of that.

THE CANDIDATE REMEDY, offered not taken: the idle control already prices the extra per-leg sampler read (rf2-ojehu measured it at 16 B per leg). If that constant is stable, a stride-3 run could be corrected to stride-2 bytes and the two made comparable, which would let a byte-for-byte witness be screened by all three gates. That is an instrument change needing a hermetic build and a ruling, not a quiet box. It may also simply be judged not worth it — in which case the honest alternative is that pages taking byte-for-byte comparisons SAY that the third gate did not screen them, as the 2026-08-17 record does.

title: hicasso: V2's arm-floor does not cancel the write exactly — write-page reads below write-all at 8 of 8 mid-rung comparisons
description:
MEASURED by rf2-2rtt6.140's V1/V2 re-run window, 2026-08-17. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-certifies-and-the-control-does-not.md.

CONTEXT: V2's criterion became evaluable for the first time. The floor went from certifying 0 of 6 in BOTH 2026-08-13 runs on BOTH segments to 4-6 of 6, so (arm - floor) finally has a certified floor to subtract. The floor drops 1,769 B (9.1%) on reagent-subs and 1,765 B (8.9%) on uix-subs, which is the half of V2's criterion that HOLDS.

THE FINDING. (arm - floor)/B is meant to cancel the write's fixed cost F exactly, so the two writes must give the same per-boundary figure. Across the 13 comparable rungs they differ by -4.28% to +8.81%, absolute median 1.48%, and 10 of 13 certified per-round ranges overlap. That is close. But the RESIDUAL HAS A CONSISTENT SIGN:

  segment       arm       rung   all      page     page-all
  reagent-subs  hicasso   R3     6,984    6,687    -4.25%
  reagent-subs  hicasso   R7    14,447   13,829    -4.28%
  reagent-subs  reagent   R3     7,795    7,664    -1.67%
  reagent-subs  reagent   R7    15,408   15,180    -1.48%
  uix-subs      hicasso   R3     6,691    6,538    -2.28%
  uix-subs      hicasso   R7    13,752   13,520    -1.69%
  uix-subs      uix       R3     5,211    5,164    -0.90%
  uix-subs      uix       R7    11,405   11,347    -0.51%

Eight of eight in one direction, across both segments and both substrates. Under a null of random sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement. Estimator: (arm - floor)/B from each window's own leg median, then the MEDIAN across rounds where BOTH the arm and that segment's floor certified — not a mean, and not pooled beyond that median.

The two R=1 hicasso rungs carry the largest disagreements in the OTHER direction (+1.11%, +8.81%) and are also the noisiest cells on the page, with round-to-round spread of 22-35%. The sign consistency is in the mid rungs, whose spread is 1-7%.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. V2 exists to detect the case where 'the new write provokes different per-boundary work' (allocation-instrument-rework.md:217-220), for which the stated consequence is that the write half is WITHDRAWN rather than re-tuned. This residual is small — a few percent — and at most rungs does not exceed the round-to-round spread. So it is not obviously that case. But it is not obviously noise either, and 8-of-8 is the observation that says so.

THE DECISION NEEDED is whether ~1-4% of non-cancellation is tolerable for the equivalence argument, which is a RULING and not a measurement. The window deliberately did not make it.

SECOND ITEM, RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN SEPARATELY: the R=20 rung still produced certified windows under both writes on only ONE of its four arm families (uix-subs | uix R20). reagent-subs|hicasso, reagent-subs|reagent and uix-subs|hicasso produced NO certified pair. That reproduces the 2026-08-13 window exactly, so it is structural rather than incidental, and V2's most informative rung remains unassessed on three quarters of the arms. DO NOT WIDEN A GATE TO ADMIT IT.
