comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RE-ANALYSIS, rf2-0gjqi, 2026-08-18. Record: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-eight-signs-are-one-block.md (PR #8458). NO WINDOW WAS TAKEN and no rig file was touched.

VERDICT. The CAUSE of the sign residual is UNRESOLVED and the committed corpus cannot decide it. The INFERENTIAL claim in this bead's description -- eight of eight in one direction, a 1-in-256 arrangement -- is REFUTED at source. The thirteen descriptive cells stand exactly as published; one sentence about eight of them does not.

WHY, and the third reason is new rather than the audit restated.

(1) MEASUREMENT ORDER, ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE. ALLOC_WRITE is read once from process.env at module scope (implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs:1504), and ALLOC_WRITE_SPECS has exactly two members with no paired or interleaved option (:1490). One process therefore drives one write, and the resolved kind is passed into every arm window of the run (:2335, :2342). The two arms of every comparison are two sequential process runs. The record declares the order: all was run 2, page was run 3, brackets 01:48:27 / 01:50:09 / 01:51:44. Write and run-position are perfectly confounded across all eight cells. Within-run position is NOT a confound and that sharpens the point -- segment order alternates on round parity (:2269) and arm order is slot-order(n, round) (order_guard.cljc:149), a pure function, so both runs measured every arm at the same within-run position.

(2) ONE FLOOR PER SEGMENT PER WRITE. The estimator differences each arm window against that segment's floor window in the same round. The reagent-subs floor certified 4 of 6 under all, and all four of that segment's mid-rung cells report n = 4 under all, so those four cells difference against THE SAME FOUR FLOOR WINDOWS. A level term common to them shifts all four cell medians identically. Four cells, one draw.

(3) AND THAT TERM IS PAGE-GLOBAL, WHICH MERGES EVEN THOSE TWO. rf2-77gz8 measured the second floor mode moving reagent-subs and uix-subs by EXACTLY the same 3,792 B. So the segments do not draw separately either. Eight cells, ONE draw, probability 1 -- not 1/256.

MAGNITUDE, first-hand. A shared floor offset of 2,472 B/write on reagent-subs and 928 B/write on uix-subs reverses all eight signs (B = 4, so eps = 4 x |delta|; largest mid-rung deltas are 618 and 232 B/boundary). Re-derived here from the eight committed alloc-9jrhi datasets -- population: the floor arm's certified windows; statistic: median of rise/W across certified rounds, per segment per run -- three runs at ONE revision (4a1537cb71) under ONE write span 3,852 B/write (reagent-subs) and 3,912 B/write (uix-subs). Both exceed what would flip every sign. Two runs at 88411ed803 span 1,645 B/write on uix-subs, which still exceeds that segment's 928.

BUT THE MODE ACCOUNT IS NOT ADOPTED. A shared floor offset is additive and identical across a segment's arms; the observed mid-rung offsets span 1,948 B/write within reagent-subs and 740 B/write within uix-subs, and within an arm family the residual is closer to a constant proportion (page/all reads 0.9575 and 0.9572, 0.9832 and 0.9852, 0.9771 and 0.9831, 0.9910 and 0.9949). So rf2-77gz8 is of sufficient magnitude and the WRONG SHAPE to be the whole of it. Not excluded, not supported.

WHY NO NEW WINDOW, verified at source rather than assumed. All EIGHT alloc-9jrhi datasets carry writeSelector "all", plan floor, B = 24 -- NO committed dataset carries write-page, and none carries a ladder rung under any write selector. The only committed full ladder (alloc-2rtt6-138/run1.json) predates the selector AND predates rf2-erre5, so it carries neither writeSelector nor samples. The V1/V2 re-run window COMMITTED NO DATASET AT ALL: there is no alloc-2rtt6-140 directory, so the eight disputed cells cannot be recomputed from anything in the tree. And a fresh window would reproduce the same confound at a new timestamp, because the rig can only drive one write per process.

LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY. The audit's obligation -- compare matched certified pairs after the paired mode lands -- is unmet, and closing would drop it. Filed rf2-irxrw as the work that would decide it. Two things it needs, stated so they are not rediscovered: the FLOOR must be paired too, because the floor is the dominant shared term; and rf2-77gz8 must be resolved alongside, because whether the ladder ARMS carry the floor's second mode is untested -- it was observed on a floor-plan run with no arms in it -- and that single unknown decides whether a page-global level cancels in arm minus floor or not.

WHAT THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION SHOULD NO LONGER BE READ AS SAYING: "Under a null of random sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement." That null is not the one this design admits. Everything else in the description stands.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
THE PAIRED MODE HAS LANDED (rf2-irxrw, PR #8461). This bead stays OPEN: its audit obligation -- compare matched certified pairs -- is unmet until a window is taken through the new mode, and closing would drop it.

WHAT IS NOW POSSIBLE THAT WAS NOT. P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired drives :p0/write-page AND :p0/write-all at every arm inside every round, on the same page, in the same process. That is the same-page/same-run pair allocation-instrument-rework.md:231-232 requires and the instrument could not take, and it removes the confound this bead's re-analysis established at source: the two arms of every published comparison were two sequential PROCESS runs in a fixed order.

FOUR THINGS IT MAKES AVAILABLE TO A LATER WINDOW.

  1. MATCHED WITHIN-ROUND DIFFERENCES. Every recorded window names its own write and carries pairKey -- the arm key its legs share -- so an estimator groups a round's windows by that field and differences the two legs directly. It does not reconstruct a pair from two files, and it does not parse a key.

  2. A PAIRED FLOOR. The floor is an arm of the plan, so the leg pass takes it under both writes like every other arm. This bead's own note said the floor must be paired because it is the dominant shared term, and it is: (arm - floor) can now be formed within one round under each write, against a floor measured under that same write in that same round.

  3. THE WRITE IS NO LONGER CONFOUNDED WITH POSITION. The leg order alternates on round parity exactly as the segment order does, so over six rounds each write leads three times. A drift within a run no longer reads as a difference between the writes.

  4. rf2-77gz8's UNKNOWN BECOMES ASKABLE. The paired mode puts an arm window and a floor window under both writes in one round for the first time, which is what deciding whether the ladder ARMS carry the floor's second mode requires -- and that single unknown decides whether a page-global level cancels in arm minus floor or not.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, stated so it is not assumed. The two legs of a pair are separated by one segment pass rather than being adjacent windows, so a mid-run transition of the kind rf2-77gz8 describes can still fall between them; that is a large improvement on a whole process but it is not zero. NO WINDOW WAS TAKEN and no figure moved -- the build carries no measurement, and the thirteen descriptive cells in this bead's description stand exactly as published.

SEQUENCING UNCHANGED: rf2-77gz8 should be resolved alongside or first.

comments.text:
PAIRED WINDOW TAKEN, rf2-0gjqi, 2026-08-18 14:26-14:31 AUSEST. Record:
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-sign-follows-the-pass-not-the-write.md (PR #8473).
Datasets committed: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-0gjqi/.

tolerance was touched.

THE AUDIT OBLIGATION IS DISCHARGED. #8424 required matched certified pairs once
the paired mode landed, an independent-block count over run-pair/order blocks
rather than rungs, and a correction to the measurement page, the studio index and
this bead together. All three move in PR #8473; the block count is below.

DESIGN, FIXED BEFORE THE FIRST RUN. Two runs, P0_ALLOC_PLAN=full
P0_ALLOC_CELLS=1 P0_ALLOC_WRITE=paired, B = 4, six rounds. Two were declared and
two were taken; none added after a result, none dropped. The estimator was
written down before the first run.

THE ESTIMATOR, NAMED FOR WHAT IT IS. Per round r, segment s, arm a:
  d_all  = (arm@all .legMedian - floor@all .legMedian) / B
  d_page = (arm@page.legMedian - floor@page.legMedian) / B
  Delta  = d_page - d_all
A round contributes ONLY IF ALL FOUR windows certified in that round. Cells are
reported twice because they are different statistics: RATIO-OF-MEDIANS (median of
d_page over the cell's rounds over median of d_all over the SAME rounds, less 1 --
the form comparable to the published table) and MEDIAN-OF-RATIOS. Neither is a
mean and neither is a run-mean.

THE RESIDUAL DISSOLVES.
  - Across the 16 mid-rung cell medians (8 cells x 2 runs), page reads below all
    at 10 OF 16 on ratio-of-medians and 9 of 16 on median-of-ratios. The
    published window read 8 OF 8.
  - Magnitudes: 0.06% - 2.98% absolute, absolute median 0.46%. Published: 0.51% -
    4.28%, absolute median 1.68% on the same eight cells.

AND THE SIGN IS SET BY MEASUREMENT ORDER, NOT BY THE WRITE. Block = the ROUND,
because within a round every arm of a segment differences against the same floor
pair and rf2-77gz8's term is page-global. Taking the median of Delta/d_all over
each round's certified mid-rung cells: THE LEG PASS THAT RAN SECOND READS LOWER
IN 10 OF 12 BLOCKS -- 6 of 6 in run 1, 4 of 6 in run 2 -- WHICHEVER WRITE
OCCUPIED IT. Decomposed under an additive position model, the pass-order term
reads +0.68% and +0.21% (same sign both runs) and the order-free WRITE term reads
-0.33% and +0.24% (OPPOSITE signs). Filed as rf2-fk6pj.

INDEPENDENT BLOCKS, COUNTED AS THE AUDIT ASKED. TWO independent process blocks.
The twelve round blocks share a session inside each run and are NOT twelve
independent trials; the nominal one-sided sign test over twelve gives
p = 79/4096 = 0.019 and is quoted only as what the nominal test says. The claim
that survives the stricter count is the weaker one: both process blocks put the
second pass lower.

V2's FLOOR-DROP HALF HOLDS, AND IS NOW WITHIN-ROUND. 1,652 B (8.6%) on
reagent-subs and 1,652-1,658 B (8.4%) on uix-subs, the same number on both
segments to within 6 B, spanning 1,644-1,664 B across 21 paired certified rounds.
Published unpaired: 1,769 / 1,765 B.

THE CONTROLS. Both runs' positive control passed -- differential 8.00 B/double
against a predicted 8, direct 8.08, 0 unverified read-backs. Both captured EXIT 1
on the falls gate (55 and 54 collections inside measured windows), so NO SLOPE IS
QUOTED from either. And a null arm the previous windows did not read: R = 0 mounts
boundaries that read nothing, so arm - floor must be zero under either write --
over 38 paired certified observations its Delta reads a median of 0 B/boundary,
absolute median 1.5, 90th percentile 4.5. That is what licenses reading mid-rung
differences of 5-198 B/boundary at all.

WHAT IS NOT CONCLUDED, and it is a long list on purpose.
  - THE TWO WRITES ARE NOT SHOWN TO BE EQUIVALENT. No interval is offered for the
    write term. Two process blocks give -0.33% and +0.24%: consistent with zero,
    and NOT a bound. Its magnitude is UNRESOLVED.
  - THE CAUSE OF THE PUBLISHED 8-OF-8 IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The measured pass-order
    term is of the right sign but SMALLER than the published 1.68% absolute
    median, and it is a within-round effect where the published confound was
    between two PROCESSES. Different estimand; right sign, wrong size.
  - rf2-77gz8 IS NOT RESOLVED. Its second mode did NOT appear here -- the
    certified floor spans 46-58 B over six rounds in all four (run, segment)
    cells under both writes, with no 3,792 B step -- but that is B = 4 on the
    `full` plan against its B = 24 on the `floor` plan, and absence in two runs is
    not absence. What DID change is that the estimator no longer turns on the
    answer: a page-global level present in a round enters all four of that
    round's windows and cancels. Its sequencing note ("resolve alongside or
    first") is therefore satisfied in the sense that mattered.
  - NO RULING IS MADE ON TOLERABILITY. The description's question -- whether
    ~1-4% of non-cancellation is acceptable -- was posed of a figure this window
    does not reproduce, so as posed it is MOOT. Whether anything is left to rule
    on is Mike's, not this window's.
  - LEG ORDER IS NOT SEPARATED FROM ROUND PARITY (the rig ties them), no
    mechanism is proposed for the pass-order term, and no cause is assigned to the
    two R = 0 excursions (-96.5 and -56.5 B/boundary, both uix-subs|uix at round 3,
    one per run, reproducing across runs).
  - NO BOUND ON WITHIN-RUN QUIETNESS. Brackets are before-and-after only. The box
    was loaded (5.7-8.0% of 24 cores, 0 java at every bracket) and that is
    correct for a census of monotone counters.
  - THE INTRA-LEG GATE SCREENED NOTHING. Stride 2, so allocIntraLegRefusals
    returns [] by construction.

WHAT THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION SHOULD NO LONGER BE READ AS SAYING. The whole
paragraph beginning "THE FINDING" retains its thirteen descriptive cells, which
stand as published; but "Eight of eight in one direction", "Under a null of random
sign that is a 1-in-256 arrangement", and "it is not obviously noise either" are
each now MEASURED not to hold under the pairing the design always required. The
DECISION NEEDED paragraph is moot as posed.

THE SECOND ITEM CARRIED OUT RATHER THAN DROPPED. R = 20 again certified on one of

Filed as rf2-onozm with the refusal signature (a single leg near -800,000 B) and

CLOSING. The obligation #8424 set is met and its answer is on the record; what

title: hicasso: a collection INSIDE a leg passes both allocation gates — the by-site stream sees it and the certificate does not
description:
MEASURED by rf2-ojehu's by-site window on 2026-08-16 (quiet box, 6 runs, 72 floor-arm windows at P0_ALLOC_BY_SITE=1). Filed rather than fixed: a measurement window does not amend the instrument it is measuring on.

THE OBSERVATION. 24 of 72 arm windows carry at least one NEGATIVE site step — a reclamation inside a single leg. 21 of them are already refused by the falls gate. THREE have falls === 0, so the falls gate saw nothing at all, and TWO of those three ALSO certified at tau:

  s3-c6-page round 0 uix-subs  leg 3: dispatch +199,980 B, drain -178,496 B, leg total +21,484 B — falls 0, CERTIFIED
  s3-c6-page round 2 uix-subs  leg 4: dispatch +305,392 B, drain -285,292 B, leg total +20,100 B — falls 0, CERTIFIED
  s3-c24-page round 0 reagent  leg 2: dispatch +279,024 B, drain -259,996 B, leg total +19,028 B — falls 0, refused on another leg

WHY BOTH GATES MISS IT, and neither is defective on its own terms. The falls gate walks the COLLAPSED stride-2 stream, where the leg is one step; a reclamation bracketed by a larger allocation inside that step turns nothing negative, so nothing falls. The leg tolerance is the gate written for exactly that blind side (the driver's own comment says so) and it passes these because the leg's NET is inside tau of the cohort median — +1,330 B and +2,008 B against medians of 20,154 B and 18,092 B.

WHAT IT COSTS. A certified window is one whose six legs are asserted to be repetitions of ONE work unit. A leg carrying a 285 KB collect-and-reallocate is not that, and the window under-reads its true allocation by an unknown amount — the same failure mode the leg tolerance exists to catch, arriving through the seam the tolerance cannot see.

THE OPEN QUESTION, not answered here. Whether the certificate should read the BY-SITE stream when the mode is armed. rf2-rs8q6 deliberately reads it off the collapsed stream so that allocSteps never sees a by-site stream and rise/falls/maxStep cannot move — that fence is load-bearing and any repair has to keep every published row byte-identical. A cheaper shape may exist: a DIAGNOSTIC negative-site-step count reported beside the certificate without adjudicating it, which would have surfaced all three windows without touching a published quantity.

EVIDENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-dispersion-is-in-the-dispatch-site.md, section 'An intra-leg collection the falls gate cannot see'.
notes:
BUILT (2026-08-16). A THIRD GATE, additional to the two, reading the by-site
stream that already saw this. `allocIntraLegRefusals` refuses a window carrying
a NEGATIVE measured site step; `allocWindowVerdict` unions the two gates'
refusals and keeps each list named so the exit can attribute a failure to the
gate that made it. Both in implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs.

THE OPEN QUESTION IN THE DESCRIPTION IS ANSWERED, and the answer is the cheaper
shape the description itself floated — with one correction. The certificate does
NOT read the by-site stream: `allocSteps` is handed the collapsed stride-2 stream
still, so rf2-rs8q6's fence stands and `rise`, `falls`, `maxStep`, `legs`,
`legMedian` and `legWorstDeviation` are byte-identical on every window at every
stride (pinned by driving both functions over all three named windows). But a
pure DIAGNOSTIC was rejected: a count printed beside a certificate that still
reads CERTIFIED leaves the certificate asserting something false, which is the
cost this bead names. The refusal list is the diagnostic that also adjudicates,
and it moves no published quantity to do it.

NOT A WIDENING, AND τ IS UNTOUCHED. The gate can only ever ADD refusals. There is
no threshold in it to calibrate or dial — the test is a SIGN, the same sign test
the falls gate already makes, applied one stride finer. `ALLOC_LEG_TOLERANCE`
stays 0.25 with its uncalibrated marker; the gate does not read it, and the two
windows refuse identically at τ = 0.01, 0.25 and 0.99.

WHAT CHANGES ON THE 72 MEASURED WINDOWS — replayed through the new code against
rf2-ojehu's own raw record, whose falls/τ/certified counts (23 / 33 / 39)
reproduce that window's published figures exactly:

  - 48 of 72 are untouched: no measured negative site step at all.
  - 24 of 72 gain at least one intra-leg refusal REASON.
  - 22 of those 24 were already refused (21 on falls plus τ, 1 on τ alone).
  - EXACTLY 2 OF 72 CHANGE CLASSIFICATION, certified -> refused, and they are
    precisely the two this bead names. Certified count 39 -> 37 of 72.
  - Of 108 control windows, 1 carries a negative measured site step and it was
    already refused by the falls gate, so no control flips.

NO PUBLISHED CONCLUSION MOVES. rf2-e9wr's window was taken entirely at stride 2,
where `allocSiteSplit` yields no site legs, so the gate is inert by construction
(verified against that run's own raw record: siteLegs is empty in all 12 arm and
all 18 control windows). rf2-ojehu's page already excluded exactly these two by
hand — its headline population is "collection-free, no excursion, no intra-leg
reclamation", 41 of 72, and its own refusals section says the population
"additionally excludes ... the two windows carrying an intra-leg reclamation".

ONE NUMBER ON THAT PAGE WOULD READ DIFFERENTLY ON A RE-RUN, named here rather
than edited there (the fence on published records): it reports "39 of 72
certify"; under this gate that is 37 of 72. It is a count of what the driver
refused, not a conclusion — the page quotes nothing from a refused window, and
both newly-refused windows were already outside every figure it publishes.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, stated on the bead so a later reader is not misled. A
reclamation bracketed inside ONE SITE — collected and re-allocated between the
same two readings — is invisible here for the reason it is invisible to the falls
gate one stride up. This gate MOVES the blind spot from the leg to the site; it
does not remove it. Reaching further needs a seam `p0-heap/alloc-window!`
deliberately does not cut.

rf2-stals NOT TAKEN. Its `worst-dev site` heading is in the same function this
bead edits one clause of, but they are different claims and do not belong in one
commit; the heading is untouched by this change.

PR #8420 (draft -> ready). Gates: `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` PASS, captured exit 0,
0 FAIL lines; the owning pin `p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs` 82 passed (74 before),
both directly and inside the spine; sabotage of the sign test reddened 4 pins and
the restore was verified by content hash.

title: method: an aborted pull has a THIRD cause the runbook does not name — 'Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches'
description:
MEASURED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-16 19:36 AUSEST, immediately after merging PR #8407.

THE RUNBOOK NAMES EXACTLY TWO CAUSES, in two places, and insists on
discriminating between them by the message text:
  - .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md: 'AN ABORTED PULL HAS TWO CAUSES WITH
    DIFFERENT REMEDIES, AND THE MESSAGE SAYS WHICH'
  - CLAUDE.md's post-merge bullet says the same thing in the same words.
Both name 'local changes would be overwritten' (uncommitted tracker state ->
checkpoint, checkout, pull) and 'Not possible to fast-forward' (your own
checkpoint diverged -> pull --rebase, then push).

A THIRD MESSAGE EXISTS AND NEITHER REMEDY TOUCHES IT:

  git pull --ff-only origin main
  From https://github.com/day8/re-frame2
   * branch                  main       -> FETCH_HEAD
     0b3ca111ea..362c2a217c  main       -> origin/main
  fatal: Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches.
  exit 128

WHY BOTH DOCUMENTED REMEDIES ARE INERT HERE, which is what makes this worth
writing down rather than filing as noise:
  - 'git status --porcelain' was EMPTY. Nothing to checkpoint, nothing to
    clear, so the first remedy has no object.
  - 'git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main' read '0  2' — 0
    ahead, 2 behind. NOTHING HAD DIVERGED, so the second remedy's premise is
    false, and a fast-forward was not merely possible but trivially so.
A reader following the runbook's own instruction to branch on the message
therefore finds no branch to take, and the natural fallbacks (re-run the pull,
reach for --rebase) either loop or rewrite history for no reason.

THE CAUSE: git resolved MULTIPLE FETCH_HEAD entries and refused to pick one.
Every worker worktree in this repository is a LINKED worktree sharing one
.git, and .git/FETCH_HEAD is therefore SHARED STATE — a concurrent 'git fetch'
in any worker worktree rewrites it under the mayor. Six workers had been
running for the previous hour. This is the same shared-FETCH_HEAD hazard
mayor-posture.md already names when it explains why the strand discriminator
reads the LOCAL ref rather than the remote; that paragraph reasons about the
contamination correctly and then stops at the liveness question, so the pull
path never inherited it.

THE REMEDY, and it is a one-liner that sidesteps FETCH_HEAD entirely:
  git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main
Ran clean at once: exit 0, HEAD == origin/main, tree still clean. Used again
on the very next merge (#8410) with the same result.

WHAT TO CHANGE: add the third case to the discrimination in BOTH places that
carry the two-cause list — .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md and CLAUDE.md's
post-merge bullet — keyed on its message text like the other two, with the
FETCH_HEAD-is-shared reasoning and the ref-not-FETCH_HEAD remedy. Say
explicitly that it presents with a CLEAN tree and ZERO divergence, because
that pair is what rules the other two out and is the fastest discriminator.

CHECK BEFORE WRITING, because it may be worth more than an added case: whether
'git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main' should simply
REPLACE 'git pull --ff-only origin main' as the standing post-merge command.
It is immune to this failure by construction, it keeps the same fast-forward-
only guarantee, and it removes a shared-state dependency from the one command
this loop runs after every single merge. If it is strictly better, say so and
change it rather than documenting a workaround for a command we did not need
to keep. If there is a reason to keep the pull form, record that reason.
close_reason:
PR #8412. ANSWERED THE BEAD'S QUESTION: REPLACE, not document. 'git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main' now IS the standing post-merge command; the pull form is retired in all three surfaces.

THE REASON IS STRONGER THAN THE BEAD'S: a contaminated FETCH_HEAD does not fail honestly, so NO added case keyed on message text could have covered it. Measured on git 2.53 in a scratch repo: (1) with a multi-ref FETCH_HEAD and a feature branch ahead of main, 'merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD' exited 0 and SILENTLY FAST-FORWARDED THE TRUNK ONTO feature-x; (2) with one divergent branch it aborted 'Not possible to fast-forward' on a CLEAN, 0-2 tree — wearing the SECOND documented cause's message while that cause's premise was false and its remedy inert. Undiscriminable by text. Both documented aborts reproduce VERBATIM under the merge form, so the two-cause list is unchanged and the swap costs nothing.

ONE BEAD PREMISE CORRECTED: linked worktrees do NOT share one FETCH_HEAD on git 2.53 — each gets .git/worktrees/<name>/FETCH_HEAD. Proved twice: a peer worktree's fetch left the primary's .git/FETCH_HEAD md5-identical, and in this repo .git/worktrees/r6c-9sz2t/FETCH_HEAD holds 7 refs while the primary's holds 1. The hazard is real but narrower: the PRIMARY checkout's own FETCH_HEAD, raced by any concurrent git process there — and the mayor checkout is the one every agent reaches into to add a worktree. Prose states the measured mechanism, not the inherited one.

Could not re-derive the literal 'Cannot fast-forward to multiple branches' on git 2.53 (it reduced the heads and reported the diverging message). The bead's verbatim capture stands; the ruling does not depend on the message — which is itself the argument for replacing rather than documenting.

THREE COPIES FOUND, NOT TWO: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md had ALREADY grown a third bullet (carrying the false shared-FETCH_HEAD mechanism) while mayor-merge.md and CLAUDE.md still said 'exactly two causes' — the known two-copies-disagree defect, caught in flight. Reasoning now lives in .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md; CLAUDE.md points at it; loops.md's third bullet is REMOVED and hoisted into the standing instruction, since under the new command that case cannot fire.

Out of scope by choice: the 'git pull --rebase origin main' recovery path is untouched — not the every-merge command, and its four outcome checks already catch a bad result.

title: method: the worktree->agentId ledger does not survive a /clear — 8 of 8 ids unresolvable, 7 of 8 transcripts zero-byte
description:

both halves of it fail independently.

session's /clear, every one of them with its id recorded at DISPATCH time
exactly as the rule prescribes, returned the same error to SendMessage:

  storytb-kttom      a2374eb51f16753bc   No transcript found
  recert-hic090      acf62ddaa8adcd940   No transcript found
  r6dtail-mgrsl      a3ac69cf3ed406c20   No transcript found

  guidefix-mv7oh     ad503ca68c8e0befa   No transcript found
  docsdirgate-5exqc  ac9cd92cae780a33d   No transcript found
  tmplreload-r0kk7   aa65d5d2b8113e68e   No transcript found
  xraydocs-3bwos     a414fd099f059a60e   No transcript found

POSITIVE CONTROL, because 8 identical failures could equally mean SendMessage
is broken: agent a5928ac0328f05c97, dispatched by the CURRENT session, resumed
successfully on the same call shape and answered. So the mechanism works and
the discriminator is which session dispatched the agent.

HALF TWO — THE TRANSCRIPT IS EMPTY ANYWAY. Reading the files directly, they
exist under the session tasks directory but SEVEN OF EIGHT ARE ZERO BYTES. The
eighth, guidefix-mv7oh, holds 986,011 bytes and its last assistant text is an
interim progress note ('4 still IN_PROGRESS'), not a completion report — so it
would not satisfy the reap test even though it survived. Recovering the report
from disk is therefore not an available fallback either.

CONSEQUENCE. The reap rule is unchanged and still correct: it fails safe, and
nothing has been lost. What accumulates is directories. 16 worktrees are now
permanently unreapable on this machine — the 8 pre-ledger ones rf2-cp0dd
already identified, plus these 8, which the ledger was supposed to save. Two
more join the set at every /clear.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT ASKING FOR. Not a weakening of the reap test, and not the
bounded amnesty rf2-cp0dd considered and rejected — that reintroduces the
inference the rule exists to forbid. The question is whether a DURABLE record
of the report TEXT is now warranted after all. rf2-cp0dd rejected that as more
expensive than an id plus a message, and it was right on the evidence it had;
this measurement removes the cheaper option's foundation. A fifth field on the
existing TSV line, written when the report arrives, costs one append and needs
no new machinery. It has a known gap — a report that arrives after the clear
is never written — but that gap is strictly smaller than today's, where the
report is unrecoverable in every case.

FOR THE OPERATOR: the alternative is accepting that worker worktrees are
single-session-lifetime and are cleaned up by some other authority (a periodic
operator-run sweep of trees whose PRs merged more than N hours ago). That is a
policy call, not a mayor call.

The one transcript with no completion report is guidefix-mv7oh (interim note) — the same agent the bead singled out, but it is the sole NON-report rather than the sole survivor.

WHERE THE 'ZERO BYTES' CAME FROM. A different file wearing the same id: the scratch background sink tasks/<agentId>.output, created at dispatch and in this configuration never filled. Its emptiness carries NO information — it is zero bytes for a current-session agent that completed and returned normally (verified control). Reading it is a READ, not an inference — the agent's own words verbatim. 16 worktrees are therefore recoverable, not permanently unreapable.

title: [docs-defect] the Hicasso install chapter does not yield a project that boots
description:
FRESH-READER DEFECT (rf2-hic-069, FRICTION 3,4,5,6,7,22). A no-context agent following docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md produced a tree that compiles but could not be shown to boot. Six gaps, all in one chapter:

1. THE deps.edn CANNOT BUILD. :32-33 says 'Hicasso interprets Hiccup at runtime, so it needs no compiler hook, macro allow-list, or build flag. A normal shadow-cljs browser build is enough' -- then gives {:deps true ...} in shadow-cljs.edn, which makes shadow read its classpath from deps.edn, which declares neither thheller/shadow-cljs nor org.clojure/clojurescript. Needs the dependency line or an 'npm i -D shadow-cljs' step.

2. NO CLONE INSTRUCTIONS. :15 says the artefact 'lives in the re-frame2 monorepo, so today you resolve it ... from a checkout using :local/root'. No URL, no branch, no tag. Unlike docs/xray/01-installation.md:7 ('a re-frame2 clone sitting BESIDE your project directory'), it never states the sibling requirement -- the reader infers it only from the ../ in the path.

3. THE EXAMPLE DOES WHAT THE BOOT RECIPE FORBIDS. :89-93 puts (defonce root (h/mount! ...)) at namespace top level. docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:206-208 says 'Keep create-root, render, and browser listener installation out of top-level namespace code', and :220-222 gives the structurally identical anti-pattern. Its stated reason (:225-227, 'The namespace may be loaded by a test host, a Story tool') applies to Hicasso equally.

4. NO :init-fn. Following from 3: :41 writes :modules {:main {:entries [counter.core]}} with no init hook, while boot-and-mount-an-app.md:55-56 says 'Wire run as the build's :init-fn'.

5/6. NO package.json AND NO REACT VERSION. :29 says 'npm install react react-dom' with no version and no package.json, while the documented surface depends on React 18+/19 behaviour: useId prefixing (api-reference.md:160-165), StrictMode double-invoke (00-installation.md:216, 02-views-and-reads.md:141-143), createRoot/createPortal/React.lazy (api-reference.md:177, 359).

close_reason: PR #8397. Verified by doing it, not by reading: a project built from the chapter, in an empty directory outside the repo with the monorepo as a sibling, now compiles clean and in headless Chromium mounts, seeds to 'Clicked 0 times' and reaches 'Clicked 1 times' on a click with no console errors. Before: exit 1, 'Could not locate shadow/cljs/devtools/cli'. Gaps 1-4 were real and are fixed ({:deps {:aliases [:shadow]}} over a :shadow alias; clone line plus the sibling requirement; the mount moved off namespace top level into an ^:export init wired as :init-fn, and the two-root example with it). title: RIG: amp-merge clock keeps no per-round vector for its EFFECT or its NULL (per-element-ns vs ns-terms)
description:
FOUND by rf2-adld3's measurement window, and FILED rather than fixed because the rig is frozen inside a window.

'amp_merge_clock_app.cljs' has TWO ns/field summarisers. 'ns-terms' keeps ':per-round' beside the summary and is used for the ladder's four rungs. 'per-element-ns' keeps only {:n :min :max :p50} and is what ':per-element-ns {:effect .. :null ..}' is built from.

So the NULL — the figure rf2-adld3's whole window turns on, and the figure whose 1.4737 round opened rf2-6ta5r — is the one quantity NOT retained round by round. Same for the effect's ns/field.

rf2-adld3 recovered the null's per-round ns/field EXACTLY by arithmetic on what the rig did print (the whole rung's per-round ns and ratio give each round's :expanded median as ns/(2500*(r-1)); the null's is that times (r_null-1)*2500), and checked all three runs against the rig's own printed {min max p50} — exact match in every one. That recovery works only because the ladder rungs exist. An instrument should not need a sibling row to be re-adjudicable.

REMEDY: point the effect and null rows at 'ns-terms' instead of 'per-element-ns', or delete 'per-element-ns'. The docstring's reason for keeping it — 'so the two published rows keep the shape they were published in' — is about the SHAPE OF THE SUMMARY, and ns-terms is a superset: it assocs :per-round onto exactly the same map. Verify that before changing it.

DO NOT take a window in the same PR: this is an edit half. Surface: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/amp_merge_clock_app.cljs
close_reason: FIXED in PR #8376 (worker/w-rig2, merged 2026-08-16T02:23:09Z, rebased onto 0eac98dd53). Premise HELD at source: per-element-ns returned lane/summarise's {:n :min :max :p50} only, while ns-terms assoc'd :per-round and served the ladder's four rungs. Remedy is the bead's own: per-element-ns deleted, both the EFFECT and the NULL rows routed through ns-terms, both per-round vectors printed. DELTA the worker established against the bead's text: only the NULL was genuinely unretained. The effect's per-round ns/field was already in the record at :ladder :whole :ns-per-site :per-round, since ladder-rung ratios p50s :merged :expanded is the identical quantity — which is why rf2-adld3's window had to reconstruct the null and only the null. No published figure invalidated; the summary now runs over the round4'd vector (<=5e-5 ns/field on figures printed to 1 dp), so it is exactly reproducible from :per-round. Red proof: mechanism hoisted out of the round loop, 48 failures exit 1, restored and hash-verified.

title: MEASURE: re-read the amp-merge clock's NULL arm on the warmed rig (rf2-6ta5r follow-on)
description:
RAISED by rf2-6ta5r's rig repair (PR #8371), which was the EDIT HALF and deliberately took no window.

WHAT CHANGED. 'amp_merge_clock_app.cljs' now runs {:warmup 8 :samples 12} instead of {:warmup 3 :samples 6}. The SEVEN ARMS ARE UNTOUCHED: rf2-6ta5r settled the arm-count question with the schedule arithmetic rather than by shrinking the ladder.

WHAT rf2-6ta5r ESTABLISHED. The seven-arm schedule is NOT implicated. Replaying lane/rounds! against order-guard/slot-order at n = 4, 5, 7 and 8 gives every arm 30 banked samples per run, the same phase strata (rounds 1-2 at 3-15 prior executions against rounds 4-5 at 32-44) at EVERY arm count, and the null's true predecessor distribution unchanged in kind. title: hicasso: read_profile phase B's delta estimator carries a ~+0.022 ms/commit positive offset of unestablished cause
description:
FOUND BY rf2-3l6hf's null-control window (2026-08-16, PR #8360, instrument
blob ef7a0d3787). Three runs, exit 0, both order guards reportable, positive
control passing, residue gate never firing.

THE MEASUREMENT. c-null is c-local again — the same C-FULL mode through the
same constructor under a second id — so c-local - c-null has a TRUE COST OF
EXACTLY ZERO by construction. It read:

  +0.0234 / +0.0219 / +0.0234 ms/commit

Three run-level readings within one grid step (0.0015625) of each other, on a
quantity that is exactly zero. So the pooled-median delta at this shape
carries a positive OFFSET of about +0.022 ms/commit.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every phase-B term is a c-local - X delta on this instrument,
so every one of them is displaced by roughly that amount. Against each run's
own null the terms are only a few multiples of it: activation capture
1.5-2.0 nulls, cell-map insert 2.3-2.9, watch wiring 2.8-3.6, reader
membership 1.0-1.8. Only the reaction build (19-21) is clear by any margin.
The four terms rf2-07rnj would republish are therefore all of the same order
as a bias whose size is measured and whose cause is not.

THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND THAT WINDOW'S DATA DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE.
Three candidates are live:
  (a) a residual ARM-POSITION effect — c-local sits at slot 1 of the arms
      vector and every arm it is differenced against sits at a higher slot,
      so any monotone within-sweep drift biases c-local - X positive for
      EVERY X, which is exactly the pattern observed;
  (b) within-sweep thermal or cache drift;
  (c) the pooled median's own behaviour on this arm's right-tailed
      distribution (a max around twice the p50).

The arm-order guard reporting 'reportable' on every run does NOT exclude (a):
its tolerance is 0.10 and this offset is 3.2-3.6% of c-local, well inside it.

WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM, stated as candidates and not as a ruling: NULLS AT
SEVERAL ARM POSITIONS. One null differences slot 1 against slot 2; reader
membership differences slot 1 against slot 6. A second and third C-FULL arm
placed at higher slots would make the offset's dependence on slot distance
directly measurable, and (a) predicts a monotone relationship where (b) and
(c) do not. Whoever takes it must treat it as its own measurement window
under Shape 6 — adding arms is a rig change and belongs BEFORE the window,
which is why rf2-3l6hf filed this rather than adding them mid-series.

DO NOT subtract the null from the published terms as a correction and call
them corrected. The null calibrates a slot-1-vs-slot-2 difference; applying
it to a slot-1-vs-slot-6 difference assumes the very thing (a) is about.

DO NOT read the offset as a bound on anything. It is a measured property of
the ESTIMATOR, not of any term.
close_reason:
PREMISE WITHDRAWN BY MEASUREMENT. 2026-08-19 00:43 AUSEST, on Mike's standing delegation.

THIS BEAD'S SUBJECT IS A +0.022 ms/commit OFFSET OF UNESTABLISHED CAUSE. The window ran (PR #8422, rig half PR #8384) and THE OFFSET DID NOT REPRODUCE. Three runs, count fixed at three BEFORE run 1, all exit 0, both arm-order guards reportable, phase-A positive control passing, residue gate never firing.

THE DECISIVE COMPARISON, and it is a clean one: rf2-3l6hf read +0.0234 / +0.0219 / +0.0234 on c-null — three readings inside ONE grid step. This window's c-null spans THIRTY-TWO grid steps (+0.0109 / -0.0188 / +0.0313). The thing this bead exists to explain was not present to be diagnosed, and three candidates cannot be separated on a signal that did not appear.

SO THE BEAD CLOSES ON ITS OWN TERMS rather than by fiat: it asks why an offset is there; the answer is that it is not.

WHAT THE WINDOW ESTABLISHED ANYWAY, preserved in the bead's comments which survive this closure:
  (a) arm-position — SUPPORTED as a component of RUN-LEVEL error, NOT as the cause of an offset. c-local and its twin rose together by +0.0531 and +0.0625 between runs 2 and 3 while the other two nulls moved +0.0031 and +0.0078. Three caveats were recorded rather than smoothed over: it rests on ONE of two transitions, there is NO SECOND NULL PAIR, and it is ABSENT at round granularity.
  (b) thermal or cache drift — OPEN, and NOT SEPARABLE from (a) by this rig, because the twin cancels any function of sweep position whatever its cause.
  (c) pooled-median behaviour — DISFAVOURED as a cause of a systematic offset on a source-level argument: identical distributions give the same expected median under any estimator, so an estimator yields variance, not bias. Not excluded as a variance contributor.

(b) STAYING OPEN IS NOT THIS BEAD'S OBLIGATION. It is a known limit of the rig, correctly stated, on a question this bead did not ask. Closing here does not bury it; it is on the record above, and any bead that needs to separate (a) from (b) will need a rig that can, which is a different piece of work with a different fence.

A RIG LIMIT FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED, carried here because it governs how future readings are interpreted: c-null-curve's claim that 'a linear drift cancels' is EXACT for an arithmetic MEAN and only FIRST-ORDER true for the MEDIAN the rig actually reports — two arms sharing only the mean differ at second order in the position multiset's variance (7.25 vs 5.25). SO A NON-ZERO CURVE READING DOES NOT ESTABLISH CURVATURE. Nothing was concluded about linearity, and nothing should be until that is fixed.

NO BOUND IS PUBLISHED AND NONE IS DERIVABLE from a null spread — a null says what the instrument cannot SEE, never how large the invisible thing is. The sibling rf2-07rnj has already been the vehicle for exactly that error once, when a refuted '< 0.006 ms/commit' bound reached a live brief. It must not recur here.

comments.text:
RIG HALF LANDED — THIS BEAD IS NOW WINDOW-ONLY. PR #8384 (worker/slotnulls-lo7uy)
adds the discriminating arms and takes NO measurement, per Mike's 2026-08-14
ruling on rf2-2rtt6.140 and this bead's own "adding arms is a rig change and
belongs BEFORE the window". Four workers were compiling on the box throughout,
so any window taken would have measured the fleet.

WHAT LANDED. Two C-FULL nulls, APPENDED so no existing arm moves — every arm
rf2-3l6hf published keeps its slot (commit 0 … b-build 8), and
frames-per-window (32), b-rounds (8) and b-sampling ({:warmup 2 :samples 8})
are untouched. The arm COUNT necessarily changes, 9 -> 11, because n is an
input to lane/slot-order; eleven arms is a new series exactly as nine was
against eight.

THE LAYOUT, AND WHY IT DISCRIMINATES. rounds-async! hands lane/slot-order the
SAMPLE index, not the round, so the schedule repeats identically every round
and an arm's multiset of sweep positions is fixed for the whole run. No number
of rounds averages a positional bias away — which is worth setting beside a
null that repeated to within one grid step across three runs. The new
slot-footprint fn reads that multiset out of lane/slot-order itself. At n=11:

  slot  1  c-local       [1 3 4 5 6 7 8 10]  mean 5.500
  slot  2  c-null        [0 0 2 4 5 6 7  9]  mean 4.125
  slot  9  c-null-twin   [1 3 4 5 6 7 8 10]  mean 5.500
  slot 10  c-null-curve  [2 3 4 5 6 7 8  9]  mean 5.500

c-null-twin occupies c-local's footprint EXACTLY, so any cost that is a
function of sweep position — of any shape, not merely linear — cancels term by
term; c-null-curve shares the mean position on a different footprint, so a
linear drift cancels and a curved one does not; c-null stays where the
published window had it. The window therefore separates three outcomes:
all three nulls alike -> not sweep position (candidate b as a global drift, or
c); c-null offset with the twin at zero -> positional (a); twin at zero and
curve away from zero -> positional AND non-linear.

A NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S OWN WORDING. The bead framed (a) as predicting a
MONOTONE relationship with SLOT DISTANCE. Reading the schedule out rather than
assuming it: the rotation makes the physical quantity the position FOOTPRINT,
not the distance, and the naive distance prediction and the footprint
prediction are different shapes on the same three arms (distances 1, 8, 9). The
rig reads both, so the window discriminates either way and nothing was assumed.

WHAT THE WINDOW STILL NEEDS, when the fleet is next idle: three runs of
run.cjs with HICASSO_INIT_FN=re-frame.bench.hicasso.read-profile-app/-main on a
quiet box, bracketed Processor Queue Length readings outside the measured
windows, exit 0, both order guards reportable, phase-A positive control
passing, residue gate never firing. Read the three null deltas TOGETHER against
the table above. The transcript now carries :read-profile-slot-plan, so the
layout travels with the numbers.

STILL PROHIBITED, unchanged: do not subtract a null from a published term and
call it corrected (c-null calibrates slot 1 against slot 2; reader membership
differences slot 1 against slot 6), and do not read any null as a bound on
anything — it is a measured property of the ESTIMATOR, not of a cost.

rf2-07rnj remains blocked on this bead.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
WINDOW HALF RAN — THE OFFSET DID NOT REPRODUCE, SO ITS CAUSE IS STILL NOT
ESTABLISHED. PR #8422 (worker/nullwindow-lo7uy). No rig edited; two files land,
a result record and one appended studio blockquote.

WHAT RAN. Three runs of run.cjs with
HICASSO_INIT_FN=re-frame.bench.hicasso.read-profile-app/-main. THE RUN COUNT WAS
FIXED AT THREE BEFORE RUN 1 STARTED — the count the 04:55:51Z comment specified

WHAT REFUSED: NOTHING. All three runs exit 0 (captured by me, not reported by

rig printed matches the 04:55:51Z table exactly, and I re-derived that table
independently from order_guard/slot-order before running.

THE THREE NULLS (run-level deltas, ms/commit; each a difference of two POOLED
MEDIANS over 64 kept samples divided by the 32-frame window — lane/summarise's
:p50, an order statistic, NOT an arithmetic mean of samples):

  c-null       slot  2  [0 0 2 4 5 6 7 9]   +0.0109  -0.0188  +0.0313   range 0.0501 (32 steps)
  c-null-twin  slot  9  [1 3 4 5 6 7 8 10]  -0.0031  +0.0047  -0.0047   range 0.0094 ( 6 steps)
  c-null-curve slot 10  [2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9]   -0.0281  -0.0250  +0.0203   range 0.0484 (31 steps)

THE HEADLINE IS A NEGATIVE. On the SAME arm pair rf2-3l6hf measured the offset
on — c-local slot 1 against c-null slot 2, both arms at the slots that window
published them at — this series read +0.0109 / -0.0188 / +0.0313: sign-changing,
spanning 32 grid steps where the predecessor spanned ONE (+0.0234 / +0.0219 /
+0.0234). The stable +0.022 offset was NOT PRESENT IN THIS SERIES TO BE
DIAGNOSED, on any of the three nulls. n went 9 -> 11, so the two series are not
arm-by-arm comparable; what is established is only that a +0.022 offset stable
to one grid step is not a reproducible property of this instrument across a
change of layout.

WHERE (a), (b) AND (c) STAND.
- (a) residual ARM-POSITION effect — SUPPORTED as a component of the RUN-LEVEL
  error, NOT established as the cause of the offset. c-null-twin, the only arm
  sharing c-local's kept-sample footprint exactly, is the only one of eight
  deltas with a small run-level range (0.0094 against 0.0360-0.0515 for the other
  seven, both other nulls included). The raw pooled medians show the mechanism:
  c-local 0.5922/0.5875/0.6406 and the twin 0.5953/0.5828/0.6453 rose TOGETHER by
  +0.0531 and +0.0625 between runs 2 and 3, while c-null moved +0.0031 and the
  curve +0.0078 across the same transition.
- (b) within-sweep thermal or cache drift — LEFT OPEN, and NOT SEPARABLE from (a)
  by this rig. The twin cancels ANY function of sweep position whatever its
  physical cause, so a residual arm-position effect and a within-sweep drift fall
  on the same side of it.
- (c) pooled median on a right-tailed arm — DISFAVOURED as a cause of a
  systematic OFFSET, on a source-level argument that does not need the data: two
  arms with identical true distributions have the same expected median under any
  estimator, so an estimator can produce VARIANCE between them but not BIAS. Not
  excluded as a contributor to run-level variance.

THREE CAVEATS ON THAT ONE POSITIVE FINDING, none optional. It rests on ONE of the
two transitions three runs afford (run 1 -> 2 is weak: c-local -0.0047, twin
-0.0125, c-null +0.0251, curve -0.0078). There is NO SECOND NULL PAIR to
corroborate it — c-local's footprint is shared only with the twin, and every
other footprint-sharing pair (c-null/b-build, commit/c-null-curve,
c-noactivate/c-nomap, c-nowatch/c-noreaders) puts two DIFFERENT WORKLOADS
together. And it is ABSENT AT ROUND GRANULARITY: over the window's 24 rounds the
within-round p50 deltas' standard deviations are 0.0415 (twin), 0.0447 (c-null),
0.0460 (curve) — ratios of 1.08 and 1.11, so position control removes essentially
nothing from the round-to-round scatter.

A LIMIT FOUND IN THE RIG, RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED. c-null-curve's
stated job is to cancel a LINEAR drift by matching c-local's MEAN position. That
is exact for an ARITHMETIC MEAN and only first-order true for the MEDIAN this
instrument actually reports. Two arms sharing a footprint exactly have identical
pooled mixtures and therefore identical medians for ANY drift — the twin's
argument survives the estimator — but two arms sharing only the mean differ at
second order in a term carrying the VARIANCE of the position multiset, and those
are not equal here: 7.25 for c-local against 5.25 for the curve. So a non-zero
curve reading does NOT establish curvature, and THIS WINDOW CONCLUDES NOTHING
ABOUT WHETHER THE DRIFT IS LINEAR. Not repaired, because n feeds lane/slot-order
and touching the roster moves every published footprint and starts a third
series.

WHAT WAS NOT CONCLUDED. Not that the offset is fixed, gone, or was an artefact of
nine arms. Not that any candidate is its cause — it was not observed. Not any
separation of (a) from (b). Not whether the drift is linear. NO BOUND ON ANY TERM
— no null was subtracted from any term and no null spread is quoted as a bound;
both standing prohibitions hold. Nothing about within-run quietness beyond the
bracketing. The five ablation figures this eleven-arm series recorded are its own
and supersede nothing.

THE BOX. \System\Processor Queue Length sampled ON ITS OWN and OUTSIDE every
measured run, five samples at 1 s, on a 24-core host: 0,0,0,0,0 at 00:42:46;
0,0,0,0,1 at 00:45:40; 0,0,0,0,0 at 00:47:05; 0,0,0,0,0 at 00:48:32 (all +10:00).
A second counter, % Processor Utility, read in the same brackets, never above
32.3% including the sampler's own cost. Nothing sampled inside a run, so the
quietness claim is a BRACKETING claim and nothing stronger. Zero open PRs and no
other worker in flight, verified at start-up and re-derived before the edit.

GATES. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0, captured by me on one command line in one
shell; verdict line "PASS fast PR spine" appears exactly once and the exit

column counts in both edited pages verified by hand.

question — the offset's CAUSE — is unresolved, and closing this would

whose cause is still unestablished. The WINDOW half is now done and should not be

title: bench(hicasso): the amp-merge clock's NULL arm degraded on the 7-arm schedule — one round read 1.4737
description:
RAISED by rf2-z143r's measurement window (2026-08-16, worktree w-z143r).

THE OBSERVATION. rf2-z143r added two ladder arms to 'amp_merge_clock_app.cljs', taking the schedule from five arms to seven, and left 'sampling' at {:warmup 3 :samples 6} and 'rounds' at 5 deliberately — a re-tune would have changed the conditions under which the five published arms are measured. The run passed every gate it has: arm-order guard REPORTABLE on all seven arms by predecessor and by phase, lane/control-verdict-strict inside the band on 5 of 5 rounds with :outside empty, fairness gate agreeing five judged arms on one 1,001-element page and proven able to answer false, 0 unverified writes of 360.

THE NULL DID NOT HOLD UP. ':expanded-b'/':expanded' read [0.9467 1.4737 1.0294 1 0.9853]. Four rounds sit within ±5.3% of 1.0; one reads 1.4737, which on the per-field arithmetic is +4,500 ns on a difference that is ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION. Compare the two published windows, whose null RUN-MEANS ran 1.001-1.013 and 0.970-1.027. The consequence is stated on the page: an impossible reading bounds nothing, so that window claims NO term outside instrument resolution, its own included, and the apportionment rests on a per-round sign pattern instead.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT KNOWN. The box was bracketed by 16 Processor Queue Length samples, 8 each side, every one 0 — and never sampled inside a measured window. So the box is not implicated by anything measured, and neither is it cleared: a bracketed run says nothing about its own interior. Whether the cause is the longer round (7 arms x 9 samples where there were 5), under-warming of the same family rf2-h904p names on 'direct_return_clock_app.cljs', or something else, this window did not test and does not guess.

THE REPAIR IS THE ARM, never the adjudication — more warm-up, fewer arms per round, a longer measured window. It is a RIG change and therefore not rf2-z143r's to make inside its own window. Note that fewer arms per round is in tension with the ladder existing at all, and that rf2-v5oto wants ANOTHER arm on the same rig: whoever takes this should settle the arm count first.

Surface: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/amp_merge_clock_app.cljs — 'sampling' {:warmup 3 :samples 6}, 'rounds' 5, seven arms.
close_reason:
PR 8371 merged as f58fc3c615. Five clauses verified at head 6e32de17e55e: 100 contexts, 53 SUCCESS plus 47 SKIPPED, no non-terminal, no new job keys. EDIT HALF ONLY — no window taken.

*** THE ARM-COUNT LEAD IS DEAD, AND IT WAS KILLED WITH ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN A RUN. *** This bead premise was that the NULL arm degraded ON THE SEVEN-ARM SCHEDULE, after rf2-z143r added two arms. Replaying rounds! against slot-order at n = 4, 5, 7 and 8: every arm banks 30 samples; the phase strata are rounds 1-2 (3 to 15 prior executions) against rounds 4-5 (32 to 44) AT EVERY ARM COUNT; and the null true predecessors are invariant (expanded 20, merged 10). THE NULL POSITION DID NOT MOVE WHEN THE LADDER LANDED.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is the one that matters downstream: the ladder stays whole, and RF2-V5OTO EIGHTH ARM IS NOT BLOCKED by this finding.

WHAT THE IMPOSSIBLE ROUND ACTUALLY IS: round TWO, inside the least-warmed span. And p50-of-6 cannot move 1.47x on one outlier, so at least 3 of the 6 were elevated — a ramp shape rather than a spike.

NOT CLAIMED: that warm-up produced the 1.4737. CHECKED AND REJECTED: the 3:1 mount asymmetry from :ctl-2x reusing expanded-arm is real, but each boundary runs 100 times per mount so both heads are far past tier-up.

THE FIX THAT LANDED IS THE SHARED-LOOP ONE described on rf2-h904p: collect! carried :prev across the warm-up gap, and on the seven-arm schedule THE ARM THAT LANDS UNDER A FALSE ADJACENCY IS THIS NULL — 4 of its samples filed under floor. Two apps had already fixed this privately with byte-identical bodies while lane/rounds!, ridden by ten bench apps, had not. It is now one function, lane/observe!.

RED PROOF is on rf2-h904p and covers both beads: 24 failures with the defect planted, 20 in the predecessor-truthfulness test across four arm counts and 4 in the self-predecessor test at n=5.

FOLLOW-ON FILED: rf2-adld3, re-read the amp-merge NULL arm on the warmed rig, with the worker own sequencing note to READ THE NULL FIRST. Correct separation — the repair and the re-measurement are two instruments.

title: docs(mayor-method): distinguish command acceptance from mutation confirmation
description:
RAISED by the merged-PR audit of PR #8355.

The new rule correctly rejects parsing incidental output as a command verdict, and its two motivating incidents were both non-zero refusals. But its general conclusion says to confirm a mutation "by its exit status, or by re-reading the thing it was supposed to change." A zero exit status proves only that the command reports success; it does not prove that state changed. Idempotent/no-op commands can legitimately exit zero, and durable operations can acknowledge locally before the required remote/postcondition is true. That repeats the same false-confirmation class at a different signal and conflicts with the paragraph's own claim that this rule reaches every command the mayor runs.

Keep this bounded and ergonomic: distinguish the two layers. Always check the command's own exit status so refusals cannot masquerade as success; when actual state change or a durable postcondition matters (or no-op success is possible), re-read the exact target. The two incident examples need no expansion and no new mechanism.

Preserve the concise examples and avoid adding a workflow framework.

The or is the defect. A zero exit proves the command REPORTED SUCCESS, not that state changed: an idempotent call legitimately succeeds having done nothing, and a durable operation can acknowledge locally before the remote or the postcondition is true.   :hiccup  FIRST-THIRD n=10 p50 2.3000 ms [2.1000-4.9000]

title: [mayor-method] “Newest by embedded date” is not tracker chronology
description:
Merged-PR audit #8352 (merged 2026-08-15T18:11:57Z as the three-commit landed range 36679023b3c2c40c26586383adc22c94245d07ac..d80c18abcbf2d46d4b55180d1213459091f0ec26) found a residual correctness flaw in the replacement for the retired bottom-up rule.

The PR correctly proves rendered position is not chronology and correctly requires re-enumerating children. But all nine replacement sites now tell the reader to find the newest material by grepping CURRENT PROSE for `AUDIT` or ISO-looking dates and choosing the latest date. Those are content, not mutation timestamps: the newest scope correction may be undated; an old description can cite a later deadline/release date; a fresh note can cite older evidence; and `bd update --description` can make the supposedly oldest description the most recently edited field. The rule therefore still permits a stale brief while claiming to order the item.

Beads already exposes structured evidence: `bd history <id>` provides issue versions with commit dates and logical `updated_at`, `bd comments <id> --json` provides comment `created_at`, and `bd show <id> --json --include-comments` exposes the current structured fields. Replace the prose-date heuristic with the smallest reliable history/timestamp procedure. Do not build a new parser or chronology subsystem. Preserve the useful child re-enumeration rule and the unrelated absent-exit / zero-search additions.

Duplicate searches for newest note/text, bottom-up beads, rendered-position dates, bead chronology, dated notes, append-note timestamps, and tracker-item chronology returned no owner.
acceptance_criteria: The mayor commands and published method no longer treat dates mentioned inside issue prose as ordering metadata. They direct a Beads user to structured issue history/comment timestamps (and explain how to identify the changed material), explicitly cover undated field edits, retain child re-enumeration, and remain copyable. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh` pass; no new tool or abstraction is introduced.
notes:
AUDIT-REOPEN — merged PR #8356 (94b7f512e61c839d727629df6f4afd1189a5fd62, merged 2026-08-15T19:00:58Z).

The repair correctly removes the prose-date grep from the five operative blocks, directs chronology to tracker timestamps, preserves child re-enumeration, and keeps the procedure small. The exact acceptance is still unmet at its practical seam: it required explaining how to identify the changed material. Live `bd history rf2-nj5bg` prints commit id/time/author plus the same issue title/status for each entry; it does not say which field changed or show the changed text. Thus a reader can know that a newer mutation exists but cannot learn whether it changed description/notes or what instruction now governs. `bd history <id> --json` does carry full `Issue` snapshots, so the bounded repair is to name the JSON/snapshot comparison (or another actual changed-field route) rather than claiming the plain history listing is sufficient.

Also reconcile the two surviving active summaries so the old vocabulary cannot be pasted back: `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` still says “find the newest note by date” in §3, and `dispatch-prompt-template.md`’s failure table still says “newest note found by date.” Say tracker timestamp there. No new parser or chronology subsystem is needed.
AUDIT-REOPEN — merged PR #8358 (56e5b6091763fd009e24078bf7e98b5f478c5601, merged 2026-08-15T19:22:57Z).

The PR correctly adds `bd history <id> --json`, fixes both paste-back summaries, preserves comments/children handling, and stays within the requested no-parser/no-framework boundary. Its final instruction still stops too early: all four copies say to compare the newest snapshot against its predecessor.

Live proof on this exact owner after the PR closed it: `bd history rf2-nj5bg --limit 8 --json` returned the newest pair with NO changed Issue field. The next informative pair changed only close_reason/closed_at/status/updated_at, followed by four more identical adjacent pairs; the latest governing text delta (`notes,updated_at`) appeared only at the seventh pair. Beads history therefore contains duplicate checkpoint snapshots and non-text mutations. Comparing one pair can truthfully report no changed material while an earlier, still-latest instruction change governs.

Bounded repair: say to walk adjacent snapshots newest-first, skipping identical and non-instruction-only deltas, until the first text-bearing field change (description/notes/acceptance/design as applicable) is found; keep comment `created_at` and child enumeration separate. No parser or chronology subsystem is needed. rf2-17t9u's acceptance-vs-mutation repair is complete and should remain closed.
close_reason:
PR 8359 merged as f2a1dc10c4. Five clauses verified at head 69adc98ae9de: 100 contexts, 24 SUCCESS plus 76 SKIPPED, no non-terminal, no new job keys.

ROUND FOUR OF ONE CHAIN, and the audit was right a fourth time. Its premise was REPRODUCED AT SOURCE on this very bead before anything was written — bd history rf2-nj5bg --limit 8 --json, comparing each adjacent pair:

  pair 0  identical
  pair 1  identical
  pair 2  notes, updated_at        <- the governing change
  pair 3  status, updated_at
  pair 4  identical
  pair 5  status, updated_at, closed_at, close_reason
  pair 6  identical

So the newest pair is a DUPLICATE CHECKPOINT and reports no changed material, while the instruction change that actually governs sits two pairs back behind a status-only mutation. A reader following the previous wording gets a TRUTHFUL 'nothing changed' and acts on superseded text — precisely the stale read this whole chain exists to prevent.

All four copies now say to walk adjacent pairs newest-first until the first change to a TEXT-BEARING field: description, notes, acceptance, design. Comment created_at and child enumeration stay separate, as the audit asked. No parser, no chronology subsystem, no new tool.

THE CHAIN, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED. Four rounds, each found by the merged-PR audit of the round before, each strictly NARROWER than the last:
  8352  position is not chronology
  8356  prose dates are not chronology
  8358  a plain history listing is not the changed field
  8359  one adjacent pair is not the changed field either
That is convergence, not thrash. Do not read a further reopen of this class as a regression, and do not re-open the settled halves.

All four rounds were authored by the mayor directly, at the operator's instruction, and all four defects were caught by the merged-PR audit rather than by the author. A worker's brief carries the premises-are-claims sentence and a fence someone else set; the mayor's own edits carry neither. That asymmetry is worth weighing when deciding how much method work the mayor should do by hand.

The same PR also carried a second commit from the method-reread loop, adding three Shape 6 rules that were being enforced in every live measurement brief and written nowhere: the CLOCK versus COUNTER estimand classification (a counter census reads the same on a loaded box and must not consume a drain), sample the counter ON ITS OWN (a reading of 59-77 was the dispatcher's own directory copy in the same command), and never sample INSIDE a measured run (that measures the benchmark).

W3 depends on rf2-0yp7w.8's spec deletion. THAT DELETION IS NOT HAPPENING PRE-CUT. The R5 worker reproduced why: spec/conformance/freehand/ is a COMPILE-TIME INPUT to implementation/freehand/test/ — conformance.cljc inlines fixtures/*.edn at macro-expansion time and roster.cljc does the same with conformance-index.md, so removing the corpus fails the COMPILE and reds jvm-freehand, cljs and cljs-browser. Full evidence is on rf2-0yp7w.8.

SO THE LANDING-ORDER RULING HOLDS IN GENERAL AND FAILS FOR THIS ONE INPUT. Unpoint-first is right for prose, links, catalogues and teaching surfaces. It cannot apply to a tree that a surviving test compiles against: there is nothing to unpoint, because the reference is not a pointer — it is an ingredient.

THE QUESTION FOR W3, stated so it can be answered rather than re-derived:

W3's charge is DELETE spec/004D + inbound links + gate-visible donor prose in spec/. Only part of that is entangled. 004D itself (2,588 lines, filed by spec/Ownership.md to the artefact being deleted) is NOT a compile input to anything — check that at source before ruling, because it is the whole question. IF THE SPLIT IS CLEAN, W3's dependency on rf2-0yp7w.8 comes OFF and (a) dispatches immediately. If 004D turns out to be compiled against too, W3 rides R3b entire and the pre-cut wave is W4 alone.

title: [story] Story-level :substrates does not reach the compiled plan — render-variant falls back to :reagent while the canvas honours it
description:
MEASURED while landing rf2-2dbpd, and deliberately NOT fixed there (both files are outside that bead's fence). A narrower residue of the disagreement rf2-3afns closed.

THE FACT. plan/variant-plan folds :substrates from the VARIANT body and its :extends chain only. It resolves the parent STORY for decorators and tags (plan.cljc's `sid` / `story-deco-lk` / `eff-tags`) and for nothing else — so a story-level :substrates never reaches [:world :substrates].

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is the same shape as rf2-3afns's:
  - the CANVAS honours a story-level declaration: canvas/variant-substrate-set calls multi-substrate/resolve-substrate-set, whose rule is (or variant-body story-body #{host}).
  - canonical/render-host-scope does NOT: it reads (get-in plan [:world :substrates]) and feeds it to single-render-substrate, which sees nothing declared and answers the :reagent host default.

So a story declaring :substrates #{:uix} (or #{:hicasso}) once, with variants that inherit it, paints correctly on the live canvas and renders under REAGENT through render-variant. rf2-3afns fixed the case where the declaration was on the variant; this is the same defect with the declaration one level up.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE, not inferred: a test asserting (= #{:hicasso} (get-in (plan/variant-plan child) [:world :substrates])) for a story-level declaration FAILS with nil (captured during rf2-2dbpd, JVM arm). The same assertion passes for a variant-level declaration and for an :extends-inherited one.

FIX SHAPE, for whoever takes it — one of:
  (a) fold the parent story's :substrates into the plan alongside the decorator/tag resolution that already reads it, which makes [:world :substrates] mean the same thing the canvas means; or
  (b) have render-host-scope read through the same resolve-substrate-set the canvas uses.
(a) is likely right: the plan is meant to be the single source of truth the canvas and render-variant both read, which is what rf2-3afns established. Note that :component has the SAME asymmetry (story-level :component does not reach [:world :component] either, and the renderers each fall back with their own (or variant story) read) — worth deciding whether to fix both together or to state plainly that the plan carries variant-scope only.

WITNESS TO ADD: the arm rf2-3afns built (tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/canvas_substrate_routing_cljs_test.cljs) distinguishes WHICH substrate rendered; a story-level-declaration row there would have caught this and does not exist.

FENCE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc, tools/story/src/re_frame/story/canonical.cljc, tools/story/test/**. Not hot zone.
close_reason:
PR 8370 merged as dbc22ef581. Five clauses verified at head 1a76a5f23cae: 100 contexts, 39 SUCCESS plus 61 SKIPPED, no non-terminal, no new job keys.

THE CAUSE, CONFIRMED AT SOURCE: plan.cljc compile-body resolved the parent story for DECORATORS AND TAGS ONLY, so [:world :substrates] was nil for a story-level declaration; canonical.cljc:139 then fell back to the :reagent host default while canvas.cljs:479 honoured the story. That is the split this bead reports.

*** IT MEASURED THE OPEN QUESTION THE BEAD FLAGGED RATHER THAN LEAVING IT. *** With a throwaway probe: render.cljc:253 reads [:world :component] with NO fallback of its own, so render-inputs :view was NIL for the normal authoring shape where the parent story carries the subject. Not cosmetic — render-variant painted nothing. So it fixed both, which is the fix-both-together branch this bead offered, and that is the only place the PR differs from the stated scope.

THE FIX IS SHAPE (a), a fold in compile-body mirroring resolve-substrate-set precedence exactly: seq variant chain, then seq story, then absent. sid hoisted and bound once; story-body bound once and reused by the tag fallback.

AND IT BOUNDED THE CHANGE RATHER THAN GENERALISING IT: :substrates and :component are the ONLY TWO context-keys with a [:world ...] reader anywhere in tools/story/src, so this is a two-slot fix, not a new inheritance rule. NO SPEC CHANGE — 001-Authoring.md:357 and schemas/VariantBody already documented story-level declaration as the variants default; the compiler simply had not implemented it. That is the code being wrong rather than the spec, established by reading both.

RED PROOF ON BOTH ARMS, defect planted back at all three call sites: JVM exit 1 with 8 failures of 10 tests; node exit 1 with 11 failures and 1 error, naming rows in BOTH new namespaces — which is also the proof the node lane DISCOVERS them rather than merely compiling them. title: [method] workers open PRs before they are done and the mayor merges them green — use draft PRs as the interlock
description:
THE MERGE LOOP AND THE DISPATCH BRIEF CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND THE MAYOR IS THE ONE WHO WROTE BOTH. Twice in one session a PR was merged while its author was still working on it.

THE TWO RULES, both of them mine, both individually right:
  DISPATCH BRIEF: "PUSH AS YOU GO, not at the end — pushed commits are the only durable worker state ... OPEN THE PR as soon as commits exist; a PR is not a claim of green."
  MERGE LOOP: merge on the five-clause criterion the moment it is met, and never block on CI.

Put together they say: workers publish PRs before they are finished, and the mayor merges them the moment CI goes green. **The gap between "CI is green" and "the author is done" is where both incidents happened.**

INCIDENT 1, 2026-08-15 ~11:55. #8323 merged while worker/hicaudit-5zmul was live. GitHub's delete_branch_on_merge removed its branch server-side; the worker's next push recreated it against a main that already carried its commits, producing DUPLICATE PR #8325 with a byte-identical three-file diff. Closed by hand after verifying the duplication rather than assuming it.

INCIDENT 2, 2026-08-16 ~01:33. #8333 merged while worker/w-lane-est was still running gates. Its own words: "#8333 — MERGED by the mayor while gates were still running; full gate table posted as a comment on it." It recovered well — cherry-picked the one wording fix the merge had not carried onto current main as #8339, and re-ran the doc gates on that branch — but that is a whole extra PR and an extra review cycle for work that would have ridden the first one.

NEITHER MERGE VIOLATED THE CRITERION. Both PRs were genuinely green on all five clauses when merged. The criterion is not the defect; the missing coordination is.

*** THE FIX, and it uses a mechanism that already exists rather than inventing a rule to remember. *** Brief workers to open the PR as a DRAFT and mark it ready for review as their last act before reporting done. `gh pr merge` REFUSES a draft, so the interlock is enforced by the host rather than by anyone's memory — which is the property the stash ban and the beads-boundary hook both have and the reason they hold. It preserves everything the push-as-you-go rule buys: commits are still pushed continuously and still survive a worker's death, and the mayor can still read the diff and the gate output at any time.

WHAT TO CHANGE:
  - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md — the push-as-you-go clause gains "open it as a DRAFT; mark it ready as your last act before reporting done."
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 1 — the merge criterion gains a line noting a draft PR is not a merge candidate, and WHY: the five clauses test the CHANGE, not whether its author has finished with it.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md — the same line, concretely: skip drafts in the sweep.

THE ALTERNATIVE, rejected: have the mayor check worker liveness before every merge. It works, but it is a rule that must be remembered on every merge forever, and it re-introduces exactly the worktree-activity sweep the merge loop deliberately does not do. The draft flag costs one command at the end of a worker's run and cannot be forgotten by the mayor at all.

SCOPE FENCE: those three files. HOT ZONE method surface — SOLE TOUCHER, never parallel with another method-file bead. Note rf2-4228y also targets loops.md; SEQUENCE the two, do not run them together.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus mkdocs build --strict, which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/. Run mkdocs as `python -m mkdocs` — bare `mkdocs` returns exit 127 in Git Bash on this box because it is not on PATH, and 127 is NO VERDICT, not a pass. No fenced code blocks added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched; say so in the PR body.
close_reason: Draft-PR interlock landed in all three files. dispatch-prompt-template.md gains a Publishing the change section (push continuously, publish as a draft, mark ready as the last act, rejected liveness-check alternative recorded), Shape 1 names the draft, failure-mode list gains its row; loops.md section 1 states a draft is not a merge candidate and why (the clauses test the CHANGE, not whether its author is finished); mayor-merge.md skips drafts in the sweep concretely via isDraft off gh pr list. PREMISE CORRECTION: the bead says the push-as-you-go clause GAINS the instruction, but that clause does not exist in the tracked template (grep -rn 'PUSH AS YOU GO' matches only .beads/issues.jsonl, a bd memory and this bead); the nearest text was Shape 1's 'push and open the change'. The clause was written, not amended. PR #8341.

title: [method] loops.md section 5 has no containment test — ancestry and ahead-count both fail under rebase-merge
description:
FOUND BY rf2-cyt80's WORKER, which declined to widen its own scope and flagged this instead — correctly. The mayor's bead text is the defect here, not the worker's reading of it.

WHAT HAPPENED. rf2-cyt80's drift 3 OBSERVED that "neither mayor-hygiene.md nor loops.md section 5 contains the words cherry, patch-id or patch-equivalent". Its FIX clause then named only mayor-hygiene.md. The worker implemented exactly what the fix clause said and reported the gap rather than quietly extending its fence. So the concrete command file now carries the containment test and THE GENERIC PUBLISHED METHOD STILL DOES NOT.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 5 ("Branches") says to delete merged branches and never one whose change is not verifiably merged. It says nothing about HOW to establish containment — and under rebase-merge the obvious test is wrong in both directions.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE GENERIC DOC SPECIFICALLY. loops.md is the method as published for other repositories, and rebase-merge is not a local quirk. A reader adopting the method there gets the rule and not the trap. Measured here on 2026-08-15 over 63 worktrees: 60 branches read "ahead of main by 1 to 3 commits" and 58 of them were FULLY MERGED, because a rebase gives every merged commit a new SHA so it never becomes an ancestor of the trunk. Deleting on ancestry would have kept all 58 forever; ignoring the reading would have destroyed worker/receipts-hic081's 3 genuinely unmerged spike commits. `git cherry <trunk> <branch>` settled both directions in one command — `-` means an equivalent patch is already upstream, `+` means genuinely new.

WHAT TO WRITE, keeping loops.md's register — GENERIC, no bd commands, no repo paths, no PowerShell, no bead ids:
  - ancestry and the ahead-count are both useless for containment when the project merges by rebase, and they fail in OPPOSITE directions;
  - the test is patch-equivalence (`git cherry`), which answers both directions at once;
  - the measured warrant, stated without repo-specific identifiers: 60 branches read ahead, 58 were merged, 1 was not, one command separated them.

Cross-reference rather than restate: loops.md section 4 and the command files already explain why the ahead count misleads for LIVENESS. This is the same trap on a different question — containment, not liveness — and saying so is cheaper and more durable than a second copy of the reasoning.

SCOPE FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md ONLY. mayor-hygiene.md already has its half from rf2-cyt80; do not touch it again. This is a hot-zone method file, so SOLE TOUCHER, never parallel with another method-file bead.

Note that bare `mkdocs` returns exit 127 in Git Bash on this box because it is not on PATH — 127 is NO VERDICT, not a pass; run it as `python -m mkdocs`. No fenced code blocks are added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched; say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.
