title: read_profile_app documents c-noactivate as the noise floor; it is a real term and must not be read as one
description:
FOUND BY rf2-3l6hf's measurement window (2026-08-16). This is the
INSTRUMENT-side half of rf2-19usn, and it is filed separately because it
misleads the reader of a published page rather than costing runtime.

THE CLAIM IN THE FILE. `read_profile_app.cljs`'s namespace docstring says
of the `c-noactivate` arm:

  "**`c-noactivate` should read at the noise floor ON THIS HOST, and that
  is the point of quoting it** (rf2-lzpfj). This app installs the UIx
  adapter, and `interop/activate-derived-value!` is a routed no-op on the
  React-hook spine -- ... the delta prices one cached hook lookup that
  misses, per key, and nothing else."

and the run prints the same expectation under the delta line: "routed
no-op on this UIx host -- expect the noise floor".

WHY IT IS WRONG. `late-bind/get-fn-cached` does NOT cache nil
resolutions -- its own docstring says so -- and
`:adapter/activate-derived-value!` is never published on the React-hook
spine. So the lookup is not cached, it is the one lookup that can never
be cached, and it runs in full 141 times per commit. Measured over three
`exit 0` runs at 32 frames/window:

  c-local - c-noactivate:  0.0406 / 0.0250 / 0.0406 ms/commit

against the terms it sits beside in the same table:

  watch wiring        0.0687 / 0.0563 / 0.0672
  cell-map insert     0.0375 / 0.0375 / 0.0469

The arm reads LARGER than the cell-map insert in two runs of three. An
arm documented as the noise floor, reading above a term the same table
asks you to believe, is a trap: it invites the reader to conclude the
window is failing when the window is working.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. rf2-07rnj is the phase-B re-decomposition and will
read this file. Left as is, the docstring tells it to treat ~0.04 as
noise -- which would condemn a window that in fact resolves two of the
three terms rf2-3l6hf was opened to recover.

THE REPAIR is a docstring and a printed line, not a measurement change:
say that on the React-hook spine the arm prices 141 UNCACHED double map
lookups, quote it as a real term, and name rf2-19usn as the reason it is
not zero. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE in rf2-3l6hf's own PR so that the three
published runs correspond byte-for-byte to the blob they were taken on.

A NOISE FLOOR IS STILL NEEDED and this bead does not invent one.
rf2-3l6hf used the arithmetic-impossibility residual instead: the
`c-noreaders` term must be positive and reads -0.0000 / -0.0062 /
-0.0000, so the floor is about +/-0.006 ms/commit. That is a measurement,
not a control, and a real negative control (an arm ablating nothing at
all) would be better if anyone wants one.
notes:

Do not replace that claim with rf2-3l6hf's arithmetic-impossibility residual as a calibrated ±0.006 floor. c-noreaders has an unknown positive true cost, so its negative estimate is not a zero-difference control and cannot establish a symmetric error band or the claimed <0.006 reader-membership bound. State that no measured null currently exists; coordinate any genuine null/control arm with reopened rf2-3l6hf, or leave reader membership explicitly unresolved.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8338 (branch worker/w-tcffa). Both premises verified at source before acting: late_bind.cljc's get-fn-cached memoises positive resolutions only ('Nil resolutions are NOT cached'), and :adapter/activate-derived-value! is routed by make-ratom-adapter alone (spine.cljs:3728) — never by make-react-adapter, which is what the UIx adapter builds through. The docstring states that no measured null exists on this instrument, that c-noreaders has an unknown positive true cost so its negative reading bounds nothing, and points a genuine negative control at rf2-3l6hf. Reader membership left explicitly unresolved. This now agrees with the ruling already published in the studio page, which the instrument had been contradicting.

Annotation only — no arm behaviour, no window shape, no sampling constant, no figure. The only non-docstring line in the diff is the printed string. Transcripts under data/readprofile-07rnj/ and their blob pin stand.

title: interop/activate-derived-value! pays an UNCACHED double lookup per cell on the React-hook spine
description:
FOUND BY rf2-3l6hf's measurement window (2026-08-16), and it is a
SHIPPING-CODE finding rather than an instrument one. Evidence is three
`exit 0` runs on a quiet box, phase B of `read_profile_app`.

THE MECHANISM. `re-frame.interop/activate-derived-value!` (interop.cljs
:115-119) is:

    (when-let [hook (late-bind/get-fn-cached :adapter/activate-derived-value!)]
      (hook derived))

and `late-bind/get-fn-cached` (late_bind.cljc:131-135) is:

    (or (get @fn-cache hook-key)
        (when-let [resolved (get @hooks hook-key)]
          (swap! fn-cache assoc hook-key resolved)
          resolved))

with its own docstring stating the rule: **"Nil resolutions are NOT
cached -- a deferred publication is visible on the next call."**

`:adapter/activate-derived-value!` is DELIBERATELY never published by the
React-hook spine -- `late_bind/directory.cljc:990` says so in terms
("NOT published by the React-hook spine (UIx / Helix / re-frame.ui /
Freehand) ... the routed chain-bottom returns nil and the port's call is
a no-op"). So on those hosts the key resolves to nil on EVERY call, the
memo never populates, and each call performs TWO atom derefs and TWO map
lookups. Permanently. The caching exists precisely to stop this and
cannot, because the case it cannot cache is the case that repeats.

WHAT IT COSTS. The observation port calls it once per cell at commit
(`substrate/observation.cljc:1982`). Phase B's `c-noactivate` arm ablates
exactly this call and nothing else, over a 141-key commit:

  c-local - c-noactivate:  0.0406 / 0.0250 / 0.0406 ms per 141-key commit

i.e. ~0.18-0.29 us per key, ~3-6% of the whole commit half, paid by every
UIx / Helix / re-frame.ui / Freehand app on every boundary commit, to
discover a hook that is documented as never existing on that host.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE. `read_profile_app`'s docstring asserts this arm
"prices one CACHED hook lookup that misses, per key, and nothing else"
and "should read at the noise floor ON THIS HOST". The word "cached" is
where it goes wrong: the miss is exactly what is not cached. Filed
separately as the instrument-side defect.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, not a ruling: cache the nil (costs the deferred-
publication property `get-fn-cached` documents, so it is a real
trade-off, not a free win); or give the spine a published no-op so the
memo populates once; or hoist the resolution out of the per-cell loop at
the observation-port call site. The third is local and keeps every
late-bind property intact.

NOT the mint, NOT the index, NOT anything rf2-dabt3 or rf2-lzpfj moved.
notes:
CROSS-CHECK, and it explains why this cost went unnoticed for so long.

rf2-d360z's own three run logs (still on the measurement box) record the
`c-noactivate` delta at the OLD 4-frame window as:

  -0.0375 / -0.0375 / +0.0250 ms/commit

Negative twice. The bead rf2-d360z filed (rf2-3l6hf) quoted four terms
and did NOT quote this one — so the single arm that prices this defect
was straddling zero, was never tabled, and read as nothing.

At rf2-3l6hf's 32-frame window the same arm reads:

  0.0406 / 0.0250 / 0.0406 ms/commit

positive on all three runs. **The cost did not appear; the instrument
started being able to see it.** It has presumably been paid on every
React-hook-spine commit since `interop/activate-derived-value!` was
routed there.

This also means the "expect the noise floor" annotation printed beside
the arm was never once contradicted by a reading, because until the
window widened the arm could not produce a reading that would contradict
anything. A term quoted only where it cannot be measured is not quoted.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8328 SCOPE CORRECTION (2026-08-16): the measured lookup cost is per wire-cell!/activation call, not “on every boundary commit”. In the shipping Hicasso collector, acquire-cell! calls wire-cell! only when !cells misses for a new unique key; stable later boundary commits reuse the durable cell and merely add reader membership. wire-cell! runs again when substrate invalidation rewires that cell. The observation port has its own acquisition path, but read_profile's c-local copy measured the Hicasso cold-cell path. Keep this optimization owner, but quantify frequency/aggregate impact against new or rewired cells and remove the every-commit claim before choosing a repair.
close_reason: REFUSED after quantification, as the bead's own ruling directed. Mechanism holds (uncached nil miss, late_bind.cljc:132-135 from interop.cljs:117) but the frequency claim is refuted at source: both call sites are cold path (collector.cljs:947 cells-map miss / :967 rewire; observation.cljc:2160 per acquire), never per commit. The '141 per commit' figure is the bench arm's own loop, not shipping. Host set re-derived at tip is ONE shipping adapter (UIx): Helix has no adapter in-tree, re-frame.ui + Freehand are 607 of open PR #8322's deletions. All three candidate repairs disqualified: caching nil breaks the deferred-publication property (documented in 3 places, maintained by invalidate-cache!); a spine no-op is forbidden by spec/006:209 ('Absence is the correct answer... not an omission to be diagnosed'); hoisting is not implementable (no loop at either call site). ~0.035 ms per cold mount does not buy any of that back. Full rationale in the 2026-08-16 11:48 comment. Residue filed as rf2-ml3kt.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MAYOR 2026-08-16 01:24 — I REPORTED THIS FINDING TO THE OPERATOR MORE STRONGLY THAN IT DESERVED, AND THE AUDIT OF #8328 CORRECTED IT. Recording so the overstatement does not survive in the record.

WHAT I SAID, in chat at 00:25: "once per cell, per commit, permanently" and "every boundary commit, every UIx/Helix/re-frame.ui/Freehand app". I took that from the filing worker's own summary and passed it on without checking the call path.

WHAT THE AUDIT ESTABLISHED: the measured lookup cost is per wire-cell!/activation call, NOT on every boundary commit. In the shipping Hicasso collector, acquire-cell! calls wire-cell! only when !cells MISSES for a new unique key. Stable later boundary commits reuse the durable cell and merely add reader membership. wire-cell! runs again when substrate invalidation rewires that cell. The observation port has its own acquisition path, and read_profile's c-local copy measured the Hicasso COLD-CELL path specifically.

SO THE MECHANISM IS REAL AND THE FREQUENCY IS NOT WHAT WAS CLAIMED. get-fn-cached still cannot cache a nil, :adapter/activate-derived-value! is still never published by the React-hook spine, and the memo still never populates on those hosts — that part stands and is worth fixing. What is refuted is the "every commit" multiplier, which is what made the number sound large.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE RETRACTED BOUND ON rf2-3l6hf, and it is the third time tonight: a worker's summarising sentence stated its evidence more strongly than the evidence carried, and I propagated it. The write-up clause now in dispatch-prompt-template.md (landed via rf2-cyt80, PR #8330) exists for exactly this, and the mayor-side half of it applies here — a number I repeat is a lean too.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DISPATCH: this bead is NOT ready for a repair worker. The audit's instruction is explicit — "quantify frequency/aggregate impact against new or rewired cells and remove the every-commit claim BEFORE choosing a repair." A worker sent to optimise it today would be optimising against a frequency nobody has measured, and could easily spend more than the defect costs. Quantify first, then decide whether a repair is worth it at the real frequency. It may well not be, and that is an acceptable outcome.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
WORKER 2026-08-16 11:48 AUSEST — QUANTIFIED AS THE RULING ASKED. THE MECHANISM IS
REAL; THE CASE FOR REPAIRING IT IS NOT. Recommending REFUSAL, with the numbers and
the source locations that decide it.

MECHANISM: HOLDS, with line drift. The uncached miss is real —
`late_bind.cljc:132-135` (bead said 131-135), reached from `interop.cljs:117`
(bead said 115-119; only the `when-let` line matters and it is 117 at tip). A key
no adapter publishes misses `@fn-cache` then `@hooks`: two derefs, two map misses.
That part of the bead stands exactly as written.

FREQUENCY: REFUTED AT SOURCE, confirming audit #8328. Both call sites are COLD
PATH, and there is no third.
  * `collector.cljs:947` (cells-map MISS, new unique key) and `:967` (post-
    invalidation rewire) are the only routes from `acquire-cell!` to
    `wire-cell!`; `:775` is the deferred-rewire microtask. A steady-state commit
    reaches `:968` — `.push` a reader — and nothing else.
  * `observation.cljc:2160` calls `build-node-handle!` once per `acquire!`, i.e.
    once per observation handle.
So: per new-or-rewired cell, per handle acquire. NEVER per commit.

WHERE THE "141 PER COMMIT" CAME FROM. It is a property of the BENCH ARM's own
loop, and `read_profile_app.cljs:126` says so in terms — "141 calls per boundary
commit IN THIS ARM'S OWN LOOP". `c-local` mints a fresh cell every iteration, so it
runs the cold path 141 times per window. Shipping code runs it 141 times ONCE, at
cold mount, then zero. Aggregate at the real frequency: ~141 x ~0.25us ~= 0.035 ms,
once per mount, against a path that in the same breath does a full `subs/subscribe`
(registrar lookup + reaction build + cache insert), a full `@reaction` compute, an
`add-watch`, and an `add-on-dispose!`.

HOST SET: RE-DERIVED AT TIP, AND IT IS ONE ADAPTER, NOT FOUR. The bead says "every
UIx / Helix / re-frame.ui / Freehand app".
  * Helix — NO SUCH ADAPTER EXISTS. `implementation/adapters/` is reagent,
    reagent-slim, test-react, uix; `find -iname "*helix*"` is empty. The name is
    stale prose in `directory.cljc:995`, not a host.
  * re-frame.ui and Freehand — retired and BEING DELETED. Open PR #8322
    (`worker/retire-final`) is 666 deletions / 56 modifications, of which 607
    deletions are under `implementation/ui/` and `implementation/freehand/`.
  * UIx — real, and the only SHIPPING host that pays this. Plus test-react
    (test-only) and plain-atom.
So the blast radius is one adapter on a cold path, and it shrinks by half the day
#8322 lands.

ALL THREE CANDIDATE REPAIRS ARE INDEPENDENTLY DISQUALIFIED.
  1. CACHE THE NIL — destroys the deferred-publication property, which is
     documented in three places and actively maintained by a fourth: the
     `fn-cache` comment (`late_bind.cljc:57-63`), `get-fn-cached`'s docstring
     (`:121-122`), `set-fn!`'s docstring (`:79-82`), and `invalidate-cache!`
     (`:65-72`). Adapters publish at ns load; call order against load order is not
     guaranteed. Latching a nil permanently disables activation for any call that
     lands first — a silent, once-only correctness failure of exactly the class
     rf2-phabt just repaired next door.
  2. PUBLISH A SPINE NO-OP — FORBIDDEN BY THE NORMATIVE SPEC. `spec/006:209`:
     "the React-hook spine, the plain-atom adapter, test-react and the JVM derived
     value publish nothing at all, and the routed call bottoms out as a no-op.
     ABSENCE IS THE CORRECT ANSWER for a host with no capture step to perform, NOT
     AN OMISSION TO BE DIAGNOSED." Publishing a no-op purely to populate a memo
     makes absence into a thing to be worked around. It would need a Spec 006
     change plus `directory.cljc` — which open PR #8322 already modifies — plus
     the drift test.
  3. HOIST OUT OF THE PER-CELL LOOP — NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS DESCRIBED. There is no
     loop at either call site; `wire-cell!` and `build-node-handle!` each call it
     ONCE. The only loop is `collector.cljs:1497` (`mapv acquire-cell! reads`),
     three frames above the lookup and inside the hicasso tree. Hoisting from
     there means threading a pre-resolved late-bind hook through `acquire-cell!`
     -> `wire-cell!` -> the public `interop/activate-derived-value!` signature,
     which inverts the entire point of the late-bind port. The bead called this one
     "local and keeps every late-bind property intact"; it is neither.

AND THE CLARITY ARGUMENT, WHICH OUTLASTS THE PERF ONE.
`activate-derived-value!` is one of ~8 sibling ports in `interop.cljs` that all
share the identical `(when-let [hook (get-fn-cached k)] (hook ...))` shape —
`add-on-dispose!` (:123), `dispose!` (:129), `reactive?` (:135). `add-on-dispose!`
is called on the NEXT LINE of `wire-cell!` (`collector.cljs:693`) with the same
profile on hosts that do not publish it. Making one of eight bespoke to save
0.25us on a cold path trades a uniform, readable port table for a special case.

SHIPPING DOCS NEED NO CORRECTION — THEY NEVER MADE THE CLAIM. `interop.cljs`
says activation happens "at observation-port ACQUIRE TIME, not at construction";
`directory.cljc:995` says "before installing its PER-HANDLE watch". Both accurate.
The "every boundary commit" overstatement was created in the measurement write-up
and the bead, never in the code. Nothing in the shipping tree needs editing, which
is why this lands as a comment and not a PR.

NOT ACTIONED, DELIBERATELY: `get-fn-cached` has a benign TOCTOU (read `@hooks`,
then `swap!` into `fn-cache`, racing a concurrent `set-fn!` + `invalidate-cache!`
-> a stale fn cached). CLJS is single-threaded and JVM hooks publish at boot, so
it cannot bite today. Recording it rather than fixing it; manufacturing that work
would be the over-engineering this bead is already an argument against.

RESIDUE FILED SEPARATELY: `read_profile_app.cljs:127` still reads "rf2-19usn
carries that cost where it is paid in shipping code", which will keep propagating
the every-commit framing into the next measurement write-up. That file is the live
bench lane and not mine to edit — filed as its own bead.

RECOMMENDATION: CLOSE as won't-fix. The mechanism is genuine and the write-up of it
was not; at the real frequency, on the one real host, every available repair costs
more in correctness, spec surface or clarity than the ~0.035 ms per cold mount it
would buy back.

title: hicasso: the-cold-read-mount-term's commit-half decomposition needs a whole re-take, not a two-cell restatement
description:
FOUND BY rf2-d360z's measurement window (2026-08-15). rf2-d360z was scoped to
re-take two absolutes and restate the share columns, on rf2-gttif's finding
that only rf2-aqgr2's keyword mint had moved under the table. THAT PREMISE IS
INCOMPLETE. Two further changes have landed under the same table, both AFTER
rf2-gttif and rf2-d360z were written on 2026-08-03, and neither is accounted
for anywhere on the page. Verified by reading the tree, not inferred:

1. rf2-dabt3 (383ba2d645, authored 2026-08-03 20:51) RETIRED THE SUB-INDEX
   INTO THE CELL TABLE. front/sub_index.cljs is DELETED. The shipping commit
   half no longer performs an index/mount! plus a whole-set record-reads!; it
   pushes one reader slot per key ((.push (.-readers cell) reg)). The same
   commit replaced read_profile_app.cljs's c-noindex arm with c-noreaders.

   CONSEQUENCE: the-cold-read-mount-term.md section 1 publishes
   '| - index write (c-local - c-noindex) | 0.0750 | 8.7% |'
   which PRICES A STRUCTURE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS, through an arm that no
   longer exists. Section 4 quotes the same term as its 5.6% share.

2. rf2-lzpfj (04bb0fa73a) ADDED interop/activate-derived-value! to
   commit-local! so the copy matches wire-cell!'s shape. c-local now performs
   work it was NOT performing when the published 0.8625 denominator was taken.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE FIXED BY RE-MEASURING TWO CELLS. Every share in that table
divides by c-local. c-local has since LOST the index write, LOST the mint, and
GAINED the activation, so it is not the arm that produced 0.8625. Dividing
2026-08-02 numerators by a 2026-08-15 denominator is arithmetic across two
instruments -- the precise thing this page's discipline exists to prevent. The
share column therefore cannot be repaired by re-taking its denominator, which
is why rf2-d360z declined to restate it and marked the row instead.

WHAT IS OWED: a single phase-B run that takes EVERY arm at ONE commit and
republishes the whole commit-half decomposition -- absolutes, deltas and
shares together -- with the c-noindex row retired and c-noreaders in its place.

BLOCKED BY rf2-3l6hf. Phase B currently cannot resolve three of the four terms
that must be positive (they read negative on at least one run of three), so a
re-decomposition taken today would publish noise. Fix the window first.

SCOPE NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: this is a clock estimand, so it needs the
quiet box and Shape 6 in full. rf2-d360z's window measured the dispersion that
makes this bead necessary: the commit arm moved 0.4500-0.5500 across three
runs of one binary in one session, four grid steps, nothing changing between
them.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8327 COMPLETENESS (2026-08-16): this existing whole-re-take owner must also sweep the live narrative derived from the retired sub-index; no duplicate Bead was created. In docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md, the “Reading it” conclusion still states that the index write is 8.7% and that batching it was declined. In docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-in-page-mount-term-decomposed.md, the conclusion still proposes batching the index write. Both read as current even though rf2-dabt3 deleted that structure. Retire or qualify those statements when this decomposition is republished.

Evidence caveat: this Bead's “nothing changing between them” wording is stronger than the window record. Queue length was 0 on 82/85 samples; two non-zero samples may have overlapped run 3. Preserve the re-take requirement, but do not attribute all observed dispersion solely to the instrument.
rf2-3l6hf's measurement window has run (2026-08-16, blob e1701c41af, PR
#8328). THE BLOCKER IS PARTIALLY LIFTED, and the part that is not lifted
is now bounded rather than unknown.

THE WINDOW. 4 frames -> 32 frames/window, 24 -> 64 samples. Grid falls
0.0125 -> 0.0015625 ms/commit. Three runs, exit 0, positive control
passing on each, residue gate never firing.

WHAT YOU CAN NOW DECOMPOSE (three runs, one sign each):

  reaction build + cache insert   0.4734 / 0.5016 / 0.4578
  watch wiring                    0.0687 / 0.0563 / 0.0672   <- recovered
  cell-map insert                 0.0375 / 0.0375 / 0.0469   <- recovered

WHAT YOU STILL CANNOT, AND ITS BOUND:

  reader membership              -0.0000 / -0.0062 / -0.0000

Still at or below zero at 8x the resolution. Its floor is measured by
arithmetic impossibility (the term must be positive), giving the
instrument a floor of about +/-0.006 ms/commit. So quote the fused
reverse edge as **< 0.006 ms/commit, under 1% of the commit half** — a
bound, not a figure. Do not quote a number for it.

TWO THINGS THAT WILL BITE YOU IF YOU DO NOT READ THEM FIRST.

1. **`c-noactivate` is NOT the noise floor the file says it is** — see
   rf2-tcffa, and rf2-19usn for the shipping cost behind it. It reads
   0.0406 / 0.0250 / 0.0406, LARGER than the cell-map insert in two runs
   of three, because `get-fn-cached` cannot cache a nil resolution and
   the React-hook spine never publishes that hook. If you read it as
   noise you will wrongly condemn a window that works. It is a real term
   and belongs in the decomposition as one.

2. **The shares are NOT window-size-invariant.** Reaction build is 56% of
   `c-local` at 4 frames, 62% at 4 frames on a same-day control run, and
   66.9-68.4% at 32 frames. Take every arm at ONE window shape and STATE
   the shape beside the table. Shares from different shapes do not
   compose, which is the same class of error the page's discipline
   already forbids across commits.

NOT CONCLUDED, and left to you or to a later window: whether ~128-256
frames would bring reader membership clear. The floor fell by about the
factor the window widened (0.04-0.05 -> 0.006 for 8x), which suggests it
is still window-limited rather than dispersion-limited, so a further
4-8x is the estimate. That is a PREDICTION from two floor readings, not
a measurement, and it was deliberately not attempted mid-window.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8328 CORRECTION (2026-08-16): supersedes this Bead's instruction to quote reader membership as “< 0.006 ms/commit, under 1%”. The c-noreaders arm removes real work with unknown positive cost; observing -0.0062 does not calibrate a symmetric ±0.0062 floor and cannot upper-bound the true cost. The old/new “floor scaled 8x” comparison also selects different positive-cost arms. Treat reader membership as unresolved, not bounded, and remain blocked by reopened rf2-3l6hf until a genuine null/control or valid direct bound exists. The recovered watch-wiring and cell-map observations remain useful.
MEASUREMENT WINDOW RUN 2026-08-16, PR #8329, commit a43aa8609f, instrument
blob 6d2b67b5b0. THE RE-TAKE RAN AND DECLINES TO PUBLISH. Bead stays OPEN
and BLOCKED.

THE WINDOW SHAPE, chosen once before the first run and held for every arm
of every run: 32 frames/window, 8x(2+8) = 64 kept samples per arm, grid
0.0015625 ms/commit — rf2-3l6hf's widened shape exactly as it landed. No
gate, tolerance or knob moved; instrument blob identical before and after.
Three runs, exit 0 each, both arm-order guards reportable on every run,
phase-A positive control passing on every run, phase-B residue gate never
firing. Every arm of a run taken in ONE process, interleaved.

ARMS (ms per 141-key commit, p50):

  arm             run 1     run 2     run 3
  commit          0.6953    0.7516    0.7203
  c-local         0.6594    0.6969    0.6875
  c-noactivate    0.6172    0.6484    0.6313
  c-nowatch       0.5875    0.6313    0.6094
  c-nosub         0.2156    0.2250    0.2188
  c-noreaders     0.6547    0.7109    0.6750
  c-nomap         0.6156    0.6703    0.6375
  b-build         0.4938    0.5688    0.5406
  c-local/commit  0.9483    0.9272    0.9544

TERMS (c-local minus arm):

  reaction build + cache insert   0.4437 / 0.4719 / 0.4688
  watch wiring                    0.0719 / 0.0656 / 0.0781
  activation capture              0.0422 / 0.0484 / 0.0562
  cell-map insert                 0.0437 / 0.0266 / 0.0500
  reader membership              +0.0047 / -0.0141 / +0.0125   <- STRADDLES ZERO

WHY IT DOES NOT PUBLISH. Four of five terms resolve with one sign on every
run. Reader membership does not: it straddles zero across three runs of one
binary in one session, and a negative delta is arithmetically impossible
when c-noreaders does strictly less work than c-local. A decomposition that
cannot see one of its terms is not one — this bead's own founding argument,
now applied to its own re-take. Nothing in section 1's table or section 4
is restated, and NO SHARE IS COMPUTED.

THE "< 0.006 ms/commit" BOUND IS WITHDRAWN, NOT PUBLISHED, on two
independent grounds. (1) A most-negative reading cannot bound a positive
quantity: if an observed delta is an unknown positive cost plus estimator
error, -0.0062 shows only that one negative excursion exceeded 0.0062 PLUS
that cost; it neither calibrates a symmetric floor nor caps the cost, and
comparing most-negative readings at two window widths cannot demonstrate an
8x floor scaling. (2) Run 2 read -0.0141 on this box — more than twice the
figure that was to be published. Agrees with the merged-PR audit of #8328.
THE WINDOW WAS NOT WIDENED to chase the term: whether 128-256 frames would
recover it is a prediction, not a measurement, and a rung added between runs
makes the series two instruments.

MAYOR 2026-08-16 00:35 — I PROPAGATED A REFUTED BOUND INTO A LIVE WORKER'S BRIEF, AND THE AUDIT CAUGHT IT BEFORE THE WORKER PUBLISHED. Recording the error and the correction.

WHAT I DID. rf2-3l6hf's window recovered two of three terms and reported the third, reader membership, as "bounded: < 0.006 ms/commit, under 1% of the commit half". I read that as a finding, wrote it into rf2-07rnj's dispatch brief as guidance — "quote the BOUND, not a figure ... Publish that bound" — and reported it to the operator the same way.

WHY IT IS WRONG, per the merged-PR audit of #8328, whose reasoning I have checked and accept. Let an observed delta y equal an unknown positive true cost t plus estimator error e. A reading of y = -0.0062 proves only that the negative error excursion exceeded 0.0062 + t. It does NOT establish that +/-0.0062 is a calibrated, symmetric floor, and it CANNOT upper-bound t. A most-negative observation is a statement about the error term, not about the quantity.

THE SECOND HALF, same shape: comparing the most-negative readings from DIFFERENT positive-cost arms at 4 frames and 32 frames cannot prove an 8x floor scaling. Two error excursions from two different arms are not two measurements of one floor.

SO READER MEMBERSHIP IS UNRESOLVED, NOT BOUNDED, until a genuine null/control arm exists or another valid bound is derived. And rf2-07rnj stays BLOCKED: rf2-3l6hf owned resolving the decomposition, one of its original terms still does not resolve, and a decomposition with an unresolved term is not one - which is rf2-07rnj's own founding argument turned on itself.

*** THE GENERAL RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO CARRY. *** An impossible reading tells you the instrument's error reached at least that far. It does not calibrate the error, and it does not bound the thing being measured. Treating "the worst negative I saw" as "the floor" is the same move as treating "no test failed" as "the code is correct" - it converts an absence into a guarantee. Whenever a worker reports a bound derived from readings that should have been positive, ASK WHAT NULL ARM PRODUCED IT. If the answer is "the impossible readings themselves", it is not a bound.

HOW IT REACHED A WORKER, and this is the process failure rather than the arithmetic one. The premises-are-claims sentence was in rf2-07rnj's brief, and it did not protect against this, because I passed the bound as GUIDANCE ("publish that bound") rather than as a premise to check. That is exactly the failure mode docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md already names for a LEAN: a worker reads guidance as instruction and a premise as a claim, so anything phrased as guidance bypasses the check. A NUMBER I ASSERT IS A LEAN TOO. Demand the evidence that produced it before writing it into a brief - here, one question would have caught it: what null arm produced that bound?

RECOVERY: the live worker was messaged the moment the audit was read, before it published. It was told to keep every measurement it had taken, publish no bound, not chase the term by widening the window, report, and leave rf2-07rnj open and blocked.

title: hicasso: read_profile phase B cannot resolve reader membership — it reads at the null
description:
FOUND BY rf2-d360z's measurement window (2026-08-15, 2c95c22386), three runs on a certified-quiet box (Processor Queue Length 0 across every measurement sample), exit 0 and all controls clean on each.

THE SYMPTOM. Phase B's ablation deltas straddle zero across runs:

  cell-map insert   (c-local - c-nomap)      0.1125 / 0.0250 / -0.0500
  watch wiring      (c-local - c-nowatch)   -0.0125 / +0.0375 /  0.0000
  reader membership (c-local - c-noreaders) -0.0375 / -0.0375 / +0.0250
  reaction build    (c-local - c-nosub)      0.2875 /  0.2250 /  0.2500

A NEGATIVE DELTA IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE. Every c-* arm does strictly
less work than c-local, so a negative reading is the instrument reporting a
term below its own floor, not a real saving. Three of the four terms that must
be positive are there. Only the reaction build + cache insert resolves.

WHY. Phase B's window is 4 frames x 141 acquisitions against a raw 0.1 ms
clock, giving a 0.025 ms/commit grid; b-sampling is 4 rounds x (2 warmup + 6
samples) = 24 samples. The absolute itself moved 0.4500-0.5500 across three
runs of ONE binary in ONE session with nothing changing between them, so the
run-to-run dispersion of the arm (0.100 ms, four grid steps) is larger than
three of the terms it is asked to decompose.

WHAT IS LIKELY NEEDED, stated as candidates and not as a ruling: more frames
per window (the window is deliberately sized to clear the 100 us clock clamp,
not to resolve a 0.025 ms term), and/or more samples per arm. Whoever takes it
must treat this as its own measurement window under Shape 6 -- a rung added to
an instrument mid-run makes the series two instruments, which is exactly why
rf2-d360z filed this rather than widening the window itself.

DO NOT widen a gate or a tolerance to make the terms come out positive. The
negative readings are the instrument being honest.

BLOCKS the full phase-B re-decomposition, because a decomposition taken on a
window that cannot see three of its terms is not one.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8327 CORRECTION (2026-08-16): the opening premise “Processor Queue Length 0 across every measurement sample” is superseded by the landed PR. The window sampled 85 times; 82 were 0, and readings 1, 1, and 2 were retained. Two non-zero readings cannot be proven outside run 3's measurement phase. The negative ablation deltas still show that this window cannot resolve three terms, so this Bead's work and priority stand; do not use the all-zero claim or attribute the 0.100 ms spread solely to the instrument.
MEASUREMENT WINDOW RUN 2026-08-16, PR #8328, commit e1701c41af,
instrument blob 6d2b67b5b0. Four runs, all exit 0, positive control
passing on each, residue gate never firing.

THE WINDOW SHAPE, chosen once and held: 4 -> 32 frames/window, 24 -> 64
samples (8x(2+8)). No gate and no tolerance moved.

WHY FRAMES AND NOT SAMPLES. The bead's "and/or" hides that the two knobs
do different jobs. `lane/summarise` takes the MEAN OF THE TWO MIDDLE
order statistics on an even sample count, halving the 0.1 ms clamp to
0.05 ms, and the row divides by the frame count -- so a delta can only
land on a `0.05/frames` grid, which at 4 frames is 0.0125 and is exactly
the spacing every delta this bead quotes is a multiple of. A median of
quantised readings is itself a grid value whatever the sample count, so
MORE SAMPLES COULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT. Frames are resolution; samples are
stability. Both moved; the code now says which is which.

RESULT.

  term                  4 frames (3 runs)          32 frames (3 runs)
  reaction build        0.2875/0.2250/0.2500       0.4734/0.5016/0.4578
  watch wiring         -0.0125/+0.0375/ 0.0000     0.0687/0.0563/0.0672  RECOVERED
  cell-map insert       0.1125/ 0.0250/-0.0500     0.0375/0.0375/0.0469  RECOVERED
  c-noactivate         -0.0375/-0.0375/+0.0250     0.0406/0.0250/0.0406  RECOVERED
  reader membership    -0.0375/-0.0375/+0.0250    -0.0000/-0.0062/-0.0000  NOT RECOVERED

**FOUR terms were unresolvable at 4 frames, not three.** The
`c-noactivate` row is recovered from rf2-d360z's own run logs, still on
the box; this bead's description never quoted that arm, and it was
straddling zero exactly like the others.

THE ONE THAT DID NOT COME BACK is now BOUNDED rather than unknown. The
floor, measured by arithmetic impossibility (a term that must be positive
reading negative measures precisely that), is about +/-0.006 ms/commit.
So the fused reverse edge is < 0.006 ms/commit, under 1% of the commit
half. rf2-07rnj should quote a BOUND there, not a figure -- noted on it.

THE FLOOR SCALED WITH THE WINDOW: ~0.05 at 4 frames, 0.0062 at 32, an 8x
fall for an 8x widening. That is a floor still set by the window rather
than by irreducible dispersion, so a further 4-8x (128-256 frames) is the
estimate for reader membership. PREDICTION, not measurement, and
deliberately not attempted -- a rung added between runs makes the series
two instruments.

TWO FINDINGS FILED RATHER THAN ACTIONED HERE:
  rf2-19usn -- `interop/activate-derived-value!` pays an UNCACHED double
    map lookup per cell on the React-hook spine, ~0.18-0.29 us/key on
    every boundary commit, because `get-fn-cached` cannot cache a nil and
    that hook is never published there. A shipping-code cost.
  rf2-tcffa -- the instrument documents `c-noactivate` as reading the
    noise floor. It does not; it reads larger than the cell-map insert in
    two runs of three. Left uncorrected ON PURPOSE so the published runs
    match their blob byte-for-byte.

ALSO NOT CONCLUDED: whether the shares are window-size-invariant. The
reaction-build share is 52.9-59.0% at 4 frames (rf2-d360z), 62.0% at 4
frames on a same-session control, and 66.9-68.4% at 32. Suggestive that
it moves with the window; run order and thermal drift are not excluded.
Either way a decomposition must take every arm at ONE shape and state it.

BOX: 109 PQL samples, 100 zero. Nine non-zero, all quoted in the PR. The
two big ones (18, 82) are the shadow-cljs `:advanced` compile, which
saturates this box and which `run.cjs` performs unconditionally on every
run -- worth knowing for whoever measures here next. Exactly one non-zero
(a 1) lands inside a measurement phase, in S1.

I did NOT repeat this description's claim that the founding runs were on
a box reading 0 across every measurement sample; its author withdrew that
sentence on the published page. I relied on the corrected version in
PR #8327.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8328 (2026-08-16): reopened this exact owner; no duplicate Bead created.

CORRECTNESS — the 32-frame window genuinely recovers the watch-wiring and cell-map terms, but the reader-membership result is not bounded by <0.006 ms/commit. If an observed delta y equals an unknown positive true cost t plus estimator error e, y = -0.0062 only proves that the negative error excursion exceeded 0.0062 + t; it does not make ±0.0062 a calibrated, symmetric floor and cannot upper-bound t. Comparing the most-negative readings from different positive-cost arms at 4 and 32 frames likewise cannot prove an 8x floor scaling. The published reader-membership estimates remain unresolved until a genuine null/control arm or another valid bound exists.

COMPLETENESS — this Bead owned resolution of the decomposition and one of its original terms still does not resolve. Retract the bound guidance copied into rf2-07rnj and keep that downstream re-decomposition blocked. Existing rf2-tcffa owns the false c-noactivate-arbiter documentation.

But the source claims the frame count sets resolution “here and nowhere else” while b-rounds/b-sampling are separate and no contract preserves even parity; an odd kept total would restore a 0.1/frames grid while the design line still prints 0.05/frames. Derive or assert the parity-dependent grid, add the narrow regression witness, and update the stale “phase B setup: four identically-seeded frames” comment.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8329 (2026-08-16): the full re-take independently confirms this exact owner remains open. At the unchanged 32-frame / 64-kept-sample shape and instrument blob 6d2b67b5b0, reader membership read +0.0047 / -0.0141 / +0.0125 across three cleanly completed runs. It still straddles zero, and the -0.0141 excursion further disproves the superseded “<0.006 ms/commit” guidance; no bound is published. The other four ablation terms are positive on all three runs, so no duplicate instrument-resolution Bead is warranted. Continue to require a genuine null/control or other valid resolution/bound, alongside the already-owned parity-dependent grid and stale-instrument-prose repairs.

MAYOR 2026-08-16 00:35 — I PROPAGATED A REFUTED BOUND INTO A LIVE WORKER'S BRIEF, AND THE AUDIT CAUGHT IT BEFORE THE WORKER PUBLISHED. Recording the error and the correction.

WHAT I DID. rf2-3l6hf's window recovered two of three terms and reported the third, reader membership, as "bounded: < 0.006 ms/commit, under 1% of the commit half". I read that as a finding, wrote it into rf2-07rnj's dispatch brief as guidance — "quote the BOUND, not a figure ... Publish that bound" — and reported it to the operator the same way.

WHY IT IS WRONG, per the merged-PR audit of #8328, whose reasoning I have checked and accept. Let an observed delta y equal an unknown positive true cost t plus estimator error e. A reading of y = -0.0062 proves only that the negative error excursion exceeded 0.0062 + t. It does NOT establish that +/-0.0062 is a calibrated, symmetric floor, and it CANNOT upper-bound t. A most-negative observation is a statement about the error term, not about the quantity.

THE SECOND HALF, same shape: comparing the most-negative readings from DIFFERENT positive-cost arms at 4 frames and 32 frames cannot prove an 8x floor scaling. Two error excursions from two different arms are not two measurements of one floor.

SO READER MEMBERSHIP IS UNRESOLVED, NOT BOUNDED, until a genuine null/control arm exists or another valid bound is derived. And rf2-07rnj stays BLOCKED: rf2-3l6hf owned resolving the decomposition, one of its original terms still does not resolve, and a decomposition with an unresolved term is not one - which is rf2-07rnj's own founding argument turned on itself.

*** THE GENERAL RULE, WHICH IS THE PART TO CARRY. *** An impossible reading tells you the instrument's error reached at least that far. It does not calibrate the error, and it does not bound the thing being measured. Treating "the worst negative I saw" as "the floor" is the same move as treating "no test failed" as "the code is correct" - it converts an absence into a guarantee. Whenever a worker reports a bound derived from readings that should have been positive, ASK WHAT NULL ARM PRODUCED IT. If the answer is "the impossible readings themselves", it is not a bound.

HOW IT REACHED A WORKER, and this is the process failure rather than the arithmetic one. The premises-are-claims sentence was in rf2-07rnj's brief, and it did not protect against this, because I passed the bound as GUIDANCE ("publish that bound") rather than as a premise to check. That is exactly the failure mode docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md already names for a LEAN: a worker reads guidance as instruction and a premise as a claim, so anything phrased as guidance bypasses the check. A NUMBER I ASSERT IS A LEAN TOO. Demand the evidence that produced it before writing it into a brief - here, one question would have caught it: what null arm produced that bound?

RECOVERY: the live worker was messaged the moment the audit was read, before it published. It was told to keep every measurement it had taken, publish no bound, not chase the term by widening the window, report, and leave rf2-07rnj open and blocked.

h/defview (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:221-240) already computes view-name "<ns>/<sym>" (:224) and a source coord (:225), hands both to collector/mint-view!, and registers nothing. title: check_guide_samples R2 pools aliases globally, so a code block missing its own :require still resolves
description:
FOUND BY rf2-h3tke / rf2-hic-060 (PR #8316) while repairing two 'the guide teaches something untrue' defects. FILED, NOT FIXED: fixing R2 is a gate change, not a docs change, and neither bead's fence covered it.

THE FINDING. implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py's guide_aliases() builds ONE alias map for the WHOLE guide:

    def guide_aliases(pages): 
        out = {}
        for text in pages.values():
            for ns, alias in _REQUIRE_RE.findall(text):
                out[alias] = ns
        return out

Every page's :require forms are folded into a single {alias: namespace} dict, and qualified_uses() then resolves every block against it. So a code block whose OWN ns form omits a require still resolves, as long as ANY page anywhere in the guide declares that alias.

WHAT IT LET THROUGH. cookbook.md's 'A draft the user can abandon' recipe (then L170-183) declared no re-frame.core, while the rf/reg-event block four paragraphs later in the SAME recipe used rf/. R2 was green throughout, because other guide pages declare [re-frame.core :as rf]. A real shadow-cljs compile reported 'Use of undeclared Var rf/reg-event' immediately. Same class hid the missing [re-frame.hicasso.server :as server] on the SSR determinism block.

THE SECOND HALF, and it is by design rather than a bug. Auto-resolved KEYWORDS are invisible to R2 — its own self-test asserts it: check("an auto-resolved KEYWORD is not a var use", ...). That is correct for what R2 is for (resolving hicasso VERBS), but it means a block using ::subs/row-count with no subs alias is unseen. cookbook.md L297-316 was exactly that and was a HARD ClojureScript READER failure ('Invalid keyword: ::subs/row-count') — a recipe that could never have compiled, sitting green behind R1 and R2 for as long as it had been printed. The same blind spot is why ch08 could teach a ':demand true' OPTION that nothing implements (rf2-h3tke): ':demand' is a keyword inside a map.

WHY IT MATTERS. R1 pins bytes, so it certifies 'nobody edited this', not 'this is true'. R2 is the only rule that reads meaning, and its alias pooling makes it structurally unable to catch a per-block require gap. The cookbook's own promise is that each recipe is 'a whole thing you can copy into an application', which is precisely the property R2 cannot currently check.

REPAIR SHAPE (not prescriptive). Resolve aliases PER BLOCK-GROUP rather than per guide: a block that opens with an (ns …) form establishes the alias scope for itself and for the ns-less blocks that follow it in the same section; only then does an unresolved alias mean something. Consider whether it is cheaper to lint the auto-resolved-keyword case the same way, since that is where the two worst instances landed. Note the guide legitimately contains ns-less continuation blocks, so the rule has to inherit scope rather than demand an ns form per block.

WORTH WEIGHING FIRST: whether this is better served by actually COMPILING the guide's blocks in CI rather than by growing the static checker. The harness that found all of this was ~60 lines of extraction plus a scratch shadow-cljs project with stub namespaces for the imaginary my.app.* aliases, and it is strictly stronger than any alias analysis — it catches reader errors, undeclared vars and missing requires in one pass. It is also slower and needs stubs maintained. An operator call, not a worker's.

title: hicasso test kit answers :assert-it-at-l3 for a runtime-owned refusal
description:
FOUND BY rf2-5zmul's R10 on its first run -- the new runtime-anchor arm of check_complaint_catalogue.py. It is a TRUE POSITIVE and the reason that PR is red; do NOT green the PR by weakening R10.

THE SITE. implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs, the :foreign arm of the L2 walk (around line 1057):

    :foreign
    (if (delay? x)
      (refuse-opaque! :rf.error/hicasso-deferred-read-at-boundary ...)
      (refuse! :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed ... :fix-the-child ...))

refuse-opaque! hardcodes the recovery :assert-it-at-l3. So the kit reuses the RUNTIME's id and answers with the kit's own opacity recovery, while Spec 009 rows that id :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body.

WHY IT IS WRONG, BY THE KIT'S OWN STATED RULE. The same namespace's docstring says: 'A form the runtime REFUSES is refused here with the runtime's own id ... each carrying the runtime's recovery rather than one of this namespace's.' It also records that a previous audit found exactly this class -- '[:> :div] answered :assert-it-at-l3, which tells the programmer to mount, in a browser, a form that will not mount anywhere.' An unforced delay at a boundary crossing is refused by the runtime too, so :assert-it-at-l3 sends the programmer to L3 where the same refusal is waiting.

The sibling arms of the very same case expression already do it correctly: :true-child uses refuse! with the runtime's :use-nil-or-false, and the non-delay :foreign arm uses refuse! with :fix-the-child. Only the delay arm forwards to refuse-opaque!.

THE FIX (one call, and it is the emit fence's, not the gate's): use refuse! with :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body, matching the sibling arms.

THE ALTERNATIVE, if a sitting decides the kit is right: add :assert-it-at-l3 to that id's Spec 009 Hicasso row. Then R9 also needs the troubleshooting index checked. The kit's own docstring argues against this reading.

BLOCKS: the rf2-5zmul PR (worker/catgate-5zmul) cannot go green until one of these lands. No existing gate could see this -- R1-R9 are document-to-document.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8318 (merged 2026-08-15T10:15:54Z as 961f865798) — REOPEN THIS EXACT OWNER; do not file a duplicate.

WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: the :foreign delay arm now calls refuse! with :rf.error/hicasso-deferred-read-at-boundary and :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body. That matches the runtime guard, Spec 009, troubleshooting, and the namespace-level rule; refuse! merges identity over payload correctly. All five PR-head workflow families passed. The absent recovery-parity row is already owned precisely by open rf2-tsdik; do not duplicate it.

COMPLETENESS / CORRECTNESS MISS IN THE SAME FILE: implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs:1201-1202, inside the public tree function docstring, still lists “an unforced delay” with defhost/raw React among forms that are “opaque, with a pointer to L3.” That is the exact recovery this PR removed, and now contradicts both the namespace docstring at 176-183 and the implementation at 1059-1074.

REPAIR: remove the delay from that opacity bullet and state its runtime-owned id/recovery alongside the function’s refusal summary, using the same compact distinction already written at the namespace top. Keep rf2-tsdik open until the parity table asserts both id and recovery.

QUALITY: this is a local docstring consistency repair, not a request for another abstraction or gate.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8318, MERGED, and verified ON LANDED MAIN rather than on the PR's say-so: the :foreign/delay arm of implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs now carries the runtime's own :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body (2 occurrences), and grepping the delay arm for :assert-it-at-l3 returns 0. FOUND BY R10 ON ITS VERY FIRST RUN, as a true positive. The kit was violating a rule its own docstring states as law: 'A form the runtime REFUSES is refused here with the runtime's own id ... Opacity is a claim about a form L2 cannot read, and it is honest only where the runtime CAN read it.' The runtime does refuse an unforced delay, and Spec 009 separately pins that the kit raises the runtime's id rather than a kit-private twin — so the rule was unambiguous and no ruling was needed. ONE CALL, plus one docstring sentence in the same file that the fix falsified. refuse-opaque! keeps its four other call sites; no runtime, Spec 009 or gate file was touched. THE SEQUENCING WORKED AS DESIGNED. PR #8315 sat DELIBERATELY RED on this, with 'do not green it by weakening R10' as its first line. This fix landed, #8315 rebased, and its catalogue red cleared ON ITS OWN — no exemption, no rule change. Its author verified R10 was not blunted afterwards by planting a rename and confirming it still reds. A worker that finds a real bug with its own new rule, refuses to blunt the rule for a green tick, files the bug outside its fence and links it as blocking is the behaviour to reward. Its author also filed rf2-tsdik: the runtime-parity table has a row for every other member of this class but none for the unforced delay, which is why a DOCUMENT gate caught this instead of a test.

title: [story] A synthetic DOM event's async dispatch has no settle rung — the play runner still needs [:wait ms] after a :click
description:
MEASURED while landing rf2-ek9qb (PR #8313, 2026-08-15) by trying to delete the sleeps and watching the browser lane fail. Two runs of npm run test:story-play-scripts, both captured exit 1, both quoted below. Not a hypothesis.

rf2-ek9qb installed the :settled-boundary-hooks producer and made every DOM-touching step establish its :dom boundary first, committing the substrate synchronously through the installed adapter's flush-render!. That closed the RENDER race. It did not close two others, and Story's own CI fixture (:story.counter-play-script/dom in tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories.cljs) still needs its wall-clock [:wait ms] because of them. That fixture is therefore STILL non-deterministic by construction — [:wait ms] is spec/017's explicit determinism OPT-OUT that assert-deterministic refuses.

FINDING 1 — THE EVENT QUEUE AFTER A SYNTHETIC DOM EVENT HAS NO SETTLE RUNG. This is the substantive one.

Deleting only the post-click [:wait 300] (the one whose own comment reads 'the wait ensures the next render cycle has flushed before we read the DOM') fails at the NEXT step:

  MISS story.counter-play-script/dom[type-click-and-assert-dom] expected=pass actual=fail steps=8
       step 5 assert - expected 42 at [:count] but got 0 expected=42 actual=0

Steps 1-4 pass, so the mount, the :assert-dom read, the :type and the :click all worked. exec-click! fires a synthetic DOM event; React runs the handler; the handler dispatches; the router schedules an ASYNC drain via interop/next-tick (re-frame.router/ensure-drain-scheduled! - genuinely deferred, never inline). flush-render! commits RENDERS. Nothing drains the EVENT QUEUE. The run-loop's setTimeout 0 yield after an async-class step drains the microtask queue, which is not the same thing.

So the ladder has a hole exactly where the bead rf2-ek9qb named: an interaction step's CONSEQUENCE is not settled, only its repaint. Note runner_events.cljc:1004-1006 already says exec-click!/exec-type!/exec-focus! 'fire a synthetic DOM event directly and never call boundary/dispatch-and-settle!' - this is that comment's cost, measured.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN #8313 AND SHOULD NOT BE DISPATCHED AS A REROUTE. The obvious move - have exec-click! settle the router after firing - is a DESIGN QUESTION, not wiring:
  - the :headless rung's verb is drain-sync! which DISPATCHES an event; there is no 'just drain what is queued' verb in the hooks contract at all, so honouring this needs a new rung verb, and inventing one was out of scope;
  - the framework's own reachable primitive may be [:wait-until [:queue-empty]], which the runner already has (queue-empty?, runner_events.cljc:994-1023) and which spec/017 calls DETERMINISTIC - but exec-wait-until! is documented as ONE-SHOT (non-polling) in headless, so it cannot await an async drain without a bounded poll that the spec assigns to 'the adapter caller';
  - so the honest options are (a) add a drain-only rung verb to the flush-hooks contract, (b) make the interaction executors settle via a bounded [:wait-until [:queue-empty]]-shaped poll, or (c) rule that an interaction's async consequence is the author's to await and document [:wait-until] as the supported form. Pick before building.

FINDING 2 - MOUNT ORDERING, smaller and separable. Deleting the LEADING [:wait 300] fails differently:

  step 1 assert - expected '[data-test=count-display]' text-content = '0', but selector matched no node expected='0' actual=:missing
  step 2 type - type failed - no node matched '[data-test=count-input]'

The component has not MOUNTED - not rendered stale. flush-render! commits work the substrate has already scheduled; it cannot conjure a mount nobody requested. The auto-run fires as soon as the lifecycle machine reaches :ready, which can precede the canvas mounting the variant. The fixture's own comment guessed this correctly ('can race ahead of React's render flush') but mis-attributed it to a flush. No settle rung can close a mount-ordering gap; this wants the auto-run gated on first-render rather than on :ready (canvas/mark-variant-rendered! and the first-rendered sentinel already exist and may be the hook).

VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING: re-run npm run test:story-play-scripts with the sleeps removed and confirm both failures reproduce. Do not trust this description over the lane.

FENCE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/**, tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories.cljs, tools/story/test/**. NOT hot zone. GATES: clojure -M:test from tools/story, npm run test:cljs, and npm run test:story-play-scripts (this bead's whole point is the browser lane - a unit-only green proves nothing here).

PAYOFF: Story's own DOM fixture becomes deterministic and stops opting out of Story's determinism gate. That is the half of rf2-ek9qb's promise that is still outstanding.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8319 (2026-08-15; completeness/correctness/implementation quality) — REOPENED exact owner.

COMPLETENESS: the patch removes all four fixture sleeps and its state-based queue/selector predicates close the measured happy-path races. CI is green, including the real browser story lane. The committed unit tests exercise the private predicates, however, not the run-loop's new timeout/refusal branches, so the failure contract is not yet witnessed end to end.

CORRECTNESS — TWO SMALL, CONCRETE GAPS:
1. `run!` documents and accepts an explicit hand-built `spec` without passing it through `fold-spec`. For `[:assert-dom selector :hidden]`, `step-required-selector` treats every raw `:assert-dom` as presence-requiring, waits for the deliberately absent node, and fails after 2 seconds. The same assertion in the normal folded form correctly has no presence precondition and passes on absence. This makes behavior depend on which supported entry path supplied the same step.
2. While a precondition is unmet, the poll calls `settle-substrate-for-step!` and discards its returned step-fail. That return is non-nil when a flush throws or exceeds its boundary budget. The comment says `exec-step!` will report it when the step runs, but a selector that remains absent never reaches `exec-step!`; the loop instead repeats the bad flush and eventually replaces the real settle error/refusal with the generic precondition timeout.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / NARROW REPAIR: keep the useful bounded, observed-condition poll. Restore one semantic path by folding explicit `run!` specs (or equivalently making the raw hidden arm mode-aware), and when polling settlement returns a failure, record that exact result and advance rather than discarding it. Add focused CLJS run-loop witnesses for raw hidden-on-absence and a failing settle while the selector remains absent; also pin that a genuine precondition timeout advances exactly once and lets the following step run. No new public rung, timer API, or generalized scheduler is needed.
close_reason:
LANDED. PR #8336 merged; verified on main at b02d5e9ab4 'fix(story): a step means one thing, and a failed commit is not a timeout'.

TWO GAPS, both from audit #8319, both held at source:

(1) step-required-selector read every raw :assert-dom as PRESENCE-REQUIRING, inverting :hidden and burning the 2-second budget. The raw arm now folds through the same fold-assert-step that exec-step! applies and reads the requirement off the canonical atom — one semantic path, tolerant of a malformed step.

(2) The poll DISCARDED its own settle failure, re-ran the broken flush every tick, then reported the generic timeout in place of the real error. It now records that exact result and advances.

NO NEW PUBLIC SURFACE, as the bead requires: no new rung verb, no timer API, no generalized scheduler.

WITNESSES: dual-lane pure coverage of the raw hidden arm and malformed tolerance, plus a CLJS-ONLY run_loop_settle_cljs_test.cljs driving run! behind a document that misses every query — the only way to express 'selector absent and stays absent', which is the state both defects live in. Planting all three defects reddened exactly the right tests and left the mode-aware control green.

The 'advances exactly once' pin is a new pin on EXISTING behaviour, so it has no defect to restore; the worker proved it load-bearing with a double-record mutation instead — 3 results, following step never ran. That is the right substitute and it was stated rather than skipped.

THE ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE THE BEAD ASKED FOR: npm run test:story-play-scripts exit 0, with story.counter-play-script/dom[type-click-and-assert-dom] passing at 7 steps and NO [:wait ms] — which is the whole point of the bead.

The worker ran that gate because the BEAD names it and my brief's gate list omitted it. Bead governs; it said so and ran it.

title: hic: the ai/ sources still spell h/handler, so republication will revert rf2-hic-090's fix

title: hicasso: the naming census cannot see a name minted by h/defview (forms/buffered-field)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 while writing rf2-hic-060's API reference.

`implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_naming_census.py` reports **103 public
names across ten namespaces, 0 unrostered**. The shipped public surface is
**104**. The missing name is `forms/buffered-field`, and it is missing for a
structural reason rather than a data one.

## What is wrong

`roster()` finds definitions with

    DEF_HEAD_RE = re.compile(r"\((def" + SYMBOL_TAIL + r"*)")

i.e. a form whose head token begins `def`. `re-frame.hicasso.forms` mints its
one view with the package's OWN defining macro:

    implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/forms.cljs:324
    (h/defview buffered-field "..." [props] ...)

The head is `h/defview`, not `defview`, so the regex does not match and the
name is invisible to the census. `forms/buffered-field` is a genuine public
name: naming-ledger row 32 rosters it (`forms/buffered-field` and its five
props, 'keep as taught'), `docs/core/hicasso/05-forms.md` teaches it, and the
forms module exists for it.

Today this is exactly one name. It is the ABSENCE direction that matters:
a new public view or crossing minted by `h/defview` / `h/defhost` /
`n/defcomponent` in any shipped namespace escapes the census silently, which
is the failure the census's own docstring says it exists to prevent ('a name
escapes when the SOURCE grows').

## The fix is one regex, and a sibling already has it

`check_guide_samples.py`'s `_DEF_RE` already handles this case and says why
in its own comment -- '`(h/defview buffered-field ...)` mints
`forms/buffered-field`, and reading only bare `def*` heads would miss it':

    r"\((?:[a-zA-Z0-9.*+!?<>=_-]+/)?(def[a-z-]*)\s+"

Porting the optional qualifier into `DEF_HEAD_RE` is the change. The census
has a `--self-test` with synthetic corpora, so the new arm is drivable there
(plant a `(h/defview ...)` in a fixture namespace and assert the count rises).

Expect the count to move 103 -> 104. `naming-ledger.md` already carries the
name in a code span, so no ledger edit should be needed -- confirm rather than
assume.

## Not in scope for rf2-hic-060

That bead owns `docs/core/hicasso/**` only. Its API reference documents all
104 names and states this discrepancy in its own 'How this page is kept
honest' section, naming the census as the side that is wrong.
close_reason: PR #8309. DEF_HEAD_RE now carries check_guide_samples.py's optional alias/ qualifier, ported unchanged. Live census 103 -> 104, still 0 unrostered; the full delta is exactly one name, forms/buffered-field, and naming-ledger row 32 already rosters it so no ledger edit was needed. The self-test did NOT cover the case (the unfixed script's --self-test passes, exit 0); two arms added, 10 -> 12 checks, both redden when the qualifier alone is reverted. Planted-name proof on a scratch mirror: unfixed 103/0/exit 0 (never counted it), fixed 105/1/exit 1 naming motion/qualified-escape-wyazi. check_facade_inventory unmoved at 16 names / 43 rows. No src edited.

title: [story] The workspace variant cell bypasses the substrate registry too — it has no substrate axis at all
description:
FOUND WHILE FIXING rf2-3afns (2026-08-15), verified at source, deliberately LEFT OUT of that bead's PR because it is a different question, not a bigger version of the same one.

rf2-3afns routed the canvas single-pane path and the render-variant host hook through 'substrate->render-fn'. There is a THIRD render site with the same shape:

  tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/workspace.cljc, 'variant-cell-inner' — the ':else' branch is
    (let [resolved-view (rf/view view-id)] ...)
  then embeds '[resolved-view eff-args]' as a Reagent hiccup vector, exactly as the canvas did before rf2-3afns. Verified at source: the missing-view diagnostic string ':component <id> is not registered as a view' appears there as it did in canvas.cljs.

WHY IT WAS NOT FOLDED INTO rf2-3afns. The canvas already RESOLVED the declared substrate set ('variant-substrate-set') and then ignored it — the fix was to stop ignoring a value already in hand. The workspace cell has NO substrate axis whatsoever: it never reads ':substrates', and its own docstring pins it as 'canvas/canvas-inner at a smaller scale — SINGLE SUBSTRATE'. So making it substrate-aware is NEW BEHAVIOUR, not the removal of a bypass, and it needs a decision first.

THE DECISION, and it is the whole bead: should a workspace cell honour the variant's declared ':substrates'? A workspace lays out MANY variants at once (':grid', ':tabs', ':variants-grid', ':prose', ':custom'). Three defensible answers:
  (a) Honour it per-cell — a ':substrates #{:uix}' variant paints under UIx in its cell. Consistent with the canvas; a few lines ('multi-substrate/resolve-substrate-set' is public and pure, 'single-render-substrate' now exists to reduce a set to one).
  (b) Keep the workspace host-substrate-only and SAY SO — the cell renders under the shell host regardless, with the declared set surfaced somewhere rather than silently ignored. Cheapest honest option.
  (c) Refuse the case — a workspace containing a variant whose declared substrate is not the host's is an authoring error worth naming.

TODAY IT IS (a)-shaped BY ACCIDENT AND (b)-shaped IN EFFECT, silently: the cell paints Reagent whatever the variant declared, and nothing tells the author. That silence is the same cost rf2-3afns removed from the canvas, which is why this is filed as a bug rather than a feature — but the remedy is a ruling, not a reroute.

SCOPE NOTE: 'workspace.cljc' also re-uses 'canvas/safe-decorated-view', so whatever lands must not decorate twice — the same trap rf2-3afns navigated (render-decorated-view resolves decorator refs WITHOUT the mode / cell-override run-opts, so the canvas consumes 'render-view' and keeps its own wrap).

FENCE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/workspace.cljc + tools/story/test/**. NOT hot zone. Do not touch spec/*, implementation/**.

DO NOT dispatch as a mechanical reroute. Answer the question first.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #8313 (commit 52fcd701ef). VERDICT: (c) on the premise, resolving to (a) on the remedy — no ruling was needed.

The bead's OBSERVATION is correct and reproduced: workspace/variant-cell-inner carried the same (rf/view view-id) shape rf2-3afns removed from the canvas, down to the shared ':component ... is not registered as a view' diagnostic.

Its GATING PREMISE does not hold at source. The bead says the cell 'has NO substrate axis whatsoever'. It has one, and was already reacting to it: run-variant-with-shell-opts! (workspace.cljc:326) threads :substrate (:substrate shell) into every runtime/run-variant call, and variant-cell (:481-484) keys its re-runs on canvas/run-key, which carries :substrate for the expressly stated purpose of covering 'substrate flips' (canvas.cljs:383, workspace.cljc:473). The cell re-ran on a substrate change and then painted Reagent regardless — which made that re-run a lie. So this is a bypass removal, not new behaviour, and 'it needs a decision first' does not survive the read.

The DECISION the bead asked for is likewise already written into the fn the fix uses. canvas/variant-substrate-set's resolution order IS the answer: the variant's declared :substrates, else the parent story's, else the shell's host substrate. Option (b) ('keep the workspace host-substrate-only') is not a rival to option (a); it is (a)'s FALLBACK — a variant declaring nothing still renders under the shell host, asserted by undeclared-substrate-falls-back-to-the-shell-host. Option (c) (refuse the case) was not needed: an unregistered substrate already degrades loudly via render-view.

rf2-1gy4e does NOT gate this. That ruling is about how a story NAMES a hicasso view; this registers no substrate, widens no enum and adds no hicasso support. Like rf2-3afns it fixes UIx today.

variant-substrate-set became public rather than copied, so one resolution policy serves both surfaces (the same sharing run-key and safe-decorated-view already have). The scope note's decorate-twice trap was navigated the same way rf2-3afns did: render-decorated-view resolves decorator refs WITHOUT the mode/cell-override run-opts, so the cell consumes render-view and keeps its own safe-decorated-view wrap.

WITNESS distinguishes WHICH substrate rendered, since the bug is a working path painting the wrong thing: probe view emits reagent-view-render, the :uix stub emits uix-stub-render, and every case asserts one present AND the other absent. Five cases incl. the unregistered-substrate and missing-view degradations.

RUNNER: workspace.cljc's body is entirely inside #?(:cljs ...), so clojure -M:test LOADS the file and sees none of the code under test — this is witnessed by npm run test:cljs and only by it (13950 tests/70394 assertions, 0 failures, captured exit 0). tools/story JVM also green (1848/6775, exit 0) and the Playwright play-script lane green (30 rows, 0 unexpected, exit 0).

SPEC: 003-Render-Shell.md unchanged because this changes no rendering CONTRACT — it makes the workspace cell obey the routing rule rf2-3afns already wrote there.

title: [story] Nothing installs :settled-boundary-hooks — the live Reagent shell plays at :provides :headless and settles on setTimeout 0
description:
FOUND BY rf2-5czki's phase-1 survey (2026-08-15). SUBSTRATE-INDEPENDENT — this is broken for Reagent today, and it is why an interaction story cannot honestly claim a render settled on ANY substrate.

Story's play runner is built to take its settle behaviour from the host. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/settled_boundary.cljc:29-40 says so in the ns docstring: "The runner MUST NOT hard-code `dispatch-sync`. It takes a flush-hooks map from the adapter-aware caller: {:dispatch! ... :provides :headless|:cljs-reactive|:dom|:browser :flush! {...} :timeout-ms ...}". The consumer is runner_events.cljc:476-487, reading the `:settled-boundary-hooks` late-bind key.

NOBODY INSTALLS IT. `rg -n 'settled-boundary-hooks' tools/story` returns FOUR hits: three in runner_events.cljc (the consumer and its docstring) and one in tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:903. Zero producers in src, zero in test. The fallback is `boundary/headless-flush-hooks` (settled_boundary.cljc:206-220), whose `:flush!` is `(fn [_frame-id] nil)`.

CONSEQUENCE: THE LIVE REAGENT SHELL RUNS PLAYS AT `:provides :headless`. Story src calls no React or Reagent flush anywhere — `rg 'r/flush|reagent.core/flush|flushSync' tools/story/src` finds only three prose mentions. The real settle after an interaction is a bare macrotask yield, runner_events.cljc:1512-1517 (`js/setTimeout ... 0`), because exec-click!/exec-type!/exec-focus! fire a synthetic DOM event and never call `dispatch-and-settle!` at all — runner_events.cljc:1004-1006 says so explicitly. The one genuine settlement read (runner_events.cljc:1019-1023) is router-queue-only: EVENT settlement, not RENDER settlement.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE ONCE HICASSO ARRIVES, without being caused by it: Hicasso's whole witness discipline is explicit synchronous commit — impl/mount.cljs:39-48, "every door here commits before it returns: render! renders inside flushSync, and settle! is the empty flushSync that lets an already-scheduled sync-lane notification land." Its test kit already ships the verbs a host would install: `settle!` (test_kit/.../mounted.cljs:979), `settle-until!` (:1024), `dispatch-and-settle!` (:1162), `advance-clock!` (:1087). A `setTimeout 0` host would be strictly worse than what the substrate offers.

TWO NEIGHBOURS FOUND IN THE SAME PASS, worth recording here rather than as their own beads:

title: [story] Register the :hicasso substrate render-fn over h/as-component, and widen the one closed SubstrateSet enum
description:
PHASE C of rf2-5czki. BLOCKED ON rf2-3afns (the registry must actually be consulted before registering into it means anything) AND ON rf2-1gy4e (the naming ruling decides how `:component` resolves). Do not dispatch before both land.

THE GOOD NEWS THE SURVEY FOUND, and it is why this phase is small rather than a port:

Hicasso needs NO new root, NO second React tree and NO plumbing to render inside Story's canvas. The door already exists and was built for exactly this crossing — implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:581-596, `h/as-component`:

  "the outward bridge (rf2-hic-032). Answers a real React component for a hiccup head, so a native parent — n/defcomponent, UIx, or plain JavaScript — mounts a minted Hicasso view UNDER THE FRAME IT IS ALREADY IN ... the frame comes from React context, and no second root, state owner or props ABI appears anywhere."

And Story's canvas already establishes that context. canvas.cljs:606 and :632 wrap the subject in `[rf/frame-provider {:frame variant-id} ...]`, whose provider is `re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:100) — and implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:32-37 states that this is "the same object every React-shaped adapter reads ... so a Hicasso subtree and a UIx subtree under one provider resolve the same frame."

So the variant frame reaches a Hicasso boundary for free. `h/mount!` is NOT needed and must not be used here — it creates a root, and Story's canvas is already inside one.

THE WORK, and keep it to this:
 1. A `:hicasso` render-fn registered through the existing public `register-substrate!` (multi_substrate.cljs:104-115). Shape is the registry's own contract `(fn [variant-id view-id args] ...)` returning something that splices into a Reagent hiccup tree.
 2. `h/as-component` is declared ONCE PER VIEW at top level by design (hicasso.cljc:586 "Declared once at top level, beside the view"). Calling it per-render mints a new component identity every pass and remounts the subtree. Either memoize on the resolved view, or require the author to register the bridged component. STATE WHICH AND WHY — this is the one real design decision in the phase.
 3. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc:288 — `[:set [:enum :reagent :uix]]`. THE ONLY CLOSED SUBSTRATE ENUM IN THE REPO (verified: `rg -n 'enum :reagent' .` returns this line and one unrelated Spec-Schemas.md row). A one-line widen — BUT read rf2-1gy4e's closing section first: the docstring above it claims to mirror a framework-supplied closed set, and the set it points at (spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md :2718 / :2800-2809) does not contain hicasso. Either the docstring is corrected in the same edit or the widen is dishonest.
 4. Reagent's interop head is `:r>`, NOT `:>` — `:>` calls `(name kw)` on prop values and drops keyword namespaces (canvas.cljs:614-619, provider.cljs:84-95). A Hicasso boundary takes an ordinary CLJS props map, so `:r>` is the correct head.

DO A SPIKE FIRST AND SAY WHAT IT SHOWED. Nothing in the repo renders a Hicasso boundary inside a REAGENT tree today: `rg -l 're-frame\.hicasso' --glob '*.cljs' implementation testbeds examples | xargs rg -l 'reagent\.core'` returns EMPTY, and every `h/as-component` call site is a Hicasso test or a UIx/native parent. The crossing is designed and documented but Reagent is not among its witnessed parents. Prove one boundary paints under Reagent + `rf/frame-provider` before writing the registration. If it does not, STOP and report — that is a Hicasso finding, not a Story one, and it is a different bead.

Adding one is a reversal of a recorded decision and needs it argued in the PR body, not slipped in.
