RULING CASCADE (2026-08-15, delegated + operator-reversible) from rf2-1gy4e, which is now CLOSED as RULED: **option (b)** — h/defview registers its authoring-time name with the :view registrar, minimal shape (keyword id + coords + minted head under :hicasso/component, NO :handler-fn, debug-gated, replace-on-reload; full ruling in rf2-1gy4e's comments). This bead is unblocked by that ruling but now DEPENDS ON rf2-5qaf4, the new Hicasso-side registration carrier (this bead's fence excludes implementation/**, so it cannot carry that half). This dossier's Codex recommendation AND the root dossier's were both weighed; the two decision points are ruled:

IDENTITY STRATEGY — **A primary: the render-fn returns (h/as-element [resolved-view eff-args]), a direct element mint.** No cache, no props round-trip. Basis (verified at source): defview already mints ONE stable React.memo wrapper per head at definition time (codec.cljs stable-boundary! :1180-1212; boundary-element/element-type :1214-1219), so a fresh ELEMENT per pass rides a STABLE component type — the memoization option would re-implement exactly that machinery one layer up. h/as-component exists to decode camelCase props from a NATIVE parent (outward-props, codec.cljs:3782-3793); Story already holds the kebab-keyword CLJS args map, so bridging through it would convert kebab-to-camel purely so hicasso can convert straight back. A React-element return is the registry's documented second shape (multi_substrate.cljs:110-112).

**B (memoized as-component, keyed on the resolved head; hot reload yields a new head hence a new entry) stays PRE-AUTHORIZED as fallback with a NARROW trigger**: take B only if the spike shows the element-splice specifically misbehaving under Reagent reconciliation while the crossing itself paints. Do NOT build B pre-emptively, and do not add speculative wrapping or caching. If the crossing does not paint AT ALL, STOP and file a Hicasso finding (this bead's own standing instruction; both reviewers agree). Option C (author registers the bridged component per story) is REJECTED — per-story ceremony against the low-friction clause, and it hollows the substrate entry into a :uix story.

SPIKE FIRST (mandated, unchanged): nothing in the repo witnesses a Hicasso boundary painting inside a Reagent tree — prove one paints under Reagent + rf/frame-provider before writing the registration. The spike does NOT need the registrar entry (reference the view value directly), so it may run first thing, even while rf2-5qaf4 is still in flight.

PLACEMENT — **1: host-registered, exactly like :uix.** Story ships the enum widen + corrected docstring + a tested recipe (the CLJS arm registers the real render-fn and asserts dispatch and degradation); rf2-kttom's testbed registers it for real; a consumer copies ~5 lines at boot. tools/story/deps.edn UNTOUCHED — the fence's "ONLY if genuinely needed" conditional resolves to NOT NEEDED: hicasso/src is already on the top-level shadow :source-paths (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:160), so the CLJS test arm rides npm run test:cljs with no deps.edn or shadow-cljs.edn change, and tools/story's JVM clojure -M:test never compiles .cljs. Placement 2 (Story-shipped install-hicasso-substrate!) REJECTED as GA-era ergonomics — reopen as its own bead only if hicasso GA makes zero-config Story support a requirement.

ENUM WIDEN: SubstrateSet -> #{:reagent :uix :hicasso} AND rewrite the schemas.cljc:281-288 docstring in the SAME edit, per rf2-1gy4e's axis sub-ruling: :substrates is Story's OWN authoring-layer render-strategy axis (which registered render-fn embeds the subject), not a mirror of the framework adapter enum — the current "framework supplies the closed set" claim is false. Do not ship the widen without the correction. No :rf.adapter/hicasso anywhere.

RENDER-FN CONTRACT DETAILS: resolve the view LATE (per render — preserves HMR late binding; re-evaluating defview replaces the registrar entry behind the same id and the story picks up the new head with no story change); on resolution failure return the same style of inline missing-view diagnostic as the Reagent renderer; read the head from the entry's :hicasso/component slot; if any Reagent interop head is needed use :r>, not :> (stock :> drops keyword namespaces — provider.cljs:84-95).

ARGTYPES: hicasso stories hand-author :argtypes — auto-Controls is deferred by the root ruling (hicasso has no props-schema notion; do not add one here).

ACCEPTANCE (folding both Codex evidence lists — distilled): mount one real defview result through the registered renderer inside Story's actual Reagent tree: it paints, observes the variant frame from rf/frame-provider, updates when that frame changes, and does NOT remount when the Reagent parent rerenders with the same head. Cover public-registry dispatch plus missing-view and missing-substrate degradation. Pure tests show plan compilation, variant->edn/MCP round-trips, and snapshot identity retain the keyword and DISTINGUISH two hicasso view ids. Gates: clojure -M:test from tools/story + npm run test:cljs, foreground to completion. The full painted-deck browser proof is phase D (rf2-kttom).

comments.text:
WORKER REPORT (worker/w-2dbpd, PR #8344). Both halves landed as ruled; the spike answered, and it found one thing the ruling did not anticipate.

THE SPIKE: THE CROSSING PAINTS. A h/defview boundary, minted by h/as-element, spliced into a REAGENT hiccup tree under rf/frame-provider, committed through reagent.dom.client into a real DOM — it paints, and it reads the VARIANT frame the Reagent provider scoped (alpha/7; the default frame would read 0). A Reagent-parent re-render re-renders it WITHOUT remounting, measured on DOM node identity across three renders. So the bead's stop-condition ("does not paint AT ALL") is NOT met and the registration stands.

THE FINDING: IT IS THEN DEAF. A write into that frame after the commit never re-invokes the body (run counter 1 -> 1) — a missing notification, not a stale read. Filed rf2-phabt (P1) with a LIVE CONTROL: same boundary, same subscription, same Reagent adapter, same drain, only the mounting route varying. Under h/mount! it repaints; crossed with h/as-element it is deaf; crossed with a MEMOIZED h/as-component it is deaf identically. So the outward-bridge DOOR is not the variable — which means THIS BEAD'S PRE-AUTHORIZED FALLBACK B IS NOT THE REMEDY, and I did not take it (B was run as an experiment and removed). Also ruled out: adapter, drain, provider object (both routes provide over the same frame-context), frame resolution, React reconciliation.

rf2-kttom IS NOW BLOCKED ON rf2-phabt (dependency added). A worked hicasso testbed cannot have an interactive story until the deafness is fixed. The non-interactive surface is fine.

DECISIONS TAKEN, each as ruled: identity strategy A (direct element mint, no cache) — verified at source that codec/memoize-boundary! + element-type already give one stable React.memo type per head, so the cache would re-implement it; placement 1 (host-registered like :uix) — Story ships no installer, deps.edn UNTOUCHED (verified: hicasso/src is already on the top-level shadow :source-paths and the JVM arm never compiles .cljs); enum widen + docstring correction in the same edit; late per-render resolution off (rf/handler-meta :view id) reading :hicasso/component; no :r> needed (the renderer returns a React element and adds no Reagent interop head).

ALSO FILED: rf2-sc5g0 (P2) — plan/variant-plan folds :substrates from the variant and its :extends chain but NOT from the parent story, so a story-level declaration reaches the canvas and not render-host-scope, which falls back to :reagent. A narrower residue of rf2-3afns, not about hicasso, both files outside this fence.

GATES, captured exits: npm run test:browser 0 (1562/9881); npm run test:cljs 0 (13976/70345); clojure -M:test from tools/story 0 (1861/6815); check-no-hardcoded-paths 0. RED proofs for both new files with hash-verified restores — enum revert reds the .cljc file (7, JVM), render-view pinned to :reagent reds the .cljs file (7 of 24, node).

title: [bug] the fence rule says 'never from your own memory of who you dispatched', but a SIMULTANEOUSLY-dispatched peer appears in no derivable source
description:
FOUND BY the mayor's method-reread loop, 2026-08-15 14:56 AUSEST, step 2 — checking an enforced rule against what the tree actually does. Surfaced by a worker's own observation rather than by reasoning.

THE RULE, verbatim from .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md: derive the fence enumeration at dispatch time from 'gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,files plus git worktree list, NEVER FROM YOUR OWN MEMORY OF WHO YOU DISPATCHED'.

THE RULE'S INTENT IS RIGHT AND SHOULD SURVIVE. It exists because a remembered list goes stale inside the dispatch's own lifetime — measured: on a six-worker fleet with an 11-minute merge cadence, a fence can be wrong by the time the brief is finished, and one worker found only one of the four holders its fence named still had an open PR.

BUT IT OVERSTATES, AND THE GAP IS MEASURED. worker/mount-7mtcf reported: 'docsguide-hic068 and method-63y4v HAD NO WORKTREE AT ALL — neither had started, so the check-its-file-list instruction had nothing to check.' All three were dispatched by the mayor in ONE message. At mount-7mtcf's start-up its two peers had:
  - no open PR            -> invisible to gh pr list
  - no worktree           -> invisible to git worktree list
  - no branch, no commits -> invisible to the three-dot diff
  - no working tree       -> invisible to git status --porcelain
FOUR SIGNALS, ALL BLIND. The mayor's memory of the dispatch was the ONLY source that could warn it, and the brief's enumeration is what did.

SO THE MAYOR'S DISPATCH-TIME KNOWLEDGE IS LOAD-BEARING FOR EXACTLY ONE WINDOW: between dispatching a worker and that worker creating its worktree. Inside that window memory is not a stale substitute for derivation — it is the only evidence that exists.

THE FIX: one clause. Keep 'never from memory' as the rule for workers ALREADY RUNNING, and add that a peer dispatched in the SAME message or the same tick appears in no derivable source, so the brief must name it from the mayor's own dispatch knowledge and say so — flagged as 'dispatched alongside you, may not exist yet; re-derive at start-up and again before your first edit'. The worker's own re-derivation still governs everything else.

WHY THE DIRECTION MATTERS: omitting a simultaneously-dispatched peer is a stale-NARROW fence, which mayor-dispatch.md itself names as the expensive direction — two workers on one file merge-conflict and can silently revert each other. The other direction costs one re-derivation.

VERIFY BEFORE LANDING. Confirm the quoted sentence is still present and unchanged, and confirm the file does not already cover the case: a grep for 'not yet started|no worktree yet|dispatched.*same message|simultaneous' returned ZERO at filing.

DO NOT ADD MACHINERY. No registry, no dispatch log, no script. One clause, consistent with rf2-6ng7's standing (c)-narrow ruling.

DO NOT put it in docs/the-mayor-method/ without argument — that tree names no tool or command. If you judge the generic layer needs the PRINCIPLE (a signal that derives from artefacts cannot see work that has not produced an artefact yet), say so with reasoning, keep it tool-free, and run a leak check over the added lines. Concluding the generic layer already covers it is equally correct and should be stated with the line reference — a worker did exactly that an hour ago on loops.md and was right.
close_reason: Landed as PR #8296 (worker/fencetick-a30v2), one clause into .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md line 21, purely additive (+1185 bytes, zero removed segments). title: hic: publish day8/re-frame2-hicasso — release wiring, and the second-in-repo-dependency shape it does not fit
description:
Split out of rf2-hic-061, whose surface line flagged `.github/workflows/*` as hot-zone "if a release workflow is added". It is, and `.github/workflows/test.yml` was held by open PR #8279 at the time, so the wiring was FILED rather than attempted. The policy page (docs/design/hicasso/product/release-policy.md, §2 and §6) states the shape and this bead executes it.

## Why it is owed

rf2-hic-061's own acceptance reads "a tagged release installable by the tiny consumer app from the artefact (not the repo)". That is unmeetable from a docs page: nothing publishes today. Measured at source on 2026-08-15:

- `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn` carries NO `:clein/build` alias (its header says so, deliberately).
- `.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh`'s `ARTEFACTS` array names thirteen artefacts and Hicasso is not one.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s `deploy-leaf` matrix and its `deploy-ssr-ring` companion name every coordinate a tag publishes; Hicasso appears in neither.
- Repo-root `VERSION` reads `0.0.1.alpha` and `git ls-remote --tags origin` returns NOTHING — this repository has never carried a release tag, for any artefact.

## The design question — this is not a checklist

Hicasso's published `:deps` would name a SECOND in-repo artefact besides core: `day8/re-frame2-ssr`, for the `re-frame.hicasso.server` module. That is exactly the property that put `ssr-ring` in its own `deploy-ssr-ring` stage AFTER the leaf matrix instead of inside it — under the matrix's `fail-fast: false`, such a leaf can publish a pom that does not resolve while the leaf it names is red (rf2-p4a93's reasoning, in release.yml's own comments).

So: Hicasso publishes in a post-matrix stage beside ssr-ring, or the packaging shape changes. Decide it before wiring anything.

## Deliverables

1. `:clein/build` alias in `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn` (version via the relative `../../VERSION` path, per the lockstep mechanism).
2. Entries in `verify-version-lockstep.sh`'s `ARTEFACT_PATHS` / `ARTEFACTS` / `NON_CORE`. The script already REFUSES a `:clein/build` with no inventory entry, so 1 without 2 reds — which is the right failure direction and why this cannot be done piecemeal.
3. A deploy stage in `release.yml` implementing the decision above, plus the release-notes row.
4. `spec/Conventions.md` §Packaging conventions: Hicasso joins the artefact tier tables and the published-coordinate count moves off thirteen.
5. The knock-on: Hicasso is currently THE ONE coordinate `release-xray.yml` deliberately leaves at `:local/root` while rewriting the other nine, with `preflight-xray-package.sh` refusing the deploy. Publishing Hicasso is what unblocks Xray's own publishability.
6. Then, and only then, rf2-hic-061's acceptance is executable: cut a tag, install the tiny consumer app from the coordinate rather than the repo.

## Fences — ALL HOT ZONE, sequence it

`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh`, `spec/Conventions.md` and `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn`. Sequence against any other workflow or Conventions bead; never parallel.

## Also owed, and NOT this bead's

§4's per-surface SSR/hydration row in the policy page stays OPEN because `checkpoint-4-coverage.md` returned NOT MET on the Phase 4 exit. That is rf2-hic-064's audit, not this wiring.
close_reason:
SHIPPED IN PR #8314 (branch worker/release-gra70). MERGING IT PUBLISHES NOTHING: release.yml and release-xray.yml are tag-triggered only, so a merge to main starts no deploy job. Cutting a v* tag stays the operator's act and this repo has still never carried one.

THE DESCRIPTION'S SIX DELIVERABLES, EACH ANSWERED. (1) :clein/build in implementation/hicasso/deps.edn with :version "../../VERSION", plus the :clein alias it needs and :src-dirs ["src" "resources"] because the clj-kondo export reaches a consumer over the CLASSPATH -- a jar without resources/ silently ships no lint layer. (2) verify-version-lockstep.sh: ARTEFACT_PATHS / ARTEFACTS / NON_CORE, and the ssr-ring second-coordinate block generalised into a two-entry loop since hicasso names the same second coordinate. Gate prints 'all 19 artefacts (14 implementation/ + 5 tools/) ... 33 in-repo :local/root coordinate(s), every one of them inventoried', exit 0. (3) A deploy-hicasso stage + the release-notes row. (4) spec/Conventions.md: thirteen -> fourteen, a new artefact-set row, and a paragraph saying a published view SUBSTRATE is not automatically an ADAPTER (hicasso declares no :kind and implements no Spec 006 contract; it is authored on top of UIx). (5) The Xray knock-on, executed -- see below. (6) rf2-hic-061's acceptance is now EXECUTABLE and still unexecuted; the tag is Mike's.

THE DESIGN QUESTION -- IT FITS, AND WHERE WAS ALREADY DECIDED. Hicasso's published :deps name day8/re-frame2 (../core) AND day8/re-frame2-ssr (../ssr), the IDENTICAL set to ssr-ring, and rf2-p4a93 already built the shape for exactly that property. So deploy-hicasso, needs: [deploy-core, deploy-leaf]. A SEPARATE JOB rather than a second value of deploy-ssr-ring's matrix: two values of one matrix cannot be ordered against each other, which is the whole reason the split exists; and folding them together would have renamed a job key that 25 references across 6 files point at. The two stages are siblings -- neither names the other in its pom -- so they run in parallel. _release-dag-policy.test.cjs moves 13 -> 14 publishers, derived from the workflow's own job graph, and gains an acceptance case plus two teeth cases for the new stage, both reconstructed from the CURRENT model so they cannot rot away from the file under test.

title: [bug] merge clause 5 must verify git diff before counting job keys; the replacement pipeline still false-zeros
description:

  gh pr diff 8279 -- .github/workflows/test.yml  -> 0 lines
  git diff origin/main...origin/worker/ciarm-st1x5 -- .github/workflows/test.yml -> 104 lines
The file IS in the PR. gh accepts the pathspec, exits 0, prints nothing. No error, no warning.

WHY IT MATTERS: clause 5 asks whether a workflow change moved the CHECK SET, and the discriminator counts new top-level job keys in the diff. An empty diff gives zero, which reads as 'steps only, band unchanged' — the reassuring answer. THE CHECK FAILS OPEN, in the direction that admits a PR computed against a superseded matrix.

THE MAYOR DID THIS EARLIER IN THIS SESSION and reported a conclusion it had no evidence for: checking #8270 it ran gh pr diff 8270 -- .github/workflows/test.yml, got empty, and said 'steps only, band unchanged'. That was TRUE by luck; the same command prints empty for a PR adding ten jobs.

THE FIX: in .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md clause 5, wherever the job-key discriminator is written, make the command explicitly git-based against the three-dot merge base, and add ONE sentence recording that gh pr diff silently ignores a pathspec so the count comes back zero regardless. Both halves of the test are then pinned: the two-space indent AND the tool.

  git diff origin/main...origin/worker/<branch> -- .github/workflows/ | grep -cE '^\+  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$'

VERIFY BOTH HALVES AT SOURCE BEFORE LANDING, against a case whose answer is known NON-zero. #8279 is that case today: it adds hicasso-naming-census, so git returns 1 and gh returns 0. If #8279 has merged by the time you run this, pick another PR that adds a job — a discriminator only ever tested on zero-answers is untested, which is precisely how both of these defects survived.

DO NOT ADD MACHINERY. No wrapper script, no gate. One command correction and one sentence, consistent with rf2-6ng7's standing (c)-narrow ruling.

DO NOT put it in docs/the-mayor-method/ — that tree names no tool or flag by construction, and this is a fact about one CLI.

WHY THE MAYOR DID NOT JUST EDIT IT: the mayor checkout's pre-commit hook refuses commits to worker-tracked surfaces, which is the hook working as docs/the-mayor-method/README.md predicts. NOTE .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md IS CURRENTLY HELD by worker/method-63y4v (rf2-byoxk + rf2-63y4v) — sequence this AFTER that PR merges, or route it to that worker if it is still live.

It was told to verify against a case whose answer is known NON-zero (#8279 today), and to quote its own numbers rather than mine.

The PR correctly replaces the unsupported `gh pr diff <n> -- <pathspec>` call with `git diff` and corrects the mechanism (gh rejects the extra args; the filter sees empty stdout). But the landed recommendation still directly pipes `git diff` into `grep -cE`. That preserves the same producer-failure class it explains: a failing `git diff` emits no stdout, the filter counts that empty stream as `0`, and the pipeline does not preserve the producer's status.

title: [bug] mayor-merge.md's check-count band reads 97; the tree carries 98 after #8264 added a SKIPPED required-check row
description:
FOUND BY the mayor's merge loop, 2026-08-15 01:12 AUSEST. THIRD time this constant has gone stale in about six hours (93 -> 96 -> 97 -> 98). That recurrence is NOT evidence the clause is wrong -- clause 1 already says 'the measurement is the clause; the constant is only its most recent result', and that sentence is exactly right. Resist adding machinery.

WHAT MOVED IT, AND WHY THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT FROM THE PREVIOUS TWO. PR #8264 (rf2-qpk2l) added a 'Provenance pins (full corpus)' job to lint.yml conditioned 'github.event_name != \'pull_request\'', so IT NEVER RUNS ON A PR. It nevertheless appears in every PR's check list as SKIPPED, and 'gh pr checks --json state | length' COUNTS A SKIPPED ROW. So the band moved WITHOUT adding a second of CI time. The previous two moves came from jobs that actually run. A future mayor reasoning 'nothing new runs on a PR, so the count cannot have moved' would be wrong: THE BAND COUNTS CHECK ROWS, NOT EXECUTED JOBS.

MEASURED, per clause 1's own standard -- on PRs MERGED AFTER the matrix change, which is the standard rf2-nfgib followed for 97:

  #8266  merged 2026-08-15 01:05  total=98
  #8267  merged 2026-08-15 01:11  total=98
  #8268  merged 2026-08-15 01:11  total=98

Plus #8264 itself, which read 98 while its sibling #8265 read 97 on the same tree -- the discriminating pair.

Measurement command, per the file: gh pr checks <pr> --json state --jq 'length'.

THE FIX. In .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md clause 1, replace the '**97 as measured 2026-08-14 23:05 +1000**' reading with 98, naming #8264 as the matrix change and #8266/#8267/#8268 as the post-change confirmations. Then update the moves-N-times sentence -- it currently says FIVE TIMES and names 97 the sixth reading; 98 is the SEVENTH. RE-MEASURE BEFORE WRITING; more PRs will have merged and a count is a claim.

ADD ONE CLAUSE, AND ONLY ONE: that a check row can be SKIPPED and still count, so a job conditioned never to run on a PR still moves the band. That is a genuine gap in the clause as written -- the reader currently has no reason to expect a no-op job to change the number. Do NOT add a script, a gate, or an auto-update.

WHILE YOU ARE IN CLAUSE 1, VERIFY A SECOND THING IS ALREADY THERE. PR #8254 added a third cause of a band-minus-one reading: the 'All required checks passed' aggregator is NOT CREATED until its needs: resolve, so any PR still in flight reads band-minus-one whatever its matrix is. That cause was confirmed empirically twice today (#8247, then #8266 at 01:00). Its remedy is to WAIT -- update-branch is actively wrong for it and re-triggers everything. Check the clause names all three causes and their three different remedies (stale base -> update-branch; genuine gap -> investigate; in flight -> wait). If it does, change nothing there.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS WORTH ONE SENTENCE IF ABSENT: diff the check NAMES between the suspect PR and a known-good one, never reason from the count. That single command resolved a false refutation at 00:52 today in which the new SKIPPED row was PRESENT and the total still read 97 -- the missing row was the aggregator, not the new job.

DO NOT put a number in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md. That layer is deliberately numberless ('measure the band; never trust a number written down') and correct as it stands.

title: hic: HS-23's n/dollar Activity route has its WITNESS and owes a DISPOSITION — Client-only is disproven on the route the lane note recommends, and defhost/[:>]/n-dollar disagree
description:
## The finding

Successor to **rf2-04ekn**, filed by the record-keeping sweep (rf2-lbn9o / rf2-04ekn) on
`main`@`e3ab11213a`, 2026-08-15.

rf2-04ekn was filed on the reading that HS-23's remaining `n/$` route "has no live owner". That
half holds. What it did **not** establish — and what this bead exists to record correctly — is
**which** of the two things HS-23 could owe is actually outstanding, because they have different
answers:

* **A witness is NOT owed. It landed.**
  `client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs:488`,
  *through-n-dollar-a-visible-activity-subtree-reaches-the-response*, drives an `<Activity>`
  constructed through `n/$` under a real `renderToString`, in both modes. Visible: the hosted
  subtree and its `h/sub` read are in the response. Hidden: nothing, and the row states that this
  is React's own omission rather than a refusal. It landed with `rf2-cfriw` as `2b3a916ead`
  (re-verified an ancestor of `e3ab11213a`), and [`dispositions.md`](dispositions.md)'s HS-23 cell
  already cites it. rf2-04ekn's first acceptance clause is therefore already met, and a bead
  dispatched to write that witness would be writing it twice.

* **A DISPOSITION is owed, and nothing owns it.**
  HS-23's Target policy reads `Client-only`. On the `n/$` route the measured behaviour is
  **Render**. The cell states the behaviour and stops; it never says what the policy IS on that
  route. Section 2.1 note 3 says an unproved refusal is not a disposition — here the refusal is
  not merely unproved, it is **disproven**, on the route
  [`lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md`](lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md):56 recommends first.

## The sharper fact, which rf2-04ekn did not carry

The two undeclared escapes to the same foreign `<Activity>` behave in **opposite** directions on
the server, and both directions are witnessed:

| Route | Server behaviour | Witness |
|---|---|---|
| `h/defhost`, no `:server` | refuses at the declaration source, both arms | `client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs`:432 |
| raw `[:>]` | renders nothing, and *cannot say otherwise* | `raw_escape_dom_cljs_test.cljs`:215 |
| `n/$` | the visible subtree reaches the response, read and all | `client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs`:488 |

`[:>]` is (per HS-19) `defhost` with the declaration erased, so it inherits the default gate.
`n/$` is the native tier's own construction and passes through no gate at all. So an author reaches
one React component by two undeclared spellings and gets opposite server bytes, and no page states
that. That asymmetry — not the missing witness — is what is undispositioned.

## Why it is a decision and not work

The three candidate dispositions are not equivalent in cost or in law, and choosing among them is
not a records call:

1. **Accept it: "the subtree renders, by design."** HS-23's cell states a per-route policy, and
   `lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md`:56's recommendation stops naming three routes as if they
   were interchangeable. Docs only.
2. **Make the refusal real on `n/$` too.** A gate on the native tier's own form. This is a code
   change, and it runs at [React 4](lanes/design-laws.md#react-and-ownership), which cedes Activity
   to React, and at the two-hook ceiling that `react-compatibility-notes.md`:54 already invokes to
   refuse an adjacent repair.
3. **Rule it out of HS-23's scope.** A foreign component head under `n/$` is arguably HS-25's row
   rather than HS-23's, in which case HS-23 narrows to the `defhost` route and says so. Note this
   does not dissolve the question, it moves it: HS-25's disposition is *Client-only by default*,
   which the same measurement contradicts.

## Surface fence

* WRITE: `docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md` (HS-23's operative-disposition cell, and
  HS-25's if disposition 3 is taken), and
  `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md`:56 if disposition 1 or 3 is
  taken.
* Do NOT touch `docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md` — the ledger keeper's.
* Do NOT touch `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/hot-path-architecture.md` — see the note below;
  it is a separate record with a separate finding.
* If disposition 2 is chosen, `implementation/hicasso/` is in scope and a new error id would owe a
  `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` row, which is hot zone — stop and file rather than take it.

## An adjacent finding, recorded here rather than acted on

[`lanes/hot-path-architecture.md`](lanes/hot-path-architecture.md#canonical-native-tier-acceptance-checklist)'s
checklist **row 5** (*Server and hydration*) is the row that owns "server bytes or source refusal"
for native surfaces, and its Deciding evidence cell enumerates the native tier as **"HS-24 to
HS-30"**. HS-23 is an Activity-hosted subtree reached through `n/$` — a native-tier route — and it
falls outside that enumeration, so row 5's own evidence cell does not reach the surface this bead
is about. That page was deliberately not edited by the sweep. Whoever takes this bead should decide
whether row 5's enumeration is short by one, or whether HS-23 is correctly outside it.

## Acceptance

One of the three dispositions above is taken and recorded in HS-23's cell in terms — naming the
route it applies to — with `lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md`:56 amended to match if the chosen
disposition changes what that sentence recommends. No row is upgraded from Client-only without
section 2.4's five clauses.
design:
RULING (2026-08-15, delegated decision, operator-reversible): **Disposition 1 — accept the render; docs only.** The implementation is not wrong; the paper is. Both the dossier's original analysis and the Codex second review were weighed; they independently converge on this option, and this ruling adopts it. Options 2 and 3 are REJECTED (reasons below).

THE PRINCIPLE the edits must state: Hicasso server policies attach to DECLARATIONS, and the native tier is the author writing React. `defhost` and `n/defcomponent` are the two declaration doors, both witnessed carrying both arms of the policy on this exact seam (`client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs:461` — the `:server :render` control; `native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs` — the component door). A foreign head under `n/$` has no declaration, so it has no Hicasso policy; React's own server semantics govern, and React renders it. The `[:>]`/`n/$` asymmetry is a principled TIER BOUNDARY, not an inconsistency: the interpreted tier gates undeclared foreign components because hiccup is Hicasso's semantics and an undeclared component must not silently enlarge the matrix (dispositions.md:308-310, note 2); the native tier is explicitly outside that semantics (design-laws.md:11 — "not another Hiccup mode").

Mechanism, independently verified by both reviewers (cite, don't re-derive): the `$` macro passes every non-intrinsic head unchanged to `el`, which calls `React.createElement` directly (`native.cljc:348-363, 967-978, 1029-1052`); `native_grammar_cljs_test.cljs:96-113` pins the resulting head identity. A server policy appears only when `n/defcomponent` mints a component (`native.cljc:519-594`). `[:>]` deliberately interposes the shared Client-only gate (`mint-server-gate`, `native.cljc:468`). Not recent drift: direct `createElement` was the stated design when the native tier landed (`ca1c8800eb`); the hard-gated raw escape predates it (`90f4704c47`). React's own Activity SSR guidance matches the witness: visible content in the response (inside Activity markers), hidden omitted.

EDITS (docs only; the WRITE fence is EXTENDED by this ruling beyond the description's original list):
1. `docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md` — HS-23's operative cell states the per-route policy IN TERMS: Client-only at the `defhost` declaration (witness `client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs:432`); HS-19's hard refusal on `[:>]` (witness `raw_escape_dom_cljs_test.cljs:215`); native transparency on `n/$` — no Hicasso policy on that route, React's own server semantics govern — bytes witnessed (`client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs:488`), no hydration claim made.
2. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md:56` — stop recommending the three routes as interchangeable; state the server difference among them.
3. `react-compatibility-notes.md:16` (canonical matrix default sentence) AND the class row at `:29` — amend "unclassified native component heads default to Client-only": that is the sentence the measurement disproves. This is a policy amendment to the canonical matrix; this ruling is its authority, so the PR must not be bounced for touching those lines.
4. HS-25 stays about `n/defcomponent` and its actual declaration. Do NOT move the foreign `n/$` head into HS-25.

WORDING GUARD (hard constraint): the `n/$` route must NOT be upgraded to "Render". Section 2.4 (dispositions.md:464-477) requires five clauses — deterministic bytes, matching hydration, mismatch attribution, two roots, exact cleanup — and only the bytes are witnessed on this route. Honest phrasing: "no Hicasso policy on this route; React's own server semantics govern — bytes witnessed, no hydration claim made." It is conduct outside Hicasso's declaration policy, not a third hidden declaration policy.

NO CODE: add no runtime branch, wrapper, gate, warning, public option, error id, or duplicate test. No witness is owed — `client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs:488` (`through-n-dollar-a-visible-activity-subtree-reaches-the-response`) IS the witness, landed with rf2-cfriw, already cited by HS-23's cell. Preserve the existing head-identity, raw-escape, and visible/hidden Activity witnesses.

REJECTED — Option 2 (gate `n/$` foreign heads): the `$` macro cannot discriminate a foreign head at expansion, so the gate would be a render-time wrapper fiber on every foreign head — a permanent client-side cost to enforce a server default; it breaks `n/$`'s documented "ALWAYS native React" promise (native.cljc:30); it fights React 4 (design-laws.md:10) and the two-hook ceiling react-compatibility-notes.md:54 already invokes to refuse an adjacent repair; and it would make SSR of native trees containing any foreign component silently emit nothing — a strictly worse server story. Machinery for hypothetical misuse; trust the author who chose the raw tier.
REJECTED — Option 3 (reassign to HS-25): the same measurement disproves HS-25's "Client-only by default" the moment a foreign head is read into that row, so it rewrites two cells instead of one, splits the Activity story across two rows, and still needs this ruling inside HS-25's cell. It moves the contradiction; it settles nothing.

REVISIT TRIGGER: a real consumer bitten in anger by unexpected server execution of a browser-only foreign component under `n/$` (a `renderToString` dying mid-page with no source-located error). If that arrives, price the repair through the ceiling's own adjudication exactly as react-compatibility-notes.md:54 prescribes for its neighbour — never as a quiet gate.

FOLLOW-UP: the adjacent row-5 finding (`lanes/hot-path-architecture.md:49`, deciding-evidence enumeration "HS-24 to HS-30" is short by one ROUTE — HS-23's `n/$` route) stays fenced from this bead and is owned by a separate follow-up bead filed with this ruling (depends on this bead; land after this bead's PR merges).

VERIFICATION (docs/design tree is outside `mkdocs build --strict`): run `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (and `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` covers changed hicasso pages in docs.yml); verify anchors and table column counts by hand and say so in the PR body.
acceptance_criteria: Disposition 1 (accept the render; docs only — see Design for the full ruling) is recorded: (a) HS-23's operative cell in dispositions.md states the per-route policy in terms — Client-only at the defhost declaration, HS-19's hard refusal on [:>], native transparency (no Hicasso policy; React's own server semantics govern) on n/$ — with NO route upgraded to Render (section 2.4's five clauses are not met on n/$; only bytes are witnessed, so the cell says 'bytes witnessed, no hydration claim made'); (b) react-compatibility-notes.md:56 no longer presents the three routes as interchangeable and states the server difference; (c) the canonical matrix default sentence at react-compatibility-notes.md:16 and the class row at :29 are amended for the native-tier carve-out — the WRITE fence is explicitly extended to those lines by the 2026-08-15 ruling; (d) HS-25's cell is untouched (stays a n/defcomponent row); (e) no code changes, no new tests, no new error ids; existing head-identity, raw-escape, and visible/hidden Activity witnesses preserved; (f) scripts/check_doc_slugs.py green, anchors and table column counts hand-verified and stated in the PR body.

title: hic: HS-23's remaining n/$ route has no live owner — dispositions.md says so in terms, and rf2-cfriw has closed
description:
## The finding

Found by **rf2-clldl** (the CHECKPOINT 3 §1 Completeness closure re-run) while closing the
`rf2-9ywe` ledger row, on `main`@`006399e9db`. It is OUTSIDE that bead's ledger-only fence,
so it is filed rather than fixed.

`rf2-9ywe`'s finding text ends *"HS-23 likewise has no witness"*. That sentence is NOT
inside `rf2-9ywe`'s acceptance — the bead's acceptance is about driving the two native hooks
under a real Activity hide/reveal, and its fence names the HS-23 row only conditionally
(*"if the witness lands"*). `rf2-9ywe` closed correctly without touching it, and
`dispositions.md` records that it was right to.

What is left is a real hole with no owner, and `dispositions.md:272` states it in its own
words: HS-23 is honest on ONE of the three routes an author has — through `h/defhost` the
refusal fires at the declaration source, through the raw `[:>]` escape it is HS-19's — but
**through `n/$`, the route `lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md` tells an author to take,
there is no declaration and so no policy to consult: a VISIBLE Activity's subtree reaches the
server response, read and all.** The cell closes: *"no live bead owns that remaining route,
and that cell says so rather than naming an owner"*.

Verified at source rather than taken from the page: `rf2-cfriw` — the bead that
server-rendered the three routes and found the refusal honest on one — is **closed** in the
tracker (re-checked 2026-08-14). So the route named above is owned by nobody.

## Why it matters

`rf2-hic-064` gates on zero unresolved correctness/coverage rows, and `dispositions.md`
§2.1 note 3 is explicit that *an unproved refusal is not a disposition*. A published route
whose policy is 'there is no policy' is exactly that.

## Surface fence

- READ: docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md, lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md,
  implementation/hicasso/**.
- DO NOT touch docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md — it is the ledger keeper's.

## Acceptance

EITHER a witness for the `n/$` route's Activity behaviour under a server render, OR a
source-located disposition saying what that route's policy IS (including 'the subtree renders,
by design') with the sentence in react-compatibility-notes.md amended to match — OR a ruling
that the route needs neither, recorded on the HS-23 row with a named owner.

title: [bug] the derive-the-fence rule prescribes gh pr list --json number,headRefName — which returns branch names, not the files a fence needs
description:
FOUND BY the mayor's method-reread loop, 2026-08-14 23:52 AUSEST, step 2 (check the rules you are ENFORCING against what the tree does). The rule this bead corrects landed only 40 minutes earlier, in PR #8254 (rf2-nnc7a), and its defect was visible in worker reports within the hour.

WHAT THE RULE SAYS. .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md now says: 'DERIVE that enumeration at dispatch time from gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName plus git worktree list, never from your own memory of who you dispatched', and tells the brief to have the worker re-run 'those same two commands' at start-up. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md carries the generic half.

THE DEFECT. --json number,headRefName returns BRANCH NAMES. A fence is about FILES. A branch name cannot tell you whether a PR holds one file or a whole tree, so a mayor following this rule exactly still writes a fence by guessing which files a branch probably touches -- which is the same guess the rule was written to eliminate, one step further in.

MEASURED, three times in one hour, by three different workers who each ignored the prescribed command and checked files instead:
- worker/ssrseed-lb1xi: 'The brief's sharpest fence was wider than reality: implementation/hicasso/** was NOT held as a tree -- #8255 held four named files, and neither check_guide_samples.py nor the SSR test was among them, so I could take the witness.' The over-broad fence would have cost real coverage.
- worker/dispnote-zg5oy: 'the brief's list was stale in both directions... The brief's ssrseed-lb1xi, globals-9ccio and ledger-clldl fences have no open PR behind them.'
- worker/globals-9ccio: 'Only two PRs were open... #8255 (implementation/hicasso/deps.edn + scripts, NOT src). Neither touched my file.'

All three phrased it the same way -- they checked the changed FILES, not the branch NAMES. The rule is being routed around by every worker that follows it correctly, which is the clearest possible signal that the prescribed command is wrong rather than the rule.

THE FIX, verified in this repository at 2026-08-14 23:52 before filing. gh pr list accepts 'files' in --json, in ONE call, so the correction costs nothing:

  gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,files

Sample output confirming it works here:
  #8261 worker/globals-9ccio files=1
  #8260 worker/ssrseed-lb1xi files=3
  #8259 worker/dispnote-zg5oy files=1

EDIT 1 -- .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md: change the prescribed command to include 'files', and add one clause saying the fence is written from the FILE LISTS, not the branch names -- a branch name cannot distinguish a PR holding four named files from one holding a whole tree, and the over-broad direction costs coverage while the under-broad direction costs a conflict.

EDIT 2 -- docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md: the generic layer must gain the PRINCIPLE without the command. Something like: a fence is a claim about FILES, so derive it from what each open change actually touches rather than from its name. KEEP THE LAYERS APART -- no tool name, no flag, no repository detail in the generic tree; that tree is published for other projects and currently contains none.

DO NOT expand this into a fence-checking script or a registry. rf2-6ng7's standing (c)-narrow ruling forbids new machinery for this class, and the repair here is one flag and one sentence.

WHY THE MAYOR DID NOT JUST EDIT IT: the mayor checkout's pre-commit hook refuses commits to worker-tracked surfaces, which is the hook working as docs/the-mayor-method/README.md predicts.

FENCE: .claude/commands/ and docs/the-mayor-method/ are a shared surface; check for an open PR against either tree before dispatching.

title: hicasso: a server render leaves a permanent !frame-ops row per request
description:
Found while writing globals.md's request-scope disposition (rf2-8ylqp). NO ISOLATION DEFECT — this is retention.

re-frame.hicasso.server/render mints a fresh per-request frame id via
fresh-frame-id's (gensym "request-"), and destroys the frame in a finally.

impl.collector/run-once binds (frame-dispatch frame-kw) UNCONDITIONALLY around
every boundary body (collector.cljs:1609), so every server-rendered boundary
reaches impl.frames/frame-row. For a live frame the incarnation token is
non-nil and no row exists yet, so frame-row takes its :else branch and does
(swap! !frame-ops assoc frame-kw fresh) at frames.cljs:122.

Nothing removes it. frame-row's ONLY eviction is the successor's first lookup
for the SAME key — the rf2-hic-013 mechanism, which works because a client
frame id is reused across incarnations. A gensym has no successor. And
forget-frame-ops! (frames.cljs:132-134) is documented RESET AND HYGIENE ONLY:
'The sole runtime caller is the whole-runtime reset; the rest are test
fixtures' — that caller is impl.collector/reset-runtime! (collector.cljs:2068),
a fixture door. rf/destroy-frame! is core's and nothing hicasso-side hooks it
(the only occurrence in src is server.cljs:363, the call itself).

So a long-lived Node SSR process retains one !frame-ops row per request served,
each holding that request's captured dispatch bundle keyed by an id that can
never recur. Linear growth in requests served.

CONTRAST: !entries has the same per-request write pattern and is FINE.
render-body calls entry-for on every body run so entries ARE minted on the
server, but they are never claimed (S1: useSyncExternalStore never calls
subscribe), so refs stays 0 and arm-entry-reaper!'s setTimeout at
entry-reap-horizon-ms drops each one. Bounded by requests-per-horizon.
!frame-ops has no equivalent.

SURFACE: implementation/hicasso/src — impl/frames.cljs and/or server.cljs.
Candidate repairs, not ruled between:
  (a) server/render calls frames/forget-frame-ops! with the frame-kw arity in
      its finally, beside destroy-frame! — the one-arity door already exists;
  (b) frame-row evicts a row whose frame-incarnation-token has gone nil;
  (c) a destruction hook on the core side.
(a) is the smallest and keeps the cost on the module that mints the gensyms;
note frames.cljs's own docstring argues eviction-on-destruction was measured to
'make the fault universal rather than to cure it', so (b) needs that measurement
re-read before it is chosen.

ACCEPTANCE: a witness rendering N requests in one process shows @!frame-ops
bounded rather than growing with N; whichever repair is chosen, frames.cljs's
docstring on why eviction is not the safety mechanism stays accurate.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. globals.md's request-scope section (rf2-8ylqp) already
names this bead as the repair's home.
close_reason:
PR #8274. MECHANISM VERIFIED AT SOURCE, premise holds in every particular: !frame-ops is impl.frames' (frames.cljs:72), frame-row's ONLY eviction is its :else branch (the successor's first lookup), forget-frame-ops!'s 1-arity has NO src caller (the sole runtime caller is collector/reset-runtime! on the 0-arity at collector.cljs:2068, a fixture door), and rf/destroy-frame! occurs once in hicasso src at server.cljs:363 with nothing hicasso-side hooking it. inventory.cljs only counts the table, tool.cljs only reads its keys. No missed eviction path.

OWNER CHOSEN: FRAME DESTRUCTION, not the server render path. The row is per-INCARNATION state (a capture-frame bundle + the closure over it, both pinned), so it is dead the moment that incarnation is, whoever created the frame and however the id was spelled; the per-request gensym is bounded as a CONSEQUENCE rather than as a special case, and a client app minting per-route / per-test ids that never recur is fixed by the same line. impl.frames now publishes :hicasso/on-frame-destroyed! on core's late-bind registry and destroy-frame! fires it at step 7, one line below the :freehand/on-frame-destroyed! sibling that releases Freehand's frame-keyed ledger for the same reason. NO NEW MACHINERY: ten artefacts already reach teardown through that registry, both other view substrates among them. No reaper, TTL, weak-ref or counter. No incarnation token needed unlike Freehand's, and that is a claim: a same-id successor is constructable only AFTER the step-10 dissoc, so every row standing at step 7 is already a dead incarnation's.

BEAD CANDIDATE (b) REJECTED ON MECHANISM, not on the NC6 docstring: evicting a row whose token has gone nil is LOOKUP-driven, and the whole defect is that a per-request gensym is never looked up again. It fixes nothing here. Candidate (a) was unavailable anyway (server.cljs was fenced by PR #8266 at dispatch; that PR has since merged with a docstring-only change).

ACCEPTANCE MET. frames.cljs's docstring stays accurate and now separates the two claims explicitly: eviction-on-destruction remains REJECTED as the reincarnation SAFETY mechanism (PR #7749 NC6, lazy replacement is still the whole safety argument), and is ADDED as a retention bound -- dropping an already-unreachable row earlier changes no lookup's answer.

WITNESS proven both ways on the FINAL code: frame_ops_retention_cljs_test.cljs, two rows each with its own non-vacuity control (section 1 asserts the row is PRESENT via collector/frame-dispatch before asking whether destroy removes it; section 2's control is collector/body-runs). Sabotage -- the single set-fn! line commented out, restored and verified by git hash-object 3cc94797 before and after -- gives captured exit 1 / 3 failures (row survives destroy; 1 request leaves 1 row; 3 more leave 4). Restored: captured exit 0, 0 failures.

GATES (captured exit codes, never the harness's): hicasso node lane 0 (1207 tests / 4906 assertions), hicasso JVM 0 (3/92), core late-bind-drift 0 (8/677), test:hicasso-invariants 0, test:hicasso-lint 0, check_doc_slugs 0, check_provenance_pins 0, test-fast-pr.sh 0 (PASS, its CLJS lane 13916 tests / 70277 assertions) -- spine on the pre-rebase base, every surface-touching gate re-run on the final base 98198076c5.

title: hicasso: the SSR request-scope question globals.md deferred is now live for all 21 owners
description:
Found by rf2-hic-087's post-kernel mutable-global re-sweep against main@c3a36406b3.

globals.md's closing section, Two things this page does not cover, reads:

  'SSR request scope is vacuous today. ... this package publishes NO server-render door. impl.mount/hydrate-root! is built and witnessed, but its counterpart - re-frame.hicasso.server - does not exist ... Every owner on this page is therefore a PAGE question and not yet a REQUEST question. The day a server-render entry lands, all twenty-one become request-scope questions at once, because a Node process serving two requests concurrently shares every one of them; whoever files that bead should start here.'

THAT DAY HAS COME. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs landed on 2026-08-14 (PR #8236, on main at c3a36406b3), 389 lines, publishing server/render on react-dom/server's renderToString. This is the bead the page asked for; nobody had filed it.

The page's own sharpest caveat names where to start: the two dynamic vars, impl.intent/*dispatch* and impl.intent/*frame*. In ClojureScript binding is with-redefs - a global set! restored in a finally - so it is exactly as safe as the call being synchronous. A Node process interleaving two renderToString calls at an await would have the second request's *frame* visible to the first's continuation, and unlike a keyed table there is no key to tell the two apart.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No defect is claimed and none is known. server.cljs's own docstring argues renderToString is synchronous so one request's render completes before another's begins, and server.cljs itself introduces ZERO module-level owners (verified: the seven census arms find none in that file). This bead is the DISPOSITION the page says is owed, not a bug report.

Any repair the disposition finds necessary is a SEPARATE bead against implementation/hicasso/src, not this one.

close_reason: PR #8261. SETTLED per the bead's own acceptance, not merely framed: all 21 owners have a stated request-scope answer (7 classes covering 19, plus the two dynamic vars argued individually), verified by script -- roster-minus-covered and covered-minus-roster both empty. NO RULING NEEDED: every answer is derivable from the code. THE BEAD'S PREMISE (and the page's) WAS TOO STRONG and correcting it is the deliverable -- the question is NOT live for all 21. The door is renderToString, and a server render runs strictly less of the runtime than a client mount does. The two dynamic vars are argued individually as required, and *dispatch* is bound at two of the three sites, not three -- root-element withholds a dispatch on purpose. title: re-frame.hicasso.server leaks five unrostered helpers into its public API
description:
Found by the merged-PR audit of #8236 at landed 99ca4dfcdd7b28fa54327d3408a524ec1888499a.

The namespace and naming-ledger row 22 promise one product door: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render`. The implementation nevertheless uses ordinary public `defn` for `fresh-frame-id`, `setup-events`, `payload-script`, `document`, and `render-twice` in addition to `render`; only `render-options` is private. These mechanics/test helpers therefore become discoverable API even though no guide, inventory row, or naming decision owns them.

This matters pre-alpha: accidental publics become compatibility pressure and make the minimal optional-module API harder to understand. `render` already returns the useful intermediate values, so callers do not need lifecycle/test mechanics merely to customize their HTTP shell.

NARROW REPAIR. Keep internal mechanics private. If `document` or `payload-script` is intentionally an extension hook, explicitly roster and document that choice; otherwise make it private too. Reuse an existing public-surface check if a ratchet is cheap—do not mint a new checker just for this namespace.
acceptance_criteria: The intended public var set for re-frame.hicasso.server is explicit; unowned lifecycle/test helpers are private; any deliberately public composition helper is named in the product contract; existing focused tests still exercise determinism and document construction without widening the supported API accidentally.

title: mayor-dispatch.md does not say to DERIVE the in-flight fence at dispatch time — the mayor shipped stale fences twice in one session
description:
FOUND BY the mayor's method-reread loop, 2026-08-14 22:53 AUSEST, step 2 (check the rules you are ENFORCING against what the tree does). This is a defect in the ENFORCING layer, caused by the mayor and observed by workers.

WHAT THE COMMAND FILE SAYS TODAY. .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md tells the mayor to give each dispatch 'an explicit file-ownership fence + enumerate other in-flight clusters' surfaces'. It does not say where that enumeration COMES FROM, and it does not say the worker should re-derive it.

WHAT HAPPENED, TWICE, MEASURED. The mayor enumerated fences from its own memory of who it had dispatched, rather than deriving them at dispatch time. Both times the list had gone stale inside the dispatch's own lifetime:

1. rf2-hic-038's brief named four live workers holding surfaces. The worker reported: 'The brief's fence list was also stale: the bead's fence (propbugs-42vlw, uixinterop-ap7w, hookwit-sr19) had CLEARED -- all three merged -- and only one of the brief's four named workers had an open PR.' It re-derived and proceeded; the cost was one re-derivation.
2. Several later briefs named worker/X as live when X had already reported done and merged. Under a six-worker fleet with an 11-minute merge cadence, a fence list is stale in roughly the time it takes to write the brief.

WHY IT MATTERS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is the part worth writing down. A STALE-BROAD fence costs a re-derivation and some confusion -- the worker is told to avoid a file nobody holds. A STALE-NARROW fence is the dangerous one: it omits a worker dispatched after the mayor last looked, and two workers on one file merge-conflict and can silently revert each other. The same defect produces both, and only the second is expensive.

THE FIX, and it is two sentences in one file. In .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, at the point where it says to enumerate other in-flight clusters' surfaces, add that the mayor DERIVES that list at dispatch time from 'gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName' plus 'git worktree list' rather than from memory of what it dispatched -- and that the brief must TELL THE WORKER to re-derive the same two commands at start-up and treat what it finds as authoritative over the brief's list. The second half is what makes the rule robust rather than merely correct: a list written even one minute before the worker starts can be wrong by the time it reads it, so the worker needs standing permission to override it, not just an accurate list.

The mayor has already been adding that instruction to briefs by hand since 22:40. This bead is to put it in the file so it stops depending on one mayor remembering.

KEEP THE TWO LAYERS APART. This is a fix to .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md ONLY. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 2 carries the GENERIC body and deliberately names no tool, command or repository -- its existing text ('items whose surface a live worker holds' in the filter-out list) is correct and must NOT gain a command name. If the generic layer needs anything at all it is at most a clause saying a fence list is derived rather than remembered; weigh whether even that earns its place, because the method tree's value is that it carries no mechanics.

WHY THE MAYOR DID NOT JUST EDIT IT: the mayor checkout's pre-commit hook refuses commits to worker-tracked surfaces, which is the hook working as docs/the-mayor-method/README.md predicts.

FENCE: .claude/commands/ and docs/the-mayor-method/ are a shared surface; two concurrent editors there conflict by construction. Check for an open PR against either tree before dispatching -- PR #8238 held it earlier today and has merged.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8254. .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md now carries both halves at the enumerate-in-flight-surfaces point: the mayor DERIVES the list at dispatch time from 'gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName' plus 'git worktree list' and never from memory of who it dispatched, and the brief must TELL THE WORKER to re-run those same two commands at start-up and treat what it finds as authoritative over the brief's list. The asymmetry is written down as the reason the second half is the load-bearing one: stale-BROAD costs one re-derivation, stale-NARROW omits a worker dispatched after the mayor last looked and two workers on one file merge-conflict and can silently revert each other; accuracy alone cannot reach the second because it expires between writing the brief and reading it. GENERIC LAYER — I departed from the bead's lean, and here is why. The bead is right that the DERIVE half is already generic: step 3 of 'Write the brief in this order' says 'Establish the fence by asking who is live, not what is open'. What was absent is the WORKER-RE-DERIVES half plus the cost asymmetry, which is method rather than mechanics, and which completes a pattern the page already establishes — the page tells the worker the brief's premises are claims to re-check at source, and the fence was the one premise not covered by it. So docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md's Fences section gains ONE paragraph naming no command, tool, repository, PR number, bead id, path or OS mechanic; leak-grepped and clean. loops.md untouched. This bead's own rule was applied to its PR: fence re-derived at start-up (23:03) and again at push (23:11), by listing each open PR's changed files rather than reading branch names.

title: hic: rf2-hic-085's closure question is now unowned — rf2-iay8 was ruled and deliberately left S6/C2 standing custody untouched
description:
FOUND BY rf2-hic-085's own doc-side execution pass (2026-08-14). Surfaced, not
decided: this is an operator question, and the recorder does not rule it.

THE THREAD THAT NOW DANGLES. rf2-hic-085's notes say, in terms: "WHAT WOULD
ACTUALLY CLOSE IT is a ruling on rf2-iay8: what is the Authority column FOR? ...
That question is with Mike."

rf2-iay8 has since been RULED and CLOSED (PR #8142, commit 768ab8f3dc). The
ruling is the two-mode rule, now written into budgets.md beside the Authority
definition: a live route while a transition remains; the deciding bead, closed
or not, once the recorded state is settled; the discriminator is never bead
liveness.

But that ruling explicitly declined to settle this bead. Its close reason says
"rf2-hic-085's S6/C2 standing custody untouched", and it repointed nothing.
budgets.md :1100 (S6) and :1110 (C2) still name rf2-hic-085 today.

SO THE POINTER IS STALE IN THE WAY THAT MATTERS. A future reader follows
rf2-hic-085's notes to rf2-iay8, finds it closed, and reasonably concludes the
closure question was answered. It was not — it was answered for S1/S2/C5 and
left open here.

WHY IT CANNOT BE CLOSED BY A WORKER. rf2-hic-085's acceptance criteria reads
"Closure requires an explicit K1 amendment-route successor for S6/C2". The K1
amendment route IS rf2-hic-085 (k1-price-acceptance.md:162 — "rf2-hic-085,
which owns that field, is the only route to a change"), so a successor would be
this same standing recorder under a second id, which the bead's own audit note
forbids. PR #8134's body recorded the same contradiction and handed it up.

THE QUESTION. Under the now-ruled two-mode rule, are S6 and C2 in mode one (a
live route remains, so rf2-hic-085 stays named and stays open) or mode two (the
recorded state is settled — K1 is RATIFIED and its amendment window closed on
2026-08-13 — so a closed id is acceptable and rf2-hic-085 may close)?

Both readings are defensible on the text. Mode two is arguable because
k1-price-acceptance.md:162 records the amendment window as CLOSED, leaving only
back-fills, which are not amendments. Mode one is arguable because the same
sentence names this bead the only route to a change, and a route is a live
thing.

WHAT IS NOT AT ISSUE. No figure, threshold, verdict, ceiling or row status
turns on this, and nothing is blocked behind it. Both governance records are
complete: k1-price-acceptance.md:115 and k3-disposition.md:401 both carry
filled effective-revision fields. This is a tracker-hygiene and
records-legibility question only.

DO NOT resolve this by filing a successor bead — that is the move the audit
note forbids and it would recreate the same shape one id along.
close_reason: RULED (2026-08-15, delegated, operator-reversible): S6/C2 are SETTLED MODE under the two-mode Authority rule — the K1 disposition is a taken, complete ruling carrying its own 7.1/7.2 machinery, and a remaining contingency is not a live transition (parallel: S1/S2/C5 on closed rf2-0xx2). rf2-hic-085's standing custody retires; it closes only AFTER rf2-10lyy's alignment PR (beside-amend k1 s9 + budgets.md :1044-1063 + :1229-1242; Authority cells byte-unchanged) verifiably MERGES. No successor recorder. K4/K6 carried open in the record alone (validation.md kill table), trigger-driven. Full ruling, preserved counterpoints, reopen evidence and rejected findings: this bead's final comment.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULING (2026-08-15, delegated per this bead's dispatch; operator-reversible on sight): S6 and C2 are in SETTLED MODE under the two-mode Authority rule (rf2-iay8, PR #8142). rf2-hic-085's standing custody is retired; it closes AFTER the alignment PR carried by rf2-10lyy MERGES (closing condition below). Its Authority cells stay byte-unchanged, naming rf2-hic-085 as the bead that TOOK the recording — exactly parallel to S1/S2/C5 keeping closed rf2-0xx2. NO successor recorder is filed: the audit-note prohibition is honoured, not routed around.

THE TEST, ON THE RULE'S OWN TERMS. The discriminator is never bead liveness; it is whether a live transition remains (budgets.md:1044-1063). S6/C2's disposition — the K1 price acceptance, RATIFIED 2026-08-13, effective revision filled — is a taken, complete ruling carrying its own reopen (7.1) and revert (7.2) machinery: the settled-mode test verbatim. What remains is a contingency (a possible future amendment or reopen), and a contingency is not a live transition — it is the same state S1/S2/C5 are in, which rf2-iay8 itself ruled settled. The live-route reading rests on document sentences naming the bead as the route; but those sentences are the only thing keeping it "live" — the bead is called live because the documents say it must stay open, and the documents say so because the cells name the bead. That circularity is broken by amending the documents (pre-alpha, no back-compat), and bd reopen rf2-hic-085 preserves the same-id address forever: closure loses no route.

WHAT DECIDED IT beyond the text: the open sentinel's cost is demonstrated, not hypothetical — one wrong close, one wrong stranded-sweep status flip, and repeated re-litigation across mayor/audit cycles in six days. It monitors no witness, catches no lapse, enforces no handoff (check_budget_ledger.py reads the cell for shape, not life). And every 7.1 reopen returns the record to the decider by the record's own machinery regardless of any bead. A governance sentinel that exists only to be re-explained is itself a cost.

FOUR OPINIONS WEIGHED (two dossiers, each with a Codex review): this bead's dossier argued live-route; the rf2-hic-085 dossier and both Codex reviews argued settled. Settled wins on the discriminator, not by vote.

CLOSING CONDITION for rf2-hic-085 — rf2-10lyy's PR, docs/design/hicasso/product/ only, must MERGE first (until it lands the documents describe live-route, and closing would create the exact defect class the two-mode rule names):
1. Dated beside-amendment to k1-price-acceptance.md section 9 (:162): the route to a future change becomes the escape-hatch pattern — when a concrete amendment is proposed, file a named route bead scoped to that amendment; 7.1/7.2 return the record to the decider regardless. Logged in section 9's own amendment table. No threshold, verdict, or figure touched.
2. Beside-amend budgets.md :1044-1063 — S6/C2 leave the live-route example list; the "worked example" sentence records the retirement. The definition's discriminator text is untouched.
3. Beside-amend budgets.md section 9.2's S6/C2 paragraph (:1229-1242), which currently says the opposite ("stays open while this record stands").
4. Authority cells S6 (:1100) and C2 (:1110) stay exactly rf2-hic-085, byte-unchanged.
5. correction-ledger.md:123's row transition is the ledger keeper's per that file's own protocol; this ruling does not override it.

K4/K6, ruled explicitly so custody is not silently dropped: both stay carried open IN THE RECORD alone (validation.md's kill table), trigger-driven, with no bead custodian. K4's criterion text stands and still bites (WebKit half discharged by rf2-hic-016; the wider matrices landed green with rf2-hic-040, closed 2026-08-14). K6 activates only if a compiler/analyzer/dual mode is ever proposed as necessary to meet K1-K3. rf2-hic-085's close reason must restate both triggers.

THE LOSING SIDE'S STRONGEST POINTS, preserved on the record:
(a) k1 section 9's present-tense "rf2-hic-085 ... is the only route to a change" is a forward-looking normative sentence that a closed bead falsifies — which is exactly why the alignment PR is a hard PRECONDITION of closure, not optional cleanup.
(b) 7.1's three un-fired reopen conditions and 7.2's still-unwitnessed lapse (owed by open rf2-hic-011/025/074) are genuinely live machinery, and :150 names 7.1 "the live path in the meantime". Answered: that machinery returns the record to the decider by its own text and needs no tracker sentinel to function; nothing watched the trigger even while the bead sat open.
(c) Amending the two-mode definition's worked example two days after it landed risks churning precedent. Answered: the definition's discriminator is untouched; only the example's classification moves, and it moves BY the definition's own test — applying a rule to its own worked example strengthens it.

REOPEN EVIDENCE — what would put this question back on the table: a 7.1 condition actually firing (most plausibly a new clean clock-of-record row once rf2-85og2's deferred measurement lane runs) or a 7.2 lapse, WITH the on-demand route then proving slow or confusing in practice. The fix at that point is the escape hatch's own answer — a named route bead scoped to that concrete change — a per-record repair, not a reversal of this ruling.

REJECTED, and why: (a) this dossier's claim that live-route "changes no document and costs nothing" — the six-day re-litigation record refutes the cost half, and a permanent tax accepted to avoid a one-time small diff is the wrong trade; (b) the "deferred contradiction" objection — a change-scoped route bead filed when an amendment is concretely proposed is not the forbidden successor shape (that shape is STANDING custody under a second id); (c) the leaner execution boundary in this dossier's Codex review, insofar as it would leave k1 section 9 naming a closed bead as the sole route — that sentence is normative and must be beside-amended before close (the rf2-hic-085 dossier's fuller three-site scope is adopted); (d) the rf2-hic-085 dossier's Options C (hold the full sitting now — over-scope while the measurement lane is deferred by operator direction) and D (decide nothing — the tax continues).

MAYOR/OPERATOR ACTIONS (none performed by this ruling agent): dispatch rf2-10lyy (SEQUENCE it against rf2-3e4iq — both edit budgets.md); at rf2-10lyy's verified MERGE (not PR-open — this bead's history shows why), close rf2-hic-085 citing this ruling; the correction-ledger row transition per its own protocol. Both decision dossiers (ai/decisions/rf2-4h0l8.s6-c2-custody-mode.md, ai/decisions/rf2-hic-085.standing-custody-or-close.md) deleted after both beads verifiably carry this ruling.

title: Add a nightly full-corpus provenance-pin audit now that the backlog is clear (rf2-g7m6y ruling (b))
description:
RULING FROM rf2-g7m6y, which fixed the 7 findings and STOPPED at the workflow edit because .github/workflows/* was fenced to another live worker. This bead is the (b) half.

WHAT CHANGED THAT MAKES THIS POSSIBLE. docs.yml lines 561-567 record why the gate is scoped to changed pages, and the reason is NOT cost: 'The corpus still carries the stranded pins the census catalogued and left standing ... A full-corpus gate would therefore be red on main from the day it landed. Scoped, it holds every new and edited page to the rule from today, and the audit (python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py, no flag) reports the backlog for whoever works it off.'

That backlog has now been worked off. As of PR for rf2-g7m6y the full-corpus run is exit 0, 0 findings, 107 pages / 482 cited pins. The documented blocker has expired.

WHY (b) AND NOT (a). The scoped job responds to one trigger: a page appearing in the PR diff. Every one of the 7 findings arrived by a route that trigger cannot see, and there are two such routes:
 1. LEGACY. All 5 finding pages were last edited 2026-07-31..2026-08-06, and the gate landed 2026-08-06 22:52 (4b9ee1f811). The census repair sweep ca831062aa landed 22:14 — 38 minutes EARLIER — so the page that sweep itself repaired still carried a finding and CI has never once inspected it.
 2. HARDENING, and this one recurs. The checker gained rules six times in eight days (rf2-kqac1 x3, rf2-xlsh x2, rf2-styo x2, rf2-dmrm x2, rf2-qfrrp). Each hardening reclassifies the WHOLE corpus, but only touched pages are re-checked, so each one silently mints a fresh backlog on pages nobody edits.
Neither trigger is a page edit, so (a) guarantees the next silent backlog.

WHY (b) AND NOT (c). (c) is now possible (corpus is green) but couples every future gate-hardening PR to a corpus-wide repair — and the gate refuses to re-pin by design, so each repair needs a human. That is exactly the 'punish the careful ones and be routed around within a week' pressure the checker's own docstring names. (c) also blocks docs PRs on pages they did not touch. Cost is not the discriminator (full run ~58s); blast radius is.

SUGGESTED HOME: .github/workflows/lint.yml. It already runs nightly (cron '30 3 * * *') and already checks out with fetch-depth: 0.

fetch-depth: 0 IS LOAD-BEARING — do not drop it. Per docs.yml:556-559 the gate asks 'merge-base --is-ancestor' about SHAs months old, so a shallow or depth-limited clone answers 'not an ancestor' for pins that are perfectly landed and reds the whole corpus.

Invocation is exactly: python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py   (no flag = full corpus). Nightly only; do NOT add it to the PR path.

NO NEW MACHINERY (rf2-6ng7): one step in an existing scheduled workflow. No meta-checker, no roster, no drift detector.

ALSO STALE, same edit: the docs.yml comment at 561-567 still asserts a full-corpus gate 'would be red on main from the day it landed'. Once this lands that sentence should say the backlog was cleared by rf2-g7m6y and the nightly now holds the corpus.

title: hicasso: re-frame.hicasso.server names a zero-rent guard that does not cover it
description:
Found by rf2-hic-072's aggregate-rent census, re-run at merge base 0e4d0c546f after re-frame.hicasso.server landed (rf2-b6jkj, PR #8236) mid-bead. The first run of the census, one base earlier, could not have found this -- the module did not exist yet.

THE DEFECT IS A FALSE CLAIM IN A SHIPPED MODULE'S OWN DOCSTRING.
implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs lines 8-10 read:

  'The door names it nowhere, so a browser build that never requires it
   carries none of it -- scripts/check_optional_module_reachability.py
   is what keeps that true.'

It is not what keeps that true. That gate does not mention the module:

  grep -c 'hicasso.server' implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_optional_module_reachability.py   -> 0
  grep -c 'hicasso.server' implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_bundle_isolation.cjs              -> 0

The gate's MODULES roster is motion, overlay, native, forms (+ a UIx
forbidden-import rule). The bundle gate's SENTINELS are native x2 and forms x2.
The server module is in neither.

THE PREMISE HOLDS TODAY; ONLY THE GUARD IS MISSING. Every occurrence of
're-frame.hicasso.server' under implementation/hicasso/src/ is prose in a
docstring or comment -- there is no :require of it anywhere outside its own
docstring example, so a browser build really does carry none of it right now.
What is absent is anything that would NOTICE if that changed. The module is the
fourth in a family (its own docstring says so, beside forms, overlay and motion)
and it is the only one of the four with no roster row.

WHY THE DOCSTRING MAKES IT WORSE THAN A PLAIN GAP. A missing row is a hole a
reader can find. A missing row plus a sentence naming the specific script that
allegedly closes it is a hole a reader is actively steered away from -- and the
next person to touch SSR wiring will read that sentence, not the roster.

REMEDY, two parts and the order matters:
1. Add the server module to MODULES in check_optional_module_reachability.py
   (door 're-frame.hicasso.server'; decide whether it has engine namespaces the
   way motion and overlay do, or is door-only the way the native tier is).
2. Only then is the docstring sentence true. Do not fix the docstring by
   softening it -- the sentence describes the right design, and the gate is
   what is missing.

RELATED: rf2-ot28g (motion and overlay have no BUNDLE-side sentinel). Same
census, different instrument. With server counted, the aggregate rent coverage
is 4 of 5 optional surfaces source-side and 2 of 5 bundle-side.

FENCE. rf2-hic-072 owned only release-scans.md and its scan script; implementation/hicasso/** was another worker's.

Surface: implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_optional_module_reachability.py
close_reason: PR #8255. Added the door-only `server` row to MODULES in check_optional_module_reachability.py, per the bead's remedy part 1 — the roster was missing, not the docstring overreaching (re-derived: grep -c answered 0 against both gates at base ebceb2e8d2). Docstring left untouched per remedy part 2; it is now true. Proof the row bites: a planted :require of re-frame.hicasso.server in the public door reds the gate naming the server module (captured exit 1), while the SAME plant against the roster at HEAD is green (exit 0). Side benefit measured, not assumed: the roster also drives the compile gate (rf2-okhdf), so server.cljs is now compiled by a warnings-fatal :advanced compile that had never reached it — 139 namespaces, 0 warnings, 8 optional-module namespaces.

At the landed SHA 99ca4dfcdd7b28fa54327d3408a524ec1888499a, the new server namespace says `check_optional_module_reachability.py` keeps it out of browser reach, but that script and `check_bundle_isolation.cjs` contain zero `hicasso.server` references; the optional-module gate still exits 0. title: prod-gate-naming-drift is a FIFTH repo-wide walk in jvm-core with the same arming hole (rf2-cujx class)
description:

NOT actioned there: rf2-cujx names exactly four suites, and this file was under an
explicit dispatch fence (open PR #8234) for most of that worker's run.
