implementation/core/test/re_frame/prod_gate_naming_drift_test.clj from a depth-1
.listFiles over one artefact's test tree to a RECURSIVE file-seq from the
implementation root (see its own line ~170 and the docstring at ~25 recording both
prior narrowings). That makes it the same shape as the four suites rf2-cujx just
covered: a repo-wide source WALK that lives in implementation/core/test/, runs only
in jvm-core, and is therefore scheduled only by implementation_jvm.

WHY THAT IS A HOLE. Measured on main at fdaca65075,
bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh <path>:
  implementation/hicasso/src/x.cljs   implementation_jvm=false
  implementation/ssr-node/src/x.cljs  implementation_jvm=false
  implementation/core/src/x.clj       implementation_jvm=true   (control)
So this walk now READS hicasso and ssr-node while nothing in those trees schedules
it -- a violation introduced there merges green and the red lands on main for the
next unrelated implementation PR. That is the rf2-61ar shape and it is exactly what
rf2-cujx closed for the other four.

THE REPAIR IS ONE LINE, BY CONSTRUCTION. PR #8242 added the unconditional
jvm-repo-source-walks job in .github/workflows/test.yml, deliberately shaped as ONE
STEP PER NAMESPACE (a missing namespace inside a multi--n selector is silent --
measured: exit 0, runs the rest, no warning -- so per-namespace steps each take the
quiet runner's default floor of 1 and red on their own). Adding this suite is a
fifth step:
  - name: Production-gate naming drift (recursive walk of implementation/)
    run: clojure -M:test -n re-frame.prod-gate-naming-drift-test
No arming change, no roster change, no new machinery. Cost is one extra JVM start
(~7s; the four existing steps measure 28s total against 15s for a single combined
run).

VERIFY BEFORE ACTING, per the usual rule: re-run the two probes above at trunk tip,
and confirm the namespace still resolves -- #8234 landed hours before this bead and
the file has been rewritten twice.

WIDER QUESTION WORTH ONE RULING, NOT A CHECKER. This is the second time in one day
a walk widened without its arming following (rf2-2cu7f did the same for
impl-source-corpus/src-roots). rf2-6ng7 already REJECTED a universal
input-declaration checker as over-engineering, and that rejection should stand. The
cheap standing answer is the lane itself: any future repo-wide walk in
implementation/core/test/ joins jvm-repo-source-walks as one more step. Worth
stating once, in that job's comment, rather than building a mechanism to detect it.
notes: FENCE CLEARED 2026-08-14 22:57 AUSEST (mayor backlog reread). PR #8242 (worker/armfix-cujx) has MERGED, carrying rf2-cujx, rf2-1gycj and rf2-7v5vx. The classifier surface it held -- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh, implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, .github/workflows/test.yml -- is free. DISPATCHED NOW as a four-bead cluster with rf2-sk5hf, rf2-n4a2b, rf2-in6c4 and rf2-skvce under one owner, because all four touch that same surface and two workers on it conflict by construction. It removed the CONDITIONALITY, adding an unconditional jvm-repo-source-walks job wired into all-required-passed, with the classifier byte-unchanged and the census identical before and after. So a bead here that assumes the repair must be an arming change is reasoning from the superseded shape -- the fourth shape is available and is usually cheaper. title: hicasso: motion and overlay have no bundle-side zero-rent sentinel (2 of 4 optional surfaces)
description:
Found by rf2-hic-072's aggregate-rent census at merge base 94136dbf7a.

THE GAP. Four optional surfaces are covered by the SOURCE-side gate
(check_optional_module_reachability.py: motion, overlay, native, forms all
unreachable from the public door). Only TWO are covered by the BUNDLE-side gate
(check_bundle_isolation.cjs SENTINELS: native tier x2, forms x2). Motion and
overlay have NO sentinel row.

NOT AN INFERENCE FROM SILENCE. 're-frame.hicasso.motion/presence' appears in
check_bundle_isolation.cjs exactly once, at line 453, as a NEAR-MISS CONTROL
STRING in the self-test -- a string the gate is asserted NOT to fire on. So the
file knows the module exists and has chosen not to scan for it.

WHY IT MATTERS, narrowly. The source-side gate is the stronger of the two and
both modules pass it, so this is not a live leak. What is missing is the
confidence the bundle gate exists to add, and check_bundle_isolation.cjs states
it in its own docstring: 'what this one adds is confidence about the COMPILER and
the LINKER: that an unreferenced namespace really does leave nothing behind after
Closure has run, on the real graph, at the real optimisation level.' Motion and
overlay have that confidence for nobody.

REMEDY. Add one load-bearing sentinel per module, paired with a reachable
positive control, per the file's own stated idiom. Each sentinel must be a string
its surface cannot function without (the tier's is an unchecked-set property NAME;
forms' are a view name and an app-db concern keyword) -- a marker planted beside
the code would be dropped by Closure whether or not isolation held, and the gate
would pass for the wrong reason. Whether motion/overlay have ONE reachability
shape or two is the design question to settle first: forms has one (registers at
namespace load), the native tier has two.

ALSO NOTE, and it may want its own bead: re-frame.hicasso.server (PR #8236, in
flight at the time of this census) reaches NEITHER roster. If it ships as an
optional module it owes rows in both.

is why rf2-hic-072 filed rather than fixed.

title: [bug] check_provenance_pins.py is red on main — 7 findings across 5 studio pages, invisible because CI scopes to changed pages
description:
FOUND BY worker/codecarm-m4rpa (PR #8235, 2026-08-14 21:50 AUSEST) while running its own gates. Reported unprompted, out of that bead's fence, and filed rather than fixed. THIS IS A CLAIM, NOT A FINDING -- re-run the gate at source before acting on it.

THE REPORT: a FULL-CORPUS run of scripts/check_provenance_pins.py reds today with 7 pre-existing findings across 5 pages under docs/design/hicasso/studio/ -- 2 described as unresolvable and 5 as stranded. The worker's own scoped run passed: 'check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main = exit 0, 4 pages / 60 pins / 0 findings'. So the two runs disagree, and both are correct about different questions.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE, AND WHY THAT IS THE INTERESTING HALF. The docs.yml job scopes the checker to CHANGED pages. That is a reasonable design -- it keeps a PR accountable for what it touched -- but it means the corpus can rot without any PR ever going red, because a page nobody edits is a page nobody checks. This is the same fail-open shape as rf2-cujx and rf2-2cu7f, one surface over: a gate that is armed, runs, and reports green having verified only a subset. Note the difference from those two, because it changes the repair: there the walk was accidentally narrow, here the scoping is DELIBERATE and defensible, so the question is not 'widen the walk' but 'what reads the corpus, and when'.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is a cost ruling rather than a mechanism:
(a) fix the 7 findings and leave the scoping alone -- cheapest, but the corpus rots again the moment a page goes unedited;
(b) fix the 7 and add a periodic (nightly / release) full-corpus run -- catches rot without charging every PR for the whole corpus;
(c) fix the 7 and make the PR job full-corpus -- simplest to reason about, but every PR then pays for, and can be blocked by, pages it did not touch.

READ THE 2 'UNRESOLVABLE' FINDINGS FIRST. If a pin genuinely cannot be resolved, the honest repair may be to record why on the page rather than to satisfy the checker -- and that answer changes which of (a)/(b)/(c) is even coherent. Do not pick an option before reading them.

FIRST STEP: re-run 'python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py' with no --changed-since at current main and reproduce the 7. If the count differs, say so -- a count is a claim and this one was measured on a worker's branch, not on main.

FENCE: docs/design/hicasso/studio/ is edited by several workers. Check for live holders before dispatching.
close_reason:
Reproduced on origin/main (exactly 7 findings, 2 unresolvable + 5 stranded — the claim held), fixed all 7, and ruled (b). Full corpus now exit 0 / 0 findings; scoped run exit 0. PR #8246.

The 2 unresolvable were misclassified DIGESTS, not broken pins: 22e7e6f4... is a blob per git cat-file, and 83b865f8 is an FNV-1a-32 the page names in its own sentence (nearest left word was 'stamps'). Repaired in prose — no pin re-pointed, no figure moved. The 5 stranded got their landed SHA, each verified twice (identical patch-id AND the page's own named blobs resolving there).

RULING (b), and (a) is refuted empirically rather than on taste: the scoped job triggers only on a page appearing in a PR diff, and none of the 7 arrived that way. All 5 pages were last edited BEFORE the gate landed (gate 4b9ee1f811 at 08-06 22:52; the census repair sweep ca831062aa at 22:14, 38 min earlier — so the page that sweep itself repaired still carried a finding and CI never once inspected it). Second, recurring vector: the checker hardened six times in eight days, and each hardening reclassifies the whole corpus while only touched pages are re-checked.

The documented blocker for a wider gate has expired: docs.yml:561-567 scoped it because 'a full-corpus gate would be red on main from the day it landed' and nominated the unflagged run as the manual audit 'for whoever works it off'. That backlog is now worked off. (c) rejected over (b) because it couples every future gate-hardening PR to a corpus-wide human-decided repair — the 'routed around within a week' pressure the checker's own docstring names — and blocks docs PRs on pages they did not touch; a full run is ~58s, so blast radius is the discriminator, not cost.

WORKFLOW EDIT NOT DONE — .github/workflows/* fenced to worker/armfix-cujx. Filed as rf2-qpk2l (one nightly step in lint.yml, which already has cron + fetch-depth: 0).

title: [bug] impl-src-roots walks implementation/*/src at depth 1 only, so both conformance gates skip the entire adapters tree (14 production files)
description:
FOUND BY worker/walkroots-cujx while measuring rf2-cujx. NOT the arming defect rf2-cujx
describes — this one is a fail-open INSIDE the gate, and no arming change fixes it.

THE DEFECT. `impl-src-roots` in
implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj (~line 280)
enumerates artefact source roots as `.listFiles(implementation/)` mapped to `<dir>/src`.
That is DEPTH 1 ONLY. The four adapter artefacts nest one level deeper —
implementation/adapters/{reagent,reagent-slim,uix,test-react}/src — so they are not roots
and are never walked. egress_chokepoint_conformance_test.clj reuses the same
`impl-src-roots` / `non-test-source-files`, so it inherits the hole.

MEASURED, by calling the suite's OWN non-test-source-files (not a reproduction) at 704bf0dc9c:
  error-catalogue / egress   377 files walked, 16 roots, ADAPTER FILES = 0
  no_rf_default floor lint   835 files walked, adapters = 14, tools = 410
  warn_once governance       425 files walked, adapters = 14, tools = 0
The two file-seq-over-implementation-root suites reach adapters correctly; only the two
`impl-src-roots` consumers miss them. 14 production .clj/.cljc/.cljs files are invisible.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ARMING HOLE. implementation/adapters/*/src DOES arm
implementation_jvm=true (probed). So on an adapter PR the gate is armed, jvm-core runs,
both conformance suites execute, walk past the adapter tree entirely, and report GREEN. An
uncatalogued :rf.error/* channel or an unrouted payload-bearing egress fan-out added in an
adapter passes both ratchets today. rf2-cujx's exposure at least requires an unarmed tier;
this one fails open with the gate fully armed and running.

REPAIR (cheap, local, no arming change). Make the root enumeration reach nested artefacts —
either walk `implementation/` for any directory named `src` not under `/test/` (the shape
the other two suites already use and which demonstrably reaches all 14), or add an explicit
second level for `adapters/*`. Prefer the former: it cannot re-drift when the next artefact
nests. Then assert the walked set is NON-EMPTY for adapters so the hole cannot silently
reopen — the suites currently have no floor on what they walk, which is why this was
invisible.

EXPECT NEW FINDINGS when the tree is actually walked: 14 previously unscanned production
files enter two conformance ratchets at once. A resulting red is the gate doing its job,
not a regression — do not re-narrow the walk to go green.

Its docstring names this bead and states the property the bead asked for -- 'Depth-independent BY CONSTRUCTION (rf2-2cu7f): implementation/core/src sits at depth 1, implementation/adapters/reagent/src at depth 2, and a future artefact may nest deeper still.' title: No :advanced build compiles the optional overlay module — externs regressions in optional modules are structurally uncaught
description:
FOUND BY rf2-9zz0y's worker (2026-08-14), unasked, while fixing four pre-existing infer-warnings in impl/overlay.cljs.

THE GAP. The :hicasso-release :advanced build's entry point does not reach the optional overlay module. Measured: grep -c anchorName on the produced bundle answers ZERO. So no advanced-compiled artefact in this repository contains that module's code at all.

WHY THAT MATTERS AND IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY. The four warnings the worker fixed were on (.. el -style -anchorName) — an un-externable property access. Under :advanced those would have been MANGLED, silently breaking the trigger claim at runtime in a way no test sees, because no test compiles that code under :advanced. The worker fixed them with ^js hints and took browser warnings from 8 to 4. But the CLASS remains: any externs regression in any optional module ships uncaught.

THE SHAPE IS FAMILIAR AND IS THE DAY'S RECURRING THEME. A gate that never compiles a module reports nothing about it, and absence reads as green — the same family as a browser gate passing over a namespace that failed to compile, and a provenance gate exiting 0 having inspected zero files. Three instances, one shape: silence mistaken for a pass.

WHAT A FIX MIGHT BE, none preferred and all needing a look at source: add an :advanced build whose entry reaches every optional module, purely to compile them; or assert in the release gate that the bundle contains a symbol from each optional module; or have the module roster itself drive an advanced-compile check, so a new optional module is covered by construction. The third is most in keeping with how this repository has closed sibling gaps today — the roster becomes the authority rather than a hand-maintained list.

DO NOT WIDEN THIS INTO A GENERAL BUILD-COVERAGE AUDIT. The finding is specific and measured: optional modules are not advanced-compiled anywhere. Fix that, and report anything else you notice rather than absorbing it.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST — confirm the bundle really lacks the module and that the entry really does not reach it. It is a claim, and four of my own measurements were refuted by workers today.
close_reason:
Re-closed on all three checks (mayor, 2026-08-14). (a) DELIVERABLE: the module roster now drives the compile coverage — three files carry the roster emission and its reader; PR #8219 MERGED. (b) OBLIGATIONS: zero markers. (c) SIBLING: rf2-swhjb carries the residual this worker found in its OWN contribution and is separately dispatched.

TWO OF MY PREMISES WERE REFUTED BY THIS WORK AND THE CORRECTIONS ARE THE VALUABLE PART. First, the modules ARE compiled — twice — but one build disables inference and the other infers and then exits 0, because that compiler exits 0 on warnings. The gap was never coverage: COMPILED IN TWO PLACES, JUDGED IN NONE. Second, one of my three candidate fixes was INCOHERENT: asserting the release bundle CONTAINS a symbol from each optional module would have asserted the negation of a shipped invariant enforced by its own checker.

THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THE FIX HOLD: rowing a new optional module is ALREADY MANDATORY for the reachability invariant, so the same edit buys the warning gate for free. Same roster, opposite directions — one arm forbids anything outside a module requiring it, the other compiles it by name.

AND THE PLANT WAS THE HISTORICAL FAULT rather than a synthetic one: dropping the type hint that had genuinely been missing gave exit 0 with zero warnings before, exit 1 with two named warnings after.

title: Decide the fate of the measure-before-paint recipe: rewrite on Hicasso's native tier, or retire it
description:
docs/core/how-to/measure-before-paint.md answers a real and durable problem — geometry is a host fact that only exists once the element is in the document — but it is written entirely on Freehand's registered behaviors: :timing :layout, :config value-equality re-fire, v/defbehavior, v/describe.

rf2-pzu4g pulled it from the nav and gave it a notice, because it was teaching a retiring substrate to readers today. That is a HOLDING action, not the decision.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE: Hicasso has no counterpart door. Greps over implementation/hicasso/src/ for 'defbehavior', ':timing', ':layout', 'useLayoutEffect' and 'layout-effect' all return EMPTY, and the guide's 23 chapters teach no before-paint primitive. So the recipe cannot be re-pointed; it can only be rewritten or dropped.

THE DECISION, and it is a design question rather than a docs one:

  (a) Rewrite on the NATIVE TIER (docs/core/hicasso/10-native-tier.md). That
      chapter already rules hooks are the native tier's business — 'React
      hooks use their normal rules' — so react/useLayoutEffect is available
      there directly. Cheapest, and needs no new Hicasso surface. It also
      makes the recipe markedly less declarative than the Freehand one: the

title: Hicasso guide-sample gate has no CI lane on a docs-only PR
description:
check_guide_samples.py (rf2-qgbu5) pins all 188 fenced blocks in docs/core/hicasso/ and resolves every hicasso verb the guide names. It is chained into 'npm run test:hicasso-invariants', which reaches CI through test.yml's 'cljs' job.

THE HOLE, measured rather than assumed:

  .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md
  -> cljs_node_test=false

The 'cljs' job is armed by implementation/hicasso/** and the freehand bench tree. A guide-ONLY edit arms neither, so the gate that exists to catch a guide edit does not run in required CI on exactly that change class. It DOES run in the local fast-PR spine (scripts/test-fast-pr.sh), unconditionally, so the gate is not inert - it is just not required.

      'hicasso-complaint-catalogue' and 'hicasso-budget-ledger' already use.
      Both of those ALSO read docs/core/hicasso/ and both are unconditional

      .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh. Cheaper to write but it
      arms the whole ~10-minute node build for a prose typo, which is the

.github/workflows/test.yml.

  - h/hframe stays, and 2.1 or 2.2 gains a row for it (2.2 looks likelier: a frame-id read mints no node, so its server behaviour is HS-02's shape); or

title: skills/ markdown links and anchors are validated by NO gate — the two link checkers mutually defer
description:
MEASURED AT SOURCE on 2026-08-14 while doing rf2-r4j91 (PR #8200). Verify before actioning; this is a claim.

THE SHAPE. Two gates validate markdown link targets and heading anchors, and neither validates skills/.

1. scripts/check_readme_links.py DELIBERATELY SKIPS skills/. Its DOCS_GATE_ROOTS frozenset is {docs, spec, migration, skills}, with the comment 'Top-level subtrees the docs gate already validates. README.md files under any of these are skipped - check_doc_slugs.py is authoritative.' It runs unconditionally in test.yml's verify-readme-links job, so it is ALWAYS green on a skills diff, having checked nothing there.

2. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DOES list 'skills' in DEFAULT_ROOTS (line 96) - so it is the checker that would catch a broken skills/ link. But it runs ONLY in docs.yml's MkDocs build job, and that workflow's push.paths filter deliberately excludes skills/**, with an explicit comment at .github/workflows/docs.yml:24-29 saying neither skills/ nor tools/ is copied into docs_dir. The PR-side detect classifier matches. So a skills-only PR runs it NOWHERE.

The result is not merely 'an uncovered surface' - it is a surface each gate believes the other covers. docs.yml:426-434 already records this exact shape for a DIFFERENT gate (the inject-cofx residue gate), and the remedy taken there was to move that gate into test.yml's always-on verify-skill-mcp-drift job rather than widen the docs surface, because widening would buy a ~15-minute MkDocs build on every skills PR. The slug gate was never given the same treatment.

WHAT THIS LETS THROUGH. A skills/*.md relative link to a moved or deleted file, and a #anchor that no heading generates. skills/ carries 10 skills, ~127 markdown files and heavy internal cross-linking between SKILL.md and its references/ leaves, so the exposure is not theoretical. rf2-r4j91 rewrote six reference leaves in skills/reagent-migration/ and had to verify their link targets and anchors BY HAND, and said so in the PR body, because nothing at PR time would have.

LIKELY REMEDY, not ruled: follow the precedent docs.yml itself names - add a scoped invocation of check_doc_slugs.py over skills/ (and, if it is equally uncovered, tools/*/spec/) as a step in test.yml's 'Repo invariant checks (skills, MCP, catalogues, namespaces)' job, which is unconditional and pure-Python. Check first whether check_doc_slugs.py takes a roots argument; if not, that is the change. Pair it with a self-test as every sibling gate there does.

ALSO CHECK, same measurement: whether tools/*/spec/ has the same hole. check_readme_links.py skips it too (the _TOOL_SPEC_RE prefix, same 'the docs gate covers it' reason), and tools/**/spec/** IS on docs.yml's paths filter - so that one probably IS covered. Confirm rather than assume.

title: The shipped Hicasso guide has no digest pinning and no executed samples
description:
Measured under rf2-0yp7w phase 5, by a planted probe rather than by reading a
constant: a line added inside the first fenced block of
`docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md` left
`re-frame.freehand.guide.samples-coverage-jvm-test` at exit 0. That is the
CORRECT result — its `guide-dir` is the literal `"docs/core/freehand"` — and
it is also the hole.

The asymmetry is stark. The Freehand guide has a roster pinning 138 fenced
blocks, 114 of them owned by fixture vars that a `deftest` actually RENDERS
(the suite checks reachability, not merely resolution, precisely because a
fixture that only loads proves no render-time law). The Hicasso guide has 23
chapters of samples proved by nothing: a renamed verb, a changed option key or
a wrong `;; =>` comment ships silently.

That matters more than usual here, because the guide is deliberately ahead of
the code in four named places (see the Status block on
`docs/core/hicasso/index.md`) — `h/fn`/`h/frame` vs `h/hfn`/`h/hframe`,
`h/mount!` vs `h/root!`, an unexported `h/hydrate!`, and a
`re-frame.hicasso.server` that does not exist. Prose cannot notice when one of
those gaps CLOSES either, and a guide that stays wrong after the code catches
up is the failure the freehand roster was built to end.

The mechanism is worth rebuilding rather than losing: it is not a markdown
interpreter, it splits on fences, hashes bytes and compares two sets, and it
carries its own teeth-test against synthetic input. Its natural new home is
`implementation/hicasso/` beside the package it would pin, with fixtures on
the public `re-frame.hicasso` door.

SEQUENCING: this does NOT block rf2-7cuns (deleting the freehand pages and
roster). But the roster dies with the freehand tree, so if this is not built
first the mechanism has to be reconstructed from git history rather than
copied from a live tree.
close_reason:
Re-closed on all three checks (mayor, 2026-08-14). (a) DELIVERABLE on main: implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py is PRESENT and passes — 188 fenced blocks pinned across 25 pages, 34 verb use-sites resolved. PR #8204 MERGED. (b) OBLIGATIONS: zero markers in the notes. (c) SIBLINGS: rf2-r5iy7 arms it in CI and has its own PR; that is arming, not a defect in this deliverable.

WORTH KEEPING, because it is the part a later reader will not reconstruct: the Freehand suite this replaced was TWO guarantees in one coat — a digest roster over each fenced block, AND a roster column naming a CLJS fixture a deftest actually renders. Re-pointing failed on both halves for reasons that were not budget. The fixture half WOULD HAVE LAUNDERED ITS OWN ABSENCE: the guide deliberately leads the code in several places, so a fixture would have proved a DIFFERENT PROGRAM while its roster row read as coverage.

AND A THIRD GUARANTEE LANDED THAT NOBODY ASKED FOR: the declared-gap ledger is LIVE — it reds when a declared gap CLOSES. So when a form the guide says does not exist starts existing, the guide's own note becomes a build failure rather than quiet staleness. Prose, a digest and a fixture all miss that alike, and the donor suite never had it.

title: hic: an anchored overlay/popover has NON-DETERMINISTIC server bytes — the CSS anchor ident comes from a page-wide process counter
description:
MEASURED by rf2-cfriw, 2026-08-14, in the witness that bead landed: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs, row an-anchored-popover-does-not-produce-deterministic-server-bytes.

THE DEFECT. impl.overlay/make-cell mints each overlay instance a CSS dashed-ident from next-anchor-ident, which reads !anchor-seq -- a page-wide (defonce (atom 0)). When :anchor is supplied the ident is written into the panel's style attribute as position-anchor:--rf-overlay-N, so it reaches the SERVER BYTES.

Two renderToString calls over ONE immutable request snapshot therefore produce DIFFERENT bytes:
  <div popover="auto" style="position-anchor:--rf-overlay-1;position-area:...">
  <div popover="auto" style="position-anchor:--rf-overlay-2;position-area:...">
Normalise the ident away and the two are byte-identical, so the counter is the only non-determinism. Measured, both arms, in the witness above.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND DETERMINISM. The counter is scoped to the PROCESS, not to the request. A long-lived server keeps incrementing across every request it serves, while a freshly loaded page starts its own counter at 0. So the ident baked into the response and the ident the client mints at adoption disagree by an amount that grows with server uptime -- a hydration mismatch on a style attribute, on every anchored popover, and one whose size is a function of traffic rather than of the page.

NOT A REGRESSION IN THE PAGE-WIDE DECISION. globals.md and rf2-hic-017 rule the counter page-wide deliberately, and that reasoning is CORRECT and should not be reverted: a CSS anchor name lives in one namespace per DOCUMENT, not one per React root, so two roots each minting --rf-overlay-1 would put two live overlays on one name. The defect is that a server render has no document to be page-wide with respect to, and the counter has no request scope to fall back on.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE INVENTORY. dispositions.md HS-32's operative cell now records this: section 2.4's FIRST upgrade clause (deterministic server bytes from an immutable request snapshot) is unreachable for the anchored arm by construction, so HS-32 cannot be upgraded to Render until this is repaired. The unanchored popover and the modal are deterministic and are witnessed so in the same file.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, ruled on by nobody -- this bead states the defect, not the fix:
1. Derive the ident from React's own useId, which is already prefix-scoped and already matches across a server render and its adoption (HS-11/HS-14 carry what useId does and does not do here, including the sibling-closer obstruction).
2. Scope the counter to a render/request rather than to the process, which needs a server-side seam the package does not have today (see HS-33's open-adoption-window! for the shape of that argument).
3. Move the anchor name off the served bytes entirely -- claim it in the ref callback, where the module already claims the TRIGGER's anchor name, so nothing anchor-related is serialized.

ACCEPTANCE. Two renderToString calls over one snapshot of an anchored overlay/popover are byte-identical; the existing row in client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test is turned around onto the repair in the same edit (it is asserted in the direction the runtime behaves TODAY and says so, exactly as rf2-42vlw's conformance row was); and HS-32's cell is re-read.

FENCE: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/overlay.cljs, that one witness row, and HS-32's cell. Minting a new error id would owe a spec/009 row and spec/* is hot zone -- this repair should need none.
close_reason: Repaired in PR #8206. The panel's position-anchor is claimed in the ref callback beside the trigger's anchor-name, so the page-wide counter's output never reaches the served bytes and two renderToString calls over one snapshot are byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION. The counter is untouched and stays page-wide (rf2-hic-017 is correct and the repair depends on it). A useId-derived name was costed first and refused at source: HS-11's second obstruction (adoption closer is a SIBLING of the app subtree) would have traded a drifting mismatch for a fixed one on the same attribute, and spent a third React hook. Witness turned around onto the repair and asserts the determinism PROPERTY rather than a name. Client behaviour unchanged, proved by planting anchor-panel! as a no-op and watching overlay-dom-cljs-test's geometry row red on real Chromium (panel.left=615.2 vs trigger.left=0), then revert to green. HS-32's cell re-read is rf2-hsz6f (dispositions.md was held by worker/rostergate-gz4bq).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
SURFACED BY rf2-cfriw's worker, unasked, while measuring whether the overlay module refuses (mayor, 2026-08-14). This is a real SSR correctness defect, not a documentation gap.

THE DEFECT. An anchored overlay or popover bakes its CSS anchor NAME into the served style attribute, and that name is minted from a PAGE-WIDE defonce counter. Two renderToString calls over ONE IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT answer --rf-overlay-1 and --rf-overlay-2. Same input, different output.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY A BUG IN THE COUNTER. Page-wide is CORRECT for a client and it is deliberate — rf2-hic-017 chose it. The problem is that a SERVER HAS NO DOCUMENT TO BE PAGE-WIDE WITH RESPECT TO. The counter's scope is a property of the browser session; on the server there is no session, so the scope has no referent and the counter simply increments across renders that should be independent.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS A HYDRATION MISMATCH ON AN ATTRIBUTE HYDRATION MUST MATCH. The served markup carries an anchor name the client will not reproduce. And section 2.4's first clause is unreachable there BY CONSTRUCTION — not merely unwitnessed.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST DECIDE, and the options are genuinely different in kind: make the counter render-scoped on the server so each render restarts it; derive the name deterministically from something already stable in the tree rather than from a counter at all; or refuse the anchored overlay on the server and say so, which is honest but removes a capability.

THE SECOND IS PROBABLY RIGHT AND IS THE ONE TO COST FIRST — a name derived from stable tree position needs no counter, needs no server special case, and makes the client and server agree by construction rather than by discipline. But that is a recommendation, not a ruling; verify what is actually stable in the tree at that point before committing to it.

VERIFY THE PREMISE AT SOURCE. Reproduce the two renderToString calls over one snapshot and confirm the names differ. Four of my own measurements were refuted by workers today, and this one is second-hand to me.

title: Xray's Mounted Views panel requires re-frame.freehand.tool — a real product capability that dies with Freehand

title: Re-aim the Reagent migration skill and codemod at hicasso (UIx DEFERRED by Mike)
description:
MIKE'S RULING 2026-08-14: Freehand and re-frame.ui are being RETIRED. The architecture is a Reagent adapter and a UIx adapter, plus hicasso as re-frame2 native. This bead replaces rf2-7kus, which proposed a UIx-to-Freehand path and is closed as targeting a retiring substrate.

THE STATE TODAY, verified at source when rf2-7kus was filed. skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md migrates Reagent VIEW code to Freehand (re-frame.freehand, alias v) — hiccup views become v/defview, subscribe derefs become v/sub, handlers lift to event vectors, Form-2 atoms and Form-3 lifecycle re-home. migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/ backs it with a real codemod. skills/re-frame2-ui/SKILL.md covers re-frame.ui and describes it as the DONOR being absorbed into Freehand, routing new porting work to the Reagent skill. Nothing migrates UIx view code anywhere.

title: check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since fails OPEN on uncommitted work: exit 0 having inspected zero files
description:
FOUND BY rf2-hic-045's P12 worker (2026-08-14), unprompted, while using the gate normally.

THE DEFECT. 'python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main' diffs COMMITTED refs. Run before committing — which is the natural moment to run a doc gate — it inspects ZERO files and returns exit 0. The worker's first run did exactly that. It re-ran after committing and got the real answer (4 pins, 4 landed).

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. This gate is nominated in essentially every documentation dispatch in this repository, and it is the gate that catches STRANDED PROVENANCE PINS — a page citing a pre-rebase authored SHA that a rebase-merge left unreachable. That class has been found three times today alone: once on a per-keystroke page, once as two rows in the correction ledger (rf2-nzgby), and once caught live by this same gate. A vacuous green on the pre-commit run is therefore a fail-open on the exact defect the gate exists to catch, at the exact moment a worker is most likely to run it.

IT IS ALSO SELF-CONCEALING. Exit 0 with no output looks identical to exit 0 having verified everything, because the gate is silent on success. Nothing in the output distinguishes 'checked 4 pins, all landed' from 'checked nothing'.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, none attempted and none preferred here — this needs someone reading the script: report the number of files inspected on every run, so zero is visible; or refuse with a non-zero exit when --changed-since resolves to an empty file set, on the grounds that a gate asked to check a range and finding nothing to check should say so rather than pass; or make the flag consider the working tree as well as committed refs. The first is the smallest and may be sufficient — a gate that says '0 files inspected' cannot be mistaken for a pass.

VERIFY THE PREMISE AT SOURCE FIRST. Reproduce the vacuous green before changing anything: make an uncommitted edit to a page under docs/design/hicasso/ that would fail the gate, run it with --changed-since origin/main, and confirm exit 0.

DO NOT WIDEN INTO THE SCRIPT'S OTHER MODES. --self-test and the docs.yml job path are working and are not in question.
close_reason:
PR #8207. BOTH MODES NOW REPORTED; NEITHER RULE CHANGED.

MODE 1 REFINED AT SOURCE — the bead's stated mechanism is wrong. changed_markdown runs 'git diff <base> -- <root>' with NO --cached, which reads the WORKING TREE, so an uncommitted, unstaged edit to a TRACKED page IS inspected (measured: exit 1 naming validation.md:7). The vacuous green is an UNTRACKED file only. 'git add' alone ends it — no commit needed, measured both ways. The gate's message now names staging, not committing.

MODE 2 CONFIRMED and reported without re-ruling. Full-corpus findings are byte-identical before and after: 7 findings, same paths, lines, tokens.

Every run now prints one unconditional line: '107 pages inspected, 473 cited pins - 358 landed, 107 stranded, 7 unresolvable, 1 foreign; 107 accompanied in scope; 7 findings.' That 107 accompanied was invisible. Under --verbose each absorbed pin is listed beside the landed pin that answered for it, which is the diagnostic a planted-SHA control needs.

UNCONDITIONAL is the load-bearing choice: both scheduled callers (fast-PR spine, docs.yml) already pass --verbose, so the reader the defect actually fooled was a worker running the brief's nominated command by hand without the flag.

Sibling's shape transferred but ADAPTED: check_doc_slugs.py prints a per-root TABLE because it has eleven roots; this gate walks one, so one line rather than a wall.

Self-test 61 -> 68. Proved red under 'python -O' (exit 1 broken / 0 restored), asserted via a failures counter rather than bare asserts.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
SECOND FAIL-OPEN MODE IN THE SAME GATE, found by rf2-hic-048's worker (mayor, 2026-08-14). Fold both into one repair.

MODE 1 (this bead as filed) CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, on the same tree in one session: run BEFORE committing, the gate inspected 0 files and returned exit 0; run AFTER committing, it reported 3 files, 34 pins, 32 landed, 2 stranded. Same working tree, opposite verdicts, and the vacuous one is indistinguishable from a pass because the gate is silent on success.

MODE 2, NEW AND WORSE FOR THE PLANT DISCIPLINE: a stranded pin PASSES when its own block carries a landed pin alongside it. So a worker planting a stranded SHA in the natural place — beside an existing citation, where SHAs already live — gets exit 0 and concludes THE GATE DOES NOT REACH THIS FILE. It does; the plant was neutralised by its neighbour. Re-planted in a paragraph carrying no landed pin, the same SHA gave exit 1 naming line 264 and [STRANDED]. Both arms were measured.

WHY MODE 2 IS THE MORE DANGEROUS OF THE TWO. The entire plant discipline rests on the inference 'if the gate does not redden, it does not reach my edit'. That inference is sound only when the plant is genuinely fatal to the property under test. A block-scoped rule absorbs a plant without absorbing a real defect, so the worker concludes a covering gate is not covering — and then either skips the control or reaches for a weaker one.

NOTE THAT MODE 2 MAY NOT BE A DEFECT AT ALL. A stranded pin sharing a block with a landed one is arguably fine, since the block still cites something reachable — that is presumably why the rule exists. If so, the repair is not to change the rule but to make the gate SAY what it did: report files inspected and pins classified on every run, so both 'checked nothing' and 'absorbed by a neighbour' become visible. That single change may close both modes at once, and it is the smallest thing that could.

TWO STRANDED PINS CURRENTLY LIVE UNDER MODE 2 and are known: correction-ledger.md lines 71 and 73, tracked as rf2-nzgby, each sharing its row with a landed pin — which is exactly why the gate stays green over them. That bead already carries the verified landed replacements.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
A SECOND GATE IN THIS FAMILY NOW SAYS WHAT IT INSPECTED, and it was the cheaper fix as predicted (mayor, 2026-08-14).

The rf2-v7fui worker added --verbose per-root counts to check_doc_slugs.py: docs 400, spec 60, skills 176, migration 8, plus seven tools/*/spec entries — and it lists every DEFAULT_ROOTS entry EVEN AT ZERO. About thirty lines. Its own words: it closes the family rather than the instance.

THAT IS THE SAME REPAIR THIS BEAD SHOULD TAKE. check_provenance_pins.py has two fail-open modes — a vacuous exit 0 when run before committing with zero files inspected, and a plant absorbed when a stranded pin shares its block with a landed one. Both are invisible because the gate is silent on success. Making it report files inspected and pins classified on every run makes both visible without changing either rule, and the sibling gate has now proved the shape works.

DO NOT CHANGE WHAT COUNTS AS A PASS. A stranded pin sharing a block with a landed one may well be correct — that is presumably why the rule exists. The defect is that the gate does not SAY so, not that it is wrong.

title: hic: row 7's deciding evidence names an 'opaque foreign subtree' the Xray projection cannot compute - amend or re-rule the phrase
description:
## Why this is filed rather than done

`rf2-t2d3` asked, in its acceptance, for two things in the contingency that the Xray causal
projection cannot distinguish *opaque because foreign* from *opaque because React owns paint*:
**say so at source**, and **amend the row's deciding evidence rather than leaving the phrase
unearned**.

The contingency is the one that obtained, and the first half landed in
`worker/xrayforeign-t2d3` (spec 028 plus the `hicasso_causal.cljc` docstrings). The second half
is deliberately NOT done there, for two reasons:

1. The phrase lives in `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/hot-path-architecture.md` — the
   CANONICAL native-tier checklist — which is outside `rf2-t2d3`'s own stated surface fence
   (that fence names only `tools/xray/test/.../hicasso_causal_cljs_test.cljs`,
   `tools/xray/src/.../hicasso_causal.cljc` and `tools/xray/spec/028-Hicasso-Advisor.md`).
2. It is the criterion CHECKPOINT 3 scored row 7 against. Amending the criterion from inside
   the bead that failed it is a ruling, not a worker's edit.

## The finding it would record

`hot-path-architecture.md`, Diagnostics row, deciding evidence:

> One causal trace with an opaque foreign subtree and production-erasure proof

**The Xray projection never computes "a foreign subtree".** `causal/slice` is a pure function
of the four Hicasso evidence envelopes and a trace window, and not one of them carries a node,
a child, an element or a component. The producer states the same at its own door:
`re-frame.hicasso.tool`'s naming projection is `:basis :opaque`, `:complete? false`, because
*"the runtime mints no boundary identity and keeps no view registry"* — a boundary IS the
projected edge set it holds. Links 5-7 come from the constant `causal/host-opaque-links`, and
`link-host` reads no argument `slice` was given, so an interpreted-only boundary, one rendering
an `n/defcomponent` island and one rendering a `[:>]` foreign escape produce three IDENTICAL
rows.

This is now WITNESSED rather than argued:
`tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/hicasso_causal_native_island_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
takes two slices on one runtime — one over a boundary whose subtree crosses the fence twice,
one over a boundary with no native tier under it — and asserts links 5-7 are equal field for
field, with a non-vacuity control proving the two slices otherwise differ.

Making the producer publish a tree so the discrimination could exist would contradict
`lanes/design-laws.md` §7 (*"Xray may name and time the native boundary and observe reads made
through supported native hooks. The inner React tree is otherwise explicitly opaque"*), so the
phrase is unearnable as written rather than merely unearned.

## Proposed amendment (exact wording, for the mayor to accept, edit or reject)

In `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/hot-path-architecture.md`, Diagnostics row, replace the
deciding-evidence cell:

- FROM: `One causal trace with an opaque foreign subtree and production-erasure proof`
- TO:   `One causal trace taken over a native-tier subject — an n/defcomponent island read
        through n/use-sub, with a foreign React subtree beside it — showing the boundary named
        and timed, the inner tree absent from every roster, and the host-opaque links proved
        SUBJECT-INVARIANT; plus production-erasure proof`

The amendment does not weaken the row. The original phrase could be satisfied by a label the
projection would have had to fabricate; the replacement asks for the two facts the projection
genuinely holds (name + time, and total structural opacity) and for the invariance to be
demonstrated rather than assumed — which is a harder reading, and the one the landed witness
meets.

## Also worth a ruling

If the mayor prefers to keep the phrase and treat it as an obligation on the PRODUCER instead
(i.e. Hicasso should publish enough tree for Xray to say *this subtree is foreign*), that is a
different and much larger bead against `implementation/hicasso/`, and it collides with
design-laws §7. Say which, and rf2-t2d3's ledger row can be closed either way.

## Surfaces

- `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/hot-path-architecture.md` (Diagnostics row only)
- possibly `docs/design/hicasso/product/checkpoint-3-native.md` §Row 7 and
  `docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md` row `rf2-hic-038` / `rf2-t2d3` — both held
  by the ledger-keeper lane, so sequence behind it.
notes:
WITNESS NOTE (worker/xrayforeign-t2d3): the row's REQUIREMENT column is now fully witnessed;
only the DECIDING EVIDENCE phrasing is unearnable.

Row 7 requirement: "Xray names and times the boundary, reports supported-hook reads, labels the
inner tree opaque and adds no production evidence machinery" — all four clauses are asserted in
hicasso_causal_native_island_dom_cljs_test over a genuine n/defcomponent island plus a foreign
[:>] subtree:

  names + times     — the advisor ranks the island's edge set with :axes :time :ms a number
  supported-hook    — the n/use-sub read is its own census row; slice links 1-4 evidenced
  inner tree opaque — eight markup needles absent from every string/keyword/symbol in all four
                      evidence envelopes AND the slice; the naming projection is :basis :opaque
  no prod machinery — no implementation/ file touched by the PR at all

So the amendment below is a phrasing correction, not a weakening: the checklist would go from
asking for a label the projection must fabricate, to asking for the two facts it genuinely holds
plus a demonstrated invariance.

EVERY PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE in the worktree, not carried from the bead: causal/slice is a pure function of four evidence envelopes and a trace window with none carrying a node/child/element/component (namespace docstring, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/hicasso_causal.cljc); host-opaque-links is a CONSTANT at line 147 and link-host reads no argument slice was given; the producer's naming projection is :basis :opaque, :complete? false; the witness hicasso_causal_native_island_dom_cljs_test.cljs is on main. The REQUIREMENT column was left untouched - it is already fully witnessed on all four clauses.

title: hic: a :value on a file input reaches React's element.value assignment and throws InvalidStateError with no Hicasso attribution
description:
MEASURED by rf2-hic-040 in Chromium 147.0.7727.15, Firefox 148.0.2 and WebKit 26.4, all three agreeing.

THE DEFECT. impl.controlled/controlled-text-tag? asks only 'is this an input/textarea carrying a non-nil :value', so an <input type=file> with a :value off a subscription IS a controlled-text-tag: it gets the shadow component, convergeable? then answers no (file is not in caret-types) and the props go through by identity. React then does what it does for every controlled input: react-dom@19.2.0 initInput reaches 'element.value = value' and updateInput reaches 'element.value = "" + getToStringValue(value)' for every type but number. HTMLInputElement.value refuses every assignment but the empty string on a file input, so that write THROWS InvalidStateError - verified directly in all three engines (spec.cjs, file-input-is-uncontrollable).

AND REACT 19.2 CARRIES NO CONTROLLED-FILE-INPUT WARNING. Grepped: the only occurrence of the string "file" in react-dom-client.development.js is an event-plugin branch. So what an author gets is an engine exception naming no view, no framework and no recovery - which is the failure mode spec SN section 3.6 exists to remove.

THE SUPPORTED PATH IS FINE and is witnessed green in three engines: the input is left uncontrolled and h/hfn reads .files, which is the example the facade's own hfn docstring uses.

WHY rf2-hic-040 DID NOT FIX IT. A source-located refusal mints an error id, and an error id owes a row in spec/009-Instrumentation.md - hot zone that bead was fenced out of.

THE REPAIR, not ruled on: one clause in impl.controlled/install!, on the branch that already established controlled-text-tag?, so a page with no controlled inputs pays nothing - refuse tag=input + type=file + non-nil :value, naming the recovery 'leave the file input uncontrolled and read .files through h/hfn'. It is the same shape as the existing :rf.error/hicasso-revision-not-controlled guard two lines above.

dispositions.md section 2.3's File input row records this as a finding and certifies only the uncontrolled path.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8180 FOLLOW-THROUGH (2026-08-14). Keep this exact runtime-finding owner open. The recurring `file-input-is-uncontrollable` section currently proves two separate facts: the supported UNCONTROLLED Hicasso path carries `.files`, and a direct DOM assignment `node.value = "anything"` throws `InvalidStateError`. It never renders or invokes the unsupported Hicasso spelling — `<input type=file>` carrying a non-nil `:value` — so repairing `impl.controlled/install!` to refuse that spelling would leave this section green. That contradicts dispositions.md's claim that each finding witness reds on repair.

When implementing this Bead, retain the direct platform assignment as the control, and add one compact Hicasso-level witness for the actual source-located refusal/pass-through seam (in a focused refusal test if putting a permanently throwing control on the shared page would poison it). Update the disposition citation so the finding cannot remain green after the runtime is repaired. No broader file-upload abstraction or browser framework is warranted.
BLOCKED BY FENCE, measured rather than inferred (worker propbugs-42vlw, 2026-08-14).

The repair needs a new :rf.error/ id, and a new id CANNOT be minted from a checkout fenced out of spec/. Proven, not assumed: a probe id planted at impl.controlled/install! made scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py exit 1 with 'CHECK A - 1 emitted id with no Spec 009 catalogue row ... add the catalogue row in spec/009-Instrumentation.md (co-edit invariant - do it in the SAME PR as the emitting change)'. The plant was reverted and the revert verified by git hash-object. So this bead needs a dispatch that OWNS spec/009-Instrumentation.md; no prop-pipeline worker can close it.

THE PROPOSED PREDICATE IN THIS BEAD IS WRONG AND WOULD BREAK A WORKING SPELLING. The bead says 'refuse tag=input + type=file + non-nil :value'. That refuses :value "", which is legitimate and is the standard reset idiom. Read at source in react-dom@19.2.0: initInput is 'isHydrating || value === element.value || (element.value = value)' and updateInput is 'element.value !== ""+getToStringValue(value) && (element.value = ...)'. Both SKIP the assignment when the value already equals the element's. A file input's .value is "" when empty, so :value "" never assigns; and where a file IS selected, .value is "C:\fakepath\..." so the assignment does happen but is the empty string, which is the ONE write HTMLInputElement.value accepts - it clears the control. PR #8180's own merged row corroborates this from the other side: file-input-is-uncontrollable asserts clearOk === true, 'while the empty string - the one legal write - is accepted'.

So the refusal must be on a NON-EMPTY :value, not a non-nil one. Refusing "" would take away the only way an author can clear a file input from the model.

ALSO NOT WORTH DOING SEPARATELY: excluding type=file from impl.controlled/controlled-text-tag? looks like an in-fence tidy-up (it stops a file input being wrapped in the composition shadow component for nothing) but changes NO user-visible behaviour - React throws either way - and it would flip a type=file input carrying ::h/revision from ACCEPTED to REFUSED, which contradicts the coverage sentence in that id's Spec 009 row. So it crosses the same fence and was declined rather than shipped as cosmetic churn.

At landed tip 6672dbd9, docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md:336 still says the controlled-file refusal is the PLATFORM'S rather than Hicasso's, calls it NOT CERTIFIED, and cites only the pre-repair `file-input-is-uncontrollable` record. That is now factually false: impl.controlled/install! emits :rf.error/hicasso-file-input-value-prop before React's write, and file_input_value_dom_cljs_test supplies the Hicasso-level witness this bead's earlier audit note explicitly required.

title: hic: ::h/value on a <select multiple> silently under-reads the selection to one option
description:
MEASURED by rf2-hic-040 in Chromium 147.0.7727.15, Firefox 148.0.2 and WebKit 26.4, all three agreeing.

THE DEFECT. impl.intent/marker-readers lowers ::h/value to (.-value target). On a <select multiple>, HTMLSelectElement.value is the FIRST selected option and never the selection. So [:tb/pick ::h/value] on a multiple select is a correct-looking expression that quietly means something else: the user chooses two options, the handler receives one, the controlled echo writes that one back, and the second choice is DISCARDED inside the turn. Nothing refuses it, nothing warns, and the author has no signal at all.

WITNESSED, in the direction the runtime behaves, so the row reds when this is fixed as well as if it degrades: implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs section reserved-marker-under-reads-a-multiple-select, beside select-multiple-supported which drives the SAME control through h/hfn and keeps both options. Both green in three engines.

WHY rf2-hic-040 DID NOT FIX IT. A source-located refusal mints an error id, and an error id owes a row in spec/009-Instrumentation.md, which is hot zone that bead was fenced out of. The measurement and the disposition row are that bead's deliverable; the repair is this one's.

THE OPTIONS, not ruled on: (a) a source-located refusal at the codec when a select carrying :multiple has a change handler lowered from an intent carrying value-marker - render-time, so no per-event cost; (b) a second reserved marker (::h/values or ::h/selected) reading selectedOptions, which is the one-line addition to marker-readers and adds a roster entry rather than a refusal; (c) rule it authored-around and document h/hfn as the only spelling, which is what dispositions.md section 2.3 says TODAY and which the acceptance 'no control silently unsupported' arguably does not permit.

dispositions.md section 2.3's Select (multiple) row records this as a finding and does NOT certify the marker spelling.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8193. impl.intent/target-value reads .selectedOptions on a <select multiple> and .value everywhere else, so ::h/value now carries the whole selection as a vector ([] when nothing is picked) instead of HTML's first-selected-option answer. A correction rather than a refusal or a second marker, so no new error id and no API widening. Shape adopted from spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md's normative ruling for the same DOM control. Red-then-green witnessed twice in select_multiple_value_dom_cljs_test — a stand-in carrying HTML's rule for :node-test, and a real <select multiple> in the browser lane whose execution was proven by a planted fault.

title: C8's population is escapes taken FOR A BENEFIT, not every landed escape — the interop escape is a fail-closed
description:
FOUND BY rf2-hic-071's first pass (2026-08-14, PR #8177), while checking whether C8 had a population yet.

THE CLAIM. budgets.md section 4 registers C8 as 'An escape recovers >= 20%, saves >= 2 ms p95, or converts a failed budget to a pass', with the disposition 'an island missing its threshold is simplified or removed — thresholds do not widen to keep it'. Ruling 2 (rf2-5yn9) makes its population SITE-LEVEL: one adjudication per landed escape site, with rf2-hic-071 as the enforcement authority.

THE HOLE. Not every h/as-element call is an escape claiming recovered time. The ONE such call in the shipped example applications is implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ledger/views.cljs:226 — the ledger screen handing a Hicasso view to a third-party virtualizer's renderRow callback, which demands a React element. Nothing is claimed to be recovered there; the escape exists because the vendor API has no other door.

CONSEQUENCE. A C8 gate written over 'every landed escape site' would adjudicate that call against a 20% / 2ms / budget-flip threshold it was never taken to meet, find it missing, and demand under its own acceptance that it be 'simplified or removed'. There is nothing to simplify it to. That is a fail-CLOSED gate — the exact mirror of the fail-open rf2-mwr2 found in U5, and it is worth settling BEFORE the gate is built rather than after it reds on main.

THE REPAIR (proposed, not taken). C8's registered population is 'escapes taken for a BENEFIT'. An interoperability escape — one whose alternative is not a slower spelling but no spelling at all — is outside it, and says so at the site. The distinction needs to be written into the row or into Ruling 2's wording, not left to the gate author to infer.

NO MEASUREMENT NEEDED. This is a question about what C8's registered population IS, not about any figure.

OWNER: rf2-hic-071 owns C8's enforcement, so this is a defect in the row that bead would gate on — the same shape as rf2-mwr2, and it should be folded into whichever pass finally builds the escape-benefit gate. C8 stays UNPINNED meanwhile, correctly.

No threshold moved (token census unchanged), no gate built, C8 stays UNPINNED. Gates: check_budget_ledger 0, --self-test 0, check_doc_slugs 0, check_provenance_pins 0; five live-document sabotages each captured red with hash-verified restores.

title: hic: react-compatibility-notes assigns Activity to the native tier, and no native-hook row runs under <Activity>
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. Canonical native-tier
checklist, ROW 3 (Frame and store lifecycle), §1 Completeness + §2 Correctness.

Row 3 requires n/use-sub and n/use-frame to use the shared substrate across a
named list of states, and "Activity hide/reveal" is on it.

and activity_suspense_dom_cljs_test.cljs carry hide-releases-committed-ownership,
reveal-reacquires, a stale-membership row, two NEGATIVE-CONTROL rows and a
three-lifecycle-states row. Every one of them drives commit-boundary! / h/defview.
Both files' :require blocks contain NO re-frame.hicasso.native (verified: grep -c
"hicasso.native" returns 0 for both).

What makes this sharper than an ordinary coverage hole is the documentation.
docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md closes its Activity
section with:

  "Activity should be used through native React construction—Hicasso-native, UIx,
   or a `defhost` declaration. Hicasso needs compatibility, not an Activity DSL."

That sentence ASSIGNS Activity to this tier rather than deferring it. So the
product tells an author to reach for Hicasso-native when they need Activity, and
the route it names has no witness. dispositions.md's HS-23 (Activity-hosted
subtree) likewise has no witness.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_hooks_dom_cljs_test.cljs
  (preferred home — it already owns the lifecycle roster and the residue census)
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/activity_suspense_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md HS-23 row, if the witness lands

DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md. DO NOT touch budgets.md.

## Acceptance

EITHER a row driving n/use-sub (and n/use-frame) under a real <Activity>
hide/reveal, asserting the same observables the boundary-tier rows assert —
ownership released on hide, reacquired on reveal, no resurrection of stale
membership, exact residue on teardown — with the existing negative controls
carried across; OR a source-located statement that the native hooks inherit the
boundary shell's Activity behaviour BY CONSTRUCTION (they resolve through
collector/resolve-frame! and collector/hook-entry, which is arguably true), with
a test pinning that shared-substrate identity so the inheritance cannot silently
stop holding — plus an amendment to the lane doc's sentence if the recommended
route is not in fact the witnessed one.
close_reason:
PR #8195 (MERGED). W8 on native_hooks_dom_cljs_test drives an island under a real <Activity>, constructed through n/$ - the route the lane note recommends, end to end. Hide releases the committed ownership without destroying the fiber (React's own useState survives, the node is retained and out of the layout); a write while hidden reaches nobody; a prop change while hidden moves the read set and publishes nothing; the reveal reacquires the CURRENT set with a registration that is NOT identical to the one the hide released. n/use-frame asserted across the same hide: its bundle is the runtime's memo row for a frame incarnation, so it crosses unchanged and pre-hide ops still address the live frame.

ACTIVITY SUPPORT IS REAL, not merely documented - established by measurement, not by reading. So the doc was correct and under-witnessed rather than wrong. react-compatibility-notes amended only to make the recommendation carry the matrix immediately above it, plus use-frame's asymmetry.

dispositions.md HS-23 deliberately NOT touched: outside this worker's fence, and its own text already says why it stays open - no suite server-renders an Activity-hosted subtree, so its Client-only refusal is still unproved and was never inside this bead's acceptance.

title: hic: native grammar refusals are not source-located, and are structurally unreachable inside an n/defcomponent body
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. Canonical native-tier
checklist, ROW 1 (Native-form grammar), §2 Correctness.

The row's required result ends: "... and SOURCE-LOCATED refusal of Hiccup/intent
semantics". The refusals themselves are well witnessed — stable :rf.error/id,
:where, non-blank :reason, :recovery, each with non-member controls
(native_grammar_cljs_test.cljs, native_fence_cljs_test.cljs). What is NOT
witnessed, anywhere, is the SOURCE LOCATION.

1. No test asserts :source (file/line/column) on ANY grammar refusal —
   hicasso-native-hiccup-child, -intent-in-prop, -map-as-child, -slot-collision,
   -children-in-props. The only :source assertions in the tier
   (native_fence_cljs_test.cljs:287, :297) are about the n/defcomponent
   DECLARATION MAP, not about grammar.

2. It is structurally unreachable as landed. impl/error.cljc stamps :source from
   !origin, set by declaring!/declared! (declaration extent) or by
   traced-boundary (a defview boundary). native.cljc's `component` (:470) does
   NOT wrap with error/traced-boundary. So a grammar refusal raised inside an
   n/defcomponent island body carries neither :view nor :source — and no test
   pins it either way, so the absence is invisible.

## Why correctness rather than coverage

The row states source-location as a required RESULT, and the artefacts contradict
it: the ladder sells the native tier as the narrowest useful escape for a measured
hotspot, and an author who lands a hiccup vector in a native child position inside
an island gets a refusal that cannot say where. This is the ledger's "a claim the
artefacts contradict".

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc (the `component` seam)
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/error.cljc (only if the origin
  seam genuinely needs a new entry point — prefer reusing traced-boundary)
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_grammar_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_fence_cljs_test.cljs

DO NOT touch docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md — a corrective PR
never edits the ledger (that file's own protocol, and merged-PR audit #7726).

## Acceptance

EITHER (a) a grammar refusal raised inside an n/defcomponent body carries a
:source coordinate naming the island, with a test asserting file/line and a
non-member control proving the coordinate is not constant; OR (b) a source-located
refusal is ruled out of scope for the native tier at source, with the row's
required-result sentence amended in hot-path-architecture.md to say what IS owed
instead — a refusal that names the tier and the prop is a defensible line, but it
must be the WRITTEN line rather than the accidental one.

Either way the two-languages fence rows must stay green and the refusal shape row
(a-native-refusal-carries-the-stable-shape) must still pass.

title: EPIC: no migration path from UIx view code to Freehand — Reagent has one, UIx does not
description:
ASKED BY MIKE 2026-08-14: is there a skill for migrating a Reagent or UIx codebase to hicasso? Answer: Reagent yes, UIx no.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, verified at source.
- skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md migrates Reagent VIEW code to Freehand (re-frame.freehand, alias v): a Reagent hiccup view becomes a v/defview mounted in brackets and never called; @(subscribe ...) becomes (v/sub ...); #(dispatch ...) handlers lift to event vectors; Form-2 atoms and Form-3 lifecycle re-home to re-frame or to a registered behavior. It correctly positions itself as the OPTIONAL SECOND step, after the required re-frame v1 to re-frame2 move.
- migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/ backs it with a real codemod.
- skills/re-frame2-ui/SKILL.md covers re-frame.ui, described there as the DONOR being absorbed into Freehand, and routes new porting work to reagent-migration.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST. Nothing migrates UIx view code to Freehand. UIx appears in the skills tree only inside skills/re-frame-migration as one of the substrate ADAPTERS a v1 app can land on — that is a different axis entirely (which adapter runs your existing views) from what this epic is about (rewriting UIx view code into Freehand views).

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING AND WHY IT IS NOT JUST A COPY. UIx is a first-class supported adapter, so a UIx app is a legitimate and likely starting point for someone adopting the re-frame-native view layer. But the source language differs from Reagent in ways that change the work: UIx views are React function components declared with defui and $ rather than hiccup vectors; hooks (use-state, use-effect, use-memo, use-callback) have no Reagent analogue and map onto view-local state, behaviors and re-frame in different places; props are JS-object-shaped at the boundary; and the escape hatches to raw React differ. A codemod written against hiccup vectors will not read $ forms.

SCOPE THIS AS AN EPIC, not one bead. Plausible children, to be split rather than treated as a checklist: (1) a source-language survey of UIx constructs and their Freehand images, including the ones with NO image, which are the interesting half; (2) the skill itself, mirroring reagent-migration's structure and its required-first-step framing; (3) codemod support for the mechanical subset, if a mechanical subset genuinely exists — verify that before assuming it; (4) a worked example app.

TRIAGE HONESTLY BEFORE BUILDING. If the survey finds the mechanical subset is small and the judgement-call surface is most of it, then a SKILL WITH GOOD GUIDANCE AND NO CODEMOD is the right answer, and building a codemod anyway would be exactly the over-engineering the stance rejects. A reasoned 'guidance only, no codemod' is a complete outcome for child (3).

SEQUENCING: this sits downstream of the hicasso naming packet (rf2-hic-065) and the mechanical rename sweep (rf2-hic-066). Writing a migration skill against a name that is about to change would guarantee a rewrite. Note that the tree already carries the mismatch — the skills say Freehand, the design tree says hicasso, and migration/reagent-to-hicasso/ says hicasso in a path.
close_reason:
CLOSED — IT TARGETS A RETIRING SUBSTRATE (Mike's ruling, 2026-08-14).

MIKE'S DIRECTION, stated in chat today: Freehand is going to be RETIRED, and so is re-frame.ui. The plan is a Reagent adapter and a UIx adapter, plus hicasso as re-frame2 native.

WHY THAT CLOSES THIS EPIC. It proposed building a UIx-view-code-to-FREEHAND migration path to match the Reagent one. Building a second path to a substrate that is being retired is work with a known expiry date.

BUT THE FINDING UNDERNEATH IT SURVIVES AND GETS LARGER. The asymmetry this epic named is real; it was just mis-aimed. Under the new architecture the honest statement is not 'UIx lacks a path that Reagent has' — it is that NEITHER has a path to where things are going. skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md migrates Reagent views to Freehand, and migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/ backs it. Both point at a retiring target. So the question Mike originally asked — migrate a Reagent or UIx codebase to HICASSO — is unanswered for both.

AND THE STORY IS NOW TWO-TIER, WHICH CHANGES WHAT A MIGRATION SKILL SHOULD SAY. With first-class Reagent and UIx adapters, an existing app KEEPS its view code and needs no rewrite at all. Rewriting into hicasso becomes a genuinely optional second step chosen for what hicasso gives, not a step required to land on re-frame2. A skill written on the old premise will over-state the need.

title: MEASURE: the WINDOWED arm's clock control has no discriminating power at the committed window size
description:
FOUND BY rf2-m6i0's measurement window (2026-08-14), on the run that
certified the other three arms.

rf2-m6i0 replaced the degenerate changed-set control with a rendered-scale
one and it PASSES on fine, coarse and chunked. It REFUSES on `virtual`, and
the refusal is not the same fault the changed-set control had.

MEASURED. Quiet box (\System\Processor Queue Length 0.00 before/during/after),
Chromium 147.0.7727.15 headless, :advanced, 20 commits under one clock, 12
samples x 5 rounds, arm-order guard [ok] by predecessor, 0 unverified of 300
probes.

  w 20 -> 40 at B=1000, predicted 1.9901 (201/101 from elements-for),
  band [1.4926, 2.4876]
  rounds 1.5490 / 1.5577 / 1.5200 / 1.4600 / 1.5111  -> REFUSED ON THE BAND

NOT NOISE, and NOT a model error. Five rounds agree within 0.10, sign is
right every round, guard clean, every probe verified. The arm's WORK doubles
exactly, and the deterministic census proves it: 4 -> 8 rows of markup,
21 -> 41 boundaries, 41 -> 81 read edges, 101 -> 201 elements.

THE CAUSE IS THE CLOCK, NOT THE ARM. The windowed arm's whole commit is
0.125 ms at w=20 and 0.195 ms at w=40 — one to two of Chrome's 100 us
performance.now() quanta (rf2-d2tzk's clamp). The per-commit floor that does
not double — dispatch, the flushSync boundary, the commit React schedules
regardless — is a large fraction of a reading that small, so the ratio
compresses toward 1. batch-k of 20 lifts the WINDOW clear of the clamp but
does not remove the floor, because the floor is paid per commit and batching
scales it with everything else.

WHAT IS NOT THE REPAIR. Widening the band: it was registered before the run
from the same elements-for arithmetic as the three arms that passed, and
1.46 is far outside it. Re-deriving the prediction now that the data is in.
Both retro-admit every run the gate exists to catch.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, none attempted (Shape 6 forbids improving a rig mid-
window; this is the file-it half):
  1. A larger window pair (w 100 -> 200) so the scaling work dominates the
     per-commit floor. Costs faithfulness: the tournament's committed
     window-size is 20, so the control would certify a page unlike the arm.
  2. Many more operations under one clock, with the floor measured
     separately and subtracted — the additive-constant treatment
     census_clock_run.cjs already computes as `additiveConstant`.
  3. Accept that the windowed arm's clock cells are unresolvable on this
     instrument and hand them to rf2-hic-080 phase 2 as unaddressed, which
     the tournament page's own pre-registration already provides for.

Option 3 may well be right and is cheap. Note the arm is ALREADY exempt from
cross-arm comparison by construction (topo/arms.cljs: "every virtual figure
is a figure about a different page"), so its refusal does not withhold any
cross-arm comparison the tournament wants to make.

Runs as its own quiet-box measurement window, Shape 6, if options 1 or 2 are
chosen. Option 3 needs no measurement at all — only a ruling.
close_reason: Ruled: candidate 3. Windowed arm's clock cells UNADDRESSED, handed to rf2-hic-080 phase 2. PR #8170. No measurement taken or owed.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
FENCE + ROUTING (mayor, 2026-08-14). Filed from inside rf2-m6i0's live window, which is the right place for it — the window certified the rendered-scale control on fine, coarse and chunked and refused on virtual, and the refusal is a DIFFERENT fault from the degeneracy that made this control necessary.

THE MEASUREMENT IS UNUSUALLY WELL-CONDITIONED, which is why this is a finding rather than a re-run: quiet box with processor queue length 0.00 throughout, five rounds agreeing within 0.10, sign right every round, arm-order guard clean by predecessor, 0 unverified of 300 probes. Predicted 1.9901 in band [1.4926, 2.4876]; rounds 1.5490 / 1.5577 / 1.5200 / 1.4600 / 1.5111.

AND THE PREDICTION IS NOT A MODEL ERROR — the deterministic census proves the arm's work doubles exactly: 4 to 8 rows of markup, 21 to 41 boundaries, 41 to 81 read edges, 101 to 201 elements. So the virtual arm does twice the work in about 1.5 times the time. That is a real sublinear result about the arm, not an instrument fault, and it is worth understanding rather than tuning away.

DO NOT WIDEN THE BAND TO ADMIT IT. A band widened to swallow a 1.5 where 2.0 was predicted stops being able to see the degeneracy this whole control was built to catch.

FENCE: rf2-m6i0's window owns this surface until it reports. CLEARS WHEN: that worker finishes. Whoever takes this bead should read m6i0's PR first — the refusal, its guard output and its census are all in that branch.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULED — candidate 3, no measurement taken. PR #8170 (docs-only, topology-tournament.md 2.6 + Part-2 headline).

THE FINDING IS NOT THE REFUSAL: this control has NO DISCRIMINATING POWER on the windowed arm in either direction. The lane's own additive constant (census_clock_run.cjs, c = tared*(P-R)/(P-1)) fits c = 0.059 ms against a 0.125 ms commit — 47% of the reading. An affine cost of that shape predicts 1.52, which is what was measured, and 1.52 sits 1.8% above the band floor of 1.4926 — 0.70 of the run's own round sd of 0.0385. Under the strict every-round rule over 5 rounds a PERFECTLY HEALTHY instrument certifies this arm about ONE RUN IN FOUR. A PASS would have been as uninformative as the refusal.

CANDIDATE 1 (w 100->200) REJECTED — certifies the wrong regime, not merely an unfaithful one. Margin is recoverable (E[R]=1.75 at w~50, within 5% of prediction at w~160-180), but the committed window is 20 and the cells are taken there. At w=100 the floor is ~15% of the reading; at w=20 it stays 47%. A green light issued in one regime over cells published in another.

CANDIDATE 2 (subtract a separately-measured floor) REJECTED on three counts, any one sufficient:
 (a) the band admits any c in [-0.007, 0.081] ms against a true 0.059, so it tests the floor ESTIMATE to within a factor of two, not the instrument. This holds EVEN IF the floor is perfectly additive.
 (b) no stable floor exists to measure: the same formula on the three certified arms returns NEGATIVE constants (fine -8.1%, coarse -4.5%, chunked -12.3%) because all three read ABOVE their prediction. +47% on one arm and negative on three is a model intercept, not a rig property.
 (c) tournament 1.7 forbade an estimator mid-series IN ADVANCE.
Its other half — more operations under one clock — is ARITHMETICALLY INERT: ratio (c+P*s)/(c+s) is independent of batch size.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S TITLE: the fault is NOT the performance.now() clamp. batch-k=20 and window! takes one now-ms pair around the whole batch, so the readings are 2.50/3.90 ms = 25/39 quanta; quantisation is at most 4.0%/2.6% against a 24% compression. The bead BODY had it right (per-commit floor); the title inherited the page's misattribution, now corrected on the page.

NO GATE LOOSENED AND NONE NEEDED: control_witness_dom_cljs_test.cljs already asserts (< 1.471 lo) on every arm's band floor, so admitting virtual's low round of 1.4600 is ALREADY RED in CI. That is why this PR changes no code.

UNEXPLAINED, FLAGGED NOT CHASED: the three certified arms read consistently ABOVE prediction (2.0809/2.0448/2.1229 vs derived 1.9996, chunked ~4 sigma). In band, threatens nothing, but suggests elements-for slightly under-predicts at 2500->5000 elements.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
TITLE CORRECTED, AND THE REASON MATTERS (mayor, 2026-08-14). The old title blamed the performance.now() clamp. The worker showed that is wrong at source: batch-k is 20 and window! takes ONE now-ms pair around the whole batch, so the readings are 2.50 and 3.90 ms — 25 and 39 quanta, with quantisation of at most 4.0% and 2.6% against a 24% compression. The bead BODY had this right; the title inherited a misattribution from the page, which the worker also corrected there. Retitled to name the actual fault: no discriminating power at the committed window size.

THE FINDING IS STRONGER THAN THE REFUSAL, and this is the part worth carrying forward. Fitting the lane's own additiveConstant to the recorded run gives c approximately 0.059 ms against a 0.125 ms commit — 47% of the reading. An affine cost of that shape predicts 1.52, which is exactly what was measured, and 1.52 sits 1.8% above the band floor of 1.4926 — 0.70 of the run's own round standard deviation of 0.0385. So under the strict every-round rule over five rounds, A PERFECTLY HEALTHY INSTRUMENT ON A PERFECTLY QUIET BOX CERTIFIES THIS ARM ABOUT ONE RUN IN FOUR. A PASS would have been exactly as uninformative as the refusal. That is a power argument, not a signal argument, and it is what makes candidate 3 correct rather than merely safe.

WHY THE OTHER TWO WERE REJECTED, both worth keeping. Candidate 1 does not just sacrifice faithfulness — it CERTIFIES THE WRONG REGIME: the margin is recoverable at larger windows, but the committed window is 20 and the cells are taken there, so it would green-light one regime over cells published in another. And separately the floor is not additive at all — the same formula returns negative constants on the three certified arms, which makes it a model intercept rather than a rig property.

IT DECLINED TO ADD A GUARD, correctly: the widening is ALREADY red in CI, because control_witness_dom_cljs_test.cljs asserts a band floor above 1.471 on every arm and admitting virtual's low round of 1.4600 would require going under it. Adding a second guard would have been gold-plating.
