title: post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml resolves github.event.before but checks out at fetch-depth 2, so a multi-commit push fails OPEN
description:
FOUND WHILE FIXING rf2-34yg (PR #8164); not touched there because .github/** is one-toucher-at-a-time and that bead's fence was the classifier only.

THE DEFECT. .github/workflows/post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml applies the rf2-7hq4l remedy correctly at line 89-95 -- it resolves the base from github.event.before with an all-zeros fallback to HEAD^ -- but its checkout at line 83 is 'fetch-depth: 2  # need parent commit for the diff'. Depth 2 holds HEAD and HEAD^ only. On a push of 2+ commits the accepted base is deeper than that and is NOT in the clone, so:

    changed=$(git diff --name-only "$before" HEAD -- '.github/workflows/*.yml'       | xargs -n1 -I{} basename {} || true)

git diff fails, the '|| true' swallows it (and swallows pipefail with it), changed is empty, and the step reports 'No workflow files changed in this push.' and exits 0. The workflow that exists to DISPATCH the workflows a push changed dispatches nothing, silently, on exactly the multi-commit pushes rf2-34yg showed are routine.

It is the same shape as rf2-34yg one file over: the base resolution is right and something upstream of it makes the base unreadable. rf2-34yg's own caller (test.yml detect_changed_surfaces) is safe because it checks out at fetch-depth: 0.

REMEDY, already in this repo. portability.yml:230-250 is the worked answer for exactly this — it keeps a shallow checkout and fetches the accepted base by name when the clone does not hold it:

    if [ -n "$base" ] && ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
      git fetch --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules --depth=1 origin "$base"
    fi

Either adopt that, or set fetch-depth: 0. Additionally the '|| true' should not be able to convert a git failure into 'nothing changed' -- fail closed, or dispatch everything, rather than silently dispatching nothing.

SECOND, SMALLER POINT. This file interpolates ${{ github.event.before }} directly into the run body. portability.yml passes the same context value through env: and states the reason (injection-safe whatever the event carries). rf2-34yg's fix followed portability.yml. Worth aligning here.

CONSTRAINTS: .github/** is hot-zone -- sequential, never parallel with another workflow-touching bead. Note this file is itself in the .github/workflows/*.yml paths filter it dispatches on.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8165. post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml now fetches the accepted base by name (portability.yml idiom) instead of relying on fetch-depth 2 to hold it; base arrives via env: rather than interpolated into the run body; the reachability check peels to ^{commit} (rf2-uol6); '|| true' removed so set -euo pipefail reds any residual failure. An unresolvable base (force-push to main) REDS and names the base rather than mark_all -- this canary gates nothing, so a red blocks nobody, while dispatching everything would spend the nightly matrix and leave no trace that the base resolution broke. Proved by implementation/scripts/_post-merge-sanity-base.test.cjs: 9 arms against a real 3-commit push in a clone shallower than its own accepted base, with the pre-fix body frozen as ARM 1 (reports 'No workflow files changed', exit 0) and a git cat-file fixture invariant preventing a vacuous pass.

comments.text: FENCE (mayor, 2026-08-14): .github/** is hot-zone and takes one toucher at a time. worker/classbase-34yg holds it on open PR #8164, which fixes the same defect class one file over (rf2-34yg, the classifier reading only a push's tip). Fail-open, defeating the very fix it applies, on exactly the multi-commit pushes rf2-34yg showed are routine. CLEARS WHEN: #8164 merges. title: five more defects in every hic bead's embedded worker protocol — two are wrong-in-effect, and one already caused PR #6677
description:
FOUND BY rf2-prbe's WORKER (2026-08-14) while repairing item 3 of the same block. It read that block more closely than anyone has and was asked what else was wrong. These are CLAIMS for triage, not work it took.

THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY PROVEN. rf2-prbe rewrote item 3 across 19 beads by exact-string anchor: the block is BYTE-IDENTICAL across all carriers (1543 chars, exactly one occurrence per bead, one distinct variant), and the pass changed exactly 19 of 1123 descriptions, every delta exactly +267 chars, zero collateral, zero movement in title/status/priority/type/owner/labels/dependencies. So a second pass over the same block is cheap and low-risk — the anchoring problem is solved.

POPULATION, measured not estimated: 88 carriers — 67 closed, 18 open, 2 in_progress, 1 deferred. Scope this the same way rf2-prbe did: rewrite open + deferred, leave closed alone (nobody dispatches from a closed bead), and SKIP in_progress under the standing 'never amend a bead once in_progress' rule — those workers read the text at dispatch, so an edit cannot reach them anyway, while mutating a bead under a live worker is the exact risk that rule exists to prevent.

THE FIVE, in the reporter's priority order.

1. ITEM 5 UNDER-STATES THE .beads RULE, AND THIS ONE HAS ALREADY COST THE PROJECT. It says never commit '.beads/* DATABASE FILES'. The actual prohibition covers .beads/issues.jsonl and .beads/metadata.json, which are EXPORTS, not database files. A worker reading it narrowly concludes the JSONL is fair game — and that is precisely what PR #6677 did, landing 135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral and time-travelling the tracker (beads closed since reopened, beads filed since vanished). CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section is the authority; item 5 should name the two paths explicitly and say why: a worker branch carries a snapshot from when its worktree was created.

2. ITEM 7'S HOT-ZONE LIST IS A STRICT SUBSET OF THE PROJECT'S. It names only shadow-cljs.edn, deps.edn and .github/workflows/*, omitting the spec/*.md hot files. So a hicasso bead touching spec/004-Views.md is AFFIRMATIVELY TOLD it is not hot-zone. Wrong-in-effect rather than impossible, which is worse: a worker obeys it confidently and gets the wrong answer.

3. ITEM 10 POINTS AT A CLOSED BEAD INSTEAD OF THE ARTEFACT. The correction ledger is docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md; rf2-hic-073 is closed. The still-open checkpoint beads (hic-038, hic-048, hic-064) are exactly item 10's audience, so this is live text pointing somewhere useless.

4. THE PATH MAP IS STALE. It says 'Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist' — hic-000 is closed and all three documents exist in-tree, verified. Dead text inside a mandatory block.

5. NO GATE IS NAMED FOR docs/design/hicasso EDITS, though hic-060, hic-068 and hic-069 are doc beads. mkdocs --strict deliberately EXCLUDES that tree (mkdocs.yml exclude_docs), while check_doc_slugs.py and check_provenance_pins.py cover it, and anchors plus table column counts need hand-verification stated in the PR body. A gap rather than a contradiction — but the reporter flags it as the LIKELIEST NEXT IMPROVISATION, because the newly repaired item 3 now tells a doc worker to size its gate against the harness ceiling without telling it which gate it owns.

TRIAGE NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: 1 and 2 are the ones that matter and both are wrong-in-effect. 3 and 4 are stale-pointer minutiae, cheap to fix in the same pass and not worth a pass of their own. 5 is a genuine gap and the only one that requires deciding something rather than correcting something.

MANDATORY MECHANICAL WARNING, learned the hard way in rf2-prbe: 'bd show --json' PIPED through the shell on this box mangles non-ASCII — U+2014 came back as replacement characters, inflating a 2644-char description to 2660. REDIRECT TO A FILE and read UTF-8; never pipe. Piping would have silently corrupted every em dash in all 19 descriptions. This block is full of em dashes.

It was reopened at 07:19 by the mayor's stranded sweep — its worker had finished and its PR merged, but a bead left open for an unfinished half does not reset the claim, so it sat in_progress with nobody holding it. Reason unrelated to this pass; no work lost.

Replacing the whole 1543-char block with the whole 3217-char block avoids that entirely. The composition was proved first: 1543 + rf2-prbe's item-3 line == the 1810 variant byte-exactly, and +267 plus +1407 == the +1674 observed, so the one-shot lands on exactly the text the other 19 carry.

title: the changed-surface classifier reads only the TIP of a multi-commit push to main, so a rebase-merge can leave the trunk run classifying nothing
description:
FOUND WHILE AUDITING rf2-2ddm (that bead's own question was refuted -- 'JVM http' is armed by implementation_jvm, the classifier's BROADEST output, gating 22 jobs including jvm-core, and it DOES run on pushes to main: 10 of the last 25 trunk runs, all green). This is the separate defect that audit turned up. Same finding, distinct owner and surface -- not a second report of rf2-2ddm.

THE DEFECT. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:24-38 resolves its base from the event. The pull_request branch uses 'origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}...HEAD' and is correct. EVERY OTHER EVENT, including push to main, falls through to:

    files="$(git diff --no-renames --name-only HEAD^ HEAD 2>/dev/null || ...)"

One push event produces ONE workflow run, at the tip SHA. A PR rebase-merged with N commits therefore has its trunk run classified on commit N alone; commits 1..N-1 are invisible to the classifier and get no run of their own.

ALREADY NAMED AND ALREADY FIXED TWICE IN THIS REPO. .github/workflows/portability.yml:175-190 documents the exact defect verbatim: 'push to main: github.event.before, the tip main pointed at before this push. On a MULTI-COMMIT push HEAD^ is only the second-to-last commit of this same push, so a path first tracked in an earlier commit and retained at the tip is present on both sides and escapes (the rf2-7hq4l defect).' portability.yml (rf2-ow7dz / rf2-7hq4l) and post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml:89-92 BOTH resolve the base from github.event.before with a zero-SHA fallback to HEAD^. The changed-surface classifier -- which gates 35 outputs and ~22 JVM jobs -- still uses bare HEAD^.

TWO REPRODUCED INSTANCES.

(a) PR #8159, a 4-commit push (351acca2 -> 858f22fe). Only the tip got a run (31742435731); the other three have no run at their SHA. Classify tip alone (docs/design/hicasso/product/topology-tournament.md) -> NOTHING armed. Classify the whole push (adds 4 implementation/freehand/test/** files) -> implementation_jvm, cljs_node_test, cljs_browser, examples_compile, cljs_prod, migration_hicasso_codemod. Run 31742435731 reported 'All required checks passed' on main having run only the always-on spine: 78 jobs, every surface-gated one skipped.

(b) THE rf2-mvq7 REPAIR ITSELF WAS SWALLOWED. Commit ebd92e12d2 ('ci: give the narrow-armed gates an arm against main') touched expensive-tests.yml AND TESTING.md -- both mark_all triggers. Its push tip was 74c7d2971f, touching only scripts/test-rigorous-local.sh. Classify tip only -> 0 outputs true. Classify whole push -> 32 outputs true. The full-matrix run that editing TESTING.md exists to FORCE never happened on main.

RATE: over the last 60 main commits, 5 code-carrying commits got no test.yml run at their SHA -- c0edf2b6e2, e4863e0a9e, b01fd1d3c9, 6c31c345d1, ebd92e12d2.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY COSTS, STATED HONESTLY. It creates NO exposure relative to the PR gate: each of those commits was fully classified and gated on its PR against the correct base...HEAD diff. What it degrades is the POST-MERGE net -- the run whose job is to catch a semantic conflict between two PRs each green alone, and to honour mark_all when CI's own configuration changes. On a multi-commit push that net currently reports 'All required checks passed' over a run that executed no code gate. That is why this is P2 and not P1.

REMEDY (small, and already written twice here): in report-changed-surfaces.sh, resolve the base from github.event.before when GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=push, with the zero-SHA fallback to HEAD^ that post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml already uses; keep the pull_request branch exactly as is. Copy the idiom rather than inventing one.

CONSTRAINTS: .github/** is hot-zone -- sequential dispatch, never parallel with another workflow-touching bead. Note report-changed-surfaces.sh is itself a mark_all trigger, so the PR that changes it runs the full matrix. ACCEPTANCE: a multi-commit push to main classifies over the whole push; state in the PR body which of the 5 named commits above would have armed what.

comments.text:
AUDIT OF PR #8164 — implementation quality / local-gate portability.

The production push-range logic is sound, and the separate post-merge-workflow-sanity fail-open is already owned exactly by rf2-8oh5. The six new regression tests, however, are red from this repository's supplied PowerShell environment. `node implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` exits 1 on the whole-push and unresolvable-base cases because `execFileSync("bash", ...)` resolves to `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` (WSL); WSL imports only variables named in WSLENV, so the helper's `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` and `CHANGED_SURFACES_BASE_REF` never reach the classifier. A direct probe reads both as empty, and the classifier correctly falls back to HEAD^. Running the identical suite under `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` passes all 354 cases, which isolates the defect to the test transport rather than the production classifier.

Minimal repair: make `classifyViaGitDiscovery` transport its three test-controlled environment values across the Windows→WSL launcher (for example by extending WSLENV on win32 or by a safe argv/stdin export wrapper), while preserving Git Bash/Linux behavior. Pin that the child actually sees the supplied base. The ordinary documented `node ...` gate should not depend on which `bash.exe` PowerShell finds first.

CLOSED AND EXEMPLARY — recording two things worth keeping (mayor, 2026-08-14).

THE PREMISE WAS STARKER THAN THE AUDIT PUT IT. The audit framed the fault as depending on 'which bash.exe PowerShell finds first'. Eight sibling suites under implementation/scripts/ also spawn bash: seven pass no env at all, and one uses a cleanEnv() that only DELETES — which is safe under WSL, because a variable that never crosses is already absent. It concluded 'no follow-up bead needed' and was right; a worker that filed one per sibling would have created eight beads for zero defects. That is the stance's 'a finding is a CLAIM, not a queue' applied by a worker without being asked.

title: U5's registered estimand cannot see a coarse arm that inlines its rows
description:
FOUND BY rf2-hic-036's topology tournament (2026-08-14), on measured integers.

U5 is registered in docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md §4 as 'Narrow-update body work scales with changed rows, not all mounted rows', family DETERMINISTIC, estimand BOUNDARY BODIES RUN, pinned as D1-D4.

THE HOLE. The tournament's coarse view-model arm rebuilds ALL B rows for a ONE-row change -- exactly what U5's English forbids -- and reads 1 boundary body, so it PASSES U5 as registered. Measured, all three row counts:

  arm       bodies on a narrow update   rows of markup built   U5 as registered
  fine      1                           1                      passes
  virtual   1                           1                      passes
  chunked   1                           25                     passes
  coarse    1                           B (100/300/1000)       PASSES

WHY D3/D4 DO NOT ALREADY COVER IT. D3/D4 exist precisely to catch a coarse topology and do catch one -- 'coarse shape with closure props moves it to 26/101' -- because that witness's coarse shape still holds PER-CELL BOUNDARIES to count. A coarse shape that INLINES its rows has no boundaries beneath the family at all, so the same instrument reads 1. That is not an exotic spelling; it is the ordinary way a view-model arm is written, and it is the arm the hot-path lane recommends for cheap bulk (lanes/hot-path-architecture.md, read-topology guidance).

CONSEQUENCE. A gate built on U5's current estimand would certify the one topology this tournament shows fails the property, at every row count, untunably.

THE REPAIR IS A SECOND COUNTER, not a wider line: rows-of-markup-built (or an equivalent work counter) alongside bodies-run. rf2-hic-036 already ships one -- implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/topo/arms.cljs increments :markup inside the single shared row-markup fn, and its census cross-checks it against arm1.runtime/body-runs on all 48 cells.

OWNER: rf2-hic-071 / rf2-hic-089 own turning budget rows into gates; this is a defect in the row they would be gating on. Filed rather than patched in the hic-036 window because budgets.md rows are hic-071's to update by its own fence.

Deterministic family -- needs NO quiet box and no measurement window.

title: MEASURE: a non-degenerate positive control for the COARSE-family topology arms
description:
FOUND BY rf2-hic-036's measurement window (2026-08-14), and it is the single thing blocking that bead's clock half.

THE FAULT. rf2-hic-036 pre-registered rf2-7iqb5's prescribed changed-set-doubling control (hold page size fixed, double the changed set, predict 2.00x on commit-side work) and built it: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/topo/control_app.cljs, over the :topo/bump-stride write in topo/model.cljs.

It is DEGENERATE on two of the four arms, and this was derived from the tournament's own measured integers rather than guessed:

  arm       markup at stride 10   at stride 5   predicted
  fine      B/10                  B/5           2.00  discriminating
  virtual   2                     4             2.00  discriminating
  coarse    B                     B             1.00  DEGENERATE
  chunked   B                     B             1.00  DEGENERATE

coarse and chunked rebuild every row whichever stride runs, so doubling the changed set doubles nothing they do. A control predicting 2.00x there would refuse a healthy instrument; one predicting 1.00x discriminates nothing. Either way those arms have NO positive control, and since every interesting tournament comparison crosses between a fine-family and a coarse-family arm, the whole clock table is withheld.

THE REPAIR, which is a DIFFERENT control rather than a wider band. For the coarse family the update cost genuinely IS proportional to the page, because the arm rebuilds everything on any write. So page-doubling — the control rf2-7iqb5 correctly rejected for update rows in general — is VALID here, for precisely the reason it was invalid there. Predicted factor comes from element arithmetic (topo/model.cljs elements-for), not from a flat 2.00, per the census_clock_arms/ctl-predicted discipline.

Acceptance: each of the four arms carries a positive control whose predicted factor is bounded away from 1.00 and derived from committed arithmetic; the control refuses on sign as well as band (PR #7634's fix); rf2-hic-036's clock cells are then taken or refused on the control's verdict rather than for want of one.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN THE hic-036 WINDOW: adding a rung between runs makes the series two instruments. Shape 6 forbids improving the rig mid-window; this is the file-it half of that rule.

Runs as its own quiet-box measurement window, Shape 6, in the lane order rf2-2rtt6.140's notes carry.
close_reason:
Acceptance met, on a scope the work itself corrected (mayor, 2026-08-14). Original acceptance was 'a non-degenerate positive control on all four COARSE-family arms'. Delivered: a rendered-scale control that CERTIFIES fine, coarse and chunked (PR #8166, merged), and a source-located RULING that the windowed arm's clock cells are unaddressable at the committed window size (rf2-4t36, PR #8170, merged). Three certified, one ruled — nothing further is owed.

WHY THE FOURTH ARM IS A RULING RATHER THAN A GAP. rf2-4t36 showed the control has no discriminating power on virtual in EITHER direction: fitting the lane's own additiveConstant gives c approximately 0.059 ms against a 0.125 ms commit, 47% of the reading. An affine cost of that shape predicts 1.52, which is what was measured, and 1.52 sits 0.70 of the run's own round sd above the band floor — so a perfectly healthy instrument on a perfectly quiet box would certify that arm about one run in four. A PASS would have been exactly as uninformative as the refusal. That is a power result, not a failure to measure.

WHAT THIS BEAD PRODUCED BEYOND ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE. The design constraint that explains both predecessor failures: A MANIPULATION CERTIFIES AN INSTRUMENT ONLY WHEN EVERY COST IN THE WINDOW MOVES WITH IT. Both earlier controls were right about one arm and degenerate elsewhere — one fault in two directions — because each moved only part of the cost. That sentence is the reusable output.

BAND NOT WIDENED, PREDICTION NOT RE-DERIVED after seeing data, and a test asserts every band still refuses the 1.331-1.471 run it replaced.

WHAT REMAINS ELSEWHERE, and it was never this bead's: rf2-hic-036's clock table is still withheld entire because topo/ HAS NO CLOCK DRIVER — the 4x4 cells were never instrumented. The control refusing first masked that absence. rf2-hic-080 phase 2 now receives the windowed arm's cells as UNADDRESSED in its own frozen vocabulary rather than as pending an instrument.

comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS FROM THE RUN, added by rf2-hic-036's window after the control was actually taken (2026-08-14). The control did not merely turn out degenerate on coarse/chunked -- it REFUSED on fine, the arm where it is non-degenerate, and the run diagnosed why.

Measured, B=1000, fine arm, 20 commits under one clock, 12 samples x 5 rounds, arms interleaved, box queue length 0.00, arm-order guard PASSED by predecessor and by phase:

  round   d10 p50 (ms/20)   d5 p50    ratio
  1       44.80             59.65     1.331
  2       44.35             61.50     1.387
  3       44.45             63.30     1.424
  4       44.50             65.45     1.471
  5       48.35             64.05     1.325

Predicted 2.00, band [1.60, 2.50]. REFUSED ON THE BAND. Exit 1 captured from the runner.

NOT NOISE: five rounds agree to within 0.15, ranges are tight, sign is right every round, and the order guard found no positional effect. It is a strong stable signal that is not 2.00.

WHY. The measured window holds three costs and only one doubles. :topo/bump-stride reduce-kv's the WHOLE thousand-row table at both strides; the subscription layer re-evaluates all 1000 [:topo/row i] cells at both strides; only the 100->200 rows of markup actually double. The shared constant term compresses the ratio toward 1 -- which is the SAME failure rf2-7iqb5 recorded for page-scaling controls, reappearing inside the control built to replace them.

SO THIS BEAD GROWS A SECOND HALF. A valid changed-set control needs the event handler AND the subscription layer to cost in proportion to the changed set, not just the render. An indexed write (assoc-in per changed row) and a per-row sub that is not recomputed for unchanged rows are the shape to test. Until that holds, 'hold the page fixed and double the changed set' does not certify an update row either.

NOTHING WAS WIDENED. The band stands at [1.60, 2.50] and the 2.00 prediction was not re-derived after seeing the data.

title: mayor-posture.md: the stranded sweep reads the REMOTE tip, which lags a linked worktree and false-signals a strand
description:
The stranded sweep's step 1 tells the mayor to read a worker's branch tip with `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/worker/<name>`. In THIS repo that is the wrong ref, and it lags in the one direction that reads as death.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 05:15 AUSEST, three live workers at once. `git ls-remote` reported every one of them UNCHANGED since the previous tick (ciretire-cluster 42244fecca, walkctl-1huc 2bff6ed748, legexcess-oiy1 absent). Their LOCAL refs at the same instant read ciretire-cluster b26de366d4 (committed 04:59) and walkctl-1huc 73508c1339 (committed 05:08). All three were healthy and mid-gate. Step 3 applied mechanically on the remote reading would have reopened five beads (rf2-oiy1, rf2-1huc, rf2-oae1, rf2-mvq7, rf2-8z9q) and redispatched a second executor over live work — the exact failure "no concurrent workers same branch" exists to prevent.

WHY THE REMOTE LAGS HERE. Every worker worktree is a LINKED worktree sharing one `.git`, so a worker's commit updates the local ref the instant it lands. `origin` only moves when that worker chooses to push, which a briefed worker does at milestones rather than continuously. The remote is therefore a lagging indicator of liveness.

WHY THE OLD WORDING'S REASON DOES NOT APPLY. The "ask the REMOTE" instruction was imported from the PULL path, where the concern is real and documented: a fetch there reads what the shared `.git/FETCH_HEAD` left behind. But `git rev-parse <branch>` consults the local ref directly and performs NO fetch, so it never touches that file. The contamination the rule guards against cannot reach this read.

SECOND HALF, EQUALLY LOAD-BEARING. An unchanged SHA must be corroborated with worktree file activity before it means anything, because a worker inside a 25-minute gate commits nothing BY DESIGN — a still SHA is the expected reading for the commonest healthy state, not a warning. `find <worktree> -newermt '20 minutes ago' -type f | grep -v '/\.git/' | wc -l` settles it in one command: the three workers above returned 8,025, 10,443 and 5,517 touched files, and ciretire-cluster carried a `.scratch/test-fast-pr.run` marker naming the gate outright. Near-zero is what a strand actually looks like.

THE EDIT — one file, `.claude/commands/mayor-posture.md`, replace the whole of numbered item 1 in the stranded-sweep list.

REPLACE THIS LINE EXACTLY (it is line 22 at the time of filing):

1. **Has that bead's branch TIP SHA moved since the last tick?** `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/worker/<name>`, against the SHA you recorded last tick. **Never a commit count, and never `%ar`.** `mayor-hygiene.md` carries why each misleads and is the one place that reasoning lives — the short of it is that the ahead count and the author date are both replayed unchanged by a rebase, while the tip SHA and `%cI` move (rf2-0vvw). Ask the REMOTE; a fetch first reads what the shared `.git/FETCH_HEAD` left behind.

WITH THIS:

1. **Has that bead's branch TIP SHA moved since the last tick?** `git rev-parse worker/<name>`, against the SHA you recorded last tick. **Never a commit count, and never `%ar`.** `mayor-hygiene.md` carries why each misleads and is the one place that reasoning lives — the short of it is that the ahead count and the author date are both replayed unchanged by a rebase, while the tip SHA and `%cI` move (rf2-0vvw).

   **Read the LOCAL ref, not `git ls-remote` — this line said "ask the REMOTE" until 2026-08-14 and it produced a false strand signal on three workers at once.** The remote rule was imported from the *pull* path, where the concern is real: a fetch there reads what the shared `.git/FETCH_HEAD` left behind. But `git rev-parse <branch>` consults the local ref directly and performs no fetch, so it never touches that file — the contamination this rule was guarding against cannot reach it. Meanwhile every worker worktree here is a LINKED worktree sharing one `.git`, so a worker's commit updates the local ref the instant it lands, while `origin` only moves when that worker chooses to push — which a briefed worker does at milestones, not continuously. The remote is therefore a LAGGING indicator, and lagging in exactly the direction that reads as death. Measured on 2026-08-14 05:15: `ls-remote` reported all three live workers unchanged since the previous tick, while their local refs showed `ciretire-cluster` at `b26de366d4` committed 04:59 and `walkctl-1huc` at `73508c1339` committed 05:08. All three were healthy; step 3 applied mechanically would have reopened five beads and redispatched over live work.

   **And corroborate an unchanged SHA with worktree activity before it means anything.** A worker inside a twenty-five-minute gate commits nothing by design, so a still SHA is the *expected* reading for the commonest healthy state. `find <worktree> -newermt '20 minutes ago' -type f | grep -v '/\.git/' | wc -l` settles it in one command: the three workers above returned 8,025, 10,443 and 5,517 touched files, and a `.scratch/test-fast-pr.run` marker named the gate outright. Near-zero is what a strand looks like.

ACCEPTANCE. `.claude/commands/mayor-posture.md` item 1 reads as above. Nothing else in the file changes — in particular the STANCE block at the top is untouched, and the closing sentence "A MOVED SHA says alive; a STILL SHA authorises nothing on its own" already agrees with the new text and stays exactly as it is.

WHY A WORKER AND NOT THE MAYOR. The mayor tried this edit directly and the pre-commit hook refused it, correctly: `.claude/commands/**` is a worker-tracked surface and only `.beads/issues.jsonl` and `MEMORY.md` are permitted in a mayor commit. That refusal is the hook working as documented in docs/the-mayor-method/README.md, and the sanctioned response is to file the item with the fix written out and dispatch it. This bead is that.

title: hicasso: walk_profile_app has no positive control — run.cjs's control exit path is dead for this arm
description:
FOUND BY THE 2026-08-14 rf2-y1jkm MEASUREMENT WINDOW, and deliberately NOT repaired there: building an instrument mid-window is what the measurement discipline forbids.

`run.cjs` reads `window.HICASSO_CONTROL_FAILED` and exits 1 when a positive control did not see the change its own arithmetic predicts. `walk_profile_app.cljs` never sets it and never calls `lane/control-verdict`, so for the walk-profile arm that exit path is dead. Seven sibling arms DO set it (coldmount_app, direct_return_clock_app, inpage_ladder_app, p0_converge_app, p0_reagent_app).

CONSEQUENCE: every figure the walk profile has ever published — the studio page's section 1 attribution, its section 2 in-process A/B, and the 2026-08-14 section 7 re-take — is guarded against ORDERING (lane/guard!, exit 2) and against PAGE FIDELITY (the twin-parity gate, fatal) but NOT against the instrument having signal at all. That is a rig property, not a defect in any one run.

THE RAW MATERIAL IS ALREADY THERE, unasserted. Two arms do strictly MORE work than `local` by construction — `parse-raw` (every tag parsed fresh) and `no-propless` (567 propless elements forced through the map path) — and one does strictly more than `ship` (`ship-lazy`). In the 2026-08-14 run all three read in the predicted direction (parse-raw 1.0000 > local 0.7125; no-propless 0.7313 > local 0.7125; ship-lazy 1.6500 > ship 0.5500), but nothing checks it, so a run where they inverted would still print a table and exit 0.

CANDIDATE, to be costed not assumed: adapt `lane/control-verdict` to the `parse-raw` arm, whose prediction is the cleanest — the page's 1,202 tag parses at the micro table's measured fresh-minus-cached cost. Note lane/control-verdict carries its own KNOWN DEFECT (its overlap rule is weaker than hd8-rows/positive-control!'s every-round-inside rule, documented on the fn and needing an operator ruling); a new control should not inherit the weak rule silently.

The bead that found this: rf2-y1jkm, PR from worker/mountwalk-y1jkm.
notes:
CORRECTION to this bead's close reason, same worker, 2026-08-14. I wrote that the
three link probe apps (link_decomp/link_inner/link_term) 'call lane/control-verdict
without ever setting it, which is a separate dead-exit-path instance'. That is
WRONG and I checked it only after writing it. All three DO act on a failed control:
they `throw` on `(not (:ok? ctl))`, the surrounding `.catch` routes it through
`lane/fail!` -> `HICASSO_ERROR`, and `run.cjs` exits 1 on that branch. Their
controls bite. What is true, and is minutiae rather than a defect, is that the lane
has two conventions for one outcome — five arms set the flag, three throw — and only
the flag route prints run.cjs's specific control-failure message. Both exit 1. Not
filed as a bead.

The bead's own count is also slightly off and equally inconsequential: it says seven
sibling arms set HICASSO_CONTROL_FAILED and names five; five is right.

Directly invoking the exact function compiled from merge 825cd611c8cd193c4344cd7b5a9208780b1de4b4 reproduced both fail-open cases:

title: hicasso controlled-input: the re-navigation mount-wait has no ceiling (anonymous 30s), webkit flake ~1/40
description:
`implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs:914` waits for the testbed root after a
re-navigation with NO ceiling:

    await page.goto(`${base}?arm-ms=${ARM_MS}`,
      { waitUntil: ctx.navWaitUntil, timeout: ctx.navTimeoutMs });
    await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="hicasso-controlled-testbed"]');

The `goto` on the line above correctly carries the runner's ceiling — the
section even REFUSES to run if `ctx.navTimeoutMs` is absent, with a comment
naming the anonymous-30s defect. The mount-wait immediately after then takes
Playwright's anonymous 30s anyway. The runner's own equivalent wait
(`serve-and-run-hicasso-controlled-testbed.cjs:679`) names its budget
explicitly: `{ timeout: SPEC_TIMEOUT_MS }` (90000).

So one operation — navigate, then wait for the app to mount — is bounded by two
different budgets depending on which of the two places performs it, and the
second budget is invisible in the source and unreachable from
`HICASSO_TESTBED_SPEC_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## Observed

PR #8146 run 31705997516, job 94467926267: chromium PASS 97/13, firefox PASS
97/13, webkit FAIL in the last section, `armed-edges-are-wired`:

    page.waitForSelector: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
      - waiting for locator('[data-testid="hicasso-controlled-testbed"]') to be visible
      at armedEdgesAreWired (implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs:914:14)

webkit completed the preceding twelve sections in about six seconds, then spent
thirty on the re-navigation's mount. The 90000ms lane budget sat unused. That is
exactly the failure shape `_navigation-ceiling-policy.test.cjs` was written
about: its own header says «"Timeout 30000ms exceeded" reads like the lane's own
timeout, so the fix reached for is a bigger lane timeout, which cannot move it».

Rate, measured over the 120 most recent `test.yml` runs (2026-08-13T02:36 →
2026-08-13T13:39, the window in which the job ran 42 times): 38 success, 3
cancelled, 1 failure — the one above. So roughly 1 in 40, not a hard break.

## Why the sweep did not catch it

`_navigation-ceiling-policy.test.cjs` sweeps
`NAV_METHODS = ['goto','reload','goBack','goForward','waitForNavigation']`.
Element-wait APIs are outside that list, so a bare `waitForSelector` is not a
sweep violation today — it is the same defect (an anonymous 30s that no lane
knob can reach) wearing a name the sweep does not police.

Repo-wide there are 22 `waitForSelector` calls and exactly three are bare:

- `implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs:914`
- `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/jsfb_ours_run.cjs:626`
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/live-e2e-fixture.cjs:379`

## Not settled here, deliberately

Whether webkit was merely SLOW (in which case a named ceiling fixes it) or
genuinely HUNG (in which case a named ceiling only relabels the failure) is not
established — the failure did not reproduce locally. `npm run
test:hicasso-controlled` on `worker/gatearm-6ng7` rebased onto `c5f4c68795`
passed all three engines, captured exit 0, 97 checks across 13 sections each.
So this bead is the finding, not a proven remedy. Whoever takes it should
establish the mechanism before choosing between "name the number" and something
larger.

Suggested shape, in ascending cost:
1. Give line 914 the lane's budget, the way the runner's own wait does.
2. Consider whether the policy sweep should cover element-wait APIs at all, or
   whether that is over-reach for three call sites.

Discovered from the rf2-6ng7 gate-arming audit (PR #8146) purely because that
PR touches `.github/workflows/test.yml`, which arms `hicasso_controlled`. It is
unrelated to that PR's subject and nothing in #8146 can affect it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8149 (commit 961dbe14af). MECHANISM ESTABLISHED AS HUNG, NOT SLOW, on three readings: (1) the CI artefact — the stack puts the failure inside the spec's own wait and the runner's buffered log for that engine carries NO pageerror, so the app did not throw, the goto succeeded and the mount never arrived; (2) a measurement of the operation itself — 40 consecutive local webkit re-navigations with the same multi-second idle gap the real section has read p50 80ms, max 108ms, zero stalls, so 30,000ms is 375x the median; (3) the lane had budget — SPEC.run is already wrapped in a 90,000ms withTimeout and only ~6s had been spent, so the anonymous ceiling ended it, not the lane. The MECHANISM of the stall is NOT established (0 stalls in 40 local trials), so the remedy is the named ceiling AND a self-diagnosing failure: on timeout the wait now reports whether the bundle arrived, whether it began executing, whether anything mounted and whether the root is present-but-invisible, which separates every candidate including waitForSelector's default 'visible' state being itself the bug. The next occurrence closes the question instead of re-filing. Ceiling is ctx.navTimeoutMs — the section's own stated principle applied to the half of the operation it had not reached (under waitUntil 'commit' the mount-wait IS the navigation's second half) — and strictly under the 90,000ms lane budget so it fires first and names the call site. All three bare waitForSelector sites fixed and the sweep now polices the name, which is the sweep's own argument (it already lists three navigation methods with no call in the repo 'because they are the same defect wearing a different name'); sweep proven to bite by re-baring one call. Three engines PASS, 97 checks x 13 sections each, unchanged. PREMISES THAT DID NOT HOLD: the bead says shape 1 is 'give line 914 the lane's budget', but ctx carries only navTimeoutMs (60000), never SPEC_TIMEOUT_MS (90000) — the spec cannot reach 90000; and because SPEC.run is already wrapped at 90000, a 90000 inner ceiling could never fire, so that shape would have moved the failure to withTimeout and LOST the call site.

title: [bug] three source-walk roots reach jvm-core's repo-wide lint suites but do not arm implementation_jvm (rf2-6ng7 audit finding)
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-6ng7 bounded audit of non-local input edges. Filed rather than
fixed there, because the repair is a COST RULING rather than a mechanism: the
cheap arm is broad, and the narrow arm does not exist.

THE EDGE. Four JVM suites in `implementation/core/test/` are repo-wide source
WALKS, not core tests. They discover their inputs by `file-seq` / `.listFiles`
over trees outside their own artefact, and every one of them runs in `jvm-core`,
which only `implementation_jvm` gates:

  no_rf_default_floor_lint_test.clj      walks implementation/**/src AND
                                         tools/**/src (its own docstring:
                                         "extended to also cover the sibling
                                         tools/ tree")
  egress_chokepoint_conformance_test.clj `impl-src-roots` = EVERY directory
                                         under implementation/ that has a src/
  error_catalogue_channel_conformance_   same `impl-src-roots` construction
    test.clj
  warn_once_clear_governance_test.clj    file-seq over implementation/

MEASURED ON MAIN at d70b671b7b, `bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh
<path>`:

  tools/xray/src/day8/x.cljs             implementation_jvm=false
  tools/story/src/x.cljs                 implementation_jvm=false
  tools/mcp-base/src/x.clj               implementation_jvm=false
  implementation/hicasso/src/x.cljs      implementation_jvm=false
  implementation/ssr-node/src/x.cljs     implementation_jvm=false

(Every other implementation artefact's src DOES arm it -- core, adapters, ui,
machines, routing, flows, http, ssr, ssr-ring, resources, security, schemas,
epoch, freehand, spec-resource, test-quiet all read true. These three roots are
the holes.)

SO: a `tools/`, `implementation/hicasso/src/` or `implementation/ssr-node/src/`
change that introduces an `(or frame-kw :rf/default)` floor, an egress-chokepoint
violation, an uncatalogued error channel or a warn-once governance breach merges
GREEN, and the red lands on main for the next unrelated implementation PR to
discover. That is the rf2-61ar incident shape exactly (PR #8068 left five
assertions red on main until an unrelated PR happened to arm the tier).

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED UNDER rf2-6ng7. The other four instances that audit found
had a cheap narrow repair. This one does not:

  (a) arm implementation_jvm for tools/** + implementation/{hicasso,ssr-node}/src
      -- correct, one-line-ish, and it queues the whole 22-job JVM tier on every
      tools/ and hicasso/ source edit. Those are two of the busiest trees in the
      repo; this is the expensive option and it is a standing tax.
  (b) move the tools/ half of the floor lint into a tools-side suite, so
      `tools_jvm` arms it -- narrower, but it is a code change that splits one
      invariant across two homes, and a split invariant is the class this bead
      belongs to.
  (c) accept the exposure for the three roots and say so in the suites'
      docstrings, so the next reader is not misled about coverage.

There is no narrower OUTPUT to reach for: `implementation_jvm` is the single
flag all 22 per-artefact JVM jobs gate on, and rf2-w9ip established (and
rf2-6ng7 re-affirmed) that minting a second output would have to be taught to
`scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` as well and then held in step with the classifier --
a fresh instance of this very class.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) for the two implementation roots (hicasso and ssr-node are
the only artefacts paying nothing today, and every sibling artefact already
pays), and a ruling on tools/. Whichever is chosen, the fix pins its own arming
in `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` in the same patch, per
the rf2-6ng7 codicil -- derived from `impl-src-roots` / `repo-tools-root` in the
suites' own source, never restated.

title: Concurrent heavyweight gates wedge the machine, and no block warns a worker or bounds the dispatcher
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 19:43 AUSEST by rf2-qw0o's worker, reported in its completion report. Not yet independently reproduced by the mayor — treat the numbers as that worker's measurement.

WHAT HAPPENED. Two workers ran 'npm run test:cljs' concurrently, each holding about 3.5 GB, and BOTH WEDGED. Neither failed cleanly; both hung. The worker recovered by correlating its own build artefact's mtime against process start times, killing only its own process, after which the sibling recovered once memory freed.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES THIS. The gate-mechanics block in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md covers a great deal about how a gate is run — absolute paths, captured exit codes, per-attempt artefact names, orphaned children, sabotage restores. It says NOTHING about a gate that is heavyweight enough that two of them cannot coexist. And nothing on the dispatch side bounds how many workers may be inside a heavyweight gate at once: mayor-dispatch.md targets six concurrent workers and reasons only about FILE-surface collisions, never about a shared RESOURCE.

So the failure is invisible to both layers. A worker following every rule perfectly can still wedge a peer that is also following every rule perfectly.

THE SHAPE OF THE HAZARD IS DIFFERENT FROM THE ONE ALREADY DOCUMENTED. The existing rules protect against two workers writing the same ARTEFACT (scratch collisions, orphaned writers, per-attempt naming). This is contention for the MACHINE, and the artefact rules do nothing for it — both workers had correct, distinct filenames throughout.

FIX SHAPES, none ruled — and the honest answer may be more than one:
(a) name the hazard in the gate-mechanics block so a worker recognises a wedge instead of diagnosing it as its own bug. The recovery this worker used — correlate your own build artefact mtime against process start times, kill only yours — is worth writing down; it is not obvious under pressure.
(b) bound the dispatcher: treat a heavyweight gate as an EXCLUSIVE RESOURCE the way loops.md already treats a measurement window, and sequence rather than parallel when several dispatches will all run one.
(c) refuse: argue six workers rarely gate simultaneously and the cost is a re-run. Weigh this honestly — the wave that produced this had four to six workers live.

A RELATED ERROR FROM THE SAME REPORT, worth folding in wherever (a) lands: that worker also 'briefly mis-killed a healthy run by misjudging elapsed time — I assumed 17 minutes had passed when it was ~2'. That is the same defect class the mayor hit in the stranded sweep and rf2-0vvw fixed: TIME-BASED REASONING ABOUT A RUNNING PROCESS. Before killing anything on elapsed time, read the clock. The generic lesson is that elapsed-time inference is unreliable on both sides of the fence.

SEQUENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/** is a shared surface and PR #8135 is currently OPEN against it. Do not dispatch a second editor onto that tree.
notes:
HELD 2026-08-13 19:43 AUSEST for the same reason as rf2-z6or: the mayor announced a deliberate fleet drain to reach the quiet-machine condition Mike's standing authorisation requires. Also SEQUENCED behind PR #8135, which is open against docs/the-mayor-method/.

NOTE THE IRONY AND DO NOT LOSE IT: this bead is about heavyweight gates contending for one machine. The measurement windows it would compete with (rf2-hic-036, rf2-hic-045) are fenced for EXACTLY the same reason — they need a quiet machine. Fix shape (b) proposes treating a heavyweight gate as an exclusive resource the way loops.md already treats a measurement window. That is not a coincidence; it is the same constraint seen from two directions, and whoever takes this bead should say so rather than inventing a second vocabulary for it.
close_reason: Landed in PR #8141 (worker/methoddocs-cluster), MERGED. Shapes (a) and (b) built, (c) rejected on this bead's own evidence. (a): the gate-mechanics block in dispatch-prompt-template.md now names the wedge and the recovery - correlate your own build artefact's mtime against candidate process start times, and kill only what you can show is yours. (b): loops.md section 2 now bounds the dispatcher, written as THE CONSTRAINT A MEASUREMENT WINDOW IS ALREADY FENCED UNDER, SEEN FROM THE OTHER SIDE - Shape 6 already had the vocabulary, so none was invented and there is no second idiom to keep in step. (c) refuse-as-proportionate was rejected because the wave that produced the incident had four to six workers live, and both runs WEDGED rather than failing, so the cost was never a re-run. Folded in: read the clock before killing on elapsed time, explicitly labelled the same defect class as rf2-0vvw running in the other direction - count-based and time-based inference about a running process are both unreliable. Closed by the mayor on the merge; the worker reported closing it but the tracker showed OPEN with no close reason.

comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8141 (2026-08-13) — reopened the exact owner; no duplicate filed. Adding that rule only to generic loops.md does not change the command that executes dispatches, so the original “no block bounds the dispatcher” defect can recur. title: hic: budgets.md Authority column RULED two-mode — amend :760 definition + add Section 9.2 S1/S2/C5 paragraph; cells stay on rf2-0xx2
description:
FOUND BY the rf2-hic-085 custody handoff, 2026-08-13, while repointing the four rows that bead owned. Not actioned there: those four are inside that bead's acceptance fence and these three are not, and the fix here needs a ruling rather than a cell edit.

THE FACT, verified at source on main. budgets.md:783, :784 and :800 -- rows S1, S2 and C5, all `BREACH` -- name `rf2-0xx2` in the Authority column. `bd show rf2-0xx2` reads CLOSED (2026-08-13, 'Discharged by closure path 2: the operator's delegated ruling accepts the breach, SCOPED'). So three not-green rows name an owner that cannot act, which is the exact defect the correction ledger's rf2-hic-019 re-run row (correction-ledger.md:69) filed and PR #8073 fixed on 2026-08-13 -- and it re-broke the same day, because the bead PR #8073 repointed those rows AT is the bead that then discharged them and closed.

WHY IT KEEPS RECURRING, which is the part worth ruling on. budgets.md:695 defines Authority as 'the bead that owns the row's disposition today', and check_budget_ledger.py:430 (L3) enforces only that the cell matches ^rf2-[a-z0-9-]+$. The gate says so itself at :768 -- 'An Authority cell is read for SHAPE, not for life ... a row can name an owner and have none'. A bead that DISPOSITIONS a row closes when it has dispositioned it, so pointing the row at that bead guarantees a dead cell one merge later. The convention and the lifecycle are in direct tension, and no gate can see it: check_budget_ledger.py has no tracker access by design.

THE OPTIONS, none of them obviously right, which is why this is a ruling and not a chore:
1. Point every not-green row at rf2-hic-071 -- the ledger's own standing owner ('budgets.md rows updated by this owner only', its Surface line) which stays open until the budgets are enforced. Structurally cannot go stale before the rows do. Cost: the Authority cell stops naming who actually ruled the disposition, and for S1/S2/C5 that is real information -- the scoped acceptance was rf2-0xx2's ruling.
2. Rule that a closed disposition bead is a legitimate Authority once the row's Disposition cell resolves to the taken ruling -- i.e. redefine :695 from 'owns' to 'took'. Cost: the rf2-hic-019 finding stops being a defect, so decide deliberately rather than by drift.
3. Keep the current convention and accept a recurring sweep. Cost: it has now fired three times in five days and nothing can detect it.

NOT IN SCOPE. Do not change any figure, band, threshold, ceiling, line cell or row STATUS -- S1, S2 and C5 stay BREACH. Do not edit check_budget_ledger.py without ruling option 2 or 3 first; a tracker-reading gate is a different and larger question (the gate reads two markdown files and has no bd access, deliberately).

NOTE ON THE THIRD PATH. correction-ledger.md's rf2-0xx2 deferred-items row says the remaining path for these rows -- a shell arm landing under 1,024 B on the package -- 'stays live and deliberately unowned'. So option 1 is not merely bookkeeping: it would give three rows a live owner where the programme has deliberately declined to name one for the work itself. Say which of the two things the Authority column is for.
design:
RULING (delegated decision, recorded 2026-08-13 21:29 AUSEST; operator-reversible). OPTION 2: the Authority column's meaning follows the disposition's state.

- LIVE-ROUTE MODE: while a row's disposition is still open or amendable through a bead (the UNPINNED rows waiting on rf2-hic-071's instruments; S6/C2, whose K1 price record is amendable only through rf2-hic-085; S3/C6 handed onward because real work remained), Authority names the LIVE bead that can actually move the row. A closed id in this mode is a real defect — exactly what the rf2-ltmd finding was.
- SETTLED MODE: once the row's Disposition cell records a taken, complete ruling whose record carries its own reopen and revert machinery (budgets.md Section 5 has all five specification.md Section 6 fields for S1/S2/C5), Authority names the bead that TOOK the ruling, and a closed id is then correct — the decision outlives the decider.

Consequences: S1/S2/C5 stay on rf2-0xx2 — those cells are ALREADY CORRECT and carry real information (the scoped acceptance was rf2-0xx2's ruling; its close reason is the audit trail). The recurrence engine dissolves by definition: a disposition closure stops being a defect. The rf2-ltmd finding narrows retroactively but the PR #8073 repairs remain correct — at that time no disposition had been taken and a live owner genuinely was owed. The mayor's rf2-hic-085 ruling for S6/C2 is untouched; it is the live-mode half of the same rule. The discriminator is NOT bead liveness; it is whether a live transition remains to be made.

IMPLEMENTATION (wording diff only):
1. One dated clarifying amendment BESIDE the definition sentence at budgets.md:760 ("Authority is the bead that owns the row's disposition today.") stating the two-mode rule above. This tree's convention: amend beside, never rewrite history.
2. A short Section 9.2 paragraph for S1/S2/C5 mirroring the existing S6/C2 one (budgets.md:863-876): rf2-0xx2 took the scoped acceptance (budgets.md:348-415), closed with the decision complete, and the remaining path — a shell arm landing under 1,024 B — stays live and deliberately unowned (correction-ledger.md:102), so no live Authority is owed.
3. OPTIONAL, same PR: in implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_budget_ledger.py change only explanatory uses of "owner" to "bead reference" so its messages match the ruling. NO logic, regex (_AUTHORITY_RE at :231, L3 check at :430), or tally changes; the gate's shape-only check and its "SHAPE, not for life" caveat (:768-772) already describe this semantics.

DO NOT: edit any Authority cell, figure, band, threshold, ceiling, line cell, or Status (S1/S2/C5 stay BREACH); add tracker access, a liveness gate, cell annotations like "(closed; ruling taken)", a second column, or a recurring sweep. An explicit role column may be reconsidered only from evidence of actual reader confusion, not speculatively.

SUPPORTING FACTS an implementer can lean on (verified by both reviews): the checker requires a bead-shaped Authority on EVERY row including MET, but a Disposition link only on non-MET rows (check_budget_ledger.py:429-451). Twenty-one current rows are MET and many already name closed beads (rf2-hic-089, rf2-hic-033, rf2-hic-034, rf2-hic-070, rf2-hic-018) — the column has never been a uniformly live-owner field in practice, so this ruling describes existing reality. Current ledger tally: 38 rows = 21 MET, 5 BREACH, 2 UNRESOLVED, 10 UNPINNED. History showing the real discriminator: f5011d92fb handed seven unfinished rows to live beads; 7992e6af87 completed the shell decision; 9893e6e5b9 handed S3/C6 onward because work remained.

FUTURE ESCAPE HATCH (record, do not build): if a taken disposition ever needs amending and no route exists, give THAT record a named standing amendment-route bead per the K1 pattern (rf2-hic-085) — a per-record fix, never a reversal of these semantics.

(1) budgets.md:760 gains a dated beside-amendment stating the two-mode Authority rule (live route while a transition remains; deciding bead once the recorded state is settled — closed id then valid). (2) Section 9.2 gains a short S1/S2/C5 paragraph mirroring the S6/C2 one, citing the Section 5 scoped acceptance and the deliberately-unowned third path. (a) It names a LIVE OWNER. Then closing a bead that dispositions a row must repoint the cell, no gate can enforce that, and this defect recurs on every disposition — which is what three recurrences in five days is telling us. The remedy is a liveness check with tracker access, or a convention that a dispositioning bead repoints before it closes.

(b) It names WHO DECIDED, historically. Then a closed id is correct and this bead is moot — close it with that reasoning recorded, and the two sibling repairs already made become unnecessary bookkeeping.

title: [bug] the stranded-sweep discriminator is invariant under rebase, so a rebasing worker reads as stalled
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 19:20 AUSEST on a live worker, not reasoned about.

THE RULE AS WRITTEN. .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md says: 'The cheap, reliable discriminator is git rev-list --count <branch> against what you recorded last tick — a worker committing as briefed advances it'. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 4 (Posture, and the stranded sweep) carries the same rule: 'Has the commit count on that item's branch moved since the last tick? A moved count says alive.'

THE DEFECT. git rev-list --count IS INVARIANT UNDER REBASE. A worker that rebases onto a moved trunk replays the same number of commits, so the count is identical before and after — while the worker is demonstrably working. Under a fast-moving trunk, rebasing is what a briefed worker does constantly; the dispatch template tells it to.

THE MEASUREMENT. worker/smallmisc-cluster, read twice about 11 minutes apart:
  tick 1: 3 commits ahead
  tick 2: 3 commits ahead        -> the rule says 'says nothing', so I messaged rather than reaping
  but the tip SHA had changed and the three commit objects were different.
At the second read, 13de5d6db6:
  author date:    2026-08-13 18:37:11 +1000   (43 minutes old)
  committer date: 2026-08-13 19:17:54 +1000   (2 minutes old)
The worker had rebased two minutes earlier. Author date does NOT move on rebase; committer date does.

SO TWO FIELDS MISLEAD, NOT ONE:
  - git rev-list --count   invariant under rebase
  - %ar / author date      invariant under rebase
  - %cr / committer date   MOVES
  - the tip SHA            MOVES

I used the count AND %ar, and read a worker that had just rebased as unchanged for two consecutive ticks. It was mid-flight and had in fact committed all three of its beads.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE TICK. The rule is load-bearing in the direction that protects a live worker, and it currently fails toward 'looks stalled'. That direction is the safe one — the sweep's next step is to MESSAGE, not to reap, and messaging is harmless. But the same rule is quoted in mayor-hygiene.md right beside the reaping rule, and a reader who trusts 'a moved count says alive' will read its converse as evidence. It is not evidence in either direction under rebase.

FIX SHAPE (not ruled): record the TIP SHA, not the count, and compare SHAs across ticks. A changed SHA says alive under every case the count covers PLUS rebase. If a second signal is wanted, committer date is the one that moves. Keep the existing sentence that a still reading NEVER authorises a reap on its own — that half is correct and is what saved this case.

ALSO CORRECT A SECOND-HAND CLAIM RATHER THAN INHERITING IT: another agent reported the same commit as '75 seconds old' while I read '43 minutes'. Neither was wrong; it read committer date and I read author date. Do not write the fix as though one of us had misread — write it as the two-clock fact, because that is what a future reader needs.

SCOPE: .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md and docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 4. Keep loops.md GENERIC — no repository names, tracker ids, PR numbers, paths or tool names; the command file may name commands.
acceptance_criteria:
- `.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md` and `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` do not claim that bare `git rev-list --count <branch>` is invariant under a rebase onto an advanced trunk.
- The text accurately identifies the measured invariant as an ahead/range count (or otherwise states the exact counted set), while retaining remote tip-SHA comparison as the recommended discriminator.
- The generic page remains generic, and both layers retain that an unchanged tip never authorizes reaping on its own.
- Relevant documentation/link gates pass.
notes:
BOTH LAYERS CARRY THE SAME IMPRECISION AND HAVE NOT DIVERGED FROM EACH OTHER — measured by the method-reread loop $D, and it is good news for whoever fixes this.

  docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, section 4 step 1:
    "Record the revision id, not a count of changes — a count survives a rebase unchanged"
    Generic register, names no command. Says WHICH count nowhere.

  .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md:
    "The discriminator is git ls-remote origin refs/heads/worker/NAME against the SHA you
     recorded last tick — NOT git rev-list --count, which is invariant under rebase."
    Names the BARE form and calls it invariant. That is the false one.

So this is ONE fix applied in two places, not a reconciliation between two rules that drifted apart. Repair both in one change or the layers WILL diverge — loops.md section 6 says two copies of one rule disagree within days.

ALSO CHECKED THIS PASS and clean, so nobody re-derives it: the worktree-boundary block and the gate-mechanics block each appear in exactly ONE file, docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md. No command file carries a second copy of either. That drift class is currently closed.

THE RECOMMENDATION IS STILL CORRECT IN BOTH LAYERS and must not be softened: compare the tip revision, and an unchanged tip authorises nothing on its own. Only the justification is loose.
close_reason:
PR #8141, commit 5fe054061f (rebased 97a1813ca6's parent chain). Both layers now NAME THE COUNTED SET rather than softening the claim.

.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md: the discriminator clause said 'NOT git rev-list --count, which is invariant under rebase' -- that names the BARE form and is false. It now names the AHEAD count, 'git rev-list --count origin/main..worker/<name>', as the invariant one, and says the bare form reads 21677 on the same branch whose ahead count reads 3 because it reaches everything the trunk gained. Adds the point the bead's own note makes: the ahead count is both the invariant one AND the one you naturally reach for, which is exactly why it misleads.

docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 4 step 1: 'a count survives a rebase unchanged' -> 'an AHEAD count, the changes your branch carries beyond the trunk, survives a rebase unchanged', then says which count does move and why. Stays generic -- no repo names, ids, PRs, paths, tool names.

Acceptance criteria, each met: (1) neither layer now claims bare rev-list --count <branch> is invariant; (2) the measured invariant is named as the ahead/range count; (3) tip-SHA comparison is retained as the recommendation in both layers, unchanged; (4) loops.md remains generic; (5) both layers retain that an unchanged tip authorises nothing on its own -- the sentence that saved the measured worker is untouched, as is the two-clock paragraph. title: [bug] the routing path-census reads implementation/hicasso/test but a hicasso diff does not arm implementation_jvm, so route collisions reach main unchecked
description:
MEASURED AT SOURCE 2026-08-13 19:10 AUSEST, at main after PR #8131 merged. Found by rf2-aiq7's worker, which worked around it by hand; verified independently by the mayor before filing.

THE COUPLING. implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_path_census_test.clj is a JVM suite whose app-roots list INCLUDES implementation/hicasso/test. Its own comment at line 236 says why (rf2-p5og): hicasso's example applications compile into the SAME node as the routing apps, so two artefacts can claim the same route path and collide. Line 142 names the expected prefixes (/slice, /hicasso-todo) and line 197 carries the failure message that tells an author to prefix their paths.

THE HOLE. A change confined to implementation/hicasso/** does NOT arm that suite:

  $ bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh implementation/hicasso/test/foo.cljs
  implementation_jvm=false
  cljs_node_test=true
  cljs_browser=true
  ... (all others false)

So the census that READS hicasso's test tree is not armed by edits to it. A hicasso PR that adds or renames a route path reaches main with the collision check never run. PR #8131 added two routes and would have been exactly that case — its worker ran implementation/routing's JVM suite on its own initiative and reported doing so. The next author will not.

THIS IS THE FAIL-OPEN CLASS THE PROJECT HUNTS ELSEWHERE: a control that cannot catch its own case. The gate is green about a class it does not cover, and nothing announces it.

WHY THE EXISTING REASONING DOES NOT COVER IT. TESTING.md's cljs_node_test row explains that hicasso 'stays deliberately off implementation_jvm' because the runtime requires React, so every suite hicasso OWNS is CLJS and its :test alias is a --probe classpath check. That reasoning is sound and is about hicasso's own suites. It does not account for a DIFFERENT artefact's JVM suite reading hicasso's files. The narrowing was correct when written and the rf2-p5og coupling landed later.

FIX SHAPE, NOT RULED — and the choice matters, so weigh it rather than taking the first:
(a) arm implementation_jvm from implementation/hicasso/test/** only. Narrow, but queues the whole JVM tier for a CLJS-only diff — the cost TESTING.md's own note warns about for docs diffs.
(b) give the path census its own surface predicate armed by every app-root it actually reads, derived from the suite's app-roots list rather than restated. A rule written as a class does not re-drift; a second hand-maintained list does.
(c) refuse: argue the collision is caught downstream and the census is belt-and-braces. If so, say where, and delete the census's claim to cover hicasso.

(b) looks right to me because the census already knows its own roster. That is a recommendation, not a ruling.

VERIFY BEFORE ACTING: every claim above is a claim. Re-read routing_path_census_test.clj's app-roots at the current tip and re-run the classifier yourself — the roster moves.

title: docs/the-mayor-method: 'put all three in every editing brief' is unsatisfiable on a prose-only brief
description:
dispatch-prompt-template.md:52 says 'Put all three in every editing brief'. The third of the three is:

  **The control is the deliverable.** Show it red when the property is removed, restore, and verify the restore by hashing the bytes.

That is unsatisfiable on a prose-only editing brief. A comment truth-up, a documentation correction or a governance-record edit has no property to remove and no control to show red. The SAME FILE concedes the case at line 374: 'where a surface genuinely has no automated coverage, the honest brief says no automated gate covers this surface; the worker verifies it by hand and says so in the change body'. Where there is no gate there is no control.

And loops.md:586 names this exact defect class and prescribes the check:

  **Unsatisfiable quantifiers.** 'Every gate prints X' when a third of them do not. Workers facing an unsatisfiable rule do not stop - they improvise, and the improvisation varies. **When a rule says every, check the quantifier.**

So the document carries the rule that condemns its own line.

EVIDENCE THAT IT ALREADY BITES, and it is the mayor rather than a worker: on the 2026-08-13 18:30 AUSEST dispatch tick four editing briefs went out. Two were prose-only (rf2-hic-085, rf2-juht). Both carried sentences one and two verbatim. NEITHER carried sentence three, because there was nothing to show red. That is improvisation, not compliance - precisely what loops.md:586 predicts, observed on the enforcing side.

FIX SHAPE (not ruled): scope the quantifier rather than deleting the sentence. The sentence is correct and load-bearing wherever a control exists - a gate, a guard, a checker, a test that proves a property. Something like 'put the first two in every editing brief; put the third in every brief whose deliverable includes a control'. Say what a brief with no control does instead, so the honest alternative is named rather than left to improvisation - line 374 already supplies that wording for the gate menu and can be pointed at.

KEEP IT GENERIC. docs/the-mayor-method/ is published for other projects. No repository names, tracker ids, PR numbers, paths, tool names or OS mechanics in the new text.

SCOPE: dispatch-prompt-template.md only. Do NOT reopen the five-loop table question - rf2-juht owns that.
