title: a surface-armed browser gate skipped on main hid a regression until an innocent PR paid for it
description:
Filed from rf2-8yyd, which the mayor merge loop found on PR #8118. Scoped
OUT of that fix deliberately — rf2-8yyd fixes the Story harness; this is the
scheduling hole that let the regression reach main unseen.

## What happened

`fcf866ea1d` (rf2-fu75, PR #8108) changed
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc` to print an unowned
promoted error to `console.error` in dev browser builds. That is correct
behaviour and was wanted. It also redded the `Story/Xray browser gates
(PR-smoke)` job outright — 227 console errors in the Story feature-load spec,
0 page errors — because the Story harness runs deliberately-failing variants
and the runner treats a console error as fatal.

Nobody saw it, for two compounding reasons:

1. The gate is SURFACE-ARMED. `detect_changed_surfaces` did not arm
   `story_xray_browser` / `story_full_gate` for a diff confined to
   `implementation/core/src/re_frame/`, so #8108's own PR run skipped the job
   that its diff broke.
2. On main pushes it is likewise skipped — verified on runs 31675735554 (the
   fallback commit itself) and 31678098717, both `conclusion: skipped`.

So the job reported green by not running, twice over, and the failure
surfaced days later on an INNOCENT PR (#8118, workflow header comments +
TESTING.md prose) whose only sin was touching a surface that arms it. That PR
paid for another PR's regression, which is also how the diagnosis cost got
paid.

The nightly sweep in `expensive-tests.yml` would have caught it on the next
run, so "indefinitely" overstates it — but the observed cost is real: a
red-on-main window, an innocent PR blocked, and a diagnosis that started from
the wrong branch.

## The question, not the answer

Which core surfaces should arm a browser tier they can demonstrably break?
`error_emit.cljc` changed what a dev browser build PRINTS, and every browser
runner in the repo asserts on browser output — console errors in the Story
feature-load runner, `pageerror` in the others. That is a real edge from
`implementation/core/src/**` to the browser gates that the classifier does
not model.

Candidate shapes, none of them ruled:

- Arm the cheap `story_xray_browser` smoke tier on changes to the always-on
  observability surfaces (`error_emit.cljc`, `event_emit.cljc`, `trace.cljc`)
  — narrow, and pays one smoke compile on a rare diff.
- Arm it on any `implementation/core/src/**` change — safe, and much more
  expensive on the commonest diff in the repo.
- Leave PR scheduling alone and instead make a red nightly block the next
  merge, so the window is bounded by a day rather than by whoever next
  touches an arming surface.
- Refuse: the nightly caught it, the cost was one blocked PR, and widening
  the classifier buys a compile on every core PR forever.

The last one is a legitimate outcome. This bead is a decision, not a task.

## Not in scope

Do not change the fallback (correct, wanted, keep). Do not reopen rf2-8yyd's
fix. Do not weaken the Story feature-load runner's console-error assertion —
that is the gate doing its job.
close_reason:
DUPLICATE of rf2-2uy8, which was filed ~40 minutes earlier from the same diagnosis and carries the operator decision framing (four named options A-D, held for Mike's ruling). Not a wasted filing — it was the correct instinct, and it carried one mechanism detail rf2-2uy8 lacked, which has been copied onto that bead: detect_changed_surfaces does not arm story_xray_browser / story_full_gate for a diff confined to the surface fcf866ea1d touched.

rf2-2uy8 is DEFERRED pending Mike's ruling, which is why an open-bead search did not surface it — the defer hides it from duplicate detection as well as from dispatch. Recorded there.

The actual regression is rf2-8yyd and is in flight; nothing about this consolidation touches it.

title: loops.md's clause 2 accepts SKIPPED without saying that a skipped gate's green is not evidence about the trunk
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-13, checking the rules being ENFORCED against what the tree does. The gap is in a file the mayor wrote an hour earlier, which is the loop working as intended.

WHAT loops.md SAYS. Clause 2 of the merge criterion reads, in full:

  2. **Every check in a passing or skipped state.** A *cancelled* check is completed but not passed; a tally keyed on completion counts it as green.

That is CORRECT as stated and must not be reversed. A surface-armed job that legitimately does not apply to a PR must not block it, and making SKIPPED fail would be over-engineering that grounds the whole fleet.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY, AND WHAT THAT COST TODAY. Accepting SKIPPED at the PR gate is a statement about ONE PR. It is silently taken as a statement about the TRUNK, and it is not one.

Measured: `Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke)` is surface-armed, so it is SKIPPED on almost every main push. On run 31675735554 - which IS commit fcf866ea1d, the commit that broke it - its conclusion was skipped. Same on 31678098717. Main's rollup read success throughout while a real regression sat there. It surfaced only because PR #8118 happened to touch `.github/workflows/*`, one of the few surfaces that arms the job. See rf2-8yyd for the regression and rf2-2uy8 for the policy question.

THE MAYOR-FACING CONSEQUENCE IS THE PART TO WRITE DOWN, because it inverts a reflex. When a PR reds a gate that main is green on, the reflex is 'this PR broke it', and the reflex prescribes a fix-worker onto that PR's branch. Both were wrong here. #8118's diff was workflow header COMMENTS and TESTING.md prose - it could not have caused a browser failure. The defect was on main, so the fix belonged on a NEW branch off main, and sending a worker at the innocent branch would have produced a workaround living on the wrong branch.

WHAT TO ADD. Under clause 2, or in the *After each merge* section, whichever reads better: a short paragraph saying that a skipped check is not evidence about the trunk, that a surface-armed job can be skipped on the very push that broke it, and that when a PR reds a gate main is green on, you CHECK WHETHER THAT JOB ACTUALLY RAN ON MAIN before concluding the PR caused it - and if it did not, the fix goes on a new branch off the trunk, not onto the red PR's branch.

KEEP IT GENERIC. That file is written to be usable on any repository: no repository or product names, no tracker ids, no PR numbers, no job names, no absolute paths, no OS mechanics. Keep the SHAPE and the direction of the failure; drop the specifics. The counts that argue for frequency may stay.

SEQUENCED behind PR #8122, which is open on `dispatch-prompt-template.md` in the same tree. Do not dispatch until it merges.

SCOPE: `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md`. NOT `README.md` - the operator has ruled it stays the human-facing piece. Do not restructure the criterion, do not renumber clauses, and do NOT make SKIPPED fail.

GATE: `mkdocs build --strict` does NOT cover `docs/the-mayor-method/` - that tree is not in the site nav, so it would exit green having read none of it. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` does cover it. `scripts/check_readme_links.py` covers command-file references into it.
acceptance_criteria: The Mayor Method treats a missing trunk gate run as uncertainty, requires a clean-trunk/base reproduction or equivalent comparison before assigning cause, and chooses the fix branch from that result; skipped checks remain acceptable and rf2-2uy8 remains the separate policy owner.
notes:
FENCED 2026-08-13 18:44 AUSEST (mayor merge+dispatch tick). Surface is docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, which PR #8129 (rf2-juht) has OPEN against it — that PR adds a new section 3 and renumbers 4/5/6. Its worker has reported, so no live agent holds the file, but a second editor branching off a main that lacks #8129 is still two concurrent editors on one document. CLEARS WHEN #8129 MERGES.

PLANNED SHAPE WHEN IT CLEARS: dispatch as ONE cluster agent with rf2-uc1e and rf2-k13d. All three are method-layer beads, one agent owns the surface and cannot collide with itself, and rf2-k13d's own instruction to keep the generic-method and private-command layers apart is a rule the single owner can hold. Order smallest-cleanup to biggest-correctness.

THE AUDIT'S FINDING IS CORRECT, AND THE MAYOR USED THE REFUTED REASONING THIS SESSION. On this tick I called PR #8118 'innocent' because its failing gate is SKIPPED on main pushes, and dispatched no fix worker on that basis. That is exactly the inference loops.md:96-100 licenses and this audit refutes: absence of a trunk run leaves causality UNKNOWN, and the red PR may itself have introduced the failure. I never reproduced the gate on a clean trunk checkout. The call happens to look right — #8126 landed and #8118's rollup then carried no FAILURE — but the reasoning was the flawed one, and the outcome does not validate it. Record this in the repair as a worked example if it helps; it is the live case.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8132 (commit ec77dc0aba), docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md clause 2. Actioned the BOTTOM note (the audit's refutation), not the description's original 'WHAT TO ADD' - which prescribed the very inference the audit refuted. The paragraph established correctly that a skipped check is not evidence about the trunk, then concluded 'if it did not run on the trunk, the defect is the trunk's and the fix belongs on a new branch off it'. That does not follow: absence of a trunk run is silent about BOTH sides and the red change may itself have introduced the failure. Replaced with the acceptance criterion's shape - reproduce the actual failing check on a clean checkout of the change's base or an equivalent controlled comparison, then choose the fix branch from that result (new trunk branch only if it reproduces there, else the change's own branch). Recorded the live worked example (a call that looks right in the record and was not reasoned) because its point is that the outcome does not validate the inference. Also pointed 'When a change is not green' at what establishes cause, since that is the branch-choice sentence the refuted inference misled. SKIPPED remains accepted, clause list unchanged, no renumbering, rf2-2uy8 NOT folded in. Kept generic. Gates: fast-PR spine exit 0, mkdocs --strict exit 0 (all six loops.md anchors 1-merge..6-method-reread verified intact in the built site artefact), check_doc_slugs exit 0, check_readme_links exit 0. NOTE: this bead's own GATE line says mkdocs does not cover docs/the-mayor-method/ because it is not in the site nav - that is WRONG, mkdocs renders pages outside the nav and site/the-mayor-method/loops/index.html carries the new text.

title: a required gate that is surface-armed reports green on main by being SKIPPED, so a regression can sit there indefinitely
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-8yyd, 2026-08-13. Filed separately because the remedy is a policy question, not the repair.

THE EVIDENCE, measured rather than argued. The job `Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke)` is surface-armed: it runs only when a change touches the surfaces it covers. On main PUSH runs it is therefore almost always skipped. Confirmed on two consecutive runs:

  run 31675735554 (main @ fcf866ea1d) -> Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke): SKIPPED
  run 31678098717 (main @ ec66696147) -> Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke): SKIPPED

`fcf866ea1d` is the very commit that introduced the regression rf2-8yyd records. So the gate was skipped on the push that broke it, and on every push after, and main's rollup read success throughout. The regression was found only because PR #8118 happened to touch `.github/workflows/*`, which arms the gate — days could have passed instead.

WHY THIS IS THE PROJECT'S OWN FAVOURITE DEFECT CLASS. A skipped check and a passing check are the same colour in a rollup. The merge criterion already knows this at the PR level: clause 2 counts SUCCESS and SKIPPED as acceptable precisely because a legitimately-inapplicable job must not block. That is right for a PR. It is wrong as a claim about MAIN, where 'this gate has not run since the commit that broke it' is exactly the thing nobody is told.

THE QUESTION FOR THE OPERATOR, and it is a trade rather than a bug:

  A. Arm the expensive browser gates unconditionally on main pushes (not on PRs). Costs CI minutes on every push; catches this class the same day.
  B. Run them on a schedule against main - nightly, say. Cheaper; a regression lives up to a day.
  C. Leave it, and accept that a surface-armed gate's silence on main means nothing. Free; relies on a PR eventually arming it.
  D. Report skipped-on-main distinctly from passed-on-main somewhere a human reads, so at least the silence is visible.

DO NOT IMPLEMENT ANY OF THESE WITHOUT A RULING. This is a CI-cost and cadence decision, which is the operator's.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT: it is not a request to make skipped checks fail, and not a request to widen path filters on PRs. Both would be over-engineering; the PR-side behaviour is correct.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. rf2-8yyd fixes the actual regression and should proceed regardless of what is decided here.
notes:
OPERATOR DECISION REQUIRED — deferred out of bd ready until Mike rules between A, B, C and D. Surfaced in chat 2026-08-13.
DUPLICATE CONSOLIDATED IN, 2026-08-13. rf2-9eta was filed independently from rf2-8yyd for the same finding and is closed against this bead. It carried one MECHANISM detail this bead lacked, kept here:

  detect_changed_surfaces did not arm story_xray_browser / story_full_gate for a diff confined to the surface that fcf866ea1d touched. So the arming decision is made by that classifier, and THAT is the concrete lever any of options A-D would pull.

WHY THE DUPLICATE HAPPENED, and it is a cost of the remedy rather than anybody's mistake. I deferred this bead to take it out of bd ready while it waits for Mike's ruling. Deferring changes its STATUS, so it no longer appears in an open-bead search either — which is exactly how a worker looking for an existing owner failed to find it and filed a second. The defer mechanism hides a bead from duplicate detection as well as from dispatch.

That is worth knowing but is NOT an argument against deferring: an operator-held bead resurfacing in every ready list each tick is a worse cost, and the fix here took one close and one note.
close_reason: Ruled B+ under delegated authority (2026-08-13, operator-reversible): the remedy the bead asks Mike to weigh was already built — expensive-tests.yml runs the exact failing gate nightly against main and rf2-6sg25's signature-change alerting lands a new red in a Mike-assigned issue; verified incident timeline bounds this exposure class at ~24h. A rejected as disproportionate, literal D as nag-diagnostics, C as a regression from the status quo. Full ruling incl. the weighed Codex review is in the bead comment; the one live gap (narrow-armed gates with no nightly arm) is rf2-mvq7.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULING (2026-08-13, delegated decision — Mike delegated authority for this dossier to a decision worker; operator-reversible). Both the original dossier analysis and a second Codex review were weighed; the dossier is deleted, this comment is the record.

RULED: B+ — affirm the already-implemented nightly backstop as the chosen remedy and CLOSE this bead; one bounded follow-up bead (see linked discovered-from child) extends the nightly superset to the narrow-armed gates it does not yet cover. No change to PR-side arming; no change to the browser-gate arming on main pushes.

WHY B IS ALREADY THE ANSWER (verified, not argued):
- .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml runs on cron 17 15 * * * against main, and its browser-bundle-and-story-gates job runs the exact command that was red in the incident (npm run test:story-feature-load, plus full xray-feature-gate, story-play-scripts, story-static, bundle isolation, adapter smokes). TESTING.md:63 states the superset policy.
- The nightly is not silent: the always-run nightly-result job (rf2-6sg25) files/edits/closes a tracking GitHub issue assigned to mike-thompson-day8 via .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py, alerting on change of failure signature, with per-step granularity from the rf2-wh5to restructure. Issue #7710 demonstrates the path works end to end.
- Verified incident timeline: regression fcf866ea1d landed 06:56 UTC Aug 13; both fix halves on main ~10:11 UTC; the nightly would have gone red ~15:17 UTC the same day and edited the tracking issue. Exposure for this class is bounded at ~24h, not "indefinite" as this bead's framing feared.
- Caveat adopted from the Codex review: cron is a cadence, not an SLA — GitHub documents that scheduled runs can be delayed or dropped under load. Accepted as proportionate for a pre-alpha trunk with no continuous delivery.

REJECTED A (arm expensive browser gates on every main push): main takes dozens of pushes/day; the three-gate sweep alone measured 509-564s before setup. Hundreds of CI-minutes daily plus a doubled flake surface, to compress a bounded ~24h window for a class observed once. Disproportionate. For an unusually risky cross-surface change, the author uses expensive-tests.yml's existing workflow_dispatch door (Codex's point, adopted).

REJECTED literal D (report skipped-on-main distinctly): on main nearly every push would report the browser gates skipped — the always-firing alert that rf2-6sg25's measured anti-mute design already rejected. Nag-diagnostics. The useful form of D — actually run the gate against main and alert on red — is what already exists.

REJECTED C: not the status quo; it describes the world before expensive-tests.yml and rf2-6sg25 existed. Nobody should choose it.

THE ONE LIVE GAP (carried into the follow-up bead): the strict-superset claim holds for the expensive browser class but NOT for a handful of narrow-armed gates that run only surface-armed at PR time with no arm that ever runs against main. Verified 2026-08-13 by grep: test:ssr-node (test.yml:5326), test:hicasso-controlled (:1532), test:hicasso-hmr (:1642), test:testbed-tenant-switcher (:4580), test:tools-machines-viz (:4921) — none appear in expensive-tests.yml; the ui G-gates need the same check. A cross-surface break of one of those on main sits until a PR arms it — this incident's shape, one tier down. Broad-armed suites (test:cljs, JVM core) arm on every code surface and are not exposed.

CODEX RECOMMENDATION WEIGHED: its core ruling (B as implemented, close, no CI change on this bead, workflow_dispatch for risky changes, no skip-notifications) is ADOPTED. Its rejection of the narrow-armed-gate extension is OVERRULED on a verified factual point: its "gate-scheduling audit reports no known unscheduled gate commands" is true but answers a different question — scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py counts a gate as scheduled when any workflow run: value reaches it, which a surface-armed PR job satisfies, so the audit is structurally blind to "no unconditional arm against main". The extension is established practice, not a new programme: rf2-xwa4n and rf2-zl8ao added nightly supersets for the Freehand gates on exactly this reasoning, and the cost is minutes of nightly runtime off every PR's critical path.

REOPEN ONLY IF: a regression survives past a nightly (that indicts the alerting or the superset, not the cadence); a new failure signature produces no assigned issue; or the delivery posture makes ~daily detection too slow.

title: hic: add hm/settle-until! — L3 mounted facade door for 'work is enqueued in the router; let it land' (rf2-6m4w ruled A)
description:
## Ruling this implements

rf2-6m4w ruled Option A (2026-08-13, decision delegated by Mike; both dossier reviews — primary and Codex — independently recommended it): the L3 mounted facade gains a thin promise-returning condition door over `re-frame.test-support/poll-until`, spelled **`hm/settle-until!`**.

## Contract

```clojure
(hm/settle-until! handle pred)
(hm/settle-until! handle pred opts) ; => js/Promise<handle>
```

- `opts` pass through UNCHANGED to `re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (`:timeout-ms` default 2000, `:interval-ms`, `:label`).
- On success: call the existing `hm/settle!` ONCE, then resolve with the SAME handle (handle-first threading, like the facade's other promise doors `hydrate!`/`residue`/`assert-clean!`).
- On failure: preserve poll-until's canonical `:rf.error/poll-until-timeout` rejection untouched.
- COMPOSE poll-until; never copy its scheduler, timeout, or error machinery (commit `88b20f1d22` removed exactly such a duplicate, `wait-until` — do not recreate it).

## Why the trailing settle! matters (carry this into the docstring)

The condition reads app-db, which moves when the drained router handlers run; React's commit for the store notification may still be pending, so a DOM read on the next line flakes without the flush. That poll-then-flush pairing is the trap this door packages — five test suites spelled it locally (two independent discoveries, three by adoption).

## Mechanics (established by rf2-jljf — do not relitigate)

- `impl.mount/settle!` is `(react-dom/flushSync (fn [] nil))` — it cannot run queued router work.
- `router/dispatch!` drains via `interop/next-tick` (goog.async.nextTick), a MACROTASK — a synchronous `drain!` is impossible, and a drain has no fixed tick count (an fx reply may schedule another dispatch). Condition + deadline is the only honest contract, and that is poll-until's contract.
- `{:clock true}` cannot answer it: the clock replaces the `setTimeout` that poll-until's interval uses, and firing a timer only ENQUEUES the reply. Continue stating that a clocked mount and wall-clock polling are alternative test strategies.

## Work items

title: hicasso: check_optional_module_reachability's ns_of reads an inert (ns ...) form, silencing the gate for that file
description:
Found while fixing rf2-t9kd (PR #8114), asking the generalising question of the fence-coverage checker's siblings.

check_optional_module_reachability.py's ns_of does NS_FORM.search(code_only(text)) and takes the FIRST match. code_only blanks strings and line comments but not reader-discarded or comment-macro forms, so an inert ns form above the real one wins.

Reproduced against the landed script:

  src = '#_(ns re-frame.hicasso.motion)\n(ns re-frame.hicasso.core (:require [re-frame.hicasso.motion :as m]))'
  ns_of(src) -> 're-frame.hicasso.motion'   (the real ns is re-frame.hicasso.core)

That direction is a false GREEN, same class as rf2-t9kd: scan() skips any file whose declared ns is in 'owned' ('the module may of course reach its own engine'), so a file carrying a discarded (ns <module>) above its real one is exempted from the reachability check entirely.

check_freeze.py's declared_namespace has the identical first-match behaviour, and definitions() counts a discarded '#_(def a 1)' as a definition -- but both of those fail RED on divergence rather than green, so they are cosmetic by comparison and can ride along or be left.

Remedy: reuse the strip_inert/form_end pair rf2-t9kd added to check_example_fence_coverage.py (the three shapes and no more -- do not write a general Clojure reader), and add the negative self-test row. Whether the two scripts should share a helper module or each carry its own copy is a judgement for the implementor; the family's idiom today is self-contained scripts.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8120 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/8120), commit 6687bf796d. REPRODUCED FIRST against the landed script exactly as filed: ns_of('#_(ns re-frame.hicasso.motion)\n(ns re-frame.hicasso.core (:require [...motion :as mo]))') returned re-frame.hicasso.motion, and scan() returned [] -- a false GREEN -- while the identical file without the discard yielded one problem. Remedy as prescribed: PR #8114's strip_inert/form_end pair (reader discard, (comment ...), quote, and no more; unhandled shapes named in the docstring), composed into code_only rather than special-cased in ns_of, so both readers downstream get live forms and a discarded :require no longer reads as a require either. #8114 is unmerged so the pair is not importable and is COPIED; lifting it into a shared module would have meant editing that PR's file and conflicting. The copy drops #8114's character-literal branches because code_only removes character literals before strip_inert runs. Self-test rows pin both directions (fault reds, legitimate case stays green): three disguises flagged, plus honest file flagged, genuine door-reaches-own-engine exemption still granted with a discard above it, live ns beside a discarded one still declaring, trailing-quote symbol not swallowing the require after it, discarded :require not flagged. CHECK_FREEZE CONFIRMED NOT A DEFECT and left alone: declared_namespace's result is compared against the row's pinned :ns, and definitions' roster is the DONOR's, so both produce MOVED failures (RED). title: docs/the-mayor-method: fold the second-edition retrospective into bootstrap.md and dispatch-prompt-template.md, keeping both generic
description:
OPERATOR RULING, Mike, 2026-08-13 (chat). Three clauses, all binding:

  1. Use the retrospective at `ai/findings/the-mayor-method/` to improve `docs/the-mayor-method/`.
  2. LEAVE `README.md` ALONE. It is the human-facing philosophy piece and Mike wants it readable by people. Do not push operational detail into it.
  3. KEEP IT GENERIC. Nothing specific to this repository, to Mike, or to Windows.

SEQUENCED — do not dispatch until rf2-qivw's PR merges. worker/clause4-qivw holds `docs/the-mayor-method/` and `.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md`. Two editors on that tree conflict by construction.

## The source

`ai/findings/the-mayor-method/` — README.md, loops.md, dispatching.md. It is a RETROSPECTIVE written by a different mayor after a long continuous run. It is a finding, not a ruling: material to mine, not text to obey. Where it disagrees with `docs/the-mayor-method/` or with `.claude/commands/mayor-*.md`, the committed files govern; note the disagreement rather than silently adopting the retrospective's version.

READING IT REQUIRES THE MAYOR CHECKOUT. `ai/` is gitignored, so a fresh worktree will not contain it. READ-ONLY access to the mayor checkout is permitted and necessary for this bead. Every WRITE still goes to the worktree — the boundary rule forbids editing the mayor checkout, not reading it.

## What 'generic' means here, concretely

`dispatch-prompt-template.md` already states the principle: project-specifics live with the project; that file is the reusable, OS-neutral method. Hold the same line in `bootstrap.md`.

REJECT, or rewrite into a class:
  - Repository, product, tool and file names belonging to one project.
  - Tracker ids of any kind.
  - An operator's name or preferences.
  - Windows-only mechanics — junctions, `cmd /c rmdir`, PowerShell, drive-letter paths, CRLF translation.
  - A named CI provider, a named shell, a named test runner.
  - Any absolute path.

KEEP, because they are the method:
  - The failure and its shape. 'A worker read a peer's exit code as its own' is generic. The path it was written to is not.
  - The count, where it argues for frequency. 'Seven times in three days across five workers' tells a reader how hard to look. Delete the count and the rule reads optional.
  - The discriminator that separates a real hit from a legitimate one.
  - The direction a control fails — open or closed — because the remedy differs.

The test to apply to every sentence: WOULD THIS STILL BE TRUE AND USEFUL ON A DIFFERENT PROJECT, ON A DIFFERENT OS, WITH A DIFFERENT TRACKER? If not, either generalise it or drop it.

## What the retrospective actually carries that the committed docs do not

This list is a CLAIM. Check each against the committed files before writing — several may already be present in different words, and a duplicate makes both documents worse.

  - The mayor's BRIEFS are the main source of error, measured at roughly twenty worker-caught corrections in one run. That framing is stronger than anything in bootstrap.md.
  - Named defect classes: the control that cannot catch its own case; the HOLLOW GATE and its mechanical test (delete the signal, keep the fault - if it stays green it was proving nothing); measured honestly then interpreted too generously; the artefact a consumer copies still teaching the broken form; the unsatisfiable instruction and the quantifier check; stale by chronology rather than by error.
  - Reopened items are usually the system working, and the reflex to re-close destroys a real finding.
  - Two tensions the method does NOT resolve, stated as unresolved: keeping workers busy starves work that needs the machine quiet; and 'reap only on the worker's own report' leaves residue that never clears. Naming an unsolved tension is more useful than pretending it is solved — keep that honesty.
  - Deciding what is actually the operator's: separate 'needs a decision' from 'needs work under a decision', and RECORD WHAT A HELD DECISION IS COSTING.
  - The method-reread loop earns its place by checking DRIFT, not by re-reading unchanged files.

## Scope

`docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md` and `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` only. NOT README.md. Do not create a new file in that directory unless the material genuinely will not sit in either, and say why if you do.

Prefer amending an existing section over appending a new one — these documents are already long, and a reader who cannot find a rule does not follow it. If folding something in lets you DELETE weaker prose, do that and say so; the deliverable is a better document, not a longer one.

Do not link anything under `ai/` from a committed file. The strict-docs link validator fails the build in cascade on a gitignored target. Inline the substance instead.

## Gate

Check the site config's exclusion list before nominating the docs build — it may not cover this tree, and a gate run over an excluded path exits green having verified nothing. The doc-slug checker validates link targets and heading anchors and does cover it. State honestly in the PR body what covered the change and what did not.

title: ci: portability.yml's ai/ ratchet job spends 211 of its 216 seconds on a fetch-depth:0 checkout to do 1 second of work
description:
AUDIT FINDING from rf2-m08s (read-only CI cleanup audit), 2026-08-13 15:28 AUSEST. THIS CONTRADICTS THE AUDIT BEAD'S OWN THROUGHPUT PREMISE and I am recording that plainly, because it changes the answer.

THE PREMISE I WAS GIVEN. rf2-m08s states: 'NONE of these is on the critical path. On a recent full main run the longest jobs were JS harness self-tests (64s), README link slugs (33s) and repo invariant checks (21s); no freehand or portability job appeared in the top set at all. So retiring them is a HYGIENE question, not a speed one.'

WHAT I MEASURED. Job durations from the GitHub Actions API, three portability runs including run 31667180411 — the exact run the operator asked about:

  run 31667180411   216s  No newly tracked files under ai/
                     15s  No hardcoded personal/home paths
                     14s  No re-frame.ui view-lifetime residue
  run 31669300851   216s / 16s / 14s   (same three jobs)
  run 31669464024   233s / 16s / 15s   (same three jobs)

At 216s the ai/ ratchet is over three times the longest job in the cited top set. It did not appear there because that set was read off a main run's top jobs; it is nonetheless the single most expensive job among the three workflows this audit covers, by a wide margin, and it runs on every pull request and every non-beads push to main.

WHERE THE TIME GOES. Step-level timings for that job on run 31667180411:

      1s  Set up job
    211s  Run actions/checkout@de0fac...        <-- fetch-depth: 0
      1s  Shellcheck the ratchet script
      0s  Resolve the accepted base
      0s  Run the tracked-ai/ ratchet
      0s  Post Run actions/checkout
      0s  Complete job

211 of 216 seconds is a full-history clone. The gate itself is one second of shellcheck and two zero-second git invariants.

WHY fetch-depth: 0 IS THERE, and it is a real reason. portability.yml:155-170 (rf2-ow7dz, rf2-7hq4l): the ratchet compares the tracked ai/ set against the event's ACCEPTED base — github.event.before for a push, github.event.pull_request.base.sha for a PR — not HEAD^. On a multi-commit push HEAD^ is only the second-to-last commit of that same push, so a path first tracked earlier in the push and retained at the tip is present on both sides and escapes. That was a real measured defect. 'The accepted base can be arbitrarily deep, so a full checkout is the only depth that is guaranteed to hold it.'

THE GAP IN THAT REASONING. A full checkout is not the only depth that holds one named commit — it is the only depth that holds ALL of them. The job already RESOLVES the base sha explicitly in a later step, so the sha is known before the history is needed. A shallow checkout plus a targeted fetch of that one sha would hold exactly what the comparison needs.

DO NOT WEAKEN THE RULE. The rule is live and its end state has been reached — `git ls-files ai/` returns 0, so this ratchet is now the only thing holding CLAUDE.md's 'nothing under /ai/ is tracked'. This bead is about the 211 seconds, not the gate. The remedy must keep the accepted-base semantics exactly, and the script's existing fail-closed guard (a base that cannot be resolved FAILS rather than passing vacuously) is what makes a shallower shape safe to attempt: a fetch that misses the base reds, it does not pass.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS. A PR that keeps the same base resolution and the same verdict on every event shape, and measures the job under 30s. implementation/scripts/_ai-tracking-ratchet.test.cjs:362 currently asserts 'portability.yml checks out with fetch-depth: 2' — a pin that already disagrees with the file, which says 0; reconcile it in the same PR.

FENCE: .github/workflows/* is a sequential hot zone.
close_reason: Closed

  # The job id and display name stay `index` / `Freehand conformance index` even

title: hic: the roster of WHICH example packages are fenced is itself hand-written, and it rotted within 24h
description:
Split out of rf2-hcgo (that bead adds navigation's own fence; this one is the level-up question its description raises as option 2).

## The finding, and it is not hypothetical

rf2-ccuw (PR #8090) made each fence's POPULATION derived, so a new namespace inside a fenced package cannot escape. It does nothing for a whole PACKAGE that no fence covers, because the roster of fenced packages is spread across six files' ns forms and adding an eighth package fences nothing until somebody writes a seventh file.

Dated evidence that this rots in practice, on this repo, at this cadence:

  editor+grid fence   2026-08-11
  slice fence         2026-08-11
  todo fence          2026-08-11
  forms fence         2026-08-12
  navigation LANDS    2026-08-12  <- unfenced
  typeahead fence     2026-08-12
  ledger fence        2026-08-13  <- still nobody noticed

navigation arrived the day AFTER four sibling fences already existed, and two more fences were authored after it without anyone noticing the gap. Under this repo's parallel-worker model nobody holds the whole tree in view, so 'somebody will remember' is not a mechanism. This is CHECKPOINT 2's sixth hand-written-roster finding.

## Three design constraints anyone picking this up should not have to rediscover

1. The package->fence mapping is n:m, not 1:1. witness_surface_cljs_test.cljs at the examples/ root fences editor AND grid. So the cheap check — 'every package dir contains a surface_cljs_test.cljs' — is WRONG: it false-reds two packages that are properly fenced. A correct check must read which packages each fence actually claims, from its ns :require list (the fences must require their app namespaces literally, which is precisely what makes the analyzer see them).

2. Do NOT derive this at macro-expansion time. The tempting shape is: require-graph accumulates package syms into a JVM-side atom as each fence expands, and a root macro emits the accumulated set. That inverts rf2-ccuw's warm-cache boundary onto the DANGEROUS side. #8090 measured and documented that boundary (a plant deleted from disk was still named by a warm expansion) and concluded it falls on the safe side — stale residue, CI compiles cold. A registration atom does not: a fence namespace that a warm incremental build does not recompile never re-registers, so the root suite sees a partial registry and goes RED on a package that is perfectly fine, in every local dev loop. The check must read the FILESYSTEM at test-run time, not the compiler at expansion time.

3. The obvious home is not cheap here. A JVM deftest under implementation/hicasso/test/ looks like the natural fit and is not: hicasso deliberately runs ZERO JVM tests behind a declared --probe exemption, and its deps.edn says so in terms — 'If a JVM-runnable suite ever lands in test/, drop --probe and take the floor... a JVM lane exists only through the artefact rosters, a roster entry is only legal with a matching test.yml job, and .github/workflows/ is hot-zone.' So that route costs a hot-zone workflow edit plus surrendering an exemption.

## The proportionate shape, if this is done

The artefact's OWN established pattern for exactly this class of check — a repo-structure invariant that is not a runtime test — is a checker script hooked to an existing npm script. deps.edn names two precedents itself: scripts/check_freeze.py (npm run, digest pinning) and scripts/check_lint_export.py (npm run test:hicasso-lint). A third in that family, ~50 lines, walking examples/ for package dirs and the fence files' ns forms and asserting coverage, needs no new CI job, no hot-zone edit, and no macro. That is the version worth pricing.

## The judgement to make

Eight packages is small enough that 'just keep the list right' is a defensible answer, and the stance rejects a framework where a list would do. But it also rejects a list that silently rots, and this one demonstrably did — inside 24 hours, with four exemplars already on screen. Verdict wanted on whether the ~50-line checker above is proportionate, or whether navigation's fence closes it and this bead is minutiae to be closed.

Depends on PR #8090 merging (it establishes require-graph/package-directories, the classpath walk any such checker should reuse).
close_reason: Closed

title: The method never tells a worker to diff against origin/main before pushing, or to re-run gates after a rebase
description:
FOUND BY the method-reread loop, 2026-08-13, and verified by grep across the whole method surface.

THE GAP. Neither docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md nor any .claude/commands/mayor-*.md contains the word 'rebase', or any instruction to diff against origin/main before pushing. Measured: 0 occurrences of 'rebase' in the template and in mayor-dispatch.md; 0 occurrences of the trunk-moved rule in all eight method and command files.

I HAVE BEEN PASTING BOTH RULES INTO BRIEFS BY HAND ALL SESSION, escalating the count as evidence accumulated — 'five siblings found the trunk had moved under them', then seven, then nine. That is a rule living in my working memory and in whatever brief I happen to write, which is exactly the state the method exists to prevent. A fresh mayor inherits none of it.

WHY IT EARNED ITS PLACE — two measured incidents, both serious:

1. A worker's FIRST PUSH WOULD HAVE REVERTED A CONCURRENT LEDGER REWRITE. It caught that by diffing against origin/main before reporting, NOT by any gate. No gate in this repo protects against reverting a sibling's landed work in a shared document; only the diff does.

2. PR #8080's worker rebased FOUR times past ELEVEN landings, and re-running its gates on the final base CHANGED THE ARTEFACT: fixes for three of its own five findings had merged in the interval, the slice no longer reached ::h/revision, and facade-freeze.md would have published a membership count FALSE OF MAIN had it pushed the pre-rebase tree. A governance record publishing a false count propagates into every later citation.

So the two halves are distinct and both are needed:
  BEFORE PUSHING: diff against origin/main. Protects siblings' landed work.
  AFTER REBASING: re-run the gates on the final base. Protects your own claims, because a pre-rebase green is evidence about a tree that no longer exists.

WHERE IT BELONGS: the gate-mechanics section of dispatch-prompt-template.md, which is pasted VERBATIM into every editing dispatch and is already the home of the sibling rules (capture the exit code, verify the restore by hashing, scope the plant). Do NOT put it in .claude/commands/* — those cite that section rather than duplicating it, deliberately, and a second copy is the same drift one level down (rf2-w5pj).

KEEP THE REGISTER. Every rule in that section states what it cost. Both incidents above are the cost; use them.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST: re-run the greps. My counts are a claim, and this file has been edited four times today.

GATES: python scripts/check_readme_links.py, python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, python -m mkdocs build --strict (the-mayor-method IS in the site corpus; the bare mkdocs command is not on PATH). Prove selection with a negative control at a line you add; verify the restore by hashing bytes. These gates print no gate-root banner, so the planted red is the only proof one read your worktree.

Command files left clean per rf2-w5pj. Gates 0/0/0; negative control planted at an added line reddened check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs --strict, restore hash-verified.

title: hic: examples/navigation has NO import fence at all — the one witness package with no surface_cljs_test
description:

Seven witness application packages live under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/. SIX of them carry an import fence asserting they were written on the public door and nothing else:

  slice/surface_cljs_test.cljs
  todo/surface_cljs_test.cljs

This is the same class rf2-ccuw fixed one level up: rf2-ccuw made each fence's POPULATION derived so a new namespace inside a fenced package cannot escape. 1. Write navigation/surface_cljs_test.cljs like its six siblings. Closes today's gap; the NEXT package added is unfenced again.

2. Derive the package roster too. A single suite at the examples/ root asks the directory which packages exist (any dir under examples/ holding a non-test .cljs) and asserts each is named by some fence. require-graph/application-namespaces already does the classpath directory walk this needs. That makes an unfenced package RED the day it lands, which is the property rf2-ccuw bought one level down.

Worth pricing option 2 against the project's anti-over-engineering stance before doing it — but the hand-written-roster smell is exactly the one CHECKPOINT 2 has now found six times.

title: [OPERATOR-DECISION] hic: does the L3 mounted facade gain a door for 'work is enqueued in the router; let it land', or is poll-until the settled answer?
description:
## The question, and why it needs a bead of its own

[OPERATOR-DECISION] — not worker-dispatchable as filed.

`authoring-report-slice.md` finding 6 and `authoring-report-todo.md`
finding 6 are the same finding from two directions, and it is the one
finding of the checkpoint-2 set that got WIDER on the second reading: the
slice met it on an async save against a stand-in server; the Todo class
has no server, no async mutation and no `reg-fx` of its own and meets the
identical wall on a plain filter link.

The gap, stated at source:

  **The L3 mounted facade has `settle!` for work React already holds and
  `dispatch-and-settle!` for a dispatch it makes itself, and no verb at
  all for "work is enqueued in the router; let it land."**

Both reports assigned the remedy to `rf2-hic-027`, which closed
2026-08-10 (VERIFIED-DUPLICATE) — before either report was written. So
nothing open owned it. rf2-jljf corrected `settle!`'s docstring and both
reports' attributions and filed THIS bead as the owner, on rf2-zk87's
reasoning: a bead that closes cannot own an obligation that outlives it.

## What rf2-jljf established at source, which narrows the question

**The gap is real.** `mounted.cljs` defines mount!, hydrate!, render!,
settle!, advance-clock!, dispatch-and-settle!, unmount!, residue,
assert-clean!, census, bodies-run, shadow!. There is no `drain!` and
`settle!` takes no options — its whole signature is `[handle]`.
`impl.mount/settle!` is `(react-dom/flushSync (fn [] nil))`.

**But an author is NOT without a spelling, and the spelling is
first-class.** `re-frame.test-support/poll-until` is a published core
door (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc`), not an
internal reached past a facade. Fourteen files under
`implementation/hicasso/` already reference it — thirteen DOM test files
plus one witness helper — not two: activity_suspense, imperative_sdk,
kernel_commit_owns, lazy_boundary, read_extent, reincarnation_paint,
examples/forms/flow, examples/navigation/conduct,
examples/slice/{a11y_focus,extension,flow}, examples/todo/flow,
examples/typeahead/{demand,service}. So the
second-caller argument is stronger than the reports state AND the
"authors have nowhere to go" argument is weaker — what is missing is
facade VOCABULARY, not a capability.

**Neither candidate spelling survives contact as written.** The reports
propose `hm/drain!` or a `:until` option on `settle!`.

- `interop/next-tick` is `goog.async.nextTick`, a **macrotask**. A
  synchronous `hm/drain!` is therefore impossible: it cannot be a
  `flushSync`, and it cannot be awaited on a microtask either, so it
  must return a promise. That puts it with `hydrate!` and
  `assert-clean!` and outside the facade's "every door takes the handle
  first and answers it" threading contract.
- A `:until` option would make the one SYNCHRONOUS door conditionally
  asynchronous — the same door returning a handle or a promise depending
  on an option. That is worse than a second verb.
- A drain has **no fixed tick count**: an fx that replies with a
  dispatch may itself schedule another. A `drain!` that waits "one
  drain" is a guess, and a guess is the flake this facade exists to keep
  out. Any honest door needs a CONDITION and a DEADLINE — which is
  exactly `poll-until`'s contract. So the live candidate is a thin
  promise-returning condition door over `poll-until`, wearing the
  facade's handle-first shape, rather than a drain primitive.

**And `{:clock true}` cannot be the answer.** The clock replaces the
global `setTimeout` that `poll-until`'s own interval uses, and firing a
timer only ENQUEUES the reply — the drain is a task the clock
deliberately does not drive. Recorded as finding 7 in both reports.

## The decision

1. Does the L3 facade gain a door for the enqueued-work wait, or is
   `re-frame.test-support/poll-until` the settled answer for it?
2. If it gains one, its SPELLING is a naming question — naming-ledger
   row, per `mounted.cljs`'s own fence — and the shape is
   promise-returning, handle-first, condition-and-deadline.
3. If it is declined, the decline is stated ON THE DOOR (it currently
   points at `poll-until` as the spelling that works today, which is a
   statement of fact and forecloses nothing).

## Acceptance

- Either the door lands with a witness that FAILS without it (click a
  route-link, assert on the next line; red before, green after) and both
  witness applications' local poll helpers are replaced by it — which is
  what makes the second-caller claim real rather than asserted; or the
  decline is recorded and the door's existing `poll-until` pointer is
  promoted from "what works today" to "this is the spelling".
- Either way, `settle!`'s docstring stops naming this bead.

## Surface fence

`implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs`
and its witness `.../test_kit_mounted_dom_cljs_test.cljs`; the two
witness helpers at `examples/{slice,todo}/flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs`; the
naming ledger. No production code, no `re-frame.core` facade export, no
hot-zone file, no build id, no `:dev-http` port. Do NOT run
`npm run test:hicasso-hmr` (binds `:dev-http` 8061).
notes: RULED 2026-08-13 (decision delegated by Mike via ai/decisions dossier): Option A — the facade gains the door, spelled hm/settle-until!. Both dossier reviews (primary + Codex) concurred; Codex's five-helper evidence re-verified against main. Full ruling in the comment below; implementation carried by rf2-aiq7 (contract, fence, acceptance all on that bead). Hold discharged.
close_reason: Ruled Option A: facade gains hm/settle-until! (thin promise-returning condition door composing poll-until + one settle!). Ruling recorded in comments; implementation transferred to rf2-aiq7.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULING (2026-08-13, decision delegated by Mike via the ai/decisions dossier): **Option A — the L3 mounted facade GAINS the door, spelled `hm/settle-until!`.** Implementation is rf2-aiq7, which carries the full contract, work items, fence and acceptance; a worker can proceed from that bead alone.

Both dossier reviews were weighed and CONCURRED on adding the door: the primary review recommended A on the two-identical-witness-helpers signal, and the Codex Recommendation (explicitly considered) independently recommended A, supplied the `settle-until!` spelling and contract, and widened the evidence. Codex's evidence was re-verified against main before ruling and is correct: FIVE local helpers carry the identical poll-until-then-settle! composition (~10 call sites) — `drained` in examples/todo/flow, examples/slice/{flow,a11y_focus,extension} plus `settled` in examples/typeahead/demand. (hmr_remount's `settled` is a different mechanism — inventory/quiesced! — and is out of scope.)

Why A, distilled:
1. Five in-tree helpers spelling the same composition is the ecosystem writing the missing verb — two independent discoveries, three by adoption.
2. The wrapper is NOT sugar: the trailing `hm/settle!` flush is a real correctness step (the condition reads app-db; React's commit for the store notification may still be pending, so the next-line DOM read flakes without the flush). Packaging exactly that trap is what the facade is for — settle! itself exists to package one flushSync.
3. The facade's sync/promise split is already principled (sync doors commit what React holds; hydrate!/residue/assert-clean! wait on the world). This door falls on the promise side of that existing line, so "async door in a sync facade" does not hold.

Spelling ruled here rather than left to a ledger sitting (the dossier flagged ledger-stall as the failure mode): `settle-until!` over the witnesses' working name `drained` — drained/drain! falsely suggest queue quiescence when the honest contract is condition+deadline, and settle-until! composes with the existing settle! vocabulary while making the handle useful rather than ceremonial. The naming-ledger row records the decision (with drained, drain!, and a `:until` option as rejected alternates) in the implementation PR.

Rejected — over-engineering, or already settled by rf2-jljf and not relitigated: a `drain!` primitive (macrotask; no fixed tick count), a `:until` option on settle! (makes the one sync door conditionally async), fixed-tick drains, `{:clock true}` mediation (the clock replaces the very setTimeout the poll uses; firing a timer only enqueues), queue introspection, a new error id, a Testing Library dependency, any production export, and duplicating poll-until's retry/deadline/error test matrix in the mounted kit (core poll-until tests remain that authority). Per 88b20f1d22 (removal of the unadopted `wait-until` duplicate), the door composes poll-until and never copies its machinery.

This ruling discharges the operator hold; the bead closes with the obligation transferred to rf2-aiq7.

title: hic: RULED (a) — :on-submit data-intent auto-prevent is law; docs-only sweep aligns every surface (spec §4.1, ergonomics-api, design-laws, invariants, guide, freeze row, ledger)
description:
## The conflict

rf2-hic-026's freeze is specified as "deterministic application of the
**pre-resolved spec dispositions** (spec §4 + codex/ergonomics-api.md), not
reviewer governance". For one ordinary law those two documents forbid what the
shipped surface does, no ruling supersedes them, and the checkpoint therefore
cannot apply them.

**What the dispositions say:**

- `specification.md` §4.1 (`:158`): "**Explicit prevention is uniform rather
  than special-cased for submit.**"
- `lanes/ergonomics-api.md` §Surface boundaries and exclusions (`:98`):
  "**Prevention is explicit everywhere; there is no submit-only
  auto-prevention.**"

**What the code does** — `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:841-843`:

    (defn- prevent-by-default? [k]
      (let [n (name k)]
        (or (= n "on-submit") (= n "onSubmit"))))

and states it as a policy default at `:175-178`: "**`:on-submit`
auto-prevents** (authoring.md, census-weighted), and the opt-out for the rare
form that wants a real submission is the existing `h/fn` escape". It applies to
the DATA spelling only; an `h/fn` is handed the event and the runtime does not
reach in after it (`:567-570`).

## What the Phase 2 evidence says

`authoring-report-todo.md` N5 records the shipped behaviour as a POSITIVE and
the Todo application depends on it: *Enter adds a to-do* is not key handling, it
is a `<form>`, and the whole of it is `{:on-submit [::events/add]}` with no key
test, no `preventDefault` and no callback. The report's own summary: "the
census-weighted default did the census-weighted thing, and the marker an author
would otherwise have reached for (`::h/prevent`) never appears in an ordinary
Todo application at all."

Neither witness application wrote `::h/prevent` once.

## The checkpoint's recommendation (evidence, not a ruling)

**Keep the auto-prevent; amend the two documents.** The asymmetry the code gives
is principled and is stated at `intent.cljs:188-191`: a click cannot auto-prevent
the way a submit does, because a modifier-click on a real link must still open a
tab — so the anchor-acting-as-a-button needs the explicit `::h/prevent` opt-in
and a submit has no such counterpart. "Uniform" would cost every ordinary form
a marker to buy consistency with a case that does not exist.

But this overturns two published normative sentences in the product's own
specification, so it is not the reviewer's to take. It is the same species as
rf2-0xx2: a conjunct of a published contract that only the operator can move.

## What is NOT in question

The `::h/prevent` head itself, its head-rather-than-metadata spelling and its
HD-026 reasoning are settled and witnessed; this bead is only about whether
`:on-submit` is exempt from needing it.

## Surface fence

`docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md` §4.1 and
`docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/ergonomics-api.md` §Surface boundaries — OR
`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs`, depending which
way the ruling goes. Not both. Do NOT run `npm run test:hicasso-hmr` (binds
:dev-http 8061).

## Acceptance

1. The operator rules: keep the auto-prevent and amend both sentences, or
   remove the special case from `prevent-by-default?` and take the consequent
   change to both witness applications.
2. Whichever way it goes, `specification.md` §4.1 and `ergonomics-api.md`'s
   exclusion line say the same thing as the code, in the same words.
3. `facade-freeze.md`'s row for explicit prevention stops reading "cannot be
   applied" and states the frozen law.
design:
RULED (a) 2026-08-13 — docs-only sweep. Keep `prevent-by-default?` (intent.cljs:841-843) and all runtime behaviour EXACTLY as shipped. Amend every doc surface stating the superseded "uniform prevention" rule so all surfaces state one law: prevention is explicit via `::h/prevent` at every position EXCEPT `:on-submit`, whose DATA spelling auto-prevents; a callback (`h/fn` / plain fn) always owns its own event and is never auto-prevented; no second auto-preventing position may be added.

## Approved replacement drafts (use these words or equivalents in the page's register)

- specification.md §4.1 (:158), replace "Explicit prevention is uniform rather than special-cased for submit." with:
  "Prevention is explicit everywhere except `:on-submit`, whose data spelling auto-prevents by deliberate law: a prevented submit forecloses no browser affordance the way a prevented click forecloses a modifier-click, and the rare real submission opts out through the function escape, which owns its event."
- lanes/ergonomics-api.md (:98), replace the exclusion bullet with:
  "- Prevention is explicit at every position except `:on-submit`, whose data spelling auto-prevents as the census-weighted default; no second auto-preventing position may be added, and a callback always owns its own event."
- facade-freeze.md explicit-prevention row (§3) →
  "**Explicit prevention** — frozen: explicit via `::h/prevent` at every position except `:on-submit`, whose data spelling auto-prevents (operator ruling rf2-j6fn, 2026-08-13); `specification.md` §4.1, `ergonomics-api.md` and the door docstring now say the same thing in the same words."
  Retitle §4 (e.g. "The one law that was amended") and record the ruling there; the freeze then reads 14 of 14 laws frozen.
- correction-ledger.md:72 — flip `open` → resolved, dated 2026-08-13, resolution = "ruled (a) on rf2-j6fn: auto-prevent is law; both dispositions amended".

## Full sweep roster (grep-verified 2026-08-13; every tracked surface stating the superseded rule)

Product tree (docs/design/hicasso/product/):
1. specification.md:158 (§4.1) — draft above.
2. lanes/ergonomics-api.md:98 — draft above.
3. lanes/design-laws.md:28 (law 4: "Prevention is explicit and uniform. The same handler form never changes meaning by position.") — reword to carry the submit exception. Careful with the second sentence: it stays true of the FUNCTION form (a callback means the same thing everywhere and owns its event); the data spelling's prevention default IS position-dependent by this law. State both halves explicitly.
4. lanes/corpus-insights.md:80 ("Submit-only automatic prevention creates position/value-dependent behavior; prevention stays explicit.") — this is a historical corpus-analysis record: ANNOTATE with a dated correction pointing at the rf2-j6fn ruling rather than rewriting the historical conclusion.
5. invariants.md:22 (I10, clause "...prevention is explicit and uniform") — reword the clause to carry the submit exception, same law wording.
6. README.md:31 (facade-freeze summary: "one law could not be applied...") — update to reflect the amended/resolved state after retitling facade-freeze §4.
7. facade-freeze.md §3 explicit-prevention row + §4 (:147-164) — draft above.
8. correction-ledger.md:72 — draft above.

Draft guide (docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/):
9. 03-events-as-data.md — §"Prevent browser defaults explicitly" (:47-89: "An intent does not automatically call preventDefault, including at :on-submit"), :71 ("Hicasso does not prevent clicks or submits by default"), troubleshooting row :261 ("A form dispatches and then reloads the page"). Rewrite to teach the actual law: submit data intents auto-prevent (show the bare `{:on-submit [:todo/submit]}` idiom); clicks stay explicit (modifier-click rationale); the reload troubleshooting row now points at callback forms that did not call `.preventDefault`, since the data spelling cannot produce it.
10. 05-forms.md — :248 example: change `[::h/prevent [:todo.editor/submit]]` to bare `[:todo.editor/submit]` (teach the idiom; the explicit head still composes but is no longer the taught form); :295 troubleshooting row ("Hicasso does not auto-prevent") — reword as in (9).
11. glossary.md:268 ("Hicasso does not auto-prevent clicks or form submits.") — reword: does not auto-prevent clicks; the `:on-submit` data spelling auto-prevents.
12. REWRITE-NOTES.md:101 ("No form submit is auto-prevented...") — correct to the ruled law.

Surfaces ALREADY agreeing with the code — leave untouched: architecture.md:81, charter.md:292, authoring.md:107, decisions.md HD-026 (:1736, :1892), studio/the-dogfood-preference-case.md (:72, :241), product/authoring-report-todo.md N5, product/checkpoint-2-slice.md rows, the door docstring (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:124-125), intent.cljs docstrings (:175-178, :566-572, :188-191) and all tests.

## Fence and verification

- Docs-only: NO changes under implementation/, no test changes, no new mechanism. Fence = the files listed above; all under docs/design/hicasso/** (not hot-zone; parallel-safe vs implementation work).
- mkdocs --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** (excluded from the site). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py validates link targets/anchors (fast-PR spine + docs.yml); scripts/check_provenance_pins.py validates changed docs/design/hicasso/ pages. Nothing validates tables/rendering — verify anchors and table column counts BY HAND and say so in the PR body.
- Do NOT run `npm run test:hicasso-hmr` (binds :dev-http 8061). No build/test gate needed beyond the doc checkers for a docs-only diff.
- Existing runtime tests already witness the frozen law (no action, listed so the PR body can cite them): submit vector prevents and dispatches once; callback submit not auto-prevented; non-submit vectors explicit via `::h/prevent` (intent_cljs_test.cljs:455-471, :695-716; core_view_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:162 witnesses explicit-head composition at submit).
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every surface in the design-field sweep roster states the same law in compatible words: prevention is explicit via ::h/prevent at every position except :on-submit, whose data spelling auto-prevents; a callback always owns its own event; no second auto-preventing position may be added. 2. Grep check: no tracked doc still states 'prevention is uniform', 'no submit-only auto-prevention', 'does not auto-prevent ... submits' or equivalent unqualified (case-insensitive grep for auto-prevent / uniform / submit-only over docs/design/hicasso/); corpus-insights.md:80 may keep its historical sentence only with a dated correction annotation. 3. facade-freeze.md's explicit-prevention row states the frozen law (no longer 'cannot be applied'), §4 records the ruling, correction-ledger.md:72 is resolved with date + rf2-j6fn reference — freeze reads 14 of 14. 4. NO change under implementation/, no test change, no new mechanism (no allow-default marker/option/warning/config). 5. Anchors and table column counts verified by hand and stated in the PR body (mkdocs strict does not cover docs/design/**).

comments.text:
RULING (delegated decision agent, authority delegated by Mike; 2026-08-13 17:30 AUSEST): **Option (a)** — keep the shipped submit-only auto-prevent for DATA intents at `:on-submit`/`:onSubmit`, and amend every documentation surface that states the opposite rule so all surfaces speak one law. No runtime, example, or test changes. Dossier drafts approved verbatim (carried into the design field).

Both reviews were weighed and CONCUR on (a): the dossier's checkpoint analysis and the independently-researched Codex Recommendation reach the same verdict on partly independent evidence. The Codex review additionally verified: (1) the special case is already narrow — `prevent-by-default?` recognizes only the two submit spellings and applies to vector intents only; tests witness that a submit vector prevents+dispatches, a non-submit vector does not prevent, and a callback at submit is left alone; (2) all 19 application/example files elsewhere in this repo containing `:on-submit` repeat `.preventDefault`/`:prevent-default true` — the ceremony (b) would impose is concrete and recurring, not hypothetical; (3) history shows drift, not correctness — the runtime special case landed 2026-07-31, HD-026 explicitly preserved it and rejected an allow-default companion 2026-08-02, and the contrary product snapshot (2026-08-09) and guide rewrite (2026-08-11) followed with no corresponding runtime/test change. Codex's implementation boundary (also adopted): sweep the draft-guide surfaces that independently repeat the opposite rule, not just the two spec sentences.

GROUNDS (distilled from both reviews):
1. The asymmetry is principled, not accidental. A prevented click on a real anchor destroys real affordances (modifier-/middle-click must open a tab, and no framework can know which anchors are "real") — so click needs the explicit `::h/prevent` opt-in. A prevented submit forecloses nothing in an SPA: the native full-page GET/POST is precisely what nearly every SPA form exists to avoid. "Uniform" was a symmetry the domain does not have, written before the census existed to test it.
2. Failure modes are asymmetric. Under (a) the rare deliberate author finds a documented escape (`h/fn` owns its event, can allow native submission). Under (b) every beginner diagnoses a silent full-page reload that evaporates app state — the classic raw-React rite of passage.
3. Census evidence is one-sided. Neither Phase 2 witness app wrote `::h/prevent` once; authoring-report-todo.md N5 records the auto-prevent as a positive ("Enter adds a to-do" is one attribute: `{:on-submit [::events/add]}`).
4. Framework-tier practice. Remix/React Router `<Form>` auto-prevents and re-routes; react-hook-form and Formik `handleSubmit` call preventDefault; Vue ships `@submit.prevent`. Auto-prevent is the mainstream ergonomic at Hicasso's altitude; manual prevention belongs to the raw-platform tier this product rises above.
5. Blast radius of (b): four example apps, the testbed, intent tests plus three l2 suites, the door docstring, authoring.md and both reports — all changed to tax the common case for a symmetry the census refuted. Against the pre-alpha posture (minimal ergonomic API, trust the programmer) this is the wrong trade.
6. The one-rule invariant survives intact: whoever holds the event owns it. Auto-prevent is a property of the DATA spelling (an intent vector never sees the event, so the runtime must decide for it); `h/fn` at submit is untouched. `::h/prevent` still composes harmlessly at submit for anyone wanting the ceremony (witnessed at core_view_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:162).

REJECTED (with reasons):
- Option (b), uniform prevention: taxes every ordinary form; beginner failure mode is a silent page reload; wide churn; the "uniformity" it buys has no principled basis (see ground 1).
- Option (c): not distinct from (a) — any wording where the code stands and the sentences change IS (a). The approved drafts already state the exception as deliberate law with a closed roster ("no second auto-preventing position may be added").
- Any `allow-default` marker, options map, nag-warning, or config switch (both reviews concur): speculative machinery for a case with zero observed demand; HD-026 already rejected the allow-default companion. Reopen ONLY if dogfooding produces a real site needing BOTH native submission AND equality-visible intent data — that evidence, not symmetry, would justify it. The progressive-enhancement / deliberate-native-GET-POST case is already expressible via the `h/fn` escape.

Precedent cost ("spec bends to code") is contained: docs/design/hicasso/product/ is a working design record with an amendment mechanism built for exactly this — correction-ledger.md:72 already rows this conflict as open. Honest history: the sentences predate the census that falsified them; written before the evidence, amended when the evidence arrived.

Effect: this ruling clears the operator hold. The bead is now dispatchable as a docs-only sweep (plan in the design field). Completing it closes the last open row of the rf2-hic-026 facade freeze (14 of 14 laws frozen).

title: hic: the public door never states the four event-value shapes — the key map is invisible unless an author opens the namespace the door tells them not to
description:
## The finding

`authoring-report-todo.md` N1, confirmed at source by CHECKPOINT 2 on
`main`@5d54f50d76 (2026-08-13).

The key-map form is a first-class lowered shape:

    :on-key-down {"Enter"  [::events/commit id]
                  "Escape" [::h/clear db/draft id]}

built once per render into a plain string→handler map, one `.key` lookup per
event, composition-gated centrally so an IME's Enter commits nothing. It is why
the Todo witness's `views.cljs` contains NO callback at all — no `h/fn`, no
`.-key` test, no `.preventDefault`.

**It is absent from the door.** `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc`
is 607 lines and contains zero occurrences of `on-key`, `key-map` or `keymap`
(grep -c, run at CHECKPOINT 2). Its docstrings enumerate the markers (`:40-42`),
`defview`, `defhost`'s `:slots`/`:callbacks`/`:server`/`:fallback`, `portal`,
`as-element`, `as-component` and the root lifecycle — and every event example on
the door is an intent vector (`:12`, `:225`, `:452`, `:488`).

The four shapes are written out in exactly one place a reader can reach them:
`impl/intent.cljs:14-25`, a table in the namespace docstring — inside
`re-frame.hicasso.impl.*`, which the door's FIRST PARAGRAPH tells authors is
below the line they write against (`hicasso.cljc:4-5`). The draft guide's
`03-events-as-data.md` and `docs/design/hicasso/authoring.md` both teach it
well; neither is the door, and neither is what an editor shows on `h/`.

`::h/prevent` has the same shape of problem one notch smaller: it appears in the
door's marker list at `:40-42` and is never explained anywhere on the door.

## Why it matters more than a missing doc line

An author who reads only the door and needs Enter-and-Escape reaches for the one
callback form, hand-writes a `.key` test, LOSES THE COMPOSITION GATE, and pays a
closure per row per render for what is one map lookup. The failure is a working
application that is subtly wrong for every user who composes — i.e. it is not
caught by the author, by the linter, or by any test they would think to write.

Two independent ordinary applications are the evidence for the shape's
ordinariness: the Todo class reached for it immediately, and it is the ONE thing
the Todo witness added to the union of names the two applications needed.

## Surface fence

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc` docstrings only. **Nothing
about the runtime changes** — this is a documentation defect on a shipped
surface, not an API change. Not hot-zone. Do NOT run `npm run test:hicasso-hmr`
(binds :dev-http 8061).

## Acceptance

1. The door states the four shapes a value at an `on-*` prop may take — vector,
   map, `hfn`, plain fn — in one paragraph, most naturally in `defview`'s
   docstring beside the intent-vector example, with a key-map example carrying
   Enter and Escape.
2. The paragraph says the key map is composition-gated, because that is the half
   an author cannot re-derive and the half whose absence ships a subtly broken
   application.
3. `::h/prevent` gets one line saying what it does, since the door already names
   it in its marker list.
4. It does not restate `impl.intent`'s position table — the door owes the
   ORDINARY shapes; the position/contract taxonomy stays where it is, with a
   pointer.

The newly merged facade-freeze.md nevertheless says at lines 70, 93, and 187 that the key-map/event-value shapes are missing or absent from that door, while the same file at line 148 and checkpoint-2-slice.md at lines 266 and 318 correctly record the fix as landed and closed.
