title: hic: the L3 facade has no door for 'work is enqueued in the router' — the finding both witness apps confirmed is assigned to a CLOSED bead, and settle!'s docstring over-promises
description:
## The finding, and why it has no owner

`authoring-report-slice.md` finding 6 and `authoring-report-todo.md` finding 6
are the SAME finding reached from two directions, and it is the one finding of
the set that got WIDER on the second reading: the slice found it on an async
save against a stand-in server; the Todo class has no server, no async mutation
and no `reg-fx` of its own and meets the identical wall on a plain filter link.

Both reports name the same owner for the remedy:

- slice: "*Candidate for the freeze, and it belongs to rf2-hic-027 rather than
  to the facade:* an `hm/drain!` or a `:until` option on `settle!`"
- todo: "*The candidate remedy stands unchanged and belongs to rf2-hic-027*"

**rf2-hic-027 was CLOSED on 2026-08-10** (as VERIFIED-DUPLICATE — the seven
facade functions already existed). Both reports were written after that:
rf2-hic-025 closed 2026-08-11, rf2-hic-086 closed 2026-08-11. So the remedy for
the checkpoint's most-confirmed finding was handed to a bead that was already
closed when the sentence was written, and nothing open owns it. This is the
shape CHECKPOINT 1 filed as rf2-zk87.

## Verified at source (CHECKPOINT 2, `main`@5d54f50d76, 2026-08-13)

`implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs` (1998
lines) defines `mount!`, `hydrate!`, `render!`, `settle!`, `advance-clock!`,
`dispatch-and-settle!`, `unmount!`, `residue`, `assert-clean!`, `census`,
`bodies-run`, `shadow!`. There is no `drain!` and `settle!` takes no options —
its whole signature is `[handle]` at `:974-987`.

Both witness applications therefore reach PAST the L3 facade to
`re-frame.test-support/poll-until`
(`slice/flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs:75,151`; `todo/flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs:69,172`),
each wrapping it in its own local helper. Two independent ordinary applications
needing the same non-facade door is the second-caller evidence this project
uses to justify a surface.

## The second half: settle!'s docstring makes a promise it does not keep

`mounted.cljs:974-984`:

    "Call it after anything that stimulated the page from outside a facade
     door: a `user-event` sequence, a raw `.click`, a resolved promise, a
     timer you fired yourself. After it returns the DOM is the one a user
     would be looking at."

A raw `.click` on a `route-link` is in that list by name, and after `settle!`
returns the DOM is NOT the one a user would be looking at:
`re-frame.routing/activate-link!` ends in `router/dispatch!`, the async door,
and the router drains on `interop/next-tick`. `settle!` is an empty
`flushSync` and nothing is scheduled in React yet. The same is true of every
async reply in every re-frame2 application, since a `reg-fx` that replies with
`rf/dispatch` is enqueued.

This half is a defect on its own terms even if the new door is rejected: an
author who reads the docstring and writes the next assertion reads the page as
it was, and nothing tells them why.

## Surface fence

`implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs` and
its witness `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/test_kit_mounted_dom_cljs_test.cljs`.
No production code, no facade export, no hot-zone file, no build id, no
:dev-http port. Do NOT run `npm run test:hicasso-hmr` (binds :dev-http 8061).
A new L3 verb is a naming question — append it to the naming ledger rather than
settling a spelling here.

## Acceptance

1. `settle!`'s docstring no longer claims the post-return DOM is what a user
   would see for work that is merely ENQUEUED; it names the router drain and
   points at whatever the answer is.
2. Either the L3 facade gains the door — a `drain!`, or a condition option on
   `settle!` — with a witness that FAILS without it (click a route-link, assert
   on the next line, show it red before the door and green after); or the door
   is explicitly declined, and the decline says which supported spelling an
   author uses instead, on the door itself rather than in a report.
3. If the door lands, both witness applications' local poll helpers are replaced
   by it, which is what makes the second-caller claim real rather than asserted.
close_reason: LANDED AS PR #8088 (branch worker/facadedoc-cluster, commit 99f1497055). THE DOCSTRING HALF IS DELIVERED; THE MISSING DOOR IS REPORTED, NOT ANSWERED, and rf2-6m4w is its named owner. VERIFIED AT SOURCE: impl.mount/settle! is (react-dom/flushSync (fn [] nil)); the arm's own dispatch is collector/mint-frame-dispatch closing over :dispatch-sync, so an intent lowered in a body drains synchronously and settle!'s promise HELD for that case; routing.link/activate-link! ends in router/dispatch! (enqueue), and interop/next-tick is goog.async.nextTick, documented in interop.cljs:16-32 as a MACROTASK, not a microtask — which is the sharp fact, because it means awaiting a promise cannot close the gap either (a .then runs at the microtask checkpoint ahead of the drain). settle!'s docstring now says what it commits, what it cannot reach, names the router drain, and points at re-frame.test-support/poll-until; the ns docstring's one-line version of the same claim is corrected with it. WHAT I CONCLUDED ABOUT THE DOOR: the gap is real (no drain!, settle! signature is [handle]) but it is a VOCABULARY gap, not a capability gap — poll-until is on core's published :paths with its own Spec 008 audience-split section, and FOURTEEN files under implementation/hicasso/ already reference it, not two. That makes the second-caller evidence stronger than the reports state and 'authors have nowhere to go' weaker. Neither proposed spelling survives: a macrotask drain admits no synchronous hm/drain! (it must return a promise, leaving the facade's handle-first threading contract), a :until option would make the one synchronous door conditionally asynchronous, and a drain has no fixed tick count (an fx reply may schedule another) so an honest door needs a condition AND a deadline — which is poll-until's contract. The live candidate is a thin promise-returning condition door over it. That is an API addition plus a naming question: an operator decision, not a documentation fix. OWNER: a NEW bead, rf2-6m4w ([OPERATOR-DECISION], P2), NOT this bead — matching rf2-zk87's reasoning that a bead which closes cannot own an obligation that outlives it, and naming a closing bead would reproduce the exact defect this bead exists to fix. Both authoring reports' assignment lines and settle!'s docstring now name rf2-6m4w; the docstring's poll-until pointer is framed as 'the spelling that works today', which forecloses nothing rf2-6m4w may rule. PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD: the bead's 'both witness applications reach PAST the L3 facade' framing implies poll-until is an unsupported reach-around; it is a sibling PUBLIC door and the corpus-wide norm. Gates (exit codes I captured): npm run test:cljs 0 (13823 tests / 69923 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors), negative control 1 reddening at mounted.cljs:1036 — which also PROVES hicasso/test_kit/src is on the :node-test compile path, restore hash-verified; test:hicasso-invariants 0; check_doc_slugs.py 0 with negative control 1; check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main 0 (2 files, 0 cited pins) with negative control 1. No table row added or touched in either report; column counts unchanged (2-col Reached/Used-for with 8 rows, 3-col Suite/Suffix/Lane with 2 rows, on both pages).

title: hic: rf2-hic-085 owns four red budget rows and two effective-revision fields, and its activation trigger no longer exists
description:
FOUND BY rf2-ltmd (2026-08-13 11:49 AUSEST) while establishing the live owner of each non-MET budget row. This is the residual finding that bead's fence would not let it fix: the owner it installed is open, but it is waiting on an event that has been cancelled.

WHAT rf2-ltmd DID. budgets.md rows S3, S6, C2 and C6 now name rf2-hic-085 in their Authority column, because that is the owner established at source:

- k1-price-acceptance.md:162 -- 'After ratification the effective revision governs and rf2-hic-085, which owns that field, is the only route to a change.' S6 and C2 are the 1.10x cold-mount rows; rf2-0xx2 rules them out of its own scope and routes them to this record's owner.
- k3-disposition.md:6-8 -- 'rf2-hic-085 records what that decider rules and fills the effective-revision field in section 9.' S3 and C6 are the per-read rows that record governs; budgets.md section 9.2 says 'C6 the day the K3 record is taken.'

THE GAP. rf2-hic-085 is titled '[DORMANT until 2026-08-27] Record the sitting's outcomes' and its worker note says 'Activates on the operator's sitting notes. Until then, dormant.' There is no sitting. k3-disposition.md:13-14 says so in terms -- 'The forum changed on 2026-08-13, and only the forum. This record was written to be re-pinned at the sitting of 2026-08-27; there is no sitting.' -- because the operator pre-empted it by ruling the P2 fork graduate-as-success in chat on 2026-08-13 at 04:57 AUSEST.

So the bead that owns four red rows and both governance records' effective-revision fields activates on notes that will never be written. Its K1 half was already discharged around it (rf2-2rtt6.144 filled that field directly). Its K3 half is not: k3-disposition.md:22-24 says the field 'stays unfilled: a re-pin is a ruling on K3, the ruling of 2026-08-13 did not give one, and it is now owed by an operator ruling rather than by a meeting on the calendar.'

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC. It is the same shape rf2-zk87 found for the shell and answered with rf2-0xx2: an obligation whose named owner cannot act. The difference is only that here the owner is open rather than closed, so the Authority column reads true and nothing trips. A dormant bead on a dead trigger is invisible in exactly the way a closed one is not.

WHAT TO DECIDE (a ruling, not a fix -- do not silently re-title the bead):
1. Re-scope rf2-hic-085 to activate on an operator ruling rather than on sitting notes, dropping the DORMANT-until date; or
2. split the live half out as an explicit [OPERATOR-DECISION] bead for the K3 re-pin, the way rf2-0xx2 was split out for the shell, and leave rf2-hic-085 to whatever the sitting would still have covered; or
3. rule that the K3 record stays OPERATIVE-by-default with its effective revision permanently blank, in which case say so on the record and S3/C6 need a different disposition.

Whichever is chosen, budgets.md rows S3, S6, C2 and C6 follow it.

notes:
DELEGATED STRUCTURAL RULING (operator-authorised delegation, 2026-08-13): OPTION 1 ADOPTED — rf2-hic-085 is re-scoped in place as the standing [OPERATOR-RULING RECORDER]: the dead sitting trigger is replaced by "activates when the operator gives the relevant ruling, in chat or another durable decision record", the DORMANT-until date is dropped, the four budgets.md Authority cells (S3/S6/C2/C6) stay on rf2-hic-085 unchanged, and the bead immediately carries the dispatchable doc-side execution of the ratified K3 ruling with K4/K6 carried open on it. == RATIONALE ==

The remaining work has one decider, one activation event, one recording surface — re-scoping the open bead restores that shape while moving ZERO pointers: k1-price-acceptance.md:162 ("the only route to a change"), k3-disposition.md section 9's blank field, correction-ledger.md:95 ("no longer dated ... awaits an operator ruling") and all four budgets.md Authority cells already name rf2-hic-085 and already describe the operator-ruling trigger. == FRESH FACTS FOLDED IN (postdate the dossier and its review) ==
- The K3 ruling IS recorded on rf2-hic-085 (note headed DELEGATED K3 RULING, 2026-08-13): the drafted section 7 disposition RATIFIED, per-read axis accepted as a recorded miss, governed row a-ii, effective 2026-08-13, section 8 forward rule from 2,115 B/read (trip 2,326.5), enforcement home rf2-hic-071; the ruling explicitly cannot green S3/C6. The dossier's "open and unmerged" and its closed-bead (hic-070/hic-018) table are stale; NO Authority-cell edit is needed anywhere.

A budget-ledger checker DOES exist: implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_budget_ledger.py. The checker runs in CI (.github/workflows/test.yml ~lines 986-989: --self-test then full run) and locally via `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` from implementation/ (package.json line 65). == K4/K6 FORUM DISPOSITION (the mayor's 2026-08-12 question on rf2-hic-085, explicitly left open by the K3 pass) ==

- Consequence: the mayor's DO-NOT-DISPATCH hold on rf2-hic-085 (pending this answer) is RELEASED under this delegation; operator may reverse.

title: hic: [OPERATOR-DECISION] the read-free boundary-shell disposition — re-register the 1,024 B line, accept the breach, or bring the shell under
description:
# The read-free boundary-shell disposition — the operator decision the Phase 1 exit is conjoined on

**NOT WORKER-DISPATCHABLE.** Only the re-frame2 product operator can discharge this. A worker
who picks it up has nothing to do: no figure moves, no line is re-registered, no threshold widens,
and no measurement is re-taken by this bead.

**Filed by**: rf2-zk87 (hic-019 CHECKPOINT 1 finding G2), as the named owner the correction
ledger's *Deferred items and the release decision* table requires.

## What is owed

`specification.md` §12 conjoins the **Phase 1 exit** on this, verbatim:

> Exit at zero stale reads, cross-frame operations, tears, or residual ownership and only when
> the shell meets its frozen line or carries its separate prospective disposition.

Neither disjunct holds today.

- **The shell does not meet its line.** The line is the literal `1,024 B`, frozen by the operator
  on 2026-08-12 (`budgets.md` §5). The R=0 package shell reads **1,100 B** (Reagent segment) and
  **1,095 B** (UIx segment), with all twelve readings at or above 1,087 B, so the band-crossing
  rule does not fire — a plain red (`substrate-decision.md` §5.2). Rows S1, S2 and C5 in
  `budgets.md` carry it.
- **And it carries no disposition.** `substrate-decision.md` §5.2 attempted remediation through
  the collector substrate, as §6 directs, and **refused** to re-register the line — on stated and
  good grounds: the line was ruled earlier the same day, it is reached by a measured arm
  (994 / 992 B) so it is unreached rather than unreachable, and no number that page could propose
  would be anything but reverse-engineered from the measurement it had to accommodate. It handed
  the decision up: *"**Decider**: the operator. The `1,024 B` reading is his ruling and only he can
  move it."*

## The form the decision must take

`specification.md` §6: a separate prospective re-registration or scoped acceptance, decided by the
same product operator before the runtime ABI freezes, **must name the reason, ceiling, effective
revision, reopen conditions, and revert trigger**. The K1 ratification does not pre-authorize it,
and a relative regression allowance cannot recolour the red shell row.

`substrate-decision.md` §5.2 has already drafted three of those five fields — reason, decider and
revert — for the operator to accept, amend or discard. It deliberately proposes no ceiling.

## What discharges this bead

Any one of:

1. The operator **re-registers** the line prospectively, in the five-field form §6 requires; or
2. the operator **rules the breach accepted** on the same five fields; or
3. a shell arm lands under `1,024 B` on the package, at which point the registered line is the one
   that stands and the question dissolves — the first disjunct of the exit clause is met and no
   disposition is needed.

Until one of those happens the row stays **red**, and the Phase 1 exit is not adjudicable.

## Why this is a separate bead and not part of another

- `rf2-hic-018`, the Phase 1 substrate adjudication, is **closed**, and its verdict 3 is precisely
  the refusal to take this decision. A closed bead cannot own a live obligation.
- `rf2-hic-085` covers the **K1 amendment and K3 disposition** records only. The shell disposition
  is a third, separate operator decision, named separately by `specification.md` §6 and again by
  the Phase 1 exit clause.
- `rf2-hic-064` §1 Completeness names "the byte-exact shell disposition", so the final audit would
  eventually trip over it. That is a backstop, not an owner.

## Where this bead is named

- `docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md`, *Deferred items and the release decision*
  (filed by rf2-zk87).
- `docs/design/hicasso/validation.md`, the non-kill rows paragraph of the graduation kill table
  (filed by rf2-zk87).
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md`, the **Authority** cells of rows S1, S2 and C5 — owed by
  `rf2-ltmd`, which is the wider measurement of the same gap and which asked rf2-zk87 to establish
  this owner. Note for that bead: S6 and C2 are the `1.10×` **cold-mount** rows, not shell rows;
  their disposition is the K1 price acceptance, so they belong to that record's owner, not here.

No dependency edge is drawn to `rf2-hic-064`. The correction ledger's design is that a deferred
item is carried by a **row and a verdict colour**, not by blocking the audit — the audit reports
standing state rather than being unable to run.
acceptance_criteria: The operator has either re-registered the 1,024 B line prospectively in the five-field form specification.md 6 requires (reason, ceiling, effective revision, reopen conditions, revert trigger), or ruled the breach accepted on the same five fields, or a shell arm has landed under 1,024 B on the package. The disposition (or its absence) is written into the correction ledger's deferred row and budgets.md rows S1/S2/C5. No figure moves and no threshold widens by any other route.

2026-08-13 11:50 AUSEST — named as the obligation's owner in PR #8072 (rf2-zk87): docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md, Deferred items and the release decision (one row: gates the Phase 1 exit and implementation-audit-complete, three closure paths), and docs/design/hicasso/validation.md's non-kill rows paragraph, which no longer names the closed rf2-hic-018. Still owed in budgets.md: the Authority cells of rows S1, S2 and C5 — rf2-ltmd's fence, not this PR's. NOT worker-dispatchable: only the operator can discharge it.
DELEGATED RULING (operator-authorised delegation, 2026-08-13): the breach is ACCEPTED, SCOPED, with the line unmoved — the frozen 1,024 B line stays registered, S1/S2/C5 stay red-with-disposition, HD-028's memo wrapper stays the default, and the acceptance covers only the pinned band edges (1,107 B Reagent / 1,101 B UIx). Recorded by a decision agent after the reviewed dossier; operator may reverse. REVERSIBLE.

[2026-08-13 13:48 AUSEST]

== THE FIVE-FIELD DISPOSITION (specification.md §6 form; this block is the ruling — copy verbatim into budgets.md §5) ==

- REASON: Retain HD-028's value-equality memo wrapper as the internal default: it removes measured parent-driven body cascades (under HD-006, one page-chrome write re-rendered 300 value-equal card boundaries) without an author-facing switch, and meeting 1,024 B today would require overturning that ruled, evidence-driven default — the "breaking a higher-order law" condition §6 sets. The registered estimand prices the design at the one rung it is deliberately worst at: per-boundary machinery paid by a boundary that reads nothing, the same structural choice that wins −692 B on every read against the spine donor. The line stays registered at 1,024 B precisely because it is reached by the unwrapped shell (994/992 B) — unreached, not unreachable. This record prices the breach; it does not pass it (the K1 pattern: acceptance of a price is not a pass).

- CEILING: Unchanged at 1,024 B. The acceptance covers the measured breach only: up to 1,107 B (Reagent segment) and 1,101 B (UIx segment) — the pinned bands' upper edges on the same instrument. These are acceptance bounds, not replacement pass lines. Any same-instrument reading beyond either bound is an unaccepted, undispositioned plain red this record cannot be cited against.

- EFFECTIVE REVISION: The 2026-08-12 package re-pin (rf2-fe0l, PRs #7939/#7941; S1/S2 = 1,100/1,095 B as pinned in budgets.md §4; package evidence anchor ce31a30b77). Operative from this ruling (2026-08-13), and only while the shell, wrapper, comparator, React version (19.2.0), build mode, and measurement contract remain materially equivalent.

- REOPEN CONDITIONS: The next measured shell arm on the package (any S1/S2 re-take); HD-028 reopened, amended, or overturned; any substrate-decision §3 reopen condition firing; any material change to the effective-revision inputs; a package A/B showing a cheaper design with the same correctness and authoring properties; or real application/pilot evidence that fixed shell retention is a meaningful constraint. NOT a reopen: the mere existence of an unmeasured byte-saving idea.

- REVERT TRIGGER: The acceptance is deleted — never kept as a floor — the moment a qualifying shell arm lands under 1,024 B on the package: full band at or below 1,024 B on BOTH canonical segments, with the memo/correctness/browser witnesses preserved (equal-prop bail-out, subscription/context propagation, changed-prop rendering, teardown). The registered line then governs without exception and the Phase 1 exit's first disjunct is met. Conversely the acceptance lapses immediately if a same-instrument reading exceeds the scoped ceiling, whereupon the undispositioned plain red resumes.

== RATIONALE ==

The dossier's recommendation and the reviewer's independent recommendation CONCUR on scoped acceptance; this ruling adopts it. It is the only branch that (a) discharges the Phase 1 exit's second disjunct ("carries its separate prospective disposition", specification.md §12) without incurring the reverse-engineering cost the record itself names — substrate-decision.md §5.2 refused to re-register on three grounds (line ruled earlier the same day; reached at 994/992 B so unreached-not-unreachable; any proposed number would be reverse-engineered from the measurement it must accommodate); (b) mirrors the K1 pattern already ratified (K1 stays recorded MISSED; acceptance of a price is not a pass); (c) keeps HD-028 without pretending its wrapper is free; and (d) invents no number — the scoped ceiling is the measurement's own band edges, where provenance FROM the measurement is honesty, not laundering. It also meets §6's before-ABI-freeze deadline. Branch 1 (re-register at 1,130 B = 1,024 + 105.5 wrapper premium, rounded; both terms independently provenanced, tight above S1's band top by 23 B inside the ~75 B shape sensitivity) remains the least-arbitrary re-registration if the operator ever reverses — recorded here so the number and its derivation are at hand — but it would let the implementation's first miss define its own success criterion and would carry §5.2's "silent-normalisation path wearing a name-tag" sentence beside it. Branch 3 (wait) leaves the exit hostage to unowned, unmeasured work.

REVIEWER POINTS ADOPTED AS BINDING (none overridden; the reviewer concurred with the dossier's branch):
1. Revert requires the FULL BAND at or below 1,024 B on both segments with the memo/correctness/browser witnesses preserved — not a point estimate (strengthens the dossier's "lands under" wording).
2. Effective revision is anchored at ce31a30b77 and holds only while shell/wrapper/comparator/React/build-mode/measurement-contract remain materially equivalent.
3. "Do not reopen merely because an unmeasured byte-saving idea exists."
4. VETO on the dossier's optional decomposition bead: commissioning byte-shaving only to change a ledger colour is gold plating; no product or pilot evidence says the 71-76 B overage is a limiting cost. NO decomposition bead is filed. Discharge path 3 stays live but deliberately unowned.
5. Propagation is RECORDS-ONLY: do not remove the wrapper, do not adopt frame-prop-shell, do not introduce :memo configuration, do not create optimization work for this gap.
6. Evidence bar for any future claim that the exception can be removed: one production-build package A/B/A run with the existing known-size, donor, floor, structural, and arm-order controls, plus the mounted package witnesses (equal-prop bail-out, subscription/context propagation, changed-prop rendering, teardown). A point estimate or a green ledger-consistency gate is not sufficient.

== ANALYSIS PRESERVED FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION AGENT (load-bearing facts from dossier + review) ==

- The breach: package shell 1,100 B [1,091-1,107] Reagent / 1,095 B [1,087-1,101] UIx; all twelve readings >= 1,087 B, so the band-crossing UNRESOLVED rule never fires — plain red. 1.074x/1.069x. Survived bench-tree -> package within 3 B: a property of the design, not the prototype. Donor, floor, linearity, arm-order, structural-readback, known-size controls all passed at tree ce31a30b77 (1,200 read-free boundaries, six rounds per segment).
- Attribution: HD-028's memo wrapper costs +105.5/+105.0 B per boundary (paired A/B/A, disjoint bands, unchanged per-read slopes, R-independent). Without it: 994/992 B — under the line in every round. LIMITATION (reviewer-verified): the no-wrapper and one-hook ablations were NOT repeated through the package seams — their package figures are bench-tree inference, not package results (the wrapper arm reproduced within a few bytes; substrate-decision §5.2 quotes the A/B as guide, not promoted).
- Alternatives priced: one-hook frame-prop-shell 1,054/1,051 B — still over. Removing the wrapper is an operator's trade (measured heap row vs measured re-render cascade), not engineering. Attack-the-shell's-own-bytes is unmeasured and undecomposed; the shell already yielded 147 B (~1,247 -> ~1,100) to two deliberate index-structure eliminations — the easy bytes were taken once.
- Substrate is inert: the two substrates' shells are five bytes apart ("an R=0 boundary holds no reaction") — no adapter in the number.
- Measurement scope caveat: one physical profile (React 19.2.0 / Chromium, P-DEV-1); proves a real package breach on that instrument, not a portable byte count across engines/hardware.
- The executable path still has the measured shape (reviewer-verified): collector/shell calls useContext + useSyncExternalStore; mint-view! installs one stable wrapper; codec/boundary-props= compares rfFrame plus complete rfProps, false on comparison failure; no executable change between the package evidence anchor and the review.
- The benefit is exercised, not asserted (reviewer-verified): package browser tests show parent updates with fresh-but-equal props leaving child bodies at zero runs, changed-child subscription updates still rendering; grid witness holds two body runs at 25 and 100 cells while the fresh-closure sabotage grows 26 -> 101. React's memo/useSyncExternalStore contracts confirm the mechanism; the repo's mounted tests remain the acceptance evidence.
- Meanwhile-cost: budgets.md §7 keeps the distributional family out of blocking PR thresholds, so the red costs no gate while it stands.
- Consequences of this ruling: the Phase 1 exit's second disjunct is met and the exit becomes adjudicable; rf2-hic-064's "implementation audit complete" verdict no longer trips on an undispositioned red (its §1 Completeness backstop finds a carried disposition); HD-028 stands; no threshold widens; the rows stay visibly red-with-disposition unless engineering lands — which is the point.

== IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (doc worker; records-only, one PR) ==

Targets, all under docs/design/hicasso/ (mkdocs --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** — hand-verify every anchor and table column count and SAY SO in the PR body):

Do NOT touch Authority cells; no sequencing fence with rf2-ltmd remains.

title: hic-019 G3 — all seven non-MET budget rows name a CLOSED bead as the authority owning them 'today'
description:
# Every non-MET budget row names a closed bead as the authority that owns it "today"

**Filed by**: rf2-hic-019 CHECKPOINT 1 re-dispatch, protocol §1 Completeness.
**Severity**: coverage — an obligation with no accountable owner, per `correction-ledger.md#severity`.
**Surface fence**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md` — the **Authority** column of the seven
non-`MET` ledger rows, and nothing else on that page. **No registered line, no current value, no
status, no population, no instrument, no disposition link moves.** No budget goes from red to green,
and no threshold widens. Optionally one sentence in `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_budget_ledger.py`'s
summary; the script's logic is correct and is **not** to be taught to query the tracker.

## The claim, at source

`budgets.md:681-682` defines the column, in the present tense:

> *Authority* is the bead that owns the row's disposition **today**.

`npm run test:hicasso-invariants` on `main`@`d079143b91` (exit **0**, captured) certifies:

> 38 ledger rows -- 21 MET, 5 BREACH, 2 UNRESOLVED, 10 UNPINNED. Every registered line has a row;
> **every row that is not MET names an owner and a disposition that resolves.**

Seven rows are not `MET`. Their Authority cells, read off `budgets.md:704-721`:

| Row | Status | Authority | That bead's tracker state |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | `BREACH` | `rf2-hic-018` | **CLOSED** |
| S2 | `BREACH` | `rf2-hic-018` | **CLOSED** |
| S6 | `BREACH` | `rf2-hic-018` | **CLOSED** |
| C2 | `BREACH` | `rf2-hic-018` | **CLOSED** |
| C5 | `BREACH` | `rf2-hic-018` | **CLOSED** |
| S3 | `UNRESOLVED` | `rf2-hic-070` | **CLOSED** |
| C6 | `UNRESOLVED` | `rf2-hic-070` | **CLOSED** |

Seven of seven. Not one non-`MET` row in the ledger is owned by anything that is open.

And in both cases the closed bead did not merely finish — it **handed the question up and said so**:

- `rf2-hic-018` (`substrate-decision.md:391-419`) declines to re-register the shell line and records
  "**Decider**: the operator. The `1,024 B` reading is his ruling and only he can move it."
- `rf2-hic-070` (`k3-disposition.md:8-25`) leaves its §9 effective-revision field unfilled and says the
  re-pin "is now owed by an **operator ruling** rather than by a meeting on the calendar".

## Why the gate cannot see it, and why that is not the gate's fault

`check_budget_ledger.py:433-451` checks that the Authority cell is non-empty and that the Disposition
link resolves to a real anchor naming the row. Both hold. The script reads two markdown files and has
no tracker access, so *"names an owner"* is all it can mean, and asking it to resolve bead states in CI
would be the wrong repair. The defect is in the cells, not in the check.

But the emitted line reads *"every row that is not MET names an owner and a disposition that
resolves"*, and a reader takes that as **owned**. The script's closing sentence is careful about the
budgets — "This is a verdict about the RECORD. It is not a statement that any budget is met" — and
says nothing equivalent about the owners.

## Why this is a coverage row

`rf2-hic-064` reads this ledger, and `specification.md:406` conjoins the **Phase 1 exit** on the shell
row specifically: "only when the shell meets its frozen line or carries its separate prospective
disposition". The shell rows are five of the seven. A red row with a live owner is a programme in
progress; a red row whose owner closed while handing the decision elsewhere is a red row nobody is
going to touch — and it looks identical in the ledger and identical to the gate.

This is filed alongside `rf2-zk87`, which is the shell half of the same gap seen from the specification
side. They share a remedy and can be taken together; this one is the wider measurement.

## What would close it

1. Each of the seven Authority cells names a bead that is **open** on the day it is written — the
   operator-ruling owner for S1/S2/S6/C2/C5 (see `rf2-zk87`), and `rf2-hic-085` for S3/C6, which is
   the bead that actually fills K3's effective-revision field and is open.
2. `git grep` of the Authority column against `bd show` shows no closed bead against a non-`MET` row.
3. Optionally, one sentence in the gate's summary saying what the owner check does and does not mean —

title: CI: the Playwright browser cache is on 4 of 21 install sites — the one that failed had none
description:
MEASURED while fixing rf2-swos (2026-08-13).

Twenty-one CI steps run `npx playwright install --with-deps <browsers>`.
Only FOUR of them are preceded by an `actions/cache` of
`~/.cache/ms-playwright` (test.yml:1384, 1472, 1586; freehand-bench.yml:412).
The other seventeen download the browser from the network on every run.

Job 94299983393 ('JVM tools/template', the job rf2-swos was filed from) is one
of the seventeen. A cache hit would have skipped the download entirely and the
failure could not have occurred, because the failure WAS the download: a Google
Cloud Storage 403 'this service is not available in your location' on the
Chrome-for-Testing bucket that cdn.playwright.dev redirects to.

rf2-swos deliberately shipped only the annotation half of the remedy, because
neither measured failure is one a retry envelope would have caught (see that
bead and .github/scripts/playwright-install-failed.sh). CACHING is the lever
that would actually remove the exposure, and it was left out of scope there
because it is 17 new steps across 6 workflow files, not a one-line change.

WHAT TO DECIDE, not assume: the four existing cache steps use
`key: ${{ runner.os }}-playwright-<suffix>-${{ hashFiles('implementation/package-lock.json') }}`.
Whether that shape is right for all seventeen (the browser sets differ:
chromium; chromium+webkit; chromium+firefox+webkit) and whether the cache
should be shared or per-browser-set is the actual design question. A cache MISS
still goes to the network, so this narrows the window, it does not close it.

HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/* is sequential.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8065. Cache added at the 8 uncached install sites; 21/21 now fronted by a cache. Census re-run: 21 install sites confirmed, but cached was 13 not 4 (rf2-f79t8/e6enf/5v0dg7 landed 9 more since the bead was filed), so 8 sites not 17. Two keys: 19 impl-rooted sites take the existing key verbatim; docs.yml:build + test.yml:tools-playground run under docs/tools/playground (playwright 1.60.0 vs impl 1.59.1) and key on their OWN lockfile under the same <os>-playwright-<scope>-<hash> spelling. --with-deps kept unconditional at all 21: apt libs live outside ~/.cache/ms-playwright, so a hit skips the browser DOWNLOAD only. Removes rf2-swos's GCS 403 geo-denial; does NOT remove its apt-hop timeout.

title: dispatch-prompt-template's gate-artefact rule is worktree-scoped; a worker racing ITSELF across a kill defeats it
description:
FOUND BY the method-reread loop, 2026-08-13, from a measurement PR #8058's worker reported.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md's fifth gate-mechanics bullet ('Put every gate artefact where git ignores it, and name each one FOR your worktree') closes exactly one mechanism: TWO WORKERS colliding on one filename in the shared session scratchpad. Its whole evidence base is that case — two of six workers writing gate-fastpr.exit, one reading a peer's 0 while its own spine was still running.

IT DOES NOT CLOSE ONE WORKER RACING ITSELF. Measured by worker/trusted-il7b: a foreground test:cljs was SIGTERM'd at the harness's ten-minute cap, SURVIVED the kill, and later wrote to the same .log AND the same .exit as the restarted run — producing 'exit 0' beside 18 real failures. The worktree suffix was present and correct throughout. It cannot help: both writers are the same worktree.

WHY P2. This is the same failure the bullet exists to prevent — a PR body quoting an exit code that belongs to a different run, reading as a clean pass — arriving by a mechanism the rule does not cover. And it is MORE likely than the two-worker case now, because detaching a long gate is the sanctioned path (the harness kills foreground at ten minutes, the spine needs twenty-five), so kill-and-restart is routine rather than exceptional.

THE FIX IS SMALL: name gate artefacts per-ATTEMPT, not merely per-worktree — e.g. gate-fastpr-<worktree>-1.log / .exit, incrementing on each re-run. State the mechanism (a survivor of a killed run writing after its replacement started) alongside the existing two-worker one, so a reader knows why one suffix is not enough. Keep the existing evidence; this is an addition, not a replacement.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST: read the bullet as it stands and confirm it is worktree-scoped only. My reading is a claim.

FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, and the WORKTREE BOUNDARY block inside it carries the same rule — the file's own text says the two must be kept in step, so check both. Do NOT edit .claude/commands/* — they cite this section rather than duplicating it (verified: zero occurrences of gate-fastpr across all five), and a second copy is the same drift one level down (rf2-w5pj).

GATES: python scripts/check_readme_links.py, python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, python -m mkdocs build --strict (the-mayor-method IS in the site corpus). Prove selection with a negative control at a line you add; verify the restore by hashing bytes.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8064 (2026-08-13; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). The per-attempt suffix is the right small defence and all three carriers inside dispatch-prompt-template.md now agree, but the authoritative worker rule remains stale in AGENTS.md:96-115. It still requires only the worktree name and gives `gate-fastpr-<worktree>.log/.exit`, so a worker following the live instructions reuses exactly the paths #8064 says must never be reused. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:617-623 independently calls that AGENTS example a FIXED path and names it as the cause of observed NUL-riddled interleaving. Reopen this exact owner; update AGENTS and make the gate comment historical/current-accurate rather than creating another Bead. Also correct one mechanism detail while those carriers are aligned: the documented command opens `.exit` only in `echo "$?"` after the gate returns, so an orphaned node child inherits and splices the redirected `.log`, not that later exit file. A surviving wrapper may later write the exit; a child-only survivor instead leaves old log output paired with the replacement's exit. State the shared safety consequence without claiming the child holds both descriptors. Keep the manual `-1`, `-2` rule; do not build an artefact allocator or process framework.
close_reason: PR #8074: AGENTS.md gate-artefact rule now requires worktree AND attempt number, with both mechanisms stated; test-fast-pr.sh comment made historical. Sweep found no other carriers.

title: CI: Playwright's browser fetch has no retry envelope — a fourth network install that fails the gate before it runs
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 on PR #8055, job 94299983393 ('JVM tools/template'), run 31652348747.

WHAT HAPPENED. The job died inside playwright-core/lib/server/registry/browserFetcher.js during a browser download — a ChildProcess exit propagating to '##[error]Process completed with exit code 1'. No test ran. The diff under test was a corpus fix and a docstring correction, neither of which can reach a browser download.

THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS, on a third tool. rf2-xsfr fixed .github/scripts/install-clojure-cli.sh (six attempts, jittered backoff, explicit infrastructure annotation instead of a fall-through). rf2-gfvy fixed lint.yml's clj-kondo curl and test.yml's Babashka loop the same way. Playwright's browser fetch is a network install with no envelope of its own, and it fails the same way: the gate never runs, and the red is indistinguishable at the rollup from a real defect.

WHY P2. Ten-plus install failures were measured in three days before the first two were fixed, each costing a diagnosis plus a re-run cycle, and each one training the reflex that a red gate is probably infrastructure — which is precisely the reflex the merge criterion cannot afford. The remaining unguarded path will keep producing that.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST: read how Playwright browsers are installed in this repo — whether via a workflow step, a postinstall, or a script — and establish whether any retry already wraps it. A verified 'already guarded, this was a hard failure' is a complete deliverable.

THE PRECEDENT TO FOLLOW, and do not invent a third style: rf2-xsfr's remedy is (a) a widened retry envelope with jitter, because roughly 59 jobs install concurrently and would otherwise retry in lockstep, plus (c) an explicit '::error title=... CI infrastructure, not this diff' annotation and a non-zero exit instead of falling through to a later 'command not found'. rf2-gfvy applied the same shape to two more sites and verified the gap map was unmoved. Read both PRs (#8030, #8036) before choosing.

WATCH THE COUPLING rf2-gfvy found: scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py classifies a step as setup only when EVERY command line matches SETUP_PATTERNS, so adding a loop or a separate echo line to a setup step can turn its job into an unrun gate in the gap map. Measure --list before and after and quote both.

HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/* is sequential. Check no other bead is in that lane before dispatching, and sequence if one is.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8061 (2026-08-13; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). The single executable handler, all-21-site coverage, same-line classifier preservation, and refusal to add a futile outer retry are strong. REOPEN for the handler's unconditional visible verdict: every nonzero `npx playwright install` is titled `CI infrastructure — not this diff` and the body says the red says “nothing whatever” about the diff. The handler cannot know that. A PR can itself break the install by changing its browser arguments, workflow `env`/download host, `working-directory`, runner/setup, or dependency inputs. The caveat is also incomplete: the merged tree already has a second Playwright root at `docs/tools/playground` (1.60.0), while the message names only `implementation/package-lock.json` (1.59.1); rf2-169n/#8065 independently records those two lock scopes. Even when the caveat applies, the rollup-facing title still says `not this diff`. Keep the useful fact and the low-friction tool: make the title state only `Playwright browser install failed — no gate ran`, retain the measured infrastructure modes and re-run guidance as conditional guidance, and tell the reader to inspect the diff whenever provisioning inputs changed. Add one compact negative control (for example an invalid browser name or download-host edit) proving a diff-caused install failure is not labelled `not this diff`. Do not add runtime diff inspection or another retry framework.
close_reason:
PR #8077 (open). The audit's charge held on both halves and both were verified at source.

VERDICT. The handler's unconditional 'CI infrastructure — not this diff' title is gone. It now says only what the process can support — 'Playwright browser install failed — no gate ran' — and prints $PWD, the one fact that identifies which Playwright root failed. Every measured infrastructure mode and the re-run remedy are RETAINED, moved behind an explicit 'check whether this PR touches a provisioning input' list (browser arguments, working-directory/env/download host, runner/setup-node/cache inputs, this script, the Playwright pin). Not softened to vagueness: the reader gets a decision procedure with a branch for each outcome. This follows the rule resolve-clojure-deps.sh already states after the #7132/#7221 audits — a fault the script cannot classify degrades to 'we do not know', not to 'not your diff' — so it is not a fifth style.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, hermetic. npx shimmed on a sanitised PATH, the step's command run verbatim, old handler (git show HEAD) beside new, two regimes. A diff-caused failure (Unknown browser 'chormium') under the OLD handler is labelled 'CI infrastructure — not this diff' — the reopen reproduced. Under the new one it is not. Non-vacuity guards fired for real: the first proof run was vacuous (Git Bash splits a C:/… PATH element at the drive colon, so the shim never resolved and all four cases died with 'npx: command not found'); re-run with cygpath -u.

SECOND ROOT, established. TWO roots, not one: implementation pins playwright 1.59.1 exactly (19 of 21 sites); docs/tools/playground asks ^1.60.0 and locks 1.60.0 (2 sites — docs.yml job 'build' and test.yml job 'tools-playground', both after an npm ci in that root). The annotation now names both lockfiles. Consistent with rf2-169n/#8065's two cache keys.

RETRY REFUSAL UNCHANGED, as directed. No outer envelope, no runtime diff inspection, no second framework. No workflow file touched.

GATES. gap map 96 -> 96, output byte-identical, with a planted-fault discriminator moving it to 97 to prove the gate read the worktree (restore verified by md5, not by git diff). check_gate_scheduling.py 0. Workflow SHAPE compare vs origin/main across 13 files: 0 drift (job ids, names, needs, if, runs-on, strategy, every step name). YAML: 13 parsed. shellcheck 0.11.0 over the CI roster verbatim: 0. bash -n: 0.

SPUN OUT: rf2-h082 (P3) — install-clojure-cli.sh's title carries a raw comma, which the workflow-command grammar treats as a property separator; reasoned, not measured, and outside this lane.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
Mayor (2026-08-13): I ACTED ON THIS VERDICT AND IT MAY HAVE BEEN WRONG. Recording that here because it changes the finding's weight, not just its wording.

Since #8061 merged I have re-run failed Playwright install jobs on the strength of the handler's message — it says 'CI infrastructure — not this diff', so I re-ran rather than investigated. If the verdict can be wrong, so were those decisions, and the failure mode is exactly the one the merge criterion cannot afford: a red that the tooling tells me to disregard.

That is a stronger reason to fix it than the audit's own framing. The audit says the handler CANNOT KNOW the claim; the operational consequence is that a mayor reading it stops looking.

WHAT I DO NOT WANT: the wording softened until it is vague. A message that says nothing costs a diagnosis every time instead of sometimes. The handler knows its exit code and its own environment; the fix should say what IT can support and name what the reader must check to conclude infrastructure.

title: mayor-merge clause 1's band constant is stale: main now produces 93 checks, not 92
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13, immediately after PR #8042 merged.

WHAT CHANGED. #8042 (bead rf2-n8vp) added a required CI job — node-ssr-node — plus its aggregator entry, so the matrix on main grew by one. Evidence: #8042 itself carried 93 checks (92 SUCCESS + 1 SKIPPED) because it introduced the job; #8054 and #8050, both branched before it, carried 92. The lane is confirmed on main: implementation/package.json (1 reference) and .github/workflows/test.yml (2 — the job and the aggregator).

THE DRIFT. .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md clause 1 reads '92 as measured 2026-08-13, when six consecutive merged PRs, #8000 through #8005, each carried exactly 92 checks'. That is now one short.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING BOOKKEEPING. Clause 1 exists to reject a SHORT rollup — a fraction of the checks reading green. With the constant stale, a mayor sees 93 against a written 92 and has to decide whether that is out-of-band or a matrix that grew, and there is nothing on the page to settle it. Worse in the other direction: a PR branched before #8042 legitimately carries 92, and a PR that is genuinely one job short also carries 92, and the number alone cannot separate them.

UPDATE the constant to 93 with today's date and the evidence above. KEEP the clause's existing self-correcting language intact — it already says the band MOVES, that the measurement is the clause and the constant only its most recent result, and that it had already moved twice inside this programme (~86 then ~91 then 92). This is the fourth reading, not a settled value; do not present it as one.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST: re-measure with gh pr checks --json state --jq 'length' on two or three PRs merged AFTER #8042, not before it. A PR branched earlier will still read 92 and is not evidence.

WORTH RECORDING IN THE SAME EDIT, because it is the clause-1/clause-5 interaction and it bit this tick: when a merge adds a required job, PRs already open are computed against the superseded matrix. They read band-minus-one legitimately. The remedy is gh pr update-branch on them before judging clause 1, which is the same remedy clause 5 already prescribes for the coverage question.

FENCE: .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md only. Do NOT edit docs/the-mayor-method/** — those files delegate the current measurement to this clause deliberately, and duplicating it there recreates the drift one level down (see rf2-w5pj).

GATE: python scripts/check_readme_links.py covers .claude/commands markdown.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8062 (commit 341ca5fbaa). Clause 1 now reads 93, re-measured at source: #8042 (which added the required node-ssr-node job + aggregator entry) carried 93, and #8053 and #8057, both merged after it, each carried 93; #8054 branched before it and read 92, which is why it is not evidence. Self-correcting language kept intact — 'moved TWICE' -> 'moved THREE TIMES', and 93 presented as the FOURTH reading, not a settled value. Also recorded the clause-1/clause-5 interaction in two sentences: a PR open when a required job lands is computed against the superseded matrix and legitimately reads band-minus-one, indistinguishable by count from a PR genuinely one job short; remedy is gh pr update-branch before judging clause 1. docs/the-mayor-method/** deliberately untouched per the fence (rf2-w5pj). Gate: python scripts/check_readme_links.py, captured exit 0, proven to read this worktree by a negative control at the edited line (captured exit 1, naming .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md:14), restore verified by sha256 (cd87639e...673d both sides).

description:
MEASURED by worker/recipes-hic054 (rf2-hic-054, PR #8045) while building the async-routing recipes. Recorded inline there and filed here because it is a runtime defect, not that bead's subject.

THE FAILURE. Resource targets are maps — {:resource ... :params ... :scope ...}. Write one as a VECTOR, [id params], and the whole write is silently deleted: zero requests issued, status :idle afterwards, nothing logged. The mechanism is that optimistic arms run BEFORE lowering and REJECT rather than drop-and-warn, so the malformed target never reaches the point that would complain about it.

WHY P2. This is fail-silent on a write path. The consumer sees a no-op and has nothing to read — no error, no warning, no request in flight, and a status that looks like a completed idle rather than a refused one. Every other refusal in this substrate is loud and carries a reason; this one is not, and a write that vanishes is the worst shape for it to happen on.

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATE: the worker notes this reproduces rf2-06lp's symptom FROM A SECOND CAUSE. Read rf2-06lp before acting — if its remedy already covers this path the right answer may be to fold them, and a verified fold is a good deliverable. If it does not, keep them separate and say why.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST: reproduce the vector-shaped target and confirm the three observations (0 requests, :idle, silence) before changing anything. This is a second-hand report from a worker doing something else; a verified 'does not reproduce' is complete.

THE REMEDY IS A JUDGEMENT, not obvious: make the malformed target a loud refusal with a reason attached, in the idiom the rest of the substrate uses. Do NOT add a nag-diagnostic to the happy path, and do NOT make the optimistic arm tolerant of shapes it should reject — the rejection is right, the silence is the defect.

SURFACE: the resource/optimistic write path under implementation/. Check for live workers before dispatching.

EVIDENCE: PR #8045's body records the measurement inline.
close_reason:
PR #8053 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/8053). PREMISE PARTLY DID NOT HOLD; the non-holding is the deliverable. NO runtime source changed.

REPRODUCED, all three observations, JVM witness through a real frame with a capturing :rf.http/managed fx and *out*/*err* bound: requests issued 0 (last-managed-args nil); the passive [:rf/mutation] read answers {:settled? false :status :idle :result nil :optimistic? false :error nil :pending? false :error? false :affected-keys nil :success? false}, byte-identical to never-written; instance row nil; nothing escaped dispatch-sync; both streams empty strings.

THE FIRST TWO ARE CORRECT, NOT THE DEFECT. The refusal runs at phase 1.5 (mutation_events.cljc:1342) before the request lowers and before the new runtime-db is returned, so no instance row is ever committed -- exactly rf2-06lp's granularity line, and for its reason: an instance minted and left :pending with no request behind it would be a write reporting itself in flight forever.

THE THIRD DOES NOT HOLD. The same run captured :rf.error/handler-exception carrying the whole ex-info: :rf.error/mutation-invalid-target, :recovery :fix-mutation-target, :arm :optimistic, :target quoted, and a message naming the map form. Thrown at mutation_runtime.cljc:830 (validate-target-key!, the :strict policy turning classify-target-key's [:skip :non-map-target] into a throw), catalogued already at spec/009:2358. The reason exists and is delivered to every :errors listener; it just never becomes a CONSOLE byte, because the router CAPTURES the throw and re-frame2 ships no default console sink. That residual is rf2-fu75's -- framework-wide, core + spec/009, HOT ZONE -- not this arm's.

rf2-06lp: FOLD THE DISPOSITION, KEEP THE BEADS SEPARATE. Its ruling covers this path entirely and was followed rather than re-decided (refuse at source with a canonical id -- already true; deliberately do NOT mint an :error instance for a source defect, which is why :idle is the RULED answer not a hole; residual silence is rf2-fu75's). Separate because 06lp is closed and its subject was the :mutation REGISTRAR guard -- different id, different file, its own rows. What folds is its FINDING: a hollow gate beside a real refusal.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING was the gate. git grep invalid-target over the three optimistic suites: EMPTY. And resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc:973-979 says in its own comment that the dispatch path is proven "by OBSERVING no partial cache mutation" -- precisely the hollow claim rf2-06lp diagnosed. New deftest vector-shaped-optimistic-target-refuses-readably in resources_optimistic_validation_cljs_test.cljc, in rf2-06lp's own record-error-records! / :errors-axis idiom: the hollow rows kept deliberately, plus the half they cannot make (the ex-data id/arm/recovery/target and the message), plus a positive twin proving the map spelling still lowers and paints. Notes inline the DELIBERATE asymmetry with the rf2-o5ca8k :optimistic-tags warn-and-skip beside it (tags are a best-effort broadcast; an exact target asserts cache identity, and rf2-1vpbld's pre-write :strict policy rejects because no server write has landed).

BOTH DIRECTIONS RED ON DEMAND. (A) signal deleted, refusal kept (bare host throw): exit 1, 6 failures, ALL SIX in the readable block -- and the 0-requests/:idle/no-paint rows stayed GREEN, which is the proof that the bead's three symptoms are on their own a hollow gate. (B) arm made tolerant (classify-target-key returns [:apply target]): exit 1, 6 failures -- and accepting the vector does not even produce a working write, it produces an unmapped host NPE deeper in phase 1.5. Both plants reached the runtime (failure text quotes the planted strings verbatim); mutation_runtime.cljc hashes f7a4319e9904e4bbff9a6b85eb3839dc7e7469955831c4eff7c7d5feba01981d before plant A, after restore A and after restore B (CR-stripped SHA-256, matching the HEAD blob under the same normalisation).

NO new error id, NO spec/009 row, NO facade export, NO hot-zone file, NO production code. One test file.

GATES (captured, never the harness summary): JVM implementation/core 2240 tests / 11675 assertions 0F/0E; JVM implementation/resources 818 / 7284 0F/0E; npm run test:cljs EXIT=0, 13763 / 69618 0F/0E; focused namespace EXIT=0, 18 tests / 122 assertions (17 deftests before). scripts/test-fast-pr.sh EXIT=1 red ONLY at the node tier on a missing node_modules in a fresh worktree -- same lane green at EXIT=0 once junctioned, on the identical tree; gate root line named this worktree. Node lane observed the new test positively: the runner's compiled test list (shadow_node.js) contains vector_shaped_optimistic_target_refuses_readably. No async row added, so rf2-u0j8's truncation hazard is not armed. test:hicasso-hmr not run (port 8061).

PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD, recorded: "the malformed target never reaches the point that would complain about it" -- it does; validate-target-key! IS that point. The report was made from the console, the one channel a re-frame2 refusal never reaches on its own.

title: dispatch-prompt-template claims EVERY gate prints 'gate root:' — only the 8 shell gates do, so the mandatory check is unsatisfiable for Python gates
description:
FOUND BY the method-reread loop, 2026-08-13, and verified at source. Two drifts in one bullet-neighbourhood of docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, section 'How a gate is run, not just which one'.

=== DRIFT 1 — the gate-root claim is false, and the instruction it grounds is unsatisfiable ===

The second bullet (around line 206) says: 'every gate now prints gate root: <path> as its first line — check that line against your worktree before believing any colour', and closes 'So treat it as a mandatory step on EVERY gate run rather than an aside.'

MEASURED AT origin/main: 'gate root' appears in EIGHT files, all shell gates under scripts/ — test-core-prod-gate.sh, test-fast-pr.sh, test-freehand-prod-gate.sh, test-jvm-implementation.sh, test-jvm-tools.sh, test-rigorous-local.sh, test-routing-prod-gate.sh, test-ssr-prod-gate.sh. It appears ZERO times in scripts/check_doc_slugs.py, and the other Python gates (check_provenance_pins.py, check_fast_pr_gap.py, check_gate_scheduling.py, check_readme_links.py) and the node policy tests do not emit it either.

RE-RUN THAT CENSUS YOURSELF at origin/main before editing — a count is a claim.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTRY: a worker told the check is mandatory on every gate run, who then runs check_doc_slugs.py and finds no such line, has been handed an instruction it cannot satisfy — and the method's own experience is that a worker facing an unsatisfiable rule improvises. Two workers hit this in one day. One reported it precisely: 'check_doc_slugs.py prints nothing on success and emits no gate root: line, so the proof it read my worktree is the negative control's path, not a banner.'

THE FIX, and note the improvisation is already the right answer: scope the claim to the gates that actually print it, and document the substitute workers have independently arrived at. For a gate that emits no banner, the proof it read YOUR worktree is the FILE PATH ITS NEGATIVE CONTROL PRINTS — plant a fault, read the path in the failure. Keep the bullet's force; it is a good rule. Do not weaken it to 'check where available' without naming what to do where it is not, which is the half that leaves a worker stuck.

=== DRIFT 2 — the harness/captured exit-code disagreement is understated ===

The third bullet says the number the harness reports 'has disagreed' and cites ONE instance: 2026-08-11, a gate surfaced as completed exit 0 while its captured status was 1.

MEASURED 2026-08-13: it happened at least FOUR more times in one day, across three workers — worker/routing-hic042 (a real compile failure from an unbalanced paren, surfaced as exit 0), worker/ssrsvc-hic056 and worker/cliretry-xsfr (both spine runs), and worker/a11y-hic049 TWICE, one of them a genuine two-assertion failure.

WHY THIS IS A CALIBRATION CHANGE, NOT EVIDENCE-PADDING: 'has disagreed' once reads as a rare anomaly and invites a worker to treat the harness number as usually fine. Five instances across four workers in three days is ROUTINE. The rule already says quote the captured number, and workers are obeying it — but a worker calibrating how hard to look reads the frequency, not just the rule.

Update the evidence to reflect the measured frequency. Do not restructure the bullet.

=== FENCE AND METHOD ===
Surface: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md ONLY. Do NOT edit .claude/commands/* — they cite this section rather than duplicating it, deliberately, and a second copy is the same drift one level down.

This file is re-read by the 55m method loop and pasted verbatim into every editing dispatch, so wording changes propagate immediately. Keep the register: each rule states what it cost.

GATES: python scripts/check_readme_links.py (covers repo-root and .claude/commands markdown), python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py (covers docs/**), python -m mkdocs build --strict (mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs does NOT exclude the-mayor-method/, so the site build reads this file; the bare mkdocs command is not on PATH here). Prove selection with a negative control at a line you edit, restore, and verify the restore by hashing bytes.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8047 (completeness): REOPENED. The correction is sound in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, but its exact false claim remains in the higher-priority live carrier AGENTS.md:55-64. That section says every gate script under scripts/ derives its root from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` and every gate prints `gate root: <path>`; Python gates do neither. Sweep and scope both clauses to the shell gates, and give bannerless gates the same planted-fault discrimination #8047 now teaches. This is the same rf2-804e drift one carrier over, not a new issue.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8054 (merged 2026-08-12T23:41:16Z as c82647129ef8384a88862ec3276da886b0a03492) — REOPEN AGAIN for two residual carriers under the same exact owner; no duplicate created. The AGENTS.md census and repair are correct: all eight scripts/test-*.sh gates use BASH_SOURCE and emit the banner, the 38 scripts/check_*.py gates emit none, and the negative-control route is sound. Completeness contradiction: the PR dispositioned docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md as fully correct, but that file still says at line 68 to check "a gate's printed gate root line" before believing its colour, and begins the detailed bullet at line 198 with "The gate scripts derive their repo root from BASH_SOURCE". The first again presupposes every gate has a banner; the second again asserts the root mechanism for the whole class before later narrowing only the banner clause. Scope both residual phrases to the shell/banner gates and point the executive sentence at the documented negative-control alternative for bannerless gates. Keep the landed AGENTS.md repair intact.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8062 (commit c6034766ec). A carrier DID remain, and a fourth one was found by measurement. (1) The two residual phrases the #8054 audit named in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md are both repaired: the pasted WORKTREE BOUNDARY block's 'check that a gate's printed gate root: line' now names both routes (banner where a gate prints one, planted-fault red where it does not), and the detailed bullet's opening 'The gate scripts derive their repo root from BASH_SOURCE' is scoped to the shell gates. (2) NEW, and it would have been the fourth reopen: #8054's own AGENTS.md repair introduced a FALSE mechanism claim — 'the Python gates resolve their rosters against the cwd, so invoking one by absolute path buys no protection the cd did not already give.' Disproved two ways: check_doc_slugs.py:2236 and check_readme_links.py's --repo-root default both resolve to Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent; and check_doc_slugs.py run by ABSOLUTE path from a directory outside every checkout came back exit 1 naming a fault planted only in this worktree. The consequence is the reverse of what it taught — the absolute path matters MORE for a Python gate, because python scripts/check_x.py resolves the relative script path against cwd first, so a leaked cwd runs the SIBLING'S copy which then pins faithfully to the sibling's tree. Corrected; the rest of #8054's repair kept intact. CENSUS at this tree: 8 scripts/test-*.sh all emit the banner; 38 scripts/check_*.py emit none; 3 check-*.sh siblings emit none; 1 node runner does (implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs) — written as a class, not a count. Prose carriers of either claim across the whole tracked tree: AGENTS.md and dispatch-prompt-template.md only. Gates: check_readme_links.py 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0, mkdocs build --strict 0 (all captured, not harness-reported); negative control at dispatch-prompt-template.md:208 gave captured exit 1, restore verified by sha256 (df92712b...7f95 both sides).

title: hicasso guide: true up the select-only dropdown to the repaired combobox witness
description:
Merged-PR audit #7914 (recorded on rf2-hic-049) found the guide's select-only dropdown is not an accessible combobox: the trigger carries `aria-activedescendant` for a sibling listbox but has neither `role="combobox"` nor `aria-controls`/ownership, so the active-descendant model is invalid and the position is never announced. `aria-selected` also follows the transient `:active` while the committed value moves only on Enter/click.

rf2-hic-049 discharged the WITNESS half: the repaired view, the guide's view as a positive control, and the sweep that separates them now live in `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/combobox_keyboard_dom_cljs_test.cljs`. That namespace is the source of truth for the corrected markup.

The DOC half is left because the guide tree was another worker's fence on that wave:

- `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/13-overlays-and-focus.md` — the code block under *Build a dropdown from a popover*. Take the four changes from `select-dropdown`'s docstring: `role="combobox"` on the trigger; `aria-controls` naming the listbox; both emitted only while open (a closed overlay has no DOM node, so an unconditional `aria-controls` would point at nothing); and `aria-selected` following the COMMITTED value rather than `:active`.
- `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/22-accessibility.md` — its 'Menu or listbox navigation' row calls this example the whole contract, so it moves with it.

Do not restate the witness in prose; link it.
notes:
FENCE CLEARED $D. rf2-hic-092 is CLOSED on Mike's ruling: the corpus on main IS the end-state guide, and the "two competing rewrites" escalation that fenced this bead was a stale reading by the mayor - every rewrite branch was patch-equivalent to main, verified with git cherry.

So this bead is no longer fenced. It is DISPATCHABLE against the corpus that is on main right now.

READ THE LANDED CORPUS, NOT THE BEAD'S REMEMBERED LINE NUMBERS. The guide was rewritten on 2026-08-11 in a two-step sequence, so chapter numbering and prose may both have moved since this bead was filed. rf2-me76's own note already records one such move: the migration chapter renumbers from 20 to 19. Re-locate every carrier at the current tip before editing, and say in the PR body what you re-located.
close_reason: Landed in PR #8140 (worker/guidefix-cluster), MERGED. All four changes from the witness docstring applied to the ch13 dropdown, with the witness linked rather than restated. Ch22's dependent row moved with it, plus its ARIA-state bullet - not named by the bead, but it listed two of three attributes. ONE CHANGE THE BEAD DID NOT ANTICIPATE and the worker found: the for-binding had to become {v :value l :label}, because {:keys [value label]} shadowed the outer value prop, so aria-selected could not read the committed value at all. title: An async test row under a positional fixture silently aborts the whole browser run, every later namespace included
description:
FOUND BY worker/vendor-hic047 (rf2-hic-047, PR #8026) on its first browser run, and recorded in that PR body as one of three witness defects. Filed here because it is a TESTING-INFRASTRUCTURE hazard, not that bead's subject, and nothing owns it.

THE FAILURE. An async row placed under a positional fixture aborts the ENTIRE npm run test:browser run — silently — and every namespace scheduled after it is skipped. The run does not report the abort as a failure of the offending row; the later namespaces simply never execute.

WHY THIS IS P2 DESPITE BEING A TEST-HARNESS ISSUE. It is a fail-open shape in the exact instrument the merge criterion leans on. A worker adding an async row in the wrong place gets a browser run that LOOKS like it passed while an unknown number of namespaces never ran, and the PR body then quotes a green it did not earn. This repo spends its days hunting that shape in its own instruments; the test harness is not exempt.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, in order:
1. REPRODUCE IT. Construct the shape deliberately - an async row under a positional fixture - and show the run aborting and later namespaces not executing. Quote the raw exit code and the namespace counts with and without. If it does not reproduce, say so with evidence and close: a verified 'does not reproduce' is a complete deliverable and this is a second-hand report.
2. Establish WHERE the abort happens - the runner, the fixture mechanism, or cljs.test itself - and name the file and line.
3. Make it LOUD. The minimum acceptable outcome is that this shape fails the run visibly rather than truncating it. Whether that is a runner-level guard, a fixture-level refusal, or a lint rule is the implementer's call - argue it in the PR body.

DO NOT redesign the browser runner or add a general-purpose test-authoring framework. One loud failure at the point of the defect. Reject anything larger at triage.

SURFACE: the browser test runner and fixture support under implementation/. Check for live workers before dispatching - this tree is busy.

EVIDENCE TO READ FIRST: PR #8026's body records all three witness defects its first run caught; this is the sharpest of them and the reporter's own words are the best available description.
close_reason:
Reproduced, located and made loud. PR #8038.

REPRODUCED. A namespace with a positional fixture ((use-fixtures :once (fn [f] (f)))) plus one (async done ...) row, planted in implementation/core/test/. Control: 223 namespaces / 1428 tests / 8819 assertions / captured exit 0. Plant: 8 namespaces announced (the probe sorted 8th of 225), NO summary line at all, 217 namespaces never executed, captured exit 1. Cause appears once in the trail at [+11.62s] as a pageerror: 'Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps.  Testing aborted.'

FRAMING CORRECTION. The bead calls this fail-open ('looks green'). It does not present as green: no summary means no 'Ran N tests' line, and the runner already refuses to pass without one. It is fail-SLOW and fail-VAGUE — the full BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS (360000ms default) burnt, ending in 'Timed out ... waiting for cljs.test summary. (source: not found)', with the real cause at trail line 2885 of 2892.

LOCATED. cljs/test.cljs:547 (execution-strategy maps all-fn fixtures to :sync) -> shadow/test.cljs test-vars-grouped-block :sync branch (wraps bodies in ct/disable-async) -> cljs/test.cljs:479 (test-var-block* rethrows a bare STRING). cljs/test.cljs:439 run-block has no try/catch and shadow.test runs the whole lane plus its closing summary inside ONE run-block, so the throw unwinds everything. Our part: implementation/scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs held the pageerror already but only consulted it after a summary it would never get.

MADE LOUD. The poll loop now breaks on that one terminal class and names it (namespace it stopped at, count reached, map-fixture remedy); a matcher-free backstop reports any summary-less run with page errors the same way, so drift in the ClojureScript literal costs immediacy, not correctness. No lint, no new gate, no verdict change. Sabotage-controlled both halves (hash da89849d -> bc4643b3 -> da89849d, and the run's own arm changed).

FLAGGED, NOT CHANGED: three browser-lane namespaces use positional fixtures today (ui/adapter_conformance_dom_cljs_test, ssr/multi_root_hydration_dom_cljs_test, ssr/failed_root_isolation_dom_cljs_test) — correct as written, one async row from taking the lane down. Mayor to rule.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
Mayor (2026-08-13): CORRECTING THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE, from its worker's measurement (PR #8038).

I filed this as P2 calling it 'a fail-open shape in the exact instrument the merge criterion leans on — a run that looks green while namespaces never ran'. THAT IS WRONG, and the worker proved it rather than accepting it: no summary means no 'Ran N tests' line, and the runner already refuses to pass without one. THE RUN REDS.

MEASURED (control vs plant, same tree):
  control  223 namespaces announced, 1428 tests, 8819 assertions, captured exit 0
  plant      8 namespaces announced, no summary printed,           captured exit 1
217 namespaces never executed, and the run still failed.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY COSTS is diagnosis, not a false pass: the full BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS (360,000 ms) is burnt, then the run reports 'Timed out ... waiting for cljs.test summary' — which reads as a hang and sends you to the timeout knob — while the real cause sits at trail line 2885 of 2892, under roughly 2,700 React act(...) warnings. FAIL-SLOW and FAIL-VAGUE, not fail-open.

THE REMEDY DIFFERS ACCORDINGLY, and the worker took the right one: name the cause, do not tighten a floor. The poll loop now breaks on one terminal class and names it (the namespace it stopped at, the count reached, and the map-fixture fix), with a matcher-free backstop for any summary-less run carrying page errors. It rejected a lint rule — positional fixtures are legal without async rows, three such namespaces exist today, so a source regex would stand in for a fact the runner can observe directly — and rejected 'break on any pageerror', which would truncate a run that was about to report.

FOR THE RECORD, because it bears on how I triage: a P2 escalation resting on 'this is the fail-open class' should be checked against the instrument's actual behaviour before it goes out. The bead was still worth doing at the priority it got — a 360-second misleading timeout on a gate every PR runs is real — but for the right reason.

title: ssr-node ships with no npm script and no CI job, so nothing gates its 73 test rows on main
description:
ROUTED from worker/ssrsvc-hic056 (rf2-hic-056, PR #8028), which fenced this out deliberately and said why. Confirmed at source: 'ssr-node' appears in neither implementation/package.json nor .github/workflows/ on origin/main.

THE GAP. PR #8028 lands implementation/ssr-node/ — 26 files, 73 test rows across 7 suites, runnable today with 'node implementation/ssr-node/test/run.cjs' (exit 0 locally). Nothing on main runs it. A package whose suite nobody invokes rots silently, and the five bounded guarantees it was built to hold (state isolation, fail-closed allowlists, one in-flight render per isolate, timeout plus hard termination, latency envelope) become claims rather than gates the moment someone edits it.

WHY THE WORKER DID NOT DO IT, and the reasoning is good: one line in implementation/package.json arms ELEVEN expensive CI lanes — including hicasso_hmr — that this package's files arm none of. So a naive script addition makes every ssr-node edit pay for the whole Hicasso browser matrix. And scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py couples the script and its CI job, so they are one piece of work, not two.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES. A gate that runs ssr-node's suite, armed by ssr-node's OWN surface and nothing else. description:

BOTH are in .github/workflows/**, which is hot zone and was fenced out of that worker's brief, so they are reported rather than fixed.

1. lint.yml, "Install clj-kondo" (~line 283) — SHARES THE ENVELOPE HALF.
   A single `curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3`, no
   outer loop at all: a ~15 SECOND envelope, strictly narrower than the
   two-minute one that just failed four times. PR #8009's "five 503s" is
   exactly curl's five retries. The masking half is milder — `-f` means it
   dies at the curl with curl's own message rather than `command not found`
   — but the red still aggregates into `Lint required` and reads as a lint
   failure.

   MINIMAL FIX, one line:
     curl -fsSL --retry 12 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 15 --retry-max-time 420 \

   COUPLING — check before landing. scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py reads the
   clj-kondo version pin off this exact step (_KONDO_PIN_RE), and classifies
   the step as SETUP rather than a gate only when EVERY command line in the
   run body matches one of its SETUP_PATTERNS (`^curl .*clj-kondo/releases/
   download/`, `^unzip .*clj-kondo`, `^sudo install .*/clj-kondo$`,
   `^clj-kondo --version$`). Widening flags on the existing curl line
   preserves both. ADDING NEW COMMAND LINES DOES NOT — a `for` loop or a
   separate `echo ::error` line drops the body out of SETUP_PATTERNS and the
   gap map then reports the lint job as an UNRUN GATE. If the ::error
   annotation is wanted too, it must be an `|| { echo ...; exit 1; }`
   appended to the SAME logical line behind the existing backslash
   continuations. Re-run `python scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` either way.

2. test.yml, "Set up Babashka" (~line 5651) — SHARES BOTH HALVES.
   A line-for-line copy of the old three-attempt loop, falling through to
   `bb --version`, i.e. the identical exit-127 mask. Zero measured instances
   (it runs only on changed skill paths), which is why it is P2 and not
   higher. test.yml was additionally held by PR #8019 at the time.

   Either apply the same widening + ::error annotation inline, or extract to
   .github/scripts/install-babashka.sh and reduce the step to a two-line
   call, matching what rf2-e7ja9 did for the Clojure CLI. The #8030 worker
   deliberately did NOT pre-land that script: an installer nothing calls is
   unproven code, and one dead file plus a later hot-zone edit is worse than
   one later hot-zone edit.

NOT a defect, checked and deliberately left alone: .github/scripts/resolve-clojure-deps.sh has the same three-attempt shape but is already correct on the half that matters — guarded final backoff, ::error title= annotation, explicit exit 1, no fall-through. Its 45s envelope is short, but it retries a CLASSPATH BUILD against Maven Central where each attempt is expensive, and it has no measured instances. Widening it would be on spec.

REFERENCE for whoever takes this: PR #8030's install-clojure-cli.sh is the worked example of both halves, and its PR body carries the shim-based harness design that proves a failure path without waiting for a real outage.

NEW EVIDENCE, measured 2026-08-13 on PR #8027 (worker/advisor-hic037, diff confined to tools/xray/** — so not a real gate result). Seven instances today across six PRs now, up from four.

This is the second measured instance of the lint.yml step (with #8009), and it settles the shape question: the clj-kondo path dies AT the curl under -f, so its exit code is whatever curl returns for the transfer's failure mode (56 here, 22 for a plain HTTP error). Two consequences for whoever lands this:

2. If the optional ::error annotation is added, it must NOT be keyed on an exit code: the number varies with the transfer's failure mode. Use 'curl ... || { echo "::error title=..."; exit 1; }' on the same logical line, which fires whatever curl returned.
