title: CI: install-clojure-cli.sh 503 storms fail gates open — four PRs blocked in one session, exit 127
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 across FOUR separate PRs in one session. Every instance identical in shape.

WHAT HAPPENS: .github/scripts/install-clojure-cli.sh curls the Clojure CLI tarball, gets HTTP 503, retries, and exhausts its three attempts inside roughly two minutes. Line 48 then runs 'clojure' anyway, which is not installed, and the step dies with 'clojure: command not found', exit 127. The gate the job exists to run NEVER EXECUTES, and the job reports FAILURE indistinguishably from a real defect.

INSTANCES (all exit 127 at 'Set up Clojure CLI'):
- PR #8007, schemas-boundary gate — re-ran green.
- PR #8009, clj-kondo — 'Install clj-kondo' failed with five 503s, 'Run clj-kondo' skipped; re-ran green.
- PR #8017, Splint (job 94250184863, run 31636758975) — eighteen 503s across three retry rounds; 'Lint required' then aggregated the failure and blocked the merge. Re-ran green; PR merged.
- PR #8019, UI scaffold smoke (job 94252635127, run 31637553728) — eleven 503s, same exit 127.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN RE-RUNNING FOREVER: each instance costs a full mayor tick to diagnose (read the log, establish it is the install step and not the diff) plus a re-run cycle. More seriously it TRAINS THE WRONG REFLEX: a red gate that is usually infrastructure invites --admin, and the merge criterion has no --admin bypass. The failure is also fail-open in the opposite direction — a job that never ran its gate reports red, so nobody ships a defect, but the signal is noise and noise is what erodes the criterion.

THE RETRY WINDOW IS THE PROXIMATE CAUSE: three attempts at 10s/20s/30s backoff covers about two minutes. The observed 503 storms lasted longer than that in at least two instances (#8017 spanned 20:20:32 to 20:22:20).

CANDIDATE REMEDIES, not ruled between - the worker should establish which is right and say why:
(a) widen the retry envelope (more attempts, longer backoff, jitter) so a multi-minute storm is survived;
(b) cache the toolchain in the runner image or via actions/cache keyed on the CLI version, so a healthy run does not hit the network at all;
(c) fail the step EXPLICITLY as an infrastructure error distinguishable from a gate failure, so the merge loop can tell them apart without reading logs;
(d) some combination.

(c) has independent value even if (a) or (b) lands: right now the only way to tell 'the gate failed' from 'the gate never ran' is to read the raw log, which is exactly the manual step this bead is about.

SURFACE: .github/scripts/install-clojure-cli.sh, and possibly the workflow steps that call it. .github/workflows/* is HOT ZONE and sequential — sequence this behind any other in-flight workflow edit. Check whether a sibling install script (clj-kondo, per #8009) has the same shape and needs the same repair; the sweep is part of the job.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST: read install-clojure-cli.sh as it stands on origin/main before changing anything - the retry counts above are read from logs, not from the script.

title: dispatch-prompt-template.md understates its own poll-fallback, and reads grudging where it should read correct
description:
`dispatch-prompt-template.md` OWNS the gate-mechanics text, and its wording of the
poll-fallback is weaker than the rule that wording is supposed to carry. Found by
worker/loopdrift-oieu while closing rf2-oieu, and deliberately NOT fixed there:
the file was outside that bead's fence and is held by another worker, and
duplicating the corrected wording into the command file would have recreated the
very drift rf2-oieu closed.

## Why this matters rather than being a style note

The template is the single source of truth for gate mechanics. `mayor-dispatch.md`
now cites it as a must-paste (rf2-oieu, PR #8010) instead of restating it. So the
words in the template ARE the words that reach every worker. If they are grudging
or incomplete, the defect regenerates no matter how correctly the command file
points at them.

MEASURED COST of the current wording: three workers stranded in one hour on
2026-08-13 -- shadow-kyum, ssrwitness-hic046, gatehyg-qzm8. Each detached a long
gate, ended its turn, and waited for a "monitor" or "completion event" to wake it.
Nothing wakes a stopped worker. All three had pushed, so the cost was latency, not
data, and all three resumed correctly on one message.

## The two corrections

Both are in section "How a gate is run, not just which one", first bullet.

1. INCOMPLETE: it says "poll its log on a timer". The log is not the artefact that
   carries the verdict -- the `.exit` file is, and the same section says so
   elsewhere ("the number you quote is the one you captured"). A worker polling
   only the log has to infer completion from output rather than read it. Say: poll
   the log AND the `.exit` file, in a bounded loop, WITHIN THE SAME TURN.

2. GRUDGING REGISTER, and this is the more important half: "If you background a
   gate anyway" reads as tolerating a deviation. Two of the three stranded workers
   APOLOGISED for detaching. That is the finding -- the grudging register is
   precisely what stopped the polling instruction landing, because a worker that
   believes it has already erred is reading for how to atone rather than for what
   to do next. The section already establishes that detaching is FORCED (the
   harness hard-kills a foreground command at ten minutes; the spine needs about
   twenty-five), so name it outright as CORRECT and not a violation, then give the
   poll instruction as the ordinary path.

The four other things the paste must convey -- absolute-path invocation, the
`gate root:` check, `$?` captured on one command line into a worktree-suffixed
file, and quoting the number from that file rather than the harness's -- are
already conveyed squarely and need no change.

## Sequencing -- READ BEFORE DISPATCHING

`docs/the-mayor-method/` is HOT-ZONE-ADJACENT in practice: worker/gatehyg-qzm8 was
editing method docs when this was filed (PR #8008). DO NOT dispatch this alongside
any worker touching that tree. Verify at source that no live worker holds it, and
re-read the section at HEAD before editing -- it may already have moved.

## Fence

`docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` only, and within it only the
first bullet of "How a gate is run, not just which one". Do NOT edit
`.claude/commands/**` -- rf2-oieu just settled those, and a second copy of this
text in a command file is the drift this bead exists to avoid. Do NOT restate the
mechanics anywhere else.

## Gate

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` covers `docs/**` including this tree. Prove it
reached your file rather than reporting a silent exit 0: it is silent on success,
so plant a bogus anchor at the exact site you edited, quote the exit 1 naming file
and line, restore, and VERIFY THE RESTORE BY HASHING THE BYTES -- not by reading
`git diff`, which reads clean both for an unchanged file and for a patch that
never applied. `mkdocs --strict` does NOT cover `docs/design/**` but does build
`docs/the-mayor-method/`; nominate it only if you establish that at source.
close_reason: PR #8013. First bullet of 'How a gate is run, not just which one' rewritten: detaching a long gate named CORRECT outright (ending the turn is the defect), and the poll now covers the log AND the .exit file, bounded loop, same turn. Other four mechanics left untouched; .claude/commands/** untouched. check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, proved to select the file by a planted anchor at the edited line (exit 1, line 186) with the restore verified by sha256 (7228e03c... before and after). mkdocs skipped: not installed locally; established at source that exclude_docs does not exclude the-mayor-method/.

title: Two drifts between the mayor-*.md loop commands and the method they source from
description:
Two drifts between the codified loop bodies in `.claude/commands/mayor-*.md` and
the method they are supposed to be the single source of truth for. Found by the
55m method-reread loop on 2026-08-13, which instructs the mayor to fix the
command file when a method rule and its command no longer match. The mayor made
both edits, and the mayor-checkout pre-commit guard correctly REFUSED them:
source/doc/script changes must originate from a worker worktree. Hence this bead.
Both edits are small and fully specified below; apply them as written or improve
on them.

## Drift 1 — `.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md`, clause 1: a stale measured band

`bootstrap.md` designates clause 1 of this file as THE one place the measured
check-count band is kept current ("one place to keep current rather than two").
It currently reads `~91 as measured 2026-08-11`. Measured 2026-08-13: six
consecutive merged PRs, #8000 through #8005, EACH carry exactly 92 checks.

Replace the clause-1 band sentence with the 92 measurement, its date, and its
evidence, and keep the existing instruction to re-measure rather than trust the
constant. Note the band has now moved TWICE inside one programme (~86, then ~91
on 2026-08-11 via PRs #7874/#7875, then 92) — which is the argument for the
re-measure instruction, so make that history visible rather than replacing one
constant with another and leaving the reader thinking it is now settled.

Reproduce with:
  for n in $(gh pr list --state merged --limit 6 --json number --jq '.[].number'); do
    gh pr checks $n --json name,state | python -c "import sys,json;print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))"
  done

## Drift 2 — `.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md`: gate MECHANICS are not a must-paste

The Dispatch paragraph enumerates what to paste into every brief — the worktree
boundary block, the stance block, the bead list, the fence, the gate MENU, the
`## Quality gates` section, the no-stash guard, and so on. It does NOT enumerate
the gate MECHANICS block from `dispatch-prompt-template.md` section "How a gate
is run, not just which one".

That asymmetry is the defect. The template owns the mechanics text and the
command file delegates to the template generally, so this is drift by OMISSION
rather than contradiction — but the loop body is what the mayor actually reads
each tick, and everything else it enumerates gets pasted while this does not.

MEASURED COST, 2026-08-13: three workers stranded in one hour — `shadow-kyum`,
`ssrwitness-hic046`, `gatehyg-qzm8`. Each detached a long gate, ended its turn,
and waited for a "monitor" or "completion event" to wake it. Nothing wakes a
stopped worker. All three had pushed, so the cost was latency rather than data,
and all three resumed correctly on one message.

THE CLAUSE THAT GOES MISSING IS THE FALLBACK, because it reads as secondary and
is in fact the half that governs the hard case. The harness hard-kills a
foreground command at ten minutes; `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` needs roughly
twenty-five. So "run gates in the FOREGROUND to completion", pasted alone, is
UNSATISFIABLE for the spine, and a worker with no sanctioned path improvises the
forbidden one every time.

Add a clause to the Dispatch paragraph naming the gate-mechanics block as a
must-paste alongside the boundary and stance blocks, plus a short paragraph
saying why the fallback specifically keeps being compressed away. CITE the
template section rather than duplicating its text — the template stays the single
source. The paste must convey:

- Detaching a gate that outruns the ceiling is CORRECT and is not a violation.
  Two of the three stranded workers apologised for detaching, which is precisely
  why the poll instruction had not landed. Naming the detachment as correct is
  what makes the instruction land.
- Then POLL the log and the `.exit` file in a bounded loop WITHIN THE SAME TURN.
- Invoke the gate by ABSOLUTE path.
- Check the printed `gate root:` line names your own worktree.
- Capture `$?` on ONE command line into a `-<worktree>`-suffixed file.
- Quote the number read FROM THAT FILE, never the exit code the harness reports
  about the same run — those are different measurements and have disagreed.

## Fence

`.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md` and `.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md` only.
Do NOT edit `docs/the-mayor-method/**` — the method docs are correct as they
stand; both drifts are in the command files. Do NOT restate the mechanics text in
the command file; cite the template.

## Gate

`python scripts/check_readme_links.py` — that is the gate that covers
`.claude/commands/*.md`, and it resolves markdown PATH REFERENCES only.
`check_doc_slugs.py` does NOT cover this tree and must not be nominated for it;
`mkdocs --strict` does not build it either. If you add no markdown link, say
plainly in the PR body that the link gate had nothing to validate in this diff
rather than reporting its exit 0 as coverage. Verify prose and structure by hand
and say so.
close_reason: Both drifts closed in PR #8010 (worker/loopdrift-oieu). Drift 1: mayor-merge.md clause 1 now records 92, independently re-measured 2026-08-13 (PRs #8000-#8005 each exactly 92, not copied from this bead), keeps the re-measure instruction, and shows the band moving twice in one programme (~86 -> ~91 -> 92) so 92 does not read as settled; adds the one-command form gh pr checks <pr> --json state --jq 'length' to make re-measuring cheap. Confirmed clause 1 is still the only live copy (bootstrap.md:93 cites ~86 as history and delegates here). Drift 2: mayor-dispatch.md Dispatch paragraph now enumerates the gate-mechanics block as a must-paste BY CITATION to dispatch-prompt-template.md section 'How a gate is run, not just which one', plus a paragraph on why the fallback half is the one compressed away (unsatisfiable-when-trimmed; three stranded workers; the apology observation). Template text NOT duplicated. Method docs untouched. Gate: check_readme_links.py exit 0, and proven non-vacuous by a negative control -- it covers .claude/commands/*.md by bare-filename reference (rf2-1yy75) and exited 1 naming mayor-dispatch.md:21 when the added reference was broken; restore hash-verified. Residual noted in PR body: the template's own wording says 'poll its log on a timer' (not 'log and .exit file, bounded loop, same turn') and 'if you background a gate anyway' reads grudging rather than naming detachment correct -- both template-side, out of this fence, candidate follow-up.

title: HMR rig: three timeout knobs soften the gate when raised and leave no trace in the log
description:
FOUND BY worker/hmrengines-l92i (rf2-l92i, PR #8004) while fixing the sibling defect. LISTED, NOT FILED by that worker per its fence; filed here so the finding has an owner.

THE DEFECT. implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-hicasso-hmr-testbed.cjs honours three environment knobs that all SOFTEN the gate when raised:
  HICASSO_HMR_SAVE_TIMEOUT_MS
  HICASSO_HMR_BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS
  HICASSO_HMR_SPEC_TIMEOUT_MS

Raising a timeout to make a flake pass is the exact move rf2-odh3's bead forbade IN PROSE: 'DO NOT EXTEND THE 90s TIMEOUT — lengthening a timeout to make a flake pass is the fail-open shape this repo has spent two days deleting, and the watch is demonstrably healthy inside it.' The prose ban is not enforced, and worse:

NOTHING PRINTS THE VALUE THE RUN USED. So a raised ceiling leaves NO TRACE in the log at all. A run that passed only because someone widened a threshold is indistinguishable from one that passed on merit — including to the mayor reading the PR body, and including to a future reader trying to reproduce it.

CONTRAST, and it is the remedy's model: HICASSO_HMR_REGISTER_DELAY_MS (added by rf2-odh3) is ALREADY CORRECT — it announces itself up front, as does the narrowing banner rf2-l92i added for HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES. HICASSO_HMR_PORT cannot fail open since #7998's bundle digest. So three knobs out of five are honest and three are not.

REMEDY, the honest minimum: every timeout knob whose value differs from the default PRINTS that fact in the run's own summary, in the same register as the existing narrowing banner. Consider also whether a raised timeout should degrade the verdict token the way rf2-l92i degraded a narrowed run to 'HICASSO HMR PARTIAL PASS' — a run that needed a wider window than the contract allows arguably did not pass the contract. That second half is a judgement call, not obviously right; decide it on merit and say why.

DO NOT extend this into a general audit of every env knob in the repo — that is rf2-6ng7's class question and it awaits an operator ruling. This bead is the three named knobs in one file.

SEQUENCING — READ THIS BEFORE DISPATCHING. The deciding gate here is the HMR gate, and IT IS MACHINE-EXCLUSIVE: two workers running it collide on :dev-http 8061 and the loser is refused by assertOwnBundle. Do not dispatch this alongside any worker whose surface arms cljs-hicasso-hmr (that job arms on ANY implementation/hicasso/** path). See the bd memory 'hmr-gate-is-machine-exclusive'.

VERIFY AT SOURCE at or after PR #8004 merges — that PR changed this same file (+134/-2) and took its mutation teeth from 28 to 34.
notes:
LANDED — PR #8008 (worker/gatehyg-qzm8, on main as 4b8ca72467). implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-hicasso-hmr-testbed.cjs, +155/-18.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE AFTER #8004 MERGED, as the description required: that PR had already made the rig honest about a narrowed ENGINE SET, but had NOT generalised to the timeout knobs — all three still parsed inline off process.env with nothing printing the value used. The premise held.

REMEDY, matching rf2-l92i's pattern rather than inventing a second one:
- TIMEOUT_DEFAULTS is one table owning defaults, parse and disclosure, so the ceilings a run ENFORCES and the ones it DISCLOSES cannot drift. resolveTimeouts/timeoutOverrides are pure and exported, which is what makes them bitable.
- Every non-default value announces itself up front in main(), in the same register as the HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES narrowing banner and for the stated reason: a run about to spend half an hour should not leave the reader to discover in the last line that it was not running under the contract's windows.
- A RAISED ceiling closes with the EXISTING 'HICASSO HMR PARTIAL PASS' token — no third verdict string — with the sentence naming the knob and its default.

THE JUDGEMENT CALL THE DESCRIPTION LEFT OPEN ('consider also whether a raised timeout should degrade the verdict... decide it on merit and say why') DECIDED YES, on two grounds. First, the banner alone leaves the CLOSING line — the line PR bodies quote and greps find — still reading 'HICASSO HMR PASS', so the fail-open survives at exactly the point of quotation. Second, without instrumenting every wait, a run under a wider window cannot demonstrate it would have passed under the contract's, so the full token is unearned. A LOWERED ceiling is stricter than the contract: disclosed up front, verdict untouched — the asymmetry is deliberate and tooth-pinned.

OPERATOR CONTROL UNTOUCHED: the knobs stay tunable and a weakened run still exits 0. Only the silence is gone. No nag-diagnostics: a default run prints nothing new at all.

MUTATION TEETH 34 -> 41: default env overrides nothing; setting a knob TO its default is not an override; a raised ceiling is an override in the fail-open direction; a lowered one is an override but not a raised one; a raised ceiling costs the full verdict and the line names the knob; a lowered one leaves the full verdict intact; a narrowed run under a raised ceiling names BOTH causes. The pre-existing verdict teeth now pass an explicit overrides list so they stay hermetic when the gate itself runs under a raised environment — verified 41/41 with HICASSO_HMR_SAVE_TIMEOUT_MS=180000 exported.

PROVED BY RUNNING IT, not by reading it (all exit codes read from captured .exit files):
- Proof run, HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES=chromium + HICASSO_HMR_SAVE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000, exit 0: banner 'RAISED from its default 90000ms' up front, closing 'HICASSO HMR PARTIAL PASS (chromium only; ...NOT performed; HICASSO_HMR_SAVE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 raised the 90000ms ceiling...) — 12 real shadow reloads'.
- Full deciding run, default env, exit 0: 'HICASSO HMR PASS (chromium + firefox + webkit) — 36 real shadow reloads', 105 checks x 8 sections on each of three engines, and grep -c for the override banner over that whole log returns 0 — the disclosure is inert at default.
- Hot file views.cljs sha256 9b2f7c82e967d9ba21b4befe53852d835b7642002147f9584d38b66c5b9f704a identical before, after the proof run and after the full run, git status clean at each point. No source plant was needed: the knob is an environment variable, so the weakening applies without touching the tree — which is precisely why the defect was invisible.

FENCE HONOURED: the three named knobs in one file. No general audit of env knobs elsewhere (rf2-6ng7's class question, still awaiting its ruling), and .github/workflows/* untouched — that was worker/gatearm-6ng7's surface in the same wave. The CI job passes no narrowing and no timeout override, so its verdict token is unaffected.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8008, merged to main as part of 4b8ca72467. Merge evidence: 92 checks (33 SUCCESS + 59 SKIPPED), nothing nonterminal, all five workflow runs COMPLETED at head 5496bec757, no workflow commit on main since the merge-base so the check set was computed against the current matrix. Diff was AGENTS.md plus implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-hicasso-hmr-testbed.cjs -- no hot-zone file. Closed by the mayor because the PR merged while the worker was still live; if the worker intended further work under either id, it files a follow-up rather than reopening.

title: HMR rig: HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES can silence the cross-engine comparator while the run still prints PASS
description:
FOUND BY worker/hmrrace-odh3 (rf2-odh3, PR #7998) and deliberately NOT fixed there — it was outside that bead's fence, which was the GEN-1 registration race.

THE DEFECT. implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-hicasso-hmr-testbed.cjs honours HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES, which can narrow the run to a single engine. divergenceReport returns nothing below two engines, so the cross-engine comparator SILENTLY DISABLES ITSELF — and the run still prints 'HICASSO HMR PASS'. Nothing asserts the variable was unset.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is the fail-open family the repo has spent the week deleting, in the rig built to catch races. A one-engine run is a legitimate developer convenience; the defect is that its output is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a three-engine run that actually compared. A PASS that means 'I compared three engines and they agreed' and a PASS that means 'I ran one engine and skipped the comparison' must not print the same words.

The same PR found and fixed a sibling of this shape: waitForBuild's probe could get its 200 from ANOTHER worktree's shadow-cljs watch holding :dev-http 8061, so with a leftover watch from the same worktree the gate would go green on code the run never compiled. That one is fixed (the served bundle is now digested against what this watch wrote). This one is not.

CI DOES NOT SET HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES TODAY, so there is no live hazard on main — which is exactly why this is P2 and not P1. The hazard is that nothing prevents it being set, and nothing would say so afterwards.

REMEDY SHAPES (worker's judgement, not ruled):
(a) When fewer than two engines run, the summary says so in terms and the run does NOT print an unqualified PASS — e.g. 'HICASSO HMR PASS (1 engine; cross-engine comparison NOT performed)'.
(b) Additionally, assert in CI that HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES is unset, so the full matrix cannot be narrowed by an environment change nobody reviews.

(a) is the honest minimum and is what the stance points at — it makes the output tell the truth without forbidding a useful developer mode. (b) is a second gate and may be over-engineering for a variable CI does not set; decide on merit rather than adding it reflexively.

DO NOT extend this into a general audit of the rig's other env knobs — that is rf2-6ng7's class question, which is awaiting an operator ruling.

SURFACE: implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-hicasso-hmr-testbed.cjs. Verify at origin/main at or after 89b8bf9668 (PR #7998), which rewrote much of this file — teeth went 19 to 28.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8004 (correctness/completeness): the repair distinguishes a one-engine run, but its stronger shipped invariant is still false for a TWO-engine narrowing. HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES=chromium,firefox yields `HICASSO HMR PASS (chromium + firefox)`, so a grep for the token the new comments call the full-matrix verdict is answered even though WebKit never ran. `comparedAcrossEngines` correctly owns the >=2 comparator floor but is also used as the full/partial verdict discriminator, conflating "comparison happened" with "the pinned matrix ran". Keep the comparator floor; make the verdict disclose every narrowed matrix (or narrow the documented contract explicitly), and add the missing two-engine tooth. Reproduced directly from exported verdictLine at origin/main after 046b836dfe.
close_reason: Landed and MERGED as PR #8015 (branch worker/hmrverdict-l92i), verified on main: implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-hicasso-hmr-testbed.cjs (+209/-37) and implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs. Remedy chosen was DISCLOSE every narrowed matrix, not narrow the contract: comparedAcrossEngines keeps the >=2 comparator floor, and a new pure exported ranFullMatrix became the verdict's discriminator. Teeth 41 -> 46. The one item #8015 could not take is owned by rf2-agps (.github/workflows/test.yml, hot zone), whose PR #8019 is open.

title: Gate arming class RULED (c)-narrow: bounded audit of non-local input edges; every fix pins its own arming
description:
RULED 2026-08-13 under authority Mike delegated for the rf2-6ng7 decision dossier (delegated, operator-reversible). The former hold ("DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL MIKE RULES") is LIFTED — this bead is now dispatchable as the bounded audit described below. Both the dossier's recommendation and the appended Codex recommendation were weighed; they converged on (c) and this ruling adopts Codex's narrower scoping of it.

THE RULING: option (c) in narrow form, plus a no-new-machinery codicil.
- REJECTED (a), the universal input-declaration checker: gate read-sets are heterogeneous (shell case arms, Clojure rosters inside test files, Python globs, source walks, literal doc reads) and not mechanically derivable, so the declarations would be a second hand-maintained list subject to exactly the rot being treated. Over-engineering at this count.
- REJECTED bare (b), fix-as-found: discovery is demonstrably luck — instance 4 (rf2-w9ip) was found by a worker running an unrelated suite on its own initiative, and rf2-61ar (closed) shows the same class recurring OUTSIDE the four catalogued instances (prose surfaces pinned by JVM tests arming nothing). Waiting to trip over instance six is too weak for the gates the merge decision rests on.
- ADOPTED (c)-narrow: one bounded audit of the exceptional edges only, each mismatch fixed with the cheapest local repair, and every fix pinning its own arming in harnesses that already exist.

THE CLASS, for the auditor. CI gating is two-layered: .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh classifies a PR diff into ~32 boolean surface outputs, and .github/workflows/test.yml (~80 jobs) conditions jobs on them. Each gate declares what it READS somewhere else entirely (its own source, a roster in a JVM test file, an npm script's args). When read-set and arming drift, the gate is perfectly correct, perfectly scheduled, and never fires on exactly the edits it polices — CI green, meaning nothing. Existing meta-checks ask different questions: check_gate_scheduling.py asks "does this gate run anywhere?", check_fast_pr_gap.py asks "does the local spine match CI's required set?". Neither follows an input edge into its arming predicate.

AUDIT SCOPE — narrow, per the ruling. Audit ONLY conditional gates with NON-LOCAL input edges: gates that read outside their natural owner tree, or whose input population comes from a roster, glob, source walk, manifest, or literal document read. Do NOT enumerate all ~80 test.yml jobs / ~85 required jobs / 43 npm test:* scripts — ordinary same-tree test jobs are out of scope. Find the exceptional edges by searching for their signatures: slurp, file-seq, repo-root walks, cross-tree classpaths, external fixture rosters, workflow-owned target lists. For each edge record exactly four facts: gate, input root, scheduled job, and a classifier probe result (bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh <representative-path-under-input-root>). A mismatch = the probe does not arm the job that runs the gate.

REMEDY TOOLKIT per mismatch — cheapest local repair, all already demonstrated on main:
1. Make a sub-second static check unconditional and required (instances 1–2: hicasso-complaint-catalogue, hicasso-budget-ledger — pure-Python checks are cheap to always-run).
2. Derive the arming predicate from the gate's own roster when that roster is genuinely machine-readable, so it cannot re-drift (the rf2-w9ip fix shape: census arming derived from the suite's app-roots list, not restated).
3. Add a positive "path X arms output Y" assertion PLUS one negative control (unrelated path stays cheap) to implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs — NOTE the harness lives in implementation/scripts/, not .github/workflows/ as an earlier comment here said.
4. Give a script-owned lane a --classify/--self-test arming probe (instance 3: scripts/lint_kondo.py --self-test proves the once-missed file arms the lane).

THE CODICIL (standing policy, zero new machinery): every mismatch fix — the audit's and any future accidental find's — pins its own arming in those existing harnesses IN THE SAME PATCH. Review rule going forward: a change that adds a non-local read adds its arming proof in the same patch. This accretes (a)'s protection instance-by-instance exactly where drift actually happens, without taxing gates that never drift.

title: Sabotage guidance: a hash-verified plant can still yield a false green from a stale compile
description:
FOUND BY worker/mcpwire-hic059 (rf2-hic-059, PR #7997) while proving its egress negative control was non-vacuous.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md tells workers to verify a sabotage plant and its restore BY HASHING THE FILE BYTES, never by reading git diff. That rule closes one hole — 'the patch never applied', which reads identical to an exact restore. It does NOT close the hole one step downstream: THE PATCH APPLIED TO THE SOURCE AND THE RUNTIME NEVER SAW IT.

WHAT HAPPENED, measured. The worker planted a single-line egress fault in implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/tool.cljs and ran its live wire witness. IT CAME BACK GREEN. The hashes differed (2c6ecbed…5148 before, 915aaf91…e424 planted), so the plant HAD applied and a hash check reported success. But re-frame.hicasso.tool is not in the host build's module graph, so shadow-cljs watch never noticed the edit and served the PRE-PLANT COMPILE. Restarting the watch produced the expected red and the correct message ('EGRESS: the read-mounted-boundaries envelope carried the seeded secret at the wire').

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A ONE-WORKER SLIP. The whole purpose of the plant is to prove an assertion CAN fail. A green sabotage run is read as 'the control is vacuous, my witness proves nothing' — or, worse, the worker adjusts the witness until the sabotage reds, chasing a fault that was never being compiled. Either way the conclusion drawn is about the wrong artefact. This is the same fail-open family the repo has spent the week deleting: a check reporting a result about a case it never exercised. The hash rule makes it MORE dangerous, not less, because the hash is genuine evidence for a narrower claim than the worker needs.

THE DISCRIMINATOR the worker used: the run must show POSITIVE evidence the runtime observed the plant, not merely that the file changed. Restarting the watch was sufficient here. Other shapes worth naming: assert the plant's own marker appears in the served bundle; or check the build reported a recompile of the file you edited.

REMEDY (bounded): amend the sabotage paragraph in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md so the hash rule is followed by its downstream twin — hashing proves the SOURCE changed; a watch/compile/bundle check proves the RUNTIME changed; a green sabotage run is not evidence until BOTH hold. Cite this incident. Keep it to that paragraph.

DO NOT build a gate or a script for this. rf2-j9tl and rf2-maiw both declined analogous tooling as over-engineering; this is guidance, and the same judgement applies.

SEQUENCING: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md was last edited by rf2-maiw part (a), PR #7996, merged 7413b6c772. Verify at that HEAD or later.

Names the three discriminators (restart the watch; assert the plant's marker in the served bundle; confirm the build reported recompiling the edited file) and cites the rf2-hic-059 / PR #7997 incident with its hashes. title: Sibling workers share one scratchpad, so an un-suffixed gate log reports another worker's exit code
description:
FOUND BY worker/gatereach-x1mz (rf2-x1mz/rf2-uomk) while capturing the fast-PR spine's exit code.

Every worker dispatched into a wave gets the SAME scratchpad directory -- the path carries the SESSION id, not the worktree. Observed simultaneously in one directory:

  gate-fastpr.log / .exit              (gatereach-x1mz, mine)
  gate-fastpr-tail4.log / .exit        (rf2-o0n1)
  gate-fastpr-codemod-m4hm.log / .exit (a third worker)

THE FAILURE. The dispatch brief's own worked example names the file un-suffixed:

  sh <abs>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > gate-fastpr.log 2>&1; echo "$?" > gate-fastpr.exit

A worker following it literally writes to a shared name. Another worker's run had ALREADY created gate-fastpr.exit containing '0'. Reading it returned that 0 while my own spine was still running -- 'ps -ef' showed my pid 2227553 alive and the monitor was reporting '==> JVM implementation/core' at the same moment. The log was interleaved by two writers at independent offsets (a line began mid-word: 'moke the built bundles').

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TIDINESS COMPLAINT. The brief instructs workers to 'quote the exit code YOU captured, never the harness's', precisely so a green is earned. This collision makes the captured code SOMEBODY ELSE'S, and it reads as a clean pass -- a worker reports green, the mayor merges on it, and nothing anywhere records that the gate never finished. It is the same fail-open shape as rf2-x1mz and rf2-uomk: a check reporting success over a case it never exercised.

I caught it only because the lane list in the log did not match the run I was watching. A worker not watching would not have.

REMEDY OPTIONS (operator's call):
  a. The dispatch brief's example names a worktree-suffixed file, the way it already requires for pr-body-<slug>.md. Cheapest; relies on workers reading carefully, which is what failed here.
  b. Give each worker a scratchpad keyed by WORKTREE rather than session. Closes it by construction; harness change, outside this repo.
  c. Have the spine itself refuse to write a report file that already exists and is not its own -- a repo-side guard, but it only covers this one script.

(a) plus (c) is probably the honest minimum. Filed rather than fixed: the brief lives outside this repo's write surface and the choice is a process decision.
notes:
SECOND CONFIRMED INSTANCE, SAME WAVE, DIFFERENT WORKER (mayor, 2026-08-12).

worker/codemod-m4hm (rf2-m4hm + rf2-cvjp, PR #7993, since merged as 7a97c5e706) hit this independently and reported it: 'my first spine run was clobbered by a sibling worker — its gate root: read gatereach-x1mz — because I used a generic scratch name. Caught it via the gate root: line, discarded that log and exit code, re-ran under a unique name.'

So the defect is not hypothetical and not one worker's slip: two of six workers in a single wave collided on the same scratchpad, and the loser READ A GREEN BELONGING TO ANOTHER WORKER'S CODE. That is a fail-open of the merge decision itself — the exit code a PR body quotes is the artefact this bug corrupts.

WHAT SAVED IT BOTH TIMES was the gate's printed 'gate root:' line, not the naming convention. That is worth keeping in mind when choosing the remedy: a naming rule is advisory and was in fact present in both dispatch briefs, and was still not followed. The 'gate root:' check is a positive verification the worker performs on evidence it received, which is the stronger shape. Consider whether the remedy should make the check mandatory-and-mechanical rather than merely tightening the naming guidance that already failed twice.

MAYOR MITIGATION ALREADY IN PLACE, so this is not urgent-blocking: dispatches from this point (rf2-odh3, rf2-hic-041) carry a hardened instruction naming the log file FOR the worktree and stating the 'gate root:' check as the backstop rather than as an aside. That mitigates new dispatches only; it does not fix the template's worked example, which is the root cause this bead names.

SUGGESTED PAIRING: rf2-59zp is the other mayor-method process fix currently open (.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, count-claims). Both are small, both are method-surface, and neither is on any in-flight worker's tree — a natural two-bead cluster for the next free slot.
REMEDY (a) HAS LANDED — PR #7996 (worker/scratchname-maiw, branch commit 790b1bf39d). Bead deliberately LEFT OPEN for (b) and (c), which remain the operator's call.

THE BEAD'S BLOCKING PREMISE DID NOT HOLD. The description says this was 'filed rather than fixed: the brief lives outside this repo's write surface'. It is not outside it. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md is TRACKED here — 'git ls-files docs/the-mayor-method/' returns README.md, bootstrap.md and dispatch-prompt-template.md — and it carried the offending worked example verbatim at line 227. So (a) was always an in-repo fix, and the only thing blocking it was the belief that it wasn't.

WHAT MADE (a) IN-SCOPE WITHOUT AN OPERATOR RULING: the file contradicted itself. Its WORKTREE BOUNDARY block, pasted verbatim into every editing dispatch, already required worktree-suffixed scratch names (pr-body-<worktree>.md, never pr-body.md), while the worked example under 'Put every gate artefact where git ignores it' showed the bare gate-fastpr.log / gate-fastpr.exit. A worker copying the example literally was OBEYING the document. Repairing that is a consistency fix, not a policy choice.

LANDED IN (a):
- Worked example now writes gate-fastpr-<worktree>.log / .exit, plus a paragraph on why the suffix is load-bearing (the exit code a PR body quotes is exactly the artefact the collision corrupts).
- The boundary block — the text workers actually receive — adds the gate artefacts to its example list and now carries the 'gate root:' check.
- The 'gate root:' bullet now states that THAT CHECK, NOT THE NAMING RULE, is what caught both incidents, and that the naming rule was present in both dispatch briefs and followed in neither. This answers the note above asking whether the remedy should make the check mandatory-and-mechanical rather than tightening guidance that already failed twice: within (a)'s bounds the strongest available move was to put the check into the verbatim-pasted block, so every worker receives it as a step rather than an aside.
- Failure-modes index entry now names the exit-code / merged-on-an-unearned-green case.
- One disclosed correction beyond naming: the example invoked <WORKTREE_ROOT>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, but per the file's own placeholder list <WORKTREE_ROOT> is the PARENT dir holding worktrees and has no scripts/. Corrected to <ASSIGNED_WORKTREE>.

STILL OPEN, NOT IMPLEMENTED:
(b) scratchpad keyed by WORKTREE rather than session — harness change, outside this repo. Closes the defect by construction and is the only remedy that does; (a) still relies on workers reading carefully, which is precisely what failed twice.
(c) spine-side guard refusing to overwrite a report file that already exists and is not its own — repo-side but changes scripts/test-fast-pr.sh's behaviour, which this dispatch was fenced out of. The description's own view is that '(a) plus (c) is probably the honest minimum', so (c) is the live question.

A FOURTH VARIANT OF THIS ARTEFACT-TRUST CLASS, measured 2026-08-13 by worker/benchdoc-4uhh (rf2-4uhh, PR #8003). Noted here because this bead is the open owner of the scratchpad-artefact question; it does NOT change remedy (a), which has landed.

A KILLED GATE CAN POISON A LATER LOG AT THE SAME PATH. The worker's first 'npm run test:cljs' hit the harness's ten-minute foreground cap and was SIGTERM'd. Its ORPHANED CHILD kept writing into the same log path after the next run had truncated it, briefly showing 15 'FAIL in' blocks against a '0 failures' tally in one file. The FAILs were spawn-runner children exiting 0xC0000142 because the harness had killed their process group, in implementation/test-quiet/ — a different artefact with no bench/hicasso dependency, so they were not even about the code under test. The worker re-ran into a fresh filename and quoted only that clean result.

WHY IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AND WHY IT IS NOT COVERED. The four variants now on record all corrupt the evidence a PR body quotes:
1. A PEER overwrites your artefact (this bead, two instances).
2. A STALE COMPILE serves pre-plant code to a hash-verified sabotage (rf2-hs3i, landed).
3. A STALE .exit from an OOM-killed earlier run fires a monitor (worker/ssrwitness-hic046).
4. An ORPHANED CHILD of a killed run writes into a path a later run reuses (this note).

Remedy (a) suffixes artefacts per WORKTREE, which closes variant 1. It does NOT close 3 or 4, because those are collisions with your OWN earlier runs in your OWN worktree. The increment that would is per-RUN uniqueness rather than per-worktree, plus the discipline both workers converged on independently: key completion on the log's own summary line, and quote only the exit code captured by the run that produced the matching log.

DELIBERATELY NOT ACTIONED. This is a small increment on a rule that just landed, and the stance says close minutiae rather than action it. Recorded here so that IF the operator rules on (b) — a worktree-keyed scratchpad — the design accounts for same-worktree run collisions too, since (b) as described would not close variants 3 and 4 either.

MAYOR CORRECTION, 2026-08-13. I CLOSED THIS BEAD TWICE TODAY AND BOTH CLOSES WERE
WRONG. Reopening. Nothing about the work changed; my reading of the record did.

DELIBERATELY REOPENED it, reporting: "its own notes say it is deliberately open
for remedies (b) and (c), which are the operator's call -- the bead governs over

"a bead I closed now reads open": a genuine revert (no new note -- re-close with
evidence) and an audit reopen (a MERGED-PR AUDIT note naming a defect -- leave it,

title: hic — five ruling-citing amendments live only in the SNAPSHOT copies, which the next republication overwrites
description:
Surfaced by rf2-2aag (PR #7987) rather than actioned, because the remedy is the operator's.

product/README.md's Refresh contract says in terms: 'The copies here are decision-brief.md, specification.md, and everything under lanes/ ... Those are written and revised under ai/, in the operator's sessions. **Do not edit them here: the next publication overwrites the edit, and the operator who owns the original never sees it.** A correction to one of them is made to the source, and arrives by republication.'

Three worker passes have now amended those two copies in place — correctly, because each amendment was explicitly authorised by an operator ruling and named in its bead's deliverables:

- rf2-sh56 (PR #7978): specification.md §7 Forms row; decision-brief.md Phase 5.
- rf2-xpq9 (commit 50bc1adb9d): specification.md Phase 5 preamble; decision-brief.md Phase 5 section.
- rf2-2aag (PR #7987): specification.md Phase 5 ladder item 2.

So FIVE dated, ruling-citing amendments to published snapshots currently exist ONLY in the tracked copies. If the operator-local originals under ai/ do not carry the same amendments, the next republication of either file silently reverts all five, and the reverted text is the superseded position — a helper waiting for a second caller, a phase held past v0 — with nothing on screen to say it moved. rf2-n3b8's ten sites will add more.

Two things are wanted, and only the operator can do either:

1. Carry the five amendments into the ai/ originals (or confirm they are already there), so a republication is idempotent.
2. Say whether the Refresh contract's 'do not edit them here' now has a standing exception for operator-ruled amendments cited at their site, and write that exception into the contract — because three beads in a row have taken it, and the next worker reading the contract literally will refuse an edit its own bead names.

Note the same paragraph is the live fence on lanes/**, which every one of these passes respected. Whatever is decided here should not weaken that.
notes:
MISSED FROM THE OPERATOR DECISION LIST $D - recorded so it is not missed twice.

When Mike asked for his decision beads, the mayor gave him NINE: rf2-2rtt6.140, rf2-5yn9, rf2-iay8, rf2-6ng7, rf2-glut, rf2-2uy8, rf2-hic-092, rf2-uelji, rf2-5rqn. THIS BEAD SHOULD HAVE BEEN THE TENTH.

HOW IT WAS MISSED. The mayor scanned the tracker export with a regex for operator-decision language, got 24 hits, judged most to be beads that merely MENTION an operator, and hand-excluded this one. That exclusion was wrong. This bead is operator-only in terms, twice over:

  - a worker cannot edit the mayor checkout's ai/ tree, so one remedy is physically not a worker's;
  - writing the standing exception into the Refresh contract IS the ruling this bead requests, and
    the README's own close says moving the living home is "an operator and Codex decision... not a
    worker's to take".

THE DEFER ITSELF IS CORRECT AND SHOULD STAND. The #8006 audit deferred it to 2026-08-20 precisely so bd ready would stop advertising an operator-only bead for worker dispatch, matching the rf2-5rqn precedent. That is the hold working as designed - and it is also exactly why a ready-list scan will never surface it. A DEFERRED OPERATOR BEAD IS INVISIBLE TO THE PROJECTION THAT THE DEFER EXISTS TO PROTECT IT FROM.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which is the same one this session already learned about the measurement lane: bd ready is a projection, and every hold that works by deferring removes the bead from it. Build the operator list from the RAW list with the defers included, never from bd ready.

WHAT IT IS WAITING FOR, so the cost is visible: five ruling-citing amendments live only in the snapshot copies, and the next republication overwrites them. That is a data-loss risk with a trigger nobody controls - it fires whenever republication next happens, not on a date.

SURFACED TO MIKE $D alongside the answered nine.
close_reason: DISSOLVED by the rf2-rbme3 ruling (2026-08-16, delegated). Both asks are answered: (1) carrying the five ruling-citing amendments into the ai/ originals is moot — the snapshot contract is retired, republication is abolished, the tracked copies ARE the documents and already carry all five amendments; (2) the standing-exception question is answered in the stronger form — in-place amendment of decision-brief.md, specification.md and lanes/** is now the NORMAL mode, with the one fence this bead asked not be weakened carried forward into the rewritten contract: substantive semantic amendments name their authorizing bead or ruling at the site. description:
FOUND BY worker/lintfix-7976 while repairing PR #7976's clj-kondo red. TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, EITHER SUFFICIENT — SO NO LOCAL GATE IN THIS REPO COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT.

1. VERSION SKEW. scripts/check_lint_export.py resolves clj-kondo via shutil.which — whatever is on PATH. On this machine that is 2025.10.23; CI PINS 2026.04.15. Measured on the exact file: local 2025.10.23 gives `errors: 0, exit 0`; the pinned 2026.04.15 gives `errors: 2, exit 3`. The script's own docstring claims it runs "at the version CI pins" — TRUE ONLY IN CI, where the job installs the pin before running.

2. PATH COVERAGE. That lane's only --lint targets are lint-fixtures/positive.cljs, lint-fixtures/negative.cljs and hicasso/testbed. IT NEVER LINTS hicasso/src/. So implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/overlay.cljs was outside every local lane REGARDLESS of version.

WHAT IT MISSED, so the cost is concrete rather than theoretical: two `(aset f "displayName" "...")` calls stamping a React displayName onto a FUNCTION. `aset` is the ARRAY accessor. clj-kondo 2026.04.15 reads the TYPE rather than pattern-matching the form — ten lines earlier the same file calls `(aget claimed 0)` on a genuine `#js []` and kondo left it alone.

THE LATENT COST, verified from cljs/core.cljc 1.12.145 rather than assumed: with :checked-arrays OFF (the default, unset repo-wide) `aset`'s 3-arity emits character-identical output to `unchecked-set`, so today the consequence is NONE. With :checked-arrays :warn it routes to checked-aset and asserts `(or (array? array) (goog/isArrayLike array))` and `(number? idx)` — a function fails the first, "displayName" fails the second, two assertion failures per stamp. WITH :checked-arrays :error IT THROWS, and because these are top-level def forms THE THROW LANDS AT NAMESPACE INITIALIZATION — turning on a standard hardening flag would take the ENTIRE OVERLAY MODULE OUT AT LOAD TIME, not degrade one path.

REMEDY IS HOT-ZONE, WHICH IS WHY THE FINDER STOPPED: pinning the local resolver to CI's version and/or widening the lane's --lint paths touches scripts/ and .github/workflows/. Sequence it as a lone spec/workflow writer.

RELATED: rf2-uomk is the same SHAPE one gate over — a check that cannot fire on the edit it polices. Consider ruling them together.

ONE OBSERVATION THE FINDER RAISED FOR TRIAGE RATHER THAN FIXING (do NOT gold-plate it): the browser dev build emits 8 `Cannot infer target type` notes for `(.. el -style -anchorName)` at overlay.cljs:160/161/179/180 — untouched lines, same interop-hygiene family. The :advanced release build, where property renaming actually happens, is 0 warnings and its bundle checks pass, so THERE IS NO LIVE HAZARD.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7994 (merged e7b9924f4b). Local clj-kondo lane now pins CI's version rather than resolving via shutil.which, and the lane's --lint paths widened to cover implementation/hicasso/src/ — the two independent reasons no local gate could catch PR #7976's red. Adds scripts/lint_kondo.py; touches .github/workflows/test.yml, scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py, scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_lint_export.py. Mayor merged on all five clauses (92 checks, 90 SUCCESS + 2 SKIPPED, all 5 runs at head sha COMPLETED, matrix unchanged since base). Note the deliberate non-action: the 8 'Cannot infer target type' notes at overlay.cljs:160/161/179/180 were left alone as the bead directed — :advanced release build is 0 warnings, so there is no live hazard and fixing them would be gold-plating.

title: hic — four product docs still say the buffered-field helper is post-v0 / second-caller-gated
description:
rf2-sh56 shipped `re-frame.hicasso.forms` under the operator ruling of 2026-08-12 and amended the FOUR published snapshots that ruling explicitly authorised: specification.md §7 forms row, decision-brief.md Phase 5, requirements-mine.md forms row, decisions.md HD-019's post-v0-ladder note.

Four more sites in the same tree still carry the superseded position, and none was in the authorised set — an unexplained edit to a published snapshot is indistinguishable from an accident, so rf2-sh56 reported them rather than widening its own licence:

1. `docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md` Phase 5 ladder, item 2 — 'forms recipes and a buffered-draft helper after its second consumer'. This is the SAME sentence as decision-brief.md's Phase 5, which the ruling did authorise, so the two documents now disagree.
2. `docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md` Forms row — 'buffered-draft helper at its second caller'.
3. `docs/design/hicasso/product/README.md` — 'the reasoning that did not extract a buffered-field helper ... Read it before proposing re-frame.hicasso.forms'. A reader is now sent to a refusal for a module that ships.
4. `docs/design/hicasso/product/forms-recipes.md` — the whole page argues the helper is not extracted and states 'naming-ledger.md row 16 stays exactly as it is'. Row 16 is now settled as shipped. The page's reasoning was sound on its own ground and is worth keeping as a record; what it needs is a dated header note saying the operator overruled it on different ground, not a rewrite.

Each edit should cite the ruling at its site, as rf2-sh56's four did. This bead exists so the fifth-through-eighth edits are a decision rather than a worker widening a fence.

title: core: a captured handler exception reaches NO channel unless a listener is attached (measured on rf2-06lp)
description:
Measured while verifying rf2-06lp, whose premise did not hold: `:rf.mutation/execute` DOES refuse an unregistered mutation id (`mreg/require-mutation-spec!`, first statement of `execute-handler`, canonical `:rf.error/mutation-not-registered` naming the id). The finder's four browser runs were not spent on a missing guard. They were spent because the refusal reached no channel they were watching.

## Measured, JVM lane, four controls

Each dispatched, with stdout and stderr bound to a StringWriter and an `:errors` listener attached:

| case | stdout | stderr | :errors record |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:rf.mutation/execute` with an unregistered id | "" | "" | `:rf.error/handler-exception` |
| a plain `reg-event` handler that throws | "" | "" | `:rf.error/handler-exception` |
| a foreign top-level effect key (the rf2-04tx refusal) | "" | "" | `:rf.error/effect-map-shape` |
| dispatch of a completely unregistered EVENT id | "" | "" | `:rf.error/no-such-handler` |

So the silence is NOT mutation-specific and not resources-owned. Every framework refusal is invisible to a developer who has attached no listener — including the case where the event id itself is a typo.

## The specific spec claim that does not hold

spec/009 §Observability channels #5 says: "Native browser machinery — uncaught exceptions still reach `window.onerror` / `window.onunhandledrejection`. A re-frame2 event handler that throws in production still surfaces there."

It does not. `re-frame.router` CAPTURES the chain exception into `:rf/interceptor-error` rather than re-throwing (router.cljc:1004 states this in terms — "the drain must not abort"), so the throw never propagates out of `dispatch` OR `dispatch-sync` and never reaches `window.onerror`. Confirmed: nothing escaped `dispatch-sync` in the JVM repro. Channel #5 is therefore load-bearing in the catalogue and false in the code — it is the channel a reader would count on when deciding they need no listener.

## What this is NOT

Not a request for a nag-diagnostic, and not a second mechanism. The always-on error-emit registry is the right substrate and Xray is the right consumer. The question is narrower and is a RULING, not an implementation detail:

- either channel #5's claim is made true (the ordinary handler-exception path surfaces to the host's uncaught machinery in a dev build), or
- a dev-only default sink is registered so `goog.DEBUG` builds print an `:rf.error/*` record once, or
- channel #5 is corrected to say what the code does, and the docs say plainly that a dev build needs a listener attached before any framework refusal is legible.

## Fences

Surface is `implementation/core` plus `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (hot zone, sequential). rf2-06lp's worker did not touch either; its own deliverable was test-only. Evidence, both sabotage directions, and the four-control table are in the rf2-06lp PR body.
notes:
REFUSAL — NEEDS AN OPERATOR RULING. No code changed, no spec changed, no PR opened. 2026-08-12 23:09 AUSEST, worktree quiet-fu75 (WORKTREE_ROOT=/c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/quiet-fu75).

The bead asks a question it explicitly labels "a RULING, not an implementation detail" and offers three options. It carries no notes (comment_count 0, updated_at == created_at), so nothing settles which. Per the standing stance — do not invent a policy and ship it — I stopped. What follows is the verification and the option costing, so the ruling is cheap to make.

=== EVERY PREMISE ON THIS BEAD HOLDS. Independently re-measured, not taken on trust. ===

JVM lane, re-frame.debug DEFAULT (on), plain-atom adapter under the suite's own reset-runtime fixture, stdout and stderr each bound to a fresh StringWriter, and the dispatch wrapped so an escaping throwable is caught and named rather than assumed absent:

  throwing handler                stdout="" stderr="" escaped=NOTHING records=[:rf.error/handler-exception]
  foreign top-level effect key    stdout="" stderr="" escaped=NOTHING records=[:rf.error/effect-map-shape]
  unregistered EVENT id (typo)    stdout="" stderr="" escaped=NOTHING records=[:rf.error/no-such-handler]
  throwing handler, NO listener   stdout="" stderr="" escaped=NOTHING records=n/a

The fourth row is the developer's actual situation and is the bead's point: with no listener attached, a framework refusal reaches NO channel at all. "escaped=NOTHING" is measured, not inferred — dispatch-sync returned normally in every row.

Mechanism confirmed at source, and the code states it in terms:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc:124-132 — the chain APPENDS to :rf/interceptor-errors and sets :rf/interceptor-error rather than re-throwing.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:999-1004 (emit-pipeline-exception! docstring) — "The chain captures the exception into `:rf/interceptor-error` rather than re-throwing (the drain must not abort)".
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc — contains NO println / js/console / *err* write anywhere. There is no default sink. Verified by grep, not by absence of memory.

So spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1285 channel #5 ("A re-frame2 event handler that throws in production still surfaces there") is FALSE as written. Confirmed.

=== ONE CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S FRAMING, AND IT MATTERS TO THE RULING ===

The silence is NOT total in a tooled dev build. Xray registers a TRACE-stream collector (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs:45, :rf.xray/trace-collector), and the same router site that fans the always-on record ALSO forwards to the dev-only trace/emit-error! (router.cljc:1142). So :rf.error/* records DO reach the trace stream and DO show up in Xray.

The failure mode is therefore narrower and sharper than "re-frame2 is silent": it is the UNTOOLED dev build — no Xray, no listener — where a typo'd event id produces literally nothing. That is exactly the lane rf2-06lp's finder was in (a :browser-test build), and it is what cost them four runs.

This cuts both ways and the operator should weigh it, not me: it weakens option (b) (the shipped answer to "I want to see errors in dev" is already "install Xray"), and it sharpens the question of what an untooled dev build owes a developer who typo'd an event id.

=== THE CARRIER SWEEP — done in full, so a ruling can be executed in one pass ===

Blast radius is entirely inside spec/009-Instrumentation.md. Discriminator applied per the brief: is the passage describing the LISTENER channel (correct) or claiming an UNCONDITIONAL native channel (stale)?

STALE — three carriers, all in spec/009, all needing the same edit under options (b) or (c):
1. :1285 — channel #5 itself. "A re-frame2 event handler that throws in production still surfaces there." Flatly false.
2. :1327 — decision-matrix "What to avoid" cell: "Don't rely on `window.onerror` alone — it sees the bare exception without re-frame2's structured frame/event-id context." Softer, same wrong idea: for a handler exception window.onerror sees NOTHING, not a bare exception.
3. :1394 — "Native-SDK fallback": recommends installing the monitor's native SDK, which "captures window.onerror ... the monitor sees the bare exception, not the cascade context." This is an actively misleading RECOMMENDATION — for the handler-exception case that fallback captures nothing at all. Note this one is false under ALL THREE options as the bead words them, since option (a) is scoped to a DEV build and :1394 is about production.

CORRECT AS WRITTEN — left standing, no edit needed. All six contrast the structured listener record against what a bare window.onerror would have given you, i.e. they describe the listener channel:
- docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md:17 and :43 (the second is a historical statement about v1)
- docs/core/observability.md:423
- docs/resources/tutorial/05-test-and-ship.md:297 and :316
- skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/production-observability.md:31

Note also that spec/009's two lists number their surfaces DIFFERENTLY — "Native browser machinery" is #5 in the §What IS available in production list (where error-emit is #2), but the later five-surface decision matrix has no native-machinery entry at all (its #5 is the Performance API channel). Whoever executes the ruling should not assume "#5" means one thing.

=== THE THREE OPTIONS, COSTED ===

(a) Make channel #5's claim true in a dev build — re-surface the captured exception to the host's uncaught machinery.
    SEAM EXISTS AND HAS IN-REPO PRECEDENT. implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/root.cljs:1197 report-globally! and implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1053 report-recoverable-default! both already do exactly this: (js/reportError e) when globalThis.reportError exists, else console.error. reportError dispatches a window "error" event, so it genuinely reaches window.onerror — this is the standard way to hand a CAUGHT exception to the host's uncaught machinery. A goog.DEBUG-gated call at the error_emit.cljc fan-out would do it.
    FOR: makes the existing spec sentence true rather than retreating from it; zero new vocabulary; reuses a pattern the repo already ships twice; the host's own machinery (and any already-installed Sentry SDK) becomes the zero-config dev channel.
    AGAINST: it is a console-shouting default by another name, which is the shape the stance rejects; the drain deliberately does not abort, and reportError re-introduces host-visible noise per refusal, including for expected-refusal tests; no JVM counterpart (reportError is browser-only), so the JVM/SSR lane stays silent and the channel becomes platform-asymmetric.

(b) A dev-only default sink printing one :rf.error/* record per refusal under goog.DEBUG.
    FOR: directly fixes the untooled-dev-build case, which is the actual reported harm; cheapest thing to reason about; cross-platform (a println/console.error works on both lanes).
    AGAINST: this is the nag-diagnostic the bead pre-emptively disclaims ("Not a request for a nag-diagnostic"); duplicates Xray, the shipped and supported dev consumer; needs a suppression knob the moment a test suite exercises refusals deliberately, and that knob is new API surface on a minimal-API project.

(c) Correct #5 to describe what the code does, and say plainly that an untooled dev build needs a listener.
    FOR: no runtime change, no new API, no new noise; honest; the whole edit lands in one file I already own this wave; consistent with "trust the programmer" and with Xray being the answer.
    AGAINST: leaves the ergonomic failure exactly as it is — a typo'd event id in an untooled dev build still produces nothing, and the next finder pays the same four runs. It documents the trap rather than removing it.

My read, offered as input and NOT acted on: (c) is the only option that is certainly correct as far as it goes, because all three stale carriers are wrong under every option and must be fixed regardless — but (c) ALONE does not answer the harm the bead reports. If the ruling is (a) or (b), the spec edit is still needed, just with a different destination sentence. So the carrier sweep above is work the ruling needs in every branch.

=== OPERATIONAL: rf2-j9tl SHOULD BE UNBLOCKED NOW ===

rf2-j9tl was deliberately held until this bead's PR merged, because both want spec/009-Instrumentation.md. There is no PR and no edit to that file from me. The hold has nothing left to wait for — release it. This bead did not touch its two h/boundary complaint descriptions.

WHAT I DID NOT CONCLUDE: which option is right; whether the JVM/SSR lane should behave the same as the browser lane; and whether the :1394 native-SDK-fallback recommendation should be deleted outright or merely qualified.

EXECUTED — the ruling-invariant intersection. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/8012 (branch worker/silence-fu75, worktree silence-fu75). 2026-08-13 05:52:14 AUSEST

No ruling had landed on this bead (comment_count 0; the 2026-08-12 refusal note was the latest text), but the dispatch brief directed implementation, so what shipped is exactly the work the refusal note's costing shows is needed under EVERY one of the three options — nothing that pre-decides between them:

1. spec/009 carrier corrections, all three stale carriers from the sweep, nothing else touched:
   - :1285 channel #5 — now states native machinery observes only throws OUTSIDE the cascade (view code, async callbacks, third-party, caller-observed pure throws); a cascade-captured failure propagates out of neither dispatch nor dispatch-sync and reaches the :errors stream ONLY; and plainly: with no :errors listener attached — and, in dev, no trace consumer such as Xray — a framework-captured failure is invisible: nothing throws, nothing prints.
   - :1327 decision-matrix "What to avoid" — window.onerror sees NOTHING for a cascade failure (was "sees the bare exception").
   - :1394 — "Native-SDK fallback" reframed to "Native-SDK complement — NOT a fallback for cascade failures". QUALIFIED, not deleted: deletion vs qualification was an open sub-question in the refusal note; qualification makes the passage true without a ruling (the native SDK genuinely covers non-cascade throws), so it does not pre-decide.
   - The six docs carriers the sweep classified correct-as-written were re-checked and left standing; git grep confirms no other tracked file quotes the old sentence.

2. Runtime witness: re-frame.on-error-cljs-test/captured-refusal-escapes-no-caller-and-reaches-no-host-channel (started by the prior worker in this worktree, kept on the merits). Two-sided per case — nothing escaped the caller AND the record arrived on :errors — across three refusal classes (throwing handler, :rf.error/effect-map-shape, :rf.error/no-such-handler). Sabotaged in BOTH directions with byte-hash-verified restores: fan-out silenced -> RED at the record-arrival halves (exit 1); chain re-throws -> RED at the no-escape half (exit 1); restored -> exit 0 (47 tests / 189 assertions / 0 failures). The test deliberately does NOT assert that nothing is printed, so a future (a)/(b) runtime addition would not red it.

WHAT REMAINS THE ACTUAL RULING, still open for Mike: whether an untooled dev build should ADDITIONALLY surface refusals to the host — (a) goog.DEBUG-gated js/reportError at the fan-out, or (b) a dev-only default sink. No runtime change shipped. The spec now tells the truth about the trap; it does not remove it — a typo'd event id in an untooled dev build still produces nothing. The refusal note's costing of (a)/(b) stands unchanged. If either is ruled, it is a small follow-up bead against error_emit.cljc, and the corrected #5 sentence is the one to update.

OPERATIONAL: rf2-j9tl merged independently (PR #7991, spec/009:2549-2550) and this branch is rebased past it — no hot-zone conflict. This PR is now the live spec/009 hot-zone holder until merged; sequence any other spec/009 bead behind it.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8012 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): the merged spec correction and two-sided runtime witness are sound; required checks and the focused on-error suite pass. The only remaining scope is explicitly an operator ruling between optional dev surfacing choices (a)/(b). Deferred to 2026-08-20 so bd ready does not dispatch another worker into the already-recorded refusal; reopen sooner on operator direction. No runtime behavior or policy option is changed by this triage.
DELEGATED RULING (operator-authorised delegation, 2026-08-13): an untooled dev build DOES surface framework refusals — via a dev-build, CLJS-only console.error fallback in error_emit.cljc that fires only when the error-listener registry is empty; NOT via reportError, with no new API knob and no JVM/SSR change. Recorded by a decision agent after the reviewed dossier; operator may reverse.

=== RATIONALE, and how the review was weighed ===

The dossier's original recommendation was (a) goog.DEBUG-gated js/reportError at the fan-out. The reviewer (Codex annotation) defeated it on two verified grounds, and I am OVERRIDING (a) on those grounds:

1. reportError dispatches a genuine window "error" event (HTML Standard: reported "in the same fashion as an unhandled exception"). A probe against this checkout's Playwright 1.59.1 / Chromium 147 emitted one pageerror per reportError call. The canonical browser runner, implementation/scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs, deliberately treats console output as diagnostic-only but FAILS an otherwise-green run on any pageerror ("only pageerror is fatal", ~line 182 — re-verified at HEAD). Multiple DOM tests intentionally exercise promoted refusals, so (a) turns expected framework outcomes into runner failures unless each test cancels window "error" — which would weaken the useful invariant that a genuinely uncaught page error fails the browser lane.

2. reportError is semantically false here: a re-frame2 refusal is caught, normalized, and dispatch returns normally. Several categories (notably :rf.error/no-such-handler) carry no exception at all, so (a) would synthesize an Error whose stack points at the reporting site, not the cause. The two in-repo reportError precedents (freehand/root.cljs ~1196 report-globally!; substrate/spine.cljs ~1051 report-recoverable-default!) preserve React's OWN default for uncaught/recoverable React callback errors — a different situation; they are not precedent for a caught-and-normalized refusal, and this ruling does not touch them.

I am also overriding the original dossier's critique of option (b), because the reviewer's narrowing answers each point: the suppression-knob objection dissolves under the empty-registry condition (an app that registered a listener via the existing register-error-listener! API has taken ownership; the fallback self-suppresses; zero new API); the "framework console dialect" objection dissolves by passing the structured record itself as a console argument rather than a flattened formatted string; and the Xray-duplication objection is moot because docs/resources/tutorial/index.md ALREADY promises failures appear in both console and Xray — the console half is currently unimplemented, so this ruling reconciles docs with reality rather than adding a second voice.

Option (0) is rejected: the trap is measured and recurring — rf2-06lp cost four browser runs, rf2-e4y9 cost a full escalate-investigate-exonerate cycle with Mike himself escalating a correct refusal as a P2 fail-silent defect. Silence in the untooled default lane is the opposite of low friction; trust the programmer does not mean test the programmer's faith. This is not the nag-diagnostic shape the bead disclaims: it is one dev-only line per actual captured failure that would otherwise reach ZERO channels, statically eliminated from production, self-suppressing the moment the app takes ownership.

=== IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF ===

WHAT: a private, CLJS-only, dev-gated (goog.DEBUG / interop debug-enabled?, statically eliminable) console.error fallback in implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc.

WHERE (verified at HEAD): the listener registry is the private `listeners` atom (~line 65); "empty registry" means no registered error listeners. There are TWO fan-out sites, not one chokepoint — dispatch-on-error! (~line 268, event-centric always-on path) AND dispatch-error-record* (~line 664, union-record path). Invoke the fallback exactly once per fully built record, at both sites, under the same continuation/ownership conditions as publication, only when the registry is empty. Do NOT place it in the shared generic substrate (emit_substrate.cljc serves non-error events too) and do NOT install it as a registry member (that would change empty-registry semantics and listener ordering).

BEHAVIOUR:
- Stable prefix (e.g. "[re-frame2]") + the complete structured error-record map passed as a SEPARATE console argument; retain the original :exception object as its own argument when present (preserves real stacks). No flattened string, no synthesized exception, no reportError, no rethrow.
- Check console.error is callable; wrap the diagnostic in try/catch so observability can never abort the drain (the drain must not abort — router.cljc ~1000).
- The outer debug gate must be statically eliminable; the closure-defines mechanism is not proof by itself — acceptance inspects the advanced goog.DEBUG=false artifact for ABSENCE of the stable prefix and the fallback call path.
- No suppression knob. If genuine knob demand ever materialises from a consumer, that is a new, evidenced decision — do not pre-build it.

SAME PR (hot zone): spec/009-Instrumentation.md is HOT ZONE, sequential — sequence behind any live spec/009 holder. Update the corrected channel #5 sentence at ~line 1285 with the precise rule: the always-on structured listener remains the production contract; an unowned promoted error additionally gets a browser-console diagnostic in development. The 1327/1394 corrections from PR #8012 stand unchanged. TRAP: "#5" is ambiguous in spec/009 — "Native browser machinery" is #5 in the "What IS available in production" list (error-emit is #2 there), but the later decision matrix's #5 is the Performance API; do not assume the number. Also verify docs/resources/tutorial/index.md's console+Xray promise now holds as written.

ACCEPTANCE (from the review, symbols verified against this checkout):
1. Browser test: stub console.error AND reportError, leave the registry empty, exercise the three refusal classes (throwing handler, :rf.error/effect-map-shape, :rf.error/no-such-handler) — exactly one structured console diagnostic each, zero reportError calls, zero pageerrors, dispatch returns normally.
2. With a registered listener: the listener receives the same record exactly once and the fallback is suppressed; existing trace/Xray emission and frame-sink routing remain exactly-once and unchanged.
3. At least one non-event union record proves dispatch-error-record* follows the same fallback rule.
4. The canonical browser runner stays green on expected refusals while retaining fatal treatment of genuinely uncaught pageerrors.
5. The focused suite re-frame.on-error-cljs-test (47 tests / 189 assertions at HEAD) stays green AND quiet on the JVM; the advanced goog.DEBUG=false build contains neither the prefix nor the fallback path; production listeners still receive their records.

TEST EXPECTATION, stated so nobody re-litigates it: the #8012 witness (captured-refusal-escapes-no-caller-and-reaches-no-host-channel) deliberately does NOT assert that nothing is printed — this runtime addition must not red it, and by design it will not.

=== PRESERVED INSIGHTS (from dossier + review, so they are not lost) ===
- emit_substrate.cljc's fan-out short-circuits to nil on an empty registry (one deref + empty? check), so the fallback's empty-registry test is hot-path cheap and mirrors an existing pattern.
- Xray visibility rides the separate dev-only TRACE axis (router.cljc ~1142 forwards to trace/emit-error!; tools/xray install.cljs registers a trace collector) — so the silence only ever bit UNTOOLED dev builds, exactly rf2-06lp's lane. The fallback may duplicate an Xray row; the tutorial frames console+Xray as complementary — accept the duplication.
- Dev-noise cost is bounded: a browser test that intentionally triggers refusals without a listener sees console noise only (runner records console without failing); a test needing exact control installs the same listener it uses to assert the record.
- JVM/SSR lane stays listener-only by design: that lane is REPL/test code where the caller observes the dispatch directly and a listener is one line; both measured costs were in browser lanes; a JVM print is where it is least needed and most polluting.
- The freehand/spine reportError call sites remain correct for THEIR case; nothing here touches them.

STATUS: un-deferring to open — the ruling makes this dispatchable as one small bead (error_emit.cljc + spec/009 sentence + tests, single PR).
