=== RATIONALE ===

The ratification dossier and its independent Codex review CONVERGED on RATIFY, each after re-verifying the two load-bearing facts on this checkout: (1) run-browser-tests.cjs lines 180-183 states and implements "only pageerror is fatal" (console output diagnostic-only, rf2-mwx08), and a probe on Playwright 1.59.1 / Chromium 147 confirmed console.error(prefix, record, exception) emits one console event and ZERO pageerrors while reportError emits one pageerror per call — so (b) is safe in the canonical browser lane and (a) is not; (2) error_emit.cljc has no sink at HEAD (last touched 259ed51382, 2026-07-21, before the bead was filed; the #8012 landing changed only the witness b1d73d6f86 and spec a93936c75b) — the ruling's premises have not drifted. Reversal to (a) would need new evidence against a measured result and is semantically false (refusals are caught and normalized; :rf.error/no-such-handler carries no exception, so (a) would synthesize a stack pointing at the reporting site). Standards backing, for the record: HTML Standard defines reportError as reporting "in the same fashion as an unhandled exception"; Console Standard defines console.error as an error-level log over a list of arguments. Reversal to (0) re-arms a trap with two measured recurring costs (rf2-06lp: four browser runs; rf2-e4y9: a full escalate-investigate-exonerate cycle) and leaves the tutorial's console-and-Xray promise (docs/resources/tutorial/index.md:252) false. No reviewer point was overridden; the review's refinements are adopted below.

=== BINDING REFINEMENTS (adopted from the Codex review; amend the cycle-1 implementation brief accordingly) ===

1. HOST BOUNDARY (the one substantive narrowing): this is a browser-development fallback, NOT a generic CLJS print. A bare #?(:cljs ...) is too broad — Node-targeted CLJS and CLJS SSR also have a console and must remain listener-only, by the same rationale the ruling already applies to the JVM lane (caller observes the dispatch directly; a listener is one line; neither measured incident occurred there). Gate = debug-enabled?/goog.DEBUG (statically eliminable) AND a browser-host check AND callable console.error, all in one private helper in error_emit.cljc. Acceptance adds: Node-targeted CLJS lanes stay quiet.
2. OWNERSHIP RULE IN THE SPEC SENTENCE: registering ANY :errors listener takes corpus-wide ownership — the fallback stays quiet even if that listener ignores categories or itself throws. This implicit-ownership subtlety was the steelman's strongest point; the spec/009 sentence in the same PR must state it in one clear sentence. Conversely Xray and frame-owned sinks do NOT populate this registry (Xray rides the trace stream), so the console line may coexist with an Xray row — the tutorial already frames those as complementary; accept the duplication.
3. ACCEPTANCE MECHANICS: assert console.error CALL ARGUMENTS (record identity, original exception identity), never rendered console text — console presentation is implementation-defined. Add the resume case: with one listener the fallback is suppressed; after unregistering it, the next record uses the fallback. Keep the genuine-pageerror control red.
4. ACKNOWLEDGED CONSEQUENCE, NO MACHINERY: the record's raw :exception (the intentional advanced-listener contract; :event already past the elision boundary) now also reaches a local dev console. Acceptable for a local dev diagnostic. Per-category ownership, sink discovery, a formatter, deduplication, a suppression setting, and JVM parity all remain REJECTED as premature.

API NAMING, so the implementer does not chase a ghost: the public off-switch is (rf/register-listener! :errors id f) (core.cljc ~2325), which routes to the internal error-emit/register-error-listener! — the cycle-1 note's "register-error-listener!" and the review's "rf/register-listener! :errors" are the same switch at two layers. Measured while building rf2-hic-051's forms recipes.

## What happens

`[:rf.mutation/execute {:mutation :m/unregistered :params {...} :instance :i :reply-to [...]}]` mints NO instance, issues NO request, settles nothing, and reports nothing at all. The passive read `[:rf/mutation {:instance :i}]` answers the idle empty-state map afterwards -- byte-identical to what it answers before any write has ever run:

    {:settled? false :status :idle :result nil :optimistic? false
     :error nil :pending? false :error? false :affected-keys nil :success? false}

No console error, no thrown ex-info, no trace-visible warning.

## How it was found, and why the silence costs

In the `:browser-test` build a witness application's `reg-mutation`, performed at ns-load, was gone by the time a row ran (the reset fixture restores a registrar baseline and the resources artefact's own per-test reset clears the mutation kind). Every symptom pointed at the TRANSPORT: the form submitted, the gate passed, the handler ran, `:attempted?` was set -- and the `:rf.http/managed` recorder stayed empty. Four browser-lane runs were spent proving in turn that it was not the `:fx [[:dispatch ...]]` turn, not the mounted facade's frame, and not `with-new-frame`, before reading `rf/mutation-meta` showed `false`. Re-registering inside the row made the same execute work on the next line.

The same lane in `:node-test` was green throughout, which is what made it look like a build difference rather than a registration one.

## The ask

`:rf.mutation/execute` should FAIL LOUD on an unregistered mutation id -- the artefact's own `ex-info` with a canonical `:rf.error/id`, naming the mutation id, in the shape `reg-mutation`'s own fail-closed registration boundary already uses (`:rf.error/mutation-bad-spec`). A write the runtime cannot perform is not the same fact as a write nobody has asked for, and today the read cannot tell them apart.

Check the resource read path for the same hole before deciding the shape.

## Where it was met

implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/forms/events.cljs (register-save!) documents the workaround the witness uses.
close_reason:
PR #7975 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7975).

PREMISE DID NOT HOLD, and the verified non-holding is the deliverable. :rf.mutation/execute already refuses an unregistered mutation id, in exactly the shape this bead asked for: mreg/require-mutation-spec! is the FIRST statement of execute-handler (mutation_events.cljc:1182) and throws :rf.error/mutation-not-registered naming the id, with :recovery :fix-registration, catalogued at spec/009:2079. The event ABORTS -- which is why there is no instance and no request. require-resource-spec! is the symmetric twin on the read path (this bead asked me to check it): four :rf.resource/* handlers, the route integration, the sub. No hole there either.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN was the gate. execute-unregistered-is-loud asserted only (nil? @last-managed-args) -- a claim a SILENT NO-OP satisfies exactly as well as a refusal does. Proven, not argued: sabotaging execute-handler into the bead's exact feared behaviour (early {} return -- no instance, no request, ERROR-RECORDS => [], stdout and stderr empty) left that test GREEN at EXIT=0. The replacement goes red at EXIT=1 with 7 failures + 1 error, and the assertions that survive the sabotage are precisely the old test's whole content.

Both directions proven. Sabotage B widened the guard from the :mutation registrar KIND to 'any known id' (correct shape, wrong identity): a registered :m/save then raised a spurious refusal, AND :r/article sailed through so the runtime lowered a resource's GET as a mutation write under a :pending instance row. Both new tests red. Sources restored and verified by hashing the bytes (mutation_events.cljc = c30ec6e6...); NO runtime source is changed by the PR.

GRANULARITY LINE vs rf2-04tx: same law, drawn strictly EARLIER. rf2-04tx refuses at the router's final-effects boundary because a malformed effect map is only knowable after the handler ran; a mutation id is knowable on line one, and waiting is worse -- a refusal after mint would leave a DURABLE instance stuck at :pending with no request behind it. Deliberately NOT extended to mint an :error instance: that would make a source defect look like a runtime failure of a real mutation, and the repo's own precedent one registrar up (:rf.error/no-such-handler for an unregistered EVENT id) mints no record either. No new mechanism, no new id, no catalogue row, no spec change, no public export, no hot-zone file.

Gates (captured): resources JVM clojure -M:test EXIT=0 (814 tests / 7252 assertions); npm run test:cljs EXIT=0 (13525 / 68199); scripts/test-fast-pr.sh EXIT=0 (PASS fast PR spine).

FOLLOW-UPS FILED, not fixed here:
- rf2-fu75 (P2, core + spec/009, HOT ZONE -- stopped and reported): the silence the finder met is framework-wide, not mutation-specific. Four controls, stdout and stderr bound, all with EMPTY stdout/stderr: unregistered mutation id, a plain throwing handler, rf2-04tx's own effect-map refusal, and an unregistered EVENT id. re-frame2 ships no default console sink, and spec/009 §Observability channels #5's claim that a throwing handler 'still surfaces' at window.onerror is contradicted by router.cljc:1004 -- the chain CAPTURES rather than re-throws, so nothing escapes dispatch or dispatch-sync. That, not a missing guard, is what cost this bead's finder four browser runs.
- rf2-w67y (P3): nothing in the corpus asserts :rf.error/resource-not-registered -- the read-path twin, same hollow-gate shape, different suite file.

title: hic — the error region is exported as h/boundary and documented as h/error-boundary
description:
The Hicasso error-region surface is exported as `h/boundary`, and almost every
document that names it calls it `h/error-boundary`. One of the two is wrong and
a worker cannot decide which, so rf2-hic-041 left both sides alone and filed
this.

## What is at source

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc` exports `boundary`:

    (def ^{:doc "`h/boundary` — the runtime's own error boundary
      (HD-020(c)); takes `:fallback`, `:reset-key` and `:on-error`. …"}
      boundary impl-boundary/boundary)

There is no `error-boundary` var anywhere under
`implementation/hicasso/src/`. Code written from the guide does not compile.

## Where the other spelling is

`h/error-boundary` appears in:

- `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/17-errors.md` (5 occurrences, including the
  chapter's opening example)
- `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/21-code-splitting.md` (3)
- `docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/18-ssr-and-hydration.md`, `glossary.md`
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/`: `dispositions.md` (HS-09 row),
  `invariants.md`, `specification.md` §5, `naming-ledger.md`,
  `lanes/ergonomics-api.md`, `lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md`

`naming-ledger.md` row 12 reads `| 12 | h/error-boundary | keep | keep | open |`
— so the ledger, which is the normative naming record, rules for the spelling
the code does not have. That is why this is a decision and not a typo sweep:
either the export is renamed to match the ledger, or the ledger and eleven
documents are corrected to `h/boundary`.

## What rf2-hic-041 did and did not do

It repaired the ONE implementation-internal occurrence — `n/lazy`'s docstring in
`native.cljc` said `h/error-boundary`, which made `native.cljc` disagree with
`codec.cljs` and `hicasso.cljc` — and left every document alone. The published
snapshots under `docs/design/hicasso/product/` are not a worker's to edit, and
the draft guide has live authoring worktrees.

## Bounded repair

Rule the name, then make one pass. If `h/boundary` wins, the ledger row and the
eleven documents change and the export stands. If `h/error-boundary` wins, the
export is renamed (pre-alpha, no shim) and the two implementation comments
follow it.
notes: OPERATOR RULING (Mike, in session, 2026-08-12 17:18 AUSEST) — OPTION 1: RENAME THE EXPORT TO h/error-boundary. The naming ledger (row 12, 'keep h/error-boundary') and the eleven documents stand as written; the code moves to match. Pre-alpha, no shim, no alias: rename the hicasso.cljc export (impl-boundary/boundary binding) to error-boundary and follow with the two implementation comments rf2-hic-041 identified. Rationale recorded: 'error boundary' is the React term of art and h/boundary is under-specified against Suspense boundaries; the ledger wins by default; smallest blast radius vs an eleven-doc sweep colliding with live guide worktrees. Ordinary worker work — dispatchable now. Ruling recorded by the session agent at Mike's direction.
close_reason: PR #7973 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7973. Operator ruling implemented: the export re-frame.hicasso/boundary is renamed to error-boundary, pre-alpha with no alias and no shim. The naming ledger row 12 and the documents stand unedited and are now correct — verified, ten of them (not eleven; the bead's own bullet list also enumerates ten), 18 hits, every guide code example's props matching the class's closed roster #{:fallback :reset-key :on-error :children}. Swept 60 base h/boundary hits: 26 changed (all under implementation/hicasso/ — the export, the five call sites, the two implementation comments rf2-hic-041 named in native.cljc and impl/codec.cljs, the two user-facing refusal MESSAGE strings that named a var a caller can no longer type, and the package's own test prose); 34 left with named discriminators (published product/ snapshots under a digest-pinned refresh contract, dated design records under decisions/studio/validation, the measured frozen bench donor tree, a verbatim HD-020(c) quotation kept intact and annotated in place, 10 hh/boundary-slug false positives in tools/xray, and 2 hot-zone hits in spec/009). The impl module keeps its short name deliberately — impl.boundary/boundary is what the stable :rf.error/hicasso-boundary-* ids and their Spec 009 rows are named after, so renaming it would move a diagnostic id for a spelling. Both directions proven: the new spelling drives five live DOM/L2 assertions; the old one raises 'Use of undeclared Var re-frame.hicasso/boundary' (captured), and the full 1223-file browser compile raised zero undeclared-var warnings. Gates all exit 0: test:hicasso-invariants, test:cljs (13523 tests / 68184 assertions), test:browser (1349 tests / 8320 assertions, 0 failures), build:hicasso-release (0 warnings, erasure + bundle isolation). Nothing wanted a shim. FOLLOW-UP for the mayor: spec/009-Instrumentation.md lines 2549-2550 still say h/boundary in two complaint descriptions (hot zone, fenced for this worker; no gate reds because register-to-Spec-009 binding is by id, not prose), and the published product/ snapshots owe a republication.

title: cljs.test: a closure that closes over done finishes the row — 32 chains outside freehand
description:
THE THIRD CLASS, found by rf2-o0n1's reproduction control and closed inside implementation/freehand by PR for rf2-o0n1. This bead is the REMAINDER, outside freehand.

THE SIGNATURE GAP. rf2-fyba's scanner sees a literal (done) in a chain step. rf2-29ua's sees a helper that TAKES done as a parameter. NEITHER sees a let/letfn-bound closure that CLOSES OVER the row's done:

    (let [finish (fn [] (restore) (teardown! container root) (done))]
      (-> p (.then (fn [_] ... (finish)))
            (.catch (fn [e] (is false ...) (finish)))))

Same defect exactly: the .catch sits downstream of a step that FINISHED the row, so it claims whatever a later namespace throws, prints it against this row's label, and fires done a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay and re-running the offending namespace. run-browser-tests.cjs promotes 'Async test called done more than one time' to a FATAL match (since #7190), so each of these can red the browser lane.

MEASURED, with a closure-aware s-expression reader (top-level defns taking done; letfn bindings; let-bound fns; plus cross-ns run-async/each-mode): 37 chains in 12 files repo-wide. 5 in 2 files were freehand's and are repaired under rf2-o0n1. THE REMAINING 32, in 10 files:

  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/form_3_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs            4  (done!)
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/frame_provider_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs      4  (done! / finish / teardown-and-done!)
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/views_synthetic_event_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs 1  (finalize!)
  implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_strict_mode_dom_cljs_test.cljs        1  (done!)
  implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_synthetic_event_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs 1  (finalize!)
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs                   9  (fail-and-finish!)
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_hooks_dom_cljs_test.cljs                 8  (fail-and-finish!)
  implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machine_view_unmount_teardown_mounted_dom_cljs_test.cljs 2  (done!)
  tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/port_to_build_test.cljs                     1  (.finally after done)
  tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/a11y_stale_settlement_cljs_test.cljs                      1

NOTE the two hicasso native_* files are ALSO the only two the LITERAL signature still sees (17 chains) — they are the same rows counted twice, not 17 + 17. Repairing them once closes both censuses.

THE CURE, unchanged: the rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the step that finishes. Rename the closure so its name stops promising to finish (teardown-clean! / release / report-failure!), drop the (done) from it, return nil, and put exactly one (done) at the tail with nothing after it. Do NOT hoist teardown mechanically — across six batches the split ran roughly half hoisted, half left in place, and the dominant reason to leave it is the failure arm doing LESS.

PROVE IT with the campaign's reproduction control: a throwaway ns sorting as a PREFIX EXTENSION of the target, carrying a fn-form :each fixture plus an async row, which makes cljs.test throw a bare String synchronously inside whichever done continuation is running. Reverted it reproduces the misattribution and the double-done; repaired, the throw escapes attributed to nobody. rf2-o0n1's PR carries a three-run gradient (2 claims -> 1 -> 0) as the worked example.

GATES: npm run test:browser decides the -dom-cljs-test files; tools/story and the MCP tool have their own lanes.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7974 (merged 2026-08-12T08:12:36Z; completeness/correctness/implementation quality) — REOPENED. The done-continuation reordering is correct, but the teardown disposition for the native mount-live! rows is based on caller visibility rather than ownership. In both native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs and native_hooks_dom_cljs_test.cljs, mount-live! synchronously creates container + handle, then returns a wait-until! promise; a timeout/false result throws after the root exists. The caller catch receives no handle, reports, and reaches trailing done, leaving that internally owned root live. The native-ABI two-frame row has the same partial-success shape one level higher: if alpha resolves and beta rejects, alpha is in the inner closure but the outer catch cannot release it. Repair at the ownership boundary: make mount-live! release its created handle on any pre-delivery failure (then rethrow for the row diagnostic), and ensure the two-frame composition releases alpha when beta cannot be delivered. Add deliberate wait rejection/timeout controls and prove the following row sees no root/runtime residue. Keep the landed positional done fix and its census intact.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED by the mayor 2026-08-12 (revert wave 3 — this bead has now reverted twice). LANDED AS PR #7974. THE COUNT HELD — 32 chains in 10 files, file for file, the first bead in this family whose census was right, and its scanner reproduces ALL FOUR published campaign landmarks exactly. It first had to fix two bugs in its OWN scanner: treating ' as a symbol terminator split db' and SILENTLY SKIPPED 106 FILES, and it did not descend into defn-hosted chains. CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S TEXT: the two hicasso/native_* files are NOT the only two the literal signature sees — it sees 19 chains in 4 files — but 'the 17 are one set, not two' HOLDS and is stronger than stated, because the closure signature SUBSUMES the literal one. So 32 = 19 literal-class + 13 genuinely closure-only. TWO SECOND-ORDER DEFECTS: two rows returned a bare js/setTimeout — a NUMBER — from a chain step, settling the chain so assertions ran off the end of it (a throw there hung the lane with no diagnostic); and port_to_build called (done), then .finally, then (done) again — an unconditional double-done on EVERY green pass, while on rejection .finally re-throws so NEITHER fired, and it had no .catch at all. THE ESCAPING CLAIM LANDED NOWHERE: all three censuses read ZERO repo-wide across implementation/, tools/, examples/ and testbeds/.

title: Route-path census is blind to the app trees under implementation/ (two holes)
description:
rf2-wqnl's route-path census (implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_path_census_test.clj) has two blind spots, and TOGETHER they hide the exact application whose collision motivated it.

HOLE 1 - the tree roster. `app-roots` is ["examples" "testbeds"], repo-relative. The Hicasso witness applications live under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ (slice, todo, and now navigation, rf2-hic-042). They load into the SAME shared node bundle (`hicasso/test` is a :node-test source path), so their paths are just as process-global as an examples/ app's - and none of them is censused.

HOLE 2 - the column-1 filter. Those applications register through a `(register!)` FUNCTION called at column 1, because re-frame.test-support's reset fixture rolls back a registration made before the fixture snapshot. The `reg-route` forms therefore sit INDENTED inside a defn, and `top-level-reg-route` (#\"(?m)^\((?:[^...]+/)?reg-route\s\") cannot see them. So even adding implementation/hicasso/test to `app-roots` would census nothing.

EVIDENCE: rf2-hic-042 added implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/navigation/routes.cljs registering "/navigation" and "/navigation/article/:slug" at namespace load. `cd implementation/routing && clojure -M:test` ran 522 tests / 3086 assertions before AND after - an identical count, i.e. zero new claims seen. The prefix was verified BY HAND instead.

The slice's own routes.cljs docstring is the irony: it is the app that broke twelve RealWorld assertions, and the census cannot see it.

REMEDY (a suggestion, not a ruling): widen `app-roots` to include implementation/hicasso/test, and widen the claim scanner to see a reg-route indented inside a top-level defn that is CALLED at column 1. The second half is the harder one and may want a different instrument (e.g. reading the analyzer, as examples/require_graph.clj does) rather than a wider regex. Note the allowlist would then have to absorb nothing - slice, todo and navigation are all already prefixed.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7972 (merged 2026-08-12T07:45:53Z; completeness/correctness/implementation quality) — REOPENED. The replacement correctly reaches the three existing Hicasso apps, but its structural claim still has two compact blind directions. (1) load-time-forms descends through quote, so a data sample such as (def example (quote (routing/reg-route :demo/x {} "/x"))) is counted as an executed registration even though the form is inert; syntax-quoted examples need the same control. (2) it deliberately skips fn/fn* bodies and follows only defn/defn-, so (def register! (fn [] (routing/reg-route ...))) followed by a top-level (register!) is silently missed, even though it is the same namespace-load-time registration shape the gate exists to catch. The suite currently proves the def-bound function is ignored only when uncalled. Teach the walk quote as inert and either follow a called def-bound function to the existing fixpoint or report it unresolved; add positive controls for quoted inert data and a called def/fn registration. Keep the scope to source-classification; the app-root/defn/id repairs themselves stand.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED by the mayor 2026-08-12 (revert wave 3). LANDED AS PR #7972. The route-path census could not see the apps whose collision motivated it. THREE HOLES, NOT THE TWO THE BEAD NAMED — and the third would have defeated the obvious fix: even at column 1 the reader SILENTLY DROPPED ANY CLAIM WHOSE ID WAS NOT A KEYWORD LITERAL, and all three witness apps write the id as a def'd symbol, so the bead's suggested 'widen the regex' remedy would ALSO have measured 39 -> 39 and looked like a working fix. Proved layer by layer: widening app-roots alone took 101 files to 231 and left claims at 39. THE DESIGN ATTACKS THE DECLARED FAILURE MODE: clojure.tools.reader at :features #{:cljs} replaces the regex+edn pair; load-time reachability is answered STRUCTURALLY — never descend into a function body, follow a defn only when load-time code mentions its name, TO A FIXPOINT so one indirection cannot hide a registration; and A REACHED reg-route WHOSE ID OR PATH IS NOT A RESOLVABLE LITERAL IS REPORTED, NEVER SKIPPED. Planted collision named BOTH claimants with file and line, through the register! function. Claims 39 -> 45; routing lane 522/3086 -> 523/3105. Both allowlist entries verified LOAD-BEARING and neither needed changing. It also flagged rather than assumed: one clause in TESTING.md became false on landing, offered as a standalone commit.

title: cljs.test: 40 HELPER-FORCED promise chains the rf2-fyba scanner signature cannot see (freehand 184 -> 224)
description:
FILES — 40 chains the rf2-fyba campaign's scanner signature CANNOT SEE, in four
implementation/freehand files named in NO bead:

  freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/typeahead_witness_dom_cljs_test.cljs   12
  freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/virtual_collection_dom_cljs_test.cljs  11
  freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/splitter_dom_cljs_test.cljs             9
  freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/controls_kit_dom_cljs_test.cljs         8

THE BLIND SPOT. rf2-fyba's stated signature flags "a step whose body contains
(done), followed by a .catch step". These four files route BOTH arms through
local helpers, so no chain step contains a literal (done) anywhere:

  (defn- finish! [container root done]
    (ms/destroy-root! container root)
    (ms/residue-clean! "FH-CTRL-018 — after teardown")
    (done))

  (defn- fail-and-finish! [container root done]
    (fn [e]
      (is false (str "the browser step rejected: " e))
      (ms/destroy-root! container root)
      (done)))

  (-> (render! root plain-field)
      (.then (fn [_] … (finish! container root done)))
      (.catch (fail-and-finish! container root done)))

The .catch IS downstream of a step that finishes, so the chain exhibits the full
signature — foreign claim, double done, namespace re-run. The scanner reports
these four files as ZERO.

THIS IS THE THIRD BLIND SPOT, and the first two are already recorded: rf2-53uz
found (1) nested steps splitting a chain under strict equal-indent grouping
(freehand 179 → 184) and (2) `(done)` living in the `->` head expression
(pair-MCP only). This is (3), and it is the largest: freehand 184 → **224**.

NOT SPECULATION — REPRODUCED IN THE BROWSER. Under rf2-d2xz's reproduction
control (a throwaway ns sorting as a prefix extension of the target, fn-form
:each fixture + async row, rethrowing a bare String inside the running `done`
continuation), with rf2-d2xz's five files REPAIRED, `npm run test:browser`
still printed:

  Testing re-frame.freehand.substrate-dom-cljs-test-zz-control-dom-cljs-test
  FAIL in (a-row-that-needs-async) (:)
  the browser step rejected: Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps.
  WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.

`the browser step rejected: ` is `fail-and-finish!`'s own message — one of these
four files claiming a foreign namespace's throw as its own row's failure. With
the same five files REVERTED the same run printed THREE such claims and announced
the control namespace THREE times; repaired, it is down to this ONE, and this one
comes from here.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE CAMPAIGN. rf2-o0n1 (4 of 4) says "take every
implementation/freehand hit NOT claimed by parts 1-3" — but it derives that set
from the same signature, so a worker following it lands on 0 for these files and
the 40 are missed by the whole four-part split. `git grep` for the file names
across the tracker returns nothing: they are named in no bead at all.

THE CURE is the one the campaign has landed four times, plus the helper rename
#7942 used for the three Hicasso `fail-and-finish!` helpers and #7951 used for
`exact_render_capture`'s `unexpected!`: rename `fail-and-finish!` to
`report-failure!`, DROP the `done` parameter, return nil. `finish!` keeps `done`
and becomes the single trailing step. Per chain:

  (-> (render! root plain-field)
      (.then (fn [_] … ))
      (.catch (report-failure! ))
      (.then (fn [_] (finish! container root done))))

Note `finish!` already carries the shared teardown (`ms/destroy-root!`) that
`fail-and-finish!` duplicates — so hoisting is the natural shape here rather
than a judgement call. But `finish!` ALSO calls `ms/residue-clean!`, which
`fail-and-finish!` deliberately does NOT ("a second failure attributed to the
leak rule would bury the one that actually happened"). That asymmetry is
load-bearing and MUST survive: the trailing step cannot simply call `finish!`
on both paths without changing what a failing row reports. Read the two arms
before writing the trailing step.

GATE: `npm run test:browser` from `implementation/` — all four are
`-dom-cljs-test` suites. It sits at 1293 tests / 8010 assertions on main as of
2026-08-12 (NOT the 8008 several beads still quote — that figure is from #7951
and two assertions have landed since). No deftest is added or removed, so a
moved count is a mistake.

REBUILD THE SCANNER with all three corrections. Signature: steps matching
^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, chains kept on a STACK so a nested step does
not split its parent; a step counts as finishing if its body contains `(done)`
OR calls a local `defn`/`defn-` that takes a `done` parameter and calls it; and
check the `->` head expression too. Beware `\b` in the helper-name regex —
Clojure names end in `!`/`?`/`*`, which are non-word characters, so `\b` never
matches after them and the whole class silently reports zero. That is exactly
how these 40 went missing.

PROVE IT with rf2-fyba's reproduction control, both directions, and delete the
control verifying the restore BY HASHING THE BYTES.
close_reason: Repaired in PR #7964 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7964), branch worker/helper-29ua. All 40 helper-forced chains in the four files repaired: finish! -> teardown-clean! (drops done, success arm only), fail-and-finish! -> report-failure! (drops done, returns nil), one done at the tail. The ms/residue-clean! success-only asymmetry preserved in all four; teardown deliberately NOT hoisted. 16 nested catches absorbed by their parents. Census reproduced exactly at source (12/11/9/8) by an independent s-expression reader, calibrated against 184 blind / 224 helper-aware on the pre-repair tree. Post-repair the four scan to ZERO and freehand drops 140 -> 100. Control both directions: reverted = 3 foreign claims + control ns announced 3x + double-done, exit 1; repaired = 0 claims, announced once, throw escapes. Restore hash-verified. Browser gate 1293/8010 0F0E before and after, captured exit 0.

title: hic-033 follow-up — the direct-return delta's CLOCK half, on a pinned quiet window
description:
# The clock half of the direct-return delta

`rf2-hic-033` delivered Rung 3's contract and the DETERMINISTIC half of the
direct-return delta (budgets.md D10-D13: entries into `codec/vec->element`,
`codec/convert-props`, `intent/lower-prop`, `controlled/install!`, each read
against the crossing's own floor, with a one-line control that moves all four).

It did NOT take the clock. Spec §6's bounded experiment set asks for a pinned
interleaved run on BOTH named reference profiles, published with witness,
instrument and confidence. The machine available to hic-033 was carrying three
concurrent compiles, which is not a window a duration can be attributed in, so
the worker stopped rather than publish a number it could not attribute.

## What this bead owes

NO BAND-NARROWING RE-RUN. Under site-level adjudication nothing hinges on whether the corpus-wide recovery is 18% or 26%; per-site decisions turn on site size and the semantic trade (a direct return gives up intent lowering, controlled repair, and the L2 assertion tier - already on the record in D10-D13's note). title: cljs.test: 54 promise chains in the freehand long tail catch downstream of their own done (4 of 4)
description:
FILES (4 of 4) — 54 chains across the 24 files carrying 3 or fewer. Rebuild the scanner
and take every implementation/freehand hit NOT claimed by parts 1-3. Includes
root_preflight_dom, presence_nil_key_dom, ownership_motion_dom, host_mounted_dom,
controlled_input_matrix_dom, buffered_controller_dom, bench/hicasso/ssr/spike (3 each);
root_teardown_dom, projection_roster_dom, presence_dom, presence_commit_ownership_dom,
ownership_radix_dom, ownership_maps_dom, compiled_keyed_run_dom, bench/hicasso/ssr/spike_dom,
bench/hicasso/ssr/instance_key_payload_dom (2 each); and 15 files at 1.
NOTE: compiled_keyed_run_dom and ownership_maps_dom were PARTIALLY repaired by #7942 (one
chain each) — the repaired chains are the model, the others are the work.

implementation/freehand carries 179 of rf2-fyba's 248 remaining chains across 46 files —
too many for one dispatch, which rf2-fyba says explicitly. Split into four by file, roughly
equal, heaviest first. The four are PARALLEL-SAFE with each other: disjoint file sets, all
under implementation/freehand/test/, no shared file. rf2-fyba's own comment carries the full
derivation and the count reconciliation.

MOUNT_SUPPORT IS ALREADY CORRECT — DO NOT RE-REPAIR IT. #7942 fixed `each-mode` and
`run-async` in implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/mount_support.cljs, and their
docstrings now state the rule. Chains that already route through those helpers are fine.
Equally, DO NOT convert these chains TO `run-async` to avoid the work — measured under
rf2-fyba, its handler reports the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", so wholesale
adoption would replace every row's own diagnostic with one string, and only 51 of the 179
sit in files that even `:require` mount-support today.

`ms/destroy-root!` IS THE TEARDOWN TO WATCH. rf2-fyba's counter-example lives in this tree —
behaviors_dom_cljs_test.cljs:179 calls `(ms/destroy-root! container root)` on BOTH arms, so a
naive swap destroys the root twice. Hoist it into the single trailing step (written once, run
once per path); do not leave it on both sides of a swapped chain.

GATE: `npm run test:browser` from implementation/ — every one of these is a -dom-cljs-test
suite, so the browser lane is the one that decides. It sits at 1293 tests / 8008 assertions;
a moved count is evidence and must be explained. Run `npm run test:freehand` too (these files
are in the :node-test-freehand build). The bench/hicasso/* files are NOT in the browser-test
build (its ns-regexp excludes ^re-frame\.freehand\.bench\.) — check which lane covers each
before claiming it green.

THE DEFECT (established rf2-d3tc, generalised rf2-qpns/#7942, re-proved under rf2-fyba).
cljs.test/run-block hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously. A .catch downstream of a step that calls `done` claims whatever a later
namespace throws as this row's failure, prints it against this row's label, and calls
`done` a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay, RE-RUNNING the offending
namespace, and stalling the lane with no summary line at all.

THE CURE. The rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the .then that calls `done`: it reports
and returns nil but NEVER finishes. Exactly one `done` sits at the tail with nothing after
it. Worked example, and the reasoning, now live in the docstring of
`re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc).

THIS IS NOT A MECHANICAL SWAP — that is the whole reason rf2-qpns did not do it.
Where the two arms do the SAME thing (an idempotent `restore`, a `destroy-frame!`, an
`unmount!`), hoist it into the single trailing step: written once, still run once per path.
Where they DIFFER, leave it. Two real examples from the repaired trees: a defensive
`(try (.unmount root) (catch ...))` that is failure-only because the success path already
unmounted upstream, and a `force-release!` that is failure-only because the success path
asserts the orderly `uninstall!` — hoisting either would have changed behaviour.

TWO SHAPES TO EXPECT (both hit in the repaired trees):
- THE .catch THAT IS THE ROW'S SUCCESS PATH — the row asserts the promise REJECTS, so
  `(is false "must reject")` sits in the .then and the real assertions in the .catch. Make
  the two handlers SIBLINGS of one TWO-ARG .then, then one trailing `done`. This is still
  an instance: the fulfilment arm calls `done` with the .catch downstream of it.
- HELPER-FORCED SHAPES — a local `(defn- unexpected! [done label e] ... (done))` takes
  `done` and calls it, so no caller can be repaired without it. Rename to `report-failure!`,
  drop the parameter, return nil (what #7942 did for the Hicasso `fail-and-finish!` helpers).

DO NOT adopt mount_support's `run-async` wholesale to avoid the work. Its handler reports
the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", which would REPLACE every row's own
diagnostic with one string. Measured under rf2-fyba: only 51 of freehand's 179 even
`:require` mount-support today. `run-async` stays right for NEW matrix cells.

DO NOT retune any suite to dodge the async window (the rf2-hic-029 refusal stands), do not
weaken assertions, and do not drop teardown to make a swap typecheck.

REBUILD THE SCANNER, do not trust line numbers (they drift). Signature: steps matching
^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, grouped into chains by equal indent with no intervening
lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains (done) is followed by a
.catch step. Strip ;; comments first. The count is an UPPER BOUND — every chain needs
reading, and a source-located "left correct" is a fine disposition.

PROVE IT. A green aggregate is not proof — the runner echoes the console only on failure.
Use rf2-fyba's reproduction control: a throwaway ns whose name is a PREFIX EXTENSION of the
target ns (so nothing sorts between them), carrying a fn-form :each fixture plus an `async`
row — that selects cljs.test's :sync path, wraps the test in `disable-async`, and rethrows a
bare String synchronously inside whichever `done` continuation is running. Red before (the
target's own .catch message printed against the CONTROL's test name, control ns announced
TWICE, "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time", no summary), gone after (an
honest unhandled rejection naming the real cause, attributed to nobody). Delete the control;
verify every restore BY HASHING THE BYTES, not `git diff`.

cljs.test/run-block hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously. A .catch downstream of a step that calls `done` claims whatever a later
namespace throws as this row's failure, prints it against this row's label, and calls
`done` a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay, RE-RUNNING the offending
namespace, and stalling the lane with no summary line at all.

THE CURE. The rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the .then that calls `done`: it reports
and returns nil but NEVER finishes. Exactly one `done` sits at the tail with nothing after
it. Worked example, and the reasoning, now live in the docstring of
`re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc).

`unmount!`), hoist it into the single trailing step: written once, still run once per path.
Where they DIFFER, leave it. Two real examples from the repaired trees: a defensive
`(try (.unmount root) (catch ...))` that is failure-only because the success path already
unmounted upstream, and a `force-release!` that is failure-only because the success path
asserts the orderly `uninstall!` — hoisting either would have changed behaviour.

  `(is false "must reject")` sits in the .then and the real assertions in the .catch. Make
  the two handlers SIBLINGS of one TWO-ARG .then, then one trailing `done`. This is still
  an instance: the fulfilment arm calls `done` with the .catch downstream of it.

  `done` and calls it, so no caller can be repaired without it. Rename to `report-failure!`,
  drop the parameter, return nil (what #7942 did for the Hicasso `fail-and-finish!` helpers).

DO NOT adopt mount_support's `run-async` wholesale to avoid the work. Its handler reports
the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", which would REPLACE every row's own
diagnostic with one string. Measured under rf2-fyba: only 51 of freehand's 179 even
`:require` mount-support today. `run-async` stays right for NEW matrix cells.

DO NOT retune any suite to dodge the async window (the rf2-hic-029 refusal stands), do not
weaken assertions, and do not drop teardown to make a swap typecheck.

^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, grouped into chains by equal indent with no intervening
lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains (done) is followed by a
.catch step. Strip ;; comments first. The count is an UPPER BOUND — every chain needs
reading, and a source-located "left correct" is a fine disposition.

downstream of it. Split from rf2-fyba by tree; rf2-fyba's own comment carries the full
derivation and the count reconciliation.

CENSUS (rebuild it — see below). Heaviest: nrepl_test 8, cljs_eval_value_test 5,
ensure_connection_single_flight_test 4, port_file_stability_test 3, shutdown_test 3,
unknown_tool_test 3, build_id_cache_test 2, closed_world_test 2, instructions_budget_test 2,
writes_test 2, plus ensure_connection_retry_test, probe_test, raw_state_test, tail_build_test
at 1 each.

START WITH probe_test.cljs:287. #7942 listed it as "left correct — a genuine error path, not
the defect". THAT DOES NOT HOLD AT SOURCE. `assert-ladder-rejects-with-reason` is
  (.then  (fn [_] (is false "must reject") (done)))
  (.catch (fn [err] ... (done)))
— the fulfilment arm calls `done` and the .catch IS downstream of it, so the moment the row
regresses it exhibits the full signature. It is LATENT, not a non-instance. It is also a
shared helper, so repairing it repairs every rung that routes through it.

GATE: `npm test` from tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/ (a fresh worktree has no node_modules there —
junction it, and remove the LINK last).

THE DEFECT (established rf2-d3tc, generalised rf2-qpns/#7942, re-proved under rf2-fyba).
cljs.test/run-block hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously. A .catch downstream of a step that calls `done` claims whatever a later
namespace throws as this row's failure, prints it against this row's label, and calls
`done` a SECOND time — re-forcing run-block's unrealized delay, RE-RUNNING the offending
namespace, and stalling the lane with no summary line at all.

THE CURE. The rejection handler goes UPSTREAM of the .then that calls `done`: it reports
and returns nil but NEVER finishes. Exactly one `done` sits at the tail with nothing after
it. Worked example, and the reasoning, now live in the docstring of
`re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc).

THIS IS NOT A MECHANICAL SWAP — that is the whole reason rf2-qpns did not do it.
Where the two arms do the SAME thing (an idempotent `restore`, a `destroy-frame!`, an
`unmount!`), hoist it into the single trailing step: written once, still run once per path.
Where they DIFFER, leave it. Two real examples from the repaired trees: a defensive
`(try (.unmount root) (catch ...))` that is failure-only because the success path already
unmounted upstream, and a `force-release!` that is failure-only because the success path
asserts the orderly `uninstall!` — hoisting either would have changed behaviour.

TWO SHAPES TO EXPECT (both hit in the repaired trees):
- THE .catch THAT IS THE ROW'S SUCCESS PATH — the row asserts the promise REJECTS, so
  `(is false "must reject")` sits in the .then and the real assertions in the .catch. Make
  the two handlers SIBLINGS of one TWO-ARG .then, then one trailing `done`. This is still
  an instance: the fulfilment arm calls `done` with the .catch downstream of it.
- HELPER-FORCED SHAPES — a local `(defn- unexpected! [done label e] ... (done))` takes
  `done` and calls it, so no caller can be repaired without it. Rename to `report-failure!`,
  drop the parameter, return nil (what #7942 did for the Hicasso `fail-and-finish!` helpers).

DO NOT adopt mount_support's `run-async` wholesale to avoid the work. Its handler reports
the generic "an async matrix cell rejected: ", which would REPLACE every row's own
diagnostic with one string. Measured under rf2-fyba: only 51 of freehand's 179 even
`:require` mount-support today. `run-async` stays right for NEW matrix cells.

DO NOT retune any suite to dodge the async window (the rf2-hic-029 refusal stands), do not
weaken assertions, and do not drop teardown to make a swap typecheck.

REBUILD THE SCANNER, do not trust line numbers (they drift). Signature: steps matching
^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b, grouped into chains by equal indent with no intervening
lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains (done) is followed by a
.catch step. Strip ;; comments first. The count is an UPPER BOUND — every chain needs
reading, and a source-located "left correct" is a fine disposition.

PROVE IT. A green aggregate is not proof — the runner echoes the console only on failure.
Use rf2-fyba's reproduction control: a throwaway ns whose name is a PREFIX EXTENSION of the
target ns (so nothing sorts between them), carrying a fn-form :each fixture plus an `async`
row — that selects cljs.test's :sync path, wraps the test in `disable-async`, and rethrows a
bare String synchronously inside whichever `done` continuation is running. Red before (the
target's own .catch message printed against the CONTROL's test name, control ns announced
TWICE, "WARNING: Async test called done more than one time", no summary), gone after (an
honest unhandled rejection naming the real cause, attributed to nobody). Delete the control;
verify every restore BY HASHING THE BYTES, not `git diff`.
close_reason: Repaired in PR #7954 (branch worker/mcp-53uz). 59 chains across 15 files in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp, not the 38 the census named: +3 from nested chains a flat equal-indent grouping loses, and +18 the bead's stated signature CANNOT see because the (done) lives in the -> HEAD expression rather than a .then step (handler_meta_test 14 — the whole file was invisible — and tail_build_test 4). Extended scanner re-run repo-wide: the head-expression shape occurs nowhere else, so the sibling beads' file lists stand, but correction (1) lifts freehand 179->184 and hicasso 16->17. Repo-wide remainder after this PR: 216. probe_test:287 CONFIRMED a miss by #7942 and agreed at source — the fulfilment arm calls done, the .catch is downstream, and the file's five other .catches already carry the repaired shape, so the row was inconsistent with its own siblings; repaired via two-arg .then in the shared helper, fixing every rung. No asymmetric teardown in this tree — every pair was the identical idempotent restore! thunk, all hoisted to the trailing step. Left correct: ensure_connection_retry's repeated-failures row (.catch is the sole terminal step). Gates CAPTURED: npm test baseline 0 (1224/4440), shipped 0 (1224/4440, no movement), control+reverted 1 (foreign claim + double-done + no summary), control+fixed 1 (honest unhandled rejection, attributed to nobody), check:descriptors 0, check_fast_pr_gap --list 0.

title: hic-089b — CI reachability for the budget-ledger gate (hot-zone workflow job)
description:
## Why

`rf2-hic-089` landed `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_budget_ledger.py` and chained it into `npm run test:hicasso-invariants`. That chain's only hosted invocation is a step of test.yml's `cljs` job under `needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.cljs_node_test == 'true'`.

The gate's inputs are docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md (the ledger), the same directory's substrate-decision.md (the disposition sections L3 resolves), and the witness files under implementation/hicasso/**. ONLY THE LAST ARMS THAT OUTPUT. Verified by direct classifier probe at the hic-089 branch head:

  $ bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md
  cljs_node_test=false
  $ bash .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_budget_ledger.py implementation/package.json
  cljs_node_test=true

So a LEDGER-ONLY edit — exactly the edit this gate exists to police — skips every PR check. Same defect, same chain, same repair as test.yml's `hicasso-complaint-catalogue` job (its own comment records the identical hole at test.yml:875-905).

## What to add

An UNCONDITIONAL pure-Python job in .github/workflows/test.yml, a near-copy of `hicasso-complaint-catalogue`: checkout, setup-python 3.12, then `--self-test` and the live run. Unconditional rather than a new classifier output, for the reason that job's comment gives — a new arm is a fresh chance to make the same mistake and needs re-widening every time the checker learns to read another file. Sub-second static read; no node, no JVM.

It STAYS chained into test:hicasso-invariants: that chain is the local spine lane and the artefact's one-command run; the job is the CI reachability the chain cannot give it.

## Notes

HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/test.yml. Operator sequences it. The hic-089 worker stopped and reported rather than touching it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7994 (merged e7b9924f4b), clustered with rf2-x1mz as the same shape one gate over — a check that cannot fire on the edit it polices. Both landed in one PR because both edit the hot-zone scripts/ + .github/workflows/ surface, which must have exactly one owner. Mayor merged on all five clauses. See rf2-x1mz's close reason for the merge evidence.

title: cljs.test: 280 promise chains still catch downstream of their own done (the non-positional remainder of rf2-qpns)
description:
The remainder of rf2-qpns, measured rather than estimated. rf2-qpns fixed 22 chains
(PR: see that bead); this is the 280 it deliberately did not, and the reason they are a
DIFFERENT and larger job rather than more of the same.

THE DEFECT (unchanged, established by rf2-d3tc and re-proved under rf2-qpns).
`cljs.test/run-block` hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the
run synchronously. A `.catch` placed downstream of the `.then` that calls `done` claims
whatever a later namespace throws, prints it against this row's label with a blank
message slot and a zeroed teardown census, and calls `done` a SECOND time — which
re-forces run-block's unrealized delay and RE-RUNS the offending namespace, then stalls
the lane. Captured on the browser lane under rf2-qpns with a throwing control:

  Testing re-frame.hicasso.read-extent-dom-cljs-test
  Testing re-frame.hicasso.read-extent-zz-control-dom-cljs-test
  FAIL in (a-delayed-row-that-needs-async) (:)
  activity-reveal witness --  | ownership {:cells 0, :cell-refs 0, :boundaries 0, :edges 0}
  Testing re-frame.hicasso.read-extent-zz-control-dom-cljs-test   <-- ns RE-RAN
  FAIL in (a-delayed-row-that-needs-async) (:)
  suspense-retry witness --  | ownership {:cells 0, :cell-refs 0, :boundaries 0, :edges 0}
  WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.

...followed by `Timed out after 360000ms waiting for cljs.test summary` — exit 1, no
summary line at all. The whole browser lane hangs.

WHY THESE 280 ARE NOT rf2-qpns's REPAIR. rf2-qpns took every chain whose done-calling
step is the BARE `(.then (fn [_] (done)))`. That literal is not cosmetic: when the
trailing step is nothing but `done`, moving the `.catch` above it is purely positional —
a `.catch` falling through to it cannot re-run assertions or re-tear-down. In these 280
the `done` is buried among assertions and teardown, so the same swap is NOT behaviour-
preserving. The counter-example, `behaviors_dom_cljs_test.cljs:179`:

  (.then  (fn [_] ... (ms/destroy-root! container root) (done)))
  (.catch (fn [e] (is false ...) (ms/destroy-root! container root) (done)))

A naive swap destroys the root TWICE on the failure path. Each of these needs `done`
split out into its own trailing step first, and whether the teardown belongs on both
paths is a judgement per site — sometimes it is idempotent (a `reset!`), sometimes it is
not (a root teardown, a released handle).

CENSUS (structural: a chain step containing `(done)` with a `.catch` step downstream of
it in the same `->` thread). 280 chains in 78 files. By tree:

  implementation/freehand        170
  tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp        39
  implementation/http             21
  implementation/hicasso          15
  tools/xray                      13
  implementation/ui               10
  implementation/adapters          8
  tools/story                      1
  tools/machines-viz               1
  implementation/resources         1
  implementation/core              1   (a docstring example, not a live chain)

Heaviest files: http_cljs_test 20, behaviors_dom 16, pilot_overlay_dom 13,
compiled_mount_dom 12, pilot_react_interop_dom 10, nrepl_test 9, native_abi_dom 9,
lane_window_dom 9, behavior_async_dom 7.

The scanner that produced this is ~60 lines of Python and is worth rebuilding rather
than trusting this list verbatim (line numbers drift). Signature: steps matching
`^\s*\((\.then|\.catch|\.finally)\b`, grouped into chains by equal indent with no
intervening lower-indent line; flag any chain where a step whose body contains `(done)`
is followed by a `.catch` step.

SIZING. This is not one bead. Suggest splitting by tree — freehand alone is 170 across
~45 files and would time out as a single dispatch. `implementation/freehand/test/
re_frame/freehand/mount_support.cljs`'s `each-mode` / `run-async` were already repaired
under rf2-qpns, which fixes the contract for every caller that routes through them, so
the freehand count may fall once someone checks how many of the 170 could simply ADOPT
those helpers instead of being repaired in place. That check is the right first move.

DO NOT retune any suite to dodge the async window (the rf2-hic-029 refusal stands), and
do not weaken assertions or drop teardown to make a swap typecheck.
notes:
SCANNER + LANE CALIBRATION from rf2-0r3j (PR #7955), for the remaining batches. (1) An independently rebuilt scanner — same stated signature, ;; comments stripped and string literals respected — reads 170 chains in implementation/freehand at origin/main 0221daf44f, not 179. It reproduces the per-file counts of rf2-0r3j's three files EXACTLY (16/13/12=41) and of rf2-ua8r's behavior_matrix (5), and reads 129 after #7955 (170-41), so the 9-chain gap is in files none of the dispatched batches has read yet. Re-measure rather than inheriting 8008. Two children came back VERIFIED ALREADY FIXED this wave, both discharged by rf2-e8kc / PR #7974 (worker/closure-e8kc, merged 2026-08-12T08:12:36Z; commits e6601b21e1 native-abi, d844756426 native-hooks, ae230c8cc0 teardown, 4de7cf5c3c tools):

The 248-remainder table's 'implementation/hicasso 16' row is DISCHARGED — do not hunt for it in the next reconciliation.

ALL THREE SIGNATURES read zero over implementation/freehand and zero repo-wide over implementation/ and tools/.

IT REPRODUCES ALL FOUR PUBLISHED CAMPAIGN LANDMARKS EXACTLY, which is what makes the zero credible rather than merely convenient: 184/46 at 1662f3cc8e (rf2-qpns pre-repair), 100/38 at 2f33b56649 (rf2-d2xz #7955), 55/29 at e9aef48d19 (rf2-29ua #7964), 55/29 at 195a7cb1d0 (#7968's base). A disagreement with any of those numbers would therefore be about WHEN a count was taken, not about HOW.

RECONCILIATION OF THIS BEAD'S OWN 280, AND THE NUMBERS THAT LOOKED WRONG. None of them was wrong; each predates a landing. comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
rf2-53uz (pair-MCP, PR #7954) found the SCANNER SIGNATURE has a blind spot, so the census is a lower bound as well as an upper one — worth passing to the remaining sibling beads.

(1) NESTED STEPS SPLIT A CHAIN. Grouping strictly 'by equal indent' closes the outer chain the moment a deeper-indented .then appears inside a step body, so an outer .then->.catch pairing straddling a nested chain is lost. Keeping open chains on a STACK (pop only on a step or non-blank line at indent <= the chain's) recovers them. Effect measured on the shipped tree: implementation/freehand 179 -> 184, implementation/hicasso 16 -> 17; tools/xray 13, tools/machines-viz 1, tools/story 1 unchanged.

(2) (done) NEED NOT BE IN A STEP OF THE FLAGGED CHAIN. The stated signature looks for a STEP whose body contains (done). pair-MCP's dominant idiom put it in the -> HEAD EXPRESSION instead — inside the body-fn handed to a stub harness:

  (-> (with-canned-eval! canned
        (fn [] (-> (tool ...) (.then (fn [r] ... (done))))))   ; <- done in the HEAD
      (.catch (fn [e] (is false (str "rejected: " ...)) (done))))

The .catch is still downstream of a done and exhibits the full signature (foreign claim, double done, no summary) — the scanner simply cannot see it. 18 such chains in pair-MCP: handler_meta_test 14 (the ENTIRE file was invisible to the census) and tail_build_test 4. Fix: for each .catch step, test the region from the chain's head line (nearest preceding non-blank line at LOWER indent, scanning back past deeper ones) to that .catch for (done), rather than only the preceding steps' bodies.

I re-ran the extended scanner repo-wide: shape (2) occurs NOWHERE outside pair-MCP, so the sibling beads' FILE LISTS stand. Only their counts move, by (1).

Repo-wide remainder after PR #7954: 216 chains in 55 files.

Also note the half-repair trap this exposed: adding the trailing (.then (fn [_] (done))) WITHOUT removing the success arm's own (done) leaves the row calling done TWICE. Re-running the scanner after the edit catches it — a repaired chain must scan to zero, not merely gain a trailing step.

title: cljs.test: 21 remaining promise chains catch downstream of their own done
description:
Same defect rf2-d3tc fixed in reincarnation_paint_dom_cljs_test, in a second file, PROVEN BY CAPTURE rather than by resemblance.

SITE. implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/read_extent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:672-673

    (.then (fn [_] (done)))
    (.catch (fail-and-finish! done "activity-reveal witness" handle))

WHY IT IS A DEFECT. cljs.test/run-block hands 'done' a continuation that runs the
WHOLE REMAINDER of the run synchronously (this file's later rows, then every
namespace after it). Anything out there that throws unwinds back into the callback
that called 'done'. A .catch placed AFTER that callback claims the foreign failure
as its own: it prints this row's label against whichever test is current by then,
reads a DOM its own teardown already emptied, and calls 'done' a second time --
which does not merely warn, it re-forces run-block's delay, because a delay whose
body threw is still unrealized.

CAPTURED EVIDENCE (npm run test:browser, local Windows, branch worker/donefix-d3tc
with rf2-d3tc's fix applied and a throwing control namespace present):

    FAIL in (a-delayed-row-that-needs-async) (:)
    activity-reveal witness --  | ownership {:cells 0, :cell-refs 0, :boundaries 0, :edges 0}
    WARNING: Async test called done more than one time.

The blank message slot is the signature: what cljs.test throws there is a bare
String, which has no .message. The row is attributed to a foreign namespace's test.

FIX. The same positional repair rf2-d3tc took, and it is the shape
re-frame.hicasso.checkpoint-support/at-the-checkpoint already uses: split
fail-and-finish! into a report-only handler, put the .catch UPSTREAM of the .then
that calls done, and leave exactly ONE done at the tail of the chain with nothing
after it. Do not weaken the row's assertions.

NOT DONE IN rf2-d3tc because that bead's dispatch fenced the change to one file.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7937 (landed 727c185db792f9542a31b08c4a25b07313064b82) — broaden this exact owner beyond the one captured row. PR #7937 correctly repaired all three chains in reincarnation_paint_dom_cljs_test, but a landed-tree census finds 21 mechanically identical `.then (fn [_] (done))` then `.catch ... (done)` sites still present: 6 in Freehand (compiled_keyed_run:191, custom_element:302, mount_support:446/462, ownership_maps:541, pilot_react_interop:243); 10 in Hicasso (activity_suspense:408/582/720, kernel_commit_owns:323/401/460/566, read_extent:532/601/672); 4 in http_cljs_test:566/610/647/678; and 1 in Pair raw_state_test:367. Every one sits downstream of cljs.test/run-block's synchronous continuation and can claim a later row's throw, then call done twice. BOUNDED REPAIR: sweep these exact 21 sites, moving each rejection handler before one trailing done while preserving assertions and teardown; reuse each file's existing local helper shape and do not add a framework or broaden into unrelated async cleanup. Run the surface-appropriate browser/node lanes and retain a representative foreign-failure control long enough to prove attribution and no duplicate done, then remove it.

title: hicasso: no public or kit instrument answers 'how many boundary bodies ran'
description:
Found by rf2-hic-078 while measuring the per-keystroke budget from the two witness applications.

THE PROBLEM. Product specification §6 states a budget in bodies — *narrow-update body work scales with changed rows rather than all mounted rows* — and asks the four-field editor and the controlled grid to publish "state writes, subscription recomputations, boundary runs, write amplification, commit, and visible echo". There is no public or test-kit door that answers the boundary-run half.

WHAT EXISTS, AND WHY EACH IS NOT IT.

- `re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted/census` counts `:cells :cell-refs :boundaries :edges :entries` plus `:frames`. Those are RESIDUE — what is retained — not work done. A keystroke that ran a hundred bodies and a keystroke that ran one leave the same census.
- Spec 009's `rf:render:<view-name>` measures are the right shape, and are compiled out unless `re-frame.performance/enabled?`. No PR-lane build sets it (`node-test`, `browser-test` and the bench lane are all `:none`; the perf-on builds are nightly). So a PR gate cannot read them.
- `re-frame.hicasso.impl.collector/body-runs` is the instrument, it is always-on by an explicit ruling (rf2-2rtt6.84 (6)), and it is an INTERNAL.

CONSEQUENCE. `examples/editor/flow_dom_cljs_test` and `examples/grid/scaling_dom_cljs_test` both `:require` `impl.collector` to measure the budget of the applications they are witnesses for. The applications themselves name nothing but the public door and the fence in `examples/witness_surface_cljs_test` proves it — a test is allowed the reach an application is not — but an application cannot measure its own stated budget without one.

WHO ELSE NEEDS IT. rf2-hic-045 (publish the per-keystroke mechanics) and rf2-hic-071 (budget enforcement gates) are both downstream of rf2-hic-078 and both need this number.

CANDIDATE REMEDY, for whoever owns the kit surface: one door on `re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted` — `(hm/body-runs)` / `(hm/bodies-run handle f)` — delegating to `impl.collector/body-runs`. It is a test-kit surface, so it costs a production bundle nothing, and it puts the specification's own unit in the vocabulary of the facade that mounts the thing being measured. Whether the door should be per-boundary rather than page-wide is the real design question: page-wide is what the counter is, and per-boundary attribution today is done by arithmetic over an exact expected total.

NOT filed as a defect in the counter. `body-runs` is well-designed for what it is; the gap is that it has no public counterpart.
notes:
RESOLVED by PR #7931 (worker/bodycount-5mxe). Landed as a TEST-KIT door: hm/bodies-run on re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted, delegating to impl.collector. No public export, no hot-zone file, nothing new in a production build.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE — all three 'what exists and why each is not it' claims hold. census is residue (counted = [:cells :cell-refs :boundaries :edges :entries]). rf:render:* is emitted by hicasso (collector/mint-view! and mint-frame-prop-view! both wrap the component fn in performance/mark-and-measure :render) but compiled out: exactly two builds flip performance/enabled? — :node-test-perf-nightly (nightly, ns-regexp '-emit-nightly-test$', cannot select a -cljs-test$ suite) and :examples/counter-perf (bundle probe, runs no tests). body-runs is the instrument, always-on by rf2-2rtt6.84 (6), internal.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FRAMING.
(1) The reach-through was never a breach and is not two files. witness_surface_cljs_test states the ruling in terms — 'a test may reach past a door the application may not ... which is the whole reason the two are held to different rules' — and its fence is over APPLICATION namespaces only. 19 test files read the counter; 58 require impl.collector. The real cost was narrower: an application witness could not state its budget in the vocabulary of the facade that mounted it, and a CONSUMER's test would have to name an impl. namespace deps.edn calls 'not a consumer surface'.
(2) The Spec 009 path answers a DIFFERENT question, not merely an expensive one. The measure bracket deliberately spans the generation fence's whole retry loop ('the generation fence emits once'); body-runs bumps per body INVOCATION. On a fence re-run the two disagree by design, so the measure stream could not reproduce these numbers even with both goog-defines flipped.

PLACEMENT ARGUMENT. test.mounted already requires impl.collector (reset-runtime!), so no new dependency edge. test_kit/src is off the published :paths (deps.edn lists it only under :aliases/:test/:extra-paths) so build:hicasso-release cannot see it. Both consumers already require hm. Every one of the counter's 19 consumers is a test. Page-wide and handle-free beside census: a per-boundary form is UNAVAILABLE, not withheld — attribution needs a durable per-boundary id, which impl.collector states costs a third React hook and breaks the HD-020 budget hook_budget_cljs_test enforces.

The 17 runtime suites keep reading impl.collector directly, deliberately: runtime suites read the runtime's counter, application witnesses read the kit's door.

GATES (captured): build:hicasso-release 0 (erasure OK, door absent from the advanced bundle); test:browser 0 (1284 tests / 7971 assertions); test:browser SABOTAGE 1 with exactly 2 failures proving both rows execute through the door — actuals (not (= 3 2 2)) and (not (= 9 2)); test:cljs 0 (13329 / 67165); test:hicasso-invariants 0; clj-kondo pinned 0 errors 0 warnings. No measured number altered.

    Use of undeclared Var re-frame.hicasso/fn

The build completes, and the page throws at render. The second and third lines are the loud ones and they name the author's own argument symbol rather than the missing macro.

REMEDY (candidate, for whoever owns it): either rewrite the docstring examples to `h/hfn` today, or land the `h/fn` rename and leave them. Doing neither is the only wrong answer — the two docstrings are the most-copied statement of the one callback form.

Grep for the corpus: `git grep -n "(h/fn "` — prose mentions of `h/fn` are correct and should not be touched; only the CODE EXAMPLES are wrong.
