title: hic: route PATHS are process-global strings, so two apps in one node bundle collide silently
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-hic-025 WORKER (PR #7920) when the fast-PR spine went red — and the spine was THE ONLY GATE THAT COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT.

WHAT HAPPENED. The new vertical slice registered the routes `/` and `/article/:slug`. Twelve assertions in the RealWorld suite failed, naming the slice's routes. Cause: route IDS are namespaced keywords and therefore safe, but route PATHS are plain STRINGS in a PROCESS-GLOBAL registry — and the node test bundle loads a dozen applications into ONE process. So any two apps that both claim `/` collide, and the second registration wins for everybody.

NOTHING WARNED. `:rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score` requires EQUAL rank, and the log carried zero occurrences. So the collision is silent at registration, silent at dispatch, and surfaces only as another application's tests failing for reasons that name YOUR routes. The worker fixed its own case by namespacing every path under `/slice`, and `test:cljs` went from 12 failures to 0.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A CONVENTION NOTE. Every witness app this programme is about to add hits it. `rf2-hic-086` (Todo-class), `rf2-hic-078` (two public-package witness apps) and `rf2-hic-074` (pagination + runtime content) all live in the same bundle, and the natural path for a demo app is `/`. The next one to claim it breaks a suite it has never heard of, and the failure names the wrong file.

THE QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, and it is a design call, not a fix:
  (a) Is a process-global path registry correct, with the remedy being a CONVENTION — every in-bundle app namespaces its paths — plus something that ENFORCES it? A convention nobody can violate accidentally is worth more than one written down.
  (b) Or should the registry be frame-scoped or root-scoped, so two apps in one process cannot see each other's paths at all? That is the shape re-frame2 uses for nearly everything else, and a global registry is the exception rather than the rule here.
  (c) Or should registering a path that already exists REFUSE, rather than silently shadow? Note this is adjacent to the open ruling on rf2-04tx — whether the closed effect map should refuse an unknown key rather than ignoring it. Do not answer that one here, but read it: the argument shapes are the same, and so is the counter-argument about nag-diagnostics on a hot path.

ESTABLISH THE COST BEFORE RECOMMENDING. Read the registry, say what each option costs at registration and at dispatch, and whether a check can be dev-only and erased in production (the release build's erasure gate is the precedent). Then STATE THE CASE and stop — this is an operator call.

WHAT NOT TO DO: do not widen `:rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score` on a hunch; its equal-rank condition may be deliberate. Do not rename other apps' routes. Do not treat "namespace your paths" as landed just because the slice did it — that is one app obeying a rule nobody wrote.

VERIFY AT SOURCE: confirm the registry really is process-global and really is keyed by string path, and confirm the warning's equal-rank condition, before building any argument on this description. It is a worker's report, relayed by the mayor.
notes:
CORRECTION FROM THE REPORTING WORKER, and it removes an option a reader would otherwise reach for first.

"MAKE THE EXISTING WARNING LOUDER" IS NOT A FOURTH OPTION. `reg-route` does carry :rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score, and it NEVER FIRED — because the ranks DIFFERED. So the guard had nothing to say while the resolution was already wrong. It is asking a different question from the one that matters: it detects an ambiguous TIE, not a silent OVERWRITE across applications that share a process.

That distinction is the whole finding. A reader who sees a route-shadowing warning already exists will assume the mechanism is covered and the threshold merely needs lowering. It is not covered. Widening the equal-rank condition would fire on cases the warning was deliberately written to allow, and would still miss this one whenever the ranks differ — which is the common case, since two applications' paths rarely rank the same.

So the three options on this bead stand as the whole option set: convention plus enforcement, a scoped registry, or a refusal at registration. Do not add a fourth arm about tuning the existing warning, and if the ruling lands on convention-plus-enforcement, note that the enforcement CANNOT be that warning.

ONE DOCUMENTATION RESIDUAL, reported and deliberately not actioned: finding 8 of docs/design/hicasso/product/authoring-report-slice.md explains this collision and the /slice fix but CITES NO BEAD, because this bead's id did not exist when the report was written. Worth one line whenever that report is next touched. Not worth a dispatch of its own.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-12, operator-overturnable):

RULING: Option (a). The route registry stays process-global. The in-bundle path-prefix convention gets written down once and enforced by one repo-side census gate with a one-entry allowlist. No registration refusal, no scoping. Dossier ai/decisions/rf2-wqnl.route-path-collision.md reviewed, every load-bearing claim re-verified at source (head 3ed7a442e6), file deleted per protocol; all analysis preserved below.

WHY (a):
1. The class bites exactly one composition - many apps loaded into one node test bundle - which exists only in this repo. A consumer's own registry holds only their routes (authoring-report finding 8, premise verified). Build the guard where the hazard lives.
2. The gate delivers the whole observable improvement refusal would give THIS repo - load-time failure naming both routes and both files, at the bundle boundary where the class bites - with zero framework surface, zero registration/dispatch cost, zero consumer-facing change.
3. Symmetric with the framework's own precedent: cross-source collision on a registration ID gets namespacing convention + a provenance-aware dev warning (:rf.warning/registration-collision, registrar.cljc:430-495), not refusal. Paths should not be held to a stricter standard than ids while rf2-04tx (refuse-vs-ignore, same argument shape) is still open; nothing here answers 04tx.
4. REJECTING (c) reg-route refusal: it refuses a LIVE legitimate usage - hicasso route_link_cljs_test.cljs:29 registers :conduit.profile/show at "/profile/:username", identical to RealWorld's :realworld.profile/show, emission-only (href synthesis by id, never URL ingress), coherent and harmless (verified). It forces the todomvc/RealWorld "/" pair to be resolved NOW with no allowlist possible, breaking a teaching example's URL fidelity (RealWorld routing.cljs follows the official contract "to the letter"; todomvc's / /active /completed are canonical TodoMVC, and guide code blocks are digest-pinned = multi-file change). Hot-reload id-rename (same path, new id, stale id seated) throws until cleared. And it would set the refuse posture by side effect while 04tx awaits ruling. Nag-diagnostics shape the posture rejects (u53yy.7).
5. REJECTING (b) frame/root-scoped table: scoped resolution ALREADY EXISTS opt-in - EP-0023 image-built frames resolve registrations generation-routed (registrar.cljc:861-870, verified: a generation-scoped query sees only the frame's own image's ids). Defaulting or duplicating that is new API surface or a fleet migration, taxing the single-app norm to fix a repo-internal testing artifact, and it mismodels the domain: the browser URL is one process resource with one owner. The bead's premise "frame-scoped is the shape re-frame2 uses for nearly everything else" is not accurate - the global static registrar is the rule for EVERY kind; per-frame is state plus opt-in image resolution.

VERIFIED MECHANISM (preserved from the dossier; re-checked at source 2026-08-12):
- One defonce registrar atom for all kinds (implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:152-157). The path pattern is route metadata; match-url (implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1226) takes ONLY a url - no frame, no app - and walks one rank-sorted table of ALL registered routes, short-circuiting on first match. One process = one shared match table.
- Ties go to the EARLIER registration: rank = structural 5-tuple + (- reg-index) (registry.cljc:499,506). Two identical patterns always tie structurally, so the earlier wins every URL forever and the later is unreachable for URL ingress. Namespace load order decides which app wins.
- IMPRECISION CORRECTION to this bead's earlier note: "the warning never fired because the ranks DIFFERED" is wrong for the observed pair. /article/:slug vs /article/:slug are IDENTICAL patterns - structural ranks EQUAL, and patterns-intersect? reports them co-matchable - so the scan's condition was satisfiable. The verified reasons nothing surfaced: (i) :rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score is delivered via trace/emit! into the instrumentation ring buffer and NOTHING in the node lane reads it - no console sink for trace warnings anywhere in core/src (grep-verified); (ii) prod builds erase the emit entirely (pinned by implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_trace_emit_elision_prod_test.cljs); (iii) the first registrant scans before the second exists, and test-support restore-registrar! reseats the registrar wholesale without re-running reg-route, so no scan runs on restore. For the GENERAL cross-app case (one app's literal under another's capture) ranks genuinely differ and the guard is structurally blind - that half of the note stands. NET, AND BINDING ON FUTURE WORK: no widening or tuning of this warning can be the enforcement arm, because even when it fires nobody in the failing lane can see it. Its tie-only condition is deliberate (rf2-6gzobp - warning on the tie alone floods every ordinary multi-page app). DO NOT BUILD ON THE PHANTOM WARNING.
- LIVE ARMED DUPLICATE today: examples/core/todomvc/events.cljs:28 registers :todo/all at "/"; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:40-60 registers :realworld/home at "/". Both load into the node bundle. Asymptomatic only because todomvc suites never feed a URL in and RealWorld suites never ingress "/". The slice trap, armed.
- LIVE LEGITIMATE DUPLICATE: the route_link test above - emission-only registration is coherent; match-dead is harmless. Duplicate paths are not always a bug, which is a load-bearing reason refusal is wrong.
- The prefix convention has been independently invented 3x, written nowhere normative: /slice (rf2-hic-025, PR #7920), /hicasso-todo (rf2-hic-086), and the route-path per-substrate prefix helper in core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs. The freehand bench (freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/shapes/model.cljs:298-300) still claims bare /, /profile/:username, /article/:slug in its own lane.
- DOSSIER CORRECTION (raised by the Codex advisory, verified correct at source): :rf.error/duplicate-url-binding is EMITTED (trace/emit-error!, implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_bound.cljc:97,162), NOT thrown as the dossier body claimed. Exclusivity is still enforced - the incumbent keeps its claim position and a duplicate appends after it, never stealing ownership. The architecture point stands: the framework enforces single URL OWNERSHIP; what it does not police is single AUTHORSHIP of the match table every loaded app writes into.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one worker, one PR; DISPATCHABLE now):
1. TESTING.md paragraph (not hot-zone): every app/witness loaded into the shared node test bundle namespaces its URL paths under a distinct leading segment (as /slice and /hicasso-todo do). Bare "/" and unprefixed top-level paths belong to the teaching examples that hold them today. Note that distinct leading literals can never co-match, so the prefix convention also prevents the non-identical overlap class (literal-under-capture) that exact-duplicate grouping cannot see. Cite rf2-wqnl.
2. Census gate: one new node-lane *-cljs-test in implementation/routing/test/ (existing source path - no shadow-cljs.edn edit, no hot zone). Under the standard fixture (the stable ns-load baseline, rf2-7hwnu), walk registrar/registrations :route, group by canonical :path, and FAIL when two different ids share a pattern. The failure message names BOTH ids AND their source coords (registrations carry :ns/:line), states the prefix convention, and cites rf2-wqnl. Shape the census core as a pure function over the registrations snapshot, with one self-test feeding a synthetic unallowlisted duplicate and asserting it is reported (adopted from the Codex advisory in reduced pure-function form: a gate that cannot demonstrably go red repeats this bead's own phantom-warning failure mode; no temporarily-break-the-bundle ritual).
3. Allowlist at birth, exactly one entry: {:todo/all, :realworld/home} at "/" - two teaching apps whose URL shapes are fidelity claims, neither of whose suites ingresses the other's URLs. Justifying comment required. The worker RE-RUNS the census at implementation time rather than trusting this note's list; fixture-local emission-only registrations (route_link) should not appear in the ns-load baseline, but any that do are allowlisted with the emission-only justification.
4. One-line rf2-wqnl citation in docs/design/hicasso/product/authoring-report-slice.md finding 8 (tree is outside mkdocs --strict; worker verifies anchors/tables by hand and says so in the PR body).
5. Close rf2-wqnl on merge.

FENCES:
- NO registration refusal: do not introduce :rf.error/route-path-duplicate or any reg-route duplicate-path throw.
- NO frame- or root-scoping of the route table; no new registration door; no testbed migration to EP-0023 images for this.
- NO widening, tuning, or re-sinking of :rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score.
- Consumer apps UNAFFECTED - this is a repo-side gate only; zero framework/spec surface.
- rf2-04tx remains open and is NOT answered here.
- No namespace-based app-ownership inference, no rank-different intersection analytics, no bespoke Xray UI (Xray's Static Routes catalogue and Simulate-URL already show seated state and match winners).
REVISIT TRIGGER: reconsider (c) only if a consumer-side collision surfaces in the wild, or if the rf2-04tx ruling lands on "refuse" and the operator wants the postures aligned.

CODEX ADVISORY WEIGHED: it concurs with (a), narrowly scoped - adopted. Its emitted-not-thrown correction on duplicate-url-binding verified correct and adopted into the record. Its negative-control fixture adopted in reduced pure-function self-test form. Its stop-there list adopted into the fences. Nothing rejected on substance.
close_reason:
Implemented in PR #7938 (branch worker/route-wqnl). Option (a) as ruled: convention written down in TESTING.md, enforced by implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_path_census_test.clj. No refusal, no scoping, no warning widening; rf2-04tx untouched.

MECHANISM DEPARTURE, measured. The ruled node-lane registrar walk was built first and sees 20 of 39 top-level app-tree route registrations, order-dependent; the invisible half contained :todo/all and realworld-http's :realworld/home, the very pair the ruling's allowlist names. Widening it by adding requires would reorder registrations (order decides which duplicate wins), and the id-keyed registrar hides realworld-http/realworld-resources entirely. Census therefore reads source: every column-1 reg-route under examples/ and testbeds/, canonicalised via match/canonical-route-pattern. Complete, order-independent, perturbs nothing. Runs in CI's always-on jvm-routing job; local fast-PR spine skips it on a diff not touching implementation/routing.

ALLOWLIST is the measured birth state, two entries not one: / (six ids) and /articles (:resources.app/articles + :routing.app/articles - inherited, not a fidelity claim, first to retire).

GATES (captured): npm run test:cljs EXIT=0 (13329 tests / 67165 assertions); routing clojure -M:test EXIT=0 (522 / 3086); check_doc_slugs EXIT=0; check_provenance_pins --changed-since origin/main EXIT=0. Gate proven red then green then red again on a live negative control.

title: hic-019 F5 — ::h/mounting outside a presence tray's direct child is a silent no-op and leaks to the DOM
description:
# `::h/mounting` written anywhere but a tray's direct child is a silent no-op — and leaks to the DOM

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §3 Quality. Severity: quality (see the note — the ruling this surface already carries argues for `correctness`).**

## What is wrong

`with-phase` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:178-231`)
is applied to exactly one thing: the tray's own frozen entries.
`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:344-348` maps it over
`(:order state)` and nothing else. So the override keys are stripped and merged only on
a `motion/presence` tray's **direct** children.

Written anywhere else — on a grandchild, on a node inside a child view's body, on any
element in a body with no tray above it at all — `::h/mounting` / `::h/unmounting` are
seen by nothing in `impl/presence.cljs`. A repo-wide search confirms `override-keys`
(`presence.cljs:105`) has no reader outside that file.

The prop then falls through to the ordinary codec walk, which has no arm for it.
`convert-entry` at `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:783-788`
skips only `:key` and the revision key, then takes `(name k)` — which drops the
namespace and yields the emitted slot `"mounting"` / `"unmounting"`. That name is not
reserved, not an event position, not the class or ref slot, so the override MAP is
converted and written onto the props object handed to React. It reaches the DOM.

Two consequences from one legal-looking declaration:

1. The animation the author declared never happens, and nothing says so.
2. A stray `mounting` / `unmounting` attribute lands on the element.

## The sentence that outlived the behaviour

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:184-185`:

> The two override keys are always removed, so an override never reaches the DOM as an attribute.

That is true of `with-phase`, and it is the sentence a reader relies on for the whole
feature. Outside a tray's direct children the second clause is false.

## The ruling this contradicts

Twelve lines below that sentence, at
`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:207-215`, an override
written on a **view head** raises `:rf.error/hicasso-presence-override-on-a-view`,
with the rationale:

> the boundary cannot see inside an opaque view, and **silently dropping the map is the class of failure this whole ruling exists to delete**.

The identical silent drop survives one level down on a native node, un-refused. The
ruling closed one door of two. This is the same shape as `{:slots #{:constructor}}`
(commit `5e5c21f5fc`): a legal-looking declaration, a walk that never reaches it,
nothing thrown.

## Where

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:105` — `override-keys`, the roster, read only in this file
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:172-176` — `override-for`, the only consult
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:184-185` — the universal-sounding sentence
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:207-215` — the view-head refusal, and the ruling
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/presence.cljs:344-348` — `with-phase` applied to `(:order state)` only
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:783-788` — the walk that emits it to React

## What should change (sketch)

Refuse an override key at the codec's own prop walk, where every element passes.

The cost is affordable and should be stated rather than assumed: `PropSlot`
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:328`) is a cached
per-prop-name record already carrying `reserved?`, `event?`, `ref?`, `class?`. An
`override?` field computed once at mint makes the runtime check one boolean field read
per prop — the same cost class as the `reserved?` skip that already sits in that walk.
No new map lookup, no per-render allocation.

On a hit, `fail!` naming the element, the key, and the recovery: *an override belongs
on a `motion/presence` tray's direct child; a node deeper than that is not one the tray
can see.* Reuse `:rf.error/hicasso-presence-override-on-a-view` or mint a sibling — the
complaint catalogue checker (`npm run test:hicasso-invariants`) governs which, and it
counted 67 live rows at filing time.

Then correct the `:184-185` sentence to say what it means: *within a tray's direct
children the two keys are always removed; anywhere else they are refused.*

Do NOT make the codec presence-aware in any other way, and do NOT add a runtime
warning that fires per commit — one refusal at the offending element.

## Done when

- `[:div {::h/mounting {:class "in"}} …]` nested below a tray's direct child, or with no tray above it, raises naming the element and the recovery.
- A tray's direct children are unaffected: `motion_presence_dom_cljs_test.cljs` and `presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs` stay green.
- No `mounting` / `unmounting` attribute can reach the DOM by any route.
- The `presence.cljs:184-185` sentence states its scope.
- `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` passes.

## Tests / checks that matter

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/motion_presence_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `presence_cljs_test.cljs`, `presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/codec_cljs_test.cljs` — the prop-walk home for the new refusal
- `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-hicasso && node out/node-test-hicasso.js` (553 tests / 2508 assertions green on `main`@`89029ac46d`)
- If the `PropSlot` field is added, confirm the bench compile gate is unaffected — PR #7907 is open on that gate.

## Severity note for the mayor

Filed `quality` because the supported placement behaves correctly. The ruling at
`presence.cljs:207-215` — *"silently dropping the map is the class of failure this
whole ruling exists to delete"* — is an argument for `correctness`, and the ledger's
severity table would then make it blocking. The mayor decides which row it takes.

## What NOT to touch

- `with-phase`'s merge semantics, the `without-structural` filter and its `:key`/`:ref` rationale (`presence.cljs:187-198`) — correct and load-bearing.
- The view-head refusal and its message.
- `:rf/phase` as the boundary-child channel.
- `impl/codec.cljs`'s host-declaration arms — `cbguard-hic035` is live on
  `implementation/hicasso/src` and `test`; this bead's codec surface is the generic
  prop walk (`convert-entry` / `PropSlot`), not the `:callbacks` / `:slots` arms.
  Sequence behind that worker.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7923. Both halves refused: the DOM leak (an internal marker reaching the page) and the silent no-op. New id :rf.error/hicasso-presence-override-out-of-reach, raised at convert-entry AND host-entry — one refusal at two prop doors, check-ref!'s shape. Matched as the EXACT keyword rather than on the canonical slot (revision-key's doctrine exception): a name-derived PropSlot field, as the bead sketched, cannot tell ::h/mounting from a plain :mounting, and claiming the slot would confiscate an attribute the author is entitled to write. Both key defs moved to impl/codec.cljs beside revision-key; presence reads them from there. The 184-185 sentence now states its scope. Sabotage both ways: guard removed = 9 failures + 1 error on the node lane and 2 more in the browser lane (one of them the leak measured: [mounting] matched 1 painted node); guard widened to the slot = 5 failures + 2 errors, all in the too-eager control. Gates captured: node 561/2570 exit 0, browser 1278/7892 exit 0, hicasso-invariants exit 0, keyword-drift exit 0, hicasso-release exit 0, fast-PR spine exit 0.

title: hic-019 F2 — n/defcomponent's declaration map is recorded, never validated, never consulted
description:
# `n/defcomponent`'s declaration map is recorded, never validated, and never consulted

**Filed by rf2-hic-019 (CHECKPOINT 1), protocol §3 Quality. Severity: correctness (validation half) + coverage (witness half).**

Two faults on one surface, and the second is the reason the first survived.

## Fault 1 — the declaration map has no roster, and `:server`'s value is never checked

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:755-772` takes any map as the
declaration and reads exactly one key:

    server (get decl :server :client-only)

Nothing checks the map's key set and nothing checks the value's membership. So all of
these mint clean, with no refusal anywhere:

- `{:ssr :render}` — the `defhost` spelling, on the sibling door. Silently `:client-only`.
- `{:sever :render}` — a typo. Silently `:client-only`.
- `{:server :rendr}` — a typo in the value. Stamped as the string `"rendr"` at
  `native.cljc:333`, and read back by `n/marker` as `"rendr"`.
- `{:server :render :fallback [...]}` — the extra key vanishes.

`mint-host!` refuses exactly this on the neighbouring door
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1643-1653`, roster at
`:1246`), and its message is the ruling: *"Reading past an option it does not know is
how a policy comes to be set and never applied."* `h/reg-state` refuses it too
(`impl/state.cljc:275-284`). `n/defcomponent` is the one declaration door in the
package with neither a key roster nor a value roster.

## Fault 2 — nothing on any runtime path reads the field, and the witness asserts the recording

`native.cljc:333` stamps `#js {:name … :server (name server)}` onto the tier sentinel.
The only other sites that touch that field in `implementation/hicasso/src/` are
`native.cljc:439` (`n/lazy` hard-codes `"client-only"`) and `carry!` at
`native.cljc:372-373`, which copies the marker object wholesale without reading it.
There is no server walk, no SSR branch and no gate that consults it. A verified grep
over `implementation/hicasso/src/` and `implementation/hicasso/test/` finds every
remaining reader inside test files.

And the witnesses assert precisely the recording:

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_fence_cljs_test.cljs:192-195` —
  *"and an explicit `{:server :render}` is recorded. Narrowing caught: ignoring the
  declaration map entirely, which would pass the default row above"* →
  `(is (= "render" (.-server (n/marker server-rendered))))`
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:320` — the same shape.

That row was written against the right risk and lands one step short of it: a
declaration that is recorded and then consulted by nothing satisfies it perfectly.
It is the same instrument fault as asserting an fx is present in the registrar when
the fx is never reached.

Meanwhile the namespace's own headline example is `{:server :render}`
(`native.cljc:13`) and `n/lazy`'s docstring at `native.cljc:429-432` argues about
whether a component's declared policy may be overridden — prose that reads as though
the field decides something on the server. Today it decides nothing.

## Where

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:755-772` — `defcomponent`, `(get decl :server :client-only)`, no roster
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:333` — the only write
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:372-373` — `carry!` copies, does not read
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:13`, `:429-432` — the prose that implies an effect
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_fence_cljs_test.cljs:192-195` — the recording assertion
- Comparators that refuse: `impl/codec.cljs:1246`, `:1643-1653`; `impl/state.cljc:275-284`

## What should change (sketch)

**Fault 1 is unambiguous and small.** Give `defcomponent` the same two rosters
`mint-host!` has: an option-key roster (`#{:server}` today) and a value roster
(`#{:client-only :render}` — whatever the settled set is), both refused at the
declaration where the author's stack still points at it, via `impl.error/fail!`.

**Fault 2 needs a ruling before code.** Either
(a) the native tier's `:server` policy IS wired to a server path, in which case the
witness must assert the EFFECT (bytes emitted / withheld) rather than the marker; or
(b) it is deferred to Phase 3 by design, in which case say so where the declaration
is written — `native.cljc:13`'s headline example and `:429-432`'s prose currently
imply a live policy — and the witness row's wording changes from "is recorded" to
"is recorded; the policy is not yet consulted (Phase 3)". Recording the declaration
is a legitimate thing to test; presenting it as coverage of the policy is not.

**Scope note the mayor should weigh**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/adversarial-risks.md:18`
defers native-surface risks to Phase 3 ("Native-surface risks enter only when Phase 3
introduces that optional surface"), so this does NOT block the Phase 1 kernel exit.
It is filed here because the code has shipped and the trap shape is the one this
checkpoint was told to hunt.

## Done when

- `{:ssr :render}`, `{:sever :render}` and `{:server :rendr}` on an `n/defcomponent` each raise at the declaration, naming the offending key or value and the roster.
- `{:server :render}` and an absent declaration map are unaffected.
- Either the `:server` field has a runtime consumer with a witness asserting its effect, or the deferral is stated in `native.cljc` and in the witness row's own wording.
- New refusal ids (if any) are rowed in `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md` and Spec 009; `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` passes.

## Tests / checks that matter

- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_fence_cljs_test.cljs` — the roster rows, and the reworded/strengthened `:server` row.
- `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test-hicasso && node out/node-test-hicasso.js` (553 tests / 2508 assertions green on `main`@`89029ac46d`).
- `npm run test:hicasso-invariants`.

## What NOT to touch

- `n/lazy`'s hard-coded `"client-only"` (`native.cljc:439`) and its rationale — that is correct and witnessed.
- The two-languages fence, `n/$`, the ABI helpers, or `carry!`'s wholesale marker copy.
- The `:name` back-fill window in `n/lazy`.
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/` — `cbguard-hic035` is live there.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7923. Fault 1 (the missing rosters) is closed: declared-server validates and ANSWERS — key roster #{:server}, value roster #{:client-only :render} — reached as an argument inside defcomponent's own try, after the emitted declaring! wrote the ledger, so fail!'s ambient :view/:source name the author's declaration. New ids :rf.error/hicasso-native-unknown-option and :rf.error/hicasso-native-bad-server-policy. component's signature untouched, so the eight existing n/component call sites are unaffected. Fault 2 is answered as a STATED DEFERRAL, not as code: the :server field is still consulted by nothing, adversarial-risks.md defers native-surface risks to Phase 3, and building a server walk would be inventing the machinery. The deferral is now stated in the namespace headline example, defcomponent's docstring and declared-server's, and the witness row's own wording says the policy is recorded and not yet consulted. native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:320 deliberately left alone — there the recording is the CONTROL for n/lazy's hard-coded client-only, which IS consulted. Follow-on filed: rf2-ggnp (P3) carries the wiring or the removal. Nothing renamed; rf2-mo4o still owns :ssr -> :server. Sabotage both ways: rosters removed = 15 failures naming themselves; widened to require :server present = the lane cannot LOAD, because quote-cell* carries a docstring and no declaration map.

title: hic: nine ported prototype suites still have their bench originals — a port is a move, and one pair has already drifted
description:
# The nine ports whose originals still stand

**Source: rf2-hic-008's verification pass, 2026-08-11 16:37 AUSEST.** Recorded in
`docs/design/hicasso/product/prototype-suite-triage.md` under
"The nine ports whose originals still stand", which carries the full measurement.

## What is wrong

rf2-c78g ruled the convention: **executing a PORT verdict MOVES the suite; it does not copy it.**
It was ruled while eleven ports were already on the ground (rf2-a15c, PR #7842) and it resolved
only the two it was written about (the `:ssr` pair). The other NINE bench originals still stand.

## The nine (4,338 lines)

`arm1/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (453, 7 deftest) · `arm1/callback_form_dom_cljs_test.cljs`
(156, 3) · `front/codec_cljs_test.cljs` (1593, 67) · `arm1/hframe_cljs_test.cljs` (360, 8) ·
`arm1/hframe_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (458, 5) · `arm1/keywarn_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (190, 3) ·
`arm1/presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (460, 8) · `arm1/raw_escape_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (403, 6) ·
`arm1/state_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (265, 4)

All under `implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/`. Each package port is under
`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/` at the same basename.

## Why they are duplicates by MEASUREMENT, not by name

Each package file carries its bench original's whole `deftest` roster — same names, same count.
The discriminator separates the other class too: `arm1/first_registration_cljs_test.cljs` shares a
basename with a package file and is NOT one of these — 5 deftests against the package's 1, different
claims — because it is a RE-AUTHORED row (rf2-wjag). A basename match cannot make that distinction;
a roster comparison can.

## The drift has ALREADY happened

`presence_intent_dom_cljs_test`'s eighth row is
`presence-costs-three-hooks-and-the-shell-still-costs-two` in the bench tree and
`presence-costs-four-hooks-and-the-shell-still-costs-two` on the package. rf2-6tmu gave the
package's presence a root-scoped adoption window (a second `useContext`); the prototype never got
it. **BOTH ARE GREEN** — the assertion is over `(distinct tail)` and the fourth call collapses into
a name already present, so the entire divergence lives in the deftest NAME and the prose. That is
rf2-c78g's predicted failure mode ("the stale one keeps passing; nothing goes red to announce it")
observed five days after the ruling.

## Deletion safety, already measured

- **Reverse-dependency scan is CLEAN.** Each of the nine namespaces is named by its own `ns` form
  and nothing else in the repo.
- Two docstring mentions survive and NEITHER is a `:require`:
  `arm1/raw_escape_dom_cljs_test.cljs:6` wiki-links `front.codec-cljs-test` (both are in the nine,
  so they go together), and
  `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/roots_frames_support.cljs:53` cites
  `arm1.hframe-dom-cljs-test` as provenance. **The second dangles on deletion — this bead owns
  re-pointing it.**
- **No exception is available.** rf2-c78g measured the only recognised exception (a JVM host the
  package copy lacks) shut for this file class: `check_test_lane_bijection.py`'s `loadable_by`
  gives JVM lanes `.clj`/`.cljc` only. All nine are `.cljs`.

## THE BLOCKER — sequence, do not race

`implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/compile_gate.cjs` DERIVES the lane roster by
walking the directory rather than listing it (deliberately: "a roster in this file would be the
staleness class the gate exists to catch"). Deleting nine files changes what it compiles.
**rf2-bl0j is rewriting that gate right now**, and its version widens the walk to include the
`*_cljs_test.cljs` files these nine are.

**Sequence this AFTER rf2-bl0j's PR merges.** Do not race it.

`MIN_NAMESPACES` is NOT the obstacle and must not be quoted as one: it is 40 in both versions
against a lane of ~101 namespaces, so 92 clears it comfortably.

## Acceptance

- The nine bench originals deleted; `npm run test:hicasso-compile` green on the narrowed lane.
- `roots_frames_support.cljs`'s provenance citation re-pointed or restated.
- `npm run test:cljs` and `npm run test:browser` green (they select these namespaces by regexp,
  so the deletion must not orphan a require).
- The triage document's "The nine ports whose originals still stand" section updated to record
  execution.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7906 — fold this bounded documentation correction into this owner’s already-required triage-section update; do not open another Bead. The landed measurement and nine-file cleanup scope are sound, but prototype-suite-triage.md is now internally inconsistent in three places: (1) lines 86-87 say all nine pairs have the same deftest names and count, while lines 97 and 112-120 correctly record presence_intent’s one renamed row; describe eight identical rosters plus one measured drift instead. (2) lines 23-31 still call 15 PORT / 45 STAYS the standing verdict, although the new corrections at 348-361 explicitly reclassify front/codec and arm1/raw_escape from STAYS to executed PORT; the standing classification is therefore 17 PORT / 9 RE-AUTHORED / 43 STAYS, while the original 13/9/47 census remains dated history. (3) lines 37-38 say the current 61-file tree is 24,222 lines, while the new landed measurement at 101-102 and an independent landed-SHA count are 61 / 24,223. When recording the nine deletions, reconcile these summary/current-inventory statements and preserve the document’s deliberate dated-census convention; no broad renumbering or new tooling.

OUTSIDE_LANE_ENTRIES needed NO update and compile_gate.cjs is untouched: the nine live inside the walked directory (walk narrows 129 -> 120), and bl0j's roster names four files that all live outside hicasso/. No collision with the concurrent worker on that file.

title: hic: a testbed handler returned a v1-shaped top-level :dispatch-later, which the closed effect-map silently dropped
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-hic-016 PHASE-1 WORKER before it typed a single key, and it is the most valuable thing that dispatch produced. Repaired in PR #7896; this bead exists because the CLASS is wider than the two handlers it fixed, and because the gate that should have caught it was green throughout.

THE DEFECT. The testbed's `:tb/arm` handler returned a v1-shaped map with a TOP-LEVEL `:dispatch-later` sitting beside `:db`. re-frame2's effect map is CLOSED — `#{:db :rf.db/runtime :fx}` — so nothing carried the key and the timer was never scheduled. The armed edges NEVER FIRED. Measured: 15 seconds after the click the readout still read `armed`, while a plain `setTimeout(5000)` in the same page returned in 5006 ms.

WHY IT SURVIVED, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. The gate `armed-edges-are-wired` was GREEN IN THREE ENGINES the whole time, because it asserts the LABEL and that NOTHING HAS HAPPENED YET — and a dead timer satisfies "nothing has happened yet" perfectly. That is the exact fail-open shape this project hunts everywhere else: a check that verifies the absence of bad news rather than the presence of good news. It passed because the feature was broken in the one way the assertion could not distinguish from working.

WORSE, THESE WERE THE OPERATOR INSTRUMENTS. They were added in PR #7815 and sharpened in #7846 SPECIFICALLY to reach a live IME composition. So the instrument built to answer the operator's question had been inert since it landed, and every green run said otherwise.

WHAT #7896 ALREADY DID, so this bead does not redo it: both handlers fixed; the gate section now WAITS FOR THE FIRE behind a `?arm-ms=300` override (under a second per engine, not the thirty seconds the #7815 audit refused); pins updated (section 5 to 9, sum 91 to 95, TESTING.md twice). Sabotage-proven: sabotaged `:tb/arm` exits 1 with "the armed bump never fired within 5000ms", restored exits 0.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS — the class, not the instance:
1. SWEEP for other v1-shaped top-level effect keys returned by handlers anywhere in the tree. `:dispatch-later` is one spelling; `:dispatch`, `:dispatch-n`, `:deregister-event-handler` and any other v1 top-level effect would be dropped the same silent way. Search handler return maps, not the effect registry.
2. DECIDE whether the closed effect map should REFUSE an unknown top-level key rather than ignoring it. This is the real question and it is an operator-facing call: a refusal turns a silent no-op into a source-located error at the point of the mistake, which is this project's whole posture on crossings — but it is also a behaviour change on a hot path, and the stance rejects nag-diagnostics. **Do not implement a refusal without a ruling.** Establish the cost, state the case both ways, and surface it.
3. AUDIT the sibling assertions in the same testbed gate for the same fail-open shape: any row that asserts a label plus "nothing has happened yet" cannot distinguish armed-and-working from armed-and-dead.

DO NOT re-fix the two handlers, do not re-run the IME rig, and do not widen into unrelated testbed work.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED — PR #7940 (branch worker/fxrule-04tx). Option C shipped as ruled: a foreign top-level effect key (case a) or a non-sequential :fx value (case b) in the FINAL effects map aborts the event in-band, uniformly in every build — no :db, no :rf.db/runtime, no classification install, no :fx. Case (c), a malformed entry inside a well-shaped :fx vector, keeps :logged-and-skipped per-entry recovery; its channel promoted with the rest of the category.

SHAPE. events/police-effect-map-shape! + fx-value-ok? + police-final-effects! replaced by the PURE first-defect-or-nil carrier events/effect-map-defect (the elision/classification-effect-defect pattern). commit-fx-effects no longer polices and is NOT a second abort site: it projects the handler return VERBATIM so a handler-returned key and an :after-inserted key reach the same single check. router/emit-effect-map-shape! reuses the exact in-band arm of emit-legacy-runtime-root! / emit-classification-effect-shape! (no throw). The envelope arm is ordered FIRST among the three effect rejections. Always-on record carries :offending-key only; :value and :reason stay dev-trace; :failing-id == :event-id so emit-error-both!'s lift never drags :reason on. emit-fx-error! gained a record-attrs arity so all three cases share ONE record shape.

SPEC (hot-zone, flagged in the PR body). 009 row -> Channel always-on, per-case recovery cells, ONE row kept, NO count added. Spec-Schemas §:rf/effect-map drops the 'legal siblings still apply' promise for a/b. Conventions §No silent swallow gains one instance row. Implementor-Checklist runtime-shape-policing row + two-planes paragraph flip. migration M-8 hazard INVERTED. Fixtures bad-top-level-key + bad-fx-value FLIP (no commit, :fix-effect, always-on record asserted); bad-fx-entry + surplus-entry-field STAY as the control; conformance README updated. The :tags cell is UNCHANGED so the three-arm co-edit invariant needed no schema/exercise edit. api-manifest untouched; no facade export.

GATES, CAPTURED. core JVM 2239/11669 exit 0; prod-gate lane (-Dre-frame.debug=false) 1982/8684 exit 0 with the new namespace IN the roster (the no-build-fork witness); all 19 implementation artefacts green; tools/xray JVM 1289/6051 exit 0; npm run test:cljs 13336/67196 exit 0; python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0; check_doc_slugs exit 0; six static checkers exit 0; clj-kondo delta zero (all findings reproduce on origin/main). SABOTAGE BOTH WAYS: (A) shape-defect forced nil -> exit 1, 51 failures/4 errors, first red names effect_map_shape_record_cljs_test.cljc:125; (B) closed set narrowed to drop the four legal EP-0025 keys -> exit 1, 93 failures on the LEGAL path (sensitive-effect-records-path-and-redacts-at-egress etc). Restore verified by sha256sum -c, not git diff.

Mayor merges. Bead closed on PR open per protocol.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7940 (2026-08-12 AUSEST; completeness, correctness, implementation quality).

COMPLETENESS: the PR correctly puts one pure envelope check at the final-effects boundary, refuses foreign top-level keys and malformed :fx values without partial commit, retains per-entry :fx recovery, and updates the conformance/spec surface. The shipped rejection itself is complete.

CORRECTNESS: the new production egress is not bounded as claimed. `events/effect-map-defect` accepts any Clojure map key and returns it verbatim as `:offending-key`; `router/emit-effect-map-shape!` then lifts that value onto the always-on off-box record. A direct JVM witness with `{"secret-bearing-key" {:token "sekrit"}}` returns `{:offending-key "secret-bearing-key", ...}`. That violates Spec-Schemas' `EffectMapShapeTags` contract (`[:offending-key :keyword]`) and the PR's claim that the slot is safe app program structure; an arbitrary string, collection, or sensitive value used as a malformed key can survive production egress.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY: the single-boundary/pure-carrier architecture is otherwise crisp. Keep the refusal for every foreign key, but make the always-on discriminator total and bounded: preserve keyword keys, project every non-keyword key to one fixed framework keyword sentinel, and leave the raw key on the dev-only trace. Add a production-gate witness with a secret-bearing non-keyword key that pins both schema conformance and absence of the raw secret. No API widening or general diagnostic framework is needed.

This exact residual belongs here: rf2-04tx owns effect-map envelope refusal and its record shape. rf2-eg61l is not a duplicate owner; it covers the classification category's closed four-keyword domain.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED by the mayor 2026-08-12 — same revert. OPERATOR RULING UNCHANGED: Option C, REFUSE, landed as PR #7940. A foreign top-level key or a non-sequential :fx value now ABORTS THE EVENT IN-BAND at the router's final-effects boundary — nothing commits. Case (c), a malformed entry inside a well-shaped :fx vector, keeps :logged-and-skipped per-entry recovery; only its channel moved. THE GRANULARITY LINE IS THE COMMIT BOUNDARY. commit-fx-effects deliberately does NOT police and is NOT a second abort site, so a handler-returned key and an :after-inserted key reach the same check and get the same verdict. Its too-eager sabotage is the proof of exactness: narrowing the closed set to drop the four legal EP-0025 keys produced 93 failures ON THE LEGAL PATH.

title: hic-028b — rename defhost's :ssr to :server + a sibling :fallback (the canonical two-policy spelling)
description:
# hic-028b — the `:ssr` -> `:server` + `:fallback` rename

Split out of rf2-hic-028 (portal helper + host server-policy witnesses),
whose PR landed the portal and the missing server-policy witness and
DELIBERATELY did not take this. Reasons, all verifiable at source:

## What the rename is

`defhost`'s declaration option is spelled `:ssr` today with THREE legal
values -- `:client-only`, `{:fallback <hiccup>}`, `:render`
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs`,
`declared-ssr` + `host-options` = `#{:callbacks :slots :ssr}`).

Every normative source spells it as TWO policies plus a sibling option:

- `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md`:11-14
  -- "one of two v0 policies: Render / Client-only", the fallback
  optional and belonging to Client-only.
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/ergonomics-api.md`:58 -- the
  `n/defcomponent` ABI, verbatim: `{:server :render}` / `{:server
  :client-only}`, omission means Client-only.
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md` row 21 -- recommendation
  "keep `:server`", status `open`.
- The 22-chapter draft guide is uniform on it: ch09:58 says "The
  declaration takes four options: `:callbacks`, `:slots`, `:server`, and
  `:fallback`", and ch06/09/10/17/19 agree
  (`draft-guide/REWRITE-NOTES.md`:17-18 records the verification).

So: `:ssr` -> `:server` with values `#{:client-only :render}`, and
`:fallback` hoisted to a sibling declaration option legal only under
Client-only (Render + `:fallback` refuses -- the guide already teaches
that refusal, under the EXISTING id
`:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy`, so no id is minted or retired).

## Why rf2-hic-028 did not take it

1. **It is spec/009 hot-zone work on rows the bead did not introduce.**
   Two live catalogue rows describe the option by name and would go
   factually wrong: `:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy` (its
   description names `:ssr` and "the three the policy admits"; its
   sixth-column payload key IS `:ssr`) and
   `:rf.error/hicasso-host-fallback-boundary-head` (description `:ssr
   {:fallback ...}`, recovery keyword
   `:write-inert-hiccup-or-declare-ssr-render`). Both have parallel rows
   in `docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md`. hic-028's dispatch
   fence permitted appending a row for a NEW refusal and forbade
   changing any row it did not introduce.
2. **`docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md` is the rename's own record** --
   HD-011's addendum, the rf2-l0wfx third-value ruling and the roster
   `#{:callbacks :ssr}` all spell `:ssr` there across ~10 passages -- and
   it was fenced to a concurrent docs worker (rf2-dwku).
3. **The naming ledger's header rule is "nobody renames mid-flow"**, and
   row 21 is still `open`. Row 23's precedent (rf2-0ckh reconciling the
   test kit) shows an open recommendation MAY be applied as a default --
   which is why this is a bead rather than a refusal -- but it wants to
   be one deliberate pass, not a side effect of a portal PR.

## Scope when it runs

- `impl/codec.cljs`: `host-options`, `declared-ssr` -> the two-value
  policy + a separate `:fallback` read, `mint-host!`'s gate selection,
  `host-ssr` -> `host-server`, and every docstring/comment naming `:ssr`
  (the ns docstring, `mint-host!`, `mint-host-gate!`,
  `refuse-deferring-heads-in-fallback!`, `host-element`).
- `re_frame/hicasso.cljc`: `defhost`'s docstring block.
- `impl/portal.cljs`: the declaration reads `{:slots #{:fallback} :ssr
  :render}` and its docstrings explain the `:ssr`/surface distinction --
  both respell.
- Tests: `host_ssr_dom_cljs_test`, `fallback_contents_cljs_test`,
  `portal_dom_cljs_test`, and any test-kit server-policy reader
  (`:rf.error/hicasso-test-not-a-host` names one).
- Catalogues: the two spec/009 rows + the two complaints.md rows above.
  HOT ZONE -- sequence, do not parallel with another spec/009 bead.
- `docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md` -- only once rf2-dwku has landed.
- Naming-ledger row 21 moves off `open`.

## Acceptance

Zero `:ssr` option spellings in `implementation/hicasso/**` (the frame
metadata key `:ssr` in core, and `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`, are a
DIFFERENT surface and stay); ch09:58's four-option sentence true as
written; the existing refusal id unchanged; gates green (focused hicasso
node lane, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run build:hicasso-release`,
`check_complaint_catalogue.py`, `check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py`,
fast-PR spine).
notes:
MAYOR — SEQUENCING, 2026-08-11. This bead is CORRECTLY SCOPED and NOT yet dispatchable. Recording why, so the next reader does not mistake the hold for neglect.

ITS SURFACE IS HELD. rf2-mo4o renames declared-ssr and host-options in implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs. The rf2-hic-028 worker holds that exact file right now and its PR #7892 is OPEN and unmerged. Two workers on one file is how two changes silently revert each other, so this waits for #7892 to merge — it does not wait on a decision.

the stamped server node, while its tray-free control adopts cleanly; its hand-scoped control changes

`codec/adopted?` is false during server rendering and hydration's first pass, and true on a fresh
client mount. Its inverse is exactly the fact presence needs to decide whether a newly encountered
child is born present. React documents that `getServerSnapshot` is used both while generating server
HTML and during hydration's initial client render
([`useSyncExternalStore`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore#adding-support-for-server-rendering)).

needs no mutable request state, and works for direct React server APIs as well as any future Hicasso
server entry. Keep the root window for mismatch attribution; do not build a public server renderer or
request provider solely for presence.

  renders, no React/framework mismatch, and retention of stamped server nodes; retain a fresh
  `createRoot` control that begins `:mounting`, plus the existing multi-root attribution and teardown

title: mayor-method: the posture loop carries only half the stance, so every brief it shapes loses the restraining clauses
description:
FOUND BY THE HOURLY METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-11. The mayor's own drift check found drift in the mayor's own command files. Both files below are TRACKED, so the mayor cannot fix them — the mayor-side commit guard refused the staged edit, correctly, which is how this became a bead.

## SITE 1 — .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md (the real defect, P2)

That file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the stance the mayor injects VERBATIM into every dispatch preamble. It has not been touched in two months, and it currently states the stance as only:

  "primary lenses ELEGANCE + CLARITY + CORRECTNESS + GOOD PRACTICE; no back-compat shims; perf/completeness serve the lenses"

THE OPERATOR'S ACTUAL STANDING STANCE IS ROUGHLY TWICE THAT, and every clause missing from it is a clause that RESTRAINS a worker:
  - POWER is a fifth lens, absent entirely.
  - NOT over-engineering and NOT gold-plating.
  - TRUST THE PROGRAMMER — the goal is high productivity for them and the AI they use, via a library with excellent ergonomics, a minimal API, excellent tools and low friction.
  - We do not need to litigate every last fine detail or drown in minutiae: reject over-engineering and nag-diagnostics AT TRIAGE, and CLOSE minutiae rather than actioning it.
  - An audit finding is a CLAIM, not automatically work; the mayor may reject stale, moot or over-engineered remedies.
  - A source-located REFUSAL is an acceptable and possibly correct deliverable.

WHY THE ASYMMETRY MATTERS, and it is the point of this bead. The five lenses tell a worker what good looks like. The clauses after them tell it WHEN TO STOP. A file carrying only the first half does not read as incomplete — it reads as a stance that wants more of everything, which is precisely the failure mode ("preserve everything just in case", gold-plating, nag-diagnostics) the second half exists to prevent. So the omission is not neutral; it biases every brief the loop shapes.

EVIDENCE THAT THE MISSING HALF IS LOAD-BEARING: in one session, three of six dispatches came back as reasoned REFUSALS (rf2-jkdy, rf2-5gka, rf2-u5b4) and each was worth more than the work would have been — a migration performed on a false premise costs far more than a bead. A worker briefed only on the five lenses has no licence to return one.

ALSO MISSING: the operator's standing request for ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English in CHAT replies — short sentences, active voice, one idea per sentence, technical names (bead ids, paths, commands) kept exact. He has asked repeatedly and the drift returns within about ten turns, so it belongs in the recurring loop rather than in a session's memory. It applies to CHAT ONLY; bead text, PR bodies and documents keep their own register.

WHAT TO WRITE. Restructure the file so the stance is a single quoted block that can be pasted verbatim, followed by a short paragraph explaining which half restrains and why a paraphrase drops it; then the voice rule; then the existing one-line orchestration-not-implementation reassertion, unchanged. Widen the drift-detection list at the end, which currently names only mayor-coding, missing worktree-boundary block, absent stance and --admin misuse: add "stance PARAPHRASED rather than pasted", "minutiae actioned instead of closed", and "an audit finding dispatched without its premise checked at source". Keep the front-matter description line as it is.
DO NOT let this grow into a second copy of bootstrap.md. It is one command file; the method document remains authoritative for the reasoning.

## SITE 2 — .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md, clause 1 (trivial, P4-sized, do it while there)

Clause 1 gives the rollup band as "~86". Measured 2026-08-11, PRs #7874 and #7875 both carried 91 checks. Refresh the figure to ~91 with that date and those two PR numbers as the evidence, and ADD one sentence recording that the band MOVES as the workflow matrix grows — it read ~86 earlier in the same programme — because that is exactly why the clause already tells the reader to measure rather than trust the constant. Change nothing else in that file; the rest was updated three hours ago and is current.

## WHAT IS NOT DRIFTING, verified in the same pass — do not touch these
mayor-dispatch.md (updated 4h ago, carries the current routing rule and matches bootstrap.md), mayor-hygiene.md (updated 9h ago, carries the six reap-proxies, the husk modes and the SendMessage liveness signal), mayor-cluster.md (2 months old but still matches dispatch-prompt-template.md Shape 4 exactly). The three method documents under docs/the-mayor-method/ are themselves current; the drift is one-way, from method into these command files.

BOUNDED REPAIR: point the dispatch command/template at the verbatim mayor-posture.md block and reconcile/remove the stale bootstrap constant. Keep rf2-uqh6 closed; its scratchpad collision repair is complete.
