title: hic: promote the capability-receipt design — one per-attempt tap, five derived fields, self-time killed
description:
PROMOTION OWED BY THE rf2-hic-081 SPIKE. The spike graduated NO code (its surface line says "nothing retained without graduation"), but it produced a design finding that must reach a tracked record or it is lost. The full verdict is on rf2-hic-081; this bead owns landing it.

THE FINDING. Five of the six named receipt fields need NO tap on any hot loop. They are derivable post hoc, at the end of an attempt, from state the runtime already retains:
  - read calls   = the scratch array's length (read-key! already pushes every call)
  - unique reads = its distinct count
  - cache hits   = whether !cells holds a live reaction for each scratch key
  - codec nodes  = a walk of the returned element
  - attempts     = counted at the tap
THE LOAD-BEARING STEP is that the cache-hit answer is STABLE ACROSS THE ATTEMPT, because cold-read! retains nothing and the generation fence guarantees a pass observes one commit. That is what deletes the per-read counter.

RESULT: ONE TAP, IN run-once, PER ATTEMPT — the same cost class as the bodyRuns increment already there, three orders of magnitude below a per-read or per-node tap. Attempts and commits stay on two seams (the existing evidence sink's :commit already counts commits) rather than becoming a flag on one record.

MEASURED, on two boundaries with opposite profiles:
  {:view "spike/deep" :attempts 1 :read-calls 4 :unique-reads 3 :cache-hits 0 :codec-nodes 2}
  {:view "spike/wide" :attempts 2 :read-calls 2 :unique-reads 1 :cache-hits 0 :codec-nodes 22}
Gate: 530 tests / 2465 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors; the 524 pre-existing tests unmoved by the tap. Cache hits answered both ways (4 of 4 once the read set was committed). Attached-only allocation PROVEN and negatively controlled: 20 detached renders attach nothing and leave no table, and a render after detach! re-attaches nothing.

SELF TIME IS KILLED, and this is a decision, not a deferral. It is the only underivable field and the only one putting an instrument inside the body. Chrome clamps performance.now() to 100 microseconds while the quantity is single-digit microseconds (this repo's frozen standard: 6.8-12.6 us marginal cost PER CELL). Per-attempt intervals therefore read 0-or-100 us, giving relative error ~sqrt(19/n) — 10% would need ~1,900 attempts per boundary. Worse, the observer effect scales as n_i*c, PROPORTIONAL TO ATTEMPT COUNT rather than true cost, so two boundaries close in true time but different in attempt count INVERT. An independent corollary kills the naive codec tap too: as-element costs 8.9 ns/child (this repo's walk_vs_reagent_app table), so a per-node deref+nil-test lands proportional to child count — precisely the axis a hot-view ranking discriminates on.

WHERE IT GOES: docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md section 11, and docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/left-field-ideas.md under "Capability receipts". A suggested section-11 row is recorded on rf2-hic-081 — read it there rather than re-deriving.

SEQUENCING — THIS IS WHY THE BEAD EXISTS RATHER THAN A ROUTED MESSAGE. Both target files were held by the doctruth-dsnq worker when the spike finished, so the spike correctly did not edit them. Land this only AFTER that worker's PR merges, and re-read both files as they then stand.

ACCEPTANCE ALSO INCLUDES THE WITNESS THE SPIKE DID NOT TAKE. Cache-hit stability is presently ARGUED from invariant 5, not sabotage-witnessed. The spike named that witness as "the first thing a graduated counts receipt owes". If this bead graduates the design as code rather than only as a record, the witness lands with it; if it lands as a record only, say on the record that the witness is still owed.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7882: BOUNDED DOC CORRECTION. specification.md:357 promises derived attempt facts with “no hot-loop tap”, while left-field-ideas.md:31 says the receipt costs one tap per attempt at run-once; the retained spike implementation confirms that sink deref/nil-test tap. State the actual design consistently: one per-attempt tap, with no per-read or per-node tap. Also, left-field-ideas.md:29 still promises codec nodes/props/foreign/intents, but rf2-hic-081 and its retained spike derive/witness only codec nodes among that group. Narrow the adopted list to the decided fields or mark props/foreign/intents as undecided; do not imply they graduated. Runtime remains untouched. The separate stale decision-brief roster is already exactly owned by open rf2-sxl5; do not duplicate it.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7890 — REOPEN. The new exactly-one-tap-per-attempt claim is false for abrupt attempts in retained spike fece72f80a: collector.cljs increments bodyRuns, then evaluates the body and codec/as-element before record-attempt!, so a thrown body, Suspense promise, or lowering failure records no receipt. Define whether receipt attempts include abrupt outcomes. If yes, make recording exception-safe with explicit unavailable/partial facts and witness a thrown/Suspense attempt; otherwise narrow the documents to completed attempts. No production runtime implementation is required by this bounded correction.
close_reason: Decided YES: abrupt attempts count. An attempt is counted from the moment its body is entered, so a thrown body, a Suspense promise and a failed lowering are recorded attempts; codec nodes reads the envelope's unknown rather than zero, while read calls / unique reads / cache hits stay derivable because the scratch is cleared at the START of an attempt. Confirmed the audit at source in fece72f80a (bodyRuns at :1593 before the try; record-attempt! at :1608 inside the let, after codec/as-element). Two things did not hold as briefed: the spike code is NOT on main (no impl/receipt.cljs), so there is no runtime to make exception-safe and the correction is purely to the design record; and run-once ALREADY has the finally the fix needs, so exception-safety relocates the one tap rather than adding one. Decision argued from three independent grounds: bodyRuns already counts abrupt runs and would silently disagree; specification.md section 10 already requires an attempt outcome and already names throw/abandoned work; Suspense throws on every attempt until data arrives. Thrown/Suspense witness recorded as OWED alongside the cache-hit-stability witness. No runtime work. PR #7898.

title: hic test kit: the virtual clock crosses the real-timer boundary lossily
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7861 — correctness finding in the new virtual-clock boundary.

Two concrete cases contradict the implementation's own interoperability promises:

1. VIRTUAL IDS CAN ALIAS LIVE PLATFORM IDS. The saved platform scheduler returns numeric browser timer ids, while the virtual scheduler restarts its own numeric sequence at 1. `disarm!` decides whether to delegate to the real clearer only by looking for that number in `:pending`. If a pre-install real timer and a virtual timer have the same id, `clearTimeout`/`clearInterval` clears the virtual timer and leaves the real one alive; after the virtual timer fires, a normal cleanup clearing its stale id can instead cancel the unrelated real timer. The docstring says the unknown/pre-install case remains honest, but the two id domains are not disjoint.

2. INTERVAL HANDOVER LOSES ITS NEXT DEADLINE. `release-clock!` promises every outstanding timer is re-armed with the time it had left. Timeouts use `(:due e) - now`; intervals call the saved `setInterval` with the full period. A 1000 ms interval released after 999 virtual ms therefore fires after another 1000 ms, not the promised 1 ms, shifting its phase.

BOUNDED REPAIR: give virtual handles a collision-free identity while the wrapper is installed, preserving the browser rule that either clearer can cancel either timer kind. At final release, preserve an interval's remaining first deadline and then its original cadence. The existing statement that handles cannot clear a timer after handover may remain; do not grow this into a general fake-timers framework.

PROVENANCE: PR #7861 merge c3b64aa4c02c75f15ecca6b424bf7e34437ff037, `implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs`.
acceptance_criteria: Add deterministic browser-level controls with no wall-clock sleeps: (a) a captured/stubbed real timer and a virtual timer cannot alias, and clearing each — including clearTimeout/clearInterval cross-use — reaches only its own scheduler; (b) a periodic timer advanced to one millisecond before its tick and then handed back asks the captured real scheduler for a one-millisecond first delay, then resumes the original period. Preserve callback arguments and the existing Date.now/settle semantics.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7883: mounted.cljs:341-345 invokes the first handed-over interval callback before arming the real setInterval. If that callback throws, control never reaches the re-arm and the interval silently dies. The HTML timer algorithm reports the handler exception and then reinitializes a still-live repeating timer (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/timers-and-user-prompts.html#timer-initialisation-steps, steps 9.7 and 9.11). The witness at test_kit_clock_dom_cljs_test.cljs:629-641 covers only a successful callback. BOUNDED REPAIR: guarantee re-arming with try/finally or equivalent while preserving exception reporting, and add a recorder witness whose first bridged callback throws but later cadence remains armed. Keep rf2-4mvd closed.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7902. release-clock! re-arms the handed-back interval's cadence in a finally, so a throwing first tick no longer disarms it, and the throw still escapes to be reported — both halves of HTML's timer initialisation steps 9.7/9.11. Witness W8 (a-throwing-tick-does-not-disarm-the-handed-back-interval) in test_kit_clock_dom_cljs_test.cljs; proved red under the planted pre-fix behaviour (captured exit 1, 2 failures both in that row) and green restored (byte-hash verified). Gates: npm run test:browser exit 0 (1264 tests), npm run test:cljs exit 0 (13267 tests), scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0. rf2-4mvd left closed.

title: core: adapter use-frame memoises on the frame keyword, so a same-id reincarnation keeps serving the destroyed frame's bundle
description:
`re-frame.adapter.use-frame/use-frame` in CORE — used by the UIx adapter, which is first-class and actively supported — memoises its ops bundle on the resolved frame KEYWORD, compared by `=`.

THE DEFECT: a frame keyword is `=` across a same-id reincarnation. So after a frame is destroyed and recreated under the same id, that hook keeps handing out THE DESTROYED INCARNATION'S `capture-frame` bundle for the remainder of the mount. Nothing signals it; the keyword still compares equal, the memo still hits, and the consumer holds a bundle addressed to a frame that no longer exists.

THIS IS THE WARM HALF OF THE rf2-hic-013 FAILURE, IN CORE RATHER THAN IN HICASSO. The same class was already diagnosed and fixed on the Hicasso side; this is the same mistake living in the shared adapter surface, where it reaches every UIx consumer.

PROVENANCE: found by the rf2-hic-031 worker (PR #7855) while building `n/use-frame`. It did NOT touch it — outside its fence, and core's contract is core's to rule on. Correct conduct: it reported rather than followed.

WHY HICASSO'S OWN HOOK IS NOT AFFECTED, which is also the shape of the likely fix: `n/use-frame` keys on `impl.frames`' INCARNATION ROW rather than on the keyword, so a reincarnation is a different key and the memo correctly misses. A frame keyword is an ADDRESS, not an identity — the same distinction `native.cljc` draws about component names, and the same one that makes memoising on the keyword wrong here.

VERIFY BEFORE FIXING: read the current `use-frame` and confirm the memo key is still the keyword. Then establish whether any consumer DEPENDS on the bundle surviving a reincarnation before changing it — a memo that starts missing where it used to hit will re-run work, and that is a behaviour change for UIx consumers even though it is the correct one.

A WITNESS ALREADY EXISTS TO COPY THE SHAPE FROM: `native_hooks_dom_cljs_test`'s W6 (landing in PR #7855) drives exactly the destroy-and-recreate that would catch this. Any fix here needs a witness that reds without it — a same-id reincarnation, then a read through the hook, asserting it reaches the LIVE incarnation and not the dead one.

SURFACE: `implementation/core/**` (the adapter's use-frame) plus its witness. Not hot-zone, but core is a shared surface — check what else is in flight before dispatching.
close_reason:
Landed via PR #7868 (merged, rebased onto main). Green on all five merge clauses at 91/91, five runs completed/success, no workflow commits after its base. Clean reap on the worker's report; canary held at 103/2933/2.

THE PREMISE HELD, and the worker established it rather than accepting it — which mattered, because this bead came from ANOTHER worker's reading (rf2-hic-031's) and I had not independently confirmed it. The memo condition was `(if (and (some? prev) (= (aget prev 0) frame)) …)`, and `frame` comes from `frame/require-current-frame!`, whose own docstring says it returns "the frame stamp (id)" — a keyword. An ADDRESS compared by `=`.

THE OTHER HALF IS WHAT MAKES IT A BUG RATHER THAN A SMELL, and it is the part neither I nor the filing worker had: `make-capture-frame` PINS the incarnation live at capture (rf2-9pyles), and BOTH `capture-dispatch!` and `capture-subscribe!` REFUSE a superseded target (rf2-tdjv7p). Pinned bundle behind an address-keyed memo means that after a same-id reincarnation the hook served the DEAD incarnation's bundle for the rest of the mount, with EVERY OPERATION THROUGH IT SILENTLY RECOVERING.

THE FIX: key on the frame AND `frame/frame-incarnation-token` (the `:drain-lock` identity) by `identical?`. A `nil` token is a legitimate key rather than a special case — it pairs with the unpinned, address-directed capture `capture-frame` makes when the id is not live, and the frame appearing later moves it off `nil`.

BLAST RADIUS ESTABLISHED AND NOT MATERIAL, so no decision was needed: callers are the UIx re-export (every UIx consumer), four example sites, one template site, five freehand bench sites and the suite probe. Steady state costs one registry read per render — atom deref plus map lookup, no allocation — less than the `capture-frame` a miss performs, and negligible beside the neighbouring `use-subscribe`. THE DECISIVE ARGUMENT: the memo now misses only where it previously hit WRONGLY, and no consumer can depend on the bundle surviving a reincarnation BECAUSE CORE'S OWN FENCE ALREADY REFUSES EVERY OP ON IT — "surviving" means "silently dead".

THE WITNESS DISCRIMINATES, and avoided the trap I flagged in the brief: NOTHING ASSERTS EQUALITY, because the dead and live bundles compare `=` — that is the disguise. Three of four rows red with the fix broken, verbatim: `(not (identical? ops-1 ops-2))` → `(not (not true))`, and twice `(= 7 (:n (rf/app-db-value uf-frame)))` → `(not (= 7 100))` for the post- and pre-reincarnation bundles. THE STABILITY CONTROL PASSED under sabotage, which is the right result — the memo worked; only its key was an address.

FOLLOW-UP FILED, and it is the sharpest thing here: rf2-ow4e. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` and `spec/API.md` say the bundle is "reference-stable across re-renders for the same resolved frame" — a sentence A KEYWORD-KEYED MEMO SATISFIES PERFECTLY. The spec described the buggy behaviour as the contract. Dispatched.

A frame keyword is an ADDRESS, not an IDENTITY — the third time this session that distinction has been a defect's root.

title: mayor-method: the post-merge pull aborts for an undocumented cause and the documented remedy is inert
description:
THE POST-MERGE PULL NOW ABORTS FOR A CAUSE THE DOCS DO NOT NAME, AND THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY DOES NOTHING FOR IT. Hit three times in one session.

WHAT THE DOCS SAY. CLAUDE.md (two places) and the method treat a pull abort as caused by an UNCOMMITTED .beads/issues.jsonl — message "local changes would be overwritten" — with the fixed remedy: checkpoint, then `git checkout HEAD -- .beads`, then pull. bootstrap.md:211 mentions "Not possible to fast-forward" but only as one of three symptoms of a racing automated push, whose stated remedy is naming the remote and branch.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS NOW. `sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` COMMITS. So by the time the pull runs, .beads is clean and there is nothing to clear — and the pull still aborts, with "fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.", because the local checkpoint COMMIT has diverged from origin's newer commits. The post-merge audit hook pushes to main asynchronously seconds after each merge, so origin gains commits while the mayor gains its own. Measured tonight: div=1/2, then div=2/9.

THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY IS INERT HERE. Clearing an uncommitted file that does not exist changes nothing, and naming the remote and branch does not fast-forward a divergent branch. The working remedy is:

  git pull --rebase origin main

then VERIFY THE OUTCOME rather than the message: no rebase in progress (.git/rebase-merge and .git/rebase-apply both absent), clean `git status`, HEAD == origin/main, and the tracker row count equal in the working file and at HEAD.

WHY THIS IS WORTH ONE PARAGRAPH RATHER THAN NOTHING: the loop hits this after nearly every merge now, so a mayor following the documented sequence will clear .beads for no reason, see the same abort, and have no next step. Worse, the two causes have DIFFERENT REMEDIES and one of them (the checkout) is dangerous in the wrong order — CLAUDE.md documents that clearing .beads after a bd close reverts the close.

THE FIX: distinguish the two aborts by their MESSAGE, which is unambiguous.
  - "local changes would be overwritten" -> uncommitted tracker state. Checkpoint, checkout, pull. (Unchanged.)
  - "Not possible to fast-forward" -> your own committed checkpoint has diverged from a racing push. `git pull --rebase origin main`, then verify the tree.

SURFACE: .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md is where the post-merge step lives; CLAUDE.md's two bullets name the cause. Make them agree rather than saying it twice differently. docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md:211 already has the symptom and may only need a pointer.

A RELATED TRAP TO MENTION IN THE SAME BREATH, because it defeats any fallback written carelessly: `git pull --ff-only ... | tail -1 || fallback` NEVER RUNS THE FALLBACK — a pipeline's exit status is its last command's. Redirect to a file, capture the code, then trim for display. I wrote exactly that bug into the merge loop tonight while briefing workers not to.

FENCE: this is a documentation fix, one paragraph plus a pointer. Do not add a script, a wrapper or a retry loop.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7833 (2026-08-11): the two-abort diagnosis and message-based branch are correct, but the fast-forward-divergence remedy omits the push required by its own outcome check. The authoritative block says `git pull --rebase origin main`, then requires `HEAD == origin/main`. A rebase preserves the local checkpoint commit by replaying it on top of origin, so before a push HEAD is necessarily ahead, not equal.

The repo captured the exact live counterexample on the first use immediately after this PR: main reflog records `084e142164 ... pull --rebase origin main (finish) ... onto 450dae1c` (#7833); 084e's sole parent is 450dae1c and its subject is `chore(beads): checkpoint`. `git rev-list --left-right --count 084e142164...450dae1c` is `1 0`. The rebase succeeded and preserved the checkpoint, yet the documented equality check was impossible. Repeating pull stays ahead; forcing equality would discard the checkpoint the drill exists to protect.

Keep the repair in the one authoritative surface: after a successful rebase, push the rebased checkpoint to origin (retry fetch/rebase/push if the asynchronous writer wins again), then verify the remote and local refs agree and the ledger row is present. Alternatively state the pre-push `ahead 1 / behind 0` condition, then push and verify equality. Do not add a wrapper or retry subsystem. The pointer surfaces need changes only if their short `then verify` wording becomes false.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7833 finding ACCEPTED. QUEUED — all six worker slots are full; the surface (.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md) is free and this goes out at the next opening.

THE FINDING, and it is exact: the two-abort diagnosis and the message-based branch are correct, but THE FAST-FORWARD-DIVERGENCE REMEDY OMITS THE PUSH REQUIRED BY ITS OWN OUTCOME CHECK. The block says `git pull --rebase origin main`, then requires HEAD == origin/main. But A REBASE PRESERVES THE LOCAL CHECKPOINT COMMIT BY REPLAYING IT ON TOP OF ORIGIN — so before a push, HEAD is NECESSARILY AHEAD BY ONE, never equal. The documented equality check is unsatisfiable at the point the drill asks for it.

THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IS MY OWN RUN, captured on the FIRST USE immediately after that PR merged. main's reflog records 084e142164 ... pull --rebase origin main (finish) ... onto 450dae1c (#7833). 084e's sole parent is 450dae1c and its subject is chore(beads): checkpoint. git rev-list --left-right --count 084e142164...450dae1c is "1 0". The rebase SUCCEEDED and preserved the checkpoint, and the documented check was still impossible. Repeating the pull stays ahead; forcing equality would DISCARD THE CHECKPOINT THE DRILL EXISTS TO PROTECT.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING BEYOND THE FIX: my actual practice is already correct — checkpoint, pull/rebase, checkpoint, PUSH, then verify HEAD == origin/main, and it has been right through ten merges tonight. THE DOCUMENT DESCRIBES A SUBSET OF WHAT I DO, and the missing step is the one that makes its own verification possible. A drill that cannot be followed as written will be followed as remembered, which is exactly how it drifts.

AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT A CORRECTION REPRODUCED THE CLASS IT WAS CORRECTING: a PR proving a dependency false then miscounted requirers the same way; a lint repair whose new rows all passed while the rule it added was wrong; and now a pull-abort drill that omits the step its own check needs. Corrections are written under the belief that the fault has been understood, which is precisely when the next instance is least visible.

BOUNDED REPAIR, from the audit: keep it in the ONE AUTHORITATIVE SURFACE. After a successful rebase, push the rebased checkpoint to origin — retrying fetch/rebase/push if the asynchronous audit writer wins the race again — then verify the remote and local refs agree and the ledger row is present. Alternatively state the pre-push "ahead 1" as the EXPECTED state and move the equality check to after the push. Either is fine; say which and why.

DO NOT restructure the block, and do not add a script or wrapper — the surrounding text was deliberately kept to one inline block so a mayor mid-loop reads it without opening another file.
close_reason:
PR #7841 merged. AUDIT #7833's finding is closed: the drill's own outcome check is now reachable.

REPAIR (b) CHOSEN — state the pre-push 'ahead 1' as EXPECTED, then push, then verify — and the worker's reasoning for preferring it over (a) is about the mayor, not the mechanics: (b) subsumes (a) since the push is named either way, but it additionally names THE STATE A MAYOR ACTUALLY OBSERVES MID-DRILL. Its words: the failure mode is not 'forgot to push', it is a mayor seeing an unexplained inequality and reaching for reset --hard, DESTROYING THE CHECKPOINT THE DRILL EXISTS TO PROTECT. A step you are told to take without being told what you will see is a step people improvise around.

It verified the counterexample in the repo rather than trusting my brief: 084e142164 is chore(beads): checkpoint, sole parent 450dae1c (#7833's own commit), rev-list --left-right --count giving 1 0.

The push's rejection case (the audit-hook race) is ONE CLAUSE — fetch, rebase, push again — not a retry subsystem. The four outcome reads are unchanged; they now run AFTER the push, where they are answerable. One inline block, no restructure, no script. CLAUDE.md and bootstrap.md untouched, because their 'then verify' wording does not become false — CLAUDE.md's equality sentence resumes the ordinary --ff-only flow where no local commit exists.

IT PROVED A GATE'S BLIND SPOT RATHER THAN CLAIMING A GREEN: a bogus anchor planted in docs/index.md gave exit 1; the same planted in .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md gave EXIT 0 WITH ZERO OUTPUT. So neither check_doc_slugs.py nor mkdocs validates the file this PR changed — it read the sentence by hand and claimed nothing more.

It also hit the harness-vs-.exit-file trap itself and diagnosed it correctly as SELF-INFLICTED: its concurrent plant experiment had docs/index.md mid-plant when the spine's anchor step read it. Incidentally a live demonstration that the spine really runs that validator and really goes red on it.

title: hic lint: six more binding forms are missing from direct-view-call's roster, each a build-blocking false ERROR
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-hic-022 worker (PR #7818) AFTER its own repair landed, each reproduced as a live false ERROR at the CI pin (2026.04.15). Fenced out of its bead, so filed here.

THE DEFECT CLASS. The export README says the check "refuses any call whose name has been rebound", but the roster of binding forms it actually reads is FINITE. Six binding forms are not in it, so a legal local bound by any of them is reported as a direct view call — at ERROR, which STOPS THE BUILD. This is the same build-blocking programmer-friction class that reopened rf2-hic-022 twice.

THE SIX, with the worker's probes:
  dotimes                 (dotimes [v 3] (v))
  this-as                 (this-as v (v))
  reify method param      (reify Object (toString [v] (str (v))))
  specify! method param   (specify! (js-obj) Object (toString [v] (str (v))))
  extend-type method param (extend-type T Object (toString [v] (str (v))))
  defmethod param         (defmethod mm :k [v] (v))

`dotimes` is literally one symbol short in the let-shaped set. The other five are one small arm each, of the same class as the existing `catch` and `as->` arms. Reuse `fn-locals` where the form is a fn tail — PR #7818 showed a fnspec IS a fn tail and deleted code by delegating to it rather than adding a branch.

FENCES, inherited and still binding: keep the SMALL syntax-local walker and the conservative whole-form silencing. NO whole-program analysis. **Do not use api/resolve** — PR #7804 established by probe that it returns nil for the cases that matter and never sees locals. A binding silences the whole form it heads; silence is the only failure these hooks are permitted, and the README says so.

WITNESS, DERIVED FROM THE GRAMMAR NOT FROM YOUR FIX — this is the instruction that finally worked on this surface. For each of the six, enumerate the form's legal shapes and drive each as an independent negative row, where the view's name is THE ONLY THING bound in that row so it cannot pass on a neighbour's coverage. Add at least one POSITIVE row per form too: a genuine self-call inside the same construct must still fire, which guards the over-silencing direction. State in the PR body which shapes you drove AND which you did not, with reasons — the second list is the valuable half.

MUTATION PROOF: revert each arm, quote the verbatim red, restore BYTE-IDENTICALLY and confirm green. Verify the mutation actually applied before believing any result — PR #7818 did this by sha256 before and after plus a token grep, because a worker on this exact surface had a heredoc silently mangle a mutation so that none applied while the suite reported green.

TREE-WIDE ACCOUNTING, to #7804's and #7818's standard: clj-kondo at the pin over lint.yml's exact path list, cold cache both sides; report errors and warnings before and after and diff the sorted finding sets. Both prior PRs held at errors 0 / warnings 4542 with an empty diff.

USE THE PINNED ALIAS: `clojure -M:clj-kondo` gives 2026.04.15; the npm binary on this host is 2025.10.23, and a pass from a mismatched version proves nothing either way.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7829 (2026-08-11) — REOPEN THIS EXACT ROSTER OWNER; no duplicate. WHAT HOLDS: all four authored/landed patch ids match; the first-arity witness is discriminating; the added binding-parameter rows and shared read-shadow repair pass the live export gate at the CI pin. GAP 1, FALSE ERROR: cljs.core/areduce is still absent. Its grammar is (areduce a idx ret init expr), and macroexpand binds idx plus ret in a loop. With ret initialized to (fn [x] x), a legal (ret idx) in expr is reported as re-frame.hicasso/direct-view-call at ERROR when ret shares the enclosing view name. The pinned stdin probe reproduced exit 3. Add the bounded core-form arm and a negative row whose ret is callable; no scope engine. GAP 2, FALSE SILENCE INTRODUCED HERE: fn-tail-locals feeds method lists to fn-locals, which adds the method HEAD as an optional named-fn self binding. A reify/extend method name is not lexical. The README now states the false rule that a method binds its own name. Pinned probe: (h/defview toString [_] ... (reify Object (toString [_] (toString nil)))) returns zero findings, although the correctly-arity view call is a real direct self-call. Separate letfn fnspec reading (include its local function name) from method reading (parameters of every arity only); add the same-name positive control while preserving all method-parameter negatives. Do not broaden beyond these grammar fixes.
MAYOR RULING — the amap extension is ACCEPTED, not trimmed.

The worker went one symbol beyond the audit's letter, flagged it prominently in the PR body so it could be trimmed, and asked. That is the right way to raise it, and the answer is keep it.

WHY. areduce and amap are the SAME GRAMMAR one argument apart — `(areduce a idx ret init expr)` and `(amap a idx ret expr)` both bind an index symbol and an accumulator symbol, which is precisely the shape direct-view-call's roster was mishandling. The worker did not reason by analogy and stop there: it REPRODUCED the identical false ERROR with amap at the pin, and landed a witness for it (`self-call-in-amap`). So this is not a second defect speculatively pre-empted, it is the same defect with the same cause, sitting one line away in the same roster.

Trimming it would mean knowingly shipping a build-blocking false ERROR that we have already reproduced, in order to honour the letter of a bead that was written before anyone knew the sibling existed. That is not scope discipline; it is scope discipline used against the point of the work. The bead's subject is "six more binding forms are missing from the roster" — a roster completeness bug — and a class-completeness fix is what a roster bug wants.

THE LINE, so this is not read as licence: the extension is accepted because it is the SAME GRAMMAR, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED, and WITNESSED. A symbol that merely felt related, or one added without a failing case of its own, would have been trimmed.
close_reason: Landed via PR #7843 (merged, rebased onto main): the six missing binding forms are in direct-view-call's roster, each of which was a build-blocking false ERROR. Green on all five merge clauses at 91/91, five runs completed/success, no workflow commits after its base so the matrix was identical. The worker's one-symbol extension to amap is ACCEPTED per the ruling noted on this bead — same grammar as areduce one argument apart, independently reproduced at the pin, and witnessed by self-call-in-amap.

title: hic: the kit's L2 entry point is render/:reads but naming-ledger row 23 recommends tree/:subs — decide and land one
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-hpoy worker (PR #7817), which correctly DECLINED to settle it from the docs side. Read its reasoning before doing anything — it is the substance of this bead.

THE CONFLICT. The shipped kit's L2 entry point is `ht/render` taking `{:reads ...}`. The guide teaches `ht/tree` with `{:subs ...}`. No `tree` has ever existed (`git log -S "(defn tree"` is empty; the entry has been `render` since 7919d9f03b). But `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/naming-ledger.md` ROW 23 owns exactly this question and RECOMMENDS KEEPING `ht/tree`, on the argument that L2 returns data and never DOM — and the kit's own docstring agrees with that reasoning ("It is not a renderer").

THE CHRONOLOGY IS THE POINT. Row 23 landed at 16:32. The kit minted `ht/render` + `{:reads ...}` at 19:03 THE SAME DAY, against the ledger's own rule that prototype names are used consistently everywhere. So the code did not supersede a settled decision; it diverged from an open one.

WHY THE WORKER WAS RIGHT NOT TO FLIP THE GUIDE: doing so would settle an open naming question BY ATTRITION and leave the ledger's own "current name" cell wrong. Row 23 has been amended to record both live spellings and the chronology; its status stays open. The principle it applied is worth keeping: NAMES FOLLOW THE LEDGER, BEHAVIOUR FOLLOWS THE SHIPPED KIT.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD OWES: which spelling wins, `ht/tree` or `ht/render`, and correspondingly `{:subs ...}` or `{:reads ...}`. Weigh row 23's argument on its merits — does "returns data, never DOM" make `render` actively misleading to a reader, or is `render` the more familiar word for what a testing kit does? State the options and recommend; this is a facade-shape call.

THEN LAND IT IN BOTH PLACES IN ONE PR: the kit and the ledger's current-name cell, plus the guide chapters if the answer is `tree`. Until it lands, `ht/tree` is uncallable and the guide teaches a call that does not exist — the residue of rf2-hpoy that a docs-only fence could not close.

STANCE: pre-alpha, NO back-compat shims and no alias. One name wins and the other disappears. Do not add a deprecation path, and do not add a diagnostic that tells the caller they used the old name.

FENCES: the test kit is a shipped surface, so a rename carries its own witnesses — update every call site and prove the suite green. spec/* is hot zone. Coordinate with rf2-hic-027, which is building the L3 mounted facade in the same kit.
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION — MY FRAMING OF THIS BEAD WAS WRONG, and the ledger says so plainly. I wrote "decide and land one". There is nothing to decide: THE DECISION IS ALREADY RECORDED.

WHAT I FOUND BY READING naming-ledger.md ROW 23 IN FULL rather than the summary I was working from:
  - Its recommendation column already says: KEEP ht/tree — "L2 returns a data tree and never DOM, so `render` both misdescribes it AND COLLIDES with h/render! (row 13) and server/render (row 22); the shipped kit's own docstring says 'It is not a renderer'."
  - It records the chronology as a DIVERGENCE, not a supersession: "The kit minted ht/render on 2026-08-10 (rf2-hic-020, 7919d9f03b) two and a half hours AFTER this row recorded the recommendation, and against the header rule that prototype names are used consistently everywhere — so this is a divergence to reconcile, not a ruling that supersedes the row."
  - Row 15 pins the NAMESPACE; the entry name, the fixture shape and the helper set are unpinned.
  - The row's own status is `open`, and rows 23-26 are all settled the same way.

AND THE PROCESS IS EXPLICIT, in rf2-hic-065: "The single naming consolidation point. PROTOTYPE NAMES RUN EVERYWHERE UNTIL HERE. The packet presents every name with a recommendation. The flow does not wait: on packet publication the recommendations apply as DEFAULTS and hic-066 sweeps immediately. The operator's one sitting overrides any row asynchronously." rf2-hic-065 is Phase 6 / Wave F tail and is BLOCKED behind nine beads, so the packet is far off.

SO THE WORK IS NOT A DECISION, IT IS RECONCILIATION, and it is smaller than I said. Two coherent options and I want the reasoning stated, not just the edit:
  (a) BRING THE KIT INTO LINE with the recorded recommendation now — ht/render -> ht/tree, {:reads ...} -> {:subs ...} — which is applying a default early, exactly what hic-065 says happens at packet time, and which the sitting can still override. This makes the guide true and unblocks rf2-hpoy.
  (b) LEAVE BOTH LIVE until the packet and make the guide honest about the divergence instead.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (a), because rf2-hpoy is a P2 whose whole content is that the guide teaches an uncallable function, and (b) leaves a user-facing chapter describing a call a reader cannot make for as long as hic-065 stays blocked — which is indefinitely. The collision argument in row 23 is also independently strong: `render` already means two other things in this codebase.

WHAT MUST MOVE TOGETHER IF (a): the kit entry and its fixture key; the just-landed mounted facade if it references either; the guide chapters (ch14, ch21 and the glossary, ~17 references to ht/tree today); and row 23's CURRENT-NAME cell, with its status left `open` so the sitting still owns it. Do NOT mark the row settled — that is the sitting's to do.

ALSO NOTE row 24: the re-render verb has THREE live spellings (ht/rerender!, "rerender" in spec §9, render! in the testing lane) and row 24 says the sitting settles it, warning that `render!` would collide with h/render!. Do NOT touch that one — it is rf2-e2al's and the sitting's, and this bead must not widen into it.

FENCE: no back-compat alias and no deprecation path — pre-alpha, one name wins. But equally, do not sweep other ledger rows; this bead is row 23 only.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7828 (2026-08-11) — KEEP/UPDATE THIS EXACT RENAME OWNER; no duplicate. WHAT LANDED CLEANLY: ht/tree + {:subs …} are consistent across the public kit, all tracked call sites, guide, and naming-ledger current-name cell; all three authored/landed patch ids match; focused Hicasso node lane passes 291 tests / 1327 assertions; doc and complaint gates pass. The deliberately deferred recovery/spec wording already has exact open owner rf2-6640; do not absorb or duplicate it here. CORRECTNESS / ERGONOMICS: the public arity is ([form {fixtures :subs :or {fixtures {}}}]). Map destructuring validates neither opts itself nor its key set, so every unknown key is silently ignored. In particular the supposedly retired {:reads …} spelling still succeeds outright for a body with no reads, while a reading body ignores the supplied fixtures and raises hicasso-test-missing-read-fixture instead of identifying the bad option. The existing :subs-is-checked test covers only a non-map VALUE under a correctly spelled :subs key, so neither path is witnessed. This violates the package's own closed-option rationale: an ignored option is a setting its author believes is in force. BOUNDED REPAIR: make opts a map with the closed key roster #{:subs}; reject non-map opts and unknown keys through the kit's structured-refusal contract, without an alias, deprecation path, or old-spelling-specific shim. Add a no-read-body {:reads …} control (load-bearing because missing-read detection cannot catch it) and one non-map/unknown-key control. Keep the one-arg default and valid :subs behavior unchanged.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7828 finding ACCEPTED. QUEUED, NOT DISPATCHED — the repair is in implementation/hicasso/test_kit/**, which worker/txmount-hic027 holds for rf2-hic-027. Dispatching now would collide.

THE FINDING, and it is a real hole the rename created rather than a cosmetic residue: the {:reads ...} spelling is now SILENTLY IGNORED. A body with no reads SUCCEEDS OUTRIGHT with the old spelling, and a reading body ignores the supplied fixtures and raises hicasso-test-missing-read-fixture — identifying the wrong problem rather than the bad option. The existing :subs-is-checked test covers only a non-map VALUE under a correctly spelled :subs key, so NEITHER path is witnessed.

WHY IT MATTERS IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN TERMS, quoting the audit: this violates the package's closed-option rationale, because AN IGNORED OPTION IS A SETTING ITS AUTHOR BELIEVES IS IN FORCE. A rename that leaves the old spelling silently accepted is worse than one that breaks loudly — pre-alpha, we break loudly.

BOUNDED REPAIR: make opts a map with the CLOSED key roster #{:subs}; reject non-map opts and unknown keys through the kit's existing structured-refusal contract — NO alias, NO deprecation path, NO old-spelling-specific shim. Keep the one-arg default and valid :subs behaviour unchanged.

TWO CONTROLS, and the first is the load-bearing one: a NO-READ-BODY {:reads ...} control, load-bearing precisely because missing-read detection CANNOT catch that case; plus one non-map / unknown-key control. Drive both — a row that only exercises a reading body would pass against the current hole.

This bead BLOCKS rf2-hpoy again. I dispatched rf2-hpoy before this reopen landed; its work is a docs-only enumeration of what the kit exposes, which does not collide, but its conclusion may move once this lands. Worker messaged.
close_reason:
Landed via PR #7851 (merged 11eaf5f4ac, rebased onto main). Green on all five merge clauses at 91/91, five runs completed/success, no workflow commits after its base. Clean reap on the worker's completion report; canary held at 103/2933/2.

THE RENAME HAD ALREADY LANDED in PR #7828 — the worker grepped before editing, and ht/tree plus {:subs ...} were already consistent across the kit, the call sites, the guide and the ledger's current-name cell. So the naming is tree/:subs, on row 23's own argument: L2 RETURNS A DATA TREE AND NEVER DOM, so `render` both misdescribes it and collides with h/render! (row 13) and server/render (row 22). The kit's own docstring already said "It is not a renderer". Row 23 stays open — that is the naming sitting's to close, not this bead's.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY OUTSTANDING was this bead's merged-PR audit finding: {fixtures :subs} destructuring validated no key set, so {:reads ...} was SILENTLY ACCEPTED — the old spelling kept working with no complaint, which is the worst outcome of a rename. The roster is now closed at #{:subs} via a new two-armed :rf.error/hicasso-test-bad-option, mirroring reg-state's. MUTATION-PROVEN rather than asserted: with the check off, the no-read-body row goes red because the render SUCCEEDS, and the reading-body row reports missing-read-fixture — the audit's wrong-problem diagnosis reproduced exactly.

MY FENCE WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER WAS RIGHT TO CROSS IT — ratified here. I fenced spec/009-Instrumentation.md and complaints.md as hot-zone/contended. But rf2-6640 names spec/009 as one of its THREE ATOMIC SITES and carries the hold-briefly protocol, and my own brief says the bead governs the brief. A half-landing is the one thing that bead forbids, so honouring my fence would have violated the bead. The worker verified #7839's hunks did not overlap, took the file, and the rebase merged clean. It also flagged the crossing prominently rather than burying it, which is the conduct that makes the judgement safe to extend. RULING: when a bead ENUMERATES a hot-zone file as part of an atomic change, the bead wins over a generic fence — and the worker says so in its report, as this one did.

rf2-6640's sites turned out to be FOUR, not three: test.cljs:1117, test_kit_cljs_test.cljs:558, spec/009:2613, and complaints.md's ruling sentence, which falsely claimed the rewrite had already happened. All in one commit (83a01ba064), which is what "atomically" required. The general ruling was also tightened off the untrue "branched on by nothing" onto the contract. The id does not move.

rf2-wjag's witnesses each discriminate, and the halves were proven to red SEPARATELY: removing the generation binding reds only the narrow-image row; disabling the flush reds only the same-tick row. Host-hatch's probe-needing row ported into the node lane (server render separates the door's hook from the widget's — sharper than the prototype's browser mount); cold-probe section 5 rebuilt on an explicit-image frame.

TWO FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING from the attempt: rf/image FAILS LOUD on a zero-match :include-ns pattern, and a reg-sub at namespace load is NOT carried by an explicit :select-ns image in this suite while one issued live IS — which is why the earlier attempt's row could not be made to bite.

THE LOCAL SPINE FAILURE WAS VERIFIED, NOT ACCEPTED. The worker reported test-fast-pr.sh exit 1 on read_profile_baseline_cljs_test/one-bare-macrotask-lands-in-front-of-the-reap-horizon — a timing assertion in the frozen bench tree, green twice in isolation and on the full clean re-run, on a surface this diff cannot reach. Rather than take the flake claim, I checked the same gate in CI on this PR: "CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)" is SUCCESS, along with browser, controlled-input and HMR. The claim holds.

CLOSES rf2-0ckh, rf2-6640 and rf2-wjag together.

title: hic: release! is a test-fixture door on the public facade and tears down the whole page
description:
DESIGN FINDING from the rf2-hic-008 worker (PR #7814), reported rather than decided. Verify against the source before acting — this is a claim about behaviour.

THE CLAIM. h/release! sits on the PUBLIC facade but is unmount! plus collector/reset-runtime!. unmount! REMOVES THE CONTAINER FROM THE DOCUMENT, and reset-runtime! drops every cell, edge and frame bundle PAGE-WIDE. So a consumer with two roots who releases one has torn down the other runtime AND lost its mount point.

WHY THAT IS THE WRONG PUBLIC MEANING. It is exactly right for a TEST FIXTURE, where one app owns the page and teardown should be total. It is wrong for a public teardown door, where "release this root" should mean this root. A consumer cannot reasonably guess that releasing one of two roots destroys both, and nothing in the name says so.

title: the fast-PR spine cannot complete on the Windows host — bash spawn failure in test:script-policy
description:
INDEPENDENTLY REPORTED BY TWO WORKERS on different diffs and different worktrees, with matching diagnoses. That is what raises it above "flake".

THE SYMPTOM. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh clears its always-on repo-invariant steps (54 of them, 0 failures) and then dies inside `npm run test:script-policy` at implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, with:
  Command failed: bash -lc ./.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh PATH

THE EVIDENCE IT IS A HOST SPAWN FAILURE AND NOT A TEST FAILURE, from both reports:
  - Run that suite ALONE on the same worktree and same diff: 322 passed, exit 0. Also 13/13 exit 0 on the other worker's tree.
  - The failing CASE DIFFERS BETWEEN RUNS (~477 vs ~1537 on one host; deploy-leaf "flows" then "routing" on the other). A deterministic assertion cannot do that.
  - One run printed the mechanism outright: dofork: child -1 ... exit code 0xC0000142, errno 11, then "fork: retry: Resource temporarily unavailable". Exit 127 is the bash -lc child never starting. 0xC0000142 is STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED.
  - Both failures happened while other agents were running concurrently; both hosts were under load.
  - It is unreachable from the diffs in question by construction — one was five markdown files and a comment, the other a script that classifies hard-coded path strings.

WHY P2, AND WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SYMPTOM. Every worker brief in this repo tells the worker to run the spine to completion and quote its exit code, and CLAUDE.md nominates it as the pre-checkin gate. If it cannot finish on this host under load, then either workers report a red they must argue away — costing a full re-run each time — or, far worse, someone learns to discount a real red because "the spine is flaky on Windows". A gate that cries wolf gets ignored, and that is how a genuine failure ships.

WHAT TO DO, in order:
  1. REPRODUCE UNDER LOAD, deliberately — run the spine with several concurrent node/JVM processes. If it does not reproduce, say so and stop; do not fix by inspection.
  2. Establish whether the fix belongs at the CALL (fewer concurrent bash -lc spawns from _changed-surfaces.test.cjs; batch the classifier invocations, or reuse one shell) or at the HARNESS (bounded concurrency, a retry on the specific spawn errno).
  3. A RETRY IS THE LAST RESORT, NOT THE FIRST. Retrying a spawn hides genuine classifier failures behind the same code path. If you retry, retry ONLY on the spawn signature (exit 127 with no output), never on a non-zero exit from the script itself, and say in the code why the two are distinguishable.

DO NOT weaken or skip the classifier assertions to make the symptom go away — that suite is what proves changed-surface routing is correct, and rf2-hic-021 has just shown what a mis-routed gate costs.

CROSS-PLATFORM: Mike is on Windows, maintainers are on Mac and Linux. Whatever lands must work on all three and must not make the POSIX path slower or more complex to serve the Windows one.
notes:
THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION, from the rf2-hic-023 worker (PR #7820), on a different diff and a different worktree again.

ITS OBSERVATION, and it is the strongest evidence yet because of the CONTROL it happened to run: the first spine run, on a box already loaded with the 13k-test node suite, produced 142 SPURIOUS changed-surfaces reds — every `bash -lc` classify call failing to spawn, AND EVEN A `git ls-files`. Meanwhile THE MAYOR CHECKOUT PASSED THE SAME HARNESS 322/322 CONCURRENTLY, a single classify call reproduced clean, and the quiet-box re-run was exit 0.

WHY THAT CONTROL MATTERS: it rules out the harness, the assertions and the repo state, and leaves process creation under load. And `git ls-files` failing alongside `bash -lc` widens the diagnosis — this is not specific to login shells; it is spawn exhaustion, and the login shell is merely the heaviest and most frequent caller.

Its diff touched no .cjs, no workflow and no .sh, so it cannot be causal.

RUNNING TALLY: three workers, three diffs, three worktrees — prosetruth-hic012, consumerapp-hic008, evidencev2-hic023 — plus the spawnfix worker's own measurements. The magnitude is quantified: 447 login shells per run at 713ms each on the base, 920s under load; 245 spawns and 83s on the fix branch for the same 324 assertions; `bash -lc` 713ms vs `bash <script> argv` 75ms.

NOTE FOR THE FIX WORKER (rf2-fal5, in flight): the crash signature has still not reproduced deliberately despite ~4,000 induced login-shell spawns. Reducing 447 spawns to 245 is a real and defensible improvement on its own merits, but IT IS NOT THE SAME CLAIM AS FIXING THE CRASH. Say which one the PR is claiming. If the honest position is "the mechanism is 11x smaller and the crash was never reproduced under controlled conditions", that is a good deliverable and should be written that way — it is exactly the claim-exceeds-coverage failure this repo has hit five times today, and a fix report is as exposed to it as a test is.
close_reason:
PR #7821 merged. CLOSING WITH THE VERDICT STATED PRECISELY, because the worker was scrupulous about what it did and did not establish and that distinction must survive in the record.

WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED: the cost, reproduced and quantified. 447 spawns over 235 distinct argument lists. Per invocation: bash -lc 713ms, bash -c 114ms, bash <script> <argv> 75ms — so ~319s of pure shell startup, with the login shell forking all of /etc/profile.d/ every time. Base: 478.3s quiet, 920.7 / 1003.9 / 1006.0s under load. Branch, same load: 245 spawns, 82.6s. AND THE SPINE COMPLETED UNDER THE LOAD ON WHICH IT PREVIOUSLY DIED — exit 0, PASS fast PR spine, gate root naming its own worktree.

WHAT WAS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND THE WORKER SAID SO IN THE PR BODY AND IN A CODE COMMENT: the crash did not reproduce. 18,289 deliberate bash -lc spawns, three concurrent copies of the suite on base code (the exact 'two agents running the spine' shape both original reports were under), a 150-path sweep instrumented to print status/signal/stderr on any child failing to start, and free RAM driven 14.3GB -> 4.1GB. No dofork / 0xC0000142 / Resource temporarily unavailable ever appeared.

Its own words: 'the causal step from 18x fewer, 9.5x cheaper spawns to the reported crash cannot recur is an inference, and I have said so plainly.' THAT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE OF CLAIM and it is why this closes rather than lingering: the fix stands on its measured merits — 18x fewer spawns, 9.5x faster, POSIX strictly faster too, nothing platform-gated — independent of whether it also removes the crash.

THE FIX IS AT THE CALL SITE, both halves: spawn the script as bash's argv (no login profile, and the hand-rolled shell quoting disappears because there is no shell to quote for), and memoize on the argument list (the classifier is pure over explicit paths). NO RETRY — the brief allowed one as a last resort and it was never reached; a retry would have hidden genuine classifier failures behind the same code path. Prior art cited: _playground-sci-inputs.test.cjs recorded the same lesson (56s -> 3s for 144 files).

TEETH PROVEN, not assumed: broke the implementation/core/*) arm's ui_gates=true and quoted four verbatim failures, restored byte-identically (git hash-object back to b9035b66..., clean status), 324 passed. Run in a THROWAWAY DETACHED WORKTREE so the in-flight spine was never disturbed, then removed via the script with all canaries identical.

ONE UNSOLICITED CORROBORATION worth keeping: mid-session an ordinary bash heredoc of the worker's own died with 'child_copy: cygheap read copy failed' / 'couldn't create signal pipe, Win32 error 5' — the same msys2 fork emulation giving way under the same load, on a command unrelated to this suite. That is consistent with process-creation exhaustion rather than anything specific to this test.

IF IT RECURS AFTER THIS, that is new evidence and warrants a fresh bead rather than reopening — the mechanism will have changed.

title: docs(hicasso): the native-IME manual checklist claims app-db stays clean until commit, and the runtime says otherwise
description:

A tester who sees app-db change mid-composition will read a correct implementation as broken, or — worse — will "confirm" the checklist by not looking.   - §4 and §5 should point at the new trace table and the armed bump/unmount buttons the testbed gained in #7815. FENCES: no runtime source edits from this bead — the test kit is a shipped surface and a rename there is its own change with its own witnesses. spec/* is hot-zone and out of scope.

GATES: mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** (exclude_docs). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DOES validate link targets and heading anchors there, and IS SILENT ON SUCCESS — prove it saw your files by planting a bogus anchor, quoting the exit 1 naming file and line, then restoring byte-identically. title: hic: testing-xray.md promises L2 renders a STORED/REGISTERED view body, but mint-view! retains nothing — decide retention or correct the documents
description:

test kit. It measured the gap, shaped `ht/render`'s grammar so the fix is purely additive,

TWO NORMATIVE DOCUMENTS DESCRIBE A MECHANISM THAT DOES NOT EXIST.

  tools/xray/spec/testing-xray.md  — L2 invokes "the STORED view body"
  the same document, section 9    — "REGISTERED bodies"

Nothing stores one and nothing registers one. `collector/mint-view!` closes over `body-fn`
and keeps no reference to it; `boundary-head?` is a single property read, and the docstring
states the design in terms — "no registry, no map", the returned value is still the
function, and per the rf2-2rtt6.52 ruling no memo object escapes as the public
representation. The retention the test kit needs was never part of the shape.

THE OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE. `ht/render` can take a body fn, but handed a MINTED HEAD it must
refuse, because there is no way back to the body. The kit therefore refuses with
`:rf.error/hicasso-test-boundary-body-not-retained` and points at L3. Sabotage S3 measured
what happens if that refusal is removed: `Cannot read properties of null (reading
'useContext')` — a React internal error, from the runtime's own guts, with nothing naming
the real cause. That is the failure a consumer would meet.

`collector/mint-view!`, attaching the body to the minted head under a dev-only property, so
L2 can recover it. `ht/render`'s grammar is already shaped so this lands purely additively —
no signature change, no new public API.

DECIDE, DO NOT ASSUME, and the decision is the substance of this bead:
  (a) retain the body dev-only and let L2 render a minted head; or
  (b) keep the runtime as it is and CORRECT BOTH DOCUMENTS to say L2 takes the body fn,
      not a minted head — the refusal then becomes the documented contract rather than a
      shortfall.
Either is defensible. (a) buys an ergonomic the kit's own users will expect; (b) keeps a
deliberately registry-free runtime registry-free, which is a stated design property and not
an oversight. What is NOT defensible is leaving two normative documents describing storage
and registration that no code performs.

  namespace names itself in the bundle before anything else does. Copy that shape; a
  sentinel that cannot fail is the fail-open class this repo hunts.

title: gate: check_doc_slugs cannot see an indented fence, so links inside admonition and list-item code samples validate as prose
description: FOUND BY THE rf2-re0m WORKER (PR #7780, merged as 97d6acecf) and PROPOSED rather than built, correctly — it judged that widening the fence matcher changes corpus-wide validation and deserves its own bead. Verified by the mayor in source before filing. THE BLIND SPOT. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py:159 _FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^(```|~~~)") Anchored at column 0, with no indent tolerance. Used at line 493 to track whether the scanner is inside a fenced block. So a fence that is INDENTED — four spaces inside an admonition, two inside a list item — is never recognised as a fence at all, and the code inside it is scanned as ORDINARY PROSE. WHAT THAT COST, CONCRETELY. rf2-re0m: a bulk link pass rewrote six lines inside three Clojure examples, adding seven Markdown links that render literally and make copied code invalid. Worse, Markdown parsed the samples' own square brackets as link text, so the rewrite ATE OPENING BRACKETS — `(let [cell-props ...]` became `(let cell-props ...]`, and `[inbox-pane {}]]` lost its `[`. Three fences shipped unbalanced. check_doc_slugs.py passed the whole time, and it was right to by its own lights: every one of those seven links RESOLVED. The gate asks "does this link have a target", never "should this be a link at all", and it could not have asked the second question anyway because it did not know it was looking at code. THE FIX SHAPE (decide, do not assume). Teach the scanner about indented fences. Note that this is NOT simply relaxing the anchor to `^\s*`: - CommonMark allows a fence to be indented up to THREE spaces in ordinary context; - inside a list item or admonition the fence is indented by the container's content indent, which can be far more, and the closing fence must match the opening one's indentation; - a run of four or more spaces in ordinary context is an INDENTED CODE BLOCK, which is a different construct the scanner may also be mishandling — check. So the honest fix tracks container context, or is explicitly bounded and says what it does not cover. A regex that matches any leading whitespace will call a four-space-indented line a fence when it is something else. MEASURE BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THIS IS THE MAIN RISK. Widening the matcher means content previously scanned as prose becomes correctly skipped as code. That is the point — but it can also HIDE a real dangling link that the gate currently catches by accident. Report the full-corpus finding count before and after with the set difference in BOTH directions on the same merge base, and account for every link that stops being checked. A gate that gets quieter is not automatically a gate that got better. THE SECOND HALF, from the same worker's proposal: once fences are recognised, add the assertion that motivated this — a Markdown link (`](`) must not appear inside a fence under docs/design/hicasso/. That is the check that would have caught rf2-re0m at the gate instead of in a merged PR. Decide whether it belongs to this checker or beside it, and whether the scope is that one tree or the corpus. PIN IT. Add self-test cases for: a fence indented inside a list item; one inside an admonition; a fence at column 0 (must not regress); and an indented code block, which is not a fence. CONFIRM EACH REDS AGAINST THE CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION BEFORE FIXING — that ordering is the proof, and it is how rf2-re0m was found. This checker already carries self-tests; follow their shape rather than inventing a harness. FENCES. Do not weaken any existing check. Do not add an ignore mechanism. Do not touch the corpus — this bead is the checker only; the documents rf2-re0m repaired are already correct. ALSO NOTED BY THAT WORKER, PRE-EXISTING AND UNTOUCHED, worth a look while you are in here but NOT this bead's obligation: 50 explicit ids in glossary.md duplicate the generated slug of the heading they precede (`` above `### **portal**`). The anchors work; the checker's duplicate gate only covers HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS, so it does not see them. Report whether that is harmless redundancy or a latent ambiguity; do not mass-edit it here. GATES: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --self-test (or its equivalent — read the file), then the full-corpus run, then sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh. Run each ALONE and echo $? to its own file; never append a filter to a gate's command line.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7785 (2026-08-10; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). COMPLETENESS: valid list/admonition/ordinary indented fences are now recognised; the scoped LINK INSIDE A FENCE tooth, red-first fixtures, corpus delta accounting, and explicit limits landed. Existing rf2-1cpt exactly owns the intentionally deferred blockquoted-fence and colliding-id work. Do not close rf2-mmyc yet. CORRECTNESS: an independent differential used MkDocs' actual load_config('mkdocs.yml') extension/config set as the oracle against _strip_fences. The normal exact fence control agrees. Five malformed/end cases do not: for a longer closer and an unclosed top-level opener, MkDocs renders TOK_IN and TOK_AFTER as prose while the scanner blanks both; for a shorter closer, a closer carrying info, and a less-indented container closer, MkDocs renders TOK_AFTER as prose while the scanner blanks it. Thus a broken link or heading after those lines is invisible. The PR's renderer-derived claim confused “superfences does not accept this pair as a fenced block” with “a fence opens and continues”; Python Markdown instead falls back to ordinary/inline prose. QUALITY: py_compile, diff-check, doc-slug self/full, and README self/full all pass, proving the committed teeth encode the same wrong assumption. Add small exact-MkDocs oracle cases for valid, unclosed, marker-length, info-string, and container-deindent shapes, and make the source-line classifier blank only the block the renderer recognises; keep this bounded rather than growing a second Markdown parser.
OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-10 ~20:45 AUSEST, Mike, in session) — BOUNDED.

The audit of PR #7785 found five malformed/end fence cases where the scanner disagrees with
MkDocs' actual renderer, and noted the committed teeth encode the same wrong assumption. The
scope question inside that finding is now ruled: FIX THE FIVE CASES THE ORACLE ACTUALLY
DISAGREES ON, AND STOP THERE.

Explicitly: make the source-line classifier blank ONLY the block the renderer recognises,
and add small exact-MkDocs oracle cases for the valid, unclosed, marker-length, info-string
and container-deindent shapes. Do NOT grow a second Markdown parser — the audit says so in
those words, and the ruling ratifies it.

The five disagreements, from the audit, so the scope is unambiguous:
  - a longer closer, and an unclosed top-level opener: MkDocs renders TOK_IN and TOK_AFTER
    as prose while the scanner blanks both;
  - a shorter closer, a closer carrying info, and a less-indented container closer: MkDocs
    renders TOK_AFTER as prose while the scanner blanks it.
The consequence being repaired is that a broken link or heading after those lines is
currently invisible to the gate.

THE ORACLE IS THE RENDERER, NOT THE SPEC, AND NOT A PROBE. The PR's renderer-derived claim
confused "superfences does not accept this pair as a fenced block" with "a fence opens and
continues"; Python Markdown instead falls back to ordinary/inline prose. Use MkDocs'
`load_config('mkdocs.yml')` extension/config set as the oracle, exactly as the audit did —
that is what caught the error in the first place.

FENCES UNCHANGED: do not weaken any existing check; no ignore mechanism or allowlist; keep
the in-fence predicate on `.md`/`#fragment` destinations rather than bare `](`, because
`(fn [x](inc x))` is legal Clojure and the stance forbids nagging valid code.

AND THE MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE THAT THIS FILE HAS ALREADY EARNED TWICE: before/after counts
in BOTH directions on the same merge base, every link that stops being checked accounted
for, and a `--prove` mode on every counting script that runs its own machinery over
synthetic known-bad input and requires non-zero. Two workers got false zeros here without
it.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #7795, merged to main as 5216c9626, one file (scripts/check_doc_slugs.py). THE FIX: a fenced block is a MATCHED PAIR. superfences collects from an opener until it finds THAT opener's closer, and failing that restores the source so python-markdown reads the lines as prose. _strip_fences drew the opposite conclusion — it left the fence open and blanked the body and everything after it. An opener is now committed to only once _fence_close finds its closer; where it does not, nothing is blanked. THE ORACLE WAS THE RENDERER: mkdocs.config.load_config('mkdocs.yml') feeding a real markdown.Markdown built from its own 11 extensions, driven three ways (per-line span, gate-level href/heading-id sets, and the audit's token-level probe), with the span instrument validated against four already-agreeing controls before it was trusted. Disagreements: span 12 to 3, gate-level 10 to 1, token 7 to 3, every residual accounted for. Corpus over 718 files is byte-stable in both directions — 0 links newly checked, 0 lost, 0 ids gained or lost — because a census found 0 malformed fence-marker lines in the tree today; the repair is against a class that exists, not one currently instantiated. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE AUDIT'S OWN READING: the five shapes are blinder than described (with realistic content the renderer recognises no fenced block in ANY of the five, so the blindness covered TOK_IN too, not just TOK_AFTER), and FIVE committed teeth encoded the same wrong assumption and had to be flipped — fixing the classifier alone would have left them red. A --prove mode drives the production walk over a planted known-bad page and requires 3 moved items; it earned its keep twice, once catching a planted fixture whose closer was actually valid so nothing moved, and once catching a self-test that printed nothing about the fence cases because it died on a script-relative fixture root first — a silence indistinguishable from success. The worker also caught a regression it introduced itself: the refactor dropped the indent <= content_column + 3 guard on the container-stack push and ALL 96 self-tests still passed, so nothing covered it; restored and pinned by two renderer-derived cases. Declined and recorded: a sixth shape that is not a fence question at all — it reproduces with no fence present, belongs to _inline_blocks (rf2-8wcbe), and fails in the safe direction. That decline is worth its own bead.

title: docs(agents): CLAUDE.md still prescribes 'gh pr merge --rebase --admin' and a bare 'git pull --ff-only' — the fourth policy surface rf2-vfsrd could not reach
description:

docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md and .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md — so that all three
agree: the five-clause merge criterion admits NO exception, `--admin` bypasses no clause,
and the ONLY `--admin` the method sanctions is `MERGEABLE=UNKNOWN`, GitHub's own
merge-state recompute lag, which is not a check at all.

  CLAUDE.md:91
  "Run `git pull --ff-only` as the very next step after
   `gh pr merge ... --rebase --admin --delete-branch`."

THIS IS WORSE THAN THE README PARAGRAPH #7775 JUST FIXED, for two reasons.

FIRST, CLAUDE.md IS LOADED INTO EVERY AGENT'S CONTEXT IN THIS REPO. It is not a page a
mayor consults; it is the standing instruction every worker and every mayor session reads
at startup. So it teaches `--admin` as the house merge command to everyone, silently, on
every dispatch.

SECOND, THE `--admin` IS INCIDENTAL TO THE RULE IT SITS IN. That bullet's actual subject
is "pull main immediately after every PR merge"; the merge command is quoted only to say
what "the very next step" comes after. An unconsidered example is exactly the kind of text
that hardens into policy because nobody reads it as a claim.

TWO DEFECTS IN THAT ONE LINE, not one:

     `gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch`. Evidence: NINE PRs merged on 2026-08-10
     (#7769, #7770, #7768, #7765, #7771, #7772, #7774, #7773, #7775), every one with
     `--rebase --delete-branch`, every one reaching state=MERGED, and `--admin` used
     ZERO times.

     surfaces #7775 touched say to write `git pull --ff-only origin main` and say why:
     the bare form both silently no-ops and outright refuses when the audit-hook push
     races it. CLAUDE.md's bare form is the one the method warns against.

WHILE YOU ARE THERE, CHECK — do not assume — whether the same bullet should also carry the
post-pull test. The method's invariant is `git rev-parse HEAD` must EQUAL
`git rev-parse origin/main`, not that HEAD "moved", and one mismatch is not yet evidence
because an asynchronous audit push can land between the two reads. CLAUDE.md's bullet
justifies the pull by "staleness leaves Mike with a wrong picture", which is a reason to
pull but states no verification at all. Decide whether adding the equality test here is
the right call or duplication of the method file, and say which you chose and why. Do NOT
copy the whole passage across; CLAUDE.md is a pointer-and-rules file, not a second copy of
the method.

FENCES. Change nothing else in CLAUDE.md. Do NOT restructure the Workflow section. Do NOT
touch docs/the-mayor-method/** or .claude/commands/** — #7775 already settled those three
and a second writer would undo it. This bead is CLAUDE.md only.

title: gate: check_provenance_pins fails OPEN on an unusable repository — a failed git diff reads as 'nothing changed', and a shallow clone reads as mass STRANDED
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-i19d WORKER (2026-08-10 16:17 AUSEST) while greening PR #7765. It
could not file this itself (a worker branch must never carry .beads). The mayor
verified both clauses in source before filing. This is the FIFTH fail-open in this
one checker; four were found and repaired on 2026-08-09 (per-block accompaniment
shielding a stranded sibling, _left_context reading across a table-row start,
trailing URL material, a case-sensitive .git rejection).

THE UNIFYING DEFECT: the gate does not fail toward refusal when the REPOSITORY
itself is unusable. It only reasons about the corpus. Both clauses below are the
same shape — an unanswerable question read as a clean answer.

--- CLAUSE 1: a failed `git diff` is read as "nothing changed" ---

scripts/check_provenance_pins.py, Git.changed_markdown, lines 681-692:

    base = self._run("merge-base", since, "HEAD")
    ref = base.stdout.strip() if base.returncode == 0 and base.stdout.strip() else since
    diff = self._run("diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=d", ref, "--", root)
    return {line.strip() for line in diff.stdout.splitlines() if ...}

title: hic: cell-readers promises a copy and can hand back a live alias — every reader-counting witness rests on it
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-vsgq WORKER while building the HMR browser suite. Its own control caught it: a "snapshot" baseline had silently become the POST-save reader list, so a correct runtime read exactly like a leak. It could not file this itself (a worker branch must never carry .beads) and it changed no runtime source.

THE DEFECT IS A FALSE GUARANTEE IN A DOCSTRING. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/inventory.cljs, cell-readers (around line 87):

    (vec (.-readers c))

with the docstring "A witness reader, answered as a vector SO A CALLER CANNOT MUTATE THE LIVE LIST."

In ClojureScript `vec` on a JS array does not necessarily copy. It goes through PersistentVector.fromArray WITHOUT cloning, so for an array inside the tail threshold the returned vector ALIASES the underlying JS array. The collector `.push`es readers into that same array in place (three .push sites in collector.cljs). So a caller holding the "snapshot" watches it change underneath them.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY SHARP EDGE. The docstring states the opposite of the behaviour, and it names its own purpose: "it is what the reader-counting rows assert against". Every reader-count witness in this package is built on a guarantee the function does not provide. A test that captures a baseline, performs an action, and compares cannot see a leak - because the baseline mutated into the result. That is precisely how it presented: a CORRECT runtime looked like a leak, and by symmetry a leaking one could look correct.

FIX SHAPE (decide, do not assume): either make the copy real - `(into [] (array-seq ...))` or an explicit `.slice` before `vec` - or change the docstring to state that the result is a live view and must be copied by the caller. The first is almost certainly right, because the docstring names the witness use-case and witnesses need a stable baseline. Do NOT simply delete the sentence; that would leave every reader-counting row resting on an unstated assumption.

PIN IT. A test that captures cell-readers, triggers a registration that .pushes, and asserts the captured value is UNCHANGED. Confirm the test reds against the current implementation before you fix it - that ordering is the whole proof, and it is how this was found.

CHECK THE SIBLINGS in the same namespace while you are there: boundary-reads and any other accessor that hands out a collection derived from a live mutable structure. Report what you find rather than widening the fix without saying so.

GATES: the hicasso node suite and compile, the freeze gate, and sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh in full. Run each ALONE and echo $? to its own file; never append a filter to a gate's command line. NOTE the fast-PR spine now takes about 40 minutes, past the tool ceiling - run it detached and block on its exit file IN-TURN rather than ending the turn.
close_reason: PR #7779 clones the live reader array before vector wrapping in both package and bench donor, and focused snapshot witnesses cover remount, departure, arrival, and a non-vacuous live-list control.

title: hic: realize-deep cannot see a deferral parked in a mutable reference — a real hole in I7's enforcement
description:

THE HOLE. title: codemod: the printed defhost sketch emits an untaught :fn contract, and authoring.md still calls the tool a hoist
description:

migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/hicasso/report.clj:84 builds the defhost sketch as:
    (for [s slots] (str s " :fn"))

This is the worst shape a diagnostic can take: the tool tells you what to write, and what it tells you is wrong. The doc worker documented the suggestions block WITHOUT quoting the sketch, precisely so the guide would not teach the defect — so the docs are currently protecting readers from the tool.

DECIDE WHAT THE SKETCH SHOULD EMIT. It cannot always know the right contract from a call site, so the honest options are: emit a placeholder that is obviously a placeholder rather than a plausible-but-invalid keyword; emit the contract when it IS inferable and a marked placeholder when it is not; or omit the callbacks map and say why. Do NOT invent a fourth contract to make :fn valid. Whatever you choose, pin it with a corpus case that asserts the emitted sketch is acceptable to the door — a sketch nobody round-trips is how this defect survived.
