title: hic: the reincarnation correction is macrotask-deferred, but React law 3 requires correction before visible paint
description:
RECORDED BY THE rf2-hic-013 WORKER (PR #7749) as a separate open item, deliberately not ruled inside its own bead and deliberately not folded into the successor-write repair.

THE QUESTION. Design law React 3 requires a render/commit tear to be 'corrected before visible paint'. The correction this runtime actually performs is MACROTASK-DEFERRED, which carries no such ordering guarantee. Measured shape: commit-basis ties at 1 -> 1 after a reincarnation, so snapshot-of ties and React schedules no re-render; the repair arrives a macrotask later as snapshot 1 -> 2, producing exactly one notification.

SO THE CORRECTION HAPPENS, BUT ITS TIMING IS UNGUARANTEED relative to paint. Whether that satisfies React 3 is a spec-conformance judgement, not an implementation detail: either the law means something stricter than the runtime provides, or the law's wording is looser than its name suggests and should say so.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF THE SUCCESSOR-WRITE FIX. That repair pins the incarnation into the closure at mint time and changes WHERE a delayed callback writes. This item is about WHEN the correction becomes visible. A worker fixing the first could quietly change the second by altering the deferral, and that would be a spec decision taken by accident.

WHAT TO DECIDE: whether React law 3's 'before visible paint' is (a) a hard ordering requirement the runtime currently violates, (b) satisfied by a macrotask correction in practice, or (c) worded more strongly than intended and owed an amendment. Read the law and its owner before ruling; the page's own rule is that where a row and its cited owner disagree, the owner governs and the row is the defect.

EVIDENCE: PR #7749's negative control NC5 removes the macrotask deferral and reds 6 assertions, so the deferral is load-bearing for current behaviour rather than incidental.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7749 (2026-08-10; completeness/correctness). Independent rerun confirms only eventual macrotask repair: snapshot and notification stay tied at successor seating, then move later. The non-browser commit-seam harness cannot prove React law 3 before-visible-paint ordering. Keep this exact owner open for an owner ruling or a paint-order witness and runtime correction; do not infer conformance from the green 30 ms eventual-repair test.
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): OPTION (a). React law 3 stands as written — a hard pre-paint guarantee — and the runtime is repaired. Option (b) (satisfied-in-practice) rejected: it redefines 'before paint' as 'eventually'. Option (c) (amend the law) rejected: its premise is disproved, see below.

WHY (a). The case for (c) rested on 'painted values are already correct because reads are address-directed'. Verified false as a claim about the SCREEN: address-direction makes a FRESH body run correct (invariants.md L112), but the same paragraph records that no re-render is scheduled — commit-basis ties 1->1, snapshot ties, and per the useSyncExternalStore contract React re-renders only on subscription notification + changed snapshot. The committed fiber and DOM therefore retain PREDECESSOR-rendered values until the deferred mark-dirty! fires; collector.cljs's own comment concedes it ('a boundary that painted before the disposal painted the retired computation, and this is the commit that corrects it'). So this tear IS value-visible — exactly the class the strict clause exists for. Same-id reincarnation is a realistic SPA lifecycle (account/tenant switch, route/root recycling, HMR, test remounts); briefly presenting the predecessor's data is not cosmetic when it is another account's, and it self-heals before ordinary inspection — the worst diagnostic shape. A setTimeout(0) task has no ordering guarantee ahead of the browser's next rendering opportunity (HTML event loop: rendering may update between tasks), so the correction can miss a paint. (c) also under-priced the donor contract: Spec 006 invariant 5 (L1316) independently requires the host to correct BEFORE PAINT with reincarnation named (L1320-1321), so amending the design law would desynchronize it from the normative spec or force amending both. The value-visible vs write-routing vocabulary from the (c) draft survives as ANALYSIS vocabulary (x874's dead-controls tear is the write-routing side, with its own repair) — it just does not enter the law, because this window is value-visible. No real-browser paint witness exists yet, so the stale paint is an inference, not a measurement — but it is the conservative, technically direct inference, and W1 below turns it into a measurement.

THE REPAIR (proportionate; keep it this small):
1. In impl/collector.cljs invalidate-cell!, move ONLY the deferred phase from js/setTimeout 0 to a true microtask (js/queueMicrotask; Promise.resolve().then as fallback where needed). Preserve the two-phase split and the deferral itself: NC5 (PR #7749) made the rewire IMMEDIATE (setTimeout -> synchronous) and red 6 assertions, proving in-stack rewiring is unsafe — it says nothing against microtask deferral, and the docstring's own rationale (this callback runs inside the registrar's replacement/registration hooks and frame teardown, 'none of them is a place to subscribe') is fully satisfied once the stack unwinds at the microtask checkpoint. HTML event-loop pre-paint argument: the microtask checkpoint drains ALL microtasks — including ones queued while draining, hence also React's own microtask-scheduled sync-lane flush for the useSyncExternalStore notification — before the update-the-rendering step of the SAME task, so rebuild + mark-dirty! + React render/commit all complete before the next visible paint. setTimeout gets no equivalent promise.
2. Do NOT touch arm-cell-reaper!'s setTimeout: its one-macrotask grace for keyed unmount/remount reuse is a deliberate, separate contract.
3. Behavioural delta to watch, not fear: the rewire window narrows from one macrotask to the current microtask checkpoint. A successor seated in a LATER task now finds the cell disposed and recovers via cold-read!'s probe on the next render; section 3 of reincarnation_cells_cljs_test (branch chosen by frame LIVENESS at fire time) keeps its meaning — only the fire time moves earlier. The existing suite seats the successor synchronously, so it stays inside the window.
4. COLD/STAGED-PATH CHECK before calling the repair complete: a boundary rendered under incarnation A but committed after B seats may hold NO cell whose disposal can schedule any repair, while commit-basis is documented to tie across the transition (invariants.md L112: the frame term restarts and neither other term is a frame fact) — leaving A-rendered committed content above a B-baselined cell, corrected only when B's value happens to change. If the supported public lifecycle can produce that interleaving (destroy+recreate between render and commit; concurrent rendering/transitions are the suspects), repair it by making ONLY the existing cold snapshot branch incarnation-sensitive — a stable frame token or a monotone incarnation stamp in the basis — so the committing acquisition's incarnation mismatch forces the one corrective re-render. If the public lifecycle CANNOT produce it, prove that with the same mounted witness and add NO machinery. Fence either way: no universal hook, no per-boundary dependency ledger — design laws State 5 and State 6 (the two-hook shell is a ceiling) govern the remedy's shape.
5. WITNESSES — exactly three, no more:
   W1: a real React DOM case keeping a boundary MOUNTED across a synchronous A->B same-id reincarnation, proving the FIRST browser render opportunity observes B — and RESTORING THE setTimeout MUST MAKE IT FAIL (the sabotage control Evidence law 3 requires; the green 30ms eventual-repair test cannot witness paint order, per the merged-PR audit note above).
   W2: the same case forced through the staged render->commit gap, OR a proof that the public root lifecycle excludes that gap (this discharges item 4).
   W3: the existing no-successor cleanup case, proving the new scheduling still disposes exactly — zero cells, references, boundaries and edges.
6. Re-run the do-nothing/read-free boundary shell controls (Economics law 1 standing controls) to confirm no standing-cost regression; NO new performance programme.
7. When the repair lands, update invariants.md's 'Two open items' row: the second item (this question) becomes settled-by-ruling with W1 as its witness; the first item stays until rf2-x874's fix lands.

SEQUENCING vs rf2-x874 — conceptually and mechanically separate, keep them so: x874 changes WHERE retained callbacks write (incarnation pinned into the closure at mint time; impl/frames.cljs surface); this bead changes WHEN the correction becomes visible (impl/collector.cljs scheduling). Neither blocks the other; no dependency edge added; this decision did not wait on x874 because the collector's notification timing is orthogonal to callback write routing. BUT both repairs touch the reincarnation test namespaces, so per the parallel-dispatch rules sequence the PRs (second rebases over the first) rather than editing the same suite concurrently, and run the combined reincarnation suite after BOTH land (this preserves the original recommendation's re-measure intent — there is no wording left to finalize, so the re-measure becomes the combined-suite run). NC6's prediction discipline carries over: a mismatch against the existing witnesses is evidence about the fix, not staleness of the control.

Priority stays P2 (the window is short and self-healing; x874's durable silent successor-write outranks it at P1). This bead is the repair carrier — the merged-PR audit already holds it open for 'a paint-order witness and runtime correction', which is exactly what this ruling orders.
MAYOR 2026-08-10 ~17:15 AUSEST — ONE STALE SENTENCE THIS RULING SETTLED IS STILL WRITTEN AS OPEN, IN A PARAGRAPH NOBODY OWNS.

FOUND BY THE rf2-hicdocs-cluster WORKER (PR #7774, merged as ce1859e83) and deliberately
NOT fixed by it, correctly: no audit note names the paragraph, and it sits outside the
three beads that PR carried. It reported it rather than widening its own scope, which is
the right call and the reason it is recorded here instead of being lost.

THE SITE. docs/design/hicasso/product/invariants.md, the paragraph beginning
"**Two windows a rendered assertion cannot see, and this is where the narrowing bites.**"
It still ends:

  "... which carries that freeze's open question with it: a correction deferred to a
   macrotask has no ordering guarantee against paint, and [React 3] requires one.
   Not settled here either."

THAT QUESTION IS SETTLED, by this bead. The ruling on rf2-2l17 chose option (a) — React
law 3 stands as written as a hard pre-paint guarantee and the RUNTIME was repaired rather
than the law qualified. The repair landed: the deferred phase now runs at the MICROTASK
CHECKPOINT, which the event loop drains in full (including microtasks queued while
draining, so React's own sync-lane flush joins it) before the same task's rendering
update; and the re-stamp is floored at one above the stamp it replaces, because a same-id
reincarnation restarts the frame term and the basis alone could land on the number the
cell already carried — measured in Chromium at epoch 3 -> 3.

So the trailing clause contradicts a settled ruling that is stated FOUR PARAGRAPHS ABOVE
IT on the same page, where the "Two open items" passage now reads as settled-by-ruling
with its witness named. A reader arriving at the later paragraph is told the question is
open by the same document that already told them it is closed.

WHY IT SURVIVED. Two separate PRs edited within a few lines of it and neither owned it:
9cda6c7f (rf2-vsgq) rewrote the subsection two lines below while landing the HMR rows, and
PR #7774 corrected the "Two open items" passage above. Each stayed inside its own slot,
which is the discipline working — but it means the sentence needs an owner named
explicitly or it will keep being edited around.

THE FIX IS ONE SENTENCE. Replace the trailing clause so it points at the settlement rather
than restating the question: the macrotask deferral it describes was the pre-repair
behaviour, the correction now runs at the microtask checkpoint, and the ordering guarantee
React 3 requires is met. Do NOT delete the clause outright — the paragraph's subject is
what a rendered assertion CANNOT see, and the two-phase repair is a real instance of that;
only its "not settled" verdict is stale.

Whoever takes this should verify the wording against the settled passage above rather than
against this note, and should check whether the same "not settled" phrasing survives
anywhere else on the page.

CROSS-NOTE from rf2-hic-014 (delegated dossier review, 2026-08-11, operator-overturnable): the Activity concurrent-reveal question — same law, different mechanism — is ruled OPTION (b): the bounded, gated, at-most-one-frame stale window for concurrently scheduled reveals is ratified through the react-compatibility lane, with design law React 3 untouched. That ruling does NOT overturn this bead's (a): here the runtime owned the deferral (its own collector retired the cell and scheduled setTimeout 0 in code we own) and was repaired; at hic-014 React owns the deferral (passive-effect re-subscribe after a bailed-out reveal), no cell was retired, and this bead's microtask repair is unreachable there. ONE PRINCIPLE, SEEN TWICE: we never defer a correction we schedule past paint; where React owns the deferral, the contract states the measured, gated ceiling. Residual still owned HERE: invariants.md L126 still ends "Not settled here either" about the question its own page settles at L114 — the hic-014 contract sweep is explicitly fenced off that sentence, so its cleanup remains this bead's.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7899 — REOPEN. invariants.md now corrects the later unresolved-questions paragraph, but the same page's present-tense What is witnessed paragraph still says the reaction rebuilds a macrotask later. title: hic: retiring the arm1 rows left the public door's three macros unpinned — the authoring surface is now the least-checked thing in the package
description:
RAISED BY THE rf2-hic-001 WORKER (PR #7748, merged) as an explicit follow-up. It did not invent schema to avoid it, and it did not hide it — which is why the gap is precisely describable.

WHAT WAS LOST AND WHY. PR #7744 split impl/runtime.cljs into six modules. The freeze manifest's `:renames` is a ONE-TO-ONE table from bench namespace to package namespace and cannot express a 1-to-6 split, so four rows became inexpressible: arm1/boundary.cljs, arm1/mount.cljs, arm1/presence.cljs and arm1/lang.clj. They were retired per the manifest header's own third response ("retire the row rather than re-pin it"). Seven front/* rows remain, all whole-file, and the gate is green at 7 rows on main.

**RETIRING DROPS THE DONOR DIGEST TOO, not just the MOVED comparison.** #7744's worker had kept those rows precisely to preserve that half. Combined with the earlier retirement, NOTHING under the bench tree's arm1/ is pinned by anything now.

THE DISPROPORTIONATE LOSS IS arm1/lang.clj, AND IT IS THE PUBLIC AUTHORING SURFACE. That file defines the three macros the package's public door exposes. Only `defview` actually re-points to a new namespace; `hfn` and `defhost` still match their donor EXACTLY. But a row is judged whole — the alternative is a per-shape exemption, which is the one thing this gate must never grow — so all three went unpinned to retire one. The consequence: **the authoring surface is now the least-checked thing in the package.**

THIS IS RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN, which is what makes it actionable: case 8 of check_freeze.py's mutation self-test deliberately demonstrates the blind spot as GREEN rather than omitting it, and frozen-sources.edn's header states the cost. Read both before designing anything.

DO NOT: prune the rename table. 2 of the 5 now-retired entries (arm1.presence, arm1.lang) are still load-bearing for surviving front/* rows; pruning would red them. The worker checked this deliberately.
DO NOT: add a per-shape exemption mechanism to the freeze gate. That is the failure mode the whole-row judgement exists to prevent.

WHAT TO DECIDE (mayor/operator ruling, not worker work): how the three public macros regain coverage. Candidate shapes, none chosen:
  (a) a split-aware manifest field (many-to-one renames) — the worker deliberately did NOT add this, correctly, since schema is a design change;
  (b) re-pin the macro file alone under a narrower contract, accepting that `defview` needs a rename the current table cannot express;
  (c) cover the authoring surface by a different instrument entirely — the door has tests, and the freeze gate may simply be the wrong tool for a file whose namespace legitimately moved;
  (d) accept the gap and record it as permanent, on the ground that arm1/ is prototype provenance and the package is now the artefact.
RECOMMEND weighing (c) and (d) first. The freeze gate answers "is the package the prototype, moved". Once a module split makes that question unanswerable for a file, forcing the answer may be the wrong instinct — but the public door being the LEAST checked thing in the package is not an acceptable resting state either.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): Option (c) plus the (d) record, in the Codex-refined form — a SMALL public-door contract-witness addition to the existing package test lane. NOT byte-for-byte macro-expansion snapshots (incidental symbol/metadata/def-layout detail would make safe pre-alpha refactoring noisy for zero consumer confidence). Option (a) split-aware manifest schema REJECTED (turns a rigid extraction check into a transformation engine; every future refactor shape becomes a schema request). Option (b) narrow re-pin REJECTED (option (a) in miniature — defview needs a rename the one-to-one table cannot express). No freeze-schema extension, no new harness, no JVM lane.

REALITY CHECK (2026-08-10): freeze gate green at 7 rows, all front/*, all whole-file; nothing under arm1/ pinned; the blind spot is demonstrated rather than hidden — PR 7748 mutation-proof case 8 altered the hfn expansion and the gate exited 0. The dossier predates rf2-hic-012/013: the package lane NOW exercises h/defview (smoke + roots/reincarnation suites) AND h/defhost (roots_frames_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs:122 — defhost around a tiny React fn with {:ssr :render}, used as a hiccup head, real-DOM render). h/hfn is the one door macro with ZERO package-test usage.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one worker, package tests only, the :node-test-hicasso lane):
(1) Witness A — the callback macro, current prototype spelling h/hfn (hicasso.cljc:90). Consumer-shaped: define one through the public door; assert it is an ordinary function, that invoking it returns the author value, and that impl.intent/callback? recognizes it (one own-property read); also assert a plain (fn ...) is NOT callback?, so the witness discriminates.
(2) Witness B — h/defhost. The isolation-test usage is incidental to a containment row and could refactor away silently; make the contract deliberate: assert the minted var is a host head (impl.codec/host-head?) and renders through ordinary Hicasso hiccup with one option forwarded ({:ssr :render} suffices, proving argument forwarding). Smallest diff wins: a tiny dedicated witness OR explicit assertions promoted onto the existing usage.
(3) The existing defview smoke is the third witness — unchanged.
(4) The (d) record: add ONE dated line to the frozen-sources.edn header — arm1/ provenance-pinning ended at the module split (PR 7744; retirement in PR 7748); the package is the artefact from that commit forward. The header already states the cost; this is a one-line disposition, not a rewrite.
(5) HARD FENCE: never prune the rename table — the arm1.presence and arm1.lang entries are load-bearing for surviving front/* reconstructions (front/presence.cljs, front/intent.cljs); pruning reds them.
(6) HARD FENCE: never add a per-shape exemption mechanism to the freeze gate. A row is judged whole; that rigidity is the value.
(7) MUTATION CHECK: each witness must be shown able to fail exactly once — temporary mutation applied, red observed, reverted, stated in the PR body — the same discipline as the PR 7748 mutation proof.
(8) NAMING: witnesses target the PROTOTYPE spellings that exist today (defview, hfn, defhost); the naming review recommends h/event for the callback form — the rename-sweep updates the witnesses mechanically when it lands; do not pre-empt it here.
(9) STOPPING RULE: if the fix starts requiring freeze-parser changes, expansion normalization, a new runner, or exhaustive macro edge-case tables — STOP. That is provenance litigation, not better SPA ergonomics.

UNBLOCKING: landing the two witnesses green (with the one-time mutation demonstration recorded) closes this bead and CLEARS the rf2-hic-001 blocker — no further freeze-gate work is owed for the authoring surface.

Consumer-shaped hfn and defhost contract witnesses join the existing defview smoke, both new witnesses were mutation-proven red, the arm1 provenance retirement is durably recorded, and neither the rename table nor freeze schema was weakened. All 22 scheduled GitHub checks passed.

title: hic — ratify the authoring names: h/fn vs hfn, h/frame vs hframe, and mount's unfrozen root!/release!
description:
# Close the gap between Hicasso's var names and its authoring surface

**Found by**: rf2-hic-001, which was instructed to keep the prototype's names and did.
**Surface**: `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc` (the public door) + guide prose.

The prototype spells two authoring verbs one way and DOCUMENTS them another, because in the
bench tree they were `:refer`red into the consuming namespace and the intended product
spelling is qualified:

| authoring surface (docs, 49 + 65 mentions) | var in the package today | prototype's stated reason |
|---|---|---|
| `h/fn`    | `hfn`    | "spelled `hfn` here because `h/fn` is qualified in the product and a bare `fn` would shadow `cljs.core/fn` on a `:refer`" |
| `h/frame` | `hframe` | "Spelled `hframe` here … a bare `frame` would shadow" |

Now that the package exists and the intended consumer spelling is
`(:require [re-frame.hicasso :as h])`, both reasons are spent: `h/fn` and `h/frame` are always
qualified through the alias, so the vars COULD be named `fn` and `frame`. That is a naming
decision with a real trade-off (a consumer who `:refer`s either one gets a shadow warning, and
`fn` shadowing `cljs.core/fn` is nastier than the warning suggests), so rf2-hic-001 did not
take it — it renamed nothing.

Note the marker keywords need no such decision and already work: `::h/value`, `::h/prevent`,
`::h/navigate`, `::h/mounting`, `::h/unmounting`, `::h/revision`, `::h/checked` and
`::h/clear` were minted as `:re-frame.hicasso/…` in the prototype, so aliasing the package as
`h` resolves them exactly as the guide teaches.

Also unresolved and cheap to fold in: `impl/mount.cljs`'s own docstring says "the names stay
unfrozen (HD-021 pins the semantics, not the spelling) and nothing here is a public API", yet
`root!` and `release!` are on the door because a package that cannot mount is not usable.
Ratify or replace that pair.

## Acceptance

- A ruling recorded, and the door matching it.
- If anything is renamed, `implementation/hicasso/frozen-sources.edn`'s `:renames` table and
  the note in `re-frame.hicasso`'s namespace docstring are updated in the same PR.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): ROUTE ALL THREE QUESTIONS TO THE NAMING LEDGER; RENAME NOTHING NOW. Dossier Option A's process — the only one consistent with the ruled machinery (ledger accumulates -> rf2-hic-065 packet applies recommendations as defaults -> rf2-hic-066 sweeps once -> operator's single sitting overrides asynchronously) — with the recommendation columns informed by the Codex analysis where I verified it against the repo. Ledger rows landed via PR #7753 (docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md rows 1, 13, 18). The door keeps the prototype names until the sweep; frozen-sources.edn :renames untouched (nothing renamed). Acceptance met: ruling recorded; door matches it (no rename ordered now).

THE THREE RULINGS (as ledger recommendations, all settled finally at the operator sitting):
(1) hfn (taught h/fn) — row 1 now carries BOTH candidates, h/handler (spec section 4 facade table) and h/event (Codex naming view), with h/event RECOMMENDED. Verified in-repo: the established cross-adaptor vocabulary reserves "event" for convert-the-invoker's-arguments-to-one-event-vector-or-nil (spec/004-Views.md:653 v/event; spec/004D-Freehand-Compiled-Grammar.md:1079 ui/event, nil => no dispatch) and "handler" for imperative return-ignored work (004-Views.md:654 v/handler; 004D:1080 ui/handler). Hicasso's form has exactly the event contract (capture frame; run later; dispatch returned vector; nil = no event), so h/handler would be a cross-adaptor false friend. Never a var named fn: alias-qualified h/fn is technically viable, but fn shadows cljs.core/fn for any :refer user (silent behavior change for every anonymous fn in that namespace) and says only "callable", not "the return is an event". Either surviving candidate kills the shadow hazard outright.
(2) hframe (taught h/frame) — new row 18 carries candidates "frame" (mechanical rename) vs RETIRE in favour of the core doors, with retire RECOMMENDED. Verified: specification.md section 4 (line ~139) already says "Existing rf/current-frame-id and rf/capture-frame remain the frame doors; Hicasso should not duplicate them", and hframe returns a frame-id KEYWORD while ui/frame and n/use-frame name frame OPERATIONS — a second false friend. The retire path is SEMANTIC, not mechanical: Hicasso currently refuses ambient frame resolution during its body, so the refusal seam must be corrected to admit exactly :current-frame-id and zero-arity :capture-frame during a Hicasso render extent, resolving to the body's known extent frame (the refusal record already carries :extent-frame, and require-current-frame! already receives the attempted operation — no adapter hook, no collector edge). Ambient rf/subscribe and rf/dispatch MUST stay refused (they would bypass Hicasso's read and intent accounting); outside a frame-bearing render the core doors keep their loud no-context behavior. Per hic-066's own law (a rename that turns out semantic stops the row and files a bead), the sweep files a dedicated bead for this seam correction rather than improvising. The committed hframe witnesses (multi-root, foreign-callback, reincarnation, SSR) prove the capability is real and must survive the retirement.
(3) root!/release! — RATIFIED PROVISIONAL until the sweep (a package that cannot mount is not usable; impl/mount.cljs's own docstring says the names are unfrozen and nothing there is public API). Row 13 recommends the spec section 4 lifecycle: mount! (from root!, a create-and-render), hydrate! (from the already-implemented hydrate-root!), render!, unmount!. All four underlying operations already exist in impl/mount.cljs (root! :105, hydrate-root! :233, render! :89, unmount! :293), so the rename exposes real states rather than inventing concepts, and matches React's public client model (createRoot/hydrateRoot each yield a root with render and unmount). release! is NOT root-lifecycle vocabulary: verified it calls process-wide collector/reset-runtime! (mount.cljs :313/:323) — a test-fixture door, unsafe as lifecycle in a multi-root product; it moves to the test kit under an explicit test-wide-reset name, off the application facade.

REJECTED: Option B (rename to fn/frame now) — buys the core-shadowing hazard for :refer users and then a likely second rename at the sweep; two churns, one hazardous, against the one-sweep ruling. Option C (ratify prototype names as final) — the guide would have to teach h/hfn (noise) and the facade disposition would be silently overturned without the evidence the freeze process expects. Codex's decide-now framing is adopted only as recommendation-column content: the physical rename still happens exactly once, at the sweep; no compatibility aliases ever (pre-alpha; hic-066 already bans shims).

NO ACTION on: guide prose (keeps teaching the target spellings until the sweep; the door/guide gap is the ledger rule working as designed, and a one-line "prototype names until the sweep" note is at the sweep-owner's discretion); marker keywords (::h/value, ::h/prevent, ::h/navigate, ::h/mounting, ::h/unmounting, ::h/revision, ::h/checked, ::h/clear already resolve exactly as taught — no decision needed).

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE FOR hic-065 (contract behind the recommended names, preserved from the dossier before deletion):
- The event form is a dispatching callback, not a position-sensitive marker: it captures the rendering boundary's exact frame incarnation, runs later with the invoker's arguments, dispatches one returned event vector, and treats nil as no event. A declared :handler or :render position should REJECT the form rather than reinterpret it; ordinary fn remains the imperative/render-callback escape. At an undeclared raw React escape it remains an ordinary callable carrying its own event semantics — the programmer deliberately chose the untyped edge. (Today impl/intent.cljs gives the marker positional treatment at :event/:handler/:render; the product specification already rejects positional meaning and asks for one event-producing form — the packet confirms one invariant meaning under whichever name wins.)
- Root contract: (h/mount! container frame hiccup) creates and initially renders, returning an opaque handle; (h/hydrate! container frame hiccup) adopts server markup and returns the same handle shape; (h/render! handle hiccup) updates either kind of live handle and returns it; (h/unmount! handle) is idempotent, cleans only that root, returns nil, must NOT remove a caller-owned container, and must NOT erase global collector state to manufacture a clean result — root-teardown residue after quiescence is a defect to expose, not to reset away.
- Core-door admission stays narrow: during a Hicasso render extent rf/current-frame-id returns the extent frame and (rf/capture-frame) captures that exact incarnation; no collector edge and no React hook is added; rf/subscribe and rf/dispatch still raise the existing ambient-frame refusal. A small correction to the refusal seam, not a second frame system.

REQUIRED WITNESSES BEFORE THE SWEEP IS ACCEPTED (carry into hic-066 acceptance):
- A clean CLJS consumer using only (:require [re-frame.hicasso :as h]) compiles the winning event form; the final public namespace contains none of hfn, fn, hframe, frame, root!, release!, nor the losing event/handler candidate.
- The event contract proved at a native event prop, a value-first declared host callback, and a retained raw callback: a vector dispatches once to the captured incarnation; nil dispatches nothing; a successor frame with the same public id is never reached by an old callback; declared handler/render slots reject the form rather than changing its meaning; a plain function returning a vector remains just a plain function.
- rf/current-frame-id and (rf/capture-frame) answer the Hicasso body's frame in two simultaneous roots, in a supplier-owned foreign render callback, and during per-request SSR; the captured operation still targets that incarnation after the body unwinds; outside a body they refuse; a sabotage proves ambient rf/subscribe and rf/dispatch still refuse and the hook/read-edge counts do not move.
- mount! and hydrate! return one interoperable handle shape; render! preserves an adopted subtree after hydration settles; unmount! is double-call safe, leaves the supplied container in place, releases only its own root, and cannot make a sibling root's evidence disappear; residue is measured BEFORE any test reset.
- A hydration witness proves that calling render! before adoption settles is either explicitly refused or follows a deliberately documented React contract; it must not silently switch the root to client rendering (React documents that early render as destructive to the server DOM).
close_reason: Routed to the naming ledger per the ruled one-sweep machinery (rows 1/13/18, PR #7753); nothing renamed now; full delegated-decision record with implementation guidance and sweep witnesses in the bead notes.

title: cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md: 3 provenance-pin findings exposed by the row scope, one needs a ruling
description:
PR #7734 (rf2-xlsh) scoped provenance-pin accompaniment to the table ROW rather than the whole table. That newly exposes three findings on docs/design/hicasso/studio/cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md. The page was left UNTOUCHED because one of the three cannot be repaired without a ruling, and a partial edit would have redded #7734's own changed-pages gate.

MECHANICAL, no ruling needed:
  :541 19a3710bc9604684ddbc7b2b72ec901dcc0f0ea7 [STRANDED]
  :541 3680992949a6eec842ba033ae50f3a9a34af7884 [STRANDED]
Row 540, directly above, already asserts -- and says it verified by identical 'git patch-id --stable' -- that f6cb3584fb (confirmed an ancestor of origin/main) is what 19a3710bc9 became when it landed. Naming f6cb3584fb inside row 541 is the census's own repair pattern and invents nothing.

NEEDS A RULING:
  :544 247fafa22c1f2caeb4cad179aa64cf444398cbc7 [UNRESOLVABLE]
This is NOT a citation defect. The row cites a commit in krausest/js-framework-benchmark and says so in its own text: 'That SHA belongs to the benchmark's repository, not to this one, so it resolves there and nowhere else.' No SHA of THIS repository belongs in that row, so there is no accompaniment to add. The gate reads 'at commit `X`' and classifies it as a local pin, which it has no way to know is false.

The options, for whoever rules:
 (i) teach the classifier a foreign-repository context, so a token the writer explicitly attributes to another repo is not read as a local pin. Closest in spirit to how the checker already separates blobs from commits by the writer's own vocabulary, and needs no page edit.
 (ii) annotate the page so the row carries no bare commit citation.
 (iii) accept the finding and leave the page red whenever it is touched. Not recommended -- it lays a trap for the next editor.

Do NOT weaken the gate or add an ignore mechanism. Whoever fixes :541 must resolve :544 in the same PR, or the page's changed-pages gate stays red.
notes:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-10, operator-overturnable): OPTION (i) AS AMENDED BY THE CODEX RECOMMENDATION — teach scripts/check_provenance_pins.py a foreign-commit citation, where "foreign" is an explicit canonical GitHub commit permalink, never a conclusion drawn from nearby prose. Prose words ("foreign", "upstream", "another repository", "belongs to") are NEVER an exemption. Rationale: prose-attribution vocabulary would be the first vocabulary that turns the gate OFF for a token rather than classifying the writer's claim, and is launderable by a magic phrase — the dossier's own stated risk. A typed permalink binds the full SHA to a repository identity mechanically, is clearer to a reader, easier for an AI tool to generate correctly, and keeps the checker's fail-toward-refusal design intact. Option (ii) rejected: the page bends to the tool and hiding the SHA from the scanner is a fail-open shape; the next outside-instrument page hits the same wall. Option (iii) rejected: a standing trap, and a red gate people learn to ignore is the exact habit the corpus forbids. FENCE PRESERVED: this neither weakens the gate nor adds an ignore mechanism — it teaches the gate the writer's explicitly-declared, strictly-typed citation form.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one worker, ONE PR: checker change + fixtures + all three page findings together, so the changed-pages gate stays green — a partial edit reds the page on every touch):

THE THREE FINDINGS on docs/design/hicasso/studio/cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md:
1. :541 19a3710bc9604684ddbc7b2b72ec901dcc0f0ea7 [STRANDED] — MECHANICAL. Row 540 directly above already asserts-and-verifies (git patch-id --stable) that f6cb3584fb is what 19a3710bc9 became when it landed; f6cb3584fb re-verified an ancestor of origin/main 2026-08-10. Name f6cb3584fb inside row 541 per the census's own repair pattern; invents nothing.
2. :541 3680992949a6eec842ba033ae50f3a9a34af7884 [STRANDED] — MECHANICAL via the same same-row landed anchor, BUT (Codex-verified) f6cb3584fb's stable patch id matches 19a3710bc9 ONLY, NOT 3680992949. The repair text must NOT describe f6cb3584fb as the landed counterpart of the second authored commit; the landed anchor in the row satisfies the row-scoped accompaniment rule for both tokens while the prose stays accurate about which authored commit it corresponds to.
3. :544 247fafa22c1f2caeb4cad179aa64cf444398cbc7 [UNRESOLVABLE] — NOT a citation defect. Foreign commit of krausest/js-framework-benchmark (Stefan Krause, "incremental run", 2026-07-28; identity confirmed by two primary sources: the surviving clone's remote https://github.com/krausest/js-framework-benchmark.git resolves it, and GitHub's canonical commit page resolves the same full SHA). No SHA of THIS repository belongs in that row; re-verified 2026-08-10 that this repo cannot cat-file the object and the row text explicitly attributes it to the benchmark repository. FIX: rewrite the citation as a canonical permalink, e.g. [krausest/js-framework-benchmark commit `247fafa22c1f2caeb4cad179aa64cf444398cbc7`](https://github.com/krausest/js-framework-benchmark/commit/247fafa22c1f2caeb4cad179aa64cf444398cbc7), keeping the row's existing provenance prose (shallow clone of master taken 2026-08-01, clone kept outside the repo, "resolves there and nowhere else").

CHECKER CONTRACT (keep the first version deliberately narrow):
(1) Canonical GitHub commit permalinks ONLY: the displayed token and the URL's final path component must be the same full lowercase 40-hex SHA; HTTPS; no query or fragment. A short SHA is NOT sufficient — abbreviation is meaningful only inside a particular object database.
(2) Represent the result as a FOREIGN citation carrying repository identity, not dropped from the citation population; verbose output counts foreign citations separately so green cannot mean silently ignored.
(3) A permalink naming this repository's own normalized origin takes the EXISTING local landed/accompaniment path — a local authored SHA must not be launderable through a GitHub-shaped link.
(4) Deterministic and offline: NO network-dependent CI check, NO repository allowlist, NO submodule, NO exception manifest for this single use case. Existence at the host is confirmed once while authoring the citation (already done for row 544) and the canonical link recorded.

REQUIRED WITNESSES (fixtures; implementation complete only when ALL are demonstrated):
- POSITIVE: a canonical foreign permalink with matching full SHA is extracted, reported as foreign, and PASSES without a local origin/main anchor in its row.
- SABOTAGE: a bare unattributed SHA — including one sitting beside the words "foreign repository" — still FAILS.
- EDGES: a mismatched label/URL SHA, an abbreviated SHA, a malformed commit URL, and a local-origin permalink each refuse or take the existing local path.
- The checker --self-test passes; the fast documentation gate passes; and after the accurate row-541 repair plus the row-544 permalink edit, the changed-page provenance gate is GREEN on this page.

FENCE (unchanged from the bead): never weaken the gate; never add an ignore mechanism.

MECHANISM ESTABLISHED (sibling rf2-abmp): this ruling establishes the mechanism class "the gate honors the writer's explicitly-DECLARED, strictly-TYPED citation form; loose prose never exempts a token". rf2-abmp's remaining decisions are the same class — its implementation should REUSE this one checker change wherever a foreign permalink applies rather than adding a second mechanism, and abmp's page-fix work queues behind this bead's checker change (dependency rf2-abmp depends-on rf2-styo added 2026-08-10).
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7754 (2026-08-10) — ACTIONABLE CORRECTNESS/QUALITY GAP; KEEP OPEN. The required gates pass (`--self-test --verbose` 0, changed-page provenance 0, doc slugs 0), and the intended page is green, but the canonical-permalink refusal boundary is not actually canonical. `_COMMIT_PERMALINK` uses a small trailing-character blacklist, so it accepts a valid-looking prefix inside malformed URLs such as `<sha>%3Fdiff=split`, `<sha>:garbage`, and `<sha>&diff=split`; `scan_file` marks the stranded token foreign and `evaluate` returns no finding. More sharply, the `.git` rejection is case-sensitive: `https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.GIT/commit/<local-stranded-sha>` is accepted, recorded as foreign repository `day8/re-frame2.GIT`, compares unequal to local `day8/re-frame2`, and suppresses the finding. This contradicts the bead/PR contract that nothing follows the SHA, malformed commit URLs refuse, and a local-origin permalink cannot launder a local head. Fix the boundary with positive whole-URL/token parsing rather than another partial suffix blacklist; reject `.git` case-insensitively after normalising repository identity. Add scan/evaluate-layer sabotage witnesses for uppercase `.GIT` on this origin and trailing percent-encoded/other URL material, asserting extraction, no foreign classification, and a retained finding. No duplicate Bead created because rf2-styo is the exact still-open owner.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7761 (2026-08-10 AUSEST; completeness/correctness/implementation quality). COMPLETE. The foreign-permalink boundary now fails closed by matching the whole rendered URL run against one canonical shape, and repository identities are normalised on both the permalink and origin sides; uppercase .GIT can no longer launder this repository and unanticipated suffix material remains inside the candidate and refuses. Independent merged-tree evidence: all 58 self-tests pass; a separate boundary drive passes six positive forms, refuses 17 suffix families, and confirms alias/origin normalisation; Python compilation, changed-surface provenance, doc slugs, and diff check pass. The full corpus still produces exactly the nine standing findings and exactly one declared foreign citation. No duplicate or residual finding; closing this exact owner.
close_reason: PR #7761 repairs both audit fail-opens with positive whole-URL parsing and normalized repository identity; independent self-tests, adversarial boundary checks, corpus census, and gates pass.

title: docs(hicasso): 27 pages still cite the closed rf2-2rtt6.1 standard; route the live-standard citations through the pointer map
description:

WHAT IS TRUE. rf2-2rtt6.1 -- the Hicasso bar, budgets and kill criteria -- was CLOSED by operator ruling on 2026-08-10 as superseded by the new governance set. 27 tracked pages still cite it, and some cite it as the LIVE standard rather than as dated provenance. SIZE WARNING: 27 pages is large for one worker. If context runs short, open a PARTIAL PR with the pages completed and list the remainder precisely -- a partial sweep that is honest about its boundary is fine; a silent partial is not.

description:

title: hic-089 — Budget gates, part 1: the early framework
description:
# hic-089 — Budget gates, part 1: the early framework

**Phase**: 2 · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-006, hic-025
**Surface**: CI gate suite + the reconciliation-table skeleton in the budgets doc (this bead owns budgets-doc status columns until hic-071 takes over)

## Goal
The split of the old hic-071: the gates that CAN exist early, so regressions are caught from the slice onward. hic-071 becomes the late population-integration gate.

## Deliverables
- The 5% same-instrument regression gate wired to the pinned ordinary-Hicasso baseline, running in CI per relevant PR.
- Slice-app user-visible gates: discrete interaction ≤50 ms p95 / ≤100 ms p99; keystroke echo within one frame — deterministic where possible, pinned interleaved where distributional; eligibility/sabotage control each.
- The budget-line reconciliation table skeleton (registered line, current value, status, authority, disposition) with the rows known today.

## Acceptance
Gates run in CI; a seeded regression reddens the 5% gate; the reconciliation table has no silent-breach rows.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)

PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).

title: check_provenance_pins.py fails open: a bad hash in a table is shielded by a landed hash in the same block
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-mcwm WORKER (PR #7727) while running an unrequested extra control on the pins gate. It substituted a known-bad hash (a PR head that is not an ancestor of main) into resource-demand-criteria.md in three places, and the gate reported only ONE of the three.

THE MECHANISM. check_provenance_pins.py enforces accompaniment PER BLOCK, not "every cited SHA must be an ancestor of origin/main". Two of the three substituted occurrences sat in the record table alongside the landed original-freeze hash c8b8de6d28. Because a landed SHA was present in the same block, the block satisfied the accompaniment rule and the bad hashes beside it were not reported. Only the prose citation, alone in its own block, was caught.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A CURIOSITY. The gate's whole purpose is to stop a page citing a commit that does not resolve. On the page it was guarding, the ROW THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS -- the operative frozen hash that rf2-hic-044 and rf2-hic-050 will cite -- lives in a table next to a landed hash. So the guard would not have caught a wrong hash in exactly the field whose wrongness costs most. It was caught only because the same value also appeared in prose.

THIS IS THE FAIL-OPEN CLASS THE REPO HUNTS EVERYWHERE ELSE: a gate that verifies the absence of bad news in aggregate rather than the presence of good news per citation. Any page that cites a hash ONLY inside a table alongside a landed one is unguarded today.

WHAT TO DECIDE (this is a ruling, not an obvious fix). Options, roughly in increasing cost:
  (a) Report every cited pin that is not an ancestor of origin/main, regardless of what shares its block. Strictest and simplest to explain; may be noisy on pages that deliberately cite historical or superseded commits.
  (b) Keep per-block accompaniment but additionally flag any cited SHA that resolves to no commit at all, since that can never be legitimate.
  (c) Treat table rows as their own blocks, so a cell cannot be shielded by a sibling cell.
RECOMMEND (b) AT MINIMUM -- an unresolvable token is never correct and the check is cheap. (a) is the honest end state if the noise turns out to be tolerable; check first how many legitimate historical citations exist in docs/design/**.

DO NOT weaken any existing behaviour, and do not silence the gate anywhere. Note also that the gate already refuses correctly on the other axis: it caught a bootstrap RNG seed (20260807) and a placeholder (abc1234) today, both false positives that cost fix-worker round trips. Whatever changes, keep that fail-toward-refusal posture -- the defect here is a fail-OPEN, and fixing it must not trade one for the other.

EVIDENCE: PR #7727's report. Reproduce by substituting 92cd524aeeb0132f51f8e3376e313d7819f8813c (a PR head, not an ancestor of main) for the operative hash in docs/design/hicasso/product/resource-demand-criteria.md and running: git fetch --no-tags origin main; python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main --verbose
notes:
WORKER STOPPED AND DID NOT IMPLEMENT (b). Measured evidence says (b) is the wrong shape; the brief instructed STOP-and-report in that case. No code change, no PR. Bead left open for a re-ruling.

THE FAIL-OPEN IS REAL AND REPRODUCED. Substituting 92cd524aeeb0132f51f8e3376e313d7819f8813c for the operative hash afbb58febc at line 19 (the "Pre-registration commit ... this is the hash to cite" row) of docs/design/hicasso/product/resource-demand-criteria.md, then running --changed-since origin/main --verbose, gives EXIT 0: "1 files, 5 cited pins (4 landed, 1 stranded, 0 unresolvable) ... every cited pin is an ancestor of origin/main or shares its block with one." The landed c8b8de6d28 one row above shields it. Confirmed exactly as described.

WHY (b) IS THE WRONG SHAPE. "Resolves to no commit at all" is not a property of the citation; it is a property of whatever happens to be in the local object store. The script's own FAILURE DIRECTION docstring already says this ("the stranded pins are precisely the objects a fresh clone does NOT have"). Measured, same corpus, same 346 citations:

  local dev checkout (PR heads fetched over time):  238 landed, 100 STRANDED,   8 UNRESOLVABLE
  fresh clone, main only:                           238 landed,   0 stranded, 108 UNRESOLVABLE
  fresh clone + all branches + all tags (= exact
  actions/checkout fetch-depth:0 shape used by
  the provenance-pins job in docs.yml):             238 landed,   0 stranded, 108 UNRESOLVABLE

STRANDED is empty in CI. Every retained authored head is UNRESOLVABLE there, because a commit that is not an ancestor of main is by definition not reachable from main, and merged worker branches are deleted. So in the only environment where this gate blocks, (b) flags all 108.

CONSEQUENCE 1 - in CI, (b) IS (a), bit for bit. Findings measured in the CI-shaped clone:
  TODAY (per-block accompaniment)   18 findings / 10 pages
  (b) + every unresolvable         108 findings / 28 pages   (+90 findings, +18 pages)
  (a) every non-ancestor           108 findings / 28 pages   (+90 findings, +18 pages)   IDENTICAL to (b)
  (c) table rows are blocks         23 findings / 13 pages   (+5 findings, +3 pages)
The ruling picked (b) expressly to avoid (a)'s noise. In CI there is no difference between them. The ruling's stated justification - "adds no false positives on pages that deliberately cite historical or superseded commits" - inverts in CI: those deliberate historical citations ARE the unresolvable tokens, and all 90 new findings are exactly those pages. That is the "punish the careful ones and be routed around within a week" outcome the script's WHAT IS ENFORCED paragraph exists to refuse.

CONSEQUENCE 2 - (b) does not fix the bead's own reproduction in a dev checkout. Prototyped (b) correctly (keep accompaniment for STRANDED, always report UNRESOLVABLE) and re-ran the probe locally: STILL EXIT 0. The probe resolves locally, so it is STRANDED, so it stays shielded. (b) catches it in CI only, and only as a side effect of also catching 90 legitimate ones.

CONSEQUENCE 3 - (b) widens the false-positive class that already cost two fix-worker round trips. Both of yesterday's refusals (the 20260807 bootstrap seed, the abc1234 placeholder) are UNRESOLVABLE tokens. Verified both still fire on current code (exit 1, both reported). Under (b) they would additionally be reported when a landed hash shares their block - strictly more of the same false positive, i.e. the fail-closed trade the brief forbids.

WHAT I RECOMMEND INSTEAD - (c), which the ruling excluded. Measured, not argued:
  * It catches the probe in BOTH environments (local run with a (c) prototype: EXIT 1, reports line 19). "Is an ancestor of origin/main" is checkout-invariant, so unlike (b) its verdict does not depend on the object store.
  * It costs 5 new findings on 3 pages, against 90 on 18 for (a)/(b). The three: studio/cross-checked-against-an-outside-instrument.md, studio/the-candidates-clock.md, studio/the-in-page-mount-term-decomposed.md.
  * It matches this bead's own title - "a bad hash in a table is shielded by a landed hash in the same block". The shielding is between ROWS; (c) removes exactly that and nothing else. Prose paragraphs are untouched, so the retained-authored-head-plus-anchor sentence the census repaired keeps passing.
  Caveat for the ruling: the docstring says the census's repairs put the landed SHA "in the same table cell or the same sentence", which is what makes (c) cheap - but the 3 pages above are the cases that relied on a sibling ROW, and each needs a human.

A fourth option, if (c)'s 5 findings are unwelcome: (d) require that a token the WRITER calls landed/effective/"the hash to cite" actually be an ancestor of origin/main, regardless of block, leaving "authored at X on worker/y" alone. Checkout-invariant, near-zero corpus cost, but it needs new vocabulary in _COMMIT_WORDS and is more machinery than (c).

METHOD, so this is re-checkable: fresh clone via `git clone --no-local --single-branch --branch main file:///C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2`, then `git fetch origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*' --tags` for the all-refs variant. Every probe reverted; worktree ends at e914fc8b7c with `git status --porcelain` empty. Gates on the clean checkout: --self-test --verbose exit 0 (all 33 passed), --changed-since origin/main --verbose exit 0, check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh does cover this script (lines 1191-1205 run both the self-test and the changed-pages gate), so any change here reds the fast-PR spine.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7734 (correctness/implementation quality): REOPENED exact owner. Citation.scope correctly prevents a LANDED hash in one row from accompanying a STRANDED hash in another, but scan_file still calls classify -> _left_context, which reads two prior nonblank source lines without respecting the new row scope. Reproduction: in a neutral table, put `bbbbbbbbbb` in a preceding `Blob hash` row and stranded `aaaaaaaaaa` in the next `Original freeze` row. scan_file returns ZERO citations: the preceding digest word repaints the next row before evaluate() can enforce row scope. A bad operative commit can therefore still fail open. Bound the repair to extraction context: never cross a prior table-row start, while retaining same-row wrapped continuations and digest-header classification; add this exact sibling-digest regression. Existing 36 self-tests, changed-page gate, diff check, and fast-PR spine all exit 0, proving the coverage gap. The already surfaced corpus findings remain owned by rf2-styo and rf2-iseb; no duplicate Bead.
Merged-PR audit #7742 (2026-08-10): PASS; the reopened owner is complete. Independent parent/tip probes show the sibling-digest fixture (including blockquote form) changes from zero citations to the operative `aaaaaaaaaa`, while a wrapped same-row digest remains excluded. All 39 self-tests and changed-page/diff gates pass. Full-corpus comparison is exact on findings: 20 before and 20 after, with no set difference; extraction rises 347→354 citations as intended. rf2-styo retains the separate page-level backlog; rf2-iseb is already repaired. No duplicate filed.
close_reason: Completed by PR #7742; merged-PR audit verified row-bounded extraction, same-row continuation preservation, and an unchanged 20-finding corpus set.

title: hic: decision-brief.md navigates readers to ai/-tree paths, violating hic-000's own no-ai-paths criterion
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-bmj8 WORKER, outside its fence. The mayor read both lines and verified every named path before filing, because the worker correctly flagged it as needing a judgement rather than a text swap.

THIS IS NOT THE DELIBERATE-GLOSS CLASS. product/README.md's 'specification.md (= synth-codex.md)' gloss maps the PUBLISHED name to the original, for a reader who knows the ai/ tree. That is helpful and stays. These two lines do the reverse: they are prose in a published document that sends the reader TO paths which do not exist in the published tree.

WHAT THE TWO LINES NAME, and what is actually there (verified against the working tree):
  decision-brief.md:7   -- 'its sibling synth-codex.md', 'the codex/ lanes', 'indexed by codex/README.md'
  decision-brief.md:156 -- synth-codex.md, 'the codex/ specification set', codex/evidence-baseline.md, codex/corpus-insights.md, 'fable/ and the three lessons-*.md', fable/dispositions.md

  codex/                      ABSENT   -> published as lanes/                      (PRESENT)

A fresh clone has no ai/ tree at all (it is gitignored), so line 156's 'the current status of every scout idea is fable/dispositions.md' sends a worker to something it cannot reach and cannot substitute.

THE PART THAT NEEDS A RULING, and why this is not a find-and-replace. Five of the named paths have exact published counterparts and should simply be renamed. Someone must decide per reference whether to (a) mark it explicitly as a local-only source not present in this tree, (b) publish the missing artefact, or (c) drop the reference. RECOMMEND (a) for all three -- it is honest, needs nothing published, and matches this repo's habit of stating what a record does not cover rather than going silent.

FENCE: docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md only. Do NOT sweep the tree: product/README.md's gloss and its rf2-hic-000 source-hash manifest are deliberate and stay.

GATES: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and (git fetch --no-tags origin main; python scripts/check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main --verbose). Both exit 0, with a sabotage control proving the checker sees the file.

title: hic: requirements-mine.md and dispositions.md both classify every section 7 job into the same five layers, with no stated precedence
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-pxk7 WORKER while indexing the product records (PR #7719). It worded its own ownership rows to avoid adjudicating this, and said it wants an owner.

THE DUPLICATION. requirements-mine.md carries a 'Home' column and dispositions.md carries a 'primary home' classification. Both assign each specification section 7 job to the SAME five layers. Two tracked files now own one classification and nothing states which governs.

WHY IT IS A DRIFT RISK RATHER THAN A TIDINESS COMPLAINT. The two files have different owners and different update triggers: requirements-mine.md grows as jobs are discovered (rf2-hic-004's maintenance rules), while dispositions.md is appended to by rf2-hic-040 and rf2-hic-046 as controls and SSR rows land. They will be edited by different workers at different times, and nothing mechanical compares them. The first divergence will be silent, and a reader hitting it cannot tell which page is stale.

WHAT TO DECIDE: name one file as the normative owner of the layer classification and have the other cite it, or state an explicit precedence rule in both. Prefer the citation, per the set review's own remedy for shared classifications at lanes/beads-review.md section 2.4 (one consolidation owner, not concurrent authorities).

DO NOT resolve this by deleting a column: both pages need the layer visible to be readable. The fix is stated precedence, not removal.
close_reason: Resolved in PR #7720 (branch worker/productdocs-cluster, commit 8b1e7caea3). OWNER CHOSEN: dispositions.md section 1.1 is normative for the layer classification. Reasoning: (1) it is the classification ledger by charter - 'Phase 0 owes two ledgers, and this document is both of them', the first being exactly this classification, whereas requirements-mine.md is chartered as an evidence ledger where the layer is context not subject; (2) dispositions.md section 3 ALREADY names an owner for the 1.1 table and constrains amendment ('never change a Home without a specification change behind it') - the mine has no comparable rule, so naming the mine normative would have meant inventing a protocol rather than recognising one; (3) 1.1 separates primary home from additional surfaces, from the bounding refusal, and from the source spec section (6 columns), while the mine fuses all three into one prose cell - reads well, adjudicates badly; (4) the mine already defers upward on the row list via its maintenance rule 4. Both columns KEPT. One sentence added to each file (5 inserted lines, 0 deletions): dispositions.md claims the classification, requirements-mine.md cites dispositions.md section 1.1 as owner and governing on disagreement. # hic-071 — Budget enforcement gates

**Phase**: 2→4 · **Wave**: C/E · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-006, hic-025 (extends over hic-078 and hic-047 apps as they land)
**Surface**: CI gate suites + the budgets document's status column (new files; budgets.md rows updated by this owner only)

## Goal
Turn the transcribed budgets into enforced gates. Transcription is not enforcement.

## Deliverables
- **User-visible gates**: representative discrete interactions reach next paint ≤50 ms p95 / ≤100 ms p99; broad operations ≤100 ms p95; keystroke echo within one frame — measured on the slice app (then the editor/grid and vendor apps as they land), deterministic-blocker style where possible, pinned interleaved runs where distributional.
- **The 5% same-instrument regression gate**: pinned ordinary-Hicasso benchmark compared per PR-relevant change; a regression blocks until the instrument owner validates and the change is fixed or reverted.
- **The escape-benefit rule enforced**: every landed escape (direct output, island) carries its measured benefit; an escape below 20% / 2 ms / budget-flip is removed by this gate's acceptance, not documented around.
- **Budget-line reconciliation table**: registered line, current value, status, authority, prospective disposition — one row per budget; checkpoints read it.

## Acceptance
- Gates run in CI on the named suites; each gate has an eligibility/sabotage control; one seeded regression reddens the 5% gate; the reconciliation table has no silent breach rows.

## Worker notes
Read spec §6 (all subsections); the evidence-protocol rules (estimand, population, refusal on unhealthy instrument).

3. comments.text:
C8's POPULATION IS NOW WRITTEN INTO THE ROW (rf2-m7xx0, PR #8179) — read this before building the C8 gate (mayor, 2026-08-14).

THE PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE. Exactly one h/as-element call exists in the shipped example applications: the ledger screen's :render-row hfn passed to the rows host. The vendor's own contract is renderRow = (index, offsetPx) => ReactNode, and h/defhost rows' docstring names the crossing 'the declared door onto the virtualizer'. Nothing there claims recovered time. Two further hits under examples/ are a test's own rig, not application sites. So the fail-closed reading was real.

THE WORDING, AND WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY. C8's rule now reads that an escape TAKEN FOR A BENEFIT recovers at least 20%, saves at least 2 ms p95, or converts a failed budget to a pass — and that an INTEROPERABILITY escape, one whose alternative is not a slower spelling but no spelling at all, is outside the population. The exclusion is given by its TEST rather than by naming virtualizers, so a second foreign API of the same shape needs no further patch.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO, and this is yours to decide: it did NOT add a site-declaration obligation ('and says so at the site'), which the bead had floated. Two reasons, both good — the obligation would have to be discharged inside implementation/hicasso/, which was another worker's fence, and WHATEVER THE GATE KEYS ON IS THIS BEAD'S CHOICE. So when you build C8, decide whether the population is inferred or declared, and record which.

IT ALSO ANSWERED THE QUESTION I ASKED ABOUT A THIRD CASE, and the answer is worth keeping. It read all eight comparative rows: there is no third unstated population, and the page does NOT need a population column. C7 is the near-miss and is not a third instance — a native island's comparator always exists and its disposition is 'co-instrumented' rather than 'removed', so a miss there cannot fail closed. The structural point is narrower: section 4's USER-VISIBLE table has an Estimand column, which is exactly why PR #8177 had somewhere to put U5's second counter; the COMPARATIVE table is id-rule-disposition with no such column, which is why C8's population had to go inline. IF a third comparative row ever needs one, add an Estimand column to that table mirroring the U-table's — do not make a third inline patch. It did not file that, correctly, since it is conditional on a case that does not exist.

TWO SMALL THINGS LEFT DELIBERATELY. C8's Disposition cell says 'an ISLAND missing its threshold is simplified or removed' — C7's noun in C8's rule, whose subject is an escape, with the same loose usage in section 3's prose. It was left byte-identical BECAUSE changing it would have destroyed the 'Disposition cell unchanged' check that makes the PR verifiable. And S8's ledger row still reads 'C8's first disjunct' — correct as written, since S8 is the mechanism's reference price per section 9.2 Ruling 2, and not drift against the new scoping.

AND THE RULING WAS NOT REWRITTEN. Ruling 2's recorded text is byte-identical; a dated clarification note sits beneath it, following this page's own C6 idiom, because rewriting a ruling to read as though it had always known the answer is what section 5 forbids.

title: hic-056 — The bounded Node/React SSR service
description:
# hic-056 — The bounded Node/React SSR service

**Phase**: 5 tail · **Wave**: — (V0 scope; no longer gated on a named caller — operator ruling 2026-08-12, rf2-xpq9) · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-046
**Surface**: SSR service package (new)

Productize the proven Node spike into a bounded, fail-closed service. The core per-surface hydration contract (hic-046) is already mandatory and does not wait for this.

Per-request frame/state isolation (immutable snapshots); allowlisted payload; one in-flight render per isolate until proven otherwise; timeout + hard termination; caller latency envelope pre-registered; hydration-byte tests against the client; JVM↔Node protocol kept separable (no "one complete string" baked into every layer, so a streaming caller later doesn't need a second semantics).

The five gates above witnessed; deployment documented; client v0 provably unaffected when the service is absent.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8028 (completeness/correctness/quality): reopen the exact delivery owner for a response-contract escape. The package repeatedly states the ruled topology is “Node returns body markup and nothing else” and calls anything else an incremental host fork, but `worker.cjs` accepts arbitrary `out.meta` from the application render module, `isolate.cjs` carries it, and `service.renderFrames()` exposes it on the public complete frame. The shipped fixtures already demonstrate that this channel can carry application state (`readTodos`, `readRoute`) as well as thread diagnostics. HTTP currently drops it, but the documented transport-independent protocol and in-process API do not, leaving an unallowlisted application-controlled egress exactly where the contract says none exists. Remove application `meta` from the production response contract (moving test observations behind test-only instrumentation), or explicitly re-adjudicate and tightly bound a service-owned metadata roster; add a control proving application data cannot cross outside body markup. The existing in-progress rf2-n8vp already owns the separately declared no-CI-lane gap and was not duplicated.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
Mayor (2026-08-13): raised P4 -> P2. The bead's original scope was a feature build and P4 was right for that; the audit reopened it on a CONTRACT VIOLATION in the fail-closed guarantee the package exists to hold, and that is not a P4.

The finding: worker.cjs accepts arbitrary out.meta from the application render module, isolate.cjs carries it, and service.renderFrames() exposes it on the public complete frame — an unallowlisted, application-controlled egress at precisely the point the contract says none exists. HTTP drops it today, which is luck of the current transport, not a guarantee: the documented transport-independent protocol and the in-process API both carry it, and the shipped fixtures already demonstrate application state crossing (readTodos, readRoute) alongside thread diagnostics.

That is the same fail-open class this repo hunts in its own instruments — a contract asserting a property the code does not enforce — and it sits in the one package whose whole point was five bounded guarantees. Fixing it after consumers exist is far more expensive than now.

NOT a duplicate of rf2-n8vp: that bead owns the missing CI lane and is in flight; this owns the egress. The audit said so explicitly.

That is hic-023's acceptance, witnessed rather than asserted.

THE COLLECTOR'S RECORDED JUDGEMENT WAS FOLLOWED, NOT DIVERGED FROM — and the reasoning is the part worth keeping. The 2026-07-31 ruling is about a GROUPED read surface competing with an AMBIENT one inside a defview body. Past the fence there is no body and no ambient extent, because React renders a component after its parent body has returned — so there is no ambient collector to compete with, and React's rules of hooks force one hook per read. n/use-sub is the single-key hook that reasoning implies, not use-subs renamed. The one visible consequence (n reads in an island = n subscriptions, where a body's n h/sub reads are one entry) is React's arithmetic, and the docstring says so.

WITNESSES, each with its narrowing named: the lane-independent native_hooks_cljs_test uses the server renderer, the only harness where WHAT A RENDER RETAINS reads as a flat zero — the cold tier answers before any commit and retains no cell, membership, boundary or edge; both hooks refuse outside every frame and each names ITSELF in :where; use-frame answers the runtime's row BY IDENTITY, so equality would pass for the wrong implementation. native_hooks_dom_cljs_test adds seven mounted rows against subscribe-once-per-render, store-wide subscription, a per-render subscribe closure, render-phase acquire under StrictMode, wrong frame resolution, memoising on the frame keyword, and a transition-awareness claim.

One of those errors was a RangeError — a registration holds its cells and a cell holds its readers, so cljs.test's printing of a failed identical? overflows the stack and produces A RED THAT SAYS NOTHING. Fixed in the same PR by asserting the boolean instead. That is exactly the class of instrument defect this project hunts, found because the worker actually ran its sabotage rather than reasoning about it.

CLOSURE RULE (rf2-hic-073) — this paragraph is part of this checkpoint's protocol.

Every miss this protocol finds becomes a real bd issue — run `bd create`, one per miss, with the surface fence and acceptance in its description — and is appended as a row in docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md carrying its severity (correctness / coverage / quality), the protocol section that produced it, and its status. It closes only when the protocol section that produced the finding is re-run against the landed fix and the result — date, section, commit, what was run, the outcome — is written into the row's Closure evidence cell. Trivial re-runs (re-read one fixture, re-run one sabotage control, re-count one roster) happen inside the corrective PR, which quotes the result. Non-trivial ones (clean-checkout suite, fresh reviewer, physical reference profile, a whole sabotage family) get a small closure bead depending on the corrective bead, named in the row. Rows are never deleted: a finding that proves mistaken closes as "withdrawn — <reason>", so the audit can see it was considered. rf2-hic-064 gates on this ledger — zero unresolved correctness or coverage rows, where unresolved means any status other than `closed`, or the audit returns a non-release verdict. build it only when a real migrator reports the manual declarations as the pain.
The 2026-08-07 corpus scan (tools/machines-viz/src, the only application-shaped
[:>] corpus in-repo) found 15 executable [:>] forms over 7 component
expressions, and NONE of the 15 triggers a text-changing fixer rewrite — that is
evidence of ergonomic value with no urgency, and it is why the gate stands.

ORDERING GATE IS MET. The ratification's condition was "dispatched after
rf2-2rtt6.103's [:>] implementation merges"; .103 is CLOSED with PR #7635 merged
(raw-head?/raw-element/raw-gate/raw-component in front/codec.cljs). The SHIPPING
precondition rf2-ani6y is CLOSED (PR #7665, shared front/slot.cljc with a
cross-host equivalence test), so the JVM prop-name is pinned equal to the codec.
The donor-side row rf2-d2mwk is CLOSED.

THE THREE RATIFIED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, which are corrections to the landed
design and must be implemented as amended rather than as written:

(A) W4 MUST CAPTURE AT PROP-EVALUATION TIME. The design's stated rewrite
(reagent-codemod-against-the-landed-escape.md:154) is (fn [& args] (apply f a
... args)), which re-evaluates every nontrivial callee/argument form on EACH
callback invocation; Reagent's make-partial-fn evaluated them ONCE at
construction. Required shape: a hygienic let capturing the callee and every
bound argument once, left-to-right, before minting the wrapper (or refuse
non-atomic arguments). Witness pins: a dereferenced-snapshot case and an
effect-count/ordering case.

(B) W2 MUST REFUSE NORMALIZED-KEY COLLISIONS. Reagent's kv-conv writes each
nested-map key under cached-prop-name, so :foo-bar/:fooBar, :class/:className
and :foo-bar/"fooBar" siblings each collapse to ONE JS property with an
iteration-order winner. Required shape: before rewriting any nested literal map,
require the normalized names to be injective; otherwise refuse the WHOLE map
with a report line naming every colliding source key. Witness pins: an ordinary
camel-case collision, a seeded rename, a keyword/string collision.

(C) KEY-SLOT REPORT ENTRY. The key-slot exclusion from the named-value rewrite
is RATIFIED (:foo and "foo" sibling keys COLLIDED under Reagent and are DISTINCT
under Hicasso; rewriting would restore the defect rf2-vrvv9 removed). But the
counter-cost is understated: a changed key resets the subtree's React state on
live reconciliation. The report must carry a dedicated entry per key-slot site
saying so.

STANDING RIDER, unchanged and quoted: the ~6-8 door-side codemod-contract-* rows
remain the only executed evidence the tool is correct — "Not optional, not
deferrable."

THE GOLDEN-FILE CORPUS IS THE SPEC (design section 5): input namespace ->
expected output + expected report, covering the rewrite, each preserve class,
each report class, and idempotence (running twice = no-op).

RESIDENCE: dev tooling operating on consumer source. Check how existing tools
are packaged and honour the bundle-isolation law (nothing in implementation/ may
:require from tools/). Verify what parsing substrate the repo already depends on
before adding rewrite-clj or an equivalent.

src/reagent/impl/template.cljs (convert-prop-value, kv-conv, cached-prop-name)
and src/reagent/impl/util.cljs (make-partial-fn/PartialFn); React v19.2.0
packages/react/src/jsx/ReactJSXElement.js (key coercion). In-repo:
front/codec.cljs (prop-name, host-prop-value, host-entry, raw-element,
vec->element), codec_cljs_test.cljs, implementation/shadow-cljs.edn (the Reagent
2.0.1 pin).
