Recorded as a warning only: the candidate fitted at 36-55 B/read against donors at 289-610, i.e. candidate-minus-donor of -234 and -574 B/read — HD-002's predicted flat-at-zero arriving in exactly the shape a systematically under-reading instrument manufactures, out of a run whose own gate says it under-read.

WHY THE ARM WAS NOT BUILT — two structural reasons, neither about the box or effort:

(1) THE AUDIT PRECONDITION ON THIS BEAD IS UNMET, and I confirmed it by reading rather than assuming. allocSteps is the only collector detector and it is a sign test on adjacent in-page deltas; cdpBracket is recorded on every arm and control and appears in NO failure path; p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs has zero allocation coverage across its 288 lines, so there is no allocation-row structural test in which to pin the masked-GC case. Filed as rf2-n6w7o and added as a blocking dependency on this bead. Its likelier route is the audit's option (b) — a measured bound that a small window cannot collect — but the bound has to be measured, which needs a per-window cumulative-garbage reading the row does not take.

(2) IT IS A NEW RUNG AND THE WINDOW FORBADE ONE. per-root is the compile-time fx/cells-n = 300, so P0_ROOTS=1 floors B at 300 and a few-dozen-boundary arm is unreachable through the rig's env surface — it is a p0_heap.cljs edit, exactly as the description says. A rung added between runs of a series makes the series two instruments.

AND THE PREMISE DESERVES COSTING BEFORE ANYONE BUILDS IT. The description argues a many-write window 'restores the averaging a fit needs'. The in-range witness did not fail for want of averaging: 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31 against a 0.98 floor with NON-MONOTONE rungs, and averaging does not linearise a non-monotone sequence. This run says the same from the other side — the candidate refused at r2 0.97538 (reagent-subs) and 0.84451 (uix-subs) while both DONORS fit cleanly at 0.99730 and 0.99446. The donors are lines; the candidate is not, at this scale. Whether that is noise a smaller unit resolves or a real non-linearity is unmeasured, and the arm should be costed against that question rather than assumed to answer it.

figure has never been published. So the prediction is a SIZING AID, NOT A
CERTIFICATE: what certifies a window is allocSteps reading that window's own
samples against the same budget, on the run. The pre-flight exists so a
configuration that cannot possibly pass is refused before twenty minutes are
spent on it, not so one that passes it may be trusted.

the floor arm: 24,108 B/write (reagent-subs), 24,730 B/write (uix-subs).

(W+1).perWrite, so at the six-write floor it allows 42,857 B/write and F
alone is 57% of it before a boundary is measured. Modelling perWrite ~
F + B.s(R): at W=6 no page of one boundary or more certifies the R=20 rung.

rf2-2rtt6.140 (P1) with the full table.

Six writes of averaging DOES resolve the non-monotone rungs for three arms

and 290 B/read [35-1,029], against donor bands [569-770] and [651-917]. An
r2 over a six-round mean can clear a floor that per-round bands like those
should have refused.

NOTHING IS PUBLISHED. Two of three preconditions failed (bound did not

title: adapter reg-view stamps displayName with a colon the rf:render: measure strips
description:
Found while fixing rf2-2rtt6.136 (freehand's identical defect, PR #7623). The bead for the freehand fix asserted the divergence was 'confined to the product path'. It is not — the ADAPTER path has it too, and that is the first-class, actively-supported substrate.

implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs, the reg-view wrapper every adapter (Reagent / reagent-slim / UIx / Helix) composes:

  L552  (performance/mark-and-measure :render id (apply render-fn args))
  L586  (when interop/debug-enabled? (set! (.-displayName ^js wrapped) (str id)))

A reg-view id is a keyword, so (str id) keeps its leading colon. React DevTools shows ':cart/total-line' while the bracket writes 'rf:render:cart/total-line'. Spec 009 §Naming convention (L1494) requires the measure's <id> and the id the substrate publishes to the developer — it names React displayName explicitly — to be ONE identifier, 'so a name read off the User-Timing stream is directly jumpable in the tooling'. Pasting the DevTools name into the documented rf:render: filter yields rf:render::cart/total-line and matches nothing; docs/core/how-to/fix-a-slow-view.md sends the reader down exactly that path.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH THE FREEHAND HALF. Two reasons, both operator calls rather than fence questions:

1. The current spelling is DELIBERATE and LANDED. rf2-fa4ly's comment at views.cljs:575 says DevTools should show '<:cart/total-line>', and implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/reg_view_devtools_cljs_test.cljs PINS it — display-name-on-wrapped-fn-matches-view-id asserts ':re-frame.reg-view-devtools-cljs-test/dn-auto' and display-name-honours-rf-id-override asserts ':rf.devtools-test/dn-explicit'. Fixing this deletes two landed assertions and changes what every existing consumer sees in DevTools.
2. It is a visible change to the shipping surface, not the EXPERIMENTAL one.

THE FIX IS ONE TOKEN if ruled. PR #7623 extracted the shared builder as re-frame.performance/entry-id (build-name's own <id> half, unchanged behaviour, all four buckets), precisely so a substrate can publish the measure's own spelling rather than re-deriving it. So this is:

  (set! (.-displayName ^js wrapped) (performance/entry-id id))

plus updating the two adapter assertions to the colon-free spelling, plus a row that asserts the two strings are EQUAL rather than each well-formed (the shape that let both halves of this ship). views.cljs already requires re-frame.performance.

DECIDE WITH THE FREEHAND HALF IN VIEW: if the adapter path keeps the colon and freehand drops it, one framework publishes two spellings depending on substrate — which is worse than either spelling chosen consistently.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #7685 (branch worker/displayname-976bw). Both reg-view assignment sites now stamp (performance/entry-id id); spec/006 item 1 amended (dated-amendment idiom) to distinguish the logical registry id from its performance/display projection, 009 left as the binding statement; data-rf-view unchanged (round-trippable encoding). The spine's stamp was SWITCHED, not removed: views/build-frame-aware-view returns a MetaFn (cljs.core/with-meta on a fn), which React cannot use as an element type, so on a React-hook substrate the spine's wrap-view head is the only React-visible name. Equality rows added on both halves and shown red-then-green by reverting each site; three mounted fiber-read assertions (Reagent class machinery + UIx hook wrapper) shown red in the browser lane. Gates: fast-pr spine 0, test:cljs 0 (12799/64391), test:browser 0 (1131/6952), test:browser-prod-elision 0 (121/530), test:perf-bundle 0, test:elision 0, clj-kondo 0 errors, mkdocs --strict 0 (spec staged), check_doc_slugs 0, beads-pr-boundary 0.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07, operator-overturnable): OPTION A — align the React displayName to the colon-free entry-id projection, shipped as a small CONTRACT-RECONCILIATION patch, not the one-token patch. The bead's own dossier and an independent Codex inspection converged on Option A; Codex's scope corrections are adopted. The overturned artefacts are named below, deliberately: rf2-fa4ly's intent comment (views.cljs:575-584, mirrored at spine.cljs:2136-2141) and the two Reagent pins in reg_view_devtools_cljs_test.cljs.

WHY (posture: pre-alpha, no compat debt; spec is the artefact; minimal surface): spec/009 §Naming convention makes displayName and the measure <id> ONE identifier — that is the tooling-jumpability contract, and performance/entry-id (PR #7623) exists precisely to be its single spelling source. Freehand already publishes colon-free, so the status quo is the bead's own worst case: one framework, two spellings by substrate, TODAY. The <:cart/total-line> aesthetic is a dev-only nicety; the round-trip is a contract.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (one PR moving all of it together):
1. BOTH assignment sites switch to (performance/entry-id id) — views.cljs:586 AND substrate/spine.cljs:2142 (the React-hook wrapper's own (str id) stamp; verified present at HEAD). If the spine inner assignment is redundant behind the shared outer wrapper, remove it with a test proving the visible UIx name; otherwise switch it to the same builder. Leaving it colonful preserves a latent substrate-dependent divergence.
2. Reconcile the normative conflict (verified at HEAD): spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md §React DevTools support item 1 (~:774-782) REQUIRES (str view-id) / <:cart/total-line>, while spec/009-Instrumentation.md §Naming convention (~:1480-1494) requires one identifier. Amend 006 (dated-amendment idiom) to distinguish the logical registry id (a keyword) from its performance/display projection (entry-id); keep 009 as the binding statement. NOTE FOR DISPATCH: spec/* is hot-zone — sequence against other spec/006 edits.
3. data-rf-view UNCHANGED: its colonful (str id) is deliberately reversible to a keyword via source-coords/parse-view-id. displayName is a display projection; data-rf-view is a round-trippable encoding. State the distinction in the PR body.
4. Tests: update the two Reagent pins (display-name-on-wrapped-fn-matches-view-id; display-name-honours-rf-id-override) to the colon-free spelling; ADD the non-vacuous equality row (performance/build-name :render id) == (str "rf:render:" (.-displayName wrapped)) for a namespaced keyword (the each-half-well-formed shape is what let the two halves drift); add equivalent hook-wrapper (UIx-path) coverage; retain production-elision/bundle checks — the spine must not leak the label builder into an elided bundle (views.cljs already requires re-frame.performance; check the spine's require).
5. Prove the visible name through the REAL component paths (Reagent class machinery + UIx hook wrapper, mounted), not only the pre-wrap fn property — static inspection found no consumer parsing the colonful displayName, but the DevTools-visible name was not exercised.

CORRECTIONS to this bead's own description (do not cite as acceptance evidence): (a) docs/core/how-to/fix-a-slow-view.md:203-257 documents entry shapes and startsWith('rf:') filters but does NOT instruct pasting a DevTools name into an rf:render: filter — that promise lives in the excluded Hicasso draft guide (docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/11-performance.md:98-105); the binding reason is spec/009's one-identifier rule plus the live freehand divergence, not the how-to. (b) 'all four adapters' is stale — three shipping adapters (Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx); Helix removed per spine.cljs:4-5.

title: RULING PREP: the production server arm — JVM structural walk (default) vs Node sidecar, priced from the spike corpus
description:
RULING PREP — THE PRODUCTION SERVER ARM, PRICED FOR THE P2/GRADUATION SITTING. Paper-only dossier bead; dispatch AFTER the X1-X5 spike witness lands (its corpus is this dossier's arithmetic). DECIDER: Mike, at the SAME P2/HD-013 sitting — one sitting, no separate gate (the 2026-08-04 adversarial reviews killed the two-sitting variant as not decision-grade).

THE QUESTION: which production server arm does Hicasso graduate with?

DEFAULT DIRECTION (to be priced, not presumed): THE JVM STRUCTURAL WALK — a JVM twin of the codec's pure analysis rules emitting the Spec 004B v1 structural tree, folded to HTML by the SHIPPED react-dom-19.2.0-pinned emit-ui-tree, reads resolving via rf/compute-sub against the request snapshot, in-process with ssr-ring (the platform's host; Spec 011's HTTP response contract stays there). Uniquely, this route also co-discharges HD-021(a)'s headless testing door (same structural-render core, two resolvers: snapshot for SSR, override-map for tests). KNOWN RISK ROWS the dossier must price from the spike corpus: (1) the walk's real surface is ~35-40 rule-bearing sites (not "~10 rules"), against a codec that was in its highest-churn phase in early Aug (wait for the walk-attack lane to stabilise before building); (2) the TEXT-SEPARATOR row — emit-ui-tree coalesces text runs (ui_tree.cljc:724-731) while React renders children as authored, so [:div "Count: " n] mismatches by construction; 004B:613 flags it [S1-CONFIRM], 011-owned — this row must be closed in the tree spec/emitter before any JVM HTML meets hydrateRoot; (3) the conformance apparatus (two-sided rules corpus + renderToString-authored parity fixtures) is an eternal maintenance tax re-opened at every react-dom bump — price it honestly.

THE ALTERNATIVE (priced beside it): A NODE SIDECAR behind an EDN render contract (JVM keeps HTTP + the event drain via ssr-ring; Node renders markup per request through the SAME entry the spike shipped). No parity tax ever; costs a second production runtime and an ops surface — and it must NOT be framed as replacing the Ring host (the adversarial review's host-fork finding: Node-native-serving-as-reference-host is rejected on the record).

INPUTS: the spike's baked-fixture corpus + feature census + tolerance probes; the live churn state of the codec lane; the HD-021 headless-door demand (does anything else need it by then); K7/P2 timing. OUTPUT: a no-verdict dossier on the standard bead (rf2-2rtt6.1's advisory-input slots) with both branches priced in beads/weeks, named tripwires for the default, and the recommendation stated — the RULING is the operator's at the sitting.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7488 (merged 2026-08-04T11:29:06Z) — REOPENED. The Node-sidecar topology and B1 estimate assume “the JVM serialises the request's db snapshot plus the root form as EDN” and price an “EDN render contract — snapshot + root form out.” The shipped Node entry instead requires `:hiccup` whose Hicasso root is `[<minted head> {props}]`; that head is a CLJS/JavaScript function created by `defview`, does not exist on the JVM, and is not an EDN value. The dossier's own §6 relies on exactly this fact when explaining why canonical EDN renders every function identically. A viable sidecar needs an application-defined stable root/entry identifier (and serializable arguments) resolved inside the per-app Node bundle, or another explicit cross-host registry; it must also state the portable serialization domain/projection for a snapshot rather than assuming arbitrary app state crosses EDN. Reprice B1/B4/B5 and the compliant-topology arrows around that real contract. While touching the census, reconcile §4's “75 top-level forms” with the same section's measured 77 top-level `def*` forms. No duplicate bead: rf2-2rtt6.88 owns this dossier and its estimates.
Merged-PR audit follow-up for #7552 (2026-08-05). The sidecar correction is real, but the same established fact is not applied symmetrically to Arm A. The amended page proves a Hicasso root head is a CLJS function minted by `defview`, and `arm1/lang.clj` deliberately has no JVM implementation. Nevertheless §1 says “a db snapshot and a root form are both in hand where a JVM walk would run,” and the asymmetry table says Arm A names the root with “a Var the JVM calls in-process, as ssr-ring already does.” No such Hicasso JVM Var/root exists today; `ssr-ring`'s root-view precedent is not a Hicasso view implementation. A structural codec twin still needs an application/root authoring contract: for example, require server-rendered views to be `.cljc` and make `defview` mint/register a JVM structural function, or introduce a stable id plus per-app JVM table analogous to the Node table. State and price that work (or explicitly include it in A1/A6) before the P2 comparison; otherwise the PR raises Arm B for a cross-host root problem while presenting Arm A as already holding the same unavailable root. Keep this on decision owner rf2-2rtt6.88; no implementation bead is warranted before the ruling.
PARKED, not ruled — mayor 2026-08-07, and the park IS the finding.

THE GATE AS WRITTEN CANNOT BE EVALUATED. The advisory offered two formulations of the codec-stabilisation condition and they now DISAGREE: 'the [:>]/.104/.107 wave fully merged' is MET (.103, .104, .107, .134 all closed), while 'two weeks with no rule-bearing codec change' is emphatically UNMET. front/codec.cljs measured today at 2,815 lines / 101 top-level definitions against 2,342 / 89 on 2026-08-06 — +473 lines and +12 definitions in ONE DAY, with the [:>] escape landing this morning. Fifth consecutive tripwire measurement, steepest yet.

WHY NEITHER ARM CAN START ANYWAY. Both advisory positions already agree Arm A must not start now. And the tree cannot start Arm A regardless: no JVM Hicasso root, no JVM emitter of Hicasso semantics, and defhost :ssr :render (landed 2026-08-05) is structurally unreachable from a JVM twin. Arm B would buy a second production runtime and ops surface permanently.

WHAT IS SETTLED AND NEED NOT BE RE-DERIVED: prep complete, audited twice (#7488, #7552). Arm A 5-8.5wk / 6 beads, Arm B 5.5-10wk / 7 beads — the BANDS OVERLAP, so this is not a schedule choice; the durable differences are one runtime vs two and one emitter vs two. SSR speed is OFF THE BAR; neither arm is owed a clock row. Node-as-reference-host is rejected on the record.

THE RULING: neither arm starts before a P2 sitting exists. This forecloses nothing and costs nothing. STOP THE RECURRING CONSOLIDATION AND THE DAILY CHURN RE-MEASUREMENT — six review rounds have produced no new information, and a ruling taken today would be taken against a codec that grew 20% this morning.

UN-DEFER WHEN: a P2 sitting is convened, or an open bead requires HD-021(a)'s headless door (verified: none exists today), which would put real weight on Arm A.

DOSSIER LANDED — PR #7488, branch worker/serverarm-2rtt6-88, commit 3bed72d29f.
Page: docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md. NO VERDICT and NO
RECOMMENDATION drawn. decisions.md, validation.md and rf2-2rtt6.1 untouched;
no runtime change, no gate, no spec edit; implementation/ssr and ssr-ring
untouched.

TWO INSTRUCTION TEXTS DISAGREE, and the page says so in its own section 0
rather than resolving it silently. This bead's DESCRIPTION asks for "the
recommendation stated"; the dispatching brief, quoting Mike later the same
day, says "do not recommend" and calls it a no-verdict dossier. The page
follows the later text. If a recommendation is wanted it is one paragraph on
top of the page, not a rewrite of it.

LANDING SITE, likewise flagged rather than assumed. The description says the
output lands on rf2-2rtt6.1's advisory-input slots; the brief fences
rf2-2rtt6.1's own notes. The conservative reading won, so the dossier is a
design-record page (the hd-002-adjudication.md precedent) indexed from
docs/design/hicasso/README.md and pointed at from draft-guide/10's "Not
settled" row. Appending the pointer to rf2-2rtt6.1 is the mayor's or the
operator's to do.

=== BOTH ARMS PRICED — the headline asymmetries ===

THE FLOOR IS HIGHER THAN THE BEAD TEXT IMPLIES. emit-ui-tree ships and is
final (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc, 1,040 lines; 004B
calls it pure, deterministic to the byte, JVM-runnable, react-dom 19.2.0
pinned four times in source). A JVM interpreted structural walk to the v1
tree ALREADY SHIPS, for Freehand — re-frame.freehand.tree (678) + node.cljc
(1,438) + conversion.cljc (906), reaching emit-ui-tree via emit-static-html
(tree.cljc:632-654) behind the Independence wall, driven by the shipped
v/render-static macro. So the walk arm's back half is a thing to be CALLED,
not built. What has no precedent in this tree is READS: Freehand's JVM walk is
a pure function of its argument, and v/render-static fails a v/sub loud with
:rf.error/view-read-outside-render rather than resolving one.

BOTH ARMS NEED THE SAME NEW SEAM. ssr-ring hard-calls ssr/render-to-string on
hiccup at ring/pipeline.clj:546 — the stock-Reagent tier 004B freezes. Named
so neither arm looks cheaper by having it quietly assumed.

THE SPIKE BUILT THE NODE ARM'S RENDER, NOT ITS TOPOLOGY. ssr-ring is JVM-only
.clj in EVERY file, so the spike's Node entry hand-writes what it cannot
reach: the #__rf_payload script tag (entry.cljs:184-200, with a docstring
obliging byte-identity with shell/payload-script-tag) and the whole page
envelope (entry.cljs:202-231). Its own docstring says "Not a production host";
the driver's serve() disclaims the response accumulator, cookies, redirects
and CRLF fail-fast. THERE IS NO JVM<->NODE CONTRACT IN THE TREE. The
R0-compliant sidecar — JVM host, JVM payload, JVM shell, Node returning a body
string — has not been built and has not been measured. That is the single
largest unmeasured thing in the dossier.

THE CORPUS SPLITS CLEANLY, and this is the reading most likely to be got wrong
at the sitting. X2/X3/X4/X5 are CLIENT-half rows: the hydration door, the
adoption, reactivity-on-React's-schedule, liveness and teardown hold whatever
produced the bytes, so they transfer to BOTH arms unchanged. Only X1 speaks to
a server half, and only Node's.

THE WALK ARM'S LIKELIEST DIVERGENCE IS THE ONE NOTHING CAN SEE. 004B: two
emitters, divergence "detected, not prevented". 011 Hydration-mismatch
detection: React-native adoption deliberately does NOT report attribute-only
mismatches (React documents no guarantee that attribute differences are
patched; neither onRecoverableError nor any production equivalent fires).
Composed: a JVM-table vs react-dom attribute disagreement is invisible at
runtime, so detection must come from the parity corpus in CI or not at all.
The Node arm cannot produce that class — one emitter makes both sides.

THE PARITY TAX, PRICED HONESTLY RATHER THAN RHETORICALLY. The apparatus EXISTS
and RUNS — parity_fixtures.cljc 643 lines / 66 cases, JVM side computed at CLJS
compile time and embedded (no checked-in goldens), emit_ui_tree_cljs_test.cljc
pinning the serialiser's table copies byte-for-byte against re-frame.ui.rules,
and implementation/ui/dev/react-conform-probe.cjs as the tool that talks to a
real react-dom. So the bump tax has a NAMED HOME and is bounded work, which is
cheaper than "eternal maintenance tax" suggests. Less comfortably: that pin
anchors the serialiser to the UI COMPILER's table. A Hicasso twin has no such
anchor and owes a second pinning relationship — new apparatus, not an
extension.

CHURN, MEASURED. front/codec.cljs was CREATED 2026-07-31 and has taken 23
commits in four days: 1 / 6 / 8 / 6 / 2. All semantic (tag shorthand onto the
emitted slot, frame-as-codec-prop, the IME composition shadow, defhost's :ssr
gate). Wider: front/ 3/11/17/19/4 and arm1/ 8/17/17/26/13 over the same days.
A twin started at the beginning of that week would have needed four semantic
amendments in four days. This is the sharpest number on the page and the one
the sitting can act on immediately.

BEADS/WEEKS (ESTIMATES, labelled as such in the page). JVM walk: 6 beads,
5-8.5 weeks (the .cljc twin 1.5-2.5, the read resolver 0.5, intents/controlled/
presence/route-link 1-1.5, the text-separator settlement 0.5-1.5 AND IT MAY
REACH THE SPEC, the parity extension 1-2, the ssr-ring seam + witness 0.5).
Node sidecar: 6 beads, 4-6.5 weeks (EDN render contract 0.5-1, a callable
process with supervision 1-2, the JVM side 0.5-1, the per-app server-bundle
build story 1-1.5, a skew detector 0.5, the end-to-end witness 0.5). THE BANDS
OVERLAP — on build cost these arms are not far apart and the choice is not a
schedule choice. The durable differences are one runtime against two and one
emitter against two, and both are permanent where build cost is paid once.

=== THE TWO INSTRUMENT FACTS ===

1. :rf/render-hash. NOTHING IN THE DOSSIER LEANS ON IT. Three observations for
rf2-2rtt6.91's owner, offered as observations and not rulings: (a) NEITHER ARM
REPAIRS IT — the degeneracy is a client-side fact, and a deep server hash the
client cannot reproduce makes every page a mismatch, which is why rf2-2rtt6.86
declined to invent one; (b) the PRODUCTION call site takes the hash from the
root hiccup BEFORE the render (lifecycle/render-document-hash at
pipeline.clj:543), so the degeneracy reaches production identically whichever
arm renders; (c) SPEC 011 ALREADY HAS A STATED POSTURE — its mismatch section
is tiered by client render-tree representation, and both the compiled tier and
native React-element roots "deliberately carry no such hash", verifying by
React-native adoption through onRecoverableError instead. Hicasso is a React
adapter minting React-element roots. On that reading .91's candidate (c) is not
a concession but 011's own existing answer for Hicasso's tier, and rf2-2rtt6.97
has already landed the door that answer requires.

2. UTF-16 BYTE ACCOUNTING: STILL UNREPAIRED. driver.cjs has exactly ONE commit
in its whole history (9214396f73, its creation). documentBytes is still
document.length (driver.cjs:176-187) and the live log still prints a
".length B" figure (driver.cjs:235-237). NO SIZE FIGURE FROM THAT MANIFEST
APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THE DOSSIER. X1(a)'s 3,101 is used only as an identity
claim, never as a size. The SHA-256 is unaffected (explicit utf8 encoding at
driver.cjs:129).

=== TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE DISPATCHING BRIEF ===

(1) THE TEXT-SEPARATOR CITATION WAS WRONG. ui_tree.cljc:724-731 is
emit-children, a str/join — the serialiser receives children ALREADY coalesced
(its own docstring says so at line 541). Coalescing lives at TREE-BUILD time,
in three independent .cljc implementations of one algorithm:
ui/tree.cljc:110-116, ui/semantic.cljc:208-219, freehand/node.cljc:359-374.
The ROW is real and open — spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:613,
[S1-CONFIRM], 011-owned — and it carries NO BEAD (the merged-PR audit rf2-7uil4
recorded it as "already an explicitly open 011-owned row, not rediscovered
here" and deliberately left it unfiled). A Hicasso JVM twin would need a FOURTH
coalescer: the CLJS codec has none, which is exactly why React's own render is
separator-correct and a structural tree's would not be. AND X1(b) DOES NOT
RESCUE IT — "the comparator skips comment nodes" is a property of
lane/canonical, and React's hydration reconciler is not that comparator; X1(b)
was also judging bytes react-dom/server itself produced. Worse, the existing
parity corpus renders its React side with renderToStaticMarkup
(parity_corpus_cljs_test.cljs:36), which emits no separators — THE GATE THAT
EXISTS CANNOT SEE THIS ROW.

(2) "~35-40 RULE-BEARING SITES" IS CORROBORATED, and the page enumerates the
roster rather than asserting the count. front/codec.cljs: 77 top-level def*
forms, 57 of them defn/defn-; the rule-bearing subset lands at 35-40, rostered
with line ranges (reserved-name? 180-202, parse-tag 241-245, prop-name 274-308,
the one-slot-per-spelling family 405-465, fold-shorthand! 488-524, merge-caller
571-618, check-ref! 624-654, convert-props 656-791, memoize-boundary! 847-945,
mint-host!/declared-ssr/mint-host-gate! 1039-1173, the lazy-seq forcing walk
1201-1414, the emission dispatch 1420-1673, vec->element 1677-1706, as-element
1708-1749, root-element 1751-1770).

=== UNMEASURED, NAMED EXPLICITLY (9 items in the page) ===

No JVM emitter of Hicasso semantics exists, so no parity row does. No
JVM<->Node seam exists, so no sidecar latency, throughput or
snapshot-serialisation figure does. NEITHER ARM HAS A CLOCK ROW AND NEITHER IS
OWED ONE — SSR speed is off the bar by HD-012 and validation.md, so a sitting
asking for a speed comparison is asking for something the programme has ruled
it does not measure. The cost of resolving reads through compute-sub on a real
page (the mechanism and a shared memo both exist — subs.cljc:2183 and
compute-sub-with-memo at :2236 — but the census seven-read archetype has never
been run). The text-separator fixture. The attribute-only class, on either arm.
HD-021(a)'s headless demand — the door is genuinely absent
(draft-guide/08-testing.md says "Not built yet", "sketch — not built", "does
not exist yet") and NO open bead requires it, so the walk arm's co-discharge is
a benefit whose absence nobody has costed. How many of the 66 parity cases need
Hicasso siblings. And Node's runtime pin is CI-only: the workflows pin node 24,
package.json carries no engines field and there is no .nvmrc.

TRIPWIRES for whichever arm is chosen are in section 11. For the walk: a parity
case where the emitters disagree about the TREE rather than the markup (004B
under-specified for Hicasso), a separator settlement that changes the canonical
form (every v1-tree consumer in scope), a rule that cannot be twinned because it
needs a live React value at render time, a third emitter appearing. For the
sidecar: anything beyond body markup crossing the contract (the rejected host
fork arriving by increments), the sidecar needing to drain events, a view-code
skew reaching a deploy, snapshot serialisation appearing in a profile.

node=false; the documentation tier ran, including mkdocs --strict at 23.53s).

three touched files, 0 mismatches (the new page carries 9 at 2/3/3/4/2/3/3/3/3
columns). shellcheck is not installed and no shell files changed. No required
check came back CANCELLED.

AUDIT #7488 DISCHARGED — PR #7552, branch worker/sidecar-2rtt6-88, commit cfcc662ae5. Page: docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md. Bead deliberately LEFT OPEN — the ruling is the operator's at the P2/graduation sitting.

THE AUDIT IS CORRECT AND THE CONTRADICTION WAS REAL. entry/render takes :hiccup ('REQUIRED. The root hiccup form'); a Hicasso root is [<minted head> {props}]; defview expands to a def of (runtime/mint-view! "<ns>/<sym>" (fn ...)) and mint-view!'s docstring insists the returned value is still the function. arm1/lang.clj states the JVM half itself: it is a .clj not a .cljc because 'the runtime it names is CLJS-only ... and a .cljc would invite a JVM-side implementation this arm does not have'. So the head has no JVM referent and is not EDN — the same fact section 6 used to explain why [#fn[] {}] hashed one constant.

THE CONTRACT AS RESTATED: a NAME, not a form. An application-defined stable entry identifier, opaque to the JVM, resolved INSIDE the per-app Node bundle against a table that bundle publishes, plus root arguments in a stated serialization domain. Not an invention — core registers views under stable ids and looks them up with rf/view. What is absent is Hicasso participating: defview DOES capture "<ns>/<sym>" and mint-view! stamps it as displayName, but that name rides ON the head and is not a key TO it. The inverse map exists in neither host.

THE SNAPSHOT DOMAIN, and this is the sharper half. payload-policy / project-app-db-egress / project-runtime-db CANNOT be reused: the payload is what the CLIENT may see, the snapshot is what the VIEWS must read, and the second is a superset by construction. So the sidecar needs a SECOND, LARGER EGRESS with no policy written for it. The failure modes are asymmetric — a narrow payload allowlist costs the client a recompute; A NARROW RENDER PROJECTION IS A SILENTLY WRONG PAGE. Spec-Schemas' machine-snapshot round-trip rule ((read-string (pr-str x)) =-equal, 'no functions, atoms, JS objects') is the right rule in the right shape but has never been stated for app-db, and nothing validates it there.

ONE ARROW THE OLD TEXT HID: R0 puts the drain on the JVM, so Node must NOT run :initial-events and everything must arrive as :snapshot. The entry's door is :rf/set-db, which seeds APP-DB ONLY — the frame's runtime-db (route slice, machine snapshots) has NO INBOUND DOOR ON THIS PATH AT ALL.

REPRICED. B1 split rather than inflated, because the audit's real finding is that one row hid three contracts: B1a entry identifier 0.5-1wk; B1b serialization domain 1-2wk AND IT MAY REACH THE SPEC. B4 1-1.5 -> 1.5-2.5 (the bundle must publish the entry table, not just build). B5 0.5 -> 0.5-1 (deploy-time identity check PLUS per-request unknown-id refusal) — and this is the one place the correction makes the arm CHEAPER, since the entry table gives skew something concrete to compare. Arm B: 4-6.5wk/6 beads -> 5.5-10wk/7 beads. Arm A untouched at 5-8.5/6. Bands still overlap across most of their range, so 'not a schedule choice' survives; the sidecar's TOP now sits above the walk's. Section 10 states the two reasons AS A PAIR so neither leans.

CENSUS RECONCILED: at a40da23a51, 18 def + 26 defn + 31 defn- + 2 deftype = 77; drop the two deftypes (ParsedTag, PropSlot) and you get 75. Both were right; neither stated its rule. 77 is now the figure under 'every top-level definition'. defn/defn- is 57 either way.

CITATIONS: every line citation on the page is now a symbol name. I could NOT reproduce the '~400 lines off' the brief reported — largest drift I measured is 144 (root-element), then 69 (render), 63, 43. Nine were still exact, which is the trap. Sweep bead filed: rf2-2rtt6.129.

NO VERDICT ADDED, and the sidecar is not reframed as replacing the Ring host — the host-fork rejection is cited twice as binding. comments.text:
OPERATOR RULING (Mike, 2026-08-08, given in chat — his wording is the artefact): "Let's go with arm B." THE RULING: the production server arm is the NODE SIDECAR (Arm B). ssr-ring remains the HTTP host and owns the request, frame, event drain, status, headers, cookies, redirects, head, hydration payload, shell, and error projection; a supervised Node process running the same compiled CLJS bundle as the client returns BODY MARKUP ONLY through a versioned fail-closed envelope. One emitter — the JVM-twin divergence class cannot exist. Arm A (the JVM structural walk) is not chosen; it remains available in principle only if the product ever deliberately names a RESTRICTED JVM SSR DIALECT with explicit exclusions and accepts permanent React-version parity ownership. OPERATIVE READING (advisory-derived, operator-overturnable): the ruled first scope is FULL, NON-STREAMING Hicasso SSR on the renderToString basis — the shape both advisories priced. Spec 011 streaming participation is NOT covered by this ruling: if graduation scope ever includes it, the recorded extra gate applies (run the streamed Node→Ring vertical spike — two overlapping real requests, one genuinely suspended boundary, pre-commit status/error handling, back-pressure/cancellation, request-scoped adoption/frame cleanup, final payload authority, deploy identity, hydration after the last chunk — and REPRICE before building that tier). The fresh probe evidence behind this gate: renderToPipeableStream returns before onShellReady/onAllReady, while the current entry relies on synchronous renderToString with a process-global adoption window closed in its immediate finally — a naive streaming substitution would tear down before completion, and overlapping streams could close each other's adoption windows. RULING != START. Per the park's own principle and the 2026-08-08 Codex pass ("do not start either production arm merely to preserve the option"): implementation dispatches only when a real production-SSR caller exists — i.e., on a P2 GO with SSR in delivery scope. If the fork lands adapters-as-success, this ruling stands recorded and nothing builds. Selecting Arm B selects a destination; it does not approve the spike as production topology (today there is no JVM<->Node request protocol, no entry registry, no supervised pool, no real body-only round trip; the Ring pipeline still calls JVM ssr/render-to-string; the driver's HTTP server is explicitly a demo). START GATES (acceptance criteria for the eventual bead breakdown, before any build — consolidated from the bead's four gates + the 2026-08-08 Codex refinement): 1. Versioned, fail-closed body-render protocol: correlation id, protocol version, application build/schema identity, stable root id, serializable arguments, validated render-state projection in; body markup or a typed error out. No function crosses the boundary. Unknown root, skewed identity, malformed/oversized input, and missing required render state all REFUSE rather than render partial nil state. 2. One per-application Node registry resolving the stable root id from the exact server bundle shipped with the client bundle. It must not grow into a per-component or per-route RPC catalogue. 3. A per-application state projector with round-trip fixtures over a representative real page and at least one NEGATIVE fixture proving an omitted server read fails. Do not reuse the client payload allowlist — the render-visible domain and the browser-egress domain answer different security questions. 4. Long-lived bounded worker pool: deadlines, cancellation, restart/health behaviour, max message/body sizes, build-skew telemetry, overload behaviour; the chosen transport honors flow control (Node's documented IPC/stream back-pressure semantics — unbounded sends are not safe). 5. The topology fence, witnessed: prove the actual JVM->Node->JVM path end to end, including timeout, worker death, malformed reply, unknown entry, build skew, and hydration of adjacent text, controlled inputs, all three defhost :ssr policies, multiple frames, and an :advanced client build. NEW DURABLE FACTS from the 2026-08-08 Codex pass (preserved here; the dossier is deleted after this note): - The existing parity corpus (parity_corpus_cljs_test.cljs) calls renderToStaticMarkup, so it CANNOT see the hydration separator row (renderToString emits
ab
; renderToStaticMarkup and the JVM emitter both emit
ab
). Load-bearing for anyone revisiting Arm A or extending the corpus. - suspense.cljc returns :rf/suspense-boundary only on CLJ; on CLJS — the branch the Node renderer runs — it returns the body ("Not React Suspense"). Spec 011's shipped stream is a JVM hiccup walker with its own marker/continuation/delta/chunk-order/failure/teardown protocol; native renderToPipeableStream emits React's protocol, not Spec 011's. Streaming is a protocol decision, not a function rename. - NAMED FALSIFIERS (unmeasured, honest): cross-process latency, and whether a representative application's full render-visible state is serializable at acceptable cost. A real application may show the projection is effectively the whole frame, or that operating Node is unacceptable — either finding can disqualify Arm B in practice. Neither overturns the semantic decision rule; both belong in the first implementation bead's measurement plan. CONSEQUENCES: the [S1-CONFIRM] text-separator row obligation DISSOLVES (it was file-only-if-Arm-A). The sitting's agenda narrows — the server-arm item is resolved ahead of it; remaining room items are the K-waiver questions and the fork. The streaming-scope question survives only as the extra gate above.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07 10:29 AUSEST, operator-overturnable): HOLD. defview keeps the context-fed mint-view! shell. The frame-as-a-prop variant is not adopted now, and its clock rows are DEMAND-GATED rather than queued — do not spend a quiet-box slot on them unless the trigger below fires. Bead moves to deferred with that trigger; the heap half's publication obligations are complete.

WHY (weighing the dossier recommendation and Codex's independent code inspection, which converged on hold but differed on adoption conditions — the stricter bar is adopted because it follows from verified code, not caution):

1. The saving does not buy a gate. -45.0 B / -4.1% (Reagent) and -46.5 B / -4.2% (UIx) are real (bands disjoint), but frame-prop+wrapper still fails the 1 KB paper line (1.05x vs context's 1.10x), returns only 45 of the wrapper's 105 B (43%), and sits below validation.md's ~75 B component-shape sensitivity. Explicitly NOT an alternative to HD-028's pre-registered fallback. A variant that changes no verdict is optionality, not need.

2. It is a performance trade, not an architectural simplification. Verified today: the provider is still installed regardless (mount.cljs render! docstring — the other React-shaped adapters, the error boundary, and the presence tray resolve their frame from context), so the variant does not remove the context channel; it ADDS a second frame-delivery channel with its own invariant: heads marked, rfFrame stamped at element creation, root-element required at ancestor-less creators, and rfFrame compared in the memo comparator (codec.cljs ~814-848, 889-906, 2044-2053, 2777-2796). React context pierces memo; props do not — so the comparator MUST account for the frame, and frame_prop_dom_cljs_test.cljs:268-287 (a-frame-change-with-unchanged-props-still-re-renders) is the witness that this failure mode is real, not theoretical. The fallback-minted-nil edge it already exposed (fenced by refusal, fallback_contents_cljs_test.cljs:34-47, 305-319) is evidence of repair AND of the ongoing maintenance cost of the second channel. Here the codec, not the author, threads the prop, so the usual explicit-data-flow benefit of props does not accrue.

3. The published heap result is mechanism evidence, not a current-tree receipt. The experiment pinned arm1/lang.clj 74cfbfab7e77, arm1/runtime.cljs 8b37dd2cbf67, front/codec.cljs cf9ef32dc8f75; verified today at HEAD 8fd35f25fd the same paths are 8c18fb0c4d43 / 3ac9dcd7579e / 378de06fdc6d. The codec has churned heavily since the runs. Any adoption decision needs the pair re-taken on the tree it would land on.

ADOPTION BAR (all three required; recorded so a future sitting doesn't relitigate from scratch):
  (a) a current-tree paired A1->B->A2 heap re-take reproducing the win on the exact tree proposed for adoption;
  (b) reportable M1 and bulk clock rows for the variant with no reportable regression;
  (c) a CONCRETE NEAR-TERM USE for the freed hook slot (context shell 2 hooks -> frame-prop 1, in a fully spent <=2 budget) — named by a sitting or a v0 heap-hardening pass. Mere future optionality is insufficient: 45-46.5 B alone does not repay a second frame-delivery invariant.
Adoption must also preserve the existing witnesses as gates: multi-frame isolation, foreign-child frame preservation, same-props frame-change, root/outward-bridge, SSR/hydration, and fallback-refusal.

TRIGGER to un-defer: a P2 sitting (or v0 heap-hardening pass) names the freed hook slot or the ~45 B as needed — then run (a)+(b) in one quiet-box window and dispose. rf2-029ed (the clock_run.cjs refusal that blocked scope item 3) is CLOSED, so the rows are runnable the day the trigger fires; the toggle remains one symbol in arm1/lang.clj's defview (mint-view! -> mint-frame-prop-view!), reverted byte-identically in the experiment, with resolve-frame-prop! raising :rf.error/no-frame-prop rather than falling back silently.

(Concurs with the census quiet-box session review: these rows do NOT join that window.)

title: MEASURE: cross-check our clock harness against krausest/js-framework-benchmark — an instrument nobody here wrote
description:
RAISED by Mike (2026-08-01), who asked whether we should be considering https://github.com/krausest/js-framework-benchmark. Verified from the repository rather than recalled.

WHAT IT IS: 12 measured operations — create 1,000 rows; replace all; partial update (every 10th row); select row; swap rows; remove row; create 10,000 rows; append to a large table; clear; plus ready/run/update memory — with additional replace-memory, repeated-clear-memory and startup metrics, and Lighthouse figures (TimeToConsistentlyInteractive, ScriptBootUpTime, MainThreadWorkCost, TotalByteWeight). Driven by chromedriver against Chrome's timeline, with 5 warmup iterations. 186 implementations. Framework entries live under frameworks/[keyed|non-keyed]/<Name>, need npm install + npm run build-prod, FIXED version numbers (no ranges), the reference implementation's exact button ids, and must pass npm run rebuild-ci.

WHY IT IS WORTH USING HERE, and it is not mainly about the leaderboard: THIS SESSION FOUND FIVE DEFECTS IN OUR OWN MEASUREMENT APPARATUS — a contaminated run under load, a stale bundle silently measured after a par-compile abort, a segment-order effect, a null a confounded design could not have produced, and a 'held-out' rung that was an exact algebraic identity of the checks it was meant to validate. Every one was caught by auditing ourselves, which worked but cost a great deal. AN INSTRUMENT NOBODY HERE WROTE SIDESTEPS THAT WHOLE CLASS.

ITS OPERATIONS MAP ONTO EXACTLY WHAT IS UNMEASURED: create-1000 is mount; partial-update-every-10th is narrow; replace-all and swap are bulk. Those are the clock rows Hicasso has never taken. And it reports memory ALONGSIDE duration, which is the direct way to see whether the 415 B/read proxy shows up on the clock at all.

THE LIMITS, stated so nobody over-reads it: its app is a table of rows with essentially trivial state. re-frame2's value is subscription fan-out, frame isolation and boundary-scoped reactivity, NONE of which that workload exercises. It can say whether Hicasso's RENDERING is competitive with React/Vue/Svelte/Solid; it cannot say whether the reactivity design earns its keep — the census-derived witnesses still own that half. There is also a real Goodhart risk in optimising for a public leaderboard rather than for the shapes the census found. AND THERE IS NO CLOJURESCRIPT ENTRY among the 186, so there is no Reagent baseline in that harness; one would have to be written for the comparison to mean anything. That is the real cost.

THE RECOMMENDED SHAPE — a CROSS-CHECK, not a new bar:
  1. Implement the benchmark app in Reagent and in Hicasso, locally.
  2. Run both under its driver.
  3. Compare the RATIO against what our own harness reports for the equivalent operations.
  4. If the two instruments agree on the ratio, our clock rows become trustworthy. IF THEY DISAGREE, THAT IS THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING AVAILABLE — it means our harness has a defect we have not found.

DO NOT upstream an entry yet. That is a maintenance commitment and pre-alpha is the wrong time; it is a separate decision once the numbers are known.

title: MEASURE: the :& attribute-merge spelling's clock cost is unmeasured (HD-023 caveat)
description:
RAISED by the rf2-2rtt6.36 worker (PR #7328), which recorded the gap in HD-023 rather than letting it pass silently.

THE OBLIGATION IT TRIPS. The 'Hicasso authors no codec' ruling (rf2-2rtt6.29, PR #7322) carries an explicit caveat: reagent-slim's codec is cheapest AS MEASURED, and Freehand's extra per-element capabilities (controlled-input door, caller split, top-layer, declared properties, id-conflict, class/style alias composition) are a CAPABILITY difference rather than pure overhead — so 'if Hicasso later needs one of those capabilities, THE COST OF ADDING IT TO SLIM'S CODEC MUST BE MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED'. The :& merge is exactly such an addition: a reserved key the codec must recognise and resolve at every element that carries one.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT KNOWN. The ergonomics case is DEMONSTRATED, not asserted — the RealWorld article editor was ported both ways with elements AND dispatched intents asserted identical, four repeated attribute maps collapsing to one helper plus four call sites, and the helper does not have to defend itself. What is NOT known is what :& costs on the clock, per element and per mount, against the same page without it.

THE WORK: price :& on the existing lane — same witness, same rounds, same arm-order discipline, the only variation being whether the page uses :& or the expanded attribute maps it replaces. Report per-element and per-mount cost with ranges, and state plainly whether it is inside instrument resolution. If it is free, say so and the caveat is discharged; if it is not, the figure belongs beside HD-023 so the ergonomic win is quoted with its price rather than without it.

SEQUENCING: needs a QUIET BOX (browser measurement) and should run after PR #7328 lands so it measures the shipped spelling. Do not re-litigate the ergonomics ruling — that is settled and demonstrated; this bead prices it.

The promised instrument and HD-023 publication landed intact: authored and landed blob hashes match for both changed files; the derived compile roster includes re-frame.bench.hicasso.amp-merge-clock-app exactly once; CI compiled all 140 rostered namespaces with zero warnings; and the slug and provenance checks pass on the landed commit.

The published estimator is named incorrectly. docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md calls the three table values “run-medians”, then calls their spans “effect medians” and “null medians”. The code does not compute those medians: lane/ratio-between constructs the five per-round ratios and stores their arithmetic average in :mean; amp_merge_clock_app prints that :mean into each run result. This is not a stylistic distinction because the separation from the NULL arm is the stated basis for “outside instrument resolution”.

Correct the publication to name the estimator it actually used, or compute the stated median from the retained per-round values, and re-check that the ~25% and resolution conclusions still follow. Do not widen into the already-separated decomposition: rf2-z143r remains the exact owner for apportioning caller map, helper/dissoc, and codec cost. The positive-control adjudication is separately recorded on reopened exact method owner rf2-egdaq.

DELIVERED — PR #8333 (merged 48c85510c4), wording follow-up PR #8339. Worker worktree w-lane-est. NO WINDOW WAS RUN; the per-round values that existed were read, not re-taken.

PREMISE CHECKED AT SOURCE AND IT HELD. lane/ratio-between builds five per-round ratios and stores their ARITHMETIC MEAN in :mean; amp_merge_clock_app prints that :mean; decisions.md called the three values 'run-medians' and their spans 'effect medians' and 'null medians'. Exactly as the audit read it.

ROUTE TAKEN: NAME THE ESTIMATOR. The median route was tested first and is CLOSED — the per-round ratios were never recorded (record! keeps :effect/:null :per-round, but the publication kept only mean and min/max, and the console log is gone), so the stated median cannot be computed from retained data, and re-running was out of scope for this dispatch. The publication now says what it is: each run's figure is the arithmetic mean of that run's five per-round ratios, each of which is a ratio of the two arms' WITHIN-ROUND median mount times — a mean over medians, not a median at the run level. ratio-between's docstring now says the same where the next publisher reads it, which is where the mislabel came from: a median genuinely IS in the pipeline one level down.

THE CONCLUSIONS STILL FOLLOW, and the check is not a formality. Both columns always were the same statistic computed the same way, so the effect-versus-null comparison that carries the claim is untouched by the correction: effect run-means span 1.217-1.270, null run-means span 1.001-1.013, disjoint. '~25% of mount' (mean of the three run values 1.2467) and '~2.4 us per site' (2,625 / 2,375 / 2,375 ns) are unmoved.

WHAT THE CORRECTION DOES CHANGE is how the existing hedge reads, and the page now says so: an arithmetic mean over five rounds is more moveable by ONE round than a median would be, which is precisely why the separation was already claimed BETWEEN runs and not within one. The correction strengthens that hedge rather than undermining it.

SWEEP: 'run-median' elsewhere in the tree was checked. shapes/census_clock_run.cjs genuinely computes a median (const median = p50(finite); rf2-8bgqq moved that ratio's headline to its median) and is correctly labelled. No other publication mislabels this statistic.

THE CONTROL HALF is on rf2-egdaq: the same three runs' positive control was adjudicated under the OVERLAP rule on cross-round aggregates, the instrument now adjudicates every round via lane/control-verdict-strict, and those three runs' strict verdict is not recoverable from what was kept. Re-run filed as rf2-20uei.

DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

MEASUREMENT WINDOW RUN AND CLOSED OUT — worker/measure-pqyxz, PR #8326. The verdict, self-contained.

WHICH CASE IT WAS IN: INSTRUMENT-MISSING. Verified at source before building. Nothing in the tree clocked ':&'. So the instrument half dispatched immediately; the box happened to be quiet, so the window ran too.

THE INSTRUMENT: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/amp_merge_clock_app.cljs, built on rf2-5yn9's direct-return arm-pair shape — one page written twice, which is exactly this bead's 'same witness, same rounds, same arm-order discipline, the only variation being whether the page uses :& or the expanded attribute maps it replaces'. Five arms: :floor, :expanded, :expanded-b (NULL — a second boundary head over the identical body), :merged, :ctl-2x (positive control, the same operation twice in one window, prediction 2.00x by construction). Rides the existing :hicasso-bench build id through run.cjs's HICASSO_INIT_FN, so no shadow-cljs.edn edit. Witness: the article-editor fieldset HD-023 demonstrates on, at 100 boundaries — 1,001 elements, 400 ':&' sites.

The NULL arm is not decoration. This bead asks the run to 'state plainly whether it is inside instrument resolution', and a merged/expanded range that straddles 1.0 says the effect was not seen, never whether it could have been. The null carries no effect by construction, so its reading IS the resolution.

WHAT RAN: three windows, strictly one at a time, back to back, same commit, same design (5 rounds x 3 warm-up + 6 samples). Chromium 147.0.7727.15, :advanced, goog.DEBUG false. All three: fairness gate agreed (three judged arms, 1,001 elements each) and was proven able to answer false; arm-order guard VERDICT reportable; 0 unverified of 270 measured mounts; positive control passed.

  run | merged/expanded | per-round range | NULL expanded-b/expanded | per :& site
   1  | 1.270x          | 1.188 - 1.386   | 1.013x                   | 2,625 ns
   2  | 1.217x          | 0.968 - 1.409   | 1.002x                   | 2,375 ns
   3  | 1.253x          | 1.195 - 1.405   | 1.001x                   | 2,375 ns

THE ANSWER: NOT FREE, and OUTSIDE instrument resolution. On a page where every input carries one, the ':&' spelling costs about 25% of mount and about 2.4 microseconds per site. The three effect medians span 1.217-1.270 while the three null medians span 1.001-1.013, and those intervals do not touch. The per-round ranges are the weaker evidence and are reported rather than leaned on — run 2's includes 1.0, which is why the separation is claimed BETWEEN runs and not within one.

WHAT REFUSED: nothing. No control refused, no gate refused, no window was abandoned.

WHERE IT LANDED: docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md, HD-023's 'Cost, stated' paragraph, now 'Cost, measured' with the table, the instrument named and the scope stated. HD-023(c")'s trailing 'its clock effect is unmeasured like the rest of :&' is corrected in the same commit — the rest of ':&' is no longer unmeasured, and the fold rides the new figure without being apportioned its own share.

WHAT WAS NOT CONCLUDED. The figure prices the AUTHORING CHANGE WHOLE — caller map, helper dissoc, codec merge-caller — and apportions nothing between them. That matters because the first two are the author's code and the third is the codec's. Filed as rf2-z143r rather than added mid-window, per Shape 6. Also not concluded: (c")'s shorthand fold in isolation; any per-mount figure for a page where only SOME elements carry ':&' (the witness is all-or-nothing by construction); and whether 2.4 us is worth acting on, which is a ruling nobody has asked for.

BOX: System Processor Queue Length sampled before certification, before each run, during and at close — 0 on every sample except two transient 1s during run 2's build phase. CPU _Total 11-53%, the peaks being the shadow-cljs :advanced compile that precedes each measured window rather than the window itself. Win32_Processor.LoadPercentage was not used.

title: docs(hicasso): the studio/design tree is excluded from mkdocs --strict, so every 'gate' run against it this session was decorative
description:
FOUND by the rf2-6i0i2 worker (PR #7312) while correcting its own earlier gate claim. VERIFIED by the mayor: mkdocs.yml:32-36 has an exclude_docs block listing 'design/freehand/' and 'design/hicasso/'. So 'python -m mkdocs build --strict' DOES NOT VALIDATE anything under docs/design/hicasso/ — it only proves the rest of the site builds.

WHY IT MATTERS. Across this session many Hicasso docs PRs cited mkdocs --strict as THE gate for edits confined to docs/design/hicasso/studio/**, validation.md, architecture.md and the draft guide. Those edits were effectively UNGATED: a broken internal anchor, a malformed table, or a dead cross-reference in the studio tree would not have been caught by the gate that was run and reported green. This is precisely the class this programme keeps hunting -- a gate that cannot go red has not verified anything -- except here it is our own docs gate, not a bench instrument.

NOT AN EMERGENCY: the excluded content is prose and tables, and at least one worker (PR #7312) checked its page by hand (15 internal anchors resolved, no inconsistent column counts) once it discovered the exclusion. Nothing is known to be broken. The defect is the missing check, not a known break.

THE EXCLUSION MAY BE DELIBERATE -- mkdocs.yml:27 says the Freehand design record is excluded as a durable record, and hicasso sits beside it. So the first question is a DECISION, not a fix: should docs/design/hicasso/ be published/validated by mkdocs at all? Options: (a) keep it excluded from the SITE but add a cheap standalone link/anchor/table checker over the tree, run in CI, so the pages are validated without being published; (b) include the tree in the site and let --strict cover it, accepting whatever nav and build cost that adds; (c) accept it as deliberately unvalidated and STOP citing mkdocs --strict as a gate for edits confined to it -- which then requires every future Hicasso docs brief to say plainly that no gate covers the change.

RECOMMENDATION (mayor): (a). The tree is a working design record, not user-facing documentation, so publishing it is wrong; but its internal anchors and cross-page references are load-bearing for the programme's own readers and are exactly what rots silently. A standalone checker is small and can go red.

Whatever is chosen, the second half is mandatory: dispatch briefs must stop nominating a gate that does not cover the surface being edited.
notes:
OPERATOR CORRECTION (Mike, 2026-07-31): 'design/freehand/ etc are not mkdocs published.' The exclusion is DELIBERATE — these trees are working design records, not user-facing documentation. OPTION (b) IS STRUCK: publishing docs/design/hicasso/ so that --strict covers it was never a real option and is not on the table.

MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION REVISED, and revised DOWNWARD. I previously recommended (a), a standalone anchor/link/table checker in CI. On reflection that is over-engineering for the failure it prevents: the tree is prose and tables read by this programme's own agents, the failure mode is a link that does not jump, and a bespoke CI job to police an internal design record is exactly the kind of machinery this project's stance rejects.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION — (c), plus one cheap check IF and ONLY IF it is nearly free:
1. THE MANDATORY HALF, which costs nothing and is the actual defect: dispatch briefs must STOP nominating 'python -m mkdocs build --strict' as the gate for edits confined to docs/design/hicasso/** or docs/design/freehand/**. It does not cover them. A brief that names a gate not covering its surface is the same fail-open class this programme hunts in its instruments, and the honest form is 'no automated gate covers this surface; the worker verifies anchors by hand and says so' — which is precisely what the rf2-6i0i2 worker (PR #7312) did once it discovered the exclusion: 15 internal anchors resolved, no inconsistent column counts, stated in the PR body.
2. THE CHEAP HALF, only if genuinely cheap: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and scripts/check_readme_links.py already exist and already walk tracked markdown with their own exclude sets (check_doc_slugs.py has EXCLUDE_DIR_REL = {docs/spec, docs/migration}). If either can be pointed at docs/design/** by adding it to an existing roster — a one-line change, no new job, no new script — do that. If it needs a new script, a new CI job, or non-trivial rework, DO NOT DO IT; item 1 alone discharges this bead.

Nothing is known to be broken in the tree today.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7318 (cursor-gap repair, 2026-08-03): REOPENED this exact owner; no duplicate. The M1 prose reconciliation is sound and later #7335 updated every affected site to the corrected five-run 1.0150x interval. The docs-gate guidance remains incomplete across active agent surfaces: PR #7318 added the exclusion warning to CLAUDE.md and the dispatch template, but AGENTS.md is the instruction file Codex workers in this repository are explicitly given and it contains no mkdocs/docs-design scope warning. Add one short cross-agent instruction or pointer stating that mkdocs --strict excludes docs/design/**, check_doc_slugs.py covers links/anchors, and tables/rendering/nav need direct verification. Do not duplicate the long CLAUDE paragraph, add a checker, or publish the design tree.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7911 — REOPEN. The replacement full governing brief opens “This document governs pages under /docs” (docs/AUTHORING.md:3) and ends “On docs PRs: mkdocs build --strict...” (:859-863). mkdocs.yml:32-37 deliberately excludes docs/design/freehand and docs/design/hicasso, so this reintroduces the exact fail-open instruction this owner fixed: a design-only PR can cite a green gate that inspected none of its pages. BOUNDED REPAIR: narrow the opening to the published guide/reference corpus or explicitly carve out durable design records, and qualify the CI paragraph so mkdocs covers only the published corpus; for docs/design/** name check_doc_slugs.py for links/anchors and direct table/render/nav verification. Do not publish the design trees or add a new gate.
RESOLVED by PR #7916 (worker/docgate-x5dvk). The #7911 reopen is discharged and the coverage mapping is now recorded in three places rather than re-derived per dispatch.

THE TITLE'S CLAIM DOES NOT HOLD AS WRITTEN. The exclude_docs half is true; "decorative" is false. Measured, not assumed:

COVERS docs/design/**
  * scripts/check_doc_slugs.py — DEFAULT_ROOTS includes "docs"; its exclusions (docs/spec, docs/migration, and the dir names findings/ai/site/node_modules/.git/.beads/__pycache__) do not touch docs/design. Of the 722 files it scans, 103 are docs/design/hicasso and 37 are docs/design/freehand. Validates intra-repo link TARGETS and heading ANCHORS, and additionally forbids markdown links inside code fences in docs/design/hicasso (FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES). Runs in the fast-PR spine and in docs.yml.
  * scripts/check_provenance_pins.py — DEFAULT_ROOT = "docs/design/hicasso". Its own docs.yml job (`provenance-pins`, fetch-depth 0), scoped to changed pages. hicasso only, not freehand.
  * implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_complaint_catalogue.py — round-trips docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md and docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/** against the runtime and Spec 009, in an unconditional test.yml job.

COVERS NOTHING THERE
  * mkdocs build --strict — and with it rendering, nav, and every published-site concern. Confirmed empirically by a local build: 295 published pages, site/design/ never created, zero pages under either design tree.
  * Tables / column counts — no checker anywhere. Hand verification remains correct and remains the instruction.
  * Prose contradiction — nothing, as expected.
  * The residue gates (check_retired_composition_vocab, check_retired_image_keys, check_inject_cofx_residue, check_retired_spellings) all scan docs/core + docs/api + docs/EP + spec + skills and stop there. The design tree is outside every one.

exclude_docs IS CORRECT POLICY. Not touched. Option (b) was struck by Mike on 2026-07-31 and nothing found here reopens it.

INCIDENTAL FINDING, recorded because it is the same fail-open class one surface over: mkdocs.yml sets no `validation:` block, so mkdocs 1.6's anchor check stays at `info`. A negative control planting a broken same-page anchor AND a broken file target in docs/AUTHORING.md aborted --strict on the target only, logging the anchor as INFO. So check_doc_slugs.py is the anchor authority for the WHOLE corpus, published pages included — not merely a stand-in for the excluded trees. AUTHORING.md already names it "the link/anchor validator", so no edit was made for this; it is noted in case a future brief nominates --strict for an anchor change on a published page.

NO NEW GATE, no CI job, no mkdocs.yml change — per the revised recommendation and the project stance. Nothing is known to be broken in the design tree today.

title: bench(hicasso): lane/control-verdict passes a control the HD-008 rule would fail
description:
*** HALF (a) IS DONE AND MERGED. HALF (b) IS AN OPERATOR CALL. DO NOT DISPATCH. ***

READ THIS BEFORE BRIEFING FROM ANYTHING BELOW. The description's file paths are DEAD - it
names implementation/freehand/..., a tree deleted by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16. Both files live
under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/ now.

HALF (a), THE ADJUDICATION CODE, LANDED IN PR #8574 and returned better than asked. The
worker SPLIT the verdict rather than answering yes or no:
- p0_app.cljs is NOT an allocation arm, it is the P0 CLOCK arm, so the Chrome-clamp carve-out
  was RULED ON it rather than needing to transfer. 80 controls re-adjudicated from the
  committed record: 80/80 pass overlap, 64/80 strict, every miss LOW and on the two rows
  whose legs are 1-3 of Chrome's 100 microsecond quanta, while the 20-plus-quantum rows pass
  strict 40/40. REFUSED, with the reasoning replacing a stale pointer in adjudicate's
  docstring.
- p0_heap.cljs IS the allocation arm the HD-008 argument fits, and WENT STRICT. Byte counter,
  no quantum, and there overlap is not merely weaker but ABSENT: under the loose rule one
  round at 0 B beside five good ones PASSES, which is the exact failure the control exists to
  catch.

WHAT REMAINS IS HALF (b) AND IT IS MIKE'S: are the published P0 rows re-adjudicated, or does
the change apply only from the next run? The bead's own instruction was to record that on
rf2-2rtt6.1, which is CLOSED and is the operator-owned STANDARD.

COST OF THAT HOLD IS LOW AND MEASURED: re-adjudication FLIPS NOTHING. Computed from committed
records with no window run, the widest excursion across ten published heap-control figures is
4,690,838 B, 0.195% below a plus-or-minus-25 percent band.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS (2026-07-30, paths superseded above) ---

Found while consolidating HD-008 onto the lane (rf2-f5roa, PR #7267).

The two positive-control adjudications in the Hicasso tree do NOT agree, and the shared one is the weaker:

  lane/control-verdict           ok? = (and (<= min hi) (>= max lo))
                                 i.e. the measured RANGE need only OVERLAP the +/- slack band.
  hd8-rows/positive-control!     :within? = (and (>= lo (* p (- 1 tol))) (<= hi (* p (+ 1 tol))))
                                 i.e. EVERY round must be INSIDE the band.

HD-008's own comment argues the stricter rule explicitly: 'a control whose worst round is wrong has caught something, and letting a good round vouch for a bad one is how an instrument stops being one.' rf2-f5roa deliberately did NOT adopt lane/control-verdict for that reason.

The lane is what the P0 arms use, so under lane/control-verdict a run with one bad round and one good one passes its own positive control. That is the shape of thing this programme keeps finding: a gate that cannot go red has not verified anything.

NOT REPAIRED IN #7267, deliberately: tightening lane/control-verdict changes the adjudication every published P0 row was taken under. Whoever takes this must decide whether the published rows are re-adjudicated (and say so on rf2-2rtt6.1) or whether the change applies only from the next run.

Files: implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs (control-verdict); implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/hd8_rows.cljs (positive-control!, the stricter rule).
acceptance_criteria: The #8531 measurement record no longer calls rf2-egdaq open and accurately summarizes or links its landed control-adjudication ruling; the arming result and retained raw-data disclosure remain unchanged.
notes:
HALF (a) IS NOW ON THE TRUNK. PR #8642 MERGED 2026-08-21 as 3c4360ab2c, verified by reading the PR state (MERGED) and by fast-forwarding the mayor checkout onto it. One file, implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs, +9/-1: the hardcoded 'lane/control-verdict-strict' literal is gone from printHeapControl's output and the dynamic rule now speaks alone. This note exists because a bead that never closed carries no merge record otherwise, and 'open' is silent about what already shipped. WHAT REMAINS IS HALF (b) AND IT IS MIKE'S: whether the ten published P0 heap-control figures are restated under the strict rule. Not dispatchable work. ONE THING THE WORKER MEASURED THAT IS WORTH KEEPING: reinstating the exact defect leaves the covering gate GREEN at 100 passed, exit 0 — printHeapControl is not exported and nothing matches its output strings, so this printed string has NO automated coverage at all. That gap is deliberate: the audit ruled a census pin out and the stance rejects one. title: hic: remaining SSR prose still calls hand-rolled renderToString the package's only server path
description:
## Owner: found while auditing rf2-s52w. This stale sentence is what PRODUCED that bead's false root cause.

`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66`, under the
header section *## What is deliberately NOT here*, still reads:

> **A Hicasso server entry.** There is none, and none is needed: the consumer calls
> `react-dom/server` and the policy is honoured by rendering. The harness here is
> `renderToString` called by hand, which is the only server path in the package.

Both halves are false at trunk tip.

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs` — 452 lines, `re-frame.hicasso.server/render`
— landed in commit `30317bfe0e` on 2026-08-14 21:28 +1000 (`feat(hicasso):
re-frame.hicasso.server/render, and h/hydrate! on the door (rf2-b6jkj)`, PR #8236). It is a real
product door, not a stub: `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/roots.cljs:50-58`
names it as one of the TWO minters of the adoption window — "once per REQUEST, closed in that
door's `finally`" — and records that because both doors call `impl.mount/tree` "the fork is
decided once for both sides of the wire". So it is neither absent nor a second server path
beside the hand-rolled harness; it is THE server path, and the hand-rolled `renderToString` in
this file is the harness beside it.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than shrugging at

Checkpoint 3 cited THIS FILE, by name and "in terms", as the evidence for a root cause it then
wrote into rf2-s52w: *"THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY. Every server witness in the package
calls react-dom/server's renderToString by hand — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in
terms."* From there it propagated into `docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md:89`,
into `checkpoint-3-native.md`, and finally into a mayor note of 2026-08-21 that raised
"Does Hicasso ship a server entry?" as an open decision for Mike — a week after it shipped.

One stale docstring, four downstream records, one moot operator question. That is the cost, and
it is why this is a bead rather than a shrug.

## It is an omission, not a convention

The bullet DIRECTLY ABOVE it in the same section was amended in place when its own condition
changed: "When this file was written the prefix was UNSPELLABLE ... The operator then ruled a
thin pass-through, so `:identifier-prefix` is now an option on both root doors and the clause is
reachable; what has not changed is that it is not a NATIVE-tier claim, which is why it is still
not here." So the file's convention is to amend and keep the reason. The server-entry bullet was
simply missed — including by the 2026-08-20 sweep that touched this file twice (`7a65ab11d7`,
`53df56d29b`).

## The repair

Amend the bullet in place, in the same shape as its neighbour: the file's own harness is still a
hand-rolled `renderToString` and that is still deliberate (these are NATIVE-tier claims and the
product door is dispositioned elsewhere), but say that `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` exists
and is the package's server path, so the sentence cannot be re-read as a fact about the package.
Keep it a *deliberately not here* bullet; do not turn it into a claim this file does not measure.

While there: check the other bullets in that section against the current tree, since this one
survived two sweeps.

## Fences and gates

- Test-file docstring only. No behaviour change; no assertion touched.
- `implementation/**` is OUTSIDE `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`'s roots — a markdown link planted
  there returns that gate GREEN. `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the gate for markdown
  beside source, and since rf2-i4nb2 its third roster covers non-README tracked markdown — but a
  CLJS docstring is neither, so NO link gate reaches this text. If the amendment adds or changes
  a link, check it by hand and say so in the PR body.
- `verdictlbl` (rf2-egdaq) holds `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/` — a
  different directory. Re-check holders before editing; the fence is a dispatch-time claim.
acceptance_criteria: native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs's 'A Hicasso server entry' bullet no longer asserts that none exists or that the hand-rolled renderToString is the package's only server path; it names re-frame.hicasso.server/render and keeps its 'deliberately not here' framing with the reason. The section's other bullets re-checked against the current tree. No assertion changed.

PR #8645 accurately fixes the two carriers in native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, but a repo-wide exact-claim sweep finds seven live carriers of the same now-false present-tense architecture statement across five other source/test files: identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:24, :93-94 and :204; core_view_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:10; client_only_arms_ssr_cljs_test.cljs:153; facade_roster_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:211; and impl/mount.cljs:182. title: hic: scope row 5's 'mismatch attribution' required result to roots a re-frame2 door opens (rf2-s52w's last acceptance clause)
description:
## Owner: this is rf2-s52w's remaining acceptance clause, not a new finding

rf2-s52w's acceptance option B has three clauses. Two are discharged:

- the source-located statement + measured witness landed in PR #8302 (`473ff5e330`) —
  `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs:30-52` header,
  measured row at `:920`, pointer from `native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:38-46`;
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md:290`'s HS-21 row was amended 2026-08-20 by
  rf2-vwo53 (PR #8559).

The third — *row 5's required-result sentence amended to scope "mismatch attribution" to roots
the package itself adopts* — is still owing, and no open bead owned it before this one.
A later audit re-finding it should recognise it as rf2-s52w's clause, not a second finding.

## The obligation and where it actually lives

Two homes, and it is the SECOND that creates the obligation:

1. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/hot-path-architecture.md:49` — the native tier's only
   release checklist ("A red row blocks publication of the native namespace"). Row 5's
   *Required result* reads "...including server bytes or source refusal, matching hydration,
   **mismatch attribution** and multiple roots".

2. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md:34` — the canonical matrix
   row 5 is measured against. Its per-row hydration column for *Root/frame provider and
   outward bridge* (`:24`) does NOT list mismatch attribution. But the blanket sentence at
   `:34` — "Every Render row runs the common hydration states: matching content, **deliberate
   mismatch with source attribution**, two simultaneous roots with stable `identifierPrefix`,
   and unmount cleanup" — puts it back on every Render row, that one included. So the row's
   omission is not a carve-out and the blanket sentence is what has to be scoped.

## What the scope IS, normatively

`spec/011-SSR.md:825` already states it in as many words: the framework reporter rides the
package's own hydrate path, and "hydrating via the substrate-native renderer directly
(`uix.dom/hydrate-root`, react-dom `hydrateRoot`) bypasses the reporter and falls back to
React's default (silent) handling". `onRecoverableError` is an option of an INDIVIDUAL root
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/roots.cljs:20-27`), so a root the package
did not open takes none of the package's options.

**Scope it by WHO OPENED THE ROOT, not by which surface.** There are two re-frame2 doors that
install the reporter on a React-element root — `h/hydrate!`
(`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:546`) and the Spec 006 client
mount entry `(re-frame.substrate.adapter/render tree mount {:hydrate? true})`
(`implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1107`, whose docstring at `:1191-1204`
names itself the only native mount route that installs it). The outward bridge is not special:
any surface under a root the consumer opened with raw `react-dom/client` is equally outside the
channel. Wording that singles out the outward bridge invites a door for the outward bridge,
which is the wrong remedy.

## Why this is worth one small edit rather than leaving it

The release checklist is a publication gate. As written, row 5 can never go green for a reason
everyone already agrees is correct and normative, so every checkpoint re-derives the same
"unmet" and pays a dispatch to refute it —
