PREMISE CONFIRMED DEAD AT TIP: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/substrate.cljs declares :kind :rf.adapter/hicasso (rf2-hvr5h, PR #8512).

THE TRUE REASON, three claims read at source in docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md 'Hicasso needs a substrate adapter' (+ spec/006:2737): nothing installs an adapter for you and there is no default-adapter registry; a Reagent adapter under a Hicasso tree 'keeps working exactly as it did, and is what you want when the page also renders that substrate's own components: every React-shaped adapter writes the same frame context, so the two subtrees resolve one frame' — a part-migrated page IS that case, which makes the new reason STRONGER for a migration skill than the one it replaces; and Hicasso's adapter is an optional module nothing under its src/ requires. The always-true half (:rf.error/no-adapter-installed until an adapter is installed) is kept everywhere.

THE EVAL (evals.json:139, eval 25 m-root-mount-ensures-frame, expectation index 2): both graded demands kept word-for-word — 'KEEPS (rf/init! ra/adapter)' and 'Does not delete it as Reagent scaffolding.' Only the justification between them moved. As written it rewarded an agent for repeating a false claim about the tree and could penalise one that correctly noticed Hicasso now ships a kind. Retired premise recorded past-tense in the file's notes field citing rf2-hvr5h — that field is where this skill keeps bead ids (already rf2-0yp7w, rf2-b6jkj); references/** carries NONE by this skill's own measured convention and gains none. It arms that surface for skills/re-frame2-pair/*, skills/shared/* and skills/re-frame2-setup/* only; skills/reagent-migration/* matches no case. title: hicasso: a blob pin in the work-census record does not resolve in a fresh clone
description:

WHY THE GATE DID NOT CATCH IT, and this is the part worth keeping: scripts/check_provenance_pins.py classifies hex tokens by CONTEXT, and blob hashes are deliberately classed as digests rather than commit pins — otherwise it would red on every SHA-1 blob, SHA-256 document digest and FNV hash in the corpus and be disabled within a week. Class sweep over 971 tracked markdown files found 17 unresolvable 40-hex tokens, of which 16 are unresolvable by design (external repo commits, sabotage-plant and toggled-arm content hashes never committed, one patch-id) and 1 is this defect, cited twice with the second occurrence deliberately preserved as the subject of rf2-77gz8's observation. comments.text:
PR #8520 — repaired, and the CLASS swept.

Controls: extractor found the known-bad token, resolver returned blob rc=0 on the known-good one and rc!=0 on an all-zero token.

EXACTLY ONE of the 17 is a defect (this one). The other 16 are unresolvable BY DESIGN, in four classes: external repo commits (krausest/js-framework-benchmark, athensresearch/athens, district0x/memefactory, day8/re-frame-10x, day8/clein), sabotage-plant content hashes in plant/restore controls (a changed hash IS the evidence; the planted state is never committed and each row's baseline+restored hashes do resolve), toggled A/B arm hashes where the A blob resolves and the B toggle was never committed, and one git patch-id --stable value which is not an object at all.

title: [story] schemas.cljc docstring says there is no :rf.adapter/hicasso — there is now
description:
`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc` (around line 298) argues why the Story substrate axis is not a mirror of the framework's adapter enum, and rests that argument on a claim that has just become false:

  "`:hicasso` is the member that separates them, and it is why the claim had to go. Hicasso ships
   NO adapter — there is no `:rf.adapter/hicasso` anywhere in the repository, deliberately — and a
   Hicasso application boots on the UIx adapter."

rf2-hvr5h shipped `re-frame.hicasso.substrate` with `:kind :rf.adapter/hicasso` (PR #8512), so the
parenthetical is wrong and "a Hicasso application boots on the UIx adapter" is no longer the
default the install chapter teaches.

PROSE ONLY — nothing in Story branches on this. But the ARGUMENT the docstring makes survives the
correction and is worth preserving rather than deleting: the two axes are still distinct, because a
Story member names WHICH REGISTERED RENDER FN embeds the subject in the canvas, not which renderer
`rf/init!` installed. `:hicasso` still separates them — a Hicasso application may now install
Hicasso's own adapter OR somebody else's and remains one authoring layer either way. Rewrite to
that, rather than dropping the paragraph.

Done in PR #8514 (branch worker/adaptkind-zkjd5), commit 'docs(story): SubstrateSet docstring — Hicasso ships a kind now'.

tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc, the SubstrateSet docstring (the bead said 'around line 298'; the paragraph is at 297-304). Prose only — verified nothing in Story branches on it; the enum itself, [:set [:enum :reagent :uix :hicasso]], is unchanged and was never wrong.

FOLLOWED THE BEAD'S EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION to rewrite rather than delete. The paragraph's ARGUMENT — that Story's substrate axis is not a mirror of the framework's adapter enum, because a member here names WHICH REGISTERED RENDER FN embeds the subject in the canvas rather than which renderer rf/init! installed — survives the correction intact, because it never rested on the absence. What was false was only its supporting claim: 'Hicasso ships NO adapter — there is no :rf.adapter/hicasso anywhere in the repository, deliberately — and a Hicasso application boots on the UIx adapter'.

Rewritten to the bead's own framing: :hicasso still separates the two axes, because a Hicasso application may now install Hicasso's own adapter OR somebody else's — the install is explicit and there is no default-adapter registry — and it remains ONE authoring layer either way (boundaries minted by h/defview, reached through :hicasso/component, crossed into with h/as-element). title: [ci] check_workflow_yaml.py has NO CI home — it is scheduled only in the local spine, which is skippable
description:
FOUND TWICE INDEPENDENTLY, 2026-08-18: first by the rf2-rsn1e worker while wiring the job-cap ratchet, then confirmed by the PR #8477 fix worker. Neither actioned it — both were correctly fenced — so it is filed here.

THE FACT, and it is a CLAIM to re-verify at source: scripts/check_workflow_yaml.py is referenced only from scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, the LOCAL pre-checkin spine. It appears in no workflow job. So nothing in CI runs it.

WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS. A local spine is skippable by construction — this project's own workflow comments repeatedly call that out as not-a-mechanism, and today's evidence is that the spine is routinely NOT run: every worker dispatched during a measurement window was instructed to skip it, and each said so in its PR body. A gate whose only home is the spine is therefore a gate that, in practice, often does not run at all. It is not fail-open — it is not-run.

THE SHARP VERSION OF THE HAZARD, learned the same day on the job next door: PR #8477 went red because scripts/check_workflow_job_timeouts.py was placed in a job that installs no pip packages, and the checker needs PyYAML. It REFUSED correctly, printing 'NOT CHECKED … This is NOT a pass' and exiting 3. But its author had run it LOCALLY and captured exit 0 — because this machine has PyYAML 6.0.2 and the CI runner did not. **A local green proved nothing about CI and actively misled.** check_workflow_yaml.py is the OTHER PyYAML-dependent workflow checker, so it carries the identical dependency and has never been exercised in a CI environment at all.

THE FIX SHAPE, and it is already demonstrated next door: give it a CI home in a job that already runs 'pip install -r requirements.txt'. PR #8477 moved the ratchet's two steps into verify-readme-links for exactly that reason — that job is unconditional, already installs requirements, and already hosts four other non-link gates. Both it and verify-skill-mcp-drift sit in all-required-passed's needs:, so relocating changed the required set not at all.

DO NOT INSTEAD ADD 'pip install' TO verify-skill-mcp-drift. That job's stdlib-only property is deliberate and recorded in THREE places — its own comment ('pure Python stdlib, no setup beyond actions/setup-python'), the verify-readme-links disposition ('dropping it beside the stdlib checkers … would have redded every PR'), and check_fast_pr_gap.py's docstring, which stays stdlib-only naming PyYAML specifically. PR #8477's worker weighed and rejected that route; do not re-litigate it without new evidence.

BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING, CHECK WHETHER IT SHOULD EXIST AT ALL. scripts/check_workflow_job_timeouts.py landed today and parses the same documents. If the two overlap substantially, the honest answer may be to merge them or to close this as minutiae rather than to wire a second parser into CI. The stance rejects gold-plating, and two checkers over one file that disagree in a year is a worse outcome than one.

HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/* is one toucher at a time. Sequence against rf2-fo4ng, which is HELD pending an operator act and will rewrite coordinates across the release workflows.
close_reason: Already closed by #8477, not by wiring — CI asserts every workflow parses via check_workflow_job_timeouts.py's parse arm (exit 2, executed). Disposition recorded in #8482; see the comment.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
CLOSED AS ALREADY-CLOSED, NOT WIRED — PR #8482. The bead's FACT holds; its
CONCLUSION does not, and the difference was settled by execution rather than
by reading.

RE-DERIVED AT HEAD. A fixed-string search finds `check_workflow_yaml.py` in
`scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` and in no workflow. Positive control, the same search
for `check_workflow_job_timeouts`: two hits in `.github/workflows/test.yml`.
So the script genuinely has no CI home.

WHY THAT IS NOT A HOLE. The CLAIM has a scheduled home even though the SCRIPT
does not. `scripts/check_workflow_job_timeouts.py`, merged the same morning in
#8477, walks the same `.github/workflows/*.{yml,yaml}` set through the same
`yaml.safe_load` and RETURNS 2 on a YAMLError rather than skipping —
deliberately: "check_workflow_yaml.py is the gate that reports this properly;
fail rather than skip, so an unparseable file cannot pass vacuously here." It
runs unconditionally from `verify-readme-links` (no `if:` on the job), which is
in `all-required-passed`'s `needs:`.

EXECUTED, NOT READ. An unmatched quote planted on line 1 of an isolated
`--repo-root` copy of test.yml: check_workflow_yaml.py exit 1 with file+line;
check_workflow_job_timeouts.py exit 2, "is not well-formed YAML (ParserError).
Run check_workflow_yaml.py." Control on the same unmodified copy: both 0.

AND VERIFIED IN CI RATHER THAN LOCALLY, which is the trap this bead itself
names. main run 32106872434's predecessor 32105342995 — the #8477 merge —
reports `verify-readme-links` step 19 as SUCCESS. So PyYAML imported on the
runner and every workflow file parsed there. A local green would have proved
nothing.

SO: wiring a second CI parse of the same files, to assert a strict subset of
the same claim, buys nothing but a second thing to keep in step — which is the
outcome this bead's own last paragraph warned against.

MERGING THE TWO IS ALSO REFUSED, AND NOT BY ME. Different charters — "is the
file YAML?" versus "does every job carry a job-level cap" — and
check_workflow_job_timeouts.py's docstring already records the reasoning for
keeping them apart. Nothing new since to re-litigate it with.

WHAT #8482 DID SHIP, both comments, no CI step and no checker:
  - a "WHY IT HAS NO CI HOME" section in check_workflow_yaml.py, so the next
    audit reaches this disposition instead of refiling the bead. What the
    spine lane still buys is the round trip: a line number, and every broken
    file rather than the first.
  - a note at the test.yml wiring marking the timeouts checker's parse arm
    LOAD-BEARING BEYOND ITS OWN CHARTER. Narrowing it to a skip would silently
    delete the only CI-side assertion that the workflows parse, and would
    reopen this bead without touching either script.

WHY check_gate_scheduling.py DID NOT CATCH THIS, since it is the tool that
exists to catch a gate running nowhere: its roster is
`implementation/package.json`'s `test:*` / `bench:*` / `build:*` npm scripts,
not `scripts/check_*.py`. A Python checker with no workflow home is outside
its domain entirely. `check_fast_pr_gap.py` covers only the other direction —
its `--list` flags `check_workflow_job_timeouts` as having "no local lane",
never a spine lane with no CI home. So NOTHING holds `scripts/check_*.py` in
step with a CI home. Recorded rather than filed: this instance turned out to
be a false alarm, which is evidence the class is low-yield, and a third
workflow-reading checker to police the other two is exactly the shape the
project stance rejects. File it if a second real instance appears.

comments.text:
MAYOR 2026-08-18, PRE-DISPATCH SOURCE CHECK — THE BEAD IS NOT 'KEEP OR DELETE DEAD CODE'. It is 'a guard on a LIVE public surface has no callers', which points the opposite way, and I nearly ruled it wrong twice. Recording both wrong turns so the worker does not take them.

VERIFIED AT origin/main c4e15cf6a7, fixed-string with a control: git grep -nF 'guard-open-drain!' -- implementation/ returns EXACTLY ONE LINE, frame.cljc:3521, the defn. Zero call sites. Control: 67 'defn ' in that same file, so the search finds things.

MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS, AND IT IS FALSE. I guessed the guard's lost caller was the retired donor's ui.test/flush!, which would have made both the guard and spec/006's paragraph donor residue, closing the bead as a sweep. **Wrong.** ui.test/flush-presence! is a DIFFERENT surface — a presence fake-clock driver — and it lives in spec/conformance/S4-view-conformance-profile.md, one of the three profiles held for the operator on rf2-h89ri. It is not what spec/006 is describing.

WHAT SPEC/006 ACTUALLY DESCRIBES, read at :1878-1893 rather than inferred: the explicit flush is THE SUBSTRATE'S OWN PUBLIC TEST FLUSH. Its words — 'The headless (JVM/SSR) host has no async render loop and drains through the explicit test flush… On CLJS, the substrate's test flush returns a Promise… On the JVM the zero-arity flush is synchronous and returns nil. **It is the sole public test flush**, and the substrate publishes no production twin of it. A call while an event drain is still open throws :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch synchronously before Promise construction, notifications, or host work.'

So the surface being guarded is LIVE, PUBLIC and SHIPPING. The guard implementing its documented throw has no callers. That is an implementation gap, not dead code — and 'delete it' would delete a guard the spec says a live public API has.

MY SECOND WRONG TURN, WHICH I STOPPED AT: pattern-matching this to rf2-cydkp. There I ruled that spec/009's catalogue row OVERREACHED, because the row said 'publish a render phase' while the guard's docstring says 'reject a synchronous REGISTRY-flush' — different events. **The same discriminator has to be run again here and may come out the other way**, because spec/006's text is narrow and specific where the 009 row was general. The question is whether the substrate's public test flush IS the registry-flush the guard implements, or a third thing. I do not know, and four greps cannot tell me.

I ALSO COULD NOT FIND THE FLUSH BY NAME: git grep -nE 'defn (flush!|flush-registry!|drain!)' over implementation/core/src/ returns NOTHING. So either it is named something else, or it is defined elsewhere, or spec/006 describes a surface that does not exist under that contract. **Establishing which is the first job**, and it is a source question, not a taste one.

THREE OUTCOMES ARE ALL LIVE, and the evidence decides:
  (a) WIRE IT — the public test flush should call the guard and does not. Then this is a real defect on a shipping surface and the priority is wrong at P3.
  (b) SPEC/006 IS STALE — the throw it documents was never implemented, or was implemented and removed with the donor. Then the prose goes and the guard follows.
  (c) THE GUARD IS THE WRONG SHAPE for the flush that exists — a registry-flush rejection where a drain-state check is wanted. Then it is neither a wiring job nor a deletion.

DO NOT DELETE guard-open-drain! WITHOUT ESTABLISHING WHICH. Deleting also removes :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch, whose sole emitter it is, from the spec/009 catalogue — a public error surface — and rewrites spec/006's Render-batch finalization text. Three surfaces, two of them HOT ZONE.

NOTE THE ADJACENCY: rf2-c6ka9 covers present-tense 'ui.test/*' prose in four sibling spec files and two more rows of spec/009, and is FENCED behind rf2-h89ri. If the investigation reaches ui.test/* prose, that is c6ka9's, not this bead's — stop and report rather than adopting it.

title: hicasso: V2's R=20 rung certifies on 1 of its 4 arm families — reproduced in three sessions, so it is structural
description:

here rather than separately". rf2-0gjqi closes on its own audit obligation; this
item is unresolved and would otherwise be dropped with it.

THE OBSERVATION, now reproduced THREE times in three independent sessions.
V2's top rung produces certified windows under both writes on ONE of its four arm
families, and only that one:

  reagent-subs | hicasso R20   none
  reagent-subs | reagent R20   none
  uix-subs     | hicasso R20   none
  uix-subs     | uix     R20   certifies

  2026-08-13  (rf2-2rtt6.140's first window)
  2026-08-17  docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-certifies-and-the-control-does-not.md
  2026-08-18  docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-sign-follows-the-pass-not-the-write.md
              -- TWO paired runs, and in both, 0 of 6 rounds on each of the three
              refusing families under EACH write, against 6 of 6 under each write
              on uix-subs | uix.

Three sessions agreeing makes it STRUCTURAL rather than incidental, and V2's most
informative rung remains unassessed on three quarters of the arms.

WHAT THE REFUSALS LOOK LIKE, first-hand from the 2026-08-18 datasets
(implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/alloc-0gjqi/). They are
dominated by a SINGLE leg -- usually leg 5 or leg 6 of 6 -- reading approximately
-800,000 B against a cohort median near 170,000 B. That is a collection of about
800 KB landing inside the window, which the leg witness catches correctly: a leg
below its cohort is a leg something removed bytes from, and nothing in the work
unit removes bytes.

DO NOT WIDEN A GATE TO ADMIT IT. The refusal is correct. An R20 window at B = 4
allocates a rise large enough that a collection inside it is close to certain, and
a tolerance wide enough to admit a -800 KB leg would admit every masked window the
leg witness exists to refuse. rf2-2rtt6.140 retired the previous bound for exactly
that reason.

CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, none preferred and none authorised here: fewer measured
writes per window at the top rung so the window's cumulative rise stays under the
first collection; a rung ladder that stops below 20; or accepting that R = 20 is
not measurable on this instrument and saying so in the validity witness rather
than carrying an unassessed rung. Each is a rig change and belongs in its own
window.

WHY uix-subs | uix SURVIVES AND THE OTHER THREE DO NOT is not established. It is
the cheapest of the four per boundary, which is consistent with the
window-size account above and is not evidence for it.

So my 'no marker' was a property of where I looked, not of the bead. Re-closing past that is precisely the failure the method warns about: re-closing an audit reopen destroys a real finding while looking like tidiness.

THE AUDIT'S FINDING STANDS AND IS DISPATCHABLE. The valid census establishes that all 72 R20 refusals contain AT LEAST ONE negative leg; the landed page strengthens that into 'one collection of near-constant size', and the raw paired-run corpus disproves the singular claim in three windows — paired-run1 round 1 uix-subs|lad/hicasso@all with three negative legs and falls=3, round 4 reagent-subs|lad/hicasso@page with two and falls=2, round 5 reagent-subs|lad/hicasso@all with two and falls=3. WHAT REMAINS VALID and must not be re-litigated: the independently reproduced 528-window identities, the 884,280 B observed ceiling, 72/0 above it, 420/456 at-or-below it, and the 5-write arithmetic. NO NEW BENCHMARK WINDOW IS REQUIRED.

title: [ci] ratchet: no new workflow job may land without timeout-minutes
description:
PROPOSED BY rf2-km7iq (PR #8469), DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT THERE. That bead's brief fenced the work to cap additions and said that any mechanism preventing FUTURE uncapped jobs be filed as a bead with its reasoning rather than smuggled into the same PR.

THE REASONING, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH JUDGING. This would normally read as over-engineering — a linter guarding a one-line convention — and the project's stance rejects nag-diagnostics at triage. Two things argue the other way here:

1. THE DRIFT WAS NOT MARGINAL. rf2-km7iq's census found 89 of 117 jobs uncapped. Uncapped was the house MAJORITY (76%), which means the convention was not being followed by default and nothing noticed for a long time. The bead that surfaced it was filed off a single wedged run, by eye, not by any sweep. Without a ratchet the same 76% re-accretes, one new job at a time, and the next detection is again a 48-minute hang someone happens to be watching.

2. IT MATCHES HOUSE STYLE ALREADY. This repo runs exactly this class of ratchet: portability.yml carries 'No newly tracked files under ai/' and 'No retired view-lifetime vocabulary, repo-wide'; scripts/ carries check_gate_scheduling.py, check_jvm_lane_rosters.py, check_ci_reproduce_commands.py and check_workflow_yaml.py. A cap ratchet is not a new mechanism, it is one more member of an existing family.

WHAT IT WOULD DO. Parse .github/workflows/*.yml structurally and fail if any job lacks a job-level timeout-minutes. It MUST parse rather than grep: a timeout-minutes under a STEP is not a job cap and a grep cannot tell them apart — that distinction is the whole check. It must also exempt jobs that call a reusable workflow via a job-level 'uses:', where GitHub rejects the key outright. rf2-km7iq built and controlled exactly such a census (positive control, negative control, and a sabotage fixture that planted both a stripped cap and a step-only cap and went red on both); that script is the natural starting point but was scratch, not committed.

WHERE IT WOULD LIVE. scripts/check_workflow_yaml.py already validates workflow YAML well-formedness and is already wired into CI — folding the cap assertion into it is probably cheaper than a new script and a new job, and avoids adding a gate.

REJECT IF. If the judgement is that 89-at-once was a one-off now permanently fixed and the convention will hold by review alone, close this — the fix has landed either way and this is only insurance.
close_reason:
BUILT, not refused. PR #8477 (worker/citimeout2-xenc6), commit eb08bbc04d. New scripts/check_workflow_job_timeouts.py, wired into test.yml's 'Repo invariant checks' job as a self-test step plus a live step.

JUDGEMENT. The bead's own REJECT-IF clause ('close this if the convention will hold by review alone') is refuted by the census that prompted the bead: 89 of 117 jobs uncapped means the convention held for 24% of instances, accreted one job at a time, and surfaced only via a 49-minute hang somebody happened to watch. Second, the failure mode is a liveness defect rather than a style complaint — an uncapped job inherits GitHub's 360-minute default, so a wedge yields a check that NEVER TERMINATES, and this project merges by reading CI verdicts. Not the nag-diagnostic class the stance rejects. Cost is proportionate: one script among 38 siblings, two steps in an existing job, no new gate, no new job, presence-only (one bit per job, nothing to tune).

DIVERGED FROM THE BEAD ON WHERE IT LIVES. The bead proposed folding into scripts/check_workflow_yaml.py and asserted that script is 'already wired into CI'. IT IS NOT — it appears only in scripts/test-fast-pr.sh, the local pre-checkin spine, and in no workflow job. A ratchet folded there would never run in CI: the 'gate that runs nowhere' shape check_gate_scheduling.py exists to catch. (Secondary reason: that script declares a single-question 'is the file YAML?' charter and disclaims Actions-grammar validation.) Hence a sibling script wired into CI, which still delivers the bead's intent of no new gate/job.

JOB-VS-STEP DISCRIMINATION, the whole check. Structural parse: a job cap is a key on the job mapping, a step cap a key on an element of its steps sequence. The confusion is LIVE here — the tree carries 4 real step-level timeout-minutes across 3 jobs (2 Playwright installs, 2 in mcp-conformance-re-frame2-pair). Reusable-workflow jobs (job-level uses:) exempted since GitHub rejects the key; none exist in-tree today, so that arm is covered by self-test, stated honestly rather than claimed as swept.

CONTROLS, both captured. Self-test exit 0: 4 accept (plain capped; job cap AND step cap; reusable-workflow call; two-job all-capped) + 5 reject (no cap; STEP-ONLY cap; uncapped job sitting SECOND behind a capped one; two uncapped where both must be named; present-but-empty key). Sabotage against REAL content exit 1: stripping the job-level cap from the real cljs-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation job (which retains a step-level cap) in an isolated --repo-root copy makes it red, naming the job and the step-only reason — a grep would have passed that file. Plant anchored to a single line behind an anchor assertion so it could not silently no-op; working test.yml verified byte-identical to its committed blob by git hash-object afterwards.

Live sweep: 117 jobs across 11 files, all capped, exit 0. check_ci_reproduce_commands.py went 43 -> 45 steps and stayed in sync; --emit resolves both new ids.

title: [dead-code] theme/tokens/panel-icon + panel-icon-style have ZERO src readers; spec/021 §14.1 already says the glyphs were removed
description:
Found while executing rf2-9g1ea (PR #8467), reported rather than widened,
because the disposition is a design call and rf2-9g1ea's fence was the
sibling map.

theme/tokens/panel-icon is a 7-key map from L4 tab keyword to a Unicode
glyph. It has ZERO readers in src. Verified repo-wide with `git grep -nF
panel-icon` over tracked files (positive control: the same pattern finds
the def itself and 12 test hits): the only src occurrences are the `def`
at tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc:822 and its own
docstring. `panel-icon-style`, the helper that would render it, likewise
has ZERO src call sites — it reads `panel-accent`, not `panel-icon`, and
nothing calls it.

That matches what the spec already records. spec/021 §14.1 (rf2-6xezz,
Mike-direction 2026-05-21) says every L4 Dynamic and Static panel
scrubbed its top-of-panel heading, and in terms: "Per-panel header icons
(§17.1.5) lived inside the deleted <h1> elements and are also removed."
Three panel tests assert exactly that at the DOM level — the
machine-inspector, reactive and routing suites each assert their
panel-icon testid is nil, one of them commenting "panel-icon span is
gone (lived in the deleted h1)".

SO THE MAP AND ITS HELPER ARE DEAD CODE that five tests keep alive, and
the roster inside it has drifted the same way rf2-9g1ea's did: it names
TWO retired ids (`:event`, superseded by `:epoch` per rf2-5gl5r, and
`:reactive`) and omits FIVE of the ten shipped Dynamic tabs (`:epoch`,
`:resources`, `:derivation-graph`, `:module-view`, `:hicasso`) per
focus/valid-panels.

PR #8467 took the truth repair only, because its docstring
cross-referenced the map that PR deletes and therefore had to be edited
anyway: the deftest `panel-icon-map-covers-every-l4-tab` — a name
claiming completeness while asserting set equality against a copy of the
map, so it could not fail on the drift it appeared to guard — was renamed
`panel-icon-map-keys-are-pinned` and its docstring corrected to state the
seven-against-ten position. The MAP, the glyph assertions and the helper
were left untouched.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD CARRIES. Either:

  (a) DELETE `panel-icon`, `panel-icon-style` and their five tests, and
      scrub spec/021 §17.1.5 plus the §17.1.3/§17.1.5 cross-references
      that survive it. §14.1 already says the icons are removed, so this
      makes the code agree with the spec. spec/021 is not currently
      contested.

  (b) KEEP them as a design asset for a future header treatment, in
      which case the glyph table is spec/021 §17.1.5's to own and the
      map should be justified there rather than surviving by inertia —
      and the roster question (does a future header want a glyph for
      Epoch, Resources, Graph, Frames, Hicasso?) is a real design call
      nobody has made.

RECOMMENDATION: (a). It is the same reasoning rf2-9g1ea settled — an
unread structure kept for a speculative future is a drift attractor, not
an asset — and here the spec has ALREADY ruled the surface removed, so
keeping the code is the position that disagrees with the tree. If a
header treatment returns, a glyph table is cheap to reintroduce and would
want its roster derived from `panel-registry/tab-ids-for-mode` rather
than hand-listed, exactly as rf2-9g1ea concluded for the accent seam.

FENCE IF DISPATCHED: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc,
tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens_cljs_test.cljc,
tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/var_resolution_cljs_test.cljs
(two of its walks read `(keys tokens/panel-icon)`), and — for option (a)
only — tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md. SEQUENCE AFTER
PR #8467 MERGES: it edits three of those four files.

COVERING GATE: `cd tools/xray && clojure -M:test` reaches
tokens_cljs_test.cljc (rf2-9g1ea re-established this with a planted
fault: red, exit 1). var_resolution_cljs_test.cljs is `.cljs` and only
the `cljs_node_test` lane covers it.
close_reason:
RESOLVED BY PR #8479 (worker/panelicon-qm2rt). Option (a) taken — panel-icon,
panel-icon-style, and the tests whose only subject they were are DELETED, and
the spec now says what the tree does.

MEASUREMENT, re-derived at merge base 1c4ef39778 before any edit. Every claim in
this bead held: ZERO src readers for panel-icon and ZERO src call sites for
panel-icon-style (positive control on the same search shape — panel-accent
returns 6 hits including a reader in panels/routing.cljs); focus/valid-panels at
ten; the map at seven keys naming the retired :event and :reactive and omitting
:epoch, :resources, :derivation-graph, :module-view, :hicasso; and spec/021
§14.1 already recording the glyphs as removed with the deleted <h1> elements.

THE ONE DELTA, AND IT DECIDED THREE OF THE FIVE FILES. This bead says the map is
"dead code that five tests keep alive". Only TWO files actually read the var.
The other three — machine_inspector_view, reactive_panel_view, routing — match
`panel-icon` as a data-testid STRING LITERAL and never touch tokens/panel-icon;
each asserts its `…-panel-icon` testid renders NIL. They are absence assertions
pinning §14.1 at the DOM level, and they are the reason the deletion is safe:
they are the only thing still enforcing that the header-icon surface does not
come back. KEPT UNTOUCHED. Deleting them as "panel-icon references" would have
removed the live guard while leaving the dead map — the exact inversion. This
bead's own FENCE was right (it lists only the two theme test files); the "five
tests" phrasing in its prose was loose, and the dispatch brief inherited it.

THE PINNING CONTROL WAS HOLLOW, AND NO EXPERIMENT WAS NEEDED BECAUSE THE FAULT
WAS ALREADY LIVE. panel-icon-map-keys-are-pinned asserted a set literal against a
copy of the map's own keys and read focus/valid-panels nowhere, so it could not
fail when map and shipped roster disagreed. They disagreed by five absent ids and
two retired ones, and the covering gate at the unmodified base ran GREEN, exit 0,
1319 tests / 6245 assertions. Fault present, control green — same result #8467
established next door. Nuance recorded for the record: after #8467's rename the
name no longer overclaims ("keys are pinned" honestly describes a change-detector
over a literal); it is hollow AS A ROSTER CONTROL, which is what it was
originally sold as. Either way it has no subject once the map goes, so it was
removed WITH the map rather than left behind as coverage guarding nothing.

NO COVERAGE LOST. The two var_resolution walks only re-derived a property of
panel-accent, which keeps its own control walking the registry-derived
focus/valid-panels roster.

SPEC CHANGED, NOT "unchanged because X" — three places in 021 plus one in 007,
because leaving them would strand cross-references at a table this PR deletes.
§17.1.5's per-panel glyph table is replaced by a RETIRED note recording both
reasons it died (the §14.1 removal AND the independent single-accent
supersession of its per-panel colour tokens, rf2-ad7zx.13 / §17.1.3 — it encoded
two dead contracts at once), and pointing any future header treatment at
panel-registry/tab-ids-for-mode rather than a hand-listed roster, exactly as
rf2-9g1ea concluded for the accent seam. §14.1 gains the fact that the CODE went
too and names the three suites now holding the line. The §17.5 follow-on
candidate — which proposed adding the very map this PR deletes — is converted to
the file's own established "DONE (retired · …)" form. 007's L4-panel-accent-
stripe section cited the header icons as an example of domain colour doing
load-bearing work inside a panel: wrong twice over, since the icons are gone and
panel-icon-style read panel-accent (the single accent), never a domain colour.
No heading added or removed, so no anchor changed; the only table touched was
removed whole, so no column count drifted.

GATES, every exit code captured by the invoking shell on the same command line as
its redirect. cd tools/xray && clojure -M:test: exit 0 control (1319/6245),
exit 1 planted (1 failure naming the planted value, counts UNCHANGED at
1319/6245 so no namespace aborted), exit 0 final (1314/6201). The delta accounts
exactly — minus 5 tests is the five deleted deftests, and minus 44 assertions is
their exact sum (1 + 7x2 + 7 + 7x3 + 1) — which is the check that no collateral
test was lost. clj-kondo --parallel --fail-level error --lint tools/xray, the
tools/xray arm of required lint.yml: exit 0, errors 0. check_doc_slugs.py (which
covers tools/*/spec/**/*.md): exit 0, and since an empty pass is not evidence, a
planted broken link turned it red at exit 1 naming the file. Both plants restored
and verified by git hash-object against the committed object.

NOT RUN, DELIBERATELY: the fast-PR spine (not run at all) and every browser /
full-example-compile lane, left to CI; per check_fast_pr_gap.py --list, 94
required checks sit outside the spine anyway. var_resolution_cljs_test.cljs is
.cljs and only the cljs_node_test lane compiles it — confirmed by the exact
-5/-44 accounting, since only the .cljc deletions appear in the JVM counts.
clj-kondo stands in statically and was verified able to see the problem rather
than assumed: planting tokens/panel-icon back into that file produced
"Unresolved var: tokens/panel-icon". Stated precisely, that is a WARNING, and
CI's clj-kondo job runs --fail-level error, so it surfaces a dangling reference
without blocking on it; the blocking coverage is the cljs_node_test lane.

PR #8467 PRESERVED INTACT — checked with a three-dot diff read for reverts rather
than conflicts, since that file was rewritten hours earlier. panel-domain->token
stays deleted (surviving only as historical prose in three docstrings #8467
itself wrote), panel-accent-is-tab-independent stays in place, and panel-accent
plus the tab-domain machinery were not revisited.

comments.text:
MAYOR 2026-08-18, BACKLOG REREAD — FENCED, NOT DISPATCHABLE. WHAT CLEARS IT: PR #8467 (worker/theme-9g1ea) merging.

This bead's surface is tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc, and #8467 is an open PR that rewrites that exact file — it deletes panel-domain->token, replaces a hollow pinning test, and renames panel-icon-map-covers-every-l4-tab to panel-icon-map-keys-are-pinned. The worker that filed this bead was working in that file and explicitly said to sequence this after #8467; two editors on one file conflict and can silently revert each other.

WHY IT IS WORTH KEEPING RATHER THAN CLOSING AS MINUTIAE, since it is dead-code removal with no user-visible effect: the case is already made at source and does not need re-deriving. panel-icon and panel-icon-style have ZERO src readers, and spec/021 §14.1 already records that the glyphs were removed with the deleted <h1>s. So the spec and the code already agree that the feature is gone; what remains is a map nobody reads. That is a smaller and cleaner question than the one #8467 settled, and it should be decided the same way — by measuring readers, not by taste.

ONE THING TO CHECK AT SOURCE WHEN IT DISPATCHES, because it is exactly the trap #8467 found next door: whether the test pinning panel-icon can FAIL when the map and the shipped roster disagree, or whether it only asserts the map equals itself. #8467's worker found the neighbouring control hollow and REPLACED rather than patched it. If this one is hollow too, deleting the map removes the map and leaves the hollow control behind unless it goes in the same change.

title: hicasso topo clock driver: correct the :noop docstring premise the window falsified
description:
The 2026-08-18 clock window (rf2-w01c) falsified a premise stated in
implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/topo/clock_app.cljs's own
namespace docstring, and the docstring still asserts it.

THE CLAIM IN THE CODE: '[:topo/noop-write] moves a key no arm reads, so its
window holds exactly the cost that does NOT move with the arm — dispatch, the
flushSync boundary, the commit React schedules regardless.'

WHAT THE WINDOW MEASURED: at B=1000 the :noop row reads 31.75 / 31.60 / 31.85 ms
on fine against 8.00 / 8.20 / 8.40 on coarse — factors of 3.97, 3.85 and 3.79
across the three runs. The floor MOVES WITH THE ARM, by about 4x. Recorded with
the full table in docs/design/hicasso/product/topology-tournament.md 2.9.7.

WHAT NEEDS CHANGING is prose, not behaviour. The row is still worth measuring
and is still placed beside the cells rather than subtracted from them; what is
wrong is the sentence describing what it holds. Two knock-ons in the same file
and its neighbours:

  * the docstring's later sentence, that a reader handed an arm-to-arm ratio
    without the floor 'cannot tell a topology result from a floor', still holds
    and gets STRONGER, not weaker;
  * floor-shares' own docstring repeats the received rule that a mostly-floor
    cell has its ratio 'compressed toward 1'. That rule assumes a SHARED floor
    and this table's is arm-specific, so it is wrong here too. 2.9.7 of the
    tournament page states the corrected reading.

DO NOT change the instrument's behaviour, the sampling, batch-k, the band or
the arms — the published table was taken on this instrument and a behavioural
change makes the next run a different one. This is a docstring correction.

DO NOT re-run the window to 'confirm' it. The three runs are published and
rf2-w01c's pre-registration fixed the count at three.
close_reason: PR #8471 (worker/topodoc-yorfi). The falsified premise is corrected in prose in three places rather than the two the bead named: the namespace docstring's floor-row section, floor-op, and floor-shares. Each now states the measured arm-specific floor (B=1000: fine 31.75/31.60/31.85 ms vs coarse 8.00/8.20/8.40 vs chunked 9.40/9.40/9.55; fine/coarse 3.97, 3.85, 3.79 across the three runs) and links topology-tournament.md 2.9.7. The 'cannot tell a topology result from a floor' sentence is kept and marked STRENGTHENED, per the bead. floor-shares' 'compressed toward 1' rule is replaced by 2.9.7's corrected reading (the limit is the table's own floor ratio, coarse/fine 0.254-0.268 at B=1000, not 1.00) with NO corrected ratio published, since that needs the additive model rf2-4t36 refused. No behavioural change: sampling, batch-k, band, arms and probe pairs untouched; window not re-run. Searched and left alone with reasons in the PR body: clock_witness_dom_cljs_test.cljs:129 (a markup claim, accurate), the walk-vs-Reagent clock_app.cljs:710 (a genuinely shared floor, different instrument, outside fence), tournament :394 (within-arm doubling control) and :872/:912 (quoting the premise in order to falsify it).

title: [method] the merge rules cover a check that FAILS and a check that fails before repo code ran, but not one that never terminates
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-18 12:10 AUSEST. Verified at source with a positive control on the same search shape: a word-bounded search for hung, hangs, stuck or wedge in .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md returns ZERO, while flake or flaky returns 1, so the pattern works and the zero is a genuine absence. (An unbounded first attempt returned 4 and 83 hits because hang matches inside change - the substring failure this corpus keeps meeting, met here by the mayor.)

THE GAP. mayor-merge.md names exactly two failure cases and a remedy for each:

  A real, repeated touched-surface failure is NOT a flake - dispatch a fix-worker to the same branch, never --admin past it.
  A failure BEFORE any repository code ran is the other case, and the failing step names itself - re-run with gh run rerun, hold the re-run to the same five clauses, never merge past it.

A CHECK THAT NEVER TERMINATES IS NEITHER. It has not failed, so neither remedy is triggered; it stays IN_PROGRESS, so clause 3 rejects the PR indefinitely. The rules as written give a mayor no move at all, and the honest reading of them is to wait forever.

MEASURED INSTANCE, today. PR #8458's MkDocs build ran IN_PROGRESS for over 25 minutes, still running, on a diff of two markdown files under docs/design/hicasso - a tree mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs keeps OUT of the site, so that job had none of the PR's content to build. Every other check on the PR had settled at 86 of the 88 band. The machine was also carrying a live worker compiling, which is a plausible cause and not an established one.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The mayor's discipline is that a pending check rejects, full stop - and that discipline is correct and has caught real problems today. But it is only safe if EVERY pending check eventually terminates. A hang converts a sound rule into a deadlock, and the pressure at that moment is to reach for --admin, which the file rightly forbids and which would be exactly the wrong response.

PROPOSED FIX, one short paragraph beside the two existing cases: name the third case and its remedy. Something in the shape of - a check that has not terminated is neither of the above; it has produced no verdict rather than a bad one. Establish it is genuinely running rather than queued, and read the clock rather than inferring elapsed time. Past a threshold well beyond that job's normal duration, re-run the job and hold the re-run to the same five clauses. Never --admin past it, and never merge on the other checks.

DELIBERATELY NOT SPECIFYING A THRESHOLD IN MINUTES. Job durations here vary by more than an order of magnitude - a standalone-example compile gate legitimately ran 17 minutes today - so a fixed number would be wrong for most jobs. Prefer a rule anchored to the job's own normal duration, or say plainly that the mayor judges it and reports the number it used.

WORKER-TRACKED SURFACE, so FILED rather than committed.

SCOPE: one paragraph. Do not restructure the merge criterion, do not touch the five clauses, and do not weaken the pending-check rule - the third case is an addition to it, not an exception to it.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8465 (branch worker/mergerule-krdb7, commit eac30af14b). The third merge-failure case — a check that NEVER TERMINATES — now exists in both files, split by the ownership rule loops.md states about itself ('this page is the generic body; your copy pins the concrete values'). docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md gains 35 lines under '### When a change is not green' carrying the generic reasoning: recognition on the clock against the job's OWN measured normal cost (never a remembered constant); the cancelled-at-the-declared-cap tell, with the corollary that downstream rollup FAILUREs are consequences of the cancellation and not findings; the discriminator between a runner-level wedge and a change-introduced hang; the two opposite remedies; and the uncapped-job trap. .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md gains one paragraph pinning the same case to gh commands and the measured instance. SCOPE HELD as the bead directed: no restructuring, the five clauses untouched, the pending-check rule not weakened — both files say EXPLICITLY that this is not a sixth clause, because clause 3 already blocks correctly and what was missing is only what the mayor should DO. ONE DEPARTURE FROM THE BEAD, reported: the bead scoped only mayor-merge.md, because that is where the search was run; re-running the same word-bounded search against loops.md found the same absence, and since loops.md is the generic body the reasoning belongs there with only the commands in the command file. POSITIVE CONTROL RE-RUN rather than trusted, and it holds: word-bounded hung|hangs|stuck|wedge = 0, flake|flaky = 1 (line 30), unbounded hang = 18 = change = 18. EVERY MEASURED NUMBER RE-VERIFIED at source on run 32094188039 attempt 1 (gh run view shows the LATEST attempt — attempt 1 needs the attempts API): jvm-tools-template 03:09:37Z-03:44:51Z = 35.2 min against its declared timeout-minutes: 35, conclusion 'cancelled' not 'failure'; tools-playground 03:09:36Z-03:58:47Z = 49.2 min uncapped; 'All required checks passed' 03:58:50Z-03:58:54Z = 4 s, FAILURE, a needs: rollup. Normal costs 10.52/10.60/8.10 and 1.45/1.67 min from 32092675548/32082472715/32080996828. COMPLEMENTARY TO rf2-km7iq, cross-referenced in both files and noted on that bead: km7iq adds the cap, krdb7 says what to do when a check hangs anyway; neither is a duplicate of the other. Gates: check_readme_links.py --ci and --self-test, check_doc_slugs.py and --self-test, all exit 0, re-run after rebasing onto the final base, and BOTH proven to read the worker tree by planted faults that red naming the exact plant, restored and hash-verified byte-identical to the committed object.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RESOLUTION OF THE MEASURED INSTANCE, mayor 2026-08-18 12:20 AUSEST. The hang resolved and the shape is now clear, which sharpens what the missing paragraph should say.

WHAT HAPPENED. Both PR #8458 and PR #8460 had their MkDocs build CANCELLED at 02:12:08Z and 02:12:39Z - the same wall-clock minute, after about thirty minutes each. A THIRTY-MINUTE JOB TIMEOUT, not a failure. The Docs required and All required checks passed entries that then read FAILURE are four-second rollup jobs failing BECAUSE of the cancellation, not findings of their own. PR #8460's browser gate was cancelled in the same minute.

NORMAL DURATION, measured rather than assumed: recent successful docs workflow runs take 4 to 9 minutes (02:13:51 to 02:18:09 is 4 minutes; 01:24:33 to 01:32:55 is 8). The two that timed out ran 40+ minutes, and a third in the same window ran 33. So roughly 5x normal.

TRANSIENT, NOT A REGRESSION. A 4-minute success ran at 02:13:51, AFTER the bad window. Three long runs clustered between 01:34 and 01:38 and nothing since. No bead filed for a permanent slowdown; if it recurs outside that window, that IS a separate bead.

A MAYOR ERROR WORTH RECORDING HERE because it bears on the diagnosis this paragraph will guide. I first attributed the slowness to load on the local machine from a live worker compiling. That is WRONG: these jobs run on hosted runners, where the local box's load is irrelevant. The plausible-sounding local explanation was reached for before checking where the job actually runs.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO THE PROPOSED FIX. The third case should say that a non-terminating check often resolves into a CANCELLATION plus downstream rollup FAILURES, and that the rollups are consequences rather than findings - reading them as two independent failures overstates the problem and points at the wrong remedy. And the discriminator that settled it here was cheap and general: TWO UNRELATED DIFFS, THE SAME JOB, THE SAME MINUTE. A diff cannot cause that. One command against the workflow's recent run durations established normal versus anomalous.

ACTION TAKEN: re-ran the failed jobs on both PRs, held to the same five clauses. Not merged past.

title: [spec-drift] 000-Vision.md carries TWO more stale rosters the 154-155 repair did not reach: a six-row tab table naming the RETIRED Event tab, and a popover Key column pointing at a Reserved section
description:
Found by re-derivation while working rf2-yecyc (PR #8460), which was fenced to the 000-Vision.md:154-155 sentence and stopped there. Both sites are in the SAME FILE and are the same roster-tail class rf2-gui26 catalogued; neither was named by any bead, and neither would have been caught by the censuses that found the sentence.

SITE 1 -- tools/xray/spec/000-Vision.md:43-50, under '### One event at a time'.

A six-row table headed 'Tab | What it shows for the focused event' whose FIRST ROW is:

  | **Event** (e) | The event vector + the six dominoes of its cascade. |

The Event/Handler tab was RETIRED per rf2-5gl5r in favour of the Epoch panel -- the same retirement the repaired 154-155 paragraph names two hundred lines further down. So the table teaches a tab that does not ship, under a mnemonic (e) that today belongs to Epoch. The remaining five rows are App-db/Views/Trace/Machines/Routing: five of the ten shipped Dynamic tabs, missing Resources (s), Graph (g), Frames (u), Hicasso (h).

WHY EVERY CENSUS MISSED IT. It is a TABLE, not a parenthetical roster, so the roster-tail census pattern did not reach it; and its mnemonics sit in a Tab column with no keystroke verb near them, so the mnemonic-as-key sweeps (rf2-91dfb, rf2-14axc) did not either. It is a third shape.

NOTE the same file at 294-305 already carries a CORRECT and COMPLETE ten-row inventory table with a Mnem column. So the file holds two tab tables that disagree, one of them 200 lines above the other. That is the design question this bead carries: whether 43-50 should be completed to ten, cut to a pointer at the ten-row table, or trimmed to a non-roster illustration. It reads as illustrative prose rather than an inventory, so completing it may be the wrong answer.

SITE 2 -- tools/xray/spec/000-Vision.md:316-324, the Popovers table.

Headed 'Popover | Key | Content' with two rows: Nav-token timeline (r) and Wire-trace (f). A KEY column, stated as keys. Neither is wired: the bare-key dispatcher spine-key-id in keybinding.cljs binds Space, l, Shift+G, j, k, comma and s and nothing else -- the same evidence rf2-91dfb closed on. 018-Event-Spine.md:1729 records the neighbouring Causality popover as dropped with 'The c key is unbound', so this is the surviving half of a set already half-retired.

Its cross-reference is also hollow: line 323 says 'See 018-Event-Spine.md section 10 for the popover invocation contract', and 018 section 10 is titled 'Reserved'.

Same claim appears at 007-UX-IA.md:28 ('Plus popovers (r nav-token timeline, f wire-trace') and 019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md:742 and :737. So a repair here is a four-site sweep, not one edit, and it needs the same adjudication rf2-91dfb gave the tab mnemonics: are these labels, a palette verb, or a genuinely unbuilt feature? 019:742 calls the nav-token timeline a 'NEW popover', which suggests unbuilt rather than merely unwired -- verify before wording anything.

MEASURED 2026-08-18 11:30 AUSEST on worker/rostertail-cluster at origin/main c8e237f6aa. Line numbers are pre-PR-8460 for site 2 and unaffected by it; site 1 is unaffected entirely.

FENCE: tools/xray/spec/**. Does NOT touch keybinding.cljs -- Mike's Option B stands, no shortcut is to be added.
close_reason:
Both sites repaired and landed on PR #8462 (branch worker/vision-9foby), which is out of draft.

SITE 1 (000-Vision.md 'One event at a time') — resolved as a POINTER, not completed to ten rows. Completing it would have left two hand-maintained inventories 200 lines apart in one file, free to drift again, which is the trap this bead was filed to disarm; the same call rf2-yecyc (PR #8460) and rf2-ilwcf made. title: [method] two cleanup obligations the mayor enforces in every brief are missing from the template: the guard-root rule stops at 'committed file', and nothing says to kill poll loops
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-18 11:20 AUSEST, comparing rules the mayor ENFORCES against what docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md says. Both verified absent at source with a positive control on the same file and search shape (a search for the neighbouring 'remove the LINK' rule returns 1, so the pattern works and the zeros are genuine absences).

DEFECT 1 - THE GUARD-ROOT RULE IS NARROWER IN THE FILE THAN IN PRACTICE.

Landed at :487 by PR #8456 (rf2-f5cma):
  Report that root to the mayor in your completion message, and never write it, or any absolute home path, into a committed file ...

Searches for PR body and tracker text on that file return ZERO.

WHY THE GAP MATTERS, and this is the fixing worker's own finding rather than the mayor's: a PR BODY and a BEAD CLOSE REASON are both durable and public, and neither is a committed file. The CI gate No hardcoded personal/home paths does not see either. So a worker that obeys the rule exactly as written can still publish an absolute home path where it persists. That worker kept paths out of both only by extending the rule on its own initiative, and said so in its report.

The mayor adopted the broader wording into every brief the same hour. So the enforced rule and the written rule have differed ever since, with the written one weaker.

PROPOSED FIX, in place: change committed file to any committed file, PR body or tracker text. That is a three-word edit to a sentence that already exists and already carries the positive form. Nothing else in the paragraph changes.

DEFECT 2 - NOTHING TELLS A WORKER TO KILL THE POLL LOOPS IT ARMED.

The template sanctions detaching a long gate and polling its log and .exit file in a bounded loop - correct, and workers use it. It does NOT say to reap those loops before reporting done. Searches for poll loop, waiter and kill loop all return ZERO.

MEASURED COST, 2026-08-18: the rf2-9jrhi worker armed several until [ -f <exit-file> ] waiters while a detached spine ran, used the pattern correctly, and reported done without reaping them. Each surviving loop then satisfied its condition independently and fired its own task-notification. About a dozen arrived AFTER the work was merged, all repeating the same result. Each one costs the mayor a turn - the same currency as a dispatch, spent on nothing. The worker diagnosed them accurately and said it would stop responding; the loops did not care. The mayor ended it with TaskStop on the finished agent.

PROPOSED FIX: one clause on the EXISTING cleanup sentence, the one that already says to remove the link into shared dependencies and never its target. Same class of obligation - a worker cleans up what it created - and it belongs in the same breath rather than as a new paragraph.

WORKER-TRACKED SURFACE, so FILED rather than committed: the mayor checkout must not commit under docs/the-mayor-method/.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE, and it is the main risk on this bead: this is three words plus one clause. The file is long and every rule in it was paid for by a real failure. Do not restructure, do not restate rules that exist elsewhere, do not add justification paragraphs. A smaller diff is the better diff. rf2-f5cma landed +7/-2 on this same file and that was the right size.

title: [method] WORKTREE_ROOT means two different directories, and the report-it-to-the-mayor-not-into-a-file rule exists only in briefs
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-18 10:20 AUSEST, checking rules the mayor ENFORCES against what the files actually say. Two defects in the same region of docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md. Both verified at source.

DEFECT 1 - A NAME COLLISION, OFF BY ONE DIRECTORY LEVEL.

  dispatch-prompt-template.md:7-9   <WORKTREE_ROOT> - the directory holding worker worktrees ... <ASSIGNED_WORKTREE> - this worker's worktree, A SUBDIRECTORY OF <WORKTREE_ROOT>
  scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh:166   printf WORKTREE_ROOT=%s with GIT_ROOT, i.e. THE WORKER'S OWN WORKTREE

Same token, two referents, one a parent of the other. The script's own header comment at :9 says WORKTREE_ROOT=<absolute git toplevel> and at :21 tells the worker to report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every dispatch this mayor writes says report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT. A worker that resolves that token against the template's glossary rather than against the script's output would believe the guard confirms it is in the PARENT directory. Worse, a brief that says your worktree is a subdirectory of WORKTREE_ROOT while the guard prints WORKTREE_ROOT= its own tree is flatly contradictory, and the worktree boundary is the one rule where a directory-level error is expensive.

IN PRACTICE NO WORKER HAS GOT THIS WRONG - every completion report this session quoted its own worktree path correctly, resolving from context. So this is latent rather than biting, and the fix should be a RENAME not a redesign.

FIX PROPOSED, small: rename the template's placeholder to <WORKTREE_PARENT> and update the three lines that use it, leaving the script alone - the script's name matches what it prints and is referenced by every brief. Do NOT rename the script's output; that would break the reporting convention across every dispatch in flight.

DEFECT 2 - A RULE THE MAYOR ENFORCES THAT EXISTS NOWHERE DURABLE.

Every dispatch now carries: report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT TO THE MAYOR IN YOUR COMPLETION MESSAGE, never write it, or any absolute home path, into a committed file. A fixed-string search for that rule, and for the CI gate it protects, returns NOTHING across docs/the-mayor-method/ and .claude/commands/.

WHY IT EXISTS. On 2026-08-18 the worker on rf2-hic-090 reddened the CI gate No hardcoded personal/home paths by committing a table row containing an absolute worktree path into its results record. The brief had said REPORT the printed WORKTREE_ROOT; for every other bead that resolves to a message back to the mayor and never touches a file, but that bead's whole deliverable WAS a written record, so report reasonably read as record it. The instruction was safe only because of where its output usually lands.

FIX PROPOSED, one sentence beside the boundary block: say where it goes, not just that it goes - to the mayor in the completion message, never into a committed file - and for record-writing beads add the positive form: what makes the guard evidence is that it RAN and exited 0, not the machine-specific string it printed.

WORKER-TRACKED SURFACE, so FILED rather than committed: the mayor checkout must not commit under docs/the-mayor-method/.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this is a rename plus one sentence. The file is long and every rule in it was paid for by a real failure; do not restructure, do not restate rules that exist elsewhere, and do not add justification paragraphs. A smaller diff is the better diff.

title: [spec-drift] theme/panel-domain->token is a stale 6-entry L4 inventory pinned by a test whose name claims completeness
description:
Found by the roster-tail census on rf2-gui26 (PR #8440), REFUSED there as a design call rather than doc drift, and reported rather than widened.

tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc:726 panel-domain->token is:

  {:event :accent :app-db :accent :views :accent
   :trace :accent :machines :accent :routing :accent}

Six entries. It carries the RETIRED :event tab (removed per rf2-5gl5r in favour of Epoch), OMITS :epoch entirely, and omits the four newest Dynamic tabs (:resources :derivation-graph :module-view :hicasso). The shipped inventory is ten (focus.cljc valid-panels).

NO BEHAVIOUR DEPENDS ON IT TODAY. Every value is :accent, and panel-accent falls back to :accent for unknown tab keywords, so every tab resolves identically whether or not it is in the map. That is why nothing caught the drift.

WHY IT IS STILL A DEFECT. The docstring states the map is deliberately "retained (rather than collapsed to a constant) so the per-tab inventory stays explicit and a future per-panel signal can re-diverge a single entry without restructuring call sites". That stated purpose is exactly what has failed: the inventory is neither complete nor current, so the map can no longer serve as the explicit per-tab roster it claims to be, and a future re-diverge would start from a wrong list.

PINNED BY A TEST THAT ASSERTS THE STALENESS. tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens_cljs_test.cljc:195 deftest panel-domain-map-covers-every-l4-tab asserts set equality against that same six-set, and its testing docstring opens "the 6 L4 tabs each get a domain colour". The NAME claims it covers every L4 tab; it covers six of ten and pins the retired :event.

WHY REFUSED ON rf2-gui26 RATHER THAN FIXED. The fix is a genuine decision, not a transcription: either (a) complete the map to the ten shipped ids, keeping the explicit-roster intent, or (b) collapse it to a constant and delete the map plus its test, accepting that the single-accent ruling (rf2-ad7zx.13 / spec/022) has made the per-panel structure vestigial. Option (b) is the smaller surface and arguably the honest one post-single-accent; option (a) preserves the re-diverge seam the docstring asks for. That is Mike-shaped, and a doc-drift PR is the wrong place to pick.

SUGGESTED: (b) unless the re-diverge seam is still wanted, in which case (a) with the roster derived from panel-registry rather than hand-listed. Either way the test name and docstring go with it.
close_reason:
RESOLVED BY PR #8467 (worker/theme-9g1ea) — the map is DELETED, and the
seam it was justified by is now the FUNCTION.

comments.text:
SEQUENCED AND RECOMMENDED - mayor, 2026-08-18 09:50 AUSEST.

SEQUENCING: hold until rf2-14axc's PR merges. That bead is live on tools/xray and is editing tokens_cljs_test.cljc - the very test that pins this map - to correct its docstring and its deftest name. It was explicitly told NOT to touch the map, because the map is yours. Two workers on a src/test pair that pin each other is a conflict waiting to happen, and the wait is one tick.

RECOMMENDATION, from reading the map rather than the bead's framing. Every one of the six values is :accent. So the map is ALREADY collapsed in its values; what is stale is only its KEYS. That reframes the two options the bead offers:

  (a) COMPLETE IT TO TEN - adds four keys and removes one, and every added key maps to the same :accent the others do. It buys nothing behaviourally and re-arms the same drift the next time a tab ships. This is the more-machinery answer.
  (b) DELETE IT and read :accent directly at the call sites.

THE MAYOR RECOMMENDS (b). A six-key map whose every value is identical is an indirection that encodes no information, and the only thing keeping it alive is a test whose NAME claims it covers every L4 tab. Under the project stance - trust the programmer, minimal API, reject over-engineering - the honest reading is that rf2-ad7zx.13 already made this map redundant when it superseded per-panel domain colours with a single :accent, and nobody removed the vestige.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THAT: if any consumer branches on the KEY rather than the value, or if a future design intends per-domain colours to return, then (a) is right and the map is a placeholder rather than a vestige. title: [design, needs Mike] the retired :rf.ssr/phase-flip has a live successor with no observability: hicasso's client-only adoption gate
description:
RAISED BY rf2-8vpzy (PR #8449), which struck the :rf.ssr/phase-flip catalogue row and retired spec/011's Phase flip section in place. The strike is correct and is not this bead. What the strike SURFACED is a question only Mike can answer, so it is filed rather than acted on.

WHAT WENT. The phase flip was the S5 half of the compiled ui/client-only macro: a hydrating root advanced from :server phase to :client phase, every client-only site in the root swapped its fallback for its client subtree in ONE root-scoped update, and the transition emitted one :rf.ssr/phase-flip info trace per hydrating root. All of it went with the compiled re-frame.ui substrate (rf2-0yp7w).

WHAT REMAINS, and it is not nothing. Hicasso's defhost carries :server :client-only as its DEFAULT policy: per implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:399, the host region renders nothing on the server and nothing on hydration's first client pass, and the foreign component mounts once the markup is adopted, with a declared :fallback rendering there instead. So the user-visible transition the phase flip described still happens on every hydrated Hicasso page carrying a client-only crossing.

HOW IT IS REALISED, and why the old contract does not bind it. mint-host! mints ONE gate per declaration whose single useSyncExternalStore answers false from its SERVER snapshot (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:1367-1388, adopted?, with gate-adopted / gate-unadopted / gate-no-subscribe beside it; implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:196-206 explains why the server needs nothing). React's own post-hydration pass does the swap. There is no root-scoped phase value, no re-frame-level flip, and git grep -ni for phase-flip or phase flip under implementation/hicasso/ returns NOTHING.

THE QUESTION. Spec 011's retired section answered a debugging question in as many words: is this region showing its fallback or its live subtree. Nothing answers it today. Three positions, and the third is a real one:
 (a) MINT A HICASSO-OWNED TRACE for the adoption gate, catalogued in Spec 009 under whatever id fits, and let the tools read it.
 (b) LEAVE IT. Xray can already show a mounted tree, the swap is one React pass, and a trace per adoption is cost for a question a screenshot answers.
 (c) DECIDE IT IS THE SUBSTRATE'S, NOT THE SPEC'S. The old row was a compiled-substrate fact that Spec 011 rostered because the compiled substrate was the paved path; hicasso's contract lives in docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md and may simply own this.

Note (a) is the option that most resembles re-aiming donor normative text at hicasso, which rf2-0yp7w.11 ruled against by name when it ruled on spec/004D. It is not the same thing -- minting a fresh id for a live mechanism is not laundering an old one -- but the ruling is the nearest precedent and should be read before deciding.

ALSO WORTH A LOOK WHILE THIS IS OPEN, same seam and same shape: the :ssr/discover-root-manifest late-bind hook binds every view substrate and NO in-repo substrate resolves it. git grep -nF for the hook keyword returns the declaration at implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:742 and the publisher at implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc, and no consumer anywhere, against a control of :ssr/render-to-string which returns eight consumer files. The directory's own description already says so. rf2-8vpzy recorded the fact in spec/011's Discovery-hook section as UNMET rather than vacuous; whether a shipped hydrating mount ought to read the manifest is the same class of question as the one above.
close_reason: Done — PR #8508. One :info trace :rf.ssr/host-adopted at the client-only adoption crossing, per the 2026-08-18 22:58 AUSEST ruling; per-declaration, only on a real crossing, at most once. Rides the already-reserved :rf.ssr/* family so no Conventions.md change is needed; the single spec/009-Instrumentation.md catalogue row is DEFERRED behind the spec fence (PR #8500) and drafted verbatim in the PR body for the mayor to file or route. A sabotage run that came back green caught the first implementation never firing (identical? on keyword literals is false in a dev build); fixed to booleans and the suite now proves the positive case in Node. See the comment above for the full account.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-08-18 22:58 AUSEST — taken on Mike's standing delegation this session.

RULING: RESTORE THE OBSERVABILITY. Emit ONE info trace at the client-only adoption transition, so the question spec/011's retired section answered in as many words — is this region showing its fallback or its live subtree — has an answer again.

WHY, and the stance clause that decides it is EXCELLENT TOOLS rather than trust-the-programmer. This project ships an instrumentation API (Spec 009) and Xray as a first-class consumer of it; observability is a product surface here, not an optional extra. The bead establishes that the user-visible transition still happens on every hydrated Hicasso page carrying a client-only crossing — defhost's :server :client-only default at implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:399 — and that its successor mechanism is completely invisible: one gate per declaration whose single useSyncExternalStore answers false from its server snapshot (impl/codec.cljs:1367-1388, adopted?), with React's own post-hydration pass doing the swap. git grep -ni for phase-flip under implementation/hicasso/ returns nothing. So a real behaviour lost its only window at the same moment its implementation changed, and nobody chose that — it fell out of a substrate retirement.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE NAG-DIAGNOSTIC THE STANCE REJECTS. A trace is not a warning. It costs the programmer nothing, it fires into the instrumentation channel rather than the console, it makes no claim that anything is wrong, and it is opt-in at the consumer. The clause that rejects nag-diagnostics is aimed at machinery that interrupts a programmer who has done nothing wrong. This interrupts nobody.

SCOPE, AND KEEP IT SMALL. One trace at the adoption transition. Do NOT reintroduce a root-scoped phase value, do NOT invent a re-frame-level flip, and do NOT re-aim the retired :rf.ssr/phase-flip keyword at hicasso — that would launder donor-era normative text into hicasso's contract, which is out under Mike's rf2-0yp7w.11 ruling. The old contract was root-scoped because the compiled substrate was; hicasso's is per-declaration, and the trace should describe what hicasso actually does rather than what its predecessor did.

THE KEYWORD IS THE ONE THING THAT NEEDS CARE. It is a new reserved :rf/* name and it lands in the catalogue, so it must be classified and justified where it is registered, per the facade-export and catalogue conventions. Pick it to describe the mechanism that exists — adoption of a client-only host region — not the mechanism that went.

This note is a CLAIM like any other. Re-derive every line and column at origin/main HEAD before acting; the bead was written against an earlier tip.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DONE — PR #8508 (branch worker/hicsub-oaksj). The mayor's 2026-08-18 22:58 AUSEST ruling is discharged: ONE :info trace at the client-only adoption transition, so the question spec/011's retired Phase-flip section answered has an answer again.

WHAT LANDED. :rf.ssr/host-adopted, emitted from re-frame.hicasso.impl.codec/mint-host-gate!. Three properties, each witnessed: PER DECLARATION (the crossing cell is closed over by the gate and mint-host! mints one gate per defhost, so two sites of one host emit ONE event); ONLY A REAL CROSSING (a fresh createRoot mount, where adopted? answers true on the first pass and no placeholder ever renders, stays silent — announcing there would report a transition that did not occur); AT MOST ONCE (the cell disarms before it emits, so re-renders and a Strict-Mode double render cannot produce a second).

THE THREE PROHIBITIONS WERE HONOURED. No root-scoped phase value was reintroduced — the old contract was root-scoped because the compiled substrate was, and hicasso's is per-declaration. No re-frame-level flip was invented — React's own post-hydration pass does the swap and this only witnesses it. The retired :rf.ssr/phase-flip was NOT re-aimed at hicasso.

THE KEYWORD, which was the one thing the ruling said needed care. It rides the ALREADY-RESERVED :rf.ssr/* family — rostered in spec/Conventions.md and a family hicasso already emits into (:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch, impl/mount.cljs) — so NO Conventions.md change is needed. It is named for the mechanism that exists (adoption of a client-only host region) rather than the one that went.

SPEC LANDING OUTSTANDING, AND IT IS ONE ROW. The catalogue row belongs in spec/009-Instrumentation.md's :operation table, beside the struck :rf.ssr/phase-flip row. I verified that 009-Instrumentation.md is NOT among PR #8500's 47 files, so the follow-up is conflict-free — but the dispatch fenced spec/ wholesale while #8500 is open, so nothing under spec/ is touched in this PR. The row is DRAFTED VERBATIM in the PR body, ready to paste. Please file or route it once #8500 merges; until then the trace ships with its catalogue row deferred, which the dispatch named as an acceptable partial.

A REAL BUG WAS CAUGHT AND FIXED IN FLIGHT, and it is worth recording because of HOW. The first implementation NEVER FIRED. Its crossing cell used a three-state keyword guarded with identical? — reference equality — and keyword literals are only the same OBJECT when the build emits them through a shared constants table, which a dev build does not. The cell never left its initial value; the announce never armed; nothing was ever emitted.

It was INVISIBLE because every row of the first suite asserted an ABSENCE (no trace on the server, no trace on a fresh mount), and a mechanism that emits nothing at all satisfies all of them. The suite was green over dead code. What found it was a deliberately sabotaged run that came back GREEN — the sabotage was supposed to make a no-trace row fail, and it did not, so the control was interrogated rather than believed.

Both halves are fixed: the cell is now two booleans (no identity to get wrong, so the failure mode is removed rather than repaired), and the suite now proves the POSITIVE case in the Node lane. Rows 2 and 3 drive the real gate, real crossing cell and real emit through renderToString while stubbing only adopted? — React's own adoption signal, the one input a document-less runtime cannot supply. Row 4 takes the same claim through a real hydrateRoot with nothing stubbed; it is browser-lane and CI owns it.

GATES (each foreground, each exit captured from the runner): clj-kondo 0; node-test-hicasso compile 0; focused run 0 (4 tests, 17 assertions, 0 failures). Each was proved to reach the worker worktree by planted fault or root banner, and each restore was verified by content hash against the committed object rather than by reading a diff. The fast-PR spine was NOT run; scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py --list reports 96 required checks it does not decide. Production elision (:advanced + goog.DEBUG=false folds the crossing away) is NOT verified locally — CI's hicasso release build and check_production_erasure.cjs own that claim, and the PR body says so.

title: [spec-drift] spec/011 hydration-mismatch detection still names the donor Hiccup and compiled tiers as live tiers
description:
FOUND BY rf2-8vpzy (PR #8449) while retiring the phase-flip section in the same file. Filed rather than widened: the phase-flip clause inside it was entangled and was repaired; the rest is a separate judgement.

spec/011-SSR.md section Hydration-mismatch detection enumerates verification channels by TIER, and two of the three tier names are the removed substrates: the Hiccup tier and the compiled tier. Both are written in the present tense as live verification channels. The compiled tier went with the compiled re-frame.ui substrate and the Hiccup tier with the interpreted walk, both rf2-0yp7w.

WHAT rf2-8vpzy ALREADY REPAIRED, so this bead does not re-do it: the parenthetical at spec/011-SSR.md:809 that named the compiled tier PhaseFlipper as the thing that clears adoption-ref. PhaseFlipper now survives ONLY as a prose reference at implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1129 and in that one 011 line; git grep -nF PhaseFlipper returns nothing else, against a live adoption-window-closer in spine.cljs:1123 and hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:302 as the control.

THE LIVE PICTURE, measured. :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch is emitted at exactly three sites, all plain trace/emit! with a :warning envelope: implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1075 (the shared React-hook hydrate path, tier-discriminated by :where), implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:379 (the Hicasso door), and implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/arm1/mount.cljs:190. Zero sites route through trace/emit-error!. So the tier axis today is substrate-spine versus Hicasso-door, not Hiccup versus compiled versus native.

THE JUDGEMENT A WORKER CANNOT MAKE: whether to re-tense the tier vocabulary onto the live discrimination, or to retire the tier axis and state the verification channels substrate-neutrally. Either is a shape change to a live normative section. Note rf2-0yp7w.11 ruled against re-aiming donor normative text at hicasso when it ruled on spec/004D, which bears on the first option.

GATES: spec/009-Instrumentation.md and spec/011-SSR.md both fall to the spec/* catch-all in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh, which arms implementation_jvm wholesale. check_doc_slugs.py covers spec/ via DEFAULT_ROOTS. spec/ is HOT ZONE, one toucher.

title: [docs-drift] reconcile flush-render! optionality with the actual three-adapter roster
description:
Found by the merged-PR audit of PR #8446 at landed commit cc33d7e48598d3c8f43e375e05cf0b3cb78f4e63. That PR's source census is correct: six shipped adapter kinds exist, and only reagent, reagent-slim, and UIx install the optional :flush-render! slot. plain-atom, SSR, and test-react do not; test-react.cljc:7-8 explicitly says the omission is intentional.

Two live contract descriptions contradict that implementation and each other:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:640 calls flush-render! a contract surface "every adapter implements", immediately before lines 642-644 describe it as optional and absent from plain-atom/SSR.
- implementation/adapters/README.md:37 says flush-render! is "implemented by all four React-shaped adapters", but test-react is the fourth React-shaped adapter and intentionally has no slot.

This is user-facing API/adapter guidance: it can make an adapter author treat an optional capability as mandatory or make a test author expect a capability test-react deliberately does not provide.

Re-check the surrounding contract prose for the same exact overclaim, without broadening into a general documentation rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Both contradictory sentences accurately state that flush-render! is optional and is installed by reagent, reagent-slim, and UIx; test-react's intentional omission remains explicit. No production code or rf2-cydkp policy ruling changes. Relevant documentation/link checks pass.
