title: [method] mayor-merge.md says what is NOT a flake but never sanctions re-running one, so the mayor improvises the discriminator
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-18 00:25 AUSEST, checking rules the mayor ENFORCES against the command file governing the moment of use.

THE GAP. .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md line 30 ends: 'A real, repeated touched-surface failure is NOT a flake - dispatch a fix-worker to the same branch (run the ACTUAL failing gate, not a local proxy), never --admin past it.' That sentence presupposes flakes exist and rules out the wrong response to a real failure. It never says what the RIGHT response to a genuine flake is, and it gives no discriminator for telling them apart. The merge loop is the moment of use and this is its file.

WHAT THE MAYOR ACTUALLY DID, 2026-08-18 00:05 AUSEST, on judgement plus a bd memory rather than on the command file. PR #8443's 'Splint (fail on errors, warnings informational)' check read FAILURE. The log showed the job died in 'Set up job': three attempts to download actions/setup-java returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, backing off 25.2s then 21.9s, then '##[error]Failed to download archive after 3 attempts'. No repository code ran. The mayor re-ran the failed job with 'gh run rerun <id> --failed'.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IT USED, WHICH IS THE THING WORTH WRITING DOWN: the failure occurred BEFORE any repository code executed, so the diff cannot have caused it. That is stronger and cheaper than the usual two-part test (diff cannot touch the surface AND the gate is green on main), because it needs no second observation - the failing step names itself.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. The 429 is self-inflicted: six saturated workers each trigger a full check matrix against a shared action-download budget. Under this fleet size, setup-phase rate-limit failures are an expected mode, not a curiosity, so the mayor will meet this repeatedly and should not re-derive the response each time.

FIX PROPOSED (one or two sentences, in mayor-merge.md beside the existing not-a-flake sentence): a setup-phase or infrastructure failure - one that occurs before repository code runs, such as an action download returning 429 - is re-run with 'gh run rerun <id> --failed' rather than dispatched to a fix-worker, and NEVER merged past; the five clauses still apply to the re-run result. State the before-repo-code-ran discriminator explicitly. Add that repeated setup failures ACROSS several PRs rather than one job indicate fleet size is the cause, and the mayor says so rather than re-running indefinitely.

WORKER-TRACKED SURFACE, so FILED rather than committed: .claude/commands/ is fenced from the mayor checkout and is the surface PRs #8427 and #8432 changed through workers.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT PR #8448 — correctness correction. The new mayor-merge rule says a failure before repository code ran cannot have been caused by the diff and needs no second observation. That phase test is too broad: versioned .github/workflows/** controls action pins, setup inputs, runner selection and permissions, so a PR can make setup-java or another setup step fail before any project command runs. It also conflicts with the immediately preceding rule that a real repeated failure on a touched surface goes to a fix-worker. Bounded repair: route to re-run only when the error itself proves an external transient (for example HTTP 429 fetching an unchanged pinned action) and the PR does not change the failed workflow/setup configuration; otherwise keep the setup failure on the touched-surface path. Cross-PR fleet attribution likewise needs the same external failure signature, not setup phase alone. Preserve the five clauses and never-merge-past rule.
close_reason: Landed in PR #8448, commit 6cabf516bd, merged to main. Verified at source on origin/main rather than from the PR body: .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md line 30 now carries the sanction - a failure BEFORE any repository code ran is the other case and the failing step names itself, so the diff cannot have caused it and no second observation is needed; re-run with gh run rerun and hold the re-run to the same five clauses, never merge past it. It also carries the correction this bead's dispatch supplied: RE-RUNNING IS NOT A CURE, since #8443's Splint job died in Set up job on the same actions/setup-java 429 twice about eight minutes apart, so when SEVERAL PRs fail that way rather than one job twice, fleet size is the cause and the mayor says so rather than re-running indefinitely. The pre-existing not-a-flake guard is untouched and the five-clause criterion is unmodified. Closed late by the mayor: the worker landed the change but did not close the bead, and the merge loop's own instruction to verify the worker closed its bead was missed at merge time.

title: [spec-drift] spec/009's open-drain guard clause quantifies over an EMPTY set and calls it 'genuinely universally' enforced
description:
REPORTED BY rf2-k9rzr's worker (PR #8429) under a fence that excluded spec/, so reported rather than widened. Filed so the finding has a durable owner rather than living in a PR body. VERIFIED AT SOURCE by the mayor at origin/main 8f6006cc5a, 2026-08-17 22:20 AUSEST.

THE SENTENCE. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2413, in the :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch catalogue row: 'Enforced by ONE implementation and, unlike the convergence bound below, genuinely universally: the SHARED open-drain guard is re-frame.frame/guard-open-drain! in CORE (ruling rf2-vxgfnd.207; moved into core by rf2-87ouj), and EVERY substrate whose synchronous flush can publish a render phase calls it.'

THE MEASUREMENT. 'git grep -nF guard-open-drain! -- implementation/' returns exactly ONE line: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:3521, which is the defn itself. ZERO call sites. Positive control: the same pattern finds the definition, so the search is not a false empty. So the quantifier's subject set is empty and the sentence is VACUOUSLY TRUE.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG, and the method names the class: 'when a rule says EVERY, check the quantifier'. A vacuously-true universal reads to every future maintainer as a live, enforced law, and 'genuinely universally' is doing work in that sentence — it draws an explicit contrast with the convergence bound, which the same row says is NOT universally enforced. A reader takes it as the strong case. What is actually true is the opposite end: nothing calls it.

THE GUARD ITSELF STAYS, AND THAT IS ALREADY SETTLED. rf2-k9rzr's worker examined guard-open-drain! as a candidate orphan and REFUSED to cut it, on the function's own docstring: both callers went with the retired donor artefacts and the guard stayed 'because the law is core's rather than theirs', retained normative surface under rulings rf2-vxgfnd.207 and rf2-87ouj. So this bead is NOT 'delete the dead function'. It is 'stop the spec asserting live universal enforcement over an empty set'.

TWO MORE CLAUSES IN THE SAME ROW LOOK STALE FOR THE SAME REASON — re-derive each rather than taking this: 'Reachability is dev/test AND production: neither substrate's synchronous render-commit is goog.DEBUG-gated, and only the ui.test/flush! call site is test-only.' Both named substrates and ui.test belong to re-frame.ui, which is RETIRED AND REMOVED (rf2-0yp7w, PR #8322). A sentence describing the gating of substrates that no longer exist is describing nothing.

THE DISCRIMINATION THE REPAIR NEEDS: say what is TRUE now — the guard is retained normative surface in core with no current caller, awaiting the substrate that needs it — without either deleting the law or claiming an enforcement that does not exist. Do not re-aim it at hicasso; the 004D precedent (rf2-0yp7w.11) is that re-aiming donor-era normative text at hicasso launders it into hicasso's contract, and Mike ruled against exactly that.

SURFACE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md only. HOT ZONE per CLAUDE.md — one toucher at a time.

MERGED-PR AUDIT PR #8438 — correctness failure in the quantifier census at merge commit 1463371bf50979cccb414d3e74fa70df50ddd8dd.

The PR proves that guard-open-drain! has zero call sites. That measures compliance, not the subject set of the sentence EVERY substrate whose synchronous flush can publish a render phase MUST call it. The subject set is not empty:

- implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:208 uses make-react-adapter; substrate/spine.cljs:1741-1780 supplies its production react-dom/flushSync implementation.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:625-653 is the live delegated entry point. It calls the installed adapter function directly; neither it nor any implementation above calls frame/guard-open-drain!.

Those three are exactly current substrates whose synchronous flush can publish a render phase. title: hicasso: the BY SITE summary's 'worst-dev site' column prints siteWitness.dominant, which is not the worst leg's site
description:
NOTICED by rf2-ojehu while reading the by-site window's own output. Cosmetic in the code, not cosmetic in what a reader quotes.

p0_run.cjs allocSiteReport prints a column headed 'worst-dev site' and fills it with w.dominant. But allocSiteWitness computes dominant from TOTALS — the sum of |per-leg deviation from that site's own median| across all measured legs — not from the worst leg. The worst leg's own site is a different field (legs[k].site) and the reporter prints its decomposition on the following line, so both quantities are on screen under one heading.

WHY IT MATTERS ENOUGH TO FILE. On rf2-ojehu's 72 windows the two happen to agree, so nothing was misread this time. The next window that quotes the column will state the estimator by its heading — 'the worst deviation is in dispatch' — when what was computed is 'dispatch holds the larger total absolute deviation'. Those are different claims about different statistics, and a measurement record naming the wrong one is precisely the class of overclaim the measurement discipline audits for.

THE FIX is a heading, e.g. 'dominant site (total |dev|)'. NOT taken by rf2-ojehu: a measurement window does not amend the instrument it is measuring on, and the mode is off by default so nothing published is affected.

EVIDENCE: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs, allocSiteReport's round/window header line and allocSiteWitness's dominant.

title: [audit] five live-code orphans and one vacuous assertion, found by R6c and deliberately not actioned
description:
REPORTED BY R6c (rf2-9sz2t, PR #8416) under a comment-only fence, which told
it to stop and report rather than reach into live code. It did exactly that.
Filed so the findings have a durable owner rather than living in a PR body.

EACH IS A CLAIM, NOT A FINDING. Re-derive every one at origin/main before
acting — R6c measured them against a moving trunk, and 'no caller anywhere' is
precisely the shape that a wrong or truncated search produces. On this tree
prefer 'git grep' to plain 'grep': plain grep gave a false EMPTY on a string
demonstrably present, a false 0 on a positive control, and ABORTED mid-run on
one spec file, all within one day. EVERY zero here needs its positive control
reported alongside it.

THE FIVE ORPHANS, as reported:
  1. 'guard-open-drain!' — no caller anywhere.
  2. 'dispatch-on-error!' — its 'route-frame?' 9-arity has no false-passer, so
     one branch is unreachable from any call site.
  3. ':ssr/discover-root-manifest' — PUBLISHED with no consumer.
  4. ':rf.frame/must-create?' — no consumer outside core's own tests.
  5. 'cljs-probe' — reconciles against a ':ui-test-signatures' sidecar key
     that no longer exists.
PLUS: a vacuous assertion in check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs.

WHY THIS IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY WORK, and the stance governs it: an audit
finding is a CLAIM, and 'unused' is the weakest kind. Item 3 is PUBLISHED
surface — a published symbol with no in-repo consumer is exactly what a
published symbol looks like, so 'no consumer' is not evidence of deadness
there and the reasoning must be different in kind. Item 4 names a keyword
whose only consumers are tests, which is either dead weight or a contract the
tests are pinning; the keyword-catalogue check may already have an opinion.
Item 5 is the sharpest, because a probe reconciling against a key that does
not exist is not merely unused — it may be silently passing.

SO THE DELIVERABLE MAY WELL BE A PARTIAL REFUSAL, and that is a good outcome.
Rank them: the vacuous assertion and item 5 look like real defects; items 1
and 2 look like ordinary dead code; items 3 and 4 need a reason before a
verdict. Close what does not survive re-derivation, with the evidence.

CONTROL IF ANY DELETION HAPPENS: deleting dead code passes every test BY
CONSTRUCTION, so a green suite proves nothing. Require before/after test and
assertion counts that match EXACTLY, and a planted fault in the SURVIVING path
proving the suite still reaches it. A peer's cut was made safe this session by
exactly that pair — 2243 tests / 11681 assertions identical either side.

SEQUENCING: PR #8416 must merge first; it is the source of these observations
and touches 59 files under implementation/.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT PR #8429 - completeness and implementation-quality correction.

The PR repaired the stale CLJS diagnostic text, but its replacement prose supplies the decisive counter-evidence to closing item 5: `cljs_probe.cljc` now says no sidecar block drives `signature-problems` today and retains it only for a possible future host-aware block. Synthetic tests prove that an orphan behaves on synthetic data; they do not make it part of the manifest gate.

The orphan is a two-host cluster, not one diagnostic string. Re-derived at PR head fcaf1e2c0c275fd09ca869e538adfaf0a4d143be and still present on origin/main 3b5511e6edc0a22317618045f28023849fd6d8bf:

Their analyzer-arity helpers therefore feed no live project contract.

So #8429's conclusion that item 5 was resolved is incomplete. A test-only island retained for a hypothetical future caller is maintenance surface with no present requirement, and the untouched JVM half still teaches the removed donor by name. Reopening this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate.

Bounded disposition: remove the dormant two-host signature lane and its synthetic-only tests/imports/helpers, unless a current named surface and real sidecar authority are first identified and wired through both lanes. Preserve the active existence/tier manifest reconciliation. Because deletion greens by construction, keep this bead's original before/after-count and planted-fault control on the surviving manifest path.

title: [packaging] the Hicasso test kit ships in no jar: test_kit/src is off :paths AND off :src-dirs
description:
FOUND WHILE FIXING rf2-0ircf gap 2. Filed rather than fixed: this is a packaging change with its own gates and blast radius, and that bead is the docs corpus.

THE FACT, at source in implementation/hicasso/deps.edn. `test_kit/src` -- the root carrying re-frame.hicasso.test (ht) and re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted (hm), the supported L0-L3 testing surface -- appears in exactly two places: the in-repo :test alias's :extra-paths, and implementation/shadow-cljs.edn's :source-paths. It is NOT on the artefact's :paths ["src" "resources"], and it is NOT on :clein/build's :src-dirs ["src" "resources"]. :src-dirs is what determines jar content.

CONSEQUENCE. Today nothing is published, so a consumer resolves Hicasso by :local/root and CAN reach the kit by naming the checkout path explicitly -- which is what rf2-0ircf's new 15-testing.md section now documents, and it is correct for today. The day the first v* tag is cut and day8/re-frame2-hicasso resolves from Clojars, that instruction stops working and NO instruction replaces it: the jar will not contain the files, and there is no separate test-kit coordinate (`.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh`'s ARTEFACTS list has no such entry).

So the docs written for rf2-0ircf carry a publication-dated expiry. Either the kit joins :src-dirs (off :paths still gives the zero-production-reachability property the deps.edn comment is defending -- :paths governs a :local/root consumer, jar content governs a Maven one, and they are not the same lever), or it becomes its own coordinate, or the guide must say the kit is monorepo-only.

Compare re-frame.test-support, which ships from core's src/ and is on both :paths and :src-dirs.

DEPENDS: worth deciding before the first release tag, since after it the answer is visible to consumers.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8468: test_kit/src joins :clein/build's :src-dirs, so day8/re-frame2-hicasso's jar carries re-frame.hicasso.test and re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted. Verified by building the jar both ways with clojure -M:clein jar — 39 entries and zero kit entries before, 42 entries with both kit namespaces after. No jar-content verification outstanding. No new coordinate, so the version-lockstep gate is unarmed and rf2-fo4ng's held rename is not pre-empted. Unblocks the movable half of rf2-hic-061.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: COST OF THE HOLD, recorded by the mayor 2026-08-17 22:00 AUSEST. Two beads sit behind this packaging decision: rf2-hic-061 (versioned artifacts, compatibility matrix, upgrade policy) depends on it directly, and rf2-v04s (pilot prep package) depends on hic-061 in turn. Neither can be dispatched until this is ruled. hic-061's other dependency, rf2-uelji, is FROZEN on Clojars verified-group policy, so this bead is the half of that pair a ruling can actually move. THE MAYOR'S RECOMMENDATION, stated so the ruling is cheap: put test_kit/src on :clein/build's :src-dirs and leave it OFF :paths. The bead's own reasoning supports it — :paths governs a :local/root consumer while jar content governs a Maven one, so keeping it off :paths preserves the zero-production-reachability property the deps.edn comment defends, and adding it to :src-dirs stops rf2-0ircf's new 15-testing.md guidance expiring silently at the first release tag. The alternatives are a separate test-kit coordinate (more surface, needs a verify-version-lockstep.sh ARTEFACTS entry) or documenting the kit as monorepo-only (cheapest now, worst for consumers).

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
RULED AND SHIPPED — PR #8468 (worker/testkit-rxf49), 2026-08-18.

VERDICT: option 1, the mayor's recorded recommendation. test_kit/src joins :clein/build's :src-dirs; :paths is left alone. No new coordinate.

EVERY FILED CLAIM HELD AT SOURCE. test_kit/src was on exactly two roots (the :test alias :extra-paths and implementation/shadow-cljs.edn :source-paths), on neither :paths nor :src-dirs; no v* tag exists; verify-version-lockstep.sh's ARTEFACTS list (14 entries) has no test-kit coordinate.

:src-dirs IS the jar-content key, read out of the build tool rather than inferred: clein's create-jar is clean -> copy-src -> b/jar, and copy-src is b/copy-dir over (concat :src-dirs :resource-dirs) into :class-dir (noahtheduke/clein.cljc L115-132, pinned sha 2b83503246). deploy and install share copy-src.

PROVEN BY BUILDING BOTH WAYS with clojure -M:clein jar, the same build-only invocation release.yml uses as its deploy dry-run: BEFORE = 39 entries, ZERO test-kit entries. AFTER = 42 entries, re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs + re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs present. The defect was real and is fixed. No jar-content verification remains outstanding.

AN EXISTING PATTERN ANSWERED THE DESIGN QUESTION. Four publishable artefacts already ship a consumer-facing testing surface inside the main jar from src/ (re-frame.test-support and re-frame.test-helpers in core, plus http/, resources/ and routing/ test-support). Across all 14 publishable artefacts there is no separate test-kit coordinate, and :paths equals :src-dirs everywhere except hicasso. A second coordinate was weighed and rejected: real machinery (lockstep ARTEFACTS entry + release.yml deploy stage + release-notes row) for two files, zero precedent, and it lands in the hot zone.

THE DEV-ONLY PROPERTY IS UNAFFECTED, and the deps.edn comment defending it was overstating what the separate root buys. re-frame.hicasso.evidence and .tool ship from src/ and are dev-only by REACHABILITY; check_production_erasure.cjs is what checks it, and the kit is ALREADY on that roster under the rf.error/hicasso-test- sentinel, whose entry states the rule itself: no src/ namespace may require the kit. A classpath entry costs no bundle bytes; a :require does.

DOES NOT ARM THE VERSION-LOCKSTEP GATE: no coordinate added, so no ARTEFACTS/release.yml edit needed. Gate re-run and passes unchanged. Nothing pre-empts rf2-fo4ng's held day8/* rename.

DOCS: 15-testing.md said 'Neither namespace arrives with the artifact' and taught one route; both routes are now spelled. api-reference.md and docs/design/hicasso/product/release-policy.md carried the same literals and are corrected. All doc edits prose-only (every fence in docs/core/hicasso/** is digest-pinned by check_guide_samples.py).

title: [design] a Hicasso-only app must still depend on UIx or Reagent, purely for the reactive substrate
description:
SURFACED, NOT FIXED — a judgement for Mike, raised by rf2-ypct8's
from-scratch install run (2026-08-16).

Hicasso is described as the re-frame-native view layer, and a reader
following docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md now writes:

  {:deps {day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:local/root "..."}
          day8/re-frame2-uix     {:local/root ".../adapters/uix"}}}

The second coordinate exists only to supply an ADAPTER. Hicasso mounts
through react-dom itself and interprets its own Hiccup, but `h/mount!`
ensures a frame, `rf/make-frame` asks the adapter for a state container,
and there is no adapter unless the consumer installs one — so the app
takes a dependency on com.pitch/uix.core (via day8/re-frame2-uix) whose
notation it never writes. Reagent and reagent-slim are the same trade in
a different currency.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE:
- implementation/hicasso/deps.edn ships NO adapter ("Test-only: shipping
  source names no adapter at all") and its test lane adds
  day8/re-frame2-uix under :test for exactly this reason.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/consumer_app.cljs:147-162
  and .../examples/editor/app.cljs:71-77 both open with
  `(rf/init! uix-adapter/adapter)` and say why: the headless plain-atom
  adapter's derived value is not IWatchable, so a moving subscription
  under it notifies nothing.
- Measured: deleting the `rf/init!` line from the install chapter's own
  example compiles fine and throws in the browser —
  :rf.error/no-adapter-installed, :where rf/make-state-container.

THE QUESTION. Is a Hicasso-shaped adapter (its own six required contract
fns over a plain reactive container, no third-party view library) worth
having, so that a Hicasso app depends on core + hicasso and nothing
else? Or is riding a shipped adapter the intended, permanent shape — in
which case the guide's current sentence, "this guide passes
uix-adapter/adapter because that is what Hicasso's own witnesses run
on", is the whole answer and this bead closes.

NOT A BUG. Everything above works, is documented, and is now stated on
the install page. This is a packaging/ergonomics call, priced at P3.
close_reason:
BUILT, per the mayor ruling of 2026-08-19 01:05 AUSEST. PR #8512 (worker/hicadapter-hvr5h) ships `re-frame.hicasso.substrate`, so a Hicasso application depends on core plus Hicasso and nothing else; `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md` now has a reader write ONE coordinate and `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)`.

The sizing held. The adapter is an assembly over `re-frame.substrate.spine` — React's own useMemo/useCallback/useContext, a frame-provider component, `:kind :rf.adapter/hicasso` — and it COMPILES, which the sizing said it had not proved. One enrolment file into core's parameterised React-adapter suite gives 92 forwarders; the focused Hicasso CLJS lane is 1326 tests / 5407 assertions, 0 failures, and the enrolment was proved to target THIS adapter by sabotage rather than by reading a count. Reagent, reagent-slim and UIx are untouched; the adapter is an OPTIONAL module, so an application that installs one of them pays no spine bytes.

TWO THINGS THE RULING ASKED FOR THAT THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE, both named in the PR body:

1. THE BUNDLE DELTA IS STILL NOT MEASURED. Measuring it needs a shadow-cljs release build, which contends for the machine exactly as a bench run does, and the mayor instructed mid-task that no release build or other heavyweight gate was to run while worker/disp-rs8q6 held the box. Direction unchanged (down, uix.core leaves); magnitude never measured, here or in the sizing. The mayor is dispatching it as its own bead once the machine is free.

2. THE REGISTRATION TAIL, which the sizing priced at zero because it looked only at code. A shipped adapter kind is registered surface in rosters beyond the fence. Filed rather than left: rf2-auiy5 (spec — the canonical :rf.adapter/* member in Conventions, 006 x2 and API.md; spec/ is one-toucher and was fenced off), rf2-zkjd5 (P1, FUNCTIONAL — tools/xray's react-element-render-kinds denylist reasons from 'there is no :rf.adapter/hicasso', so a page installing this adapter now gets an uncaught React child error where a clean diagnostic used to be), rf2-4rozj (P3 prose — tools/story's schemas.cljc says the same). comments.text:
MAYOR 2026-08-18, BACKLOG REREAD — CORRECTLY HELD FOR YOU, AND THE COST OF HOLDING IT IS RISING BECAUSE OF WHERE THE PROGRAMME NOW IS. Nothing is blocked; this is about timing rather than blockage.

THE QUESTION, unchanged: a Hicasso-only app must still depend on UIx or Reagent purely for the reactive substrate. h/mount! ensures a frame, rf/make-frame asks the ADAPTER for a state container, and there is no adapter unless the consumer installs one — so a reader following docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md writes a second coordinate, day8/re-frame2-uix, whose notation they never use. Reagent and reagent-slim are the same trade in a different currency.

WHY THE TIMING MATTERS NOW. This is a FIRST-IMPRESSION defect against the headline claim that Hicasso is the re-frame-native view layer, and the audience that meets it first is the PILOTS. rf2-hic-063's two blinded pilots are ratified and sit behind rf2-hic-061, whose sole remaining blocker is your Clojars act on rf2-uelji. So the pilots could start within days of that badge landing, and a blinded pilot's friction log is exactly where 'why am I installing UIx to use the React-free view layer?' gets written down.

THE ASYMMETRY, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT: answering this BEFORE the pilots costs one ruling. Answering it after costs a ruling plus a documented friction item in the pilot record, and a pilot finding is harder to retire than a design note because it is evidence about a real reader. If the answer is 'this is by design and the docs should say so plainly', that is a cheap docs change now and an awkward correction later.

I AM NOT RULING IT. It is a product-shape call about what re-frame-native means and what the minimal dependency set is, and rf2-oaksj sits beside it as a second design question of the same kind (the retired :rf.ssr/phase-flip's successor — hicasso's client-only adoption gate — has no observability). Neither blocks anything today. Both are worth a few minutes before the pilots rather than after.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MAYOR, 2026-08-18 22:45 AUSEST — SPLITTING THE DECISION FROM THE WORK, AND RELEASING THE HALF THAT IS TRUE UNDER EITHER ANSWER.

I am NOT ruling the build tonight, and I want to be explicit that this is a choice rather than an omission. Mike's standing grant this session is 'don't ask me for permission, get hicasso to 0 beads', and I have used it to rule four other beads. This one I am handling differently, because it is the one on the list that changes what the library IS rather than how it is documented, tested or released. A new shipped adapter is public surface with a maintenance tail, and 'what kind of project is this trying to be' is the category the method reserves.

BUT LEAVING IT WHOLLY UNTOUCHED WOULD BE THE OTHER ERROR. The bead asks one question that cannot be answered without work — is a Hicasso-shaped adapter WORTH having — and the sizing of it is true under either answer. So:

RELEASED NOW, dispatchable without a further ruling: SIZE IT. Establish, at source, exactly what a Hicasso-shaped adapter would have to implement — the six required contract fns over a plain reactive container — and what the gap is between that and the headless plain-atom adapter that already exists. The bead already names the crux: the headless adapter's derived value is not IWatchable, so a moving subscription under it notifies nothing (verified at implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/consumer_app.cljs:147-162 and examples/editor/app.cljs:71-77, both opening with rf/init! uix-adapter/adapter and saying why). The deliverable is a sized answer with evidence: which of the six are already satisfied, what an IWatchable container costs, and what it would mean for bundle size and test surface. NO NEW ADAPTER IS BUILT under this half.

HELD FOR MIKE: whether to ship it.

MY RECOMMENDATION, so the decision is cheap when he reaches it: BUILD IT, unless the sizing comes back large. The defect is real and it is on the first page a user reads. docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md has a reader write two coordinates, and the second exists only to supply an adapter — the app takes a dependency on com.pitch/uix.core whose notation it never writes. Hicasso is described as the re-frame-NATIVE view layer; requiring a competing view library purely for the reactive substrate is exactly the friction the stance's 'excellent ergonomics, minimal API, low friction' lens exists to remove, and Reagent and reagent-slim are the same trade in a different currency. Against that: it is new shipped surface, and the stance also says not to gold-plate. The sizing is what decides between those two readings, which is why it goes first.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY RECOMMENDATION: if the sizing shows an IWatchable plain container drags in real machinery rather than a small wrapper, the honest answer becomes 'document the dependency clearly and move on', and the install chapter gets one sentence saying WHY the second coordinate is there. That is a legitimate outcome and the sizing worker should say so if it finds it.

The sizing half is read-and-measure work that does not load the box, so it can be dispatched beside a live measurement window.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
SIZING DELIVERED (rf2-hvr5h released half) — PR #8508, docs/design/hicasso/reactive-substrate-adapter-costing.md. NO ADAPTER BUILT, no shipped surface added, and the ship decision remains HELD FOR MIKE. Leaving this bead OPEN for that reason.

VERDICT: THE SIZING COMES BACK SMALL, and it comes back small because the bead's own framing points at the expensive path. The bead asks what an IWatchable plain reactive container would cost. The answer is NOTHING, because core already ships one.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the bead's summary, read against Spec 006's normative table rather than prose: subscribe-container is OPTIONAL, not one of the six (the core falls back to inline invalidation inside replace-container!), and render-to-string IS one of the six. The six required are make-state-container, read-container, replace-container!, make-derived-value, render, render-to-string.

WHICH THE HEADLESS PLAIN-ATOM ADAPTER ALREADY SATISFIES: four of six outright (make-state-container, read-container, replace-container!, render-to-string — the first three from the shared re-frame.substrate.atom-container, 35 lines). It REFUSES render by design, throwing :rf.error/render-on-headless-adapter. And it supplies make-derived-value in SHAPE but not in BEHAVIOUR: it reifies IDeref and the re-frame-owned IDisposable, registers no watch, and recomputes on every deref. Its own comment says why — "No caching: derived values recompute on every deref" — and that is correct for SSR. This is the crux the bead names, and it is verified at source.

BUT THE PLAIN-ATOM ADAPTER IS NOT THE BASE A HICASSO ADAPTER WOULD BUILD ON, and that is the finding that reframes the whole bead. The push-based reactive container ALREADY EXISTS IN CORE, at implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs (3762 lines), whose own docstring names the intended consumer: "Shared substrate-spine helpers for React-shaped adapters that lack a native reactive-atom primitive (UIx and ANY FUTURE MINIMAL-REACT-WRAPPER SUBSTRATE)". Hicasso is exactly that. The spine wires ONE WATCH PER SOURCE at construction and coalesces through a per-adapter epoch scheduler so a multi-input derived value recomputes glitch-free and notifies once per coherent input epoch; Spec 006 records that its derived value "is live the moment it exists" and needs no activation hook.

WHAT A SUBSTRATE ACTUALLY SUPPLIES, at source: spine/make-react-spine takes SEVEN inputs — a substrate-name string, three gensym prefixes, and three hook fns (use-memo, use-callback, use-context) — and RETURNS a map already carrying all six required contract fns. spine/make-react-adapter then takes that map plus :kind and :frame-provider, and its docstring states the rule outright: "every React-hook adapter calls this with the same shape — the only inputs are their already-substrate-specific spine-fns map, :kind, and native :frame-provider". The ENTIRE UIx adapter is 211 lines, mostly docstrings; its substrate-specific content is three React hooks, two native defui components (native only to preserve UIx's own prop marshalling — a NOTATION concern, not a reactivity one), and one set! pinning controlled-input behaviour.

Hicasso already imports react directly, already calls React hooks (useSyncExternalStore is the whole of its client-only gate), and already renders a frame provider over the SAME shared context object every React-shaped adapter reads (re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context, written by re-frame.hicasso.impl.mount/provider). Every ingredient make-react-spine asks for is something Hicasso has in hand. So the deliverable would be a small ASSEMBLY namespace in the shape of the UIx one — a wrapper, not machinery.

BUNDLE SIZE: down. re-frame.core does NOT require the spine (verified), so the spine arrives with whichever adapter needs it either way; what LEAVES is com.pitch/uix.core, a compiler and hook wrappers and element marshalling a Hicasso app never invokes. No new machinery is added to move it back up. DIRECTION is read off the dependency graph; MAGNITUDE IS NOT MEASURED — no release build was run for this sizing, because a bench-class measurement held the box, and the page says so rather than implying a number.

TEST SURFACE: one enrolment file. The React-adapter suite is ALREADY PARAMETERISED — implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs is 6740 lines in CORE, and UIx enrolls through a single 94-line entry file whose docstring states the contract: "any future React-hook adapter picks up the whole surface by adding one entry file like this one". That file reduces to an adapter :require, a fixture, a cfg map and one macro call, generating roughly fifty deftest forwarders. UIx's other eight test files are substrate-NOTATION specific (controlled-input defaults, defui-shaped provider/hook tests), and Hicasso's own suite already covers the equivalent ground for its notation.

AGAINST YOUR RECOMMENDATION'S FALLBACK CONDITION: you wrote that the recommendation flips to "document the dependency clearly and move on" IF the sizing shows an IWatchable plain container drags in real machinery rather than a small wrapper. THAT CONDITION DOES NOT HOLD. The machinery exists, is push-based, is in core, and was written for this case.

TWO HONEST CAUTIONS AGAINST, recorded on the page rather than buried: (1) it is still NEW SHIPPED SURFACE — a published coordinate carries a maintenance tail, a release-DAG slot and a version-lockstep entry, none of which this sizing prices; (2) NOTHING WAS COMPILED — the assembly is argued from two adapter factories' stated contracts and from what Hicasso already imports. A strong argument, not a green build.

The decision remains Mike's. Its cost, if taken, is a small assembly namespace and one test-enrolment file — not a reactive engine.

MAYOR RULING, 2026-08-19 01:05 AUSEST — THE HOLD IS RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVES BY THE CONDITION I PUBLISHED RATHER THAN BY A CHANGE OF MIND.

WHAT I SAID AT 22:45: 'BUILD IT, unless the sizing comes back large', and I named the fallback explicitly — 'if the sizing shows an IWatchable plain container drags in real machinery rather than a small wrapper, the honest answer becomes document the dependency clearly and move on'.

RULING: BUILD IT. A Hicasso-shaped adapter, so a Hicasso app depends on core plus hicasso and nothing else.

WHY I AM RULING RATHER THAN CONTINUING TO HOLD. I held this because it 'changes what the library IS', and that was the right instinct against an unknown cost — a new shipped adapter with a maintenance tail is Mike's call. The sizing has removed the unknown. What is actually proposed is enrolling hicasso in a spine core already ships for exactly this purpose, at a bundle cost that is negative. That is not a new subsystem; it is using the seam as designed. Holding further would be the deference failure the method names — carrying an item 'for the operator' that the project's own stance and its own shipped code already answer.

THE DEFECT IT FIXES IS ON THE FIRST PAGE A USER READS. docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md has a reader write two coordinates, and the second exists only to supply an adapter whose notation the app never writes. A CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S OWN TEXT, established by the sizing worker against Spec 006's normative table: the bead says 'its own six required contract fns' and gets the membership wrong in two places. subscribe-container is OPTIONAL, not one of the six. render-to-string IS one of the six. Whoever builds this works from Spec 006's table, not from the bead's sentence.

SCOPE WHEN DISPATCHED: enrol hicasso in re-frame.substrate.spine and ship the adapter; update the installation chapter so a reader writes ONE coordinate; one enrolment file for the parameterised suite. Do NOT rewrite the adapter contract, do NOT touch the existing three adapters, and do NOT remove UIx or Reagent support — this adds an option, it does not withdraw any.

title: [retire] frame-closing? has no consumers left — decide its disposition
description:
R4 (rf2-0yp7w.7) removed the :ui/on-frame-destroyed! call site. frame.cljc:1364 'frame-closing?' was introduced (rf2-vxgfnd.61) as the linearization read the COMPILED-VIEW ViewCell commit consults so a cell enrolling mid-teardown does not publish ownership onto a dying frame. That consumer left the tree with re-frame.ui (R2b).

VERIFIED at tip: git grep -F 'frame-closing?' returns matches ONLY inside implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc itself (its defn, two docstring mentions, one comment). ZERO callers anywhere else in the tree.

The predicate and its 'destroying-frames' registry (12 refs in frame.cljc) are still WIRED — populated at the top of destroy-frame! and cleared in its terminal finally — so this is dead-but-live code, not a broken surface. R4 left both in place (out of scope) and only reworded the docstring so it no longer names the deleted :ui/on-frame-destroyed! hook.

DECISION NEEDED: delete 'frame-closing?' + 'destroying-frames' outright, or keep them as the substrate-neutral seam any future cell-commit path would consult. Check whether the marker registry has a second job (the re-entrancy guard at ~frame.cljc:4416 references it) before cutting — it may be load-bearing independently of the predicate.
close_reason:
CUT frame-closing?; KEPT destroying-frames. PR #8403.

DECISION + EVIDENCE.

frame-closing? is CUT. Not merely because it has zero callers (re-verified at tip: git grep -F returns 5 lines in ONE file, frame.cljc itself — 2 comments, the defn, 2 docstring mentions; positive control 'destroy-frame!' = 274 files, negative control exits 1). It is cut because Spec 002's destroy recipe linearizes on the EXACT-INCARNATION claim and states 'a stale claim for incarnation A does not fence a fresh same-id incarnation B' — and frame-closing? is bare-id. Its own docstring recorded that it 'would wrongly tear down a cell that owns B' and sent callers to frame-incarnation-closing? (rf2-vxgfnd.94). Keeping it as a reserved seam would reserve the reading the spec forbids.

The 'a future substrate will need it' argument is already answered in the negative by the substrate that shipped: Hicasso — the re-frame-native view layer and the live cell-commit path — consults frame-incarnation-token (impl/collector.cljs:773, impl/frames.cljs:133, impl/mount.cljs:269), never a bare-id read.

NO SPEC MANDATES IT. git grep -i -E 'frame-closing|closing\?|close lifecycle|destroying-frames|frame-incarnation-closing' over spec/ and docs/ returns ZERO, controlled — the same shape returns spec/002-Frames.md:1962 for frame-disposed-for-drain and 4 hits for 'destroy recipe'. Spec 002's recipe was read at current post-R4-renumbering text (spec/002-Frames.md:669).

destroying-frames is KEPT — the bead's 'delete both outright' option is REFUSED on evidence. It is load-bearing three ways: (1) the re-entrancy guard in claim-frame-destroy!, which Spec 002 mandates outright ('the re-entrancy guard closes the window BEFORE :destroyed? flips to true'); (2) frame-incarnation-closing?, 5 call sites in router.cljc; (3) frame-disposed-for-drain?, router.cljc plus the drain! recipe in spec/002-Frames.md:1962.

CONTROLS. A green suite proves nothing when the removed fn had no callers, so: JVM core 2243 tests/11681 assertions before AND after (zero delta); CLJS :node-test 11771/59589 before AND after, with the 'before' taken by swapping origin/main's frame.cljc back in and re-running, not inferred; :node-test compile roster 1985 files, 0 warnings, either side — the namespace-count control. Red proof planted in the SURVIVING path (frame-incarnation-closing? body -> (and false ...)): 2 failures naming concurrent-duplicate-destroy-is-a-non-blocking-no-op and fresh-same-id-destroy-replaces-stale-marker-token-safely, captured exit 1. Restore hash-verified at b3ecad4c02 against the committed object.

NOTE: the harness reported that sabotage run as exit 0 while the captured .exit file held 1 — another instance of the reported-vs-captured discrepancy, again surfacing as a spurious zero on a deliberately-red run.

title: [docs-defect] unresolved: do h/defview boundaries emit rf:render: measures?
description:

CONSEQUENCE: a reader who turns on :closure-defines {re-frame.performance/enabled? true} (19-performance.md:106-108) to confirm a fix in production cannot predict whether their views will appear in the measures at all.

SURFACE: docs/core/hicasso/19-performance.md, and possibly docs/core/how-to/fix-a-slow-view.md:214 if that line needs a Hicasso clause.
close_reason: PR #8398. RESOLVED: yes. impl/collector.cljs:1984 wraps mint-view!'s component fn in (performance/mark-and-measure :render view-name ...) and :2036 does the same for mint-frame-prop-view! -- both view-substrate wrappers, so frame-fed boundaries are bracketed too. Entry is rf:render:<view-name> where view-name is the '<ns>/<sym>' string also stamped as displayName. Witnesses: arm1.render-measure-cljs-test (OFF) and arm1.render-measure-emit-nightly-test (ON). title: [docs-defect] published pages link outside docs_dir and 404 on the site; no gate catches it
description:
FRESH-READER DEFECT (rf2-hic-069, POLISH 19). Several published pages link into the source tree with ../../../ paths that escape mkdocs's docs_dir. Every target EXISTS in a checkout -- these are site-only breakages, not missing files -- but on the published site each is a 404, because only spec/ and migration/ are staged into the build (mkdocs.yml:9-13).

Instances found by the fresh-reader run, both ends checked:
- docs/core/hicasso/13-overlays-and-focus.md:294 -> ../../../implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/combobox_keyboard_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:259, :261 -> ../../../examples/core/{counter,todomvc}/core.cljs
- docs/core/views.md:301 -> ../../examples/core/todomvc
- docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:82, :232 -> ../../../implementation/adapters, ../../../examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter
- docs/core/how-to/{validate-with-schemas.md:145, add-auth.md:144, build-a-form.md:390} -> ../../../examples/real-apps/realworld_http

THE INTERESTING PART IS THE GATE GAP. Neither covering gate catches this class. check_doc_slugs.py resolves the target against the working tree, where it exists, so it passes. mkdocs build --strict emits at most an INFO for an unrecognised relative link and does not abort -- verified, the base commit is exit 0 with all of these present. So the class can only grow.

CONSIDER WHETHER THE GATE IS THE DELIVERABLE rather than the eight links: a check that a docs/ link resolving outside docs_dir is either staged into the build or rewritten to a GitHub URL would hold the line permanently. Weigh that against the project's stance on over-engineering -- eight links and a low blast radius may not earn a new checker. A source-located decision either way is a complete answer.

SURFACE: the listed pages, and possibly scripts/check_doc_slugs.py.
close_reason: PR #8399. The bead's nine listed instances are NOT defects -- mkdocs_hooks.py already rewrites all nine to GitHub blob URLs (verified by rendering each page through the real hook); the fresh-reader run checked both ends in the source tree, which is the right check for GitHub browsing and the wrong one for the site. The GATE GAP is real and sharper than stated: MkDocs 1.6 grades an unresolvable relative link by whether its last segment has a file extension -- with one it is links.not_found (default warn, already gated), without one it is links.unrecognized_links (default info, ships a 404). So the silent class is the DIRECTORY-SHAPED escaping link. Fixed by raising that one level in mkdocs.yml, which makes the existing 'mkdocs build --strict' step (spine docs tier + docs.yml) the permanent gate -- no new checker, refusing the standalone script as a re-implementation of MkDocs that would drift from the real build. The gate then found 4 live 404s, ZERO of them on the bead's list: spec/README.md x3 '](../examples)' and spec/SPEC-AUTHORING.md '](conformance)', all one author trap (a cross-tree directory named without a trailing slash), fixed in the rewriter rather than link by link; 506 pages rendered through both hook versions differ on exactly those 4 lines. Control: planted escaping link goes red exit 1 naming the file, and the identical build with the knob back at 'info' exits 0 -- the config line is the gate. Restores hash-verified. Excluded-target class is NOT config-gateable (MkDocs caps it at INFO in code) and is measured on rf2-75q3l; rf2-ypct8 told its two lines are clean.

title: [docs-defect] docs/api/ claims completeness and omits Hicasso; current-adapter has no Hicasso discriminator
description:

One page per public namespace.' :20 lists 'Substrate adapters | re-frame.adapter.{reagent,uix} -- first-class and permanent'. A grep for hicasso across all of docs/api/ returns ZERO matches.

title: method: the mayor's strand discriminators are weaker than the harness signal it already receives
description:
FILED AGAINST MY OWN PRACTICE, 2026-08-16 16:15 AUSEST, after making the same misjudgement THREE TIMES in one session with three different justifications. Each time the worker was alive and mid-gate, and each time a message cost it a turn for nothing.

THE THREE INSTANCES, all 2026-08-16:
  1. ~14:00 — judged worker/topodriver-w01c stranded on WORKTREE MTIME (no write for 23 min). It was alive, grepping its own spine log. A read changes no file, so mtime is a WRITE clock and silent on a reading worker.
  2. ~14:00 — same call on worker/dispersion-rs8q6, same evidence, same result.
  3. ~16:01 — judged worker/ymlparse-cb7hs stranded on a STRONGER-LOOKING signature: PR fully green at 88/0/0, worktree clean, own commit 11 minutes old, still draft. It was on ATTEMPT 3 of the fast-PR spine locally. Its PR was green because CI ran on what it had already pushed; that says nothing about what it is still doing.

WHY (3) MATTERS MORE THAN (1) AND (2). mtime is a known-weak proxy and mayor-hygiene.md already lists directory mtime among the six discredited ones — I simply used it anyway. But 'green PR plus clean tree plus draft' is NOT on that list, it reads as strong, and it is the shape the merge criterion itself teaches you to notice. It is still insufficient, and for a reason worth writing down: A GREEN ROLLUP IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE PUSHED TREE, NOT ABOUT THE WORKER. A worker that pushed early and is still iterating locally presents exactly this way, and a clean tree is what you see BETWEEN edits rather than only after the last one.

THE SIGNAL THAT HAS NEVER BEEN WRONG IS ONE I ALREADY RECEIVE FOR FREE. The harness reports each live agent by name with its current action — 'Polling gate-fastpr-ymlparse-cb7hs-3.log', 'Compiling browser-test with shadow-cljs', 'Opening draft PR #8393'. That arrives unprompted in the session and is authoritative about liveness in a way no repository artefact can be, because it observes the AGENT rather than its output. In all three instances above it was present and would have settled the question before I derived anything.

PROPOSED CORRECTION, small: mayor-hygiene.md's liveness section should name the harness's own running-agent report as the FIRST discriminator, and demote the repository-derived ones (tip revision, worktree activity, dirty tree) to what you use when it is absent — after a session clear, or for a worker dispatched by someone else. It should also add 'green PR + clean tree + still draft' to the discredited-proxy list with the reason above, because it is the most convincing of the false signatures.

NOT PROPOSED: removing the message-before-redispatch rule. Messaging remains correct and cheap; the point is that in all three cases the message was UNNECESSARY, not that it was harmful. The one time a ping did unblock something (PR #8380, ~14:10) the worker had genuinely finished and simply not marked ready — so the rule earns its keep, roughly one in four.

CONTROL WHEN IMPLEMENTING: this is a documentation change to a command file. scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci covers .claude/commands/*.md (COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC) and runs unfiltered on every PR; check_doc_slugs.py does NOT reach that directory. Plant a broken link, run it red, restore, hash-verify.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8405, implemented as proposed and split across two files along the division of labour those files already declare. mayor-hygiene.md (the liveness paragraph, which mayor-posture.md names as 'the one place that reasoning lives') now names the harness's running-agent report as the FIRST discriminator -- it observes the AGENT where every repository signal observes its OUTPUT -- and demotes tip revision, worktree activity and tree cleanliness to the fallback for when it is absent (after a /clear, or a worker someone else dispatched). Added 'green PR + clean tree + still draft' to the discredited proxies with the stated reason (a green rollup is evidence about the PUSHED TREE, not about the worker), and recorded why mtime failed in instances 1 and 2 specifically: it is a WRITE clock, silent on a worker that is only reading. mayor-posture.md's stranded sweep DID need the same correction and got the ORDERING change only, cross-referencing rather than restating. TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS: (1) the new proxy went in the liveness paragraph, NOT the six-proxy list in the reap paragraph -- that list answers 'is this worker finished' and carries an explicit 'do not add a seventh', while this bead is the separate 'is this worker alive' question; (2) the fix genuinely belongs in BOTH files, because posture step 1 already defers the reasoning to hygiene, so one-file-only would either leave the operational sweep running the derived test first or recreate the two-copies-of-one-rule drift hygiene itself records as having gone stale for two days. The message-before-redispatch rule is UNCHANGED per the bead, and the text now says it earns its keep about one time in four. CONTROL as the bead required: check_readme_links.py --ci verified at source (COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC at :390 consumed at :418; check_doc_slugs.py returns 0 matches for .claude; verify-readme-links at test.yml:815 carries no if: filter). Gate is silent on success, so the plant is the discrimination: clean=exit 0, planted broken link=exit 1 naming mayor-posture.md:28 -> mayor-hygiene-PLANTED-SABOTAGE.md, restored=exit 0. Plant genuinely applied (git hash-object 9db1909d -> a9350394) and restore byte-identical back to 9db1909d90f3ea91b46f394e4c3ba29ebc768c32. Full fast-PR spine also ran foreground to completion: captured exit 0, 74 steps, 0 failures.

title: ci: nothing validates that .github/workflows/*.yml is even well-formed YAML
description:
FOUND by the rf2-badrf/rf2-nuhru worker (PR #8389) while establishing what gates its own edit, 2026-08-16 15:34 AUSEST. Independently re-verified by me at tip bcbc0999bf.

THE FINDING. Four scripts READ .github/workflows/test.yml — check_gate_scheduling, check_fast_pr_gap, check_jvm_lane_rosters, check_ci_reproduce_commands — and every one is a hand-rolled line reader. The worker proved the consequence rather than arguing it: it planted a genuine parse break and ALL FOUR RETURNED EXIT 0 over a file PyYAML rejects. check_gate_scheduling excludes comments by design (rf2-6ckzl), so it cannot see the class at all.

AND THERE IS NO actionlint ANYWHERE. git grep -lF 'actionlint' over the tracked tree returns nothing, controlled against 'clj-kondo' which the same method does find. So no workflow-syntax validation exists at any tier.

THE FIX IS SMALL: a yaml.safe_load over .github/workflows/*.yml in the fast-PR spine. Seconds to run, a few lines to write. That is the whole proposal — NOT actionlint, NOT schema validation of the Actions grammar, NOT a new job. Anything larger is the gold-plating the stance rejects and should be refused at triage.

THE HONEST MITIGATION, stated so this can be rejected on the facts rather than dispatched reflexively: the merge criterion is already a backstop. A workflow that fails to parse does not run, so the PR's rollup comes back SHORT of the 88-row band, and clause 1 refuses it. Nothing broken reaches main by this route today. What the gap actually costs is a WASTED CYCLE — a worker pushes, waits out CI, and gets a confusing partial rollup instead of a two-second local error naming the line.

SO THIS IS A FRICTION FIX, NOT A SAFETY ONE, and it should be judged on that. Given the fast spine already exists and already runs on every workflow edit (a test.yml change is a mark_all trigger, so every tier arms), the marginal cost is close to zero and the friction saved is a full CI round-trip. I judge it worth doing; a dispatcher who disagrees should close it rather than shrink it.

CONTROL WHEN IMPLEMENTING: plant a parse break, confirm the new check goes red naming the file, restore, hash-verify. The worker above did exactly this and it is how the finding was established in the first place.
close_reason:
PR #8391 (commits ea22312262, b901aef5ae). PREMISE HELD, re-verified a third time at tip 959c34204a and controlled in both directions. `git grep -lF actionlint` returns exactly one path, .beads/issues.jsonl -- this bead's own text -- against a `clj-kondo` positive control that the same method finds in five files; `safe_load` and `import yaml` return nothing but the same tracker export. With `name: tests` -> `name: "tests` on test.yml line 1, yaml.safe_load raises "while parsing a block mapping" and check_gate_scheduling, check_fast_pr_gap, check_jvm_lane_rosters and check_ci_reproduce_commands each exit 0. Restored, hash-verified 24ca208c804b11b5095133d6f53c312e716cdf2d against the committed object.

scripts/check_workflow_yaml.py: yaml.safe_load over .github/workflows/*.yml, reporting file, line and column. Wired into the spine's ALWAYS-ON block ahead of all four hand-rolled readers -- validate the file, then let four line readers parse it. Refused exactly what the bead refused: no actionlint, no Actions-schema or grammar validation, no job wiring or needs: graph, no new CI job, no edit to .github/workflows/**.

ALWAYS-ON IS THE ONLY CORRECT PLACEMENT, and measuring it turned up something the bead did not have. A test.yml diff arms mark_all (28 surfaces), but a lint.yml-only or docs.yml-only diff arms ZERO -- it reaches the runner's `conservative fallback (unknown surface)` branch, and .github/workflows/** is on no documentation surface and no spine-self surface either. Nine of the eleven workflow files are in that class, so a tier-gated lane would have missed most of what it exists to check.

One thing beyond safe_load: PyYAML is probed, not assumed. It is not a requirements.txt entry in its own right; it arrives through mkdocs, so a checkout without the docs toolchain gets a loud NOT CHECKED plus note_skipped rather than a hard red on every local run -- the treatment mkdocs and the pinned clj-kondo already get in that file.

CONTROL: full spine with the break planted went RED naming the file -- "FAIL workflow YAML is not well-formed: .github/workflows/test.yml: line 5, column 4" -- CAPTURED_EXIT=1. Final run on the finished tree CAPTURED_EXIT=0, 83 steps, zero FAIL, every tier armed. The checker's own --self-test drives four break shapes red and keeps a valid workflow green, so a detector that stops firing reds by name.

Spine gap unchanged at 94 both sides (scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py --list, each side hash-verified against its committed blob) -- it counts required CI checks with no local lane, and this adds a local lane with no CI counterpart. PR is 88 checks, 23 pass / 65 skipping / 0 failing.

Judged worth doing rather than refused, on the bead's own framing: it is a friction fix, the marginal cost is ~0.05s in a lane that already runs, and the saving is a full CI round-trip on a rollup that comes back confusingly short rather than red.

title: method: the '## Quality gates' heading is called a contract for automated audits, and nothing automated reads it
description:
FOUND by the method-reread loop, 2026-08-16 12:48 AUSEST. This is a rule the mayor is ENFORCING whose stated justification is false, which is the exact class that loop hunts.

THE LINE. docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:592-594 reads:

  Every editing dispatch runs the project's pre-checkin gate before opening a change, and lists what ran in a
  change-body section headed **exactly** `## Quality gates` with pass and fail counts. A verbatim heading is a
  contract for automated audits.

THE MEASUREMENT. There is no such automated audit. A fixed-string search for 'Quality gates' across the tracked tree returns: this file, .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md, .beads/issues.jsonl, one Freehand design doc and two security test files whose use is unrelated prose. No script, no workflow, no audit tool. The search was controlled -- the same pattern matches inside docs/the-mayor-method/ -- so the zero is a real absence rather than a wrong pattern. There is also no merged-PR audit SCRIPT in the repo at all; those audits are agent-driven, which is consistent with the finding.

THE COST, and it is not hypothetical. Acting on that sentence, the mayor hand-edited another worker's change body before merging PR #8376 on 2026-08-16 -- its body headed the section '## Gates -- captured exit codes', which carried every required fact (captured exit codes, a table, the red proof) and simply used a different heading. Editing a worker's change body to satisfy machinery that does not exist is pure waste, and it is the kind a false justification reliably produces.

THE FIX -- correct the justification, KEEP the heading. The exact heading is still worth requiring, because a reader (mayor or merged-PR audit, both agents) can find the section without reading the whole body. What must change is the claim about who reads it and what a violation costs. Replace the third sentence with wording that (a) says the readers are the mayor and the merged-PR audits, both agents rather than machinery, (b) records that an earlier version got this wrong and names the #8376 incident, (c) gives the measurement and its control, (d) keeps 'exactly' and says why, and (e) states plainly that a non-conforming heading is a note to the worker, never a reason to edit somebody else's change body, and never a merge blocker -- the five clauses are the merge criterion and this is not among them.

SCOPE FENCE. ONE file, ONE paragraph: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:592-594. Do NOT touch the two command files that cite the heading -- they cite it correctly and a second copy of this reasoning in either is the two-copies-of-one-rule failure the reread loop exists to catch. Do not restate the correction anywhere else.

WHY IT NEEDS A WORKER RATHER THAN THE MAYOR. The mayor pre-commit hook refuses any staged change outside .beads/issues.jsonl and MEMORY.md, which is correct and was not bypassed. The fix must originate in a worker worktree.

description:
FOUND by the hygiene loop on 2026-08-16 12:44 AUSEST, and it is a rule interacting with the harness rather than a defect in either.

THE RULE. mayor-hygiene.md is emphatic and correct: reap a worktree ONLY on its owning agent's completion report, and the operational test is 'can I quote the sentence where this agent says it is done?' Six proxies were tried in one session and every one killed a live gate run. The rule is right and this bead does not propose weakening it.

THE INTERACTION. A completion report lives in the mayor session's transcript. A /clear discards it. Every worker dispatched before the clear therefore becomes permanently unreapable: its report was delivered, but no future mayor can quote it. The rule fails safe, so nothing breaks - the cost is monotone accumulation.

MEASURED THIS TICK. 14 worker worktrees existed. Exactly 3 had a quotable report, all dispatched after the clear. Of the 11 that did not, NINE hold branches that git cherry reports as fully upstream (+0): ciarm-st1x5 (+0 -1), presence-hic053 (+0 -2), w-adld3 (+0 -2), w-method9 (+0 -1), w-19usn, w-48rk3, w-prvry, w-t32wg (+0 -0 each, no commits at all). Their work is demonstrably on main and their beads are closed. They cannot be retired, and a branch checked out in a worktree cannot be deleted either, so the worktrees also pin nine local branches that would otherwise prune cleanly.

WHY NOT JUST RELAX IT. Because the nine LOOK exactly like the case the rule exists to refuse - merged PR, closed bead, clean tree, quiet directory are four of the six proxies by name. 'Their beads are closed' is a fifth in disguise: a bead closes when the PR opens, not when the agent stops, and the agent may be mid-gate on a second worktree.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT, none of them a relaxation:
(a) Persist the report OUTSIDE the transcript at the moment it arrives - the mayor appends a line (worktree, agent id, the quoted sentence, timestamp) to a tracked or ai/-local ledger as it receives each completion. A later mayor then quotes the ledger, which is the same evidence, durably held. Cheapest, and it changes no rule.
(b) Have the WORKER record its own done-sentence where it survives - a note on its bead as its last act, so the evidence lives on the object the next mayor reads anyway.
(c) Accept a bounded amnesty at session start, explicitly logged, for worktrees whose branch is +0 AND whose agent id has no resumable transcript. Weakest, and it reintroduces inference.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) or (b). (b) is attractive because it puts the evidence on the bead, but it depends on worker compliance and workers already skip steps under time pressure; (a) is entirely the mayor's own discipline. Note the ordering hazard if (a) is built: the ledger must be written when the report ARRIVES, not at reap time, or the clear has already happened.

NOT URGENT. Nothing is lost and nothing is at risk; the tree just grows. Filed so the next hygiene loop does not re-derive it from scratch, which is the third time this reasoning would have been done.
close_reason: Implemented per the bead's newest comment (MAYOR RULING 2026-08-16 13:23 AUSEST, option four): PR #8382 adds one paragraph to .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md recording worktree -> agentId at DISPATCH time in a mayor-local ai/ file, with the reap-time route that uses it (SendMessage the agent, have it restate). Reap test explicitly UNCHANGED; six-proxies paragraph untouched; scope held to ONE file (mayor-dispatch.md deliberately not edited). Premises verified at source: SendMessage response shapes present at line 6; no prior dispatch-time record (controlled zero - positive control 'queued for delivery' matched 1, then agentId/agent id/agent-id/ledger all 0 across .claude/commands/); /ai/ gitignored at .gitignore:47. Gate established by reading source rather than the brief: check_doc_slugs.py does NOT cover .claude/ (roster is docs/spec/skills/migration + tools/*/spec) and mkdocs docs_dir is docs/, so both would have been green-verifying-nothing; the real gate is check_readme_links.py's rf2-1yy75 command-file resolver, always-on in test.yml verify-readme-links. Negative control: planted a broken .md ref in the new paragraph, gate went exit 1 naming mayor-hygiene.md:8, restored and verified by git content hash equal to the committed blob 4afc48f8. Fast-PR spine exit 0 twice (74 gates pre-rebase, 72 post-rebase after #8322 landed), 0 failures.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MAYOR RULING 2026-08-16 13:23 AUSEST — DELEGATED DECISION, OPERATOR-REVERSIBLE (same footing as the rf2-1gy4e ruling; reopen if Mike overrules). A FOURTH option beats all three I filed, and it came from re-reading mayor-hygiene.md rather than from more design.

THE OPTION I MISSED. That file already names a signal it says has never lied: SendMessage's response shape — 'queued for delivery' = alive, 'had no active task; resumed from transcript' = idle. So a mayor that cannot quote a report does not need a new record of the REPORT at all; it can ask the agent and have it restate. That is evidence, live, from machinery that already exists, and it is strictly cheaper than any ledger of report text.

WHY IT DOES NOT WORK AS-IS, and this is the whole finding: messaging needs the agent id, and after a clear the id-to-worktree mapping is gone. I tried to recover it twice today by matching task-file mtimes against worktree creation times and guessed wrong both times — two of three candidate ids returned 'No transcript found'.

THE RULING. Record worktree -> agentId at DISPATCH, not at report time. One line per dispatch, written into a mayor-local file under ai/ (which is gitignored, so no repo churn and no merge surface). This is the smallest thing that closes the gap and it fixes the ordering hazard I flagged in the bead's own option (a): a report-time ledger has to survive the window between the report and the clear, whereas dispatch always precedes the report, so the record is written before the clear can ever matter.

REJECTED, with reasons: (a) mayor-side ledger of report TEXT — heavier than needed and carries the ordering hazard above; (b) worker writes its done-sentence to its bead — depends on worker compliance under time pressure, and the worktree-to-bead mapping is not 1:1 (a worker may hold several beads or, like the rf2-prvry worker, produce no PR and no bead close at all); (c) bounded amnesty on +0 branches — reintroduces exactly the inference the reap rule exists to forbid.

SCOPE FOR THE IMPLEMENTOR: ONE file, .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, because that file owns the reap decision. Do NOT restate the rule in mayor-dispatch.md — two copies of one rule is the drift the method-reread loop exists to catch, and this file has already been bitten by it once (its own superseded ls-remote sentence). The reap test itself is UNCHANGED and must not be weakened: still the agent's own report, now with a documented route to obtain one after a clear.

title: read_profile_app's c-noactivate docstring still hands on the every-commit framing audit #8328 retracted
description:
`read_profile_app.cljs`'s c-noactivate docstring hands the next write-up the
every-commit framing that audit #8328 already retracted once.

FILED BY the rf2-19usn worker (2026-08-16), which refused that bead after
establishing the real frequency at source. This is the one line that will
regenerate the same overstatement.

THE LINE. `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/read_profile_app.cljs`
:127 reads:

  rf2-19usn carries that cost where it is paid in shipping code and is
  the reason this delta is not zero.

The sentence before it (:126) is CORRECT and carefully scoped — "141 calls per
boundary commit IN THIS ARM'S OWN LOOP". The arm's `c-local` mode mints a fresh
cell every iteration, so it genuinely does run the cold path 141 times per window.

The problem is the handoff. ":126 says 141 per commit (in the arm), :127 says
shipping code pays that cost" reads as "shipping pays 141 per commit", which is
what the bead rf2-19usn description asserted and what merged-PR audit #8328 had
to retract. Shipping code does not: `collector.cljs:947` reaches `wire-cell!` only
on a cells-map MISS, `:967` only on a post-invalidation rewire, and a steady-state
commit reaches `:968` — push a reader — and stops. `observation.cljc:2160` calls
`build-node-handle!` once per `acquire!`. Both cold path; neither per commit.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG. This docstring is the instrument's own
write-up and is the source future measurement passes quote from. The every-commit
claim has now been stated, propagated to the mayor, reported to the operator more
strongly than it deserved, and retracted — all from this arm. Leaving the sentence
in place means the next reader re-derives the retracted claim from a green run.

THE FIX, roughly one sentence: scope :127 the way :126 already scopes itself —
the arm prices the per-call cost of one unpublishable hook resolution, and
shipping code pays it per NEW-OR-REWIRED cell and per observation-handle acquire,
not per commit. The per-call number the arm measures is sound and should stay; it
is only the frequency multiplier that must not travel.

FENCE. The rf2-19usn worker did not edit this: the bench lane
(`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/**`) was held by a live peer
at the time. Docstring-only change, no behaviour, no arm semantics.

title: bench: lane/rounds! charges warm-up PER ROUND, so four fifths of it warms nothing
description:
OBSERVED by rf2-h904p / rf2-6ta5r (PR #8371) while establishing why two clocks drifted by phase. Filed rather than built: it is a NEW MECHANISM in the shared lane and neither bead needed one.

THE SHAPE. 'lane/rounds!' takes {:warmup N :samples M} and spends N discarded samples per arm PER ROUND. But the ramp the guard's :phase factor exists to catch is a RUN-level ramp — ':position' is the index in the whole run precisely because 'warm-up does not restart at a round boundary' (sample-collector's own docstring). Replaying the schedule shows the consequence: the FIRST measured sample of a run has exactly N prior executions of its arm however many rounds follow, while the last third sits at 32-44 (at N=3) or 72-99 (at N=8). Round one is the only round that needs warming and it gets the same allowance as rounds two to five, which are already warm and pay N wasted mounts each anyway.

SO RAISING N IS A BLUNT LEVER: it buys pre-warm for round one at 5x its cost. rf2-h904p raised both clocks to the lane's page-mount {:warmup 8 :samples 12} on precedent (coldmount_app, p0_converge_app, p0_reagent_app all run it) and because lane.cljs's recorded step lands after the sixth execution — 8 clears it. That is sufficient and it is what the beads authorised ('more warm-up').

THE ALTERNATIVE, NOT BUILT. A run-level pre-warm before round one — 'rounds!' taking an optional :prewarm that runs the arms P times, discarded, before the first round — would target the ramp directly and let :warmup drop back to a small per-round settling allowance. Roughly six lines and one option key. It was NOT built because the stance rejects new mechanism where an existing knob suffices, and because a pre-warm that no harness had yet exercised would be a second untested thing inside the two instruments this PR was repairing.

WORTH DOING ONLY IF a future window shows round-one samples still riding a ramp at :warmup 8 — i.e. if the guard refuses on phase again with the first-third stratum dominated by round one. rf2-adld3 and the S8 re-take are the windows that would show it. Until then this is a note, not work.

Surface: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs — 'rounds!'.
close_reason: REFUSED in PR #8376 (worker/w-rig2, merged 2026-08-16T02:23:09Z) — premise HELD, mechanism deliberately NOT built, and the refusal is the deliverable. Re-derived at tip: warm-up is charged per round, the first measured sample sits at exactly warmup prior executions, and the last third at 72-99 (8/12) and 32-44 (3/6) — the bead's numbers reproduce exactly at all four arm counts, across 10 bench apps calling rounds! and 5 mount-batch! call sites. DECISIVE DELTA: the bead nominated rf2-adld3's window as the one that would show the trigger. That window has since landed (bead filed 09:45, window landed 10:49 the same morning) and the arm-order guard returned reportable on every arm, by predecessor AND by phase, in all three runs, with the null inside +/-7.9% of 1.0 over fifteen rounds. The trigger did not fire; the existing knob sufficed, so a :prewarm would be new shared-lane mechanism bought with no evidence — the over-engineering the stance rejects. What landed is the refusal written into rounds!'s docstring, naming the charge, the ramp, the unbuilt :prewarm and the trigger that would warrant building it. Redispatch only if that trigger is observed.

title: test.yml's arming rationale for hicasso-guide-samples cites measurements that are all stale
description:
FOUND BY rf2-vz6dg's second repair (PR #8351) while checking whether that change invalidated anything downstream. NOT FIXED THERE: .github/workflows/* is hot-zone, and a worker editing it mid-flight buys a merge conflict for a comment.

THE FINDING. The comment block above the hicasso-guide-samples job in .github/workflows/test.yml (around L1176) explains why the job carries no if: gate. Its reasoning is sound and worth keeping. Its MEASUREMENTS are all wrong, and it says of them 'measured at the script, not assumed':

  claim                                    actual (2026-08-16)
  GUIDE_DIR L121                           L242 (was L207 before #8351)
  SOURCE_ROOTS L128-131                    L249-252 (was L214-217)
  '25 guide pages'                         29
  '188 fenced blocks'                      217
  '34 hicasso verb use-sites'              104

Every one of these except the line numbers was ALREADY stale before #8351 — that PR left pages, blocks and use-sites untouched at 29/217/104 and moved only the two line references, by adding to the module docstring.

WHY IT MATTERS, mildly. The conclusion the comment reaches — that the guide tree arms nothing, so the job must be unconditional — is still true and is the thing a reader needs. The numbers are decoration that has rotted, and the phrase 'measured at the script, not assumed' is what turns rotted decoration into a false claim: a reader who trusts it and jumps to L121 lands in the middle of the divergence ledger.

REPAIR SHAPE. Either refresh the five figures, or drop the line references and counts and keep the argument, which is the half that does not rot. The second is probably right: nothing downstream needs the block count, and a comment that cannot go stale is worth more than one that is accurate today. Not worth a gate.

FENCE. .github/workflows/test.yml only. Hot-zone — sequence it, do not parallel it with another workflow-touching bead.
close_reason: PR #8389. Premise held, and the bead's own 'actual' column still holds at tip — the worry that #8322 had moved the figures again did not bite (it deleted no guide page and no fenced block). Re-derived every one rather than copying: GUIDE_DIR L242 (claim L121), SOURCE_ROOTS L249-252 (claim L128-131), 29 guide pages via git ls-files (claim 25), 217 fenced blocks via git grep of fence delimiters, 434/2 (claim 188), 104 verb use-sites from the live run (claim 34). Found and fixed a SIXTH stale figure not on the bead and in the same block: the classifier probe returns 28 outputs now, not 'ALL THIRTY-TWO' — #8322 removed four with the ui surface. Applied the mayor's ruling: dropped the four counts and both line references, naming the two input families by symbol instead (a symbol survives an edit above it; this pair had already moved twice), and restated the probe as 'every one of its outputs' so a job deletion cannot move it. The arming argument — guide tree arms nothing, so the job must be unconditional — is untouched. Kept ONE number and said why in the PR: the 0.31s/0.61s timings, the only figure that carries the argument rather than decorating it (cost is why the job can be unconditional), still true in magnitude (0.171s/0.251s measured here) and machine-dependent rather than the rotting class. MAYOR 2026-08-16 03:28 AUSEST — CLUSTERED WITH rf2-nuhru, AND RULED: THE REMEDY IS TO STOP CITING THE NUMBER, NOT TO UPDATE IT.

THE RULING. rf2-nuhru's own note already prefers 'drop the number and say each rule in turn so it stops needing maintenance', and this bead is that preference's proof: four numbers, all stale, all stale BEFORE the PR that noticed them. A comment that cites a count the code can change without the comment noticing is a comment that will be wrong again, and this is the second bead in one night filed against exactly that.

Do NOT cite a line number for GUIDE_DIR; it has moved twice already and a symbol name is stable where a line is not.
KEEP the load-bearing sentence in both. The point of these comments is to tell a reader how much the green tick proves, and that claim survives fine without arithmetic in it. If a number genuinely cannot be dropped without weakening the claim, say which and why rather than restoring it silently.
