title: Hicasso test kit tells an already top-level opaque prop to hoist to its own site
description:
FOUND while auditing merged PR #8337. That PR correctly fixes rf2-dr0ad's exact owner: an unforced delay in boundary props now borrows the runtime's specific id and recovery. Its source and parity-table explanation deliberately leave this separate generic-arm defect unendorsed.

`opaque-prop` reports every other non-data value with `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` and recovery `:hoist-it-to-its-own-site`. That advice is meaningful when `path` is non-empty: move a nested opaque value out to a legitimate site. It has no exit when `path` is empty, because the value is already the complete value of key `k`—already at its own top-level prop/attribute site. The pre-existing `[:div {:data-x #js {"a" 1}}]` parity row has exactly this shape; so does a realized delay in a boundary's props. A programmer following the named recovery can only write the same failing form again.

This is not a request for a new validator or exhaustive diagnostic taxonomy. Make the existing generic refusal's recovery honest at the one distinction the walk already knows. For a top-level opaque value, point to a real exit appropriate to the contract (for example assert the runtime-compatible form at L3, hand a function at a legitimate opaque site, or replace it with EDN); retain `:hoist-it-to-its-own-site` where a nested path makes hoisting possible. Preserve PR #8337's specific unforced-delay crossing branch.

ACCEPTANCE: pin recovery, not merely id, for at least one top-level host-object/prop witness and a nested non-data control; prove the top-level instruction changes while nested hoisting remains; keep the repair local to the existing walk and complaint vocabulary unless the vocabulary genuinely lacks an honest answer.
close_reason:
PR 8348 merged as 478a0128ae. Five clauses verified at head 432f0fff2e8f: 100 contexts, 55 SUCCESS plus 45 SKIPPED, no non-terminal, no new job keys. RE-CLOSED at 04:35 after the first close evaporated without leaving a reason.

The worker overturned this bead's own predicate and was right to. The bead frames the split as empty path against non-empty path; checked at source that test is wrong in BOTH directions. Non-data leaves path empty at two NESTED positions, a set or seq member and a map key, so the parity table's oldest nested row already carried a non-empty path and a literal seq-path implementation would have STRIPPED correct advice from it. And a nested host object has a non-empty path with still no exit. The real predicate is fn?: a function is the one non-data value with a site of its own, recorded by 004B's opaque marker. Everything else meets the identical refusal at a new site, so hoisting is a loop wherever it sits.

The code was wrong, not the spec. Spec 009's row only rosters the kit's recovery keywords. While making that sentence true the worker found the row was also omitting pass-the-tree-the-node-came-from, corrected in the same clause, cell count unchanged at 8.

RED proof: planting the pre-fix recovery back gave test:cljs exit 1 with exactly the three no-site rows failing while the two hoist rows stayed green, so the rows test the split rather than a keyword. Restored, sha256 identical.

CORRECTION TO MY BRIEF, which reaches past this bead: I said test:hicasso-invariants gates a recovery change on this id. It does not. That id is one of 3 corpus-owned spellings rowed in the main catalogue rather than the Hicasso section, proved by planting a bogus recovery at the emit site and watching the catalogue still exit 0. The parity table is the only gate that notices.

Gates: test:cljs 0, test:hicasso-invariants 0, check_doc_slugs 0, check-no-hardcoded-paths 0.

MAYOR RULING 2026-08-16 03:20 AUSEST — FROZEN-OR-CORRECTED IS DECIDED, AND IT SPLITS ON THE KIND OF TEXT, NOT THE DIRECTORY.

The sweep half landed as e37b1a971d: the five authoring.md sites, authoring-report-slice.md:51 and authoring-report-todo.md:109 all now teach h/event, and the worker correctly left the historical records alone. What it deferred is this bead's stated deliverable — whether the dated design records are corrected or frozen — so that is what this note decides.

title: bench(hicasso): direct_return_clock_app's control is aggregate + overlap, on legs that clear the quantum
description:
RAISED by rf2-egdaq's worker (PR #8333), which installed lane/control-verdict-strict for amp_merge_clock_app and did NOT widen into this one.

direct_return_clock_app.cljs (rf2-5yn9, S8 published at 0.770x) has the IDENTICAL control shape amp-merge had before this change:

    ctl (lane/control-verdict
          (* 2.0 (:p50 (get abs :hiccup)))
          (let [s (get abs :ctl-2x)] {:min (:min s) :max (:max s) :mean (:p50 s)})
          control-slack)

Two defects, the same two the audit of PR #8326 found on amp-merge:

1. It adjudicates on OVERLAP. The 2026-07-31 ruling on rf2-egdaq keeps the overlap rule only for legs sitting on Chrome's 100 us performance.now() clamp, and names a batched window clear of the quantum as its own revisit trigger. Whoever takes this must FIRST check at source whether this instrument's legs clear the quantum (amp-merge reads ~4 ms judged / ~8 ms control, forty to eighty quanta clear; this one's absolutes are not checked here). If they do not, the overlap rule is correct for it and the right deliverable is a REFUSAL saying so.
2. It adjudicates on CROSS-ROUND AGGREGATES — a prediction built from the across-round p50 against the across-round range of the control — which never puts a round beside its own denominator. lane/control-verdict-strict takes (:per-round (lane/ratio-between ratios :ctl-2x :hiccup)) against a 2.00x prediction instead.

NOT DONE HERE DELIBERATELY. S8's figure is published, and tightening the adjudication of a published row is a ruling rather than a refactor — exactly the ground the 2026-07-31 ruling covers. And its per-round control values are not retained either (record! stores only summarise's n/min/max/p50), so a re-adjudication of the published run is not possible from what was kept; only a future run under the new rule can answer it.

Files: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/direct_return_clock_app.cljs. Rule: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane.cljs (control-verdict-strict).
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8340. The bead's precondition was checked at source FIRST: S8's published control predicted 4.500 = 2.0 x the judged p50, so the legs read ~2.25 ms judged / ~4.3 ms control — twenty to forty-three of Chrome's 100 us quanta clear, the batched-window case the 2026-07-31 ruling named as its own revisit trigger. So the fix, not a refusal.

direct_return_clock_app now calls lane/control-verdict-strict on (:per-round (lane/ratio-between ratios :ctl-2x :hiccup)) against 2.00x, and records :per-round for the control. lane.cljs untouched.

RED proof: a new assertion, the-aggregate-rule-cannot-even-ask-the-question, drives one five-round dataset through both shapes. The old shape passes it by CONTAINMENT (control range 4.40-4.60 ms inside a [3.375-5.625] band), so this is NOT the overlap-vs-containment difference the existing test already pins — round 4's judged leg ran fast (1.50 ms) and its ratio is 3.00x its OWN denominator, which the cross-round prediction never looks at. Strict names it and refuses.

DURABILITY: not recoverable here either. record! parks what the caller hands it and the caller handed summarise's n/min/max/p50 per arm; run.cjs persists nothing; no dataset file exists for this instrument. budgets.md 4 had read run 1's control as passing 'the strict every-round-inside rule' — that is every-round containment against an ACROSS-ROUND denominator, not what control-verdict-strict asks. The page now says so and claims no strict verdict for either run. 0.7418x untouched (an escape figure, not a control one).

title: MEASURE: apportion the :& spelling's 2.4 us between call site, helper and codec (rf2-pqyxz follow-on)
description:

WHAT THAT FIGURE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SAY. It prices the AUTHORING CHANGE WHOLE — the caller map each call site builds, the 'dissoc' the helper performs on it, and the codec's 'merge-caller'. That is the right denominator for HD-023's ergonomic claim, because ':&' without a wrapper to forward into is not a spelling anybody writes. But it apportions nothing, and the three have very different standing: the first two are the AUTHOR'S code and an author can change them, while 'merge-caller' is the CODEC'S and only this programme can. A reader deciding whether 2.4 us is a price worth paying needs to know which.

Nor does it isolate HD-023(c")'s shorthand fold, which rides the same measurement — the witness's title field routes its class through ':&' — and whose own line in decisions.md now says exactly that rather than claiming 'unmeasured'.

THE WORK. Add arms to implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/amp_merge_clock_app.cljs that separate the three: a helper arm taking explicit args and writing no ':&' (call-site map plus helper call, no merge), and a no-dissoc arm. Keep the existing five arms untouched so the published figure is not re-derived — this is a decomposition beside it, not a replacement. The NULL arm stays and remains the resolution.

title: hicasso test kit gives its generic id for a delay in a boundary's props
description:
FOUND BY rf2-tsdik while measuring the parity table's new row. NOT FIXED:
this is a ruling about which id L2 owes, not the coverage question that
bead held, and freezing today's answer into the parity table would read as
an endorsement of it.

THE MEASUREMENT, run through the parity file's own two probes
(implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/test_kit_runtime_parity_cljs_test.cljs,
`runtime-kind` and `kit-outcome`), on a `(h/defview a-boundary [props] ...)`:

  form                          runtime                    kit
  [:div (delay [:p])]           [:foreign #object[Delay]]  deferred-read-at-boundary
                                                           :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body
  [a-boundary {:x (delay 1)}]   [:refused                  :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed
                                 deferred-read-at-boundary  :hoist-it-to-its-own-site
                                 :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body]
  [:div {:data-x (delay 1)}]    [:element "div"]           :rf.error/ui-tree-malformed
                                                           :hoist-it-to-its-own-site

THE FINDING is the middle row. For the ONE form the runtime actually
refuses -- an unforced `delay` reachable from a boundary's props, which is
what `codec/realize-deep` guards and what the id is literally named for --
the kit answers its own generic `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed` with
`:hoist-it-to-its-own-site`. The runtime answers
`:rf.error/hicasso-deferred-read-at-boundary` with
`:hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body`.

So the kit gives strictly vaguer advice than the runtime at exactly the
crossing the refusal exists for, while it DOES borrow the runtime's id for
the child spelling the runtime does not refuse at all. That is the same
class as rf2-llps1 -- the kit answering with its own generic where the
runtime has a specific -- with the two cases the other way round.

WHY NO GATE SEES IT. R10 of check_complaint_catalogue.py reconciles a
raised recovery against its Spec 009 row, and `:hoist-it-to-its-own-site`
is correctly rowed for `:rf.error/ui-tree-malformed`; a right recovery for
the wrong id is invisible to it. That is the limit R10's own header states.

THE RULING NEEDED. Either L2's tree grammar legitimately owns a
props-position non-data value (in which case say so on the kit's `:foreign`
arm, and the parity table should carry the divergence with a `:why` that
justifies it, as the opacity rows do), or the kit should test `delay?`
before the malformed arm in the props path exactly as it does in the child
path. The second is a few lines in
implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs and would
make the middle row a SHARED row of the parity table -- both sides
refusing with one id, one recovery, which is the strongest shape that
table has.
notes:
REPAIRED, not refused — PR #8337.

The bead was filed as a ruling ('pinning today's answer into the parity table would read as endorsement'). Two things found at source say the ruling was already made and the kit was simply out of step with it:

1. Spec 009's row for :rf.error/hicasso-deferred-read-at-boundary states its trigger as 'An UNFORCED delay was reachable from a boundary's props' — the position, in those words — with recovery :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body. The same document's kit-surface section already records the kit as raising this id 'for the condition rather than a kit-private twin, per rf2-hic-020'.

2. The advice the kit gave had no exit. :hoist-it-to-its-own-site tells an author to move the value to a prop site of its own, and in the measured form [a-boundary {:x (delay 1)}] the delay was ALREADY at its own site. Pointing back at what was just written is the rf2-llps1 fault verbatim — not merely a different id but the wrong instruction — which makes this a defect rather than a choice.

The bead's option (a) could not be the answer: L2 does not OWN a props-position non-data value, it refuses one too. Both sides refuse the same form, so there was no divergence for a :why to justify, only a choice of words. The middle row is now a SHARED row, which the bead itself named as the strongest shape the table has.

CHANGE: opaque-prop takes the SITE. :crossing (a boundary's props) borrows the runtime's id and recovery for an UNFORCED delay and names the offending key and path; :attr (native attributes and handlers) keeps the generic id, because realize-deep never walks them and the runtime refuses nothing there — measured, the runtime answers [:element "div"] for [:div {:data-x (delay 1)}]. realized? is carried across from the runtime's guard, so a delay the author already deref'd still gets the honest generic refusal.

Parity table gains two rows: the shared refusal and its realized-delay control. Both sabotaged one at a time and each red the row it is about; restores hash-verified.

No spec or catalogue change — the id/recovery pair was already rowed and already raised by the kit's child arm.

NOT DONE, deliberately: :hoist-it-to-its-own-site is odd advice for ANY non-data value already at its own top-level prop site (the pre-existing #js host-object row has the same shape). Separate finding about the generic arm's wording, outside this bead; the control row asserts the id ALONE rather than pinning a recovery the table has no business endorsing.
close_reason: Closed

title: hicasso test-kit runtime-parity table has no row for the unforced delay
description:
The parity table in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/test_kit_runtime_parity_cljs_test.cljs carries a row for every other member of the runtime-refuses-it class -- `[:>]`, `[:> nil]`, `[:> :div]`, the empty vector, the `true` child -- and NO row for an unforced `delay` at a boundary crossing.

That gap is why rf2-llps1 survived to be caught by a document gate (R10 of check_complaint_catalogue.py) rather than by a test. The kit answered `:assert-it-at-l3` for `:rf.error/hicasso-deferred-read-at-boundary` -- the runtime's id with the kit's own opacity recovery -- and the only existing test over that path (test_kit_cljs_test.cljs, 'raw-react-is-opaque-at-l2') asserts the `:rf.error/id` ALONE, so it stayed green throughout.

THE ROW. Modelled on the existing `true-child` row, which is the precedent for a runtime-owned id the KIT raises (so no `:where` assertion -- `:where` is asserted only on the rows the runtime itself raises through codec/vector-kind):

  {:case    "an unforced `delay` carries the runtime's id AND its recovery"
   :form    [:div (delay [:p])]
   :runtime [:refused :rf.error/hicasso-deferred-read-at-boundary
             :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body]
   :refuses {:rf.error/id :rf.error/hicasso-deferred-read-at-boundary
             :recovery    :hand-a-function-or-deref-it-in-this-body}
   :why     "...opacity is honest only where the runtime CAN read the form; it refuses this one, so :assert-it-at-l3 pointed at a tier where the identical refusal waits (rf2-llps1)."}

Check the `:runtime` arm's shape against how that table drives the runtime side for a props-position value -- the delay must reach a BOUNDARY's props for codec/realize-deep to refuse it, which may need a boundary in the form rather than a plain `:div`.

- ONE-WAY HISTORY. Since publication ae77d063e9 (2026-08-09), 42 reviewed, CI-gated commits amended the tree copies (18 on specification.md, 11 on decision-brief.md, 28 on lanes/**; 16 distinct files), while all fifteen ai/ sources still hash byte-identical (sha256) to the README's publication manifest — zero source edits. - REPUBLICATION WOULD REVERT OPERATOR LAW. ai/findings/hicasso-next-steps/synth-codex.md:158 still reads "Explicit prevention is uniform rather than special-cased for submit. h/handler has one meaning everywhere" — both halves superseded (the rf2-j6fn auto-prevent ruling, written into specification.md 4.1 and lanes/ergonomics-api.md at 5250dc87b5 and cited by facade-freeze.md 4 as settled; and the operator-ruled h/handler -> h/event rename). h/handler survives at 5 source sites (2 in synth-codex.md, 3 in codex/ergonomics-api.md — rf2-4f5s9's counts, re-verified). Publication rewrote relative links (rf2-lo5r, e626e833c9: ../synth-codex.md -> ../specification.md etc.), so source and copy can never be byte-identical in either direction; republication is an unscripted manual copy-plus-transform (no script exists anywhere in scripts/), and "reconciled" can never be verified mechanically. WORKER STEP — this bead is now dispatchable implementation; no operator hold remains on it. Rewrite the Refresh-contract section of docs/design/hicasso/product/README.md once:

Ordinary corrections (typos, link fixes) need no ceremony.

Note docs/design/** is outside mkdocs strict build; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py covers link targets/anchors — verify anchors and any table column counts by hand and say so in the PR body.

OPERATOR STEP — Mike, local, ~5 minutes, not a worker's: archive or mark retired the fifteen mirrored files under ai/findings/hicasso-next-steps/ (the normative mirrors only — lesson reports, fable/, and future exploratory drafts remain useful non-normative source material). Cheap preflight per Codex before archiving: confirm no newer operator-only copy exists on another machine; this checkout's sources are all still at publication hash.

DEPENDENTS DISSOLVED. rf2-4f5s9 and rf2-0qpu are closed with this ruling: both fire on "the next republication", and republication is abolished — the tree copies already carry the correct text (h/event, the five ruling-citing amendments, the rf2-j6fn alignment), so nothing needs reconciling anywhere. Interim-vs-permanent custody does not revive them: the eventual relocation (rf2-ps7ia) is an ordinary tracked git move landed by PR, not a republication from retired sources. The audit residue previously stranded on "files no worker may touch" (rf2-h3tke, the published-copy remainder of rf2-0fd3b) is unstranded: those files are now ordinary bead-worked surfaces.

REJECTED, AND WHY:
- Option (b), reconcile the tree back into the ai/ sources: unverifiable (link rewrites preclude mechanical comparison), recurring (observed amendment rate 42 commits in six days), and operator-only labour on exactly the scarcest resource. With rf2-0qpu's standing-exception variant it becomes guaranteed-lossy in-place editing PLUS a doomed mirror — the worst of both worlds.

CODEX RECOMMENDATION: weighed. title: hicasso: nothing reconciles the runtime's :recovery argument against its Spec 009 row
description:
Found and DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN by rf2-hic-068's R9, which names it as its own blind spot in the gate header rather than pretending to cover it.

THE GAP. Two gates read Hicasso's diagnostic ids and neither reads the recovery beside them:
check_complaint_catalogue.py reconciles ids (R1/R2/R6) and scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py reconciles :rf.error/* ids. rf2-hic-068 added R9, which reconciles the guide's troubleshooting index against Spec 009's recovery cell -- but that is DOCUMENT to DOCUMENT. Nothing compares what the RUNTIME passes as :recovery against what Spec 009 rows for that id.

WHY IT MATTERS, with the evidence already in hand. rf2-15bqc is exactly this failure: four :recovery keywords went on spelling the callback form 'h-fn' after rf2-hic-066 renamed it to h/event, and survived three attempts, BECAUSE the emitter and the Spec 009 row agreed with each other. Every gate was green. The complaints register says so in its own words: 'a recovery keyword that disagreed with what the runtime raises would be silent untracked drift rather than a red build.'

R9 CLOSES ONE HALF ONLY. After rf2-hic-068, a page that keeps a spelling Spec 009 has moved on from reds. A runtime that keeps one still does not.

WHAT IT TAKES. Parse the :recovery ARGUMENT out of each emit site and compare to Spec 009's recovery cell. Two shapes, both real: the positional (fail! <id> <where> <reason> <recovery> <payload>) -- where <reason> is usually a multi-line (str ...) with balanced parens -- and hand-built refusal maps carrying :recovery directly (see test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/codec.cljs). At least one site computes it conditionally: (if (fn? head) :call-it-or-make-it-a-view :supply-a-valid-hiccup-head), so the answer for an id can be a SET rather than one keyword. check_complaint_catalogue.py's mask() already removes strings and comments, which is most of the way to a paren-balanced argument scan.

MEASURED ALTERNATIVE, REJECTED AT rf2-hic-068. A cheaper arm was tested: require every recovery token the guide shows to occur as a plain-keyword literal in the package emit surface. On the tree at the time that was 75/76 clean, the single exception being :rf.error/no-frame-context's :supply-frame, which is corpus-owned and emitted outside implementation/hicasso. It was left out because it buys a partial anchor at the price of a hand-maintained exemption list, and the stance rejects that accretion. Recorded so the next attempt does not re-derive it.

SCOPE NOTE. This is a real gap, not a nag. If the parse turns out to need per-site exemptions to stay green, that is evidence the rule is not worth its keep -- say so and close. A source-located refusal is an acceptable outcome.

The close reason justifies only the constructor definition forwarding its id parameter, but the code drops every such call. A focused fixture reproduced the false green: start with one readable fail! site for :rf.error/example / :known-recovery, then add a sibling site calling fail! with (choose-id x) and literal :unknown-recovery. title: [template] tools/template scaffolds only :reagent and :uix — a new project cannot choose the native substrate
description:
FOUND IN PASSING BY rf2-5czki's phase-1 survey (2026-08-15). Adjacent to "complete hicasso" rather than to "get story right", and small.

tools/template scaffolds a new re-frame2 app and asks the user which substrate they want. Its answer set is two:

  tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:27-35
    (def ^:private substrate-registry
      {:reagent {:label "Reagent" :badge-url ...}
       :uix     {:label "UIx"     :badge-url ...}})
    (def ^:private valid-substrates (set (keys substrate-registry)))

`coerce-substrate` (hooks.clj:37-72) rejects anything outside that set with `:rf.error/template-substrate-must-be-one-of`. So a programmer scaffolding a new project CANNOT choose the native substrate — the same inversion rf2-5czki names for Story, in the surface a user meets first.

DO NOT ASSUME THIS IS SIMPLY MISSING. Two things need establishing before any code:
 1. Hicasso ships no adapter and rides UIx (`rg ':kind :rf.adapter' implementation/hicasso` is empty; both hicasso testbeds boot `(rf/init! uix-adapter/adapter)`). So a `:hicasso` template variant is a `:uix` adapter boot plus Hicasso authoring — establish what actually differs in the emitted app before deciding it is a third variant rather than a flag on the UIx one.
 2. hooks.clj already carries substrate-conditional logic that would need a third arm — :269 and :283 gate Story and SSR inclusion on `(not= substrate :reagent)`, and :307-362 branch Xray wiring, index.html host slots and README text on `:uix`. Read those before costing it. The `(not= substrate :reagent)` shape in particular is a two-value idiom that a third value silently changes the meaning of.

GATE: the template's emitted-app smoke is nightly, not PR — .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml:331-397, job `template-emitted-app`, working-directory tools/template. Budget for a slow feedback loop. tools/template/spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md and API.md both enumerate the valid set and would need updating in the same PR.

FENCE: tools/template/**. .github/workflows/* is HOT ZONE — only touch it if the gate genuinely needs a new arm, and sequence it if so.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED AS THE IDIOM-ONLY DELIVERABLE (PR #8334). No :hicasso variant added.

GROUND 1 RE-VERIFIED AND STILL MOOT, BUT ITS FACTS HAVE MOVED. rf2-gra70 has
MERGED since the last note: release.yml now carries a deploy-hicasso stage
(grep -c hicasso .github/workflows/release.yml == 28, not the 0 that note
recorded), so the release WIRING exists. What does not exist is a release --
git ls-remote --tags origin returns nothing. Independently corroborated from
the emitted side: every scaffold, including :reagent, emits
day8/re-frame2 {:mvn/version "0.0.1.alpha"}, a coordinate Clojars has never
seen, which is why the nightly emitted-app job rewrites coords to local roots.
The trigger remains the first v* tag.

GROUND 2 WAS REAL AND WORSE THAN "AN IDIOM THAT NEEDS CARE" -- it was a live
fail-OPEN. The file carried TWO spellings of the same Xray question:
:xray-npm-deps asked (= substrate :reagent) while every sibling {{xray-*}}
value asked uix? == (= substrate :uix). Those agree only at cardinality two.
Proven by injecting a third registry value BEFORE changing anything: the
emitted project got the Xray preload, the [data-rf-xray-host] slot, the host
CSS and a README promising the panel, while :xray-npm-deps emitted EMPTY --
so its first `shadow-cljs watch app` dies on a missing JS dependency, the
exact failure the :xray-npm-deps comment already records being bitten by
(rf2-b16va). The (not= substrate :reagent) Story/SSR guards were the SAFE
half (they fail closed); their defect was prose only -- "UIx variants follow"
is wrong text for any refused substrate that is not UIx.

FIX: :xray? / :story? / :ssr? are DECLARED per substrate in substrate-registry
and read through one `capability` accessor that THROWS on an undeclared key
rather than reading a missing key as false. No default arm remains for a new
substrate to fall through. Refusal prose derives its supported set from the
registry.

THE BEAD'S QUESTION 2 ANSWERED ON EVIDENCE -- AND IT IS "VARIANT", NOT "FLAG",
CONTRARY TO THE EARLIER NOTE'S LEAN. The per-substrate transform emits exactly
three files and a Hicasso variant would change ALL THREE: deps.edn gains
day8/re-frame2-hicasso while KEEPING day8/re-frame2-uix (the adapter is still
UIx's); core.cljs swaps uix-dom/render-root + frame-root for explicit
rf/make-frame + h/mount! (verified against
implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:878-884); views.cljs
is rewritten in the h/defview model. That is a variant's worth of divergence.
RECORDED IN THE SPEC, NOT ACTED ON -- it is blocked on publication regardless,
and whether :substrate is even the right axis still wants a ruling.

SPEC AUDIT DEBT FROM THIS BEAD'S OWN NOTE, DISCHARGED: 001-Substrate-Variants.md's
false "release.yml publishes twelve coords" is corrected to thirteen (core +
eleven deploy-leaf values + ssr-ring in its own job), with the twelve
artefact: rows named as the non-core leaves. re-frame.ui NOT added to the roster.

EMITTED OUTPUT PROVABLY UNCHANGED: scaffolded six variants (reagent,
reagent+tailwind, reagent+story, reagent+ssr, uix, uix+tailwind) from the
pre-change hooks.clj and the post-change one and diffed the trees --
118 files, byte-identical, diff exit 0. So the nightly template-emitted-app
job has no new input to exercise.

GATES: tools/template `clojure -M:test` exit 0 (64 tests / 677 assertions /
0 failures). check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh exit 0.
Both gates verified to read the worktree by planting a fault: re-planting the
original bug turned the suite red at exactly one assertion, and breaking the
new anchor turned the slug gate red. CI on #8334: 15 pass, 4 pending
surface-detection, 0 fail.
Merged-PR audit #8334 (landed 765a16740f0ebd3bf2e643fc6e02bf2a401617b6, merged 2026-08-15T15:35:20Z) reopened this exact owner for the still-undelivered native scaffold.

Completeness: the PR fully resolves Ground 2. Xray, Story and SSR are declared capabilities; the former mixed Xray dependency/wiring state is unrepresentable for a declared substrate; refusal prose derives the supported set; current Reagent/UIx output remains unchanged. But Ground 1 and this Bead's title remain true: a new project still cannot choose Hicasso. The PR establishes that Hicasso needs a real third variant, then closes the only owner because no v* tag has published its coordinate. That publication is a dispatch precondition, not evidence the product gap is complete, and no separate exact owner was found. Keep this owner alive until the first release makes the variant implementable (or an explicit product ruling retires it); do not emit an unresolvable scaffold before then.

Correctness: source inspection confirms every live Xray substitution branches on the single declared value, Story/SSR selection fails closed, and the focused landed suite passes 64 tests / 677 assertions. All 28 executed PR checks passed and diff-check is clean.

Implementation quality: the three booleans, one accessor, supported-set derivation and hypothetical-third-substrate tests are a small, coherent repair. No second Bead or broader variant framework is warranted.

Ground 2 is untouched and is still genuine feature work: hooks.clj's (not= substrate :reagent) is a two-value idiom whose meaning a third value silently changes (:269, :283), and :307-362 branch Xray wiring / index.html host slots / README text on :uix. Also unchanged: Hicasso ships no adapter and rides UIx, so establish what actually differs in the emitted app before deciding it is a third variant rather than a flag on the UIx one.

title: [xray] mount.cljs's substrate refusal roster is stale — it names freehand (being removed) and never names hicasso, which rides :rf.adapter/uix
description:
THE SECONDARY FINDING rf2-5czki ASKED TO BE VERIFIED AT SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Filed separately, as that bead directed, because it is an Xray finding and not part of the Story plan.

THE PREMISE HELD, AND THE WORRY DID NOT. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs (1,421 lines) names helix, reagent, reagent-slim, uix, ui and freehand, and contains ZERO hicasso mentions — while tools/xray/src carries nine hicasso-aware files including five dedicated panels (`rg -il hicasso tools/xray/src`, cross-checked with `grep -rli`, both 9).

BUT IT IS NOT A CORRECTNESS GAP. mount.cljs mounts XRAY'S OWN CHROME into the host page, not the inspected app (ns docstring :2-8). Its load-bearing datum is the refusal set at mount.cljs:203-220:

  (def ^:private react-element-render-kinds
    "Adapter :kinds whose :render slot takes substrate-native React ELEMENTS
     (the shared React-hook spine), not hiccup — Xray's hiccup shell cannot
     mount through them (rf2-qgfo4) ..."
    #{:rf.adapter/ui :rf.adapter/uix :rf.adapter/helix :rf.adapter/freehand})

Hicasso SHIPS NO ADAPTER — `rg ':kind :rf.adapter' implementation/hicasso` is empty, `rg '\(def adapter' implementation/hicasso/src` is empty, and there is no `:rf.adapter/hicasso` string anywhere in docs/ spec/ tools/ examples/ testbeds/. A Hicasso host installs the UIx adapter (implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:880 and hicasso_hmr_testbed/core.cljs:456 both `(rf/init! uix-adapter/adapter)`), per the EP-0038 addendum of 2026-07-31: "Hicasso is a React adapter". `:rf.adapter/uix` is ALREADY in the refusal set, so a Hicasso host refuses the inline mount correctly today, for the right structural reason, by accident of inheritance.

SO WHAT IS WRONG IS THE ROSTER, NOT THE BEHAVIOUR — and it is wrong in both directions at once:
 - It still carries `:rf.adapter/freehand`, whose own docstring says that substrate "is being removed (rf2-0yp7w)".
 - It never names the substrate that REPLACED Freehand. Nothing in mount.cljs, and nothing in tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:472-475 — which repeats the same stale roster verbatim ("UIx / Helix / Freehand") — tells a reader that a Hicasso host presents as `:rf.adapter/uix` and is therefore already handled.

A reader of this file today learns the wrong thing about which substrates Xray's shell can mount on. That is the whole defect: one sentence of missing provenance and one stale entry.

WHAT TO DO — small, and resist making it larger:
 - Say in mount.cljs:203-220 that a Hicasso host presents as `:rf.adapter/uix` and is covered by that entry, with the same "defensive footing" phrasing the file already uses for helix and freehand.
 - Correct the roster in tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:472-475 to match.
 - The `:rf.adapter/freehand` entry travels with rf2-0yp7w; do NOT remove it here unless that epic's tree deletion has already landed.

COORDINATE: a `retire-survey` worker is planning work that will touch tools/xray/src. Read its beads before dispatching this — the freehand half of the roster is squarely in the retirement's path and should not be edited twice.

FENCE: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs and tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md. THE STANDING XRAY RULE APPLIES — every dispatch touching tools/xray updates tools/xray/spec/* in the SAME PR, which this one does by construction. GATE: `clojure -M:test` from tools/xray.
close_reason: Duplicate of earlier exact owner rf2-wtznc. Both concern react-element-render-kinds omitting Hicasso; this bead supplied the decisive source result that Hicasso hosts ride :rf.adapter/uix and runtime behaviour is already correct. That evidence and the two-file documentation scope were folded into rf2-wtznc.

title: [xray] document that Hicasso hosts ride :rf.adapter/uix; retire stale roster prose with Freehand
description:
FOUND WHILE SURVEYING rf2-0yp7w, 2026-08-15. This is an XRAY HEALTH question, not retirement work — the retirement needs no change here.

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:220` holds

    (def ^:private react-element-render-kinds
      #{:rf.adapter/ui :rf.adapter/uix :rf.adapter/helix :rf.adapter/freehand})

That is a LIVE SET the mount path reads, not a comment: `refuse-unsupported-substrate!` consults it against `(current-adapter)` and publishes the `:unsupported-substrate` diagnostic when the installed adapter's `:render` takes React ELEMENTS, because Xray's shell is hiccup.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n 'rf\.adapter/hicasso' .` — zero hits, whole tree.
2. `rg -n 'rf\.adapter/' implementation/hicasso/src` — zero hits.
3. Read `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:203-240` — `react-element-render-kinds` and `refuse-unsupported-substrate!`, which consults it.

Observed: the refusal set names two RETIRING substrates (`:rf.adapter/ui`, `:rf.adapter/freehand`), one REMOVED one (`:rf.adapter/helix`, gone at S7/W13, rf2-d6epb), and no hicasso kind — because none exists anywhere in the tree.

Expected: on the substrate becoming re-frame2 native, the mount decision is made by a mechanism this survey could locate. It could not.

## What needs no action

`:rf.adapter/freehand` and `:rf.adapter/helix` are both on a deliberate DEFENSIVE footing and the docstring already says so, already names rf2-0yp7w, and already records that Xray no longer reads a Freehand host at all (rf2-l86mm). `docs/design/hicasso/product/tool-consumer-census.md` reaches the same disposition — "fold into rf2-hic-062, no follow-up bead". Leave those two alone.

## The question

The set may be entirely correct: hicasso may install no adapter, in which case the `:kind` set is simply not the mechanism by which Xray decides whether it can mount on a hicasso host. But then something ELSE is that mechanism, and this survey did not find it. Separate the two possibilities explicitly:

(a) hicasso hosts an adapter-less runtime, Xray's mount decision on a hicasso page is made somewhere else, and this set needs only its dead members trimmed once the retirement lands; or

(b) a hicasso page presents some adapter kind this set does not name, and Xray would attempt a hiccup mount through an element-shaped `:render` — the exact uncaught React child error the refusal exists to turn into a diagnostic.

Establish which, then act. Mike has separately asked to get Xray right, which is why this is filed rather than folded into rf2-0yp7w.
acceptance_criteria: A source-located answer to whether a hicasso host can reach Xray's mount path, and by what mechanism Xray decides. If (b), the set or the decision is fixed and a test pins it. If (a), say so on the bead and close — a source-located refusal is an acceptable deliverable.
notes:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. rg -n 'rf\.adapter/hicasso' . 2>/dev/null    # => zero hits, whole tree
2. rg -n 'rf\.adapter/' implementation/hicasso/src    # => zero hits
3. Read tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:203-240 — react-element-render-kinds and refuse-unsupported-substrate!, which consults it against (current-adapter).

Observed: the refusal set names :rf.adapter/ui and :rf.adapter/freehand (both retiring) and :rf.adapter/helix (removed at S7/W13, rf2-d6epb), and names no hicasso kind because none exists.
Expected: the mount decision on a hicasso host is made by a mechanism this survey could locate. It could not.
Merged-PR audit #8301 — duplicate collapse and source resolution. rf2-f0ajt independently reached this exact Xray roster finding 103 seconds after this earlier owner. Its source work resolves this bead's question: Hicasso ships no adapter of its own; both Hicasso testbeds initialise uix-adapter/adapter, so a Hicasso host presents as :rf.adapter/uix, which react-element-render-kinds already refuses. Runtime behaviour is correct. The remaining work is deliberately small: document that Hicasso provenance beside the set in mount.cljs, align tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md, and let :rf.adapter/freehand leave with rf2-0yp7w rather than removing it early. rf2-f0ajt is closed as the later duplicate; its rf2-5czki discovery lineage and exact evidence are preserved here.
close_reason:
PR #8310. ANSWERED (a), THEN FIXED THE REASONING RATHER THAN THE BEHAVIOUR.

The bead asked to separate two possibilities and establish which. It is (a), with a correction: hicasso does not host an adapter-less runtime — it installs the UIx adapter and mounts boundaries through it. Both testbeds: (rf/init! uix-adapter/adapter) then (h/mount! ...). So current-adapter returns :rf.adapter/uix on a Hicasso page, :rf.adapter/uix is ALREADY in react-element-render-kinds, and the refusal fires correctly today for the right structural reason — the element-shaped :render in play IS UIx's. Not (b): no unnamed kind reaches the mount path, so there is no uncaught-React-child exposure to fix.

:rf.adapter/hicasso confirmed non-existent at source: exactly ONE hit in the whole tracked tree (docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md:303) and it is prose asserting the keyword does not exist. Neither roster invents it; both express hicasso as a substrate whose React adapter is UIx.

BEHAVIOUR UNCHANGED — the repair is documentation, in three places: the mount.cljs docstring, tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:470, and tools/xray/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md's Adapter-resolution section, which 011 CITES as its authority (fixing 011 alone would have left the cited authority stale). :rf.adapter/freehand left alone per the bead — it travels with rf2-0yp7w.

ADJACENT DRIFT FIXED: both spec rosters read 'UIx / Helix / Freehand' and omitted :rf.adapter/ui, which is in the live four-member set and is element-shaped for the same reason Freehand is (spine/make-react-adapter, ui/substrate.cljs:105).

THE CLAIM IS TEST-PINNED, NOT JUST PROSE. Removing :rf.adapter/uix from the set turns mount-cljs-test/open!-on-react-element-substrate-refuses-cleanly red and nothing else (captured exit 1); intact it is green at 13927 tests / 70339 assertions, 0 failures.

GATE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: 'clojure -M:test in tools/xray' does NOT cover mount.cljs — it is a JVM runner and cannot load a .cljs file. It passed the sabotage GREEN with byte-identical counts. The lane that reaches it is npm run test:cljs (:node-test puts ../tools/xray/src + ../tools/xray/test on the build). Anyone briefing an xray .cljs change should nominate that, not the JVM alias.

title: [retire] R6 — the prose sweep: ~237 files of spec, docs, skills and source comments (needs splitting at dispatch)
description:
Largest by count, lowest by risk, and the LAST phase. 237 of the 508 referencing files are prose. THIS BEAD IS TOO BIG FOR ONE WORKER and should be split by sub-surface when dispatched — spec is ONE TOUCHER, everything else parallelises.

THE SUB-SURFACES, with counts measured 2026-08-15 (rg -il --hidden over the union of 'freehand' and re-frame.ui spellings, the two trees excluded):
- docs/design/freehand/ - 37 files. **KEEP. DO NOT DELETE.** The word "Deletes." that stood here was an ERROR, ruled so by rf2-0moc4 (closed 2026-08-18) after R6b refused it; this line is that ruling's Consequence A, applied 2026-08-20 after a SECOND worker re-derived the same error from the uncorrected text. THE DECIDING REASON is the hicasso coupling: docs/design/hicasso/ carries 11 inbound links across 8 files, and deleting the tree takes scripts/check_doc_slugs.py to exit 1 with 4 broken targets, measured independently by R6b and again on 2026-08-20. docs/EP/EP-0036 cites it 17 times and asserts the tree remains. mkdocs.yml exclude_docs already hides it from the site, so keeping it costs the published docs nothing. (The ruling's point 5, 11 links from spec/004-Views.md, has lapsed because that file is deleted. Point 3 is the one that decides.)
- docs/api/*.md - 12 files. **NOT GENERATED  the word "GENERATED" that stood here was WRONG.** Established at source 2026-08-20 by the rf2-jzv5x worker: the api-manifest chain has exactly one spit, gen.clj:430, and it writes spec/api-manifest.edn  NOT these pages. doc_api_check.clj READS docs/api as a projection to VALIDATE against that manifest (scope table at :84; success line "OK: docs/api page+member coverage in sync"). So these are HAND-AUTHORED prose checked against a generated manifest, not output of it. The error propagated four hops before anyone checked it  this line, into a dispatch brief, into that worker's report, into bead rf2-jzv5x, into a second brief  and cost one dispatch. Edit them by hand like any other prose, and keep them in sync with spec/api-manifest.edn because doc_api_check.clj will red if they drift.
- skills/re-frame2-ui/ — 5 files, a whole skill dedicated to the retiring substrate. Deletes, including .claude-plugin/plugin.json and the generated references/ui-context.md. Also skills/README.md, skills/reagent-migration/* (4), skills/re-frame2-setup (2), skills/re-frame2 (2), skills/re-frame2-improver, re-frame2-implementor, re-frame2-xray, re-frame-migration.
- spec/ prose remainder — Conventions.md (the whole 'Freehand — one public namespace' section, the :rf.adapter/* row's freehand member, the :rf.ui/* and :rf.ui.compile/* and :rf.ui.evidence/* and :rf.ui.tool/* rows), 006-ReactiveSubstrate.md's adapter table row and §Adapter introspection list, API.md's rows, Ownership.md, 001, 002, 008, 011, 012, AI-Audit.md, Security.md, Privacy.md, README.md, Principles.md, Spec-Schemas.md, Tool-Pair.md, Cross-Spec-Interactions.md, the Pattern-* pages, 000-Vision.md. HOT ZONE — one toucher, sequenced.
- source comments and docstrings — ~27 lines in core/src, ~45 in core/src for re-frame.ui, 4 in ssr/src, 3 in ssr-ring/src, plus tools/xray/src (5 files), tools/story, tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp, implementation/routing/src, implementation/hicasso/src (9), implementation/adapters READMEs.
- mkdocs.yml nav; root README.md, CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, TESTING.md; docs/AUTHORING.md, docs/release-process.md, docs/skills.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1 and migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod comments.

DO NOT DELETE, and this is a judgement rather than an oversight:
- docs/EP/EP-0030 through EP-0036 (10 files) are HISTORICAL PROGRAMME RECORDS. A withdrawn programme's EP is the reason the withdrawal is legible; deleting it leaves the retirement unexplained.
- docs/design/hicasso/ (65 files) cite Freehand as the substrate hicasso replaced. That is hicasso's record, not Freehand's. Leave it. docs/design/hicasso/product/tool-consumer-census.md in particular already carries ruled dispositions for the retiring adapter ids.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs's react-element-render-kinds set — see rf2-0yp7w.10; it stays on a deliberate defensive footing.

Full survey: docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md
acceptance_criteria: Split into per-surface child beads at dispatch, with spec/ as a single sequenced toucher. Each child: no live reference to either retired tree remains on its surface, the EP and docs/design/hicasso exclusions above are respected, and python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py passes foreground with a captured exit.
notes:
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-21 00:15 AUSEST — THE SLICE-REMAINDER NOTE IS STALE AND WOULD SEND A WORKER AT WORK ALREADY DONE.

The 2026-08-18 17:42 note says "OUTSIDE THAT SLICE'S FENCE AND STILL UNFIXED: implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:5, which slice 4 handed over as its 'highest-visibility residue' ... whoever takes the next implementation-prose slice takes it."

MEASURED AT origin/main TODAY: that file carries ZERO donor hits. `git grep -cE 'freehand|re-frame\.ui' -- implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md` exits 1, and the POSITIVE CONTROL is that the same pattern still returns 247 files tree-wide with .beads excluded — so the zero is "nothing there", not "wrong pattern". Line 5 now reads as a Hicasso-alongside-the-adapter-tier sentence citing EP-0038, with no donor name in it.

REPAIRED BY `d9b666f17c`, subject "docs(readmes): stop two READMEs teaching a deleted substrate as live (rf2-0yp7w.9)" — a later slice under THIS BEAD. So the remainder was picked up by the owner the note correctly identified; only the note was never updated. `b22a0fef4c` (the 106-README GDS restyle) also touched the file afterwards.

The rest of that note stands, and it is the useful half: of 16 in-fence files carrying a donor hit, only 6 were teaching a removed surface as live; the other 10 are tombstones, schema changelogs, design-provenance ledgers or already-corrected prose. That ratio is the shape of this whole sweep and is the reason a hit count is not a work count.
MAYOR 2026-08-21 02:05 AUSEST — THE CENSUS REGEX THIS SWEEP HAS BEEN USING IS DEFECTIVE, AND IT INFLATES EVERY SLICE'S COUNT. Measured by rf2-v14sq's worker, which refused its whole slice on the strength of it.

THE DEFECT: 're-frame2-ui' MATCHES 're-frame2-uix' AS A SUBSTRING. The UIx adapter is FIRST-CLASS AND LIVE — 16 tracked files under implementation/adapters/uix/, rostered at spec/Conventions.md:1833, with its own declared coordinate. So every census run with a bare 're-frame2-ui' alternation counts live UIx references as donor residue.

MEASURED ON THE skills/ SLICE: the file count drops from TEN to FOUR when the pattern is corrected to 're-frame2-ui([^x]|$)'. SIX of the ten hits were never about the retired substrates at all — they were the live day8/re-frame2-uix coordinate in dependency tables, routing tables and a peer-naming sentence.

USE 're-frame2-ui([^x]|$)' IN EVERY REMAINING SLICE BRIEF. I wrote the bare form into rf2-v14sq's brief myself, so this correction is against my own dispatch and not against a worker.

AND THE PARENT'S ~237-FILE ESTIMATE IS SUSPECT FOR THE SAME REASON. It may be materially overstated. Re-derive it with the corrected pattern before splitting any further slice, and do not carry the 237 forward as though it were measured — it was measured, but with this pattern.

THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME LESSON, and this bead already states it in its own words: 'a hit count is not a work count'. On the corrected four-file set, ALL FOUR were correct tombstone prose — an eval-fixture note explaining a deliberate id gap, a negative guard telling an author NOT to carry a retired spelling across, a provenance ledger marking a lock RETIRED, and a 'what the skill does NOT consume' section. Zero edits were needed and the slice closed as a refusal. So the corrected pattern removes the false positives and the classification step removes most of what is left.

A FORWARD-LOOKING MEASUREMENT FOR THE spec/ SLICE, from the same worker and outside its fence: the four literal donor hits in spec/Conventions.md:104 and spec/Ownership.md:40-42 are ALSO tombstones, each saying 'removed on 2026-08-16'. The :rf.ui/* reservation is deliberately still live because re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree consumes the tree ABI. Expect the same ratio there and brief accordingly.
MAYOR 2026-08-21 03:10 AUSEST — THE REMAINING SURFACE, MEASURED WITH THE CORRECTED REGEX AND PARTITIONED. Recorded so the next split is sized honestly rather than off the stale ~237.

WHOLE-CORPUS CENSUS at origin/main with 're-frame\.(ui|freehand)|re-frame2-ui([^x]|$)|re-frame2-freehand', tracker export excluded: 88 markdown files. THAT NUMBER IS NOT A WORK COUNT and most of it is already spoken for:

  EXCLUDED BY THIS BEAD'S OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — docs/EP/** (13 files) and docs/design/hicasso/** (21). The criteria say the EP and docs/design/hicasso exclusions are respected; they are not a backlog.

  GOVERNED BY A FRESH RULING, NOT BY THIS SWEEP — docs/design/freehand/** (~25 files). rf2-72vvj's repair merged this tick and settles it: KEEP, no deletion anywhere, editing bounded to EP-0036's FOUR correction classes (stale status, broken links, factual errors, contradictions with rulings), and studio/ ABSOLUTELY FROZEN. A slice here must brief that bound, not re-derive it.

  ALREADY SWEPT BY A CLOSED CHILD — CHANGELOG.md, TESTING.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/release-process.md were rf2-0yp7w.9.2's; the three non-xray tools/*/spec hits are rf2-0yp7w.9.4's four deliberate past-tense LEFT STANDING entries; skills/** was rf2-v14sq's, closed as a full refusal with all ten classified.

  IN FLIGHT — implementation/** is rf2-5z6bb; spec/009-Instrumentation.md is worker/specmin-cluster.

  GENUINELY UNSWEPT AND NOW FILED — tools/xray/spec/** (4 files) as rf2-n9hno, dispatched this tick. rf2-0yp7w.9.4's own close reason says 'tools/xray/ untouched', so this is its fenced-off complement.

  STILL UNFILED, and it is the hard one — spec/** (10 pages: 004C, 006, 008, 011, API, Conventions, Ownership, Pattern-StatefulComponents, README, plus 009 in flight). ALL HOT ZONE, one toucher per page, so it is ONE worker taking them sequentially rather than a parallel wave. rf2-0yp7w.9.4 also stopped on spec/004-Views.md's Freehand v/ alias prose and recorded it as held on rf2-h89ri — check that bead before briefing the spec slice, and note the page has since been deleted, so verify rather than carry it.

THE RATIO STILL GOVERNS. Two slices have now closed as full or near-full refusals on this sweep, which is the measured shape rather than a run of bad luck: a hit count is not a work count.
MAYOR 2026-08-21 03:45 AUSEST — A LIMIT ON THIS SWEEP'S OWN INSTRUMENT, measured by rf2-5z6bb's worker and worth more than the slice it came out of. Filed separately as rf2-ue4kv.

SCRUBBING A NAME HIDES A LIVE DEFECT FROM THE REGEX HUNTING IT. Every slice here finds residue by grepping for a donor NAME. Where someone has already replaced the identifier with a phrase — 'the retired compiled tier' — and left the surrounding CLAIM standing, the census returns that file as clean, permanently. MAYOR 2026-08-18 — SLICE 3 CLOSED (PR #8474). ONE FINDING THAT CHANGES EVERY REMAINING SLICE, AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT A SWEEPER WOULD ASSUME.

**:rf.ui/* IS NOT A RETIRED SPELLING. IT IS LIVE SURFACE.** spec/Conventions.md:104 records that the structural render-tree ABI namespace OUTLIVED the substrate that minted it. It is the live keyword family for re-frame.ssr/emit-ui-tree and the Hicasso test kit. A sweeper who adds ':rf.ui' to a donor-residue pattern will delete or rewrite working surface, and every gate would stay green while doing it, because the spelling is legitimately everywhere.

WHAT IS RETIRED, and only these: :rf.ui.compile/* and :rf.ui.tool/*, which are struck-through RETIRED tombstone rows in the Conventions table. Note the shape — the retired names are SUB-namespaces of a live parent, so a prefix match on ':rf.ui' catches the live one and a match on the full retired names catches neither by accident. This is the third distinct prefix trap in this bead's history, after 're-frame2-ui' matching 're-frame2-uix' and 'hang' matching 'change'.

THE WORKING PATTERN IS UNCHANGED and still the one to use, with both controls run before any count is believed:

    git grep -ciIP 'freehand|re-frame\.ui(?!x)|re-frame2-ui(?!x)|implementation/(ui|freehand)/|004D'

    negative control  README.md = 0
    positive control  docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md = 64

SECOND FINDING, ABOUT WHAT A GATE-SCRIPT SWEEP COSTS AND SAVES: of 58 hits across 11 scripts, 52 WERE CORRECT AND WERE LEFT UNTOUCHED. The 6 that were residue were all present-tense claims about deleted things — a docstring teaching a failure class from the deleted jvm-freehand job, a hand-kept 'twenty-three per-artefact JVM jobs' comment against a roster that now reads 21, two comments naming a donor grep that zero workflows use, an exemption justifying itself by contrast with a workflow that does not exist, and a paragraph quoting two cells of a Conventions row that is now a struck-through tombstone. description:

    Its worktree is already gone.

VERIFIED STRANDED, NOT GHOSTS. For each I checked the tip's commit SUBJECT against origin/main and got ZERO matches, which is the test that survives a rebase-merge's hash rewrite. A ghost's subject is always locatable on main. Both are also pushed, so the work is DURABLE on origin and nothing is at risk from leaving them alone.

WHAT IS OWED: triage, not automatic revival. For each, decide whether it is (a) still wanted -- open a PR, rebase onto current main, run the gates; (b) superseded by work that landed since -- delete the branch with a reason recorded; or (c) a spike whose CONCLUSION is worth keeping while the diff is not -- promote the finding into whatever tracked record owns the surface, then delete.

READ THE DIFFS BEFORE CHOOSING. receipts-hic081 is 4 days old and its subject says 'spike', which is exactly the class where the finding outlives the code; hicasso's runtime has changed a great deal since 2026-08-11, including the h/mount! door contract landing today, so a rebase may be substantial. fontlic-trei is a one-commit docs fix about FONT REDISTRIBUTION LICENSING -- that one has a legal flavour and should not be discarded without reading it; if we are shipping a font we are not licensed to redistribute, that outranks its age.

PREMISE RE-CHECKED INDEPENDENTLY, with --state all rather than the open-only default: of 6 remote worker branches, exactly 3 have no PR in any state -- worker/fontlic-trei, worker/receipts-hic081, and worker/seam-t32wg (a live worker mid-flight, correctly not in scope). The bead's two are the right two.

=== worker/fontlic-trei -- (b) SUPERSEDED. Recommend DELETE. ===

THE FONT LICENSING PROBLEM DOES NOT EXIST ON MAIN, and the answer is not 'already fixed the way this branch proposed' but 'fixed more strongly by a different route'. Verified: git ls-tree -r origin/main matching \.(otf|ttf|woff2?|eot)$ returns NOTHING -- zero font binaries tracked anywhere. docs/assets/fonts/ does not exist on main. docs/stylesheets/fonts.css is a generic system cascade (fe3e36d511, 'use the generic system font cascade'), wired via theme.font: false + extra_css. ALREADY ADJUDICATED. rf2-trei is CLOSED on exactly this, and its close reason says so explicitly: 'Worker/fontlic-trei was dispatched at this and stood down mid-flight without opening a PR; its bead claim was released.' It also states Mike took the stronger route -- removing the class of problem rather than trading one vendored font for another -- and that it incidentally killed an unfiled second defect (PR #8103's Google Fonts CDN @import for Source Code Pro sitting next to the font: false that exists to stop exactly that).

NOTHING IS LOST. I read the branch's full diff and its LICENSE.md before recommending discard, as the bead required. Its one durable finding is ALREADY PRESERVED verbatim in rf2-trei's close reason: Routed Gothic's SIL OFL 1.1 status established four ways, decisively by the complete OFL text embedded in the .ttf name table (name ID 0) so the grant travels with the binary; the upstream sha256s (11f90db9... regular, 3fa6c2a2... italic); and the confirmation that docs/assets/fonts/ was the only non-image asset directory, so no other unlicensed binary asset exists under docs/assets/. No promotion owed.

LANDING IT NOW WOULD BE A REGRESSION: it re-adds two TTF binaries (57KB + 66KB) main deliberately does not carry and re-introduces a self-hosted font stack that fe3e36d511 deliberately replaced. Its worktree at C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/fontlic-trei is CLEAN -- HEAD == the pushed tip, nothing uncommitted, nothing unpushed -- so the worktree can be reaped with the branch.

=== worker/receipts-hic081 -- (c) CONCLUSION KEPT, and it is ALREADY PROMOTED. Recommend KEEP THE BRANCH. ===

THIS ONE IS NOT STRANDED. The hygiene loop's 'pushed, unlanded, no PR' heuristic misclassified a DELIBERATELY RETAINED spike record. rf2-hic-081 'Spike: capability receipts' is CLOSED with a full verdict, and its close reason ends: 'Spike commits are pushed on worker/receipts-hic081 and retained as the experiment's record; nothing from them lands on main.' title: hicasso: the warnings-fatal compile does NOT police cross-namespace private-var access (measured)
description:
MEASURED FINDING from rf2-34sdz (PR #8289), filed because a ruling has already relied on the belief that this gate catches it, and the next one might.

rf2-sc1dt's ruling listed as acceptance evidence: 'Warnings-fatal Hicasso compile finds no private cross-namespace use.' That gate cannot find such a use. This is not a defect introduced by rf2-34sdz -- nothing was changed in response, and rf2-34sdz's own claim was re-established by other means -- but the belief is wrong and is worth recording where the next ruling will meet it.

THE MEASUREMENT, on implementation/hicasso, via npm run test:hicasso-compile:

  plant a real cross-namespace call to the now-private
  re-frame.hicasso.server/fresh-frame-id, from a namespace the gate compiles
                                          -> exit 0, 441 files, ZERO warnings
  same plant swapped for an undeclared var (planted-server/no-such-name-xyz)
                                          -> exit 1, names the exact line
  BOTH faults on adjacent lines, .shadow-cljs/builds/hicasso-bench cleared
                                          -> EXACTLY ONE warning (:undeclared-var)

So the gate is live on the file and fails closed on a var problem; it simply does not see private access. The green run was treated as a stop rather than a pass, which is how it was found.

CAUSE, identified rather than guessed. cljs.analyzer defaults :private-var-access to TRUE (analyzer.cljc:133) and warns in the resolve* :default method when (not= current-ns full-ns) and (:private sym-ast) (analyzer.cljc:1186-1194). shadow-cljs substitutes its own resolution -- shadow.build.cljs-hacks/resolve-cljs-var and /resolve-ns-var, which merge the def AST and return, carrying NO private check. Nothing in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn disables the warning (only :redef false appears anywhere), so this is shadow's resolution path rather than repo configuration. Confirmed against shadow-cljs 2.23.3 and clojurescript 1.11.132 in this repo's .m2.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN:

  - A defn- in this codebase is a DOCUMENTED intent plus a census/roster fact.
    It is NOT compiler-enforced against other namespaces under shadow-cljs.
  - What actually catches an out-of-namespace use of a private name today is a
    grep, plus check_naming_census.py for the roster question (is the name
    PUBLIC), which is a different question from whether anything CALLS it.
  - JVM Clojure differs: there a private var access is a hard error, so .cljc
    shared code would be caught on the JVM half and not the CLJS half.

NOT PROPOSING A NEW GATE. rf2-sc1dt's adopted guardrails explicitly reject a bespoke public-surface checker, and a private-access checker is close enough to that rejection to need its own ruling rather than an inference from this one. The cheap and possibly sufficient outcome is simply that acceptance criteria stop naming the warnings-fatal compile as evidence for privacy and name the grep + census instead. Filing so the choice is made deliberately.

WITNESS: PR #8289's Quality gates section carries the full plant/restore record, including the hash-verified restore (git hash-object da484c35ff9f37f823b3b10ee400bafd4554cb2b, byte-identical).
close_reason:
CLAIM REPRODUCED, INDEPENDENTLY AND AT SOURCE. Disposition: recorded as a bd memory, no code, no doc change, no gate, no PR.

THE MEASUREMENT REPRODUCES. Fresh plant, different site from PR #8289's: a real cross-namespace call to the now-private re-frame.hicasso.server/fresh-frame-id added to re-frame.bench.hicasso.hd8-witnesses, a namespace this gate compiles. npm run test:hicasso-compile returned CAPTURED_EXIT=0, '[:hicasso-bench] Build completed. (441 files, 440 compiled, 0 warnings)'. Not a skipped file: the emitted JS carries the direct call (out/hicasso-compile-gate/cljs-runtime/re_frame.bench.hicasso.hd8_witnesses.js -- 'return re_frame.hicasso.server.fresh_frame_id'), so the compiler resolved the private var and said nothing. Plant verified by git hash-object 49cdc059 -> d94eb847 and restored byte-identical to 49cdc059, plant grep 1 -> 0, tree clean.

THE CAUSE HOLDS, BUT THE BEAD CITED THE WRONG ARTEFACTS. The description says 'Confirmed against shadow-cljs 2.23.3 and clojurescript 1.11.132 in this repo's .m2'. Those are stale jars sitting in .m2; the build actually resolves shadow-cljs 3.4.10 + clojurescript 1.12.145 (read off .shadow-cljs/classpath.edn for the run above). Re-verified in the CORRECT versions: :private-var-access defaults true at analyzer.cljc:135 and is emitted in exactly one place, (defmethod resolve* :default) at analyzer.cljc:1248-1260; shadow's install-hacks! does (replace-fn! #'ana/resolve-var shadow-resolve-var) at cljs_hacks.cljc:1273, and shadow-resolve-var resolves via resolve-fqn-sym / resolve-ns-var / resolve-cljs-var, none of which tests (:private sym-ast). resolve* is never reached. grep -n private over the whole of cljs_hacks.cljc returns only comments and alter-meta! ... dissoc :private lines. Confirmed implementation/shadow-cljs.edn carries only :redef false; nothing disables the warning.

DISPOSITION: bd remember, key shadow-cljs-does-not-police-private-var-access. Memories are injected at bd prime, so it reaches every session and every agent -- including the next author of an acceptance criterion, who does not have to know to go looking. The memory states it as a TOOLCHAIN property (every shadow-cljs compile in the repo, not one gate), names the substitution point, carries the reproduction, and says what to cite instead (a grep/corpus sweep; the census answers the different question 'is the name rostered public').

REJECTED -- a line in the document that governs how privacy is asserted: THAT DOCUMENT DOES NOT EXIST. Surveyed check_naming_census.py (enforces rostering; silent on the compiler; treats defn- as an escape hatch with no bar), naming-ledger.md (no section headings at all), naming-packet.md (has a Witness column, defines nothing about it), spec/Conventions.md facade policy (requires a justification, never says what backs it), spec/API.md:54 (taxonomy only), dispositions.md section 3 (public => row, silent on going private), TESTING.md (zero occurrences of 'warning' or 'compile'; no gate-blind-spot section anywhere). Row 50 itself asserts 'no out-of-namespace caller of either name anywhere' with NO instrument named. Writing the governing document that is missing is a new governance surface and far beyond a triage.

REJECTED -- a line in compile_gate.cjs's LIMITS section (lines 239-252). Real candidate, and the closest call: the section exists, is forward-referenced from line 30, already enumerates blind spots, and this gate genuinely compiles re-frame.hicasso.server (it is in the optional-module roster at check_optional_module_reachability.py:332). Rejected because the blind spot is NOT this gate's -- it is shadow-cljs's, shared by test:cljs, browser-test, the freehand sibling gate, check-examples-compile.cjs and every release build. Recording it in one gate's LIMITS localises a toolchain-wide fact and implies by omission that the other five compiles do police it. A memory states it at the scope it actually has, and costs no PR, no merge slot and no fence. If some future PR is already editing compile_gate.cjs, a one-line cross-reference there is welcome as a free rider -- it does not earn a PR of its own, and no bead is filed for it.

REJECTED -- nothing at all. The bead is searchable, but the audience is people writing acceptance criteria who do not know this bead exists. bd prime injection is the difference.

NOT PROPOSED, per rf2-sc1dt's adopted guardrails and the project stance: no checker, no lint rule, no CI job, no nag diagnostic.

NO RESIDUAL RISK TODAY: of 51 open beads, the only one whose description mentions 'warnings-fatal' is this one, so no live ruling currently rests on the false belief. The exposure was prospective, which is what the memory closes.

No diff produced, no PR opened.

title: server module: privatise fresh-frame-id + setup-events, keep document/payload-script/render-twice (row 50 override, ruling on rf2-sc1dt)
description:
RULING TO IMPLEMENT (Option B of rf2-sc1dt, decided 2026-08-15 under Mike's delegated decision authority; operator-reversible). The sitting's Operator-override pass on naming-ledger row 50 ("keep all five server helpers as shipped" — an applied census default, never argued name-by-name) is OVERRIDDEN as follows:

- `fresh-frame-id` and `setup-events` -> PRIVATE.
- `payload-script`, `document`, `render-twice` -> CONFIRMED KEEP (now as an actual ruling, not a census default).

Module public surface after this change: exactly four names — `render`, `payload-script`, `document`, `render-twice`.

WHY (distilled from the rf2-sc1dt dossier + Codex review, both of which independently recommended this split):

- The dividing line is evidence, not taste: each survivor has a concrete thing an external host does with it that `render`'s returns alone cannot do; the two going private have none.
- `payload-script`: a host that mutates the payload and re-pr-str's it must re-wrap it, and the tag must stay byte-identical to `re-frame.ssr.ring.shell/payload-script-tag` — the id is the client bootstrap's getElementById contract and the body goes through the EDN-aware escaper that fails loud on a `</script` breakout. Public is what stops a host hand-writing the tag and getting the escaping wrong.
- `document`: a host post-processing `:html` (e.g. a CSP nonce) must rebuild the envelope; by hand that means re-spelling `escape-html`/`escape-attr`. architecture-census.md: "the one string of HTML in this package that is not React's".
- `render-twice`: nondeterminism is a host-authored bug class (a view reading `Date.now`, a random id) and this is the ready-made host-side CI diagnostic, with `:differs-at` making a red run diagnosable. Zero incidental cost (double work only when called). It cannot move to a test kit without dragging `react-dom/server` into the kit's dependency graph — its only sane home is beside `render`.
- `fresh-frame-id`: structurally indefensible as public — `render` always mints its own id, installs it over `:frame-opts` (docstring: `:id` "cannot be overridden"), and destroys the frame before returning, so NO public path consumes this function's return value. The current docstring's claim that it lets "a host assemble a non-standard shell" is false for this name: shell assembly needs `document`/`payload-script` plus `render`'s returns, never a frame id, and rebuilding the pipeline is impossible from public parts anyway (`impl.mount/tree` and `impl.roots/open-adoption-window!` are impl namespaces).
- `setup-events`: entirely derivable — a three-line cond-> over `:rf/set-db` plus ordinary events that `render` already accepts directly as `:snapshot` and `:initial-events`. Near-zero external value; public names for either of these two invite callers to couple to choreography `render` deliberately owns.
- Provenance: all five arrived together with the server entry (30317bfe0e), after the same shapes existed in the benchmark entry (9214396f73); none has consumer-driven provenance.

VERIFIED BLAST RADIUS (dossier + Codex both swept, incl. qualified/string/resolution-style spellings):

title: [bug] the stranded sweep's step 3 prescribes REDISPATCH, which is impossible when the strand was caused by quota exhaustion
description:
FOUND BY the mayor's method-reread loop, 2026-08-15 08:55 AUSEST, step 2 — checking an enforced rule against what the tree actually does. LIVED THROUGH IT ninety minutes earlier rather than reasoning about it.

WHAT HAPPENED. Two background workers terminated simultaneously with: 'Agent terminated early due to an API error: You've hit your weekly limit · resets Aug 20, 11am (Australia/Sydney)'. worker/rename-hic066 (rf2-hic-066, the mechanical rename sweep) and worker/ciarm-st1x5 (rf2-st1x5 + rf2-bo8lq).

WHY THE EXISTING RULE ALMOST COVERS IT. .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md's stranded sweep step 3 reads: 'Only when there is no live task AND no movement in the tip: push whatever commits the branch already carries — pure durability — then bd update <id> --status open with a note saying what was found and what was salvaged, and redispatch.' A quota death presents EXACTLY as that condition: no live task, no tip movement. So the discrimination is right and the SALVAGE half is right — I followed it and it worked. worker/ciarm-st1x5 had an unpushed commit; pushing the branch made rf2-st1x5's naming-census gate durable, and its four uncommitted files (the epoch prod-gate work for rf2-bo8lq) were correctly LEFT ALONE under the standing rule that only the worker knows whether its working tree forms a coherent change.

THE GAP IS THE LAST TWO WORDS: 'and redispatch'. Under quota exhaustion redispatch CANNOT SUCCEED — every Agent call fails identically until the reset. A mayor following step 3 mechanically burns attempts discovering that, and each failed attempt is itself a call.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE ERROR TEXT, AND IT IS UNAMBIGUOUS. A quota death names a limit and a reset time. That is categorically different from a crash, a harness timeout, or a worker that detached a gate and ended its turn — the last being the COMMONEST strand, recovered by SendMessage, and the one step 2 already handles. Read the termination reason before choosing a remedy.

THE FIX: one clause on step 3. Say that when the termination reason names a quota or rate limit, the salvage half still applies IN FULL — push the branch, record what was salvaged, note the uncommitted work as the worker's — but redispatch is unavailable until the stated reset, so the bead is left open with the reason and the reset time recorded, and the mayor stops dispatching rather than retrying. Add that MERGING is unaffected: an open PR that reaches green can still be merged, which is how rf2-hic-066 landed (#8278) after its worker had already died.

DO NOT ADD MACHINERY. No quota probe, no retry-with-backoff, no scheduler change. One clause.

DO NOT put it in docs/the-mayor-method/. That layer names no host, tool or vendor by construction, and 'weekly limit' is a fact about one provider's plan. The README's Warnings section already carries the generic form ('This is not free. You will spend tokens, a lot of them'). If a reader judges the generic layer needs the PRINCIPLE — a remedy that depends on a resource the failure itself has exhausted is not a remedy — say so with reasoning and keep it free of vendor names, and run a leak check over the added lines.

WHY THE MAYOR DID NOT JUST EDIT IT: the mayor checkout's pre-commit hook refuses commits to worker-tracked surfaces, which is the hook working as docs/the-mayor-method/README.md predicts. AND IT CANNOT BE DISPATCHED RIGHT NOW FOR THE VERY REASON IT DOCUMENTS — quota resets 2026-08-20 11:00 Australia/Sydney. This bead is written to be dispatched cold at that point.
close_reason: PR #8280. One clause on mayor-posture.md step 3: when the termination reason names a quota or rate limit, the salvage half applies in full but redispatch is unavailable until the stated reset, so the bead stays open with the reason and reset recorded and the mayor STOPS dispatching rather than retrying. Records that MERGING is unaffected (gh pr merge spends no agent quota; #8278 merged after its author died, unblocking seven beads), so the order is salvage, merge everything green, then stop. Discriminator is the error TEXT, distinguished from a crash, a harness timeout and step 2's detached-gate strand. Generic layer WAS edited (one vendor-free sentence in loops.md step 3, which carried the identical 'and redispatch' defect): a remedy that draws on the resource whose exhaustion caused the failure is not a remedy. The README's 'not free / you will spend tokens' is about cost, not remedy availability, so it did not cover the case. Leak check over the added lines: clean. No machinery added.

title: hic: h/mount! is a contract, not a rename — root! takes no :initial-events (naming row 13)
description:
**Filed by rf2-hic-066.** Naming-ledger row 13 rules `root!` -> `mount!` (Mike, 2026-08-11). rf2-hic-066 STOPPED on that half: it is not a mechanical rename, and the packet's own "rename two constructors" is false for this one when read at source.

## Measured at source, 2026-08-15

The guide teaches `h/mount!` as `(node config view)` with a config map carrying `:frame` AND `:initial-events`:

```clojure
(h/mount! (js/document.getElementById "app")
          {:frame          :rf/default
           :initial-events [[:counter/initialise]]}
          [counter])
```

(`docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md`, and again in `glossary.md`: *"associates a DOM container, a frame, optional `:initial-events`, and one root view … Initial events run in order before first paint."*)

Shipped `impl.mount/root!` is `(container frame-kw hiccup opts)` — frame keyword POSITIONAL, and `opts` carries exactly one key, `:identifier-prefix`. **`:initial-events` is implemented nowhere in `impl.mount`.** `re-frame.hicasso.server` has its own `:initial-events` handling for the SSR pipeline; the client root has none.

So renaming the var alone publishes `h/mount!` against six taught call sites it cannot serve — a green CLJS compile and a runtime failure, which is exactly the shape a rename sweep must not ship.

## What this bead owes

1. `:initial-events` on the client root — ordinary events, in order, before first paint. This is the new behaviour.
2. The `(node config view)` adaptation, which has a precedent to copy exactly: `h/hydrate!` is a `defn` rather than an alias for this reason, and its docstring says so. Row 20 keeps the config map as taught.
3. Rename the door `root!` -> `mount!`, and move facade-inventory row HS-10 with it.

`impl.mount/root!` may keep its own name: `hydrate!` already aliases `impl.mount/hydrate-root!` and that asymmetry is documented on the door.

Guarded on frame/frame-incarnation-token, because re-make-frame-ing a live id is idempotent REPLACEMENT and would have silently refreshed the creator's config.
