title: [bug] clause 5 treats any .github/workflows change as a matrix change; a STEP added to an existing job is not one
description:
FOUND BY the mayor's method-reread loop, 2026-08-15 01:56 AUSEST, step 2 (check the rules you are ENFORCING against what the tree does). This is a rule the mayor has been applying correctly ALL SESSION with a refinement that is NOT WRITTEN DOWN — so the next mayor either re-derives it or pays for not having it.

WHAT CLAUSE 5 SAYS. '.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md' clause 5: 'when a merge changes the workflow matrix (a new required job, a changed classifier, a re-scoped path filter), the PRs behind it whose surface that change covers do NOT inherit its verdict: gh pr update-branch them and re-check'.

THE GAP. The parenthetical enumerates three KINDS of matrix change, but the operational test a mayor actually runs is 'did .github/workflows/* change since this PR's merge base?' — and that test returns TRUE for a change that moves nothing. A STEP added to an EXISTING job changes the file without changing the CHECK SET: no new row appears in any PR's rollup, so no PR behind it is measuring a superseded matrix, and update-branch buys nothing while restarting CI for everything.

MEASURED TODAY, TWICE, BOTH TIMES BY THIS EXACT SHAPE:
  #8256 (rf2-n4a2b) added a fifth per-namespace step to jvm-repo-source-walks. workflows-since-base read 1 for #8259 and #8260. Neither needed updating; both merged at the then-current band.
  #8270 (rf2-6ng7) added two more steps to the same lane. workflows-since-base read 1 for #8274. It merged at 98 — the band did NOT move, and the band worker had explicitly PREDICTED it would ('if #8270 lands, 98 goes stale again'). That prediction was wrong for exactly this reason, and the prediction is on PR #8273's body where the next re-measurer will read it.

THE TEST THE MAYOR HAS BEEN USING, and it is one command:

  git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -cE '^\+[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:$'

Zero new top-level job keys means the check SET is unchanged, so clause 5 is satisfied without update-branch. Non-zero means a new job — re-check properly. It correctly cleared three PRs this tick (#8270, #8271, #8272) and #8274 the tick after.

THE FIX: one clause in clause 5, after the parenthetical. Say that the operational question is whether the check SET moved, not whether the FILE moved; that a step added to an existing job changes neither the rollup nor any PR's coverage; and give the job-key test as the discriminator. Keep it to that.

WHICH DIRECTION THIS FAILS, because it decides the priority. Getting it wrong costs UNNECESSARY CI RESTARTS, not a bad merge — clause 5's real danger (a PR inheriting a verdict from a superseded matrix) is unaffected. That is why this is P3 and not P2. But at an 11-minute merge cadence with six workers, update-branch on every PR behind every workflows commit is real waste, and clause 5's own text says a burst is precisely when the base will not hold still.

DO NOT ADD MACHINERY. No script, no gate. One clause and one command, consistent with rf2-6ng7's standing (c)-narrow ruling for this class.

DO NOT put this in docs/the-mayor-method/. The generic layer names no tool, flag or path by construction, and this refinement is a fact about one CI host's check model. If you judge the generic layer needs the PRINCIPLE (a fence-style 'ask whether the thing you gate on actually moved'), say so with reasoning and keep it free of tool names — two workers today ran leak checks over added generic lines to keep that tree clean.

WHY THE MAYOR DID NOT JUST EDIT IT: the mayor checkout's pre-commit hook refuses commits to worker-tracked surfaces, which is the hook working as docs/the-mayor-method/README.md predicts.
close_reason: PR #8280. The dispatched premise was stale: the corrected two-space regex had already landed via #8276/47b3f5a563, verified (366e4fca79 reads 1 indented, 0 unindented). Acted on the reopening COMMENT instead. Clause 5 no longer claims a job-key zero clears the check set: zero is necessary and not sufficient, and on zero the mayor must read the intervening diff and confirm it is step-only. Probes: the regex matches '+  browser:' but not a matrix arm, a widened glob, a name: change, or a new classifier output; test.yml gates ~30 jobs on detect_changed_surfaces, so a widened glob flips SKIPPED->executed under an unchanged name and clause 1's band does not move. Generic layer NOT edited: loops.md:184-195 already carries the principle ('the count alone gives opposite verdicts for the same number ... you only know by reading') and the command file had regressed against it.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: Post-merge audit of PR #8276 (47b3f5a563195a5338518d8b3da8ff273b2c51ec, merged 2026-08-14T16:11:43Z): REOPENED the exact owner. The two-space regex correctly detects newly added job keys, but the landed clause makes the stronger and false claim that zero matches means the check set is unchanged and clause 5 is satisfied. Clause 5's own preceding sentence names changed classifiers and re-scoped path filters: either can turn an existing row from SKIPPED into required execution without adding any job key, so a trailing PR can carry the same check names and still have stale coverage. An existing job's strategy.matrix can also add check rows without a new job key; this repository contains matrix jobs. Direct probes: the regex matches '+  browser:' but not '+          - webkit', a classifier widening line, or a job display-name change. The 20-commit validation used job-key-set differences as its ground truth, so it proves job-key detection, not the stated check-set/coverage equivalence. Keep the useful step-only exemption, but make it conditional on inspecting that the intervening workflow diff is actually step-only (or otherwise discriminate classifier/path/matrix/name changes); job-key count zero cannot by itself clear clause 5. No new script or broad machinery is required.

title: hic: arm check_naming_census.py — npm chain, unconditional job, and the required-checks pin
description:
rf2-hxbhe landed implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_naming_census.py as a runnable, self-proving gate but did NOT wire it: .github/workflows/* is hot zone and the dispatch brief fenced it out. The gate is green today (105 public names across 10 shipped namespaces, 0 unrostered, exit 0) and its --self-test carries a seeded positive control, so nothing is broken -- but nothing re-runs it either. Until this lands, dispositions.md section 3's constraint (adding a public surface adds an id) is checked on ten namespaces only by whoever remembers.

THREE EDITS, and the third is the one that is easy to forget.

(1) THE NPM CHAIN. implementation/package.json's test:hicasso-invariants already chains seven checkers as `--self-test && live` pairs. Append the same pair:
    python hicasso/scripts/check_naming_census.py --self-test && python hicasso/scripts/check_naming_census.py "$PWD/.."
NOTE THE ARGUMENT. Every other checker in that chain derives its own root; this one REFUSES to, by design (rf2-hxbhe: a script deriving its root from its invocation path can walk a sibling worktree and report that as the census). The chain runs with cwd = implementation/, so the repo root is one level up. Whoever wires this must confirm the spelling actually resolves on both POSIX and Windows rather than assuming -- the gate exits 2 on a relative path, which is a loud failure, so a wrong spelling cannot pass silently.

(2) THE UNCONDITIONAL JOB. The chain's only hosted invocation is a step of the `cljs` job under needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.cljs_node_test == 'true'. That arms on implementation/hicasso/*, which is the direction that matters most -- THE ESCAPE HAPPENS WHEN A NAMESPACE GROWS. But this gate reads a second input family that arms nothing:

    implementation/hicasso/src/**, test_kit/src/**   the ten namespaces  -> arms cljs_node_test
    docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md     the ledger         -> arms NOTHING

docs/** measures false at every classifier output, so a PR deleting a ledger row would run this gate NOWHERE and next redden on somebody else's source PR, over a row they did not write. That is exactly the shape hicasso-complaint-catalogue, hicasso-budget-ledger, hicasso-facade-inventory and hicasso-guide-samples were each split out to repair. Add a fifth sibling, hicasso-naming-census, modelled on hicasso-facade-inventory at test.yml:1146 -- self-test step first, then the live run, sub-second pure Python, nothing to gate for.

(3) THE REQUIRED-CHECKS PIN, per rf2-6ng7. That bead's finding is that an arming census which excuses a false arm by NAMING an unconditional lane needs that lane's contents pinned, or the excuse outlives the coverage. The pin in this workflow is the all-required-passed job's needs: list (test.yml ~6660), which already names hicasso-complaint-catalogue, hicasso-budget-ledger, hicasso-facade-inventory and hicasso-guide-samples. hicasso-naming-census MUST be added there in the same PR. A job that exists but is not needed by all-required-passed runs and gates nothing, which is a comment claiming coverage over a lane that has none.

NAMING IS ALREADY COMPLIANT, and here is the constraint so it is not rediscovered. scripts/check_ci_reproduce_commands.py audits the AGGREGATED repo-invariant job (verify-skill-mcp-drift), where a checker step is one whose inline run: is `python scripts/check_*.py` or which carries a check_* id; it measured exit 0 / 43 checker steps in sync at rf2-hxbhe. This gate lives in implementation/hicasso/scripts/ and gets its own job, exactly like hicasso-facade-inventory, so it sits OUTSIDE that audit's scope and no id is required. IF anyone later moves it into the aggregated job, its id must be check_naming_census for the live step and check_naming_census_selftest for the --self-test step -- that guard asserts an id ends in _selftest IFF the real run: carries --self-test.

ALSO REPOINT: docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-packet.md section 7 currently ends with a paragraph saying the gate is not yet wired and naming this bead. Delete or amend that paragraph when this lands.

ACCEPTANCE: test:hicasso-invariants runs the census self-test and live pair green with a correctly-resolving absolute root; hicasso-naming-census exists as an unconditional job and is listed in all-required-passed's needs:; check_ci_reproduce_commands.py still exits 0; naming-packet.md section 7's not-wired paragraph is gone.

SEQUENCING: .github/workflows/test.yml and implementation/package.json are shared surfaces -- sequence this against other workflow beads rather than running it in parallel with one.
notes:
VERIFIED AGAINST LANDED MAIN — mayor, 2026-08-15 13:14 AUSEST, after merging PR #8279. TWO OF THREE EDITS LANDED. The bead STAYS OPEN for the third.

CONTEXT: this commit was written by a worker killed mid-session by an API quota limit. It never reported, so no author-side gate evidence exists and CI was the entire gate. The mayor pushed the orphaned branch for durability, opened #8279 with that provenance stated, and merged it green at 99/99. This note is the verification that #8279's own body said was still owed.

EDIT 2 — THE UNCONDITIONAL JOB: LANDED. .github/workflows/test.yml:1278 'hicasso-naming-census', name 'Hicasso naming census (rf2-st1x5)'. VERIFIED GENUINELY UNCONDITIONAL: zero 'if:' keys between the job header and its steps. It runs the script's --self-test as well as the live check.

EDIT 3 — THE all-required-passed PIN: LANDED. test.yml:6820 carries '- hicasso-naming-census' and the owning job is all-required-passed, which starts at line 6770 — confirmed by walking back to the nearest top-level job key rather than eyeballing indentation. EDIT 1 — THE NPM CHAIN: NOT LANDED. grep for 'naming-census' in implementation/package.json and the repo-root package.json returns ZERO. The job invokes the script directly via 'run: python implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_naming_census.py', so there is no npm entry point at all.

WHY THE MISSING THIRD IS NOT COSMETIC, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING PART. scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py DERIVES THE REQUIRED-CHECK SET FROM AGGREGATOR needs:. Edit 3 just put this job in that set. So the gap tool will now report 'Hicasso naming census' as a required CI check WITH NO LOCAL LANE — a real reported gap, created by landing edit 3 without edit 1. Before the pin it was invisible to the tool; now it is a line in every gap listing.

Note the shape: the two edits that landed are the two that make the gate BITE, and the one missing is the one that makes it RUNNABLE LOCALLY. WHAT REMAINS, precisely: add an npm script that invokes implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_naming_census.py (and plausibly its --self-test), so the required check has a local counterpart. ## Acceptance

Each of the three rows carries either `closed` with the section, the base commit, what was executed
and the captured exit code written into its evidence cell, or `resolved` with the failure recorded
and a fresh corrective bead named.

title: naming row 50: three of the server module's five helpers have a weaker case than 'keep' — standing input for the sitting
description:
STANDING INPUT FOR THE NAMING SITTING, not a repair and not a request to dispatch. Filed by rf2-52xpx (PR #8266) because both documents the sitting reads -- naming-ledger.md and naming-packet.md -- were live on other workers (worker/cites-c0agr, worker/naming-hic065) when this was measured, so a bead is the only place it can be recorded without racing them.

ROW 50 IS AN APPLIED DEFAULT FROM rf2-hic-065'S COMPLETENESS CENSUS, one of rows 47-54, and the ledger header is explicit about what that means: of the 60 public names the census found carrying no row, 'all 60 read *keep* -- the cheap version of that failure'. It is not an operator ruling (those are rows 1, 13, 18, 24, 31) and it was not argued name-by-name. rf2-52xpx REFUSED to overturn it from a worker seat, correctly: the ledger says the sitting overrides asynchronously and rf2-hic-066 re-runs the sweep as a diff. This bead carries the per-helper reading to that sitting.

TWO OF THE FIVE EARN PUBLIC ON THEIR OWN, independently of row 50's blanket:

- server/payload-script -- a host that mutates the payload and re-pr-str's it must re-wrap it, and the tag must stay byte-identical to re-frame.ssr.ring.shell/payload-script-tag: the id is the client bootstrap's getElementById contract and the body goes through the framework's EDN-aware escaper, which fails loud on a </script breakout. Public here is what stops a host hand-writing the tag and getting the escaping wrong.
- server/document -- a host post-processing :html (a CSP nonce, say) has to rebuild the envelope, and by hand that means re-spelling escape-html/escape-attr. architecture-census.md already records it as 'one string of HTML in this package is not React's'.

THREE HAVE A WEAKER CASE, and the third is the one worth the sitting's time:

- server/render-twice -- squarely a test affordance, and it doubles render cost. Row 50 defends it as 'the determinism check run where the renderer is rather than trusted to a docstring', which is a good reason for it to EXIST and a thinner one for it to be shipped API.
- server/setup-events -- a three-line cond-> over two framework doors (:rf/set-db plus ordinary events) that render already accepts directly as :snapshot and :initial-events. Entirely derivable; near-zero value to an external caller.
- server/fresh-frame-id -- THE SHARPEST, because it is structural rather than a matter of taste. render mints its own id, and its own docstring says of :frame-opts that ':id and :initial-events are this module's and cannot be overridden'. So there is NO PUBLIC PATH THAT CONSUMES THIS FUNCTION'S RETURN VALUE: a caller can obtain the keyword and can do nothing with it through this module's surface. Whatever the sitting decides about the other four, this one is public without a caller.

NOTE THE COUPLING BEFORE MOVING IT. rf2-fn62g's bundle-side sentinel is the string fresh-frame-id mints, (keyword "hicasso.ssr" ...), and check_bundle_isolation.cjs's premise check pins the literal '(keyword "hicasso.ssr"' in server.cljs. Making fresh-frame-id PRIVATE does not disturb that -- the sentinel is about reachability from render, which is unchanged. RENAMING the keyword namespace would break the premise check, loudly and by design, and that file is the second place to edit.

The bead's own description (rf2-52xpx) argued the same direction from a different premise -- 'render already returns the useful intermediate values, so callers do not need lifecycle/test mechanics merely to customize their HTTP shell' -- which is right about payload-script and document being returned by render, and does not reach the case where a host modifies them.
close_reason: Sitting-override ruling recorded 2026-08-15 (delegated decision, operator-reversible): Option B — fresh-frame-id and setup-events go private; document, payload-script, render-twice confirmed keep. Both the dossier analysis and the Codex recommendation were weighed and agreed. Implementation filed as rf2-34sdz (self-contained: defn- edits, docstring roster rewrite six->four, ledger row 50 override entry + packet mirror, sentinel warning, acceptance evidence). Full rationale and rejected options in the closing comment on this bead.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DECISION (2026-08-15, delegated by Mike to a decision worker; recorded as delegated and operator-reversible). Acting as the sitting's Operator-override pass on naming-ledger row 50, the ruling is OPTION B of the dossier:

- `fresh-frame-id` and `setup-events` -> PRIVATE (`defn-`).
- `document`, `payload-script`, `render-twice` -> confirmed KEEP, now as an actual ruling rather than a census default.
- Module public surface becomes exactly four names: `render`, `payload-script`, `document`, `render-twice`.

BASIS. Both the original dossier analysis and the appended Codex Recommendation were weighed; they independently recommended the same split, and the evidence line is clean: every surviving public name has a concrete thing an external host does with it that `render`'s returns alone cannot do (envelope reassembly with the framework's pinned payload id + EDN-aware/HTML escaping for `payload-script`/`document`; host-side determinism CI with `:differs-at` for `render-twice`, which cannot move to a test kit without a wrong-direction `react-dom/server` dependency). The two going private have zero external callers and zero consumer story — `fresh-frame-id` structurally so: `render` mints its own id and forbids overriding it, so no public path consumes the function's return value, making the current docstring's "assemble a non-standard shell" rationale false for that name. Verified blast radius: no out-of-namespace caller of either name anywhere; only helper consumer repo-wide is `render-twice` (3 test call sites, staying public), so zero test churn; guide ch18 teaches only `server/render`; the `(keyword "hicasso.ssr"` bundle-isolation sentinel is untouched by a privacy change.

REJECTED:
- Option A (ratify the blanket keep): would convert an unargued census default into a ruling while the shipped docstring's rationale is demonstrably false for `fresh-frame-id`; pre-alpha is exactly when accidental publics are cheapest to remove.
- Option C (also privatise `render-twice`): purist but breaks three test call sites under the warnings-fatal gates and deletes a genuinely useful host diagnostic that has no other sane home.
- Option D (`fresh-frame-id` alone): pays the full process cost to remove one of two names with identical evidence, leaving the docstring defending `setup-events` on grounds that don't apply to it.
- Codex's guardrails are ADOPTED as part of the ruling: no speculative nonce/attribute bags, no shims, no new namespace, no bespoke public-surface checker, no deprecation period, no new tests for two unused pre-alpha names.

title: the derive-the-fence rule's WORKTREE half still returns names only — git worktree list cannot answer a file-level fence
description:
FOUND BY worker/fencecmd-b1ybz while landing rf2-b1ybz (PR #8262), 2026-08-15 00:03 AUSEST. That bead fixed the PR half of the rule; this is the same defect on the other half of the same command pair, and it is the DANGEROUS direction.

THE RULE NOW SAYS, correctly for its first half: derive the fence from 'gh pr list --state open --json number,headRefName,files' PLUS 'git worktree list', and write each entry from the FILE LISTS rather than the branch names.

THE DEFECT: git worktree list returns PATHS AND BRANCH NAMES. It carries no file information at all. So the rule's own second command cannot satisfy the rule's own requirement, and a mayor following it exactly still writes the worktree half of the fence by guessing.

WHY THIS HALF IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. A worktree with no open PR is a worker that has started and not yet pushed -- which is exactly the stale-NARROW case the rule already names as the expensive direction: an omitted holder means two workers on one file, and they can silently revert each other. The PR half, now fixed, mostly produces stale-BROAD errors, which cost a re-derivation.

THE TECHNIQUE, ALREADY PROVEN IN PRACTICE. The rf2-b1ybz worker hit this gap and closed it by hand rather than guessing: it diffed every worker/* branch against origin/main restricted to the paths it cared about, and found SEVEN branches touching them, none with an open PR -- including worker/method-nfgib, whose PR #8254 had already merged. That is the file-level answer for the worktree half, and it distinguishes a live unpushed worker from a merged leftover, which a name cannot.

  git diff --name-only origin/main worker/<branch> -- <paths of interest>

THE FIX: one sentence in .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, beside the sentence rf2-b1ybz added. Say that git worktree list answers WHO, not WHAT, so a worktree with no open change is resolved by diffing its branch against the trunk for the paths in question. Keep it to that -- rf2-6ng7's standing (c)-narrow ruling forbids new machinery for this class, and a per-branch diff over a handful of paths is cheap.

DOCS/THE-MAYOR-METHOD: weigh whether the generic layer needs anything at all. rf2-b1ybz already added the PRINCIPLE there ('a fence is a claim about FILES... ask your change-listing tool for the paths, not just the names'), and that sentence arguably covers this case already, since a worktree listing is a change-listing tool that returns names. IF SO, THE GENERIC LAYER NEEDS NO EDIT AND SAYING SO IS THE CORRECT DELIVERABLE. Do not add a tool name, flag, path or id to that tree -- it currently contains none, and the rf2-b1ybz worker's leak check over its added lines came back with zero hits across twenty tokens.

FENCE: .claude/commands/ and docs/the-mayor-method/ are a shared surface. PR #8262 holds both right now; this bead waits for it to merge.
notes:
LIVE MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-15 13:07 AUSEST — the mayor's stranded sweep just reproduced this bead's gap on two healthy workers at once, which is the strongest evidence yet that the remainder is real.

Six live workers, read with BOTH discriminators in the same command:

  worker/mount-7mtcf        tip=e494ab9eaa  modified=18
  worker/docsguide-hic068   tip=e494ab9eaa  modified=6
  worker/carry-0jl8s        tip=e9096321ae  modified=1
  worker/releasepol-hic061  tip=e03d3769b3  modified=0
  worker/rerun-hic048       tip=5130d7a5a0  modified=0
  worker/fencewt-42bj2      tip=d3842c37f0  modified=0

e494ab9eaa IS THE TRUNK TIP THOSE BRANCHES WERE CUT FROM. So mount-7mtcf and docsguide-hic068 have UNMOVED TIPS and EMPTY THREE-DOT DIFFS -- and between them hold 24 MODIFIED FILES. The committed-diff test alone would have called two healthy workers dead in this tick, and a fence derived from it would have omitted both: the stale-NARROW direction, which the landed rule itself names as the expensive one because two workers on one file can silently revert each other.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THIS REVEALS, worth landing alongside the clause: the two workers reading empty are the ones that have been running LONGEST. A worker commits at milestones, so the committed diff is emptiest exactly when a worker is deepest into a large change -- which is when omitting it from a fence costs the most. The signal is not merely incomplete; it is anti-correlated with the risk.

THIS ALSO CORROBORATES THE OTHER HALF OF THE SWEEP: an unmoved tip is the EXPECTED reading for a healthy worker mid-gate, so mayor-posture.md is right to require worktree activity as corroboration before an unmoved tip means anything. The dispatch rule needs the same corroboration for the same reason.
close_reason: PR #8282. The audit note's bounded repair landed: .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md now names git status --porcelain inside the worktree as the THIRD fence source alongside the three-dot diff and the PR-state check, says an empty three-dot diff is not an empty worktree (three-dot compares COMMIT TREES, so a worker that has edited but not committed reports nothing and its branch ref still equals the trunk), and says a worktree clean on BOTH sources has not started rather than owning nothing - its paths are in the bead it was dispatched under. Gap verified at source, not assumed: of five live workers reading <none yet> by committed diff, worker/mount-7mtcf held 18 modified files and worker/docsguide-hic068 held 1 modified plus 2 untracked. VERDICT ON THE ACCEPTANCE NOTE: it is a forward-looking CRITERION for the reopen, not a claim that work landed (structure: WHAT SURVIVES / REMAINING FALSE NEGATIVE / BOUNDED REPAIR imperative / ACCEPTANCE; bead was OPEN). Read as a description of landed state it would be WRONG rather than imprecise - nothing in the file named a working-tree source or said where pre-edit intent comes from; absent content, not loose words for 'unpushed'. GENERIC LAYER: edited, one tool-free sentence in dispatch-prompt-template.md Fences - rf2-b1ybz's 'paths, not just the names' corrects names->paths and does NOT cover a source blind to uncommitted work; leak check 0 hits across 24 tokens. No script, no gate, no registry - rf2-6ng7 (c)-narrow.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8265 (landed 8b5a28d5425dec721d25b902cbcb285e94f2a486) — REOPENED on the same worktree-half obligation.

WHAT SURVIVES. PR #8265 correctly changed the proposed two-dot comparison to origin/main...worker/<branch> and correctly pairs committed branch changes with PR state. That eliminates the measured trunk-advance false positives and merged-leftover false fences.

THE REMAINING FALSE NEGATIVE. A three-dot comparison with two named refs compares COMMIT TREES. It cannot see that worktree's index or working directory. The PR-side gh file list likewise sees only the remote head. Therefore an active worker that has staged, unstaged, or untracked source changes but has not committed/pushed them is still reported as touching no such file. That is not an edge outside this bead: its own risk case is “a worker that has started and not yet pushed,” and the dangerous window is precisely before the first commit. A worktree that has been dispatched but has not edited yet is also not evidence of an empty fence; its intended paths live in the assigned bead/brief, not Git.

DIRECT DISCRIMINATION. Auditing the currently registered worktrees found a live untracked path on worker/presence-hic053 that appears in neither the three-dot branch diff nor any open PR file list. It is a PR-body artefact rather than a source collision, so it is not itself the defect; it proves the information channel is structurally blind. A staged, unstaged, or untracked source path has identical visibility.

BOUNDED REPAIR. Keep the landed branch-diff and PR-state rules. Add only the missing instruction: for each listed worktree, union the committed three-dot paths with that worktree's staged, unstaged, and untracked paths; when no path has been touched yet, consult the durable assigned bead/dispatch fence and never interpret “clean branch” as “owns nothing.” Do not add a registry, daemon, or checker. A tiny worked command/example that plants an uncommitted path and shows the derivation includes it is sufficient evidence.

ACCEPTANCE. The dispatch rule no longer treats an active no-PR worktree as empty merely because its branch ref matches the trunk; it names both committed and live working-tree sources, and says where pre-edit intent comes from. scripts/check_readme_links.py green.

title: hic: correction-ledger rows whose beads have CLOSED still read open — rf2-cfriw at least, and the gate counts them as unresolved
description:
## The finding

Found by **rf2-clldl** (the CHECKPOINT 3 §1 Completeness closure re-run) on `main`@`006399e9db`,
outside its ledger-only fence — the six cells it may write are rf2-hic-038's, and this is a
different row, whose transition is the **ledger keeper's** under
`correction-ledger.md`'s own 'Who writes the row, and in which commit' table. Filed rather
than written.

`rf2-cfriw` (rf2-hic-048, §1 Completeness — *HS-31, HS-32, HS-34 and HS-23 are Client-only with
no witness and no live owner*) is **closed** in the tracker, verified 2026-08-14. Its
correction-ledger row still reads `open` with `—` as its Closure evidence.

That is not a cosmetic lag. `rf2-hic-064` gates on **zero unresolved rows**, where unresolved
means any status other than `closed`, so a row left at `open` behind a closed bead fails that
gate exactly as a genuinely open finding does — and, worse, it is indistinguishable from one
by reading the ledger, which is the single artefact the final audit consults.

## What this bead is NOT

It is not a request to mark the row `closed`. The closure rule is explicit that a row closes
only when the producing protocol section is re-run against the landed fix and the evidence is
written in. `rf2-cfriw` did land real work (`client-only-arms-ssr-cljs-test`), and part of
its finding did NOT close — the HS-23 `n/$` route, now filed as **rf2-04ekn**. So the correct
transition may well be `open` -> `resolved`, or `closed` with a stated remainder naming
rf2-04ekn. Deciding which is the keeper's call.

## The wider check this bead asks for

Do the same comparison for EVERY row: for each row not reading `closed`, is its bead still
open in the tracker? rf2-clldl checked only the rows adjacent to its own six and found one
mismatch on the first look, so the population is worth a sweep rather than a spot check.

## Surface fence

- WRITE: docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md (status + Closure evidence cells only).
- Rows are never deleted and no severity moves.

## Acceptance

Every non-`closed` row's bead status re-checked in the tracker, each mismatch transitioned per
the closure rule with evidence written in, and the sweep's date recorded so the next reader
knows how stale the answer is.

title: check_allocation_non_claim lets sibling Markdown rows qualify an unrelated claim
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8244 — core fail-open in the new warm-allocation publication scan.

scripts/check_allocation_non_claim.py says a per-write figure passes only when its own paragraph carries the qualification. Its paragraphs() helper actually splits only on blank lines, then unqualified_claims() applies CLAIM and QUALIFIERS to the whole block. Tight Markdown list items and every row of a Markdown table normally share one blank-line block. An unrelated sibling item/row containing “quality floor”, “unmet”, “refused”, or another qualifier therefore makes an unqualified product figure elsewhere in the block green.

Minimal landed-tree reproduction:
- "| Product cost | 2,031 B/boundary/write |
| Separate instrument | quality floor unmet |" => []
- "- Product cost: 2,031 B/boundary/write
- Separate instrument: quality floor unmet" => []
A plain unqualified sentence correctly returns a finding, so this is association scope rather than the claim regex.

Bounded repair: recognize table rows and tight list items as independent claim/qualification units (or otherwise bind each matched figure to its own sentence/row/item), without building a general Markdown parser or tightening ordinary prose into a false-positive machine. Add the two cross-sibling cases to --self-test. rf2-yptjt separately owns CI wiring; coordinate so the corrected scan is what gets wired.
acceptance_criteria: An unqualified per-write figure fails when a different table row or tight-list item contains a qualifier; the same figure passes when its own row/item is honestly qualified; the existing five self-test fixtures and the live repository scan remain green.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #8271 (worker/gatescripts-b9707).

THE SCOPE RULE, ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE. The gate already STATED the right rule in three places -- the module docstring ('its own paragraph'), the QUALIFIERS comment ('in the same paragraph') and paragraphs()'s own docstring ('blank-line-separated block'). Only the implementation was wrong, and the bug report's diagnosis was exact: in Markdown a whole table and a whole tight list are ONE blank-line block, so the stated scope and the implemented scope diverge precisely where a publication surface puts its numbers. Both minimal reproductions confirmed on the landed tree before any edit: table => [], tight list => [], plain sentence => a finding.

THE REPAIR. claim_units() replaces paragraphs() and subdivides a block by THREE LINE SHAPES: a table row is its own unit and nothing continues it; a tight list item is its own unit INCLUDING its wrapped continuation lines; everything else stays prose at block scope. Prose keeps block scope deliberately -- an English sentence routinely carries its qualification onto the next line, and a per-line scan would be exactly the false-positive machine the bead warned against. No Markdown parser: the gate never needs to know what a table MEANS, only that two rows are two claims.

ACCEPTANCE MET IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the fixtures are falsifiable rather than assumed. Four added: table cross-sibling RED, tight-list cross-sibling RED, table row self-qualified GREEN, list item qualified on its own WRAPPED line GREEN. Run against the PRE-FIX module from HEAD on identical inputs, the two red fixtures were GREEN before and are RED after; the two green fixtures and both pre-existing cases (prose wrapped-qualified GREEN, plain unqualified RED) do not move. So the fail-open closed and nothing over-tightened. The GREEN pair is load-bearing, not decoration: a repair that simply stopped honouring qualification would pass the red pair while silently deleting the gate's third property.

The existing five fixtures stay green (9 total, exit 0) and the live repository scan is unchanged at 235 publication-surface files / 0 claims, exit 0 -- the bead's remaining acceptance clause.

COORDINATION NOTE the bead asked for: rf2-yptjt has since LANDED, so this gate is now CI-live in docs.yml (self-test + live run), armed by its own path in the docs-surface list. The corrected scan is therefore what is wired, and this PR self-arms that job.

edit. requirements-mine.md carries an EARLIER, DATED pass entry that does still

text — for the same reason rf2-uo68y worded its two repairs against the RULING
instead of against another page's current wording. A cell that cites another
page's text falsifies the moment that page is edited, which is the whole
mechanism of this cascade.

migration population finding (rf2-hic-055, which ran).

everywhere it could reach: `docs/core/hicasso/13-overlays-and-focus.md`'s
"Initial focus" prose and its troubleshooting row, and
`docs/core/hicasso/22-accessibility.md`'s focus-ownership row. Two surfaces
carrying the SAME wrong recipe were held by `worker/complete-b6jkj` at the
time and are left here rather than edited under a live fence.

THE MEASURED TRUTH, re-derived at source and unchanged by this bead:
`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/overlay_dom_cljs_test.cljs`,
`the-focus-one-shot-is-the-platforms-focus-delegate-and-not-reacts-autofocus`.
NEITHER spelling reaches the platform. `:auto-focus` camelCases to React's own
`autoFocus`, which React honours by calling `.focus()` during the commit —
child-first, one commit before the module's ref attaches and calls `showModal`,
at which point the dialog is still `display:none` and nothing inside it is
focusable — and emits no attribute. `:autofocus`, unhyphenated, React rejects
outright (`Invalid DOM property autofocus. Did you mean autoFocus?`). The
platform's dialog-focusing steps then take the first focusable control in tree
order, and the witness asserts exactly that: focus lands on `#first`, not on
`#chosen`, and `#chosen` carries no `autofocus` attribute.

WHAT IS LEFT, both on `worker/complete-b6jkj`'s surface:

1. `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/overlay.cljs` — the SHIPPED
   public door. Line ~123 states "**Initial focus** is `:autofocus true` on the
   control that should have it" and line ~130 claims "`:autofocus`,
   unhyphenated, reaches the DOM as the attribute the platform reads". Both are
   contradicted by the witness in the same package. Line ~131's "A modal with no
   autofocus target focuses its first focusable control" is correct and is in
   fact the whole recipe. The public `overlay/modal` example at line ~204 uses
   `[:button {:autofocus true …} "Delete"]` and should teach tree order instead.

2. `docs/core/hicasso/13-overlays-and-focus.md`'s modal example (the fenced
   block around line 113) still carries an inert `:auto-focus true` on the
   `.danger` Delete button. Removing it is a TWO-FILE change: every fenced block
   in `docs/core/hicasso/` is digest-pinned by R1 of
   `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py`, whose `ROSTER`
   (line ~491) holds the digest, and that file was held too. Under the corrected
   prose the example's behaviour is already right — "Keep it" is first in tree
   order and is the safe default for a destructive confirmation — so what is
   left is the dead key, not a behaviour change.

NOT IN SCOPE, and deliberately: minting
`:rf.error/hicasso-overlay-anchor-missing` for the missing-anchor no-op. That
refusal was verified at source and stands: `complaints.md`'s reserved table
carries the id, `naming-ledger.md` rows 30 and 40 hold the spelling provisional
until the naming packet (rf2-hic-065, open) sits, and R6 of the
complaint-catalogue gate would require a `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` row,
which is hot zone. It follows rf2-hic-065.
acceptance_criteria: overlay.cljs's docstring and its public modal example teach tree order and no longer claim :autofocus reaches the DOM; the ch13 fenced modal example drops the inert :auto-focus true and check_guide_samples.py's ROSTER digest for that block is updated in the same PR (the gate prints the row to paste). Both files must be unheld when this is dispatched.

title: hic: caret-types compares the HTML type attribute exactly, so a shouted type silently loses the same-turn converge
description:
FOUND BY rf2-h6qm7 (the sibling case-sensitivity hole), reported rather than fixed because that bead's ruled repair was 'only the file-type comparison' and 'every non-file control stays as PR #8205 ruled them'.

THE COMPARISON. impl.controlled/caret-type? asks (contains? caret-types t) against (unchecked-get js-props \"type\"), where caret-types is #{\"text\" \"search\" \"url\" \"tel\" \"password\"} (controlled.cljs:484,501). Same props object, same reader, same case-sensitivity as the file bug: codec/convert-prop-value hands strings and keyword names on unchanged, so :type \"TEXT\" arrives as \"TEXT\" and misses every member.

REACHABLE, and by the identical door rf2-h6qm7 proved open. caret-type? is a conjunct of convergeable?, so a miss means install! wraps no change handler and shadow-component renders the bare tag. [:input {:type \"TEXT\" :value ... :on-input ...}] therefore silently loses the same-turn converge and the caret restoration that are the whole point of the namespace.

NOT THE SAME SEVERITY, which is why it is filed rather than folded in. The file bug reached an engine exception the author could not even catch; this one degrades to React's own end-of-event restore — the field still works, the caret goes to the end. No throw, no id, no warning: a silent loss of an optimisation, on a spelling almost nobody writes.

DISPOSITION IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A FORMALITY. Folding case here costs a .toLowerCase on the caret path, which is hotter than the file path (every controlled text field, every render). Closing this as minutiae is a legitimate answer; so is folding it for symmetry with file-input-value?. What is NOT legitimate is leaving one folded and the other not with nothing written down, which is what this bead prevents.

SEE ALSO, same class, deliberately out of scope: install!'s (case tag (\"input\" \"textarea\")) compares HTML TAG names exactly, and slot.cljc's #{\"aria\" \"data\"} and {\"class\" ... \"for\" ... \"charset\" ...} compare attribute NAMES exactly. Neither is the same defect: React itself keys off those exact strings, so a shouted spelling never reaches the controlled path at all rather than reaching it unguarded.

title: hic: uppercase file input types bypass the value refusal and still throw InvalidStateError
description:
FOUND BY merged-PR audit #8205 (2026-08-14), correctness lens.

THE HOLE. `impl.controlled/file-input-value?` identifies a file control with `(identical? "file" (unchecked-get js-props "type"))`, against the prop object BEFORE React creates the element. `codec/convert-prop-value` deliberately returns strings unchanged (and turns a keyword into its unchanged name), so `:type "FILE"` reaches that predicate as `"FILE"` and misses the new refusal. `controlled-text-tag?` still accepts the valued input, React then applies the type, the platform normalises it to file, and the following non-empty value write throws the same unattributed InvalidStateError rf2-u2tza was meant to replace.

MEASURED IN CHROMIUM 147.0.7727.15 at the landed tip: after `n.setAttribute("type", "FILE")`, `n.getAttribute("type")` is `"FILE"` while `n.type` is `"file"`; `n.value = "budget.csv"` throws InvalidStateError with the filename-only message. This is a standards-valid spelling of the same enumerated input type, not an unknown control.

SMALLEST REPAIR. Make only the file-type comparison ASCII-case-insensitive before React (or otherwise compare the semantic type), retain the non-empty value predicate exactly, and add one focused spelling-variant witness. Do not turn this into general attribute validation or normalisation; every non-file control and `:value ""` stay as PR #8205 ruled them.
acceptance_criteria: A valued input whose HTML type spelling case-normalises to file (at minimum "FILE", including the equivalent keyword spelling if public props admit it) raises :rf.error/hicasso-file-input-value-prop before React; :value "" remains accepted; lowercase file and non-file behaviour remain covered by the focused suite.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8216 (branch worker/upcase-h6qm7, commit 4419baa898).

file-input-value? now folds ASCII case at the comparison: (and (string? t) (identical? "file" (.toLowerCase t))). js-props is NOT normalised — that object is what React consumes and what reaches the DOM, so the attribute that ships stays the one the author wrote.

ACCEPTANCE, each measured in Chromium via the :browser-test lane:
- "FILE", :FILE, "File" and "fIlE" all raise :rf.error/hicasso-file-input-value-prop before React. RED 5 failures / GREEN 0, same test file, source hashes 3d0c1b037f -> 063c77c19e.
- :value "" still accepted, at the lowercase spelling AND the shouted one. The non-EMPTY predicate is byte-for-byte unchanged; its original witness passed in both states.
- lowercase file and every non-file control still covered; "profile"/"filename" and a numeric :type all pass through.

BOTH IDS INTACT AND UNMERGED. No new id was needed, so spec/009 was not touched. The spine's check_complaint_catalogue confirms: 76 live rows, every live row emitted and rowed in Spec 009.

SHARPER THAN THE BEAD RECORDED. React caught the InvalidStateError inside its own commit and re-reported it as an UNCAUGHT PAGE ERROR — thrown-by around the flushSync returned nil. The author had neither an id nor an exception to catch, only a console entry naming React internals. A new mount row measures that.

MARKER PATH NEEDED NO FOLD, and a row now proves it rather than assuming it: intent/target-value reads a live element and asks .files, so the platform has already normalised the type by the time it looks. That row passed red AND green.

SWEEP RESULT: one further same-class comparison found, caret-types (controlled.cljs:484), reachable through the identical door. Filed as rf2-7ae61 rather than folded in, per this bead's 'only the file-type comparison' ruling — it degrades silently rather than throwing, and folding it costs a .toLowerCase on a hotter path. Tag-name and attribute-name comparisons are a different class and are named on that bead as out of scope.

GATES: fast spine PASS; test:browser 1545/9793 green; test:cljs 13944/70429 green; test:hicasso-invariants, test:hicasso-controlled green.

title: Two readers of one shadow-cljs 'Build completed' line — unify when a third lane wants it
description:
FOUND BY rf2-qfrrp/rf2-4a6ei's worker (2026-08-14), while adding the second one.

TWO PARSERS, ONE LINE. shadow-cljs prints 'Build completed. (N files, M compiled, W warnings, Ts)' and two gates now read it independently:

  * implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs — parseBuildSummaries, for the :examples/* builds, red on warnings > 0, and an unparseable/missing summary is a FAILURE (rf2-nlnd9y.1).
  * implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs — buildTally, for every :node-test-family lane, same rule, same refusal direction (rf2-4a6ei).

WHY THEY WERE NOT SHARED, measured rather than assumed. The examples parser anchors on a build id containing a SLASH (`\[(:[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+)\]`), which matches ':examples/login-helix' and matches NO ':node-test'-family id, so it could not be called from the new site as it stands. Generalising it would have meant editing the examples gate — outside the fence of that dispatch, and a wider blast radius than the bug warranted.

THEY ALSO DIVERGE, deliberately: the examples gate treats a singular '1 warning' as unparseable and fails; the node-test one reads it and fails NAMING the count. Both red, so the divergence is currently harmless.

THE ACTUAL RISK, and it is small: a shadow-cljs release that rewords the line disarms neither (both refuse an unreadable summary), but it would have to be fixed twice. This is a P3 because two four-line readers are cheaper than one shared module until a THIRD lane wants the line — at which point mint one reader and call it from all three.

DO NOT ACTION THIS AS A REFACTOR FOR ITS OWN SAKE. If no third caller appears, closing this as won't-do is the correct outcome.
close_reason:
RESOLVED AS A RECORDED REFUSAL, with the bead's own trigger re-tested. PR #8225 (comment-only).

THE TRIGGER HAD ALREADY FIRED, unnoticed. The bead says 'until a THIRD lane wants the line — at which point mint one reader and call it from all three'. There are three: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/lane_build.cjs has parsed the same line since 2026-08-03 (d8f4559d3c), reaches the same verdict (unreadable summary = FAILURE), cites the same examples gate, and gives the SAME slash-anchor reason for not reusing it. compile-node-test.cjs said the same thing eleven days later without knowing it existed.

UNIFYING IS STILL THE WRONG CALL — measured against the live parsers, not assumed:
  * examples regex vs [:hicasso-bench] / [:node-test]      -> 0 matches
  * lane_build regex vs a summary with no [:id] bracket    -> 0 matches
  * compile-node-test vs that same bracket-less summary    -> reads it, deliberately
  * examples gate given an UNREQUESTED id                  -> FAILS
So no single pattern serves all three as they stand, and the examples slash is a FILTER rather than a capture — reconcileRequestedBuilds fails on any summary whose id was not requested, so an id-agnostic shared pattern would hand that gate every id shadow prints and re-open a settled question inside a gate over 54 builds.

WHAT DIFFERS IS THE SELECTION POLICY, NOT THE REGEX: reconcile a requested SET / every row must read zero / take the LAST row so a dependency summary is never mistaken for the lane's. A shared module removes three regexes and leaves three policies — the smallest part.

AND THE DUPLICATION CANNOT FAIL QUIETLY. All three refuse an unreadable summary, so a shadow-cljs reformat yields three RED gates and one afternoon's work, never a silent pass. That is what makes three copies affordable.

THE REAL DEFECT THE COUNT EXPOSED WAS DISCOVERY — two authors, one wall, neither found the other. Fixed by stating the roster in all three files, with the full argument in compile-node-test.cjs (whose closing claim was falsified) and short pointers in the other two, so the prose has one owner and cannot drift.

THE COUNT IS REPLACED BY A POLICY TEST rather than incremented: a lane whose selection policy one of the three already implements calls that reader's export (all three export their parser); a lane with a genuinely new policy writes its own four lines and adds itself to the roster. 'Three' was not a checkable trigger — it fired and was still wrong.

title: Prose inside a test namespace is invisible to the browser gates — only compile catches a broken string literal
description:
FOUND BY rf2-hmrcov's worker (2026-08-14) while editing a citation in a CLJS test namespace.

WHAT HAPPENED. It wrote a citation quoting a retired sentence, using a bare double-quote inside a CLJS string. That terminates the string. The HMR browser gate — 153 checks across 10 sections in three engines — STAYED GREEN through it.  caught it.

WHY THE BROWSER GATE STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE IT. A browser gate runs the namespaces its selector picks up. A namespace whose string literal is broken does not compile, so it is not in the build, so the gate never runs it — and a gate that never runs a namespace reports nothing about it. The absence reads as green.

THE GENERAL SHAPE: ANY EDIT TO A TEST NAMESPACE'S PROSE — docstrings, citations, comment text carrying quotes or escapes — IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY BROWSER GATE. Only a compile step sees it. That matters because prose edits feel safe and get made without re-running the compile, especially late in a dispatch when the behavioural gates have already gone green.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A NOTE. This programme requires workers to write reasoning INTO test namespaces — that is deliberate and good, and it is why several suites carry long docstrings explaining what an assertion witnesses and why. So the repository actively encourages the edit that this hole makes unsafe.

CANDIDATE REPAIRS, none preferred and all needing a look at source: make the browser runner FAIL when its selector matches fewer namespaces than the previous run rather than passing on a smaller set; or have the browser gate assert its own expected namespace count; or ensure a compile step is unconditionally part of every lane that runs a test namespace. The first is the most general — it turns a silently-shrinking test set into a red, which is the same fail-open family as a gate that inspects zero files and exits 0 (rf2-qfrrp).

VERIFY THE PREMISE AT SOURCE FIRST: reproduce the broken string in a test namespace, run the browser gate, and confirm it goes green. It is a claim.
close_reason:
PR #8207. PREMISE REFUTED AT SOURCE; A DIFFERENT AND BETTER DEFECT FIXED.

MEASURED TWICE in implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/ssr_escaping_security_cljs_test.cljc via 'npm run test:security':
  - bare quote in the NS DOCSTRING: the ns form does not read, the BUILD FAILS exit 1 naming file and line. Already caught.
  - bare quote in a DEFTEST DOCSTRING, one form lower: the quote closes the string early and REOPENS it before the line ends, so the file still READS. 'one frame per app' becomes four bare symbols; in JavaScript an undeclared var is undefined and evaluating it is harmless. Build completes, suite runs, exit 0, and the counts are IDENTICAL to clean: 'Ran 93 tests containing 705 assertions. / 0 failures, 0 errors.' Only the tally moved: 0 warnings -> 4 warnings.

SO THE BEAD'S MECHANISM IS WRONG. The namespace never left the build and the test count never dropped, so the bead's preferred candidate — fail when the selector matches fewer namespaces than expected — WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS. Nothing was missing. The HMR gate is also not the culprit: it drives an APP build that never contained a test namespace, so it reported nothing about the edit because the edit was not in it.

WHAT WAS MISSING was a reader for the number shadow-cljs had already printed. compile-node-test.cjs — the one wrapper every :node-test-family lane goes through — ran shadow-cljs under stdio:'inherit', so the tally streamed past it uninspected. It now captures while streaming (spawn+tee, not spawnSync, so a long compile does not go silent), parses 'Build completed. (N files, M compiled, W warnings, Ts)', and reds on W > 0. An UNREADABLE tally reds too: unknown and clean must not converge.

MEASURED BEFORE ARMING: all seven lanes are warning-free today (node-test 2395 files, security 216, testbed-support 693, ui 343, freehand 488, hicasso 457, perf-nightly 159 — 0 warnings each), so a floor of zero cannot go stale. No env escape by design.

THIRD FAMILY MEMBER FOUND: check-examples-compile.cjs already does exactly this for :examples/* (rf2-nlnd9y.1), including the same refusal on an unreadable summary. Not shared — its regex anchors on a slashed build id no :node-test lane carries. Filed rf2-040s1 for the moment a third lane wants the line.

Red-then-green on the same plant: exit 0 green before, exit 1 naming 4 warnings after. Six parser cases added, proved red (exit 1 broken / 0 restored).

title: The Suspense-retains / Activity-releases asymmetry is measured on both tiers and documented in no lane doc
description:
FOUND BY rf2-sr19's worker (2026-08-14) and correctly NOT actioned by it — the gap is pre-existing and outside that cluster's fence.

THE ASYMMETRY, now measured on BOTH tiers. A Suspense fallback RETAINS the hidden island's subscription state; an Activity hide RELEASES it. Two further measurements make the shape precise and should be carried into whatever doc takes this:

RETENTION IS IN THE TABLES, NOT IN THE PAINT. A Suspense-hidden island does not repaint on a store write inside a sync-lane flush — React simply does not render an Offscreen-hidden subtree there. The worker polled four seconds for a repaint that never came, while the residue read cells 1, cell-refs 1, boundaries 1, edges 1: the subscription was fully installed the whole time. So a doc that says state is retained must not imply the view updates.

A RELEASE IS NOT A NOTHING-OWNED CENSUS. Dropping a membership drops reference, boundary and edge together and leaves the CELL to a reaper — measured cells 1, cell-refs 0, boundaries 0, edges 0. A row asserting all-zero after a release would be wrong; all-zero is exact only where nothing ever committed.

WHY IT IS UNDOCUMENTED. The boundary tier measured this first and did not write it down; the native tier has now measured it too. So it is a pre-existing gap that the new work merely made visible on a second tier.

THE VALUE IS PRACTICAL: an author choosing between Suspense and Activity to hide a subtree is choosing between retaining and releasing subscription state, and today nothing tells them so.

VERIFY BOTH MEASUREMENTS AT SOURCE before writing them down — they are claims, and the census shapes above are exact numbers that a later change could move.
close_reason: PR #8239. Both measurements VERIFIED AT SOURCE before being written down, exactly as the bead demanded, and both landed in the form that does not invert them. RETENTION IS IN THE TABLES, NOT THE PAINT: native-hooks-dom-cljs-test/an-island-under-a-post-commit-suspension-keeps-exact-ownership-across-the-retry — a write dispatched during the suspension lands with the subscription fully installed (residue {:cells 1 :cell-refs 1 :boundaries 1 :edges 1}, registration identical? to the mount's) and the hidden island does NOT repaint, because mount/dispatch! flushes on the sync lane and React does not render an Offscreen-hidden subtree there; the row's own comment records the four-second poll that timed out with the census unchanged. The new text says outright that retention is about ownership and never about the view being current. A RELEASE IS NOT A NOTHING-OWNED CENSUS: roots-frames-support/released is {:cell-refs 0 :boundaries 0 :edges 0} — three counts, :cells deliberately excluded because the cell belongs to a reaper a macrotask later — and the native suite's own note records {:cells 1 :cell-refs 0 :boundaries 0 :edges 0} on the run that first drove W8. All-zero including :cells is nothing-owned, exact only for an abandoned attempt that never committed. LANE DOC CHOSEN: lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md, new section 'Suspense retains where Activity releases' placed immediately after 'Activity lifecycle witness' and cross-linked to it. WHY: that lane's own opening declares it owns how these surfaces participate in Activity and external stores, and it already carries the Activity release conduct, both reveal shapes and their schedules, the refused repair, and the explicit rule that n/use-sub and n/use-frame owe the boundary shell's conduct rather than inheriting it — i.e. it already owns both tiers of precisely this surface, and only the other mechanism was missing. Rejected: evidence-baseline.md (owns measurements and their admissibility, but this is a compatibility contract an author acts on, not a number) and hot-path-architecture.md (owns the performance workflow; Suspense/Activity is one checklist row there). Both witnesses named on the page so the claim is reachable from the document that makes it, and lanes/README.md's ownership map gets a row so the surface is reachable from the index — the same defect class rf2-1qws fixed. Gates: check_doc_slugs 0 (it validated the new anchor from README), check_provenance_pins 0 (3 pages, 0 findings), fast-PR spine 0. Column counts by hand: README ownership map 2x16; the new section is prose only, no table or fence.

KEEP the two true parts of that line — that technical names (bead ids, paths, commands) stay exact, and that it applies to CHAT ONLY while bead text, PR bodies and documents keep their own register. The frozen store is injected into agent system prompts as a one-line bullet, so an agent reads it as a live operator preference. That is the generator of this bead, and of the identical brief that produced this second dispatch. Not a cron statement anyone has verified.

WHAT SHIPPED. No normative change. One provenance paragraph after line 12 naming the two memory keys, the command that returns them, and why the older record does not win — because this line has now been re-filed twice and the file gave a reader no way to check it. +2/-0. title: check_doc_slugs.py polices skills/ but no PR-time job runs it on a skills-only change — rf2-6ng7 class, the twin of the inject-cofx fix
description:
Found by the rf2-skvce tree-claim meta-check while writing the declared list's reason strings.

THE DEFECT. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py's DEFAULT_ROOTS is docs, spec, skills, migration (plus tools/*/spec). It runs in exactly one PR-time place: docs.yml's 'build' job, which is gated on that workflow's docs_surface classifier. That classifier's case list is docs/*|spec/*|migration/*|mkdocs.yml|mkdocs_hooks.py|TESTING.md|README.md|CHANGELOG.md|SKILL-REDIRECT.md|AGENTS.md|CLAUDE.md|...|testbeds/*|tools/*/spec/*|.github/workflows/docs.yml — and skills/* is NOT on it. Measured: a skills-only path lights docs_surface false and arms zero outputs in test.yml's classifier too.

So one of the gate's four scan roots sits outside its own arming. A skills/**/*.md PR that plants a broken markdown link target or a dangling heading anchor runs the slug validator NOWHERE at PR time. (test.yml's push filter also paths-ignores 'skills/**/*.md', so the post-merge run does not catch it either; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh does run it, but a local spine is not a mechanism.)

THIS IS THE EXACT DEFECT test.yml:713-724 ALREADY NAMES AND FIXED ONE GATE OVER. rf2-6ng7 moved scripts/check_inject_cofx_residue.py out of docs.yml's build job for this very reason — 'a case list carrying docs/*, spec/*, migration/*, testbeds/* and a dozen named files, but NOT skills/*. One of the gate's four scan roots was therefore outside its own arming.' The remedy chosen there was explicitly NOT a wider docs_surface (that buys a ~15-minute MkDocs build on every skills PR) but 'no surface at all' — relocating the sub-second pure-stdlib check into test.yml's always-on 'Repo invariant checks' job. check_doc_slugs.py has the same shape (pure Python, self-testable via --self-test) and the same three other roots.

WHAT THE FIXER MUST CHECK BEFORE COPYING THAT REMEDY. check_doc_slugs.py is 2300+ lines and considerably heavier than the inject-cofx residue scan; measure its wall clock over the full corpus first. If it is cheap, the always-on job is the answer and docs.yml's copy retires. If it is not, the alternatives are (a) a skills-only invocation in the always-on job with the full corpus staying in docs.yml, or (b) adding skills/* to docs_surface and accepting the MkDocs cost, which test.yml:721 already argues against.

NOT A DUPLICATE of the arming half: skills/re-frame2-pair/*, skills/shared/* and skills/re-frame2-setup/* DO arm skills_structural, and the prose skill trees ARE reached by the always-on verify-skill-mcp-drift job (check_skill_mcp_drift.py + check_inject_cofx_residue.py). What no PR-time job reaches is the SLUG/ANCHOR validation of skills markdown.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8197. Premise VERIFIED at source: docs_surface's case list, evaluated verbatim against skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md, returns false; check_doc_slugs.py is invoked by run: in exactly two places, both in docs.yml's docs_surface-gated build job. 176 skills markdown files were unvalidated at PR time.

ONE PREMISE REFUTED. The bead proposed test.yml's always-on verify-skill-mcp-drift job on the grounds that this gate is 'pure Python, self-testable' like check_inject_cofx_residue.py. It is NOT pure stdlib: check_doc_slugs.py:76-84 hard-requires pymdown-extensions and exits 2 without it. That job has no pip install, so the literal remedy would have redded every PR. Landed in verify-readme-links instead — unconditional, already installs requirements.txt for the same slugifier, and is this gate's declared companion (check_readme_links.py imports SLUGIFY from it).

Cost measured, not assumed: verify-readme-links 0.5 min vs a 15.2 min longest job (run 31765523222), so the corpus scan is off the critical path and no wider docs_surface was needed. Moved not copied; docs.yml's copy retired, and the gate's source removed from test.yml's push paths-ignore.

SAYS-WHAT-IT-INSPECTED shipped too — --verbose now prints per-root file counts (docs 400 / spec 60 / skills 176 / migration 8 / seven tools/*/spec), so reach is on the page beside the verdict and a root dropping out of scope shows as a 0. Four documents claiming the gate runs in docs.yml (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, TESTING.md, docs/AUTHORING.md) corrected in the same patch.

Red-then-green: plant at skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:254 (plain link, column 0, outside every fence) -> exit 1; restored hash d4cfb3e6 == committed blob. Corpus is CLEAN today (753 files, exit 0), so arming reds nothing.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
CORRECTS SOMETHING I HAVE BEEN PUTTING IN BRIEFS ALL SESSION (mayor, 2026-08-14). I have told workers that check_doc_slugs.py's roster is docs, spec, skills, migration plus tools/*/spec, as shorthand for what it covers. That is accurate about the ROSTER and misleading about COVERAGE: the script runs only inside docs.yml's build job, gated on docs_surface, which excludes skills/*. A worker editing skills markdown who nominates this gate gets a green that means nothing.

THAT IS THE SAME VACUOUS-PASS SHAPE AS rf2-qfrrp, where check_provenance_pins run before committing inspects zero files and exits 0. Two gates, same failure: a pass that is indistinguishable from a real one because the gate is silent on success.

THE REMEDY IS KNOWN AND SMALL. test.yml lines 713-724 already solved this exact shape for check_inject_cofx_residue.py — that is the pattern to copy rather than design something new.

VERIFY BEFORE FIXING: confirm at source that docs_surface really excludes skills/*, and that no OTHER workflow runs check_doc_slugs.py on a skills path. The premise is a claim, and a sibling claim of this shape was refuted at source today when an exclusion pattern turned out not to match the namespace it was thought to exclude.

THE GENERAL LESSON WORTH CARRYING INTO THE FIX: a gate's ROSTER, its SCHEDULE and its REACH are three different things. This is the third instance today where quoting one as though it settled the others manufactured false confidence — the others being the provenance gate's vacuous green on uncommitted work, and the same gate absorbing a plant placed beside a landed pin. If the fix can make the gate SAY which trees it actually inspected on a run, that closes the whole family rather than this instance.

title: tools/deps.edn + tools/shadow-cljs.edn classify to ZERO outputs — the tool-tier coordinators are unarmed
description:
Found by the rf2-skvce tree-claim meta-check on its first run (the check's declared list records this as a HOLE rather than as covered).

WHAT IS DARK. The four files directly under tools/ (.gitignore, README.md, deps.edn, shadow-cljs.edn) arm no output of .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh — measured, all four at zero. Two of them are load-bearing build configuration:

  * tools/deps.edn is the tool-tier build COORDINATOR: a :deps map of six :local/root artefacts plus the aggregate :test alias with five :extra-paths and five -d flags. tools/shadow-cljs.edn resolves its classpath through it (:deps true).
  * tools/shadow-cljs.edn aggregates re-frame2-pair-mcp's :server and :server-test builds at the tools/ root so 'shadow-cljs compile <build>' works from tools/ as well as from tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/.

The big case in the classifier has arms for tools/story/*, tools/xray/*, tools/template/*, tools/machines-viz/* and so on, but a bare tools/<file> matches none of them.

WHY THIS WAS NOT FIXED IN THE rf2-skvce PR, and what the fixer must weigh. Picking the output needs measurement, not a guess, and the classifier's own comments are emphatic about the failure mode (see the tools_jvm_machines_viz / tools_jvm_testbed_support notes: an output that fires four unrelated probes and STILL leaves the changed file unexercised is worse than nothing).

  * tools_jvm fires four jvm-tools-* probes, and NONE of them runs 'cd tools && clojure -M:test' — tools/deps.edn's own comment says production CI runs each tool's :test alias separately. So tools_jvm would schedule four jobs that never read the edited aggregate.
  * The honest consumer of tools/shadow-cljs.edn is the pair-mcp server build, which mcp_conformance / mcp_live gate. That is the more promising arm and should be measured first.
  * A third possibility is that the aggregate alias has no CI consumer at all and the right answer is to say so — a declared hole with a reason, next to the 3-engine ones in expensive-tests.yml.

Whatever lands, per the rf2-6ng7 codicil it pins its arming in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs in the same patch, and removes the tools entry from DECLARED_NO_SURFACE_OUTPUT in that file (the meta-check fails on a STALE declaration, so the two cannot drift).
close_reason:
Settled in PR #8197 as a REASONED REFUSAL, not an arm. Re-measured: tools/deps.edn + tools/shadow-cljs.edn arm all 32 outputs false.

The filer's refusal to guess was correct and is upheld. Converted from an open TODO into a checked finding on five source-located facts: (1) no workflow runs from tools/ — every working-directory in .github/workflows is tools/<artefact>, never the bare root; (2) scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh iterates per-tool dirs and never the aggregate :test alias; (3) tools/deps.edn says so itself ('Production CI runs each tool's :test alias separately (per-tool gates)'); (4) CI compiles the pair-mcp server from tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/shadow-cljs.edn — tools/shadow-cljs.edn is by its own comment a MIRROR nothing in CI takes; (5) verify-version-lockstep.sh reads per-artefact deps.edn, and the coordinator is explicitly not a published artefact.

So no output would EXERCISE either file. tools_jvm was the candidate and would fire four probes that never read the edited file — the failure the tools_jvm_machines_viz note calls worse than nothing. Developer-convenience aggregates; breakage surfaces on the next 'cd tools && clojure -M:test'.

The entry also stopped OVERSTATING the hole: tools/README.md IS covered — verified in check_readme_links.py's _iter_scanned set, walked by the always-on verify-readme-links job. coveredBy now names it, so the reason stays a checked claim. DECLARED_NO_SURFACE_OUTPUT entry kept (correctly — the meta-check would fail a stale declaration only if the tree started arming, which it does not).

title: hic: ::h/value on a file input silently reads C:\fakepath\<first file>, not the files
description:
THE FOURTH OF THE SHAPE. rf2-42vlw, rf2-u2tza and rf2-n71ma were dispatched as a
three-bug cluster in the prop/attribute pipeline. This is a fourth member of the
same family that nobody had filed, found while fixing rf2-42vlw.

THE DEFECT. impl.intent/target-value lowers ::h/value to (.-value target). On an
<input type="file">, HTMLInputElement.value is in FILENAME MODE: it answers
"C:\fakepath\" followed by the FIRST selected file's name. So
[:app/upload ::h/value] on a file input is a correct-looking expression that
quietly means something else — it names one file out of however many were
chosen, the path is a deliberate fiction the spec mandates for privacy, and
nothing downstream can open it or turn it back into a File. Exactly rf2-42vlw's
shape: a plausible non-empty string that is not the answer, with no refusal and
no warning anywhere.

ALREADY WITNESSED, NOT YET RULED. PR #8180 recorded it —
implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs, file-input-is-uncontrollable, the
w.record('file-input-marker-reading', ...) block asserting
'names-the-first-file-only' and 'is-not-the-file-list'. It is a RECORD rather
than a w.eq, so no row goes red either way, and no bead carried it.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED ALONGSIDE rf2-42vlw. The select-multiple repair was a
correction — ::h/value already meant "the control's current value" and a
multi-select's current value is its selection. This one is not the same move.
The guide rules the file input OUT of the marker's surface on purpose:
04-controlled-inputs.md:17 "File inputs use h/fn because the platform owns their
value", and the supported-controls table's File input row reads "no controlled
value | :on-change with h/fn, reading .files". Making ::h/value answer a FileList
would WIDEN the marker onto a control the design deliberately excluded, so it is
a design question rather than a bug fix.

THE OPTIONS, not ruled on: (a) a source-located refusal when ::h/value is
lowered at a control whose tag/type is input/file — which mints an error id and
therefore owes a spec/009-Instrumentation.md row, the same hot-zone dependency
that blocks rf2-u2tza, so the two should be sequenced together into one
spec-owning dispatch; (b) let the marker answer .files, which contradicts the
taught h/fn path above and widens the surface; (c) rule it authored-around and
say so in dispositions.md 2.3's File input row, which reads "Owed | Owed" today.

(a) plus (c) is the cheap combination, and the refusal sentence is nearly written
already by the guide's own line.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8205 REOPENED (2026-08-14). The implementation chose and correctly shipped option (a), the source-located ::h/value refusal, but left this bead's option (c) explicitly owed. Section 2.3's sole File input disposition still says only that React/the platform refuses a controlled :value; it says nothing about ::h/value now refusing at impl.intent/target-value, and it cites only the old testbed record rather than file_input_value_dom_cljs_test.

The PR's claimed owner worker/refusals-cfriw had already merged as PR #8201 before #8205 landed, so no live owner will absorb the follow-through. Amend the existing File input row in place to cover :rf.error/hicasso-file-input-value-marker and its focused witness, alongside rf2-u2tza's prop half. Do not invent a new table or broader upload abstraction; the guide already teaches h/fn/.files and the catalogue's `Taught in —` remains honest.
close_reason:
Re-closed on all three checks (mayor, 2026-08-14), same reasoning as rf2-u2tza. (a) DELIVERABLE on main via PR #8205 — ::h/value on a file input now refuses with a source-located id rather than silently handing over the fakepath string. (b) OBLIGATIONS: zero markers. (c) SIBLING rf2-h6qm7 is a new audit finding about CASE-SENSITIVITY in the shared predicate, not a reversal of this repair.

WORTH KEEPING FROM THAT WORK, because it is the reasoning a later reader will need: the normative spec tree has NO Hicasso feature Spec — spec/009's own Hicasso section says so and names the emitting function as the emit-site of record. So the deciding authority was the design record, and it was explicit: the guide rules file inputs out of the marker's surface because the platform owns their value, and the posture is that UNSUPPORTED CONTROLLED SHAPES ARE REJECTED RATHER THAN APPROXIMATED. That is what ruled out answering with .files, which would have widened the API against the taught design.

TWO IDS RATHER THAN ONE, and the reason is durable: different seam, different phase, and decisively DIFFERENT RECOVERY — delete a prop versus replace a marker. The catalogue carries one recovery value per row, so a single id could not have carried both honestly.

title: gate-classifier meta-check: every tracked tree must classify to >=1 output or sit on a declared prose-only list
description:
Found by the 2026-08-14 20-PR gating audit (machinery pass, findings N5+N4). The repeated incident shape in this repo is a NEW directory landing dark — five recorded instances: implementation/hicasso (rf2-hic-001), both codemod trees, implementation/ssr-node, story feature-load (rf2-65ajl). check_gate_scheduling.py covers commands-not-trees; _changed-surfaces.test.cjs pins KNOWN arms only; nothing asserts coverage of the tree itself. Proposal: ONE harness test in _changed-surfaces.test.cjs that walks git ls-files' top-level + second-level directories, classifies a representative path from each, and fails if a tree classifies to zero outputs and is not on an explicit declared prose-only allowlist (docs/, ai/, .beads/, spec prose already partially armed, etc.). This is NOT the rf2-6ng7-rejected input-declaration checker (that was a second hand-maintained model of gate INPUTS; this asserts tree CLAIM, a much cheaper invariant with no per-gate maintenance).

Supporting file-level evidence (N4, fix alongside or note as accepted): .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py classifies to NOTHING — the alerting wire's own edits get no PR-time proof; the in-run self-test (expensive-tests.yml:648) bounds the exposure at one nightly cycle, but the failure mode is the alarm channel itself. Weigh whether the meta-check should also cover .github/scripts/*.py surfaces or whether that stays a declared hole.
notes: FENCE CLEARED 2026-08-14 22:57 AUSEST (mayor backlog reread). PR #8242 (worker/armfix-cujx) has MERGED, carrying rf2-cujx, rf2-1gycj and rf2-7v5vx. The classifier surface it held -- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh, implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, .github/workflows/test.yml -- is free. DISPATCHED NOW as a four-bead cluster with rf2-sk5hf, rf2-n4a2b, rf2-in6c4 and rf2-skvce under one owner, because all four touch that same surface and two workers on it conflict by construction. WHAT #8242 CHANGED THAT YOU MUST RE-DERIVE AGAINST: it did NOT fix the arming. It removed the CONDITIONALITY, adding an unconditional jvm-repo-source-walks job wired into all-required-passed, with the classifier byte-unchanged and the census identical before and after. So a bead here that assumes the repair must be an arming change is reasoning from the superseded shape -- the fourth shape is available and is usually cheaper. Note also the job runs ONE STEP PER NAMESPACE rather than one -n list, because a missing namespace inside a multi--n selector is SILENT (exit 0, runs the rest, no warning); preserve that property in anything you add to it.
close_reason: PR #8256 — the tree-claim meta-check landed in PR #8189 and passes (two tests: every tracked tree arms an output or is DECLARED, and every DECLARED tree plus its named coverage still exists). THE OPEN QUESTION IS RULED, inside the bead, without the operator: .github/scripts/*.py STAYS A DECLARED FILE-LEVEL HOLE; the meta-check stays tree-level. Three findings, each checked at source. (1) The cheap PR-time repair costs a MECHANISM, which is the signal rf2-6ng7's (c)-narrow ruling names for leaving a hole declared: the right semantic home is verify-skill-mcp-drift, the always-on pure-stdlib spine that took check_gate_scheduling.py for exactly this reason, and every step in it is audited by scripts/check_ci_reproduce_commands.py for a single-line 'run: python scripts/check_<name>.py' with a matching check_* id — nightly_failure_alert.py is at .github/scripts/ and is not a check_*, so a step there means teaching that guard a new path shape. The other always-on job, verify-readme-links, would take it without a fight and is a markdown-slug job; a checker parked in an unrelated job is how the next reader loses it. (2) THE EXPOSURE IS SMALLER THAN THE FINDING SAID: the self-test is continue-on-error so the live arm still tries, and the re-raise still ends the nightly RED the same night, so what is at risk is one night's tracking-issue edit and not the signal. (3) File-level is the rejected option (a) in a new costume — a second hand-maintained model, of files, nagging on every README/.gitignore/image. RE-MEASURED rather than assumed: the self-test is 0.19s, exit 0, pure stdlib, and the expensive-tests.yml:648 citation is exact. It is cheap; it is the HOME that is not free. The reasoning is written into the comment beside the check so it cannot be re-litigated from scratch. Gate: classifier suite 376 passed, exit 0.

title: correction-ledger: two rows cite pre-rebase AUTHORED SHAs for PR #8088, and the gate cannot see them
description:
FOUND BY rf2-d7nps's keeper pass (2026-08-14) and DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED THERE. That bead's scope was two rows and their terminal states, and it says in terms: if a third row looks stale, report it rather than fixing it in the same pass, because a keeper pass that quietly widens is how a ledger stops being trustworthy. So this is filed instead.

THE DEFECT. docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md's rf2-jljf row and rf2-lu0s row each cite a LANDED commit that is not one. PR #8088 rebase-merged as TWO commits on main:

  ce3ea7a730  docs(hicasso): state the four event-value shapes on the public door
