title: hic: a kebab KEYWORD prop on a custom element lands camelCased, so the dashed attribute the author wrote never appears
description:
MEASURED by rf2-hic-040 in Chromium 147.0.7727.15, Firefox 148.0.2 and WebKit 26.4, all three agreeing.

THE DEFECT. impl.slot/prop-name camelCases every kebab keyword except aria-*, data-* and --custom-property. That is right for HTML and right for SVG, where React maps camelCase back to the presentation attribute. It is wrong for a CUSTOM ELEMENT, because React 19 has no name table for one: it passes an unknown prop through as an attribute under the name it was given. So [:x-widget {:my-other-attr "v"}] lands as the attribute 'myotherattr' (HTML lower-cases attribute names) and never as 'my-other-attr'. A custom element reading its own dashed attribute - which is what observedAttributes conventionally names - sees nothing.

WITNESSED in the direction the runtime behaves, so the row reds either way: implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs, custom-element-attributes. The two spellings that DO survive are witnessed beside it: a STRING key, which prop-name takes verbatim, and data-*, which the rule exempts outright.

NOTHING REFUSES AND NOTHING WARNS. dispositions.md HS-04 already records the SSR side of this correctly ('a custom element passing dashed attributes through verbatim') - that row is about the string spelling, and the keyword spelling is the one nobody had asked.

THE OPTIONS, not ruled on: (a) leave it and TEACH the string spelling for custom elements, which is what dispositions.md section 2.3 records today and is defensible - the escape already exists and costs nothing; (b) exempt a DASHED TAG from camelCasing in the codec, which is a tag-dependent slot rule and would break impl.slot/prop-name's purity - it is a pure function of the KEY, and the [:>] migration codemod on the JVM asks it without a tag; (c) a lint-time or dev-time diagnostic. Option (b) is the one to be careful of: prop-name's namespace docstring states the purity as load-bearing.

Low priority deliberately: the workaround is one character, and this is not a silent WRONG ANSWER the way rf2-42vlw is - the attribute is simply not the one written.
notes:
DECLINED at source, with the spec checked first (worker propbugs-42vlw, 2026-08-14). Recommend closing as authored-around; left open for the mayor's ruling.

THE SPEC IS UNRULED HERE, AND WHAT IS WRITTEN DOWN DESCRIBES TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR. dispositions.md 2.3's 'Custom elements' row reads 'Owed | Owed' - no support-or-refusal policy, no witness. The only thing the guide states is the general rule, with no custom-element carve-out: 02-views-and-reads.md:184 'Kebab-case becomes camelCase, so :on-click becomes onClick. :aria-*, :data-*, and CSS custom properties beginning -- pass through.' HS-04 is about the STRING spelling ('a custom element passing dashed attributes through verbatim'), and the string escape is taught twice for exactly this - 10-native-tier.md:120 and lanes/ergonomics-api.md:53, both 'String keys pass verbatim.' So option (b) would not be fixing a spec violation; it would be inventing a semantics the spec has not ruled, which is the one thing a bug fix must not do.

THE COST IS ALSO REAL, AND LARGER THAN THE BEAD'S SUMMARY. Three things, not one:

1. canonical-slot IS cached-prop-name, and codec.cljs states the identity as the mechanism: 'the thing a deny asks is the thing the emitter will do'. Every deny, dissoc and structural-slot check asks it WITHOUT a tag. A tag-dependent emitter makes the emitted name and the asked name differ for dashed keys on dashed tags.

2. prop-cache is keyed by (name k) ALONE and is process-global. A tag-dependent answer cannot use it, and codec.cljs already documents what sharing one entry between two answers does: it 'would make canonical-slot answer differently depending on what had rendered first, which is exactly the order dependence the owned-literal law exists to remove.' So option (b) needs a cache bypass on every custom-element prop.

3. The [:>] migration codemod asks slot/prop-name on the JVM without a tag. Making the runtime tag-aware and leaving the codemod tag-blind reproduces the exact defect slot.cljc exists to delete - 'a corpus pins the tool, a DOM suite pins the runtime, and nothing pins them equal'. Giving prop-name a 2-arity keeps purity but does not close this: the codemod would have to learn tags too.

For a P3 whose workaround is one character (a string key), against a rule the guide states plainly and a disposition row that is Owed, that is over-engineering. Option (c), a lint/dev diagnostic, is a nag diagnostic and is rejected on the same stance.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: a ruling on dispositions.md 2.3's Custom elements row. If the project decides Hicasso should adopt something like Freehand's declared mechanism - spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:667, '(v/custom-element tag {:properties #{...}})', an explicit property/attribute split rather than a blanket pass-through - then this stops being a codec patch and becomes a designed surface, and the cost above is paid for something.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS AUTHORED-AROUND, on the worker's recommendation and the stance (mayor, 2026-08-14).

THE BEHAVIOUR IS REAL: a kebab keyword prop on a custom element lands camelCased, so the dashed attribute never appears. A string key and data-* both survive.

WHY IT IS NOT WORK. The disposition row reads Owed and the guide states today's behaviour, so a fix would INVENT unruled semantics rather than restore ruled ones. The workaround is one character — use a string key.

AND THE COST IS LARGER THAN THE BEAD'S SUMMARY, measured at source by the worker: canonical-slot IS cached-prop-name and is asked everywhere without a tag; prop-cache is keyed by name alone and is process-global, so a tag-dependent answer needs a cache bypass; and the JVM codemod asks prop-name tag-blind. Making the answer depend on the element tag reproduces the exact tool-versus-runtime divergence slot.cljc exists to delete.

THAT IS OVER-ENGINEERING FOR A ONE-CHARACTER WORKAROUND. 'Not over-engineering or gold-plating' and 'trust the programmer' both point the same way here. Reopen if the naming packet or a ruling makes dashed custom-element attributes normative — at that point it becomes restoring a ruled semantics rather than inventing one, and the cost is worth paying.

I RE-CLOSED THIS WRONGLY, THREE TIMES, AND A WORKER FOUND IT (mayor, 2026-08-14).

The notes carried an explicit obligation added AFTER that deliverable landed: keep this requirements-mine owner open until the false premises are corrected there. rf2-gvysu had also been closed as a duplicate OF this bead. So both owners were closed while all three false rows were still on main, and the work was stranded until the rf2-records-gvysu worker read both beads and reopened.

THE DISTINCTION I COLLAPSED, which is the lesson: verifying a deliverable is NOT checking for unmet obligations. My own backlog-reread rule says to grep the notes for AUDIT-REOPEN, unmet and obligation before re-closing anything, and I substituted the easier check — does the thing this bead was filed to produce exist on main. Both are necessary. A bead can have its original deliverable landed and still carry a later obligation that keeps it open, and the second is invisible to a source check on the first.

AND THE REPETITION ITSELF WAS EVIDENCE. A bead that reopens three times is not behaving like a flag flipping; something was actively holding it open. I read the repetition as noise rather than signal.

title: hic: CHECKPOINT 3's own §2 sabotage family was not re-run - four independent sabotages outstanding
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. This row is filed by the
checkpoint against ITSELF, so the final audit sees the omission rather than
inferring it from a silence.

rf2-hic-038's §2 Correctness asks for a clean-checkout re-run of the three-way
matrix and the bundle gate, and FOUR independent sabotages: the bundle-rent gate,
one frame/store lifecycle row, one HMR-residue row, and one server-refusal row.

NONE WAS TAKEN. Three workers were live, one inside a long spine run; the bead's
own fence gated this section on a free box and the box was not free; and the
operator's standing direction (recorded on rf2-w01c) defers measurement so
implementation can proceed. The hicasso bundle gate is reachable only through a
full :advanced release build, and the sabotage families need the browser lane.

## What this omission can and cannot do, stated exactly

It is ONE-DIRECTIONAL with respect to the verdict. A sabotage that fails to redden,
or a re-run that fails, ADDS a finding. Neither can turn an unaddressed clause into
a met one. Checkpoint 3's verdict is "Phase 3 exit NOT MET", reached on documentary
facts no execution could reverse — C7 carries no reading and no re-run creates one.
So the un-taken work cannot have produced that verdict; what it could have produced
is MORE misses than the twelve filed.

## What WAS done in its place, and it is weaker

Documentary existence checks only. Every sabotage target was confirmed to EXIST:
the two-languages fence carries its matched pair ({:on-click [:fence/go]} ordinary
on one side, refusing on the other, so an implementation with either language
leaked into the other fails one half or the other); the bundle gate carries four
reachable positive controls plus a self-test; the lifecycle and server-refusal rows
carry in-suite armed and disarmed halves. EXISTENCE IS MET; REDDENING IS
UNADDRESSED.

## Surface fence

None — this bead runs gates and writes one ledger cell. It edits no product code.
Its worker MUST NOT be whoever authored the artefacts being sabotaged.

## Acceptance

On a quiet box, from a clean checkout of main:
1. npm run build:hicasso-release (three-way matrix's bundle half + the rent gate),
   captured exit code quoted;
2. the four independent sabotages, each planted BY THE RUNNER rather than read from
   an in-suite control: bundle-rent (plant a native sentinel into the interpreted
   entry and show the gate reds naming it), one frame/store lifecycle row, one
   HMR-residue row, one server-refusal row;
3. each sabotage restored and the restore verified byte-identical with
   git hash-object against the committed object;
4. the result — date, section, the landed main commit, what was run, the outcome —
   written into this row's Closure evidence cell in
   docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md.

A sabotage that does NOT redden is a new correctness finding and gets its own bead.

title: hic: re-frame.hicasso.native's public var surface is unclassified, and Phase 3 would freeze an unstated membership
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. §3 Quality, and the
naming fragment (docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-findings-cp3.md, row C3-1).

specification.md §12 has Phase 3 freeze "the grammar and ABI"; specification.md
:137 says Phase 3 "freezes the grammar and ABI only when every row of the
canonical native-tier checklist passes". A freeze is a deterministic act over a
stated membership. The native namespace's membership is not stated.

Fourteen vars are public in re-frame.hicasso.native. Five have naming-ledger rows
(n/$ row 7, n/props row 8, n/defcomponent row 9, n/use-sub + n/use-frame row 10,
n/memo + n/lazy row 29). SEVEN have no row and no classification:

  n/prop-slots (:194), n/check-child! (:242), n/el (:299), n/props* (:316),
  n/declared-server (:357), n/component (:470), n/marker (:512)

They are not uniform in kind, which is the point:
- n/component and n/marker read as SURFACE — a witness mints through
  (n/component "app/hot-cell" :client-only island-body) by name, and n/marker is
  the seam every ABI helper and both embedding directions read.
- n/el says of itself "reached from an [[$]] expansion".
- n/prop-slots is asserted as a PUBLIC EQUALITY against the macro's own emission
  (native_grammar_cljs_test.cljs, the-macro-and-the-runtime-share-one-rule-rather-
  than-two-copies) — a good property, but it is why the var cannot simply be made
  private without thought.

So the set spans doors, seams and expansion targets with nothing marking which is
which. This repository already applies the opposite rule elsewhere: a facade export
is classified and justified when it lands.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed here

A checkpoint that edited the surface it audits could not certify it. The
classification is also a judgement about what the tier's public contract IS, which
belongs with the naming packet (rf2-hic-065) rather than with a reviewer.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc (defn -> defn- only
  where the classification says internal; NO behaviour change)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md (rows for whatever is ruled surface)
- implementation/hicasso/test/ (only where a test reaches a var that becomes
  private and needs a supported route instead)

NOTE: implementation/hicasso/ may be held by another worker's fence. Check first.
DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md.

## Acceptance

Every public var in re-frame.hicasso.native is classified as surface or internal,
with one line of justification each; the internal ones are made private or moved
behind the package's existing impl convention, except where a macro expansion must
be able to name them, which is stated as the reason; and the surface ones have
naming-ledger rows so rf2-hic-065's packet is complete. No name is RENAMED by this
bead — classification only, per the no-renaming-mid-flow rule.
notes: Post-merge audit of PR #8184 (054536cfcccdf9098681844ec52e4d932ca0cc39, merged 2026-08-14T01:50:37Z): the source-location and compile-time expansion work is correct, and the exact Hicasso Node and production-erasure gates pass. rf2-e0d2 is incomplete on its own acceptance. That acceptance requires internal vars to be private or behind the existing impl convention, except where a macro expansion must name them. The PR classifies n/prop-slots as INTERNAL, explicitly proves that no expansion names it, yet leaves it public solely so native_grammar_cljs_test can call the rule directly. Test reach is not a public-API reason, especially during a Phase 3 surface freeze. Bounded repair: make prop-slots private or move it behind the existing internal convention and keep the parity evidence through supported expansion/runtime behavior or a same-implementation test seam. Do not add a new abstraction or reopen the otherwise sound source-location/expansion work.
close_reason:
Re-closed after BOTH checks, not just one (mayor, 2026-08-14). Comment-less status flip. (a) DELIVERABLE verified on main: native.cljc carries the classification table and check-child! is private; PR #8184 MERGED. (b) OBLIGATIONS: zero markers in the notes — no AUDIT-REOPEN, no unmet, no keep-open. (c) SIBLINGS: no other open bead holds this work.

I am naming all three checks because I got this wrong today on rf2-d6ai8: I verified the deliverable, skipped the notes, and re-closed a bead whose notes carried an explicit obligation — stranding work until a worker found it. Verifying a deliverable is not checking for obligations.

WHAT SHIPPED: ten surface vars and four internal-but-public classified one line each in the docstring, check-child! made private, and native_surface_cljs_test pinning membership against the compiler's census AND checking the internal half's licence by reading the expansions that name el, props*, declared-server and component. Ledger rows 43-46.

TWO THINGS RECORDED FOR THE OPERATOR SITTING rather than decided here: n/prop-slots stays PUBLIC against C3-1's recommended disposition, because no expansion names it so the expansion-target licence does not apply and what buys its publicity is the three-way parity witness — making it private would delete the property C3-1 itself calls good, and it is naming-ledger row 46 so the sitting can overrule deliberately. And the namespace has FIFTEEN public vars rather than fourteen: n/tier-sentinel was absent from CHECKPOINT 3's census, which is exactly the unstated-membership freeze this bead existed to prevent.

title: hic: outward-bridge hydration mismatch attribution is unreachable by construction (no Spec 011 reporter)
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. ROW 5 (Server and
hydration), §2 Correctness.

Row 5 requires every native surface to satisfy its row "including server bytes or
source refusal, matching hydration, MISMATCH ATTRIBUTION and multiple roots".

The native tier's own SSR rows are the best-evidenced part of the row: HS-24 to
HS-30 are witnessed through real react-dom/server bytes on BOTH policy arms by
native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, and that file records the defect it was written
against — a Client-only island appearing in the server bytes because the recorded
:server policy was consulted by nothing (rf2-u9lk, rf2-ggnp) — as found and fixed.
Checkpoint 3 searched specifically for a semantic-tree claim standing in for
server bytes and found none anywhere.

MISMATCH ATTRIBUTION for the OUTWARD BRIDGE is a different matter, and it is not a
missing test — it is unsatisfiable without a door. HS-21's bytes half is proved
(native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:124, renderToStaticMarkup). But an outward-bridged root
is built by the CONSUMER'S own createElement, so impl.mount/hydrate-root! cannot
adopt it, and a hand-rolled hydrateRoot installs no Spec 011 reporter. There is
therefore no path by which a mismatch inside a bridged subtree is attributed to
source.

Root cause, shared with two other open gaps: THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY.
Every server witness in the package calls react-dom/server's renderToString by
hand — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in terms ("There is no Hicasso server
entry... the only server path in the package"). Row 5 is therefore proved against
a hand-rolled harness rather than a shipped door.

## Not this bead's, and named so they are not duplicated

- HS-11/HS-14 (root/frame provider Client-only under a measured, unrepaired
  obstruction: the package's only server path emits no counterpart to the adoption
  closer, so a tree minting a useId hydrates into an id mismatch).
- HS-33 (motion/presence measured to satisfy NEITHER policy, repair decided and
  unlanded).
Both are outside the native tier and already carried. Checkpoint 3 files nothing
against them.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs and/or impl/roots.cljs
  (only if a door is the chosen route)
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_cljs_test.cljs
- docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md HS-21 row

DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md.

## Acceptance

EITHER a hydration path for an outward-bridged root that installs the Spec 011
reporter, with a deliberate-mismatch row attributing to source; OR a source-located
statement on HS-21 that mismatch attribution is out of reach for a consumer-built
root, with row 5's required-result sentence amended to scope "mismatch attribution"
to roots the package itself adopts. The second is a defensible line — the consumer
owns that root — but it must be written down rather than left as an unmet clause.
notes:
MAYOR 2026-08-21 01:00 AUSEST — NOT DISPATCHED, AND THE REASON HAS CHANGED. The earlier note said "not dispatched this tick because six workers are live... dispatch on the next free slot". A slot is free now. I read the bead instead of taking it, and it splits into two halves that do not belong to the same person.

THE FENCE QUESTION IS SETTLED AND THE ANSWER IS PARALLEL-SAFE. That note asked whether spec/011 collides with spec/009 in the hot zone. Measured at CLAUDE.md:91 today: the hot-zone list is an ENUMERATION of eight named spec pages — 002-Frames, 005-StateMachines, 006-ReactiveSubstrate, 009-Instrumentation, API, Conventions, Spec-Schemas, Tool-Pair. spec/011-SSR.md is NOT among them, so this bead never needed to queue behind a spec/009 toucher. That fence was over-broad, not wrong, and it is now retired.

WHY IT STILL DOES NOT GO OUT. The bead's own surface fence says "implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs and/or impl/roots.cljs (ONLY IF A DOOR IS THE CHOSEN ROUTE)". Whether to ship a door is the question, not the work. The bead's stated root cause is THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY — every server witness in the package calls react-dom/server's renderToString by hand, and native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs says so in terms. Adding a shipped server entry is a PUBLIC-SURFACE product decision for Mike, not a bounded fix, and dispatching a worker at an undecided design is how a migration gets performed on a false premise.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, so the operator half is not overstated: the HS-21 half was handled by rf2-vwo53 (PR #8559). Its worker amended the dispositions.md row to STATE THE SCOPE AND ITS MEASURED WITNESS and deliberately did NOT upgrade it, because rf2-s52w's own close record confirmed the finding rather than repairing it. So the record is truthful today; what is missing is the capability, not the description of it.

FOR MIKE — THE DECISION AND ITS COST. Does Hicasso ship a server entry? Today mismatch attribution inside an outward-bridged subtree is unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION: the consumer's own createElement builds the root, impl.mount/hydrate-root! cannot adopt it, and a hand-rolled hydrateRoot installs no Spec 011 reporter. COST OF THE HOLD: Checkpoint 3's row 5 stays proved against a hand-rolled harness rather than a shipped door, and two other open gaps (HS-11/HS-14 and HS-33, both already carried elsewhere) share the same root cause. Nothing is broken while it waits and no other bead is blocked behind it.
AUDIT 2026-08-21 13:40 AUSEST (rf2-s52w audit pass, read-only). Filed rf2-0brem — the last undischarged clause of THIS bead's acceptance option B (row 5's required-result sentence). Verdict and the other premise corrections follow in the next note.
AUDIT VERDICT 2026-08-21 13:45 AUSEST — read-only pass on origin/main@94f23109d2. LEFT OPEN
DELIBERATELY: the operator hold in the 2026-08-21 01:00 note stands, but the question it asks
is stale and is re-put below. THE FINDING IS REAL AND THREE OF THIS BEAD'S FOUR PREMISES ARE
WRONG AT THE CURRENT TIP. 0 correctness defects. Filed rf2-0brem and rf2-981ka.

P1 "no Spec 011 reporter" — FALSE AS WRITTEN. Spec 011 defines the reporter for exactly this
tier: spec/011-SSR.md:811 (Hydration-mismatch detection), :825 (the adoption channel for
React-element roots), :846-856 (the trace shape). Hicasso implements it —
impl/mount.cljs:363 emit-hydration-mismatch!, :380 hydration-reporter, :415
hydrate-root-options, installed at :546 inside hydrate-root!. What the BODY of this bead says
— "a hand-rolled hydrateRoot installs NO Spec 011 reporter" — is the true statement, and it is
a statement about WHO OPENED THE ROOT. (correction-ledger.md:89 cites mount.cljs:427-447 and
hydrate-root!:560; those numbers have drifted to 380-412 and 546. Not filed — minutiae.)

P2 "attribution unreachable for a consumer-built root" — TRUE, AND MEASURED, AND THE WITNESS
SURVIVES THE ANTI-VACUITY TEST. onRecoverableError is an option of an INDIVIDUAL hydrateRoot
(impl/roots.cljs:20-27 builds the whole per-root design on that). native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs
:891 consumer-element (deliberately not reaching impl.mount/tree), :920 the deftest, :952 the
CONTROL run FIRST asserting exactly one diagnostic through the package's own door, :1013 the
measurement (= [] seen). I applied the mechanical test — delete the signal, keep the fault —
and it holds: removing the reporter install from hydrate-root! reddens :952, so the row cannot
stay green on a broken mechanism. The zero is additionally bounded below by three live readings
in its own arm (the server bytes really said "#7 server"; React really recovered to
"#7 client", awaited rather than assumed; the console really captured the complaint). AND the
listener is not shared — watch-mismatches! (roots_frames_support.cljs:424) mints a gensym key
per call, so the second watch is a fresh registration, which was the specific way this row
could have been vacuous. It is the good version of the pattern, not the bad one.

P3 "unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION" — OVERSTATED, AND THE OVERSTATEMENT IS WHAT KEEPS GENERATING
THE FINDING. The boundary is not the outward bridge; it is which renderer opened the root, and
the bridge is not special in it. TWO re-frame2 doors install a root-scoped Spec 011 reporter on
a React-element root: h/hydrate! (impl/mount.cljs:546) and the Spec 006 client mount entry
(re-frame.substrate.adapter/render tree mount {:hydrate? true}) at spine.cljs:1107, whose
docstring at :1191-1204 names itself the only native mount route that installs it and repeats
Spec 011's boundary sentence verbatim. onRecoverableError fires for recoverable errors ANYWHERE
in that root's tree, so a consumer whose app is mounted through the Spec 006 door with a
Hicasso view bridged in under mount/provider would get :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch for a text
divergence inside the bridged subtree — tagged :where re-frame.substrate.spine/make-render
rather than Hicasso's site, but emitted. REASONED FROM REACT'S ROOT-OPTION CONTRACT PLUS THE
TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS; NOT MEASURED FOR THE BRIDGED CASE, and not claimed as measured — no suite
renders Hicasso under a UIx parent at all (rf2-ap7w's subject). The accurate wording is the one
spec/011-SSR.md:825 already uses: attribution is scoped to roots a re-frame2 door opens.

P4 "root cause: THERE IS NO HICASSO SERVER ENTRY" — FALSE AT TIP, AND IRRELEVANT EVEN WHERE IT
WAS TRUE. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs (452 lines,
re-frame.hicasso.server/render) landed in commit 30317bfe0e on 2026-08-14 21:28 +1000
(rf2-b6jkj, PR #8236) — about seven hours after this bead was filed and a week before the
2026-08-21 note that repeats the claim. It is a real door: impl/roots.cljs:50-58 names it one
of the TWO minters of the adoption window, "once per REQUEST, closed in that door's finally",
the fork decided once for both sides of the wire. The rest of the tree already describes it as
shipped (naming-ledger.md rows 22 and 50, invariants.md:85, globals.md:192,
architecture-census.md:168, dispositions.md:336, docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md,
api-reference.md:376). AND THE PREMISE IS IRRELEVANT: a server entry produces BYTES; the
reporter is a CLIENT root option. No server door of any design can install an option on a root
the consumer opens on the client. The two facts were never causally linked. The stale sentence
that produced the claim is native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66 — filed as rf2-981ka.

ACCEPTANCE STATUS — option B is 2/3 discharged. (a) source-located statement plus measured
witness: DONE, PR #8302 / 473ff5e330. (b) dispositions.md:290 HS-21 row amended: DONE
2026-08-20 by rf2-vwo53 / PR #8559. (c) row 5's required-result sentence scoped: OWING, and no
bead owned it — now rf2-0brem. Its two homes are hot-path-architecture.md:49 (the native tier's
only release checklist) and, the one that actually creates the obligation,
react-compatibility-notes.md:34's blanket sentence "Every Render row runs the common hydration
states: matching content, deliberate mismatch with source attribution, ...". The matrix ROW for
Root/frame provider and outward bridge (:24) omits mismatch attribution, so that omission is
not a carve-out — the blanket sentence puts it back on every Render row.

THE OPERATOR QUESTION, RE-PUT. The 2026-08-21 note asks "Does Hicasso ship a server entry?" —
it does, since 2026-08-14, and it would not have helped. The live question is narrower: SHOULD
THE PACKAGE EXPOSE A WAY FOR A ROOT THE CONSUMER OPENED TO CARRY THE FRAMEWORK REPORTER?
RECOMMENDATION: NO. (1) A consumer who wants the diagnostic already has two doors — h/hydrate!,
or the Spec 006 adapter render with {:hydrate? true} if their app is React-rooted. Trusting the
programmer means letting them mount through a door rather than shipping a second mechanism for
not doing so. (2) It is not the one-liner it looks like: exporting hydration-reporter alone
would emit NOTHING, because the emit is gated on roots/adopting? and a consumer-built tree
carries no adoption window and no adoption-window-closer, so the flag reads closed —
impl/roots.cljs:59-64 states exactly this for a hand-rolled renderToString. A real door means
publishing the window, the closer and the option-builder, which naming-ledger.md row 50 already
flags as "a larger decision" (making impl.mount/tree and impl.roots/open-adoption-window!
public). (3) Nothing is broken: React still complains on its own channel and the divergence is
a deterministic bug either way; what is missing is a TRACE, on a root the framework does not
own. If Mike wants it anyway it is a public-surface programme, not a bounded fix. rf2-0brem
does NOT wait on this ruling — the doc clause is true under either answer.

DECLINED, and why: no PR (read-only brief, and both candidate edits are the ledger keeper's
surface — native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs:48-52 states the principle, "a witness may not amend
the row it witnesses", which binds an auditor the same way); no third bead for the door (the
stance rejects the remedy, so a bead filed to be refused costs more than this recommendation);
no edit to correction-ledger.md (fenced out by this bead); no edit to checkpoint-3-native.md (a
dated checkpoint record — whether it is amended in place is the ledger keeper's convention, not
an auditor's); no bead for the drifted line numbers in correction-ledger.md:89.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS BEAD: Mike ruling on the door question above. rf2-0brem then discharges
the last acceptance clause independently. Nothing else on this bead is owed.
FOLLOW-ONS FILED BY THIS AUDIT (both name rf2-s52w as owner, so a later audit re-finding either recognises it as this bead's clause rather than a second finding): rf2-0brem — scope row 5's 'mismatch attribution' required result to roots a re-frame2 door opens (this bead's last acceptance clause; react-compatibility-notes.md:34 and hot-path-architecture.md:49). rf2-981ka — native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:66 still says 'there is no Hicasso server entry', false since 2026-08-14, and it is the sentence Checkpoint 3 cited that seeded this bead's P4 root cause. NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S TITLE: '(no Spec 011 reporter)' is false as written — Spec 011 defines the reporter and Hicasso installs it on its own doors. Title left unchanged because several committed docs cite this bead by id beside that phrasing; the P1 paragraph above is the correction. Returning to open — no worker holds it.

Reopen only on real consumer demand; then it is a public-surface programme, not a fix.

title: hic: no UIx parent renders Hicasso, and the inward three-route interop tree runs under a single frame
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. ROW 4 (Same-root
interop), §1 Completeness.

Row 4's required result: "Hicasso-native, UIx and raw React parents can render
Hicasso, and Hicasso can render each native route, without another root, frame or
state owner", with deciding evidence "BOTH EMBEDDING DIRECTIONS ACROSS TWO FRAMES,
retained callbacks, provider/compound components, errors and teardown".

The inward direction is complete and strong: all three routes declared as hosts in
ONE h/defview body, under one frame, in one commit, painting byte-identical
normalised outerHTML; plus both inward spellings (h/defhost and [:>]) in one body
with the raw-JS props ABI asserted across the crossing. Retained callbacks are the
best-instrumented rows in the tier (a memoising vendor that knows nothing about
Hicasso, nine carriers against one number, four of them controls, a liveness row
proving the grid can fail, and abandonment and reincarnation each with a negative
control beside it). Provider/compound, teardown and the no-second-owner claim are
all covered.

Two gaps:

1. NO UIx PARENT RENDERS HICASSO. h/as-component appears in exactly two test files
   repo-wide — native_abi_cljs_test.cljs and native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs — plus
   prose mentions. A native parent bridges on a fiber; a raw React parent bridges
   in the NODE lane only (server render, no fiber). defui appears in only two
   Hicasso test files and in both the UIx component is a CHILD reached through
   h/defhost, never a parent rendering a bridged view. So one of the three named
   parents is unlanded, and a second is never exercised on a real fiber.

2. "ACROSS TWO FRAMES" HOLDS FOR THE OUTWARD BRIDGE ONLY. two-frames-are-two-cells-
   across-the-bridge covers outward. The inward three-route tree runs under a
   single frame (::parity-dom). There is no two-frame run of the native /
   raw-React / UIx inward routes.

Thin, and recorded rather than separately filed: no error crossing involves a UIx
subtree, and none runs in the outward direction (a foreign parent catching a
Hicasso view's throw).

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/three_way_parity_dom_cljs_test.cljs

NOTE: implementation/hicasso/ may be held by another worker's fence. Check first.
DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md.

## Acceptance

A UIx parent (defui, built with uix/$) rendering an h/as-component bridge on a real
fiber, asserting what the native-parent row asserts — one cell under the
SURROUNDING frame, the prop round trip, and a write through the surrounding frame
reaching the bridged view, proving the bridge resolves no frame of its own. Plus
either a two-frame run of the inward three-route tree, or a stated reason the
single-frame run is sufficient given that the outward bridge already carries the
two-frame claim.
close_reason: PR #8194. UIx parent lands over the SAME minted bridge the native parent uses (a-uix-parent-mounts-the-same-view-under-the-frame-it-is-already-in): paint, decoded key set, one cell under the surrounding frame, write-through. The row's narrowing was corrected by measurement -- a planted :articleId left every assertion GREEN, because UIx's dash-to-camel sends :article-id and :articleId to the same articleId slot, so the bridge cannot tell them apart. The real narrowing is WHICH ABI arrives (UIx's #js {:argv props} carrier vs real React props), so the row asserts the key set. Second gap closed by two-frames-are-two-cells-through-the-inward-door-as-well -- a different mechanism from the outward two-frame row. The three-route parity tree keeps ONE frame with the reason at source: those routes are prop-fed, so a two-frame run there measures prop plumbing; and it cannot be made three-wide because a handwritten React component subscribes through no hook by construction.

title: hic: n/use-sub and n/use-frame have no witness under Suspense or under retry/abandonment
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. ROW 3 (Frame and store
lifecycle), §1 Completeness.

Row 3 names eight states. Five are covered with instruments that read what React
cannot forge — no-provider failure (both hooks, each naming itself, under a
fixture pinning :ambient-frame nil so the refusal cannot be faked), two frames,
frame replacement as same-id reincarnation, StrictMode double mount, and unmount
with exact cleanup. Two more are missing for the native hooks:

1. SUSPENSE. grep for Suspense in native_hooks_cljs_test.cljs and
   native_hooks_dom_cljs_test.cljs returns 0. The suspension-retention result
   exists twice — activity_suspense_dom_cljs_test.cljs and
   lazy_boundary_dom_cljs_test.cljs — and in both the suspending reader is an
   h/defview boundary reading h/sub, not an island. n/use-sub's docstring
   (native.cljc:813-818) rules AGAINST suspending on the store, but that is prose
   in the source rather than an executable refusal.

2. RETRY / ABANDONMENT. The rows exist at the boundary-shell tier only
   (kernel_commit_owns_dom_cljs_test.cljs: suspended-attempt-acquires-nothing,
   aborted-transition, body-that-throws-after-its-reads); that file requires no
   re-frame.hicasso.native. The one native throw/retry row —
   imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test.cljs:799 — drives an n/defcomponent that owns an
   SDK instance and calls NEITHER hook, so it prices SDK acquire/release, not
   hook subscription ownership across a retry. Closest partial is
   a-native-read-under-a-live-frame-answers-without-committing-anything, which
   covers the abandoned FIRST render from a server render rather than a
   concurrent-root abandonment.

Both results are therefore inherited BY ARGUMENT — the hooks resolve through the
same collector doors as the shell — rather than by measurement. The argument is
probably right. It is not a witness.

Also recorded, smaller: "frame replacement" is proven as same-id reincarnation
only. No row swaps a DIFFERENT frame keyword onto the provider above a live
island.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_hooks_dom_cljs_test.cljs
  (it already owns the lifecycle roster, the residue census and the
  declared-population assertion — new rows belong there)
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_hooks_cljs_test.cljs

NOTE: implementation/hicasso/ may be held by another worker's fence. Check first.
DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md.

## Acceptance

A native-hook row under Suspense (retention across suspension, exact ownership on
arrival) and one under a concurrent-root retry/abandonment (an abandoned attempt
acquires nothing; the retry acquires exactly once), each ending in the file's
teardown census as its siblings do — OR a pinned shared-substrate identity test
plus a source-located statement that the native hooks inherit these states by
construction, so the inheritance cannot silently stop holding. The
declared-population roster must be extended either way, since it is what makes the
file's coverage claim checkable.
close_reason:
PR #8195 (MERGED). Two rows on native_hooks_dom_cljs_test: W9 a POST-COMMIT suspension (island commits and subscribes, sibling suspends, ownership exact across the cycle - same count, same registration object), and W10 an ABANDONED attempt (gate throws on first render; React runs the island body, hooks and all, and discards it; the attempt acquires nothing, the retry acquires exactly once). Declared-population roster extended with :hooks/suspense-retention and :hooks/abandoned-attempt.

MEASURED, and it refuted the draft: RETENTION IS IN THE TABLES, NOT IN THE PAINT. A first draft polled 4s for the suspended island to repaint on a store write and timed out with residue {:cells 1 :cell-refs 1 :boundaries 1 :edges 1} - the subscription fully installed, React simply not rendering an Offscreen-hidden subtree inside a sync-lane flush. The row now asserts that as a ceiling instead of waiting on a schedule it cannot drive.

Also recorded: a RELEASE is not a nothing-owned census (the cell outlives the membership until its reaper), so W8 reads support/census while W10 keeps the all-zero constant.

Frame-replacement-with-a-DIFFERENT-keyword (the smaller item in the description) NOT done - out of this cluster's acceptance. File separately if wanted.

title: hic: the native-boundary law's 'nor UIx' clause has no executable gate on either side of the seam
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. ROW 6 (Dependency and
rent) and ROW 3's deciding evidence, §1 Completeness.

The native-boundary law reads: "an interpreted-only production dependency graph
and bundle contain neither native-tier runtime NOR UIX CODE". Row 6 restates it;
row 3's deciding evidence separately names "a dependency check proving NO UIX
IMPORT".

The native-tier half is gated superbly. check_bundle_isolation.cjs carries four
REACHABLE positive controls, a fail-closed empty-input check, a premise check that
reddens if a sentinel's source string is renamed, a self-test that plants each
sentinel and drops each control individually, and a too-eager battery of
shape-adjacent legal strings. check_optional_module_reachability.py parses ns
forms (never prose) and guards the native door edge, with both-direction
self-tests.

The UIx half is gated by NOTHING, on either side:

- The BUNDLE gate declines it explicitly and honestly (:113-135): "THE MEASURED
  BUNDLE CONTAINS UIx, and it is not a defect" — Hicasso ships no adapter, the
  exemplar picks UIx, so rf-uix-sub- is carried as a PRESENT CONTROL rather than
  a sentinel. It then refers the clause on: "that is the source-side gate's kind
  of question, not a bundle's. It is reported rather than quietly re-scoped."
- The SOURCE-side gate never asks it. Its `native` row comment quotes the law in
  full and calls itself "the DEPENDENCY-GRAPH half of that sentence", but the row
  guards one edge — nothing outside requires the door — and has no UIx assertion
  anywhere. Grep confirms: the only "uix" occurrence in the file is inside that
  quoted comment.

Each artefact is individually honest. The clause falls through the seam between
them. The property HOLDS TODAY — implementation/hicasso/src names UIx only in
docstrings, verified — but nothing reddens if it stops.

Second clause, no artefact at all: "native bundles contain no UIx unless the
application imports it". There is exactly one release build (:hicasso-release) and
it is the interpreted-only one, which deliberately installs the UIx adapter. No
native-tier release build exists.

A template for the missing gate already exists and was never pointed here:
implementation/scripts/check-ui-adapter-isolation.cjs is a genuine two-arm no-UIx
gate (module closure + clojure -Stree coordinate rejection, with a positive
control), scoped to day8/re-frame2-ui and containing zero hicasso mentions.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_optional_module_reachability.py
- implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_bundle_isolation.cjs (only its comments, if
  the referral sentence needs to name the new gate)
- implementation/hicasso/deps.edn
- implementation/package.json script wiring

DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md. .github/workflows/* is HOT ZONE — if CI wiring
is needed, flag and sequence.

## Acceptance

An executable assertion that no namespace under implementation/hicasso/src
requires UIx, with a positive control proving it reddens when one is added
(a planted require must fail the gate and name the namespace). If the second
clause is to be gated too, a native-tier release build is needed; if that is
judged not worth its cost, say so at source and amend row 6's second clause
rather than leaving it unmeasured.
notes: AUDIT PR #8194 (2026-08-14): Reopened after completeness/correctness/quality review. The new COORDINATE arm parses only Hicasso's literal top-level `:deps` map, not the resolved production dependency graph promised by native-boundary law clause 6 and matrix row 6. Evidence: `scan_forbidden_coordinates('{:deps {acme/wrapper {:local/root "../wrapper"}}}')` returns clean; any UIx coordinate declared by that wrapper is invisible because the checker never resolves or reads downstream dependencies. The repository's existing analogue, `implementation/scripts/check-ui-adapter-isolation.cjs`, uses `clojure -Stree` for this exact graph-vs-direct-declaration distinction. Bounded acceptance: resolve Hicasso's production dependency graph and reject transitive UIx coordinates, with a synthetic local-root wrapper whose own deps introduces UIx as the planted red and a real-graph positive control. Preserve the legal test-alias UIx dependency and the source arm; no native bundle or general dependency framework is needed. Focused gates passed: diff-check, checker/live and self-test, and `test:hicasso-invariants` (all exit 0).
close_reason:
Re-closed on all three checks (mayor, 2026-08-14). The single obligation-marker in its notes is a FALSE POSITIVE — the matched text reads 'careful filing is still filing, not a queue', which is CHECKPOINT 3's reasoning about its own verdict, not an obligation on this bead. (a) DELIVERABLE: PR #8194 MERGED, carrying the nor-UIx source-graph gate. (b) SIBLINGS: none hold it.

WORTH KEEPING FROM THAT WORK: the hypothesis that one piece of work would serve both this bead and rf2-ap7w was REFUTED at source. This is a source-graph claim over src/; ap7w is a runtime-fiber claim in test/. Test code requiring UIx is legal and that PR added more of it — so if anything the two pull apart, and more UIx in test/ makes it MORE important that this gate scopes to src/. Two separate small pieces was the honest answer.

title: hic: the native tier appears nowhere in the real HMR reload gate, and no single component crosses every wrapper
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. ROW 2 (Component ABI and
identity), §1 Completeness.

The row's required result ends "... display/source metadata and HMR", and its
deciding evidence is "ONE MATCHED COMPONENT exercised through EVERY wrapper and
ONE HMR REPLACEMENT CYCLE". Neither named artefact exists in the form stated.

1. HMR. The real reload gate is testbed/hmr_spec.cjs — eight sections driven by
   implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-hicasso-hmr-testbed.cjs rewriting the
   rf2-vsgq:HOT-LINE under a live shadow-cljs watch. It exercises NO native
   component. testbed/hicasso_hmr_testbed/views.cljs requires exactly ["react"],
   re-frame.core and re-frame.hicasso — grep -c "hicasso.native" returns 0 for
   both views.cljs and core.cljs. What is landed for the tier is
   a-fresh-mint-replaces-the-subtree-and-that-is-the-hmr-contract
   (native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs), which allocates a second component IN PROCESS
   and renders it in place of the first. The module is never re-evaluated and
   shadow-cljs is never involved. Its own comment calls this "The reload,
   performed" — which is the claim this bead disputes.

2. One matched component. Coverage is spread across FOUR distinct components:
   quote-cell* (memo, react/memo control, lazy), island-body (n/component, memo,
   defhost, [:>], simulated re-mint), "app/ref-cell" (ref), "app/arrived" (lazy
   arrival). The declared-population roster asserts ten MECHANISMS ran; it does
   not claim, and they did not, one component through ten wrappers.

Also unaddressed and folded in here: "there is no parallel fast ABI" is argued in
native.cljc's docstring (:981) and gated by nothing — no surface census would
redden if a second props door were added.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_hmr_testbed/views.cljs
- implementation/hicasso/testbed/hmr_spec.cjs
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_abi_dom_cljs_test.cljs

NOTE: implementation/hicasso/ is presently held by another worker's fence
(worker/transitions-hic045 at the time of filing). Check before dispatching.
DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md.

## Acceptance

The HMR half: one native component in the real reload gate, surviving a genuine
shadow recompile — the tier marker, displayName and :server policy still readable
after the save, and the subtree's ownership exact across it. The matched-component
half: one component carried through every wrapper the row names (defcomponent,
memo, lazy, ref, defhost, [:>], re-mint), or an explicit statement in the roster
that the population is per-mechanism by design, with the row's deciding-evidence
phrase amended to match.
close_reason: PR #8198, same fixture as rf2-y5x6j. PREMISE CONFIRMED and sharpened: the native tier appeared NOWHERE in the real HMR gate — hmr_remount has ZERO native mentions, not one, and hmr_spec.cjs's three are all nativeSet (the browser's value setter). One island now crosses every wrapper the row names: n/defcomponent -> n/memo -> n/lazy -> defhost AND [:>], with a callback :ref through both and the save's re-mint over the top. The tier marker, displayName and :server policy are asserted readable on the far side of the save, on objects that are all new. Ownership claimed on the whole retained census; the island deliberately holds no subscription (recorded at source) because a subscribing island would race React's scheduler against the runtime's reap horizon in every other section.

title: hic: no macro-expansion fixtures for n/$, and the compile-time refusal path is witnessed by nothing
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 3 (rf2-hic-038), main@f455316fbf, 2026-08-14. ROW 1 (Native-form
grammar), §1 Completeness.

The row's deciding evidence reads "MACRO-EXPANSION FIXTURES plus client DOM and
React server witnesses against handwritten createElement". Two of the three exist
and are strong (a nine-row matched corpus, byte equality under renderToString
against a literal react/createElement arm, plus a DOM lane). The macro-expansion
fixture leg does not exist in ANY form: no JVM lane in this artefact (deps.edn
says zero JVM tests is the correct outcome and waives the runner's floor), no
macroexpand/macroexpand-1 call anywhere under implementation/hicasso/, no golden
or snapshot expansion file, no lint-fixture carrying n/$ content.

The consequence is not cosmetic. native.cljc:968's `$` calls check-child! on the
child FORMS at expansion, and literal-props calls prop-slots at expansion — so a
literal hiccup vector in a native child position, or a literal colliding props
map, is a BUILD FAILURE. Every landed refusal row uses a let-bound local to force
the RUNTIME path instead. native.cljc's own declared-server docstring states the
gap: "this package has no JVM test lane at all, so a compile-time refusal would be
witnessed by nothing this repo runs."

So the grammar has two refusal paths and only one is witnessed.

## What is NOT owed

A byte-for-byte expansion snapshot. public_door_macros_cljs_test.cljs:24 records
that those were considered and rejected, and the substitute that landed —
the-macro-and-the-runtime-share-one-rule-rather-than-two-copies, asserting
three-way equality between macro emission, n/prop-slots and n/props* — is a
stronger property than a snapshot. This bead does not reopen that.

## Surface fence

- implementation/hicasso/deps.edn (only if a JVM test alias is the chosen route)
- implementation/hicasso/test/ (a new JVM lane, or a CLJS-side compile probe)
- implementation/hicasso/lint-fixtures/

DO NOT touch correction-ledger.md. Top-level implementation/deps.edn and
implementation/shadow-cljs.edn are HOT ZONE — if the route needs either, flag it
and sequence rather than editing in parallel with another worker.

## Acceptance

The compile-time refusal path is witnessed: a literal hiccup child and a literal
canonical-slot collision each shown to refuse AT EXPANSION with the right error id,
by whatever mechanism this repo can actually run — a small JVM lane for the macro
namespace, or a compile-probe build whose failure text is asserted. A stated,
source-located REFUSAL is also acceptable: if the artefact should stay JVM-testless
and the compile path is deliberately unwitnessed, say so in native.cljc and amend
row 1's deciding-evidence phrase so it no longer names a fixture that will never
exist.

title: dispatch-prompt-template.md:74-80 still scopes the THREE SENTENCES by prose-versus-code — the axis rf2-g6jd corrected one section down
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP (mayor, 2026-08-14) checking whether a corrected rule propagated to its siblings. It did not.

THE DEFECT. Lines 74-80 justify scoping the third of the three sentences like this: 'The third is scoped because a prose-only brief cannot satisfy it. A comment truth-up, a documentation correction, a governance-record edit: none of them has a property to remove, so none of them has a control to show red.'

THAT CLAIM IS FALSE, and it is the exact claim rf2-g6jd's audit refuted for the gate-mechanics section at line 406, which now reads 'the axis is the NOMINATED GATE'S CAPABILITIES — not prose versus code'. The correction landed one section down and never reached this one.

FALSIFIED THREE TIMES TODAY, all by doc-only briefs that did have a control and did show it red:
- rf2-g6jd's own third-iteration worker planted a broken link target in this very file and got check_doc_slugs.py red naming the plant, restore hash-verified.
- rf2-hic-080's worker planted a bad anchor, red naming line 281, restore verified by hash.
- The rf2-fg7e/rf2-g6jd cluster planted faults in TWO files and got two different gates red — including scripts/check_readme_links.py, which is neither heavyweight nor a link-and-anchor validator, and which that worker called the sharper demonstration of the capability axis than the link gate is.

SO THE REPAIR IS THE SAME AXIS, applied here: scope the third sentence by whether the nominated gate affords a safe, bounded, discriminating plant — not by whether the brief is prose. A documentation correction covered by a link or anchor validator DOES have a control and should be told to show it. Point to manual verification only where no covering gate affords a plant, which is the branch the same bead's third iteration just built at 433-435.

WHAT NOT TO DISTURB. The measured evidence in that passage stays: four editing briefs on one tick, two of them prose-only, both carrying the first two sentences and neither the third, with nobody having decided to drop it. That observation is real and is the reason the section exists. What is wrong is the EXPLANATION attached to it — the briefs improvised because the rule was unscoped, not because prose has no controls.

NOTE ON SEQUENCING. This is a DIFFERENT section from the paragraph rf2-g6jd patched three times, so it is a first patch rather than a fourth. But that bead's closing judgement applies to the file as a whole: the section is at its limit, its fragility is accumulated self-narration rather than logic, and a further finding should trigger rewriting the section whole with the HISTORY compressed and the branch logic preserved. Whoever takes this should decide which of the two this is, and say so.
notes: REOPENED BY THE MAYOR'S STRANDED SWEEP, 2026-08-14 22:10 AUSEST. Stale in_progress claim: the worker died with the previous session. WHAT LANDED: 758358c7ea 'docs(method): scope the third sentence by the gate's capabilities, not by prose (rf2-f9m0)', on main. So the bead's core defect -- the THREE SENTENCES section scoping by prose-versus-code rather than by the gate's capabilities -- appears discharged. WHOEVER TAKES THIS VERIFIES THAT FIRST at source and closes it as landed if so; a verified 'already fixed' is the likely and correct outcome. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED is the judgement the bead's last note leaves open, and it is a real decision rather than paperwork: that note observes the section is at its limit, that its fragility is accumulated self-narration rather than logic, and that a further finding should trigger REWRITING THE SECTION WHOLE with the history compressed and the branch logic preserved -- while also recording that this is a DIFFERENT section from the paragraph rf2-g6jd patched three times, so it is a first patch rather than a fourth. Decide which of the two this is and SAY SO on the bead. MAYOR'S OWN EVIDENCE, offered as a claim to weigh rather than a finding: across eight dispatches this session the gate-mechanics block varied in length between briefs, which is the same improvisation-under-an-unscoped-rule this bead describes, observed on the enforcing side. That is weak evidence FOR the whole-rewrite arm. It is one mayor's practice, not a measurement, and should not settle the question by itself. FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/ was held by PR #8238 until it merged minutes ago; it is free now, but check for a newer open PR against that tree before dispatching -- two concurrent editors there conflict by construction.
close_reason: VERIFIED ALREADY FIXED — no edit made. Checked at source in a fresh worktree off origin/main: dispatch-prompt-template.md lines 76-86 now read 'The third is scoped by the nominated gate's capabilities — not by prose versus code' and explicitly include documentation corrections ('a documentation correction is emphatically included, because the cheap validators that run over a docs tree red on one broken link target or one bad heading anchor and go green again on restore'). THE OPEN JUDGEMENT, DECIDED: this is a FIRST PATCH, not the whole-section rewrite. Four reasons. (1) The section's logic is intact and every branch is load-bearing — the rule, the measured evidence for sentence one, the capability axis, and the no-plant-available pointer that correctly splits into its two already-settled wordings; nothing in it contradicts anything else. (2) The nearest thing to accumulated self-narration is the line recording that this was 'the same wrong axis this section carried until it was corrected one section down', and that line is doing LOGICAL work rather than historical: it records WHY scoping on the shape of the deliverable is wrong, which is the guard against a fourth regression to the same axis. (4) Rewriting a section one patch after its correction landed, and before that correction has been observed working, is gold-plating. Recorded in PR #8254's body. If a further finding lands ON THIS SECTION the whole-rewrite arm becomes live again; a finding on the gate-mechanics section does not, since that is a different section with a different history.

title: Measure the layer-1 vs layer-2 recomputation contrast the per-keystroke census names
description:
rf2-hic-045's census measured, on implementation/hicasso's own witness applications, that a keystroke in the 100-cell grid runs 111 subscription bodies to run 2 view bodies — one recomputation per mounted cell, scaling linearly with the page, against a boundary count that is flat.

The mechanism is not in doubt and is not a defect: every subscription in both applications is a LAYER-1 reader, registered as (fn [db query-v] ...), so re-frame.subs.memo's layer-1 wrapper memoises it on the whole of app-db. A keystroke moves app-db, so every mounted layer-1 cell that is derefed re-runs its body, and the equality gate on the OUTPUT is what keeps notification narrow.

## The question this bead is for, and it is NOT a remedy

per-keystroke.md section 4 names the contrast and explicitly declines to claim it: a derived read stated as a LAYER-2 subscription over its own inputs is memoised on THOSE inputs rather than on app-db, so it should not re-run when they have not moved. Nothing in this corpus has measured that, and naming it was not proposing it.

The row to watch is ::row-total, not ::cell. A cell's body is one get-in — a hundred of them is a hundred map lookups and cheap. A row total is a cols-wide fold with a parseInt per cell, so at 10x10 the grid does ten such folds per keystroke and nine of them recompute a value that did not move. On a page with an expensive derived read per row, that is the term that bites first.

## Shape

A measurement window, Shape 6, deterministic half at least: the existing counting instrument in examples/per_keystroke_dom_cljs_test.cljs already counts author-body invocations per sub id and needs no rig change to answer it. Restating ::row-total as a layer-2 sub over its row's cells and re-running the census is the whole experiment.

## What must NOT happen

The witness applications model proper re-frame2 and are evidence about the public door. If a layer-2 spelling wins, changing examples/grid is a separate decision with its own bead — this one measures a contrast, it does not adopt one. Put the contrast arm in the suite, where the coarse anti-shapes already live, and not in the application.
acceptance_criteria: The contrast is measured on the same instrument at both grid sizes and published, or refused with the reason at source; the witness applications are unchanged either way.
close_reason:
PR #8346 merged as 54c1dce59d. Verified on all five clauses at head 56c2073bee29: 100 contexts (the full band), 55 SUCCESS + 45 SKIPPED, no non-terminal, no new job keys.

THE WINDOW. One accepted keystroke into cell [3 4], both arms measured in one file on the census's own counter (made public rather than copied — no second instrument).

  subscription recomputations        5x5    10x10
  ::row-total as layer-1 (shipped)    31      111
  ::row-total as layer-2 over cells   27      102

Attribution, layer-1: {cell 25, row-total 5, dimensions 1} and {cell 100, row-total 10, dimensions 1}. Layer-2: {cell 25, row-total-l2 1, dimensions 1} and {cell 100, row-total-l2 1, dimensions 1}. Boundary runs 2 in both arms at both sizes.

THE RESULT, STATED THE WAY THE PAGE NOW STATES IT: the row-total term goes from rows to one and stops following the mount. THE LINEAR TERM SURVIVES — ::cell is layer-1 in both arms, so a hundred bodies run either way. The saving is exactly rows - 1: 9 of 111, 4 of 31. That is the honest headline and it is smaller than 'layer-2 removes the recomputation'.

WHY THIS ONE NEEDED NO QUIET BOX, and the classification is worth keeping: it is a COUNTER census, and monotone counters read the same on a loaded machine. Only CLOCK estimands need quiet. The bead's own fence (CLEARS WHEN rf2-m6i0 reports) was superseded by its 2026-08-14 03:57 note carving counter estimands out of the quiet-box constraint, and the worker found that itself. No quiet slot was consumed.

WHAT IT REFUSED TO CONCLUDE, which is why the number is trustworthy: no clock, so nothing claims the saving is measurable in time; no general claim about layer-2 from one derived read on one page at two sizes; no adoption — examples/grid/{subs,views}.cljs untouched, the arm lives in the suite.

AND IT REPORTED A COST RATHER THAN BURYING IT: a :parametric input-fn is pure in the query vector, so the row's width must arrive in the query ([::row-total-l2 row cols]). A derived read whose input set is not knowable from its query vector CANNOT take this spelling at all. That is a real limit on the technique and it is now published beside the win.

INSTRUMENT PROVED, not assumed. Sabotage run went red naming the file with actuals printed (102 and {25,1,1} on the failure path, independently of the assertion); runs 1 and 3 on the restored tree read identically. Positive control on liveness: row 3's rendered total moved 345 -> 652.

FLAKE DISCRIMINATED FROM FAILURE THE RIGHT WAY. Runs 4 and 5 were red in suites this change does not touch (two poll-until back-button timeouts, one absent requestGC handshake). Runs 4, 5 and 6 were the identical tree AND the identical compiled bundle, and run 6 was green — that, not habit, is what licenses calling them flakes.

GATES, captured exit codes, runner matched to extension (.cljs, so browser + node lanes; no clojure -M:test): browser lane 0 / 1 (sabotage) / 0 / 1 / 1 / 0; test:cljs 0 (13,973 tests, 70,350 assertions); test:hicasso-invariants 0; check_doc_slugs.py 0 with a planted broken anchor driving it to 1; check_provenance_pins.py --self-test 0 (68) and --changed-since origin/main 0; lint_kondo.py 0; check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh 0.

ONE DECLARED GAP, and declaring it is correct: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh attempt 1 has NO VERDICT. It reached mkdocs --strict with every prior gate green, then the harness killed the shell inside the final clj-kondo step at the 10-minute cap and no .exit was written. A missing .exit is no verdict, not a pass. The one unverified step was re-run alone: exit 0.

PUBLICATION. docs/design/hicasso/product/per-keystroke.md 4.1. Correctly tested against the exhaustive published-copy list (decision-brief.md, specification.md, lanes/) and it is not on it. Section 7 scoped to say 4.1's figures come from a different suite with its own run table; section 8's 'a measurement nobody has taken' bullet corrected. All 11 tables column-checked by hand because nothing gates that; published arithmetic re-derived.

MAYOR NOTE — two worker claims that did not hold at verification: it reported a measure-07rnj worktree in git worktree list, and there is none (checked the full list). Its ' M .beads/issues.jsonl' observation in the mayor checkout is expected rather than damage — bd rewrites its export in every checkout on any read, and the checkpoint regenerates from Dolt rather than trusting the file.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: FENCE (mayor, 2026-08-14): the estimand here is RECOMPUTATION COUNTS, which are monotone counters — so under the refined rule this bead does NOT need a quiet box (counters read the same on a loaded machine, budgets section 2, established and published by rf2-hic-045's worker). But it is still a browser-lane measurement, and running that lane is heavy: it is MACHINE contention rather than quiet-box contention, and rf2-m6i0's clock window is live. The distinction matters for scheduling — this bead can run alongside light work freely, and must not run alongside a clock round. CLEARS WHEN: rf2-m6i0 reports.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

title: hic-045 follow-up — register the per-keystroke census's figures as ledger rows
description:
rf2-hic-045 published docs/design/hicasso/product/per-keystroke.md with seven deterministic per-keystroke figures on the two public-package witness applications, and registered NONE of them as rows in budgets.md section 9's reconciliation ledger.

That was a fence decision rather than an omission. Minting a new row id means editing implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_budget_ledger.py's pinned constants — DETERMINISTIC_IDS and POPULATION_PIN are hardcoded rosters covering exactly D1-D16, S1-S8, U1-U6, C1-C8 and I9 — and that script is rf2-hic-089's surface, not hic-045's.

## The figures wanting rows

All deterministic, all package population, all PR-gate lane, all witnessed by
implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/per_keystroke_dom_cljs_test.cljs:

- subscription recomputations per keystroke, editor: 10 (four ::field, four ::committed, ::revision, ::dirty?)
- subscription recomputations per keystroke, grid 10x10: 111 (100 ::cell, 10 ::row-total, 1 ::dimensions)
- subscription recomputations per keystroke, grid 5x5: 31 — the scaling contrast against a flat boundary count of 2
- subscription recomputations for a REFUSED keystroke: 0
- writes onto the glass (value property), accepted keystroke: 0
- writes onto the glass, refused keystroke: 1
- DOM mutation records per keystroke: 7 editor, 8 grid, 3 for a refusal

## Why they are worth registering rather than leaving on the page

The recomputation rows are the only figures in the corpus that SCALE with the mounted page, and section 9's ledger is where a reader looks to find out which budgets do. A figure that lives only in prose on one page is the shape the ledger exists to prevent.

## Note for whoever takes it

The rows are counts and carry no hardware profile, so they belong in budgets.md section 3 beside D1-D16 rather than in section 4. The gate's own comment says an unpinned row is the hole POPULATION_PIN exists to close, so pin each as it lands.
acceptance_criteria: Each figure has a ledger row with status, population, instrument and authority; check_budget_ledger.py passes with the new ids in its pinned rosters; budgets.md section 3 carries the rows beside the other deterministic ones.
close_reason: D17-D25 registered in budgets.md section 3 and section 9's ledger (PR #8177), all package, all PR-gate lane, all witnessed by per_keystroke_dom_cljs_test.cljs: subscription recomputations 10 editor / 31 grid 5x5 / 111 grid 10x10 / 0 refused; glass writes 0 accepted / 1 refused; DOM mutation records 7 editor / 8 grid / 3 refusal. DETERMINISTIC_IDS and POPULATION_PIN extended to D26; check_budget_ledger.py green at 49 rows. D18/D19 are readings of a LINEAR quantity and their registered lines say so with the mount size they were taken at — the pair is registered rather than one figure so neither can be read as a ceiling holding at another size. Figures transcribed from the published census, never re-derived; no measurement window opened.

title: mayor-dispatch.md never names scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py, so every brief invents its own citation for the omitted required checks
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD-REREAD LOOP (2026-08-14), step 2 — grading the mayor's own briefs against what the tree actually provides.

THE GAP IS BETWEEN THE TWO LAYERS, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT THIS LOOP'S FINDING RATHER THAN A WORKER'S.

- The generic method (docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:388) says an editing brief 'must say WHICH required checks the local gate omits — and say it by citing ONE PATH, not by re-listing them, because the required set moves. Make the project DERIVE that list rather than document it.' Correct, and deliberately tool-neutral: the generic tree carries no repository paths or script names.
- The repository HAS that derivation, and it is a good one. scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py (50 KB) 'names the REQUIRED checks the fast spine does not run, at step granularity, with the local command for each' — TESTING.md:121. Everything in it is derived: the required set from the three aggregators' needs:, each job's gate steps from its run: bodies, and coverage from the spine's own invocations. So a new required job, or a new step inside an existing one, is reported as unrun BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by somebody remembering to write it down (rf2-13zre). It has three modes: --list for the full report, --brief for the digest the spine appends to its PASS line, and the default --check as a drift ratchet that runs in the spine and in CI's verify-skill-mcp-drift job.
- NOTHING IN .claude/commands/ OR docs/the-mayor-method/ NAMES IT. Verified by grep across both trees: zero hits.

CONSEQUENCE, measured on the enforcing side. The command files are exactly where a concrete path belongs — mayor-dispatch.md's own closing line says the generic tree carries no tool names while these files may name them freely. With the connection missing, every mayor writing a brief invents a citation. This mayor invented 'citing the workflow path rather than re-listing them' and pasted it into six editing dispatches this session, which sends a worker to read .github/workflows/* BY HAND to answer a question a derived script already answers exactly. Not unsatisfiable — just wrong, and wrong in a way that varies per brief, which is the improvisation signature loops.md section 6 names.

THE REPAIR, one file, small. In .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, where the dispatch requirements are enumerated, name the script as the one path a brief cites: the brief tells the worker to run 
REQUIRED CHECKS THIS SPINE DOES NOT RUN (96) -- derived by scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py
  Green here is not green in CI. The three required status contexts are `All required
  checks passed` (test.yml), `Lint required` (lint.yml) and `Docs required` (docs.yml).
  This is not a to-do list: most are surface-gated in CI and skip on a diff that does not
  reach them. The claim is narrower and harder -- NONE of them is decided here.

  (A) STEPS INSIDE JOBS THIS SPINE DOES RUN. These report under the JOB's name, so a
      red here names a test suite for something that may not be a test at all.
      test.yml  job "Repo invariant checks (skills, MCP, catalogues, namespaces)"
        - step "Report every failing invariant check"
            $ failed=$(printf '%s' "$STEP_OUTCOMES" \
                | jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.value.outcome == "failure") | .key')
              if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
                echo "All repo invariant checks passed."
                echo "All repo invariant checks passed." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
                exit 0
              fi
              count=$(printf '%s\n' "$failed" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
              ... (27 more lines -- see .github/workflows/test.yml)
      test.yml  job "JVM freehand (clojure -M:test)"
        - step "Assert no dependency on the re-frame.ui donor"
            $ set -euo pipefail
              if git grep -n -e 're-frame\.ui' -e 're_frame/ui' -e 're-frame2-ui' -- implementation/freehand; then
                echo "::error::implementation/freehand references the re-frame.ui donor (EP-0036: the new package never depends on the donor)"
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "OK: implementation/freehand names no re-frame.ui dependency"
      test.yml  job "CLJS (shadow-cljs :node-test)"
        - step "re-frame.ui focused adapter-artifact isolation"
            $ cd implementation && npm run test:ui-isolation
        - step "Uncovered bench-namespace compile gate"
            $ cd implementation && npm run test:bspine-compile
        - step "Hicasso release build (:advanced, goog.DEBUG false)"
            $ cd implementation && npm run build:hicasso-release
      docs.yml  job "MkDocs build"
        - step "Rebuild playground bundles fresh from main"
            $ cd docs/tools/playground
              npm ci
              npm run build
        - step "Verify freshly-built SCI bundle is a valid re-frame2 build"
            $ f=docs/cljs/playground-rf2.js
              if [ ! -s "$f" ]; then
                echo "::error::$f missing or empty after build — the SCI bundle build failed."
                exit 1
              fi
              if ! grep -q "rf2sci" "$f"; then
                echo "::error::$f does not export rf2sci after build — wrong artefact."
                exit 1
              ... (2 more lines -- see .github/workflows/docs.yml)
        - step "Smoke the built bundles under headless Chromium"
            $ cd docs/tools/playground && npm run smoke
        - step "Verify committed esbuild bootstrap matches the fresh build"
            $ if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/cljs/playground.js docs/cljs/playground.css; then
                echo "::error::Committed docs/cljs/playground.{js,css} are stale on main — run 'npm run build:bootstrap' in docs/tools/playground and commit the rebuilt bundles."
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "Committed esbuild bootstrap matches a fresh build."
        - step "Stage spec/ + migration/ into docs/"
            $ rm -rf docs/spec
              cp -r spec docs/spec
              rm -rf docs/migration
              cp -r migration docs/migration
      docs.yml  job "Provenance pins"
        - step "Check provenance pins on changed pages"
            $ set -euo pipefail
              if [ -z "${GITHUB_BASE_REF:-}" ]; then
                # A push build has no base branch, so "the pages this change
                # touches" is undefined.  The self-test above still ran, so this
                # job is not a no-op; say so rather than implying a corpus verdict.
                echo "No base ref (${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}) — the changed-page gate is a"
                echo "pull-request check. Self-test above covered the checker itself."
                exit 0
              ... (4 more lines -- see .github/workflows/docs.yml)

        - beads-pr-boundary: "Beads PR boundary (no tracker database in a PR)"
            step "Self-test the beads + mayor commit guards (rf2-5z20y)"

            step "Enforce the beads PR boundary (rf2-3mh2f)"
              $ set -euo pipefail
                if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" != "pull_request" ]; then

                # Pass the BASE BRANCH. The script resolves the branch point itself

        - cljs-ui-g13: "CLJS ui G-13 exact push economics (browser + advanced elision)"

title: every hic-* bead's embedded worker protocol says 'gates run foreground, never backgrounded' — unsatisfiable, and it contradicts the method
description:
REPORTED BY rf2-hic-036's WORKER (2026-08-14), which hit the conflict, chose correctly, and said so rather than silently picking one.

THE CONFLICT. Every hic-* bead carries an identical '[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]' block, whose item 3 reads: 'Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.' The dispatch method says the opposite half: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md's 'Quality gates — how a gate is run' opens with 'Detaching a long gate is CORRECT; ending the turn afterwards is the defect', and derives it from arithmetic — the full spine needs roughly twenty-five minutes against a harness ceiling well below that.

IT IS UNSATISFIABLE, NOT MERELY INCONSISTENT. rf2-hic-036's worker reported that npm run test:browser exceeds the harness ceiling, so 'foreground, to completion' was NOT ON OFFER at all. An instruction that cannot be obeyed on some path is the exact class loops.md section 6 tells this project to hunt: workers facing one do not stop, they IMPROVISE, and the improvisation varies. This worker improvised well — it followed the brief, polled the log and the .exit file within-turn, never ended a turn waiting, and flagged the divergence in its report. The next one may improvise differently, and the likeliest wrong turn is the dangerous one: obeying item 3 literally means running a gate that gets hard-killed mid-run, whose partial log then reads as a result.

WHAT IS RIGHT IN ITEM 3, AND MUST SURVIVE THE REPAIR: 'never piped through tail' is correct and load-bearing — a pipeline's exit status is its last command's, so a red runner reads green. 'Commit and open the PR before ending the turn' is correct. Only the foreground clause is wrong.

SCALE. The block is embedded in the DESCRIPTION text of every hic-* bead — roughly twenty open ones plus the closed ones — so this recurs on every hic dispatch until repaired at source. That also means the repair is a tracker-text edit across many beads, NOT a code change, and it should be done with a scripted rewrite of the one paragraph rather than by hand.

PROPOSED REPLACEMENT for item 3, keeping the two correct halves and fixing the third: 'Gates: foreground a gate that fits inside the harness ceiling; DETACH one that does not and poll BOTH its log and its .exit file in a bounded loop within the same turn — never end the turn waiting for a completion event. Never pipe a gate through tail or any filter; redirect to a log and echo the runner's own exit code on the same command line. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.'

CHECK THE PREMISE AT SOURCE FIRST: confirm the block still reads as quoted, and confirm the bead count, before rewriting anything. A count is a claim.
