title: loops.md section 4 still says 'ask the remote for the tip', which the corrected command file now contradicts
description:
FOUND BY rf2-yfz7's WORKER (PR #8156), which was fenced out of this tree and correctly reported rather than edited.

THE CONFLICT, verified at source at docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md lines 514-516:

  '**Ask the remote for the tip** rather than refreshing first and reading what the refresh left behind — the shared fetch-head trap under *After each merge* is on this read path too, and there it is silent.'

PR #8156 changes the command file that EXECUTES this rule (.claude/commands/mayor-posture.md) to read the LOCAL ref with git rev-parse, because git ls-remote lags a linked worktree and false-signalled a strand on three healthy workers at once on 2026-08-14 05:15. So the generic body and the command file now instruct opposite reads of the same value. That is precisely the two-layer drift loops.md section 6 exists to catch, arriving one layer up from where it was fixed.

WHY THE GENERIC RULE IS WRONG RATHER THAN MERELY OUTDATED. Section 4's contrast is remote-versus-refresh-then-read. It never considers the third option — reading the local ref with NO fetch at all — which is what makes the fetch-head concern inapplicable rather than merely outweighed. git rev-parse consults the local ref and performs no fetch, so the shared .git/FETCH_HEAD the passage warns about is never touched. Every other sentence in that numbered item is correct and stays: the ahead-count/rebase reasoning, the authored-vs-committed timestamp split, and above all 'an unchanged id still says *nothing* on its own', which already agrees with the corrected text.

KEEP THE TWO LAYERS APART — this is the constraint that makes the repair non-obvious. docs/the-mayor-method/** carries NO repository names, bead ids, PR numbers, paths, tool names or OS mechanics; the command files may name all of them freely. So the generic fix must NOT say 'git rev-parse', 'ls-remote', or cite the 2026-08-14 measurement. It states the principle: read the tip from whichever ref the worker's commit updates DIRECTLY, and prefer a read that performs no fetch, because a fetch is what exposes the shared fetch-head trap; where workers share one repository metadata directory, the shared local ref moves on commit while the published one moves only when the worker chooses to push, so the published ref lags in the direction that reads as death. The command file carries the concrete commands.

ALSO WORTH ADDING, and equally generic: an unchanged tip must be corroborated with worktree ACTIVITY before it means anything, because a worker inside a long gate commits nothing by design — a still tip is the EXPECTED reading for the commonest healthy state, not a warning. Section 4 already says an unchanged id 'says nothing on its own' but does not say what would make it say something.

A GREP WILL NOT FIND THIS CLASS. The reporting worker noted that grepping loops.md for ls-remote|FETCH_HEAD|rev-parse|'ask the REMOTE' returns NOTHING — the generic body is deliberately tool-neutral prose ('tip revision', 'the shared fetch-head trap'), so command-name greps cannot locate its conflicts. They have to be read. Worth remembering for any future two-layer reconciliation.

FENCE. docs/the-mayor-method/** is a shared surface; two concurrent editors conflict by construction. PR #8155 is OPEN against that tree (rf2-oae1, dispatch-prompt-template.md). SEQUENCE behind #8155's merge.

CLUSTER WITH rf2-g6jd. That bead repairs dispatch-prompt-template.md's missing gate-block scoping rule and is sequenced behind the same PR. Same surface, same fence, both small, and one agent owning the method tree is exactly the shape that avoids a second conflict — dispatch the two together as one cluster once #8155 lands, NOT as two workers.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8161 (commit f978af94ae), cluster with rf2-fg7e and rf2-g6jd. loops.md section 4's 'Ask the remote for the tip' replaced with the generic property: read the tip from whichever ref the worker's commit updates DIRECTLY, and prefer a read that performs no refresh, because the refresh is what exposes the shared fetch-head trap. States the mechanism generically -- where workers share one repository metadata directory the shared local ref moves on commit while the published one moves only on push, so the published ref lags in the direction that reads as death. Adds the corroboration half the bead asked for: an unchanged tip says something only once corroborated with worktree activity, because a worker inside a long gate commits nothing by design. title: dispatch-prompt-template.md: the gate-mechanics block has no scoping rule, so a prose-only brief makes the mayor invent one
description:

MEASURED ON THE ENFORCING SIDE. In one session the mayor pasted FIVE different lengths of that one block across five dispatches — nearly whole for a codemod fix, roughly half for a one-line edit to a command file (dropping the scoped-plant paragraph, the leftover-artefact line, and two of the three restore-hashing cautions), and intermediate lengths for the rest. It did.

THE TEMPLATE ALREADY SOLVED THIS EXACT SHAPE ONCE, one section earlier. 'The three sentences that do the most work' scopes its THIRD sentence to briefs whose deliverable includes a control, explains that a prose-only brief has no property to remove and therefore cannot satisfy it, and then names what such a brief does INSTEAD — pointing at the 'Quality gates — which gate' wording about a surface with no automated coverage. That passage's own reasoning applies verbatim to the gate block: 'Say what a brief with no control does instead, or that gets improvised too.'

WHAT NOT TO DO. Do not shorten the block. Do not turn it into a reference the brief LINKS to rather than pastes — dispatch-prompt-template.md already warns that sending a worker to a file is how the stance gets lost, and the same argument holds here.

title: hicasso: the alloc summary's 'windows refused: N of M' counts refusal records against a window denominator
description:
OBSERVED by rf2-2rtt6.140's V1 window on 2026-08-14 (PR #8152). Cosmetic, in a
measurement instrument's summary, which is the only reason it is filed at all.

THE SYMPTOM. Every V1 run printed a line of the shape

  ;;   windows refused: 17 of 12  (worst leg deviation observed 1774.3%)

"17 of 12" is not a possible ratio. The numerator is refusedWindows.length --
one entry per REFUSAL RECORD, and a single window contributes one per deviant leg
-- while the denominator is the count of measured arm WINDOWS. The floor-only
plan measures 12 arm windows (2 segments x 6 rounds) and several of them had two
or three legs outside tolerance, so the numerator overran.

Reproduced across all six V1 runs: 17 of 12, 14 of 12, 13 of 12, 14 of 12,
16 of 12, 13 of 12.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD AND NOT JUST A SHRUG. Nothing is mis-gated -- the exit
code keys off refusedWindows.length > 0, which is correct either way, and no
published figure moves. But a summary line that reports an impossible ratio in a
row whose entire purpose is to be believed invites a reader to distrust the
figures beside it, or worse to read "17 windows were refused" and conclude the
run measured more windows than it did.

THE FIX IS A NAMING CHOICE, NOT A COUNTING ONE. Either report
"refusals: 17 across 12 windows", or count distinct windows for the numerator and
keep the reason list below. The second is the smaller change if a reader is meant
to compare the numerator to the denominator; the first is more honest about what
the list underneath actually is.

NOT FIXED IN THE WINDOW THAT FOUND IT: Shape 6 forbids improving the rig
mid-window, and this is a one-line summariser edit that would have invalidated
the nine runs it was found in.

WHERE: implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/p0_run.cjs, summariseAlloc, the
"windows refused" line; allocRefusedWindows builds the list.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #8159 (branch worker/legexcess-oiy1), commit 7183ae39f8 -- a SEPARATE trailing commit after the rf2-oiy1 P1, exactly as the routing comment on this bead directed, and it did not put the P1 at risk.

THE FIX IS THE NAMING CHOICE, taking both halves of what the bead offered rather than one: allocRefusedWindowCount(row) is the distinct-window count and is what the denominator is comparable to, and the reason count is named as reasons beside it. The line now reads 'windows refused: N of M, K refusal reasons in all (a window can fail on more than one leg)'. The reason list underneath is unchanged and still printed in full, and the exit code still keys off refusedWindows.length > 0, which was correct either way.

CONSTRUCTED, NOT ASSERTED, as the brief required. The new pin builds a window with THREE legs outside tolerance against a five-leg cohort, on two segments across two rounds: four refused windows, twelve reasons. It asserts both that the old numerator overruns its own denominator on exactly that row (12 > 4 -- the '17 of 12' shape) and that a window count cannot. The summary fixture also now derives its refusals with the shipped allocRefusedWindows instead of being handed an empty list, which is what lets it tell the two counts apart at all.

RED-THEN-GREEN: reinstating the old numerator turned the pin red with '12 !== 4', exit 1 captured from the runner; restore verified byte-identical by git hash-object (8bc77d4350686b22fb62987c586be2ee9665a85d). Green after: 66 passed, exit 0.

row.refusedWindows now carries WINDOWS (its name); row.refusalReasons carries the list length. Both are in the record so a reader of the JSON can tell them apart too.

title: ViewCell use-frame-context! bypasses the ambient-frame-refusal tier — verify intent, then gate or record rationale
description:
Spun out of the rf2-5rqn ruling (2026-08-13). Two independent reviewers confirmed the same source reading while ruling on that bead, so the premise is verified at main ef3881981c.

THE OBSERVATION: the compiled ViewCell's frame resolution, use-frame-context! (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell.cljs:317-322, landed by rf2-2rzx0), resolves via (or frame/*current-frame* (context-value->current-frame ctx)) — it never consults *ambient-frame-refusal*. By contrast, the function-component path routes through frame/resolve-current-frame (implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:758-764), which deliberately WITHDRAWS the ambient tier while a refusal is in effect (rf2-2rtt6.122) and refuses a carried stamp naming another frame inside a declared :extent-frame (rf2-nqj22), surfacing :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused. So a refusing extent binds UIx hooks (and, after the rf2-5rqn repair, still binds them under SSR) but does NOT bind compiled views.

THE TASK, in order:
1. Verify INTENT: is the refusal tier meant to bind compiled-view frame resolution too? Check rf2-2rtt6.122 / rf2-nqj22 for scope, and whether any spec text (006 compiled-view sections, extent-frame rules) speaks to compiled views specifically.
2. If yes: gate the ViewCell resolution on the refusal tier (route through the shared resolution rather than the bare or-expression), with a witness that a refusing extent produces :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused from a compiled sub.
3. If deliberately no: record the rationale in a comment at the ViewCell site and close — do not add machinery.

This is a consistency question between two substrates' frame laws, not a hypothetical-misuse guard. Do NOT bundle it into the rf2-5rqn repair PR; rf2-5rqn's ruling explicitly fences it out.
notes:
WORKER FINDING + STEP 3 TAKEN (2026-08-14, PR #8153). The bead's premise is VERIFIED at
viewcell.cljs:317-322 and frame.cljc:758-764 exactly as written. Step 1 answered NO, so
step 3 (rationale at the site, no machinery) is what shipped.

THREE FINDINGS, each sufficient on its own:

1. A ViewCell can never be inside a refusing extent. Spec 002 §The refusal tier scopes an
extent to a substrate's own SYNCHRONOUS render call, and call-with-ambient-frame-refused
records why nesting is untracked: React invokes a child fiber only after the parent's
render function has returned, under react-dom/server as much as the client renderer. The
only producers in the tree are hicasso impl/intent/with-frame (boundary, collector,
overlay, presence-react) plus the freehand bench twin and test probes; each binds around a
body eval + codec/as-element, which CREATES elements rather than invoking components. A
compiled view is a React FC, so its render — and the leading hook with it — always runs
after the binding unwinds.

2. Gating it would have a substrate refuse itself. use-frame-context! answers WHICH FRAME
THIS COMPONENT IS IN — the question a substrate answers BEFORE it refuses, and whose answer
it hands core as :extent-frame. The refusing substrate resolves it the same way:
hicasso/impl/collector/resolve-frame! reads the shared context DIRECTLY and says so
verbatim, "Deliberately NOT frame/require-current-frame!'s dynamic-var -> context chain …
a body's dynamic extent has unwound by the time React renders the component it returned".
The ambient (sub …)/dispatch doors that the refusal IS addressed to already reach it via
require-current-frame! -> resolve-current-frame, under re-frame.ui as everywhere.

3. STEP 2'S SUGGESTED ROUTE IS NOT AVAILABLE — a premise of the bead that does not hold.
"Route through the shared resolution" would put the hook back on
adapter-context/function-component-current-frame, the private _currentValue read rf2-2rzx0
deliberately moved it OFF because react-dom/server does not populate that slot (the defect
rf2-5rqn is repairing). Step 2 as worded would revert rf2-2rzx0.

NO SPEC TEXT speaks to compiled views under a refusal, and what Spec 002 does say cuts the
other way: its motivating case is a compiled-view boundary that OPTS IN by establishing an
extent. re-frame.ui does not — it binds *current-frame* around the compiled body precisely
so ambient reads resolve (with-current-frame, rf2-4rwtd). Permitting ambient reads in a
compiled body is re-frame.ui's substrate policy, deliberately different from Hicasso's.
rf2-2rtt6.122 and rf2-nqj22 are both scoped to the Hicasso body render extent throughout.

ADJACENT HAZARD CHECKED AND REJECTED, so no follow-up bead. The ViewCell honours tier-1
precedence, so a host rendering it inside rf/with-frame :b beneath an :a provider resolves
:b — reachable (flushSync mount under a scope, renderToString under one, test-support's
:ambient-frame default). It is NOT rf2-nqj22's defect: re-frame.ui threads that one
resolved value everywhere (with-current-frame, events/with-capture destination,
render-frame), so the view is wholly :b-consistent. One frame, not two. Per EP-0002 the
carried stamp wins and re-frame.ui declares no :extent-frame to contradict it.

GATES: clj-kondo (CI's gate, covers implementation/) exit 0, errors 0. Negative control —
unbalanced delimiter planted at the (let [ctx-frame line — exit 3, errors 8, all naming
viewcell.cljs at the planted line; restore proven byte-identical by git blob hash. The
harness reported exit 0 for that sabotage run; the shell's own captured code was 3.
close_reason: Step 3 taken: rationale recorded at the ViewCell site, no machinery added (PR #8153). Step 1 established that the refusal tier is not meant to — and structurally cannot — bind the ViewCell's resolution of its own extent frame: a refusing extent is a substrate's own synchronous render call and has unwound before React invokes a child fiber; the hook answers the question a substrate answers BEFORE it refuses (the one it hands core as :extent-frame), which the refusing substrate itself resolves by reading the context directly (hicasso collector/resolve-frame!); and routing through resolve-current-frame would put the hook back on the private _currentValue read rf2-2rzx0 moved it off. No spec text speaks to compiled views under a refusal, and Spec 002's motivating case is a substrate that OPTS IN. Full evidence in the notes and the PR body.

title: Extend the nightly sweep to narrow-armed gates with no scheduled arm against main (rf2-2uy8 B+ ruling)
description:
FROM THE rf2-2uy8 RULING (B+, 2026-08-13, delegated). The nightly expensive-tests.yml sweep is documented as a strict superset of the surface-armed PR gates (TESTING.md:63). That holds for the expensive browser class but NOT for a handful of narrow-armed gates that run only when detect_changed_surfaces arms them at PR time and have no arm that ever runs against main. A cross-surface regression in one of those sits green-on-main until a PR happens to arm it — exactly the rf2-8yyd/rf2-2uy8 incident shape (fcf866ea1d: a core error_emit.cljc change broke the Story feature-load gate, which the classifier does not arm for a core diff), one tier down.

TASK:
1. Enumerate authoritatively: diff the set of npm run test:*/bench:*/build:* commands reachable from .github/workflows/test.yml against those reachable from .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml (and any other scheduled workflow, e.g. freehand-bench.yml). Candidates verified 2026-08-13 by grep — none appear in expensive-tests.yml: test:ssr-node (test.yml:5326), test:hicasso-controlled (:1532), test:hicasso-hmr (:1642), test:testbed-tenant-switcher (:4580), test:tools-machines-viz (:4921); also check the ui G-gates. Broad-armed suites (test:cljs, JVM core) arm on every code surface and are OUT of scope.
2. Add the cheap ones to expensive-tests.yml as their own NAMED steps — per-step names are what give nightly_failure_alert.py its failure-signature granularity (rf2-wh5to), so a newly-red gate becomes a new signature and lands in the Mike-assigned tracking issue.
3. Any gate deliberately left out as too expensive for the nightly: record the accepted exposure in a workflow comment beside it (the repo's declared-hole idiom, cf. check_gate_scheduling.py's `unscheduled` kind), so the omission is a decision rather than an accident.
4. Do NOT touch PR-side arming or the classifier — the PR behaviour is correct and the rf2-2uy8 ruling explicitly leaves it alone. Do NOT add skipped-job reporting.
5. Do NOT extend scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py to model arming conditions — over-engineering; its "scheduled" deliberately means "reachable from some workflow run: value", which is why it cannot see this gap (a surface-armed test.yml job satisfies it). The one-time diff in step 1 is sufficient.

PRECEDENT: rf2-xwa4n and rf2-zl8ao added nightly supersets for the Freehand gates on the same "safety net for everything outside the arm" reasoning; the rf2-6ckzl census normalised "every gate has a scheduled home".

CONSTRAINTS: expensive-tests.yml is hot-zone (.github/workflows/*) — sequential dispatch, never parallel with another workflow-touching bead. Budget: a few minutes of nightly runtime; nothing on any PR's critical path. post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml will dispatch expensive-tests.yml within minutes of the merge touching workflow YAML, giving same-day verification of the edit itself.

ACCEPTANCE: every surface-armed test:/build: gate command in test.yml either appears as a named step in a scheduled workflow, or carries a workflow comment recording the deliberately accepted exposure. State which gates fell in each bucket in the PR body.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8155. ENUMERATED by diffing every npm run test:/bench:/build: reachable from test.yml against the scheduled workflows (expensive-tests.yml, freehand-bench.yml, lint.yml), each command mapped back to its job's if: so broad arms could be told from narrow. ADDED (13, each its own NAMED step for nightly_failure_alert.py signature granularity, all riding setup the jobs already do): browser/bundle sweep -- test:ssr-node, test:perf-bundle, test:schemas-bundle, test:ui-g1, test:ui-g13, test:ui-facade-isolation, test:reagent-slim:smoke, test:testbed-tenant-switcher, test:tools-machines-viz, build:machines-viz-viewer; mcp-live -- test:unit, test:flag-gates, test:stdin-eof-shutdown. DECLARED (4, exposure recorded beside each in the workflow): test:hicasso-controlled / test:hicasso-hmr / test:ui-g8 need Firefox+WebKit this job does not install and (HMR) a live watch on its own dev-http origin -- not the few minutes the ruling budgeted; test:re-frame2-pair-live-overflow would run VACUOUSLY (exits 0 on a SKIP marker without nREPL) and its real coverage is the hermetic suite already in the same job; test:cljs (tools/mcp-base) has NO cross-surface input to miss, its deps.edn stating the artefact must not depend on implementation/, so tools_jvm arms on precisely its inputs. Two bare 'npm run build' (re-frame2-pair-mcp, docs/tools/playground) are outside the test:/build: population and covered anyway. TESTING.md's superset sentence qualified to say WHICH superset and where the holes are declared. A PIN CAUGHT A HOLE THE CHANGE OPENED: _rigorous-local-inventory.test.cjs (rf2-lm5mu9) holds test-rigorous-local.sh to every command in the nightly browser/bundle job; the ten additions put the local mirror behind it and the spine went red naming all ten. Fixed on the same branch, with the comment recording why the three declared holes are absent there too. Not touched per the bead: PR-side arming, the classifier, skipped-job reporting, check_gate_scheduling.py. BAND UNMOVED at 93 -- expensive-tests.yml is schedule+workflow_dispatch only, so it contributes no PR checks; these are steps inside existing jobs. Gates (captured, not harness-reported): fast-PR spine 0 on the final tree, check_gate_scheduling 0 + --self-test 0, check_fast_pr_gap --check 0 (85 required jobs, unchanged), _rigorous-local-inventory 0 (6 passed), bash -n 0, YAML parse 0.

title: Re-measure the merge check-count band after PR #8118 changed three workflow files
description:
BAND RE-MEASUREMENT OWED $D. PR #8118 merged and it CHANGED THREE WORKFLOW FILES - freehand-bench.yml, freehand-conformance.yml and portability.yml, 65 insertions.

I read the change before merging rather than counting it, which is what clause 5 asks. Job counts either side were unchanged - 5 to 5, 4 to 4, 6 to 6 - and the diff added no job name, no new condition and no new job-level entry. So the additions are steps and comments inside existing jobs, the matrix is intact, and the band should still be 93.

THAT IS A PREDICTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The band is a measured constant and it has moved four times in this programme. Clause 1 says to measure it on PRs merged AFTER the last workflow change, and #8118 IS that change. There are currently ZERO open PRs, so there is nothing to measure against yet.

WHAT THE NEXT TICK MUST DO: the first PR opened after #8118 is the measurement. Run 'gh pr checks NNNN --json state' and count. If it reads 93, the prediction held and mayor-merge.md needs no edit. If it reads anything else, mayor-merge.md's written constant is stale and must be corrected in the same tick - it is written down, it moves, and it goes stale exactly where it has to be right.

Do not merge a PR on a count you have not re-measured after this change.
notes:
PROVISIONAL READING $D, recorded because it may already be the answer and the next tick should not have to rediscover it.

PR #8138 currently reports 92 CHECKS, with one still in progress (the tests workflow, 15 minutes in - a normal full-matrix duration, not a stall). The written band is 93.

92 IS NOT YET A MEASUREMENT. An unsettled rollup can still gain checks: matrix jobs surface as they start, so a total read mid-run is a floor rather than a count. Do not conclude the band moved from this.

BUT IF IT SETTLES AT 92, THAT IS A REAL MOVE and mayor-merge.md's constant is stale. Correct it in the same tick, naming #8138 as the measuring PR and #8118 as the change that moved it.

TWO THINGS THAT WOULD MAKE 92 INNOCENT, check both before editing anything:
1. A STALE BASE. #8138's branch predates #8118 in origin, though its merge-base was verified to contain #8118's workflow change - so this one is already excluded. Re-verify with git merge-base if the number surprises you.
2. A JOB-LEVEL CONDITION rather than a skip. The band counts SKIPPED checks, so arming differences do not change the total; a job gated by an if: at the workflow level does not appear at all. #8118 added 65 lines across three workflow files. The mayor verified job counts were unchanged either side - 5 to 5, 4 to 4, 6 to 6 - and that no job name or condition was added. If 92 settles, that verification was wrong somewhere and the diff is worth re-reading.

DO NOT MERGE #8138 ON 92 WITHOUT SETTLING THIS. It is the first PR after the workflow change, which makes it both the thing to merge and the instrument.
close_reason:
MEASURED 93 - THE BAND HELD, and the written constant needs no edit.

PR #8138 settled at 93 checks (56 SUCCESS + 37 SKIPPED, 0 non-pass). It was the first PR opened after #8118, and its merge-base was verified to contain #8118's workflow change, so it is a valid instrument rather than a stale-base reading.

mayor-merge.md's "93 as measured 2026-08-13" stands. No correction owed.

THE PREDICTION AND HOW IT WAS MADE. #8118 changed three workflow files, 65 insertions. Before merging it I read the diff rather than counting lines: job counts were unchanged either side (5 to 5, 4 to 4, 6 to 6), and no job name, job-level entry or condition was added. So the additions were steps and comments inside existing jobs, the matrix was intact, and the band should not move. It did not.

That is clause 5 working as written - the same line count gives opposite verdicts, and only reading the diff tells you which.

AN INTERMEDIATE READING OF 92 WAS RECORDED AND CORRECTLY NOT ACTED ON. Two ticks running, #8138 reported 92 with one check still in progress. A mid-run total is a FLOOR, not a count: matrix jobs surface as they start. Had that 92 been treated as a measurement, mayor-merge.md would have been "corrected" to a number that was never true, and every subsequent merge judged against it. The rule that saved it is the one already in clause 1 - a partial rollup is not a green one, and it is not a count either.

CLOSED on the measurement.

title: loops.md section 4's STRANDED SWEEP half has no command file; mayor-posture.md carries only the posture half
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 19:38 AUSEST at main. Found by rf2-0vvw's worker, which correctly REFUSED to act on it — my brief had claimed mayor-posture.md runs the stranded sweep, and it does not. Verified independently: grep -in 'strand|in.progress|rev-list|commit count' .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md returns NOTHING.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md:451 is headed '## 4. Posture, and the stranded sweep' — two halves. .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md carries the FIRST half only: the stance block, the voice reassert, the one-line orchestration-not-implementation line, and the drift checklist. The stranded-sweep half — find in-progress items, discriminate alive from stranded, message before redispatching, push-then-reopen only when both signals are dead — has no command file at all. It currently lives INLINE in the operator's scheduler prompt.

THAT IS THE EXACT DRIFT rf2-k13d EXISTED TO CLOSE, one level down. rf2-k13d measured the loop-to-command-file mapping and found backlog-reread and method-reread had no file; it added both. It counted 'posture -> one file' as covered, which is true at the LOOP level and false at the BODY level, because loop 4 has two bodies and the file holds one. bootstrap.md's rule is one command file per loop; the substantive question is whether one file can hold two bodies, and if so this file should hold both.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS: an inline body is a second copy of a rule. loops.md section 6 says in terms that two copies of one rule disagree within days, and this project has now measured that twice — the count-vs-tip-revision defect (rf2-0vvw) was live in BOTH loops.md and mayor-hygiene.md and had to be fixed in both. An inline scheduler body cannot be fixed by a PR at all; it is fixed only by the mayor remembering to re-register the entry.

FIX SHAPE (not ruled): extend .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md with the stranded-sweep half, pinning the concrete commands the way its siblings do — and pin the CORRECTED discriminator, the tip revision id, not the commit count, per rf2-0vvw / PR #8135. Do NOT restate the generic reasoning; loops.md section 4 owns that and the command file pins commands.

THEN THE MAYOR REPOINTS the posture scheduler entry at the file and drops the inline body, exactly as was done for method-reread and backlog-reread under rf2-0dsr.

ALTERNATIVE, and it is a fine outcome: rule that posture and the stranded sweep are deliberately one file because they share a tick, and record that on this bead. Say so explicitly rather than leaving the asymmetry undocumented.

GATE: .claude/commands/ IS gated — scripts/check_readme_links.py:390 defines COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC = '.claude/commands/*.md' and walks every tracked match. Do not repeat the mayor's earlier error of calling that tree ungated.
notes:
FENCE RE-TESTED AND ITS CONDITION REWRITTEN $D, because the old one can no longer be met on its own terms.

The old note said "CLEARS WHEN the measurement lane is done, or Mike says otherwise". THE LANE IS NOT RUNNING AND IS NOT WAITING ON MACHINE TIME. rf2-5yn9 ran and published (PR #8138). The next lane bead, rf2-2rtt6.140, carries criterion 5: its V1 to V3 windows need a GRANTED quiet box, and the mayor's standing authorisation does not name that bead. So the lane is STALLED ON AN OPERATOR GRANT.

A fence whose condition is "wait for a thing that is itself waiting on a decision" is a hold with no measurable release, and this loop exists to catch exactly that. The cheapest-looking item in a list is the one that stays there longest.

NEW CONDITION, which is measurable: dispatch when worker/testingmd-cluster reports and the machine is free. This bead does NOT need a quiet box - it is a documentation change, and it was only ever queued to keep the machine clear for a measurement. If the grant on rf2-2rtt6.140 has not arrived by then, take this bead rather than idle.

IF THE GRANT DOES ARRIVE FIRST, the measurement wins - it is P1 and blocks two further P1 beads. This bead is P3 or P4 and blocks nothing. Say which you chose and why.

THE REFUSAL ROUTE THE MAYOR OFFERED WAS NOT AVAILABLE, and the worker found why rather than taking the exit: mayor-backlog-reread.md already said 'belongs to the STRANDED SWEEP in mayor-posture.md, not here' - a pointer to content that did not exist. A sibling command file had already asserted the file held this. Verified at source by the mayor. The worker deliberately did NOT restate the generic reasoning; loops.md section 4 owns that and mayor-hygiene.md owns the command-layer discriminator beside the reaping rule, so a third copy would be the exact drift class this bead was fixing. The scheduler entry was repointed by the mayor after merge (see rf2-0dsr) - the inline body is gone. Closed by the mayor on the merge; the tracker showed OPEN with no close reason.

title: the pre-push 'read the diff for what you would REVERT' step names a two-dot diff, which shows the trunk's advance too
description:
FOUND BY worker/specerr-bkvo, 2026-08-13, while doing exactly what the instruction said.

THE INSTRUCTION, in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md (section 'Quality gates - how a gate is run', final bullet) and repeated in every dispatch brief the mayor writes:

  'Diff against origin/main before you push, and read that diff for what you would REVERT.'

Workers read that as `git diff origin/main`, which is the TWO-DOT form. Two-dot diffs the two commits, so it shows everything ORIGIN/MAIN gained since the branch point as well as everything the branch changed. On this repository under a saturated fleet that is hundreds of kilobytes of unrelated content — the reporting worker got ~700KB spanning the mayor-method tree, .beads and facade-freeze.md, none of it its own.

WHY THAT DEFEATS THE RULE RATHER THAN MERELY ANNOYING. The step exists to answer one question: WOULD MY PUSH UNDO SOMETHING A SIBLING LANDED WHILE I WORKED? A revert of a merged change is well-formed, compiles, and passes every check the tree has, so this read is the only thing that catches it. Burying that signal in ~700KB of noise means a worker either skips the step or scans it and misses the one hunk that matters. The rule is most needed exactly when the trunk has moved most, which is exactly when two-dot is noisiest — it degrades precisely where it has to work.

THE FIX: name the THREE-DOT form.

  git diff origin/main...HEAD

Three-dot diffs against the MERGE BASE, so it shows only the branch's own changes. Equivalent and more explicit: `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)`.

ADD ONE SENTENCE SAYING WHY, because a worker who does not know the difference will 'simplify' it back to two dots. Something like: two-dot also shows what the trunk gained since your base, which is not what this step asks.

SWEEP EVERY CARRIER. `git grep` for 'diff against origin/main', 'git diff origin/main' and 'what you would REVERT' across tracked files. Known carriers: dispatch-prompt-template.md and docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md. Check .claude/commands/mayor-*.md too.

DISCRIMINATOR: only a carrier that gives the COMMAND or that a worker would copy needs changing. A carrier stating the RULE in prose ('read the diff for what you would revert') is correct and stays. Do not touch the prose ones — list them in the PR body as deliberately unchanged.

GATE: mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/the-mayor-method/ — that tree is not in mkdocs.yml's nav, so the site build would exit green having read none of it. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DOES cover it. scripts/check_readme_links.py validates .claude/commands/ references into docs/the-mayor-method/ and is the gate if you touch a command file.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8122 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/8122), branch worker/hygrule-0bmf, commit c4c64ad72b. PREMISE PARTLY STALE, DEFECT REAL. The bead quotes 'Diff against origin/main before you push'; PR #8112 had already genericised that line hours earlier to 'Diff against the trunk before you push', so there is NO literal 'git diff origin/main' command left anywhere in the tracked tree (git grep over tracked files, excluding .beads, returns nothing). The defect survived genericisation and arguably worsened: 'Diff against the trunk' is the two-dot comparison STATED IN WORDS - it names the trunk's current tip as the base - so a faithful reader still gets the noisy form and now has no command to copy that would have got it right. FIX: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:503 lead clause changed to 'Diff your branch against its MERGE BASE before you push, and read that diff for what you would REVERT', plus a new paragraph giving the reason so it is not simplified back, naming the three-dot form as '<TRUNK>...HEAD' in the file's existing placeholder convention and introduced as 'in the dominant toolchain' to stay OS/VCS-neutral per the tree's post-#8112 register. PREMISE REPRODUCED LIVE on this branch: three-dot 'git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD' showed 1 file (mine); two-dot 'git diff --stat origin/main' showed 5, four of them the trunk's and rendered AS MY DELETIONS - i.e. the noise is not merely bulk, it has the same reversed-hunk shape as the false-revert signal the step exists to detect. CARRIER SWEEP (git grep: 'git diff origin/main', 'diff against origin/main', 'what you would REVERT', 'merge-base origin/main', 'origin/main...'): ONE carrier changed, dispatch-prompt-template.md:503, the only one naming a base. LEFT STANDING as correct prose per the bead's own discriminator and listed in the PR body: loops.md:173 (merge-review 'diff matches its tracker item'), loops.md:256 (routing verification), loops.md:318 + dispatch-prompt-template.md:156 ('can silently revert each other', two workers on one surface), loops.md:603,610 (tracker-write reverts). Left standing as ALREADY CORRECT: scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:270,286, scripts/git-hooks/test-pre-commit.sh:716, scripts/_test_fixtures/test_fast_pr_docs_gate/run-self-test.sh:91 - all already merge-base form. CORRECTION TO THE BEAD: it names docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md as a known carrier; it is NOT one - loops.md carries no pre-push diff rule in any wording, because the pre-push read is a worker instruction and lives only in the dispatch template. .claude/commands/mayor-*.md checked and carries no pre-push diff instruction either; unchanged. README.md untouched per the operator's ruling. GATES (captured to .exit files on the same command line, never through a pipe): python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; python scripts/check_readme_links.py exit 0 (run because the PR touches the target side of the .claude/commands -> docs/the-mayor-method link). BOTH SABOTAGE-VERIFIED against this worktree, since both print nothing on success: a single-line broken link planted in dispatch-prompt-template.md drove check_doc_slugs.py to exit 1 naming 'docs\the-mayor-method\dispatch-prompt-template.md:511 -> no-such-file-hygrule-0bmf.md'; a single-line ref rewrite in .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md:4 drove check_readme_links.py to exit 1 naming that line. Both restores verified with git hash-object against the pre-plant blob (not sha256sum, not git diff): dispatch-prompt-template.md 68fbee2863b00e1c87da9a5f50d422df4ecd4f07 both sides, mayor-posture.md 4a10cf6b853ea74065ab7d316e564f8dfc32d4a7 both sides; mayor-posture.md is not in the diff. mkdocs build --strict deliberately NOT nominated - docs/the-mayor-method/ is absent from mkdocs.yml's nav, so it would exit green having inspected none of these pages. Hand-verified (ungated): line widths 112-118 within the file's 120 max, bold/backtick delimiters balanced, no table touched, every sentence of the original paragraph survives the rewrap with only the bolded lead clause changed.

title: docs/async/http.md is incomplete on the same fact rf2-j44x corrected in docs/machines
description:
FOUND BY worker/machdoc-j44x while fixing rf2-j44x (PR #8116). It correctly REFUSED to edit outside its fence and reported the finding instead. This bead is the owner that finding needs — without it the finding lives only in one agent's transcript and disappears when that agent does.

THE FACT. `dispatch-aborted!` (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc, around :561-645) routes every abort. For reason `:actor-destroyed` it derives the reply event's head and tests it with `actor-destroy-target-obsolete?` (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc, around :296-315, literally `(= reply-target-id actor-id)`):

  - head = the destroyed actor-id  -> NO app dispatch at all. Status `:stale`, `:rf.reply/work-status :suppressed`, stale-reason `:rf.http/actor-destroyed-target-obsolete`, trace row `:rf.http/stale-suppressed`.
  - head = an ordinary event       -> `:status :cancelled` with `{:kind :rf.http/aborted :reason :actor-destroyed}` under `:error`.

So: THE REQUEST IS ALWAYS ABORTED, BUT A REPLY IS NOT ALWAYS DELIVERED.

WHAT IS INCOMPLETE (line numbers are CLAIMS from the reporting worker and will drift — locate by text):

title: every check_*.py --self-test is deleted by python -O and prints OK having proved nothing
description:
Found while fixing rf2-t9kd (PR #8114). The control-that-cannot-catch-its-own-case class, applied to the whole checker family.

Every scripts/check_*.py --self-test in this repo is built from bare 'assert'. python -O (or PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1 in the environment) deletes every assert statement, so the function runs to its final print and returns 0 having verified nothing. The npm scripts and workflows invoke plain 'python', so nothing is broken today -- but the gate that is supposed to prove a gate fires is silenced by an interpreter flag, and it announces success while doing it.

Reproduced against the five hicasso siblings, all exit 0 under -O with their usual OK line:
  check_budget_ledger.py, check_complaint_catalogue.py, check_freeze.py,
  check_lint_export.py, check_optional_module_reachability.py

check_example_fence_coverage.py is already fixed (PR #8114) and exits 1 with a message naming the cause. The guard is five lines at the top of self_test():

  try:
      assert False
  except AssertionError:
      pass
  else:
      raise SystemExit('assertions are disabled (python -O / PYTHONOPTIMIZE), so this self-test would prove nothing. Re-run without -O.')

Scope judgement for the implementor: the ~39 scripts/check_*.py at repo root share the idiom and the hole. Copying five lines into forty files is a lot of duplication for a low-probability failure -- a shared helper, or fixing only the hicasso five, or declaring the whole thing not worth it, are all defensible answers. A source-located refusal closes this bead honestly.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8120 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/8120), commit 6687bf796d's parent. Premise verified before acting: all five hicasso siblings exited 0 under python -O printing their usual OK line. Copied PR #8114's empirical guard (assert False in a try, require the AssertionError) rather than inventing a second mechanism; it is stronger than reading __debug__ because it also catches a .pyc compiled under -O and run without it. After: plain=0, -O=1, PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1 -> 1, for all five, with a message naming the cause. SCOPE REFUSAL, as this bead licenses: fixed the five hicasso siblings only. The idiom is shared by 45 --self-test scripts repo-wide (38 scripts/check_*.py at root); copying five lines into forty files is not worth it for a hole no invocation in this repo opens (every npm script and workflow calls plain python). check_example_fence_coverage.py is the sixth sibling and was left to PR #8114, which fixes it -- touching it here would have conflicted.

description:

The commits are pushed, so they are durable — but nothing in the tracker points at them, which is the definition of unowned.

THE QUESTION, and it is small. A spike is often meant to be thrown away, and the commit subjects read that way. Two possibilities, and they need different actions:

  A. The spike served its purpose and the conclusion already landed elsewhere. Then the branch is disposable — record WHERE the conclusion landed on rf2-hic-081, and delete the remote ref.
  B. The spike concluded something that never got promoted. Then the conclusion must land in its owning tracked record BEFORE the branch goes, because a closed bead plus an unreferenced branch is a conclusion nobody can find.

READ rf2-hic-081's close reason first — it may already answer this, in which case this bead closes as a verified no-op, which is a good outcome.

DO NOT delete the remote ref until one of A or B is settled and recorded. Deleting it is the only irreversible move available here, and three commits of real spike work is a poor thing to lose to tidiness.
close_reason:
RESOLVED BY READING — route A of the two this bead set out, and no work was needed.

rf2-hic-081's close reason answers it directly: 'SPIKE COMPLETE — VERDICT: SPLIT. The counts receipt graduates as a DESIGN; the self-time field is KILLED. No PR, correctly: this bead's own surface line says nothing retained without graduation, and the spike graduated no code.'

So origin/worker/receipts-hic081's three commits are a spike that DELIBERATELY produced no PR. The absence of a PR is the design working, not an oversight, which is what this bead could not tell from outside.

AND THE CONCLUSION IS NOT STRANDED. That was the real risk — a closed bead plus an unreferenced branch is a conclusion nobody can find. It is not the case here: rf2-hic-081's close reason carries the substantive verdict in full, including the load-bearing step (the cache-hit answer is stable across an attempt, because cold-read! retains nothing and the generation fence guarantees a pass observes one commit), which is what deletes the per-read counter and reduces the design to ONE TAP, IN run-once, PER ATTEMPT. Five of the six named fields need no tap on any hot loop. That is self-contained on the bead, which is the standard.

THE BRANCH IS THEREFORE DISPOSABLE, AND I HAVE NOT DELETED IT. Deleting a remote ref is the one irreversible move available here and it is not urgent — three commits of real spike work is a poor thing to lose to tidiness, and nothing is blocked by the ref existing. title: ci: retire the donor-inventory snapshot checker — 906 lines guarding an archive that no spec or doc cites and git already records
description:
AUDIT FINDING from rf2-m08s (read-only CI cleanup audit), 2026-08-13 15:19 AUSEST. This is the ONE piece of the three workflows whose retirement trigger is available TODAY and needs nothing else to move first. It is a CLAIM for the operator to rule, not a directive.

WHAT IT IS. .github/workflows/freehand-conformance.yml runs two steps that have nothing to do with the conformance index:

  - name: Self-test the donor-inventory snapshot check
    run: python scripts/check_donor_inventory.py --self-test --verbose
  - name: Check the archived donor-inventory snapshot
    run: python scripts/check_donor_inventory.py --ci

scripts/check_donor_inventory.py is 906 lines. Since rf2-lrtwj (commit 8bfba864cc, 'archive the withdrawn donor ledger; its gate becomes a snapshot validator') its entire live function is: spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md still equals a 224-row tuple table pinned inside the checker itself (SNAPSHOT_ROWS, one sha256[:12] digest per description cell). Three arms that compared the ledger against the working tree — the donor-tree partition, the live-consumer census, the stale-row scan — were deleted with the programme.

MEASURED. `python scripts/check_donor_inventory.py --ci` — RAW EXIT 0: 'donor-inventory snapshot: 224 rows checked against 224 pinned. At the 2026-07-30 withdrawal 149 were recorded pending — undisposed when the programme stopped, owned by nobody since — and 75 done.'

WHO CITES THE ARCHIVE. I grepped the whole tracked tree for donor-inventory. The complete consumer set, excluding the checker itself and .beads:

  .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:1509-1510, 1665-1674 — cites it in order to EXCLUDE it from every surface arm ('a MEASURED EXCLUSION... it cannot observe a source change at all')
  implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:4764-4773, 5519-5525 — tests that exclusion
  scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py:112 — one comment naming an F1/pending MOVE row
  TESTING.md:194, 228 — prose about the two above
  .github/workflows/test.yml:1079 — names it as part of the measured exclusion

ZERO citations from spec/** or docs/** — including EP-0036, which withdrew the programme. Nothing normative cites this archive. Every CI reference exists to keep it OUT of the CI graph.

THE ARGUMENT. The check's whole content is 'this archived markdown file has not been edited'. Git already records that immutably, and the pre-commit hooks + PR review already sit between an accidental edit and main. Under the project's stated stance — trust the programmer, reject over-engineering — 906 lines of self-tested machinery defending an untouched archive that no record cites is the clearest candidate in the three workflows.

IT DOES NOT REQUIRE THE FREEHAND TREE TO GO FIRST. The archive is a document. It can outlive its checker, or leave with it, and neither choice is coupled to implementation/freehand/.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS. A refusal is also a fine answer: 'it costs under a second, leave it' is defensible. The audit's position is that it is the strongest retire-now candidate found, not that it must go.

title: ci: portability.yml's third job is named for a tree that is scheduled for deletion, but its rule is tree-independent — retitle before the donor goes
description:
AUDIT FINDING from rf2-m08s (read-only CI cleanup audit), 2026-08-13 15:17 AUSEST. A naming defect with a real consequence: it invites a future worker to delete a live guard as collateral.

THE ANSWER TO THE OPERATOR'S QUESTION FIRST. portability.yml has three jobs and NONE of them is historical. All three enforce a rule recorded outside the workflow:

  1. 'No hardcoded personal/home paths' (scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh) — LIVE.   2. 'No newly tracked files under ai/' — LIVE, and its baseline is now ZERO. Measured: `git ls-files ai/` returns 0 files. CLAUDE.md's 'Local working files (the ai/ tree)' section states the rule and names zero-tracked as the end state; the end state is REACHED, so this ratchet is now the only thing holding it. Its own comment anticipated this ('S7 (rf2-vxgfnd.99.1) removes the remaining trees and must never be blocked by this gate'). The 2026-07-18 incident it exists for — a force-added ai/ dossier carrying a personal worktree path, which reddened main — is unchanged in likelihood.

  3. 'No re-frame.ui view-lifetime residue' — LIVE, but MISNAMED. See below.

THE FINDING. scripts/check_view_lifetime_residue.py has NO coupling to re-frame.ui at all. Read its mechanism: it constructs a four-character stem at runtime from fragments (`_STEM`), builds one regex over that stem plus word tails (e/es/ed/ing) with a fixed-width negative lookbehind excluding two ordinary English survivors, and scans EVERY git-tracked file's content and path, excluding only .beads/**. No baseline, no ceiling, no allowlist, permitted count exactly zero. The rule is 'this word does not appear in this repository', full stop.

So it does not retire with implementation/ui/. It is precisely what stops a THIRD substrate (Hicasso) reintroducing the vocabulary the excision epic removed — which is the case it is most needed for, and the one its own title argues against.

Measured: `python scripts/check_view_lifetime_residue.py --verbose` RAW EXIT 0, 'ratchet clean: zero residue in tracked content or paths'.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. EP-0038 HD-018 rules that on a win 'the public re-frame.freehand and re-frame.ui surfaces are DELETED', and HD-029 (operator, 2026-08-13 04:57 AUSEST) graduated Hicasso. Nothing in the file says otherwise.

Separately: spec/conformance/freehand/donor-inventory.md:484 pins '.github/workflows/portability.yml | donor paths in the portability matrix | REPLACE | F6 | pending' — an undisposed row from the withdrawn absorption programme naming this exact coupling. It was never actioned and the programme stopped.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS. Retitle the job and its comment block so the rule stands on its own — the vocabulary ban is repo-wide and outlives every substrate that ever carried it — and state explicitly that it does NOT retire with implementation/ui/. title: test-support: :async? true becomes platform-guarded async-capable — fn-form on :clj, map on :cljs
description:
Hardening follow-up from the rf2-pn3d ruling (delegated ruling 2026-08-13: keep the fn-form default). Cross-refs: rf2-pn3d (the ruling and full measurements), rf2-u0j8 (the browser-lane diagnostic that names the fn-fixture+async abort in seconds).

CHANGE. In implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc, make-reset-runtime-fixture (defn ~line 580; shape-selection branch ~line 818: `(if (:async? opts) {:before ... :after ...} (fn [test-fn] ...))`) currently returns the {:before :after} map on BOTH platforms when :async? true. Make :async? true mean "async-capable" rather than "map shape": return the fn-form on :clj unconditionally, the map only on :cljs — e.g. select the branch with `(if #?(:clj false :cljs (:async? opts)) <map-form> <fn-form>)` (exact mechanics implementer's choice; the shared halves reinstate-and-snapshot! / reset-runtime! / finish-runtime-reset! are already factored, so the change is confined to the shape-selection expression). Update the docstring's :async? entry and the "Returns" line accordingly: async-capable; the fn-form IS the correct async-capable JVM shape, because clojure.test has no async tests and no map-fixture support.

THE TRAP THIS REMOVES (map-on-JVM silent swallow). clojure.test treats a fixture as IFn; a map IS IFn (key lookup), so a {:before ...} fixture on the JVM composes to a fn that returns nil WITHOUT calling the test — the namespace reports "Ran 0 tests" and reads GREEN. In-tree documentation of hitting exactly this while the suite was being written: implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_component_cljs_test.cljc:29-34. This trap is why the .cljc async consumers each dance `(cond-> {...} #?(:clj false :cljs true) (assoc :async? true))` — live at implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/render_batch_host_checkpoint_cljs_test.cljc:67 and implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc:60 (the rf2-pn3d dossier counted three .cljc async consumers; two are grep-verifiable today). Simplify those cond-> dances to a plain :async? true in the same PR — identical resulting shapes on both platforms, by construction. After this change every future rf2-il7b-style async flip is a plain :async? true with no platform thought.

SHAPE SEMANTICS (inherited analysis from the rf2-pn3d dossier). The fn-form `(fn [test-fn] ...)` wraps the sync body and establishes the ambient frame scope with a dynamic binding; it is unusable for CLJS async tests (the binding unwinds before the async body resumes; cljs.test hard-errors "Async tests require fixtures to be specified as maps" and the throw lands outside per-test accounting, unwinding the whole bundle). The map {:before :after} set!s the scope persistently in :before and tears it down in :after; it is unusable on the JVM (silent-green trap above) and cannot be mixed with sibling fn fixtures in one use-fixtures call (cljs.test: "Fixtures may not be of mixed types"). For synchronous bodies the two shapes are behaviourally equivalent; consumers depend on the fn-form's callability and composability, not on the binding itself.

ACCEPTANCE.
- No test-count change in ANY lane (per-artefact JVM suites, node test:cljs, browser lane). Trivially so: no .clj consumer passes :async?; .cljs consumers are untouched (the :cljs branch is unchanged); the .cljc cond-> sites produce the same per-platform shapes before and after the simplification.

title: hic-052 follow-up: visibility:hidden on a trailing modal control costs a missed focus wrap
description:
ROUTED from worker/radioedge-hic052 (rf2-hic-052, PR #8089), which named this at source rather than half-modelling it and flagged it to the mayor as a judgement call. I am filing it because it is the one of the four unmodelled cases with a plausible real-markup path.

THE FINDING. sequential-tab-stops now models the browser's focus order for radio groups and positive tabindex. Four cases remain COUNTED as candidates but are not real stops: an inert subtree, a disabled fieldset, visibility:hidden, and closed <details> contents. All four are documented at source WITH the measured reason they are safe: .focus() on each REFUSES (returns false), and wrap-tab! confirms the landing before taking the default action away — so a surplus candidate that cannot take focus costs a MISSED WRAP (the engine's own conduct, focus escapes to body) rather than a WRONG LANDING (focus goes somewhere it should not). That distinction is the whole argument and it is sound.

WHY THIS ONE ANYWAY. visibility:hidden on a TRAILING control inside a modal is plausible markup — a conditionally-hidden final button is an ordinary pattern. When it is the last candidate, the wrap has nothing to land on and focus reaches <body>: exactly the leak rf2-hic-052 was reopened twice to close, arriving by a fourth route.

THE REMEDY THE WORKER NAMED, and its cost: one platform call, checkVisibility({visibilityProperty, contentVisibilityAuto}), closes THREE of the four. It needs a support-matrix branch, which is why it sat outside that bead's explicitly bounded repair.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST, and this is the load-bearing step: build the case and measure it. A trailing visibility:hidden control in a modal, trusted Tab off the last real stop, and read document.activeElement. If focus does NOT reach body — because the engine drops it from the candidate set for a reason the worker's .focus() probe did not capture — then this is not a defect and a verified refusal closes the bead. The worker measured .focus() refusing; it did not measure the wrap failing.

DO NOT model the other three speculatively. If checkVisibility closes them as a side effect of closing this one, say so and keep them named in the comment. The stance rejects half a model with no statement of its own boundary — which is what produced the radio-group bug in the first place.

THE CONTROL IS THE DELIVERABLE: the row must go RED against the current sequential-tab-stops and green with the fix. Scope the plant to the module (an assertion failure, never a crash — the browser lane runs in one block and a crash stops every namespace after it while the log still looks plausible), and compare namespace and assertion counts against a control run.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING: #8089 retired a FALSE claim already in that file — the old tab-stop? docstring said getClientRects filtered content inside a closed <details>, and it does not (measured rects: 1). Trust the current comment over any older one.

FENCE: the Hicasso overlay implementation and its witnesses. rf2-umjv owns the overlay anchor refusal and the focus one-shot recipe — do not absorb it. Do NOT edit the trusted-input bridge.

GATES: npm run test:browser decides it; quote the raw CAPTURED exit code, never the harness's.
close_reason:
Reproduced and fixed; PR #8093 (stacked off #8089, rebased onto main after #8089 merged mid-task).

MEASURED, on activeElement rather than .focus()'s return: a modal holding [reason ok cancel ghost] with ghost visibility:hidden, trusted Tab, pre-fix predicate in place —
  forward  (from #reason): [ok cancel BODY reason ok]
  backward (from #reason): [BODY cancel ok reason BODY]
The wrap does fail and focus reaches <body> at BOTH edges. Forward leaks because ghost is mistaken for the last stop; backward leaks because the wrap aims at ghost, .focus() declines, preventDefault is correctly withheld, and withholding it hands focus to the engine. So this was a real defect, not a refusal.

FIX: rendered? asks checkVisibility({visibilityProperty: true}), falling back to the old getClientRects reading on an engine without the method (the support-matrix branch).

PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD — the bead's named remedy was checkVisibility({visibilityProperty, contentVisibilityAuto}) closing THREE of four. Both halves are wrong, measured:
  1. contentVisibilityAuto MUST NOT be passed. A control in a skipped content-visibility:auto subtree STILL TAKES FOCUS while that option answers false for it, so passing it would drop a REAL stop — a candidate set too small puts the wrap at the wrong control, strictly worse than one that fails to fire. opacityProperty likewise off: opacity:0 is focusable.
  2. It closes TWO of the four, not three: visibility:hidden and closed-<details> contents (the latter via the bare call's UA content-visibility:hidden). inert subtrees and disabled <fieldset> both still answer checkVisibility true. content-visibility:hidden subtrees are closed as a bonus, and were not on the list at all.

LEFT NAMED at source on sequential-tab-stops, not half-modelled: inert subtree, disabled <fieldset>. Their old argument is kept but narrowed — they cost a missed wrap, and no measured markup puts either LAST in a modal, which is the only position where the cost is a leak. The <fieldset> remedy is recorded for whoever earns it: :disabled as a pseudo-class matches the effective state that the .disabled property does not.

CONTROL: a-real-tab-wraps-past-a-trailing-hidden-control. Plant = pre-fix rect predicate (assertion failure, not a crash); restore verified by sha256sum -c (OK). Planted raw exit 1, 1477 tests/9199 assertions, 3 failures — all three in this row, run continued through later namespaces. Restored raw exit 0, same 1477/9199, 0 failures. test:cljs raw exit 0 (13826/69940, 0 failures). Post-rebase test:browser raw exit 0 (1478/9204, 0 failures).

at flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs:189 — `(not (= 1 0))`, the COUNTER'S OWN ARITHMETIC.

`what-the-revision-bump-is-actually-load-bearing-FOR` stayed GREEN. Its four
DOM/model assertions, including the one whose message reads "restored. The
revision moved, so the wall opened on a value React's own diff had nothing to
say about", pass with no revision bump anywhere in the application.

## Why, at source

`impl/codec.cljs` `revision-key` states the whole delivery: "the revision is a
value the body reads, ITS CHANGE RE-RUNS THE BODY, the re-run re-commits the
element, and the commit re-asserts the model against the DOM." React 19's
`updateHostComponent` marks a host update on props-object IDENTITY (HD-004
refuses prop-object caching), so ANY re-render of the boundary re-asserts the
model over the DOM — drifted or not.

So `::h/revision` is load-bearing only where the reset leaves EVERY other
subscription the body reads `=`. The editor's discard does not: `#discard`'s
own enabled/disabled state, `::subs/dirty?` and `:draft` are read by the same
body, and the row's own setup leaves at least one of them moving. The bump is
therefore not the thing that re-runs the body, and the row cannot tell its
presence from its absence.

An independent confirmation from the same run: a probe added to the slice's flow
suite drifted a field's DOM with an EVENTLESS write (the password-manager shape
the testbed's `revision` arm uses) and then discarded, with the bump deleted from
BOTH applications. It stayed green — the drift was repaired by the discard's own
re-render.

## Not absorbed, deliberately

rf2-36bd is fenced to `examples/slice/**` and the two authoring reports, and
CHECKPOINT 2 (rf2-hic-026, worker/slicerev-hic026) was live on this surface, so
this is filed rather than fixed. It may already be owned there.

## Acceptance

1. Either the row is made to red on the deleted bump — which needs a reset that
   moves NOTHING else the body reads, i.e. a narrower read set than
   `editor`'s form body has — or it is rewritten to claim only what it
   witnesses and the load-bearing claim moves to the testbed's `revision` /
   `revision-strict` arms, which drive a bare `bump-revision` button against an
   eventless drift and are the only witnesses measured to red.
2. The corrective PR quotes the planted re-run with its CAPTURED exit code.
3. `examples/editor/events.cljs` §"The revision counter is the author's to
   invent" and `flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs`'s header claim about "what
   `::h/revision` buys" are brought into line with whatever (1) settles.

title: CI: resolve-clojure-deps.sh:149 annotation title is truncated by a raw comma
description:
FOUND BY rf2-h082 (PR #8079) while fixing the sibling defect in install-clojure-cli.sh. NOT ACTIONED there: outside that PR's fence.

THE CLAIM, and it is the SAME claim rf2-h082 verified at source rather than a new one. .github/scripts/resolve-clojure-deps.sh:149 emits

  ::error title=Dependency resolution failed - transport-level, cause not established::`clojure -P ...` failed N times ...

GitHub workflow-command properties are comma-separated key=value pairs. actions/runner src/Runner.Common/ActionCommand.cs TryParseV2 splits the property segment on ',' and each pair on '=' with count 2, keeping only pairs that yield two parts. So ' cause not established' has no '=', is dropped SILENTLY, and the rendered title is 'Dependency resolution failed - transport-level' while the command still parses. Nothing reds; the half that tells the reader the classification is HEDGED simply never appears. The runner's own unit test (ActionCommandL0 CommandParserV2Test) requires %2C for a comma to survive into a property value, and @actions/toolkit escapeProperty emits it that way.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN AT THE FIXED SITE. This annotation's whole job is to say the cause is NOT established -- 'That signature is EVIDENCE A RE-RUN MAY HELP ... but it is NOT proof the cause is external'. Truncated to 'transport-level' the title asserts exactly the confident classification the body spends a paragraph refusing. That inverts the message rather than shortening it.

SCOPE. This one site only. Its sibling at :138 ('- no transient transport signature') carries no comma and is clean, as are the three em-dash titles in lint.yml:330, test.yml:5851 and playwright-install-failed.sh:108.

FIX, and do not restyle beyond it: replace the comma with an em-dash (matching every other annotation title in the repo) or %2C-escape it. One character class.

NOT MEASURED ON A RUNNER, same as rf2-h082: this annotation fires only after the resolver exhausts its attempts with a transient signature every time, and no rendered instance exists in this repo's CI history to read. The verification above is from the vendor's parser and its own test.

GATES: bash -n, plus the CI roster's own invocation `git ls-files '.github/scripts/*.sh' | xargs shellcheck` (portability.yml:106-116).
FENCE: .github/scripts/resolve-clojure-deps.sh only. Do NOT edit .github/workflows/**.

title: hic: both witness applications' import fence walks a HAND-WRITTEN roster of namespaces, so a new app namespace escapes it entirely
description:
## The finding

CHECKPOINT 2 (rf2-hic-026), `main`@5d54f50d76, 2026-08-13.

The two Phase 2 witness applications' central evidence claim is that they were
written on the public door and nothing else, and both make it mechanical rather
than reviewed. `slice/surface_cljs_test.cljs:2-27` says why, well:

    "It is worth exactly as much as the claim that it was written on the public
     surface, and that claim is not one a reader can make by looking at seven
     `ns` forms — a reviewer reads them once, and the next commit is
     unreviewed."

and then says of the fence:

    "It is a predicate, so a namespace added tomorrow is covered the day it
     lands."

**The predicate is, but the population is not.** The population is a hand-written
literal, and it is written TWICE in each file:

- `slice/surface_cljs_test.cljs:42-53` (`app-namespaces`) and `:58-65` (the
  quoted vector handed to `rg/emit-dependency-graph`) — seven names each.
- `todo/surface_cljs_test.cljs:41-50` and `:55-61` — six names each.

`examples/require_graph.clj`'s `emit-dependency-graph` (`:83-96`) takes an
explicit `ns-syms` vector and has no enumeration mode. So a namespace added to
either application tomorrow — `slice/http.cljs`, say, requiring
`re-frame.hicasso.impl.codec` — is compiled, is loaded, is part of the
application, and is invisible to the fence, the roster and every assertion in
the file. Nothing reds. The claim the checkpoint reads off this file silently
narrows from *the application* to *these seven files*.

This is not hypothetical for a frozen artefact: rf2-hic-074 already extended the
slice after its report was written (seven more boundaries, thirteen total). That
extension went into `views.cljs` and stayed inside the fence by luck of
placement, not by construction.

## What is already right, and must not be lost

The file is otherwise a good control and the repair must not disturb it:
`the-graph-is-populated` (`:83-110`) guards the vacuous-pass case, carries four
positive controls, and `every-fence-predicate-fires` (`:142-164`) is a real
sabotage row — each predicate is shown one name it must catch AND two it must
not, including the public door itself.

## Surface fence

`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/require_graph.clj` and the
two `surface_cljs_test.cljs` files. Test-only; no production code, no facade
export, no hot-zone file. Do NOT run `npm run test:hicasso-hmr` (binds
:dev-http 8061).

## Acceptance

1. Each witness's roster is DERIVED rather than typed: the population comes from
   one place, and a source file under the application package that is absent
   from it reds a named row.
2. The repair is proportionate — `require_graph.clj` is a JVM macro and can read
   its own source directory at expansion time; roughly ten lines and one
   assertion per witness. **A larger mechanism is rejected**: no build step, no
   generated file, no manifest to keep in step.
3. The new row is shown to bite: add a throwaway namespace under the package,
   run the node lane, quote the red with its captured exit code, remove it.
4. The two existing controls (`the-graph-is-populated`, `every-fence-predicate-fires`)
   still pass unchanged.

Population derived from the package directory via require-graph/application-namespaces (classpath walk at macro-expansion time); test suites excluded by the build's own cljs-test$ rule; throws rather than answering empty. title: hic-019 G4 — after PR #8066 merges, close out kernel row 2's 'record in flight' note
description:

**Filed by**: rf2-hic-019 CHECKPOINT 1 re-dispatch. This is a loop the checkpoint itself opened, filed so

**Surface fence**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/checkpoint-1-kernel.md` §2.2 and its row-2 line in the §2
table. **Nothing else on the page, and no other page.** Do not touch any other row, the verdict, the gate
table, or the correction ledger.

## Why it exists

Checkpoint 1 ran on `main`@`d079143b91`. Kernel row 2 (process-global ownership) has landed witnesses and

> for its *record*. No bead is filed: the PR is live and owned. **The next reader of this page re-checks
> that #8066 landed.**

A sentence that asks an unnamed future reader to do something is exactly the shape this checkpoint filed
`rf2-aubc` about. This bead is the named reader.

## What would close it

1. PR #8066 reads merged on the remote and its commit is on the pulled `main`.
2. `docs/design/hicasso/product/globals.md` exists on `main` and the roster it publishes is the
   nineteen-owner census with its four re-derivable searches.

4. If #8066 is instead abandoned or materially changed, §2.2 says that rather than being deleted — the

**Do not re-run the kernel suites for this.** The witnesses were re-run at `d079143b91` and #8066 touches
three source files plus documentation; if its own gates are green, row 2's measurement is unchanged. This
bead is a record-keeping close-out, not a re-audit.
