title: Hygiene: reaping on a worker's completion report destroys the tree a later follow-up needs
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 on worker/attempt-lbve (rf2-lbve, PR #8064).

WHAT HAPPENED. The worker reported done. The hygiene loop reaped its worktree on that report — correct by the rule, which says only the worker's own completion report authorises a reap. Its PR then hit a merge conflict (two beads had been dispatched into the same block of one file). I resumed the worker to rebase, and its worktree no longer existed. In its own words: 'the rebase had nowhere to run.'

NO WORK WAS LOST, and that is the important half: both commits were already pushed, so the worker recreated the worktree on the existing branch and carried on. The commit-and-push-as-you-go rule is what made the reap survivable. But the worker spent a turn rebuilding a tree, and a less careful one might have re-derived the work instead.

THE GAP, stated precisely: 'reported done' and 'no longer needed' are not the same state. A PR can need a rebase, a fix-worker, or a follow-up long after its author reports — and this session's merge rate makes that ordinary rather than rare.

WHAT IS NOT THE ANSWER. Do NOT weaken the reap rule. Every proxy for 'this worker is finished' has been tried here and each one killed a live run; the report is the only signal that has never lied. Reaping later is not a defect.

THE ACTUAL QUESTION, and it is a judgement rather than a fix: is a worktree whose PR is still OPEN worth keeping until the PR merges? That is a one-line change to the hygiene loop's disposition — hold while an open PR names the branch — at the cost of a handful of stale directories during a busy period. Twelve pre-compaction worktrees already sit unreapable for an unrelated reason, so the marginal cost is small.

ALTERNATIVE WORTH WEIGHING: leave the rule alone and accept the recreate. It cost one turn, the worker handled it correctly and unprompted, and adding a second condition to a rule whose strength is its simplicity may be the worse trade. The stance rejects over-engineering, and this may be an instance.

WHOEVER TAKES THIS: read .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md and docs/the-mayor-method/ first, decide with the reasoning stated, and if the answer is 'leave it', close the bead with that reasoning recorded rather than actioning it. A verified 'this is correct as it stands' is a complete deliverable.

Also record, wherever the answer lands: a worker resumed after its worktree is reaped must rebuild before rebasing, and pushed commits are what make that safe.
notes: FENCED 2026-08-13 16:5x AUSEST (mayor dispatch tick). Surface is docs/the-mayor-method/ + .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, which worker/clause4-qivw holds for rf2-qivw. CLEARS WHEN: rf2-qivw's PR merges. Not a blocker on the work itself - the analysis is independent - only on the edit window.
close_reason: VERIFIED ALREADY COVERED - NO CHANGE MADE. Cross-ref PR #8122 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/8122), which carries the analysis in its body; the PR's only code change belongs to rf2-0ko8. The bead itself says 'if the answer is leave it, close the bead with that reasoning recorded rather than actioning it. A verified this is correct as it stands is a complete deliverable' - that is this close. THE ANSWER IS ALREADY IN THE TREE, IN THREE PLACES, AND IT IS 'KEEP THE RULE'. (1) docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md:477-482, under Hygiene > Reaping, states the cost, the recovery and the ruling: 'Reaping on the report is correct and still costs something. A worker can need its tree AFTER it reports, because its change hits a conflict and needs a rebase. Pushed commits make that survivable - the worker recreates the tree on the existing branch and continues. Whether to hold a worktree while its change is open is a real trade, and "leave the rule alone and accept the rebuild" is a defensible answer. Do not add a second condition to a rule whose strength is that it has one.' That is the bead's ACTUAL QUESTION posed and answered. (2) docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md:311-318, under the heading 'Two tensions the method does not resolve', carries the bead's second explicit ask - 'a worker resumed after its worktree is reaped must rebuild before rebasing, and pushed commits are what make that safe' - almost verbatim: 'Nothing is lost when that happens, because the commits were pushed, but the worker has to rebuild its tree first. Keep the rule. Let the residue accumulate, and clear it on explicit operator authority rather than inventing another proxy.' (3) docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:124-128 records the same incident from the dispatch side as the scheduling error that caused it ('Two costs from one scheduling error'). This repository's own instantiation, .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md:6, already routes the hygiene loop to that exact loops.md section and says 'do not add a seventh'. REFUSED, and the refusal is the deliverable: no seventh reap-proxy (out of scope by the bead's own words, and every proxy tried has destroyed a live run); no second condition on the reap rule (forbidden by the loops.md text quoted above); and no fourth restatement of the recovery procedure, which would be duplication rather than coverage - the stance rejects over-engineering and this would be an instance. Note for anyone reopening: the recovery is recorded where BOTH readers need it - the mayor-facing hygiene rule (loops.md) and the method rationale (bootstrap.md) - so a worker resumed onto a reaped tree is covered by the standing commit-and-push-as-you-go rule plus 'recreate the tree on the existing branch and continue'. FENCE CLEARED before work: the bead's note fenced this on rf2-qivw's PR merging; rf2-qivw is CLOSED and PR #8109 merged, so the edit window was open. No gate applies to a no-op; the PR's gates (check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, check_readme_links.py exit 0, both sabotage-verified) cover the tree this bead was verified against.

title: CI: --with-deps apt hop blew a timeout-minutes: 5 cap without ever reaching the browser download
description:
MEASURED while fixing rf2-swos (2026-08-13).

Job 93920468065 ('Tenant-switcher testbed browser smoke', 2026-08-11) died with

    ##[error]The action 'Install Playwright (Chromium + system deps)' has timed out after 5 minutes.

The whole five minutes was spent inside the `--with-deps` apt hop fetching
21.1 MB of fonts from azure.archive.ubuntu.com. Reading the log by timestamp:
Get:2 at 20:39:16, Get:3 at 20:40:19, Get:4 at 20:42:06, Get:6 at 20:43:07,
guillotined at 20:44:20. The BROWSER DOWNLOAD WAS NEVER REACHED, so this is a
second, distinct mode of 'the gate never ran' at the same step.

TWO THINGS FOLLOW, neither actioned by rf2-swos:

1. A step the runner guillotines never prints its own annotation, so
   rf2-swos's `::error` handler cannot fire in this mode. Three of the
   twenty-one Playwright install sites carry `timeout-minutes: 5`
   (test.yml:4395, 4464, 5530). Either the cap is too tight for a step that
   does apt + a browser download, or the apt half should be split out and
   capped separately.

2. `--with-deps` is doing very little on ubuntu-24.04. In job 94299983393's
   log every Chromium shared library reports 'is already the newest version';
   the only NEW packages are nine FONT packages (fonts-ipafont-gothic,
   fonts-freefont-ttf, fonts-unifont, fonts-wqy-zenhei, xfonts-*), 21.1 MB and
   79.5 MB on disk, on every one of twenty-one jobs. Whether the browser
   proofs need those fonts at all is worth establishing before paying for them
   twenty-one times per run.

VERIFY BEFORE ACTING: the 'already the newest version' reading is from ONE
runner image. Confirm against a current ubuntu-24.04 image before dropping
`--with-deps` anywhere — a missing shared library turns a green gate into an
unlaunchable Chromium, which is strictly worse than a slow apt.

HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/* is sequential.
close_reason:
REFUSAL on the substance + comment-only PR #8067. Measured, both questions answer 'no change warranted'.

Q1 (cap too tight, or apt hop too fat?): NEITHER.
- 183 samples of every 'Install Playwright*' step across 2026-08-10..2026-08-13: 183 successes, 0 failures, min 10s / p50 13s / p90 21s / p99 32s / max 49s. The 300s cap is 6.1x the observed worst case. Raising it re-widens the open-ended window rf2-e6enf added the cap to bound (#2304/#2311/#2316/#2324, 15-75+ min each on a wedged apt/dpkg lock, blocking the merge queue) - a regression, not a fix.
- The 9-package observation HOLDS AT SOURCE and is stronger than reported: '0 upgraded, 9 newly installed, 0 to remove' is invariant across ubuntu-24.04 image versions 20260720.247.2 AND 20260810.271.1, four independent jobs. ZERO Chromium shared libraries are installed - all 21 nativeDeps chromium: entries report 'already the newest version'. The 9 are fonts from Playwright's separate tools: list plus transitive xfonts-encodings/xfonts-utils.
- BUT the inference from it does NOT hold: those 21.1 MB cost ONE SECOND on a healthy mirror (job 94306922190, 2026-08-13: 'Fetched 21.1 MB in 1s (18.9 MB/s)'; also 21.5/23.4/17.2 MB/s elsewhere). Trimming saves ~1s of a 13s step; it cannot blow a 300s cap.
- And they cannot be trimmed anyway (playwright-core 1.59.1, read at source): Registry.installDeps does an UNCONDITIONAL targets.add('tools') (registry/index.js), and installDependenciesLinux already passes --no-install-recommends (registry/dependencies.js). Only lever is dropping --with-deps wholesale -> trades a loud annotated apt failure for a silent dependency on a runner-image property; a removed lib = unlaunchable Chromium. Declined, per the bead's own warning.
- ROOT CAUSE of job 93920468065: mirror-throughput collapse. Fonts came down at a sustained ~52 kB/s (55.5 / 52.8 / 44.6 / 51.4 kB/s per package off the log timestamps) while that job's OWN apt-get update fetched 11.3 MB in 1s (7831 kB/s) from the SAME azure.archive.ubuntu.com seconds earlier in the SAME step - 150x apart. No cap survives it: 21.1 MB at 52 kB/s is ~405s of download alone.

Q2 (does #8065's cache change this?): NO, measured two ways.
- #8065's diff adds cache steps at test.yml 1318/5017/5933 + docs/expensive-tests/template-release - the last EIGHT sites. All three timeout-minutes:5 sites (4395/4464/5530) already carry the cache on main. No overlap, no rebase conflict.
- Stronger: job 93920468065 scored an EXACT-KEY cache HIT ('Cache restored from key: Linux-playwright-96be61e0...') at 20:39:07 and blew the cap anyway, 100% inside apt. A hit skips the DOWNLOAD, which was never reached.

NOT DONE, deliberately: no retry loop on the apt hop (reporter's reasoning stands); no cap raise; and the guillotine-no-annotation gap is left open with reasoning - moving the cap into the command (timeout 270 npx playwright install ...) would fix it but breaks check_fast_pr_gap.py's ^npx playwright install\b setup pattern and FAIL-OPENS the gap map, the exact trap documented in playwright-install-failed.sh's header. At 0/183 failures, and with #8061 covering the common exit-1 mode, not worth taking.

PR #8067 is COMMENT-ONLY (78 insertions, 0 deletions, zero non-comment lines) recording this at the three capped sites so the next reader does not raise the number. PyYAML shape dump of test.yml byte-identical before/after (sha256 5e3439ea08ac...); gap map 96 before / 96 after with a planted-fault discriminator proving the gate reads the worktree (96 -> 97); check_gate_scheduling identical. All gate exit codes 0.

title: Browser lane: 44 namespaces are on positional fixtures, not the 3 #8038 reported
description:
PR #8038 named THREE :browser-test namespaces using positional fixtures, each one (async done ...) row away from unwinding the entire lane. It found them by grepping for a literal `(fn [f] ... (f))` in `use-fixtures`.

The shared factory hides the same shape behind a call.
`re-frame.test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture` returns the FN FORM by
default; `:async? true` is the opt-in that returns the map.

  for f in $(git ls-files '*_dom_cljs_test.cljs'); do
    grep -q make-reset-runtime-fixture "$f" && ! grep -q ':async? *true' "$f" && echo "$f"
  done | wc -l
  -> 44

So the live blast radius is 44, not 3. Each is correct AS WRITTEN — a
positional fixture is fine in a namespace with no async rows — and each
reds the whole lane the moment someone adds one.

rf2-il7b flipped three of them (the suites it owned) to `:async? true`
because it added async rows. One of those three carried a COMMENT
asserting it was already on the map shape and was not
(examples/ledger/keyboard_dom_cljs_test.cljs), which is the shape of the
hazard: the belief is cheap to hold and the factory default is invisible
at the call site.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. Flipping all 44 is a behaviour change to 44 suites
that nobody asked for, and rf2-u0j8's diagnostic now names the abort in
seconds rather than after a 360s burn, so the cost of hitting it is
diagnosis-in-seconds rather than a lost afternoon. This is a RULING
request, not a queued edit.

OPTIONS, for the mayor:
  a) leave it — the runner names it immediately, and 44 edits is churn;
  b) flip the default: make `make-reset-runtime-fixture` return the MAP
     shape unless told otherwise, so the safe shape is the one you get by
     not thinking about it. Pre-alpha, no back-compat shims — this is the
     option the project stance points at, and it is one file plus whatever
     the fn-form's dynamic-binding semantics are load-bearing for;
  c) flip only the 44 browser-lane call sites and leave the factory alone.
notes:
DELEGATED RULING (operator-authorised delegation, 2026-08-13): Option (a) — make-reset-runtime-fixture keeps the fn-form default, no call-site sweep; one hardening bead filed (rf2-e8ea) making :async? true platform-guarded async-capable. Recorded by a decision agent after the dossier (no reviewer annotations were added in the window); operator may reverse.

SPOT-VERIFIED before ruling (both hold): (i) Story's shared use-fixtures helper invokes the factory's return AS A FUNCTION — tools/story/src/re_frame/story/test_support.cljc:152-156, `(fn [test-fn] (fw-fixture test-fn))`; (ii) the factory default is the fn-form and :async? true returns the {:before :after} map on BOTH platforms — implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:580 (docstring) and :818 (shape branch, no reader conditional).

RATIONALE (measured, from the dossier ai/decisions/rf2-pn3d.async-fixture-default.md, now deleted per protocol — every load-bearing measurement carried here or on rf2-e8ea):

1. The map shape is unusable on the JVM, proven in-tree. clojure.test treats a fixture as IFn; a map IS IFn (key lookup), so a {:before ...} fixture composes to a fn returning nil WITHOUT calling the test — "Ran 0 tests", silent GREEN. Documented at implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_component_cljs_test.cljc:29-34 (the suite hit it while being written). A naive default flip silently zeroes 196 .clj suites plus the JVM side of ~212 .cljc suites.

2. The fn-form's composition semantics are load-bearing for ~95 CLJS/CLJC suites that register the factory fixture alongside a sibling fn fixture in one use-fixtures call (trace-capture-fixture 16+, capturing-transport-fixture 20+, isolate-trace-bus-fixture, listener-fixture, ...). cljs.test refuses mixed fixture types, so a flipped default reds every one of them.

3. Three call sites invoke the returned fixture as a function; under a map default the call becomes a key lookup returning nil and the wrapped body silently never runs: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/test_support.cljc:152-156 (worst — a shared helper silently skipping every Story CLJS test body), implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/http_managed_cljs_test.cljs:56, implementation/core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution.clj:837 (JVM, guard-safe).

So option (b) is not the one-file default swap its label suggests: it is a platform-guarded factory PLUS ~95 loud mixed-type breaks PLUS 2 silent fixture-as-fn failures — roughly 100 site edits that TRADE today's loud-in-seconds hazard (rf2-u0j8's runner diagnostic names the fixture abort immediately, with in-file comments citing it) for a new silent one. The fn-form is not a legacy unsafe default; it is the only shape that exists on the JVM and the only shape that composes with the repo's fixture ecology. The map is the narrow CLJS-async special case — the option framing had "safe default" backwards. Option (c) (flip the 41 browser-lane sites; the bead's 44 minus three rf2-il7b already flipped) is arbitrary scope: the hazard is any cljs.test bundle (~438 more node-lane fn-form suites), and it establishes no principle for suite 42.

RESIDUAL RISK ACCEPTED: an author adding the first async row to one of ~479 fn-form CLJS suites hits a loud, named, self-locating error (rf2-u0j8) and makes the one-line :async? true fix — the rf2-il7b precedent, twice proven, including correcting the keyboard_dom_cljs_test.cljs false-belief comment. Trust the programmer with a good diagnostic.

INSIGHT PRESERVED as rf2-e8ea: make :async? true mean "async-capable" — #?(:clj fn-form :cljs map) — so the map-on-JVM silent swallow becomes unrepresentable and the .cljc `(cond-> ... #?(:clj false :cljs true) (assoc :async? true))` dance (live at implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/render_batch_host_checkpoint_cljs_test.cljc:67 and reactive_epoch_cljs_test.cljc:60) simplifies to a plain :async? true. One file, zero behaviour change for any current consumer (no .clj consumer passes :async?). Full implementation brief, shape-semantics summary, and count-invariance acceptance are on rf2-e8ea.

MEASUREMENT DRIFT noted, not decisive: live browser-lane fn-form count is 41, not the 44 in this bead's description (rf2-il7b flipped three after filing); the dossier counted three .cljc async consumers, two are grep-verifiable today.

DISPOSITION: this bead's question is answered — closing. Implementation work continues on rf2-e8ea.
close_reason: Ruled option (a) via operator-authorised delegated decision, 2026-08-13: make-reset-runtime-fixture keeps the fn-form default. The map shape is JVM-unusable (IFn key-lookup silently swallows tests green — streaming_component_cljs_test.cljc:29-34), fn-form composability is load-bearing for ~95 suites, and 3 sites invoke the fixture as a function (worst: Story's shared helper) — a default flip would trade a loud-in-seconds hazard (rf2-u0j8 diagnostic) for a silent one across ~100 sites. Residual risk is a named, self-locating error with a one-line fix (rf2-il7b precedent). Hardening follow-up filed as rf2-e8ea (:async? true becomes platform-guarded async-capable: fn-form on :clj, map on :cljs). Full rationale and preserved measurements in the appended DELEGATED RULING note.

title: A qualified rf/dispatch from an :on-click raises :rf.error/no-frame-context
description:
MEASURED by worker/recipes-hic054 (rf2-hic-054, PR #8045) in the browser lane — its confirm-dialog buttons went red on exactly this.

THE FAILURE. A qualified rf/dispatch called from an :on-click handler raises :rf.error/no-frame-context. The handler has no frame context to resolve against, because the ambient context is established during render and is gone by the time the click fires.

WHY IT MATTERS: dispatching from a click handler is the single most idiomatic thing a consumer does. If the obvious spelling raises, the API's ergonomics claim is weakened at the most-travelled point — and this project's stance is explicitly high productivity via excellent ergonomics and low friction.

THE FIX THE WORKER NAMED: the reg-view macro's injected dispatch. Verify that at source before accepting it — the worker was doing something else and named the fix in passing, so it is a claim, not a finding.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST: reproduce the raise from an :on-click, confirm the error id, and establish whether the injected dispatch already exists and is simply not reached, or does not exist on this path. A verified 'already works, the worker hit a different cause' is a complete deliverable.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this is about making the idiomatic call work, not about inventing a new dispatch surface. If the remedy would add a facade export, that export is classified and justified where it lands, at diff time. If it needs a spec row, spec/* is HOT ZONE and sequential — STOP and report rather than editing.

SURFACE: the reg-view macro and the frame-context resolution path under implementation/. Check for live workers before dispatching.

EVIDENCE: PR #8045's body records the measurement inline.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8050 (merged 2026-08-12T23:41:05Z as 53437a51885b74e4384bf351e4b1f826cb857717) — REOPEN for one bounded documentation carrier; no duplicate created. The API verdict and runtime diagnostic are correct: qualified ambient dispatch in a later callback must fail, while reg-view's injected render-time capture is the ergonomic path. docs/core/errors.md now teaches that accurately. Completeness miss: docs/core/effects.md:352 still says a detached .then has no ambient frame "unlike a view, where the surrounding frame-provider supplies one". In this callback context that is the same misleading reassurance #8050 removed from errors.md: the provider supplies a registered view during render, not a later :on-* callback, and the sentence conflicts with the new "Being inside a view does not exempt you" guidance. Narrow repair: qualify the contrast as a registered view's render/injected capture, or explicitly exclude later callbacks; do not change the API or add a new surface.

title: Correct the react-window claim in ledger/vendor.cljs docstring
description:
The vendor stand-in's docstring mirrors the same materially false claim that rf2-hic-047 just corrected in docs/design/hicasso/product/virtualizer-recipe.md (PR #8043).

implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ledger/vendor.cljs:48-51 says:

  '@tanstack/react-virtual hands the consumer virtualItem.key and takes a
   rangeExtractor that can force an index to stay in the rendered range;
   react-window DOES NEITHER, which is exactly why the recipe names the
   property rather than the package.'

The rangeExtractor half is correct. The KEY half is false, in both react-window generations, verified against the published packages:

- react-window 2.3.0 (dist/react-window.d.ts): rowKey?: (index, data) => React.Key, applied as key={rowKey ? rowKey(index, rowProps) : index}
- react-window 1.8.11 (src/createListComponent.js:69,125,347): itemKey?: (index, data) => any, applied as key: itemKey(index, itemData) -- shipped across the whole 1.x line, 1.0.0 (2018-07-22) to 1.8.11 (2024-12-17)

Line 71 carries the same error: 'that is @tanstack/react-virtual's contract rather than react-window's style handoff, and it is the one that leaves the key in the consumer's hands' -- react-window's style handoff does not take the key out of the consumer's hands.

FIX: narrow 'does neither' to the one property react-window actually lacks (no rangeExtractor-equivalent; its rendered range is a contiguous [start,stop] loop in both generations with only overscanCount as consumer influence), and drop the line-71 clause about the key. The corrected, version-pinned comparison table is in virtualizer-recipe.md under 'Which packages have them, audited by version' -- keep the two in step.

Scope: docstring prose only. The code is correct as landed; the recommendation is unchanged (TanStack still has all three).

NOTE: the three property NAMES in the docstring table are mirrored verbatim from virtualizer-recipe.md and were deliberately left alone by rf2-hic-047 to avoid doc/code drift. If a future bead rewords them, it must move both files together. Separately worth a look: property 2's 'why it matters' cell says 'a virtualizer inserts two divs between them' -- true of react-window 1.x (outer+inner), but 2.x inserts zero (rows are direct children of the root, plus one aria-hidden sizing div).

Filed by rf2-hic-047's audit-correction worker; the file was outside that bead's fence.

Primary-source tag sweep: 1.0.0 through 1.3.1 have itemKey and only outerTagName/innerTagName; outerElementType/innerElementType first appear in 1.4.0 and persist through 1.8.11. Correct the history while fixing vendor.cljs: key control spans all 1.x, arbitrary component wrappers only 1.4.0 onward, and the earlier releases permit tag-name choice only. title: Three browser-test namespaces use positional fixtures and are one async row from taking the whole lane down
description:
ROUTED from worker/asyncabort-u0j8 (rf2-u0j8, PR #8038), which flagged them for a ruling rather than converting them — correctly, since converting is a behaviour change that bead did not ask for.

THE SITES, all :browser-test namespaces using positional fixtures today:
  implementation/ui/test/re_frame/ui/adapter_conformance_dom_cljs_test.cljs
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/multi_root_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs

WHY IT MATTERS. cljs.test's execution-strategy maps an all-fn-fixture namespace to :sync, shadow.test wraps every body in disable-async, and test-var-block* then throws a bare string that unwinds the whole lane — because shadow.test/run-tests runs every namespace block PLUS the closing summary inside one run-block with no try/catch. So adding a single (async done ...) row to any of these three takes down every namespace scheduled after it. Measured on a plant: 8 of 225 namespaces ran.

ALL THREE ARE CORRECT AS WRITTEN. Positional fixtures are legal, and these have no async rows. This is a latent hazard, not a live defect — which is exactly why rf2-u0j8's worker rejected a lint rule for it: a source regex would stand in for a fact the runner can already observe.

THE QUESTION, and it is a judgement rather than a fix: convert them to map fixtures pre-emptively (cheap, removes the trap, touches three working files for no present defect), or leave them and rely on PR #8038's runner diagnostic to name the cause in seconds if anyone ever adds an async row (no churn, but the trap stays armed).

MY READ, offered as input and NOT acted on: #8038 changed the cost of hitting this from a 360-second misleading timeout to an immediate named error, which is most of the value. Converting three correct files afterwards looks like tidying rather than repair, and the stance rejects that. But a reviewer who thinks the trap should not exist at all has a fair case, and it is three small edits.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST: re-check that all three still use positional fixtures and still have no async rows before acting either way. If one has gained an async row since, that is a live defect and no longer a judgement call.
close_reason:
MAYOR DECISION 2026-08-13: closed, superseded and its premise corrected by rf2-pn3d.

TWO REASONS, either sufficient.

1. THE CENSUS WAS WRONG BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE. This bead named THREE :browser-test namespaces on positional fixtures. PR #8058's worker measured 44. #8038 found its three by grepping for a LITERAL (fn [f] ... (f)) in use-fixtures; the shared factory re-frame.test-support/make-reset-runtime-fixture returns the fn form BY DEFAULT and hides the same shape behind a call, so the grep could not see it. Acting on 'convert three correct files' would have converted 7% of the class and left the tracker asserting the job was done.

2. THE JUDGEMENT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR IS NOW A DIFFERENT AND BETTER ONE. It offered: convert three files pre-emptively, or rely on #8038's diagnostic. rf2-pn3d offers the option neither of us had — flip the FACTORY's default so :async? is the opt-out rather than the opt-in, and the safe shape is what you get by not thinking. That is one small API-taste change instead of 44 mechanical edits, and it closes the class rather than the instances.

WHAT IS NOT LOST. The three namespaces this bead named are inside rf2-pn3d's 44. The hazard is unchanged and still latent — all 44 are correct as written, having no async rows — and #8038's runner diagnostic still names the cause in seconds if one ever appears.

MY EARLIER READ, recorded because it was nearly acted on: I had this queued to close on the stance ground that converting three correct files for a latent hazard is churn. That reasoning was right about the churn and wrong about the number, which is exactly why a count is a claim and gets re-run at source.

title: Browser gate: a trusted-input bridge, so a real Tab and a real Escape can be witnessed
description:
Three suites now state the same gap rather than measuring it, because a synthetic `KeyboardEvent` performs no DEFAULT action in any engine:

- `overlay_dom_cljs_test` — a real Escape close request; it drives `HTMLDialogElement.requestClose` instead and says so.
- `examples/ledger/keyboard_dom_cljs_test` — a real Tab press; it witnesses sequential navigation as the engine's own focusability answer over the candidate set instead, which is what Tab consumes.
- `overlay_focus_dom_cljs_test` — the same Escape gap, inherited.

What the APPLICATION owns is already driven: `:on-key-down` is a React handler and React delivers a synthetic keydown to it exactly as it delivers a trusted one, which is why `combobox_keyboard_dom_cljs_test` drives arrows and Enter for real. The gap is only the platform's own key-driven defaults.

`scripts/run-browser-tests.cjs` already owns a Playwright `page` and already has an in-page↔runner bridge: the GC protocol publishes a request on a well-known key, the runner reads it with `page.evaluate`, calls `page.requestGC()`, and writes the outcome back. A `page.keyboard.press` bridge is the same shape.

**Runner-owned, so it is not rf2-hic-049's** — that file was another worker's fence (rf2-u0j8). Sequence this after the async-abort work lands so the two do not collide in the same file.

title: Decide whether an axe run belongs in the browser gate at all
description:
rf2-hic-043 and rf2-hic-049 both carry 'axe checks' in their DELIVERABLES prose. Neither landed one, and rf2-hic-049 refused rather than improvising, for three source-located reasons:

1. **The acceptance columns do not ask for it.** The product specification's §7 accessibility row is 'Names, roles, keyboard, virtualized/overlay focus'; `requirements-mine.md` assigns rf2-hic-049 'Keyboard, virtualized and overlay focus in a browser'. Axe appears in neither acceptance.
2. **There is no axe-core in the tree.** It is not in `implementation/package.json`, not in the lockfile and not in `node_modules`. Adding it means an npm dependency plus a lockfile change, and every worker worktree junctions the mayor's real `node_modules`, so the install mutates a shared tree.
3. **The repo's own posture is that axe-core is NOT bundled.** `spec/Security.md` and `spec/007-Stories.md` record the decision for Story: axe-core loads from a public CDN precisely so bundles do not carry it. The browser gate serves from 127.0.0.1 with no egress, so a CDN axe is not available to it either.

So this is a DECISION bead, not an implementation one. Either:
- rule that the structural sweeps are the accessibility gate and strike 'axe checks' from the two beads' prose and from `lanes/completeness-audit.md`; or
- rule that axe-core enters as a devDependency, and dispatch the dependency + gate wiring as its own bead.

What already exists on the structural side, so the gap is smaller than 'no axe': `ht/unnamed-controls` (rf2-hic-043) is the missing-name sweep; `unoperable-controls` in `examples/ledger/keyboard_dom_cljs_test.cljs` is the role-promises-an-activation-the-tag-cannot-deliver sweep; `activedescendant-findings` in `combobox_keyboard_dom_cljs_test.cljs` is the aria-valid-attr-value/ownership sweep. Axe's genuinely uncovered rules are colour contrast, duplicate ids and required-children.

title: docs(xray/021): unescaped | inside code spans truncates two table rows (L3271, L3299)
description:

title: hic-046 rows HS-10/HS-12/HS-13 owe a server-context refusal that no code implements
description:
FOUND BY worker/ssrwitness-hic046 (rf2-hic-046) while attempting to witness the SSR disposition rows. Recorded here rather than invented there — the worker was right not to mint a refusal to satisfy a table.

THE FINDING, as measured. dispositions.md rows HS-10, HS-12 and HS-13 disposition surfaces as refusing under a server render. But there is NO server-context refusal anywhere in implementation/hicasso/src/: no browser? door guard, and no :rf.error/...-no-dom complaint id. So the rows describe conduct that no code implements, and no witness can be written for them without first building the refusal.

A SECOND, SHARPER HALF: the rows reference h/mount!, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST. The facade's roster is root! / render! / unmount!. So at least one row is written against a symbol that never shipped.

WHY THIS IS NOT rf2-hic-046's TO FIX. That bead's licence is to WITNESS rows, not to upgrade or implement them — 'where true' is the load-bearing phrase in its own deliverables. Minting a refusal id would also cross into hot zone: R6 of the complaint-catalogue gate requires every live complaint row to carry a spec/009-Instrumentation.md row, and spec/** is hot-zone and sequential. rf2-umjv hit exactly that wall for the overlay anchor refusal and was correctly deferred behind the naming packet rather than minting.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, and it is genuinely a fork rather than an oversight:
(a) IMPLEMENT the refusal — a server-context door guard plus a minted complaint id, which drags in spec/009 (hot zone) and the naming ledger. Substantial.
(b) CORRECT THE TABLE — if these surfaces do not in fact refuse under SSR, the rows are wrong and should be re-dispositioned to what the code does. Cheap, and possibly the honest answer.
(c) MARK THEM UNWITNESSABLE with a dated note recording that the disposition is aspirational until (a) lands.

The h/mount! half is not a fork: that symbol does not exist and the row is simply wrong however the rest resolves. Fix that regardless of which branch is taken.

MY READ AS MAYOR, offered as input and NOT acted on: establish (b) first by reading what those surfaces actually do under renderToString. A table row asserting a refusal that the code does not perform is a documentation defect, and if the code's real behaviour is reasonable then re-dispositioning is both cheaper and more truthful than building a refusal to justify a row somebody wrote in advance. Only if the real behaviour is genuinely wrong does (a) become work.

SEQUENCING: do not dispatch until rf2-hic-046's PR merges — that worker owns dispositions.md sections 2.1/2.2 right now. Also note section 2.3 is reserved for the operator's pending Firefox/WebKit IME results and for rf2-hic-040's control rows; do not edit it.

notes:
WORKER worker/ssrdispo-bjpe -> PR #8023 (docs-only). BEAD DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN: the three-way fork is an operator ruling and was not taken.

STEP 1 - the three claims, RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE. Two hold as stated; one needs a refinement that does not change its conclusion.
1. "No browser? door guard in implementation/hicasso/src/" - HOLDS, refined. The PREDICATE does exist (impl.mount/browser?, mount.cljs:524) and is the tree's only occurrence, but it is called from NOWHERE in src/; every caller is a test deciding whether to skip. So there is no door GUARD, which is what the claim is about.
2. "No :rf.error/...-no-dom id" - HOLDS. All ~60 :rf.error/... ids in hicasso/src were enumerated; none names a server or no-DOM call. The two nearest (hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy, hicasso-native-bad-server-policy) fault a DECLARATION of SSR policy and never fire at a root door.
3. "h/mount! absent from the facade" - HOLDS. hicasso.cljc's alias block is the roster: root! (:566), render! (:579), unmount! (:586). "mount!" occurs nowhere in hicasso/src at all.

NOT NAMED BY THIS BEAD, found while checking: h/hydrate! has no referent either. impl.mount/hydrate-root! exists but is NOT re-exported to the facade. Different defect from HS-10's - a MISSING door, not a misspelled one - so the PR records it in Note 1 and changes no disposition for it. Worth its own bead if the operator wants it tracked.

STEP 2 - the h/mount! row is FIXED (not part of the fork). HS-10's Public-surface column now reads h/root!. Its target-policy cell dropped the dangling "plus h/hydrate!" for "plus the hydrating door". Note 1 carried the same wrong roster and was corrected with it, otherwise the document contradicted its own table one screen later. Naming-ledger row 13 (rf2-84w6) keeps root!->mount! as ratified-provisional taste; the table now names what ships.

STEP 3 - MEASURED CONDUCT under a no-DOM/server context. Exercised on node v24.13.0 with the repo's own vendored react-dom 19.2.0, no jsdom, replicating each door's exact call sequence. THE THREE DO NOT BEHAVE ALIKE, and that is the finding the fork turns on:
- HS-10 h/root! (mount.cljs:200-208): THROWS, but it is REACT's throw - "Error: Target container is not a DOM element." - identically for nil, undefined and a plain object, with or without :identifier-prefix. No :rf.error/... id, no recovery, no mention of Hicasso. createRoot is reached with no guard of any kind. In practice a consumer's boot line dies one step earlier still, at js/document.getElementById -> "ReferenceError: document is not defined", before the door is entered at all.
- HS-12 h/render! (mount.cljs:141-143): UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION - it takes a handle and the only maker of one is root!, which throws first. Forced with a nil-rooted handle it dies "TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'render')". react-dom/flushSync is not the obstacle: it runs in node and refuses nothing.
- HS-13 h/unmount! (mount.cljs:478-482): SILENTLY NO-OPS. Neither throws nor degrades - when-some guards the entire React call on (:root handle), so a nil handle or a rootless handle returns nil with nothing said and nothing logged. That is deliberate idempotence (the docstring pins it) rather than an oversight, but it makes this the quietest of the three.
None of the three refuses at source with a recovery, which is what section 2's own definition of Client-only and Note 3 both require. Dispositions were therefore LEFT EXACTLY AS THEY WERE and the measurement recorded beside them.

STEP 4 - FORK NOT TAKEN. No branch of (a)/(b)/(c) implemented. No complaint id minted; spec/009 untouched. (a) is additionally BLOCKED rather than merely declined - R6 of the complaint-catalogue gate requires every live complaint row to carry a spec/009 row, hot zone and sequential, the same wall rf2-umjv hit.

RECOMMENDATION ONLY, NOT ACTED ON - evidence points at (b), and suggests the honest correction may be STRUCTURAL rather than textual, which makes it a fourth shape this bead does not enumerate and so squarely the operator's:
- Note 1 already concedes these doors "are client entry points; none of them emits server bytes". "Public surfaces of the product but not of the rendered tree, so they carry no Render/Client-only policy" is VERBATIM section 2.2's own admission criterion, where HS-36..HS-39 live. The two-policy matrix is about rendered-TREE surfaces; these three are imperative doors that render nothing.
- The split already exists in the table: HS-14 is the root-and-frame-provider ELEMENT and is Render. The doors that install it are a different kind of thing.
- Against (a): building a browser? guard plus a minted id would be constructing a refusal to satisfy a row somebody wrote in advance, into hot zone, for a failure React already reports in plain words and which is usually preceded by "document is not defined" anyway - the nag-diagnostic shape the project stance rejects at triage. The one genuinely unhelpful behaviour is HS-13's silence, and that silence is a deliberate fixture contract whose removal would cost more than it buys.
- Against (c): recording the rows as aspirational preserves an obligation the measurement suggests was never real.

title: Timer-to-awaited-promise conversions may leave the rejection arm without teardown (no scanner can see this)
description:

THE CLASS, AND WHY NO SCANNER FINDS IT. The rf2-fyba campaign's scanners look for a promise chain whose .catch sits downstream of its own done. This is a DIFFERENT defect that the campaign's own repairs introduced, and the chain ORDERING is already correct in every instance, so no signature flags it.

MECHANISM, measured on the two sites rf2-o0n1 fixed. PR #7968 awaited two bare timers — the right move, and it closed the original defect. But awaiting them changed WHICH ARM a throw in those assertions takes: instead of escaping as an unhandled page error, the throw now reaches the row's outer rejection handler. In both rows the mount had ALREADY resolved by then, so a live React root exists when that handler runs — and neither handler could see it. client_only's .catch could not see 'mounted'; spike_dom's X5 mutation proof could not see 'survivor'. Each reported and called done with a React root still mounted: A STANDING ROOT HANDED TO THE NEXT NAMESPACE, which is this campaign's own contamination arriving by a second door.

THE ASK. Wherever any batch in the rf2-fyba campaign converted a bare timer into an awaited promise, re-read the rejection arm for teardown coverage. The shape to grep for is a timer wrapped in (js/Promise. (fn [resolve reject] ...)).

SCOPE AND WHAT IS ALREADY DONE. That shape occurs exactly TWICE in implementation/freehand/test and both were the audit's sites — already fixed in PR #7995 (retain the handle, hoist teardown onto the single trailing step, once per path, some-> no-op where no root existed; 'doomed's unmount! stayed put because it is the act under test). So implementation/freehand is CLEAR. The open question is whether OTHER trees' batches made the same conversion: tools/xray, tools/machines-viz, tools/story, implementation/hicasso, implementation/core.

THE CAMPAIGN'S OTHER PRs to check for timer conversions: #7955 (rf2-d2xz), #7959, #7961, #7964 (rf2-29ua), #7968 (rf2-fh4/o0n1), #7974 (rf2-e8kc), #7937, #7942.

VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING. This is a claim about a class, and the class may be empty outside freehand — a verified 'no other tree made this conversion' is a complete and good deliverable. Do NOT build a scanner for it: the defect is invisible to signature matching by construction, which is the point, and rf2-j9tl and rf2-maiw both declined analogous tooling as over-engineering.

A CORRECTION WORTH CARRYING, since it was wrong in two places before this worker checked it: rf2-o0n1 was discharged by PR #7968, NOT by rf2-e8kc / PR #7974. title: hic-059 follow-on: an absent Hicasso evidence door answers a compile error, not :evidence-tier-unavailable
description:
Found by the rf2-hic-059 live wire witness (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/live-hicasso-wire.cjs), running the three Hicasso door tools against a real app for the first time.

re-frame2-pair-mcp.tools.hicasso-tool documents a degradation ladder whose first rung is: an app that does not have re-frame.hicasso.tool loaded (a Reagent/UIx app, or a Hicasso app nothing pulled the door into) gets {:ok? false :reason :evidence-tier-unavailable} with a load-the-door hint. hicasso_tool_test asserts the emitted form CONTAINS that branch.

Live, it never runs. cljs.core/exists? guards a missing VAR; it does not stop shadow's analyzer rejecting a var in a namespace the build has never loaded. Measured against :hicasso/hmr-testbed before the door was required:

  {:ok? false,
   :message "cljs eval compile error/warning: ------ WARNING - :undeclared-var ...
              Use of undeclared Var re-frame.hicasso.tool/read-mounted-boundaries",
   :reason :rf.error/eval-cljs-compile-error, ...}

So the ONE case the honest-degradation branch names is the one case it cannot reach: the hint an operator needs ('load re-frame.hicasso.tool into the running build and retry') is replaced by a raw analyzer warning. A door that is loaded but inactive (:advanced/goog.DEBUG false) is unaffected — that rung is a nil return, not an unresolved var.

The fix is a tools/-side form change (resolve the door through a runtime lookup the analyzer cannot reject, e.g. goog/getObjectByName or an exists? on the NAMESPACE object, rather than a fully-qualified var reference), plus a witness row. Deliberately NOT done under rf2-hic-059: that bead's bounded repair was a witness, and changing the emitter to make the witness's story tidier is the shape the #7986 audit forbade.

Surface: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/hicasso_tool.cljs + its two test suites. No provider change.

title: mayor-dispatch.md: the verified-redundant rule does not cover COUNT claims
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR AFTER BREAKING THIS RULE TWICE IN ONE WAVE (2026-08-12). The mayor-side commit guard correctly refused a mayor-checkout commit for it, so it needs a worker.

THE GAP. .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md line 19 ends: 'BEFORE dispatching, grep for the alleged broken symbol / missing file — if already landed, close as verified-duplicate; spot exact-title duplicates and consolidate.' That points at SYMBOLS and FILES. Both dead dispatches were COUNT claims, a shape it does not cover: a census bead asserts a number, so a symbol-shaped grep passes while the number is stale — the symbol still resolves and the count is zero.

EVIDENCE. rf2-sx7g (15 chains) and rf2-5zt9 (16 chains) were both dispatched against work already merged: rf2-e8kc / PR #7974 (worker/closure-e8kc, merged 2026-08-12T08:12:36Z; commits e6601b21e1, d844756426, ae230c8cc0, 4de7cf5c3c) discharged both roughly fifteen hours earlier. rf2-e8kc PREDICTED the overlap in its own text: 'the same rows counted twice, not 17 + 17. Repairing them once closes both censuses.' Both workers verified properly and returned a correct 'already fixed', so the cost was two wasted dispatches, not a wrong result.

REMEDY — append to line 19, after 'consolidate.':

**A COUNT IS A CLAIM TOO, AND THE GREP THAT CHECKS IT IS A DIFFERENT ONE.** A census bead ("54 chains", "15 hits", "eleven sites") asserts a number, not a symbol, so a symbol-shaped grep passes while the number is stale — the symbol still resolves, and the count is zero. Re-run the bead's own census at `origin/main` HEAD, not at the bead's text and not at your branch point. On 2026-08-12 two beads went out in one wave against work already merged: rf2-sx7g and rf2-5zt9 were both discharged by rf2-e8kc / PR #7974 roughly fifteen hours before dispatch, and rf2-e8kc had PREDICTED the overlap in its own text ("the same rows counted twice, not 17 + 17. title: hicasso HMR gate: chromium GEN-1 race — the first save can land before the runtime registers
description:
FOUND BY worker/hmrfix-7983 while proving PR #7983's HMR red was environmental. IT IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A REPRODUCTION — the worker says so itself and did not action it. But it explains a signature seen TWICE and is worth pinning before it is seen a third time.

THE SIGNATURE, IDENTICAL IN BOTH OBSERVED FAILURES: chromium ONLY, at the FIRST save (GEN-1), `page.waitForFunction: Timeout 90000ms exceeded`. Firefox and WebKit each pass 105 checks on the same bundle. The watch is HEALTHY in both — `[:hicasso/hmr-testbed] Build completed. (225 files, 2 compiled, 0 warnings, 0.25s)` — so shadow compiled the save and THE PAGE NEVER SAW IT.
  - PR #7983 (worker/capsule-hic082), job 94089849706.
  - PR #7945 (worker/ssrname-mo4o), job 93967315483, 2026-08-12T00:08 — BYTE-FOR-BYTE the same signature and the same file counts. Re-run went green (run 31548736825 attempt 2).
That second one DID change implementation/hicasso/src/**, so the two failures share a signature while differing entirely in what the diff touched — which is itself evidence the cause is the harness rather than any diff.

THE HYPOTHESIS: GEN-1 is the first save of the first engine, immediately after page load, and the ONLY moment where the runtime's registration with the shadow worker can still be in flight when the recompile lands. The worker pushes `build-complete` only to runtimes it ALREADY KNOWS ABOUT; the harness makes EXACTLY ONE save and then waits 90s. So a runtime that connects a beat late gets nothing and THERE IS NO SECOND COMPILE TO RESCUE IT. That explains why the failure is always the same engine, always the same save, and why a re-run clears it.

REMEDY BELONGS TO THE GATE'S OWN HARNESS: implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-hicasso-hmr-testbed.cjs. Plausible shapes: wait for a positive registration signal before the first save rather than for the page alone; or make GEN-1 idempotent so a missed push is retried once. DO NOT EXTEND THE 90s TIMEOUT — lengthening a timeout to make a flake pass is the fail-open shape this repo has spent two days deleting, and the watch is demonstrably healthy inside it.

ONE THING THAT LOOKS LIKE A SMOKING GUN AND IS NOT, recorded so the next reader does not chase it: the log line `[chromium:error] shadow-cljs watch for build :hmr-testbed not running!` — note `:hmr-testbed` while the watch runs `:hicasso/hmr-testbed`. shadow/build/targets/shared.clj:213 sets the client define to `(name build-id)`, STRIPPING THE NAMESPACE, and shadow/cljs/devtools/client/shared.cljs:544 prints that error when its welcome-time query matches nothing. The worker confirmed it in its own PASSING local build: `"build_id":"hmr-testbed"` is baked into out/hicasso-hmr-testbed/main.js. THE MESSAGE IS PRINTED ON EVERY RUN INCLUDING GREEN ONES; it is only VISIBLE on red because the harness dumps console output on failure. Cosmetic, pre-existing, unrelated.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the gate arms on ANY implementation/hicasso/** path (.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:1209), deliberately broad — "a hicasso diff that skipped it would be resting the whole HMR contract on the seam-driven witness". So a diff can arm this gate without entering its build at all; PATH-FILTER ARMING IS NOT BUILD INCLUSION.
close_reason:
CONFIRMED, not merely hypothesised, and fixed in PR #7998 (branch worker/hmrrace-odh3).

MECHANISM, read at source: shadow's send-to-runtimes (worker/impl.clj:55) is '(when (seq runtimes) ...)' — a runtime the worker has not met draws SILENCE, not an error, and the runtime learns of builds only by push, so a missed one is never retried. Registration happens when the relay handles the page's :hello (remote/relay/local.clj:252), sent only after the websocket opens and :welcome returns. The harness gated its first save on the app MOUNT, which is a different clock: shadow's client only STARTS the connect before :init-fn paints.

PROVED by forcing the interleaving, not by a green run. New ships-by-default-off knob HICASSO_HMR_REGISTER_DELAY_MS holds the devtools socket back while the app mounts on time. Same delay, wait bypassed: exit 1, chromium, GEN-1, 'Timeout 90000ms exceeded' under a healthy 'Build completed. (225 files, 2 compiled)' — the CI signature byte for byte, with the new census reading 'relay before this save: no devtools relay socket was ever opened' and, 90s later, 'registered with the watch' having taken ZERO build pushes. Same delay, wait in place: exit 0, 105 checks, 12 real reloads.

THE MARGIN, from this PR's own green CI run: the handshake took 726ms (chromium), 1517ms (firefox), 5027ms (webkit) — against a save-to-push window of about 1.5s. The race was wide open on a routine green run; chromium caught it only because it goes first and pays for the cold JVM path.

FIX: driveEngine waits for the reply to shadow's own post-:hello :request-clients query before the first save (observed from Node via page.on('websocket'), so nothing is injected into the runtime). The 90s ceiling is UNTOUCHED — on the failing interleaving the run now gets shorter. A relay census rides into every save's failure message so the next occurrence names itself.

SECOND CAUSE found while reproducing the first, same red, different origin, also fixed here: a second 'shadow-cljs watch' anywhere on the machine binds :dev-http 8061 first, this run's bind quietly fails, and waitForBuild's probe gets its 200 from the OTHER process. With a leftover watch from the same worktree that is a FAIL-OPEN — green on code this run never compiled. waitForBuild now digests the served bundle against the one this watch wrote.

Teeth 19 -> 28. Gates: HMR gate 3-engine x3 exit 0, proof legs 1/0 as designed, test:script-policy 0, test:script-helpers 0, fast-PR spine 0, CI cljs-hicasso-hmr green.

Left for a follow-on: HICASSO_HMR_ENGINES can narrow the run to one engine, silently disabling the cross-engine comparator while still printing 'HICASSO HMR PASS'. Reported to the mayor, deliberately out of this diff's fence.

title: codemod: a Reagent require behind a reader conditional binds nothing, so W4/W5 are dead in every .cljc file
description:
`rw/ns-context` reads the ns form through `sexpr-safe`, which answers `::unreadable` for a reader-conditional node. So

    (ns app.ssr (:require #?(:cljs [reagent.dom.client :as rdc])))

binds NOTHING: aliases #{} and referred #{}. That is the ONLY legal way to
require Reagent from a .cljc file, so in every such file W4 (r/partial capture)
and W5 (r/adapt-react-class head) are dead, and the fixer's :as-element-island
and :reagent-api-residue classes cannot fire either.

It does not look wrong, which is the problem: `:>` head detection needs no alias,
so the report stays non-empty. Verified at source with a probe (rf2-hic-055):
cases B and C below both answer {:aliases #{} :referred #{}} —

    (ns a (:require #?(:cljs [reagent.core :as r])))          ; B
    (ns a (:require #?@(:cljs [[reagent.core :as r]])))       ; C

REAL INSTANCES IN THIS REPO: examples/capabilities/ssr/{ssr,ssr_streaming,resources_ssr}/core.cljc,
all three requiring reagent.dom.client under #?(:cljs …).

rf2-hic-055 deliberately did NOT fix this. It is a FIXER behaviour change — files
the tool previously could not see would start being rewritten — and rf2-hic-055
is a reporter bead. What landed instead is the census's :unresolved-reagent-require
class, which reports the file at its ns form and every qualified roster-named call
in it as :unresolved-alias, so the hole is loud.

WORK: teach ns-context to read require clauses through reader-conditional nodes
(rewrite-clj gives the branches structurally; do not sexpr the whole form). Both
splicing and non-splicing shapes. The golden corpus has NO reader-conditional case
today — that is why this survived — so the fix lands with one.

CAUTION: a vendored/inlined Reagent (re-frame-10x ships
day8.re-frame-10x.inlined-deps.reagent.v1v2v0.reagent.core) is a DIFFERENT case and
must stay unresolved-and-reported, not guessed at.
notes: Merged-PR audit #7979 adds one acceptance edge for this exact reader-conditional owner: a file with one ordinary resolved Reagent require plus one reader-conditional Reagent require is still partially blind. Today census/scan sets `unresolved?` from whether the UNION of all aliases/refers is empty, so the ordinary alias makes it false and `(rdc/render ...)` under the unresolved conditional vanishes without either unresolved diagnostic. When teaching ns-context the conditional shapes, include a mixed resolved+conditional fixture and prove both fixer and census bind/report every intended symbol; this avoids a separate duplicate reporter issue.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #7993 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/7993).

RE-DERIVED AT origin/main (c6694fa80b) BEFORE ANY EDIT. Cases B and C reproduce exactly as described. The probe also reproduced the merged-PR-audit #7979 mixed edge: a file with one ordinary Reagent require plus one reader-conditional require left the alias UNION non-empty, so unresolved? was FALSE and the conditional half's (rdc/render ...) produced NO entry at all — neither :unresolved-reagent-require nor :unresolved-alias. That edge is why the repair reads spec-by-spec rather than retrying the whole form when the alias set comes back empty: here it never was empty, so a fallback keyed on emptiness would never have fired.

THE FIX. ns-context no longer sexprs the ns form entire (sexpr throws on a reader-conditional node, so the WHOLE form answered ::unreadable). require-specs walks the ns form's clause NODES and expands reader conditionals at BOTH the clause level and the spec level; each spec is sexpr'd on its own, because a spec node is ordinary data — only the conditional wrapper was ever unreadable. Both shapes: #? carries one branch value, #?@ carries a collection so its branch is lifted a level. All features read, not :cljs — the tool reads source text and does not resolve a platform.

THE FIXER-BEHAVIOUR QUESTION, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. This is what rf2-hic-055 declined. Ran fixer + census over all 2661 .cljs/.cljc files in the repo before and after: THE FIXER'S OUTPUT IS BYTE-IDENTICAL (16 files changed before, same 16 after, same bytes). Every difference is the census naming what it could previously only point at — :unresolved-alias becoming :root-mount / :local-reactive-cell / :with-let / :lifecycle-class across the three SSR examples, 14 tools/story .cljc files and the three reagent templates. So the capability is restored (W4/W5 CAN now fire in .cljc) without rewriting one byte anybody had not already agreed to. No refusal needed; had that diff been non-empty I would have stopped and reported instead.

THE CAUTION IS HONOURED AND ASSERTED. A namespace that merely SPELLS a Reagent name still binds nothing — re-frame-10x's vendored day8.re-frame-10x.inlined-deps.reagent.v1v2v0.reagent.core stays unresolved-and-reported. That is now the population :unresolved-reagent-require names, and the census tests that previously used the reader-conditional shape for it are re-pointed at a vendored fixture.

TESTS. Golden corpus 11 -> 14 cases (the corpus IS the spec): reader-conditional-require (non-splicing; W4/:partial-wrapper, W5/:adapt-react-class-head, :as-element-island and :reagent-api-residue ALL fire where they could not before), reader-conditional-splicing (#?@ plus the mixed resolved+conditional file), and reader-conditional-not-reagent — the adversarial negative, whose conditionals require goog.dom and a vendored Reagent, asserting zero misfire (vendored r/partial left alone, gdom/adapt-react-class head left alone, nothing rewritten). Census +3 deftests: both shapes, a conditional around the whole (:require ...) clause, :refer through a conditional, the mixed edge, a non-Reagent conditional. Suite 40 -> 43 tests, 436 assertions, 0 failures. Also probed eight malformed/edge ns shapes (empty conditional body, odd option tail, :refer :all, prefix list, tagged literal, no ns form) — none throws, none misfires; two small guards were added for that (pairwise options, :refer only when sequential).

STALE PROSE CORRECTED IN THE SAME PR. notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8007 (2026-08-13) — REOPENED FOR A CONFIRMED FALSE GREEN.

hm/shadow! compares attributes and child text, but React keeps a controlled select's current selection in DOM properties. A temporary browser witness mounted a reference select at value "two" and a candidate select at value "one" with identical option markup. It first proved the live nodes differed exactly as ["two" "one"], then checkpoint! returned {:status :green :checkpoints 1}. The full browser runner exited 1 with this as its sole added failure: expected :red, actual :green (1404 tests / 8697 assertions). A platform probe independently showed the same mechanism: changing HTMLSelectElement.value changes option.selected while outerHTML remains byte-identical. Source cause: attrs-of reads only NamedNodeMap attributes and element-difference has no live-control property comparison.

This matters to the promised migration proof: a port can visibly select the wrong option while DOM markup and intents agree. Keep the repair narrow: make shadow comparison include the user-visible selected value/state needed to distinguish this pair, add this exact false-green twin, and inspect the adjacent value/checked property slots at the same boundary so the fix is total rather than a select-name special case. Do not broaden into focus, caret, IME, layout, or paint; those remain explicit non-claims.

title: hic-052 follow-up: the overlay anchor refusal, and the focus one-shot recipe the guide teaches
description:
Two things rf2-hic-052 deliberately left, both source-located.

1. THE ANCHOR REFUSAL. `re-frame.hicasso.overlay`'s `:anchor` takes a DOM id and is a NO-OP when the id names no element: the panel opens in the top layer, visibly unanchored, and raises nothing. The guide's troubleshooting table promises `:rf.error/hicasso-overlay-anchor-missing` there, and complaints.md carries it as RESERVED. Minting it was refused for two reasons, either of which is sufficient: (a) R6 of the complaint-catalogue gate requires every live row to have a spec/009-Instrumentation.md row, which is HOT ZONE; (b) naming-ledger row 30 marks the spelling PROVISIONAL until the naming packet (rf2-hic-065) sits, and rf2-hic-052 blocks that bead. So this should follow rf2-hic-065, not precede it.

2. THE FOCUS ONE-SHOT RECIPE IS WRONG IN THE DRAFT GUIDE, measured in a browser. docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/13-overlays-and-focus.md teaches ':auto-focus true' on the control that should receive focus when an overlay opens. It does not work, and neither spelling does:
   - ':auto-focus' camelCases to React's own 'autoFocus' prop. React implements that by calling .focus() during commitMount, CHILD-FIRST — one commit BEFORE the overlay's ref attaches and calls showModal — at which point the <dialog> is still display:none and nothing inside it is focusable. The call is a silent no-op.
   - ':autofocus', unhyphenated, is rejected by React outright: 'Invalid DOM property autofocus. Did you mean autoFocus?', and no attribute reaches the DOM.
   So the platform's dialog-focusing steps find no autofocus element and take the FIRST FOCUSABLE control in tree order. re-frame.hicasso.overlay-dom-cljs-test/the-focus-one-shot-is-the-platforms-focus-delegate-and-not-reacts-autofocus pins that, and the module's door states it.

   The guide chapter needs correcting either way. Whether the MODULE should also grow a way to name the initial focus target is a RULING, not worker work — the options are (i) teach tree order and add nothing (the current state, and the minimal-API answer), (ii) an overlay option naming a selector or id, (iii) a reserved child attribute the module hoists into a real 'autofocus' attribute, which needs codec cooperation. The draft guide is a live operator surface; do not edit it from a worker branch without checking who holds it.

title: resources: no test asserts :rf.error/resource-not-registered (the read-path twin of rf2-06lp)
description:
Found while verifying rf2-06lp. `registry/require-resource-spec!` is the read-path twin of the mutation guard rf2-06lp turned out to already have — it throws `:rf.error/resource-not-registered` and is used at four `:rf.resource/*` event handlers (ensure / refetch / remove / the fourth in events.cljc), at the route integration (route.cljc), and at the subscription (subs.cljc).

The guard is real. **Nothing in the corpus asserts it.** `git grep resource-not-registered` over `implementation/` returns only the throw site itself and the spec/009 catalogue row — no test.

That is exactly the shape rf2-06lp's PR fixed one registrar over: the mutation path's `execute-unregistered-is-loud` asserted only `(nil? @last-managed-args)`, which a silent no-op satisfies as well as a refusal does, so it could not fail. The resource path does not even have that much.

## The ask

Mirror what rf2-06lp's PR landed in `resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc`, in the resource suite's proper home:

- an unregistered resource id on `:rf.resource/ensure` refuses — no entry written, no request lowered, and the always-on `:errors` axis carries `:rf.error/resource-not-registered` with the resource id named and `:recovery :fix-registration`;
- the identity half — a MUTATION id passed as `:resource` still refuses (the guard keys on the `:resource` registrar KIND, not on 'known keyword'); rf2-06lp's sabotage proved this direction is the one that silently lowers the wrong thing (widening the mutation guard to the resource registrar made the runtime lower a resource's GET as a mutation write);
- the restraint half — a REGISTERED resource raises no error record at all.

`record-error-records!` in `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc` (landed by rf2-06lp) is the helper to copy.

Surface: `implementation/resources/test/` only. No runtime change, no spec change, no new id.
close_reason: Three rows land in implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_runtime_cljs_test.cljc (the read-path twin of the mutation suite) via PR #8002: unregistered ensure refuses with the catalogued category + id + :recovery :fix-registration on the always-on :errors axis; the identity half (a MUTATION id passed as :resource still refuses, because the guard keys on the :resource registrar KIND); and the restraint half (a registered resource raises no record). Each asserts the POSITIVE PRESENCE of the error record, so a silent no-op fails them — the rf2-06lp lesson. Proven to bite: a single-line #_ plant eliding the throw in require-resource-spec! turns the suite red (exit 1, 6 failures), with restore verified by sha256 (84ce8184 -> 86203658 -> 84ce8184) rather than by git diff. No runtime, spec or id change. NOTE: the dispatch brief named implementation/core/** as the write surface; the bead's own 'Surface: implementation/resources/test/ only' governed and is where the rows landed.
