title: The spine's ambient use-subscribe cannot resolve a frame under react-dom/server
description:
Measured while writing rf2-hic-034's parity suite (PR #7962), reported rather than fixed.

re-frame.substrate.spine's ONE-ARGUMENT use-subscribe resolves the React-context tier through frame/require-current-frame!, which reaches the context by reading context._currentValue. That is a CLIENT-render fact: react-dom/server does not populate it, so the hook refuses with :rf.error/no-frame-context on the server.

Measured both ways, on the node lane, under React 19.2.0:
  - a UIx defui calling (uix-adapter/use-subscribe [::q]) inside a Hicasso tree under impl.mount/provider - REFUSED;
  - the same component wrapped in the adapter's OWN re-frame.adapter.uix/frame-provider, which SCOPES the frame the documented way - STILL REFUSED.

The two-argument explicit form (use-subscribe frame-kw query-v) works, and Spec 002's own error ladder names 'pass an explicit {:frame <id>}' as the third of three ways to establish a scope - so there IS a supported route and hic-034's UIx arm takes it, saying so where it bites.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE TEST. Every UIx-adapter use-subscribe witness in the repo is a *_dom_cljs_test - the browser lane - so the server behaviour of the ambient form has never been exercised. An application server-rendering a UIx tree hits this on its first page, and the diagnostic it gets names 'no established scope' when the author has established one.

THREE POSSIBLE DISPOSITIONS and this bead does not pick one:
  1. repair - resolve the context through React's own dispatcher (useContext) rather than by reading _currentValue, so the server renderer answers;
  2. document - state in re-frame.adapter.uix and in the SSR docs that the ambient form is client-only and the explicit form is the SSR route;
  3. refuse - decide the ambient form is a client affordance by design and make the refusal say so, naming the explicit form in its recovery.

The third is the cheapest and the current message already half-does it; the first is the one an author would expect.

Adjacent: rf2-hic-046 (per-surface SSR/hydration witnesses) is about to write SSR rows across surfaces and will meet this.
design:
RULING (2026-08-13 21:28 AUSEST, delegated decision via dossier ai/decisions/rf2-5rqn.ambient-hooks-under-ssr.md; operator-reversible): Disposition (1) — REPAIR, AT THE READER SITE. The dossier's original analysis and an independent Codex review were both weighed; they converge on this option and on this repair site. Options (2) document and (3) refuse are REJECTED — see comments.

WHY THIS IS SAFE TO TREAT AS ALIGNMENT, NOT A CONTRACT CHANGE: Spec 006 (spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2406-2465, 2642-2651) already requires views below a frame-provider to resolve against that frame, and its UIx table gives the 1-arg form the dynamic-var -> React-context -> nil chain; docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:61-103 says the same for use-subscribe and use-frame. The server refusal is the implementation violating the shipped contract, not a documented limitation. Spec 011 (spec/011-SSR.md:25) is agnostic and stays so — NO SPEC CHANGE in this PR.

THE FIX (small, one function): implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs, function-component-current-frame (~lines 337-339).
- Dynamic tier (*current-frame*) first — unchanged.
- Otherwise read context._currentValue as today.
- ONLY when that raw value is EXACTLY the no-provider sentinel, read _currentValue2 instead.
- Classify the selected value ONCE through context-value->current-frame.
- Update the reader's comments/NOTE (rf2-2rzx0) that describe _currentValue as the whole story; the documented rationale block at context.cljs:330-336 gets a matching note for the secondary slot.

WHY THE EXACT-SENTINEL GATE MATTERS: a corrupted primary value must NOT be masked — it stays on the existing :rf.error/frame-context-corrupted path. The fallback fires only when the primary slot holds the untouched default.

WHY THE FRAME LAWS SURVIVE BY CONSTRUCTION (do not re-implement them):
- Refusal tier: resolve-current-frame (implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:758-764) withdraws the adapter reader entirely while *ambient-frame-refusal* is set (rf2-2rtt6.122, rf2-nqj22), so the secondary-slot fallback cannot bypass a refusing extent.
- Tier precedence: the reader consults *current-frame* before any slot.
- Client behaviour: under the client renderer _currentValue2 holds the default sentinel, so the fallback is inert.

BLAST RADIUS (the point of the reader site): every ambient consumer routes through this one reader via the :adapter/current-frame late-bind hook (implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3250-3252) — 1-arg use-subscribe (spine.cljs:3092-3102), use-frame (implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/use_frame.cljs:104-109), ambient subscribe/dispatch inside render, rf/current-frame-id. One move, one SSR story. Acceptance must exercise the shared reader as well as one hook, so the repair is proven central rather than hook-local.

MECHANISM (measured, PR #8002 witness on main): React 19.2 contexts carry _currentValue (primary/client renderer) and _currentValue2 (secondary renderer); react-dom/server populates the SECONDARY slot in this build, and public useContext resolves it. The witness pinned all three observation points mid-render: _currentValue = :rf.frame/no-provider, _currentValue2 = the real frame, useContext = the real frame. React 19.2.0 sources confirm createContext initializes both slots and the Fizz server renderer writes/reads its selected slot (packages/react/src/ReactContext.js#L16-L26, packages/react-server/src/ReactFizzNewContext.js#L168-L215, #L271-L275). The private-slot dependency is exactly pinned evidence for react 19.2.0, not a claim about future React.

REJECTED VARIANT (keep in reserve, do not build now): call-site repair using each hook's public useContext return (the spine's 1-arg arm already fetches and discards it at spine.cljs:3096). Public-API-only is its sole advantage; it fixes one hook at a time, must be duplicated at use-frame and every future ambient hook, and the naive (or *current-frame* (context-value->current-frame ctx)) bypasses the ambient-refusal tier — the ViewCell's exact expression. It is the documented escape hatch if a future React pin removes/repurposes the private slots.

DO NOT ADD: public API, SSR mode, feature flag, renderer detection, _currentRenderer* probes, stale-slot heuristics, or a generalized renderer abstraction. If a future React upgrade breaks the witness, thread public useContext returns through the hook surfaces then.

TESTS: today's behaviour is pinned by assert-use-subscribe-ambient-under-ssr (implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3603-3690). Its header already instructs: part 1 (the refusal) goes red on repair and is REWRITTEN to assert ambient resolution (ambient markup "n=7"); part 2 (the slot measurement) is the evidence and SURVIVES. Add one provider-scoped DIRECT READER assertion. Extend the witness with the aborted-render check: after a THROWING server render in the same runtime, a provider-less render must still refuse with :rf.error/no-frame-context (i.e. _currentValue2 must not be observed stale). That staleness check is the only cheap-to-verify hazard the slot approach carries — if it FAILS, stop and re-raise on this bead before shipping; the call-site variant is the fallback.

PRECEDENT: rf2-2rzx0 repaired the same renderer split for the compiled ViewCell (implementation/ui/src/re_frame/ui/viewcell.cljs:317-322, via useContext return + context-value->current-frame); Hicasso's native tier resolves via useContext with a test comment citing this bead (implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs:592-596). This ruling ends the two-substrate SSR asymmetry.

Related follow-up filed separately (see relates_to link): the ViewCell's use-frame-context! does not consult the refusal tier — out of scope here, do not fix in this PR.
acceptance_criteria: 1) function-component-current-frame (adapter/context.cljs) falls back to _currentValue2 ONLY when _currentValue is exactly the no-provider sentinel; dynamic tier still first; selected value classified once through context-value->current-frame. 2) Part 1 of assert-use-subscribe-ambient-under-ssr rewritten to assert ambient resolution (markup n=7) under renderToString beneath the adapter's own frame-provider; part 2 slot measurement retained. 3) One provider-scoped DIRECT reader assertion proving the shared-reader repair (not a hook-local shortcut). 4) Negative controls preserved: no provider still :rf.error/no-frame-context; dynamic frame still wins; corrupted primary slot still :rf.error/frame-context-corrupted (not masked); refusing extent still :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused. 5) Aborted-render check: after a THROWING server render, a provider-less render in the same runtime still refuses (:rf.error/no-frame-context) — no stale _currentValue2 observed. 6) No new public API, flag, SSR mode, or renderer-detection machinery; no spec change.
notes:
RE-DERIVED AT origin/main HEAD (11de456e6f) — THE PREMISE HOLDS, AND THE MECHANISM IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED. A node-lane witness now exists (PR: worker/resources-w67y). Measured under React 19.2 via renderToString, ambient probe wrapped in the UIx adapter's own frame-provider: {:ambient-html nil :observed [] :ambient-error :rf.error/no-frame-context :slots {:current-value :rf.frame/no-provider <- the reader reads THIS :current-value2 :rf.uix-5rqn/ssr-ambient-frame <- the frame is HERE :use-context :rf.uix-5rqn/ssr-ambient-frame} <- and useContext ANSWERS :explicit-html "
n=7
"} So: during a server render the shared frame-context's `_currentValue` holds the NO-PROVIDER SENTINEL while `_currentValue2` holds the real frame, and the public `useContext` return resolves it correctly. The frame was never absent — only unreachable from the slot the reader reads. The explicit 2-arg form server-renders fine, so the refusal is specific to the AMBIENT tier, not to SSR. DECISION NOT TAKEN — THIS NEEDS AN OPERATOR RULING. The bead names three dispositions and picks none, and every one of them changes the SSR contract (today the ambient form refuses on the server; two of the three make it work or make it refuse differently). I shipped the witness, which is in scope under all three readings, and did NOT ship a behaviour change. Costed: (1) REPAIR — much cheaper than the bead assumed, because it is a PATTERN ALREADY LANDED IN THIS REPO, not a new mechanism. - rf2-2rzx0 already hit this exact renderer split and repaired it for the sibling caller: `re-frame.ui.viewcell/use-frame-context!` sources the frame from the `useContext` RETURN and classifies it through `adapter-context/context-value->current-frame`. That classifier's own docstring is written for TWO callers — "the public useContext RETURN" and "a direct _currentValue slot read" — so the shared half of the repair already exists. - `re-frame.adapter.context/function-component-current-frame` already carries a NOTE (rf2-2rzx0) stating `_currentValue` is client-renderer only and that React 19.2's server renderer populates `_currentValue2`. The defect is documented in source; only this caller was left on the old path. - The spine's 1-arg `use-subscribe` arm ALREADY CALLS `use-current-frame` (which is literally `(use-context adapter-context/frame-context)`) at the top of its body — for the repaint subscription — and DISCARDS the value, then resolves through `frame/require-current-frame!`. The value needed is already in hand. - THE COST IS NOT ZERO, and this is the part worth ruling on. A naive `(or frame/*current-frame* (context-value->current-frame ctx))` in the spine — i.e. the ViewCell's exact expression — would BYPASS the ambient-REFUSAL tier. `resolve-current-frame` deliberately WITHDRAWS tier 2 while `*ambient-frame-refusal*` is set (rf2-2rtt6.122) and refuses a carried stamp naming another frame inside a declared `:extent-frame` (rf2-nqj22); `require-current-frame!` turns those into `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`. A correct repair must keep `require-current-frame!` as the primary path and consult the useContext value only when the reader returned nil AND no extent has refused. (Worth noting separately: the landed ViewCell expression appears NOT to gate on the refusal tier. That is a different caller and out of scope here, but if it is a real gap it deserves its own bead.) - ALTERNATIVE REPAIR SITE, arguably better: teach `function-component-current-frame` to fall back to `_currentValue2` when `_currentValue` classifies to nil. That preserves BOTH tier precedence and the refusal tier for free, because `resolve-current-frame` never calls the reader while a refusal is in effect. It also fixes ambient dispatch, ambient subscribe and `rf/current-frame-id` under SSR rather than `use-subscribe` alone — wider blast radius, but a single consistent SSR story instead of one repaired hook. Cost: a second private React slot read. (2) DOCUMENT — cheapest, changes nothing, but leaves the author with a diagnostic that tells them to establish a scope they HAVE established. Weakest of the three now that the value is known to be one hook call away. (3) REFUSE + better diagnostic — make the refusal name the SSR cause and point at the explicit form. Honest, but it institutionalises an asymmetry the compiled ViewCell does NOT have: after rf2-2rzx0 a server-rendered compiled sub resolves its frame ambiently while a server-rendered UIx `use-subscribe` cannot. Two substrates, two SSR contracts. RECOMMENDATION: (1), at the reader site, with the refusal-tier gating verified. The measurement shows the repair is available, that the value is already in hand at the call site, and that the precedent for it is already merged. But it is a contract change and the ruling is Mike's. LEFT IN PLACE: the witness pins today's behaviour, including the mechanism, so whoever lands the repair gets a red row telling them exactly what changed and why. Part 1 of that row is EXPECTED to go red on repair and should be rewritten to assert resolution; part 2 (the slot measurement) is the evidence and should survive. STATUS: returned to OPEN, awaiting an operator ruling — deliberately NOT closed. The node-lane witness shipped in PR #8002 (the coverage half of this bead, in scope under all three dispositions), but the DEFECT REMAINS: the ambient use-subscribe still refuses under react-dom/server. Closing this bead would erase a live bug from the tracker. What is needed from Mike is a pick among repair / document / refuse — see the costed note above; the measurement makes repair look both cheap and precedented (rf2-2rzx0 already did it for the ViewCell), but it changes the SSR contract and that is not a worker's call. DEFERRED BY THE MAYOR, 2026-08-13, NOT ABANDONED. This bead's own newest note says: "DECISION NOT TAKEN -- THIS NEEDS AN OPERATOR RULING", and "returned to OPEN, awaiting an operator ruling -- deliberately NOT closed". It nevertheless sat in `bd ready` with no open blockers, because `bd ready` computes dependency-blocking only and cannot see a hold recorded as prose. Deferring makes the hold visible to the dispatch loop so no worker is sent at a decision only Mike can make. STATE: the coverage half SHIPPED in PR #8002 (the node-lane witness, in scope under all three dispositions). The DEFECT REMAINS -- the ambient use-subscribe still refuses under react-dom/server, because the frame is unreachable from the slot the reader reads, not absent. The explicit 2-arg form server-renders correctly, so the refusal is specific to the AMBIENT tier, not to SSR. WHAT CLEARS THIS DEFER: Mike picks one of the three dispositions the bead names. Each changes the SSR contract differently -- today the ambient form refuses on the server; two of the three make it work or make it refuse differently. Part 1 of the shipped witness row is EXPECTED to go red on repair and should be rewritten to assert resolution; part 2 (the slot measurement) is the evidence and survives. RULING TAKEN 2026-08-13 21:28 AUSEST (delegated decision, dossier ai/decisions/rf2-5rqn.ambient-hooks-under-ssr.md; operator-reversible): disposition (1) REPAIR, at the READER site — function-component-current-frame falls back to _currentValue2 when _currentValue is exactly the no-provider sentinel. The independent Codex review in the dossier was weighed and CONCURS with the original analysis; both reached the same option and the same repair site independently. Full implementation brief now in DESIGN; gate in ACCEPTANCE. Defer cleared — this bead is DISPATCHABLE as a normal implementation task; the operator hold is resolved. MERGED-PR AUDIT #8144 (2026-08-13), NARROW FOLLOW-UP: the reader now selects _currentValue2 when the primary holds the sentinel, but emit-frame-context-corrupted!'s :reason still says React-context _currentValue is invalid, and context-value->current-frame's caller list still describes only a direct _currentValue read. On SSR, a non-keyword Provider value or corrupted secondary therefore blames the untouched primary. Acceptance: make both texts renderer-neutral or accurately describe the selected active slot, and extend the existing corruption witness to cover primary=sentinel plus corrupt secondary. Preserve the fallback and add no renderer-detection machinery or API.
close_reason: Landed in PR #8144, MERGED. Repair-at-reader per Mike's ruling of 2026-08-13. Fix size: one executable line became five, net +4, against the bead's '~3-line fix' estimate; the rest of the diff is the comment correction the ruling asked for. THE MAYOR'S FENCE NAMED THE WRONG TREE and the worker followed the bead: I fenced implementation/ui/**, but the site is implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs. The worker diagnosed the pattern better than I had - 'implementation/ui/** is the PRECEDENT (rf2-2rzx0's ViewCell), not the site.' PROVED ON THE SERVER PATH, which is the only proof that counts here: reverting the fix reddened EXACTLY ONE test of 13,861 - use-subscribe-ambient-under-ssr, uncaught :rf.error/no-frame-context - while every client-lane ambient row stayed green. A server-only change reddening only the server row is what rules out a client approximation of the bug. FLAGGED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT GUARDED: under React 19.2.0 a THROWING server render leaves _currentValue2 pushed, and the next render pops the abandoned snapshot before running any component. Acceptance criterion 5 passes as worded, but the slot genuinely holds a stale value in that window. The worker did not guard it because that is the stale-slot heuristic the ruling rejected BY NAME; instead it pinned all three rows, so a React release that changes the error path turns the row red and routes the reader to the note. Declined to build, all named in the ruling's rejection list: renderer detection, _currentRenderer* probes, stale-slot heuristics, feature flags, generalized renderer abstraction, any new public API or SSR mode. The call-site useContext variant stays in reserve. Closed by the mayor on the merge; the tracker showed OPEN with no close reason.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DECISION RATIONALE (delegated ruling, 2026-08-13). Why (1) repair-at-reader over the alternatives:

- REJECTED (2) document-as-client-only: it would document around a defect with a ~3-line fix, leave a diagnostic that tells the author to establish a scope they established the documented way, and contradict the shipped contract — Spec 006's context-resolution chain and the UIx API docs already promise ambient resolution below a provider, so "client-only" would be a contract change dressed as documentation.
- REJECTED (3) refuse-with-better-diagnostic: honest but institutionalises a two-substrate asymmetry — after rf2-2rzx0 the compiled ViewCell (and Hicasso's native tier) resolve ambient frames on the server while UIx hooks would refuse. Only coherent if ambient resolution were ruled client-only ACROSS all substrates, which would mean unwinding the ViewCell/Hicasso repairs. Nobody argued for that.
- REJECTED variant of (1), call-site useContext threading: public-API-only but per-hook, duplicative, and easier to get wrong (bypasses the ambient-refusal tier if written naively). Held in reserve as the escape hatch if a future React pin breaks the private slots.
- Also rejected from the reviews (as over-engineering, per both reviewers): renderer-detection machinery, _currentRenderer* probes, stale-slot heuristics, feature flags, generalized renderer abstraction. Build none of it.

REVISIT IF: a React upgrade removes/repurposes the private context slots (escape hatch above), or the aborted-render staleness check in ACCEPTANCE fails (stop and re-raise here before shipping).

Both the dossier's original analysis and the appended Codex review were weighed; they independently converge on this ruling. Evidence base: PR #8002's node-lane witness (mid-render slot measurement) plus React 19.2.0 source (ReactContext.js, ReactFizzNewContext.js) — mechanism measured, not inferred.

title: routing: realworld_http and realworld_resources register the same eleven route IDS from two files, so one silently replaces the other
description:
FLAGGED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT FILED by the rf2-wqnl worker (PR #7938), because it is a DIFFERENT HAZARD from the one that bead was ruled on. Filing it here so it is not lost.

WHAT IT SAW. implementation/.../examples/.../realworld_http and realworld_resources each register THE SAME ELEVEN ROUTE IDS, from two separate files. The registrar is id-keyed, so the second load silently REPLACES the first. Whichever file loads last wins, and nothing reports it.

WHY THIS IS NOT rf2-wqnl. That bead was about route PATHS colliding across applications in one node process — two distinct ids claiming one path string. This is the mirror image: ONE id claimed by two files. rf2-wqnl's census is explicitly built not to flag it, and its self-test pins that distinction as a deliberate rule: "one id from two files is an id replacement, not a path collision."

WHY IT MIGHT STILL BE FINE. Two ports of the same demo app may legitimately define the same route ids, and only one may ever load in a given bundle. VERIFY THAT BEFORE TREATING IT AS A DEFECT — read both files and establish whether they are ever loaded together. A verified "these are alternative ports, never co-resident" closes this bead and is a good outcome.

IF THEY ARE CO-RESIDENT, the question is what the registrar should do about a duplicate ID, and that is a design call rather than a repair — note the parallel with rf2-04tx's refuse-versus-ignore question and do not answer it unilaterally. STOP AND REPORT with the evidence.

DO NOT rename anyone's routes, and do not widen rf2-wqnl's census to cover ids — that census was ruled narrowly scoped on purpose, and its author drew the id/path line deliberately.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-12 08:18 AUSEST. VERDICT: no defect. Read-only; no edit, no branch, no PR.

## The claim, checked at source, premise by premise

1. "the same eleven route ids" — HOLDS, exactly. Extracted and diffed both
   files' `reg-route` ids: 11 vs 11, identical sets, diff empty.
   :realworld/home, :realworld/home-tag, :realworld.auth/login,
   :realworld.auth/register, :realworld.user/settings, :realworld.editor/new,
   :realworld.editor/edit, :realworld.article/show, :realworld.profile/show,
   :realworld.profile/favorites, :rf.route/not-found.

2. "the second load silently REPLACES the first" — the replacement holds; the
   word "silently" does not. `registrar/register!` (core/src/re_frame/
   registrar.cljc:586) does `swap! reg assoc-in [kind id]`, so the resolver map
   is last-writer-wins. But line 598 also writes the EP-0023 provenance source
   store, where "cross-namespace duplicate (kind, id) registrations are BOTH
   retained". No provenance is lost.

3. "nothing reports it" — DOES NOT HOLD. Two surfaces fire on exactly this
   shape:
     - `:rf.registry/handler-replaced` (registrar.cljc:631) on every
       re-registration;
     - `:rf.warning/registration-collision` (registrar.cljc:485), whose
       `collision?` predicate keys on cross-source PROVENANCE — a different
       (ns, file, line) reassigning one id — which is precisely two files
       claiming one route id.
   `:route` is not incidental to that surface, it is the kind that shaped it.
   registrar.cljc:639-642 decouples the collision check from the
   handler-replaced dedup gate specifically because "a kind with no rotating
   :handler-fn — :route, :head — can be deduped-away by shape". And
   core/test/re_frame/registrar_warnings_test.clj carries an explicit
   rf2-3az1vn `:route` case (`collision-fires-for-no-handler-fn-kind-despite-
   shape-dedup`) pinning that the warning fires for routes and that the last
   registration wins. Both example files call the FACADE `rf/reg-route`, which
   is a coord-capturing macro (core.cljc:498 `rm/defreg-macro`; see also
   core.cljc:1636), so both sides carry the source-coords `collision?`
   requires. The warning fires.

## Are they ever co-resident? Two answers, and the split is the whole story

SHIPPED / BROWSER BUNDLES: NEVER. Three separate builds with three separate
output dirs — `:examples/realworld` (init-fn realworld-http.core/run),
`:examples/realworld-resources`, `:examples/realworld-resources-ui`
(implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:2199/2213/2230). Structural proof: ZERO
cross-references in either direction between the two source trees (grep both
ways, 0 hits each). Empirical proof: the built
`implementation/out/examples/realworld-resources/main.js` contains 11
occurrences of `realworld_resources.routing` and 0 of `realworld_http`.

CONSOLIDATED CLJS :node-test BUNDLE: YES. `:ns-regexp "cljs-test$"` matches
both `re-frame.realworld-cljs-test` and `re-frame.realworld-resources-cljs-
test`, both under the `adapters/reagent/test` source path. Empirical proof from
the built bootstrap `implementation/out/node-test.js`:
    3060: SHADOW_IMPORT("realworld_http.routing.js");
    3076: SHADOW_IMPORT("realworld_resources.routing.js");
http loads first, resources second, so at bundle load the registrar's 11 route
slots hold the RESOURCES table — exactly as the finding predicted.

## Why that co-residency is not this bead's defect

It is already known, already handled, and the handling names this exact pair.
rf2-h1vqa4 (+ rf2-22vzb) landed `sequester-app-namespaces!` /
`reinstate-app-namespaces!` in `core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc` for it.
The docstring at test_support.cljc:241 says it outright: "Two co-loaded example
apps that share id vocabulary (the RealWorld twins both register
:settings/load, ...)". And the registrar leg of both sequester helpers is
OWNERSHIP-GUARDED precisely for ids BOTH apps register (test_support.cljc:195,
:263) — "the registrar's single (kind, id) slot is the LAST writer's — for an id
BOTH apps register that may be a SIBLING's".

The wiring is live in the two suites:
  - realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:146 sequesters the whole
    "realworld-http." tree at ns load, and :170 re-scrubs it per test;
  - realworld_cljs_test.cljs:158 reinstates "realworld-http." in its per-test
    :init-fn, so the http suite's route-dependent assertions (the auth-gate
    matrix at :870-980, the URL-shape cases at :842-865) run against the http
    route table, not the resources one.
No other co-loaded suite requires either `*.routing` ns, so nothing else is
exposed. (ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:44-51 documents the same
bundle-co-load hazard class from the other side and avoids it by construction.)

## So there is no design call to make

The bead anticipated "what should the registrar do about a duplicate id" as an
open question paralleling rf2-04tx's refuse-vs-ignore. It is not open. Spec 001
§Re-registration of a different function already rules it: replace the slot,
retain both provenances, emit the collision warning. That ruling is
implemented, specced and tested, and the one bundle where these two files meet
already carries the hygiene that rf2-h1vqa4 built for it.

Closing as verified-no-defect. rf2-wqnl's census was NOT widened — its
id-vs-path line stands untouched. No route renamed. TESTING.md untouched.
close_reason: Verified no defect. The eleven-id overlap is real, but (a) the two apps are NEVER co-resident in any shipped bundle — three separate shadow builds, zero cross-references either way, 0 occurrences of realworld_http in the built realworld-resources main.js; (b) the ONE bundle where they do meet, the consolidated CLJS :node-test, is already handled by rf2-h1vqa4's sequester/reinstate hygiene, whose docstring names the RealWorld twins explicitly; and (c) the premise 'nothing reports it' does not hold at source — :rf.warning/registration-collision fires on cross-source provenance clash, with :route the very kind that motivated decoupling it from the shape-dedup gate (registrar.cljc:639-642, pinned by the rf2-3az1vn case in registrar_warnings_test.clj). The registrar's duplicate-id behaviour is Spec 001 ruled, so no design call is open. Full evidence in notes.

title: mayor-method: nothing tells the mayor to verify its OWN brief's factual claims, and three briefs were wrong today
description:
FOUND BY THE HOURLY METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-11 night. The method files have not drifted; this is again what they do not contain.

VERIFIED ABSENT. `grep -c` over docs/the-mayor-method/:
  - dispatch-prompt-template.md: 0 hits for premise-verification of any kind.
  - bootstrap.md: 1 hit, line 67, "Verified-redundant grep before dispatch" — which is about whether the WORK IS ALREADY DONE, not about whether the brief's own assertions are true.
  - "an audit finding is a CLAIM, not automatically work": 0 hits in BOTH files. It lives only in .claude/commands/mayor-posture.md, so a fresh mayor reading the method never meets it.

THE GAP. The method tells the mayor to check for redundancy. It never tells the mayor to check the FACTS IT WRITES INTO A BRIEF — that a named ruling exists, that a named gate covers the named surface, that a named symbol resolves.

THREE BRIEFS WERE WRONG TODAY, ALL THE SAME SHAPE, ALL CAUGHT BY THE WORKER RATHER THAN BY ME:
  1. NAMED THE WRONG GATE FOR A SURFACE. I told two workers `.claude/commands/*.md` "may have no automated gate at all". scripts/check_readme_links.py owns it. Worse, the plausible alternative is a trap: check_doc_slugs.py explicitly does NOT cover CLAUDE.md and its own notes record that briefs have nominated it and received A GREEN EXIT VERIFYING NOTHING.
  2. ASSERTED THE METHOD ALREADY CARRIED A DISCIPLINE IT HAD NEVER CONTAINED. I filed a bead saying the template "already demands plant-and-restore" and merely lacked the verification step. A grep for `sabotag|plant|negative control|restore` across the whole tree returned NOTHING.
  3. QUOTED AN ADVISORY LEDGER ROW AS A SETTLED RULING — twice in one brief. I said rf2-hic-065 row 1 "ruled" the callback macro as `h/event`. In naming-ledger.md that name is in the RECOMMENDATION column with STATUS = open, and rf2-hic-065's own note says all naming rows are reserved to the operator's sitting.

THE THIRD ONE SHOWS THE COST, and it is not pedantic: `h/event` DOES NOT RESOLVE EITHER. Had the worker obeyed, it would have replaced a non-existent name with another non-existent name — RE-COMMITTING THE EXACT DEFECT THE BEAD EXISTED TO REMOVE, in the same files, under an authority that was never granted.

TWO CLAUSES TO ADD, both short, both in dispatch-prompt-template.md beside the existing brief-writing rules:

RULE A — VERIFY EVERY FACTUAL ASSERTION BEFORE PUTTING IT IN A BRIEF. If the brief names a ruling, read its STATUS field and quote it — a recommendation is not a ruling, and in this repo the two look alike in a summary and are opposite in force. If it names a gate, confirm that gate covers that path — a gate run over an excluded path exits green having verified nothing. If it names a symbol, grep that it resolves. A brief that names the wrong gate is worse than one that names none, because the worker then trusts a green that means nothing.

RULE B — TELL THE WORKER THE BRIEF IS A CLAIM. Every brief should say, in terms, that the mayor's premises are claims to be checked at source and that a verified "already fixed" or "the premise does not hold" is a complete and good deliverable. This is the single highest-yield line in any brief here: workers caught mayor errors at source ELEVEN times today, and three of those prevented damage rather than merely correcting a word.

SCOPE: two clauses in dispatch-prompt-template.md. Do NOT add a checklist, a script or a verification step — these are things the mayor must do while writing, not machinery. Do NOT restate in bootstrap.md; one source, and the template is where a brief is written. Consider whether "an audit finding is a CLAIM" belongs in the method rather than only in mayor-posture.md, and say which you chose and why.

title: spec: the Spec 009 Hicasso row count is prose that must track a table, and it has gone stale three times in one day
description:
OBSERVED THREE TIMES ON 2026-08-11, by three different workers, each finding it independently while doing unrelated work.

THE DEFECT. spec/009-Instrumentation.md's Hicasso section states its row count in PROSE ("forty-six", "fifty-one", "fifty-two"), and that count must track the actual number of rows in the table below it. Nothing enforces the correspondence. Every PR that appends a catalogue row must also edit the prose, and the prose is nowhere near the row.

THE THREE SIGHTINGS, all on the same day:
  - PR #7905's worker found the prose saying "forty-six" twice while the table held 48 rows. It was exact at cf85bc9cd8; two rows had landed since without updating it.
  - PR #7912's worker corrected it again on the way past.
  - PR #7923's worker found it stale AGAIN — "forty-six" against 48 — and carried it to fifty-one.
Each repair was correct. Each was made by a worker who had come to do something else, and noticed.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A FOURTH MANUAL FIX. This is the "second thing to drift" pattern the project has already ruled on twice today in other places: a rollup-band constant was REMOVED from bootstrap.md rather than updated, on the reasoning that a second written number is a second thing to drift and mayor-merge.md already owned it; and a catalogue enumeration presented as exhaustive was called WRONG rather than merely incomplete. A prose count beside a table it must match is exactly that shape, and it is now the most reliably-stale statement in the repository.

THREE OPTIONS — argue one, do not implement all:
  (a) REMOVE the count. If nothing depends on it, the table is its own answer and the prose can say "the rows below" without a number. Cheapest, and consistent with the bootstrap.md precedent.
  (b) DERIVE it. If the count carries real information for a reader, generate the sentence from the table rather than writing it twice.
  (c) ENFORCE it. scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py or check_complaint_catalogue.py already read this file and already run on every PR that touches it. If either can assert prose-count == row-count in a few lines, the drift becomes impossible rather than merely discouraged.
My weak preference is (a) then (c): removing a fact nobody needs beats checking it. But establish first WHETHER ANYTHING READS THE COUNT — if a gate, a doc or a downstream check parses it, (a) is off the table and you should say so.

DO NOT widen this into a review of spec/009. The catalogue rows themselves are correct and heavily exercised; only the prose count drifts.

HOT ZONE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md is hot-zone — SEQUENTIAL, never parallel. Confirm no open PR touches spec/** before dispatching this. Note that PR #7923 is currently OPEN and adds three rows plus two count words to that exact file, so this bead waits for it to merge.

VERIFY AT SOURCE: read the current prose and count the current rows before acting. Three workers have corrected it today; it may be right at this instant and wrong again by the time you read it, which is itself the argument for the bead.
notes:
SHARPER AT SOURCE THAN THE BEAD SAYS, verified on main at 2026-08-11 after PR #7923 merged.

THE COUNT APPEARS TWICE IN ONE SENTENCE, NOT ONCE PER SENTENCE. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2511 reads:

  "**Every one of the fifty-five is a thrown `ex-info`, never a trace event**, so all fifty-five are `diagnostic` by the §Channel rule."

So a single line carries the number TWO TIMES, and an editor who repairs the first occurrence and not the second leaves the file self-contradicting inside one sentence. That is a worse failure mode than the drift this bead was filed for, and it makes option (a) — REMOVE THE COUNT — stronger than my original weak preference suggested.

THE SENTENCE DOES NOT NEED THE NUMBER. Read it without: "Every one of these is a thrown `ex-info`, never a trace event, so all of them are `diagnostic` by the §Channel rule." The claim is universal quantification over the table; the cardinal adds nothing a reader can use and everything a maintainer must keep true. The table is its own answer.

FOURTH SIGHTING IN ONE DAY. The count was "forty-six" against 48 rows when PR #7905's worker found it; corrected again on #7912; found stale AGAIN by #7923's worker and carried to fifty-one; then the rebase of that same PR had to resolve a CONFLICT in exactly these two count words, because main and the branch had each independently repaired them. That last one is the tell: THE COUNT IS NOW GENERATING MERGE CONFLICTS, not merely going stale.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION: take option (a). Remove both occurrences and rewrite the sentence to quantify over the table rather than over a number. Only fall back to (c) — enforcement in check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py — if you establish that something actually READS the count. Verify that first; if a gate, a doc or a downstream check parses it, say so and (a) is off the table.

CURRENT STATE, so the next reader can tell drift from repair: main reads "fifty-five" twice on line 2511, and the table between `hicasso-empty-vector` and the `#### Adapter-internal` heading holds 55 body rows with 55 distinct ids. That was counted by the #7923 rebase worker, not inherited from either side of its conflict.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #7933 (branch worker/rowcount-9oah). Option (a): the count is REMOVED. Established first that nothing reads it — git grep 'fifty-five' across the tracked tree returns only spec/009 lines 2511 and 2521 plus the bead's own JSONL; check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py and check_complaint_catalogue.py both read this file but parse row IDs only, with no number-word vocabulary; the two checkers that DO carry a number-word map (check_readme_inventories.py, check_skill_eval_docs.py) do not target spec/009; and the complaint register states no count. SHARPER THAN THE BEAD RECORDED: there were THREE occurrences across TWO lines, not two on one — line 2521's 'these fifty-five are the cases where repairing would mean overruling what the author wrote' had been missed by every prior sighting, including the sweep that concluded only 2511 carried a number. Both sentences make a universal claim over the table, so they now quantify over it ('Every row below is a thrown ex-info'; 'the rows below are the cases'). Row count at time of fix: 55 body rows, 55 distinct ids, lines 2527-2581. Options (b) derive and (c) enforce both rejected: (b) is machinery for a number no reader needs, and (c) was the fallback only if something read the count — with the number gone there is nothing left to check. Gates captured: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py 0, npm run test:hicasso-invariants 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict 0, check_fast_pr_gap.py --list 0.

title: mayor-method: two brief rules the mayor hand-repeats every dispatch are missing from the template
description:
FOUND BY THE HOURLY METHOD-REREAD LOOP, 2026-08-11. The method files themselves have not drifted; the gap is what they DO NOT contain. Both rules below were hand-written into roughly a dozen dispatch briefs across this session, which is the evidence that they belong in the template rather than in the mayor's head.

Verified absent: `grep -c` for each returns 0 in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md and bootstrap.md.

RULE 1 — VERIFY A SABOTAGE RESTORE BY HASHING THE BYTES, NEVER BY READING `git diff`.

The plant-and-restore discipline is how this project proves a guard is EXACT rather than merely PRESENT, and three separate workers today caught something with a WIDENED-guard control that a removed-guard control could not — one showed a near-miss stop minting, another produced 36 failures across four namespaces. So the discipline is load-bearing, and its verification step is currently unwritten.

TWO WAYS `git diff` LIES HERE, and the template must name both:
  (a) A CRLF-flipping rewrite reads CLEAN while having changed every line.
  (b) **A patch that never applied ALSO reads clean.** THIS CHECKOUT IS CRLF, and a worker today found its first multi-line patch anchor silently matched nothing — no error, no edit. It caught that only because it hashed the bytes.
`git diff` cannot distinguish "unchanged" from "not attempted". That second half is the dangerous one: a plant that silently fails to apply makes the sabotage run come back GREEN, and the worker concludes the guard fired when nothing was ever broken — A FALSE PROOF OF A REAL GUARD, which is worse than no proof.

Also worth one clause: use SINGLE-LINE anchors when patching by string match on this checkout, because any pattern crossing a newline is a coin flip.

RULE 2 — WHEN A BEAD CORRECTS A STALE FACTUAL CLAIM, SWEEP EVERY CARRIER IN THE SAME PASS.

rf2-2l17 corrected the claim "the repair arrives a macrotask later" FOUR times across THREE PRs. Every individual repair was bounded and correct. Each was found by the NEXT merged-PR audit rather than by the repair before it. That is three round-trips of mayor, worker and CI for what one `git grep` would have closed.

The wording that fixes it: "BOUNDED REPAIR" should bound the CHANGE, not the SEARCH. `git grep` the exact wording over TRACKED files, read every hit, dispose of each in one PR, and list in the PR body what was changed and what was left correct.

TWO CAUTIONS THE TEMPLATE MUST CARRY WITH IT, or the sweep does damage:
  - THE PHRASE IS OFTEN CORRECT ELSEWHERE. invariants.md's timer-callback row says "one macrotask later" and is RIGHT, because a timer callback IS a macrotask. The grep also hits core/substrate/spine.cljs, the react_shared_suite and two bench tests. Reading every hit is the work; the grep is only the index.
  - THE BRIEF MUST NAME THE DISCRIMINATOR, or the worker cannot separate stale hits from correct ones. There it was WHO SCHEDULES THE DEFERRAL — our own collector (repaired to a microtask) versus React or a timer (still a macrotask).

SCOPE: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, in or beside the existing gate-discipline block. Keep both rules SHORT — a clause each plus the one-line reason. Do NOT add a script, a checklist or a wrapper; both are brief-writing rules, not mechanisms. Do NOT restate them in bootstrap.md as well — one source, and the template is where a dispatch is written.

VERIFY BEFORE WRITING: re-run the greps. If a later commit added either rule, close as verified-duplicate saying so.
close_reason: Both rules landed in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md via PR #7922. Re-verified absent first, as the bead required: grep -c still returned 0 in BOTH the template and bootstrap.md for hash / single-line anchor / sha256 / Get-FileHash / every carrier / stale claim / git diff. (The lone 'bounded repair' hit at bootstrap.md:231 is a different rule -- a fence widened mid-flight by a second finding.) Rule 1 is a fifth bullet in '### How a gate is run, not just which one' (lead line Four->Five rules), naming both ways git diff lies about a restore, with the never-applied patch called out as the dangerous one, plus the single-line-anchor clause. Rule 2 is a new sibling subsection '### Briefing a correction -- sweep every carrier' carrying both mandated cautions (the phrase is usually right somewhere; the brief must name the discriminator). Not restated in bootstrap.md -- one source. No script, no checklist, no wrapper. Gates all captured: check_doc_slugs 0, check_readme_links 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict 0, check_fast_pr_gap --list 0; negative control on a broken MARKDOWN reference went red at captured exit 1 naming the file and line. Plant and restore both verified by sha256 (post-restore byte-identical), which is this PR's own new rule applied to itself. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: the dispatch brief asserted 'the template already demands plant-and-restore' -- it does not; grep for sabotag/plant/negative control/restore over docs/the-mayor-method/ returns nothing, so Rule 1 was written to introduce the discipline in half a clause rather than assume it.

title: hic — n/defcomponent's :server policy is validated but still consulted by nothing
description:
# The native tier's `:server` policy has a roster and still has no reader

Filed by the worker that closed **rf2-u9lk** (PR for rf2-34a7 + rf2-u9lk).
rf2-u9lk had two faults; this bead carries the half that was deliberately NOT
built.

## What rf2-u9lk fixed

Fault 1 — the missing rosters — is closed. `re-frame.hicasso.native/declared-server`
now refuses a declaration key outside `#{:server}` (`:rf.error/hicasso-native-unknown-option`)
and a value outside `#{:client-only :render}` (`:rf.error/hicasso-native-bad-server-policy`),
both at LOAD from inside the extent `declaring!` opened, so the refusal carries the
author's own file and line.

## What it did NOT fix, and why

Fault 2 — the field is consulted by no runtime path. `native.cljc` stamps it onto
the tier marker and nothing branches on it: there is no server walk in the tier and
no SSR arm. `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/adversarial-risks.md:18` defers
native-surface risks to Phase 3, so building a server path would have been inventing
the machinery rather than validating the declaration.

The deferral is now STATED rather than implied, in three places the author actually
reads: the namespace headline example (`{:server :render}  ; recorded; read in Phase 3`),
`defcomponent`'s docstring, and `declared-server`'s. The witness row at
`native_fence_cljs_test.cljs` says in its own wording that the policy is recorded
and not yet consulted, so it no longer presents itself as coverage of a live policy.

`native_abi_cljs_test.cljs`'s sibling assertion was deliberately left alone: there
the recording is the CONTROL for `n/lazy`'s hard-coded "client-only", a decision
that genuinely IS consulted, so asserting the recording is what makes the contrast
row mean something.

## Done when (Phase 3, not before)

- A server path in the native tier consults `:server`, or the field is removed.
- If consulted: the witness asserts the EFFECT — bytes emitted or withheld — rather
  than the marker, and the three deferral statements above come out.
- If removed: `component`'s third argument, the marker's `:server` slot, `n/lazy`'s
  hard-coded "client-only", `declared-server` and its two complaint ids all go with
  it, which is a bigger change than it looks and is why the deferral is the right
  answer today.

## Where

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc` — `declared-server`, `component`, the marker stamp, `lazy`
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/native_fence_cljs_test.cljs` — the reworded witness row
- `docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/adversarial-risks.md` — the Phase 3 deferral this rests on
notes:
PHASE-1 FINDING (2026-08-12 08:16 AUSEST, worker srvpol-ggnp; NO code written, no PR, no worktree —
the establish-then-report step ended the work).

VERDICT: THE PREMISE HOLDS AND THE DEFERRAL STANDS. Nothing consults `:server`; consulting it is
rf2-hic-046's chartered work, not this bead's; and the reader cannot be built here without either
inventing the second policy mechanism audit #7839 forbade or pre-empting hic-046's server door.
RECOMMENDATION: keep deferred; block this bead on rf2-hic-046 rather than dispatching it again.

1. THE CENSUS — `:server` HAS NO READER, AND NOR DOES THE MARKER THAT CARRIES IT.
   `git grep -n 'rf2:hicasso-native-tier'` over the whole tracked tree (minus `.beads`) returns
   exactly TWO lines: the definition at native.cljc:280 and the assertion at
   native_fence_cljs_test.cljs:343. `n/marker` has no caller outside native.cljc except tests. The
   `server` slot is written once (native.cljc:422, `component`) and hard-coded once (native.cljc:528,
   `lazy`); every read of `unchecked-get … "server"` in the repo is in
   native_abi_cljs_test / native_abi_dom_cljs_test / native_fence_cljs_test. No product source, no
   tool, no adapter branches on the field. The bead's own claim is exact.

2. AND THERE IS NO SERVER FOR IT TO BRANCH IN. `git grep 'react-dom/server|renderToString|
   renderToStaticMarkup'` over `implementation/hicasso/src` returns ZERO callers — only prose. The
   only server path anywhere near this tier is test harnesses calling `renderToStaticMarkup` by hand
   (native_fence_cljs_test.cljs:105/114, native_abi_cljs_test.cljs:102). `implementation/ssr/src` does
   not mention hicasso at all. This is the same census hic-046's 2026-08-11 note recorded for
   presence, re-run for the native tier: no product server entry exists.

3. WHAT "CONSULTING IT" WOULD MEAN, PRICED AT SOURCE. `:render` is already today's behaviour — a
   native component renders on the server, which is what the fence harness measures. So the entire
   content of the wiring is the `:client-only` arm, WHICH IS THE DEFAULT AND THEREFORE EVERY
   DECLARATION-LESS COMPONENT. Two shapes exist and both are owned elsewhere:
   (a) THE GATE. The host tier withholds by minting one (`codec.cljs:1469 mint-host-gate!`, whose
       `adopted?` is a `useSyncExternalStore` answering false from the server snapshot). Porting that
       shape to the native tier means `component` (native.cljc:408-423) stops answering the author's
       own function as the element type — which is the tier's stated contract, HD-011's
       "zero-wrapper, zero-fiber, zero-hook shape" (codec.cljs:1286), the rent clause of the
       native-boundary law (adversarial-risks.md:26, "Optional native-tier rent"), and
       hic-034's island band (5%/1 ms) plus its component-identity parity against handwritten React
       and UIx. One fiber and one hook per island, on the DEFAULT path. Audit #7839 ruled on exactly
       this: "Keep the native core's small metadata seam; NO SECOND POLICY MECHANISM IS WARRANTED."
   (b) THE REFUSAL/SNAPSHOT. Refusing server use at source needs a stable "we are rendering on the
       server" fact. That fact is precisely the request-scoped provider/snapshot door hic-046's
       2026-08-11 ruling charters ("the smallest honest door … true for server render and hydration,
       false for an ordinary client mount"), and the same ruling's fences forbid a per-surface
       exception to the two-policy matrix.
   Either way the wiring answers what hic-046 owns. Per the dispatch fence, STOPPED AND REPORTED.

4. THE OWNERSHIP IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, IN TWO PLACES.
   - `docs/design/hicasso/product/dispositions.md` rows HS-25, HS-27, HS-28, HS-29, HS-30 all carry
     the same current cell VERBATIM: "Client-only — refusal until rf2-hic-046".
   - rf2-hic-046's note from MERGED-PR AUDIT #7839 parks this row there in terms ("This is exactly
     rf2-hic-046's existing native-tier SSR/hydration row, not a new issue"), and the 2026-08-12
     delegated ruling re-confirms it stays in hic-046's remit, "post-mo4o … written in the final
     :server spelling". So rf2-ggnp's "Done when" IS hic-046's deliverable.

5. ONE THING THE BEAD DID NOT SAY, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT LOST. The live hazard is not that the field
   is unread; it is that `:client-only` — the CONSERVATIVE DEFAULT, chosen because a native component
   is exactly the node that may reach for `window` — does not withhold anything. A consumer calling
   `react-dom/server` on a tree containing a declaration-less island runs that island's body on the
   server. Nothing shipped does that today (see 2), so the exposure is a consumer's own server
   render, and it is the same class of gap hic-046 measured for presence. It belongs in hic-046's
   witness set, not in a second mechanism here.

6. rf2-mo4o ADJACENCY: NOT TOUCHED, AND NO GAP TO FILE. native.cljc's docstrings and two refusal
   messages narrate the OLD host spelling ("the `defhost` door's spelling is :ssr" ~:333/:385;
   "`defhost`'s `:ssr` admits a third form" ~:339; "`defhost`'s {:fallback …}" ~:402), and the fence
   row at native_fence_cljs_test.cljs:209 says the same. All of these go stale on mo4o's rename —
   and mo4o's own ruling already lists them as ADDITIONAL SITES to respell in its pass. Nothing for
   this bead to file or fix. The declaration path was read only; no edit was made anywhere.

WHAT I RECOMMEND THE TRACKER DO: leave rf2-ggnp OPEN and add `blocks: rf2-hic-046 -> rf2-ggnp`, so
the obligation survives without being dispatchable. When hic-046's native row lands, ggnp closes by
the shape its own "Done when" already states — the witness asserts bytes emitted or withheld, and
the three deferral statements (native.cljc ~:13, defcomponent ~:836, declared-server ~:365, plus the
fence row ~:192) come out in the same PR. Closing ggnp outright would work too, but the deferral
statements are a real obligation and a bead is the cheapest place to keep them.
close_reason: Closed by PR #7967 (--force: the rf2-hic-046 blocking edge was added by this bead's own phase-1 worker to hold the obligation until hic-046's native row landed; that row landed as #7966, so the edge has served its purpose. hic-046 stays open for its remaining per-surface rows). THE BEAD'S PREMISE DID NOT HOLD: all four named obligations (native.cljc ~:13, ~:20, declared-server ~:365, defcomponent ~:836, plus the fence row native_fence_cljs_test.cljs ~:192) were ALREADY retired by rf2-hic-046 (#7966, commit 2bec42fd35) and its test follow-ups — verified site by site against b6869d5150. A tree-wide sweep for the claim in every spelling it took returns zero hits outside .beads. What #7966 left behind was the OTHER half: a :client-only island now costs one fiber and one hook where it cost neither. PR #7967 arm-scopes the two places that priced the tier as free — three_way_parity_cljs_test.cljs (ns docstring, section header, one testing row, and the deftest renamed to a-declared-render-island-...; no assertion changed) and draft-guide/10-native-tier.md (which claimed a Client-only island 'emits its declared fallback' — there is no native :fallback, deliberately). No behavioural gap appeared; the mechanism, rosters and complaint ids are untouched; no export added; I9 stays at two hooks. title: mayor-method: gh pr list --search 'head:<branch>' FUZZY-MATCHES, and the hygiene loop uses it to authorise branch deletion
description:
FOUND DURING THE HYGIENE LOOP, 2026-08-11. A near-miss on a destructive operation, caught only because the mayor cross-checked before deleting.

WHAT HAPPENED. The hygiene pass maps each unpinned local `worker/*` branch to its PR to confirm the PR is MERGED before deleting the branch. The obvious command is:

    gh pr list --state all --search "head:$b" --json number,state

**IT FUZZY-MATCHES.** Asked for `head:worker/activity-hic014` it returned **PR #7909, whose head is `worker/activity-hic014b`** — a DIFFERENT branch, still OPEN, belonging to a live worker. Had the result been trusted, the loop would have read "7909 OPEN" for `activity-hic014` and (correctly, by luck) skipped it — but the same shape in reverse deletes a live branch on a merged sibling's verdict. The operator owns `activity-hic014`; the risk landed on his branch, not on one of mine.

THE RULE ALREADY EXISTS AND THIS IS ITS NEWEST INSTANCE. bootstrap.md:278 says *"Key destructive operations on identity, never on a name. Branch and worktree names repeat across sessions, so a cleanup that matches a name will eventually match a historical artefact and delete live work."* That is exactly this, one layer down: the NAME here is not a stale artefact but a PREFIX of a live one, and `gh`'s own search is what does the matching.

THE WORKING FORM, used for the actual deletions:

    gh pr list --state merged --limit 60 --json number,state,headRefName \
      --jq '.[]|select(.headRefName=="worker/<branch>")|"\(.number) \(.state)"'

An EXACT `headRefName` equality, never a `--search` substring. All fifteen deletions that tick were verified that way and every operator branch was left alone.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Add the trap to `docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md`'s identity bullet as its newest recorded instance — the method's own style is to name the instance that earned the rule, and the existing text speaks only of stale names repeating, not of a live name being a prefix of another live one.
2. Check `.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md`'s branch-deletion paragraph and make the exact-`headRefName` form the stated one. **`.claude/commands/mayor-merge.md` already mentions `headRefName`** — read how it uses it and match that idiom rather than inventing a second.

THE GAP. `npm run test:hicasso-compile` walks only its own directory. `re-frame.bench.p0-app` and `re-frame.bench.hicasso-narrow` were ABSENT from its emitted modules. Neither namespace is named `*-cljs-test`, and nothing test-shaped `:require`s either one, so no test-discovery mechanism reaches them either. So far as that worker could find, NO PR GATE COMPILES THEM AT ALL. It covered its own diff with a targeted `:hicasso-bench` compile — that is why its PR was safe — but the hole is still open for the next editor.

WHY THIS IS THE SHAPE THE PROJECT ALREADY DECIDED TO CLOSE. `rf2-2rtt6.73` built the lane gate precisely to stop a namespace compiling nowhere. This is that same fail-open defect ONE DIRECTORY OVER: a file that nothing compiles can be broken by any edit and stay green until somebody runs it by hand. A gate whose coverage is defined by a directory walk silently loses anything that moves outside the directory — and nothing announces the loss.

VERIFY BEFORE FIXING, because the premise is a worker's observation and this bead is a claim:
1. Confirm both namespaces are genuinely absent from every PR-gated compile — check `test:hicasso-compile`'s emitted module list, the shadow-cljs build targets, and whether any test namespace requires them transitively.
2. Establish whether the set is exactly these two. A directory-walk gap rarely has exactly two members; enumerate every `.cljs` under the bench trees that no PR gate compiles, and report the full list even if you only fix these two.
If they ARE covered by something you find, close as verified-duplicate citing the gate — a verified "already covered" is a good outcome and better than a redundant build id.

THE REMEDY IS A JUDGEMENT CALL — argue it, do not assume it:
- Adding the two namespaces to an EXISTING compile gate is the smallest change and probably right.
- A NEW build id or target is hot-zone (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` carries build ids and `:dev-http` ports, and `.github/workflows/**` carries the job) and is sequential, never parallel. If your remedy needs either, STOP and report rather than editing — that is my call to sequence.
- **Do NOT make the gate's coverage rule cleverer.** The failure is that coverage is implicit in a directory walk; the fix is to make the covered set explicit, not to write a smarter walker that will lose the next file a different way.

SCOPE: close the gap for the bench namespaces. Do NOT re-sweep citations (rf2-p9c5 did that, PR #7897, merged), and do NOT touch the frozen bench tree — `implementation/hicasso/frozen-sources.edn` pins exactly one row (`front/slot.cljc`), confirmed by two workers this week.

THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN DECISION. Blinding cannot be enforced by absence, and the published docs are why: docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md tells a reader that day8/re-frame2-hicasso is not published and to clone the monorepo beside their project and resolve it with :local/root, so a pilot following the published instructions CORRECTLY ends up with the whole repository on disk. The instrument is a four-value resolution field -- published / inferred / asked / unresolved -- ordered by how much each indicts the documentation. 'inferred' is the row the format exists to capture: a guess that works leaves no other trace because the code looks fine and the tests pass, and it is how a docs gap survives a successful migration. 'asked' files a bead without exception, per the ratification's rule that every question a pilot must ask a human is a defect. rf2-hic-063's revisit trigger (a) is carried in terms: a near-empty log is recorded as SUSPECT, stated at the top so nobody optimises for brevity. The blinding attestation must be written even when empty, because an absent attestation and a clean one are otherwise the same silence.

BRIEFS carry the docs-only rule as their own section, argued rather than asserted, and are free of bead ids, spec sections and repository paths -- verified mechanically against the fenced blocks the pilot actually sees (0 hits; the pattern was control-run against pages that do contain those tokens, so the zero is real). Asking a human is framed as valuable data rather than failure, because a brief that punishes asking gets a pilot that hides it. The two pilots cover different failure modes: Pilot 1 translates two existing screens (PORTING); Pilot 2 ports the board and grows a card-detail that does not exist today (AUTHORING from the guide alone), so its brief carries an extra fence against reading the other worked examples in the checkout.

SCOPE HELD: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/** and examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/** were READ ONLY -- zero files changed in either. Diff is 6 files, 708 insertions, 0 deletions.

GATES, all captured exit codes on the FINAL rebased base (trunk moved mid-work, 38849d69d8 -> 6120eff90f; nothing that landed touches these files): check_doc_slugs.py 0 (covers this path -- DEFAULT_ROOTS includes docs, no exclusion matches), check_provenance_pins.py 0 (runs over this tree but these pages cite no hex pins, so it is a no-op on this content rather than a meaningful pass), check_readme_links.py --ci 0, table column counts 0 by hand across 5 tables. mkdocs build --strict CANNOT SEE any path here -- mkdocs.yml exclude_docs carries design/hicasso/ -- and was not run. The fast-pr spine was NOT run, per the dispatch (a bench-class release build was live on worker/workcount-n1b9h). check_fast_pr_gap.py --list exit 0, reporting 96 required checks the spine does not run. Gate-reached-my-tree proven by planted fault: broke one link target in workspace.md, gate went red naming the plant at my file, restored via git checkout and re-hashed byte-identical to the committed object (24d98c9b5b9f...), re-ran green.

TWO ANCHOR DEFECTS CAUGHT rather than assumed: the specification link named a section that does not exist (#13-adoption-and-definition-of-done -> #13-definition-of-done); and that correction was then left UNCOMMITTED, so the gate had gone green against a working tree that disagreed with the pushed branch.
