title: hic: four re-authored witnesses the prototype suites cannot carry across — index laws, cold probe, registry axes, hook budget
description:
FROM THE rf2-6ync TRIAGE (PR #7824). Of 69 prototype suites, 47 STAY with the benchmark, 13 PORT (6 landed in that PR) and NINE are RE-AUTHORED — the behaviour matters but the suite is written against a runtime that no longer exists, so the mechanics cannot come across. These four are the genuine coverage gaps among them.

READ FIRST: docs/design/hicasso/product/prototype-suite-triage.md, the census committed by PR #7824. It names every suite with its verdict and reasoning. Do not re-derive the triage.

THE FOUR GAPS, largest first:

1. THE SIX INDEX LAWS OVER THE FUSED CELL TABLE. The largest of the four. The prototype asserted them against arm1.runtime, which rf2-hic-009 carved into six modules — which module answers now depends on the VAR, not the file, so a port is impossible by construction. Re-author against the package's own structure.

2. THE COLD PROBE'S CONTRACT. What the probe guarantees on a first, uncached read.

3. THE TWO REGISTRY-TRANSITION AXES.

4. THE <=2-HOOK BUDGET AT REACT'S DISPATCHER.

ITEMS 3 AND 4 NEED A PACKAGE `hook-probe` THAT DOES NOT YET EXIST. That is part of the work, and it is the reason these two are last: build the probe, then the two witnesses fall out of it. If the probe turns out to be substantial, STOP after items 1 and 2, open the PR, and say so — a partial delivery with the reason is better than a rushed probe.

WITNESS DISCIPLINE, and this surface has now reopened three beads for want of it:
  - Derive each witness from the GRAMMAR of the law it tests, not from the implementation you are testing. A witness written from the code inherits the code's blind spots.
  - AND make each row DISCRIMINATING: ask what single narrowing of the implementation would let this row pass while the law is broken. If such a narrowing exists, the row is decorative. State per law which narrowing your row would catch.
  - For the hook budget specifically, the boundary is a COUNT — so the row must fail at 3 and pass at 2, not merely observe that hooks were called.

FENCES: do NOT edit the frozen bench tree — check_freeze.py must stay exit 0, manifest unchanged. No spec/*, no .github/workflows/*, no implementation/package.json (all hot-zone). If a witness needs a new build id or npm script, STOP and report.

STANCE: pre-alpha, no back-compat shims, no over-engineering. Four honest witnesses beat nine mechanical ports — and if one of these four turns out already covered by an existing Phase-1 witness, say which and drop it. The triage already rejected 13 suites as duplicates on exactly that ground, so check before writing.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7824 SCOPE CORRECTION. The description says items 3 (the registry-transition axes) and 4 (the hook budget) both need a package hook-probe. The source evidence and the triage document do not support that grouping: disposed_cell_cljs_test.cljs and first_registration_cljs_test.cljs are node/runtime lifecycle witnesses and do not require arm1.hook-probe; only hook_ledger_dom_cljs_test.cljs plus frame_prop_dom_cljs_test.cljs require that React-dispatcher probe. Re-author the registry axes directly against impl.generation/collector without making them pay for browser/probe infrastructure. This is a scope reduction, not a new deliverable.
MAYOR: ONE MORE SUITE BELONGS TO THIS BEAD, established by the rf2-b6ja worker (PR #7832) against origin/main.

arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test needs arm1.hook-probe — the SAME blocker this bead already carries for hook_ledger and frame_prop. I had earlier placed it with the SSR pair on rf2-6rw9, on a summary that turned out wrong: that pair needs no hook-probe and no SSR entry, while host_hatch does need the probe.

So when the hook-probe is built here, host_hatch falls out with the other two. If you build the probe and stop (which the brief permits), say explicitly whether host_hatch is now portable — the next worker needs to know whether the probe covers it.

This does not widen the bead's four laws. It adds one suite that becomes portable once item 3/4's probe exists.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7835 — REOPENED FOR TWO EXACT COMPLETENESS GAPS; THE LANDED FOUR CORE WITNESSES ARE ACCEPTED.

1. The pre-merge mayor note and the corrected triage assign `arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test` to this bead: it was blocked specifically on the package hook-probe and "falls out" once that probe exists. PR #7835 built that probe, but neither ported the assigned suite nor reported its portability. Port the package-relevant host-hatch witness onto `re-frame.hicasso.hook-probe`, deduplicating rows already owned package-side. This is test work, not a new production abstraction or lane.

2. The package cold-probe witness still omits the image-loaded-frame branch that makes `live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution` load-bearing. The PR and new namespace explicitly say the same-tick registration claim is real but unwitnessed; the surviving arm1 row exercises the prototype runtime, not the package implementation. Add one discriminating package row using an image-loaded frame, and mutation-prove that removing the resolution wrapper turns it red. Do not add a generic harness.

No duplicate issue: both omissions are unfinished obligations of this exact re-authoring owner. The six index laws, held first-registration axis, general cold-probe laws, and dispatcher hook budget otherwise review cleanly.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7835 findings ACCEPTED — the four core witnesses stand; two obligations of this exact owner were left unfinished. QUEUED: implementation/hicasso/test/** is held by worker/ports-a15c (14 commits deep) and by open PR #7838. Sequence behind whichever lands first.

GAP 1 — host_hatch. My own pre-merge note assigned arm1/host_hatch_dom_cljs_test to this bead, because it was blocked specifically on the package hook-probe and would "fall out" once that probe existed. THE PR BUILT THE PROBE AND THEN NEITHER PORTED THE SUITE NOR REPORTED ITS PORTABILITY — and my brief had asked explicitly for the latter ("say explicitly whether host_hatch is now portable"). Port the package-relevant host-hatch witness onto re-frame.hicasso.hook-probe, deduplicating rows already owned package-side. Test work only: no new production abstraction, no new lane.

GAP 2 — AND THIS ONE CORRECTS A JUDGEMENT I PRAISED. The worker wrote a cold-probe row for "a reg-sub earlier in this tick is visible to this read", found its mutation red NOTHING, and DELETED it as decorative, recording the finding in the namespace docstring. I called that exemplary — the discriminating-row rule applied by a worker to its own work. It was half right. The row WAS decorative AS WRITTEN, because a make-frame frame has no stale projection to flush. But the CLAIM IS REAL AND IS NOW UNWITNESSED: the surviving arm1 row exercises the PROTOTYPE runtime, not the package implementation.

So the correct move was to REWRITE the row with an image-loaded frame — the condition that makes live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution load-bearing — not to delete it. title: hic: three prototype-suite ports need sequencing decisions — the JVM lane, the SSR trio, the measurement couple
description:
RAISED BY THE rf2-6ync TRIAGE (PR #7824), which stopped rather than touching it. This is a sequencing question, not a defect.

front/slot_cljs_test.cljc is a PORT candidate that cannot move without a hot-zone change. The chain: it is JVM-runnable, so rule B2 plus hicasso's --probe waiver mean a JVM-runnable suite living in implementation/hicasso/test/ needs a ROSTER ENTRY, and a roster entry needs a test.yml JOB. So a one-file port pulls in .github/workflows/test.yml, which is sequential-access.

THE DECISION: is a JVM lane for hicasso worth opening for this suite? Weigh honestly — hicasso's deps.edn currently declares ZERO JVM tests, and check_test_lane_bijection.py treats that as the correct outcome. Opening a lane for one suite may be right (it establishes the lane for everything after) or wrong (a whole CI job for one file). If the answer is "not worth it", record that on the triage document so the next reader does not re-derive the question — a documented no is a result.

IF IT IS WORTH IT: take the rf2-hic-021 lesson. A job gated on a changed-surface predicate is correct exactly until the thing it guards grows one more input, and nothing makes anyone revisit the predicate. And take PR #7823's better move: check whether the suite's inputs ALREADY arm an existing job's output, in which case it rides that job and needs no new predicate at all. #7823 established this by enumerating inputs from the compiler's own analysis cache rather than guessing.

TWO SIBLING SEQUENCING QUESTIONS from the same triage, decide them together or say why not:
  - the :ssr trio (host_ssr + fallback_contents + host_hatch) — owned by rf2-6rw9, blocked on the package gaining an SSR entry.
  - the render_measure OFF/ON nightly couple — a measurement pair, so it belongs to whichever tier runs measurements, not to the PR spine.

READ FIRST: docs/design/hicasso/product/prototype-suite-triage.md, the census PR #7824 committed. It names all 69 suites with a verdict each; this bead is about three of the rows it could not settle alone.

HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/test.yml and implementation/deps.edn are sequential-access. Do not dispatch alongside another toucher.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7832 (2026-08-11) — REOPEN THIS EXACT DECISION/DOCUMENT OWNER FOR ONE BOUNDED CORRECTION. The PR correctly proves host_ssr_dom_cljs_test and fallback_contents_cljs_test neither require each other nor reach ssr.entry; all three decisions otherwise reconcile with source, lane selection, and existing owners. But prototype-suite-triage.md says ssr.entry has seven requirers including ssr/fixtures.cljs. fixtures.cljs has no require of entry: its two mentions are docstring [[wiki-links]], the very false-dependency class this section corrects. Outside strings/comments the semantic consumers are six: entry_cljs_test, hframe_ssr_cljs_test, instance_key_payload_dom_cljs_test, spike_cljs_test, spike_dom_cljs_test, and ssr/node.cljs. Correct seven to six and remove fixtures from that sentence. Do not revisit the PORT verdict, add a checker, or change runtime/lane code.
MAYOR: AUDIT #7832 finding ACCEPTED, and it is the most instructive one of the session — THE CORRECTION REPRODUCED THE VERY FAULT IT WAS CORRECTING.

PR #7832's whole contribution was proving that a claimed dependency between two SSR suites was FALSE: each named the other only in a docstring [[wiki-link]], not a require. Excellent work, and it corrected a bead I had written from a bad summary.

But its own prose then says ssr.entry has SEVEN requirers INCLUDING ssr/fixtures.cljs — and fixtures.cljs has NO require of entry. Its two mentions are docstring [[wiki-links]]. The audit's phrasing is exact: "the very false-dependency class this section corrects."

Outside strings and comments the semantic consumers are SIX: entry_cljs_test, hframe_ssr_cljs_test, instance_key_payload_dom_cljs_test, spike_cljs_test, spike_dom_cljs_test, and ssr/node.cljs.

BOUNDED REPAIR: correct seven to six and remove fixtures from that sentence. DO NOT revisit the PORT verdict, add a checker, or change runtime or lane code.

WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ONE NUMBER: prototype-suite-triage.md is now the document three port beads read as authoritative — rf2-a15c, rf2-npch and rf2-6rw9 all cite it, and a worker is reading it right now. A dependency claim that is wrong in the direction of "more coupled than it is" makes ports look harder than they are, which is exactly what stalled rf2-6rw9 for hours.

AND THE GENERAL LESSON IS ONE I HAVE NOW SEEN THREE TIMES TONIGHT: a docstring [[wiki-link]] reads exactly like a dependency to a grep, and nothing in this repo distinguishes them mechanically. Whoever fixes this should say IN THE DOCUMENT that the count excludes strings and comments, so the next reader knows which question was answered.

SEQUENCING: the file is free — open PR #7836 holds docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/** and product/naming-ledger.md, NOT prototype-suite-triage.md. But worker/ports-a15c is READING the triage as its primary input right now; land this after that PR opens, so the worker is not reading a file that changes under it.
MAYOR RULINGS — all three sequencing questions settled, plus the audit's correction accepted. A worker records these in the triage document; the decisions themselves are made here.

=== 1. THE JVM LANE: NO. Do not open a CI job for one suite. ===

hicasso's deps.edn declares zero JVM tests and check_test_lane_bijection.py treats that as the CORRECT outcome, not as a gap. A whole CI job to carry one file is exactly the gold-plating this project rejects, and the "it establishes the lane for everything after" argument is speculative — nothing else is queued behind it.

BUT TRY THE CHEAPER MOVE FIRST, which PR #7823 established: check whether front/slot_cljs_test.cljc's inputs ALREADY arm an existing job's output, in which case it rides that job and needs NO new predicate at all. Establish that by enumerating inputs FROM THE COMPILER'S OWN ANALYSIS CACHE, as #7823 did — not by reading path filters and guessing.
- If it rides an existing job: port it. No roster entry, no new job, no predicate.
- If it does not: the suite STAYS in the bench tree, and the documented no goes on the triage document. The bead says it itself and it is right — A DOCUMENTED NO IS A RESULT. The point is that the next reader does not re-derive this question.

Either way, take the rf2-hic-021 lesson: a job gated on a changed-surface predicate is correct exactly until the thing it guards grows one more input, and nothing makes anyone revisit the predicate.

=== 2. THE :ssr TRIO: OVERTAKEN BY EVENTS, two of three. And the stated blocker never bound. ===

VERIFIED ON MAIN, not inferred: host_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs and fallback_contents_cljs_test.cljs are BOTH PRESENT in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/ — they landed in PR #7842 (merged fdead7d060) as part of rf2-a15c. host_hatch is still absent.

THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE STATUS: this trio was recorded as "blocked on the package gaining an SSR entry". THE PACKAGE STILL HAS NO SSR NAMESPACE IN src — a find over implementation/hicasso/src for any *ssr* file returns nothing — and the two witnesses landed anyway, as Client-only. So the blocker as written did not bind. Record that, so the next reader does not wait on a condition that was never the real one.

REMAINING: host_hatch only, owned by rf2-wjag, which already records it as confirmed portable and is in flight right now. Nothing further to sequence.

=== 3. THE render_measure OFF/ON NIGHTLY COUPLE: measurement tier, NOT the PR spine. ===

The bead answers its own question and the answer is right. A measurement pair on the PR spine makes every PR's wall-clock a gate, which is precisely the flakiness this repo has deliberately kept out — tools/story/src/re_frame/story/budgets.cljc says in terms that the CI gate does NOT assert wall-clock time because it is flaky in CI, and enforces bounded output in a single pass instead. Putting a measurement couple on the spine would reintroduce that by the back door.

Consistent with rf2-hic-006 and rf2-hic-029, both of which are measurement windows held for a quiet machine rather than run under concurrent load.

=== 4. AUDIT #7832's BOUNDED CORRECTION: ACCEPTED. ===

prototype-suite-triage.md says ssr.entry has SEVEN requirers including ssr/fixtures.cljs. fixtures.cljs has NO require of entry — its two mentions are docstring [[wiki-links]], which is the very false-dependency class that section exists to correct. Outside strings and comments the semantic consumers are SIX. Correct the count and the roster.

This is the same trap that produced a false premise on rf2-6rw9 (I transcribed "they :require each other and reach ssr.entry" onto that bead; both halves were docstring wiki-links). Worth stating in the document, because the section that teaches the lesson was itself caught by it.

=== SCOPE FOR THE RECORDING WORKER ===
Record 1, 2 and 3 as decisions with their reasons, and land 4 as a factual correction. Do NOT re-derive the 69-suite census, do NOT open a JVM lane, and do NOT touch tool-consumer-census.md — a different worker holds that file right now.
CORRECTION: my close reason names the follow-up as rf2-fxbe. That id does not exist — I wrote it before filing the bead, which is a mistake I have now made three times this session. THE CORRECT ID IS rf2-c78g (a port is not reliably a move — six ports deleted their originals, the two :ssr ports left duplicates). Nothing else in the close reason is affected.
close_reason:
Landed via PR #7850 (merged 03d59d90e2, rebased onto main). Green on all five merge clauses at 91/91, five runs completed/success, no workflow commits after its base. Clean reap on the worker's completion report; canary held at 103/2933/2.

ALL THREE SEQUENCING DECISIONS RECORDED, plus audit #7832's correction — and the JVM decision came back with a fact that INVERTS its own reasoning, which is why dispatching it was worth more than ruling it from the armchair.

The worker did that from the compiler's analysis cache, not by guessing: :node-test's dev/ana cache carries slot_cljs_test.cljc and slot.cljc, the cached :requires closure is six namespaces of which exactly two are repo files, and handing those to report-changed-surfaces.sh arms BOTH implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true. The JVM half genuinely runs today — clojure -M:test on that namespace gives 3 tests, 92 assertions, exit 0. The answer is not merely "a lane is not worth opening" but "the port would lose coverage". test.yml untouched, no lane opened.

THE :ssr TRIO — verified independently rather than taken from me: both witnesses present in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/, host_hatch absent, and implementation/hicasso/src has NO *ssr* file at all, so the recorded "package must gain an SSR entry first" blocker never bound. The worker also found rf2-wjag's package hook-probe has LANDED (35e8fecc1d), which discharges host_hatch's blocker and the two RE-AUTHORED rows citing it — noted, rows unchanged, host_hatch left to rf2-wjag.

title: ci: check_gate_scheduling.py cannot see build:* scripts — decide whether that scope limit is intended
description:
MEASURED by the rf2-qy1j worker (PR #7823), reported rather than actioned because widening it has consequences it was fenced from deciding.

THE GAP. scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py's GATE_PREFIXES is ("test:", "bench:"), so a `build:` npm script can NEVER be flagged unscheduled. The checker's whole job is to catch a command that exists but nothing runs — and an entire naming family is invisible to it.

WHY IT IS DEFENSIBLE AS-IS, and this is the argument to weigh rather than dismiss: a GATE renders a verdict; a BUILD makes an artefact. Not every build wants scheduling, and forcing one to declare a disposition is paperwork if nothing depends on it.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: PR #7823 added `build:hicasso-release` and scheduled it as a step of the existing cljs job. Its durable protection is that workflow step — NOT the checker, which cannot see it. THE DECISION TO MAKE: either widen GATE_PREFIXES and write those three dispositions, or leave the prefixes alone and record IN THE CHECKER why `build:` is out of scope, so the next reader does not mistake the omission for an oversight. Both are acceptable outcomes. What is not acceptable is leaving it undocumented — an unexplained scope limit reads as a bug to whoever finds it next.

If you widen it, take the rf2-hic-021 lesson: a scope predicate that must be kept in sync with a growing set is a standing liability. Ask what makes someone revisit GATE_PREFIXES the next time a new script family appears.

GATES: scripts/check_gate_scheduling.py itself (it self-tests), plus the fast-PR spine which runs it. Report the before and after counts — currently `44 gate commands, 38 scheduled, 6 declared (0 of them known holes with beads)`.

title: mayor-method: an interim message is not a completion report — the reap rule needs one clause
description:
EARNED IN THE FIELD TONIGHT, at the cost of a destroyed gate run. This is NOT a seventh proxy — the file rightly says do not add one — it is a sharpening of what the word "report" means in the rule that is already there.

WHAT THE FILE SAYS: "Reap a worktree only once its owning agent has delivered a completion report." Correct, and I followed it as I understood it.

WHAT I DID: the catalogrows-vkle worker sent two interim messages. The second said, verbatim, "Holding for the spine — not done yet, and I won't report a colour I don't have." Minutes later I merged its PR and reaped its worktree in the same breath. Its spine was in the JVM tier. git worktree list stopped showing the tree, .git went, gate.log was deleted mid-write. The worker afterwards found gate.exit = 1 and CORRECTLY REFUSED TO REPORT IT AS A FAILURE — that 1 was written by a script whose own checkout had been deleted underneath it. My cleanup manufactured a red.

THE GAP IN THE WORDING: I had promoted "the agent has spoken" to "the agent has reported done". Those are not the same thing, and the difference was written plainly in the message I was reading. An interim status, a progress note, a partial hand-off, a PR-opened announcement — none of these is a completion report. AND A BACKGROUND GATE STILL RUNNING IS THE WORKER STILL RUNNING, even though nothing in the branch, the tree or the PR shows it.

WHY IT LOOKED SAFE, which is the part worth writing down: every listed proxy agreed at once. PR merged, tree clean, commits pushed, no junction, agent had messaged minutes earlier. That is not evidence — it is what a DISCIPLINED worker mid-gate looks like BY DESIGN, since commit-and-push-as-you-go is what every brief demands. The better the worker, the more convincing the illusion.

THE SECOND MECHANISM, and the file already warns about it in the abstract: I had BATCHED THE REAP INTO THE MERGE PASS. The file says never pair a merge with a reap in the same breath. I did exactly that, because a merged PR is the moment a tree looks finished — which is precisely why that pull is dangerous.

PROPOSED WORDING, small and in the file's own voice: add to the existing bullet that the report must SAY THE WORK IS FINISHED, and that the operational test is "can I quote the sentence where this agent says it is done?" If the answer is no, the worktree stays. Cost of waiting: one stale directory. Also worth one clause: a gate the worker backgrounded is still that worker running, and the harness's ten-minute foreground ceiling (see dispatch-prompt-template.md) means long gates are ALWAYS backgrounded, so this is the common case rather than an edge case.

FENCES: do NOT restructure the reaping section or add a seventh proxy to the list. This is one clause on the existing rule plus, at most, one sentence of mechanism. docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md carries the full six-proxy history — if the same clarification belongs there, make the two agree rather than saying it twice differently.

GATE: mkdocs build --strict COVERS docs/the-mayor-method/ (verified: site/the-mayor-method/... exists while site/design does not). scripts/check_doc_slugs.py also validates it and IS SILENT ON SUCCESS — prove coverage with a planted bogus anchor and restore byte-identically.
close_reason:
PR #7827 merged. One clause added inside the EXISTING reaping paragraph in .claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md: the report has to SAY the work is finished, and the test is 'can I quote the sentence where this agent says it is done?' — if not, the worktree stays. Plus one sentence of mechanism: a backgrounded gate is still that worker running, and the ten-minute foreground ceiling against a ~25-minute spine makes that the COMMON case rather than an edge case.

docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md gets the same clarification inside its 'Only a worker's own report says it has finished' bullet, with the verbatim 'Holding for the spine — not done yet' message recorded there since bootstrap is the history document. The two agree rather than saying it twice differently.

DECLINED, correctly and as fenced: no restructure of the reaping section, and no seventh proxy — the file is right that six is enough.

description:

title: hic: the public door has no re-render, so a dev/after-load hook cannot be written on public namespaces only
description:
DESIGN FINDING from the rf2-hic-008 worker (PR #7814), reported rather than decided. Verify against the source first.

THE CLAIM. There is no re-render on the public door. The HMR testbed dev/after-load hook reaches into impl.mount/render! to do its job, and h/root! calls createRoot every time, so it is not the answer either. Consequence: a consumer writing an ordinary hot-reload hook ON PUBLIC NAMESPACES ONLY cannot. The consumer app that PR #7814 landed therefore deliberately carries no reload hook — that omission is evidence for this bead, not an oversight.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CONVENIENCE. Hot reload is table stakes for a CLJS view library, and rf2-hic-008 own acceptance criterion is a consumer app on PUBLIC NAMESPACES ONLY. A public surface that cannot express the single most common dev-time affordance is an ergonomics hole in exactly the place this project cares about most: high productivity and low friction, for the programmer and the AI working with them.

THE QUESTION: what is the smallest public affordance that lets a consumer re-render a mounted root after a reload — and is it a new export, or does root! grow the ability to re-use an existing React root rather than calling createRoot each time? State the options and recommend; do not silently pick.

STANCE, and it cuts both ways here: no over-engineering — do NOT build an HMR framework, a reload registry, or a lifecycle-hook system. Trust the programmer: the goal is one obvious call they can put in their own dev/after-load. Equally, do not close this as minutiae — an affordance the library own testbed needs private access to achieve is a real gap in the public surface.

SEQUENCING: rf2-hic-027 is building the L3 mounted facade (mount!/render!/unmount!) in the test kit right now. Read that PR first — it may already have settled the shape of a re-render call, and the public door should not disagree with the kit about what re-rendering means. FENCE: any new public export is classified and justified when it lands, per the standing facade-export rule.

title: mayor-method: the gate snippet is one command line for a reason the template never states
description:
FOUND IN THE FIELD by the rf2-hic-092 worker, which hit it, noticed, and re-ran.

docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md line 173 gives the canonical gate invocation:

  sh <WORKTREE_ROOT>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > gate-fastpr.log 2>&1; echo "$?" > gate-fastpr.exit

That is CORRECT. The gap is that the surrounding prose (line 166) says only "redirect to a log file, echo the runner's own exit code explicitly" — it never says the two halves must share ONE command line, or why. So the single-line property is incidental to the example rather than stated as a rule, and any paraphrase loses it.

THE FAILURE. Each Bash tool call is a FRESH SHELL. Split across two calls, $? in the second reads whatever that new shell last did — typically the `cd` — not the gate. The worker's own words: "the brief's next-command pattern silently fails here; each Bash call is a fresh shell, so $? reads the cd, not the gate."

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE. It is SILENT and it yields a plausible ZERO. That is precisely the fail-open class the exit-code discipline exists to close — the rule written to stop a pipeline swallowing a red gets defeated a different way, because the mechanism was demonstrated but not explained. The bullet at line 164 already teaches the pipeline shape; this is its sibling and belongs beside it.

THE FIX IS ONE CLAUSE, and this bead is not licence to restructure the section: extend the line-166 sentence to say the redirect and the echo go on the SAME command line, in one shell, because a separate invocation starts a new shell whose $? is not the gate's. Keep the existing snippet as the example.

MY OWN BRIEFS CARRIED THE DEFECTIVE PARAPHRASE ("echo the exit code on the very next command") for a whole session before a worker caught it — recorded in bd memory under mayor-gate-exit-code-must-be-same-command-line. That is the evidence the prose, not the example, is what gets copied.

title: gate: _inline_blocks bounds an inline code span at an indented ATX heading, but python-markdown requires column zero
description:
Found and DECLINED with reasons by the rf2-mmyc worker (PR #7795), which was fenced to five named fence shapes and correctly stopped at five. This is the sixth shape it found, and it is NOT a fence question at all — it reproduces with no fence present.

REPRODUCER

    Prose with `a code span
      ### not a heading to python-markdown
    [in](in-target.md)` closing here.

_LEAF_LINE_BLOCK_RE in scripts/check_doc_slugs.py bounds an inline block at an ATX heading indented three spaces or fewer, following CommonMark. python-markdown's HashHeaderProcessor requires COLUMN ZERO. So on an indented heading the two disagree: the gate sees two unpaired backtick runs, ends the inline block early, and extracts a link that the renderer renders as code. At column zero they agree and there is no disagreement.

DIRECTION: this is a FALSE POSITIVE, not a blind spot. The gate checks a link the renderer never resolves, so the failure mode is a spurious complaint rather than an unvalidated link. That is the safe direction, which is why it was right to leave it rather than widen rf2-mmyc's scope.

SURFACE: _inline_blocks in scripts/check_doc_slugs.py. Related to rf2-8wcbe, which owns that predicate.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING ANYWAY: check_doc_slugs.py runs in the fast-PR spine and in the docs tier, so a false positive here reds a PR for a document that renders correctly — and the fix is to match the renderer's column-zero rule, which is strictly simpler than the CommonMark rule currently encoded.

ACCEPTANCE: the predicate agrees with python-markdown on an indented ATX heading inside an inline code span; a renderer-derived case pins it in the self-test; the full corpus scan is byte-stable or its movement is enumerated.

DO NOT build a second Markdown parser. The established technique on this gate is to drive mkdocs.config.load_config('mkdocs.yml') into a real markdown.Markdown and compare against it — see PR #7795 for the working instrument, and note its --prove mode, which requires a planted known-bad page to move at least three items so a zero cannot be a false zero.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #7798, merged to main as 4d91e357c, alongside rf2-1cpt — one file, one technique: drive MkDocs' own configuration into a real markdown.Markdown and compare the gate against it. No Markdown parser was built. THE FIX: _LEAF_LINE_BLOCK_RE followed CommonMark's three-space allowance for ATX headings; python-markdown does not — HashHeaderProcessor.RE is anchored (?:^|\n)#{1,6} with no leading-space allowance, so an indented ### line is paragraph text. The ATX alternative is hoisted out of the shared prefix, while the thematic break, setext underline and table row correctly keep it, since HRProcessor.SEARCH_RE carries its own leading-space allowance. This also settles an inconsistency INSIDE the file: _HEADING_RE has always required column zero before minting a slug, so the indexer and the block-boundary predicate had disagreed about what a heading is. MY FRAMING ON THIS BEAD WAS TOO NARROW AND THE WORKER CORRECTED IT. I filed it as a false positive only. The same rule also costs the gate in the other direction: for a link whose text spans an indented heading line, the renderer emits the anchor because the three lines are one paragraph, while the gate split the unit and extracted nothing — so a REAL BROKEN LINK went unchecked. That is a blind spot, not merely a spurious complaint, and both directions are now pinned.

title: docs-tooling: the in-fence assertion misses blockquoted fences, and 118 colliding fragment ids are an armed trap for HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS
description: BOTH CLAUSES MEASURED AND EXCLUDED BY THE rf2-mmyc WORKER (PR #7785, merged 68a917359), which judged each too large a blast radius for a gate-correctness fix and documented them rather than half-doing them. That was the right call; this bead is where they land. --- CLAUSE 1: the new in-fence assertion has a blind spot in the tree it guards --- rf2-mmyc taught check_doc_slugs.py to see indented fences and added an assertion that a Markdown link must not appear inside a fence under docs/design/hicasso/. **Blockquoted fences are not covered.** `> ```clojure` is a real fence to python-markdown, and they exist in the guarded tree — verified by the mayor, `git grep '^ *> ```' -- 'docs/**' 'spec/**'` returns 12 matching lines, including docs/design/hicasso/studio/p0-converged-witness-set.md and docs/design/hicasso/studio/rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md. The worker measured 28 content lines corpus-wide. WHY IT WAS EXCLUDED, and this is the number that matters: a prototype covering blockquoted fences flipped **138 lines back to prose and minted 36 rendered ids**. That is a corpus-wide validation change, not a fence fix — far too much to carry inside a bead about indentation. SO THE WORK IS: extend the fence model to blockquoted fences, and measure it the same way rf2-mmyc did — before/after counts in BOTH directions on the same merge base, with every link that stops being checked accounted for, and every rendered id gained or lost named. If the 138/36 figures reproduce, decide explicitly whether that is acceptable rather than absorbing it silently. A gate that gets quieter is not automatically a gate that got better. --- CLAUSE 2: 118 colliding fragment ids are a loaded trap, not harmless redundancy --- Across 15 pages, an explicit `` duplicates the generated slug of the heading it precedes. The concentrations: docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/glossary.md (the mayor counts 61 explicit anchors there), docs/routing/concepts.md (18), spec/015-Data-Classification.md (18), spec/012-Routing.md (10). WHY NOTHING HAS BROKEN, and why that is not reassuring. Duplicate ids are invalid HTML; browsers take the first. In the glossary pattern the explicit anchor comes FIRST and sits above its heading, so deep-links land correctly today — by luck of ordering, not by design. THE LIVE HAZARD: all 118 are traps for `HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS`. Adding any one of them to that manifest reds the gate instantly with `DUPLICATE COMPAT ANCHOR`. Currently zero are in the manifest, so the mine is armed and untripped. Someone will eventually add one for a legitimate reason and meet a failure that looks like their own mistake. DECIDE, DO NOT MASS-EDIT. The options are not equal and the choice is the substance: (a) remove the redundant explicit anchors where the generated slug already serves — smallest corpus, but it silently changes which fragment a stale external link hits; (b) keep them and teach the duplicate gate to recognise the anchor-immediately-precedes- its-own-heading pattern as intentional, so the trap disarms without touching prose; (c) leave both and record the hazard where whoever edits HANDBOOK_COMPAT_ANCHORS will see it — the cheapest, and defensible if the pattern is deliberate house style. My inclination is (b) or (c); (a) touches the most files for the least benefit and can break inbound links. Say which you chose and why. --- FENCES --- Do NOT weaken any existing check, and do not add an ignore mechanism or allowlist. rf2-mmyc deliberately made the in-fence predicate `.md`/`#fragment` destinations rather than bare `](`, because `(fn [x](inc x))` is legal Clojure and the stance forbids nagging valid code — keep that. Corpus-wide scoping of the assertion is NOT available: 109 in-repo links live inside fences elsewhere, 88 of them in spec/Spec-Schemas.md as legitimate `;;` commentary, and the only way past that is an allowlist. --- GATES --- python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --self-test, then the full-corpus run, then python scripts/check_readme_links.py (it imports the same extractor, so it moves with you), then sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh. Run each ALONE and echo $? to its own file; never append a filter to a gate's command line. Write every counting script to a FILE and run the file — a Bash heredoc on this machine strips backslashes, so a regex silently becomes a different regex while the script still exits 0 with a plausible answer. rf2-mmyc's worker gave each of its scripts a `--prove` mode that runs the same machinery over synthetic known-bad input and requires non-zero; that caught a real false zero. Copy that pattern rather than trusting a clean count.

# hic-088 — Requirements-mine consolidation

**Phase**: 4/6 · **Est.**: S · **Depends**: hic-004
**Surface**: `docs/design/hicasso/product/requirements-mine.md` (the one consolidation owner)

## Goal
The mine must be current when the audits read it. This bead owns the updates hic-004 only seeded.

## Deliverables
Two consolidation passes recorded in the file: one before the coverage checkpoint (every row's witness link resolves; "owed by" rows re-pointed to landed evidence or open corrections) and one before the final audit (same, plus final-name updates after the sweep).

## Acceptance
At each pass: zero stale witness links; zero rows owing to closed beads without landed evidence; pass dates recorded in the file.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]

- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates: foreground a gate that fits inside the harness ceiling; DETACH one that does not and poll BOTH its log and its `.exit` file in a bounded loop within the same turn — never end the turn waiting for a completion event. Never pipe a gate through `tail` or any filter; redirect to a log and echo the runner's own exit code on the same command line. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn. DOC-SURFACE GATE: for an edit confined to docs/design/hicasso/, `mkdocs build --strict` is NOT the gate — mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs keeps that tree out of the site. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates its markdown link targets and heading anchors, and `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/; nothing validates its tables, rendering or nav, so verify anchors and table column counts BY HAND and say so in the PR body.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json` from a worker branch — they are whole-database EXPORTS, not database files, and your branch carries the snapshot taken when its worktree was created, so committing one TIME-TRAVELS the tracker: beads closed since reopen, beads filed since vanish (PR #6677 did exactly this, 135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). Any other database-derived path likewise. The human-authored config — `.beads/README.md`, `.beads/config.yaml`, `.beads/.gitignore`, `.beads/hooks/**` — IS fair game. CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section is the authority.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files only if this bead flags them — and the hot zone INCLUDES the spec/*.md hot files (spec/004-Views.md, spec/002-Frames.md, spec/API.md, spec/Conventions.md among others), not just implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn and .github/workflows/*. CLAUDE.md's Workflow section carries the canonical list; read it there rather than treating this line as complete.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues AND a row in docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md. The checkpoint's own report PR writes the `open` row; a CORRECTIVE PR never edits that file — every later transition is the ledger keeper's. Read the file's own stated protocol before touching it.

description:
# hic-087 — Final architecture and retained-mechanism census

**Phase**: 6 · **Est.**: M · **Depends**: hic-048, hic-072
**Surface**: census scripts + `docs/design/hicasso/product/architecture-census.md` (new)

## Goal
Prove the kill rules held: the finished product contains no rejected mechanism and no unconsumed retained tooling.

## Deliverables
- The mechanism census: no ViewCell-class dependency graph, no second emitter, no compiled-hiccup mode, no per-boundary callback-cell table — verified by dependency/namespace census with the search method recorded.
- The retained-tooling census: every retained diagnostic/tool surface (incl. graduated spikes) names its real daily consumer; anything without one is filed for removal.
- A post-kernel mutable-global re-sweep (the hic-017 census re-run against the final tree — later work introduced no unjustified global).

## Acceptance
All three censuses published with methods; zero unexplained rows; misses filed as corrections in the hic-073 ledger.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates: foreground a gate that fits inside the harness ceiling; DETACH one that does not and poll BOTH its log and its `.exit` file in a bounded loop within the same turn — never end the turn waiting for a completion event. Never pipe a gate through `tail` or any filter; redirect to a log and echo the runner's own exit code on the same command line. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn. DOC-SURFACE GATE: for an edit confined to docs/design/hicasso/, `mkdocs build --strict` is NOT the gate — mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs keeps that tree out of the site. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates its markdown link targets and heading anchors, and `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/; nothing validates its tables, rendering or nav, so verify anchors and table column counts BY HAND and say so in the PR body.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json` from a worker branch — they are whole-database EXPORTS, not database files, and your branch carries the snapshot taken when its worktree was created, so committing one TIME-TRAVELS the tracker: beads closed since reopen, beads filed since vanish (PR #6677 did exactly this, 135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). Any other database-derived path likewise. The human-authored config — `.beads/README.md`, `.beads/config.yaml`, `.beads/.gitignore`, `.beads/hooks/**` — IS fair game. CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section is the authority.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files only if this bead flags them — and the hot zone INCLUDES the spec/*.md hot files (spec/004-Views.md, spec/002-Frames.md, spec/API.md, spec/Conventions.md among others), not just implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn and .github/workflows/*. CLAUDE.md's Workflow section carries the canonical list; read it there rather than treating this line as complete.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues AND a row in docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md. The checkpoint's own report PR writes the `open` row; a CORRECTIVE PR never edits that file — every later transition is the ledger keeper's. Read the file's own stated protocol before touching it.

Reproduced the fail-open first against the landed script on unmodified main (planted impl.planted/!cells returned [], absolved by impl.collector/!cells; a unique name returned the finding). Self-test 8 arms -> 10, with the two-direction pair the old control lacked: the duplicate reds while the rostered impl.collector/!cells stays accepted in the SAME run. Sabotage-verified — reverting the two qualifying lines FAILs the duplicate arm and leaves the 'original accepted' arm ok, so the pair discriminates rather than co-firing. Textual recognisers and the one-direction policy untouched per rf2-6ng7 (c)-narrow; no Clojure parser, no widened kill-rule machinery. CENSUS RE-RUN under qualified identities: 23 owners found, all rostered, 0 findings — nothing the bare matcher was silently accepting, no bare-name collision in the tree. architecture-census.md's published conclusion STANDS unchanged; the page now records the matching method. notes:
MAYOR RULING — WHERE AN EXAMPLE APP LIVES, 2026-08-11. Decided on rf2-hic-025 and binding on every sibling witness app.

THE QUESTION. rf2-hic-025's bead named the surface implementation/hicasso/examples/slice/. Its worker found that path is on NO :source-paths entry, so a tree there is COMPILED BY NOTHING. It placed the slice at implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/slice/ instead — beside consumer-app, where both cljs_node_test and cljs_browser arm on implementation/hicasso/** — and asked before touching implementation/shadow-cljs.edn.

RULING: THE PLACEMENT STANDS. The bead's literal path was the error. Do NOT add the two :source-paths lines and do NOT git mv it.

WHY. Today this repository spent two beads and two merged PRs (rf2-bl0j, rf2-cfqk) closing exactly one defect: namespaces that NO PR GATE COMPILES. The enumeration found 23 of them, and the fix for the last 19 was RED ON ARRIVAL — five infer-warnings in a rostered arm whose functions had been un-typed since they were written, because nothing had ever compiled them. Creating a fresh uncovered tree hours after closing that hole would be perverse. An artefact belongs where a gate already reaches it; a path is not worth a coverage gap.

The worker's own reasoning was sound and it asked rather than guessing, which is exactly right for a hot-zone file. Asking cost one round-trip; guessing would have cost a silent coverage hole.

BINDING ON THE SIBLINGS. rf2-hic-086 (Todo-class), rf2-hic-078 (two public-package witness apps) and rf2-hic-074 (pagination + runtime content) all name paths under implementation/hicasso/examples/. THE SAME RULING APPLIES: place the app where an existing gate compiles it, do not add :source-paths entries for a new tree, and if you believe your case genuinely differs, STOP and report rather than editing shadow-cljs.edn.

VERIFY BEFORE PLACING: confirm at source which paths the lanes actually arm on, rather than trusting this note. The gate boundary is the thing that decides, and it moves.

AND ONE THING THE SLICE PROVED THE HARD WAY: route PATHS are process-global strings, and the node bundle loads a dozen apps into one process. The slice claimed / and /article/:slug and broke twelve RealWorld assertions with nothing warning. NAMESPACE EVERY ROUTE PATH YOUR APP REGISTERS. That hazard is filed as rf2-wqnl for a proper ruling; until it lands, namespacing is not optional.
MAYOR — RE-WORD THE ROUTE NOTE, DO NOT DROP IT (2026-08-12, from rf2-wqnl's worker, PR #7938).

This bead carries an earlier note saying "namespace every route path UNTIL rf2-wqnl lands". That framing is now wrong in a way that matters: NAMESPACING IS THE PERMANENT, ENFORCED RULE, not a temporary workaround.

rf2-wqnl was ruled option (a), narrowly scoped: the process-global registry is CORRECT, and the guard belongs where the hazard lives rather than in the framework. What landed is a repo-side census — implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_path_census_test.clj — that reads every column-1 (namespace-load-time) reg-route form under examples/ and testbeds/, canonicalises each path through the framework's own match/canonical-route-pattern, and FAILS when two distinct ids share one pattern, naming every claimant with file and line.

SO: if your app claims a bare top-level path, THE CENSUS REDS YOUR PR BY NAME. The convention is written down in TESTING.md under Test authoring policy. Read it there rather than from this note.

THE ALLOWLIST IS NOT A PLACE TO ADD YOURSELF. It has exactly two entries, both inherited: "/" (six ids) and "/articles" (two), the second labelled "inherited, not blessed" and named as the first to retire. Neither is a fidelity claim. Adding a new entry is not the remedy for a collision — prefixing your paths is.

ONE GATE-COVERAGE FACT worth knowing, since it decides where you will see a failure: the census is a JVM test. CI's always-on jvm-routing job runs it, but THE LOCAL FAST-PR SPINE SKIPS IT on a diff that does not touch implementation/routing. So an example-only diff can pass locally and red in CI. Run `cd implementation/routing && clojure -M:test` yourself before opening a PR that registers routes.

Otherwise this bead is UNBLOCKED — the placement ruling and the route rule are both settled, and nothing here waits on rf2-wqnl any longer.

# hic-081 — Spike: capability receipts

**Phase**: 5 · **Wave**: F · **Est.**: S (timeboxed ≤2 h) · **Depends**: hic-023
**Surface**: spike branch + report; nothing retained without graduation

## Goal
The §11 spike: mechanical attempt facts per boundary (self time, body runs, read calls, unique reads, cache hits, codec node counts) as a diagnostic receipt — attempts distinguished from commits, raw values omitted.

## Deliverables

- The kill rule applied: stop if instrumentation changes hot-view rankings or requires production retention.

notes:
SPIKE VERDICT (rf2-hic-081, timebox respected — ~2 h, no overrun). Branch worker/receipts-hic081, three commits, pushed. NO PR: nothing here graduates as code, and the spike's own surface line says so.

VERDICT: SPLIT. The COUNTS receipt GRADUATES as a design; the SELF-TIME field is KILLED. The ranking-perturbation check is REFUSED on two named controls and the kill is carried by arithmetic and by the repo's own committed measurements instead.

=== 1. THE DESIGN FINDING, WHICH IS THE SPIKE'S REAL PRODUCT ===

Five of the six named fields need NO TAP ON ANY HOT LOOP. They are derivable post hoc, at the end of an attempt, from state the runtime already retains for its own reasons:

  - READ CALLS   = the length of the scratch array. `read-key!` already pushes every call, duplicates included.
  - UNIQUE READS = that array's distinct count.
  - CACHE HITS   = for each scratch key, whether `!cells` holds a cell with a live reaction — and THAT ANSWER IS STABLE ACROSS THE ATTEMPT, because `cold-read!` retains nothing and the generation fence guarantees a pass observes one commit. Recomputing at the end is the same answer each read got, not an approximation. This is the load-bearing step and it is what removes the per-read counter.
  - CODEC NODES  = a walk of the element the attempt returned, taken AFTER the element is in hand.
  - ATTEMPTS     = counted at the tap itself.

So the receipt costs ONE tap, in `run-once`, per ATTEMPT — the same cost class as the `bodyRuns` increment already sitting there, and three orders of magnitude below a per-read or per-node tap. Attempts are ~10^3 per interaction; codec nodes are ~10^5.

ATTEMPTS vs COMMITS is satisfied by keeping them on two seams rather than by a flag on one record: the receipt counts attempts (so a fence re-run is two and a `React.memo` bail-out is none); the existing evidence sink's `:commit` event already counts commits. No new commit tap.

=== 2. WHAT WAS MEASURED ===

(a) THE RECEIPT PROJECTS, on two boundaries with deliberately opposite mechanical profiles (implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs):

  {:view "spike/deep", :attempts 1, :read-calls 4, :unique-reads 3, :cache-hits 0, :codec-nodes 2}
  {:view "spike/wide", :attempts 2, :read-calls 2, :unique-reads 1, :cache-hits 0, :codec-nodes 22}

  read-calls 4 vs unique-reads 3 is a repeated read separating the two fields. codec-nodes 22 = 2 attempts x 11 nodes (ul + 5 li + 5 strings). The two rows are the diagnostic claim demonstrated: read-heavy/node-light told apart from node-heavy/read-light, with no clock involved.

  CACHE HITS ANSWER BOTH WAYS — a second row commits the read set first and reads 4 of 4 hits, so the field is not stuck at zero.

  GATE: `node scripts/compile-node-test.cjs node-test-hicasso` then the bundle — 530 tests / 2465 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors. 524 pre-existing tests unmoved by the tap.

(b) ATTACHED-ONLY ALLOCATION — PROVEN, negatively controlled. Detached, twenty renders attach nothing and leave no table (`(nil? (receipt/rows))`); after `detach!` a further render re-attaches nothing. The guard's deref is the outermost form at the tap, so nothing a receipt would be handed is built when nobody is receipting — the same discipline, and the same falsifiability argument, as `impl/evidence`'s sink.

(c) PRODUCTION ERASURE — MEASURED, AND IT FAILED FIRST. This is the finding worth keeping.

  The first cut put the versioned envelope in `impl/receipt`, which therefore required `re-frame.hicasso.evidence`. `npm run build:hicasso-release` FAILED:

      hicasso production erasure: FAIL
        DEV SURFACE LEAKED: evidence projection — the versioned envelope (rf2-hic-023)
          sentinel: "re-frame.hicasso.evidence"

  `re-frame.hicasso.evidence` is dev-only BY REACHABILITY — nothing under `src/` requires it. A collector tap is reachable from the public door by construction, so ANYTHING THE TAP'S NAMESPACE REQUIRES BECOMES REACHABLE TOO, and the schema pin landed in the `:advanced` bundle.

  THE RULE THIS ESTABLISHES, and it governs any future runtime-tapped evidence, not just this one: raw counters live where the tap is; the ENVELOPE lives in a dev-only consumer that is not reachable from the public door (`re-frame.hicasso.tool`). After that split the same gate reads:

      OK: no dev-only Hicasso surface in the :advanced / goog.DEBUG=false bundle
          (5 sentinels absent, 3 positive controls present).

  So "production erasure unchanged" is PROVEN, by an existing gate, with the receipt in the tree — and the route by which it would have broken is now on the record.

=== 3. THE KILL: SELF TIME ===

Self time is the ONE field that cannot be derived, because time is not retained, and it is therefore the only field that puts an instrument inside the body. It fails on the bead's own kill rule — "stop if instrumentation changes hot-view rankings" — on two independent grounds:

  (i) RESOLUTION. Chrome clamps `performance.now()` to 100 us; this repo states it in a dozen places and MEASURES it per run (`hd8_rows/clock-resolution!`, rf2-d2tzk, which exists precisely because the constant was being quoted rather than read). The quantity is single-digit microseconds: the frozen clock standard's own numbers are 6.8–12.6 us of marginal cost PER CELL, against a whole tared floor page of ~4.5 ms. A per-attempt interval of ~5 us on a 100 us grain reads 0 or 100 us — Bernoulli(p≈0.05) x 100 us. The mean survives; the variance does not. Relative standard error over n attempts is sqrt((1-p)/(n·p)) ≈ sqrt(19/n), so 10% needs ~1,900 attempts PER BOUNDARY. A diagnostic receipt read after a few interactions does not have that, and a ranking built on it is ordering noise.

  (ii) THE OBSERVER EFFECT SCALES WITH THE WRONG VARIABLE. Two clock reads per attempt add a fixed cost c to every attempt, so a boundary's inflation is n_i·c — proportional to ATTEMPT COUNT, not to true cost. Two boundaries close in true self time and different in attempt count invert. That is the ranking perturbation the kill rule names, by construction rather than by bad luck.

  A COROLLARY WORTH RECORDING SEPARATELY, because it kills the per-node tap the naive design would have used: `as-element` was costed in this repo at 8.9 ns/child (`walk_vs_reagent_app` candidate table, 1,908 children; 22.5 ns/child before rf2-2rtt6.63). An atom deref plus a nil test per node is a large fraction of 8.9 ns, and it lands PROPORTIONAL TO CHILD COUNT — the exact axis a hot-view ranking discriminates on. A tapped codec counter perturbs the ranking whether or not anyone times anything. The post-hoc element walk avoids this entirely and is why the design above takes it.

=== 4. THE RANKING-PERTURBATION CHECK: REFUSED, ON TWO NAMED CONTROLS ===

  (a) QUIET BOX. The frozen clock standard (`clock_check_standard.json`, id hicasso-clock/ctl-2x-level v4) carries quiet-box as a hard refusal and was calibrated on quiet-box ensembles. MEASURED at 2026-08-11 13:04:44 +10:00 with Get-Counter, 8 x 1 s samples, one measurement at a time:
        \Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time  — min 31.52, median 41.92, max 59.70
        \System\Processor Queue Length       — min 0, median 0, max 3
        24 logical cores.
      Queue length is 0 at the median, so cores were not generally starved; but it spikes to 3 and CPU sits at 42% median with five other workers live. That is not a quiet box, and the standard's own recalibrateOn list treats harness conditions as invalidating. Publishing a timing comparison taken here would retro-admit a run the standard refuses. REFUSED rather than widened.
      (Win32_Processor.LoadPercentage was not used: it is known on this machine to read 93% against a true 11%.)

  (b) NO CONTROL ARM EXISTS. Deeper than the noise, and it would refuse on a silent box too: the receipt's own clock would be THE ONLY per-boundary timing instrument in the tree. There is no independent per-view time source to rank against, so "does the instrument change the ranking?" has no comparator. The bench lane's TaskDuration clock is per-page, not per-boundary. You cannot A/B an instrument against itself; you can only bound its perturbation from its own resolution, which is what §3 does. Building a second per-boundary instrument mid-spike was refused — a rung added between runs makes the series two instruments, and it is its own bead if anyone wants it.

=== 5. WHAT WAS NOT CONCLUDED ===

  - NO BROWSER MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN. Every number above is from the Node lane or from the existing release gate. The tap's cost has NOT been measured on a real Chromium render path; the argument that one per-attempt deref is below the noise is inherited from the `bodyRuns` docstring's own reasoning, not re-measured here.
  - THE 100 us CLAMP WAS NOT RE-MEASURED IN THIS RUN. It is cited from this repo's stated-and-instrumented constant (`clock-resolution!`) rather than freshly taken; no committed dataset in `bench/hicasso/data/` carries a `:clock-resolution` record, so the citation is to the instrument, not to a stored reading. If the self-time question is ever reopened, take that reading first.
  - THE SLICE APP USED WAS A TWO-BOUNDARY WITNESS, not `consumer-app` and not the testbed. The receipt was not driven through a real mount/commit/notify cycle in a browser, so the ATTEMPTS-vs-COMMITS distinction is demonstrated by construction (the tap sits in `run-once`) rather than witnessed against React re-running a fence.
  - CACHE-HIT STABILITY IS ARGUED FROM THE FENCE, NOT WITNESSED ADVERSARIALLY. The claim that `!cells` cannot move inside one attempt rests on invariant 5 and on `cold-read!` retaining nothing. A sabotage witness (mutate a cell mid-body, assert the derived hit count still equals the live one) was not written. If the counts receipt is graduated, that witness is the first thing it owes.
  - NO ALLOCATION LADDER WAS RUN. "Attached-only" is proven by the negative control and by the guard's structure, NOT by a heap measurement. The existing B7/B8 ladders were not used.

=== 6. WHERE THIS BELONGS IF GRADUATED ===

  The implementation-governing conclusions are (1) the derive-post-hoc rule that makes the receipt tap-free, (2) the runtime-tap reachability rule from §2(c), and (3) the self-time kill. Their owning tracked record is `docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md` §11 (the row currently reads "Capability receipts | Spike | Mechanical attempt facts only; stop if instrumentation changes rankings or exposes values") and `lanes/left-field-ideas.md` §Capability receipts.

  BOTH FILES ARE HELD BY WORKER doctruth-dsnq RIGHT NOW, so this spike did NOT edit them — a second worker on one file is how two workers silently revert each other. The mayor should route the §11 row change and the left-field protocol paragraph to that worker or sequence a follow-up bead behind it. Suggested §11 row: "Capability receipts | Adopt (counts only) | Attempt facts derived post hoc from retained state, no hot-loop tap; SELF TIME REFUSED — 100 us clock grain against microsecond bodies, and the per-attempt overhead scales with attempt count, not cost".

  §2(c)'s reachability rule is general and arguably belongs beside the erasure gate's own documentation rather than in §11.
STRANDED SWEEP CORRECTION (2026-08-18 20:52 AUSEST). This bead's close reason states 'Spike commits are pushed on worker/receipts-hic081 and retained as the experiment's record'. That was FALSE at the time of writing and stayed false for seven days: git ls-remote --heads origin returned empty for the branch, while the local ref carried all three commits (fece72f80a, 418312d680, ae14841ab3). The experiment's record existed on ONE disk, in a checkout whose worktree had already been reaped.

Pushed now — origin/worker/receipts-hic081 = ae14841ab3. Nothing else changed; the bead stays closed and the SPLIT verdict stands.

THE GENERAL LESSON, not the specific fix: a close reason is a CLAIM about durability, not evidence of it. This one read as verified because it was specific and sat among clauses that genuinely were verified. The mayor's sweep should test any 'pushed' clause against the remote rather than the prose, and the test is one command.
close_reason:
SPIKE COMPLETE — VERDICT: SPLIT. The counts receipt graduates as a DESIGN; the self-time field is KILLED. No PR, correctly: this bead's own surface line says "nothing retained without graduation", and the spike graduated no code. Timebox respected. Worker reported FINISHED; worktree reaped on that report, junction removed first, mayor node_modules verified intact.

WHAT GRADUATES. Five of the six named fields need no tap on any hot loop — read calls, unique reads, cache hits, codec nodes and attempts are all derivable post hoc from state the runtime already retains. The load-bearing step is that the cache-hit answer is STABLE ACROSS AN ATTEMPT (cold-read! retains nothing; the generation fence guarantees a pass observes one commit), which is what deletes the per-read counter. Result: ONE TAP, IN run-once, PER ATTEMPT — same cost class as the bodyRuns increment already there.

WHAT WAS PROVEN, not asserted. The receipt projects on two boundaries with opposite profiles (530 tests / 2465 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors; the 524 pre-existing tests unmoved). Attached-only allocation proven AND negatively controlled. Production erasure measured — and it FAILED FIRST, which is the most valuable thing here: the envelope's :require made a dev-only namespace reachable from the public door. That rule is now rf2-nkr3.

WHAT IS KILLED, as a decision and not a deferral. Self time is the only underivable field and the only one putting an instrument inside the body. Chrome's 100us performance.now() clamp against a single-digit-microsecond quantity gives 0-or-100us readings; worse, the observer effect scales with ATTEMPT COUNT rather than true cost, so boundaries close in true time but different in attempt count invert. The kill rule this bead set was applied exactly as written.

THE RANKING-PERTURBATION CHECK REFUSED, on two named controls, and the refusal is a correct deliverable. (1) Not a quiet box: Processor Queue Length peaked at 3 on 24 cores, and the frozen clock standard carries quiet-box as a hard refusal. Refused rather than widened — widening a threshold to admit today's run retro-admits every failure it was built to catch. (2) NO CONTROL ARM EXISTS, and this one would refuse on a silent box too: the receipt's clock would be the only per-boundary timing instrument in the tree, and you cannot A/B an instrument against itself. Building a second one mid-spike was correctly refused as its own bead.

NOT CONCLUDED, recorded so nobody reads more into this than it says: no browser measurement at all — every number is Node-lane or the release gate; the tap's cost on a real Chromium render path is unmeasured. Cache-hit stability is ARGUED from invariant 5, not sabotage-witnessed — that witness is the first thing a graduated receipt owes, and it is carried in rf2-eoo9's acceptance. The slice app was a two-boundary witness, not consumer-app. No allocation ladder was run.

The §11 spike: can committed, redacted read edges and event windows predict useful coarse/fine/chunked topology choices?

## Deliverables
- Membership savings, set stability, and co-change frequency computed for the slice app's boundaries; blinded calibration: the advice compared against the hic-036 tournament's measured outcomes without seeing them first.
- The deciding rule applied: retain only if the blinded predictions are usefully right; otherwise keep a factual worksheet and stop.

## Acceptance
- Timebox respected; verdict + evidence recorded; no retained machinery without the graduate verdict.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")

Gates: foreground a gate that fits inside the harness ceiling; DETACH one that does not and poll BOTH its log and its `.exit` file in a bounded loop within the same turn — never end the turn waiting for a completion event. Never pipe a gate through `tail` or any filter; redirect to a log and echo the runner's own exit code on the same command line. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn. 5. Never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json` from a worker branch — they are whole-database EXPORTS, not database files, and your branch carries the snapshot taken when its worktree was created, so committing one TIME-TRAVELS the tracker: beads closed since reopen, beads filed since vanish (PR #6677 did exactly this, 135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). notes:
PHASE 2 DONE 2026-08-14 09:20 AUSEST. PR #8172, branch worker/blindscore-hic080. VERDICT: STOP — nothing retained; the §11 row stays at Spike, now closed at Spike rather than awaiting phase 2. No follow-up programme proposed.

FREEZE INTACT, CHECKED TWO WAYS. git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD reports 122 insertions / 0 DELETIONS on the prediction page — purely additive — and the frozen 225 lines byte-compare identical to origin/main. No prediction, confidence, scoring-rule clause or figure was amended. The tournament held its side too (§1.7, §2.8: it declines to score its own predictor), and it had pre-committed to THIS page's 'unaddressed' clause by name at its §1.4, before its own results existed. The two frozen vocabularies interlocked with neither side adjusting. That protocol success is the one unambiguous win, and it is a win for the method of freezing, not for the advice.

THE SCORES. Under the tournament's PRIMARY estimand (the clock): all six UNADDRESSED — the clock table does not exist, for two recorded reasons (the windowed arm's control refused on the band, and, larger, the 4x4 clock table was never instrumented at all). Under its one MEASURED ordering (the deterministic census, 48/48 cells): P1 RIGHT (control), P2 UNADDRESSED, P3 WRONG, P4 RIGHT (control), P5 RIGHT, P6 RIGHT. Deciding set P2/P3/P5/P6 = two right, one wrong, one unaddressed.

WHY THAT IS NOT 'USEFULLY RIGHT'. Neither right one emits advice: P5 is the negative claim the page itself designated 'the prediction most worth being wrong about' (the four operations are each pure and cannot show chunked at its best, so being right there is a fact about the tournament's operation set), and P6 is a stability claim. The ONE deciding prediction that names a direction between coarse and fine on a resolvable operation is P3, and it is wrong: on reorder, fine builds ZERO rows of markup for a table that visibly reorders while coarse rebuilds all B. The method's actual output — coarse, from an across-family co-change of 0.78 — is contradicted on every operation the tournament could resolve and unresolved on bulk, the one where it might have been vindicated. §3.3 had said in advance that the committed evidence could not choose between 0.78 (merge) and 0.33 (keep fine); every resolvable operation favours the 0.33 reading the method could not select. Both controls came out right, so the runtime model is NOT falsified and the three quantities stay believable — what failed is the inference from them to an arm.

P2 IS THE DISCIPLINED CALL AND WAS SCORED AGAINST INTEREST. On boundary-bodies the direction P2 named is visibly there (coarse 1 vs fine's B, gap growing 100/300/1000). Banking it would have made the deciding set three right of four. It is scored UNADDRESSED because the tournament declares bulk UNRESOLVED and routes it to rf2-hic-018 — taking the bodies counter as the ordering is exactly the census-for-clock substitution both pages refused in advance.

FOUR AMBIGUITIES IN THE FROZEN RULE — RECORDED, DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED. (1) It names no ESTIMAND: 'the tournament's measured ordering' was written when one was in prospect and two materialised, one of which never got instrumented. (2) It names no COUNTER: the census publishes rows-of-markup AND boundary-bodies, and they disagree in direction on bulk and in rank-stability on P6, with no tiebreak. (3) ROLL-UP to the retain/stop verdict is unstated — it scores cells, §11 wants a verdict, nothing connects them, so 'usefully right' stayed a post-outcome judgement. comments.text:
VERDICT: STOP, NOTHING RETAINED — and the worker's integrity in reaching it is the part worth recording (mayor, 2026-08-14).

THE SCORING. Under the tournament's PRIMARY estimand, the clock: all six predictions UNADDRESSED, because no clock cell exists for any arm, operation or row count. Under its one measured ordering, the deterministic census: two RIGHT, one WRONG, one UNADDRESSED, both controls RIGHT. Neither right one emits advice — P5 is a negative claim and P6 a stability claim. The single deciding prediction that names a coarse-versus-fine direction on a resolvable operation is P3, and it is WRONG: on reorder, fine builds ZERO rows where coarse builds B. The method's actual output, coarse from co-change 0.78, is contradicted everywhere the tournament could speak.

IT SCORED P2 AGAINST ITS OWN INTEREST, which is the thing to remember. On boundary-bodies P2's direction is plainly there, and banking it would have made the deciding set three-right-of-four — a materially better-looking result. It scored UNADDRESSED instead, because the tournament withholds the bulk ordering DELIBERATELY, and taking a counter as the ordering is exactly the census-for-clock substitution that both pages refused in advance. A worker willing to lose a point rather than blur an estimand is what makes the whole blinded exercise worth anything.

BOTH CONTROLS CAME OUT RIGHT, so the runtime model is not falsified. What failed is the inference from the quantities to an arm — a narrower and more useful conclusion than 'the predictor is bad'.

THE FROZEN RULE IS AMBIGUOUS IN FOUR PLACES, recorded and RESOLVED IN NONE: it names no estimand (the tournament grew two, one never instrumented); it names no counter (markup and bodies disagree on bulk direction and on P6's rank stability, with no tiebreak); it never connects per-cell scores to a retain-or-stop verdict, so 'usefully right' stayed a post-outcome judgement; and P5 names two arms with a slash, under which reading it would be WRONG. The page's own gloss settles that last one, but by luck. Leaving all four unresolved after the outcomes were visible is correct — resolving them now would be indistinguishable from tuning.

FREEZE INTEGRITY PROVEN, not asserted: 122 insertions and ZERO deletions, with the frozen 225 lines byte-comparing identical to origin/main.

THE PROTOCOL SUCCEEDED EVEN THOUGH THE METHOD FAILED. The tournament pre-committed to THIS page's 'unaddressed' clause by name, before its own results existed, and declined to score its own predictor. Two frozen vocabularies interlocked with neither side adjusting. That is the reusable result here, and it is worth more than a graduated advisor would have been.

## Worker notes
Read spec §13 (controlled grid bullet); §4.2.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")

WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.

3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.

notes:
MAYOR RULING — WHERE AN EXAMPLE APP LIVES, 2026-08-11. Decided on rf2-hic-025 and binding on every sibling witness app.

THE QUESTION. rf2-hic-025's bead named the surface implementation/hicasso/examples/slice/. Its worker found that path is on NO :source-paths entry, so a tree there is COMPILED BY NOTHING. It placed the slice at implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/slice/ instead — beside consumer-app, where both cljs_node_test and cljs_browser arm on implementation/hicasso/** — and asked before touching implementation/shadow-cljs.edn.

RULING: THE PLACEMENT STANDS. The bead's literal path was the error. Do NOT add the two :source-paths lines and do NOT git mv it.

WHY. Today this repository spent two beads and two merged PRs (rf2-bl0j, rf2-cfqk) closing exactly one defect: namespaces that NO PR GATE COMPILES. The enumeration found 23 of them, and the fix for the last 19 was RED ON ARRIVAL — five infer-warnings in a rostered arm whose functions had been un-typed since they were written, because nothing had ever compiled them. Creating a fresh uncovered tree hours after closing that hole would be perverse. An artefact belongs where a gate already reaches it; a path is not worth a coverage gap.

The worker's own reasoning was sound and it asked rather than guessing, which is exactly right for a hot-zone file. Asking cost one round-trip; guessing would have cost a silent coverage hole.

BINDING ON THE SIBLINGS. rf2-hic-086 (Todo-class), rf2-hic-078 (two public-package witness apps) and rf2-hic-074 (pagination + runtime content) all name paths under implementation/hicasso/examples/. THE SAME RULING APPLIES: place the app where an existing gate compiles it, do not add :source-paths entries for a new tree, and if you believe your case genuinely differs, STOP and report rather than editing shadow-cljs.edn.

VERIFY BEFORE PLACING: confirm at source which paths the lanes actually arm on, rather than trusting this note. The gate boundary is the thing that decides, and it moves.

AND ONE THING THE SLICE PROVED THE HARD WAY: route PATHS are process-global strings, and the node bundle loads a dozen apps into one process. The slice claimed / and /article/:slug and broke twelve RealWorld assertions with nothing warning. NAMESPACE EVERY ROUTE PATH YOUR APP REGISTERS. That hazard is filed as rf2-wqnl for a proper ruling; until it lands, namespacing is not optional.
MAYOR — RE-WORD THE ROUTE NOTE, DO NOT DROP IT (2026-08-12, from rf2-wqnl's worker, PR #7938).

This bead carries an earlier note saying "namespace every route path UNTIL rf2-wqnl lands". That framing is now wrong in a way that matters: NAMESPACING IS THE PERMANENT, ENFORCED RULE, not a temporary workaround.

rf2-wqnl was ruled option (a), narrowly scoped: the process-global registry is CORRECT, and the guard belongs where the hazard lives rather than in the framework. What landed is a repo-side census — implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_path_census_test.clj — that reads every column-1 (namespace-load-time) reg-route form under examples/ and testbeds/, canonicalises each path through the framework's own match/canonical-route-pattern, and FAILS when two distinct ids share one pattern, naming every claimant with file and line.

SO: if your app claims a bare top-level path, THE CENSUS REDS YOUR PR BY NAME. The convention is written down in TESTING.md under Test authoring policy. Read it there rather than from this note.

THE ALLOWLIST IS NOT A PLACE TO ADD YOURSELF. It has exactly two entries, both inherited: "/" (six ids) and "/articles" (two), the second labelled "inherited, not blessed" and named as the first to retire. Neither is a fidelity claim. Adding a new entry is not the remedy for a collision — prefixing your paths is.

ONE GATE-COVERAGE FACT worth knowing, since it decides where you will see a failure: the census is a JVM test. CI's always-on jvm-routing job runs it, but THE LOCAL FAST-PR SPINE SKIPS IT on a diff that does not touch implementation/routing. So an example-only diff can pass locally and red in CI. Run `cd implementation/routing && clojure -M:test` yourself before opening a PR that registers routes.

Otherwise this bead is UNBLOCKED — the placement ruling and the route rule are both settled, and nothing here waits on rf2-wqnl any longer.
