title: hic-034 — Three-way parity + bundle isolation: the native tier's adoption evidence
description:
# hic-034 — Three-way parity + bundle isolation: the native tier's adoption evidence

**Phase**: 3 · **Wave**: E · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-032, hic-033, hic-035
**Surface**: parity test suites + bundle-analysis gate (new files)

## Goal
The ruling's adoption gates, proven: Hicasso-native against **both** handwritten React and UIx — the convenience layer cannot define its own floor — plus the zero-rent proof for interpreted-only bundles.

## Deliverables
- Matched element/component triples (Hicasso-native / handwritten React / UIx) proven equivalent across: DOM output, keys, refs, SVG and custom elements, dynamic props, children shapes, component identity, React server bytes, hydration, cleanup, and same-frame reads — each witness naming the equality it proves.
- Island performance: the same component through each route within the §6 island band (5% / 1 ms), co-instrumented in one pinned run.
- **Bundle isolation**: an interpreted-only application's production bundle contains zero native-surface runtime and zero UIx — unique-sentinel proof with reachable positive control (hic-024 pattern).
- The native-language-leakage sabotage matrix: nested hiccup in native children, native callbacks receiving intent vectors, dynamic heads/props, controlled fields inside native subtrees — every ambiguous mix refuses with source.

## Acceptance
- Full three-route matrix green; **a red island-band row blocks native-tier graduation** — the row is fixed or the surface shrinks; publication of the miss is required but is not a pass; bundle gate green with sabotage demonstrated.

## Worker notes
Read synth.md Part II adoption gates; `codex/hot-path-architecture.md` decisive experiments (native construction parity); `codex/adversarial-risks.md` native rows (all three).

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
Until rf2-hic-000 merges these paths do not exist; rf2-hic-000 runs first. References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates run foreground, to completion — never backgrounded, never piped through tail. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/*` database files from a worker branch.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn, .github/workflows/*) only if this bead flags them.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues; record their ids in the correction ledger (rf2-hic-073).
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7962 (correctness/implementation quality): the parity mechanisms are strong, but the node-suite namespace contract contradicts its own tests in two places. First, it headlines native and handwritten React as having the SAME props object, while the component-identity row correctly states and proves that React.createElement copies every config into a fresh props object and therefore compares only the key set; narrow the headline to same element type and same prop-slot shape. Second, lines 48-52 say refs, cleanup, and hydration are all decided by `three_way_parity_dom_cljs_test`, while that sibling explicitly says hydration is absent and owned by rf2-hic-046. Correct the routing statement; do not duplicate or pull hydration out of rf2-hic-046. These are bounded source-contract corrections on this exact parity owner, not a new test programme.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED by the mayor 2026-08-12 (same revert wave). LANDED AS PR #7962. Three-way parity plus a falsifiable bundle-isolation gate. Spec section 6's second sentence is why there are three arms: react/createElement is the only arm with no convenience in it, so it decides; UIx is there so the comparison cannot be gamed by matching a floor UIx itself sets. PREMISE ASSERTIONS CAUGHT THREE WRONG CLAIMS IN ITS OWN FIRST DRAFT, the load-bearing one being that [:>] and undeclared defhost are :client-only, so THE SERVER GATE WITHHELD THE UIx ARM — TWO ARMS AGREED WHILE THE FILE CLAIMED THREE. check_bundle_isolation.cjs is falsifiable both ways: tier made reachable -> exit 1 naming both sentinels WHILE THE PRODUCTION-ERASURE GATE STAYED GREEN IN THE SAME RUN (so it catches what the old gate does not); a handwritten React component through BOTH inward doors -> exit 0. It also REFUSED a row rather than writing a false one: 'zero UIx' is false and cannot be made true by this fixture, since Hicasso ships no reactive adapter and the exemplar's own requires put uix.core in the bundle. Carried as a positive control instead. Filed rf2-5rqn.

title: hicasso: reportability()'s control annotation still says a control failure is 'the reason no magnitude is published'
description: Residual of the same supersession chain, left by rf2-vr1hl, 2026-08-08.
notes:
FILED BY rf2-vr1hl, 2026-08-08, as a residual it declined to take under its own fence
("this changes a printed string and its pins"; "do NOT over-engineer").

WHAT REMAINS. clock_run.cjs's reportability() annotates a regime row's control
status with a conditional suffix:

  const predictedFailure = !r.ctlOk && !g.statementNeedsControl;
  `[clock]     positive control: ${r.ctlOk ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}${r.ctlNote || ''}` +
    (predictedFailure ? ' — expected, and the reason no magnitude is published' : '')

TWO CLAIMS IN THAT SUFFIX ARE rf2-jcm3p's AND BOTH ARE RETIRED.
  "expected" — rf2-8a746 established ctl-2x was never failing (controlVerdict
  tests per-block band membership, not the mean), so no live ruling predicts a
  control failure on this row.
  "the reason no magnitude is published" — that is THE FAILING CONTROL IS THE
  PUBLISHED REASON, the one sentence rf2-owiis named dead. Under rf2-diaud the
  reason this driver publishes no magnitude is that the published magnitude is
  an ENSEMBLE estimate through a run-preserving bootstrap whose outer unit is
  the run, and one run cannot form the interval.

So after rf2-vr1hl the mount regime's own three strings cite rf2-diaud and this
suffix, printed two lines below them, still cites rf2-jcm3p's dead premise.

WHY rf2-vr1hl DID NOT TAKE IT, stated so the judgement is reviewable rather than
assumed. It is not a roster string: it lives in reportability(), the decision
function, and it is generic over regime rows rather than owned by mount-regime.
rf2-vr1hl's bead named REGIMES['mount-regime'].bead and .publishes; it moved
.why as well, because .why is the second printed line of the same statement and
leaving it would have put the dead premise directly under a corrected bracket.
This suffix is one surface further out, and touching the decision function was
outside the bead's stated fence.

IT DOES NOT FIRE ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS. It needs ctlOk === false on a regime
row, and under the mount class rf2-x7x10 calibrated at v2 all 14 committed mount
row-runs come back IN CONTROL. It fires in the fixtures, which set ctlOk:false
deliberately (to pin that the mount regime does NOT wait on its control — that
independence survives both rulings and is the case's real subject).

THE PINS, so whoever takes it knows it is a coordinated change of the same shape:
  clock_exit_path.test.cjs  :2349 (in 'the M1 refusal now states a REGIME rather
                                   than a control that went wrong')
  clock_run.cjs             reportabilitySelfTest, 'the mount regime STATES
                            itself although its control failed'
Both match /positive control: FAIL.*expected, and the reason no magnitude is
published/. Print and pins move together or the suite goes red on a true string.

SHAPE OF THE FIX. The suffix should say what is true of a regime row whose
control failed: the regime states itself regardless of that control, so the
control's status is not what withholds a magnitude. It must NOT be deleted — the
annotation exists because the ruling that made these rows regimes is ABOUT their
controls and a reader must not have to infer one from the other (the comment
above it says so). Annotate-never-erase, in #7705's idiom, which rf2-vr1hl
matched.

FENCE, inherited: this is a printed string and its pins. Nothing computed,
adjudicated or published. publishesMagnitude stays false — the ensemble reason,
not rf2-jcm3p's.
MAYOR SEQUENCING 2026-08-08 21:56 AUSEST — HELD behind rf2-vr1hl's PR, then dispatches. Same file, live worker.

THIS IS THE THIRD LINK IN ONE CHAIN, and the chain is worth naming because it is converging rather than regressing. rf2-owiis swept clock_run.cjs's PROSE and filed rf2-vr1hl for the PRINTED line it could not take without the test file another worker held. rf2-vr1hl is taking the printed line and its pins, and filed THIS for an annotation outside its own fence ("this changes a printed string and its pins"). Each worker took exactly what it could take cleanly and filed the rest rather than reaching. That produced three small correct PRs instead of one sprawling conflicted one.

IT CONVERGES BECAUSE THE SURFACE SHRINKS EACH TIME: prose (many sites) -> one printed line and three pins -> one conditional suffix in one function. This is the last of it that I can see; if the worker finds a fourth, it should file it the same way, but it should also say plainly whether the chain is still shrinking. A residual chain that stops shrinking is scope creep wearing good manners.

THE DEFECT, and both halves are rf2-jcm3p's: reportability() annotates a regime row's control status with " — expected, and the reason no magnitude is published" when !r.ctlOk && !g.statementNeedsControl. "EXPECTED" is retired by rf2-8a746, which established ctl-2x was never failing — controlVerdict tests per-block band membership rather than the mean, so no live ruling predicts a control failure on this row. "THE REASON NO MAGNITUDE IS PUBLISHED" is retired by rf2-diaud: a magnitude IS published on M1 now, and where one is withheld the reason is the ensemble bootstrap's outer unit, not a control failure.

FENCE, and it is the same one that has held three times: annotate, never erase; change no computed value, no threshold, no verdict; do not touch publishesMagnitude, which stays false for rf2-diaud's ensemble reason. If the worker finds itself editing anything that adjudicates, it has the wrong bead. And read any figure from the published record (rows-re-adjudicated-on-the-corrected-clock.md section 4.3), never from this bead — a figure with two homes has two futures.
close_reason:
Re-cited in PR #7709 (branch worker/ctlnote-ejb9h, commit 64a644a6c9), the third and last link of rf2-owiis -> rf2-vr1hl -> rf2-ejb9h, built on merged #7708.

THE SUFFIX. Before: ' — expected, and the reason no magnitude is published'. After: ' — the regime does not wait on this control, so a failure here withholds nothing; what the row publishes and why are the two lines above'. Both retired claims were rf2-jcm3p's and both are gone; what replaces them is the one part of its account both later rulings leave standing, and the real subject of the fixture's ctlOk:false. Annotated never erased: every superseded string is preserved verbatim in a 'SUPERSEDED (rf2-ejb9h, 2026-08-08), was: ...' comment beside its replacement, in #7705's idiom that #7708 matched.

THE 'ALL 14 IN CONTROL' PREMISE WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. clock_readjudicate.cjs over both committed ensembles (clock-emvod n=8, clock-w3yxd n=6) reports IN CTRL on every run and ZERO OUT OF CTRL. So the suffix does NOT fire on the committed corpus — it is reachable only from fixtures, which is precisely why it was corrected rather than left.

NOTHING COMPUTED OR ADJUDICATED CHANGED. publishesMagnitude, statementNeedsControl, ROW_REGIME, bead, publishes and why are untouched (proved by diffing the extracted field lines against the merge base); no threshold, estimand, verdict or exit code moved. publishesMagnitude REMAINS false, for rf2-diaud's ensemble reason and not rf2-jcm3p's. Excluding comments the driver's whole diff is three things: the local predictedFailure renamed statedDespiteFailure with the expression BYTE-IDENTICAL, the suffix, and the driver's own --selftest regex. No figure is quoted anywhere; the published row is cited by path only and no doc was touched.

ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF, recorded so it is reviewable. The rename was not in the bead's named surface. It was taken for rf2-vr1hl's reason for moving .why alongside .publishes: a local asserting a PREDICTION beside a string that denies one is the same lie one surface in. The expression is unchanged.

RED-THEN-GREEN, counts established locally. Baseline on the merge base 355 passed exit 0. New suffix with OLD pins: 2/355 FAILED exit 1, --selftest FAILURES:1. Both moved: 358 passed exit 0, ALL ADJUDICATORS OK. Reverse mutation (retired suffix restored against new pins): 3/358 FAILED exit 1. A THIRD mutation printing BOTH sentences on one line: 2/358 FAILED exit 1 — and the positive-only pin at :2360 PASSES there, which is exactly what earns the two-sided negative assertions. Restored from HEAD: 358 passed exit 0. The +3 cases are the two-sided annotation case plus two fencing the conditional (a PASSED control is not annotated; a regime WITHHELD by its control is not annotated twice).

GATES all exit 0, gate root C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/ctlnote-ejb9h: node --check x2; clock_run.cjs --selftest ALL ADJUDICATORS OK; clock_exit_path.test.cjs 358 passed; npm run test:script-helpers; scripts/test-fast-pr.sh PASS fast PR spine; npm run lint:js from repo root; check-beads-pr-boundary.sh origin/main (no beads-database paths).

NO FOURTH RESIDUAL IN CODE, and THE CHAIN IS STILL SHRINKING — prose across many sites -> one printed line and three pins -> one conditional suffix and one pin -> nothing. Every remaining rf2-jcm3p mention in clock_run.cjs is either the MECHANISM (a regime declared on the row rather than inferred from the numbers, which stands) or is explicitly annotated as superseded; a git grep for the retired sentences across tracked files returns only this PR's own SUPERSEDED comments and negative assertions. The known doc-half residual (validation.md citing rf2-t2flm where rf2-diaud is in force) is already tracked as rf2-sza0w and is a ruling question, not a sweep. The chain terminates here.

TAKEN NO MEASUREMENT. No window consumed. No dataset read or written.

title: hicasso: clock_run.cjs's REGIME line still PRINTS rf2-jcm3p and DIRECTION ONLY — pinned by clock_exit_path.test.cjs
description: Residual left by rf2-owiis, 2026-08-08 20:11 AUSEST.
notes:
FILED BY rf2-owiis, 2026-08-08 20:11 AUSEST, as the half of the sweep it could not take alone.

WHAT rf2-owiis DID. It swept clock_run.cjs's PROSE — the REGIMES roster doc block,
the two inline comments above the decision gates, and the self-test's regime
section — so the SOURCE no longer states rf2-jcm3p's regime-only position as
current. rf2-jcm3p's reasoning is preserved verbatim and marked superseded, with
rf2-8a746 (the ground: ctl-2x was never failing) and rf2-t2flm/rf2-diaud (the
position: M1 publishes a magnitude, K1 MISSED DECISIVELY) named beside it.
Nothing computed or printed changed.

WHAT IT COULD NOT TAKE. The driver's LOG still reads

  [clock]   M1 [mount-regime, rf2-jcm3p] STATED — DIRECTION ONLY — hicasso mounts
            materially slower than both adapters; no magnitude

because both halves of that sentence are pinned in clock_exit_path.test.cjs:

  :2347  assert.match(all, /M1 \[mount-regime, rf2-jcm3p\] STATED/)
  :2348  assert.match(all, /DIRECTION ONLY/)
  :2386  the same bracket again, on the not-withheld case

and clock_run.cjs's own reportabilitySelfTest carries the matching regex at :2651.
Re-citing the log is therefore a COORDINATED change across the driver and that
test file, and worker/bulkgate-vp0j7 held clock_exit_path.test.cjs while rf2-owiis
ran. Two hands on one test file is the collision the sequencing rule exists to
prevent, so it was filed rather than forced.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, when it dispatches. REGIMES['mount-regime'].bead and
.publishes are the two fields; the printed bracket should name the ruling in
force (rf2-diaud) with rf2-jcm3p retained as the superseded citation rather than
dropped — annotate-never-erase applies to a log line as much as to a figure — and
the three pins above move with it in the same PR.

ONE JUDGEMENT THE FIX HAS TO MAKE, and rf2-owiis deliberately did not make it:
publishesMagnitude:false is still CORRECT on this driver for a reason that is not
rf2-jcm3p's. The published M1 magnitude is an ENSEMBLE estimate — a
floor-normalised leg ratio through a run-preserving bootstrap whose OUTER unit is
the run, over 8 and 6 runs — so no single run of clock_run.cjs can form the
interval it would be adjudicated against. The regime should keep refusing; what
should change is the sentence it refuses with. A fix that reads the supersession
as licence to flip publishesMagnitude would let a one-run capture announce a
figure the programme publishes only across an ensemble.

SEQUENCE AFTER worker/bulkgate-vp0j7's PR merges.
MAYOR SEQUENCING 2026-08-08 20:18 AUSEST — HELD BEHIND worker/bulkgate-vp0j7's PR, then dispatches immediately.

WHY IT IS HELD, and it is not a judgement about the work. The change this bead needs is to what the driver PRINTS, and that line is pinned by clock_exit_path.test.cjs — the file rf2-vp0j7/rf2-vh0e3's live worker is editing right now to add its three gated-pair pins. Two hands on that file is the collision the sequencing rule exists to prevent, and it is the exact collision that cost rf2-diaud a rebase and a force-push earlier this evening.

THE SPLIT rf2-owiis MADE WAS CORRECT and worth recording as the pattern. It took the half it could take cleanly — the REGIMES roster doc block, the two inline comments above the decision gates, and the self-test's regime section — so the SOURCE no longer states the superseded position as current, with rf2-jcm3p's reasoning preserved verbatim and rf2-8a746 (the ground: ctl-2x was never failing) and rf2-t2flm/rf2-diaud (the position: M1 publishes a magnitude, K1 MISSED DECISIVELY) named beside it. Then it FILED the half that needed a file it did not own, rather than reaching across. That is the behaviour the worktree discipline is for, and it produced a clean two-PR shape instead of one conflicted one.

WHAT REMAINS, precisely: the driver's log still emits "[clock]   M1 [mount-regime, rf2-jcm3p] STATED — DIRECTION ONLY — hicasso mounts materially slower than both adapters; no magnitude", and clock_exit_path.test.cjs pins that string. Both move together or neither does — changing the print without the pin reds the suite, changing the pin without the print pins a lie.

WHAT THE LINE SHOULD SAY is now settled by published record rather than by anyone's preference: M1 publishes a magnitude, floor-normalised, K1 MISSED DECISIVELY at 1.1718x [1.1263-1.2190] n=8 (clock-emvod) and 1.1976x [1.1504-1.2468] n=6 (clock-w3yxd), landed in PR #7704. THE WORKER MUST READ THOSE FROM THE PUBLISHED RECORD ON MAIN, not from this note — if what it finds differs, the record wins and it reports the discrepancy. Quoting figures out of a bead into a driver is how the splice this whole ruling chain retired gets reintroduced.

FENCE: this changes a printed string and its pin. It does not change what is computed, adjudicated or published. If the worker finds itself editing a threshold, an estimand or a verdict, it has the wrong bead.

title: The bulk publication rule adjudicates all three pairs, but validation.md's bulk bar names only hicasso / reagent-subs
description:
Raised by rf2-diaud's publication repair, 2026-08-08. NOT a defect found by that ruling and deliberately NOT changed by it: criterion (b) says 'bulk's path unchanged', and it was left byte-identical.

WHAT IS ASYMMETRIC. rf2-diaud made the publication rule's ESTIMAND and THRESHOLD row-class-specific. On the MOUNT class the rule is also PAIR-specific, because validation.md states K1's gate against DIRECT UIx-on-subs and says in terms that Reagent-on-subs is 'co-instrumented and reported beside the mount row, not gating it'. Without that, the mount rule would have printed 'MOUNT SHIP BAR MET' on the uix-subs / reagent-subs pair, whose interval [0.9179 - 1.0228] sits under 1.10x and which answers no question K1 asks.

THE SAME QUESTION IS OPEN ON BULK and was not touched. validation.md's bulk ship bar is '<= 1.0x Reagent-on-subs, like-for-like' — i.e. the hicasso / reagent-subs pair. The implemented rule adjudicates all three pairs of a bulk row against 1.0/1.5, so hicasso / uix-subs and uix-subs / reagent-subs are being held to a bar stated for a different comparison. It has published nothing wrong to date only because every bulk pair of the committed 42-run corpus returns INSTRUMENT-LIMITED.

WHAT TO DECIDE: whether bulk's rule gains 'gatedPairs' the way mount's has (the field exists and is set to null on bulk with a comment naming this bead), or whether the bulk bar is intended to apply to all three pairs. Either way is a one-line change in clock_readjudicate.cjs's PUBLICATION table plus a test.

Related: rf2-diaud (the ruling), rf2-8a746 (the rule), validation.md 'The bar (HD-012)'.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-08-08 18:10 AUSEST (delegated, operator-overturnable): BULK GAINS gatedPairs, NAMING hicasso / reagent-subs ONLY. This is consistency propagation of rf2-diaud's ruling, not a new policy.

VERIFIED IN SOURCE BEFORE RULING, rather than reasoned from the bead's summary. validation.md:17 states the bulk ship bar as "<= 1.0x Reagent-on-subs, LIKE-FOR-LIKE — both sides reading re-frame2 subscriptions", which names one pair. And :15-16 state the mount side in the same shape: Reagent-on-subs is "co-instrumented and REPORTED BESIDE THE MOUNT ROW, NOT GATING IT". The two bars are written identically — each names the comparison it gates and says nothing about the others.

SO THE ASYMMETRY IS AN OVERSIGHT OF SCOPE, NOT A DESIGN. rf2-diaud made the mount rule pair-specific for exactly this reason, and the bead records what that prevented: without it the rule would have printed "MOUNT SHIP BAR MET" on the uix-subs / reagent-subs pair, whose interval [0.9179 - 1.0228] sits under 1.10x and which answers no question K1 asks. Leaving bulk adjudicating all three pairs holds hicasso / uix-subs and uix-subs / reagent-subs to a bar stated for a different comparison — the same error, one row down.

WHY IT HAS COST NOTHING SO FAR, and why that is not a reason to leave it: every bulk pair of the committed 42-run corpus returns INSTRUMENT-LIMITED, so no wrong verdict has been published. That is luck about the data, not a property of the rule. The moment a bulk pair becomes resolvable, an ungated pair could print a ship verdict against a bar that was never written for it.

THE RULING: implement gatedPairs on bulk as ["hicasso / reagent-subs"], mirroring mount. The field already exists and is set to null on bulk with a comment naming this bead, so the change is the one line the bead describes plus a test pinning that a non-gated bulk pair reports its interval WITHOUT a ship/kill verdict. Do not delete the non-gated pairs' output — they stay reported, as validation.md's "co-instrumented and reported beside" language requires for mount; the change is that they stop being adjudicated.

WHY I RULED THIS RATHER THAN REFERRING IT: the operator already decided the principle on rf2-diaud part (1) — thresholds belong to the question a row answers. Applying it to the sibling row is the same species as the 2026-08-05 amendment that was itself recorded as "consistency propagation of a ruling already carried by validation.md, not a new one". title: census clock rig still carries the retired all-blocks strict rule (rf2-8a746 did not reach it)
description:
SCOPE BOUNDARY RECORDED BY rf2-8a746's IMPLEMENTATION, not a defect found by measuring.

rf2-8a746 retired, everywhere on the HICASSO CLOCK instrument, both the three-point
difference-of-differences control and the all-18-blocks strict run-rejection rule. The
grep for the ^18 semantics that the ruling asked for also lands on
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/shapes/census_clock_run.cjs:277 —
controlVerdict with rule 'strict — EVERY block inside the band'.

IT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, and the reason is the ruling's own. The census rig is a
DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT: a different driver, different rows and witnesses, its own datasets
under data/censusclock-*, and a control whose prediction comes from the row's own element
arithmetic (ctlPredicted, P times the cards) rather than from a page doubling. rf2-8a746's
frozen check standard is seeded from clock_run.cjs's ctl-2x/floor run medians on a
300-boundary page — centre 1.7207x, limits [1.5509, 1.8905], dispersion 0.568 — and
applying those limits to a rig measuring a different quantity would re-commit the exact
mis-specification the ruling retires: asserting a value that was never measured on the
instrument being judged.

WHAT IS INHERITED IS THE ARITHMETIC, NOT THE NUMBERS. p^n on a per-block pass rate below 1
is a property of the rule and not of the clock. If the census rig's per-block in-band rate
is p over n blocks, its per-run false-refusal is 1 - p^n whatever it is measuring; on the
hicasso clock that was 90.5% empirical at n=18. Whether it bites here is a measurement over
the committed censusclock-* datasets, and it needs no window.

THE WORK. (1) Compute the census rig's per-block in-band fraction and per-run pass rate over
its committed datasets, exactly as rf2-8a746 did for the clock — analysis over retained data,
NO NEW MEASUREMENT. (2) If the rule is refusing at a rate a run cannot survive, calibrate a
check standard for THAT rig, from ITS OWN baseline, versioned as data in the idiom of
clock_check_standard.json. (3) If it is not, record the measured rate on this bead and close
it: a rule with a defensible false-refusal rate is not a defect, and rf2-8a746 rejects
retiring a control merely because it shares a shape with one that failed.

Related: rf2-8a746 (the ruling and the hicasso-clock implementation), rf2-t2flm (the mount
half, concurrent).

MEASURED and RETAINED. The census rig's all-blocks strict run-rejection rule refuses at 18.2% (large-template) and 39.8% (feed) per run at n=18, against the 90.5% that retired the clock's, and the empirical rates (8 of 10, 7 of 10) agree with p^n per row. The rig's control is already level-denominated — 4.20/4.65 sigma from zero against ctl3's 2.09 — so it does not inherit the clock's ill-conditioning, and rf2-8a746 rejects retiring a control merely because it shares a shape with one that failed. The clock's frozen limits were NOT imported and no check standard was calibrated: the bead's condition for one (a rate a run cannot survive) is not met.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-08 14:35 AUSEST from committed data only. NO MEASUREMENT TAKEN — no census driver, no clock driver, no quiet box consumed. Arithmetic over the committed data/censusclock-* datasets.

THE ANSWER: the all-blocks strict run-rejection rule is RETAINED on this rig, on measured grounds. Outcome (3) of the bead's three.

THE CORPUS. Thirty row-runs — five sessions at five commits (censusclock-2rtt6-56 @7885a7c148, -y1jkm @8ccd9f4b41, -6c237 @ac09504d74, -cno31 @08344cb500 on 2026-08-02; -jv36i @752b8069be on 2026-08-07) x two adapter runs x three rows — 540 blocks, all at design 6 rounds x 3 blocks x (4 warmup + 10 samples) and controlSlack 0.25. n = 18 BLOCKS PER ROW-RUN.

THE RATE, PER ROW (p = per-block in-band fraction, 180 blocks and 10 row-runs each):

  row              p                   1 - p^18   runs passed   exact binomial two-sided p
  large-template   178/180 = 98.9%       18.2%      8 of 10      1.000
  feed             175/180 = 97.2%       39.8%      7 of 10      0.749
  ordinary          56/180 = 31.1%      100.0%      0 of 10      1.000

THEY AGREE, PER ROW. Pooled they do NOT — pooled p is 409/540 = 75.7%, which predicts 99.3% per-run refusal against 15 of 30 observed — and that disagreement is a fact about pooling a mis-centred row with two well-centred ones, not about the rule. Per-row is the honest statistic; the pooled figure is recorded here so nobody re-derives it and reads it as evidence.

WHY IT IS NOT THE CLOCK'S RULE. 18-40% is a rate a run survives; the clock's was 90.5% empirical at the same n, and its premise-meeting ctl3Layout passed 4 of 42. The census rig does not inherit that ill-conditioning because ITS CONTROL IS ALREADY LEVEL-DENOMINATED — the class rf2-8a746's ruling endorses. Tared floor 10.72 / 41.00 ms with between-block SD 2.55 / 8.82, i.e. 4.20 / 4.65 sigma from zero, against the retired ctl3 denominator's 2.09. Block IQR is 7.7% of the centre on both rows. Centres sit 24.9% and 35.4% above the band's lower edge, against ctl3's 4%.

THE CLOCK'S LIMITS WERE NOT IMPORTED, for the reason the bead gives: this rig's prediction is each row's own element arithmetic (1.9759 / 1.9943 / 1.7255), and asserting the clock's 1.7207x centre here would re-commit the mis-specification being retired.

RECOMPUTATION VALIDATED. The per-block statistic recomputed through the driver's own arithmetic reproduces every stored adjudication.ctl.perBlock and every stored ok across all 30 row-runs exactly. The only divergence is band edges, by exactly one unit in the last stored place (1e-4), because datasetFor writes r4(ctlPredicted) while the run adjudicated on the page's raw value; counting was therefore done on the STORED band, which is the band the runs experienced.

THE ONE FINDING, AND IT IS NOT THE RULE. The ordinary row refuses 10 of 10 on its CENTRE: block median 1.2264x against a predicted 1.7255x — 71.1% of P, and 5.2% BELOW the band's lower edge of 1.2941. Relaxing the run rule does not reach it (allowing 1, 2 or 3 out-of-band blocks still passes 0 of 10). Because verdict()'s ctlFailed condition is RUN-WIDE, that also means no full-shape census run can be canonical: driven on the real exported functions, a run with large-template and feed clean and ordinary's control failed returns exit 5 and destination() routes every dataset to .unpublished. FILED AS rf2-pzqy8 (P2) with both candidate directions; the choice is a ruling, not an implementation, and nothing here acts on it.

DELIVERED IN PR #7699 (branch worker/censusrule-y0pkh), which changes no behaviour, no threshold and no gate: the measured rates and the retention are stated above controlVerdict where the ^18 grep lands, the label now reads 'strict — EVERY block inside the band (rf2-y0pkh: measured and retained)' so the next grep does not re-file this bead, controlBlocks is lifted out of report and exported so the witness drives the real arithmetic, and six new cases in clock_exit_path.test.cjs recompute every figure above from the committed datasets (273 -> 279 passed). Mutation-proved: widening CONTROL_SLACK to 0.40 reds it, dropping the cite reds it, a wrong stated rate reds it, and claiming the ordinary centre is in band reds it.

title: chore: pin .beads/issues.jsonl to eol=lf so the tracker export stops churning every tick
description:
FOUND by the mayor 2026-08-08 while diagnosing a rebase abort. It is the same defect class the rf2-rguy1 worker fixed for the retained jsfb evidence in PR #7694, on the file the whole beads-durability section of CLAUDE.md is about.

THE MECHANISM. This box runs core.autocrlf=true and `.beads/issues.jsonl` is NOT pinned in .gitattributes. Every `bd export` writes LF; git rewrites the working copy to CRLF; git then reports the file MODIFIED against HEAD forever, even when the export is byte-identical in content. Confirmed today: `sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh` reported "nothing to checkpoint (3296 rows, unchanged)" while `git status` simultaneously showed ` M .beads/issues.jsonl`, with zero divergence from origin (rev-list 0/0). Every bd invocation also emits "warning: in the working copy of '.beads/issues.jsonl', LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it".

WHY IT IS WORTH A LINE OF CONFIG RATHER THAN LIVING WITH IT. A perpetually-dirty tracker file is precisely the state CLAUDE.md documents as aborting `git pull` ("local changes would be overwritten"), which silently freezes HEAD at a stale base. The mayor loop currently pays for this every single tick with a `git reset -q HEAD -- .beads` plus a `git checkout -- .beads` before it can pull — dozens of times per session — and that dance is itself hazardous, because a checkout of this file within a tick of a `bd close` reverts the close (CLAUDE.md's own warning, and it cost real closes here on 2026-08-07).

THE FIX, one line:

  .beads/issues.jsonl text eol=lf

plus, in the same change, a round-trip proof rather than an assumption: delete the file, `git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl`, confirm `git status` is clean and the file carries zero CR bytes. Copying and comparing is not sufficient — that tests the copy, not the checkout.

notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-08 12:20 AUSEST — I OVERSTATED THIS BEAD'S JUSTIFICATION WHEN I FILED IT, and the worker's own evidence is what exposed it. Recording the correction rather than letting the description stand as written.

WHAT I CLAIMED: that the missing pin left .beads/issues.jsonl PERPETUALLY DIRTY, that this is the state CLAUDE.md documents as aborting `git pull` and freezing HEAD, and that the mayor loop was paying a reset+checkout every tick because of it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, verified just now on the mayor checkout: a plain `bd ready --limit 0` read leaves `git status .beads` CLEAN. The dirtiness I kept observing came from bd WRITES — every bead update, close and create rewrites the export with genuinely changed content. That is expected and correct behaviour, not churn, and it is not what the pin addresses. The worker found the same thing from the other direction and said so plainly: git's clean filter HIDES a CRLF working copy from `git status`, so `status` was clean before and after the pin in its worktree.

SO THE PIN DOES NOT FIX A DIRTY-FILE PROBLEM, because there was not one.

WHAT THE PIN IS ACTUALLY WORTH, stated honestly and smaller than my filing implied:
- The checked-out file genuinely IS CRLF where bd writes LF — measured, not assumed: 3,297 CRs before, 0 after, with the byte delta 14,236,505 - 14,233,208 = 3,297 corroborating exactly.
- It removes the "LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it" warning that bd emits on every invocation. Real noise, small cost.
- It protects any future byte-wise use of the file (hashing, digest citation, byte comparison) from the platform-dependent-digest trap that PR #7694 had to fix for the retained jsfb evidence.
- It makes this file consistent with the seven other eol=lf groups already in .gitattributes, every one of them added for the same core.autocrlf=true reason.

VERDICT: the change is correct, harmless and consistent with established practice in the file it edits, so it merges. But it is a TIDINESS-AND-FUTURE-PROOFING pin, not the papercut-with-teeth I described. Anyone reading this bead later should not cite it as evidence that a pull-abort was fixed here, because no pull-abort was.

THE LESSON FOR ME, and it is the same one three other beads have taught this session: I filed from a plausible mechanism rather than a tested one. `git status` before and after a bd read is a five-second check and I did not run it until after the work was done.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7696 (completeness, correctness, implementation quality): REOPENED exact owner for the landed rationale, not the LF pin. The attribute itself is correct: git check-attr reports text:set/eol:lf and the current 1,882-row export has 0 CR bytes. But the committed .gitattributes comment still says the unpinned export was perpetually dirty, aborted pulls, and forced a checkout that could revert closes. This Bead's own 2026-08-08 mayor correction establishes that premise was false: Git's clean filter kept the CRLF working copy clean, and bd writes dirtied it only when content genuinely changed. Keep the one-line pin; replace the stale comment with the accurate benefits already adjudicated here — suppress the LF-to-CRLF warning, make checked-out bytes platform-stable for byte-wise tools, and align with the repository's other LF pins. No mechanism or framework.

title: hicasso: foldDecomposition accepts truncated evidence — dimensions and roster unchecked against the row's own shape
description:
STRANDED BY THE rf2-jo60g CLOSE, 2026-08-08. Filed by the worker that took the strike route on rf2-jo60g (PR #7692) so the finding keeps an owner. The 10:32 ruling settled the DOC half and says the code half is done; the MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #7681, recorded on rf2-jo60g and sitting directly above that ruling, says one code gap remains and named rf2-jo60g as its exact owner. Closing rf2-jo60g on the doc half leaves it without one. The mayor should reject this outright if the ruling was meant to retire the finding too — it is filed to be adjudicated, not assumed.

THE FINDING, quoted from the audit. PR #7681 repaired the SCALAR and INNER-SHAPE defect: foldDecomposition no longer defaults a missing, null or NaN metric to zero, requires nonempty rounds and blocks, and requires the first block's arm roster as a set in every block. But it still anchors completeness to THE FIRST SURVIVING BLOCK rather than to the row's authoritative shape. A live probe against censusclock-jv36i/uix.json (declared 6 rounds x 3 blocks; row armIds includes uix) showed foldDecomposition ACCEPT all three of:

  1. the final round removed;
  2. one block removed from round 2;
  3. uix removed from EVERY block.

Each is partial or truncated evidence, and each still returns plausible aggregates. Case 3 is the sharp one: a roster check that compares every block against the first block cannot see an arm that is missing from all of them, so the whole point of the roster check is bypassed by uniform loss.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS AFTER THE STRIKE ROUTE. The strike route settled what the CENSUS STUDIO PAGE may claim; it did not change what the fold will accept the next time a canonical census run is taken. rf2-jo60g's own close records that the split becomes recomputable on that run — this is the check standing between that run and a plausible-looking ratio folded from truncated evidence. The defect class is the one rf2-jo60g existed to close.

REMEDY, and it is bounded. Check the expected round and block DIMENSIONS and the blocksDecomp roster against the ROW'S OWN armIds at the real report/driver boundary, rather than against the first surviving block. No schema layer and no validation framework — the audit is explicit that this needs neither, and rf2-jo60g's history is a record of that restraint being the right call twice.

ACCEPTANCE: non-zero driver outcome, wrote===false and destination().canonical===false witnesses for all three cases above, in the same hermetic style as the merged 246-case suite. The audit confirms that suite, both syntax checks and diff-check all PASS today, so the gap is UNWITNESSED rather than a general breakage — expect to add witnesses, not to repair a red.

title: hicasso: the allocation preflight licenses a window below ALLOC_MIN_WRITES (audit residual of PR #7688)
description:
The bounded correctness residual the merged-PR audit of #7688 recorded on
rf2-2rtt6.138. CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT on origin/main at 42cf8db7da by
rf2-2rtt6.138's measurement window (2026-08-08), by reading p0_run.cjs.

ALLOC_MIN_WRITES = 6 is used ONLY to derive the default page (ALLOC_CELLS).
allocArmSizing().admissible is:

    admissible: writes >= 1 && boundaries >= 1 && headroom >= 0

so the preflight licenses precisely the low-averaging shape the bead and the
PR rule out. The audit reproduced two routes without launching Chromium:
P0_ROOTS=50 derives {cells:1, boundaries:50, writes:2, admissible:true}, and
an explicit P0_ALLOC_WRITES=1 on the shipped page derives {boundaries:24,
writes:1, admissible:true}. Either can proceed through every publication gate
even though a one-write window has no averaging in it -- and a one-write
window is exactly the configuration whose four fits came back at r2
0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31.

MINIMAL COMPLETION, as the audit stated it: make the allocation-row preflight
refuse ALLOC_ARM.writes < ALLOC_MIN_WRITES (including a large-root default
that cannot fit six) and name shrinking P0_ALLOC_CELLS / P0_ROOTS as the
repair; do NOT advise shrinking the window below the floor. Pin both
reproduced routes plus the shipped six-write green control in
p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs. No generic env-schema layer, no new estimator,
no threshold change, no benchmark run.

PRIORITY NOTE, added by the measurement window rather than by the audit: this
is now LOWER value than it looked when filed. rf2-2rtt6.140 measured that no
page of one boundary or more certifies the R=20 rung at six writes at all, so
the six-write floor may not survive as the right constraint. Sequence this
AFTER rf2-2rtt6.139 and rf2-2rtt6.140 are ruled on, or it will be re-done.

Touches p0_run.cjs, which rf2-2rtt6.139/.140 also touch -- sequence, do not
parallelise.
notes:

WHY PROCEEDING WAS RIGHT. The note guards against ONE risk: rework when the floor moves. The worker structured the change so that risk does not arise — the enforcement is written against ALLOC_MIN_WRITES and never against the literal 6, so a ruling that moves the floor moves the preflight and its tests with it, with no edit. That is not an override of the note; it is the correct answer to it. And the defect itself is value-independent: a preflight that licenses precisely the shape its own row rules out is wrong at any floor value. A floor that adjudicates nothing is not a floor.

MY BRIEF WAS AT FAULT, not the worker. I did not carry that priority note into the dispatch, because I briefed from an earlier reading of the bead rather than re-reading its newest notes at dispatch time. That is the third time in this session a worker has caught my brief stale or incomplete — a wrong test count, a wrong integer bound, and now this. (1) IT PINNED THREE CASES, NOT TWO. My brief asked for the two admitting routes; the bead asked additionally for the shipped six-write green control. The control is what stops the gate being vacuous — two refusal cases alone would pass a preflight that refuses everything.

(2) IT MADE admissible A REFUSALS LIST RATHER THAN A LONGER CONJUNCTION, because the refusal text has to BRANCH. A page still carrying six writes has nothing wrong with its page — the repair there is to RAISE P0_ALLOC_WRITES. A page that cannot carry six gets the page repair and has no window count named at all, because naming what such a page admits is naming a below-floor window. One undifferentiated boolean would have printed the mask-budget prose at a floor refusal and sent the operator to configure the very shape being refused. That is a real ergonomic call and the right one.

The bead and the dispatch brief both said "a p0_arms.cljs / p0_heap.cljs question"; in fact the event handler and the sub graph are in p0_fixture.cljc, with p0_arms.cljs supplying only the public door and p0_heap.cljs the window. title: jsfb comparator: the unverified-writes line sums absence to zero and prints a clean gate
description:
FOUND by the rf2-110be worker while closing the WORKLOAD bypass (PR #7687). It deliberately did NOT file this itself, to keep tracker mutations out of a worker worktree, and recorded it in the PR body and close reason instead. Verified live at HEAD by the mayor before filing.

THE FAULT. jsfb_compare.cjs:350 folds the per-benchmark unverified counts with

  const unv = Object.values(ours.summary).reduce((a, s) => a + (s && s.unverified ? s.unverified : 0), 0);

then prints it at :351 as the run's unverified-writes gate. A summary entry that carries NO `unverified` field at all contributes 0 — indistinguishable from one that carries `unverified: 0` and genuinely verified every write. So a JSON produced by a rig that never recorded the field, or by a version that dropped it, prints a clean `unverified 0` and the reader believes a gate ran.

THIS FAILS OPEN, which is what makes it the genuine sibling of the bug rf2-110be just closed, and the reason it is worth fixing rather than noting. The absence of evidence is being rendered as evidence of absence, in the one line a reader consults to decide whether the writes were verified.

CONTRAST — the neighbouring site at :347 has the same shape and is NOT a defect:

  ours.parity && ours.parity.identical ? 'IDENTICAL' : 'DIFFERENT'

A missing `parity` object prints DIFFERENT, i.e. it fails CLOSED. Leave it alone; it is the safe direction and changing it for symmetry would be gold-plating.

THE FIX, and keep it bounded to this one line: require the field rather than defaulting it. A summary entry lacking `unverified` should make the line REFUSE and name which benchmark lacked it, in the same idiom the file already uses for its other refusals — not print a number. Do NOT grow a schema validator, do NOT touch the expected-cell roster (EXPECTED_CELLS stays derived from PAIRS), do NOT touch the exit codes or the parity gate. A refusal must stay a refusal.

PROVE IT in jsfb_compare_exit_path.test.cjs (42 cases as of PR #7687, every fixture built in-test under mkdtemp): add the absent-field case and show it red before the change, green after. NOTE FOR THE BRIEF: that suite does NOT carry line-ending handling despite an earlier bead claiming it does — the rf2-110be worker checked and corrected that. If both endings matter, verify them out of tree as it did.

DO NOT RUN THE BENCHMARK. Every decision here is reachable as a pure function through the module's require.main guard.

  ;;   unverified        UNSTATED — no `unverified` count under run1k, so no total is derived

comma-separated, in PAIRS order. Nothing else in the close reason was affected;
PR #7690 carries the same text unmangled in its body.

WHAT WAS REPORTED. The worker found that a NEGATIVE unverified count cancels a positive one in the same fold: -5 against +5 still totals 0. It correctly declined to fix it, on the grounds that this is present-but-wrong evidence (rf2-110be's class) rather than absent evidence (this bead's), and that adding the guard would turn "require the field" into "validate the field", which this bead's fence forbids. That judgement was right and the restraint is exactly what the fence is for.

RULED: NO BEAD. `unverified` is a COUNTER of writes that failed verification, incremented by the rig. It cannot go negative unless the rig itself is broken, and a rig broken in that way trips other gates first — the run's own refusal paths, the parity gate, and now the UNSTATED refusal this bead just landed. So the scenario the guard defends against is not reachable by any evidence a working rig can produce, and the conjunct would be a diagnostic that can only ever fire on data no run can emit.

The session's fail-open theme is real and has been worth chasing — the ladder aggregator, the census write path, the ctl3 sign gate, the WORKLOAD bypass and this bead were all cases where a gate reported on evidence it never had. title: jsfb_ours_run.cjs does not gate positive taskNet measurements
description:

A bad value recorded at the producer still lands in a committed dataset, still gets read by anything that is not the comparator, and still has to be explained later. Refusing at the point of measurement is cheaper than refusing at the point of comparison.

SCOPE, and keep it this tight: the positivity predicate at the recording site only. Do NOT touch the parity gate, the exit codes, the arm roster, or the pinned benchmark revision. A refusal must stay a refusal — if the change would turn a currently-refusing run into a passing one, that is scope exceeded, stop and report.

PROVE IT the way 110be did: it gave a MONOTONICITY PROOF rather than a test — the predicate gained conjuncts and lost none, and positive(x) implies isFinite(x), so the new condition implies the old one, the measured set can only shrink, and the exit code can only move 0 -> 1 or stay. If the same argument holds here, state it; it is stronger than any fixture.

DO NOT RUN THE BENCHMARK. This is a rig change and the rig must stay stable across any series being compared — the same reason tranche 3 left 110be undone mid-window.

title: MEASURED: the three-point control refuses every bulk run on a quiet box (24 of 24)
description:
rf2-emvod's quiet-window ensemble (8 full-roster runs at c172f22bb0, datasets under implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-emvod/) found rf2-7iqb5's three-point control refusing on EVERY bulk run: bulk300 0/8, bulk100 0/8, narrow 0/8, against a predicted 2.0101x. The box was genuinely quiet - Processor Queue Length 0 before and after, CPU 9-18%.

TWO DISTINGUISHABLE SHAPES, and they are not the same fault:

1. bulk300 sits LOW AND TIGHT: 1.3516 - 1.7838x, mean 1.6045x. That is the same
   direction and roughly the same size as ctl-2x's undershoot on the identical
   samples (mean 1.7880x against 2.00x). A control built to difference the
   additive constant away should not inherit the constant's signature. This does
   not look like box noise.

2. bulk100 and narrow each carry ONE run whose blocks go degenerate: the
   statistic ranges to 86.05x on bulk100 run 7 and to 113.87x on narrow run 7,
   with negative blocks on both. The control's own sign gate caught these, which
   is the gate working; but a per-run rate of 1-in-8 degenerate is itself a
   finding about the estimator's stability at these block sizes.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no tolerance widened, no gate touched, no third
estimator added. The window was granted for a measurement and the refusal is the
result. Diagnosing it needs a new arm in the page half, which would have changed
the blobs this ensemble was taken at.

The datasets are retained and canonical, so this is re-adjudicable without
re-running the box:
  node freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/clock_readjudicate.cjs     freehand/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/data/clock-emvod/run*.json

rf2-5xrcd owns the control's calibration. Related: rf2-7iqb5 (the repair),
rf2-emvod, rf2-yd52q.
notes:
ELEVATED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07 — this is now the central open question of the programme, not a follow-up.

THE EVIDENCE IS NO LONGER ONE ENSEMBLE. rf2-emvod's window refused 0 of 24 bulk-class runs; rf2-w3yxd's independent census-rig window refused 18 of 18. That is 42 RUNS, NO PASS, across two independent quiet-box ensembles, both with the arm-order guard clean throughout (30 of 30 row-runs in w3yxd, 0 unverified of 42,336) and box counters showing Processor Queue Length 0 before and after.

WHY IT OUTRANKS THE REMAINING MEASUREMENT QUEUE. Six window beads remain at roughly an hour each. If the three-point control cannot adjudicate on a verified quiet box, every bulk row it gates inherits the refusal however carefully it is taken — four more tranches would produce four more correctly-refused rows. Measuring harder cannot repair an instrument that refuses. So this is sequenced BEFORE any further measurement.

IT NEEDS NO WINDOW. Both ensembles are on main (data/clock-emvod/run1-8.json and data/clock-w3yxd/*). This is analysis over committed data, not a re-take, and it must not consume the operator's quiet box.

THE TWO ENSEMBLES DISAGREE ABOUT THE SHAPE OF THE FAILURE, which is itself a clue rather than noise — rf2-5xrcd recorded that. emvod saw bulk300 low and tight (1.35-1.78, the same signature as ctl-2x's undershoot on identical samples) plus one degenerate run each on bulk100 (statistic to 86x) and narrow (to 114x) with negative blocks caught by the sign gate. Whatever explains the refusal has to explain both shapes.

ONE ROW DOES PASS AND THAT CONSTRAINS THE ANSWER: M1's ctl-2x passed 4 of 8 in emvod and 3 of 6 in w3yxd. So the control is not uniformly broken — it discriminates by row class. An explanation that predicts total failure is wrong.
MAYOR CORRECTION 2026-08-07 — my elevation note above contained TWO factual errors, both corrected by the diagnosis, and both were steers I handed the worker as constraints. Recording them so nobody inherits them.

ERROR 1. I wrote: 'M1's ctl-2x passed 4 of 8 and 3 of 6, so the control discriminates by row class; an explanation that predicts total failure is wrong.' FALSE. clock-app/ctl3-arms says the three-point arms 'exist on BULK ROWS ONLY' and arms-for appends them only for :bulk. M1 NEVER RUNS THIS CONTROL. What passes on M1 is ctl-2x — a different statistic. So the three-point control's failure IS TOTAL, 0 of 42, and an explanation predicting total failure is the CORRECT one. I inverted the key constraint and the worker had to overturn it to reach the answer.

ERROR 2. I wrote 'both ensembles are on main'. At the time only clock-emvod was; clock-w3yxd was in open PR #7671 and the worker read it via git show refs/remotes/pr/7671. (7671 has since merged, so the statement is true now but was not when I made it.)

THE REAL DISCRIMINATOR IS THE DENOMINATOR CLASS, NOT THE ROW CLASS. ctl-2x survives because its denominator is a LEVEL — the floor's whole tared reading, ~4.5 ms — carrying the same ~0.4 ms of estimator error, so 9% relative against ctl3's 48%; and its centre sits 20% above the 1.50 edge against ctl3's 4%. Those two numbers, distance-above-edge and per-block scatter, raised to the 18th, reproduce every pass rate in the programme.

AND THE TWO ENSEMBLES NEVER DISAGREED. At block level they agree within 2% on every structural quantity. The apparent disagreement was band().mean over 18 ratios whose denominator sits 2 sigma from zero: 2.5% of blocks have |den| < 0.2 ms, and one such block moves a headline from ~1.6 to 86x. Same rate in both ensembles, all three rows. rf2-5xrcd's premise dissolves; rf2-8bgqq now owns the summary-statistic half.
CROSS-REFERENCE FROM rf2-rguy1 (PR #7673), quiet-box tranche 3 — evidence that
the 42-of-42 refusal is about the CONSTRUCTION, not about bulk operations.

The jsfb harness is an outside workload adjudicated by a DIRECT RATIO against
rf2-reagent, not a difference-of-differences. Re-ran it 2026-08-07 on a quiet box
against the same bundles as the 2026-08-02 published run. On that instrument the
BULK ROWS ARE THE BEST-BEHAVED ROWS IN THE MATRIX, not the worst.

Run-to-run drift, published vs re-take, same box, same bundles:
  replace1k  (BULK)    hicasso +1.7%   uix -2.4%
  swaprows   (BULK)    hicasso +17.0%  uix +7.8%
  run1k      (mount)   hicasso +11.5%  uix +1.5%
  update10th (NARROW)  hicasso -6.3%   uix +32.9%
  clear1k              hicasso +4.3%   uix -1.3%
  create10k  (control) hicasso -1.0%   uix +4.0%

Cross-instrument agreement inside the re-take (ours vs the benchmark's own
driver): "replace all" agrees on BOTH arms (11.9%, 14.3%) and "swap rows" agrees
on BOTH (0.8%, 4.4%); the mount row disagrees on both (21.3%, 24.6%) and the
narrow row disagrees on the donor (21.3%).

So the two bulk rows are simultaneously the most reproducible across two runs of
our instrument AND the most agreed-upon between two independent instruments,
while the NARROW row is the least reproducible of all — the opposite of the
ordering the three-point construction implies.

BOUNDED HONESTLY: one app with trivial state, swaprows drifted 17% on one arm,
and two runs are not an ensemble. This does NOT establish that our bulk rows are
fine. It establishes that a bulk row on this workload is measurable to a couple
of percent by an instrument taking a direct ratio — so the 42-of-42 refusal is
evidence about the difference-of-differences denominator rather than about bulk
operations being inherently unmeasurable. Whether that carries to the census
witnesses is a separate question and is NOT claimed.

Also relevant: the jsfb positive control itself proved non-reproducible across
the two runs (an arm's pass/fail verdict flipped, 12.883x vs a published 13.583x
against an 8-13x band), so control instability is not unique to the three-point
construction either.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7698 (2026-08-09) — REOPENED, NOT DUPLICATED. The calibrated check standard correctly retires the per-block unanimity rule, but the new consumer also accepts incomplete evidence. `checkStandard` validates only a non-empty finite ratio list; a one-element list at the frozen centre returns `ok: true` with `n: 1` and `robustScale: 0`. `checkStandardFor` checks that `roundsTask` is non-empty but never compares its length with `dataset.design.rounds` or the frozen standard provenance. On the committed six-round clock-emvod corpus, truncating a row to one round leaves three segment blocks and several rows still pass the standard. This confuses retiring all-blocks-in-band with allowing blocks to be absent.

Bounded acceptance: enforce the frozen standard's expected evidence cardinality at the consumer boundary (18 blocks for v1, or an explicit expected-blocks field tied to the declared six-round/three-segment design) and reject any missing or extra round/block before computing location or dispersion. Give the direct helper an expected-N contract or keep it private behind that checked boundary. Add a truncated-round/block witness that reaches the nonzero/no-pool decision. Preserve the new location/dispersion rules and do not add a schema framework.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7700 (2026-08-09) — UPDATED EXISTING OPEN OWNER, NOT DUPLICATED. Calibrating mount makes all 14 M1 runs eligible, but the effect-interval consumer can silently select a smaller subset than the runs that cleared every gate. `ivRuns = passIdx.map(pairedLogRatios).filter(Boolean)` drops a reportable run whose raw pair readings are absent or unusable, and `effectInterval` independently filters unusable members. The output calls those 7 “reportable run(s)”, concealing that evidence was lost after eligibility was decided.

Bounded acceptance: a reportable run with unusable raw readings for the named pair must refuse that pair/run (with file and pair named) or suppress the entire interval; it must never be filtered into a new unstated subset. Require `ivRuns.length === passIdx.length` and expected per-run round cardinality before pooling, and make `effectInterval` reject rather than filter an invalid member. Add a mutation witness reaching the program's nonzero/no-pool path. This is the same raw-evidence completeness boundary already reopened on rf2-8a746 by audit #7698, so it stays on that owner; preserve the calibrated limits and estimator/publication rulings.

One worker, one PR, both fixes: enforce expected evidence cardinality at the consumer boundary (18 blocks v1 / explicit expected-blocks tied to the declared 6-round x 3-segment design; reject missing/extra with observed/expected); a reportable run with unusable raw pair readings REFUSES that pair/run by name or suppresses the whole interval — never a silent subset; require ivRuns.length === passIdx.length and per-run round cardinality before pooling; effectInterval rejects rather than filters; add truncation witnesses reaching the nonzero/no-pool path; no schema framework. ALL FOUR PARTS of the 2026-08-07 ruling, the fences, and the frozen protocol remain untouched. Bench-tree caution: a file in the rf2-hic-001 freeze manifest stops the worker (surface, do not edit). comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
DIAGNOSED 2026-08-07 18:08 AUSEST from committed data only. NO RUN TAKEN, no quiet box consumed, no gate/tolerance/band/instrument touched. Read data/clock-emvod/run1-8.json on main (3b2ee34754) and data/clock-w3yxd/run1-6.json out of PR #7671's head via git show (nothing on that branch modified). Working notes: ai/findings/2026-08-07.three-point-control-refusal-diagnosed.md.

THE MECHANISM, TWO INDEPENDENTLY FATAL HALVES.

(1) THE PREDICTION IS MIS-DERIVED FOR THE POINTS CHOSEN. (d2-d0)/(d1-d0)=2.0101 is the expectation only if T is affine in d over [1,200]. On the published TaskDuration clock it is not: marginal cost 12.64 -> 6.84 us/cell over [1,100] / [100,200] (emvod), 13.11 -> 7.51 (w3yxd). True centre 1.546 / 1.578 against a band lower edge of 1.5076 -- THE CONTROL'S OWN EXPECTATION SITS 2.6% ABOVE THE VALUE AT WHICH IT REFUSES. Blocks below band 192 of 432 and 135 of 324; above band 35 and 33. That 5.5:1 asymmetry IS the bias as a count.

THE INTERNAL CONTROL THAT PROVES IT: ctl3Layout, the same statistic on LayoutDuration over the IDENTICAL blocks and samples, reads 1.9681 / 1.9801 with marginals 5.42 -> 5.13 and 5.78 -> 5.49 us/cell (affine to 5%), and its sign gate never fired once in 756 blocks. So the arithmetic, the door, the tare and the aggregation are all sound; the PAGE is not affine on the counter the row is published on. The non-layout half carries it: 7.13 -> 1.83 us/cell, a 3.9x collapse, reproduced at 7.36 -> 1.92 on the second ensemble. Until now the paint-saturation account was inherited from a retired witness arm (clock_run.cjs:464-477 records wArm is null on every shipped run); it is now re-measured on both ensembles.

(2) THE ESTIMATOR IS ILL-CONDITIONED, AND THIS ALONE WOULD REFUSE. den = T(100)-T(1) is 1.249 ms carrying 0.599 ms of dispersion -- 2.09 sigma from zero (1.85 on w3yxd). Differencing away the constant also throws away the pedestal that made the relative noise look small: each arm's p50 over 10 samples carries ~0.4-0.9 ms of its OWN estimator error, which is INDEPENDENT between arms and therefore ADDS under differencing. Measured corr(T(1),T(100)) = 0.432 / 0.396, so differencing removes 40% of the denominator's variance where the invariance argument implicitly assumes it removes nearly all (sd(den) 0.599 measured, 0.772 if independent, 0.216 if perfectly common-mode). The construction's claim that an additive constant "cancels in each difference, whatever its size" is TRUE OF THE LEVEL and is not the problem; what destroys the control is the error in each arm's ESTIMATE of that level.

THE FALSIFIABLE CONSEQUENCE, CHECKED ON COMMITTED DATA. On a bulk row the floor arm rewrites all 300 cells of the same page through the same door, so every block already carries a fourth point at d=300. Marginals across all three intervals: 12.64 / 6.84 / 8.27 (emvod), 13.11 / 7.51 / 8.82 (w3yxd) -- [100,200] and [200,300] agree with each other and only [1,100] differs, so THE KNEE IS BELOW d=100 AND THE eps ARM STRADDLES IT. Re-adjudicating the same blocks at 100/200/300 (prediction 2.0000) gives a median statistic of 1.9975 / 2.0777: the premise HOLDS above the knee. AND IT STILL DOES NOT RESCUE THE CONTROL -- den halves to 0.696 ms while its IQR does not (0.516 -> 0.583), so in-band blocks FALL from 47% to 33%. Span the knee and the centre is wrong; avoid it and the denominator is gone. There is no third siting on a 300-boundary page.

THREE FRAMING CORRECTIONS THE EVIDENCE FORCES.

(a) M1 DOES NOT RUN THIS CONTROL. clock-app/ctl3-arms: "they exist on BULK ROWS ONLY"; arms-for appends them only for (= :bulk (:kind ...)). The three-point control's record is 0 of 42 and its failure IS total -- an explanation predicting total failure is the right one. What passes on M1 is ctl-2x, a ratio of two LEVELS not two DIFFERENCES. Its denominator is the floor's whole tared reading (~4.5 ms) carrying the same ~0.4 ms of error, i.e. 9% relative against ctl3's 48%. Centre 1.808/1.780 sits 20% above the 1.50 edge against ctl3's 4%. Per-block in-band 95.1%/95.4% -> 5 of 8 and 4 of 6 runs. On BULK rows the same ctl-2x reads 1.729/1.697 with sd 0.296/0.356 -> 84.7%/77.5% in band -> 4 of 24 and 0 of 18. Two numbers -- distance of the centre above the edge, and per-block scatter -- raised to the 18th power produce EVERY pass rate in this programme, ctl-2x's own row preference included. It is the DENOMINATOR class, not the row class.

(b) THE THREE BULK ROWS ARE THREE REPLICATES OF ONE EXPERIMENT. ctl3-arms takes no row argument: on bulk300/bulk100/narrow the control's arms are byte-identical (floor's own 300-boundary 901-element page, d=1/100/200, one door); only the substrate arms' k changes. Measured per row, T(1) p50 2.63-2.75, den p50 1.19-1.29, statistic p50 1.52-1.62, in-band 42-49% -- indistinguishable. No per-row explanation is needed and none is available.

(c) THE TWO ENSEMBLES DO NOT DISAGREE. At block level they agree to within 2% on every structural quantity. The apparent disagreement is a REPORTING artefact: the run figure is band().mean over 18 block ratios whose denominator is 2 sigma from zero. 2.5% of blocks have abs(den) < 0.2 ms; ONE of them moves a run's reported mean from ~1.6 to 86x or 114x. emvod drew such a block on bulk100 and narrow and not on bulk300 -- that is the whole of "bulk300 low and tight vs two degenerate runs". The rate is the same in both ensembles and across all three rows. The two named degenerates are den=+0.019 ms (T(1)=2.9205, T(100)=2.9395) and den=+0.026 ms (T(1)=3.5090, T(100)=3.5350); in 9 of the 10 worst blocks T(1) is ELEVATED (p50 3.40 against a population 2.66), and T(1) enters BOTH differences, so an excursion in it drives the smaller denominator to zero first. The eps arm is the estimator's single point of failure and the sign gate can only catch it after it crosses (7 of 432, 6 of 324 caught; a further 5 and 3 were positive but under 0.2 ms and were not).

THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION CARRIES ONE INFERENCE THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE: "the same signature as ctl-2x's undershoot on the identical samples". Four lines say they are two phenomena of coincidentally similar size. Per-block correlation between the two statistics is -0.023 (emvod) and +0.036 (w3yxd) over 432/324 PAIRED blocks. On the layout counter they diverge -- ctl3 becomes exact (1.968/1.980) while ctl-2x stays 4-6% short (1.9225/1.8897), because page-doubling has a non-scaling component even in LayoutDuration and the three-point construction does not. The two recovered constants disagree by ~60%: c(2x) = 1.222/1.409 ms against a three-point pedestal T(d=1) tared of 1.732/1.775 ms and a fitted c(3pt) of 1.97 ms -- a genuinely affine T gives one number both ways, and the disagreement IS the non-affinity restated. Mechanically: ctl-2x undershoots on an ADDITIVE constant in d-independent work, which the three-point statistic cancels exactly; ctl3 undershoots on a SATURATING FUNCTION OF THE VERY AXIS THE CONTROL VARIES, which no differencing removes and which ctl-2x is blind to because it never varies d.

HOW MUCH OF THE REFUSAL IS THE 18-BLOCK STRICT RULE, ISOLATED. The layout control has the right centre, healthy conditioning and a sign gate that never fires, with 84.5%/82.1% of blocks in band -- and it STILL passes only 3 of 24 and 1 of 18 runs, because 0.845^18 = 4.8%. Even a control that fully meets its premise barely survives this rule on this instrument.

NO REMEDY IMPLEMENTED AND NONE RECOMMENDED HERE. For the record only, the evidence supports exactly one direction -- a control whose denominator is a LEVEL rather than a DIFFERENCE, i.e. abandoning the difference-of-differences on this rig rather than re-siting its points, since both available sitings are shown to fail and the conditioning arithmetic says why any siting must. That is a decision about what the lane measures, not a threshold to move, and it is Mike's.

WHAT I COULD NOT SETTLE FROM COMMITTED DATA. (i) The attribution of the concave residual specifically to PAINT is inherited, not established: the datasets carry Task/Script/Layout/DevTools and style is 0 throughout -- there is no paint counter. What IS established is that the concave term is in the non-layout half, is 7.1 -> 1.8 us/cell, and saturates below d=100; paint damage-region clipping at the viewport is consistent with that and with layout staying linear, but it is an inference. (ii) The bootstrap SE of a 10-sample median is upward-biased at this n, so treat that table as order-of-magnitude; the corr = 0.43 line is the bootstrap-free version and carries the conclusion alone. (iii) Whether a DIFFERENT instrument reads these rows is not answerable from this data -- rf2-rguy1 is the bead that could.

INHERITANCE FOR THE SIX REMAINING MEASUREMENT BEADS. ctl3Verdict exists in exactly two files, clock_run.cjs and clock_readjudicate.cjs, so only rows taken through clock_run.cjs are gated by it. INHERITS: rf2-2rtt6.59 (names clock_run.cjs and the three-point control explicitly -- its bulk halves refuse on the 0-of-42 evidence, and its M1 half is ctl-2x at ~40% strict pass hunting a few-per-cent effect against a 21-32% band). DOES NOT INHERIT: rf2-pqyxz (walk_profile_app on lane.cljs control-verdict, a two-point overlap-rule control), rf2-ne3ey (arm1/hydration_support.cljs), rf2-2rtt6.138 (p0_heap/p0_run heap ladder), rf2-d360z (read_profile_app, 0.025 ms grid), rf2-rguy1 (external krausest harness). rf2-rguy1 is the one bead that can break the deadlock: its partial-update-every-10th IS the narrow row and its replace-all/swap ARE the bulk rows, on an instrument nobody here wrote whose adjudication is not a difference-of-differences. LOWER CONFIDENCE, offered as a pattern only: rf2-2rtt6.138 and rf2-d360z do not run this control but are both differential measurements whose signal is approaching their instrument's dispersion (.138's r2 of 0.75/0.28/0.94/0.31 against a 0.98 floor; d360z's own "about ONE QUANTUM" of a 0.025 ms grid) -- same class of ill-conditioning, arrived at independently, and a quiet box will not help them either.
