comments.text:
DELEGATED DECISION (operator-directed dossier review, 2026-08-07, operator-overturnable): WHAT ADJUDICATES BULK ROWS.

THE RULING, in four parts:

(1) The three-point difference-of-differences control is RETIRED AS A GATE on this instrument — not re-sited, not re-tried. Both dossier and Codex reviews converge here, and the diagnosis is arithmetic: the prediction is mis-derived (TaskDuration is not affine in d — marginal cost 12.6 -> 6.8-7.2 us/cell across [1,100]/[100,200]; the statistic's true centre 1.546-1.578 sits 2.6% ABOVE the 1.5076 refusal edge) AND the estimator is ill-conditioned (den = T(100)-T(1) is 1.249/1.230 ms carrying 0.599/0.667 ms dispersion, 2.09/1.85 sigma from zero, corr(T(1),T(100)) ~ 0.4 — the classic Fieller ratio problem; Franz, arXiv:0710.2024). Re-siting at 100/200/300 fixes the centre (1.9975/2.0777) but halves the denominator: in-band blocks FALL 47% -> 33%. Both available sitings fail; any siting must. The ctl3 statistic may keep printing as a labelled non-gating diagnostic of the page's dirty-set shape (its internal control, ctl3Layout, is healthy: 1.9681/1.9801 on identical blocks, marginals flat 5.4 -> 5.1 us/cell, all 756 numerators/denominators positive — which localises the failure to the non-affine non-layout clock, not the quotient machinery).

(2) The all-18-blocks strict rule is RETIRED WITH IT, everywhere on this instrument. It is a separate defect with its own arithmetic: the premise-meeting layout statistic has 631/756 blocks (83.5%) in-band yet passes only 4/42 runs (0.835^18 = 3.9%); ctl-2x shows the identical pathology (626/756 in-band, 4/42 strict). Swapping controls while keeping "every block" would NOT unblock bulk. Tolerance band and run-rejection rule get DISTINCT, CALIBRATED error rates.

(3) The replacement is a level-denominated, EMPIRICALLY CALIBRATED, versioned check standard — not ctl-2x's literal 2.00x prediction (asserting a theoretical value against a non-affine clock is the exact mistake being retired). Seed from the existing ctl-2x/floor run medians, whose empirical behaviour is already characterised: centre 1.721x, range 1.596-1.829x, between-run SD 0.057 across the 42 committed row-runs. Freeze run-level location and dispersion limits from an independent baseline; prove them against the sabotage fixture; recalibrate on any browser, harness, page, or clock change (NIST e-Handbook 2.3.5 check-standard doctrine). A future same-page arm with KNOWN added main-thread work near the bulk signal scale is the preferred long-term standard but is NOT required to unblock.

(4) The product claim is adjudicated on the quantity it asserts: the paired, same-round Hicasso/Reagent level ratio at fixed witness and fixed K, reported as an effect-size confidence interval from a run-preserving hierarchical analysis (paired log-ratios; resample outer runs before inner blocks — Kalibera & Jones 2013). Ship/kill publishes ONLY when the whole interval lies on the required side of 1.0 (bar) / 1.5 (architecture-kill) AND the effect clears the same-run noise band; otherwise the row publishes INSTRUMENT-LIMITED, never a magnitude. This protocol is FROZEN IN WRITING before the next bulk window opens — rows must never again be taken with no pre-registered rule to adjudicate them.

UNCHANGED: the hard refusals stay hard (read-back, canonical-DOM, page-error, arm-order, quiet-box, band-ceiling). jsfb remains the OUTSIDE CORROBORATOR, never the census witness (its bulk rows are the best-behaved in the matrix — replace1k drift +1.7%/-2.4%, cross-instrument agreement 0.8-14.3% — which is what localises the refusal to our construction; bounded honestly: one trivial-state app, two runs). The 42 committed row-runs (clock-emvod run1-8, clock-w3yxd run1-6) remain calibration/diagnostic evidence and are NOT retroactively promoted to published magnitudes.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for the implementation worker (one bounded protocol change in the driver + readjudicator; no stats research project):
  1. Bulk verdict paths stop consulting ctl3; its printout is relabelled diagnostic/non-gating; no re-siting code.
  2. The check standard lands as data (versioned expected centre + frozen location/dispersion limits) with the sabotage-fixture proof pinned by a test.
  3. The whole-interval verdict rule lands in the readjudicator with the run-preserving resampling, pinned by a test on the committed 42-run corpus (expected output: instrument-limited or a clean interval — whatever the data says, the test pins the procedure not the answer).
  4. The all-blocks rule is removed everywhere on this instrument in the same PR (grep for the ^18 semantics), with the calibrated replacement's error rates stated in the code comment.
  5. Everything above cites this ruling by bead id.

SEQUENCING CONSEQUENCE: the window beads queued behind this ruling may be scheduled once the protocol freeze (criteria 2-4) lands — rf2-2rtt6.59's bulk halves adjudicate under the new standard; rf2-pqyxz, rf2-ne3ey, rf2-d360z, rf2-2rtt6.138 do not inherit ctl3 (different instruments) but d360z/.138 carry the recorded same-class ill-conditioning caution. No new bulk window before the freeze. The mount half of the instrument question is rf2-t2flm's ruling (concurrent, separate note); one finding here feeds it by id: ctl-2x's true centre is empirical (~1.72-1.80 by row class), not 2.00x, so any mount decision function should state its expectation empirically too.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (carried, not resolved): the datasets carry no paint counter — "non-layout and saturating below d=100" is established; that PAINT specifically causes the concavity is not. Do not state paint-causation in any published row.

Working notes preserved: ai/findings/2026-08-07.three-point-control-refusal-diagnosed.md (diagnosis), a-control-that-differences-the-constant-away.md section 7 (design record). Codex independent recompute concorded with the diagnosis within rounding (pooled medians 1.5691/1.5751 vs predicted 2.0101; 0/42) from the raw roundsTask/roundsLayout arrays, verified against ctl3-arms/sample-bulk! (clock_app.cljs) and ctl3Verdict/ratioToFloor/controlVerdict (clock_run.cjs).

title: hicasso: pin the mid-adoption revision timing row on the .84 hydration harness
description:
SPLIT OUT OF rf2-zq8kh, which implemented the revision prop. R3 of docs/design/hicasso/studio/revision-prop-spec.md demoted the design's mid-adoption claim ('a revision arriving during hydration adoption lands on the first post-adoption commit, on the SERVER's node') to witness-gated intent, with the fallback pre-committed: if React deopts, the documented conduct becomes deferral past adoption.

WHAT rf2-zq8kh SETTLED. The claim is not the prop's to make. ::h/revision is consumed at the codec before emission — native-element reads it off the author's own pre-merge map and install! deletes the marker as it reads it — so React is handed a prop-identical element whether the revision moved or not. front/revision_dom_cljs_test pins that structurally: same emitted slots, same values, same element type, with the revision, with a different revision, and with none. Nothing on React's side can branch on a value it was never given. HD-019's addendum and authoring.md both document the deferral as the shipped conduct.

WHAT IS LEFT. Two hand-rolled hydrateRoot arms in that PR disagreed about node identity across consecutive runs — node lost on one run, kept on the next — which is React's own adoption race, not the prop's doing. A row that pins adoption TIMING needs the .84 hydration harness (arm1/hydration_support.cljs), which exists precisely because hydrateRoot returns before the tree is adopted and naive settling is wrong. A hand-rolled race in the DOM suite would be a flake, so it was deliberately not shipped.

SCOPE: add the timing row on the .84 harness — hydrate, bump mid-adoption, and pin whichever conduct the harness can make deterministic. If it cannot be made deterministic, say so and close: the deferral is already the documented conduct and nothing depends on the row.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #7689 — Reopened exact owner. Completeness residual: docs/design/hicasso/draft-guide/04-controlled-inputs.md still calls both exceptional cases deferrals, says the mid-hydration revision defers past adoption, says timing is not pinned, and repeats that stale state in the Not settled yet table. Correct those two locations to the measured absorption conduct. Correctness/ergonomics residual: the new records say send the revision again / caller's to send again, but equal revision values are explicitly inert; say a DIFFERENT revision value/change after adoption is required. Keep this a bounded prose repair: no runtime or harness redesign. The merged row itself is coherent and browser-green (1132 tests / 6969 assertions), hicasso compile and doc-slug checks pass, and the exact authored/applied range-diff is 2/2.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-08-08 00:38 AUSEST — FIFTH silent tracker revert this session (after rf2-ih772, rf2-w3yxd, rf2-n6w7o and rf2-2ze1h). Verified CLOSED by the mayor twice, at 23:55 and 00:04, and read OPEN again at 00:37. Nothing reopened it.

EVIDENCE FROM origin/main, not memory: c13864d7f7 ("the mid-adoption revision row on the .84 harness") and a96103be5b ("the mid-adoption revision is absorbed, not deferred") both carry (rf2-ne3ey); decisions.md:1184 carries the "Amended by rf2-ne3ey" block; PR #7689 state=MERGED at 86/86 with all five branch runs completed.

THE VERDICT: the row CAN be made deterministic, and the answer is NEITHER the design's claim NOR the pre-committed fallback. The conduct is ABSORPTION.

MEASURED on arm1/hydrate_dom_cljs_test section 6: the server's node survives (identical?, expando stamp intact); React reports on neither channel; ONE body run across the whole adoption, so the mid-adoption write produced no render of its own; the reset does NOT land, the draft typed into the server-rendered field surviving while the defaultValue mirror holds the model's; and the field is not stranded, because the next revision change after the window shuts resets it on the server's own node, without remount, on one ordinary commit.

THE MECHANISM, which also explains why rf2-zq8kh's hand-rolled arms flaked and this does not: the mid-adoption write reaches NO COMMITTED BOUNDARY — the arm acquires at COMMIT and the adoption commit is the first one — so it notifies nothing, and the already-scheduled adoption render reads the new revision as the field's FIRST, a change with no predecessor to be a change from. Hydration is a MOUNT rather than an update, so the per-commit updateInput re-assert that carries the whole reset never runs. The hand-rolled arms called root.render mid-adoption and so DID reach React's scheduler; a store write does not.

WHY IT CANNOT FLAKE — structural, not a tolerance. "Mid-adoption" is a FACT on this harness rather than a wait: hydrate-root! refuses to flushSync, so it returns before adoption and (rt/adopting?) is TRUE on the next line, with the dispatch synchronous in that same turn. Nothing can interleave; there is nothing to settle. No setTimeout, no retry loop, no tolerance. rt/dispatch! was used rather than mount/dispatch! because the latter's settle! is a flushSync, which would manufacture the very schedule this door exists to refuse. Ten consecutive narrowed runs: 10/10 identical.

RECORDS CORRECTED, and this is why the diff reached four files beyond the row: the measurement falsified the SHIPPED DOCUMENTED CONDUCT. "Lands on the first post-adoption commit" is false in both halves — there is no post-adoption commit, and the adoption commit does not re-assert — and "the reset defers past adoption" overstates it, because nothing lands later either. What survives of R3 is the NODE claim, which the row pins. Amended via the dated-amendment idiom in decisions.md (HD-019), authoring.md, revision-prop-spec.md, front/controlled.cljs and front/revision_dom_cljs_test.cljs. MAYOR REVIEW: I inspected the decisions.md diff before merging, since the epic names that file normative. HD-019's original ruling text stands and the amendment sits beneath it, with the false claim quoted inside the amendment where it is refuted rather than quietly deleted. Scope extension accepted — leaving three files asserting deferral while a fourth witnessed absorption would have been the worse outcome.

FENCES HELD: arm1/runtime.cljs read-only and never edited; entry-reap-horizon-ms untouched (the row waits on adopted!, which already stands on it); hydration_support.cljs needed no change at all — adopted! and the server-node predicates were used exactly as they stand.

title: hicasso: the census driver collects Script/Layout/RecalcStyle durations and drops them at write time
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-08-07 on the rf2-2rtt6.56 worker's hand-off (PR #7639), which left acceptance part (4) of the #7379 audit deliberately unfinished and said why.

THE FINDING. shapes/census_clock_run.cjs collects ScriptDuration, LayoutDuration and RecalcStyleDuration at lines 383-411, then DROPS them when it writes the dataset. So the studio page's cited decomposition — 'layout 2.06x, style 1.85x, script 2.3x' — is not recomputable from any committed dataset. The numbers were real when taken; nothing on disk can reproduce them.

WHY IT WAS NOT JUST FIXED IN #7639. Adding the capture is a small change, but capture alone changes nothing: the existing datasets still lack the fields, so the figures only become recomputable on a RE-RUN. That makes this measurement-coupled, and the box has been contended all day. The worker correctly declined to take a row it could not trust, and declined to add capture that would look like a fix while proving nothing.

SEQUENCING. This belongs BESIDE the matched-workload re-run, not before it — rf2-2rtt6.62's retraction established that large_template.cljs seeds 69 articles and feed.cljs seeds 300 through the same arithmetic, so the roster needs matching seeds before any cross-row row is worth taking. Do both in one quiet-box session: match the workloads, add the metric capture, re-run, republish. One window, one dataset, both problems closed.

ACCEPTANCE: the three durations present in every committed dataset, and the published decomposition recomputable from them by the same fail-closed aggregator discipline used elsewhere in this corpus (a stored figure that does not reproduce must exit non-zero).

Pre-alpha posture: do not add capture as a standalone change. Un-recomputable prose plus capture-without-data is two half-measures where one quiet run closes it properly.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7666 (2026-08-07). COMPLETENESS: the per-block persistence is the right instrument-prep slice, and the current datasets/quiet-window remainder is already exactly owned by open rf2-jv36i, so no duplicate was created for the re-run. The driver now carries the collected Script/Layout/RecalcStyle sums plus n into the dataset, and the report folds the same blocks. Current syntax passes and clock_exit_path.test.cjs passes all 189 checks.

CORRECTNESS — REOPENED THIS EXACT OWNER. `foldDecomposition` is not actually fail-closed at the evidence boundary promised by this Bead. It rejects only a non-array or an outer `[]`; `foldDecomposition([[]])` and `foldDecomposition([[{}]])` both return `{}`. More seriously, `acc[k] += a[k] || 0` silently turns a missing, null, or NaN metric into zero. A live probe on the landed function showed a partial arm lacking task/taskNet/devtools/script/layoutCount/inPage was accepted with every missing field synthesized as 0, and an explicit null script was accepted as script 0. That permits partial/corrupt persisted evidence to become a plausible ratio instead of the required non-zero refusal — the same defect class this PR is meant to close. The new committed-dataset test branches only on the truthiness of `row.blocksDecomp`, so it cannot catch this third state.

Required before re-closing: validate the actual nested evidence shape rather than defaulting it. Require nonempty rounds and blocks; the expected arm roster in every block; every accumulator field present and finite; positive counts where required; and refuse missing/null/nonfinite values. Add hermetic mutation witnesses for `[[]]`, `[[{}]]`, an absent arm, a missing metric, null/NaN, and prove the invalid row reaches a non-zero driver outcome rather than a canonical write. Keep this bounded inside the existing fold/write path; no validation framework is needed. rf2-jo60g is the exact fail-closed persistence owner.

The notes above were recovered from .beads/issues.jsonl at commit 31099a515d after the mayor overwrote them with `bd update --notes`, which REPLACES rather than appends (the correct flag is --append-notes). The mayor note that caused the loss follows, preserved verbatim.

MAYOR RULING 2026-08-07 22:45 AUSEST, on the worker's flagged question: does the newly-landed censusclock-jv36i dataset satisfy this bead's acceptance?

THE QUESTION. The worker found that censusclock-jv36i ALREADY carries blocksDecomp — the matched-workload re-take landed in 623c9341af, AFTER this bead's 03:46 comment, so the premise that all four datasets still lack the fields is stale. Its stricter validation accepts that dataset unchanged (6x3 blocks, consistent rosters, all fields finite, n=10), which is good evidence the new checks are tight rather than over-tight. But BOTH its files record canonical=false / "C56CLOCK_DATA_DIR named this destination".

RULED: ACCEPTANCE NOT SATISFIED. The re-run half stays open.

WHY. The two-tier write policy (rf2-2rtt6.31) exists to say exactly one thing: only a gate-passing, full-published-shape run may back a published claim, refused/partial/overridden runs write the same shape to a .unpublished sibling and self-describe, and CONSUMERS FAIL CLOSED. A published figure recomputed from a canonical=false dataset is precisely the case that clause forbids. It does not matter that this file's notCanonicalWhy is a PROVENANCE reason (a named destination directory) rather than a quality one — the moment we start reading notCanonicalWhy to decide which false verdicts we are willing to overlook, the field stops being a gate and becomes advisory, and it stops being a gate EVERYWHERE, not just here. rf2-emvod's whole consumer half was landed to prevent that. I am not going to hollow it out for one row.

SO THE BAR HAS MOVED BUT NOT BEEN MET, and the remaining scope is now NARROWER than the description says. Capture has landed; the re-run no longer needs to add anything. What is missing is a CANONICAL dataset carrying the fields. Do not re-brief "add the metric capture and re-run" from the description — brief "produce a canonical run of the full published shape".

THE CODE HALF IS DONE — PR #7681 (worker/foldclosed-jo60g), pending CI. foldDecomposition no longer defaults a missing, null or NaN metric to zero; it requires nonempty rounds and blocks, the first block's arm roster as a SET in every block (insertion order genuinely varies with the guard schedule, so an ordered compare would have been wrong), and every one of the nine DECOMP_FIELDS present and finite, refusing with round/block/arm/field named. A live probe against censusclock-jv36i/uix.json (declared 6 rounds x 3 blocks; row armIds includes uix) shows foldDecomposition ACCEPTS: (1) the final round removed, (2) one block removed from round 2, and (3) uix removed from every block. Each is partial/truncated evidence and still returns plausible aggregates. Complete the code half by checking the expected round/block dimensions and blocksDecomp roster against the row's armIds at the real report/driver boundary, with non-zero/no-write/noncanonical witnesses for all three; this needs no schema layer. title: Hicasso: the memo wrapper's 2x is not double buffering — what IS it?
description:
SUCCESSOR to rf2-2rtt6.61, which is closed as a VERIFIED NEGATIVE.

rf2-2rtt6.61 asked for a fiber count to test the published hypothesis that the
memo wrapper's 2x instrument disagreement (+195/+220 B per boundary on
chrome_run.cjs vs +100/+106 B on p0_run.cjs --only ladder) was React's double
buffering. That hypothesis is now EXCLUDED from the instruments' own committed
source, with no fiber count taken:

  * p0_run.cjs:588-593 — gc, pre-read, mountOne, gc, held-read. Mount and hold.
  * chrome_run.cjs:242-243 — 'the heap half, first, on a quiet page';
    heapForArms runs to completion before the clock half's runOp calls begin at
    line 264. heapOnce (164-182) is resetRuntime -> baseline -> mountArm ->
    held, with no op between mount and read.
  * Byte-identical ordering at cb179b6b3c, the commit that published the
    +195/+220 figures.

BOTH instruments mount and hold. Neither has ever read an updated tree, so the
rule 2rtt6.61 proposed — a memo wrapper costs ONE fiber held and TWO updated —
must not be adopted, and is not.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN. The ~2x itself. Both figures reproduce on their own
instrument and both are published against the shape they were taken on, so
nothing rests on this; it is about being able to state WHY.

THE ASK, and it is a DIFFERENT question from 2rtt6.61's. Classify FiberNode
objects in a heap snapshot on each instrument, by tag, and answer: is the
wrapper ONE fiber in both? If yes, the difference is in what a fiber HOLDS on
each shape, not in how many there are, and the programme should stop quoting a
Fiber as a fixed byte count. If no, the count itself is the finding and the
mechanism has to be named.

NOTE ON COST. No such capability exists anywhere under implementation/: a
tree-wide search for FiberNode, _reactInternals, memoizedState, queryObjects,
Runtime.queryObjects, writeHeapSnapshot and v8.getHeapSnapshot returns nothing.
The nearest scaffolding is snapshotTotal() in
implementation/freehand/test/re_frame/freehand/bench/reads_ladder_run.cjs:228,
which streams HeapProfiler.takeHeapSnapshot and sums self_size plus a raw node
count — it never reads the snapshot's strings table or a node's type/name, so
it cannot isolate FiberNode. Classification is a new instrument, not a flag.

NOT a clock bead: a snapshot classification is structural and does not need a
quiet box.

Shapes, for whoever takes it: chrome is 301 boundaries, each a 17-element card
reading two subscriptions, ~11 KB retained per boundary; the ladder rung is
1,200 R=0 cells reading nothing, ~1,141 B per boundary. An order of magnitude
apart in what the boundary holds, against a 2x in what the wrapper adds.

Evidence: docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md,
subsection 'Why this instrument reads half of what the card-shaped one did'
(corrected 2026-08-03 under rf2-2rtt6.61).

But it leaves the older central premise in force: “the keyword mint left the copy and the seam alike, so it cancels out of the ratio” and therefore “holds 0.9718 in place.”

Correctness: equal additive work cancels from a difference, not a ratio. For old numerator A, denominator B and removed cost m, (A-m)/(B-m) equals A/B only when m=0 or A=B. With the page's A=0.8625 and B=0.8875, removing the estimated 0.002–0.005 ms from both moves 0.971831 to about 0.971767–0.971671 even before rf2-lzpfj adds activation to c-local alone. Implementation quality: no new window or mechanism is needed for this correction. Since the new evidence already fails to reproduce 0.9718, label the old ratio as a historical reading on its provenance/basis rather than claiming it still stands by cancellation. title: hicasso: standardize native benchmark self-test flag
description: PR #8610 audit finding. The native Hicasso benchmark drivers use two spellings for the same operator-facing self-test mode: clock_run.cjs, hd8_run.cjs, and ladder_band.cjs use --selftest while the surrounding helper fleet and package scripts predominantly use --self-test. The split already caused a plausible wrong census and left ladder_band's guard unregistered until #8610. Standardize these three direct CLIs and their usage/comments/callers on --self-test; preserve the existing direct fixture exports and do not add duplicate package registrations for clock/hd8, which clock_exit_path.test.cjs already reaches. Pre-alpha means no compatibility alias is required.
acceptance_criteria: All native benchmark driver self-test CLIs use --self-test; repository searches show no executable or operator-facing --selftest residue for the three drivers; the existing helper gate still reaches the same adjudicator fixtures and remains green.
notes:
## 2026-08-21 09:15 AUSEST — audit remainder discharged (PR #8621)

The #8616 audit's three asks, all taken.

1. NO ALIAS. Unchanged and deliberate: pre-alpha, and an alias for a spelling
   nothing depends on is a compatibility shim.

2. FAIL FAST — read as strict unknown-argument rejection, not a narrower guard,
   and the reason is that for these two drivers the strict rule IS the narrow
   one. `clock_run.cjs` and `hd8_run.cjs` take every knob they have from an
   `HCLOCK_*` / `HD8_*` environment variable and no positional argument at all,
   so their flag vocabulary is closed by construction at two entries and one.
   Writing that list down is the CLI's own surface, not an argument-validation
   framework: no parser, no generated help, no did-you-mean (which would be the
   nag this repo rejects). A list of dead tokens was rejected as the shim
   wearing a refusal's clothes — it would still swallow the next typo.
   `ladder_band.cjs` does take positionals, so its rule is scoped to the flag
   namespace; its previous refusal was incidental (ENOENT on a token it took
   for a filename) and said nothing to whoever typed it.

   Measured at 8d4672db2b under a child_process preload, so the heavyweight
   path was observed and not paid for: `--selftest` took `clock_run.cjs` to the
   shadow-cljs `:advanced` release spawn and `hd8_run.cjs` to `git rev-parse
   HEAD` in the provenance block, one line above `build()`. All three now exit
   2 before anything is built.

3. THE PIN, in the existing exit-path suite as asked. Four claims per driver:
   the argv definition itself, the closed vocabulary, that a token outside it
   is refused, and that the refusal is wired above every self-test, `build()`
   and `chromium` in the head of `main`. Proven by sabotage — reverting
   `clock_run.cjs`'s argv spelling reds the suite 2/383 naming both new tests;
   the earlier suite was green against that same mutation.

   `ladder_band.cjs` is deliberately NOT repeated there: `test:script-helpers`
   invokes it directly, and a second sabotage run confirmed that invocation
   catches the same mutation (gate exit 2 at that step).

No package registration added; `implementation/package.json` untouched, as
required by the fence around rf2-lr4id / rf2-0eu1s.

Gate: `npm run test:script-helpers` exit 0 pre-rebase, exit 2 sabotaged, exit 0
on the final rebased base. `scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` exit 0. No
spine, no shadow-cljs, no browser, no JVM — an allocation window was live.

## 2026-08-21 10:05 AUSEST — the SECOND audit remainder, closed (PR #8627)

#8621's own merged-PR audit found the closed vocabulary held only on a PREFIX
of `ladder_band.cjs`'s argv. Its parser ran the self-test and returned from
INSIDE the loop, so no token after `--self-test` was ever read. Reproduced at
`origin/main` before touching anything, and the note above is where the gap
came from — it recorded that `test:script-helpers` invokes the driver directly,
which is true, but that invocation is `--self-test` alone: the PASSING case,
which says nothing about a refusal.

THE REPAIR separates PARSING from ACTING rather than adding a validating pass.
A second pass is where the care would have been needed, because `--emit` and
`--from` each consume the token AFTER them and a pass that did not know it
would read `--emit --from.json` as a flag. `parseArgv` is now pure and total:
one left-to-right read, each valued flag's value consumed as a value, returning
either the whole plan or the first reason there cannot be one. `main` is the
only thing that acts and cannot act before the parser reaches the end of argv,
so there is no prefix left to hide in. Exported, with the entry point behind
`require.main === module`, so the pin drives the rule instead of quoting it.

The flag-namespace scoping stays — this driver takes dataset filenames where
its neighbours take none — and so does the no-alias decision.

THE WITNESSES are seven in `clock_exit_path.test.cjs`, already in the
`test:script-helpers` chain; `implementation/package.json` untouched, the fence
around PR #8620 respected. THE ORDER PAIR IS THE TEST: refused BEFORE
`--self-test` and AFTER it, plus the four argv shapes the audit probed by hand
driven as real process exits, plus the valued-flag trap, plus a claim that
`parseArgv` may not call `selfTest()`, `readRun` or `process.exit`.

The four negative controls, before -> after:
  `--self-test --selftest`            0 -> 2
  `--self-test --definitely-unknown`  0 -> 2
  `--selftest --self-test`            2 -> 2
  `--self-test`                       0 -> 0

GATE `npm run test:script-helpers`, captured exits: 0 baseline (383 tests),
1 sabotaged, 0 restored (390), 0 on the final rebased base (390). The sabotage
reintroduced the early return and red EXACTLY the two AFTER-position witnesses
while the BEFORE pair stayed green — the audit's finding restored as a
measurement, and also the proof the gate read the worker's own checkout, since
that gate prints no root. Restore verified against the committed object by the
identical blob hash 88cac1b450210258a00a75f90ccd2aeb5b1968ec.
`scripts/check_retired_spellings.py` exit 0. No spine (94 required checks it
does not run), no shadow-cljs, no browser, no JVM — an allocation window was
live.

WHAT A THIRD AUDIT WOULD FIND, checked rather than waited for. Both neighbours
re-probed and both refuse in either order. No caller requires `ladder_band.cjs`.
The retired token survives in `implementation/` only where it must: the test
that refuses it, and the driver header that records what happened — which is
why this driver's "comments included" witness is deliberately narrower than the
two-driver one and exempts lines that are wholly comments.

OUT OF SCOPE AND NOT WORTH A BEAD: five sibling drivers in the same directory
(`alloc_position_confound`, `alloc_cluster_carrier`, `alloc_mode_rate_session`,
`alloc_pass_position`, `alloc_window_ceiling`) have no closed vocabulary at all,
and `alloc_pass_position.cjs` honours `--self-test` only at `args[0]`. This bead
names three drivers, none of these ever used the retired spelling, and the
fail-fast justification was refusing in twenty milliseconds rather than twenty
minutes — these are offline analysis scripts with no build and no Chromium
behind them. Extending the rule there is the argument-validation framework
#8621 declined to build. Recorded, not actioned.
close_reason: PR #8627: ladder_band.cjs now parses and validates the whole argv before any mode runs; order-pair witnesses registered in clock_exit_path.test.cjs. Gate test:script-helpers exit 0 (390), sabotage exit 1 reding exactly the AFTER-position pair.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8616 (correctness / implementation quality): exact closed owner reopened; no duplicate.

The spelling change works on the happy path, but the old spelling is not safely retired for two of the three direct CLIs. At merge commit 8d4672db2b, `clock_run.cjs` reads only `--no-build` and `--self-test`, and `hd8_run.cjs` reads only `--self-test`; neither validates unknown arguments. So `--selftest` is silently ignored and falls into the normal build/browser path instead of failing before heavyweight work. The PR body explicitly skipped that negative control for this reason. `ladder_band.cjs` happens to fail only because it treats the token as a dataset filename.

The nominated CI chain does not pin the rename for clock or HD8 either. `clock_exit_path.test.cjs` renamed four labels/comments and inspects the body of `if (SELFTEST_ONLY)`, but never asserts how `SELFTEST_ONLY` is derived; `test:script-helpers` directly invokes only `ladder_band.cjs --self-test`. A mutation of either driver back to `--selftest` (or another token) leaves those existing assertions green.

Keep the pre-alpha no-alias decision. Make the retired spelling fail fast before any build/browser (or otherwise prove it cannot enter the heavyweight default path), and add a bounded assertion in the existing clock/HD8 exit-path suite that pins both argv definitions and the absence of the legacy spelling. No duplicate package registrations or browser run are needed.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8621 (2026-08-21) — CORRECTNESS/COMPLETENESS: `ladder_band.cjs` does not actually enforce the PR's closed flag vocabulary over the whole argv. Its parser runs the self-test and returns immediately when it encounters `--self-test`, before scanning any later token. Direct probes at merge commit `2de41e2252cba83f9252ba72c5b05d256b121cbe` reproduce the order dependence: `--self-test --selftest` exits 0, `--self-test --definitely-unknown` exits 0, while `--selftest --self-test` exits 2. The same retired spelling is therefore “refused” only when it precedes the self-test flag; clock_run and hd8_run correctly reject the combined form with exit 2 because they validate all argv before dispatch.

Parse and validate the complete argument vector before executing any mode, then add registered witnesses for an unknown/retired flag both before and after `--self-test`. This is the exact acceptance gap in rf2-xk4is, so that owner is reopened rather than duplicated.

title: [bug] spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2392 has a stray pipe inside a cell, so the row parses as 9 fields and its RECOVERY column is read as :tags
description:
SURFACED BY rf2-zk1xu (twice — recorded as a sibling on that bead on 2026-08-20, then offered as a one-line PR by its worker on 2026-08-21) and deliberately NOT taken both times, because spec/009-Instrumentation.md is hot zone and single-toucher and neither dispatch was going to grow its diff for it.

THE CLAIM, to re-derive at origin/main HEAD rather than trust: the row for :rf.error/infinite-missing-next-page-param at about line 2392 carries a stray | inside a cell, so parse-catalogue-tag-rows counts 9 fields instead of 8 and reads the row's RECOVERY column as its :tags cell.

WHY IT IS ONLY P4. It is harmless TODAY and the reason is specific rather than general: no InfiniteMissingNextPageParamTags schema exists to pair with the row, so the mis-read cell is never compared against anything. That is luck, not design — the day someone adds that schema the pairing arm compares a recovery string against a tag key set and reds for a reason that has nothing to do with the change in front of them.

THE FIX IS ONE CHARACTER, and the whole job is proving it is one character. Escape or remove the stray pipe so the row parses as 8 fields. Verify by running the catalogue conformance namespace before and after and showing the test and assertion counts are UNCHANGED — this must be a no-op for every existing assertion, and a count that moves means the row was load-bearing somewhere and the change is not the one-liner it looks like.

CLOSING THIS AS MINUTIAE IS AN ACCEPTABLE OUTCOME if the re-derivation shows the parse is already correct, or that the repair costs more than a hot-zone toucher slot is worth. Say so with the measurement rather than doing it silently.

SURFACE: spec/009-Instrumentation.md only. HOT ZONE — one toucher at a time. Cluster with rf2-zmpfn if that bead is still open at dispatch: both are catalogue-prose minutiae and the two together are still smaller than one ordinary bead.
close_reason:
PR #8588. Half 2 (the parity bug) fixed; half 1 (the missing assertion) was already on main at my base via PR #8583 / rf2-6tags, commit 4b9e029c88, and is NOT duplicated here.

THE RULE. parse-catalogue-tag-rows split on a one-character negative lookbehind, so it called every backslash-prefixed pipe escaped. Markdown decides by the PARITY of the backslash run before the pipe. The rule now lives in a named table-delimiter-re and is ZERO-WIDTH: the run is inspected, never consumed, so only where columns break changes and no cell loses a character.

THE AUDIT SAID FOUR CASES WERE WRONG; IT IS TWO. Re-derived against Python-Markdown 3.10's tables extension rather than taken on trust: the old lookbehind is right on the ODD runs by luck and wrong only on the EVEN ones. Which two matters, because the error hides a defect rather than manufacturing one -- an even run really has broken the row into an extra column, and a reader that swallows the delimiter hands rf2-6tags's column-alignment invariant a field count matching the row's siblings. Under-splitting DISARMS that guard.

FIXTURE. table-delimiter-honours-backslash-run-parity, a pure parser fixture over the existing catalogue-fixture helper. It must be constructed: Spec 009 carries eleven escaped pipes across nine lines, every one a run of exactly ONE, no even run anywhere, and only the infinite-missing-next-page-param row is in this reader's section -- so the even half of the rule is unreachable from the corpus.

NON-VACUITY. 29 tests / 184 assertions before, 30 / 194 after. Reverting to the old regex reds exactly 4 of the 10 new assertions (both at run 2, both at run 4) and nothing else; counts stayed 30/194 through the sabotage, so the plant was scoped. Restore verified against the committed object by an identical git blob hash.

The fast-PR spine was NOT run and was not required; the single targeted JVM namespace was the only gate run directly, exit codes captured by this worker. spec/009-Instrumentation.md untouched; rf2-zmpfn stays closed.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text: MERGED-PR AUDIT #8576: Fixing the downstream reader rather than valid spec prose is correct, and rf2-zmpfn can remain closed. The parser half is incomplete in two coupled ways. First, no assertion pins the new behavior: the PR proves the old and new implementations both pass 28 tests / 177 assertions, because the motivating row has no paired schema, so reverting the fix stays green. Second, (?<!\\)\| checks only the immediately preceding character and treats every backslash-prefixed pipe as escaped. Markdown uses backslash-run parity: one or three backslashes escape the pipe, while two or four leave it as a column delimiter. A local Python-Markdown tables probe confirms that split, while this regex skips all four. Minimal completion: add a focused pure parser fixture covering a single escaped pipe and an even-backslash delimiter, then make the split parity-correct. Do not grow this into a general Markdown parser.

title: Spec-Schemas *Tags corpus counts in the catalogue conformance test's prose are stale (2 comments, 3 integers)
description:
FOUND BY rf2-zk1xu / PR #8573, recorded not swept (out of that PR's fence). NEEDS A RULING; closing as minutiae is an acceptable outcome.

implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj carries two dated prose measurements of the Spec-Schemas *Tags corpus:

  line 978: 'measured at the change, all 111 *Tags schemas but the one edited here are [:map-headed'

TWO SEPARATE DRIFTS, and only one is caused by #8573.

1. CAUSED: the total. #8573 retires HeadMismatchTags, so the corpus goes 111 -> 110. Both comments' '111' becomes false on merge.

2. PRE-EXISTING, and larger: the unpaired count. tags-column-paired-floor is 93. Against 111 schemas that is 18 unpaired, not 22 — the sentence is already off by four at the tip, before #8573. After #8573 it is 17. The parenthetical's own sub-split ('FxHandledTags' siblings' + '12 whose operation 009 never names') therefore cannot be right either, and re-deriving it needs a measurement the test does not currently expose.

THE CHOICE. Either (a) re-measure and correct all three integers plus the sub-split, or (b) drop the raw totals from prose that will drift again on the very next schema added, leaving the argument (which does not depend on the exact numbers) intact. (b) is cheaper and does not rot; (a) preserves the concreteness the comment was written for.

Fence if actioned: implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj only. NOT hot zone. Sequence AFTER PR #8573 merges, or the total will be re-measured against the wrong corpus.
close_reason: PR #8576. Took option (b) for the totals, (a)-by-naming for the [:map]-headedness. Re-derived from the computing code at the tip: corpus (count (parse-tags-schemas)) = 110; paired (paired-count ...) = 93, matching the tags-column-paired-floor pin; unpaired = 17; [:map]-headed = 109; distinct *Tags names cited in 009 = 4. Both predicted drifts confirmed -- #8573 took the corpus 111->110, and the 22 was already wrong before it (18 at #8573's parent, 17 now). The bead named THREE integers; there were FIVE: a fourth in the same sentence ('only 5 schema names are cited', measurement 4) and a fifth restatement ('One integer, not 22 entries'). Four hand-copied numbers in one paragraph, three wrong, none asserted -- so the totals are removed rather than corrected, keeping both durable REASONS a schema is legitimately unpaired plus a one-line re-derivation recipe. The fabricated 12 sub-split is gone; deriving it needs a measurement the test does not expose and inventing one for a comment is over-engineering. The two [:map]-headedness comments went the other way: the corpus has exactly ONE non-[:map]-headed schema, HydrationMismatchTags (:or-headed), and naming it says more than '110' did and cannot go stale. Left alone deliberately: the 'reports 22 findings' at the non-vacuity corpora is a frozen measurement against historical files at ded86cff64, not the live corpus. Comments only; 28 tests / 177 assertions unchanged.

description:

Both branches survived a cleanup that deleted 12 others, because git cherry reports them as carrying patches NOT upstream. That protection is working as designed; what is missing is a recorded reason for keeping them, so every future sweep re-derives it.

2. worker/retire-delete — ONE commit, 273 files, last commit 2026-08-15, subject 'refactor(ui): PARTIAL R2b — delete implementation/ui and its in-fence consumers (rf2-0yp7w.4)'. Its bead rf2-0yp7w.4 is CLOSED. PARTLY SUPERSEDED: implementation/ui is already gone from main (0 tracked files, executed by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16), so that half is done. BUT examples/real-apps/realworld_resources still holds 14 tracked files on main and this branch deletes them. So the branch carries a deletion main did not take, and it is not obvious whether those 14 files were deliberately KEPT or simply missed when #8322 landed the retirement by another route.

THE QUESTION FOR EACH: keep the branch, land the work, or delete the branch on a recorded decision. Do NOT delete either without one — a branch is the only copy of unmerged work, and both beads are closed so the tracker no longer points at them.

CHEAPEST NEXT STEP for retire-delete, and it is a read not a change: establish whether examples/real-apps/realworld_resources' 14 surviving files still reference the removed re-frame.ui tree. If they do, they are residue and rf2-0yp7w.9's prose sweep or a sibling owns them. If they do not, they were correctly kept and this branch is fully superseded and safe to delete.

NOT URGENT. Both branches are inert and cost nothing but a line in a listing. Filed P4 so the next hygiene sweep reads a decision instead of re-deriving the measurement.

Every search excluded the tracker export (-- ':!.beads') and every search carries a

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CLAIMS THAT HELD, all of them:
  "git cherry origin/main worker/receipts-hic081" -> 3 unmerged commits
  (fece72f80a, 418312d680, ae14841ab3); last commit 2026-08-11 13:06:01 +1000.

THE CLAIM THAT DID **NOT** HOLD — and it is this bead's stated premise:

  Verdict was SPLIT: counts graduate as DESIGN, self-time KILLED. The design is on main at

title: [ruling] does the adapters' flush-views! test door owe guard-open-drain!? rf2-cydkp ruled flush-render! and did not reach it
description:
RAISED BY rf2-p7p4f's worker (PR #8484) while establishing what spec/006's "explicit test flush" actually is. Reported rather than decided: it is a behaviour change on three shipping adapters, and rf2-cydkp's ruling does not cover it.

THE GAP. rf2-cydkp ruled that Spec 006's `flush-render!` is EXPRESSLY OUTSIDE the :rf.error/flush-in-open-epoch law — a render-commit is not the registry-flush `re-frame.frame/guard-open-drain!` rejects — and spec/009's catalogue row says so for "the three shipped adapter kinds that install a `flush-render!` slot". It says nothing about `flush-views!`, the adapters' TEST door, which is a different fn on a different slot.

WHAT flush-views! ACTUALLY DOES, read at source at origin/main 7902167197:
  - re-frame.adapter.reagent/flush-views!      -> (act (fn [] (reagent.core/flush)))
  - re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim/flush-views! -> (act (fn [] (batching/flush!)))
  - re-frame.adapter.uix/flush-views!          -> (act f); the spine impl, no queue drain
All three return nil and are test-scoped. reagent-slim additionally ships an INTERNAL one layer below its contract slot, `reagent2.dom.client/flush-views!` (reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs:122) — goog.DEBUG-gated, Promise-returning, composing microtask -> act(batching/flush!) -> microtask. That is the closest living relative of the removed `re-frame.ui.test/flush!`, which DID call the guard.

THE QUESTION. `reagent.core/flush` and `batching/flush!` drain a render queue + dirty set inside `act`, and can therefore publish a render phase. Is that the "synchronous registry-flush" the guard's law names?

THE WORKER'S RECOMMENDATION, offered as a reading and not asserted in the spec: NO. rf2-cydkp's discriminator is whether the flush drains THE SUBSTRATE'S OWN cell registry — the guard's docstring closes over `*run-frame-state-before*` and nothing else precisely because a ViewCell registry was the subject — and Reagent's component render queue is the HOST's, not the substrate's. The re-frame2 substrate these adapters install has no cell registry of its own; it delegates reactivity to ratoms / React hooks.

AGAINST that reading: a test author who calls `flush-views!` from inside a `dispatch-sync` handler gets exactly the torn read/render the guard exists to reject, and gets no diagnostic. The hazard is real, if small and test-only.

COST IF RULED THE OTHER WAY: a throw added to three shipped adapters' test doors, plus contract tests, plus a spec/006 §`flush-render!` and spec/009 row amendment. Not a prose repair.

STATE OF PLAY. spec/006 §Render-batch finalization was rewritten by PR #8484 to state the registry-flush law POSITIVELY and to say nothing about `flush-views!`'s membership in it, precisely so this bead can rule either way without a revert. P4 because nothing is broken today and the surface is test-only.
close_reason: Ruling applied by PR #8499. Added one line to each of the three contract-slot flush-views! docstrings (re-frame.adapter.reagent / .reagent-slim / .uix) saying it publishes a render phase and must not be called from inside a dispatch-sync handler. No throw, no contract test, no spec change — spec/006 Render-batch finalization already states the registry-flush law positively and is silent on flush-views! membership. reagent-slim's internal reagent2.dom.client/flush-views! deliberately untouched per the ruling (internal, not a contract slot). The three sites were re-derived at the tip: they are (def flush-views! "..." (:flush-views! spine-fns)) forms, not defns, and the bead's reading of each implementation held. Gate: clj-kondo over the three files, captured exit 0, proved to reach this tree by a planted unresolved symbol (red, captured exit 2) then restored and hash-verified.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-08-18 21:48 AUSEST — TAKEN UNDER LIVE DELEGATION (Mike, this session: 'Don't ask me for permission, get hicasso to 0 beads').

RULING: NO. flush-views! does NOT owe guard-open-drain!. No throw is added to any adapter test door.

I ADOPT THE WORKER'S DISCRIMINATOR, which is the same one rf2-cydkp used rather than a new one invented for this case: the guard's law is about draining THE SUBSTRATE'S OWN cell registry. Its docstring closes over *run-frame-state-before* and nothing else, precisely because a ViewCell registry was the subject. Reagent's component render queue and reagent-slim's dirty set are the HOST'S, not the substrate's — and the re-frame2 substrate these three adapters install has no cell registry of its own at all, delegating reactivity to ratoms and React hooks. A door that cannot drain the thing the law names is outside the law. That reading is consistent with rf2-cydkp rather than an extension of it, which is what makes it safe to rule at P4.

WHY THE 'AGAINST' READING DOES NOT WIN, and it is a real hazard rather than a bad argument. A test author who calls flush-views! from inside a dispatch-sync handler does get the torn read/render the guard exists to reject, and gets no diagnostic. I am ruling that this is acceptable, on the stance, and naming which clause does the work: TRUST THE PROGRAMMER, and reject nag-diagnostics at triage. The cost of the other way is enumerated on the bead and it is not a prose repair — a throw added to three SHIPPED adapters' test doors, plus contract tests, plus a spec/006 flush-render! amendment and a spec/009 row amendment — bought for a test-only hazard on a surface where nothing is broken today. That is the trade the stance exists to refuse.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: I am not ruling that the hazard is imaginary. It is real, small, and test-scoped.

THE REMEDY IS A SENTENCE, NOT A THROW. Add one line to each of the three adapters' flush-views! docstrings saying that it publishes a render phase and must not be called from inside a dispatch-sync handler. Say it; do not enforce it. That is the shape 'trust the programmer' asks for — tell the programmer the thing, and let them be an adult about it.

  implementation/adapters/reagent/...      flush-views!  -> (act (fn [] (reagent.core/flush)))
  implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/... flush-views!  -> (act (fn [] (batching/flush!)))
  implementation/adapters/uix/...          flush-views!  -> (act f)
Re-derive those three sites at the tip before editing — the bead read them at origin/main 7902167197 and that is a claim, not a finding.

NOTE reagent-slim's INTERNAL reagent2.dom.client/flush-views! one layer below the contract slot (goog.DEBUG-gated, Promise-returning, microtask -> act(batching/flush!) -> microtask). It is the closest living relative of the removed re-frame.ui.test/flush!, which DID call the guard. It is internal and not a contract slot, so this ruling does not reach it and it needs no change — recorded so the next reader does not mistake the omission for an oversight.

NO SPEC CHANGE IS REQUIRED. PR #8484 rewrote spec/006 §Render-batch finalization to state the registry-flush law POSITIVELY and deliberately said nothing about flush-views!'s membership, so this ruling lands without a revert and without an amendment. That was good foresight by that worker.

THIS BEAD CLOSES when the three docstring lines land. Dispatching that; it is small and touches no spec file, so it does not collide with the spec/ lane.

title: [spec-drift] 000-Vision teaches a six-tab roster via mnemonic keystrokes that were never wired - entangled with rf2-91dfb, needs one ruling not two edits
description:

  "deeper investigation is one tab away (`a` App-db · `v` Views ·
   `t` Trace · `m` Machines · `r` Routing)"

Present tense. TWO defects in one sentence, and they pull in opposite directions:

1. ROSTER: five/six entries where ten Dynamic tabs ship (focus.cljc valid-panels). Missing Resources (s), Graph (g), Frames (u), Hicasso (h).

2. Extending the parenthesis to ten mnemonics (`s` Resources · `g` Graph · `u` Frames · `h` Hicasso) would take a sentence that is wrong about five keys and make it wrong about ten - asserting MORE unwired keystrokes, which is precisely the reasoning rf2-v1fg3 used to leave 017:105 alone before #8435 ruled on it.

The same treatment 017 got: name the palette verb as the way to reach a tab, and let the mnemonics be described as tab LABELS/registry metadata (which they genuinely are - :mnem on each reg-l4-tab! entry, panel_registry.cljc:44) rather than as keys the user presses. Then the roster can be completed to ten without asserting anything false.

NOT URGENT (P4): 000-Vision is orienting prose, no gate reads it, and it is wrong in a direction that undersells rather than misleads about capability. But it should be done in ONE edit with the keystroke question settled, not two passes.

SEQUENCING: reads on rf2-91dfb having settled the palette-verb wording (#8435, merged 5b9540c5b4). That wording is now available to copy.

title: [chore] jvm-core-prod-gate's RF2_MIN_TESTS slack has drifted to 66, twice the ~33 the script mandates
description:
OBSERVED BY worker/claiming-sk5hf while running the lane for rf2-sk5hf. Not caused
by that work — it added zero tests to the lane.

  1986 tests / 8701 assertions.
  RF2_MIN_TESTS floor is 1920. Slack = 66.

scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh states the rule itself, twice. The floor stopped
being only a collapse detector at the seventh rf2-d2841 pass and became the BUDGET
FOR TAGGING: '^:requires-debug' is a var-level tag, one word in a test file, and
nothing else counts what it excluded, so the slack is what forces an author to come
to the reviewed file and move a number. The script sets that budget at ~33 and says
so: 'the rule to apply is not raise it when you add namespaces but keep the SLACK at
~33, and it wants checking whenever this lane's observed count is read, not only when
a d2841 pass lands.'

The eighth move (1900 -> 1920) was made for exactly this reason at 1953 observed. The
lane has since grown to 1986 on other beads' test files, so the tagging budget has
silently widened to 66 again — the same 'a floor left behind by a growing lane is
inert' failure arriving through the back door.

REPAIR: raise RF2_MIN_TESTS 1920 -> 1950 in scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh, and add a
NINTH MOVE note beside the eighth saying it is a budget repair rather than a pass
(tags nothing, adds no namespace). Re-read the observed count at the time rather than
trusting 1986 here.

TOUCHES scripts/test-core-prod-gate.sh only. Sequence against anything else editing
that file.

title: multi_substrate.cljs carries two independent copies of the substrate lookup and its diagnostic
description:
FOUND BY rf2-nfwbt's worker (2026-08-14) and deliberately not minted by it — reported instead, correctly.

THE DUPLICATION: multi_substrate.cljs has TWO independent copies of the substrate registry lookup and its 'is not registered' diagnostic — render-view carries one at lines 156/159, safe-render-cell carries a second at 238/245.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS: that duplication is EXACTLY WHY the existing :uix arms did not cover render-view. The tests drive multi-substrate-grid, which reaches safe-render-cell, which never calls render-view. So a reader — and the worker itself, on first pass — concludes the substrate is covered when only one of two copies is exercised.

A DUPLICATED CODE PATH IS A DUPLICATED COVERAGE QUESTION. Every test that exercises one copy reads as covering the surface, and nothing says which copy it reached. That is the same shape as the day's recurring theme: a passing test proves something about what it ran, and the interesting question is always what it did not.

SO THE JOB IS NOT SIMPLY 'DEDUPE'. Establish first whether the two copies are meant to differ — safe-render-cell may deliberately be more defensive than render-view. If they are meant to be the same, unify them; if not, say so and make the difference legible so the next reader does not mistake one for the other.

VERIFY AT SOURCE FIRST. Ten of my measurements or relayed claims were refuted today.
close_reason:
CLOSED via PR #8229 (worker/triage-z7cfs).

THE TWO COPIES ARE MEANT TO DIFFER, so they were NOT unified. They answer at
different levels and the difference is structural. `render-view` returns a
render RESULT — a fragment whose caller places it (the `render-variant` host
hook, via `render-decorated-view`) — so its miss degrades to a bare inline
`:div`, styled to match the missing-VIEW diagnostic `reagent-render` returns
twenty lines above it. `safe-render-cell` returns a whole grid CELL, chrome
included, so its miss must be a full `:error-cell` with a head and a body,
and it spends that body naming the `register-substrate!` call the author is
missing.

Neither can delegate to the other. Routing `render-view` through
`safe-render-cell` hands the host hook a red bordered cell it is not in a
grid to justify. Routing `safe-render-cell` through `render-view` makes its
`:error-cell` branch unreachable, taking the actionable remediation off the
canvas — and the error boundary needs `render-fn` closed over inside
`:reagent-render` regardless. Unifying would be a regression.

THE COVERAGE PREMISE WAS TRUE WHEN FILED AND IS NOW CLOSED. Commit
5b3adafadc ("test(story): recover the foreign-substrate render-view arm
(rf2-nfwbt)") — the same bead whose worker filed this one — added both
`render-view` arms to `story_multi_substrate_cljs_test.cljs` and recorded
the split in that namespace's comment block and in
`tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md` §`render-view` dispatch. Both copies
are exercised today.

WHAT REMAINED, AND WHAT THIS PR DID: the signal in the SOURCE. A reader
editing `render-view` consults neither the test namespace nor the coverage
table, so nothing on the page said a second lookup existed — which is the
hazard this bead named, and the one rf2-nfwbt's own worker tripped on first
pass. Both docstrings now name the sibling, the reason the two are kept
apart, and the coverage split that follows from it. Prose only: no behaviour
change, no test change, no new error id.

`re-frame.story-multi-substrate-cljs-test` +
`re-frame.story.ui.render-shell-cljs-test` exit 0 both states (20 tests, 45
assertions, 0 failures). Selector positive-controlled — a bogus namespace

title: hic: an UNRECOGNISED input type is a text field to the platform, and caret-type? still says no
description:
FOUND BY rf2-7ae61 while measuring the case fold, and filed with the argument FOR CLOSING IT already made — this may well be minutiae, and the mayor should be able to rule in one read rather than dispatching a hunt.

MEASURED, real Chromium 141, a live element per row (rf2-7ae61's scratch probe, 2026-08-14 18:50 AUSEST):

  attribute      .type      .selectionStart   setSelectionRange
  "bogus"        "text"     5                 ok
  ""             "text"     5                 ok
  "seach"        "text"     5                 ok      (a typo of "search")
  "TEXT"         "text"     5                 ok      (closed by rf2-7ae61)
  "number"       "number"   nil               InvalidStateError

THE MECHANISM. The HTML type attribute's INVALID VALUE DEFAULT is 'text',
so any unrecognised value produces a real text field with a real caret.
impl.controlled/caret-type? compares the author's prop against
caret-types #{text search url tel password}, so it answers no and the
same-turn converge is silently lost — the identical symptom rf2-7ae61
just closed for the case spelling, by the identical door.

WHY IT IS NOT THE SAME BEAD, and why the fold rf2-7ae61 landed does not
reach it. Folding case makes the predicate agree with the platform on
SPELLING. This is about RESOLUTION: agreeing with the platform here means
mapping every unrecognised value to "text" before the lookup, which is
a different rule and a real design question rather than a widening.

THE CASE FOR CLOSING IT AS MINUTIAE, which is the mayor's to weigh:
:type "TEXT" is a CORRECT, spec-valid authoring of a text input — the
author has no bug at all and silently loses a feature, which is what made
rf2-7ae61 worth its fold. :type "seach" is ALREADY an author error with
a visible symptom (they wanted a search field and got a plain one), and
the lost caret converge is the least of what is wrong with it. A
deliberately-unknown type is exotic. So the population this would serve
is 'authors who typo a type AND would notice the caret before they
noticed the wrong control', which may be empty.

THE OTHER ARM, if it is ruled IN: rather than resolving unknown to text,
INVERT the predicate to a deny-list of the caret-LESS types. That is the
same information from the other side and it fails safe in the opposite
direction — an unknown type gets the converge, which is what the platform
does. It is a larger, more brittle list, and the current allow-list is
exactly the HTML spec's selection-API list, which is why the code has the
shape it has.

NO ACTION WAS TAKEN. rf2-7ae61 was scoped to case and stayed there.
close_reason:
CLOSED — the filing worker's closing argument HOLDS at source. No code change.

THE VISIBLE-SYMPTOM TEST, checked rather than assumed. The predicate's
allow-list `#{text search url tel password}` (controlled.cljs:489) is a
verbatim citation of the HTML spec's list of input types the selection API
applies to, so for every RECOGNISED type the predicate is already correct;
the gap is unrecognised values only, where the invalid-value default is Text.
For every misspelling of a NON-text type the symptom is visible or caught:
`password` stops masking (glaring), `search` loses its clear affordance and
its searchbox role, `url`/`email` stop validating so the form submits bad
data, `number`/`date`/`range`/`color` lose their entire widget. The author
notices, and the lost caret converge is the least of what is wrong.

THE RESIDUE WHERE IT DOES NOT HOLD, which the bead did not name: an author
who intended `text` and misspelled THAT (`"tetx"`), or wrote `:type ""`.
There the invalid-value default coincides with intent — the field looks and
behaves exactly right and only the converge is lost, which IS the invisible
shape of the rf2-7ae61 uppercase bug. But reaching that residue requires
writing an explicit `:type "text"` at all, and that is redundant: omit
`:type` and `caret-type?`'s `(nil? t)` branch already answers true. So the
population is "authors who write a redundant explicit type AND fumble those
four letters", and unlike `:type "TEXT"` it is not correct authoring — it is
a typo the author owns. Thin enough to close.

Resolving unknown → `text` would be the library papering over a typo. We
trust the programmer.

A FINDING THAT REFINES THE BEAD'S ARM (b), and does not overturn it. The
bead rejects the deny-list inversion as "larger, more brittle". Larger, yes;
more brittle, no. `converge!` (controlled.cljs:468-475) reads the caret
TWICE and guards BOTH reads with `number?`, precisely because install!'s
props-time answer is one render stale by the time flushSync returns. So a
deny-list that went stale against a future caret-less type would be INERT —
wrapper installed, converge declines — not throwing. `caret-type?` is an
optimisation and a remount-avoidance choice, not the correctness gate; the
runtime guards are. Arm (b) is therefore SAFE. It is simply more code
carrying more of the platform's enumeration, and it trades a set that IS a
spec citation for a derived complement that must be maintained against
future HTML additions, to buy the converge for typo'd-`text` authors. Still
a bad trade for a masterpiece.

Finally, the narrowing is DOCUMENTED SUPPORT POLICY rather than an
oversight: `implementation/hicasso/testbed/spec.cjs` (~line 1141) states it
outright — "That is the support policy, and the narrowing is part of it
rather than a defect in it."

title: report-changed-surfaces.sh carries the same depth-100 cap under test.yml's fetch-depth: 0 -- third instance of the rf2-ihfw/rf2-4sl9 family

THE CALLER MAKES IT THE SAME DEFECT: test.yml's 'detect' job checks out at fetch-depth: 0 (test.yml:103) and then invokes this script (test.yml:130). So the cap discards precisely the history that checkout paid for -- 'git fetch --depth=N' converts a COMPLETE clone into a SHALLOW one. (portability.yml checks out at depth 2 and so must fetch its base by name; this job need not.)' The script it calls truncates that to 100 one line in.

title: codemod: subtree-has-reagent-call? counts inert forms, so a live crossing gets a spurious :as-element-island refusal
description:
Split out of rf2-xc11's repair (PR #8154), which fixed the [:>]-family SITE walk and deliberately went no further — the bead said do not broaden beyond that walk.

PROBE at PR #8154's tip:

  (cm/scan-string "(ns a (:require [reagent.core :as r]))\n[:> Foo {:x (comment (r/as-element [:div]))}]\n" "a.cljs")
  => [:as-element-island :computed-value]

The SITE is genuinely live and correctly reported. What is wrong is the extra :as-element-island refusal: rewrite/subtree-has-reagent-call? recurses through n/children without consulting rewrite/inert?, so an r/as-element inside a (comment ...) in a live site's props reads as an as-element island.

DIFFERENT POPULATION from rf2-xc11, which is why it was not folded in. rf2-xc11 is about which nodes are SITES; this is about a refusal REASON computed inside a site that is live either way. The shared predicate rewrite/inert? now exists (PR #8154 lifted it from census.clj), so the fix is likely one call in subtree-has-reagent-call?.

STAKE is a needless refusal, not a bad write: the tool declines to repair a site it could have handled, and the migrator is sent to hand-port something that does not need it. title: two copies of strip_inert/form_end after #8114 and #8120 both land
description:
SEQUENCED — do not dispatch until BOTH PR #8114 and PR #8120 have MERGED. #8114 is merged as of this filing; #8120 is open.

WHY THE DUPLICATE EXISTS, AND WHY IT WAS THE RIGHT CALL AT THE TIME. PR #8114 (rf2-t9kd) added a `strip_inert`/`form_end` pair to `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_example_fence_coverage.py` — the helper that stops a reader-discarded, quoted or `(comment …)` form counting as a live claim. PR #8120 (rf2-df9b, rf2-uyhh) needed the same pair for `check_optional_module_reachability.py`. Its worker COPIED rather than imported, and said why: #8114 was unmerged, so making the helper shared would have meant editing #8114's file and conflicting with it. That is the correct call under an unmerged sibling — the alternative is two workers editing one file.

THE ONE DIFFERENCE TO RECONCILE, recorded by that worker: the #8120 copy DROPS #8114's character-literal branches, because in `check_optional_module_reachability.py` the `code_only` chokepoint already removes character literals before `strip_inert` runs. So the two copies are not textually identical and a naive de-duplication would either reintroduce dead branches or remove live ones. Read both before merging them.

WHAT TO DECIDE, and it is a real decision rather than a foregone one: is a shared helper worth it for two callers? The stance rejects over-engineering, and a small duplicated pure function across two sibling scripts in the same directory is a defensible end state. A verified 'leave both, they are three lines and they differ for a reason' is a complete and good deliverable. Do not build a shared-utility module for two callers unless a third appears.

IF you do share it, the acceptance is that BOTH scripts' `--self-test` still pass plain AND still refuse under `python -O`, and that each still reds on its own fault while keeping its legitimate case green. Those four assertions per script are the contract; a checker that reds on everything satisfies half of it and is useless.

GATE: `npm run test:hicasso-invariants` carries the fence checker; `npm run test:hicasso-lint` carries `check_lint_export` and is NOT in the invariants chain — that distinction was measured by #8120's worker, so run both.
close_reason: REFUSED, and the refusal is the deliverable — PR #8137 (commit a975c36237, rebased). Decided NOT to share the helper, for four reasons verified at source rather than argued: (1) the copies are not the same function — #8120's worker's justification holds, check_optional_module_reachability.py:311-314 (code_only) emits a space for a backslash and skips two, so no character literal survives to reach strip_inert, which is why its copies correctly drop the three char-literal branches the fence-coverage copies need; a naive merge would reintroduce dead branches or remove live ones. (2) Reconciling that difference needs a flag argument on a twenty-line pure function — worse than the duplication it removes. (3) Duplication is this directory's architecture, not drift: all six checkers are self-contained single files with no cross-imports and no package, and self_test()/main() are each duplicated SIX times over. (4) The docstrings are the larger half and are per-gate specific; a shared helper would genericise them into uselessness. Per the stance: no shared-utility module for two callers unless a third appears. What landed instead is a cross-reference in each copy's docstring so the next reader finds a documented decision rather than an apparent accident and does not re-file this — no behaviour change. Four-assertions-per-script contract measured and holding: both --self-tests pass plain (exit 0) and correctly refuse under python -O (exit 1). Gates: test:hicasso-invariants exit 0 and test:hicasso-lint exit 0, both re-run post-rebase; gate provenance proved by a planted fault (#_ -> #~PLANTED) that reddened at exit 1 naming this worktree, then reverted with the restore verified by git hash-object. title: measurement: no committed dataset records a :clock-resolution, so the 100us clamp is an uncited constant
description:
A GAP IN THE MEASUREMENT RIG'S OWN PROVENANCE, found while rf2-hic-081 was killing the self-time receipt field.

That kill turns on ONE NUMBER: Chrome clamps performance.now() to 100 microseconds. The spike used it correctly and reached the right verdict — but it had to CITE the figure from this repo's instrument rather than take it, BECAUSE NO COMMITTED DATASET CARRIES A :clock-resolution RECORD.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The clamp is the denominator of every timing decision this project makes: it is what says whether a quantity is measurable at all. A rig that measures durations but never records the resolution of the clock it measured them with cannot answer "was this measurable?" from its own data — the answer has to come from outside, from a number somebody remembers. The project spends its days hunting instruments that verify the ABSENCE of bad news rather than the PRESENCE of good news; an unrecorded resolution is the same shape, one level down.

SCOPE, AND KEEP IT SMALL: have the measurement lane record the observed clock resolution alongside the runs it takes, so future datasets carry their own denominator. This is a field on data the rig already produces, NOT a new instrument, NOT a new gate, and NOT a re-measurement of anything already published.

DO NOT let this grow. It does not want a checker, a threshold, or a refusal arm. If recording it turns out to need a rig change rather than a field, say so and stop — that is a different and larger bead.

Note the sequencing constraint that applies to all measurement work here: the operator authorises windows only on a QUIET MACHINE. This bead is a recording change, not a window, so it does not need one — but if it cannot be verified without taking a measurement, it inherits the quiet-machine hold and must say so rather than measuring on a busy box.
close_reason:
PREMISE PARTLY FALSE, RESIDUAL GAP FIXED AS A FIELD. PR #7879 (worker/clockres-dzus). Two of the bead's three claims do not survive contact with the tree; the third does, and was a two-line serialisation defect.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE.

(1) The 100us figure is NOT uncited. docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-candidates-clock.md S2.1 -- 'The resolution figures, verified rather than remembered' -- is a table quoting each figure with its primary source, checked 2026-08-01: Chrome for Developers 'Aligning timers with cross origin isolation restrictions' and MDN Performance.now S Security requirements, with the 5us cross-origin-isolated alternative beside it. the-clock-behind-the-published-rows.md S6 goes further and names the Chromium constant itself: time_clamper.h, kCoarseResolutionMicroseconds = 100 / kFineResolutionMicroseconds = 5, plus W3C High Resolution Time's coarsen-time algorithm. That is the strongest citation form this project asks for.

(2) A committed dataset DOES record a measured clock resolution. clock_run.cjs:1414/3008 serialises 'granularity' -- the sorted distinct non-zero per-sample deltas, whose minimum it prints as the row's grain -- and 16 of the 38 committed dataset files carry it (clock-0qj9w run1-2, clock-emvod run1-8, clock-w3yxd run1-6). Verified by reading the JSON: clock-emvod/run1 M1 min 0.107 ms, keystroke 0.152; clock-w3yxd/run1 bulk100 0.094; clock-0qj9w/run1 M1 0.085. the-candidates-clock.md's published range '0.092-0.153 ms over ~980 distinct values per row' recomputes from those files, which is exactly the property the bead says is missing.

(3) The in-page clock's grain is already measured in the run it governs, by name. hd8_rows/clock-resolution! + hd8_app.cljs:225 (record! :clock-resolution clock), built as rf2-d2tzk for this bead's own stated reason. rf2-hic-081 knew this -- its verdict text names the function.

WHY THE SPIKE STILL HAD TO CITE RATHER THAN TAKE, and why no field would have changed that: taking the number needs a browser run on a QUIET BOX, which the spike correctly refused (Processor Queue Length peaked at 3). A :clock-resolution field in a committed dataset would have left it citing somebody else's run on somebody else's box, one indirection further away. The denominator that governs a measurement has to be taken in the run it governs -- which is rf2-d2tzk's ruling, already implemented. This was a quiet-machine constraint, not a recording gap.

WHAT WAS TRUE, AND IS NOW FIXED. hd8_clock_run.cjs and shapes/census_clock_run.cjs both MEASURE the grain ('if (d.task > 0) granularity.add(d.task)', on the PUBLISHED raw TaskDuration) and both PRINT it, and neither KEPT it -- datasetFor dropped the set. Both took their contract from clock_run.cjs, which keeps it; this is the part they did not inherit. Same species as rf2-jo60g (blocksDecomp collected then dropped at write time), same remedy: ONE FIELD on data the run already produces. Nothing measured changes; nothing is backfilled; the grain travels with the next canonical run.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY -- and this is the rig-change line the bead asked me to draw. The IN-PAGE performance.now() grain is still in no committed dataset, because the lane that measures it (hd8_app.cljs, driven by hd8_run.cjs) WRITES NO DATASET FILE AT ALL -- its :clock-resolution goes to console EDN and window.HD8_RESULTS. Giving it one is a destination/publication/canonical discipline plus its coverage in clock_exit_path.test.cjs (~5,800 lines pinning exactly that for the lanes that do write). That is a rig change, not a field, and it is a different and larger bead. I did not start it. Filing it is not obviously worth it: no published figure depends on the in-page clock any more (the mount-gate amendment, rf2-2rtt6.1, demoted the in-page window to DIAGNOSTIC), and hd8_clock_app.cljs measures MOUNT ONLY precisely because rf2-d2tzk found the bulk floor sitting on the clamp.

GATES, run alone, exit captured on the same line: npm run test:script-helpers exit 0 (clock_exit_path.test.cjs: 375 passed) and npm run test:script-policy exit 0. That is the gate for this surface -- one step of test.yml:3000 and of scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1355. check_fast_pr_gap.py --list: 96 required checks the spine does not decide, none reachable from a three-file .cjs diff. The three new tests are MUTATION-PROVEN: deleting the two serialised lines gives 3/375 failed naming exactly those three, exit 1; restored, exit 0. No measurement taken -- the tests drive datasetFor on a fixture row, so the busy box was never an obstacle.

INCIDENTAL FINDING FOR rf2-w8pz (do not action from here). That bead's mayor note asserts hd8_rows.cljs is 'in the frozen bench tree, kept verbatim by a hash manifest'. It is not. implementation/hicasso/frozen-sources.edn carries exactly ONE row -- front/slot.cljc -- after three recorded retirements. Its premise that an edit there 'moves a hash the freeze gate checks' is false, so the cannot-fix escape it offers is not available; the bead should be decided on its own merits (the wiki-link is prose, and closing it as not-worth-fixing still looks right).

title: core: the release bundle embeds the build machine's absolute filesystem path
description:

THE OBSERVATION, measured while scanning the release bundle: out/hicasso-release/main.js carries THE ABSOLUTE FILESYSTEM PATH OF THE BUILD MACHINE, three times. It arrives via core's production registration coordinates — prod-coords-form keeps :file and :line and drops only :column — so every reg-sub and reg-event in a release build embeds its source path.

WHY IT MAY MATTER, stated without overclaiming: a release artefact that is not path-independent differs between build machines even when the inputs are identical. That defeats byte-comparable builds, leaks a developer's directory layout into shipped bytes, and makes any future "same inputs, same output" check impossible to satisfy. None of that is broken today — nothing depends on reproducibility yet — which is exactly why this is filed rather than fixed.

THE QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, before any change: is the absolute path DELIBERATE? The coordinate machinery is core's design and it drops :column on purpose, which suggests the retained fields were chosen rather than left over. Read core's prod-coords-form and whatever spec governs it. If the path is wanted — for stack-trace mapping, say — then the answer is to record why, not to strip it.

IF IT IS NOT WANTED: the smallest fix is a repo-relative path, which preserves whatever diagnostic value the coordinate has while removing the machine dependence. Do NOT strip the coordinate entirely without establishing that nothing reads it; hic-007's source-coordinate work is recent and deliberate, and its production-elision gates are the thing that would notice.

FENCE: this is a CORE surface, not hicasso. Do not touch implementation/hicasso/**. spec/* is hot zone. If the change reaches a shipped facade or a coordinate contract, STOP and report rather than taking it.

CONTEXT: found because the erasure worker needed to know whether a filename sentinel could be used to prove defview/defhost coordinates are elided. It cannot — consumer_app.cljs appears three times in a GREEN bundle from these very coordinates, so a filename sentinel there would be red on a correct build. title: hic: the complaint-catalogue self-test leads with a Python traceback instead of its own failure report
description:
