MEASURING WHETHER A WORKER IS ALIVE: compare the TIP REVISION ID, never a commit count (2026-08-13, corrected same day by an audit).

BE PRECISE ABOUT WHICH COUNT — the first version of this memory was wrong and the error reached main:
  git rev-list --count <branch>              counts EVERY reachable commit. Measured 21677.
                                             REBASING ONTO AN ADVANCED TRUNK MAKES THIS GROW. Not invariant.
  git rev-list --count origin/main..<branch> the AHEAD count. Measured 3.
                                             INVARIANT under rebase — the same commits are replayed.

The ahead count is the one a mayor naturally reads, and it is the one that misleads.

WHAT MOVES AND WHAT DOES NOT, under rebase:
  ahead count        NO
  %ar author date    NO
  %cr committer date YES
  tip revision id    YES

So record the tip id each tick and compare ids. Committer date is a usable second signal.

AN UNCHANGED TIP AUTHORISES NOTHING ON ITS OWN. That half is load-bearing: it is what stopped a healthy worker being called stranded across two ticks. The next step after an unchanged tip is to MESSAGE, and the reply shape is the real read — 'queued for delivery' means alive, 'had no active task; resumed from transcript' means idle.

SECOND TRAP IN THE SAME MEASUREMENT: do NOT read FETCH_HEAD after a fetch whose exit code you suppressed. Linked worktrees share one .git and therefore one FETCH_HEAD, so a raced or failed fetch leaves a stale value that reads as fresh. Prefer 'git ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/worker/*' — one command, no shared state, no exit code to check.

WHEN TWO AGENTS DISAGREE ABOUT A COMMIT'S AGE, suspect two clocks before suspecting an error. One reported 75 seconds where another read 43 minutes; one read committer date, the other author date. Neither misread.

WORKER LIVENESS (Windows mayor loop): TaskList can return 'No tasks found' for background agents launched in a PRIOR turn even while they are actively running, AND their output-file mtime does NOT advance during a run (transcript flush is buffered). Both gave false 'dead' signals — a realm worker that TaskList showed as absent + mtime static for 9min actually completed a 624s run. NEVER infer a worker is dead from TaskList/mtime; NEVER recycle/--force-remove a worker's worktree on that basis (it clobbers live workers mid-edit). The ONLY reliable liveness signal is the completion/kill <task-notification>. To recycle, wait for that notification or confirm via a pushed branch with the expected commits.

Background workers and review agents MUST NOT create, claim, or close beads. Beads are mayor action only — filing them makes the mayor think they own the work. Worker outputs go in chat and ai/findings/ (local). Use background workers freely for parallel drafts/research; never bd create for that.

Worker node_modules junction destroyed the mayor's real node_modules AGAIN (2026-07-31, rf2-2rtt6.8 / PR #7311). A worker worktree with no node_modules cannot compile; the established repo convention (a live sibling worktree had exactly this) is a Windows junction: cmd /c mklink /J <wt>/implementation/node_modules <mayor>/implementation/node_modules. That works for the build, and then post-merge hygiene ran git worktree remove, which FOLLOWED the junction and emptied the mayor's REAL implementation/node_modules to 0 entries - breaking every local build in the repo. Repair is cheap and deterministic: cd <mayor>/implementation && npm ci (exit 0, restores the canary 101 entries; verify react + shadow-cljs are present). TWO fixes, both needed: (1) the WORKER should cmd /c rmdir the junction as its last act before reporting done, not leave it for hygiene; (2) HYGIENE must cmd /c rmdir <wt>/implementation/node_modules BEFORE git worktree remove, and re-check the mayor canary (~101) after each removal batch. This is the second recorded instance of the same class.

Worker path-leak mechanism (CONFIRMED 2026-07-17, rf2-r09qj + flagged by rf2-klyw5): a subagent that Reads MAYOR-checkout absolute paths during exploration can have its SUBSEQUENT Edit tool-calls carry that mayor path — so edits land in the mayor checkout, NOT the worktree. Invisible in the worker's OWN git status (the worktree looks clean); visible only from the mayor side. MITIGATION that works: the boundary-block's post-write BOTH-TREES check catches it — the worker self-recovers (git checkout-restore the mayor file, copy completed work into the worktree, verify mayor clean). HARDEN BRIEFS: instruct workers to Read AND Edit only worktree-absolute paths (never the mayor checkout, even for exploration reads), re-verify rev-parse per edit, and run the both-trees check after the first edit + any new file. Mayor-side detection: 'git status --short | grep -v .beads' in the mayor checkout should be empty; a stray modified file there = a live leak (capture the diff, don't blind-revert if the worker may be mid-recovery). This is a REAL Agent-subagent mechanism, distinct from the Workflow args-undefined misdiagnosis.

Worker PR-creation hang gotcha (2026-06-09): a worker (B6/vzld77) completed + committed + pushed its work, then hung ~1h LOOPING on 'gh pr create' with a heredoc body containing backticks/parens (bash kept mis-parsing). Mayor salvaged by opening the PR from the pushed branch. LESSON: in worker briefs, tell workers to create the PR with a SIMPLE body or '--body-file', avoid backticks/parens/heredocs in the inline body; and if a worker is committed+pushed but PR-less + idle, the mayor can open the PR for it (git -C <wt> push; gh pr create --head <branch>) rather than killing the work.

worker/receipts-hic081 IS NOT STRANDED -- do not delete it, and do not re-file it as hygiene residue (rf2-fuuqd, triaged 2026-08-15).

It is a DELIBERATELY RETAINED spike record. rf2-hic-081 ('Spike: capability receipts') closed with the verdict SPLIT and its close reason ends: 'Spike commits are pushed on worker/receipts-hic081 and retained as the experiment's record; nothing from them lands on main.' The 3 commits are pushed, have no PR and never will -- that is the design, not an oversight.

The conclusions are fully promoted and verified on main: the capability-receipt DESIGN is in docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md, decision-brief.md and lanes/left-field-ideas.md (rf2-eoo9, PR #7898); the erasure-gate reachability rule is in check_production_erasure.cjs and siblings (rf2-nkr3, PR #7878); impl/receipt.cljs is correctly ABSENT from main.

THE GENERAL LESSON for the hygiene loop: 'pushed + unlanded + no PR' is a heuristic, not a verdict. Before filing a branch as stranded, check whether a CLOSED bead retained it on purpose -- spike branches are the class where the finding lands on main and the diff deliberately never does.

Worker recovery hazard (learned 2026-06-22, the #4910/#4913 xray-testbeds incident): (1) A worker coming to rest is NOT proof it finished. The xray-testbeds worker came to rest waiting on a gate it launched; the mayor misjudged it as done, committed its UNCOMMITTED partial work as a recovery PR (#4910) — but it had not yet written standard_epochs/core.cljs, so #4910 merged an incomplete state that crashed the two-frame surface on load and left a red gate on main. RULE: only recover/commit a worker's work after a genuine final report with a PR URL; an idle worktree mid-task is not a completion signal. (2) NEVER git worktree remove --force a worktree whose worker may still be live — it destroyed the live worker's workspace AND emptied the mayor implementation/node_modules via the node_modules junction cascade (the worker had to npm install to restore the mayor tree). RULE: only remove a worktree for a worker that has genuinely completed (final report received); the junction-rmdir-before-remove step does not protect against removing a still-active worktree.

"WORKTREE-LOCAL" IS ONLY HALF THE RULE FOR WORKER SCRATCH FILES — IT MUST ALSO BE GITIGNORED (2026-08-09).

THE SEQUENCE. Earlier in the day two concurrent workers overwrote each other's helper files and PR-body drafts in the SHARED scratchpad, and one nearly published another bead's PR body. The fix put into later briefs was "write every file you create inside your own worktree". Both workers complied exactly. Both worktrees then REFUSED to reap: REMOVE_REFUSED_DIRTY, each holding one untracked pr-body-<bead>.md that the disposability classifier will not accept as build output.

SO THE TWO HAZARDS TRADE OFF AND THE BRIEF MUST CLOSE BOTH. dispatch-prompt-template.md already says it: put EVERY gate artefact where git ignores it, and warns that one leftover is enough to make a tree unreapable (nine accumulated that way once). The ignored extensions are *.log, *.exit and *-exit.txt. A file named pr-body-something.md is worktree-local, safe from collision, and still blocks the reap.

THE COMPLETE INSTRUCTION FOR A DISPATCH BRIEF: write every file you create inside your own worktree AND give it an ignored name (*.log / *.exit), or delete it before you report done. Never a shared temp directory; never an unignored leftover.

RESOLVING IT WHEN IT HAPPENS IS CHEAP BUT MUST NOT BE BLIND. --dry-run prints each offending path tagged [KEEP] or [build output]; a PR-body draft whose content is already published on the merged PR is genuinely disposable, so --force is correct AFTER looking. Do not reach for --force-disposable (it refuses anything not recognised as build output) and never spray a blanket --force across a sweep list: when that guard was written, one worktree held four analysis files for an OPEN bead and three others carried uncommitted source and doc edits.

A WORKTREE YOU DID NOT EXPLICITLY DISPATCH MAY BE YOUR OWN WORKER SPAWNING A SECOND WORKTREE — not a concurrent session. Misdiagnosed 2026-07-24. I dispatched a 4-bead cluster to ONE worker; it did 3 beads in worktree A (PR one) then created worktree B for the 4th bead (PR two). My hygiene scan found worktree B, had no record of creating it, and I concluded a concurrent session was also dispatching workers. WRONG — it was my own worker branching per bead. THE COST: the false belief made me over-cautious about that surface being externally contested. THE DISCRIMINATOR before concluding concurrent-session: a branch named worker/<desc>-<beadid> whose bead you assigned to a live worker IS that worker, even as a second worktree. Check worker completion reports and open PRs first — a worker report names every worktree and PR it created. Track by BEAD ownership (who did I give this bead to), never by worktree count: one worker is NOT necessarily one worktree or one PR. The genuinely-separate process here (the pr-audit loop) FILES beads, it does not dispatch code-editing workers, so it never contests a code surface. No harm done — I correctly did not touch the worktree or re-dispatch the bead.

A WORKER STRANDS BY ENDING ITS TURN ON A BACKGROUNDED GATE, AND IT WILL DO IT REPEATEDLY UNLESS THE BRIEF SAYS HOW TO WAIT. Observed again 2026-08-08 on rf2-2rtt6.142, twice in a row after a resume.

THE SHAPE. A gate exceeds the tool's foreground time ceiling. The worker detaches it — correctly — and then ENDS ITS TURN "waiting" for a completion notification. Nothing is guaranteed to wake it. It reports "still progressing, continuing to wait", the turn ends, and the same thing happens on the next nudge. The work is usually fine; only the waiting is broken.

WHAT DOES NOT FIX IT: telling the worker again that gates must be foreground. It already believes that, which is exactly why it detached and then waited politely. The instruction it is missing is what to do INSTEAD of waiting.

WHAT FIXES IT — put this in every brief, not just the ones with long gates:
  "If a gate exceeds the tool's time ceiling, run it detached and BLOCK ON IT INSIDE THE SAME TURN by polling its exit file in a loop. Never end a turn with a gate outstanding."
and give the literal shape:
  for i in $(seq 1 240); do [ -f gate-<id>.exit ] && break; sleep 15; done; cat gate-<id>.exit

TWO RIDERS THAT MATTER AS MUCH AS THE LOOP:
- The detached invocation must use an ABSOLUTE path to the gate script. These scripts derive their repo root from BASH_SOURCE, and a relative invocation that gets detached adopts whatever cwd the shell really has — one did that inside ANOTHER live worker's checkout and produced a complete, internally consistent verdict about somebody else's diff. Check the run's "gate root:" first line names your own worktree.
- If the invocation writes no exit file at all, that is the real defect, not the waiting. Re-run as: sh <ABS>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh > g.log 2>&1; echo "$?" > g.exit

MAYOR-SIDE RECOVERY, cheap and reliable: check the ground truth yourself rather than nudging twice. `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` and a remote-vs-local sha comparison in the worktree tell you whether the work is durable; `ls *.log *.exit` plus the log's mtime tell you whether the gate is genuinely still running or dead. On this occasion the work was already committed AND pushed, so nothing was at risk — the only outstanding step was reading an exit code.

DO NOT MISREAD THE SPINE LOG WHILE CHECKING. test-fast-pr.sh prints lines like "ok  unexpected extra dependency -> FAILED" from a negative-test harness confirming its own mutations fail correctly. Those are PASSES. The verdict is the echoed exit code, never a line in the log.

WORKER TRAP — git mv then edit (2026-07-25, found by the misc-cluster-a worker on PR #6946): after 'git mv old.cljc new_cljs_test.cljc', a subsequent 'git add <path>' does NOT pick up content edits made after the mv. The worker's first pushed commit therefore carried the RENAMED file with the OLD ns name still inside it — a commit that would not compile. It was caught only by noticing a stray 'M' in git status, then fixed by rebuilding both commits from the base and force-pushing with --force-with-lease. This is the exact shape of the rf2-dn6v7 / rf2-lgozq lane-suffix work (rename file + edit ns in one change), so it will recur. Put in briefs for any rename-plus-edit bead: after a git mv, re-run 'git add' on the path AFTER the content edit, and verify with 'git diff --cached' that BOTH the rename and the content change are staged before committing; a rename-only commit of a .cljc test file is a non-compiling commit.

A FRESH WORKER WORKTREE CANNOT RUN THE FAST-PR SPINE'S NODE TIER WITHOUT THE node_modules JUNCTION (measured 2026-08-13).

A worker on a clean worktree captured exit 1 at 'FAIL CLJS node integration' with 'Cannot find module shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js'. Nothing in its diff could reach shadow-cljs resolution. THE CAUSE WAS THE MISSING implementation/node_modules. Creating the junction turned the SAME spine green with no source change.

SO THE BRIEF'S INSTRUCTION 'run scripts/test-fast-pr.sh' IS INCOMPLETE for a doc-only worker that never expected to need npm. The failure looks like a real red, and a worker that trusts it will hunt a defect that does not exist - or worse, report a red PR as blocked.

SAY THIS IN BRIEFS THAT NOMINATE THE SPINE: if the node tier fails on module resolution, create the implementation/node_modules junction, re-run, and REMOVE THE LINK with cmd /c rmdir as your last act. Never a recursive delete - it follows the junction and empties the mayor's real tree, which has happened twice. Re-verify the canary with the script's own instrument either side.

THE SAME WORKER ALSO HIT THE HARNESS-DISAGREEMENT TRAP ON THAT RUN, which is the sixteenth observed instance: the harness reported 'completed (exit code 0)' while the runner's own .exit file read 1. It quoted the file. Had it trusted the harness it would have shipped a red spine as green. EVERY observed disagreement so far has surfaced as a harness-reported 0.

A FRESH WORKER WORKTREE HAS NO `implementation/node_modules`, AND THE SPINE FAILS ENVIRONMENTALLY THERE — the harness then misreports it (2026-08-11, rf2-gxry).

WHAT HAPPENED. A worker ran `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` in a newly-created worktree. It captured exit **1** on `CLJS node integration`, with `Cannot find module 'shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js'` — nothing compiled, because the worktree had no `node_modules`. **The harness announced "completed (exit code 0)" against that captured 1.** The worker junctioned `node_modules` at the mayor's real one, deleted the stale `.exit` and `.log`, re-ran the gate whole, and captured **0** with `[:node-test] Build completed. (2307 files, 2306 compiled, 0 warnings)`.

THE HAZARD IS NOT THE FAILURE, IT IS THE SHAPE OF IT. A missing-module error is not a test failure, but it PRESENTS as a red gate, and if a worker reads the harness's number instead of the captured one it presents as a GREEN gate over a build that never ran. Both readings are wrong in opposite directions, and the second is the dangerous one: a green that compiled nothing.

WHAT TO PUT IN A BRIEF for any worker that will run a compiling gate:
  - A fresh worktree has NO `implementation/node_modules`. If a gate needs one, create the junction to the mayor's real tree, and REMOVE THE LINK (never its target) as your last act — a later `git worktree remove` follows it and empties the shared tree. Canary the mayor's count before and after.
  - `Cannot find module` or `command not found` from a gate is ENVIRONMENTAL, not a verdict. Fix the environment and RE-RUN THE GATE WHOLE. Do not report the first number, and do not report it as a failure of the diff.
  - DELETE the stale `.exit` and `.log` before the re-run. A stale `.exit` survives the next run's `>` on its log, so the pair can disagree and the older verdict is the one you quote.

TWELFTH SIGHTING TODAY of the harness reporting a captured 1 as exit 0. The rule stands and is now in the method: THE NUMBER YOU QUOTE IS THE ONE YOU CAPTURED.

Worker worktrees have NO node_modules, so browser/shadow-cljs gates cannot run there by default. Do NOT junction into the mayor checkout's node_modules to fix it — that is the configuration that destroyed the mayor's real node_modules once and nearly again. THE SAFE ANSWER IS `npm ci` INSIDE THE WORKTREE (one worker did exactly this today, exit 0, no junction created, canary unmoved). Cost is a few minutes; the alternative is deferring every browser gate to CI. Put this in any brief whose gate menu includes `npm run test:browser`, a shadow-cljs build, or an adapter testbed spec.cjs — otherwise the worker hits 'shadow-cljs is not recognized', concludes the gate is unrunnable, and defers coverage that actually matters (the real-DOM gate catches repaint bugs test:cljs structurally cannot see). Related: [[windows-junction-detection-two-wrong-answers-before-the]].

Workers can get stuck in a monitor-wait loop on slow test suites (rul3ov burned ~770K tokens over 3 segments re-arming a Monitor for the full CLJS conformance run before committing). Recovery: SendMessage the agentId with a firm 'do NOT arm another Monitor — commit FIRST, push, gh pr create NOW; CI runs the full suite so CI is the gate, not your local terminal.' Over-cautious 'won't PR until local green' is the anti-pattern; the PR's CI is the real gate.

CONCURRENT WORKERS SHARE THE SESSION SCRATCHPAD AND OVERWRITE EACH OTHER'S FILES — including PR bodies (2026-08-09).

WHAT HAPPENED. Six workers ran in parallel on the hic-* Wave A set. The rf2-hic-004 worker reported that its verify.py and pr-body.md were BOTH overwritten mid-run by the rf2-hic-005 worker. Same filenames, same shared scratchpad directory. Its PR body survived only because gh had already read the file before the overwrite landed. A slower run would have published another bead's PR body under its own PR number.

WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT COVER IT. The brief said 'use worktree-local log paths', and every worker complied FOR GATE LOGS — they all wrote gate-slugs.log inside their own worktree. The collision was in the HELPER FILES nobody thought to fence: scratch scripts, PR-body drafts, temp verification output. The known hazard was written narrowly as a gate-log hazard; it is really a shared-temp-directory hazard and applies to every file a worker writes outside its worktree.

THE FIX FOR FUTURE BRIEFS. Say: write EVERY file you create - gate logs, helper scripts, PR-body drafts, scratch output - inside your own worktree, never in a shared temp or scratchpad directory. If you must use a shared directory, prefix every filename with your bead id.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A WRONG GATE LOG. A clobbered gate log yields a plausible-but-wrong exit code, which the echo-the-exit-code rule catches. A clobbered PR body is published verbatim to GitHub under the wrong PR and nothing checks it.

THREE WORKERS IN ONE NIGHT STALLED WAITING FOR A "COMPLETION NOTIFICATION" THAT DOES NOT EXIST (2026-08-10).

WHAT THEY EACH DID. rf2-8a6s: "Still running. I'll stop here and resume when the watcher fires - no more polling." rf2-hic-009: "The spine is still running ... I have a waiter armed on its exit code and will report the moment it lands." rf2-hic-016: "The fast-PR spine is still running; I'll wait for its completion notification rather than end the turn" - and then the turn ended. All three had briefs that said, in terms, run gates in the foreground to completion and never background one.

THE BELIEF IS SPECIFIC AND WRONG, WHICH IS WHY THE EXISTING WORDING DOES NOT PREVENT IT. They do not think they are abandoning the task. They think a watcher/notification will wake them. Nothing does. A stopped subagent resumes ONLY when the mayor sends it a message, and the mayor only knows to because the completion report reads oddly. "Run gates in the foreground" does not contradict the belief - a worker can believe it ran the gate in the foreground AND that something will tell it the answer later.

THE WORDING THAT ADDRESSES THE BELIEF, not the behaviour: "There is no completion notification. No watcher wakes a stopped worker. If you end your turn waiting for a gate, the task stops until a human notices. Run the gate in the foreground, block on it, read its exit code yourself. A long foreground gate is fine; an unfinished turn is not."

THE REAL COST IS UNPUSHED WORK, AND IT VARIES. rf2-8a6s had committed AND pushed - fully durable, only the PR was missing. rf2-hic-009 had pushed and opened a PR - only the spine result and PR body were missing. rf2-hic-016 had THREE COMMITS AND HAD NOT PUSHED - one lost worktree from losing an entire three-engine browser suite. So the recovery order is: check `git log origin/main..HEAD` and `git ls-remote` FIRST, and if it is unpushed, make PUSH step 1 of the resume message before anything else.

RECOVERY IS CHEAP AND RELIABLE: SendMessage to the agent id resumes it from its transcript with full context. All three resumed and continued correctly. Do not re-dispatch a fresh worker - it would redo work that is already committed.

DETECTION: a completion report that says "still running", "I'll report when", "waiting for", or "watcher armed" is a stall, not a status. Treat it as a resume trigger immediately, and check push state before replying.

Workers strand because the long gate outlives their TURN budget, not because they disobeyed 'run foreground'. Three workers in one session (dispatch-sync, ci-test-lanes, tags-ratchet) ended their turn mid-gate with 'Waiting on the spine/watcher' — commits pushed, NO PR, nothing mergeable. A brief that says 'run test-fast-pr.sh foreground to completion, THEN open the PR' makes stranding likely on a loaded box, because the spine can exceed the budget. BETTER BRIEF ORDER: commit -> run only the FOCUSED, fast, arm-specific gates (plus any non-vacuity/mutation proof, which is cheap and is the evidence that actually matters) -> OPEN THE PR -> name the slow gates as 'deferred to CI' in the ## Quality gates section. CI runs the same surface and IS the merge gate; the local spine never was. Recovery is SendMessage-resume, which works and keeps the worker's context.

Workflow rule (Mike, 2026-06-10): beads marked in_progress are LOCKED - never update their title/description/notes/scope (a worker is executing against them). To add findings or scope to in-progress work, CREATE A FOLLOW-UP BEAD (dep on the in-progress one if sequenced). Check status with bd show before any bd update.

`git worktree add` CAN BE KILLED BY THE HARNESS FOREGROUND TIMEOUT MID-CHECKOUT, LEAVING A STALE LOCK (2026-08-11; hit by two workers in one tick).

This repo's checkout is ~5308 files, and a fresh `git worktree add` can exceed the harness's 2-minute foreground limit. When it is killed partway (~25% in one observed case) it leaves BOTH a stale `.git/worktrees/<name>/index.lock` AND a `locked` marker reading `initializing`. The worktree exists, is registered, and is unusable; the guard script fails.

RECOVERY, in this order:
1. remove `.git/worktrees/<name>/index.lock`
2. `git reset --hard HEAD` from inside the worktree, BACKGROUNDED - it re-runs the full checkout and took ~9 minutes on this box
3. `git worktree unlock <path>`
Then the worker guard passes normally.

PUT THE MITIGATION IN THE DISPATCH BRIEF: every brief I write opens with `git worktree add`, so this is a first-command failure that costs a worker ten minutes before it has done anything. Tell workers to run the create BACKGROUNDED by absolute path and poll, exactly as they are already told to do for the 25-minute test spine - the same 10-minute ceiling applies to it and nobody expects it to.

Two workers hit this in a single tick (thirdsite-fbi4 and presence-5gka), so it is not rare. Both recovered without data loss, and both reported it rather than silently retrying - which is what made it diagnosable.

Worktree cleanup: a directory can be REUSED and re-pointed at a different branch mid-session, so a name-based safe-list goes stale while you are acting on it. Observed live: a hygiene agent was handed 'ci-test-lanes-cluster - safe to remove, PR #7116 merged', but between the list being written and the removal, a worker reused that same directory on a NEW branch (worker/xray-fuzzy-regression-pin) carrying an open PR #7119. Removing by name would have destroyed an in-flight PR worktree. Re-read `git worktree list --porcelain` IMMEDIATELY BEFORE each removal and re-verify the branch AND its PR state at that moment; never trust a safe-list compiled minutes earlier. Corollary: 'PR merged' is a fact about a BRANCH, not about a DIRECTORY. Related: [[rebase-merge-makes-a-worker-branch-look-unmerged]].

Worktree hygiene: `git status` ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH to decide whether a worktree holds work. The `/ai/` tree is GITIGNORED, so findings docs, gate logs, PR-body drafts and ad-hoc probes are INVISIBLE to git status — a worktree that looks pristine can hold real content. Sweep `ai/` (and any `.worker-logs/`, `.wt-logs/`) separately and READ any non-log file before discarding. Observed: three worktrees held hidden content (20 gate logs, a pr-body.md draft, an ad-hoc probe .clj) — all correctly judged residue, but only because they were looked at. Corollary for the other direction: a hygiene brief that says 'clean tree = safe to remove' is wrong on this repo.

THE 'NEVER WRITE THE WORKTREE PATH INTO A COMMITTED FILE' RULE IS NARROWER THAN THE RISK, AND THE CI GATE DOES NOT CLOSE THE GAP (2026-08-18).

Adopted into mayor dispatch practice on the report of the worker on rf2-f5cma, which was fixing that very rule and is the best-placed reader of it.

THE GAP: a PR body and a bead close reason are both DURABLE and PUBLIC, and neither is a committed file. The 'No hardcoded personal/home paths' CI gate does not see either. So a worker that obeys the rule as written can still publish an absolute home path where it persists. That worker kept paths out of both only by extending the rule on its own initiative.

ADOPTED WORDING for every dispatch: report the printed WORKTREE_ROOT to the mayor in your completion message, and never write it, or any absolute home path, into any COMMITTED FILE, PR BODY OR TRACKER TEXT.

AND CARRY THE POSITIVE FORM, which the template now has and my briefs lagged a revision behind: if the deliverable is itself a written record, what makes the guard evidence is that it RAN and exited 0, not the machine-specific path it printed. A worker told only what not to write still has evidence to produce and will improvise something.

SEPARATE OBSERVATION FROM THE SAME REPORT, not yet actioned: the guard prints an MSYS-style root (/c/Users/...) while the boundary block in every brief states the worktree as C:/Users/.... A worker comparing the two LITERALLY sees a mismatch, on the one rule where a directory-level error is expensive. Every worker so far has resolved it from context. If it ever bites, the fix is to state both forms in the boundary block rather than to change either producer.

GENERAL SHAPE: the worker fixing a rule is the best reviewer of the brief that carries it. Ask. Two of the three improvements here came from asking one worker whether its own setup instruction was well worded.

WSL bash.exe DOUBLE-EXPANDS a -c command string. Found by rf2-sefx0 (#6357, 2026-07-18) with a decisive probe: bash -lc with FOO=hello then printf of the escaped dollar-FOO prints the literal dollar-FOO under Git Bash (single pass) but prints hello under WSL bash (an outer pass already substituted it). CONSEQUENCE: any -c string that READS BACK a variable the SAME string assigns is broken under WSL — the outer pass substitutes the not-yet-assigned name to empty. That is how a PATH= assignment referencing a FIXTURE_DIR assigned immediately to its left silently produced /bin:<real PATH>, so stub executables were never found and 15 of 15 cases failed before reaching the code under test. Pre-existing vars (PWD, PATH) survive both passes, which is why the bug looks selective. FIX SHAPE: build one env-prefixed command whose every dollar-NAME already exists in the parent environment; let the child script read the rest from its own environment rather than from the command string. DISPROVED on the way: the semicolon separator is fine, and double-quoting is fine — do not chase those. TESTING LESSON (the important half): a BEHAVIOURAL test for this cannot protect you, because Git Bash and the Ubuntu CI runner both expand ONCE — a reintroduced self-reference stays green on CI while breaking only for Windows contributors. sefx0 pinned the STRUCTURE instead (assert the command references only pre-existing variables) with a non-vacuity guard. Generalise: when a defect is invisible on the platform your CI runs, a structural pin beats a behavioural one.

A RULING DETAIL WAS EMPIRICALLY WRONG: notifications CAN arrive before dispatch returns on the stock-Reagent adapter (found 2026-08-07, rf2-ynved).

THE RULING SAID (item 8) that notifications never arrive before dispatch returns. FALSE on this adapter: :flush-render! is (fn [f] (f) (r/flush)), so dispatch-sync DRAINS THE QUEUE ITSELF. A test written to assert the ruling literally went red.

HOW IT WAS HANDLED, and this is the part to copy: the worker did not quietly conform the test to observed behaviour, and did not quietly conform the docs to the ruling. It reported the ruling was wrong, and changed the DOCS to say the re-feed rides a Reagent flush rather than an inline callback inside the app-db write — while telling the author to code as though it lands on the FOLLOWING commit. That last clause is the useful part: teach the WEAKER guarantee even when the stronger one currently holds, because the stronger one is an implementation detail of one adapter.

SECOND FINDING from the same run: a sibling unmount COMMIT re-runs a surviving tracker against an unchanged value, so the survivor takes one idempotent re-feed. The DOM-free counterpart drives the identical release with NO React commit and sees no duplicate. So it is a property of the commit cycle, not of the recipe — and the assertion was rewritten property-based with the reason recorded.

GENERAL RULE: when a test contradicts a recorded ruling, the ruling is a hypothesis like anything else. Report the contradiction, establish which is true FROM THE ADAPTER SOURCE, and fix whichever is actually wrong. Do not assume the ruling wins; do not assume the observation wins.

title: hicasso: aggregate randomisation band breaks the declared paired two-session assignment
description:
PR #8634's aggregate band samples each of the eight run schedules independently from the 48 per-run admissible schedules (48^8). That is not the assignment support the PR designed or executed: alloc_pass_design.cjs selects two distinct non-complement schedules A/B, adds their exact complements, and pre-registration repeats [A,B,~A,~B] verbatim in session B. The complementary pairing is load-bearing because it is what cancels every round-index nuisance; the cross-session repeat is load-bearing because the page calls the session the independent unit.

Reproduction against the committed eight runs: exhaustively enumerate the ordered design-preserving support [A,B,~A,~B,A,B,~A,~B], B != A and B != ~A. There are 48*46 = 2,208 configurations. The mid-rung result is 6/2208, p=0.002717 (not the published 1/20001 = 0.00005); the null control is 268/2208, p=0.121377 (not 0.0934). Outcome 1 remains at alpha 0.05, but the reported p-values, minimum attainable p, reference quantiles, and claim that the reference uses schedules the design would equally admit are wrong.

Repair the corpus reference so every draw preserves the declared complement pairing and cross-session repeat, add a test pinning that joint support rather than only each run's 48 marginal schedules, and re-adjudicate the published page without rewriting historical provenance pins. If a different reference is intended, state and justify that assignment mechanism without calling it the executed design's randomisation distribution.

consumes `re-frame.substrate.observation` in shipped source. Fork (a) — "hicasso reaches it
indirectly through re-frame.subs / re-frame.interop" — is FALSIFIED, and by a specific
counter-route rather than by an absent grep hit.

EVIDENCE

1. No src namespace anywhere requires the port. Every `:require` in the tree is a test ns
   (2 reagent-adapter tests, core bench/read_attribution.clj,
   observation_drain_elision_prod_test.cljs, observation_port_cljs_test.cljc). Every mention
   under any src/ tree is a docstring or comment.

2. The dependency runs the OTHER WAY, so no indirect route through subs can exist.
   implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:2232 marks compute-sub-with-memo as an
   "observation-port internal entry point ... Two `^:no-doc` seams
   `re-frame.substrate.observation` consumes". The port consumes subs; subs does not consume
   the port.

3. Hicasso reaches AROUND the port, not through it. collector.cljs:1180 calls
   subs/compute-sub-with-memo directly — the same fn the port itself calls at
   observation.cljc:1691. So hicasso is a PEER consumer of the same core seam, not a consumer
   of the port. Its port mention at collector.cljs:234 is a lineage claim about following the
   port's cold-probe discipline, not a call.

4. Why the consumer went. `git log -S "[re-frame.substrate.observation"` over */src/ shows the
   real requirers were implementation/ui and implementation/freehand, deleted by the retirement
   commits ef3131f4a2 (ui) and c951808b47 (freehand). Hicasso never had the require, so this is
   not a regression in hicasso — it is the seam losing its only instances to rf2-0yp7w.

5. Consequence. port-abi-version / assert-port-abi-version! appear ONLY in the port itself and
   in core's own tests. The ABI boot guard that Conventions, Spec 006 and Spec 009 all describe
   a consumer asserting at load has no consumer side in any shipped build and cannot fire there.
   Same for the DEV-only G-13 witness (observation.cljc:642+): its value depends on a real
   consumer.

spec/Conventions.md and spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md only. The consumer clauses become the
terms the category imposes on A consumer rather than assertions about a live edge, and both
pages carry an explicit rf2-63t1i-referenced flag that no shipped namespace requires the port
today. No implementation code touched, nothing deleted, no semantics changed. The port's
specified behaviour remains fully normative.

RULING: RETIRE THE PORT — UNLESS spec/006 MANDATES IT AS A CONTRACT SURFACE. Establish that first; it decides the whole bead and it is a read, not a judgement.

WHY THE CONDITION IS NOT A FUDGE. The two answers are different KINDS of thing, and only a source read separates them. If spec/006 names the observation port as a seam a substrate MUST provide, the port is a contract with a currently-empty consumer set, and retiring it is a spec change requiring its own ruling — it is not dead code, it is an unexercised obligation. If spec/006 does not, it is an implementation detail whose consumer was deleted, and it is dead code wearing a guard.

WHY RETIRE IS THE DEFAULT AND NOT KEEP-PARKED. The stance is explicit: pre-alpha, no back-compat shims, reject over-engineering. Parking is the 'preserve everything just in case' default, and a stance exists precisely to refuse it. The five test namespaces are not independent value — they test the port itself, so they cannot vote for its survival. And the port-abi-version guard and G-13 witness are the sharper argument FOR retirement rather than against it: a guard whose value depends on a consumer that does not exist is a hollow control, and this project's own rule is that a hollow control is REPLACED, not patched, because the next reader trusts it harder for having a history of being fixed. Keeping it parked keeps two controls that assert nothing while looking like coverage.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING: give-it-a-consumer is OUT, and it needs no investigation. Writing a consumer to justify shipped code is making work to preserve a decision nobody has defended, which is the clearest case of the gold-plating the stance rejects.

SCOPE FOR THIS PASS — DO NOT RETIRE THE PORT IN THIS PR. Establish the discriminator at source, record the answer on this bead with the evidence, and STOP. If spec/006 does not mandate it, the retirement is its own dispatch with its own fence: it deletes shipped core code, five test namespaces and two controls, and it deserves a worker whose whole context is that. If spec/006 DOES mandate it, say so and the bead becomes an operator ruling on the spec, which I will surface to Mike.

OUT-OF-FENCE RESIDUE ALREADY TRACKED, so it is not swept here: rf2-2n92u carries spec/Ownership.md:31 and spec/009:1985, which still name hicasso as the consumer.

This note is a CLAIM. Re-derive every require, line number and the spec/006 text at origin/main HEAD before acting.

THE ANSWER: NO. spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md does NOT mandate re-frame.substrate.observation as a contract surface a substrate MUST provide. It says the opposite, in terms, in three places, and the strongest of them is a sentence about what adapters implement.

EVIDENCE, QUOTED.

1. spec/006:103-111, a blockquote inside the section that DEFINES the adapter contract:
   "**The internal observation port is not part of this contract.** A re-frame-native view substrate reads subscriptions through an adapter-internal observation port ... that lives **outside** this closed ten-fn map: no entry is added to the adapter spec map, no signature here changes, and existing adapters implement nothing new."
   The same blockquote already carries "though no shipped namespace requires the port today (see the scope section below)".

2. spec/006:1192-1193, the port section's own status block:
   "This port is INTERNAL -- it is NOT part of the public adapter API contract; see the scope statement below."

3. spec/006:1204, the scope heading, and 1206-1214 under it:
   "### Scope -- outside the closed public adapter contract, one named consumer"
   "The port is **adapter-internal**: a private surface between the core's sub-cache and a re-frame-native substrate's view runtime ... It is **not** an entry in the adapter spec map. The public adapter API contract remains exactly as [The adapter API contract] states it -- six required functions, three optional functions, one lifecycle function, plus the `:kind` discriminator (the 11-key adapter spec map) -- **closed for v1**. Existing adapters (Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx, plain-atom, SSR) implement none of the port's operations and are unchanged by this section. No feature predicate is added; a consumer cannot branch on the port's presence because the port is not consumable."

THE SENTENCE THAT SETTLES IT is "Existing adapters ... implement none of the port's operations". A seam a substrate MUST provide is one substrates implement. This one is implemented by CORE and consumed, in principle, by a view runtime -- the arrow points the other way. A substrate obligation it is not, and the spec closes the door twice more: the port is not in the spec map, and no feature predicate lets anything branch on it.

CORROBORATION.
- "MUST provide" and "MUST implement" occur ZERO times in spec/006. Positive control on the same file: "MUST" 37 lines, "MUST NOT" 17 lines, so the search discriminates.
- The Cross-substrate affordance summary (006:2648-2660) has exactly two columns, Reagent and UIx. No port row, no port column, no obligation.
- 006:2502-2504 speaks of "the observation-port substrate" and "the compiled UI substrate" -- a substrate KIND that used the port, not a duty every substrate carries. That kind is precisely the one removed under rf2-0yp7w.

THE ONE NUANCE, RECORDED HONESTLY BECAUSE IT SHAPES THE NEXT DISPATCH'S FENCE, NOT THE ANSWER. The port's SEMANTICS are normative: 006:1188 marks the section "Status: normative", and 006:1234-1243 -- a paragraph that already cites this bead -- ends "everything specified below states the semantics a consumer would meet, and remains normative for one." Normative-semantics-for-a-surface-that-exists is a different claim from a-seam-a-substrate-MUST-provide, and only the second would make retirement a spec change needing its own ruling. It is the second that is absent. But the retirement dispatch's fence must still include spec/006: it would remove a normative section running 1186-1980, the forward blockquote at 103-111, and the override cross-reference at 2502-2512. It is a code-plus-spec retirement, not a code-only one.

PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE. Every real :require of the port tree-wide is a test namespace -- exactly the five this bead names:
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/observation_port_activates_ratom_node_cljs_test.cljs:59
  implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/observation_port_watchable_host_cljs_test.cljs:75

BLOCKER A — THE SIX FROZEN INVARIANTS. RULING: DO NOT RENUMBER, DO NOT EXTRACT. I verified 'invariant 6' appears four times in spec/006 alone, and the worker measured three of those inside the section I just rescued, as prose rather than links. Renumbering is therefore CATASTROPHIC AND INVISIBLE — it silently repoints every 'invariant N' citation in the corpus at the wrong invariant, and check_doc_slugs.py cannot see a prose ordinal any more than it can see a docstring citation.

THIS IS THE THIRD APPEARANCE OF ONE CLASS TONIGHT. spec/004-Views.md was cited by NUMBER as well as by filename — 102 hits across 55 files that three separate sweeps missed. The render-batch law was cited by SLUG, which is why the ruling was heading-byte-identical. Now the invariants are cited by ORDINAL. Every one of these is a reference no gate resolves, and in every case the remedy is the same: PRESERVE THE CITATION SURFACE and change what sits behind it.

BLOCKER B — subs.cljc's ACQUIRE MACHINERY. RULING: RETAIN IT. acquire-cache-reaction! (:2298), *acquire-recovery* (:710), record-acquire-recovery! (:719) and the recorder calls inside compute-and-cache! / build-and-cache!* all STAY, even though retiring the port leaves them with no caller.

The port being the sole current caller does not make the machinery port-owned; it makes the port the only thing that has needed it yet. Deleting live core machinery because its one caller is going away is the 'delete a consumer to make the deletion fit' error running backwards, and this bead has already refused that error once in the other direction over read_attribution.clj.

STATE THE ZERO-CALLER CONDITION IN THE CODE when you land it, the way spec/009 states it for guard-open-drain!. An unexplained uncalled function is exactly what invites the next retirement to delete it.

A markdown-only edit under implementation/hicasso/spec/ now arms cljs_browser, hicasso_controlled and hicasso_hmr as well as cljs_node_test, because the classifier's implementation/hicasso/* arm does not discriminate .md. WHAT HAPPENED. rf2-9wmqd carried an old note (from PR #8599) listing three owed items (a), (b),
(c). A LATER note at 10:24 opened 'Do not brief from the WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWES list above; it
is stale' and concluded 'WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS IS ITEM (c) ALONE'. Items (a) and (b) had merged
in PRs #8605 and #8606 the previous evening, and (a)'s own split-out bead rf2-xc0bw was CLOSED.

The mayor read the notes with a HEAD-of-section slice, saw the #8599 list, re-derived it into a
new note at 23:05, and dispatched a worker off it. That note was now the NEWEST text on the bead.
A worker obeying 'read the newest note first' would have been sent to build something that had
existed for seventeen hours. This one instead read the whole note history in order, refused,
built nothing, and was right.

TWO RULES, AND THE SECOND IS THE NEW ONE.

1. 'bd show <id> | tail' is not a read-the-newest method -- AND NEITHER IS A HEAD SLICE. Notes do
not render in reliable recency order. Use bd history <id> --json and walk ADJACENT PAIRS
newest-first to the first change to a text-bearing field. Reading the mutation TIMESTAMPS from
plain bd history is only half the rule; the timestamps say a newer mutation exists, not what it
says. That half is easy to skip and skipping it is what caused this.

2. TIMESTAMP ORDER DOES NOT ESTABLISH THAT CONTENT IS CURRENT. The newest note can be a faithful
re-derivation of superseded text. When a note QUOTES or SUMMARISES an earlier one rather than
citing a source check, look for an intervening note that overtook it -- and prefer a note that
says 'verified at source at <tip>' over one that says 'from its own PR #NNNN note'.

CHEAPEST GUARD, and it would have caught this in one command: before briefing 'build X', check
whether X EXISTS AT TIP. Here, ls of the two named files would have ended it immediately.

description:
METHOD-REREAD DRIFT FINDING, mayor, 2026-08-21, tip 4bc3427fee. This is a
one-sentence repair to CLAUDE.md that I am doing MYSELF, not dispatching — filed so it survives
the tick rather than to hand it to a worker.

WHAT THE DOCUMENT SAYS. CLAUDE.md:91, on '.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and its
mirror implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs':

  'That last pair is one-toucher by construction rather than by convention: the test pins the
   classifier's outputs, so A CHANGE TO EITHER ALONE LANDS A TREE WHERE THE SUITE CONTRADICTS
   THE SCRIPT — they move in ONE commit, and two workers in that pair conflict every time.'

WHAT THE TREE DID. PR #8664 (rf2-xomo) changed the TEST HALF ALONE — one file,
implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs, 40 insertions / 10 deletions, no script
change — and merged GREEN at 88/88 with every check terminal. The suite did not contradict the
script. Verified just now: gh pr view 8664 reports state=MERGED, files=1.

WHY THE UNIVERSAL FORM IS WRONG, and the distinction is the whole repair. The rule assumes every
change to one half CREATES a contradiction. A change can also REMOVE one. #8664's test carried a
pin naming docs/design/hicasso/product/complaints.md, an address that ceased to exist when
PR #8661 moved the contract; the script's behaviour was never wrong and needed nothing. Its
worker put it exactly right: 'This change runs the other way: the test contradicted the script's
ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR, and now agrees with it.'

The same shape is queued again on rf2-xomo's reopen: the audit asks for a test NAME rename with
no classifier behaviour change. Under the rule as written a mayor would force a pointless
two-file diff, or block a legitimate one-file fix.

THE REPAIR — narrow the claim to what is true, do not delete it. The pair must move together when
the change alters WHAT THE CLASSIFIER OUTPUTS, or what the test PINS about those outputs. A change
that only corrects the test to match the script's existing, unchanged behaviour — a stale pin, an
overstated test name — is legitimately one file, and saying so is what keeps the rule credible.
The 'two workers in that pair conflict every time' half STANDS and must be kept: that is about
concurrency, not about diff shape, and it is what the dispatch fences rely on.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY FIXED: CLAUDE.md is currently held by PR #8666 (worker fhsweep, rf2-wppza),
unmerged. Editing it now would plant a conflict in exactly the file this rule is about. DO IT
AFTER #8666 MERGES.

EVIDENCE IN THE TREE, all measured rather than recalled:
  #8664 — test half only, 1 file, merged green 88/88.
  #8666 — both halves, comments only, one commit (afe06a9145).
  rf2-xomo reopen — a test-name rename, no behaviour change, one file.

notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7971 (merged 2026-08-12T07:12:16Z; completeness/correctness/implementation quality) — REOPENED. The recipes and their synchronous/model coverage are strong, but the two poll-until chains in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/forms/flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs (the refused-submit marker wait and valid-submit transport wait) have only a fulfillment handler. If the bounded poll rejects, cljs.test done is never called and the live hm/mount! handle is never unmounted/asserted clean; the row hangs and can contaminate later browser tests. The sibling slice suite already has the bounded finish-after shape: report the rejection upstream, tear down on both arms, and keep exactly one trailing done. Apply that shape to both rows and add a deliberate rejected-poll control proving the following row sees no retained mount/residue. Keep the correction local; no runtime or forms API change.
PR #8668 AUDIT RESIDUAL (correctness / implementation quality; the teaching-set completeness work is otherwise sound). Reopened this exact forms-recipe owner because the rule promoted into the published guide contradicts the accessibility state it exposes. At merge, docs/core/hicasso/05-forms.md says an invalid submit button stays "focusable and activatable" and relies on that activation to set :submit-attempted?, while rendering :aria-disabled true; forms-recipes.md:53 and the shipped example view/tests pin the same pattern. WAI-ARIA 1.2 defines aria-disabled=true as perceivable but disabled, "so it is not editable or otherwise operable" (https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#aria-disabled). The page therefore tells assistive technology the action is unavailable while the application requires the user to activate it to reveal errors; current DOM/L2 tests pin both halves without testing their semantic coherence. Repair the guide, recipe, example view and witnesses together: normally keep invalid submit genuinely enabled (omit aria-disabled), let submit validation reveal the error summary, and describe the errors with the appropriate relationship/live-region semantics; reserve disabled/aria-disabled for an action the handler really suppresses. Do not merely change the prose while leaving the example and tests contradictory.

The invalid submit button now claims nothing — validity is carried by the fields as aria-invalid + aria-describedby + role=alert, and aria-disabled is reserved for controls the handler really suppresses. New L2 row and DOM assertions pin the semantic coherence that nothing tested before. Two consequent pins moved in the same commit: the guide-samples roster (blocks 5 and 8) and the pooled read-set census (dropping the gate read left save-button and save-failure on an identical one-key set; verdict unmoved). THE MAYOR'S CHARACTERISTIC ERROR IS REPORTING A CLASSIFICATION IT INFERRED RATHER THAN VERIFIED. Because a mayor repeats its summary every tick, one inference becomes a standing false claim to the operator. THREE instances measured 2026-08-21/22 — and the third came AFTER this memory was first written, so writing it down did not prevent it.

CASE 1, rf2-9wmqd. Reported for hours as 'quiet-box measurement lane'. The bead's OWN FIRST
PARAGRAPH says 'EDIT-SHAPED, LOUD-BOX-SAFE ... needs NO window'. Grouped by TOPIC and the group's
label reported.

CASE 2, rf2-lau0u. Same label, same way. Its fence never asserted it — it said 'Establish FIRST
WHETHER ...; IF IT DOES, it joins the quiet-box lane.' An unresolved CONDITIONAL reported as its
consequent.

CASE 3, rf2-lau0u again, and this one is the sharpest because it wore the clothes of a source
check. I ran the 'does X already exist at tip' guard, grepped for files mentioning h/hydrate! and
files mentioning useId, read the two lists, and reported 'no such witness exists' in a brief.
A witness had existed since 2026-08-14 — server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, added by the SAME
COMMIT as the door, carrying 9 hydrate! and 13 useId references, selected by :browser-test every
PR. TWO LISTS THAT OVERLAP ARE NOT A PAIRING. I never opened a file.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, one question: does the bead SAY this, or did I conclude it? A label like
'measurement lane' or 'awaiting a ruling' — or a finding like 'no witness exists' — is a CLAIM and
needs the same source check as any other. Quote the source in the note that records it; if you
cannot quote it, you inferred it.

THREE SHAPES TO WATCH, one per case:
  - A GROUP LABEL applied by topic rather than read off the item.
  - AN UNRESOLVED CONDITIONAL read as its consequent. 'Establish whether X; if X, hold' is not
    'hold', and it reads naturally as a fence to anyone skimming.
  - A NEGATIVE EXISTENCE CLAIM built from set membership instead of from opening the candidate.
    'No X exists' needs a file opened, not two greps intersected in your head.

AND NOTE THE FAILURE MODE OF THE FIX: the guard 'check whether X exists at tip' was itself added
to the method that same evening, and case 3 is that guard being RUN AND MISREAD. A guard executed
carelessly returns the same reassuring answer as no guard at all.

title: hicasso: PR #8672's adopted-DOM async witnesses double-finish and leak on rejection
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8672 (completeness / correctness / implementation quality).

The product-door byte premise and the adopted-DOM/control readings are strong, but the two new async rows in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs have an unreliable failure path.

At merge a8641fdc3c, the-door-s-id-survives-the-adoption-and-a-real-client-render (lines 454-508) and the-hand-rolled-bytes-lose-the-id-through-the-same-door (lines 510-574) both call done in the .then callback's finally and then attach a .catch that calls done again.

That creates two distinct faults:
1. If sup/adopted! rejects before .then runs, .catch ends the row without unmounting the hydration handle or stopping the mismatch watcher. The control closes its console capture, but likewise omits unmount/watcher teardown.
2. If code inside .then throws, finally unmounts and calls done, the returned promise rejects, and .catch reports the error and calls done a second time. A failure can therefore advance the runner twice and make the following row's state/reporting unreliable.

The green success path and current sabotage controls do not exercise either branch. Keep the repair local to this test namespace; no runtime, SSR, disposition, or product API change is indicated.
acceptance_criteria: Each new async witness has one settlement path that reports a rejection, stops every watcher/capture, unmounts any created handle, and calls done exactly once on fulfillment or rejection. Add a deliberate rejected-adoption or thrown-body control that fails before the repair and proves the following row sees no retained root, frame, listener, or capture. Preserve the three witness readings and their node/browser coverage.

CHECKING WHETHER A WORKER COMMITTED .beads: a TREE diff manufactures a false positive. Ask the commit, not the trees. Measured 2026-08-22.

WHAT HAPPENED. Worker sliceclock's branch read "git diff --stat origin/main f77316d601" -> ".beads/issues.jsonl | 7 +----". My first reading was a durability violation: the one thing a worker must never commit, with a whole CLAUDE.md section and two recorded incidents behind it.

IT WAS BASE DRIFT. The worker branched at cc563fd8fb and origin/main had moved 2 commits ahead -- my own bead checkpoints. "git diff A B" compares TREES, so it reports the worker's older .beads snapshot as a difference the worker introduced. The commit touched ONE file, a 329-line pre-registration doc.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, run both directions on the same sha:
    git diff --stat origin/main SHA -- .beads/   -> 7 lines (3+/4-)   WRONG QUESTION
    git show --stat SHA -- .beads/               -> empty             RIGHT QUESTION

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN ORDINARY GIT LITERACY: the false positive fires on EVERY worker branch once the mayor has checkpointed twice, which is every branch older than about twenty minutes. So the natural check is not merely imprecise, it is reliably wrong IN THE ACCUSING DIRECTION -- and repeated false accusations train you to stop reading the one signal that catches the real thing.

SAME FAMILY AS the ahead-count trap the hygiene loop names: this repo rebases, so ancestry and ahead-count are both wrong, and patch-equivalence via git cherry is the fix. Both are TREE-COMPARISON answers to a question about AUTHORSHIP. When the question is "what did this commit do", ask the commit.

title: hicasso: identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test's four adoption rows never settle on rejection — no .catch at all
description:
FOUND BY THE rf2-sxhu WORKER (asyncsettle, PR #8675) as a sibling of the fault it was fencing, reported outside its fence and correctly left. IT POINTED AT ONE LINE (~541) AND CALLED IT 'the same shape'. I re-derived it at source and the pointer is right about the FILE and wrong about the SHAPE, which changes the repair — recording the correction here rather than inheriting the characterisation.

THE FILE: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/identifier_prefix_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs, six deftests, four of them async adoption rows.

WHAT rf2-sxhu's FILE HAD: a .catch arm that called (done) alongside a finally that also called it — a DOUBLE-FINISH — plus cleanup skipped on the rejection path.

WHAT THIS FILE HAS IS THE OPPOSITE HALF. There is no .catch anywhere in it. Measured with a working control in both directions: grep -c '\.catch' returns 0 on this file and 4 on server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs at 2d064aec99, the base rf2-sxhu repaired. So the pattern reaches this corpus and the zero is a reading.

THE SHAPE AT ALL FOUR SITES:

  (-> (sup/adopted! handle)
      (.then (fn [ok] ... (try ...assertions... (finally (stop!) (mount/release! handle) (done))))))

  adoption promise   fulfilment handler   finally
  :353               :354                 :397
  :416               :417                 :448
  :492               :493                 :540-544   <- the ~541 the worker pointed at
  :578               :579                 :603

SO ON A REJECTION NOTHING RUNS AT ALL. The .then handler is skipped, the try is never entered, the finally never fires — and therefore (done) is never called, (stop!) never stops the mismatch watcher, and (mount/release! handle) never releases the root. Three consequences, and the first is why this is worth a bead rather than a note:

1. THE FAILURE IS OPAQUE. The row does not fail; it HANGS to the async timeout, and the message names the timeout rather than the rejection. rf2-sxhu's sites at least reported something.
2. THE WATCHER AND THE ROOT LEAK INTO THE NEXT ROW, which is the same second fault rf2-sxhu names, so the following row's census is measuring residue.
3. THE REJECTION IS NEVER REPORTED, so what the adoption actually threw is lost.

:540-544 is the site whose finally spans five lines because it releases TWO roots (ha and hb) — it is the two-simultaneous-roots row, and it is the one where a leak costs most.

WHAT THE REPAIR PROBABLY WANTS, but the worker decides: PR #8675 introduced a shared settle-row! helper in the sibling namespace that carries one .then with BOTH handlers (mutually exclusive, so a throwing body cannot also reach the rejection arm), release and done beyond both, done in a finally, and a :row label carrying what the hand-written messages did. Whether that helper is lifted into the shared support namespace or the pattern is re-applied locally is a judgement about how many callers it will end up with — do not lift it on the strength of two files without saying why.

ACCEPTANCE: each of the four rows settles exactly once on fulfilment or rejection, reports the rejection with enough to identify the row, stops the watcher and releases every handle on both paths. A deliberate rejected-adoption control that fails before the repair and proves the FOLLOWING row sees no retained root, frame or listener. No assertion changes — prove that mechanically, by extracting the balanced (is ...) forms from both revisions and diffing, as PR #8675 did.

FENCE: keep it to this one test namespace. rf2-sxhu's own widening note is the precedent and its reasoning applies — bounded repair bounds the change, not the search — but the search has been done here and it returned this file.

THE PR'S OWN CHECK RUN CAN FALSIFY THE PROSE IN ITS DIFF, AND THAT CONTRADICTION IS VISIBLE AT MERGE TIME. Measured 2026-08-22, on a clause I merged and the audit reopened an hour later.

WHAT HAPPENED. PR #8678 added one paragraph to the method saying "documentation and prose changes typically arm no gated surface at all", resting on report-changed-surfaces.sh returning 0 of 28 keys for the path. Three of us took that measurement independently -- two workers and me -- and all three read it as "no gates". The merged-PR audit found it false: report-changed-surfaces.sh is the test.yml classifier, and docs.yml has a SEPARATE Detect docs surface step that maps docs/* to docs_surface=true and gates a MkDocs build on it.

THE EVIDENCE WAS ON MY OWN SCREEN AT MERGE TIME AND I DID NOT CONNECT IT. The rollup I read to clear clause 2 showed "docs: success" -- that job is docs.yml's, and its running at all is a live demonstration that the path arms a gated surface. The diff said the opposite four lines away.

THE GENERAL FORM, which is what makes this worth keeping. The merge criterion says to read the FILE LIST against the item, and I extend it: when the diff makes a factual claim about GATING, the PR's own check run is a free control on that claim, and it is already open in front of you. A claim that a path arms nothing, beside a rollup showing a surface-gated job that ran, is a contradiction you can see without running anything.

THE NARROWER TRAP UNDERNEATH IT. "0 of 28" is one classifier's answer, not a census of gates. This repo has at least three independent gating paths -- test.yml's report-changed-surfaces.sh, docs.yml's own Detect docs surface step (which report-changed-surfaces.sh:44 NAMES in its own comment as a path it does not cover), and lint.yml's. A zero from one of them says nothing about the other two. Ask for the COMPLETE covering set, never one classifier's keys.

AND THE COUNTEREXAMPLE THAT MAKES IT CONCRETE: implementation/hicasso/spec/budgets.md is in docs.yml's docs_surface case list AND arms five test.yml surfaces including three Chromium lanes and an ~11-minute compile. It is prose, and it is the heaviest change in the repo.

title: method: the reaping escape is keyed to an agent id the mapping file usually lacks, while the transcripts are on disk and findable by content
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD REREAD LOOP 2026-08-22 04:2x AUSEST, tip 73158f33e9, by testing a rule I have been ENFORCING against what the tree actually holds. The rule is sound; its escape hatch is keyed to something that is often missing, and the document does not say the escape is still reachable without it.

WHAT THE METHOD SAYS. Reaping is authorised only by the worker's own completion report, and the operational test is whether you can QUOTE the sentence where that agent says it is finished. It adds an escape: reading an agent's transcript is a READ and satisfies the test. And it already knows transcripts outlive conversations — "What the id buys is the TRANSCRIPT, not a live conversation", recording eight agents that answered "no transcript" to a message while their transcripts sat intact on disk.

WHAT I HAVE BEEN DOING WITH IT. Every hygiene pass, I map standing worktrees to agent ids through the dispatch-time mapping file, message the ones that have an id, and classify the rest as irreducible residue that clears only on the operator's authority. That is a faithful reading of the document.

THE PROBLEM: THE ESCAPE IS KEYED TO AN ID THE MAPPING FILE OFTEN DOES NOT HAVE. Measured this pass with a working control -- of 35 registered worktrees, exactly THREE carry an agent id in the mapping file. WHAT LANDED. One helper cannot omit a key for three fields out of four without an 'assoc', so 'field-explicit' writes ':class' unconditionally and BOTH new arms carry ':class nil' on the three classless fields. That is what keeps the two arms key-for-key identical and rung (2) clean, and it makes the key a passenger ADDED to rung (1) and SUBTRACTED from rung (3) in equal measure. Rung (3) came back NEGATIVE for that reason (:merged mounts faster than :no-dissoc), which is not a dissoc paying for itself.

description:
FOUND 2026-08-22 05:5x AUSEST, tip 73b6ae82d8, by a measurement window (rf2-w01c) voiding two of
its three pre-registered runs because the MAYOR wrote inside the bracket twice. Not a worker
error and not a rig fault: five invocations, all exit 0, no rig fault, voided under the window's
own registered rule.

THE DOCUMENT GIVES ONE TEST WHERE TWO ARE NEEDED. loops.md §2's heavyweight-gate paragraph tells
the mayor how to decide whether an item may be dispatched while a measurement window is queued or
running. The test it states is about the GATES the item arms: enumerate what covers the item and
confirm each of those gates leaves the machine quiet. That is a correct and well-earned test for
MACHINE LOAD, and it was strengthened only hours earlier (rf2-fif4, PRs #8678 and #8679) to stop
a category being granted the licence a measurement has to earn.

IT IS THE WRONG TEST FOR AN EXCLUSIVITY CONDITION, and nothing in the document says so. A window
may register a condition that no peer WRITES inside its bracket. That is violated by activity
which is nearly free in machine terms and which the gate test therefore waves through:

  - CREATING A WORKTREE for an unrelated doc-only item. Cheap, arms nothing, voided a run.
  - MERGING A PULL REQUEST. Costs the local machine essentially nothing, voided a run.

Both were performed by the mayor's own recurring merge-and-dispatch loop, on an item correctly
measured as arming zero of this repo's 28 test surfaces. The gate test passed and was the wrong
question. The result was a correctly-run, correctly-registered window returning TWO admissible
runs of THREE, with the two-instruments rule forbidding the third being taken later — so the
series cannot be completed, only re-run.

WHY A MAYOR DOES NOT SIMPLY WORK THIS OUT. The heavyweight-gate paragraph reads as complete: it
names the hazard (a loud machine), gives an instrument (the classifier), warns that no single
classifier's answer describes the whole set, and tells you to hold the fleet thin. Having run
that test and passed it, there is nothing left to prompt a second question. "Thin" is also
actively misleading here — it says a smaller fleet is a safer fleet, when for a registered
exclusivity condition the only safe fleet is an EMPTY one, and the mayor must additionally stop
merging.

THE REPAIR, in the heavyweight-gate paragraph where the existing test lives. Two to three
sentences, generic, no counts:

  A gate test answers whether an item makes the machine LOUD. It does not answer whether the item
  BREAKS THE BRACKET. Where a window registers an exclusivity condition, any peer write inside its
  bracket voids the run however cheap that write is — creating a worktree and merging a change
  both cost the machine almost nothing and both are writes — so for such a window the fleet is
  EMPTY rather than thin, and the mayor performs no merges either.

Wording is a starting point. Keep it inside the existing paragraph; do NOT add a section, and do
NOT restate the gate test.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH THE WORDS RATHER THAN LEAVING IT TO JUDGEMENT: the two halves point
OPPOSITE WAYS for the cheapest actions. A merge is the single cheapest thing a mayor does on the
machine and one of the most destructive things it can do to a bracket. Any rule ordered by cost
gets that exactly backwards.

one shared area). Different block, same file. SEQUENCE THESE — two workers in one file is the
collision this method sequences rather than parallelises.

title: docs(claude): mkdocs --strict does not gate in-page anchors, so check_doc_slugs.py is the only anchor gate under docs/
description:
FOUND 2026-08-22 06:1x AUSEST by the rf2-n3uw worker during its sabotage run, and RE-VERIFIED AT
SOURCE by the mayor at tip 852abfc48a before filing.

THE MEASUREMENT. A broken in-page anchor was planted mid-line in a page under docs/. Two gates
were run on it:

  python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py    -> exit 1, naming the file, the line and the anchor
  python -m mkdocs build --strict      -> exit 0

THE REASON, read out of mkdocs.yml rather than inferred. The validation block sets exactly one
key:

  validation:
    links:
      unrecognized_links: warn

There is NO `anchors` key, so anchor validation sits at the MkDocs default, and `--strict`
promotes WARNING but not INFO. The file's own comment block already documents this promotion
mechanism for the two `links` levels — it is why `unrecognized_links` was raised to `warn` under
rf2-5exqc — but it stops at links and says nothing about anchors.

THIS IS REDUNDANCY MISSING, NOT COVERAGE MISSING, and the priority reflects that. In-page anchors
under docs/ ARE gated: check_doc_slugs.py catches them, and it runs in test.yml's
verify-readme-links job on every PR, which carries no surface guard. Nothing is currently
shipping unchecked.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH RECORDING: it is a FAIL-OPEN GATE NOMINATION waiting to happen, which is the
class this project already spends words on. CLAUDE.md's Build & Test section carries a careful pin
beginning "Link validation is split across two gates, and the split does not follow the job name",
and it nominates gates by path. A reader of that passage would reasonably take `mkdocs build
--strict` to cover anchors on a page inside docs_dir — it is the strict site build over exactly
that tree. It does not, and a brief nominating it alone for an anchor change gets a green that
inspected nothing. The method's own rule is "never nominate a gate that does not cover the surface
being edited", and this is a case where the non-coverage is invisible from the gate's name, its
scope and its output.

THE REPAIR, and it is one clause in prose that already exists — do NOT add a section:
in CLAUDE.md's link-validation paragraph, say that `mkdocs build --strict` does not gate in-page
ANCHORS at all (it reports them at INFO, which --strict does not promote), so check_doc_slugs.py
is the only anchor gate for pages under docs/. Optionally note the same asymmetry beside the
existing `unrecognized_links` comment in mkdocs.yml, which is where the mechanism is already
explained.

A SECOND OPTION EXISTS AND IS NOT BEING RECOMMENDED WITHOUT A RULING: setting
`validation.anchors: warn` in mkdocs.yml would make the strict build gate anchors too. That is a
behaviour change to a shared build rather than a documentation fix, it would red the build on any
pre-existing broken anchor across the whole site, and the coverage it adds is redundant with a
gate that already runs on every PR. It should not be done as a side effect of this bead.

else editing it.

title: method: the concurrent-writers block names ONE shared area, so a write to the system temp directory reads as exempt
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD REREAD LOOP 2026-08-22 05:3x AUSEST, tip 97cc09d1ef, by testing a rule I
have been ENFORCING against my own conduct this session. The rule is right; its scope names
one resource where the hazard belongs to a class, and I walked straight through the gap while
pasting the rule into a dispatch.

WHAT THE DOCUMENT SAYS. loops.md 2.x "You are one of the concurrent writers" (around :520-530)
tells the mayor that the scratch area dispatched agents share "is keyed to the SESSION, not to
a worktree, and the mayor writes there too", that "Every naming rule you paste into a brief
binds you equally", and closes with the generalisation that earned the block its place:
"A rule scoped to a ROLE exempts whoever does not identify with the role -- when a hazard
belongs to a shared resource, scope it to the resource."

WHAT I DID, WHILE ENFORCING IT. Across this session I wrote five working files under the
SYSTEM TEMP directory using exactly the bare names the rule forbids -- a per-bead note file,
three more note bodies, and a worktree list -- in the same ticks in which I pasted the scratch-
naming block verbatim into a dispatch brief. Nothing was lost, which is the same "by luck" the
block's own cited incident records.

WHY THE RULE DID NOT REACH ME, AND IT IS THE BLOCK'S OWN DEFECT RECURRING ONE LEVEL DOWN. The
block fixed a ROLE-scoped rule by re-scoping it to a RESOURCE -- and then named a single
resource, "the scratch area ... keyed to the SESSION". The system temp directory is not that
area, so the sentence reads as not addressed to a write that lands there. Same exemption
mechanism, one level down: scoping to one resource exempts whoever writes to another.

AND THE DIRECTION IS THE COUNTER-INTUITIVE ONE, which is what makes it worth two sentences in
the document rather than a note here. Reaching for the system temp directory FEELS like
stepping outside a shared area into a private one. It is the opposite. MEASURED at this tip:
that directory holds 3,021 entries, of which 1,220 are files older than three hours and so
belong to earlier sessions and other agents, and a listing shows the bare-name pattern already
dense in it (a.txt, ab.txt, added.txt, added_loops.txt, 004.md, 009hits.txt). The session
scratch area is shared across THIS session's concurrent agents; the system temp directory is
shared across EVERY session on the machine. It is the wider exposure wearing the appearance of
a private one.

THE REPAIR, and it belongs in that block where the generalisation already lives -- not a new
section, and no restatement of the naming rule itself. Three sentences, generic, no OS-specific
paths and no counts:

  And naming ONE shared area re-creates the exemption one level down. A system temp directory
  is shared more widely than the session scratch area, not less -- every session on the machine
  writes there, where the scratch area holds only this session's agents -- so reaching for it
  changes the resource without changing the hazard, and it looks private precisely because it
  is not the directory the rule names. Qualify a name for the writer and the attempt in any
  directory you do not exclusively own.

Wording is a starting point, not a mandate; match the page's register and keep it to about that
length. Do NOT add a count -- the measured figures above are evidence for the bead, and a
number in a generic method document goes stale exactly where it has to be right.

FENCE: PR #8681 (rf2-qche, branch worker/reaproute-qche) is OPEN and unmerged against this

method sequences rather than parallelises. CLEARS WHEN #8681 MERGES.
