title: ci(lint): lint.yml's own comments understate it — the surface omits two armed paths, and a non-linter job rides the same classifier
description:
FOUND BY THE METHOD REREAD LOOP 2026-08-22, tip c2a1246061, by testing a claim I have been putting
into dispatch briefs against lint.yml's CODE rather than its COMMENT. Two inaccuracies, both in the
file's description of itself. Neither changed a dispatch outcome; both are fail-open in the
direction that makes a worker skip a gate that would have armed.

*** 1. THE `Lint surface:` COMMENT UNDERSTATES THE CLASSIFIER BY TWO ENTRIES. ***

The comment (around :45) reads "Lint surface: implementation/, tools/ (minus template/resources/),
examples/, testbeds/." The classifier it describes (around :59) reads:

  implementation/*|tools/*|examples/*|testbeds/*|.clj-kondo/*|.github/workflows/lint.yml

So `.clj-kondo/*` and `.github/workflows/lint.yml` arm the lint surface and are named nowhere in
the prose. A worker editing the shared clj-kondo config, or lint.yml itself, and reading the comment
to decide coverage would conclude lint does not arm — when it does. That is the fail-open direction:
understating coverage sends a worker to skip a gate, exactly as CLAUDE.md already warns that
"understating coverage misreports as surely as overstating it".

*** 2. THE FILE CALLS ITSELF A THREE-LINTER GATE AND HAS SIX JOBS, ONE OF WHICH RIDES THE SAME
CLASSIFIER AND IS NOT A LINTER. ***

The header says "Multi-linter CI gate. Three complementary linters run as parallel jobs" and then
describes clj-kondo, Splint and ESLint. The jobs are: detect, clj-kondo, splint, eslint,
api-manifest, provenance-pins-corpus, lint-required.

`api-manifest` ("Public-API manifest drift-check") is gated on `needs.detect.outputs.lint_surface
== 'true'` — the SAME classifier as clj-kondo and Splint. So a change to implementation/ or tools/
arms a public-API manifest drift-check as well as three linters, and the header does not say so. A
worker reading it to decide what its diff arms gets three names and four gated jobs.

(`provenance-pins-corpus` is gated on `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, so it never runs on a
PR at all — worth stating for the same reason, since its name suggests otherwise.)

WHAT THIS DID NOT BREAK, stated so the priority is not read as higher than it is. My briefs said
"lint.yml's surface is implementation/, tools/, examples/, testbeds/, so docs/ is outside it and its
expensive jobs skip job-side." That CONCLUSION is correct and I re-verified it: on a pull request
touching only docs/, lint_surface and js_surface are both false, so clj-kondo, Splint, ESLint and
api-manifest all skip, provenance-pins-corpus does not run on PR events, and lint-required
aggregates all-skipped to a pass. The reasoning was incomplete; the answer was right.

THE REPAIR: bring both comments into line with the code. Name `.clj-kondo/*` and
`.github/workflows/lint.yml` in the Lint-surface comment, and correct the header so it describes
what the file runs — three linters PLUS a manifest drift-check on the same classifier, plus a
corpus job that skips on PRs. Prose only; no workflow behaviour changes and no job moves.

SAME CLASS AS AN ALREADY-ACCEPTED REPAIR: commit e324988e13 (rf2-0tkx / rf2-xomo) was
"docs(claude)+test(classifier): make the pair's self-description true". This is that, one file over.

HOT-ZONE — SEQUENCE IT. `.github/workflows/*` is on CLAUDE.md's hot-zone list, so this is never
parallel with another workflow change. It is prose-only and not urgent; there is no reason to run it
against a busy fleet.

GATE NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: editing `.github/workflows/lint.yml` ARMS THE LINT SURFACE — the
classifier names that exact path, which is the second half of finding 1. So this change gates
itself, and the honest check is that clj-kondo and Splint actually run on the PR rather than skip.
close_reason:
FIXED by PR #8692 (branch worker/lintdesc-63il), merged and fast-forwarded onto main at ac8637b308.
One file, .github/workflows/lint.yml, +35/-4, COMMENTS ONLY — verified mechanically before merging:
zero job keys added, and zero added lines that are not comments.

*** MY FILED REPAIR WAS WRONG AND THE WORKER REPLACED IT. This is the part worth keeping. ***

I filed "append `.clj-kondo/*` and `.github/workflows/lint.yml` to the Lint-surface comment". That
would have introduced a NEW error, in BOTH directions:
  - still omitting TEN patterns — the arming set is five `case` arms and sixteen patterns, including
    .splint.edn, spec/API.md, both api-manifest EDN files, skills/*, docs/core/*,
    docs/*/concepts.md, spec/Privacy.md, docs/api/*, docs/story/api/*;
  - and newly claiming clj-kondo LINTS a YAML workflow and an EDN config directory, which it does
    not.

THE REAL DEFECT IS ONE LEVEL DEEPER THAN I DIAGNOSED: ONE PHRASE NAMES TWO DIFFERENT SETS. The
`Lint surface:` paragraph was not describing the classifier arm at all — it describes the `--lint`
TARGET paths and says so ("excluded by virtue of the explicit `--lint` paths below"), and as an

never runs on a PR.

SABOTAGE, AND THE HONEST NEGATIVE IS THE MORE VALUABLE OF THE TWO. Both plants were on targets
verified unique first and restored with git hash-object verified against blob 44ef4c13bd.
  - Plant 1, inside one of the NEW COMMENTS: both gates stayed green, exit 0 and exit 0. That
    proves the LIMIT, not the coverage — YAML discards `#` lines before any parser reads them, so

  - Plant 2, an unmatched quote in the `name:` VALUE: check_workflow_yaml.py exit 1 naming

    parse-error arm. So a green from those two is a real read of that worktree.

compares EQUAL (exit 0), with a mutated-copy control confirming the comparison discriminates.
check_workflow_yaml.py 0, --self-test 0 across 5 cases, check_workflow_job_timeouts.py 0 across

title: hic: the clock lane's :over-floor resolution gate is necessary but not sufficient for a comparative row
description:
MEASURED DURING rf2-9wmqd ITEM (c)'S WINDOW, 2026-08-22, on slice_broad_clock_app. Filed rather than fixed there because the window's own terms forbid improving the rig mid-measurement.

WHAT THE GATE IS. slice_broad_clock_app's docstring makes :over-floor's :straddles-1? the resolution test a reader must apply before quoting any :comparative range: an arm whose per-round range against an EMPTY FRAME includes 1.0 was not separated from the floor, and no ratio between two such arms is a reading about anything. lane/across-rounds computes it. It is a SOUND NECESSARY CONDITION and it did real work in that window -- :donor-theme straddled 1.0 in two evidence runs of three, so the theme pair was refused outright.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO. :over-floor asks whether ONE arm separated from an empty frame. C3 asks whether TWO arms separate from EACH OTHER at a stated line (1.25x), and C4 at 1.5x. The locale pair answered YES to the first in all three runs and NO to the second, which is the case that shows the two are different questions. Arithmetic on that run's own published p50s and nothing else: because a paint-bounded window is ~96% frame grid, a 1.25x difference in the arms' OWN work displaces the window-level ratio by only 0.3-1.1 percentage points against an observed per-round spread of 1.5-7.5 points, and a 1.5x difference by 0.6-2.2 points. The observed ~1.00x is consistent with 1.00x, 1.25x and 1.5x alike. A reader applying only the shipped gate would have quoted it as a pass.

WHAT IS WANTED, and the choice is open. Everything the second reading needs is ALREADY PUBLISHED -- :summary's per-arm :p50 including the floor's, and :comparative's per-round spread -- so this is a computation the lane does not perform rather than data it does not have. Candidates, to be settled at source: (a) publish a per-pair detectable-difference figure beside :comparative, derived from the floor and the denominator arm's excess over it, so a run says what size of difference it could have seen; (b) leave the arithmetic to the reader and put it in the driver's docstring beside the existing caveat; (c) both. DO NOT add a threshold, a band or a pass/fail -- budgets.md sec.7 routes every distributional row to pinned evidence runs and check_budget_ledger.py enforces it, and a resolution figure is an honesty aid, not a verdict.

WHOEVER TAKES THIS SHOULD READ FIRST: docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-u3-c3-c4-window-on-the-slice-broad-clock.md sec.7.7 and sec.7.8, which carry the numbers and the argument. Same mechanism serves slice_echo_clock_app and ledger_frame_clock_app, so a change to lane.cljs reaches all three -- check what each publishes before moving anything shared.

title: method: the gate-mechanics block is named by two siblings and marked in neither
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 09:28 AUSEST in the mayor method-reread loop, in the tree at eedfb487b4.

Two files instruct the mayor to paste 'the gate-mechanics block' verbatim into EVERY editing dispatch:
  docs/the-mayor-method/README.md:273  -- '...the worktree-boundary block, and the gate-mechanics block. The last 2 go into every editing dispatch verbatim.'
  docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md:25 -- '...paste the worktree-boundary block and the gate-mechanics block verbatim into every editing dispatch'

The name resolves NOWHERE in dispatch-prompt-template.md. Measured: a case-insensitive count of 'gate-mechanics block'/'gate mechanics block' in that file returns 0. Its gate material is split across two sections with DIFFERENT audiences:
  ## Quality gates -- which gate        (line 593) -- addressed to the MAYOR writing the brief ('the brief must say which required checks the local gate omits'; 'Read the exclusion config before naming the gate'; 'the honest brief says...')
  ## Quality gates -- how a gate is run (line 631) -- addressed to the WORKER, and running to the '---' before '## Reviewing what comes back' at 787

WHY IT IS MECHANICAL AND NOT COSMETIC. The template's own section '## Pasting a block' (426) mandates: 'Anchor the extraction to CONTENT, never to line numbers. A line range against a living document is a measured constant that goes stale exactly where it has to be right.' A mayor obeying that rule has NO content to anchor to for one of the two blocks it is told to paste every time.

AND THE MARKING IS ASYMMETRIC, which is the gotcha. A grep for self-declared paste markers over the whole 835-line template returns exactly ONE hit: line 459, 'Paste this verbatim into every editing dispatch. Adapt only the placeholders.', inside '## The worktree boundary block'. Meanwhile '## Pasting a block' opens 'SEVERAL blocks below travel verbatim into every dispatch' -- plural. So a mayor extracting mechanically finds one marker and none for the other, which reads as 'there is one pasteable block' rather than 'the second one is unmarked'.

SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT IN THE SAME BLOCK. The template header (lines 4-10) declares 'Placeholders:' and lists four: <MAYOR_CHECKOUT>, <WORKTREE_PARENT>, <ASSIGNED_WORKTREE>, <ITEM_ID>. A sweep of every <UPPER_CASE> token in the file returns a FIFTH in use and undeclared: <TRUNK>, once, at the 'Diff your branch against its MERGE BASE' paragraph ('In the dominant toolchain that is the three-dot form, <TRUNK>...HEAD'). It sits INSIDE the block this item marks as pasteable, under a paste instruction that says 'Adapt only the placeholders' -- so the worker is handed a token the mayor's own list does not carry. bootstrap.md and loops.md use no placeholders at all, so the template's list is the whole declaration.

This is a rule the mayor has been ENFORCING on every dispatch this session, asserted in two files and unsupported by the third.

title: method: the write-clock clause needs the worktree's age, and the obvious way to get it is wrong on exactly the worktrees that matter
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 10:03 AUSEST at tip 78c229ce28, on two live worktrees, controlled in both
directions. Found by the mayor while using its own clause.

THE CLAUSE THIS IS ABOUT. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md, the stranded-sweep write-clock bullet,
carries a sentence added earlier today (rf2-1yct's sibling repair, commit c2a1246061): the clock
"says 'no activity' in three voices and you can only tell them apart with a control", one of the
three being "a span shorter than the worktree's own age".

SO THE CLAUSE DEPENDS ON KNOWING THE WORKTREE'S AGE, AND NAMES NO WAY TO GET IT. The obvious way
is to stat the worktree directory. On this platform's coreutils that is `stat -c %y`, "time of
last modification" -- and a directory's modification time is bumped by the worker writing inside
it.

MEASURED, TWO WORKTREES, ONE LIVE AND ONE INERT:

  pasteros (live worker, mid-edit)
    %y (last modification) 2026-08-22 10:03:23
    %w (birth)             2026-08-22 09:54:25
    -> the two disagree by nine minutes, and %y was moving between successive reads

  specsize (inert since 03:18, checked out at 00:28)
    %y 2026-08-22 00:31:35
    %w 2026-08-22 00:28:02
    -> the two agree to within the 3.5 minutes the checkout itself took

THE FAILURE IS INVERTED, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH A CLAUSE RATHER THAN A SHRUG. %y gives the
RIGHT answer on precisely the worktrees where the age does not matter -- the inert ones, where
nothing has written since checkout -- and the WRONG answer on the live one, where it is the whole
question. A mayor reading %y on a live worker sees a directory "seconds old", concludes the span
is longer than the worktree's age, and fires the no-discrimination warning on every live worker
while never firing it on a dead one. That is the opposite of what the clause is for.

AND IT IS SILENT. Nothing errors; both numbers are well-formed timestamps in the same format, and
on the first worktree a mayor happens to check -- typically an idle one -- they agree. This is the
same instrument class the document already names: an instrument that answers plausibly and wrongly
when misused, whose all-clear is complete and well-formed.

THE REPAIR, and it should be SHORT. One clause on the existing write-clock bullet naming the
distinction: the age you need is the CREATION time, not the last-modification time, and a
directory's modification time is bumped by the very writes you are trying to detect. The document
is OS-neutral by its own header's rule, so name the DISTINCTION (creation versus last
modification) rather than any particular tool's flag; `%w` versus `%y` is this platform's
spelling, not the rule.

A SECOND OPTION WORTH CONSIDERING and rejecting or taking on its merits: the dispatch record
already carries a creation timestamp for every worktree, because the mayor writes one at dispatch
time. Reading the age from the record the mayor itself wrote is more robust than asking the
filesystem at all, and needs no OS-specific spelling. If that is the better clause, say so and
write that instead.

BOUNDS. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md only, and only the existing write-clock bullet. One or two
sentences. No new section, no new bullet, nothing moved. Generic: no OS-specific flag as the rule,
nothing repo-specific, no operator's name, no absolute paths.

FENCE: none on this file. A peer worker (pasteros, rf2-4j1v) is live in the same TREE but on a
different file, docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md -- no overlap. Re-check at
dispatch time.
close_reason: PR #8696 opened: one sentence on the write-clock bullet naming CREATION vs last-modification time and the inversion. Took the filesystem-distinction shape, rejected the dispatch-record shape (the method mandates no timestamp in that record, and 'one worker is not one worktree' means a worker-built gate tree has no dispatch line at all -- the sweep starts from the worktrees precisely because the records are incomplete). Gates: slug 0/1/0 baseline/sabotage/restored, strict build 0/0/0; both 0 again after rebase onto the final base. Control: broken in-page anchor planted mid-line on a line this change authored; slug gate named it by file/line/anchor. Measured that --strict exits 0 on that same plant while printing it at INFO.

value: bd search matches TITLES ONLY and excludes closed issues by default, so 'No issues found' is routinely VACUOUS. Measured 2026-08-22 in three directions: a phrase in a bead's NOTES ('loud-box-safe') returns 0; a phrase in a DESCRIPTION ('verified reverse-domain group') returns 0; phrases in TITLES ('fused reader array', 'quiet-box window') return 1 each; a nonsense token returns 0. The tool's own help confirms it: 'Text queries search titles' and 'excludes closed issues by default'. --desc-contains is a FILTER requiring a positional title query, not a standalone description search, so it cannot answer 'find any bead mentioning X' either. THE COST IS REAL: searching for the second-clock-driver work returned 'No issues found' twice, which reads identically to 'nobody filed it' and would have justified filing a duplicate. Grepping .beads/issues.jsonl instead found FOUR carriers in one command, two of them closed, including rf2-xc0bw which held the work. THE RULE: to ask whether the tracker knows about X, grep the JSONL export (it carries description, notes, comments and close reasons); use bd search only for titles, and pass --status all when you do.

title: method: bootstrap names two pasted blocks where the roster is three, and the missing one is the 60-line preamble
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 10:29 AUSEST at tip d34a263840, in the method-reread loop, ON THE MAYOR'S OWN
PRACTICE. This is a rule that did not reach its reader, and the reader it failed to reach is me.

WHAT THE TEMPLATE NOW SAYS. Since PR #8695 (43589423fe, three hours old), '## Pasting a block' in
docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md opens:

  "Three blocks below travel VERBATIM into a dispatch: the COMMON PREAMBLE into every one, the
   WORKTREE BOUNDARY BLOCK and the GATE-MECHANICS BLOCK into every editing one."

WHAT THE ENTRY POINT SAYS. docs/the-mayor-method/bootstrap.md is the PASTEABLE OPENING PROMPT -- the
first and often only operating instruction a new mayor reads. Its line 25 names TWO:

  "READ THE SIBLINGS, IN ORDER: dispatch-prompt-template.md (the worker prompts -- paste the
   worktree-boundary block and the gate-mechanics block verbatim into every editing dispatch)"

Measured: grep -i 'preamble' over bootstrap.md returns two hits and NEITHER names a block to paste --
both are about where the STANCE goes ("paste that block verbatim into every dispatch preamble").
README.md returns ZERO hits for 'preamble'. So outside the template itself, the common preamble is
never named as something to paste, anywhere.

THE SENTENCES ARE NOT FALSE, WHICH IS WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT. The preamble goes into EVERY dispatch,
the other two into every EDITING one -- a wider scope -- so "the last 2 go into every editing
dispatch" is true as far as it goes. The defect is SILENCE at the entry point about the
widest-scope block, not a false statement.

AND IT HAS BEEN MEASURED ON A LIVE MAYOR RATHER THAN INFERRED. Three dispatches this session
(gateblock/rf2-mmwt, pasteros/rf2-4j1v, wtage/rf2-fhy9) each carried the stance verbatim, the
boundary block verbatim and the gate-mechanics block verbatim -- and NONE carried the common
preamble. In its place each brief had a hand-written two-sentence summary. That is exactly the
paraphrase the same section says extraction exists to prevent: "the extraction is what makes
paraphrase impossible -- a matched range cannot reword, where a mayor retyping two hundred lines
of gate mechanics can and does."

WHAT THE PARAPHRASE DROPPED, compared line by line against the 60-line fence:
  * "Neither `bd show <id> | tail` nor a HEAD slice of the notes section is a read-the-newest
    method" -- the exact trap that caught the mayor on rf2-9wmqd this same morning.
  * the walk mechanics: `bd history --json`, adjacent pairs newest-first to the first
    text-bearing change, and `bd comments --json` for comment created_at.
  * "A WALK THAT ENDS WITHOUT FINDING ONE HAS FOUND NOTHING, NOT 'NO CHANGE'."
  * "TIMESTAMP ORDER DOES NOT ESTABLISH CURRENCY" and the quotes-versus-cites test.
  * "THE CHEAPEST GUARD IS THE TREE, NOT THE ITEM: before you brief or build X, check whether X
    ALREADY EXISTS AT TIP" -- the rule that stops a worker rebuilding what is already there.
  * the do-not-link-version-ignored-files rule, and the self-contained-verdict paragraph.

IT HAS NOT COST ANYTHING YET, AND THAT IS LUCK RATHER THAN MARGIN. All three items were single
-mutation with zero comments -- each worker reported created_at == updated_at -- so the ordering
mechanics never bit. On a bead with an accreted history the omission is the difference between a
worker reading the newest instruction and reading the oldest.

THE REPAIR. bootstrap.md line 25 is the mandatory half: name all THREE blocks with their scopes, so
the opening prompt matches the roster. Keep it to that parenthetical -- it is one clause, not a new
paragraph, and bootstrap.md is a prompt where every added line is paid for on every read.

README.md line 273 is the WORKER'S CALL. It currently reads "...the worker-prompt shapes, the
worktree-boundary block, and the gate-mechanics block. The last 2 go into every editing dispatch
verbatim." That is descriptive prose about what the file carries rather than an instruction, and
README is deliberately the human-readable one. Decide whether naming the preamble there helps a
reader or bloats an overview, and say which you chose and why.

BOUNDS. bootstrap.md, and README.md only if the worker judges it warranted. Do NOT touch
dispatch-prompt-template.md -- its roster is correct and is the thing being matched. No new section,
nothing moved, no restructuring. Generic: no OS-specific, repo-specific or operator-specific content,

CACHE THE STATIC SKELETON: most census markup is static per view; Replicant and every compiled substrate exploit this. re-frame.ui's compiler shows what static extraction buys; the question is what a RUNTIME can cache keyed on the hiccup's identity without a compiler (fences: no compiler, no analyzer — but a value-keyed cache at the codec is neither).
  2. CHEAPEN THE PER-ELEMENT PATH: prop-map conversion, keyword->string, intent classification — profile first, the walk has never been profiled element-by-element.

FENCES, all standing: Surface B; no compiler, no analyzer, no candidate ledger, no ViewCell graph; <=2-hook shell; subscribe closes over the read set alone; Hicasso consumes reagent-slim's codec — a cache AROUND the codec is in scope, a fork OF it needs a ruling.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE: the full instrument canon (raw TaskDuration, quiet box, absolutes+ratios, B/E/Q, bands, blob provenance, discarded-if-died, announced windows). Profile and optimise in the implementation lane; PUBLISHED rows only on the clock of record against same-run donors. An optimisation claiming X% must show it on the one-boundary acceptance shape AND show the feed did not regress.

AN HONEST NEGATIVE IS AN ANSWER: if the walk is irreducible within the fences, say so with the profile — that converts 'the interpreter is slow' into 'the interpreter costs exactly this, here', which is what a ship/kill decision needs.

description:

That bead's documentary deliverables — versioning and release automation, the 14-row compatibility matrix, the upgrade policy including complaint-id stability — are all DONE and closed there. THE DELIVERABLE, which is rf2-hic-061's original acceptance clause:

  2. Prove a consumer app installs Hicasso from the ARTEFACT rather than from the repo.

BLOCKED ON rf2-uelji, and the block is external rather than technical. Clojars refuses new projects in an unverified group; day8 is not a reverse-domain group; so the first tag must cut on io.github.day8/* and that needs the group sorted first. rf2-uelji is DEFERRED to 2026-09-16. Nothing a worker does before then can discharge this.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD RATHER THAN rf2-hic-061 STAYING OPEN. A bead whose acceptance is gated on a third-party account action a month away is a calendar entry, not open work. Keeping it inside hic-061 made a finished deliverable read as unfinished and — the part that cost something — kept rf2-v04s blocked on a bead whose documentary half had shipped.

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE, verified at source by rf2-hic-061's 2026-08-18 pass, so this bead is a release act and not a build:
  • :clein/build in implementation/hicasso/deps.edn, with :version pointing at ../../VERSION and :src-dirs ["src" "resources" "test_kit/src"].
  • hicasso present in verify-version-lockstep.sh's ARTEFACTS and NON_CORE.
  • deploy-hicasso present in release.yml.
So the automation exists; what does not exist is a coordinate to publish under.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: a consumer-from-coordinate preflight cannot be written before the coordinate exists, which is why rf2-hic-061's pass deliberately touched no workflow file and left its hot-zone flag unexercised. Expect this bead to touch .github/workflows/* — sequence it against any other workflow bead.

title: Retrospective facade-export classification sweep (re-frame.core, Story, Xray) for external-alpha prep
description:
The RETROSPECTIVE half of the facade-export classification audit has no bead. Surfaced 2026-07-25 while processing the rf2-fby7o api-freeze dossier; bd list across every status returned no owner for it.

## What it is

spec/Conventions.md:1198 defines the audit in two halves.

The FORWARD half is already running: every new facade export classifies and justifies itself at diff time (tier, owner, status, justification), which is why the Freehand rows in spec/api-manifest.edn all carry their four fields. That half needs nothing.

The RETROSPECTIVE half is unowned. Conventions calls it "the full retrospective sweep of every existing non-front-porch export - and the manifest table it produces" and says it "stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep".

## Scope

A repo-wide sweep of every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core - the grandfathered exceptions Conventions explicitly records - deciding keep / rename / move / internal-public for each, and producing the manifest table.

NOT a Freehand audit. Freehand's 38 members are already classified at diff time; six are :facade? true (mount, unmount!, hydrate-root, ->react, active-connections, command-log) and every one is a CLJS-only verb re-exported from the namespace that owns it, which is exactly the deliberate single-import re-export the Conventions ruling sanctions.

## Deadline

Conventions sets it itself: before re-frame2's first meaningful external alpha/beta release - explicitly NOT "before v1". The reasoning is that the moment real users copy examples, a namespace move becomes a breaking change.

## Relationship to rf2-fby7o

DECOUPLED. rf2-fby7o's release condition names this audit as half of its api-freeze gate. Two independent analyses concluded that coupling is a drafting accident rather than intent: gating a Freehand guide on a re-frame.core sweep that Conventions itself schedules for external-alpha prep does not make the guide more correct. See rf2-fby7o notes (2026-07-25 dossier fold) for the full reasoning. Mike rules on whether the coupling is struck.

## Acceptance

1. Every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core carries a keep / rename / move / internal-public disposition.
2. The manifest table Conventions describes exists.
3. Anything ruled rename or move is either executed or has a bead.
notes:
DEFERRED 2026-07-25 (mayor), with an explicit release condition so it stops being re-triaged every dispatch tick.

WHY NOT NOW: the bead's own charter defers it. spec/Conventions.md:1198 says the retrospective half 'stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep', and the FORWARD half is already running (every new facade export classifies itself at diff time, which is why the Freehand rows in spec/api-manifest.edn carry all four fields). So nothing is rotting while this waits.

THE DECISIVE REASON: it is a repo-wide sweep of every non-front-porch export on re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core, producing a manifest table. The alpha is gated on rf2-vxgfnd.99 (EPIC S7 — Helix-removal wave + alpha tag), which by its own title REMOVES a substrate and will move exactly the surface this sweep would classify. Running the sweep before S7 means classifying exports that S7 then deletes or renames, and redoing the table afterwards. Sequencing it after S7 costs nothing and saves the whole second pass.

RELEASE CONDITION — reopen when EITHER holds:
  1. rf2-vxgfnd.99 (S7 + alpha tag) closes, or
  2. Mike calls api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly.

Not a rejection: the work is real and Conventions mandates it. This is a sequencing decision only.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-22 04:0x AUSEST, tip 0fa90bd815. ONE PARAGRAPH OF THIS BEAD'S SCOPING IS VOID, AND THE DEFERRAL CONDITION IS INTACT. Measured at source; this is the smaller of the two corrections this loop found in the deferred set.

THE VOID PARAGRAPH. This bead says: "NOT a Freehand audit. Freehand's 38 members are already classified at diff time; six are :facade? true (mount, unmount!, hydrate-root, ->react, active-connections, command-log) and every one is a CLJS-only verb re-exported from the namespace that owns it."

MEASURED: spec/api-manifest.edn exists at 501 lines and carries ZERO Freehand rows. Control — the same file returns 482 hits for :facade?, so the grep discriminates and the zero is a reading. implementation/freehand was deleted by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16 (rf2-0yp7w) and its manifest rows went with it.

WHY THIS IS A SMALL CORRECTION AND NOT A RESCOPE, unlike rf2-3t2nq's. That paragraph is a REASSURANCE — it exists to stop a worker widening into Freehand. Its subject no longer exists, so the reassurance is unnecessary rather than misleading, and this bead's actual scope is untouched: re-frame.core, re-frame.story and day8.re-frame2-xray.core, which are all live. Delete the paragraph when the bead is taken; do not rescope around it.

THE DEFERRAL CONDITION IS UNCHANGED AND STILL SOURCED. spec/Conventions.md:1219 in terms: "the full retrospective sweep of every existing non-front-porch export — and the manifest table it produces — stays deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep". The bead reads that correctly and its own deadline paragraph reads it correctly too: before the first meaningful external alpha, explicitly NOT before v1, because the moment real users copy examples a namespace move becomes a breaking change.

WHICH PUTS IT BEHIND THE COORDINATE QUESTION, and it was not on the list I enumerated on rf2-kmqx3. Entering external-alpha prep requires a published artefact, and that is blocked on the io.github.day8 coordinate decision. So the Clojars hold reaches SEVEN beads rather than six — this one has a DEADLINE attached rather than merely a trigger, which is a different kind of cost: the longer the coordinate waits, the more exports accrete that this sweep will have to classify retrospectively, and the forward half only protects exports that landed after the rule.

THE PATTERN WORTH NAMING, because this is the second instance in one pass. The 2026-08-16 deletion of implementation/freehand and implementation/ui invalidated content in at least TWO deferred beads — this one's reassurance paragraph, and rf2-3t2nq's entire recommended sequence plus the architectural blocker it reserved for the operator. Neither was caught for six days, because DEFERRED BEADS ARE OMITTED BY CONSTRUCTION from both bd ready and bd list --status=open, so no dispatch tick has ever looked at them. The freehand residue sweep (rf2-wppza) covered tracked FILES; nothing swept the tracker's own deferred set. Whoever next takes a deletion of that size should re-read the deferred beads as part of it.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-22 22:08 AUSEST. THE FENCE ON THIS BEAD IS NOW A REAL TRACKER EDGE: rf2-kmqx3 blocks
rf2-2hpxo. Added this pass; cycle check clean; `bd blocked` now lists this bead.

WHY, and it is this bead's own finding acted on rather than a new one. This bead already records that
entering external-alpha prep requires a published artefact, and that the artefact is blocked on the
io.github.day8 coordinate decision. That fence lived ONLY IN PROSE, and dependency_count read 0.

THAT IS THE EXACT DEFECT REPAIRED THREE TIMES ALREADY THIS SESSION on the neighbouring beads -
rf2-hic-063 and rf2-hic-090 had NO edge, and rf2-fo4ng had a discovered-from edge that reads like a
dependency on the record and carries no force. This bead was the last one in the chain still
prose-only. The harm was latent rather than live only because the defer keeps it off both lists;
un-defer it and it would have listed as ready with its fence invisible.

THE EDGE ENCODES ONE ARM DELIBERATELY, exactly as rf2-hic-090's does. spec/Conventions.md:1219
defers this sweep to "API-freeze / external-alpha prep" - a DISJUNCTION, and only the second arm
routes through rf2-kmqx3. If API-freeze arrives first and independently, REMOVING THIS EDGE IS THE
VISIBLE ACT OF TAKING THAT ARM. Encoding the artefact arm costs nothing and stops the bead
advertising itself as ready; leaving it unencoded cost the ready list its meaning.

NOTHING ELSE CHANGES. Status stays deferred with no date - correct, because no date can express
either arm. No ruling implied. The deadline-shaped cost this bead already records is untouched: the
longer the coordinate waits, the more exports accrete that this sweep must classify retrospectively,
and the forward half only protects exports that landed after the rule.

title: method: two loop bodies bind the mayor to ai/worktree-agent-ids.tsv and the method tree never specifies it — header and rows disagree by one column, and the done-sentence column the reaping rule turns on is absent from every row
description:
FOUND BY THE HYGIENE LOOP 2026-08-22, and it cost a wrong reading in the same tick that found it.

THE GAP. Two loop bodies bind the mayor to ai/worktree-agent-ids.tsv -- the dispatch loop
("Record the dispatch in ai/worktree-agent-ids.tsv at dispatch time") and the hygiene loop
("ai/worktree-agent-ids.tsv holds the dispatch-time mapping"). THE METHOD TREE NEVER NAMES IT.
Measured under docs/the-mayor-method/ with four patterns -- 'agent-ids', 'worktree-agent', '\.tsv',
'dispatch-time mapping' -- all ZERO. Control: the same tree DOES carry 'completion report' and the
reaping rule at loops.md:849, so the greps discriminate and the zeros are readings.

So the file has no column contract anywhere, and it has drifted.

WHAT THE DRIFT IS, measured at source this tick. The file's own header line reads:
    # worktree  agentId  dispatched  beads  done-sentence (blank until the agent reports)
FIVE names. But every dispatch row carries SIX fields, because the BRANCH sits between
'dispatched' and the beads:
    <path>  <agentId>  <timestamp>  worker/revorder-csca8  rf2-csca8
The header does not name the branch, so every field after 'dispatched' is shifted by one and the
'done-sentence' column -- the one the reaping rule turns on -- IS NOT PRESENT ON ANY ROW.

HOW IT FAILED, which is the part worth keeping. Reading column 5 as the header names it returned a
DONE-SENTENCE for 17 of 30 live worktrees. Every one of those values was a BEAD ID. The read was
correct, well-formed, and answered a different question from the one asked -- the exact family
loops.md's '## Tracker mechanics' clause names. Nothing errored, and the answer was the reassuring
one: it would have authorised reaping 17 worktrees on no report at all. Caught only by looking at
the values rather than the count.

A SECOND, SMALLER STALENESS in the same header: it cites '.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md
(rf2-cp0dd)' as the file's authority. That path does not exist -- the command-file arm was retired,
and CLAUDE.md dropped it from the gate paragraph in b3782d0b14. So the header points at a document
that is gone.

AND THE MAYOR'S OWN APPENDS MADE IT WORSE, recorded rather than hidden: rows I appended this session
used a different layout again (bare worktree name in column 1 instead of the full path), which is
why a name-keyed grep returned 0 rows for 28 worktrees that do have rows.

WHAT A REPAIR LOOKS LIKE, for whoever takes it -- this is a METHOD-tree edit, not an ai/ edit:
specify the file where the loops that depend on it can see the spec, with the column list matching
what dispatch actually writes, and say explicitly which column the reaping rule reads. The ai/ file
is local-only and regenerable; the contract is what is missing.

NOT URGENT: no work was lost, and the hygiene rule's default is safe -- anything with no quotable
report STAYS, so a shifted column can only ever cause a WRONGFUL REAP, never a lost one. But that is
the expensive direction.
notes:

premise in my own description above is WRONG and must not reach a worker unchallenged.

I WROTE: "every dispatch row carries SIX fields, because the BRANCH sits between 'dispatched' and

A SECOND CORRECTION while I am here: I wrote that '.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md' does not
exist. Understated -- the whole '.claude/commands/' DIRECTORY does not exist. The header cites a

AND THE THIRD PARAGRAPH OF THE DESCRIPTION STANDS, re-measured at this tip rather than carried:

'done-sentence' all return 0 under docs/the-mayor-method/, against a control of 1 for 'completion
report'. The method tree does not specify this file anywhere.
FENCE recorded 2026-08-22 22:56 AUSEST by the dispatch tick, so no later tick re-derives it.

IN FLIGHT. Dispatched to worker 'tsvspec', branch worker/tsvspec-83z0, worktree
C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/tsvspec. The agent id is recorded in the mayor's local
dispatch log at dispatch time.

SURFACE HELD: docs/the-mayor-method/**, and loops.md in particular. That file is the hot one here --
two changes landed on it within the hour before this dispatch (PRs #8708 and #8709) and both are on
origin/main. DO NOT DISPATCH A SECOND WORKER onto the method tree while this one runs; sequence it

NOT A RULING, NOT AWAITING MIKE. This is the one bead on the board that needed no operator decision,

OBLIGATION DISCHARGED %s, in the same tick that closed this bead and recorded it.

The close reason ends: "WHAT REMAINS UNDONE ... the local file's own header still cites
.claude/commands/mayor-hygiene.md, under a directory that no longer exists ... correcting the header

DONE. The mayor corrected it. The header's field-name line now reads

THE WORKER DID NOT STOP ON IT, AND WAS RIGHT NOT TO: the falsity makes the repair SMALLER rather

A FOURTH FINDING NEITHER I NOR THE BEAD HAD. Asked which column the reap test reads, the honest

PLACEMENT, and the reasoning is normative rather than preferential. docs/the-mayor-method/README.md

title: Consolidate 73 ad-hoc IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT set/restore sites onto one shared fixture
description:
Carried over from rf2-76lhy step 2, which closed on PR #7190 having delivered step 1 (the capture-time profile). This half was never done and should not be lost with the parent.

73 test files set and restore the process-global IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT by hand, with no shared fixture. A test that throws between the set and the restore leaks the flag into every subsequent namespace in the bundle - a cross-namespace coupling that no assertion can catch and that only shows up as unexplained slowness or flakiness later in the run.

IMPORTANT CONTEXT, so this is not over-sold. rf2-76lhy originally advanced the leak as the explanation for a suspected 3-4x CI slowdown. The per-namespace profile shipped in PR #7190 dissolved that: 73% of the lane's wall clock is 7 benchmark namespaces, the three recorded CI stop points all sit at 92-97% of the lane, and the CI/local gap is a uniform ~1.7x. There is no longer evidence pointing at the leak.

So this is a HYGIENE bead, not a bug hunt. It retires a real hazard class on its own terms - one use-fixtures with the restore in a finally - and it is worth doing, but nothing is currently known to be broken by it. Size it accordingly and do not let it grow into an audit.

Fenced away from the PR #7190 runner work; this is implementation/**/test/** across many artefacts, so it wants its own dispatch.
notes:
INVESTIGATED, NOT DONE (PR #7193 worker, 2026-07-28). Recommendation: leave it, or do it per-artefact later. This is the honest 'not worth doing now'.

CENSUS IS BIGGER THAN THE BEAD SAYS: 78 files, 175 `set!` sites, across NINE trees — freehand 43, ui 15, adapters 7, ssr 6, tools/story 2, tools/machines-viz 2, machines 1, core 1, scripts 1. Not 73, and not one artefact.

THERE IS NO SMALL, OBVIOUSLY-CORRECT CONSOLIDATION TO ADOPT. The nearest existing shared fixture is `re-frame.ui.test/act-operation!`, which already does exactly the right thing (reads the prior value, sets true, restores the PRIOR value — not `false` — after React settles). But it lives in implementation/ui/SRC, a published and EXPERIMENTAL artefact surface. Adopting it from freehand / ssr / adapters / machines test trees would make those artefacts' tests depend on re-frame.ui. That is an architectural decision, not hygiene, and it is Mike's. The alternative — mint a new shared test-support surface every artefact may require — is also a decision, not a sweep.

WHAT DOES EXIST is per-artefact convergence: freehand already has mount_support.cljs and bench/b6_harness.cljs; ssr has SIX files carrying byte-identical `disable-act-env!`/`restore-act-env!` pairs. So the tractable shape is PER-ARTEFACT, ONE PR EACH — freehand first (43 of the 78 files, landing spot already present), then ssr (6 files, pure duplication), then ui.

WHY NOT NOW. (1) The motivation is gone: PR #7190's profile dissolved the 3-4x CI-slowdown hypothesis this was step 2 of, and PR #7193 confirmed it on a second box — the whole gap was seven benchmark namespaces (71% of the browser lane's wall clock), and the CI factor is a uniform ~1.7x. There is still no observed instance of the leak. (2) A 78-file mechanical edit across nine trees is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open PR touching a mounted test. (3) Every one of those trees was outside PR #7193's fence, so it could not have been done there in any case.

If someone does pick it up: rule FIRST on whether re-frame.ui.test's act door may be the repo-wide answer, because that ruling decides whether this is one shared fixture or nine private ones.
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review):

DECISION — leave the sweep undone now; bead DEFERRED. No 78-file mechanical edit during the current mounted-test churn: the motivating CI-slowdown hypothesis was dissolved by measurement (seven benchmark namespaces + a uniform ~1.7x CI factor), and the sweep is a maximal merge-conflict change against every open mounted-test PR. Pick this up only when the high-conflict Freehand work settles AND either a real leak instance bites or an artefact's mounted tests are being reworked anyway — then land it artefact-sized, not repo-wide.

RECORD CORRECTION (from the Codex second opinion; commits verified in this checkout): "no observed instance" is true of the PERFORMANCE theory only. Flag leakage itself has occurred and been repaired — 43ce4cf9f6 and 1fff5b618b (shared-page act-discipline, ~361 warnings) and 0dd432b9ed (un-restored act boundary after a negative-control run, 755 warnings). The hazard class is real and observed; the slowdown attribution is what was disproved. P3 stands.

ARCHITECTURAL ANSWER (binding — do not re-litigate):
1. DONOR DEPENDENCY FORBIDDEN. No artefact's tests may require re-frame.ui (src or test): F6e deletes the artefact, and re-frame.ui.test/act-operation! is a private defn- coupled to donor internals in any case. Its invariant is the SHAPE to copy, never the namespace to require: capture the incoming flag value and restore the PRIOR value — not a blanket false — on every exit path (synchronous throw, Promise fulfilment, Promise rejection).
2. ONE repo-private implementation, NOT nine per-artefact copies. Home: the existing lightweight dependency-free shared surface implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs (or a narrowly named sibling in the same core/test root). Verified: it is already required across an artefact boundary today (adapters/uix test) and sits on the consolidated Shadow classpath, so this mints no new architecture and survives F6e. Per-artefact is the DELIVERY boundary — artefact-sized PRs, freehand first (43 files, through its existing mount_support.cljs facade), ssr second (6 byte-identical disable/restore pairs) — not the implementation boundary. Nine permanent copies would reproduce at repo scale exactly the drift ssr's six copies already demonstrate.
3. Design floor for whoever lands it (from Codex, ratified): the helper takes the desired mode — both true (act-disciplined renders) and false (timing discriminators, hydration, deliberate un-acted negative controls) are legitimate, so no runner-wide constant. One save/restore engine with thin sync-wrapping and async-map fixture adapters (cljs.test forbids mixing the two fixture kinds; async tests need the map form) plus a Promise-aware operation bracket for callbacks that reject before done; overlapping async scopes rejected or serialized. Leave re-frame.ui.test self-contained until F6e and skip migrating ui test files the deletion gate removes.

Disposition: deferred (was open P3). Reopen against the conditions above.

THE COUNT ESSENTIALLY HOLDS: 70 tracked files carry IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT with .beads excluded, against the 73 in the description. That is close enough that the hazard class is unchanged.

BUT THE ARTEFACT ORDER IS DEAD. The ratified plan says 'freehand first (43 files, through its existing mount_support.cljs facade), ssr second (6 byte-identical disable/restore pairs)'. implementation/freehand/ was DELETED by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16 and git ls-files returns 0 under it. SO THE POPULATION DID NOT SHRINK WHEN FREEHAND WENT — IT MOVED. Hicasso now carries 50 of the 70, which is where freehand's share went. Read HICASSO FIRST wherever the plan says freehand, and re-derive its facade rather than assuming a mount_support.cljs equivalent exists.

WHAT STILL HOLDS, verified: the named home implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_test_support.cljs EXISTS at the tip, so item 2 of the ratified design (one repo-private implementation, not nine per-artefact copies) needs no re-pointing. Items 1 and 3 are about SHAPE and are unaffected by the retirement.

WHY IT IS NOT DISPATCHED THIS TICK: it is 70 CLJS test files across 10 trees and its gate is heavyweight (per-artefact npm run test:cljs). worker/retake-07rnj holds the box with a CLOCK window from 10:27. Dispatch it on a free box, artefact-sized PRs, hicasso first.

THE BLOCKER THE 2026-07-28 INVESTIGATION RESERVED FOR MIKE IS MOOT. Its words: the nearest existing shared fixture is re-frame.ui.test/act-operation!, it lives in implementation/ui/SRC, and adopting it from other trees "would make those artefacts' tests depend on re-frame.ui. That is an architectural decision, not hygiene, and it is Mike's."

implementation/ui WAS DELETED by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16 (rf2-0yp7w), along with implementation/freehand. git grep for act-operation! now returns ONE file, .beads/issues.jsonl -- that is bead PROSE, not code. The fixture is gone, so there is nothing to depend on and no decision left to make. Nobody noticed because a deferred bead is invisible to the dispatch tick by construction.

MEASURED AT TIP (git grep -l IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT, 71 hits of which one is .beads/issues.jsonl):

    implementation/adapters    7

It is now ONE TREE CARRYING 71% OF THE SITES, with the blocker gone. A single-artefact consolidation inside implementation/hicasso would retire 50 of 70 sites in one PR against one landing spot.

I AM NOT PROPOSING TO DISPATCH IT, and the reason is the bead's own and still holds: "the motivation is gone -- PR #7190's profile dissolved the 3-4x CI-slowdown hypothesis this was step 2 of, and nothing is currently known to be broken by it." A hazard class worth retiring on its own terms is not the same as work worth taking now, and the stance is explicit about not letting a hygiene bead grow into an audit.

BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-23 09:06:02 AUSEST, tip b7ebe23dd7. NOTHING NEW MEASURED; THIS RECORDS WHAT SHAPE OF HOLD THIS IS,

FOUR OF THE FIVE PREMISES DO NOT HOLD IN THIS TREE.

1. THERE ARE NO SET/RESTORE PAIRS. All 51 in-scope sites are

   — HAS NO INSTANCE HERE. There is no restore for a throw to skip.

   Repo-wide the pattern is nearly as rare: of 90 raw `set!` lines, 66 set `false`, 22
   set `true`, and exactly TWO restore a captured prior value —
   implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:3351 and
   implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/ssr_startup_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:223. Both
   are outside hicasso. The set/restore bracket the bead describes is 2 of 90 sites
   repo-wide, in two files, in two other artefacts.

2. THE PACKAGE ALREADY HAS THE SHARED HELPER, AND MOST OF THE TREE ALREADY USES IT.
   `leave-act-environment!` is defined at checkpoint_support.cljs:161 and
   roots_frames_support.cljs:76, and 34 files / 38 call sites in this very tree already
   call it. Repo-wide there are 98 converted call sites — 59 in the bench tree, 38 in

   (38 converted vs 51 raw), not 0%.

3. THE CENSUS METHOD UNDERCOUNTS BY CONSTRUCTION, and this is the correction that
   reframes the bead. A CONVERTED site does not contain the literal
   `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` — it reads `(support/leave-act-environment!)`. So
   `git grep IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` measures the UNCONVERTED TAIL, never the
   population. The recorded "69 files / 100 sites, nine trees" is a remainder. The real
   population is that remainder plus 98 already-converted call sites, and the shape of

   fixture into a tree that has none".

   the restore in a `finally`" would RE-ENTER the act environment after each test. Every
   docstring in the tree says the disable is deliberate and LANE-WIDE, not a bracket:

   violate the dispatch's own "no behaviour change" requirement. The one restoring idiom

   The fifth premise — that the population might be heterogeneous — is wrong in the safe

The two helper definitions are byte-identical and the 34 existing callers split between
them with no principle: 22 files take it from checkpoint-support (THE MICROTASK-CHECKPOINT

imperative_sdk_dom_cljs_test and native_hooks_dom_cljs_test all require the multi-root
witness harness for exactly that. That is a latent wart in the converted half.

Of the 45 raw files, only 8 already require one of the two support namespaces (a free

bd dep tree's READY/BLOCKED BADGE COUNTS ONLY *OPEN* BLOCKERS — A DEFERRED BLOCKER IS INVISIBLE TO IT, SO THE BADGE FAILS OPEN (measured 2026-08-23 09:47 AUSEST, tip f05b2c2312).

THE DISAGREEMENT. 'bd dep tree <id>' prints a READY or BLOCKED badge beside the root. It disagrees with 'bd ready' exactly when every unclosed blocker is DEFERRED:

  rf2-hic-090  blocker t32wg (deferred)   -> badge READY    not in bd ready
  rf2-kmqx3    blocker uelji (deferred)   -> badge READY    not in bd ready
  rf2-hic-063  blocker kmqx3 (OPEN)       -> badge BLOCKED  not in bd ready
  rf2-hic-064  blocker hic-090 (OPEN)     -> badge BLOCKED  not in bd ready

Two instances of the disagreement and two controls, so the discriminator is the blocker's STATUS and nothing else. 'bd ready' is the conservative instrument and the correct one for dispatch: undone work is undone whether or not somebody deferred it.

WHY THIS IS WORTH KNOWING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT. The badge does not merely differ, it fails in the direction that costs a worker, and it does so on the two beads with the tracker's hardest operator gates in front of them. rf2-hic-090 is the bead that has already consumed FOUR dispatches (PRs #8312, #8395, #8445, #8560), each running its evidence families correctly and each declining to close for the same unruled reason. A mayor who opens the dependency tree — the natural thing to do when asking 'why is this blocked?' — is shown the word READY on precisely that bead.

AND IT IS A THIRD ROUTE TO THE SAME MISTAKE, which is why the existing fence does not cover it. rf2-hic-090's own note anticipates the ready-view route and says the block was once PROSE rather than a tracker edge; that hole was closed by adding the edge. The badge route survives the fix, because the edge now EXISTS and the badge still ignores it.

THE RULE: dispatchability is 'bd ready' plus the bead's own newest note. A dependency tree is for reading the SHAPE of a chain — who pins whom — never for deciding whether to send a worker.

THREE REGISTERED WORKTREES LIVE OUTSIDE THE WORKTREE PARENT AND THE REMOVAL SCRIPT REFUSES THEM (seen 2026-08-23 09:30 AUSEST).

WHAT THEY ARE: C:/Users/miket/.grok/worktrees/code-re-frame2/subagent-019f98e1-* — three of them, all detached at 0f6fa33cb7 ('chore(beads): audit merged PR 6963', 2026-07-25), which IS contained in main. Each carries a STAGED .beads/issues.jsonl from that day. No file under any of them has been written since 2026-08-20 (find -newermt returns nothing), so they are month-old husks with no live process.

WHY THEY MATTER AND WHY THEY ARE NOT URGENT: a commit made from one of those trees would push a 2026-07-25 full-database export over the tracker — the exact time-travel failure CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section describes, a month wide. What stops it is that nothing runs there, plus the pre-commit hook's 90%-of-HEAD floor on a staged .beads/issues.jsonl, which fires from every worktree once installed. So the hazard is real but doubly latched.

THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT MATTERS FOR REAPING: these are NOT worker worktrees. scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh refuses any root outside the worktree parent (the re-frame2-worktrees sibling), by design, so the ordinary path will not clear them and retrying it is futile. They also carry no node_modules junction, which is the whole reason that script exists — so the risk it guards against does not apply here either. Clearing them is a plain 'git worktree remove' plus a prune, and the check before doing it is the same one used above: nothing written since a date well after their creation, and a head that is contained in main so nothing unpublished can be lost.

DO NOT TAKE THE DIRECTORY NAME AS EVIDENCE OF WHO MADE THEM. They sit under a .grok path, i.e. a different harness's worktree area, not this method's. That is why a worktree census keyed to the worktree parent misses them entirely — 'git worktree list' is the roster, never the parent directory listing.

bd history <id>'s NEWEST ENTRY IS A DATABASE-COMMIT TIME, NOT A BEAD-MUTATION TIME — ON A BUSY TRACKER EVERY BEAD SHARES THE SAME NEWEST TIMESTAMP (measured 2026-08-23 10:03 AUSEST, tip c951fe8ef3).

WHAT I DID AND WHAT IT RETURNED. Asking 'when did each held bead last really change?', I took the max timestamp out of 'bd history <id>' for all 21 open+deferred beads. Every one came back 2026-08-23 09:50:19 — identical to the second, across beads I had not touched in days. That is the reassuring, useless answer: it says everything changed a minute ago.

THE MECHANISM. bd history lists Dolt commits, and every bd write commits the database, so a commit appears in a bead's history whether or not that bead moved. rf2-3t2nq shows 9728 entries; its four newest snapshots (09:50:19, 09:50:18, 09:34:21, 09:06:03) diff to NO FIELDS DIFFERING against their predecessors. Entry counts differ per bead only because a bead's history starts when the bead does (rf2-hic-090 has 7137, being younger).

THE HELP TEXT IS WRONG. 'bd history --help' says it shows 'all commits where the issue was modified'. Measured, it shows all commits, full stop.

THE METHOD THAT WORKS is the one the backlog-reread loop already prescribes, and this is WHY it prescribes it: take 'bd history <id> --json --limit N', walk ADJACENT PAIRS newest-first, diff the embedded Issue snapshot, and stop at the first pair where a text-bearing field (notes, description, status, priority, close reason) actually differs. Two-sided control run at the same tip: rf2-hic-090, which I had appended a note to minutes earlier, reports its first real change at 09:50:19 on 'notes'; rf2-3t2nq, untouched, walks past three identical pairs to a real change at 09:06:03. Across the 21 beads the true newest mutations spread over two days, from 2026-08-22 11:05 to 2026-08-23 09:50 — the actual signal, which the max-timestamp read had flattened to a single instant.

TWO MECHANICAL TRAPS IN RUNNING IT. Pass --limit (default is all, and a full history is thousands of full issue snapshots). And decode the output as UTF-8 explicitly: on this setup the default codec dies with UnicodeDecodeError on any note containing an em-dash or a curly quote, which is most of them.

A POLLING PROCESS IS INVISIBLE TO THE STRANDED SWEEP'S WRITE CLOCK — IT MOVES EXACTLY ONE FILE, $GIT_DIR/FETCH_HEAD (measured 2026-08-23 10:28 AUSEST).

WHAT SIX SWEEPS GOT WRONG. The worktree pr-audit-8445 was read on seven consecutive stranded sweeps and reported each time as silent for hours: file-tree newest write 03:13:10, git index 03:38:20, both static. Each sweep correctly declined to reap it, but on the reasoning 'cannot tell from spacing alone'. It was in fact alive the whole time. Reading .git/worktrees/pr-audit-8445/FETCH_HEAD three times gave 10:26:44, 10:27:26, 10:28:08 — 42 seconds apart, twice. Something in there runs git fetch on a 42-second cadence.

THE MECHANISM. A process that only polls neither edits a file nor touches the index, so the two clocks a sweep naturally reaches for never move. But a fetch is a write, and it lands in exactly one place: FETCH_HEAD, which is PER-WORKTREE ($GIT_DIR for a linked worktree is .git/worktrees/<name>, so a fetch run from the mayor checkout writes .git/FETCH_HEAD and never the worktree's). That per-worktree property is what makes it usable as a liveness probe.

THE CONTROLS MAKE IT A DISCRIMINATOR RATHER THAN AN OBSERVATION. Every worker worktree HAS a FETCH_HEAD — hotzone 08-21 09:37:38, repoint 08-21 09:15:58, specsize 08-22 00:29:33 — each frozen at the moment that worker died. Only the live one moves. Worktrees created by a different harness had none at all. So the file's PRESENCE says nothing; two reads a minute apart say everything.

WHY IT MATTERS AND IN WHICH DIRECTION IT FAILS. The blind spot makes a LIVE process look STOPPED, which is the direction that authorises reaping. The existing guidance gets you to the right suspicion and then stops one step short: it says a worker that is only READING touches nothing. A poller is not merely reading — it writes, once per interval, to a file the sweep was not looking at.

HOW TO RUN IT: stat .git/worktrees/<name>/FETCH_HEAD twice, 30-60 seconds apart. Movement is proof of life and needs no corroboration. Absence of movement is still not proof of death — it only restores the situation the older clocks described.

FOOTNOTE ON THE TWO OLDER CLOCKS, since they disagree and both are real: .git/worktrees/<n>/index moves when the worker stages or commits; the file tree moves when it edits or checks out. Neither is wrong, they answer different questions, and the earlier sweeps' recorded numbers were the index clock.

THE TRACKER'S 'parent' FIELD IS IN USE — 37 BEADS CARRY ONE — AND ENUMERATING CHILDREN BY ID PREFIX MISSES 40% OF THEM (measured 2026-08-23 11:04 AUSEST, tip 88362471d4). This CORRECTS an earlier reading of my own that recorded the field as unused.

THE CENSUS, over all 1001 open + deferred + closed beads: 37 carry a non-empty 'parent'. Every one of the 37 is CLOSED. No open bead is a child, and — checked in the other direction, which is the one that matters for a backlog pass — NO OPEN BEAD HAS CHILDREN. The three parents named are rf2-0yp7w (the ui/freehand retirement epic), rf2-0yp7w.9 (its prose sweep) and rf2-2rtt6 (the Hicasso programme epic), all closed.

SO THE CORRECT STATEMENT IS NOT 'the field is unused'. It is 'the mechanism exists and is used, and it currently touches nothing on the board' — which is stronger, because it says the re-enumeration is a real check that happened to return empty rather than a check against a field nobody populates.

THE PREFIX TRAP, REPRODUCED WITH NUMBERS RATHER THAN QUOTED. rf2-0yp7w.9 has TEN true children by the parent field. A prefix scan for 'rf2-0yp7w.9' finds SIX and misses FOUR: rf2-5z6bb, rf2-c95do, rf2-n9hno, rf2-v14sq. Those four are generated ids that share no prefix with their parent.

AND THE MISS IS THE REASSURING KIND, which is why it is worth writing down. The six the prefix scan DOES find are .1 through .6 — a contiguous, gapless run that reads as a complete set. Nothing about the result looks truncated, so there is no prompt to go looking for the other four. That is the same failure shape as every other well-formed wrong answer in this tracker: right-looking, confidently returned, 60% complete.

HOW TO ENUMERATE: read the 'parent' field off the JSON listing and group by it. Never derive children from the id string.

title: loops.md: FETCH_HEAD absence does not prove that no fetch ever ran
description:
FOUND BY THE MERGED-PR AUDIT OF PR #8721.

THE DEFECT. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md now says each linked worktree gets its own fetch-head copy "the first time anything fetches from it", and that an absent file says "nothing has ever fetched from that tree". The first half of the correction is measured and sound: in the current repository, git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD resolves to a private metadata path for every linked worktree, and exactly four of seven linked worktrees have the file, matching the PR. The absolute inference from absence is not sound.

THE DIRECT COUNTEREXAMPLE IS PART OF GIT'S NORMAL INTERFACE, not a hypothetical deletion. Git 2.53's git fetch -h documents --[no-]write-fetch-head: a fetch can deliberately update refs without writing FETCH_HEAD. That is directly relevant to this paragraph's automated poller case. Such a poller can fetch forever while the per-worktree file remains absent. Therefore absence proves only that no fetch has written this clock in that worktree (or that the file is no longer there); it does not prove that no fetch has ever run.

IMPACT. The safe, load-bearing direction survives: movement is still proof that a writing fetch ran, while stillness proves nothing about liveness. The defect is confined to the new interpretation of absence, but that interpretation is the point of PR #8721 and can send a reader looking for the wrong history on an externally created tree.

MINIMAL REMEDY. Qualify the two new sentences in place: a linked worktree gets this file when a fetch writes FETCH_HEAD there, and absence means no fetch has written this particular clock. Briefly state that a poller configured not to write FETCH_HEAD is invisible to the clock. Preserve the four-of-seven measurement, the movement/stillness asymmetry, and the rest of the paragraph. Do not add machinery or a policy gate for this prose correction.
acceptance_criteria: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md no longer says every fetch necessarily creates FETCH_HEAD or that file absence proves no fetch ever ran. It preserves the measured four-of-seven observation and the rule that movement is positive proof while a non-moving clock cannot establish liveness. The repair remains prose-only.
close_reason:
FIXED — PR #8722 merged, closed by the mayor at tip e5429f3862, verified at source.

THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE EDIT, not taken from the bead. git 2.53.0 here, and 'git fetch -h' lists --[no-]write-fetch-head, so a fetch can update refs without writing the clock. The finding is correct and the over-claim was mine, made in PR #8721 forty minutes earlier.

WHAT LANDED, one file, +18/-15, prose only, no machinery and no gate as the bead directed:
  * 'the first time anything fetches from it' -> 'the first time a fetch WRITES that clock there', with 'a fetch ORDINARILY writes as it reads' opening the sentence.
  * absence 'says only that nothing has ever fetched from that tree' -> 'says less than it looks like saying: only that no fetch has written that clock there, which is not the same as no fetch having run, because the write is suppressible by a flag on the fetch itself — a poller configured that way is invisible to this test altogether.'
  * the guidance moved with it: absence is now a reason to reach for another signal rather than a history of the tree, while staying a hint about a tree you did not create.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, CHECKED MECHANICALLY rather than asserted: 'first time anything fetches from it' 0, 'ever fetched from that tree' 0, 'four of seven' 1, 'Movement is proof of life' 1, 'stillness restores the ambiguity' 1, 'the write is suppressible' 1. Every criterion the bead stated is met and the load-bearing direction is untouched.

THE FLAG IS DESCRIBED BY WHAT IT DOES RATHER THAN BY ITS SPELLING — 'suppressible by a flag on the fetch itself'. A literal option name in this document would be a measured constant of the kind the method-reread loop watches go stale, and it buys nothing a reader of that paragraph needs.

'git branch -d' IS NOT A GUARD AGAINST DELETING UNMERGED WORK — IT COUNTS 'MERGED TO ITS UPSTREAM' AS MERGED, SO A PUSHED BRANCH DELETES AS READILY UNDER -d AS UNDER -D (measured this session, 2026-08-23).

WHAT HAPPENED. Reaching for -d as the safe form, I deleted worker/receipts-hic081. It carried THREE commits that exist nowhere else — 'git cherry origin/main' reads +3 new — and -d deleted it without a murmur, because the branch was fully merged to its OWN upstream, which is all that refusal tests. Nothing was lost only because the commits were on origin; the branch was restored at ae14841ab3 and its upstream re-set, verified equal.

THE REAL LESSON IS NOT ABOUT THE FLAG. Ten minutes earlier I had declined to test a removal script's dry-run against a live worktree, on exactly the reasoning that an experiment on live state is not free. Then I ran an experiment on a branch because a branch felt cheap. The category was the same and only the object differed.

THE GUARD THAT ACTUALLY WORKS is patch-equivalence against the TRUNK, computed yourself before deleting anything: 'git cherry origin/main <branch>', where a leading + is a commit genuinely not in main and a leading - is one already contained. This repo merges by REBASE, which is why ancestry and ahead-count are both wrong here, in opposite directions — and why -d's own notion of merged is wrong a third way.

A RELATED TRAP LIVES IN THE SAME CONFIG. A local branch keeps its branch.<name>.merge upstream setting after the remote branch is gone and the remote-tracking ref has been pruned. Three worker branches are in that state right now. A dangling upstream silently changes what -d compares against, so the flag's behaviour depends on repository state you cannot see from the command line.

AND NOTE WHICH TEST APPLIES TO WHAT: merge state is the test for a BRANCH, never for a worktree. A worktree is reaped only on its worker's own quotable completion report.

THE CHANGED-SURFACE CLASSIFIER TAKES AN EXPLICIT PATH LIST AND RUNS LOCALLY IN SECONDS, SO A PR BODY'S 'NOT NOMINATED' LINE CAN BE MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED (verified 2026-08-23 12:25 AUSEST, tip 233639d579).

It was true, which is the dangerous kind of luck: an unchecked premise that happens to hold teaches you nothing and leaves the habit intact. ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED — PR #8724 (branch worker/nightly-2ohy), 2026-08-23 13:40 AUSEST.

## What it is

`shadow.test.env/get-test-data` is a MACRO. It expands, at the moment the
runner namespace is compiled, into a literal map naming every test var the
compiler knows about — the test roster is frozen into the runner's compiled JS.

shadow-cljs keys its per-namespace compile cache off `:immediate-deps`, which
`shadow.build.resolve/stack-pop` fills from the ns form's own requires. The
`:browser-test` target attaches the discovered test namespaces to the runner as
`:extra-requires` (`shadow.build.test-util/inject-extra-requires`), and those
are read only by `shadow.build.compiler/par-compile-one` to ORDER compilation —
they never enter `:immediate-deps`. So the roster can change completely without
invalidating the runner's cache entry.

A namespace LEAVING the roster is the destructive direction: the stale cached
expansion still dereferences vars whose namespaces are no longer in the bundle.
Under :advanced that is a property read on undefined, uncaught, inside `init` —
zero namespaces announced, no cljs.test summary, exactly the observed abort.

## The bead's hypothesis was RIGHT about the trigger, wrong about the mechanism

The correlation with the Freehand / re-frame.ui removal is REAL and causal: PR
#8322 took fourteen `*-elision-prod-test` namespaces out of this lane on 08-16.
But nothing in the prod-elision build 'still reaches a deleted surface' in the
source sense — the source is fine, and a CLEAN local run of
`npm run test:browser-prod-elision` has been green throughout (measured: exit 0,
91 tests / 289 assertions on current main). The reach-into-deleted-surface
happens in a STALE COMPILED ARTEFACT, and it needs a warm cache to exist at all.
`expensive-tests.yml` restores `implementation/.shadow-cljs` with
`restore-keys: <os>-story-xray-shadow-`, so from 08-16 every nightly served the
pre-removal runner out of cache. That is why the failure is CI-only and why it
persisted for seven nights.

The 'me' in the message is not meaningful: it is a Closure-assigned minified
property name, per bundle. The local reproduction produced the identical defect
reading '$j'.

## The fix

`{:dev/always true}` on the ns. Despite the name,
`shadow.build.compiler/is-cache-blocked?` reads that key with NO mode gate, so
it blocks caching under `release` exactly as under :dev. This is not invention —
it is what the stock `shadow.test.browser` and `shadow.test.node` runners
already carry, and what this repo's own `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node`
already carries WITH A COMMENT saying it is required because get-test-data is a
macro. The two browser prod runners were written from the stock runner's BODY
without its ns metadata.

Fixed both, because both have the defect:
  - re-frame.prod-elision-runner        (implementation/core/test/...)
  - re-frame.schemas-boundary-prod-runner (implementation/schemas/test/...)

`git grep get-test-data` over tracked .cljs/.cljc returns exactly five
namespaces; the other three already carried the metadata. Inventory complete,
no sixth site.

No workflow / cache-key / shadow-cljs.edn change — those would treat the
symptom. The cache is not wrong to be warm; the runner was wrong to be cacheable.

## Verified in both directions, by planting the real event at 1/14 scale

Removed ONE `*-elision-prod-test` namespace against a warm cache. Exit codes
captured from the runner, not reported by the harness:

  before fix, full roster      —            Ran 91 tests / 289 assertions   exit 0
  before fix, one ns removed   0 compiled   ABORTED, 0 namespaces, TypeError exit 1
  after  fix, one ns removed   1 compiled   Ran 88 tests / 285 assertions   exit 0
  after  fix, full roster      1 compiled   Ran 91 tests / 289 assertions   exit 0

Row 2 IS the CI failure, reproduced locally: same abort text, same '0
namespaces announced', same `Object.<mangled> [as init]` frame. Row 3 is the
discrimination — the identical plant goes green after the fix, with the runner
recompiling (0 -> 1) on a source file that did not change. Plant restored and
verified by git blob hash, not by reading a diff.

Also green: `npm run test:browser-schemas-boundary-prod` (exit 0, 8 tests / 15
assertions), the sibling lane the same fix covers. Both re-run after rebase onto
the final base. Both lanes are PR-gated in test.yml and this diff classes
cljs_prod=true, so CI covers them on the PR too.

opened 2026-08-16T16:01:50Z, labelled nightly-red, assigned to
mike-thompson-day8, body naming the exact failing step; edited nightly, last

downstream — the alerter edits in place, which notifies nobody, so seven reds
produced one notification, and nothing escalates an open nightly-red issue or
bridges it into beads. Filed as rf2-4a0c with the evidence and three candidate
shapes; it asks for a ruling rather than picking one, because the trade-off
against notification spam is an operator call.
