RULING 2026-08-29 15:33:14 AUSEST (delegated review per Mike, 2026-08-29): Option A - re-frame.hicasso.native shrinks to exactly two public hooks, n/use-sub and n/use-frame; n/$, n/props, n/defcomponent, n/memo, n/lazy and the 7 expansion-only names are deleted; islands are UIx defui or raw React components mounted through h/defhost or [:>].
BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:33:14 AUSEST: ruled.

HOW THIS WAS DECIDED. The dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-6c12m.3.native-tier.md, deleted after this note was verified) recommended A. A second reviewer appended a "Codex Recommendation" that also chose A and set a proportionate implementation bar. No text in the file argued for B, C or D. The delegate re-verified the evidence at tip on 2026-08-29 and adopted A WITH the Codex conditions: (1) reduce the namespace's public census to the two hooks, everything supporting them private; (2) re-spell the HMR, imperative-host and Xray fixtures in ordinary React or UIx, keeping focused proof that the hooks preserve frame isolation, subscription lifecycle, teardown and Xray visibility; (3) keep one generic direct-React-return test and a raw-React parity floor; commission NO new benchmark run to justify the deletion; retire or clearly qualify the old worked number; (4) keep the reachability rule that ordinary Hicasso does not pull in the hooks namespace; delete the grammar, marker, refusal, ledger and guide machinery that has no subject; (5) replace chapter 10 with a short islands page showing raw React/UIx through defhost and those components using n/use-sub / n/use-frame when they need Hicasso state. Posture: pre-alpha, no deprecation programme, no compatibility shim, trust the programmer - a programmer who crosses into React writes React. If real application work later shows repeated friction, add the smallest helper proven by that code then.

WHY A.
1. Only the two hooks do something React cannot. use-sub hands useSyncExternalStore the same subscribe/getSnapshot a boundary reading that key gets (collector/hook-entry), so an island's read builds the same cell, joins the same reader membership and residue census, is woken by the same commit, and is named by the same re-frame.hicasso.tool rosters Xray consumes. use-frame returns collector/frame-row's incarnation-pinned ops map: destroy :watchlist and recreate it under the same id and a callback still holding the predecessor's ops is refused by core's :rf.error/frame-destroyed fence rather than writing to whoever owns the address now; a memo keyed on the frame keyword would pass every stability test and fail exactly that one (native.cljc:792-879). Both resolve the frame through collector/resolve-frame! - one React context, no spelling reaches a sibling frame. Everything else duplicates UIx, raw React or h/defhost: defcomponent's {:server} roster is a copy of defhost's and the code says so ("A second declaration grammar for it would buy nothing", native.cljc:391-401); memo and lazy are react/memo and react/lazy carrying a marker; $ is a second element grammar with 5 refusals of its own; the 7 remaining names (el, props*, declared-server, component, marker, tier-sentinel, prop-slots) are public only because a macro expansion or a parity fixture calls them (native.cljc:161-185).
2. The second language has one non-test consumer. Consumer-shaped usage across examples/, testbeds/, tools/*/testbeds and the 8 example apps under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples: zero calls of n/$, n/defcomponent, n/memo, n/lazy or n/props. The one mention is examples/ledger/views.cljs:86-88 - "No n/defcomponent, no ref, no effect, no imperative handle, no memo hint and no second root. The application's whole native-tier surface is h/defhost and h/event" - from the app built to need an imperative SDK. Real consumers: the HMR testbed island (holds no subscription by design), one Xray test, and the reagent-migration skill's prose.
3. The guide already concedes the design. docs/core/hicasso/10-native-tier.md:260-265: a rung-3 defview may return a UIx element, a rung-4 island may be a defui, and n/use-sub / n/use-frame work inside UIx components. Option A makes the concession the design.
4. Performance does not need n/$. MEASUREMENT FACT: chapter 10 line 81 claims "moved a 21 ms p95 tick to 13 ms: 38% and 8 ms recovered" and NO measurement record for that figure exists anywhere under docs/design/hicasso. The repository's actual rung-3 measurement is implementation/hicasso/spec/budgets.md row S8 (rf2-5yn9, re-based 2026-08-18 under rf2-6zc2q; lines 397 and 1596): 0.8081x, 19.2% of mount time recovered, per-round escapes [0.6863-0.9302], observed range 7.0%-31.4% over runs A, B, C pooled across fifteen rounds on a 200-boundary mount, status UNRESOLVED because the range crosses the 20% line. The guide's own keep-rule (10:22-25) is at least 20%, or at least 2 ms at p95, or enough to move a user-visible budget from fail to pass - otherwise remove it. So by the guide's own rule the escape has not earned its place. And S8 measures skipping hiccup interpretation once a React element already exists; a raw React or UIx element returned from a defview takes that same path, so the measured benefit survives without n/$. WHICHEVER option had been chosen, the 38% figure had to be corrected to S8's numbers; under A it is retired with the chapter, and S8 stays as the record of the direct-return escape reworded from n/$ to "a defview returning a React element".
5. What keeping it costs: ~900 of native.cljc's 1,116 lines (71% prose) beyond the hooks, 12 of 14 public names, 7 refusal ids, 10 test suites (113 deftests, 6,311 lines), rows in 6 gates and ledgers, a 345-line chapter plus 114 mentions across 12 other guide pages by the dossier's grep (a broader grep that also matches the phrase "native tier" reaches 17 pages: glossary 33, api-reference 26, troubleshooting 10, 21-code-splitting 9, 18-ssr 7, escape-ladder 7), a 7-row troubleshooting table, and a second grammar with its own rules for every reader.

REJECTED.
Option B (keep n/$ and n/props for rung 3 only; drop defcomponent/memo/lazy/marker; collapse 5 grammar refusals to 2): keeps a second element grammar nobody has written outside tests, on a measurement below the guide's own threshold; would need S8 re-taken and cleared first, and the Codex bar rightly refuses to commission a benchmark to justify an API.
Option C (keep the whole tier): two authoring languages, two :server declaration sites, recurring cost on every refusal, ledger and guide change, for one non-test consumer.
Option D (delete the hooks too): WRONG. The hooks share Hicasso's cell table, census and Xray rosters and the frame row is incarnation-pinned (point 1). The UIx adapter's own use-subscribe / use-frame (implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:140-162) run on the adapter spine, not Hicasso's cell table, and Hicasso may not depend on UIx (docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/design-laws.md, Native boundary clause 1: "UIx is a comparator and optional toolkit, never a Hicasso dependency"). Deleting the hooks forks the read into a second reactive spine or pushes islands to a global rf/capture-frame that loses incarnation pinning.

THE SAME ROW THREE WAYS (material for the islands page). A row reading one subscription and dispatching one click.
Hiccup defview (rung 1): (h/defview quote-row [{:keys [sym]}] (let [{:keys [px up?]} (h/sub [:quotes/row sym])] [:tr {:class (if up? "quote up" "quote down") :on-click [:watchlist/select sym]} [:td.sym sym] [:td.px px]])) ; parent: [quote-row {:key sym :sym sym}]
Today's native island: (n/defcomponent quote-row {:server :render} [^js props] (let [sym (.-sym props) {:keys [dispatch]} (n/use-frame) {:keys [px up?]} (n/use-sub [:quotes/row sym])] (n/$ :tr {:class (if up? "quote up" "quote down") :on-click (fn [_] (dispatch [:watchlist/select sym]))} (n/$ :td {:class "sym"} sym) (n/$ :td {:class "px"} px)))) (h/defhost quote-row-host quote-row)
Under A, UIx island: (defui quote-row [{:keys [sym]}] (let [{:keys [dispatch]} (n/use-frame) {:keys [px up?]} (n/use-sub [:quotes/row sym])] ($ :tr {:class (if up? "quote up" "quote down") :on-click (fn [_] (dispatch [:watchlist/select sym]))} ($ :td.sym sym) ($ :td.px px)))) (h/defhost quote-row-host quote-row) - requires [re-frame.hicasso.native :as n] for the two hooks only and [uix.core :refer [defui $]]. The raw-React spelling is the same function over react/createElement with no UIx dependency. The second and third are the same program; the native one cost the reader a raw ^js props object, a :server map defhost carries anyway, no selector shorthand, and 5 grammar refusals to learn.

title: hicasso guide ch04: the owned-literal alternate-spelling claim is not delivered by the taught plain merge
description: docs/core/hicasso/04-controlled-inputs.md §Forward caller attributes safely (lines ~116-119 at 1af79839db) claims: 'A caller cannot replace the field's value, checked state, handler, key, or revision by supplying an alternative spelling such as :onInput or "value"; the controlled contract binds to the React slot reached by the authored literal.' That guarantee was only ever enforced by the :& merge key's owned-literal law (merge-caller denied a remainder on the canonical SLOT). The taught spelling — a plain merge with owned keys last — never delivered it: {:onInput f :on-input [...]} survives the merge as two map keys, both land on React's one onInput slot in convert-entry, and which wins is map iteration order. rf2-6c12m.12 removed :& (so no spelling delivers it now) and chose NOT to add a slot-collision refusal in convert-props — the epic's direction is fewer refusals and trust the programmer, and ch02 §Forward attributes with owned keys last already says 'Forward maps should use the same kebab-keyword spelling as Hiccup; a foreign props object's "className" string is a different merge key.' DO: bring ch04's sentence in line with ch02 — the owned literal wins by presence when the caller forwards the SAME key; an alternate spelling of the same slot is a different key, so forward maps in the same kebab spelling (or dissoc the alternates). Guide-only; dw-guide's fence (docs/core/hicasso/**). Check check_guide_samples.py's digest roster if a fenced block moves.

title: Clojars verified-group policy blocks the FIRST publish of every day8/re-frame2-* tool coordinate
description:
Surfaced by rf2-2ii52 (ruling caveat, deliberately not solved inside the vendoring PR).

Vendoring day8/de-dupe fixed the DEPENDENCY GRAPH for day8/re-frame2-mcp-base and
day8/re-frame2-story-mcp — both now generate a complete pom, and PR #7169 wires their
deploy jobs onto the existing story-v* glob. It did NOT make the coordinates CLAIMABLE.

THE POLICY. Clojars requires NEW projects to live in a *verified* group, and verification
requires a reverse-domain group name. `day8` is not reverse-domain, so it cannot be
verified. Existing projects in an old group may publish new versions; a NEW project may
not be created. This is not theoretical: day8/de-dupe's own tag-triggered publish workflow
ran on 2026-05-13 and received a 403 — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new
projects". That 403 is the reason route (a) (publish de-dupe) was ruled out.

THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE TWO NEW JARS. The same rule applies to EVERY day8/re-frame2-*
coordinate that has never been published — which, as far as anyone has checked, is all of
them: the thirteen implementation/ artefacts as well as the five tool jars. If the day8
group cannot take new projects, then no v* tag can cut a first release either, and the
whole release pipeline is gated on this rather than on any code.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING (Mike's, not a worker's):
  1. Does day8's Clojars standing permit new projects today? (An older group may have been
     grandfathered, or the account may hold a verified group already — VERIFY against
     Clojars rather than inferring from the 2026-05-13 403, which was a different group
     path.) If yes, nothing to do: tag and publish.
  2. If no: the artefacts need a verified reverse-domain group — io.github.day8/* is the
     obvious candidate, verifiable via the GitHub org. That renames EVERY published
     coordinate, which touches deps.edn :clein/build :lib for 18 artefacts, the lockstep
     gate, every release workflow's rewrite + preflight, docs/release-process.md, the
     template's pins, CHANGELOG, and every consumer-facing usage snippet in the repo.

VERIFY BEFORE TAGGING ANYTHING. Clojars has no yank, and a half-published set at a given
VERSION is recovered only by bump-and-supersede.

Flagged in .github/workflows/release-story.yml's header and docs/release-process.md
\u00a7How story-mcp and mcp-base got their publish path.
notes:
RULING (delegated by Mike, 2026-07-28, dossier review): recorded 2026-07-28 07:48 AUSEST from ai/decisions/rf2-uelji.clojars-verified-group.md (primary analysis + independent Codex second opinion, reconciled; the dossier file is deleted after this note — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD).

DECISION, in three parts:
(1) VERIFICATION-FIRST SEQUENCING STANDS, but the canary-by-tag route is REJECTED as the verification instrument (Codex position, adopted). Mike's authoritative act is the zero-mutation one: verify io.github.day8 via Clojars' self-service GitHub-org proof (see MIKE'S ACT below), optionally glancing at day8's standing from his logged-in account or asking Clojars support as belt-and-braces.
(2) RULED FALLBACK GROUP if day8 is blocked (and the evidence below says it is): io.github.day8 for ALL 18 Maven coordinates, moved in ONE sequenced rename campaign BEFORE anything publishes.
(3) NO-TAG RULE: NO v*, story-v*, xray-v*, or machines-viz-v* tag is pushed until this bead resolves (io.github.day8 badge confirmed + rename campaign merged + lockstep/preflight/release-DAG gates green on the new coordinates). This is STEP 0 of the rf2-vxgfnd.99 cut-time checklist, ahead of its existing step 1 (credentials); rf2-2ii52 step 3 (manual first publish of mcp-base/story-mcp) is equally blocked on it.

EVIDENCE AND ITS LIMITS (three independent sources; two re-verified from primary sources 2026-07-28):
- The 2026-05-13 403 on day8/de-dupe's tag-triggered publish — "Group 'day8' isn't verified, so can't contain new projects" — is real but was a DIFFERENT project path; on its own it is suggestive, not conclusive (the bead itself warns against inferring from it alone).
- Clojars' Verified Group Names wiki (fetched 2026-07-28): since 2021-04-18 "creating new libraries in non-verified groups will be disabled", while "the group does not need to be verified for new versions" of EXISTING libraries. Bare `day8` is neither reverse-domain nor a githost-org pattern, so it is STRUCTURALLY UNVERIFIABLE — there is no route to a verified bare day8, and seeking a policy exception would couple every release to an exception Clojars explicitly designed away.
- clojars.org/users/mikethompson (fetched 2026-07-28): `day8` is listed WITHOUT the verified badge; only net.clojars.mikethompson and org.clojars.mikethompson carry it. Codex traced the badge to find-group-verification in clojars-web's web/user.clj (not cosmetic) and the enforcement to check-group+project in db.clj: an unverified group is accepted ONLY when that exact group/artifact pair already exists; a new artifact is rejected as group-non-verified.
- All 18 intended day8/* coordinates 404 on Clojars (re-verified 2026-07-27, per-coordinate) — every one is a NEW project as far as Clojars is concerned, so every one enters the rejected branch. The day8 group page returning 200 with mikethompson permitted proves only maintenance rights over existing projects, not creation rights.
- LIMIT: what stays unobservable read-only is Mike's account-side view and any bespoke admin exception. That residual is why this bead stays with Mike — but it is small, and it does not justify a canary.

VERIFICATION ROUTES WEIGHED (canary trade-offs recorded):
- (a) Account/settings check or asking Clojars admins: zero-risk, zero-mutation. Fine as belt-and-braces; not required given (c).
- (b) Canary publish by pushing the ready machines-viz-v0.0.1.alpha tag: REJECTED as a probe. A 403 merely re-demonstrates documented policy at the cost of a burned tag-push cycle; a surprise success is an IMMUTABLE public act that permanently pins machines-viz to day8/* — either splitting the family when the rest moves, or accidentally committing the whole family to an unverifiable legacy group. Never use an immutable registry operation to learn an observable fact; if state might have changed, re-read the profile/API or ask support instead. title: hic: frameless overlay with :on-dismiss reaches the declared-unreachable two-owners state — needs a ruling
description: Found by rf2-dr90's coverage audit; verified at source. impl/overlay.cljs's dismissal-handler returns nil when there is no frame dispatch (~:655-659), but popover-dismissal-attrs (~:746-751) reads only the props — so a popover mounted with NO frame above it and :on-dismiss written still renders popover="auto" with no handler: the platform light-dismisses it, no intent lands, and app-db keeps open? true — exactly the open-flag/second-owner desync overlay.cljs's docstring (~:80-83) declares unreachable. Same shape on the modal (closedby="closerequest", no cancel handler). The presence module ruled its frameless case explicitly (legal until a child writes an intent, presence_react ~:50-57, tested at presence_intent ~:334-365); overlay has no equivalent ruling or witness. Needs Mike's ruling on direction before any test or fix: refuse a frameless overlay that carries :on-dismiss, or degrade the attrs to manual/none when dispatch is nil. Then the witness follows the ruling.
notes:
*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** Banner added 2026-08-29 10:31 AUSEST by the merge+dispatch tick (mayor session re-frame2-9a). The bead's own title names the hold: the frameless-overlay :on-dismiss path reaches a state the design declares unreachable, and whether the state is admitted (design amendment) or refused (code fix) is a RULING. WHOEVER RULES STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT.
2026-08-29 14:40 AUSEST - Decision dossier for Mike at ai/decisions/rf2-4e5b.frameless-overlay-on-dismiss.md (local-only, untracked): problem, options with consequences, recommendation, how to record the ruling.
DOSSIER INPUT relayed 2026-08-29 14:45 AUSEST by the mayor: the dossier recommends reusing :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary (the presence/boundary precedent) with no new refusal id. If Mike rules that way, the fix rides the refusal lane (rf2-6c12m.11's wave or after) rather than a solo dispatch. Banner stands.
RULING 2026-08-29 15:31:44 AUSEST (delegated review per Mike, 2026-08-29): Option D - a frameless overlay stays legal without :on-dismiss; an OPEN one that carries :on-dismiss with no frame dispatch refuses at render with the EXISTING :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary (the presence precedent), no new id.
BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:31:44 AUSEST: ruled; dispatchable.

WHY D, AND HOW THE REVIEWS WERE WEIGHED. The dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-4e5b.frameless-overlay-on-dismiss.md, now deleted; this note carries everything it held) recommended D. A second review appended to it ("Codex Recommendation") independently chose D on the same grounds and added implementation bounds (small guard, no id, no dispatch threading through the attrs fns, no grammar broadening, amend the one Spec 009 row, no compat layer). The two agreed, so this is adoption of a concurring recommendation rather than a tie-break. Decisive facts: (1) :on-dismiss IS an intent - the public docstring says so (overlay.cljs:79-80 "routed back as an ordinary intent - which is what :on-dismiss is") - and every other intent position in hicasso that cannot land REFUSES (require-dispatch, intent.cljs:397-402; event-callback, intent.cljs:586-595); this is the one silent path in the module. (2) Presence and the error boundary already ruled the identical frameless case exactly this way (presence_react.cljs:51-56, boundary.cljs:153-158). (3) rf2-6c12m.11 is cutting the refusal roster from 59 to ~30; a new id (option A) would add vocabulary carrying no information the existing id does not. (4) Degrading to manual/none (option B) silently ignores a line the programmer wrote - "trust the programmer" means report the impossibility, not hide it. (5) Admitting the state (option C) documents a desync and would have the witness pin a defect as a feature. One alternative both reviews left implicit is closed here: routing :on-dismiss through intent/lower-prop (intent.cljs:1212-1228) so the emitter stays in impl.intent was considered and rejected - it changes :on-dismiss's dispatch mechanics (intent-handler's per-key policy, key-maps, placeholders), which is the grammar broadening the Codex review rules out, and the popover would still need its beforetoggle direction filter wrapped around the result. Direct guard it is.

THE MECHANISM (all paths implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/ unless stated).
- impl/overlay.cljs:687-688: body resolves the frame via adapter-context/context-value->current-frame on react/useContext frame-context; with no provider above, the reader answers nil by design (core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs:330).
- :702: dispatch (when frame-kw (collector/frame-dispatch frame-kw)) - nil when frameless.
- :655-656: dismissal-handler [dispatch on-dismiss closed-only?] is (when (and dispatch on-dismiss) (fn ...)) - returns nil when dispatch is nil, silently.
- :741-744 modal-dismissal-attrs and :750-751 popover-dismissal-attrs read PROPS ONLY: :on-dismiss present => closedby="closerequest" (or "any" with :light-dismiss?) / popover="auto". So the element tells the platform "you may dismiss me" while nothing listens.
- :669 own-keys strips :on-dismiss from the props before element-attrs/lowering, and :706 hands it to dismissal-handler directly, so it BYPASSES intent/with-frame (:726) and require-dispatch (intent.cljs:397-402) - the one intent position in the module that skips the loud path. Children's intents inside the overlay do take the loud path.
- :604-631 make-cell: show! (showPopover/showModal) runs ONLY from the once-attached stable ref callback; body (:681-729) has no effect. A re-render therefore does NOT re-show a platform-closed element.

USER-VISIBLE SEQUENCE (popover, :open? true, :on-dismiss written, no frame): 1. mounts, ref callback calls showPopover once on attach, element in the top layer with popover="auto". 2. user clicks outside; platform fires beforetoggle/toggle, nothing listens, panel hides. 3. the flag driving :open? is still true - no intent ran. 4. a re-render does not re-show it (stable ref, no effect). 5. to reopen the author must flip the flag false (element unmounts; hide! is a no-op) then true again - two actions for one open, and any aria-expanded mirrored from the flag lies in between. Modal: same shape with closedby="closerequest" - Escape closes the dialog, no cancel handler runs, flag stays true. This is exactly the two-owners state overlay.cljs:76-83 declares unreachable.

WHEN FRAMELESS ACTUALLY HAPPENS. Every shipped door installs a frame: h/mount! takes {:frame ::frame} (impl/mount.cljs:141); server/render allocates a per-request frame (server.cljs:333); Story wraps every variant in rf/frame-provider (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:622, 673); a UIx/Reagent island under frame-provider or frame-root reads the same context object (context.cljs:38-40, impl/mount.cljs:33-36). An overlay under an h/defview never reaches this code because the boundary shell refuses :rf.error/no-frame-context first (impl/collector.cljs:1753-1760). So the case is reached only when the overlay is the OUTERMOST hicasso component in a React root nobody wrapped: a test mounting it alone (presence's suite does this via mount/root! with adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel), or a consumer's hand-built root / unwrapped island. Rare, mostly test-time - and it is the case where :open? cannot be an h/sub and :on-dismiss can never land, i.e. an authoring error worth naming. A frameless overlay WITHOUT :on-dismiss is a legitimate case (static manual popover, non-dismissible dialog) and stays legal.

PRECEDENT. presence_react.cljs:51-56: "No frame in scope is not an error here. Presence reads nothing, so a tray mounted outside a frame is legal until one of its children writes an intent - at which point the existing loud error fires and names the intent, which is better attribution than a generic no-frame-context throw from the tray." boundary.cljs:153-158 carries the same paragraph. Witness: test/re_frame/hicasso/presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:327-365 - frameless-root! (mount/root! (mount/fresh-container!) adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel hiccup); testing block 1: quiet frameless tray renders; block 2: a child with :on-click [...] under a boundary with :on-error raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary and (:intent (ex-data e)) equals the vector. overlay_dom_cljs_test.cljs has no frameless row (its manual witness is :652-655, :680-694).

OPTIONS REJECTED. A (new id e.g. :rf.error/hicasso-overlay-dismiss-without-frame): same trigger as D, but mints an overlay-specific id for the generic outside-boundary condition, costs rows in complaints.md (:129 area), the naming ledger, Spec 009 and check_complaint_catalogue.py, against rf2-6c12m.11's direction. B (thread dispatch into the two attrs fns so nil dispatch yields manual/none): one owner, docstring stays true, but the :on-dismiss the author wrote is silently dead - the only swallowed intent in hicasso. C (amend the docstring to say two-owners holds only inside a frame): honest but documents a desync; witness would pin a defect.

THE CHANGE (one guard, shared path, covers modal AND popover).
1. impl/overlay.cljs dismissal-handler (:633-659), called once from body at :706 for both heads while :open? is true: when on-dismiss is non-nil and dispatch is nil, (fail! :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary 're-frame.hicasso.impl.overlay/dismissal-handler "<reason>" :lower-intents-inside-a-boundary-render {:intent on-dismiss}) instead of returning nil. Keep the existing (fn [e] ...) branch untouched. title: hicasso: alloc_null_floor.cjs's section E says 'the clean prefix is three rounds long' where its own table four lines above reads round 2 at 12.3%, and it was two rounds on the 242-cell corpus too
description:
FOUND BY THE POST-REPAIR SWEEP rf2-oflj7's remainder asked for, MEASURED 2026-08-21 at
worker/nullfloor-oflj7. NOT one of rf2-oflj7's seven, and NOT stale-by-fold-in: unlike every
claim on that bead, this one appears to have been WRONG WHEN WRITTEN.

THE CLAIM. Section E, four lines below the round-index table it summarises:

  The clean prefix is three rounds long and `warmups` is 3 in every run. THIS READER HAS NOT
  TESTED WHETHER THOSE ARE THE SAME THREE, and proposes no mechanism for the structure.

WHAT THE SAME RUN PRINTS, four lines above it — rounds carrying mode-2 cells:

  round 0 : 0/22   0.0%
  round 1 : 0/63   0.0%
  round 2 : 7/57  12.3%

So the clean prefix is TWO rounds long, not three. The reader's OWN preceding sentence in the
same section says so in as many words: 'round 0 alone, heavily decimated by certification :
0/22 (0.0%)' sits directly above, and the file's header comment (line ~110) states 'Rounds 0
and 1 carry NONE AT ALL'. Three statements in one file, two of them derived, disagreeing with
the third, which is typed.

AND IT WAS NOT THE PHASE-4 FOLD-IN. On the 242-cell corpus the same table read round 0 at
0.0%, round 1 at 0.0% and round 2 at 6.7% (2 of 30) — the frozen studio page
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md prints exactly those rows at its
section E, and its own prose two lines above the claim says 'Rounds 0 and 1 carry none at
all'. The prefix was two rounds long then as well. This is a published error rather than a
figure the corpus moved out from under.

'CLEAN PREFIX' HAS NO OTHER DEFINITION IN THE REPO. git grep -F 'clean prefix' returns three
hits and they are this one sentence in its three copies (the .cjs header comment, the .cjs
report line, the studio page). The sentence's own follow-on — 'whether those are the SAME
THREE' — pairs it with 'warmups is 3', so 'clean prefix' can only mean the leading rounds
carrying no mode-2 cell. Control: git grep -lF 'warmups' returns 189 files, so the pattern
reaches this corpus and the three is a reading.

THE GUARD IS THE HOLLOW SHAPE THIS FAMILY OF BEADS IS ABOUT. The only check on the sentence is

  ck('the report proposes no mechanism for the round structure',
     /THIS READER HAS NOT\n;; {3}TESTED WHETHER THOSE ARE THE SAME THREE/.test(rep), true);

which asks whether a DIFFERENT CLAUSE of the same sentence is present. It passes whatever the
count says, and has done since the sentence was written.

WHY THIS IS A RULING AND NOT A WORKER'S FIX, which is why it was left rather than folded into
rf2-oflj7's PR. The number is load-bearing on the reader's conclusion: 'three' is what makes
the sentence a COINCIDENCE WORTH NOT EXPLAINING ('warmups is 3 ... has not tested whether
those are the same three'). Correcting it to two dissolves the pairing, and the reader then
either says nothing about warmups or says something new about a two-round prefix against a
three-round warmup — which is a claim about MECHANISM, and this reader's standing position is
that it proposes none. Same class as rf2-oflj7's items 5 and 6.

NOT VERIFIED HERE: whether 'warmups is 3 in every run' holds over the 16 runs. It is unguarded
too — no check reads it — but it was out of the sweep's scope.

THE FROZEN PAGE. docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md carries the same
sentence at its section E. That page is explicitly frozen at its 242-cell state by its own
banner ('left exactly as it was published'), so whether a published error inside a frozen
record is corrected in place or annotated is part of the same ruling.
notes:
MAYOR — THE ONE THING THIS BEAD RECORDED AS 'NOT VERIFIED HERE' IS NOW MEASURED, and it changes the shape of the ruling rather than merely filling a gap. 2026-08-22 02:3x AUSEST, tip 86702f3ed7.

THE BEAD SAID: 'NOT VERIFIED HERE: whether warmups is 3 in every run. It is unguarded too — no check reads it — but it was out of the sweep's scope.'

MEASURED NOW, by reading the sixteen committed run files the reader's own CORPORA table names (alloc_null_floor.cjs:165-215): alloc-0gjqi/paired-run{1,2}, alloc-fk6pj/seeded-run{1,2}, alloc-legorder/run{1..8}, alloc-passterm/run{1..4}.

  RESULT: warmups = 3 in ALL SIXTEEN. Uniform, no exceptions.

CONTROLLED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a recursive key search returning one constant across sixteen files is exactly the shape a broken search also produces. Asked for a key that does not exist -> ABSENT. Asked for 'samples' on the same files -> sixteen distinct varying arrays. So the finder discriminates and the uniform 3 is a reading, not an artefact.

*** WHAT THIS DOES TO THE RULING. *** The bead's reasoning for calling this Mike's rather than a worker's was that 'three' makes the sentence A COINCIDENCE WORTH NOT EXPLAINING — 'warmups is 3 ... has not tested whether those are the same three' — so correcting the prefix to two DISSOLVES THE PAIRING and forces the reader to say something new about mechanism.

Measured, the sentence carries EXACTLY ONE falsehood and not two: warmups really is 3 everywhere; the clean prefix really is 2. So the pairing the sentence declines to explain DOES NOT EXIST — the two numbers are simply different.

title: hicasso defhost: infer the callback contract by position, keep :callbacks as a 2-value override, delete :handler (executes ruling rf2-6c12m.2)
description:
Executes ruling rf2-6c12m.2 (RULED 2026-08-29 15:29:54 AUSEST, delegated review per Mike: Option B, 2 values). The FULL analysis - decisive facts, rejected options, before/after, id-by-id line pointers, doc/skill/test file lists, acceptance - is the RULING note on rf2-6c12m.2; brief from it. This description is the condensed DO.

THE RULE: a defhost or [:>] callback contract is inferred from the prop position exactly as native tags already do (intent.cljs:1200-1210 position-contract; intent.cljs:1212-1228 lower-prop): on*-spelled -> :event, any other walked prop -> :render, :ref -> React's, declared :slots -> markup. :callbacks survives ONLY as an optional override {<prop> :event|:render} written where inference is wrong (on*-named render props: Fluent onRenderItem/onRenderCell, Ant onRow/onCell/onFilter); a declared contract outranks the spelling. :handler is DELETED (a plain fn is the handler contract and already crosses untouched at every position - intent.cljs:1225,1228; codec.cljs:2865). A vector or map at a render position (inferred or overridden) crosses as data via host-prop-value, as at a native tag. An h/event at a declared :slots position stays refused.

CODE: host-entry (codec.cljs:3040-3111) :else arm -> reuse intent/lower-prop for the event/render inference, then host-prop-value; NO second classifier, warning, or compat layer. lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1255-1302) keeps :event and :render arms, drops :handler; non-callback values at :render route through host-prop-value. SEQUENCING: dispatch AFTER the wave's src-touching tasks (.11, .21, .13, .15) merge, so this is a cleanup pass and not a conflict source - refusal ids are emitted from controlled/forms/overlay, so .11 may touch them. One PR; src-only plus docs/design/hicasso; no hot-zone files.

THE RULE (binding): a docstring carries (a) what the var is or returns; (b) the contract - takes, returns, promises, effects, ordering, failure behaviour, in full for a public var, and for a private var what it does plus the one non-obvious invariant behind its shape; (c) one sentence of why; (d) where the argument lives, as a repo-relative path into docs/design/hicasso (architecture.md, studio/<page>.md, decisions.md HD-NNN). Links are repo-relative paths, NEVER [[wikilinks]] - 892 exist in src and nothing resolves them; check each retained path exists by hand and say so in the PR body. A measured figure stays only with its page named beside it. A source comment stays only where it protects nearby code from a plausible-but-wrong edit (a local correctness proof); module history, benchmark narrative, rejected alternatives, HD derivations and explanations of other namespaces' mechanisms do not. Content rule, not a number: no 40-line cap, no 1:1 enforcement, no link checker, no script. Untouched: retained-inventory's :what strings and the rf2:builder-bypass-ok block.

MOVE vs DELETE: durable design reasoning with no home in docs/design/hicasso is MOVED there - measurements and traces to studio/, rulings and rejected alternatives to decisions.md, mechanism reasoning to architecture.md; prose a design page already carries, superseded prose and change-narration is DELETED. Known for these files: controlled.cljs ns duplicates studio/controlled-input-two-implementations.md (full matrix and measured rows already there) - delete, cite the page. Check the others against the studio/ and decisions.md pages they name before moving anything. The PR body names, per essay, the path it moved to or "deleted - duplicated at <path>" / "deleted - superseded".

WORKED EXAMPLES (shape to copy; full text in rf2-6c12m.4 notes part 2): the collector ns docstring 392 -> 12 lines (what it owns, why those share a namespace, one design-record path); commit-basis 58 -> ~18 lines (three terms, why three, the .19 reincarnation counter-example kept as the one-sentence why, one architecture.md path); cold-read! 59 -> 9 lines (contract, fallback, why the memo is per read with the figure and its studio page).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) opening each file shows code and a compact namespace map, not an essay; (2) public inputs, outputs, effects, ordering and failure behaviour remain stated at the var; (3) local correctness proofs stay beside the code; history, measurements and cross-module explanation do not; (4) every retained design path resolves (checked by hand) and there is one authoritative explanation per argument; (5) node-test and browser-test compile and the files' focused suites pass, foreground, to completion; (6) scripts/check_doc_slugs.py green for any moved material, check_provenance_pins.py where commit hashes move; (7) the PR body names where each essay went or why it was deleted.

roster is SIX carriers and reconciles arithmetically (237+51+71+86+31+132 = 608 against the
ruling's stated ~608 lines). FOUR of the six were already answered on a published page and each
says so of itself, so nothing was merged for them. Two were merged, into 06-lists and 05-forms.

THE GAP. This bead's close condition names TWO things: no unmigrated teaching content AND no
operative contract. Two files in product/ still carry VIEW SPECIFICATION and fall outside every
category the ruling enumerated. Verified at source just now:
  docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   506 lines, tracked
  docs/design/hicasso/product/facade-freeze.md   247 lines, tracked
Category 2's list was executed EXACTLY by step (a) — implementation/hicasso/spec/ now holds
budgets.md, complaints.md, dispositions.md, invariants.md, naming-ledger.md and a README, and
nothing else. Neither of these two is on that list. Neither is in category 4's roster
(decision-brief, the kill table/validation.md, phase records, lanes/, pilots/, studio/). And
category 3 forbids relocating anything into root spec/.

SO THEY ARE IN NO CATEGORY. That is not a worker's call to make and the worker correctly declined
to invent one — it left them and said so, which is the reasoned refusal the stance protects.

WHAT MIKE IS BEING ASKED, and it is narrow: does view specification in specification.md and
facade-freeze.md count as OPERATIVE CONTRACT that should follow step (a) into
implementation/hicasso/spec/, or is it a working design record whose address is unchanged like
category 4? Either answer closes this bead; the first adds one more move, the second is a no-op.

rather than prose drift: docs/core/hicasso/05-forms.md disabled the submit button on
(not can-submit?) while :submit-attempted? is set only by a REJECTED submit — so the attempt that

MY BRIEF CARRIED A FENCE THAT HAD ALREADY SPENT ITSELF: I sequenced step (b) behind fhsweep

THE CLOSING QUESTION groups specification.md (506 lines) and facade-freeze.md (247) together as carrying view specification while falling into no category the ruling enumerated. Grouped, they look like one decision. Counted, they do not.

CITATION CENSUS, tracked files, .beads excluded because it is tracker prose rather than a reference:

    specification.md      16 citers
    facade-freeze.md       2 citers

  CONTROL — the five that step (a) MOVED to implementation/hicasso/spec/:
    dispositions.md  29 · budgets.md  31 · invariants.md  20 · naming-ledger.md  19 · complaints.md  14

So specification.md sits squarely inside the band of the five that were ruled normative and moved. facade-freeze.md is an order of magnitude below all six, and its only two citers are docs/design/hicasso/product-kind-census.md — the census that classified it — and dispositions.md.

AND THE COUNT UNDERSTATES specification.md, because WHO cites it decides this more than HOW MANY:

  * A GATE READS IT AND ASSERTS ON ITS CONTENTS. implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_facade_inventory.py:890
    builds the path REPO_ROOT/docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md and opens it; :894 raises
    "specification.md now names `{}`. The Source column's reach has ..." — the checker fails when the
    page changes. That is the strongest test of normativity this repo has: a page a gate reads is
    contract by construction, whatever tree it happens to sit in.
  * PRODUCTION SOURCE NAMES IT THE NORMATIVE OWNER, in those words:
    implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/evidence.cljs:100 — "Normative owner:
    `docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md` §10"; tool.cljs:119 — the same, §10.
  * .github/workflows/test.yml:1212 cites it as a live premise.
  * THREE OF THE FIVE FILES THAT ALREADY MOVED cite it — budgets.md, dispositions.md, invariants.md.
    The normative set points AT it from its new address while it stays behind.
  * The checker's own comment at :131 records that it "did NOT move", so the split is already
    visible to the code and being worked around.

facade-freeze.md's two citers include NO gate, NO workflow and NO production source.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. It does not decide either file — whether category 2's list was exhaustive is the operator's, and I am not answering it. What it does is make the two questions separable and give each one evidence: specification.md is cited like the five that moved and is read by a gate and named "Normative owner" by shipping source; facade-freeze.md is cited like a working record. A ruling that treats them as one thing is deciding the second on the first's evidence, or the first on the second's.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not read either file's CONTENT to judge whether it reads as specification. The census on this already exists (docs/design/hicasso/product-kind-census.md, which the bead quotes at VS 55% for both) and I did not re-derive it. This note is about consumers, which is a different axis and the one nobody had measured.

A SEQUENCING CONSEQUENCE IF specification.md MOVES: check_facade_inventory.py:890 hardcodes the old path and would need re-pointing in the same commit, exactly as step (a)'s gate re-pointing did. And the new address is under implementation/hicasso/spec/, which is rf2-7rzg's Chromium-toll surface — so the two operator calls touch each other here as well.
SCOPING PASS ON STEP (b), 2026-08-22 18:0x AUSEST, at origin/main tip 112310ddbc. THE BRIEF'S PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD: STEP (b) IS ALREADY MERGED. I was dispatched to establish the teaching set and scope the migration. There is nothing to scope. PR #8668 is state MERGED, mergedAt 2026-08-21T13:29:59Z, merge commit f53dd7c17e, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor f53dd7c17e HEAD` confirms it is an ancestor of a checkout whose HEAD equals origin/main exactly. Six files: 05-forms.md, 06-lists-and-collections.md, product/README.md, forms-recipes.md, virtualizer-recipe.md, check_guide_samples.py. I edited no file and dispatched nothing.

Ordering verified as instructed rather than read top-down. `bd history --json` walked newest-first over 2504 snapshots: the newest text-bearing change is 2026-08-22T04:04:02 (the notes growing 9023 -> 12609, i.e. the "two files, opposite profiles" note). Today's 17:06 and 16:xx entries are checkpoint no-ops. So the newest instruction on the bead is that note, and the description's "AWAITING MIKE / NOT DISPATCHABLE" header is discharged exactly as the brief said. Governing text is the comment "OPERATOR RULING - THE SPLIT" at 2026-08-21T10:12:55Z. Both fences the brief named are clear: rf2-wppza closed, its PR #8667 merged, and it was #8668's own base.

Below is what the brief actually asked for, delivered as an AUDIT of the merged set rather than a scope of unstarted work. I re-derived rather than trusted, and one finding closes a hole nobody had checked.

THE TEACHING SET, as established and executed - all six carriers verified by me at source. The set is the kind-3 "reader-facing answer" roster of docs/design/hicasso/product-kind-census.md, taken at ANY share rather than primary-only, which is precisely the trap the bead warned about for the contract set. Arithmetic reconciles: 237+51+71+86+31+132 = 608 against the census's stated ~608 (the per-file line attributions are the census's figures; the reconciliation is mine).

1. release-policy.md, RF 70%, ~237 lines - ALREADY PUBLISHED, not migrated. Its own :168-172 states the consumer-facing abridgement lives at docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md #supported-versions; that heading is real at 00-installation.md:111, and Sec 5.1's "An upgrade may cost you a rename. It should not cost you a rethink." stands near-verbatim at 00-installation.md:137 as "Upgrades before 1.0 may cost you a rename, and should not cost you a rethink", with the complaint-id stability promise beside it.
2. async-routing-recipes.md, RF 60%, ~86 - ALREADY PUBLISHED. Its :148 claims 08-async-resources.md and 07-routing-and-navigation.md "teach these three shapes already". I did not take the file's word for it: settle-merge -> 08 Sec "Merge a settled reply into the current draft" (:9); per-instance mutation status with optimistic plan -> 08 Sec "Track writes per instance" (:86) and Sec "Optimistic updates and rollback" (:122); dirty-navigation guard -> 07 Sec "Guard unsaved changes" (:221), with Sec "Deep links, Back, and Forward" (:287) carrying the Back-button half. All three published.
3. virtualizer-recipe.md, RF 60%, ~71 - GENUINE GAP, MIGRATED. 06-lists-and-collections.md gained Sec "Keep the focused row mounted" (:233), Sec "Announce the model's count, not the DOM's" (:262), Sec "Screen a virtualizer before adopting it" (:279).
4. forms-recipes.md, RF 55%, ~51 - GENUINE GAP, MIGRATED, and it is a DEFECT repair rather than an absence. 05-forms.md disabled the submit button on (not can-submit?) while :submit-attempted? is set only by a rejected submit, so the attempt that would set it was the one the disabled button prevented and the chapter's own display gate was dead code. Fixed by splitting the two kinds of unavailable - :disabled for in-flight, :aria-disabled for invalid - with the accessibility rationale and a new troubleshooting row. Verified in the merged diff.
5. per-keystroke.md Sec 6, RF 20%, ~132 - ALREADY PUBLISHED. 19-performance.md:15 carries the echo budget row ("the visible echo arrives within one 60 Hz frame at p95"); the keystroke trace's step 6 (:189, "React commits and Hicasso converges value and caret before the event turn ends") and step 7 (:190, the paint) carry the finding.
6. lanes/hot-path-architecture.md, RF 30%, ~31 - ALREADY PUBLISHED, and the published form is a superset. Its five-rung performance ladder is escape-ladder.md, a dedicated 214-line page that adds per-rung costs, how to take an escape, and climbing back; 19-performance.md:58 mirrors the ladder. Its Sec "Read-topology guidance" bullets map one-for-one onto 06-lists-and-collections.md: fine row reads -> Sec Fine-grained rows (:70), coarse view-model -> Sec Coarse display model (:108), chunked/windowed -> Sec Chunk the comparison sweep (:151) and Sec Window the DOM (:187), oscillating read sets -> Sec Avoid large oscillating read sets (:295).

So: four of six already answered on a published page, two real gaps closed. Nothing was duplicated, which is the right call - a duplicate in a published guide is worse than an absence.
THREE AUDIT FINDINGS FROM THE SAME PASS. Every count below carries a control.

FINDING 1 - LEXICAL PROBES CANNOT DISCRIMINATE TEACHING CONTENT IN THIS CORPUS, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. This validates the structural discriminator #8668 used as the correct instrument rather than a convenience. I checked the second-person probe that worker discarded and his control holds: 06-lists-and-collections.md, an unambiguous teaching page, contains ZERO occurrences of "you" (control: 00-installation.md 8, index.md 3, 05-forms.md 1). I then built an independent instrument - imperative density at line/bullet start over 22 verbs, normalised per 1000 lines - and it failed its control too: forms-recipes.md, virtualizer-recipe.md and release-policy.md, three of the FOUR RF-PRIMARY carriers, all score EXACTLY ZERO. The census records the cause at its own :390 - the corpus states its laws in the indicative and returns exactly one RFC-2119 keyword across all 64 files. Anyone re-opening this must read, not grep, and the bead's "do not grep for recipe" instruction generalises further than it says.

FINDING 2 - THE CENSUS HAS ONE COVERAGE GAP, AND IT IS BENIGN. product-kind-census.md classifies 59 of the 60 tracked files under product/. Measured: tracked files 60; census names 59 distinct product/ targets plus the 5 step (a) moved to implementation/hicasso/spec/ (budgets, complaints, dispositions, invariants, naming-ledger), whose links it re-pointed. CONTROL: whole design/hicasso tree 146 files, docs/core/hicasso 29, docs/core 64, and a nonsense pathspec returns 0. The unclassified file is post-rename-recertification-2026-08-20.md, 448 lines, which post-dates the census. I read it rather than inferring from its siblings: it is 100% working record - a dated fourth results record whose own header says every figure is a counter or a byte count and none is a clock reading, with Sec 7 "The controls - which gates were shown to still bite". No teaching content, so the gap does not touch the set. Recorded because the census is the instrument every downstream decision here rests on.

FINDING 3 - THE CENSUS'S KIND-3 ROSTER IS INCOMPLETE, AND THE GUIDE COVERS THE SHORTFALL ANYWAY. This is the finding of the pass, and it CLOSES rather than opens. I refused to take the census's RF roster on trust and ran two independent read-passes over 13 files it scored at 0% RF, picked as the likeliest misclassifications. Five carry material meeting a teaching criterion (addressee is an application author; the claim is standing rather than true-as-of a measurement; it is instruction rather than a gate-read row or a decision rationale): lanes/ergonomics-api.md (census VS 95%) - the n/$ grammar bullets and worked hot-row example; lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md (census VS 75%) - the Suspense/Activity retain-versus-release asymmetry; authoring-report-todo.md (census WR 100%) - N1 key map, N2/N3 reg-state placement, N4 :ref stability, N5 on-submit auto-prevent; authoring-report-slice.md (census WR 100%) - the ::h/value event-vector shape and the ::h/revision reset test; lanes/testing-xray.md (census VS 60%) - the testing ladder and its refusal rule.

BUT EVERY ONE OF THOSE ITEMS IS ALREADY PUBLISHED, each verified at page and heading:
- selector shorthand / class and id as props -> 10-native-tier.md:87
- Suspense retains where Activity releases -> 21-code-splitting.md Sec "A committed sibling keeps its reads while the fallback is up" (:229), which states it MORE sharply than the design source: "a slow chunk costs you a fallback, not a resubscribe - and if you want the opposite, hiding a pane and releasing what it holds, that is Activity's job rather than Suspense's"
- :ref must be a stable function -> 09-interop.md:353, "A top-level function keeps ref identity stable and avoids reattaching on every render", with the hoisted attach-map form shown
- key map {"Enter" ...} -> 03-events-as-data.md:194, 13-overlays-and-focus.md:252, cookbook.md:139, glossary.md:343
- ::h/value -> taught from 01-getting-started.md:60 onward; full reserved vocabulary at 03-events-as-data.md:42
- ::h/revision reset -> 04-controlled-inputs.md Sec "Reset with ::h/revision" (:127-190), including the anti-pattern warning against a view-body random-uuid or render counter, plus two troubleshooting rows
- :on-submit auto-prevent -> 05-forms.md:341 and 03-events-as-data.md:281
- testing ladder and refusal -> 15-testing.md Sec "The testing ladder" (:67), L0-L4 with Sec "L2 refuses React-only behaviour" (:267) and Sec "Use L3 for React claims" (:372)
NET: the census under-counted kind 3, and the guide over-delivers against it. The teaching migration has no residue. The set was established from an imperfect instrument and still landed complete. One item has no Hicasso guide home and correctly so - where a reg-state concern is DECLARED (todo N2/N3) is a re-frame2 application code-organisation convention, not Hicasso view authoring, and is out of this guide's scope.

THE GATE SURFACE, established rather than guessed.
(a) PUBLICATION. mkdocs.yml:14 docs_dir: docs; exclude_docs at :32 lists design/hicasso/, and "design/hicasso" matches exactly ONE line in the whole file - that exclusion, never a nav entry. Nav :265 carries "Hicasso: the view layer". Destination half built and published, source half excluded. CONFIRMED.
(b) YES, FENCED BLOCKS UNDER docs/core/hicasso/ ARE DIGEST-PINNED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING GATE FACT. implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py carries a ROSTER pinning 223 fenced blocks across ALL 29 docs/core/hicasso pages by 12-hex digest. Editing any fenced block in a guide page is therefore a TWO-FILE change - the page plus its roster digest - exactly the class of the docs/core/freehand pin. #8668's sixth file is precisely that: a +1/-1 to the roster, 05-forms.md block 8, 51950e9321d2 -> 103b4f580107. It runs unconditionally in .github/workflows/test.yml (:1321 --self-test, :1328 live) and inside npm run test:hicasso-invariants. Any future guide-editing dispatch must be briefed with this or it lands red.
(c) LINK GATES, per half. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DEFAULT_ROOTS = (docs, spec, skills, migration) at :94, so it covers BOTH halves for link targets and heading anchors. scripts/check_provenance_pins.py DEFAULT_ROOT = "docs/design/hicasso" at :247, blocking via --changed-since, so it covers the SOURCE half only. Net: design/hicasso gets both gates; core/hicasso gets check_doc_slugs plus the digest gate.
(d) THE FENCE ASYMMETRY RUNS IN THE LOSING DIRECTION FOR THIS MIGRATION. Confirmed at the constant: check_doc_slugs.py:1708 FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES = ("docs/design/hicasso", "docs/the-mayor-method"). Fenced content moving design -> core therefore leaves a tree where doc links inside fences ARE validated and lands in one where they are NOT, so a markdown link inside a migrated fence silently stops being checked. Narrow in practice - fences in these pages are Clojure and in-fence doc links are rare - and offset on a different axis, since content arriving in docs/core GAINS digest pinning it did not have. It did not bite #8668, whose two migrations added prose sections and edited one fence, but it should be stated in any future hicasso design -> core move.

PHASE 2 SHAPE: THERE IS NO PHASE 2. Zero files, zero lines, no dispatch. Step (b) is merged and I found no teaching residue after independently testing the roster it was built from.

OPERATOR: I FOUND NO SECOND QUESTION. The only live one is the one already on this bead - specification.md and facade-freeze.md still carrying view specification in product/ while falling outside both category 2's closed list and category 4's - which the 2026-08-22 04:04 note already separated into TWO rulings on a citation census. That is bucket (2)'s question, not step (b)'s, and I have not answered it.

BEAD STATE: (a) merged #8661, (b) merged #8668. The ruling closes this bead when both have merged AND product/ carries no operative contract or unmigrated teaching content. THE TEACHING HALF OF THAT CONDITION IS NOW DISCHARGED AND INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. The operative-contract half remains the open specification.md / facade-freeze.md ruling. I did not close the bead.

ONE OBSERVATION, OFFERED AS SUCH AND RECOMMENDING NO ACTION: 03-events-as-data.md:246 writes an inline :ref (fn [node] ...) closure while 09-interop.md:353 teaches that a top-level function is what keeps ref identity stable. 03's subject is rf/capture-frame composition at a foreign edge and 09 is the chapter that owns refs, so I read this as a simplification serving a different lesson rather than a defect. Recorded only so the judgement is on record.
MAYOR 2026-08-22, tip 112310ddbc — I DISPATCHED A SCOPING PASS FOR WORK THAT HAD ALREADY MERGED,
and the worker refuted the premise instead of doing the job. The refusal is the deliverable and it
was correct. Recording my own error here rather than in a transcript, and then the state.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I read this bead's note "STEP (b) IS THE ONLY THING BETWEEN THIS BEAD AND
CLOSING", confirmed its fence had cleared (rf2-wppza closed, PR #8667 merged), and dispatched.
Step (b) was already done: PR #8668, "docs(hicasso): merge the teaching set into the guide
(rf2-ps7ia step b)", MERGED 2026-08-21T13:29:59Z as f53dd7c17e, verified by me at source after the
worker reported it — state MERGED, merge commit an ancestor of origin/main, six files.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS EXACT AND IT IS EMBARRASSING. My brief pasted this sentence verbatim: "AND THE
CHEAPEST GUARD IS THE TREE, NOT THE ITEM: before you brief or build X, check whether X ALREADY
EXISTS AT TIP — one directory listing would have ended the dispatch that produced this rule." I
verified the fence, the guide's arrival, the file census, the classifier surface and the gate
coverage. I did not check whether the work itself had landed. I pasted the rule and did not apply
it, which is a more useful thing to know about briefs than any of the premises I did check.

WHY THE BEAD DID NOT SAVE ME: the note declaring step (b) outstanding and the merge that discharged
it fall on the SAME DAY, and nothing wrote the merge back onto this bead. A note that says "X is
the only thing remaining" is a claim with a shelf life, and this one expired within hours.

WHAT THE PASS DELIVERED ANYWAY, all of it worth more than the scope I asked for.

  1. THE GATE FACT, and it generalises well beyond this bead:
     implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py DIGEST-PINS 223 FENCED BLOCKS ACROSS
     ALL 29 docs/core/hicasso PAGES, and runs unconditionally in CI. EDITING ANY FENCED BLOCK IN
     THE HICASSO GUIDE IS A TWO-FILE CHANGE — the page and the roster. PR #8668's sixth file is
     exactly that roster bump, which is the pattern rather than an exception. Any future guide
     dispatch must carry this or it lands red.

  2. THE FENCE-LINK ASYMMETRY RUNS THE LOSING WAY for design->core moves: doc links inside fenced
     blocks ARE validated under docs/design/hicasso and are NOT under docs/core. So moving a fenced
     block from design into the guide moves it from checked to unchecked, and a broken link inside
     it stops being reported. Worth knowing before the next migration, not after.

  3. THE KIND-3 CENSUS ROSTER IS INCOMPLETE, and the worker flagged the instrument rather than
     letting the next reader inherit it as sound: five files scored at 0% RF do carry teaching
     material. Every item in them is nonetheless already published, each verified at page and
     heading — so the set was built from an imperfect instrument and still landed complete. That
     is luck worth naming as luck.

  4. LEXICAL PROBES CANNOT DISCRIMINATE TEACHING CONTENT IN THIS CORPUS, in either direction. The
     worker confirmed the discarded second-person control AND had its own imperative probe fail on
     three of the four primary carriers: this corpus writes in the indicative.

  5. One census file was unclassified (post-rename-recertification-2026-08-20.md). Read: pure
     working record, benign.

WHERE THIS BEAD NOW STANDS. THE TEACHING HALF — bucket (1) — IS DISCHARGED and independently
verified. What remains is the OPERATIVE-CONTRACT half and the one live operator question already on
this bead: whether specification.md and facade-freeze.md move, which is bucket (2)'s and which
nobody below the operator has answered. The worker did not answer it and neither do I.

*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** Banner added 2026-08-24 05:14 AUSEST, tip f4a61bc074, by the
backlog-reread loop. This bead ALREADY CONTAINED the phrase three times and was counted as marked by
the 2026-08-23 census. It should not have been, and the reason is worth more than the banner.

WHY THE MARKER CENSUS PASSED THIS BEAD WRONGLY. All three prior occurrences of "NOT DISPATCHABLE" in
these notes are the phrase being RETIRED, not asserted:

  @~1000  a pre-ruling note explaining why the bead was not dispatchable BEFORE the split ruling;
  @~2500  the ruling comment's own summary: "The description's 'AWAITING MIKE / NOT DISPATCHABLE'
          header is DISCHARGED; dispatch per the execution shape in the ruling comment.";
  @~13650 a worker re-confirming the same: "the description's 'AWAITING MIKE / NOT DISPATCHABLE'
          header is discharged exactly as the brief said."

Two of the three say DISCHARGED in the same sentence as the phrase. A substring scan cannot tell an
assertion from its own retraction, so the census scored this bead marked while its LIVE hold - which
sits at the very end of the notes, 27,000 characters past the newest of those three - carried no
marker at all. The failure runs in the direction that HIDES a hold rather than manufacturing one,
which is the worse direction for this particular scan.

THE HOLD THAT IS ACTUALLY LIVE, quoted from this bead's own newest note rather than re-derived:
"THE TEACHING HALF - bucket (1) - IS DISCHARGED and independently verified. What remains is the
OPERATIVE-CONTRACT half and the one live operator question already on this bead: whether
specification.md and facade-freeze.md move, which is bucket (2)'s and which nobody below the
operator has answered. The worker did not answer it and neither do I."

SO THE BEAD IS HELD, AND ON A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE ONE THE OLD HEADER NAMED. The old header
asked for the split ruling; that ruling landed on 2026-08-21T10:12:55Z and the header is correctly
discharged. What is open now is downstream of that ruling: bucket (2)'s destination for two named
files. Reading either of the "discharged" sentences as "this bead is released" is the misread this
banner exists to stop, and this pass made it before correcting it at the tail.

ORDERING, verified rather than assumed this pass: notes last changed 2026-08-22T08:22:53Z; the newest
comment carrying any instruction is the ruling at 2026-08-21T10:12:55Z, which is OLDER. The notes tail
is therefore the governing text, and it is what is quoted above.

NOTHING IS QUEUED BEHIND THIS BEAD: dependency_count 0, dependent_count 0, and it appears in neither
the blocked list nor any other bead's manifest. What the hold costs is that two files stay at an
address this bead's own description calls interim custody.
