STEP (b) EXECUTED AND OPEN FOR REVIEW — PR #8668, worker on worker/teachmerge-ps7ia, 2026-08-21 23:10 AUSEST. THE BEAD STAYS OPEN: the ruling closes it when (a) AND (b) have MERGED, and (b) is open, not merged.

WHICH TEXT I ACTED ON. The description still carries the superseded 'AWAITING MIKE / NOT DISPATCHABLE' header; the governing text is the comment 'OPERATOR RULING — THE SPLIT' at 2026-08-21T10:12:55Z, whose closing line says to brief from it rather than from the pre-ruling description. Notes newest-first confirm step (a) merged as #8661 and step (b) was the only thing left. 0 children, dep_count 0, dependent_count 0.

THE FENCE IN THE NEWEST NOTE HAD ALREADY CLEARED, and the brief did not mention it. That note fences step (b) behind rf2-wppza's fhsweep PR because it may edit async-routing-recipes.md. That PR IS my base commit — 07c23a172a, 'chore(residue): correct the freehand references that are FALSE, keep the history (rf2-wppza)' — so the fence was spent before I started. No open PR touches docs/core/hicasso/ or docs/design/hicasso/product/.

HOW THE TEACHING SET WAS ESTABLISHED, since the note explicitly forbids grepping for 'recipe'. Category 1 is teaching and how-to, which is exactly the *reader-facing answer* kind in product-kind-census.md — the census the ruling's own planning facts come from. Its kind-3 roster is SIX carriers, four primary + two minority, and it reconciles arithmetically: 237+51+71+86+31+132 = 608 against the census's stated ~608. I verified rather than trusted: an independent second-person-density probe was run and DISCARDED because its control failed (06-lists-and-collections.md is a known teaching page with zero occurrences of 'you'). The discriminator that worked was structural — where the guide raises a reader's question and routes the answer elsewhere.

FOUR OF THE SIX WERE ALREADY ANSWERED ON A PUBLISHED PAGE, each saying so of itself. release-policy.md §4 records that its consumer-facing abridgement lives at 00-installation.md §Supported versions, and §5.1's 'the semantics are frozen and the spellings are not' stands there near-verbatim. async-routing-recipes.md's own closing states that 08-async-resources.md and 07-routing-and-navigation.md teach all three of its shapes already. per-keystroke.md §6's finding is 19-performance.md's echo budget row plus its keystroke trace step 6. lanes/hot-path-architecture.md's ladder is published as escape-ladder.md, and it is category 4 anyway. Nothing was merged for those four — duplicating them would create a second thing to drift.

TWO GENUINE GAPS MERGED, and one of them is a DEFECT rather than an absence. 06-lists-and-collections.md gained three sections from virtualizer-recipe.md's Rules 3 and 4 and its 'blessed' screen: keeping the focused row mounted, aria-rowindex, and how to screen a package. 22-accessibility.md's focus-ownership table routes the virtualised case TO that chapter for an answer that was not there. 05-forms.md gained the operable-while-invalid submit button: the chapter disabled the button on (not can-submit?) while :submit-attempted? is set only by a rejected submit — so the attempt that would set it is the one the disabled button prevents, and that chapter's own submit-attempt display gate could not fire.

NO FILE MOVED AND NONE WAS DELETED. All three sources stay as evidence for specification.md §7 rows. Per this directory's own fence, forms-recipes.md and virtualizer-recipe.md each carry a dated beside-amendment naming this bead, and product/README.md records the teaching set and its disposition. The audited per-version virtualizer package table was deliberately NOT published — a dated reading of third-party releases is working-record discipline the guide does not carry, which is that page's own conclusion.

GATES, captured exit codes: check_doc_slugs.py 0; npm run test:hicasso-invariants 0 (14 scripts, incl. check_guide_samples.py and its self-test — the roster row for 05-forms block 8 moved in the same commit); python -m mkdocs build --strict 0; check_provenance_pins.py --changed-since origin/main 0, naming '3 pages inspected' which is exactly my three changed design pages; check_readme_links.py --ci 0 and covering none of my paths. An early `mkdocs build --strict` returned EXIT 127 (not on PATH in Git Bash) and is recorded as no verdict rather than read as a pass.

PLANTED-FAULT CONTROLS, both restored and verified by hashing bytes against the committed blob rather than by reading a diff. check_guide_samples.py: a comment planted inside 05-forms.md's button block gave exit 1 naming '05-forms.md block 8'; restored to bb499fc2cea9 on both sides. check_doc_slugs.py: the new anchor suffixed -PLANTED gave exit 1 naming README.md:113; restored to b5d736418389 on both sides. Both were green at base before any edit, so the discrimination runs in both directions.

THE CLOSING QUESTION — DOES product/ STILL CARRY UNMIGRATED TEACHING CONTENT? NO. All six kind-3 carriers are discharged.

ONE THING FOR THE MAYOR BEFORE CLOSING, and it is not a teaching remainder. The ruling's close condition also names OPERATIVE CONTRACT, and by the census's own measurement specification.md (VS 55%, ~278 lines) and facade-freeze.md (VS 55%, ~136 lines) still carry view specification in product/. Both sit OUTSIDE category 2's closed list — which named dispositions, complaints, invariants, the naming outcomes and budgets, and step (a) executed exactly that — and outside category 4's list. So either category 2's list is exhaustive and those two are ruled to stay, or the close condition wants a further slice. That is a ruling question, not work I should invent an answer to.

title: hic: OPERATOR CALL — U3 is reached and meets by 5.2x but on a class narrower than its name; C3/C4 refused on evidence, U4 unreached
description:
SPLIT OUT OF rf2-85og2 when its ground-1 re-test landed in PR #8595 (worker/budgetgates-85og2, 2026-08-21). This is the EDIT-SHAPED, LOUD-BOX-SAFE half — it needs NO window and can be dispatched beside anything.

WHAT PR #8589 GAVE US, and why it is not enough. rf2-xa8wo landed an interaction-to-paint clock on the slice app: slice_echo_clock_app.cljs requires re-frame.hicasso.examples.slice.{events,routes,views}, mounts through h/mount!, and its window! runs t0 -> real DOM event -> requestAnimationFrame -> setTimeout 0 -> t-paint. That instrument satisfies section 9.4's 'package-resident' test, which turns on what the instrument is POINTED AT rather than on jar residence, and it clears rf2-85og2's ground 1 for rows U1 and U2.

WHAT IT DOES NOT REACH, measured rather than assumed. The driver's OWN DOCSTRING states U3 and U4 are not served. Its four rows are a floor, two Hicasso interactions and a positive control — there is NO DONOR ARM, so C3 and C4 have nothing to compare against. The blocker for those four rows has therefore MOVED: it is no longer 'no instrument exists', it is 'this instrument's arms do not span the comparison'.

WHAT IS WANTED: a SECOND DRIVER plus a DONOR ARM, so U3, U4, C3 and C4 become reachable. Build the instrument; do not run a window. Sizing, arm choice and which donor is the honest comparator are all open and should be settled at source rather than from this text.

VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING. Re-read the driver's docstring at the tip and confirm U3/U4 are still unserved — rf2-85og2 is a bead whose refusals have already been overtaken once by a merge, which is exactly how this bead came to exist. If a donor arm has landed meanwhile, say so and close.

THE PROHIBITION THAT OUTRANKS THE TASK, carried over from rf2-85og2 and not negotiable: DO NOT WIDEN A BAND OR GUESS A THRESHOLD to make a row reachable. That programme has refused four times rather than do that, and each refusal carried more information than a pass would have. And note section 7: it routes every distributional row to pinned evidence runs on P-DEV-1 and FORBIDS converting one into a PR threshold, with check_budget_ledger.py enforcing it — so building a GATE here is out even where building an INSTRUMENT is in. That distinction is what a previous dispatch got wrong.

MOVE NO LEDGER CELL. The ledger stands at 49 rows / 31 MET / 5 BREACH / 3 UNRESOLVED / 10 UNPINNED.

SURFACE: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/. Not docs/design/hicasso/product/budgets.md, which rf2-85og2 owns.
notes:
PARTIALLY DISCHARGED by PR #8599 (worker/donorarm-9wmqd, 2026-08-21). NO WINDOW AND NO BENCH RUN WAS TAKEN; no ledger cell moves; no threshold, band or gate was created.

PREMISES RE-VERIFIED AT THE TIP, both held. slice_echo_clock_app.cljs:161 still states U3/U4 are not served; its arms are still a floor, two Hicasso interactions and :ctl-blocked, with no donor arm. PR #8595 merged mid-flight and budgets.md now carries the same finding from the ledger side.

WHAT LANDED. Two new files, pure additions, no existing file edited.
  slice_broad_clock_app.cljs  the second driver, on the slice FEED route, timing two broad
                              operations through the SAME window! the first driver publishes
                              (required, not copied): a locale switch on the published <select>
                              and a theme switch on the published button. Arms: :idle-frame,
                              :locale, :theme, :donor-locale, :donor-theme, :ctl-blocked.
  slice_donor_views.cljs      the DONOR ARM: the same feed page in UIx, same subscriptions from
                              the same registrations, same event vectors.

SO U3, C3 AND C4 NOW HAVE AN INSTRUMENT ON THE GOVERNED POPULATION. They keep UNPINNED: an
instrument is not a verdict, and a verdict needs a quiet-box window.

THREE REFUSALS, EACH SOURCE-LOCATED.
1. NO NAVIGATION ROW, and this is mechanical. Two of the three broad operations the first
   driver names (a route change, a save reply) CANNOT be bracketed by this window at all:
   routing/activate-link! ends at router/dispatch!, the ASYNC door, so the click returns with
   the operation merely enqueued and the router drains it on a next-turn task. A window that
   stops at the first paint after the click stops BEFORE THE OPERATION HAS BEGUN. The slice's
   own flow_dom_cljs_test.cljs states the split. Those operations need a DIFFERENT window,
   bounded by the drain and its paint. Not built.
2. U4 IS NOT REACHABLE ON THE SLICE. It is registered over dragging/animation and the slice
   publishes neither -- every interaction it has is discrete. A per-frame estimator over a
   scripted repetition of a discrete interaction would be the same class of error the first
   driver exists to have stopped making, and adding a drag would move the population.
3. ONE DONOR DOES NOT SETTLE C3'S 'best relevant adapter'. UIx was chosen because the process
   carries one adapter and because this lane's re-taken HD-008 rows make direct UIx the faster
   donor (the conservative direction). A Reagent-on-subs donor needs a second adapter phase and
   therefore a second page.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWES, and why it stays OPEN.
  (a) U4's INSTRUMENT, which is a THIRD DRIVER ON A THIRD PAGE. examples/ledger publishes a
      virtualized 10,000-row list over a real scroll viewport (see its virtualized_dom_cljs_test,
      which drives scrollTop and a real scroll event) -- a genuinely CONTINUOUS interaction and
      the population U4 is stated over. Same window! mechanism, but an estimator over FRAME
      INTERVALS rather than over window lengths. Worth its own bead.
  (b) A SUITE-LEVEL SELF-TEST. The sibling driver has slice_echo_window_dom_cljs_test.cljs; this
      one has none. It carries six instrument-integrity controls that run IN the driver (a
      canonical-DOM parity gate with its own negative control, four echo negative controls, the
      tally, the guard and the additive positive control), which is the stronger place by the
      sibling's own argument -- but a browser-suite row proving the repairs is still owed.
  (c) THE WINDOW ITSELF, for U3/C3/C4, on a quiet box. Note the resolution caveat the driver
      publishes: a paint-bounded window is dominated by the frame grid, so :over-floor's
      :straddles-1? must be read on each measured arm BEFORE any :comparative range is quoted.
      If the shipped seed cannot separate the measured arms from an empty frame, the honest
      conclusion is that C3 needs a BROADER POPULATION than the slice's feed page -- a finding
      about the row, never a licence to widen a band.

GATES. npm run test:hicasso-compile is the gate covering this surface; it is heavyweight and was
NOT run locally (loud box), but it auto-covers new files by walking the lane directory and runs
on every PR in test.yml, so CI gates the compile. Locally: a Clojure-aware delimiter-balance check
and a qualified-reference resolution check (45 refs in the driver, 8 in the donor views, all
resolve), each with a planted-fault discrimination proof and a restore verified by blob hash.
U4's half is now filed separately as rf2-xc0bw (a per-frame driver on the LEDGER witness, edit-shaped and loud-box-safe). This bead keeps items (b) the suite-level self-test and (c) the quiet-box window for U3/C3/C4.
AUDIT OF PR #8599 (2026-08-21) — repair before the quiet-box U3/C3/C4 window.

Two measurement-fidelity defects belong to this existing owner; no duplicate bead was created.

1. DONOR FEED READ-SET IS LARGER ON THE SHIPPED POPULATION. slice_donor_views.cljs feed-page always calls use-subscribe for [::subs/t :feed/empty], while the Hicasso feed-page calls h/sub for that value only in its empty branch. The pinned seed is non-empty, so the donor locale arm carries an extra subscription/hook that the Hicasso locale arm does not. That adds work to the denominator and can flatter the C3 Hicasso/UIx ratio. Keep the branch-local read branch-local (for example via an empty-state child boundary) and make the suite self-test prove the relevant read roster, not only canonical DOM.

2. THE THEME ARMS RUN OVER DIFFERENT LOCALE-STATE MIXES. :locale and :ctl-blocked both toggle the shared Hicasso frame's locale, while only :donor-locale toggles the donor frame. Replaying the six-arm lane/slot-order at measured slots s=8..19 shows :theme runs in the non-seed locale on 4/12 visits per round, but :donor-theme does so on 8/12. Thus the comparative theme medians are drawn from different page-state populations; the seeded-only canonical parity gate cannot see the divergence after sampling begins. Isolate the control's state/root or deterministically establish each arm's pre-state, and add a schedule-level self-test that proves paired arms see the same governed state mix.
AUDIT REPAIRS 1 AND 2 PLUS ITEM (b) LANDED in PR #8606 (worker/echoself-9wmqd, 2026-08-21). NO WINDOW AND NO BENCH RUN WAS TAKEN; no ledger cell moves; no threshold, band or gate created. ITEM (c) IS UNTOUCHED and this bead stays OPEN on it.

BOTH PREMISES RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, both held. slice_donor_views.cljs feed-page bound empty-label unconditionally in its let; slice/views.cljs feed-page reads [::subs/t :feed/empty] only inside its empty branch; the seed is seven articles at a page size of three, so the branch never renders.

THE 4/12 AND 8/12 COUNTS REPRODUCED EXACTLY, in every one of the five rounds. Replaying the six-arm lane/visit-plan (order_guard/slot-order rotate-then-reflect at k=6, indexed by the SAMPLE index, not by the round) at {:warmup 8 :samples 12} over 5 rounds: at measured slots s=8..19, :theme runs in the non-seed locale on 4/12 visits per round and :donor-theme on 8/12.

THE SAME REPLAY FOUND A SECOND DIVERGENCE THE AUDIT DID NOT NAME, in the other dimension and on the POSITIVE CONTROL'S pairing: :ctl-blocked runs in the non-seed THEME on 8/12 measured visits per round against :locale's 4/12, and control-per-round subtracts those two medians. Same mechanism, same class. Both are closed.

WHAT LANDED.
1. Repair 1 on the DONOR SIDE only (slice/views.cljs is a shipped example consumed by a11y/l0/l2 tests): an empty-state child boundary, feed-empty, which costs the measured population nothing because its branch never renders at the seed. The full read roster was then swept boundary by boundary and the result recorded in the donor namespace docstring: chrome 7/7, article-row 2/2, digest 5/5, digest-body/callout/unsupported 1/1 each, pager 5/5 at the seed, app 4 against 3. TWO other differences exist and neither is the same defect. The PAGER is a source-located REFUSAL: the same child-boundary repair would put an extra boundary on the MEASURED page (the seed always renders a pager), which is the same error in the same direction, larger and always on. The shell's missing [:rf.route/id] read runs in the DENOMINATOR'S favour.
2. Repair 2 by ESTABLISHING each arm's pre-state, not by isolating the control. Arms declare :side and :alternates; pre-state is a pure fn of the arm and its own visit index; establish-pre-state! moves the frame through the application's own events, outside every window, on parity-discrimination!'s door and settle. Paired arms then see identical mixes at EVERY schedule by construction.
   WHY THE OTHER CANDIDATE WAS REJECTED, on a replay rather than on taste: both isolating variants (control restores its locale / control on its own root) equalise the theme pair at {8,12} and STOP DOING SO at {8,13} and {8,20} -- the equality is an accident of how slot-order's rotation lands on twelve indices, and sampling's own docstring says the run reading this instrument will raise those counts. The own-root variant also leaves the control's own theme mix wrong (0/12 against 4/12).
3. Item (b): implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso/slice_broad_window_dom_cljs_test.cljs, beside slice_broad_clock_app.cljs (the driver both repairs live in; the sibling slice_echo_clock_app already has its own suite). Ten rows.

WHAT THE SELF-TEST PROVES, beyond canonical DOM -- both first-class, each with its own negative control.
- READ ROSTER: both frames' subscription caches through subs.tooling/sub-cache-snapshot (the same per-frame cache BOTH substrates go through -- Hicasso's collector calls subs/subscribe for every h/sub edge, the UIx adapter for every hook). Asserts donor-minus-hicasso is EMPTY, [::subs/t :feed/empty] is in NEITHER, [:rf.route/id] is hicasso-only, with anti-vacuity first. NEGATIVE CONTROL re-plants exactly the removed read as a UIx boundary on the donor frame in its own root and requires the comparison to go from empty to naming exactly that read.
- GOVERNED STATE MIX: replays lane/visit-plan through the driver's own pre-state and asserts the three compared pairs are one population at five schedules including {8,13} and {8,20}. NEGATIVE CONTROL models the rig PR #8599 shipped and requires the same comparison to refuse, reproducing 4-against-8 on the locale dimension and 8-against-4 on the control's theme dimension INSIDE the suite, then shows the repaired model passing at the same schedule.
- AND A BRIDGE from the arithmetic to the instrument, because a pure replay proves a model rather than a driver: one DOM row calls establish-pre-state! for both parities on both frames and reads the result back through the driver's own echo checks; another runs a tiny schedule end to end and asserts each arm's visit counter advanced exactly once per planned visit.

NO SEVENTH IN-DRIVER CONTROL WAS ADDED. The driver already runs six and in-driver is the stronger place; what was missing was the browser-suite row.

WHAT THE SUITE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RE-ADJUDICATE, stated in the file: the canonical-DOM parity gate is a RELEASE gate by construction (data-rf2-source-coord makes the two arms' attributes differ under goog.DEBUG), so a dev-compiled row asserting that equality would either fail honestly or have to strip attributes until it passed.

GATES. npm run test:hicasso-compile covers this surface and auto-covers the new file by walking the lane directory; it was NOT run locally (a peer worker held a live allocation window on the box and two heavyweight runs wedge rather than fail), and CI gates the compile. No fast-PR spine, no shadow-cljs, no browser run. Locally: a Clojure-aware delimiter-balance check and a qualified-reference resolution check over all three files -- 98 distinct in-repo refs (45 driver / 20 donor views / 33 suite), 0 unresolved, 8 further refs external and reported as out of reach rather than counted. Three planted faults, one per file, each red naming what was planted, each restore verified by identical blob hash against the committed object. Re-run green on the final base after a rebase past twelve landings. implementation/package.json was NOT touched: -dom-cljs-test$ is discovered by ns-regexp and needs no registration.
CI CYCLE 2 on PR #8606 — the browser lane read the first cut as 14 failures, ONE CAUSE plus one contract bug. Now GREEN on browser-test, node-test and every other check, on a rebased base. No assertion was weakened; one was added.

THE CAUSE, source-located. collector/!cells is a PROCESS-GLOBAL table keyed by (frame, query), and its own comment states that isolation between roots is a property of that keying rather than anything React provides. invalidate-cell! is the repair for a cell whose reaction has been retired -- including, in its own words, 'across a same-id reincarnation' -- but that repair rides the reaction's DISPOSAL HOOK, and make-reset-runtime-fixture retires a frame by resetting frame/frames to {} rather than through it. A second mount on a used frame id therefore finds a live cell holding a dead reaction: subs/subscribe is never called again (empty sub-cache) and no watch is installed (no re-render). THE FIRST RENDER IS PERFECT, which is what makes it silent.

THE EVIDENCE FIT THAT SHAPE EXACTLY: the mount row (1st mount) PASSED and every row after it failed. hic roster #{} against the donor's 34; every Hicasso-side locale/theme pre-state stayed English/light; the tally read 9 unverified of 18 -- precisely the nine Hicasso-side windows, with all six donor-side ones verified.

THE ACT-ENVIRONMENT HYPOTHESIS WAS TESTED AND REJECTED rather than assumed: every 'not wrapped in act(...)' line in that log is timestamped +12.32s / +14.36s and this namespace ran at +28.58s. Neighbouring-suite noise.

THE FIX is the discipline slice-echo-window-dom-cljs-test already keeps. boot! takes the frame ids as an argument (hicasso-frame / donor-frame become documented DEFAULTS for the bench page's single mount); a new frames reader publishes the live pair; frame-for and parity-discrimination! resolve through it, because a caller that dispatched into the default while the page rendered from a fresh id would be writing to a frame nothing reads. The suite mints a fresh pair per row. Mechanism + measurement recorded at source in boot!'s new section MOUNTING TWICE, and in teardown!, which states that it cannot fix this and why.

A REAL CONTRACT BUG THE SUITE ALSO CAUGHT: visits published the last visit INDEX under a docstring promising a COUNT, so it read one short of lane/visit-plan's per-arm count. claim-visit! now banks the count and answers the index. The bridge row earned its place on its first run.

AND THE FIRST DIRECT MEASUREMENT OF THE DONOR'S READ ROSTER, handed over by the empty-Hicasso failure: 34 query vectors, every one of them also read by the Hicasso arm, the fifteen ::subs/t strings matching one for one against the boundary-by-boundary sweep. [::subs/t :feed/empty] is ABSENT -- repair 1 confirmed on the shipped population rather than argued. The roster also reaches a :<- sub's INPUTS and not only the values a body asks for ([:rf.route/query] and [:rf/route] arrive as [::subs/page]'s input chain), which makes the comparison stronger than claimed; the docstring now says so and a new assertion pins it.

THE GREEN IS NOT VACUOUS: the red and green runs both report 1044 tests, and assertions go 5937 -> 5938 -- exactly the one assertion added. Had the DOM rows collapsed to their off-browser skips the count would have dropped by roughly forty-five.

GATES. npm run test:hicasso-compile still NOT run locally (machine contention: a peer held an allocation window throughout), and CI decided it. Browser-test is now a gate that RAN rather than one that was cited: red 14, then green, then green again post-rebase. Local static checks re-run on the final base: 97 distinct in-repo refs, 0 unresolved, exit 0; two further planted faults on this round's own edited lines, each red naming the plant, each restored to an identical blob hash.

ITEM (c) REMAINS UNTOUCHED AND THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN ON IT. No window was run, no reading taken, no ledger cell moved, no threshold, band or gate created.

MAYOR 2026-08-21 09:15 AUSEST (stranded sweep) — A DORMANT WORKTREE STILL HOLDS THIS BEAD. DO NOT DISPATCH A SECOND WORKER AT IT.

Found by sweeping the WORKTREES rather than the in_progress list, which is the only
place this surfaces: this bead reads OPEN, so a dispatch tick scanning for ready work
would take it, while worker/echoself-9wmqd's worktree at
re-frame2-worktrees/echoself is still standing against it.

WHY THAT WORKTREE IS STILL THERE, and it is deliberate rather than neglect. Its agent's
last message is "Fixed, pushed, and CI has spoken: PR #8606 is green on every check and
marked ready." That is a PR-ready ANNOUNCEMENT, not a completion report, so the reap test
is not satisfied and the worktree correctly stays. PR #8606 has MERGED, but merge state is
the most-discredited of the reap proxies and authorises nothing here.

SO THERE ARE TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS AND THEY HAVE DIFFERENT ANSWERS. The worktree stays
until its agent says it is done. The BEAD is a different matter: what remains on it is
item (c), which needs a measurement window, and the bench slot is held by
worker/revorder-csca8. So the bead is fenced on the machine regardless.

RE-DISPATCH ONLY WHEN BOTH hold: the bench slot is free, AND either that worktree has
been reaped or a fresh worktree is used under a different branch name. If a future tick
takes this bead, check re-frame2-worktrees/echoself first — two workers on one branch
loses work, and this bead's name is the only thing that would warn you.

NOT DISPATCHED THIS TICK, and the reason is the machine rather than the bead. A

MAYOR BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-21 23:0x AUSEST, tip 30d99fa8bf. I HAVE BEEN MIS-CLASSIFYING THIS BEAD FOR HOURS AND THIS NOTE CORRECTS IT.

I have repeatedly reported this bead to Mike as part of the 'quiet-box measurement lane awaiting a
drain decision'. THAT IS WRONG, and the bead says so in its own first paragraph: 'This is the
EDIT-SHAPED, LOUD-BOX-SAFE half — it needs NO window and can be dispatched beside anything.' I
grouped it by TOPIC (clock driver, measurement) instead of reading it. It is the classic case the
backlog loop names: work under a decision already made, sitting in the needs-a-decision pile.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY OWES, from its own PR #8599 note, split by whether a window is required:
  (a) U4's INSTRUMENT — a THIRD DRIVER on a THIRD PAGE (examples/ledger's virtualized
      10,000-row list over a real scroll viewport), same window! mechanism but an estimator over

DEFERRAL LIFTED — MIKE 2026-08-14: 'I want hicasso fully implemented, nothing deferred. I want a complete library. I want a sophisticated library.'

This bead was parked under the earlier direction to run measurement later. That direction is superseded. It is now live work.

ONE PHYSICAL CONSTRAINT REMAINS AND IS NOT A DEFERRAL. A clock estimand needs a quiet box: one measurement at a time, controls arbitrating, no other worker compiling. That is a property of the instrument, not a scheduling preference — a reading taken against six concurrent compiles measures the fleet, not the library. COUNTER estimands have no such constraint; monotone counters read the same on a loaded box, which is why the deterministic censuses landed while the clock tables did not.

SO THE PLAN IS: build every instrument NOW, in parallel, on a loaded box — that work is edit-shaped and unconstrained. Then run the windows themselves back to back when the fleet is idle. That is the same split that produced rf2-w01c from rf2-hic-036 and rf2-d6ai8 from rf2-hic-088, and it means the quiet-box time is spent measuring rather than writing drivers.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES, restated: if it needs an instrument that does not exist, that half dispatches immediately. If the instrument exists and only the window is missing, it queues for the next quiet period. Whoever picks it up should say which case it is in the first paragraph of its report.

title: hicasso: the fused reader array costs 91-92 B/read — the largest term this page has attributed to a container rather than a value
description:
MEASURED, NOT SPECULATED. rf2-zei9w's ablation attributes 91 B/read (Reagent segment) / 92 (UIx) to the cell's fused reader array — the container itself, not the membership it holds. Per-round bands are disjoint across all six rounds, the R=0 shell does not move, and donors moved 0.05/0.19 B/read, so this is a per-KEY term and the attribution is solid. Published in docs/design/hicasso/studio/reads-per-boundary-heap-ladder.md (2026-08-04 section), PR #7452.

WHY IT IS WORTH A LOOK. rf2-dabt3's fusion banked -60 B/read in both segments — real, and it won — but that is only ~40% of the ~151 B/read the old reverse edge cost, because the replacement array is ~2x what ONE PersistentHashSet membership costs (+46/+47 B/read, PR #7418 run D). The design predicted the surviving array would be cheap residue; it is not. It is now the largest single term this page has attributed to a CONTAINER rather than to a value.

THE OBVIOUS SHAPE, and it is only a sketch. At the fan-out this table actually sees, the overwhelmingly common case is ONE reader per key. A scalar slot that holds the single reader directly and promotes to an array on the SECOND reader would retain a pointer instead of a JSArray-plus-backing-store for that case. arm1/runtime.cljs's own section header already argues a JS array beats a persistent set here; this asks the next question down, which is whether a container is needed at all in the common case.

THIS IS NOT A DISPATCH. It wants a ruling first, for three reasons:
• release-cell!'s .indexOf, arm-cell-reaper!'s alength and stats's alength all read .-readers directly, and cell-readers/stats are witness surfaces the six laws and the ladder's structural gate are written against — a polymorphic slot touches all of them.
• It is a byte shave on a pre-alpha arm, and the stance is explicit that not every measured term needs actioning.
• The bill it would attack is +331 B/read against Reagent; 91 of that is this term. Worth knowing the size before deciding it is worth the branch in a hot path.

Precondition if it is ever taken: a quiet box, p0_run.cjs --only ladder 6 rounds with both donors as same-run controls, and the same ablation discipline rf2-zei9w used — attribute, do not infer.

from it is wrong. This is the same shape as any instrument that can answer "nothing here" — the
answer is right about what it measures and wrong about what it is being used for. A tick that
reads the fleet count and dispatches a measurement window would take its numbers against 131
resident processes and never know.

THE FENCE THEREFORE STANDS, on its own terms and unchanged. Nothing here is a clearance.

WHAT IS NEW AND WORTH THE OPERATOR'S ATTENTION: the fence is now CHEAP to clear rather than met.
No live worker contends for the box, so reaching a genuinely quiet one is a process sweep plus a
hold on dispatch for the window's duration — not a fleet drain, which is what the fence was
written to require back when five workers were live. That is a smaller ask than the recorded
condition implies.

AND A NATURALLY QUIET MOMENT IS STILL NOT A WINDOW. The dispatch loop refills the fleet on its own
cadence, so quiet-right-now decays without warning. A window needs dispatch deliberately held for
its duration, which is precisely why this remains a decision the mayor announces rather than one
that happens by default. Surfaced, not taken.

before anything above it. ***

later, on the same bead. AND MINE IS NOW THE NEWEST TEXT, so a reader doing the correct
newest-first walk lands on my error and never reaches the correction beneath it. That is exactly
the writer-side hazard the method carries a clause about — a stale note that IS the newest text,
which a reader cannot defend against.

WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS THIS BEAD, unchanged and restated so this note does not merely say "not that":
a RULING. The 2026-08-04 delegated dossier review PARKED it as K3's priced paper path, P2 -> P3,

CLOCK ROWS THAT DECIDE P2." This bead's estimand is allocation, not clock.

ERROR 2 — "131 RESIDENT PROCESSES" IS NOT A LOUD BOX, AND I MEASURED THE WRONG THING. My note
counted 22 node and 109 chrome processes with the fleet empty and concluded the machine was loud.
Counted again with a 5-second per-process CPU census at this tick:

    TOTAL BUSY: 2.56 cores of 24 — the box is about 89% idle.
    node + chrome COMBINED: 0.135 cores across 21 processes showing any CPU at all.
    Largest single consumer: the editor, at 1.329 cores. My own agent processes: ~0.4.

The residue is REAL and IDLE. Presence is not load, and a process count answers presence. So I

evidence about the machine, and the machine genuinely should be measured at both brackets rather

then and it is idle now. The instrument to use is LOAD, not a count of anything.

# hic-064 — FINAL CHECKPOINT: the §13 definition-of-done audit

**Phase**: 6 exit · **Wave**: G · **Est.**: L · **Depends**: hic-019, hic-026, hic-038, hic-048, hic-050, hic-060, hic-061, hic-062, hic-066, hic-068, hic-069, hic-071, hic-072 (re-runs the naming-ledger completeness grep — no provisional name ships)
**Surface**: read-only + final report + corrective bead files

## Goal
The independent, adversarial audit of every synth-codex §13 bullet — completeness, correctness, and quality assessed separately, by a fresh reviewer who trusts artifacts over claims.

## Review protocol
1. **Completeness**: §13 bullet by bullet, **verbatim from the spec** — package independence, small coherent language with no mode switch, explicit substrate/two-hook choices with the byte-exact shell disposition, full correctness matrix with sabotage controls, public-surface-only witnesses (incl. the hic-078 editor/grid), React-interop contract, per-surface SSR/hydration, ratified budgets met via the hic-071 reconciliation table (no silent breach rows), qualified bulk dispositions per hic-036, the warm-allocation non-claim (hic-072), native island parity vs both controls, testing ladder with honest opacity, Xray causal + privacy + erasure, every use case assigned, requirements mine + per-keystroke current, resource-demand verdict explicit (hic-050), donor independence (hic-062/076).
2. **Correctness**: clean-checkout full-suite run; re-run one sabotage per checkpoint domain (kernel, slice, native, coverage) plus the naming-census and erasure positive controls; verify the budgets reconciliation against a fresh pinned run on the physical reference profile.
3. **Quality**: the hic-069 fresh-reader result reviewed; three randomly chosen complaint ids traced id → docs anchor → recovery; the anti-cathedral check — list anything that grew beyond its witness.

## Green definition and output
**Green** = every §13 bullet green AND zero unresolved correctness/coverage rows in the hic-073 correction ledger. Anything else is a **non-release verdict** with the misses enumerated. The audit distinguishes two states explicitly: *implementation audit complete* (achievable without pilots) and *product definition of done* (red until hic-063 supplies two pilots — say so plainly). Output: `docs/design/hicasso/product/definition-of-done-audit.md` with per-bullet verdicts and the filed correction ids. Thresholds never widen to turn a bullet green.

---
[Worker context — applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates: foreground a gate that fits inside the harness ceiling; DETACH one that does not and poll BOTH its log and its `.exit` file in a bounded loop within the same turn — never end the turn waiting for a completion event. Never pipe a gate through `tail` or any filter; redirect to a log and echo the runner's own exit code on the same command line. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn. DOC-SURFACE GATE: for an edit confined to docs/design/hicasso/, `mkdocs build --strict` is NOT the gate — mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs keeps that tree out of the site. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates its markdown link targets and heading anchors, and `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/; nothing validates its tables, rendering or nav, so verify anchors and table column counts BY HAND and say so in the PR body.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json` from a worker branch — they are whole-database EXPORTS, not database files, and your branch carries the snapshot taken when its worktree was created, so committing one TIME-TRAVELS the tracker: beads closed since reopen, beads filed since vanish (PR #6677 did exactly this, 135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). Any other database-derived path likewise. The human-authored config — `.beads/README.md`, `.beads/config.yaml`, `.beads/.gitignore`, `.beads/hooks/**` — IS fair game. CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section is the authority.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files only if this bead flags them — and the hot zone INCLUDES the spec/*.md hot files (spec/004-Views.md, spec/002-Frames.md, spec/API.md, spec/Conventions.md among others), not just implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn and .github/workflows/*. CLAUDE.md's Workflow section carries the canonical list; read it there rather than treating this line as complete.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues AND a row in docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md. The checkpoint's own report PR writes the `open` row; a CORRECTIVE PR never edits that file — every later transition is the ledger keeper's. Read the file's own stated protocol before touching it.

title: day8/re-frame2 has no performance regression gate (every bench in the repo covers an UNPUBLISHED artefact)
notes:
MAYOR RULING: DEFER, on a MEASURED ground rather than a preference (2026-07-26). Do not dispatch.

THE REASON IS THE NOISE FLOOR, and it was measured today by the compiled-tier report (rf2-lnecd, docs/design/freehand/studio/compiled-tier-browser-worth-it.md): THE NO-SUBSTRATE FLOOR ARM DRIFTED 37% ACROSS ROUNDS — larger than most of the effects being measured — which is why every claim in that report is stated as a RATIO TO THE IN-RUN FLOOR rather than an absolute. On the same box, the same primitive measured 10.4ns and 21.7ns across two JVMs.

A REGRESSION GATE ON A SUBSTRATE WITH A 37% FLOOR DRIFT IS A FLAKE GENERATOR. It would red on noise, and this repo has a standing rule that A FAILING TEST ON A TOUCHED SURFACE IS NEVER A FLAKE — which is exactly the rule that makes a false red expensive to dismiss. We already have one such gate (rf2-yumaq: G-8 dying because its baseline was TOO FAST) and fixing it took a worker. Adding a second, broader one before the measurement is stable would manufacture that cost at scale.

A PREMISE CORRECTION THE BEAD INHERITS FROM ME: its notes classify the Freehand benches as covering an artefact that is "NOT published". Freehand is PRE-PUBLICATION and expected to ship — docs/release-process.md forecloses only day8/re-frame2-ui, and implementation/freehand/deps.edn:29 says staying out of the lockstep inventory "leaves the release train untouched until Freehand actually ships". I propagated that error into six briefs today. So the gap this bead describes is narrower than stated: the benches cover artefacts that are not published YET, not artefacts that never will be.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DISPATCHABLE, in order: (1) a stable measurement method — the report shows allocation via getThreadAllocatedBytes gave min = p50 = max in nearly every arm, so an ALLOCATION gate is buildable where a wall-clock gate is not; (2) a named regression the gate would have caught, because a perf gate with no historical catch is an assertion that the future will resemble a past nobody measured; (3) the alpha tag, after which "published artefact" stops being a moving target.

NOT A REJECTION. The operator has ruled that performance matters — the compiler is KEPT for performance-critical applications not yet seen. A gate is the right long-term instrument; it is the wrong instrument today because it cannot yet distinguish signal from a 37% floor.
*** THE DEFER LAPSES 2026-09-01 AND NOTHING IN THE GRAPH HOLDS THIS BEAD. DO NOT DISPATCH ON THE DATE ALONE. ***

description:
*** DISPATCHABLE BUT NOT CLOSEABLE. REMOVED FROM THE DISPATCH POOL. DO NOT RE-DISPATCH. ***

READ THIS BEFORE BRIEFING FROM ANYTHING BELOW. FOUR workers have now run this recertification
- PRs #8312, #8395, #8445 and #8560, all merged, every one correct - and every one DECLINED
TO CLOSE for the same reason: naming-ledger row 18 (retire hframe) is RULED but UNEXECUTED,
and the seam it retires in favour of is rf2-t32wg, which needs an operator ruling.

That is the bead working as designed. What is NOT working is it sitting in the ready list
between rulings, because a dispatch tick reading only "no open dependencies" sends a fifth
worker to produce a fifth correct non-closure. The graph cannot carry this fence: it is a
NOTE, not an edge. The dependency list returns one row, rf2-hic-066, CLOSED.

not block certification. Both discharges are named in the 2026-08-16T06:49:50Z ruling and
both are Mike's.

WHAT THIS HOLD COSTS: rf2-hic-064 (the FINAL CHECKPOINT, the section 13 definition-of-done
audit) depends on this bead and cannot close until it does. Its other blocker, rf2-hic-088, is
already CLOSED (PR #8568), so rf2-hic-090 is now the LAST thing standing between rf2-t32wg and
the end of the Hicasso definition-of-done chain.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS ---

# hic-090 â€” Post-rename recertification

**Phase**: 6 Â· **Est.**: M Â· **Depends**: hic-066
**Surface**: re-run roster + results record (new file); re-runs existing gates, edits nothing

## Goal
A repo-wide rename can change bundle bytes, source coordinates, macro output, and server bytes. Tests and greps are not enough. This bead re-certifies the evidence after hic-066 (and re-runs after any asynchronous override sweep).

## Deliverables
Re-run and record: bundle-isolation/rent sentinels (interpreted-only zero-rent), SSR server bytes + hydration witnesses, native macro-expansion parity, source-coordinate capture (error shapes still point at real locations), and the pinned regression gate.

## Acceptance
All five families green post-sweep; any red is filed in the hic-073 ledger and blocks the release tail per hic-064's green definition.

---
[Worker context â€” applies to every hic bead]
PATH MAP: the normative documents are published in-tree by bead rf2-hic-000:
- docs/design/hicasso/product/decision-brief.md  (= synth.md / "the decision brief")
- docs/design/hicasso/product/specification.md   (= "spec SN" / synth-codex.md)
- docs/design/hicasso/product/lanes/<name>.md    (= codex/<name>.md)
References to `fable/...` are operator-local provenance; workers do not need them.
PROPOSED-ID MAP: "hic-NNN" in any bead text = tracker id rf2-hic-NNN. The dependency manifest is authoritative over prose Depends lines.
WORKER PROTOCOL (mandatory):
1. Run the worker worktree guard before edits: sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh; report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. Read first: the path-mapped documents this bead names.
3. Gates: foreground a gate that fits inside the harness ceiling; DETACH one that does not and poll BOTH its log and its `.exit` file in a bounded loop within the same turn â€” never end the turn waiting for a completion event. Never pipe a gate through `tail` or any filter; redirect to a log and echo the runner's own exit code on the same command line. Commit and open the PR before ending the turn. DOC-SURFACE GATE: for an edit confined to docs/design/hicasso/, `mkdocs build --strict` is NOT the gate â€” mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs keeps that tree out of the site. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates its markdown link targets and heading anchors, and `scripts/check_provenance_pins.py` validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/; nothing validates its tables, rendering or nav, so verify anchors and table column counts BY HAND and say so in the PR body.
4. Never `git stash`. Commit first, then rebase.
5. Never commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` or `.beads/metadata.json` from a worker branch â€” they are whole-database EXPORTS, not database files, and your branch carries the snapshot taken when its worktree was created, so committing one TIME-TRAVELS the tracker: beads closed since reopen, beads filed since vanish (PR #6677 did exactly this, 135 insertions / 136 deletions of pure collateral). Any other database-derived path likewise. The human-authored config â€” `.beads/README.md`, `.beads/config.yaml`, `.beads/.gitignore`, `.beads/hooks/**` â€” IS fair game. CLAUDE.md's Beads durability section is the authority.
6. Beads touching tools/xray/ update tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR (or state "spec unchanged because X").
7. Hot-zone files only if this bead flags them â€” and the hot zone INCLUDES the spec/*.md hot files (spec/004-Views.md, spec/002-Frames.md, spec/API.md, spec/Conventions.md among others), not just implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, implementation/deps.edn and .github/workflows/*. CLAUDE.md's Workflow section carries the canonical list; read it there rather than treating this line as complete.
8. No AI attribution in commits or PRs.
9. If you created a node_modules junction, remove it as your last act.
10. Checkpoint findings become real bd issues AND a row in docs/design/hicasso/product/correction-ledger.md. The checkpoint's own report PR writes the `open` row; a CORRECTIVE PR never edits that file â€” every later transition is the ledger keeper's. Read the file's own stated protocol before touching it.

title: surface-review(ssr): make the bounded Node renderer a first-class ssr-ring path
description:
## Scope

Make the bounded Node/React renderer a supported opt-in renderer for the non-streaming re-frame.ssr.ring request path. The outcome includes the smallest useful Ring render seam, the JVM side of the v1 crossing, an explicit post-drain render-state projection, a supported Node package/launcher entry point, and one canonical runnable native-Hicasso example with its tests and documentation. The existing JVM/Reagent renderer remains the default.

## Findings

- The three components are individually substantial and well tested, but they do not compose into a public product path. re-frame.ssr.ring owns request frames, event/resource drain, head, hydration payload, shell, response and teardown; implementation/ssr-node owns a bounded React render service; no caller joins them.
- build-full-response* resolves a JVM hiccup root and directly invokes ssr/render-to-string. That API shape cannot name a native JavaScript root which exists only in the application bundle.
- The Node request already has a stable entry, EDN root args, build identity, and allowlisted state, but its state shape is only top-level app-db key -> EDN value text. The JVM does not produce that projection, and route/machine/runtime facts needed by a real SPA have no inbound door.
- Render visibility and hydration egress are different policies. The server must be able to render from state that is intentionally absent from __rf_payload; deriving one projection from the other would either leak server-only state or silently render nil.
- The documented consumer API imports implementation/ssr-node/src/*.cjs directly. implementation/ssr-node has README.md, src/ and test/ but no package manifest/export or supported launch command of its own.
- Existing JVM and Node suites are broad but disjoint. The Node lane proves the service in isolation; there is no JVM -> Node -> JVM witness, runnable example, or generated recipe.

## Recommended Action

Add one explicit render-body boundary at the full-response body decision, selected when constructing the Ring handler. Its input should describe the post-drain request frame plus a stable render entry and serialized root arguments; it should not require a JVM hiccup value. Keep a tiny local adapter as the default so the current JVM/Reagent path and output remain unchanged.

Implement the concrete JVM-to-Node adapter for the existing bounded service. Let applications supply one render-state projector; define the serialization domain and carry the render-visible app-db and runtime/route/machine facts a native root needs. Revise the pre-alpha v1 request directly if necessary rather than adding compatibility layers. Keep the ownership line crisp: Node returns body markup only; the JVM continues to own boot-event drain, head, hydration payload, shell, status/headers/cookies/redirects, error projection, and frame teardown.

Give ssr-node a supported package entry point and runnable server command, then exercise the path in one small native-Hicasso reference app. Document that recipe at the public Ring/SSR surface and reflect any new public symbols or artifacts in the API and distribution manifests.

## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:533-557 pins the frame, resolves root-view to hiccup, and hard-calls ssr/render-to-string at line 548.
- git blame attributes that call to 185c149a537 on 2026-06-09. The Node service landed later in commits b2b35bf6e9 through aa413ab092 and subsequent fixes; history contains no crossing implementation.
- implementation/ssr-node/README.md:17-21 says there is no caller; lines 509-512 and 540-543 name build-full-response* as unwritten separate work.
- implementation/ssr-node/README.md:434-465 teaches imports from implementation/ssr-node/src/service.cjs and src/http.cjs. A top-level listing contains only README.md, src/ and test/.
- implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs:106-113 declares the v1 request fields; lines 226-280 require a per-entry stateAllowlist; lines 370-415 constrain state to top-level app-db keys and EDN-text values.
- docs/design/hicasso/production-server-arm.md:35-40 records the Node-sidecar ruling and the hard-wired host; lines 77-98 say the Node half alone landed and identify the state projector and end-to-end witness as the two undischarged crossing gates; lines 673-688 define the intended ownership arrows.
- implementation/package.json:63 and .github/workflows/test.yml:5079 gate ssr-node itself, but an executable-source search for ssr-node, createService, or x-rf-ssr across implementation/ssr, implementation/ssr-ring, examples/capabilities/ssr and tools/template returns no match.
- Deep tracker searches for ssr-ring, Node sidecar, render seam, state projector, and no caller found no open owner. The matching records are closed and describe either the decision, the Node half, isolated CI/absence checks, or documentation drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented Ring handler option selects either the existing local renderer (the unchanged default) or the concrete Node adapter through one narrow render-body contract; no renderer registry or protocol hierarchy is introduced.
- On the Node path, the JVM drains initial events and blocking resources first, then sends a stable entry id, EDN root args, expected build id, request identity/deadline, and an application-projected render snapshot from the live request frame.
- The render snapshot can faithfully seed both app-db and the route/machine/runtime facts used by the reference native view. Its serialization rules have a round-trip corpus and one clear negative fixture for an unsupported value.
- Render-state projection is independent of hydration payload projection. An end-to-end fixture renders from a server-only value while proving that value is absent from the JVM-written __rf_payload.
- A real JVM -> Node -> JVM test launches the supported Node entry point, renders a native application entry, and proves that Node body bytes are inserted into a complete JVM-owned Ring response with JVM-owned head and payload.
- The same crossing test covers one representative refusal or deadline, shows it reaches the existing Ring error/on-error semantics without a partial success page, and proves request-frame/isolate cleanup on success and failure.
- Application authors can import and start ssr-node through a declared package export/command without reaching into implementation/ssr-node/src.
- One runnable example and one canonical documentation recipe cover build, entry-table declaration, renderer selection, state projection, startup, hydration, and build-id skew. Spec 011, public API docs/API manifest, and package/release manifests agree with the shipped surface.
- Existing SSR, Ring, and Node test lanes stay green, and CI runs the new crossing witness.

## Non-goals

- Moving HTTP request, head, payload, shell, cookies, redirects, or response ownership into Node.
- Node streaming, React Server Components, islands, or a general RPC/renderer plugin framework.
- Multi-version protocol negotiation or compatibility scaffolding; this is a pre-alpha v1 contract and may be changed coherently.
- Replacing or changing the default JVM/Reagent renderer.
- Platform-specific supervisor, container, autoscaling, or deployment automation.

## Related beads

- rf2-2rtt6.88 - ruled the production server arm as the Node sidecar and defined the crossing gates.
- rf2-hic-056 - built the bounded Node/React service (the Node half).
- rf2-n8vp - added the dedicated Node test script and CI job.
- rf2-6ovv - hardened the service absence/coupling witness.
- rf2-a8c5 - corrected status documentation and explicitly recorded the still-missing JVM half.

And does a Reagent SSR example suffice for the first witness? Mayor recommends the split, (1) and (2) first in parallel. WHOEVER RULES STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT.

title: surface-review(resources): make active-route resource replanning a first-class causal command
description:
## Scope

Add one public event-vector command for rerunning the active route's Resources plan when an app-db-derived identity input (principal, tenant, permission set, locale, impersonation) changes without navigation. Cover the Resources↔Routing late-bound seam, exact route-owner reconciliation, durable plan/blocking/readiness state, conformance tests, Spec 012/016 and API/resource docs, and the RealWorld-on-resources receipt. Keep Resources optional and vector-first.

## Findings

Named `{:from-db ...}` subscriptions deliberately re-key when resolver inputs change, but remain passive. The newly selected scoped key is therefore `:idle` until some causal path ensures it. Navigation normally supplies that cause, but identical navigation is intentionally a no-op and there is no public command that reruns the current route's effective resource plan without changing the URL.

The flagship works around this gap with the 39-line `:auth/ensure-viewer-route` event. That app event reads leaf `rf/handler-meta`, invokes each entry itself, and dispatches independent ensures. It is not the route planner: it omits inherited parent resources, local `:after` ordering, identity collapse, atomic planning, exact plan ownership diff, blocking-slot replacement, and route readiness/error repair; it also calls `:when` with nil instead of the planner's reserved `{}` ctx. A cold restore on a composed route can therefore omit a parent-owned read, and a successful hand-ensure after the initial nil-scope planning failure leaves the durable route plan/readiness facts stale.

The runtime already computes the authoritative answer once: the route planner materializes contributor/local-id, canonical params, resolved scope, scoped key and byte key-id; collapses and orders the effective parent chain; diffs prior identities; and returns the exact identity/blocking maps Routing commits under the active nav-token. The missing piece is a public causal door back through that machinery.

## Recommended Action

Ship one public command, `[:rf.route/replan-resources {:cause <edn>}]`, implemented through the existing late-bound Resources↔Routing integration. It should read the current resolved route and nav-token, rerun the canonical effective parent-to-leaf resource planner against the current app-db, and atomically reconcile the standing plan under the same route activation:

- retain/adopt unchanged usable identities without a forced fetch;
- ensure added or changed identities with the existing route owner and caller cause;
- remove that owner only from identities the replanned route no longer requires;
- replace the durable `:resource-plan` and `:resource-blocking` slots and re-project route transition/error from the new plan;
- preserve route id/params/query/fragment/nav-token and do not run guards, `:on-match`, history or scroll effects.

Use the ordinary fail-closed planner boundary: no partial ensures on a failed plan, and document/test the exact prior-owner cleanup and route-error result. Reuse the existing `:rf.resource/route-plan` evidence with an explicit replan cause rather than inventing a parallel planner or helper-function API.

Replace RealWorld's app-side planner copy with this event. Make its personalized feed admission explicit in route data (for example, only when the following-feed query arm is active) so confirmed-anonymous home does not contradict the existing strict nil-scope planning rule. Teach the account/tenant-switch recipe as: resolve/clear the old scope causally, commit the new identity, then replan the active route.

## Evidence

- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:35-50,84-120` — a `{:from-db ...}` sub re-keys reactively and reads the new key as idle until a route/event ensures it; subscriptions never fetch.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs:189-261` — `:auth/ensure-viewer-route` reconstructs the leaf route's declaration and dispatches per-entry ensures by hand.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs:54-89` — the public home route mixes viewer/session identities and currently claims a nil session feed is simply omitted, while no `:when` admits that distinction.
- `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test.cljc:198-208` — the shipped contract proves a nil named route scope is a whole-plan `:rf.error/resource-route-plan`, not a silent omission.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:700-867,1023-1260` — the canonical planner already materializes exact identities, composes/collapses the branch, applies plan diff, and returns identity/blocking maps.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:247-306` — Routing commits those maps beside `:current` under the active nav-token; the app workaround never updates them or readiness.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:1026-1139` — restore tests assert newly created entries but do not assert repaired route error/readiness, stored plan membership, or an inherited parent read.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:1386` — the spec explicitly reserves force reload as a separate named contract instead of overloading fragment/identical navigation.
- `implementation/resources/deps.edn` and `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:406-545,641-643` — Resources is optional and its event family/route behavior already installs through late binding, so the command belongs on that seam without a static Routing dependency.
- Commit `d8a0f670704abc008eb151067f13a1e7cc976c48` removed named read helpers because vectors are the semantic API identity; this command should likewise remain an event vector. `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1237-1271` has no need for a new facade function.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented public event replans the active route in the dispatching frame from its current registered effective parent chain and current app-db, while leaving URL, route address, fragment and nav-token byte-for-byte unchanged and firing no guard, `:on-match`, history or scroll work.
- Replan uses the same `:when`/ctx, params and scope resolution, schema/canonical identity, contributor attribution, `:after`, branch ordering, identity collapse, blocking and keep-previous semantics as ordinary route entry; there is one planner, not an app-visible approximation.
- A same-route scope change A→B is covered: unchanged identities are retained without a forced request, B identities are ensured and owned, A-only identities lose the route owner, and the durable plan/blocking maps equal the newly materialized plan.
- An initial unresolved-scope plan error followed by app-db resolution + replan is covered: no navigation occurs, route error/readiness is repaired, exact plan membership is stored, and required loads start. The inverse/failing replan proves no partial ensure and the documented prior-owner cleanup/error result.
- Parent-chain coverage proves a leaf replan restores an inherited parent resource; a regression that reads only leaf `handler-meta` must fail. Coverage also pins a conditional occurrence entering/leaving the plan.
- RealWorld deletes `:auth/ensure-viewer-route`'s planner reconstruction in favor of the public command and tests successful restore, failed restore/confirmed anonymous, and a composed-route deep link including route readiness and plan membership, not only cache-entry existence.
- Spec 012/016, the Resources API/reference/concepts or how-to docs, examples and test prose agree on the command, passive-sub boundary, nil-scope behavior and trace cause. API-manifest drift remains green; no named facade helper is added.
- Proportionate Resources/Routing/RealWorld test gates pass, with a negative control that fails when effective-parent composition or durable readiness/plan replacement is removed.

## Non-goals

- No subscription-driven fetch, committed-read demand, app-db watcher, or automatic replan on every resolver input write.
- No general route reload that reruns guards, `:on-match`, history, scroll, or arbitrary route metadata.
- No named helper-function sugar, compatibility alias/window, second query grammar, or duplicate planner.
- No silent global fallback and no global change making nil route scopes silently optional; conditional resources remain explicitly admitted.
- No refactor of ordinary explicit `:rf.resource/ensure`/`refetch` for non-route owners.

## Related beads

- `rf2-hic-050` — STOP verdict for committed-read resource demand; this proposal preserves that ruling by adding an explicit causal event.
- `rf2-hic-054` — blessed event/sub async-resource recipes; the proposed command removes a route-planner reconstruction those public primitives cannot faithfully express.
- `rf2-hic-044` — current-primitives resource-demand witness; no demand/runtime ownership model is reopened here.

A full title/description/notes scan of all existing beads found no active or closed task for current-route resource replanning, force reload, principal-switch replan, or `:auth/ensure-viewer-route`.

title: surface-review(xray): make Pair the single agent runtime and retire the duplicate Xray seam
description:
## Scope

Make the human/agent boundary around Xray explicit and singular for pre-alpha users:

- Xray's preload and public API own the in-app human panel.
- `re-frame2-pair.runtime` plus `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/` own out-of-process programmer/AI inspection and mutation.
- Retire the unused `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` agent contract, its sentinel, tests, manifest rows, and documentation.
- Preserve the small fail-closed egress projection that Xray itself needs when copying app-db snapshots and diff values, but keep it internal to the panel.

Review and update the affected Xray source, specs, docs, tests, testbeds/build wiring, and repository API manifests. The desired outcome is one honest setup story, not a new capability.

## Findings

1. Xray documents an agent integration that does not exist. `tools/xray/README.md` and `tools/xray/spec/API.md` say Pair MCP evaluates `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` and that Xray's preload installs the agent sentinel with no second preload. Pair MCP instead hard-codes `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, probes `js/globalThis.__re_frame2_pair_runtime` before runtime-backed tools, and contains zero references to the Xray runtime namespace or sentinel.
2. The two seams are not interchangeable. The canonical Pair preload supplies the current coarse-grained workflow (`orient`, `snapshot`, event-bundle/cascade reads, dispatch consequence/dry-run, recording/watch, DOM/UI reads, restore/replace). Xray's older runtime still exposes a parallel catalogue of trace/epoch/app-db/registrar/resource/subscription/mutation calls and explicitly leaves event-bundle reads to a follow-on.
3. The duplication is substantial and already drifting: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs` is about 91 KB / 1,700 lines and its dedicated CLJS test is about 115 KB / 1,884 lines. The Pair preload is about 230 KB / 4,000 lines and has continued evolving after Xray runtime's last direct change on 2026-07-11.
4. Xray itself does not need that public agent catalogue. Within `tools/xray/src`, the only functional callers of the runtime namespace outside the preload are three calls to `runtime/egress-value` in the palette snapshot and app-db diff copy paths. The preload requires the whole namespace solely to install the second sentinel.
5. The contract contradicts Xray's own product boundary. `spec/Principles.md` says Xray is the human surface and AI belongs in the separate Pair MCP; `018-Event-Spine.md` says the agent reads raw instrumentation rather than a Xray-curated facade. Xray already has a large panel/tab information architecture, and its restraint principle explicitly argues for subtraction rather than another surface.
6. Four Xray runtime exports are nevertheless published as post-v1 tooling rows in `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` / generated `spec/api-manifest.edn`, turning an unused pre-alpha seam into prospective compatibility cost.
7. Testbed wiring proves the real setup: `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` explicitly loads `re-frame2-pair.runtime` alongside Xray in builds that Pair MCP drives, while Xray-only and Pair-only builds load their respective preloads independently.

## Recommended Action

Take a clean pre-alpha cut:

1. Remove `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` as a public/tooling namespace, including `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime`, its preload require, external accessor catalogue, mutation helpers, streaming state, dedicated runtime test bulk, and API-manifest rows.
2. Move or re-express only the panel-local `egress-value` behavior needed by palette snapshot and app-db diff copying in a small internal Xray namespace, preferably as a thin call to the canonical framework projection. Keep its current frame-owned, fail-closed sensitive/large-value behavior and focused tests.
3. Rewrite Xray's README and specs around one accurate boundary: load `day8.re-frame2-xray.preload` for the panel; load `re-frame2-pair.runtime` and use Pair MCP for programmer/AI access. A build may opt into either or both explicitly; neither preload silently stands in for the other.
4. Remove the obsolete stable-accessor/sentinel contract and future-consumer promises from Xray's API/spec material. Link to Pair's setup and tool contract rather than duplicating it.
5. Reconcile Xray testbeds/builds and generated manifests with that boundary. Keep Pair preload entries only where the build is actually Pair-driven and Xray preload entries only where the panel is exercised.

## Evidence

- False consumer/setup claims: `tools/xray/README.md:29-32,231-235`; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:56-58`; `tools/xray/spec/API.md:256,668-697,676-953`.
- Pair's actual boundary: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_form.cljs:64`; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs:14-15`; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md:28-39,429-452`; `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs`.
- Exact searches under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` and `skills/re-frame2-pair` find no `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` or `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime` references.
- Xray-local callers: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/palette/events.cljs:181`; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_events.cljs:68-69`.
- Duplicate implementation/test: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs`; `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime_cljs_test.cljs`. The Xray trace accessor itself says event-bundle reads are deferred at `runtime.cljs:544-557`.
- Product boundary: `tools/xray/spec/Principles.md:59-79,148-157,172-178`; `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:24-29`.
- Published surface: `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:183-186` and corresponding generated rows.
- Real preload topology: `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1216,1320-1423,1460,1500-1531,1822-2120`.
- History: Xray runtime's last direct commit is `d22417a0b7` (2026-07-11); Pair runtime has subsequent direct commits through `2b0b482eb3` (2026-08-06).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Tracked product source, specs, docs, test config, and manifests contain no `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` namespace, `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime` sentinel, or claim that Pair MCP consumes/arrives through Xray. No compatibility alias, tombstone namespace, or dual-probe path remains.
2. `runtime.cljs` and its agent-contract test suite are removed. Any surviving privacy tests are focused on the two panel-local copy/export behaviors rather than re-specifying Pair's tool protocol.
3. Palette app-db snapshot and app-db diff copy still project under the observed frame and default-redact sensitive/large values. A focused CLJS test proves both a normal value and a seeded sensitive value at the actual copy boundary.
4. Xray's README/API gives copy-pasteable, separate setup for the panel and for Pair MCP. It states that loading both requires both explicit preloads and links to Pair's canonical tool documentation instead of reproducing an accessor table.
5. API manifest metadata is regenerated with zero Xray runtime rows; the manifest consistency gate passes.
6. Testbed/build preload lists match intent: Xray-only panel fixtures run without Pair, Pair-driven fixtures carry `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, and combined fixtures declare both. No Xray code depends on the skill-owned Pair namespace.
7. Xray's focused JVM/CLJS tests and browser smoke for shell startup plus the two copy paths pass. Pair MCP's conformance/runtime structural suite remains green, demonstrating that the one surviving agent path was not disturbed.
8. The implementation PR reports the source/test line reduction and names any residual public Xray namespace that remains for tool access; expected answer is none.

## Non-goals

- No new panel, dashboard, AI rail, workflow wizard, event-dossier variant, or information-architecture redesign.
- No redesign or expansion of Pair MCP, its protocol, privacy flags, write gates, or preload.
- No merged Xray/Pair mega-preload and no automatic loading of Pair from Xray.
- No deprecation period, compatibility wrapper, alias namespace, sentinel fallback, or migration framework; this is pre-alpha.
- No general rewrite of the framework egress/classification machinery.
- No broad audit of `day8.re-frame2-xray.core` facade exports.

## Related beads

- `rf2-hic-059` (closed) proves the current Pair MCP + `re-frame2-pair.runtime` path through a real emitted-eval/result flow; reuse that canonical boundary rather than creating another.
- `rf2-2hpxo` (deferred) is the broader external-alpha classification of `day8.re-frame2-xray.core` and other facades. It does not own this concrete duplicate tooling seam.
- All-status title, description, and notes searches for Xray runtime, Xray-MCP, Pair runtime, agent runtime, preload, sentinel, duplicate/retire/consolidate terms, and `surface-review(xray)` found no existing owner for this outcome.
