title: surface-review(conformance-security): stop security-tier edits from arming production and browser gates
description:
## Scope

Correct PR changed-surface routing for the four source-less, cross-artefact test partitions under implementation/security, implementation/reply-conformance, implementation/derivation-conformance, and implementation/event-conformance. The implementation change should be confined to the classifier and its executable policy tests/comments unless a directly coupled testing-policy sentence must move with them.

## Findings

- All four partitions are test-only: each deps.edn has :paths [] and :deps {}, none has a src/ tree, and none publishes production code. Their responsibilities are substantial and distinct: reply vocabulary/egress across managed-async families; derivation algebra across five graph contributors; the event facade/runtime/isolation boundary; and adversarial security properties over schema, SSR, reply, profile, error-slot, and MCP egress.
- The suites deliberately complement artefact-local tests rather than replace them. Derivation composes family projections; event tests adversarial public seams after core-owned duplicates were removed; reply tests own cross-family vocabulary while family tests own lowering; security adds generated/sentinel/fail-closed coverage beyond fixed local pins. A broad semantic dedupe would trade away confidence for little benefit.
- CLJS already has the right shape: every namespace matches the consolidated :node-test build's cljs-test$ selector, and the focused test:security build is only a local-iteration subset. JVM CI likewise keeps four required clojure -M:test jobs. Current successful run 33307155376 reports security 92 tests/698 assertions, derivation 22/522, event 49/209, and reply 27/533.
- The changed-surface classifier treats the three *-conformance trees as source-less and sets only implementation_jvm=true plus cljs_node_test=true. The same probe on an actual security test currently also sets cljs_browser=true, examples_compile=true, cljs_prod=true, and bundle_isolation=true.
- Those four extra gates cannot observe a security-tier-only edit: :browser-test selects only *-dom-cljs-test namespaces; production and bundle-isolation builds do not require the test tree; and the all-examples compiler has no edge to it. implementation/security/deps.edn is also test-only.
- This is drift from recorded intent, not a new coverage trade. Commit 5bb3cd9cd1 says adding implementation/security/* was needed specifically to fire implementation_jvm and cljs_node_test, but placed it in a generic feature-artefact arm that sets five outputs. The later src-less conformance arm at report-changed-surfaces.sh:1202-1220 explicitly says security is the precedent for omitting browser/prod/bundle gates, while the earlier executable arm contradicts it.
- The examples-compile policy test reinforces the mistake with implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc, a path that does not exist in this intentionally src-less partition, and asserts that this imaginary file can change an example closure.
- The toll is material. Security-only commit d1fa5ff493 changed deps/test commentary and its tests workflow run 29096118890 executed the relevant JVM/Node suites plus the all-examples job (10m24s), browser, two production browser builds, and bundle isolation. The all-examples job was the critical path; current direct classifier output still arms the same unrelated surfaces.
- Search across all tracker statuses and title/description/notes for conformance, security classifier/surface/tier, src-less, examples_compile, bundle_isolation, cljs_browser, and over-classification found no issue owning this exact mismatch.

## Recommended Action

Move implementation/security/* out of both the shipped-feature classifier arm and the examples_compile input arm, and classify it alongside reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, and event-conformance as a source-less cross-artefact tier: implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true only.

Update the classifier's executable mirror using real tracked security paths. Preserve the jvm-security required job, the local JVM roster entry, the consolidated Node inclusion, and the focused test:security command. Keep production artefact routing unchanged, so changes to core/schemas/machines/routing/flows/SSR still run their existing production/browser/bundle gates and continue to trigger the broad JVM and Node suites.

## Evidence

- implementation/security/deps.edn and the three *-conformance/deps.edn files: empty production paths/deps, test-only aliases.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:208-287 and 650-655: all four test roots feed the shared cljs-test$ Node build; security's focused selector is at 769-790.
- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:574 includes security in examples compilation; 973-997 includes it in the full feature fan-out; 1202-1220 gives the three sibling tiers the intended narrow routing and states that security has the same posture.
- implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:1983-2011 asserts examples compilation from the nonexistent implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc; 3283-3311 already pins the narrow sibling-tier contract.
- .github/workflows/test.yml:2149-2198 and 2482-2610: required JVM jobs; 6026 and 6040-6042: aggregator membership.
- scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh:46-90: all four JVM lanes remain in the rigorous local roster.
- Commit 5bb3cd9cd1 and workflow runs 29096118890 / 33307155376 provide the intent, observed toll, and current suite tallies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Classifying both implementation/security/deps.edn and at least one real tracked implementation/security/test/** file sets implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true, while examples_compile, cljs_browser, cljs_prod, and bundle_isolation are false.
2. Representative real files under reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, and event-conformance retain the same two-output routing.
3. The classifier policy test removes the imaginary implementation/security/src/** positive fixture, uses tracked paths for the security tier, and explicitly locks the four negative outputs so the broad arm cannot silently return.
4. jvm-security remains conditional on implementation_jvm, remains in all-required-passed, and still runs clojure -M:test from implementation/security. The local JVM roster entry, shadow :node-test root, and npm test:security focused command remain intact.
5. Production/source-bearing artefact probes retain their existing browser, production, examples, and bundle-isolation routing; this change narrows only the source-less security partition.
6. Classifier comments and TESTING.md, if touched, agree that all four source-less tiers use JVM + consolidated Node coverage and do not claim production-bundle reachability.
7. The changed-surface policy suite and gate-scheduling checks pass, with a direct classifier transcript for all four partitions included in the handoff.

## Non-goals

- Do not delete, merge, thin, or relocate semantic conformance/security tests.
- Do not combine the four JVM jobs or deps.edn files, redesign the broad implementation_jvm output, or add a new classifier output.
- Do not change security, reply, event, derivation, egress, redaction, or fail-open/fail-closed runtime behavior.
- Do not remove the focused test:security command merely because its namespaces also ride test:cljs.
- Do not narrow production artefact changes; only edits inside the source-less implementation/security partition are in scope.

## Related beads

- Historical provenance cited by the repository: rf2-oni7gz/rf2-gj2ae established JVM security coverage; rf2-dxndhc established narrow routing for the three sibling source-less tiers; rf2-gzavkm established that examples_compile should follow actual compiled-closure inputs. These historical ids are not duplicate live owners in the current tracker.

title: surface-review(epoch): make strict replay a one-call epoch-id gesture
description:
## Scope

Close the gap between the epoch runtime's recorded replay material and the public/Tool-Pair replay gesture. Cover the smallest coherent slice across `implementation/epoch/**`, the optional core facade/late-bind hook, Pair-MCP runtime/tool wiring, Tool-Pair/API/spec prose, descriptor manifest, and focused CLJ/CLJS/tool tests.

## Findings

- Every ordinary `:rf/epoch-record` already captures the complete ingredients for a faithful strict replay: `:trigger-event`, the post-generation `:rf.cofx` token (including mid-run minted facts), and the envelope's serializable `:fx-overrides` / `:interceptor-overrides`.
- The normative Tool-Pair replay contract requires replay to re-supply all of those fields and hard-wire `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :strict`; missing facts and `:rf/fn-override` must fail loud.
- No epoch public API or late-bind hook performs that gesture from an epoch id. `re-frame.epoch` exposes history, restore, replace, listeners, config, and egress projection; Pair-MCP exposes `restore-epoch`, while its `dispatch {replay true}` merely sets strict mode and requires the caller to copy the event/cofx/override fields manually.
- That manual route is not generally available to an off-box agent: `projected-record` deliberately replaces every `:trigger-event` argument with `:rf/redacted` by default, and `:include-sensitive?` is orthogonal to `:include-event-args?`. Pair-MCP's epoch egress threads only the app-db `include-sensitive` axis, so `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` cannot return the raw arguments needed to replay a normal argument-bearing event. The remaining escape is raw `eval-cljs` over `rf/epoch-history`, which bypasses the structured privacy and tool envelope.
- Existing replay tests prove the ingredients by hand-extracting a record and calling `rf/dispatch-sync`; none proves that a programmer or tool can name one retained epoch and replay it in one supported call.

## Recommended Action

Provide one dev-only replay-by-epoch-id operation, preferably `replay-epoch!`, owned by the epoch artefact. It should resolve the retained raw record in-process, build the strict dispatch opts from the record in one place, and dispatch the recorded event without exporting its arguments/coeffects/overrides. Make source-frame and target-frame semantics explicit (same frame by default; an optional explicit target only if needed), and make clear that replay runs against the target frame's current state/code unless the caller separately restores a starting epoch.

Expose the operation through the normal optional-artefact facade and as a dedicated Pair-MCP `replay-epoch` tool (or an equally direct epoch-id mode on the existing dispatch tool). Return a structured consequence/failure envelope. Fail before dispatch for an unknown/aged-out id, a non-replayable record (synthetic/halted/missing trigger or replay token), or any recorded `:rf/fn-override`; preserve the existing strict missing-cofx failure rather than minting. Use the existing dispatch authority/annotation posture—do not invent another permission system.

## Evidence

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc` builds `:trigger-event`, post-generation `:rf.cofx`, `:fx-overrides`, and `:interceptor-overrides` into each record specifically for Tool-Pair replay.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc` publishes no replay hook or public replay function; its Tool-Pair mutations are restore and replace only.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` independently redacts trigger-event args; `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc` pins that `:include-sensitive? true` still leaves them redacted unless the separate `:include-event-args?` opt is supplied.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs` threads only `:include-sensitive?` into projected epoch pages and explicitly leaves the orthogonal event-args axis closed.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs` accepts caller-supplied event/cofx/overrides plus `replay true`; it performs no epoch-id lookup. `registry.cljs` and generated `tool-descriptors.edn` contain restore but no replay-by-id tool.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` Replay and `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` Strict replay instruct callers to read and copy the four recorded fields manually.
- `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj`, `epoch_override_capture_test.clj`, `machine_minted_cofx_replay_token_test.clj`, and `join_strict_mint_epoch_replay_test.clj` all demonstrate replay through manual record extraction/re-dispatch.
- `implementation/epoch/deps.edn` confirms epoch is an optional, dev-elided artefact with an existing real production-gate lane; the new seam belongs under that same boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From only a retained epoch id plus explicit frame targeting, a public dev API can replay an ordinary argument-bearing event using the raw in-process `:trigger-event`, recorded `:rf.cofx`, and both recorded override maps under hard-wired `:strict` mint policy.
2. An end-to-end test records a generator-backed/mid-run coeffect and serializable fx/interceptor overrides, then replays by id and proves the generator/host is not consulted and the recorded effective chain is used. Include an event argument that the off-box projected history exposes only as `:rf/redacted`.
3. Pair-MCP offers the same one-call epoch-id gesture without requiring raw event, cofx, or override payloads on the wire; the descriptor, generated manifest, catalogue, and skill routing all agree.
4. Unknown/aged-out ids, halted/synthetic/incomplete records, and `:rf/fn-override` records return stable structured failures and do not dispatch. Missing declared recordable facts remain the canonical strict `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx`; no live mint fallback is introduced.
5. Docs state the state semantics plainly: replay does not implicitly restore, external effects may fire again, the target's current code/frame config applies, and the replayed dispatch records a new ordinary epoch.
6. Existing `projected-record` privacy defaults remain unchanged; no raw event-argument egress knob is added to make replay work.
7. Focused JVM/CLJS epoch tests, Pair-MCP tool tests, descriptor-manifest drift checks, and the existing epoch production-elision lane pass with non-vacuous assertions.

## Non-goals

- A branching timeline, redo stack, or general event-log framework.
- Automatic restore-before-replay or a promise that replay matches the historical `:db-after` when starting state/code differs.
- Replaying opaque fn-valued overrides, virtualising/undoing external effects, or weakening off-box redaction.
- Compatibility aliases, a generic command abstraction, or a second permission/gating system.

## Related beads

No open duplicate was found after title and full-description searches for replay-by-epoch-id, strict replay, trigger-event replay, and `include-event-args`. Historical implementation lineage visible in source/commit history: rf2-1xdotm (post-generation cofx capture), rf2-yigokd (override capture), rf2-v52xsr (strict replay flag), rf2-m7x0qb (Pair-MCP override re-supply), rf2-s3qjlw (epoch/restore strict-replay composition proof), and rf2-nm611o (fail-closed trigger-event args).

title: surface-review(template): collapse the generator to one small runnable SPA contract
description:
## Scope

Reduce `tools/template/**` to one deliberate product contract: scaffold a small client-side counter SPA that a programmer or agent can read, run, test, and replace. Keep the Reagent default and the UIx substrate selector because that choice changes authored source and adapter wiring. Remove feature/style modes and the generated policy/toolchain bundle. Update the generated resources, hook API, tests, and normative spec together; touch directly coupled template release-gate assertions only where the smaller contract requires it.

## Findings

1. The default Reagent scaffold is not minimal. Before compiled output or `node_modules`, it emits 20 files, 75,816 bytes, and 1,579 lines. The generated README alone is 677 lines; `events.cljs` is 232 lines for two tiny handlers; `deps.edn` is 76 lines. The actual counter cycle is a handful of forms.
2. The default installs decisions the app has not made: schemas, a git-pinned Xray tool plus `@xyflow/react` and `elkjs`, a trace error sink, a whole-app-db schema, a long commented HTTP handler, CSP and production-hosting policy, GitHub Actions, Lefthook, cljfmt, clj-kondo, `dev/user.clj`, and a REPL scratch namespace. These are useful recipes, not requirements for the first SPA.
3. The generator exposes three feature/style flags (`:include-story?`, `:include-ssr?`, `:css`) on top of the substrate axis, yielding eight accepted output cells and mutual-exclusion/capability machinery. `hooks.clj` is 774 lines; the template tests are 5,608 lines; the spec is 3,295 lines. Much of the suite pins explanatory prose, badges, CSP snippets, Xray layout details, and variant combinations instead of the first-run contract.
4. The shared README teaches Story even when Story was not requested. The generated source teaches HTTP, privacy/egress, production schema elision, Xray, and deployment hardening before the reader has replaced the counter. This makes both humans and agents distinguish essential code from a framework handbook on their first edit.
5. The public descriptions have already drifted under the matrix: `template.edn` advertises Story but omits the live SSR and Tailwind modes; Principles P3 says React and ReactDOM are the only npm dependencies while the default Reagent path injects Xray's two additional npm packages. The canonical Clojure name `acme/my-app` is copied verbatim into `package.json`; npm 11's bundled `validate-npm-package-name` rejects that unscoped slash form.
6. History shows accretion, not an intentional current baseline. The initial scaffold at `2313a8d85a` emitted 10 files / 8,966 bytes / 272 lines. Subsequent commits separately added the dev bundle (`d9830dc2fc`), cljfmt (`3cdc6f3b26`), Lefthook (`bfe4aa3ee8`), Xray's predecessor (`efbdd60a94`), CSP/production hardening (`f61b816163`), best-practice demos (`f6f770bfc0`), and CI (`b04c304614`). Correct later fixes hardened that accumulated shape, but no product pass re-asked what belongs in a starter.
7. Public distribution is a separate known blocker: `.github/workflows/template-release.yml` states that it rewrites emitted framework coordinates to local roots and that the advertised public template coordinate is not yet usable. Existing publication beads own that. Adding another invocation mode or a `:minimal?` flag would compound both problems.

## Recommended Action

- Make the template emit one SPA shape per supported view substrate. `:name` remains required; `:substrate :reagent|:uix` is the only template-specific option, with Reagent as the obvious default.
- Delete `:include-story?`, `:include-ssr?`, and `:css` from the hook API, resources, errors, docs, and matrix tests. Story, SSR, and Tailwind remain learnable through their focused examples/guides; do not replace the flags with a wizard, profiles, or separate compatibility modes in this task.
- Emit only the files needed to run, test, release, and understand the counter: `.gitignore`, a short README, `deps.edn`, `package.json`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, the HTML/CSS shell, `core.cljs`, `events.cljs`, `subs.cljs`, `views.cljs`, and one focused event-flow test. Remove generated CI, hook-manager/editor/formatter/linter configs, REPL scratch scaffolding, and schema source.
- Keep direct dependencies to the runnable counter: Clojure/ClojureScript, re-frame2 core, the selected adapter and view library, shadow-cljs, React, and ReactDOM. Do not preload Xray or pull schemas/tool coordinates into every Reagent app.
- Keep comments local and brief. Preserve the measured-correct `^:dev/after-load` lifecycle, but move HTTP, schema, privacy, CSP, production-host, Xray, Story, SSR, migration, and tooling tutorials to existing public docs and link to them from a compact next-steps section.
- Derive an npm-valid package name from the Clojure project coordinate instead of copying `acme/my-app` verbatim.
- Replace prose- and combination-heavy tests with a small black-box contract: exact emit manifest, parseable/valid manifests, compile/test/release, real browser boot and 0→1 counter interaction for both substrates, and absence of retired files/dependencies/options. Keep history in git rather than carrying completed migration/validation reports as live normative surface.

## Evidence

- `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:37-66` enumerates the 20-file default; lines 364-712 assert the generated handbook, CI, Xray host, CSP, privacy, schema, and HTTP prose.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md` is 677 lines and includes Hot reload, Story, Production hardening, REPL, schemas, privacy/egress, HTTP, migration, and future skill-install sections.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/events.cljs` is 232 lines; the counter handlers occupy only the small initialisation/increment blocks, while the rest is an error sink and commented HTTP exemplar.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps.edn` adds schemas, Xray, cljfmt, clj-kondo, and tools.namespace around the base app; `_shared/package.json` injects Xray npm packages and uses `{{name}}` as the npm name.
- `tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:179-291,321-643,655-741` owns the flag gate, coercions, capability-conditioned substitution prose, and file-selection matrix.
- `tools/template/spec/000-Vision.md`, `API.md`, `001-Substrate-Variants.md`, and `002-Generated-Shape.md` claim a minimal counter while specifying the larger matrix and tooling bundle.
- `.github/workflows/template-release.yml:114-129,257-273` explicitly says the release smoke masks unresolved consumer coordinates; this task must not invent a second distribution route around that separate owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The documented template API has exactly one template-specific selector: optional `:substrate` with Reagent default and UIx alternative. The removed Story, SSR, and CSS keys fail as unknown; there are no aliases, deprecation warnings, reserved gates, or compatibility shims for them.
2. Reagent and UIx emit the same small project manifest apart from `core.cljs`, `views.cljs`, and required dependency differences. The emitted tree contains the run/test/release essentials named above and does not contain `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `lefthook.yml`, `.cljfmt.edn`, `.clj-kondo/`, `.editorconfig`, `dev/`, `schema.cljs`, Story files, SSR files, or Tailwind overlays.
3. The default direct dependency graph contains no Xray, Story, SSR, schemas, machines, cljfmt, clj-kondo, or tools.namespace coordinate and no Xray-only npm package. `package.json` has an npm-valid name derived deterministically from both qualified and bare Clojure project names.
4. Each substrate's generated app parses, compiles, runs its focused test, builds an advanced release, opens its real generated page, paints the counter, and moves 0→1 on click. The correct one-time init plus `^:dev/after-load` re-render lifecycle from `rf2-r0kk7` remains covered.
5. Generated source contains the counter dataflow and the lifecycle facts needed to edit it, without embedded HTTP/schema/privacy/security/tooling tutorials. The generated README gives the run, test, release, and guide/docs links without conditional sections for modes that were not emitted.
6. Template tests assert the behavioral and manifest contract, including red witnesses for a retired flag, an advanced dependency/file reappearing, an invalid npm name, and a broken browser boot. They do not pin badges, prose paragraphs, server-specific CSP snippets, or removed variant cells.
7. Normative template docs and metadata describe the same reduced surface. Completed migration/validation records are removed from the live contract or clearly historical; no document advertises a mode the generator no longer accepts.

## Non-goals

- No new wizard, `:minimal?` switch, profile system, second template, prompt sequence, or replacement feature flag.
- No compatibility layer for pre-alpha Story/SSR/Tailwind invocations; git history is the migration record.
- No runtime, adapter, Xray, Story, SSR, Tailwind, schema, HTTP, or security-policy redesign.
- No Hicasso substrate addition.
- No operator-owned repository split, coordinate rename, Clojars verification, tag, or publication work. The reduced scaffold must compose with that work when it lands, not duplicate it.
- Do not delete the focused examples or guides that become the on-ramp for advanced capabilities.

## Related beads

- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed): established the correct generated hot-reload lifecycle; preserve its behavior while shrinking the prose.
- `rf2-48rk3` (closed): made feature capability selection fail closed; most of that machinery becomes unnecessary when feature modes are retired, while the substrate registry can remain small.
- `rf2-8urba` (deferred): proposed a future Hicasso template variant; distinct and explicitly outside this minimal-contract change.
- `rf2-uelji` (deferred) and `rf2-fo4ng` (deferred): own verified-group/public-coordinate work; this task does not bypass or duplicate them.
- `rf2-k5r9t` (open): adapter-owned client-root work may later shorten generated Reagent boot code, but is not a prerequisite for removing template ceremony.

title: surface-review(mcp-base): return the pair-only epoch diff codec to Pair-MCP
description:
## Scope

Restore tools/mcp-base to its documented role as the small library of primitives shared by the shipped MCP servers. Move the epoch :db-after diff codec and its section-grouping helper, specs, tests, Closure define, and conformance ownership from re-frame.mcp-base into tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp. Preserve Pair-MCP's tool names, arguments, result shapes, :rf.mcp/diff-from wire representation, defaults, ordering, and errors.

## Findings

- The base contract says it contains genuinely cross-cutting primitives consumed by every MCP server and explicitly says a primitive stays consumer-side until a second consumer needs it.
- Current production imports contradict that boundary: Pair-MCP alone requires re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode; Story-MCP has no source reference. section-grouping is referenced only by diff-encode.
- These namespaces are substantial: 1,324 of 4,633 physical base source lines (28.6%), plus 1,276 focused test lines, two spec pages, Malli-specific validation/test setup, and Pair/global Closure-define wiring.
- The conformance suite's use of the builder is test evidence for Pair's wire shape, not an independent runtime consumer.
- History confirms this was never a stable cross-server seam: c4abf7f799 moved Pair's diff block into the new base, while neither Story-MCP nor the former Causa-MCP ever imported the namespace; the later section-grouping surface likewise serves only Pair epoch responses.
- Keeping a single-consumer codec in the common jar enlarges the API downstream MCP authors must understand, makes Pair's epoch representation look like a cross-MCP obligation, and violates the package's own admission rule.

## Recommended Action

Rehome the two pure .cljc namespaces under Pair-MCP with Pair-owned names, carrying their JVM/CLJS tests and specs with them. Retarget Pair production calls, its Closure define, and the wire-vocabulary conformance witness to that implementation. Remove the namespaces, Malli-only diff setup, focused tests, and index rows from mcp-base. Keep the existing :rf.mcp/diff-from vocabulary and observable wire shape stable; vocabulary constants intentionally reserved across MCP tools may remain shared.

Do not introduce a generic codec protocol, registry abstraction, forwarding namespace, or compatibility alias. The implementation remains useful; its truthful owner is the only server that emits it.

## Evidence

- tools/mcp-base/spec/README.md:4 calls the library genuinely cross-cutting primitives consumed by every MCP server; lines 107-111 require a second consumer before lifting.
- Only tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/snapshot_pipeline.cljs and wire_pipeline.cljs call base-diff functions; no Story-MCP production source imports diff-encode.
- tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode.cljc is 911 lines and section_grouping.cljc is 413; their focused JVM tests total 1,276 lines.
- tools/mcp-base/spec/diff-encode.md defines epoch :db-after encoding; section-grouping.md identifies diff-encode as its consumer.
- tools/mcp-base/deps.edn carries Malli for the diff validation suite; Pair/global Shadow configs carry the re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode/validate-patches? production define.
- tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab invokes the builder only to validate Pair's marker schema.
- History: c4abf7f799 introduced mcp-base and moved Pair's implementation; git log -S searches show no Story-MCP or Causa-MCP consumer. Commit 6191a6b316 later removed Causa-MCP.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. day8/re-frame2-mcp-base no longer publishes or documents diff-encode or section-grouping; its source/spec index and test/dependency configuration contain only genuinely shared surfaces.
2. Pair-MCP owns equivalent .cljc encode/decode and section-grouping namespaces. Its production pipeline, default epochs-mode, :rf.mcp/diff-from body, section ordering/classification, error ids, and full-mode pass-through remain unchanged.
3. The complete relocated corpus runs on JVM and CLJS, including map/vector/set round trips, malformed-marker failures, Malli-present validation, Malli-absent or Closure-disabled production behavior, and section losslessness/order.
4. The wire-vocabulary conformance gate exercises the Pair-owned canonical emitter and existing fixtures/schemas without changing the marker's observable wire shape.
5. Pair's local and root Shadow builds use the new Closure-define symbol; no tracked production, test, spec, generated-manifest, or conformance file requires the removed base namespaces.
6. mcp-base JVM/CLJS gates and Pair focused/descriptor/conformance gates pass non-vacuously; a package-content check proves the base jar excludes the pair-only namespaces.
7. No forwarding namespace or deprecated alias preserves the old internal API; current pre-alpha consumers migrate in the same change.

## Non-goals

- Removing diff encoding from Pair-MCP, changing its default, or redesigning the patch/section grammar.
- Renaming :rf.mcp/diff-from, changing epoch records, or changing any tool schema/result.
- Moving genuinely shared args, cursor, cap, dedup, egress, envelope, privacy, vocabulary, or descriptor-manifest primitives out of mcp-base.
- Unifying handler arities, registries, transports, or result-envelope representations.
- Adding a general plugin/codec framework, external runtime dependency, or automated two-consumers policy engine.
- Solving the separate Clojars group-verification/publish blocker.

## Related beads

- rf2-ahjbc is an adjacent open Pair-MCP simplification touching parts of the same tool surface; coordinate file ownership if both are implemented concurrently, but neither blocks the other.
- rf2-uelji is the deferred Clojars first-publish blocker; this task improves package ownership independently.
- Exact current and closed tracker searches for surface-review(mcp-base), epoch diff, pair-only, section grouping, mcp base, diff, and related descriptions found no duplicate outcome.

The boundary argument is true, but the move's hidden cost is disproportionate: the 1,276-line test corpus is JVM .clj with Malli, and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp has NO JVM test lane (its :test alias is a shadow compile), so relocating means a new JVM alias + Malli dep in a CLJS-only npm artefact, a new test.yml job (hot zone), scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh roster + check_jvm_lane_rosters.py bijection edits, and wire-vocab's :local/root switching to Pair (dragging shadow-cljs/js-interop onto its JVM classpath). Cheap alternative, filed as the disposition: one sentence in tools/mcp-base/spec/README.md:107-111 recording diff-encode/section-grouping as a Pair-owned codec hosted in base for its JVM+Malli lane — fold into any later mcp-base prose PR. Mike may override; reopen if so.

title: surface-review(mcp-conformance): make one command explain and run the live compatibility profile
description:
## Scope

Turn the existing repository-level `test:mcp-conformance` runner into the one documented front door for understanding and running MCP compatibility. Preserve its current medium-cost default run, add one explicit opt-in mode that chains the existing hermetic live Pair suite, and make every terminal verdict state which profile actually ran. Limit implementation to the existing runner, its small regression surface, and the MCP testing docs/package entry points needed to make the command copyable; keep the split CI jobs and focused per-suite commands.

## Findings

- The compatibility corpus already has strong teeth. The Node workflows use the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` client, SDK-call every advertised tool, validate descriptor classifications and result envelopes, and run real Story and degraded Pair workflows. The JVM wire suite auto-discovers its focused namespaces and combines canonical schemas, fixtures, reachable builders, source pins, near-miss rejection, and cross-encoding checks. The high-leverage need is not another protocol checklist or host matrix.
- There is already a single repository operator command: `npm run test:mcp-conformance` from `implementation/`. It installs/builds prerequisites and chains Story JVM/stdio, Pair compile/tests, the conformance Node inventory, and wire-vocab. Commit `7f1f93234a` created it specifically because the prior workflow required reading CI and invoking commands across four directories.
- The command is not the front door of the artefact it verifies. `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md` still teaches dependency installation plus separate unit, Pair compile/e2e, Story, hermetic-live, and wire-vocab recipes, and never names the existing single command. A reader or coding agent arriving at the conformance package has to reconstruct which recipe means “compatibility”.
- The default command's final verdict loses a load-bearing distinction. `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/test-all.cjs` correctly records live rows as `SKIP` when no nREPL port is supplied and explains that the hermetic suite did not run. One level up, `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs` reduces that whole child run to one status row and unconditionally ends with `ALL MCP-CONFORMANCE GATES GREEN`.
- The outer runner's own header says it chains the six PR-time MCP gates, while the same header explicitly excludes the hermetic live suite. CI's Pair conformance job does include that suite after the SDK/degraded rows. The omission is an intentional cost profile, not a missing test, but the terminal success line makes the default profile look complete.
- `TESTING.md` knows the real split: `test:mcp-conformance` is the medium command and `test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite` is a separate expensive command. That distinction lives in a large repository testing catalogue rather than in the command's help/output or the conformance README.
- Existing inventory ownership is sufficient: `scripts/test-all.cjs` owns Node rows, `scripts/live-test-inventory.cjs` owns live rows, and the JVM runner discovers `*_test.clj`. A new manifest, report schema, compliance database, or duplicated roster would add drift without improving compatibility feedback.
- Exact current/closed tracker searches for `surface-review(mcp-conformance)`, `test:mcp-conformance`, `single entry`, `hermetic live`, `SKIP`, and the current all-green sentinel found no bead owning this outcome.

## Recommended Action

Extend the existing `implementation` runner, rather than creating a second orchestrator:

1. Keep the no-argument command as today's medium profile. Its final summary must identify the server/unit + SDK/degraded + wire-vocab layers that passed and show the existing hermetic live Pair suite as `NOT RUN`, with the exact opt-in command beside it. It must not print an unqualified “all MCP conformance gates green” verdict.
2. Add one explicit `--live` mode that runs the same default steps and then invokes the existing `test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite` entry point. A full-green verdict is available only after the hermetic runner observes every registered live sentinel and proves cleanup, preserving its existing exit-code distinction between conformance and orchestration failure.
3. Add side-effect-free `--help` output that names both modes, their prerequisites/cost boundary, what `npm test` inside `tools/mcp-conformance` does, and which mode proves live runtime behavior.
4. Front-load the two copyable repository-root commands in `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md`; keep focused scripts below them for diagnosis. Align `TESTING.md` wording if necessary, but retain one canonical project command rather than adding aliases in several packages.

Reuse the existing Node and live inventories and the wire-vocab test discovery. The improvement is an honest, executable profile boundary, not a new compliance framework.

## Evidence

- `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs:3-47` describes the six-gate operator runner, says the hermetic suite is intentionally excluded, and points to a second manual command.
- `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs:186-245` declares the current prep and six gate steps; lines 303-318 collapse their result to the unqualified all-green sentinel.
- `implementation/package.json` exposes the runner only as `test:mcp-conformance` from the implementation package.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md:101-148` gives five separate run recipes, uses `npm install` despite the committed lock/reproducible `npm ci` posture, and describes `npm test` as the Node inventory without pointing to the repository-level runner.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/test-all.cjs:13-18,87-96,130-156` derives the live rows, marks them `SKIP`, and prints the coverage caveat that the outer runner later loses.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/live-test-inventory.cjs:6-41` is the one live roster; the hermetic runner derives `INNER_TESTS` from it.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:1266-1302,1361-1378` refuses skipped/missing sentinels and emits green only after cleanup grading.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/package.json` exposes focused Node/server/live scripts but no project compatibility profile or CLI help.
- `TESTING.md:32-34` separately lists the medium conformance command and expensive live command.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml:5345-5423,5488-5500,5562-5566` shows the actual CI split and that the Pair job includes the hermetic suite.
- History: `7f1f93234a` introduced the single runner; `ddb3ec91f3` made its installs reproducible. The current package README was rewritten later in `deb03d1d01` and still exposes only the multi-command route.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From the repository root, one documented command runs the current medium compatibility profile; its terminal summary explicitly marks the hermetic live Pair profile `NOT RUN` and prints the exact `--live` invocation. No unqualified all-green sentence is emitted for that partial profile.
2. The same command with `--live` invokes the existing hermetic suite after the default steps. It reports full compatibility green only when every live row from `LIVE_TESTS` ran to its sentinel and the hermetic cleanup grade is clean; inner exit 1 and orchestration/cleanup exit 2 continue to propagate distinctly.
3. `--help` exits zero before installs, compiles, or server boots and concisely explains default versus live coverage, prerequisites, expected relative cost, and the narrower meaning of `tools/mcp-conformance/npm test`. Unknown options fail before any setup mutation.
4. A lightweight runner regression test exercises default, `--live`, help, and unknown-option selection without launching Clojure, shadow-cljs, Chromium, or either MCP server, and proves the live step is absent/present in the corresponding planned summary.
5. `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md` starts its run guidance with the two repository-root commands and a small included/omitted profile table. Focused unit, per-server, wire-vocab, and direct hermetic commands remain available as diagnostic recipes and agree with package scripts.
6. The implementation reuses `TESTS`, `LIVE_TESTS`, the current hermetic entry point, and JVM test discovery; it introduces no second test roster, copied tool catalogue, new result/report format, or new CI job.
7. Existing CI jobs, changed-surface scheduling, default medium cost, server behavior, tool descriptors, and wire schemas remain unchanged. The existing focused suites and runner policy tests pass.

## Non-goals

- No MCP certification product, compatibility score, persisted report, dashboard, badge, or release-compliance database.
- No matrix across MCP hosts, SDK languages/versions, protocol versions, transports, operating systems, or published-package combinations.
- No new protocol assertions, tool semantics, wire markers, schemas, vocabulary rules, or server launch flags.
- No consolidation of the three CI jobs, no changed-only scheduler, and no default-on Chromium/hermetic cost.
- No replacement or broad refactor of the mature Node/JVM corpus, hermetic orchestrator, source-pin strategy, or server-owned manifests.
- No second package-level “all” runner that can drift from `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs`.

## Related beads

- `rf2-gt4pf` (historical; commit `7f1f93234a`) created the current single operator entry point and deliberately kept rich reporting, changed-only mode, and CI consolidation out of scope. This task preserves that minimum-scope posture while making the existing profile boundary explicit.

- `rf2-ahjbc` (open) proposes removing Pair progress streaming and its live conformance row. It is not a dependency: this task must derive the live profile from `LIVE_TESTS`, so either inventory state is handled without a copied list; coordinate only if both edit the live runner concurrently.

title: surface-review(reagent-slim): make reagent2.core/reaction a stock-compatible macro
description:
## Scope

Restore the public `reagent2.core/reaction` call shape promised by the bounded Reagent-compat surface. Touch only the reagent-slim core macro/runtime surface, focused tests, and the directly coupled surface/migration documentation needed to make the contract truthful.

## Findings

`reagent2.core/reaction` is currently a runtime function taking a thunk (`[f]`), but the pinned stock Reagent 2.0.1 surface it claims to preserve exposes `reagent.core/reaction` as a variadic macro that wraps its body in `(fn [])`. There is no `src/reagent2/core.clj` macro namespace. A documented mechanical require rename therefore changes `(r/reaction (* @a @a))` from a lazy reactive expression into an eager call that passes the computed value as `f`; dereferencing the resulting Reaction later attempts to call that value as a function.

This is not covered by the current tests. `reagent2.core-cljs-test` says the core reaction surface has dedicated coverage but never calls `r/reaction`; `reagent2.ratom-cljs-test` covers the different `reagent2.ratom/reaction` macro. IMPL-SPEC §2.2 and §14.2 encode the same incorrect “function form” reading while §13.1 promises that `s/reagent\./reagent2./g` is sufficient inside the bounded surface.

## Recommended Action

Make `reagent2.core/reaction` a co-located CLJ macro with stock Reagent's body syntax and expansion to `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`. Remove the misleading thunk-taking runtime function from that public spelling; callers that intentionally have a thunk already have the explicit `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction` factory. Reconcile the public-surface inventory and migration prose with the actual macro contract.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
- In that artefact, `reagent/core.clj` defines `(defmacro reaction [& body] ...)`; `reagent/core.cljs` defines no `reaction` function.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/core.cljs:65-73` instead defines `(defn reaction [f] ...)`, and `src/reagent2/core.clj` does not exist.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:224` and `:1187-1191` classify the core spelling as a function, while `:1129` promises a namespace-only import rewrite.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/core_cljs_test.cljs:22-25` claims indirect coverage but contains no `r/reaction` call; the only expression-body proof is for the sibling ratom macro at `test/reagent2/ratom_cljs_test.cljs:425-432`.
- The spec cites 25 Dash8 plus 1 rf8 `reagent.core/reaction` sites as reasons this surface ships, so the mismatch is on an audited, used path rather than speculative compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With only `(:require [reagent2.core :as r])`, `(r/reaction <body...>)` compiles with the same body syntax as stock Reagent and produces a `reagent2.ratom/Reaction`.
- A focused regression proves the body is deferred until deref, captures a reagent2 atom dependency, and recomputes after that atom changes.
- Macro expansion or an equivalent structural assertion proves the body is wrapped in a zero-argument function passed to `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`.
- No public `reagent2.core/reaction` thunk-taking function remains; explicit thunk construction remains available as `reagent2.ratom/make-reaction`.
- Core namespace docs, IMPL-SPEC surface tables/§14.2, and migration guidance describe the macro accurately, with no claim that the old function form exists in stock Reagent.
- The reagent-slim package/test gates include and exercise the new `.clj` macro file from the published `src` path.

## Non-goals

- Adding dropped Reagent surfaces such as `track`, `track!`, `run!`, or `with-let`.
- Changing the Reaction kernel, batching scheduler, renderer, adapter map, or ratom macro semantics.
- Preserving the pre-alpha thunk-taking core spelling via a compatibility shim or introducing a second public factory alias.
- A broad stock-Reagent parity audit or migration codemod.

## Related beads

- Historical `rf2-6hyy` introduced the Stage-4 reagent-slim surface.
- Historical `rf2-kfpf` is the consumer audit cited for the 25 Dash8 core-reaction sites.
- Historical `rf2-n71j3q` clarified that `reagent2.ratom.clj` ships the ratom macro only; this task closes the distinct missing core macro.
- No duplicate was found across current Bead titles, descriptions, notes, close reasons, or comments for `reagent2.core/reaction`, `reagent.core/reaction`, `reaction macro`, or combined `reagent-slim` + `reaction` searches.

title: surface-review(examples-substrates): make login the runnable three-view-layer comparison
description:
## Scope

Make the existing login feature the canonical runnable comparison of re-frame2's three active browser view languages: Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso. Keep `examples/core/login/` as the Reagent arm and `examples/substrates/uix/login/` as the UIx arm; add one Hicasso arm under `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` that requires the same substrate-free `login.model` and owns only its view/root code. Add a concise `examples/substrates/README.md` that explains which comparison to read, wire the new arm through the existing example build/runner/compile path, and extend the existing login bundle-isolation proof. Correct only directly coupled catalogue and TESTING prose.

This is one worked-example outcome, not a demo framework or a substrate selector.

## Findings

- The substrate tree has UIx counter/login/dashboard and reagent-slim counter, but no landing page and no human-facing Hicasso example. `examples/README.md` still describes the family as UIx plus reagent-slim even though Hicasso now ships its own canonical view adapter.
- Hicasso already has a complete installation counter in `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md` and a Story/Xray-owned counter testbed under `tools/story/testbeds/hicasso_counter/`. Another counter would duplicate the beginner sample or send learners into tool scaffolding; neither shows a realistic model/view boundary.
- Login is already the right comparison seam. Commit `2644f42b72` (`rf2-ppbvav`) extracted roughly 19 schemas/effects/machine/events/subscriptions and `frame-config` into one substrate-free `login.model`, leaving only views and mount code in the Reagent/UIx/Helix entries. Commit `e1f38e5ddf` (`rf2-d6epb`) removed Helix, so that deliberate three-view example became a two-view pair.
- The removal left observable drift: `examples/TESTING.md` still says counter and login "triplet", "three reactive substrates", and "three login examples" although only Reagent and UIx login builds remain. `login.model` also still speaks of "three mounts". Fixing those words alone would be minutiae; supplying the current third view language restores the useful product shape they once described.
- The three small counter files deliberately repeat their tiny event/sub dataflow so each remains readable top to bottom. Extracting a counter model would weaken the smallest-app lesson for little gain. The substantial login model already amortises sharing and has model-level tests.
- Hicasso's native root door is compatible without an API change, but the boot shape must be honest. `h/mount!` accepts only `:frame`, `:initial-events`, and `:identifier-prefix`; the login demo also needs `model/frame-config`'s `:fx-overrides`. The Hicasso entry should therefore install `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, create the frame once with the existing config, and mount into that frame. Hot reload should re-render the retained Hicasso root rather than recreate the frame.
- The existing harness already supplies the needed mechanics. A normal `:examples/login-hicasso` build whose init namespace and `index.html` live under `examples/` is discovered by `serve-example.cjs`, staged with `_shared`, and swept by `check-examples-compile.cjs`; no registry or special runner branch is needed.
- Examples are intentionally test-free. The shared login behavior is already exercised outside the tree, while `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` proves the shared model does not pull a foreign view runtime. That checker currently has only Reagent and UIx arms even though the general isolation gate already owns live Hicasso sentinels and a positive-control module.

## Recommended Action

Add `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` as a direct third view over `login.model`. Keep the same fields, messages, test ids, canned success/failure flow, and shared visual assets as the existing pair. Author the view in native Hicasso idioms (`h/defview`, `h/sub`, event vectors where they fit); preserve the password event's classified map payload rather than flattening the secret into a positional intent. Use a small `h/event` callback where constructing that map requires the DOM value.

Declare `:examples/login-hicasso` beside the two current login builds, with the standard `out/examples/login-hicasso` output. Let the existing manifest-derived runner and compile checker enroll it. Add the exact repository-local run command to the new example README, while linking the Hicasso installation chapter for dependency setup and truthfully noting that the Maven coordinate is not published yet.

Make `examples/substrates/README.md` a short decision/comparison surface with two explicit tracks:

1. Same Reagent authoring language, different adapter/package: stock counter versus reagent-slim counter.
2. One substrate-free model, different view language/root: Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso login.

Link directly to the model and three thin entry points so a programmer or coding agent can compare source, not prose excerpts. Point the root catalogue at this page and reconcile the stale parity section in `examples/TESTING.md` and directly coupled login comments/READMEs.

Extend `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` and `test:bundle-isolation` to release and inspect the Hicasso login. Reuse the existing Hicasso sentinels and positive control: each login bundle must contain its own view runtime and exclude the other two. Keep compile coverage plus this structural proof; do not add a per-example browser suite.

## Evidence

- `examples/README.md:9,55-61` lists only UIx and reagent-slim under Substrates; `examples/substrates/README.md` does not exist.
- `examples/TESTING.md:82-118` calls two current pairs triplets and claims three login examples while naming only two login bundles.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljs:42-57,722-742` documents the substrate-free owner and shared frame config; only `examples/core/login/core.cljs` and `examples/substrates/uix/login/core.cljs` require it today.
- `implementation/scripts/check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs:3-45,85-103,179-235` explicitly implements a two-bundle Reagent/UIx proof.
- `implementation/package.json:41-42,53` releases only the two login builds for bundle isolation and exposes the existing compile and `dev:example` doors.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1611-1644` declares the current login pair; `:examples/hicasso-counter` at lines 1950-1959 points to the tool-owned Story testbed instead of `examples/`.
- `node ../examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs --list` includes `examples/login` and `examples/login-uix` but not the tool-owned Hicasso counter. `node scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` does include that tool build, demonstrating why compile inventory alone is not a human learning catalogue.
- `docs/core/hicasso/index.md:3-6` defines Hicasso as re-frame2's native view layer. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2130-2138` lists Hicasso's own adapter in the canonical shipped inventory.
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:549-605` and `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:115-155` bound `h/mount!` to the three root keys and show that it joins a frame already created through `rf/make-frame`.
- `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:300-332,742-746` already defines non-dev Hicasso sentinels (`hicassoBoundary`, `rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector`) and proves them present in a dedicated positive-control module.
- History establishes the sequence: shared login model on 2026-07-11 (`2644f42b72`), Helix removal on 2026-07-22 (`e1f38e5ddf`), Hicasso's own adapter on 2026-08-18 (`4cb9e16951`), and canonical adapter registration on 2026-08-19 (`5d1fd88c3f`). The examples never gained a human Hicasso arm after that change.
- Current tag and installation evidence says the example must stay repository-local for now: `git tag --list 'v*'` is empty and `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md:18-40,125` says the coordinate is unpublished and uses `:local/root`.
- Fresh open/closed title and description searches for the exact prefix, Hicasso login, login-hicasso, three-view-layer, cross-substrate, `login.model`, and `examples/substrates/hicasso` found no duplicate. The adjacent launch-command tasks `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` are distinct and explicitly remain separate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` contains a readable Hicasso entry, host page, and concise README. It imports `login.model` and contains no duplicate auth schemas, effects, machine, events, or subscriptions.
2. The Hicasso view uses native `h/defview`/`h/sub`/intent idioms and matches the Reagent/UIx pair's visible login behavior and stable test ids. Email edits remain positional; password edits still dispatch the classified `[:auth.login/edit-password {:value ...}]` shape, and submit/success/failure behavior remains owned by the shared model.
3. Boot installs `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, constructs the frame once from `model/frame-config` so the canned HTTP effect override and initial event are honored, mounts Hicasso into that frame, and retains/re-renders one root on hot reload. No expansion or compatibility shim is added to `h/mount!`.
4. `:examples/login-hicasso` emits to the standard example output root and appears automatically in both `npm run dev:example -- --list` and `npm run test:examples-compile` inventory. Its host/shared assets are resolved by the existing staging code with no hard-coded build-to-folder entry.
5. `examples/substrates/README.md` gives the two-track comparison above and links the exact model/view/root files. `examples/README.md`, `examples/TESTING.md`, `login.model`, and the three login READMEs no longer describe deleted Helix arms or incorrect triplet counts.
6. The new README gives one truthful repository-local launch path and points greenfield setup to the Hicasso installation guide; it does not advertise an unresolved Maven version or duplicate a project template.
7. `test:bundle-isolation` releases all three login builds. The existing login checker proves own-runtime presence plus foreign-runtime absence for Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso, using a non-vacuous Hicasso positive control. The Hicasso login carries no Reagent or UIx fingerprint, and the other two carry no Hicasso fingerprint.
8. `npm run test:examples-compile`, `npm run test:bundle-isolation`, the existing example staging/runner tests, and relevant docs-link gates pass. A clean repository-local launch paints the form and exercises one validation failure plus the canned successful login; no new per-example browser gate is introduced.

## Non-goals

- No runtime view-layer switcher, multi-adapter bundle, mode flag, gallery shell, code generator, or new example manifest/framework.
- No extraction of the tiny counter registrations, sharing of view code, or conversion of every example to every view layer.
- No Hicasso variant in `tools/template`, no publication workaround, and no invented compatibility coordinate while the artifact is unpublished.
- No change to Hicasso root/adapter APIs, login business behavior, or the substrate contract.
- No promotion or relocation of the Story/Xray Hicasso counter testbed; tool testbeds remain tool-owned.
- No Hicasso SSR/Node example; `rf2-8arzr` owns that separate path.
- No sweep standardizing existing substrate README launch commands; `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` own the adjacent catalogue command policy. This task only documents the new arm and follows whichever shared wording lands.
- No per-example browser-test matrix; examples stay human learning surfaces and adapter smokes stay adapter-owned.

## Related beads

- `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` - adjacent core/capability launch-command work; not duplicated here.
- `rf2-9hcyf` - executable UIx component-testing recipe; distinct from the human example comparison.
- `rf2-8urba` - deferred Hicasso template variant, gated on publication; this task does not scaffold consumers.
- `rf2-8arzr` - native-Hicasso SSR/Node reference path; explicitly outside this browser example.
- `rf2-auiy5` and `rf2-hvr5h` - established Hicasso's canonical native adapter.
- Historical `rf2-ppbvav` / commit `2644f42b72` - created the shared login model and original three-view comparison.
- Historical `rf2-d6epb` / commit `e1f38e5ddf` - removed Helix and its example arms.
- `rf2-5czki` - added Hicasso Story support and the tool-owned testbed; this task supplies the intentionally separate human surface.

title: surface-review(examples-real-apps): make offline Conduit writes survive the refetch they cause
description:
## Scope

Make both RealWorld examples honest end-to-end offline SPAs by turning the existing shared in-process Conduit demo backend into a small deterministic stateful model for the API routes the apps already use. Cover `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs`, the two thin app-local managed-HTTP override seams, the external RealWorld test wrappers, and the two READMEs where they describe offline behavior. Keep the managed-HTTP and Resources application architectures separate and directly readable; the shared backend remains the only comparison seam.

## Findings

The applications themselves exercise a credible breadth of SPA composition: boot and frame scope, URL-owned routing and guards, auth/session restore, schemas, machines, flows, managed HTTP, resources/mutations, pagination, optimistic writes, comments, profiles, settings, editor navigation, and SSR payload policy. They compile as standalone builds and have large headless integration wrappers outside the test-free examples tree.

The production demo backend does not preserve any write. `payload-for-request` is a one-request lookup over immutable `articles`, `favorited`, and `user` values. POST/PUT/DELETE branches manufacture valid response envelopes but never produce a new backend state. Subsequent GETs always read the seed corpus:

- create returns a derived slug but never inserts it; GET of an unknown slug silently falls back to the first article, so create-then-navigate can render `hello-conduit` at the new URL;
- update and delete do not change later detail or list reads;
- post-comment returns a random-id comment while GET comments is always `[]`, and delete changes nothing;
- favorite/unfavorite echo the requested flag but later article/list reads use the original articles and the Favorited tab is a fixed `take-nth` subset;
- follow/unfollow echo a flag but later profile reads always return `following false`, while the feed is permanently empty;
- settings PUT returns the original static user, and tag/author list query params do not filter the corpus.

This is most damaging in the Resources sibling because its headline is the automatic `read -> write -> invalidate -> refetch` loop. Post-comment deliberately does not populate a partial list; it invalidates comments and trusts the refetch as authoritative. The shipped offline backend answers that refetch with `[]`, so a successful comment disappears. Favorite explicitly refetches lists/feed "to truth", but the backend's truth is the pre-write seed. Fixing the client to suppress those refetches would hide the evidence rather than repair it.

The test surface misses the contradiction. `realworld_shared_backend_cljs_test.cljs` calls the pure router once per assertion and checks envelope shape, never write-then-read state. The resources integration wrapper replaces `:rf.http/managed` with a request-capture function and manually supplies every reply; its comment test asserts that a refetch starts but never settles that refetch from the production demo backend. The HTTP wrapper likewise installs bespoke canned stubs. Compile coverage proves buildability, not this user journey, and no current example wrapper mounts the DOM.

History explains the false confidence. Commit `02e6630851` consolidated two drifting fake backends and correctly fixed request routing and response envelopes, but its claim that create/update/delete/favorite/follow/settings "now actually work" was only pinned one request at a time. The shared backend is the right ownership boundary; it needs temporal semantics, not another copy or another abstraction.

## Recommended Action

Keep one shared backend, but express it as ordinary pure data plus one pure transition: seeded backend state + managed-request args -> next state + success/failure reply. Let each launched demo own an explicit, resettable instance of that state and keep `respond` as the thin adapter into the existing canned-success/canned-failure effects and 20 ms deferred reply path. Use deterministic counters/timestamps instead of `rand-int`, and make test/app reset boundaries explicit so hot reload, a fresh mount, and separate frames/tests cannot inherit accidental state.

Implement only the Conduit subset already called by these apps: login/session restore/settings, article CRUD, comments, favorite membership/counts, follow relationships/feed, profiles, tags, current-state list filtering, and limit/offset pagination. Missing article/comment routes should return an explicit Conduit-shaped 4xx failure rather than a plausible first record. Preserve the existing wire schemas, classification, bearer interceptor, frame routing, and offline/no-network default.

Replace the backend's one-shot contract tests with sequential transition tests, then add a focused full-frame receipt for each app-local fx seam using the production demo backend rather than a bespoke canned reply. The Resources receipt should prove a real mutation settles, invalidates, automatically refetches, and leaves the resource at the new server truth. The managed-HTTP receipt should perform the corresponding write and later load through its normal public events. Keep all tests outside `examples/` per repository policy.

Refresh the README claims and give readers one short try-it journey whose result survives refetch/navigation. Do not turn the backend into an example framework; the simple state transition is part of this example's evidence.

## Evidence

- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/README.md:3,11-13` calls this a complete working blog and names `read -> write -> invalidate -> refetch` as the one idea the example exists to prove.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:106-126` defines immutable article/favorite/user data and makes unknown slugs fall back to the first article.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:128-134` uses `rand-int` for comment IDs; the same file's POST branches at 190-237 return envelopes without updating any store.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/demo_backend.cljs:239-255` makes feed/comments fixed empty responses, serves Favorited from a static subset, sends tag/author queries through the full article vector, and always reads profiles as not-following.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/mutations.cljs:163-202` says favorite reconciliation refetches lists/feed to truth; lines 243-271 intentionally make comment writes invalidate and refetch rather than populate a partial collection.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:90-98,183-186` replaces the live transport with request capture. Its comment case at 1264-1300 hand-injects the write reply and only asserts that refetch began.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_shared_backend_cljs_test.cljs:20-31` explicitly treats the backend as a pure URL/method-to-payload function. Lines 88-139 assert isolated favorite/comment/list envelopes, not any later read.
- `examples/TESTING.md:5,18-23` records the test-free source-tree policy, external headless wrappers, and the distinction between compile coverage and browser behavior.
- Commit `02e6630851` is the backend's entire path history: it centralized the correct seam and added one-shot shape tests, but no state sequence.
- Full title/description searches across open and closed beads for demo/stateful/offline backend, `payload-for-request`, write persistence, mutation refetch, comment disappearance, and favorite reversion found no matching task.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The offline backend has a deterministic seeded state and one canonical transition used by both app-local fx ids; identical fresh-state request sequences produce identical replies and state in both variants.
- Article create -> GET-by-new-slug/list/author-filter, update -> later GET, and delete -> later GET/list are covered sequentially. Unknown/deleted slugs fail explicitly and never return the first seed article.
- Comment POST -> GET includes the exact saved comment and deterministic id; DELETE -> GET removes it. A Resources full-frame test uses the real demo fx and proves the invalidation-triggered comments refetch settles with that new collection.
- Favorite/unfavorite persist through detail, global/tag/author lists, and the acting user's Favorited list with correct counts. Follow/unfollow persist through profile reads and affect the demo feed consistently. Settings changes survive later user/profile reads, and a saved valid demo token can restore the session while invalid/missing credentials fail predictably.
- Tag, author, favorited, feed, limit, and offset query semantics are applied to current backend state, and each `articlesCount` describes the filtered set rather than the seed corpus or page size.
- Backend instances/reset are explicit and isolated for fresh launches and tests; generated values are deterministic; no raw timer replaces the existing `:dispatch-later`-backed canned reply path.
- At least one automated full-frame path per app variant uses its production demo override rather than a bespoke response stub and proves a write remains observable after a later normal read. Tests remain outside `examples/` and include a negative control that fails if the transition result is discarded or reads consult the seed constants.
- Both RealWorld builds compile warning-free, the focused CLJS suites pass, and README claims/try-it steps describe only behavior the served offline apps now retain across refetch and navigation.

## Non-goals

- No full Conduit server, database, network listener, service worker, persistence across browser reload beyond the existing demo-token contract, multi-user authorization system, or production backend replacement.
- No generic mock-server library, request-fixture DSL, compatibility layer, generated client, example framework, or new framework runtime API.
- No sharing of routes, handlers, subscriptions, views, app-db slices, or feature namespaces between the managed-HTTP and Resources variants; their architectural comparison stays explicit.
- No weakening/bypassing resource invalidation, pinning stale optimistic data, or changing cache semantics to accommodate a stateless backend.
- No broad visual redesign, route-id rename, source-layout reorganization, or exhaustive per-page browser suite.
- No duplicate `dev:example` launch-command standardization; the adjacent examples-core/capabilities tasks own that documentation family and this task is about temporal app behavior.

## Related beads

- `rf2-y8jjk` (open) makes active-route resource replanning authoritative; it is complementary. That task repairs which reads are planned after identity changes, while this task makes the backend truth those reads receive reflect prior writes.
- `rf2-8cevm` (closed) established the test-free examples policy; sequential and full-frame receipts stay in the external adapter test tree.
- `rf2-czvc` (closed) fixed RealWorld editor settle races through external production-source wrappers; it is the precedent for testing a real example flow rather than a copied miniature.
