title: surface-review(skill-implementor): make the pinned spec and fixtures the porting loop
description:
## Scope

Rework skills/re-frame2-implementor/** as a compact execution guide for building a minimum second implementation. Preserve the existing eight-host React+VDOM scope, the pinned-spec boundary, spec-gap discipline, and claimed-capability conformance semantics. Replace the current document/session dossier with two things: a short port profile containing only genuine implementor choices, and one repeatable EP loop driven directly by the pinned owning Specs and live conformance fixtures.

The coherent surface includes the published SKILL.md and references, their human/meta docs, the implementor-specific drift guards that currently pin copied prose, and a focused behavioural eval. It does not change the re-frame2 spec, runtime, APIs, capability vocabulary, or fixture corpus.

## Findings

1. The published skill says it routes rather than duplicates the spec, but it has become a second contract. SKILL.md plus the eight shipped reference leaves total 36,816 words / 283,139 characters. phase-2-impl-order.md alone is 15,084 words / 117,782 characters; phase-1-decisions.md is 5,337 words / 44,840 characters. Six of the eight leaves exceed the repository's existing 16 KB leaf ceiling in skills/README.md. A normal Phase-2 session is told to consult the 119 KB EP leaf, often the 28 KB conformance leaf and 25 KB reference tour as well.
2. The skill-internal context-economy claim has drifted from reality. spec/design.md:147-154 says Phase 1 is about 320 lines, a full v1 is about 1,060 lines, and the worst case is comfortably small. The current physical totals are 668 lines for phase-1-decisions.md + decision-record.md and 1,953 lines for SKILL.md + all references, with unusually dense long lines. This is not progressive disclosure when the unit of loading is a whole leaf.
3. Phase 1 records obligations as if they were choices. The kickoff prompt (references/kickoff-prompt.md:24) requires a question for every block, captures every answer, forbids implementation code, and the 254-line decision template requires every placeholder filled and a commit before work (decision-record.md:236-237). Much of D4 is fixed by the spec rather than selected by an implementor: React+VDOM, the JS event loop, no core.async public contract, one frame-state container, closed effect-map policing, structured errors, and the mandatory classification boundary. Reconfirming these in a second document adds ceremony without changing a port.
4. Phase 2 adds project-management policy unrelated to correctness. phase-2-impl-order.md:25 mandates one multi-day EP per focused session and forbids landing two together. output-format.md:31-129 requires Phase-1, per-EP, and v1 report forms; every EP report carries commit hashes, files, tests, fixture lists, carry-over, and a mandatory What surprised me section, while line 131 requires one report per session. A competent implementor should be free to choose commit/session granularity.
5. The feedback loop begins too late. The first full acceptance point comes only after the shared identity/path foundation plus EP 001, 002, 006, views, 009, and 015 (phase-2-impl-order.md:278-294). conformance.md:21 says each host first builds roughly 300 lines of harness, yet harness bootstrap is not an implementation step. The per-EP rule can simply report not run when a fresh port has no script. This allows several multi-day EPs to accumulate before the first objective signal.
6. Verification ownership is internally inconsistent. README.md:26 says compilation, tests, and conformance are the engineer's responsibility; SKILL.md:67, spec/design.md:19,40-62, output-format.md, and skills/README.md:198 say the agent runs a narrow per-EP slice. The full gates are still delegated by default even when the explicitly-invoked, code-writing agent has the tool access to run them.
7. History shows the maintenance cost of copying contract detail. The skill path has been touched by 129 commits since its 2026-05-12 introduction. The shipped router+references grew from about 12,277 words / 90,090 characters at introduction to 36,816 words / 283,139 characters now. Closed beads rf2-ihw9q and rf2-hu5uz show the failure mode directly: the Phase-2 prose pointed a porter at deleted implementation files and a deleted function, while a required checker pinned the dead token, so repairing guidance required coordinated prose/checker surgery.
8. The conformance guidance has strong principles worth preserving—derive tags from the pinned corpus, fail unknown capabilities instead of silently skipping, distinguish spec gaps from port bugs—but its copied catalogues already age. The worked command at conformance.md:183 says 136 fixtures; the current directory contains 245. The harness should enumerate fixture metadata and call/DSL operators at the pin instead of teaching a prose snapshot.
9. Host scope is not the problem. The eight JS-cross-compile-to-React+VDOM hosts and the stop for other hosts match spec/000-Vision.md and spec/Implementor-Checklist.md. Preserve that boundary, but let the checklist own its per-host option matrices instead of restating them in the skill.
10. Evaluation covers discovery only. evals/evals.json:4 explicitly defines trigger-only fixtures; nothing grades whether a TypeScript/Fable port request yields a compact set of decisions, establishes an executable feedback loop, runs the right slice, refuses silent capability skips, or reaches an honest checkpoint. The docs also visibly drift: docs/skills/re-frame2-implementor.md:46 links the current references/ directory through the deleted singular /reference URL.
11. All of this prose ships: package.json:28-33 includes SKILL.md and references/. The internal design/evals are excluded, so they cannot rescue an installed agent from an overlong or stale operational path.

## Recommended Action

Make the pinned spec and fixtures the working loop rather than mirroring them.

1. Replace the 254-line DECISIONS.md dossier with a compact port profile containing only: upstream pin/origin, host/toolchain, genuinely chosen host mechanisms, optional capability claim/known skips, and current conformance score. Fixed pattern obligations are links to their owning Spec, not fields the implementor must copy and reconfirm. For an unqualified minimum-port request, default optional capabilities to no and choose ordinary host-idiomatic mechanisms where repository context makes them clear; ask only for a missing choice that materially changes the implementation.
2. Replace the long kickoff and three report templates with one concise execution contract. Do not mandate a fresh session, per-EP commit, one EP per session, surprise diary, or a committed record before code. A checkpoint should report only changed decisions, code/result, exact test command and outcome, conformance delta, and genuine blockers/spec gaps.
3. Replace the 119 KB Phase-2 contract mirror with a small EP index: dependency order, owning Spec/API/Conventions links, capability family, and prerequisites. Every EP then follows one uniform loop: read the owner at the recorded pin; enumerate applicable fixture ids/capabilities/operators from that same pin; implement the smallest vertical slice; run the narrow slice; repair or diagnose; update the compact profile only if a real choice or claim changed.
4. Bootstrap fixture discovery and the smallest useful harness seam before or alongside the first foundational implementation slice. Grow support for handler-DSL and Mode-B operators only as live fixtures require it, while failing loud on an unknown fixture spec version, capability, DSL op, or call op. Do not invent a generated fixture translation layer or a cross-host compatibility package.
5. Let a tool-capable agent run the port's discovered noninteractive unit/conformance gates, including the full claimed-capability gate when the user asked for an end-to-end implementation. Interactive/visual work can remain a concise programmer handoff when no drivable runtime exists. Use the host agent's normal permissions instead of a skill-local engineer/agent relay policy.
6. Keep the valuable conformance and safety invariants concise and singular: pinned provenance, no silent unknown skips, passed / claimed-applicable, spec-gap-vs-port-bug diagnosis, explicit approval for upstream issue creation, and relevant tooling-security boundaries. Link to the source contract for all framework semantics.
7. Retire or narrow structural checker arms that require copied implementation tokens/paragraphs. Keep focused guards for genuinely load-bearing workflow invariants (foundation ordering, all three required capability families, no bead-id leakage, issue-filing safety), but do not require a second prose rendering of the runtime contract.
8. Add one focused behavioural eval around a small TypeScript-shaped port workspace. It should prove the default minimum-port prompt creates the compact profile without an exhaustive interview, establishes/runs the first real slice, reports observed results, and fails on a controlled wrong implementation or unknown capability. Keep the existing out-of-scope host/substrate negatives. This is one outcome witness, not a general eval platform.
9. Reconcile the published README/docs and internal design claims with the reduced workflow, including the broken references/ link and measured size/load statements.

## Evidence

- Runtime guidance census at current main: SKILL.md + eight references = 36,816 words / 283,139 characters; physical line count = 1,953.
- Largest leaves: references/phase-2-impl-order.md 119,590 bytes; phase-1-decisions.md 46,018; conformance.md 28,495; reference-impl-tour.md 26,306; cardinal-rules.md 21,203; decision-record.md 19,345. The family ceiling is skills/README.md:246-251 (at most 250 lines and 16 KB, one-level routing).
- Stated non-duplication: skills/re-frame2-implementor/README.md:37 and spec/design.md:13. Actual Phase-2 leaf contains 15,084 words of normative contract restatement.
- Ceremony: references/kickoff-prompt.md:24,53; references/decision-record.md:58,236-237; references/phase-2-impl-order.md:25; references/output-format.md:31-131.
- Late feedback and ownership conflict: references/phase-2-impl-order.md:278-294; references/conformance.md:21; README.md:26; SKILL.md:67; skills/README.md:198.
- Trigger-only eval: evals/evals.json:4-26.
- Published package surface: package.json:28-33.
- Drift examples: references/conformance.md:183 versus 245 current fixture files; docs/skills/re-frame2-implementor.md:46 singular-directory URL.
- History: 129 commits touch the skill path since 80ffd92404; initial router+references about 12,277 words / 90,090 characters versus 36,816 / 283,139 now. rf2-ihw9q and rf2-hu5uz document dead worked-example prose pinned by scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py.
- Duplicate search: all-status title/description searches for skill-implementor, re-frame2-implementor, decision record, port profile, conformance-first, kickoff prompt, per-EP wrap-up, token burden, and second implementation found no bead owning this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a pinned local spec checkout and an unqualified build a minimum re-frame2 port in TypeScript request, the skill takes no question-per-D-block or question-per-optional-EP interview. It records a compact port profile of actual choices/claims and begins the first implementation/verification slice in the same run; no fixed spec obligation is copied as a confirmation field.
2. The default route needs SKILL.md plus at most one one-level-deep operational leaf to begin work. Shipped leaves obey the existing 16 KB discipline unless a measured catalogue exception demonstrably reduces per-session tokens; the current monolithic Phase-2 leaf is not retained as an exception. Total shipped operational prose is a net material reduction, not the same text redistributed across more files.
3. The port profile contains the spec pin, host/toolchain, material mechanism choices, claimed/known-skipped capability set, fixture-less self-tests where applicable, and latest score. It has no mandatory per-session log, commit hash chain, repeated fixed obligations, or fill every placeholder rule.
4. Each foundational EP checkpoint is driven by current fixture metadata at the pin and reports an exact runnable unit/conformance slice. A fresh port cannot call successive EPs landed solely with no port script yet; the workflow establishes the minimal runner/test seam early and fails loud on unknown spec versions, capabilities, DSL ops, and Mode-B call ops.
5. A tool-capable end-to-end session runs the discovered noninteractive per-EP and full claimed-capability gates itself and reports exact commands, exits, and passed / claimed-applicable. It hands off only unavailable interactive/visual evidence, and never claims completion while that required evidence is pending.
6. The reduced EP index preserves the required order and the three foundation families (:core/*, :identity/*, :data-classification/*), host scope, spec-authority rule, no-silent-skip rule, and spec-gap approval boundary. Framework contract detail remains owned by the pinned Specs/fixtures rather than duplicated in the skill.
7. One focused checked-in behavioural eval exercises the minimum TypeScript path through compact profiling and a real first slice. A controlled bad implementation or unknown-capability mutation makes it fail, proving the signal is non-vacuous. Existing trigger routing still sends out-of-scope hosts/substrates and application-authoring requests elsewhere.
8. Implementor-specific drift checks are updated in the same change: obsolete literal-prose/token locks are retired or narrowed with self-tests, while remaining workflow/safety invariants stay enforced. No new generated manifest, prose synchronizer, or copied contract catalogue is introduced.
9. README.md, docs/skills/re-frame2-implementor.md, package/plugin metadata, and spec/{design,inputs,authoring-prompt}.md describe the same compact workflow, current verification ownership, and actual load shape; the broken references/ URL is fixed.
10. The PR reports before/after word/byte load for the default route, the behavioural eval result, focused drift-guard results, package contents, and link checks.

## Non-goals

- No change to re-frame2 framework semantics, API, capability tags, fixture expectations, eight-host scope, or React+VDOM boundary.
- No TypeScript reference implementation, second maintained runtime, cross-host compatibility layer, generated fixture translation, or generic conformance package.
- No new decision schema, progress database, report generator, session orchestrator, mandatory commit convention, or compatibility support for the old DECISIONS.md/report shapes.
- No exhaustive per-host recipe matrix or additional cardinal-rule prose; the Implementor Checklist and owning Specs retain those details.
- No weakening of conformance scoring, unknown-capability failure, spec-version checks, data-classification coverage, tooling security, or per-issue approval for upstream GitHub writes.
- No requirement to finish an entire second implementation inside the behavioural eval; the witness only needs to prove the compact start and first real feedback slice.
- No rewrite of sibling skills or the global skill routing taxonomy.

## Related beads

- rf2-ihw9q and rf2-hu5uz (closed) are direct historical evidence that copied Phase-2 implementation detail plus literal-token guards can preserve stale porting guidance.
- rf2-g9k0g (open) independently gives the application-authoring skill a closed verification loop; this task applies the same trust-the-explicit-invoker principle to a different product while retaining implementor-specific conformance.
- rf2-rc0yh (open) independently collapses the setup skill to one runnable default and a behavioural witness; coordinate only on shared skills/README.md policy wording.
- rf2-8jwb7 (open) independently removes migration paste-loop ceremony; coordinate only if verification-posture wording is edited concurrently.
- No existing open, deferred, or closed bead owns this implementor-skill profile/fixture-loop reduction.

title: surface-review(skill-xray): make one debugging question land on one first Xray surface
description:
## Scope

Treat skills/re-frame2-xray/** as one distinct published tour product. Make a concrete programmer question land quickly on the one existing Xray surface to open first, then reveal only the detail needed for that surface.

Rework the top-level skill, its panel references, README/package descriptions, eval material, and the small docs mirrors that restate the skill's routing contract. Preserve Xray's shipped two-mode UI and all current panels. Keep the actor boundary explicit: Xray is the visible human panel; re-frame2-pair is the agent-facing runtime reader and driver.

## Findings

1. The file that calls itself a “compact tour/router” is already an encyclopedia. skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md is 4,723 words / 33,441 bytes / 442 lines before any reference is loaded. A basic “which panel?” request passes through the Redux analogy, launch APIs, all hotkeys, the full 10-tab Dynamic table, the 5-tab Static table, chrome, exclusions, implementation ids, and retired-control warnings before reaching an answer.

2. Progressive disclosure does not reduce the expensive case. Every deep panel question routes to one references/panels.md catalogue: 6,380 words / 49,571 bytes / 853 lines. A one-panel question can therefore load 11,103 words / 83,012 bytes across SKILL.md plus panels.md. The repository's own leaf discipline is 250 lines / 16 KB unless a catalogue cannot be split profitably; this catalogue can be split along the existing question/scope seams, so one question need not pay for fourteen unrelated tabs.

3. Xray's useful information architecture is not adequately described by the first Dynamic-versus-Static fork. Six Dynamic tabs rebind to the focused epoch; Resources mixes process-global, observed-frame, and trace evidence; Graph, Frames, and Hicasso sit in the Dynamic shell but do not rebind to the selected epoch; Static catalogues are process-global with a few per-frame live projections. The skill knows this in its scope matrix, but the normal tour remains mode-first and inventory-first. A programmer starts with “what changed?”, “why did this render?”, “what is registered?”, or “where does this value come from?”, not with an internal tab roster.

4. The package has tab descriptions but no compact panel-tour gesture. The useful daily path is: choose frame, choose event when the question is event-shaped, start at Epoch, branch to state/render/raw/specialist evidence, and use Static only for definitions. docs/xray/02-panel-tour.md states a five-step version, but SKILL.md does not make it the entry path and neither surface handles the non-epoch Dynamic tabs cleanly. The result is a list of destinations instead of a fast route through them.

5. The Pair handoff is directionally right but its slogan is wrong. “Xray owns the seeing; Pair owns the driving” implies that a read-only live-runtime inspection belongs to Xray. Pair's actual first-contact sequence is discover-app → orient → targeted read, and it owns read-sub, get-path, snapshots, trace/epoch reads, DOM/UI reads, and Hicasso evidence as well as writes. rf2-7htk7 independently establishes the desired singular boundary: Xray for the human panel, Pair for programmer/AI runtime access. The Xray evals reject one write prompt (“dispatch this”) but have no negative read-only agent prompt.

6. The same volatile inventory and caveats are copied through SKILL.md, references/panels.md, references/shared-components.md, README.md, package.json, plugin.json, eval prose, skills/README.md, and docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md. Drift is visible now: the package README's scope sentence names Graph and Frames as non-epoch exceptions but omits Hicasso; docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md lists Esc as a focus-gated spine shortcut while the owning launch leaf says it is modal-local; docs/xray/index.md says every tab rebinds to the focused epoch, contradicting the current scope matrix. More copied warnings or prose locks will not make this easier to use.

7. The 30 evals mostly protect churn facts. Fourteen answer-quality cases pin launch calls, retired labels, exact tab counts, hidden mount facades, future hotkeys, and control precedence. Those facts have value, but there is no answer-quality route for the everyday Epoch, Views, Trace, Routes, Resources, or Hicasso questions; no read-only Pair disqualifier; no score for giving one first surface without dumping the whole inventory; and no check of which reference leaf was loaded. The harness is manual and records no observed end-to-end panel-tour result.

8. History confirms an accretion loop. The package has 69 commits since its May introduction and SKILL.md itself has 39. Commit b7798297d9 tried to tighten body ownership and add progressive disclosure, yet the body is now 4,723 words and its one panel leaf is 6,380. Commit 7cc83f0d8e / rf2-5atkk repaired the sharpest failure: the skill taught nine tabs while its own eval required ten and rejected a nine-tab answer. The next improvement should reduce the number of places that must move, not preserve the catalogue in more forms.

## Recommended Action

Rebuild the published tour around one question-first route card:

- First fork on actor and interface. “Where in the visible Xray panel do I look?” stays here. “Inspect or change my running app for me” routes to re-frame2-pair, whether the requested runtime operation is read-only or mutating.

Return the visible mode/tab label, why it is the first stop, and the first interaction (pick frame/event, open the tab, or flip Static). Name a second lens only when it is the natural next step.

A deep question about one panel family should load only that family, not all 15 tabs. Keep normative implementation anatomy in linked Xray specs/source rather than duplicating it into the tour.
- Strip internal ids, sparse order values, source-file inventories, deleted-panel archaeology, and repeated “do not invent” clauses from the normal path unless they disambiguate a live user-visible control. Trust programmers with direct current guidance.

Keep a small set of genuinely high-risk launch/control distinctions. Add no new runner, gate, policy layer, or generated compatibility table.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A concrete “where in Xray?” prompt returns one existing starting surface in the first paragraph: visible mode/tab, the reason, and the first interaction. It does not enumerate all 15 tabs unless the user asked for the inventory.
2. Representative route cases cover at least the existing focused-epoch, observed-frame/live-structure, process-global/registry, and Static-definition scopes. The answers preserve the shipped model: six focused-epoch lenses; Resources mixed; Graph/Frames/Hicasso non-epoch; Static definition catalogues process-global with their real per-frame projections. No new mode, panel, or aggregate is invented.
3. The panel-tour path is explicit and short: choose frame; choose an event only for event-shaped questions; start at Epoch for “what happened?”; branch to the exact state/render/raw/specialist lens; use Static for definitions. Non-epoch Dynamic surfaces do not pretend to follow the event.
4. The routing boundary is human panel versus agent runtime, not read versus write. A prompt asking the agent to inspect a running app routes to re-frame2-pair even when it requests no mutation; a prompt asking where a human should look in Xray remains in this skill.
5. Routine selection questions are answerable from SKILL.md alone. A deeper panel question loads SKILL.md plus at most one focused, one-level reference leaf that meets the repository's 250-line / 16-KB target. The PR reports before/after loaded words and bytes for one routine route and one deep-panel route; the 49,571-byte all-panels load is gone.
6. There is one canonical complete tab inventory and one canonical question-to-surface map inside the package. README, package/plugin descriptions, skills/README.md, and docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md summarize the role or link to that authority instead of copying detailed tab anatomy and exception rosters.

Current visible guidance is retained where it changes the user's action: inline versus overlay, the visible pop-out button, passive inspect versus Reset rewind, Graph's local projection versus top-level Static mode, and the absence of a dedicated Issues tab. Internal ids/order/source paths and retired alternatives are absent from the normal route unless the question asks for them.
8. Existing evals are revised rather than surrounded by a new framework. They grade concise first-surface routing across the scope families, a read-only Pair handoff, the explicit full-inventory request, and the focused-leaf load. The PR reports observed manual outputs for those cases.
9. The skill package and its small mirrors have a net reduction in prose and no contradictory scope/hotkey sentence among the touched surfaces. Existing JSON, package, link/anchor, skill-doc, and Xray tab-inventory checks pass; no new prose-presence test, linter, generator, or CI job is added.

## Non-goals

title: surface-review(skill-reagent-migration): teach only Hicasso's live read and navigation doors
description:
## Scope

Update skills/reagent-migration/** so the published skill teaches only the current post-dead-weight Hicasso authoring vocabulary at the two seams changed by rf2-6c12m.15:

- h/sub is the sole public subscription-read door.
- navigation is authored through h/route-link or ordinary routing events; the navigate intent head is implementation-owned and is not written as ::h/navigate.

Cover the distributable SKILL/references and the authoring-time spec/eval material that can reintroduce the old forms. Keep this a skill-only change.

## Findings

1. The skill violates its own cardinal rule 6 (“emit only what has shipped; read the door”). Current re-frame.hicasso exports h/sub and no h/use-subs, but references/mental-model.md and references/catalog-mechanical.md still teach h/use-subs as a deliberate control, while spec/inputs.md still rosters it as public.

2. The public navigate spelling also moved. rf2-6c12m.15 demoted the navigate head to re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate; h/route-link mints that internal value. references/gotchas.md still calls ::h/navigate one of two public reserved heads and says the draft guide is incomplete without it, while spec/authoring-prompt.md preserves that claim for the next reauthor. An authored ::h/navigate now resolves to a different keyword from the internal head and is not the shipped navigation contract.

3. This is high-friction in the failure direction. An AI following the read leaf can emit an unresolved h/use-subs call; one following the gotcha can emit a vector the current intent lowering does not recognize as its navigation head. The programmer is asked to choose between doors that no longer exist instead of using the single simple path Hicasso intentionally kept.

4. Progressive disclosure currently hides, rather than contains, the drift: the top-level router says “read the door,” but the false advice appears only when the relevant read/gotcha leaf is loaded. The eval corpus has no expectation that rejects either retired form, so its behavioural fixtures do not expose the contradiction.

5. This is recent history, not a request to redesign Hicasso. Commit 4c9fa03def (rf2-6c12m.15) removed h/use-subs as below the ergonomics bar and internalised navigation as part of the open dead-weight programme. Other same-wave skill updates carried hframe, native and defhost changes, but these six live teaching references remained.

## Recommended Action

Carry rf2-6c12m.15 into this skill directly:

- Teach repeated, conditional and looped reads as ordinary h/sub calls. Remove the grouped-read alternative rather than replacing it with another abstraction.
- Remove ::h/navigate from the author-facing marker/reserved-head vocabulary. Where navigation is relevant, point to h/route-link or a normal routing event; do not expose the internal intent value.
- Correct spec/inputs.md and spec/authoring-prompt.md so a future reauthor cannot resurrect either form.
- Add or amend one focused behavioural eval that grades the live outcome: h/sub is the only read emitted, and neither h/use-subs nor ::h/navigate is proposed.

Keep the explanation short. The outcome is fewer concepts and code that compiles against the current door, not a new compatibility story.

## Evidence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc: the current public door aliases h/sub and has no use-subs export.
- docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md, “Reads”: the complete current roster contains h/sub only.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:284: navigate-head is namespaced to the implementation.
- docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:68-80: route-link owns and mints that head; application authors do not.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/mental-model.md:84 and references/catalog-mechanical.md:61 still teach h/use-subs.
- skills/reagent-migration/spec/inputs.md:17 still lists use-subs on the door.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/gotchas.md:108,204 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:23 still teach ::h/navigate as public.
- git commit 4c9fa03def: “hicasso: drop h/use-subs, the grouped read control (rf2-6c12m.15)”.
- skills/reagent-migration/README.md says the skill is pre-alpha and has not been exercised end to end; the static eval set contains no retired-read/navigation control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No live instruction, source-of-truth roster, reauthoring prompt or eval expectation under skills/reagent-migration/** presents h/use-subs as callable or ::h/navigate as author-written.
- The read guidance has one direct answer: use h/sub at each read site, including conditional/loop/helper cases.
- Navigation guidance, if retained in this migration skill, uses only h/route-link or ordinary routing events and clearly leaves the opaque navigate head to Hicasso.
- A focused behavioural eval would fail an answer that emits h/use-subs or ::h/navigate and pass one that stays on the live public doors.
- Existing M/D/R routing, whole-view coherence, reporter/census workflow, compile/test verification and programmer-owned render check remain intact.
- JSON parses, skill/package structural checks pass, and the relevant markdown link/anchor gate passes. The handoff names the current public-door source that was checked.

## Non-goals

- No Hicasso runtime or public API change.
- No compatibility alias or shim for h/use-subs or ::h/navigate.
- No automated view rewrite engine, new linter, surface-sync gate or defensive policy.
- No broad API audit, catalogue expansion, reporter change, migration of application dataflow, or redesign of route-link.
- No unrelated polish or exhaustive wording sweep.

## Related beads

- rf2-6c12m.15 — exact landed facade-hygiene change this skill missed.
- rf2-6c12m — open Hicasso dead-weight epic; establishes the minimum-ceremony/trust-the-programmer direction.
- rf2-r3r00 — current complementary surface review reducing Hicasso’s clj-kondo export to useful macro-shape analysis; no dependency or overlap.
- rf2-r4j91 — original Reagent-migration retarget to Hicasso.
- rf2-0jl8s, rf2-6c12m.24, rf2-6c12m.30 and rf2-6c12m.13 — prior API changes successfully carried into this skill, useful history for the same bounded update pattern.

title: surface-review(uix-adapter): make a real UIx component test copy-pasteable and executable
description:
## Scope

Make the consumer-facing UIx component-testing path runnable from the public docs and easy to copy into a real app. Use the adapter's existing UIx/React primitives; cover the smallest honest real-DOM loop (mount a hook component under `frame-root`, drive an event, settle with `flush-views!`, assert the DOM, and tear everything down). Keep the executable witness close enough to the docs or generated scaffold that drift is caught.

## Verified Findings

- The UIx runtime surface is already substantial and well covered: `spec/api-manifest.edn:60-68` rows all nine public adapter Vars, and the adapter forwards a large shared React regression suite. This is not a request to redesign `use-subscribe`, `use-frame`, or frame scoping.
- The main view-testing guide is not substrate-neutral in practice. `docs/core/testing/views.md:5` says a view is a callable pure function returning hiccup and builds the whole recipe around JVM tree walking. A UIx `defui` that calls `use-subscribe` / `use-frame` is a React hook component and cannot use that recipe. The page's only UIx-relevant escape at line 93 says to use a real DOM and `flush-views!`, but supplies no mount, fixture, event, assertion, or cleanup shape.
- UIx's own public docs stop at the settling primitive: `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:178-191`, `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:263,273`, and `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:17` show `flush-views!` but no complete component test.
- The generated UIx app does not fill the gap. `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:272-274,309` emits only `events_test.cljs`; `_shared/events_test.cljs:5-7,24` explicitly runs DOM-free against a headless adapter. That is good dataflow coverage, but it teaches nothing about testing the UIx view the scaffold just generated.
- `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md:3,7,123-128` explicitly makes Test-React local-only, React-free, DOM-free, opaque-tree, and non-reconciling. It therefore cannot execute UIx hooks and is not a missing consumer test kit to point at.
- The desired flow already exists as framework evidence: `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` plus `testbed/spec.cjs` prove frame-root mount -> use-subscribe -> click/dispatch -> DOM rerender in a real browser. Commit `2d2f4aff53` introduced the per-adapter testbed; commit `b924dca1af` introduced the current hiccup-centric Test-a-view recipe. The missing work is to turn those two disconnected bodies of knowledge into one consumer-shaped, executable UIx recipe.

## Recommended Action

Publish one canonical, copy-complete UIx component test using existing APIs only. Put the explanation where a test author looks (`docs/core/testing/views.md` and the UIx adapter docs), point the generated UIx README at it, and back the exact shape with a focused browser-lane test or other named executable witness. Prefer a small fixture/helper local to the example over a new framework abstraction. The recipe should make lifecycle ownership obvious: one mount node/root, `frame-root` (or an explicitly created/scoped frame), a real DOM interaction, `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, an assertion, and guaranteed unmount/runtime cleanup.

## Concrete Evidence

- `docs/core/testing/views.md:5,93`
- `spec/008-Testing.md:36-48,107` (defines `flush-views!` and marks real React mounting CLJS-only, but illustrates only the Reagent call)
- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:178-191`
- `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:263,273`
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:272-274,309`
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/events_test.cljs:5-7,24`
- `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md:3,7,123-128`
- `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` and `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/spec.cjs`
- History: `2d2f4aff53` (adapter testbeds), `b924dca1af` (Test-a-view recipe), `9cf8f2e54c` (generated UIx mount/hot-reload lifecycle)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A copy-complete CLJS UIx test mounts a `defui` that uses `use-subscribe` and/or `use-frame` under a valid frame boundary, drives a real DOM event, settles through `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, observes the updated DOM, and guarantees unmount plus frame/adapter cleanup.
2. The published command for that test runs successfully in a named browser/DOM-capable lane; a focused executable test protects the recipe from API or lifecycle drift.
3. `docs/core/testing/views.md` explicitly distinguishes its fast hiccup-walk path from UIx hook components and links the runnable UIx recipe rather than implying the hiccup recipe applies.
4. The UIx adapter README/API and generated UIx project README make the first component-test path discoverable; the scaffold's existing DOM-free event/sub tests remain the recommended default for business logic.
5. The solution uses current public primitives. No new public helper namespace/API is added unless implementing the executable recipe demonstrates unavoidable repeated lifecycle machinery.

## Non-goals

- Do not publish or expand the internal Test-React adapter; it deliberately models class-3 lifecycle without React and cannot be made into UIx by adding shims.
- Do not build a Testing Library clone, add speculative compatibility layers, or create a full per-adapter test matrix.
- Do not change UIx hook signatures, frame semantics, adapter installation semantics, or the substrate contract.
- Do not require every generated project to run a browser suite by default if a documented, executable opt-in recipe gives the same low-friction path.

## Related beads

- `rf2-0c23j` (closed): ruled the `flush-views!` test door and documented its render-phase constraint.
- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed): repaired the generated UIx mount/hot-reload lifecycle; its one-root/after-load shape is the right lifecycle donor.
- `rf2-60aoj` (closed): established that Test-React intentionally omits React render flushing and is a different capability, not the UIx test path.

No matching open or closed bead was found by title searches for UIx testing/component tests and description searches across `uix`, `test-react`, `flush-views!`, `real DOM`, and `component test`.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, copy-complete UIx browser component test mounts a hook component under a frame boundary, drives a real event, settles with `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, asserts updated DOM, and guarantees cleanup; the exact recipe is executable in a named gate, is linked from the UIx adapter and generated-project docs, and the generic view-testing guide clearly routes UIx hook components to it. Existing public primitives are used unless the executable proof shows a helper is truly necessary.

Both successful paths finish with the flag forced to true; the async path also forces it false during polling. The shared React suite already demonstrates the bounded discipline at react_shared_suite.cljs:3280-3351: capture the previous value, use the required temporary state, restore it in guaranteed final cleanup. Apply that discipline locally to this recipe and its pinned docs block, preserving the false polling window and unconditional unmount; no public helper, abstraction, or broader test-harness redesign is owed. Premise verified at tip (set! at :61 and :155, no capture/restore). Bounded per the audit note; in-test restore assertion added as the durable control. Worker closes on PR-ready.
AUDIT PR #8798 (2026-08-31): REOPENED. The success-path value restoration works, but it is not failure-safe. mount! sets the global before flush-views! and returns cleanup ownership only afterward; if render or act throws, no mounted token exists and the prior flag is lost. unmount! restores only after flush-views! and node.remove, so an unmount or effect-cleanup throw skips the flag restore and, in the async .finally callback, done. This contradicts the copy-complete unconditional-teardown and exactly-as-found contract and does not carry the donor final-cleanup discipline. Keep the correction local and surgical: restore and remove through try/finally or catch around mount and unmount, ensure async done executes even when cleanup throws, and commit one sentinel pre-value regression so the check does not depend on the ambient runner already being non-true. Do not create a shared fixture or pursue rf2-3t2nq broad consolidation.
close_reason: AUDIT PR #8798 residual discharged by PR #8802: mount!/unmount! now restore the act flag and remove the node through try/catch-finally (failure-safe on render, unmount and effect-cleanup throws), the async done runs even when teardown throws, and one sentinel pre-value regression test (mount-unmount-hands-back-the-act-flag-it-found) pins the exactly-as-found restore independently of the ambient runner's flag. No shared fixture; no rf2-3t2nq consolidation. Docs pin block + two prose sentences moved in the same PR. title: surface-review(implementation-build): let Node discover the script test suite
description:
## Scope

Replace the hand-maintained file rosters behind `implementation/package.json`'s `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` with one canonical implementation-level JavaScript harness command. Cover the 42 conventionally named `implementation/scripts/*.test.cjs` files, the two intended out-of-tree `.test.cjs` support tests currently in the helpers chain, and the native-IME verdict self-test. Update the fast-PR, CI, documentation, and policy consumers that currently know the two-command spelling. Preserve each test file's behaviour, process isolation, and failure signal.

## Findings

The suite already has a complete naming convention but does not use it. `implementation/scripts/` contains 42 `*.test.cjs` files. `test:script-policy` names 34 of them one by one; `test:script-helpers` names the other 8, plus two out-of-tree `.test.cjs` files and one CLI `--self-test`. That is 45 literal `node` invocations across two 2,218-character package-script values. Every new conventional test needs a second registration edit to one contested JSON line.

The split has user-visible cost without an execution boundary. The fast spine and CI always chain both commands. `TESTING.md` records that running only the second half has already let a red through. `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` therefore pins the exact two-command string, and `implementation/scripts/_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs` parses `package.json` to assert that its own filename appears in the roster. These are guards around manual registration rather than product or test semantics.

History shows the mechanism repeatedly failing in the dark direction. Closed beads `rf2-z2xir`, `rf2-45ti9`, `rf2-9ayub`, `rf2-lr4id`, and `rf2-zu82n` each existed to append tests or self-tests that had landed but ran in no spine; their notes also record guaranteed conflicts because each insertion rewrote the same long `package.json` line. The recent bench retirement removed most exceptional flag-driven readers, leaving only one such CLI self-test in the current helpers command, so this is now a small simplification rather than a framework project.

CI pins Node 24. Node 24's built-in test runner discovers quoted `*.test.cjs` glob patterns, runs each matching file in an isolated child process, and treats the child's exit code as the file verdict; files are explicitly not required to use `node:test` internally. The existing standalone harness files can therefore retain their current code and output. `--test-concurrency=1` can preserve today's serial host-load posture.

## Recommended Action

Create one obvious command, `npm run test:scripts`, that uses the Node 24 test runner with quoted, repository-scoped glob patterns for the conventional `.test.cjs` populations and `--test-concurrency=1`. Keep `scripts/run-hicasso-native-ime-witness.cjs --self-test` as the one explicit prelude, or expose that verdict control through a tiny conventional `.test.cjs` wrapper; do not build a custom discovery runner.

Delete `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` rather than retain forwarding aliases. Point the fast spine, the `js-harness-self-tests` CI job, `TESTING.md`, and `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` at the single command. Remove self-enrolment assertions and comments that tell authors to edit `package.json`; adding a correctly named test file should be the registration act.

## Evidence

- `implementation/package.json:60-61` contains the two literal rosters: 34 policy files and 11 helper invocations.
- `rg --files implementation/scripts -g '*.test.cjs'` returns 42 files; all 42 occur exactly once across those two package scripts. The helper command separately names `core/test/re_frame/bench/lane_cache_wiring.test.cjs`, `hicasso/scripts/check_modules_compile.test.cjs`, and the native-IME `--self-test`.
- `TESTING.md:20` presents both names as one JS-harness tier; `TESTING.md:181-183` says they must be chained and records that running only the second let a red through.
- `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1489-1490` and `.github/workflows/test.yml:3131` duplicate the chained spelling; `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py:297` pins it as an exact regular expression.
- `implementation/scripts/_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs:203-208` checks its own textual enrolment in `test:script-policy`.
- Closed registration beads `rf2-z2xir`, `rf2-45ti9`, `rf2-9ayub`, `rf2-lr4id`, and `rf2-zu82n` document tests that existed but were not executed, plus contention on the one-line roster.
- Node 24 documentation lists `**/*.test.cjs` as a default discovery shape, recommends quoted globs for portability, and states that isolated test files are judged by process exit code without needing to use `node:test`: https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/test.html#running-tests-from-the-command-line
- Exact tracker searches for `node --test`, `auto-discover`, `test:script-policy`, `test:script-helpers`, `hand-register`, and `surface-review(implementation-build)` found no open, in-progress, or deferred bead owning this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- From `implementation/`, one documented `npm run test:scripts` command runs the same 44 `.test.cjs` files and the same native-IME verdict self-test that the two old commands run today, each exactly once.
- The command uses Node's built-in discovery over explicit repository-scoped globs, with process isolation and concurrency 1; it adds no dependency and no custom file-inventory runner.
- A temporary failing `implementation/scripts/*-negative-control.test.cjs` is discovered without editing `package.json`, makes the command exit non-zero, and is named in the failure output; removing it restores green. Record the red/green control in the PR.
- Baseline and replacement runs agree on the executed file population and preserve actionable stdout/stderr from a deliberately failing existing fixture or equivalent scoped mutation.
- `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` are removed, not retained as aliases. The fast spine, `js-harness-self-tests` CI job, `TESTING.md`, and fast-PR gap check all use the one canonical command.
- The self-enrolment assertion in `_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs` and stale comments telling authors to wire individual `.test.cjs` files into `package.json` are deleted or rewritten to describe convention-based discovery.
- The focused command passes on Windows and in the Node 24 Linux CI job without increasing test-file concurrency or introducing shared-fixture collisions.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting the 44 standalone test files to the `node:test` API or changing their assertion harnesses.
- Parallelising test files, changing their internal order, suppressing their diagnostics, or weakening exit-code handling.
- Auto-running every arbitrary `--self-test` mode in the repository; only conventional `.test.cjs` files are discovered, with the one current exceptional CLI control handled explicitly or wrapped conventionally.
- Folding CLJS, browser, JVM, API-manifest, bundle, benchmark, or rigorous-local suites into this command.
- Adding a watcher, third-party test framework, generated manifest, or new inventory/policy checker.

## Related beads

- `rf2-z2xir`, `rf2-45ti9`, `rf2-9ayub`, `rf2-lr4id`, and `rf2-zu82n` are closed instances of the manual-registration failure this task removes; none replaces this outcome.
- `rf2-fal5` is closed Windows host-load work inside `test:script-policy`; preserving serial process isolation respects that evidence but does not reopen or redesign the classifier suite.
- `rf2-6c12m.1` is the closed bench re-home/retirement that removed most exceptional helper registrations and made convention-based discovery a bounded change.
- No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead found in the tracker proposes replacing the two rosters with native Node discovery.

Edit only comments that INSTRUCT registration, not historical narration (30+ files mention it). HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/test.yml:3131 one line (nobody else on it); check release.yml too. title: surface-review(skills-shared): make every published skill own the instructions it ships
description:
## Scope

Treat `skills/shared/**` and every normal-operation reference, installer special case, packaging caveat, and structural gate that exists to support it as one non-skill product surface.

Make each published skill executable from the files its own package ships. Retire `skills/shared/` as a mandatory runtime dependency and put the few behavior-bearing instructions beside the consumer that actually uses them. Use a clean pre-alpha cut: no peer package, generated vendoring, fallback loader, or compatibility mode.

Sequence the improver side after `rf2-uhszv`, which already owns that product's one-pass local review contract. This task owns the remaining common-layer decision and the pair-retro, migration, pair, Xray, packaging, installer, and shared-test consequences; it does not reopen the improver review design.

## Findings

1. The three leaves do not share one kind of ownership. `retro-protocol.md` was extracted from Pair-retro for exactly two consumers, but it is a union of branches rather than a common denominator: code/session/error evidence, improver-only Edit gates, Pair-retro-only issue filing, aliased output slots, and per-consumer catalogue links. `rf2-uhszv` correctly gives improver its own workflow, leaving this supposedly shared protocol with one real consumer.
2. `issue-filing.md` has a useful two-line core, but centralization has not removed copies. Pair-retro and re-frame-migration link it; re-frame2-implementor deliberately carries a local recipe; Pair-retro's SKILL and issue template, migration's output format, implementor's cardinal rules, and `skills/README.md` all repeat summaries. A roughly 1,400-word generic recipe plus a dedicated all-consumer substring checker is more indirection than the operation needs: keep reviewed text out of shell argv, pass the body with `--body-file`, and use the consumer's known target/body shape.
3. `tool-pair-surfaces.md` openly describes itself as a pointer to authoritative owners, while `spec/Tool-Pair.md` already calls its own capability table the consolidated, complete contract and the Pair-MCP README owns the shipped tool catalogue. The shared projection has still needed 32 commits and once grew to about 3,700 words plus a 725-line token-pinning test before commit `6f0db8ca6b` slimmed it back. Pair and Xray can cite the actual owners; Pair-retro can route against the same table without another roster.
4. The distribution model is broken by construction. A skill package's `files[]` cannot include sibling `../shared/`, yet Pair-retro, improver, migration, Xray, and the private Pair package contain normal-operation shared links. Public package metadata still advertises npm/Agent Skill distribution. Commit `cd721eb179` chose README caveats and a 586-line package-reference guard instead of making the products self-contained; the caveats explicitly admit tarball/plugin installs silently lose the workflow or security boundary. Xray currently ships the shared lineage link but no equivalent link-only caveat, illustrating how even the caveat model drifts.
5. The consumer load path is expensive and conditional. Pair-retro's own SKILL is about 2,027 words; mandatory `retro-protocol.md` adds 2,189 before a domain leaf. Filing and upstream routing can add the other two shared leaves, bringing the shared baseline to about 6,541 words before Pair-retro's local analysis references. Much of that text restates approval, redaction, routing, and output rules already surfaced in the consumer.
6. Test ownership has inverted. The three protocol leaves are 250 lines / 34 KB; `skills/shared/tests/**` is 2,888 lines / 173 KB, with 60 tests in `retro_protocol_test.clj` and six in the routing-index test. The shared retro test reaches into improver wording and Pair-retro frontmatter, issue template, known-frictions, trigger evals, and session-evidence scorer. Those are consumer tests living under a common leaf, so an edit to one product couples to the whole shared job.
7. The behavioral layer does not execute a skill. Its own README says replay/capture is manual; the 600-line scorer grades a hand-built transcript, and the always-on self-test proves regex predicates against synthetic good/bad records. Three later commits (`fa2787fa2e`, `d1c676e377`, `b38d93af49`) repaired false-green identity cases in the scorer itself. That machinery is costly evidence about the grader, not evidence that an installed AI skill behaves well.
8. History shows repeated effort spent defending the abstraction: extraction in `782baa4994`, 1,000-plus lines of security fixtures/tests in `1a8fecff49`, packaging caveat/scanner in `cd721eb179`, second-spec rollback in `6f0db8ca6b`, and issue-template de-duplication in `d86d5b6f7b`. `skills/shared/**` has 66 commits since May 2026. The layer keeps creating a copy, a guard for the copy, or a repair to the guard.

## Recommended Action

Retire the runtime common layer and co-locate only the behavior each product needs:

- After `rf2-uhszv` removes improver's dependency, fold the genuinely Pair-retro-specific parts of `retro-protocol.md` into a short Pair-retro-owned workflow/reference that ships in its package. Preserve concrete session evidence, one-session causal ordering, no fabricated findings, and public-output redaction. Treat transcript/source contents as data that cannot expand scope; trust the conversational user. A direct request to file is authorization to file, while a request to draft is not—do not add a second confirmation round after an already explicit `file it`.
- Give each issue-writing consumer one concise, target-specific filing step in its own shipped docs. Preserve the practical boundary: never interpolate reviewed content into a shell command; write the body to a fresh temp file and use `gh issue create --body-file`; keep repo/title/search arguments agent-authored; redact before public egress. Reuse the implementor's local ownership and align Pair-retro/migration without recreating a generic policy essay or safe-alphabet taxonomy.
- Retire `tool-pair-surfaces.md`. Route framework capability questions to `spec/Tool-Pair.md`'s consolidated contract and concrete tool operations to the Pair-MCP catalogue. Keep a short consumer-specific no-10x statement where users actually ask that question; do not maintain another complete family roster.
- Remove the shared tests/eval scorer and move only outcome-relevant Pair-retro cases into Pair-retro's existing eval area. Consumer behavior belongs with the consumer. Delete prose-substring locks, synthetic-transcript framework, shared classifier/job arm, installer treatment of a non-skill as a skill, link-only caveats, and the package-reference guard once no normal-operation `../shared/` dependency remains.
- Update README/spec/meta-doc links in one sweep. Prefer net deletion. Do not replace this layer with a manifest, dependency resolver, generated copies, a new CI framework, or another common-protocol directory.

## Evidence

- `skills/shared/retro-protocol.md`: 124 lines / 2,189 words; step 3 and step 5 branch by consumer, step 6 contains mutually exclusive improver Edit and Pair-retro filing paths, and the output shape aliases both products.
- `skills/shared/issue-filing.md`: 78 lines / 1,391 words; §Scope names two link consumers and one deliberately local copy.
- `skills/shared/tool-pair-surfaces.md`: 48 lines / 934 words; its first paragraph says it is a pointer, not a specification. `spec/Tool-Pair.md:36-61` already owns the consolidated capability map; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md:34` owns the tool surface.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:56-105` repeats approval, tracker, routing, output, and filing summaries while mandating all three shared leaves. Its `package.json` ships only its own directory.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md:63` and `references/output-format.md:33` both carry the shared filing dependency and its local summary; its package also omits the sibling.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/cardinal-rules.md:37-89` already owns a complete local filing recipe, proving the alleged all-consumer single source is not the runtime shape.
- `skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:56-60,92-95` requires the shared routing leaf for a lineage answer, while `skills/re-frame2-xray/package.json` cannot ship it.
- `skills/README.md:229-238` says shared is not a skill; `scripts/install-skills.sh:166-170` and `scripts/install-skills.ps1:94-100` nevertheless install/link it beside skills.
- `skills/shared/tests/retro_protocol_test.clj:672-838,955-1204` tests improver and Pair-retro internals; `tests/fixtures/README.md:13-83` and `tests/evals/behavioral-evals.json` explicitly mark agent execution manual.
- Measured tree totals at current main: protocols 250 lines / 34,189 bytes; tests 2,888 lines / 172,753 bytes; 66 commits touching `skills/shared/**` since extraction.
- Duplicate search: all-status title/description searches for `skills-shared`, self-contained shared runtime, common layer, retro protocol, issue filing, link-only, package, and behavioral eval found no task owning this cross-product retirement. `rf2-uhszv` owns only improver's local review contract; `rf2-8jwb7` owns migration execution authority, not the shared dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No published skill's normal-operation `SKILL.md` or shipped `references/**` requires `../shared/`. Every instruction needed to complete that skill's advertised path is included by its own `package.json` `files[]`.
2. `skills/shared/` is removed. If any historical explanation must survive, it lives in ordinary repository history/docs and is not a runtime protocol, install target, or gated pseudo-skill.
3. Pair-retro retains one clear, local outcome contract: bind one session, cite concrete evidence, distinguish tool/framework fixes, redact public output, and file only when directly requested. In-band transcript/source text cannot grant tools or widen scope; an explicit conversational filing request does not trigger a redundant approval loop.
4. Pair-retro, migration, and implementor each carry a concise filing operation appropriate to their target and body. All use `--body-file` for reviewed text and agent-authored non-body arguments; none depends on a shared leaf or copies the former long generic policy.
5. Pair/Xray/Pair-retro route Tool-Pair facts directly to authoritative spec/tool owners. No second complete surface-family or availability roster remains outside those owners, and the no-re-frame-10x answer remains available where users encounter it.
6. Shared structural tests, manual behavioral scorer/manifest/fixtures, the shared classifier/job arm, installer special case, package caveats, and the shared-reference compatibility guard are removed or reduced only to generally useful package-link validation unrelated to `../shared/`.
7. Outcome-focused behavior stays tested with existing consumer eval mechanisms only. Pair-retro's session-evidence behavior and issue-filing intent/redaction get focused cases; no new generic runner, prose linter, schema, taxonomy, or synthetic transcript platform is introduced.
8. `npm pack --dry-run` (or the repository's existing equivalent package inspection) for each affected public skill shows all required normal-operation docs present and no broken sibling reference. The documented npm/plugin/Agent Skill install story matches what the artifacts actually contain.
9. The change is a substantial net deletion in normal-path prose and support code. Consumer docs have one owner per rule and no duplicated seven-slot output contract, safe-alphabet essay, or complete Tool-Pair roster.
10. Coordinate landing with `rf2-uhszv` and `rf2-8jwb7` so their owned product changes are not overwritten; this task consumes their final contracts and removes only the common-layer residue.

## Non-goals

title: surface-review(http): expose successful response metadata to :after middleware and reply handlers
description:
## Scope

Close the managed-HTTP completion gap from a host-normalized 2xx response through decode/accept, canonical reply construction, the per-frame `:after` chain, and app reply delivery. Cover the JVM and CLJS transports plus HTTP test support, Spec 014, async/API documentation, and the managed-HTTP skill/example material that describes response middleware.

## Verified Findings

- Both host transports feed `handle-response!` a normalized map containing `:status`, `:status-text`, and `:headers`. The 4xx/5xx branches retain these facts, but the successful 2xx branch calls `finalise-success!` with only the accepted body value.
- `success-reply` accepts only ctx plus value and builds a canonical success reply without HTTP response metadata. Therefore neither `:after` nor `:reply-to` / `:on-success` can observe status or headers for a successful request.
- Spec 014 and `docs/async/http-going-further.md` explicitly present rate-limit-header and Cache-Control parsing as `:after` use cases.
- The two motivating JVM tests do not verify that contract: their servers emit `X-RateLimit-*` and `Cache-Control`, while the interceptors hard-code `37`, `100`, and `600` after comments acknowledge that headers do not ride on the reply. The tests pass even if the emitted headers change or disappear.
- Searches of all current beads for response headers, success headers, rate-limit, HTTP metadata, ETag, Location, Cache-Control, and after-interceptor headers found no matching task.

## Recommended Action

Thread a minimal, documented successful-response metadata value through decode/accept and success finalization into the canonical reply's existing `:meta` family-extension slot. It should contain the actual numeric status, status text, and the transport's already-normalized header map; keep `:value` as the decoded-and-accepted application payload. Run `:after` over that canonical reply and deliver its result unchanged to the selected app target.

Use the existing cross-host header normalization and existing core reply `:meta` trace-elision path. Before trace egress, apply managed HTTP's immutable and app-declared sensitive-header carrier policy so exposing useful headers to app code does not expose `Set-Cookie`, auth tokens, or custom secret headers in traces. Let canned/route stubs opt into the same metadata shape without inventing metadata when it is omitted.

Rewrite the motivating middleware tests so they parse the headers actually emitted by the local server; do not retain hard-coded stand-ins.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1310-1450`: normalized response facts enter `handle-response!`; the success tail passes only `(:accepted outcome)` to `finalise-success!`.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:507-511` and `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:181-189`: success construction takes only the accepted value.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:1191-1239`: the server emits rate-limit headers, lines 1213-1214 admit headers are absent, and lines 1221-1224 hard-code the alleged parse result.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:1280-1313`: the Cache-Control server value is likewise replaced by a hard-coded map at line 1300.
- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:768,809-814` and `docs/async/http-going-further.md:38-40`: the public contract promises response-header parsing in `:after`.
- Commit `264dc7b352` introduced `:after` and both motivating tests together; blame/history show the stand-ins have not subsequently been replaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A successful live JVM request and a successful live CLJS request expose the actual response status, status text, and normalized headers at one documented location in the canonical reply seen by both `:after` and the app reply target; `:value` remains the accepted payload.
- The rate-limit and Cache-Control motivating tests read and parse the local server's real header values. Their assertions fail if those response headers are removed or changed without changing the expected parse.
- Cross-host tests pin the chosen normalized header shape, including a multi-valued header case, rather than introducing a second header representation.
- HTTP canned success and route-map stubs may supply optional response metadata so header-dependent `:after` code is testable without a network; absence remains minimal and does not fabricate lifecycle facts.
- Completion traces continue to use the shared canonical-reply elider, and tests prove built-in `Set-Cookie` plus an app-declared sensitive response-header carrier are redacted while ordinary response headers remain useful on-box. Per-call `:sensitive?` still redacts wire-bearing metadata as specified.
- Spec 014, async/API docs, and managed-HTTP skill/example material document the exact reply shape with one working header-parsing example. Manifest/conformance data is updated only if implementation introduces a new public var (the recommended shape needs none).
- Existing success decode/accept behavior, failure classification, retry, cancellation, frame routing, stale suppression, and reply-target semantics remain green on JVM and CLJS.

## Non-goals

- A Fetch/HttpClient response wrapper or host object in app state.
- New response-header parsing helpers, middleware registries, global mutable policy, or compatibility aliases.
- Upload/download progress, streaming bodies, cookie-jar behavior, or a fully realistic HTTP simulator.
- Duplicating body data or inventing status/headers for stub replies that did not supply them.

## Related beads

No matching current bead was found. Historical source/comments reference `rf2-uheqq` (the `:after` middleware work) and `rf2-ibksxg` (minimal canonical canned replies), but neither ID resolves in the current tracker; they are context, not dependencies.

Drop that surface. Dispatchable solo; owns spec/014 as its hot-zone file.

title: reg-interceptor registration coords never reach the interceptor-exception trace (Xray chip gap for the supported authoring form)
description: The Xray Epoch INTERCEPTOR (exception) row's jump-to-source chip reads :source-coord off the :rf.error/interceptor-exception trace tag; the router takes it from the interceptor map's :source-coord (interceptor.cljc error-record). reg-interceptor (the ONE supported authoring form, EP-0022) captures registration coords into the REGISTRY meta (interceptor_registry.cljc reg-interceptor* -> source-coords/merge-coords), but descriptor->interceptor lowers {:before/:after} descriptors through ->interceptor* WITHOUT threading those coords onto the built value — so an interceptor authored the supported way never gets the exception-row chip; only a VALUE registered at the migration boundary carrying its own :source-coord does. Until rf2-93sxp the ->interceptor macro was the de-facto route to a coord-carrying value (tests and the standard_epochs testbed used it); with the macro gone (PR #8791) those sites author with reg-interceptor descriptors and the testbed's exception-row chip degrades to plain text (the INTERCEPTORS registry-read step's chip is unaffected — spec 021:426 documents it off handler-meta). Candidate fix: descriptor->interceptor stamps :source-coord from the registration meta's coords (registry resolver, one site), making the chip work for the authoring form everywhere. Touches interceptor_registry.cljc + tests; check spec/009 and tools/xray/spec/021 wording. Named as within rf2-93sxp's non-goals ('no redesign of source-coordinate diagnostics'), hence this follow-up.

Regression pinned on the actual failing path (descriptor-authored throw -> trace :source-coord tag) plus factory/programmatic/framework/migration-precedence arms; control shown red with the threading removed, restore blob-hash-verified. tools/xray spec 021 unchanged - it already documents this behaviour; no spec/009 change needed.

title: surface-review(conformance-security): strip standardized oncommand from SSR HTML
description:
## Scope Close the current SSR static-markup handler-filter gap for the standardized lowercase `oncommand` attribute in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`, with focused coverage in the existing SSR escaping security suite. Keep the existing conservative attribute-name grammar and benign non-handler `on*` behavior. ## Correctness finding `attr-string` strips camelCase/kebab `on*` props structurally and lowercase handler names through a hand-maintained allowlist. The allowlist omits `oncommand`. Because `oncommand` is all lowercase, it misses the structural regex too, passes the attribute-name grammar, and is emitted verbatim into SSR HTML even though current browsers install it as executable inline JavaScript. This violates the documented invariant that server-rendered strings never carry live event-handler attributes. It is not speculative hardening: the current WHATWG HTML Standard names `oncommand` as an event handler content attribute, and the repository's installed Chromium executes it. ## Evidence - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:353-413`: the structural matcher catches only `on` plus uppercase or hyphen; lowercase names depend on `event-handler-allowlist`. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:369-397`: the lowercase allowlist contains nearby standardized handlers but no `oncommand`. - `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:591-621`: a prop not stripped is grammar-validated and serialized as an HTML attribute. - `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/ssr_escaping_security_cljs_test.cljc:22-174`: generated and named handler corpora do not include `oncommand`; the benign controls explicitly preserve `online`/`once`/`only`/`on`. - Current JVM probe: `(h/attr-string {:oncommand :pwned})` returns `" oncommand=\":pwned\""`. - Current bundled Playwright/Chromium probe: after loading `
`, dispatching `new Event('command')` reports `{"pwned":1,"handler":"function"}`. - WHATWG HTML Standard, GlobalEventHandlers/content-attribute list: `oncommand` is an event handler content attribute: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#global-attributes ## Failure scenario/invariant An SSR app spreads a user-controlled custom-attribute map into hiccup, the exact threat model documented beside `attr-string`. An attacker supplies the grammar-valid key `oncommand` and JavaScript as its value. Server rendering emits the inline handler. When a `command` event reaches that element, the browser executes the attacker's code before or independently of hydration. Invariant: every browser-recognized event-handler prop covered by the shipped SSR contract is absent from static markup in every HTML-equivalent casing, while benign non-handler names such as `online` continue to serialize. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. From `implementation/ssr`, require `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` and evaluate `(h/attr-string {:oncommand :pwned})`; observe that the returned HTML contains `oncommand` instead of the empty string. 2. Load `
` in the repository's bundled Playwright Chromium. 3. Set `globalThis.pwned=0`, dispatch `new Event('command')` on `#x`, and observe `globalThis.pwned` becomes `1` and `typeof x.oncommand` is `"function"`. ## Recommended minimal fix Add the standardized lowercase `oncommand` spelling to the existing event-handler allowlist and to the named/generated security corpus. Keep the current two-layer matcher and grammar; do not broaden it to all lowercase `on*` names, because the suite deliberately preserves benign attributes such as `online`, `once`, and `only`. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A focused CLJ+CLJS security regression passes `:oncommand`, `:ONCOMMAND`, and a mixed-case spelling with a string JavaScript payload through `h/attr-string`; each yields the empty string and contains neither the handler name nor payload. 2. An end-to-end `emit/emit-element` case renders a benign sibling attribute/text while omitting `oncommand` and its payload entirely. 3. Non-vacuity: the regression is demonstrated red on the current implementation by asserting the current exact survivor (`oncommand` is present in `attr-string`/emitted HTML); the same payload under a benign attribute is shown serializable so fixture/value omission cannot satisfy the test. 4. The existing `online`/`once`/`only`/`on` non-handler controls remain green, proving the fix did not replace the curated rule with an over-broad lowercase `on*` drop. 5. The focused SSR escaping security namespace passes on both JVM and the shared CLJS Node/security lanes. ## Non-goals - No CSP, sanitizer, DOMPurify, hydration, or renderer redesign. - No blanket rejection of programmer-authored inline script/style content. - No broad `on[a-z]` matcher that drops benign non-handler attributes. - No changes to client event binding or unrelated attribute/value escaping. ## Related/duplicate search Searched all bead statuses by `oncommand`, SSR event handler, event-handler, attribute allowlist, static markup, XSS, HTML, escaping, `ssr-invalid-attribute-name`, `html-helpers`, and description/notes matches. No bead owns this gap. The only in-progress bead is unrelated prose cleanup. `rf2-mocn3` is a distinct open SSR Form-2 arity bug; `rf2-qxg24` is a distinct test-tier changed-surface classifier task.

One-word allowlist add + security-corpus rows.
