title: Xray Trace drops every real FX argument by reading nonexistent singular tags
description:
## Scope

Repair the Dynamic Trace panel's FX target/detail projection in tools/xray. Scope is the raw-trace-to-row seam in day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.trace-helpers and its focused dual-target test. Reconcile the fixture with the framework's shipped FX vocabulary; do not redesign the panel.

## Findings

Correctness finding: target-detail reads :rf.fx/arg and :rf.fx/value, but the framework emits FX arguments under canonical :rf.fx/args. Every real :rf.fx/handled row therefore projects only its fx id, dropping the argument from the main target/detail column and hover title. The existing test is green because it fabricates the nonexistent singular :rf.fx/arg key.

## Evidence

- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:575-579 reads :rf.fx/arg / :rf.fx/value.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1234-1239 emits successful :rf.fx/handled rows with :rf.fx/id and :rf.fx/args. Exception, skipped-platform, and no-such-fx rows use the same plural key at lines 1455-1463, 1583-1601, 1617-1626, and 1651-1660.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/trace_collector.cljs:207-228 snapshots framework rings without renaming tag keys.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:853-884 writes target-detail directly to :target; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace.cljs:632-639 renders it in the target/detail column and hover title.
- tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:305-309 asserts the promised output using :rf.fx/arg, a shape no framework producer emits.
- tools/xray/spec/023-Trace-Panel.md:45-51 and line 264 promise fx-id -> arg in that column.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register :app/audit and return {:app/audit {:message "saved"}} from an event handler.
2. Dispatch the event and open Xray's Dynamic Trace panel on that event bundle.
3. Inspect the :rf.fx/handled row. The framework trace carries {:rf.fx/id :app/audit, :rf.fx/args {:message "saved"}}, but the target/detail cell and hover title show only :app/audit.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The payload distinguishing one effect invocation from another is absent from the primary diagnostic unless the operator expands raw EDN. When an FX trace row contains canonical :rf.fx/args, projected :target must include that exact value after pr-str-safe; when the key is absent, the row stays id-only. Key presence, not truthiness, is the distinction because false and nil are valid effect arguments.

## Recommended Action

Make the FX branch read canonical :rf.fx/args and distinguish an absent key from present false/nil with contains? or an equivalent sentinel. Replace the singular-key fixture with producer-shaped tags. Keep the id-only fallback for rows that genuinely omit arguments.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A focused test passes a producer-shaped :rf.fx/handled event with {:rf.fx/id :app/audit, :rf.fx/args {:message "saved"}} through target-detail or project-row and asserts :app/audit -> {:message "saved"}. The fixture explicitly contains neither singular key; this non-vacuity check fails on the current implementation.
2. The same table proves present false and present nil render as -> false and -> nil, while a control row with no :rf.fx/args renders only :app/audit. This pins key presence rather than a truthiness shortcut.
3. No production Xray code or focused test relies on the nonexistent singular FX argument tags.
4. From tools/xray, clojure -M:test -n day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.trace-helpers-cljs-test passes, and the CLJS node-test lane containing the same .cljc namespace passes.

## Non-goals

- No Trace layout, expansion, filtering, stage, or colour changes.
- No framework trace-schema change and no compatibility aliases for invented singular keys.
- No broad audit of other op families or historical fixture cleanup.
- No work on the separate Xray runtime retirement tracked by rf2-7htk7.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title searches for effect args, fx args, trace panel, target detail, target/detail, rf.fx, and effect detail found no owner. All-status description and notes searches for :rf.fx/args, :rf.fx/arg, target/detail, effect argument, fx argument, Trace panel, trace_helpers, and trace helpers also found no issue. Open rf2-tq26u concerns interceptor registration coordinates on exception traces, not FX argument projection. Open rf2-7htk7 retires the unused Xray agent runtime; it explicitly does not own the human Trace panel.

1. A producer-shaped :rf.fx/handled event carrying only :rf.fx/id and canonical :rf.fx/args projects the documented fx-id -> arg target; the assertion is red on the current singular-key reader.

3. Singular :rf.fx/arg / :rf.fx/value fixtures and production reads are absent from the focused Xray trace surface.
4. The focused JVM namespace and its CLJS node-test lane pass.

title: check-examples-assets: missing main.js bootstrap passes the host-page gate
description:
## Scope

The monorepo example host-page contract in examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs and its focused executable coverage in implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs. Cover every index.html and *.index.html already enumerated by listExampleIndexHtml, including ordinary apps, auxiliary Story hosts, and baked SSR/hydration hosts. Do not change application source, the staging runner, or the test-free examples policy.

## Correctness finding

The gate proves that every example host references the shared favicon, OG raster, and stylesheet, but it does not prove that the host loads the compiled application entrypoint. BUILD_OUTPUTS contains main.js only so reference resolution can skip a generated file; absence is never an error. A host with the only <script src="main.js"></script> line deleted therefore passes the live asset scan even though the canonical runner stages and serves a page that cannot boot, render, or hydrate.

This is a cross-example false green rather than a cosmetic metadata gap. The same miss applies to all host shapes the scanner advertises as covered. The independent compile gate compiles shadow-cljs build definitions and never consumes their HTML, while headless example wrappers require namespaces directly and likewise do not prove that a browser host loads main.js.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a disposable checkout, remove the <script src="main.js"></script> line from examples/core/counter/index.html while leaving its favicon, stylesheet, and og:image references intact.
2. Run node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs. It still reports all example host pages plus the shared tree as valid and exits 0.
3. Run node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs. Its live scan also remains green because it asserts only the errors produced by the same production scanner.
4. Launch the counter through the canonical dev:example runner. The staged index has no bundle entrypoint, so the browser shows no counter and executes none of counter.core/run.

The failure is reproducible without editing the checkout by wrapping fs.readFileSync for one real page, returning its contents with the main.js script removed, and passing that io to scanPage. That exact read-only probe returned errors=[] for examples/core/counter/index.html, examples/core/login/stories.index.html, and examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/index.html.

## Evidence

- examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs:201-209 defines REQUIRED_SHARED_ASSETS as favicon.svg, og.png, and style.css only.
- Lines 298-300 define BUILD_OUTPUTS = new Set(['main.js']) solely to avoid resolving generated output as a repository source file.
- Lines 558-663 already classify <script src> references distinctly in the shared HTML inventory, so the scanner has the information needed for a precise boot check.
- Lines 1517-1524 skip main.js during local resolution; lines 1539-1563 enforce only REQUIRED_SHARED_ASSETS. No later scanPage branch requires a script entrypoint.
- Lines 1904-1911 run that same scanPage logic over every enumerated host. The live regression at implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs:308-316 therefore inherits the omission.
- All 32 currently enumerated hosts contain a main.js script reference, which establishes a uniform current invariant rather than an exception-driven policy.
- Removing the script in memory from one ordinary host, one *.index.html Story host, and one SSR host produced only the three remaining shared refs and zero scanner errors in each case.
- examples/TESTING.md:17-20 separates compile, headless CLJS, browser-DOM, and static asset gates. None of those other lanes visits every example host page.

## Failure scenario / invariant

Every monorepo-staged example host must contain a load-bearing script reference to the generated main.js entrypoint. If that reference is deleted, commented out, or changed into a non-loading href, the host is not runnable and the always-run host-page gate must fail. Merely mentioning main.js in an anchor, canonical link, preload, comment, or other generic href must not satisfy the invariant; the proof must come from the existing tagged <script src> inventory.

Without this invariant, an index-only change can merge with a green compile, green headless tests, and green asset scan while the documented one-command runner deterministically serves a blank or non-hydrating page.

## Recommended minimal fix

Reuse extractHtmlReferenceInventory's existing assets rows and add one explicit scanPage check for a tagged <script src> whose normalized ref is main.js. Report the host path and missing entrypoint. Keep BUILD_OUTPUTS' current resolution exemption: generated main.js should be required as a host reference, not looked up in the source tree.

Add one focused synthetic mutation test plus a tag-specific negative control. No parser replacement, build-to-page registry, browser matrix, or new gate is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. scanPage reports a clear violation naming the page and main.js when an otherwise valid host carries every shared asset but has no <script src="main.js">.
2. The check consumes the existing tagged asset inventory: <a href="main.js">, <link href="main.js">, text, and commented-out script markup do not satisfy it.
3. A canonical quoted or unquoted <script src="main.js"> remains green, including the scanner's existing query/hash normalization behavior; main.js remains exempt from source-file existence resolution.
4. A focused test mutates a real currently enumerated host in memory by removing only its live main.js script, asserts the mutation actually removed one script, and proves the production scan turns red. This is the non-vacuity control and must fail against the pre-fix implementation.
5. The live test enumerates a non-empty host set and proves every current index.html and *.index.html passes the new invariant; ordinary, auxiliary Story, and SSR hosts are represented without hard-coding a second build roster.
6. node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs, node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs, and npm run test:script-policy from implementation pass after the fix.

## Non-goals

- Running every example in Playwright or asserting application-specific DOM behavior.
- Resolving generated main.js as a repository source file or inspecting its bytes.
- Supporting alternate legacy bundle names, optional entrypoints, or a generalized HTML/build manifest when every current host uses main.js.
- Changing example apps, shared CSS/images, launch documentation, shadow-cljs builds, or staging behavior.
- Replacing the focused HTML inventory with a general-purpose parser.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status beads for main.js example host, script src main.js, missing main.js, example host page, blank example page, check-examples-assets build output, entrypoint host page, runnable example HTML, and examples asset gate. A full all-status scan of 1,127 issue titles, descriptions, and acceptance fields for main.js, script src, blank page, host page/HTML, example asset, runnable example, and entrypoint found no issue enforcing this invariant.

Open rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 address stale core/capability README commands and prove the existing dev runner can stage a complete page; they do not make the host scanner reject a missing boot script. Open rf2-fmns2 adds a distinct Hicasso example and bundle-isolation coverage. None is a duplicate or owns this scanner/test slice.

## Priority rationale

P2. The repository is pre-alpha and every current host is intact, so this is not an active production outage. However, one ordinary HTML-line deletion breaks the primary runnable-example contract across every example family while all mandatory gates that claim compile/host coverage remain green. The fix is small, central, and directly restores trust in an existing always-run gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- scanPage rejects an otherwise valid host that lacks a live tagged <script src="main.js"> and names both the page and entrypoint.
- Generic hrefs, preload links, text, and commented script markup containing main.js do not satisfy the requirement.
- Quoted and unquoted live main.js script references remain accepted, and generated main.js is still not resolved as a source file.
- A focused in-memory mutation of a real enumerated host removes exactly one main.js script and turns the production scanner red; the control fails on the pre-fix implementation.
- The non-empty live host inventory, including ordinary, Story auxiliary, and SSR hosts, remains green.
- The focused scanner test, scanner CLI, and implementation test:script-policy gate pass.
notes:
--- 2026-09-01 AUSEST — implemented, PR #8855 ---

FINDING CONFIRMED at tip before implementing. A read-only in-memory probe over
the real tree (wrapping readFileSync for one page, returning it with the live
main.js script removed) returned errors=[] from the pre-fix scanPage, and the
CLI still printed "all 32 pages resolve their assets and carry the required
_shared contract". The gate proved every host was DRESSED (favicon + OG raster +
stylesheet) but never that it could RUN.

FIX. scanPage gains one check reading the EXISTING tagged asset inventory for a
live <script src> whose normalised ref is main.js (new exported predicate
loadsBuildEntrypoint, a pure function over the `assets` view). No new parser, no
build-to-page manifest. Because the proof comes from the tagged view rather than
raw HTML, a mere mention does not satisfy it: preload/modulepreload links are
tagged as links not scripts, <a href> and rel=canonical never reach `assets` at
all, prose is not a tag, and commented markup is stripped before extraction.
BUILD_OUTPUTS' resolution exemption is UNCHANGED — main.js is required as a page
REFERENCE and still never resolved as a source file. Quoted/single-quoted/
unquoted forms and the existing ?query/#hash normalisation all stay green.
The CLI failure epilogue now names the boot-script cause too.

CONTROL (AC4). The non-vacuity control mutates a REAL enumerated host in memory,
one per host shape, with the shape classified from the ENUMERATED PATH rather
than a second hard-coded build roster (which could drift from
listExampleIndexHtml). It asserts exactly one script element was removed — by
byte length AND against the scanner's own inventory in both directions — then
proves the production scanner turns red for that reason alone (errors.length===1).

RED-BEFORE EVIDENCE. The check was neutralised at its scanPage call site to
reproduce the pre-fix implementation: captured exit 1, 9 failures, all of them
the new boot-contract tests; the control reported "(no errors — the pre-fix
false green)" and the CLI under the same plant still printed "all 32 pages …
valid". The other 157 assertions passed under the plant, so the fault was scoped
and stopped no other namespace. Restored and verified by git blob hash against
the committed object, not by reading a diff. An earlier plant that neutralised
the shared helper instead was discarded: it tripped the control at its inventory
assertion rather than at the production scan — weaker evidence.

GATES (foreground, exit codes captured to file, final rebased base 4e27fbbe49):
  node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs  -> exit 0, 166 PASS / 0 FAIL (18 new)
  node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs             -> exit 0, all 32 hosts green
  npm run test:scripts (from implementation/)                 -> exit 0, 122 tests / 122 pass / 0 fail

AC6 PREMISE FAILURE — worth carrying forward. AC6 names `npm run
test:script-policy` from implementation. THAT SCRIPT DOES NOT EXIST, neither on
this branch's base nor on origin/main (no key matching /polic/ in
implementation/package.json in either). The covering gate for
implementation/scripts/*.test.cjs is `npm run test:scripts`, which is what ran;
it executes the focused suite as one of its files (18 new assertions confirmed
present in its log). Future beads citing this gate should name test:scripts.

LIVE SET. 32 enumerated hosts, every one carrying exactly one
`<script src="main.js">` — 30 ordinary index.html (three of them the baked
SSR/hydration hosts under examples/capabilities/ssr/) plus the two Story
auxiliary *.index.html showcase hosts. Uniform invariant, not an
exception-driven policy.

NON-GOALS HONOURED: no application source changed, no staging-runner change, no
example index.html edited (the mutation is in-memory only), examples stay
test-free, no alternate/legacy bundle names or generalised HTML/build manifest,
main.js bytes never inspected.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8855 (commit 23be46c684) — scanPage now requires a live <script src=main.js> read off the existing tagged asset inventory; BUILD_OUTPUTS' resolution exemption unchanged. Control mutates a real enumerated host in memory per host shape and proves the production scan turns red; verified red against the pre-fix implementation (9 failures, control reporting '(no errors — the pre-fix false green)'). Gates: focused suite exit 0 (166 PASS), live scan exit 0 (32 hosts), npm run test:scripts exit 0 (122/122). NB AC6's 'npm run test:script-policy' does not exist on origin/main; the covering gate is 'npm run test:scripts' — see notes.

title: surface-review(machines-viz): make registered topology one-click copyable as Mermaid
description:
## Scope

Complete the existing Mermaid workflow from tools/machines-viz's pure `day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.mermaid/emit` function to Xray's existing Static Machines definition-detail header. Add one accessible, direct "Copy Mermaid" action for the currently selected registered machine, focused integration coverage, and the small documentation update that makes the workflow discoverable. Keep `MachineChart` presentation-only: the Xray host already owns the selected definition and owns the user gesture.

## Findings

Machines-Viz has a mature producer but no reachable workflow. `mermaid/emit` accepts the normalised definition and returns a fenced `stateDiagram-v2` block; its dedicated corpus covers grammar, validation, parallel/compound topology, and lossy-semantics warnings. `export/copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` also exists, but its DOM-element contract is an exporter convenience rather than a host-level action.

The repository has no production call site for either `mermaid/emit` or `copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` outside Machines-Viz itself. Xray's own machine-inspector spec still labels "Copy machine as PNG / SVG / Mermaid" as "Not built". Consequently a capability explicitly described for README files, pull requests, design docs, and AI-pair chat is available only to someone who writes CLJS around the library API.

The lowest-friction host is already present. Xray's Static Machines surface is the event-independent browse of every registered machine; its definition-detail view already subscribes to the selected machine's exact definition and renders a compact header containing its id, source coordinate, state count, and live count. Mermaid is static topology, so this is a better fit than the Dynamic Machine panel's deliberately narrow three-part forensic view.

The other shipped routes do not close this gap. The share viewer is an inbound, read-only URL consumer; it must be built and self-hosted, and share encoding requires an explicit host because there is no Day8 deployment. The manifests expose tests and a viewer build but no end-user command or standalone launch path. Xray's panel gallery and machine-epochs testbed provide rich visual fixtures, yet neither exposes the Mermaid exporter.

History makes the disconnect explicit: rf2-deo2i shipped the emitter, rf2-sqhqu moved ownership into Machines-Viz, and rf2-8d7w1 shipped the export/viewer primitives. rf2-nugvv later removed Xray's heavy Share modal and URL/session-posture machinery, leaving the copy formats recorded as unbuilt. Reintroducing that modal would repeat the wrong abstraction; a single explicit copy action needs none of it.

Exact tracker searches for "machines-viz", "Copy machine", "Mermaid export", "machine mermaid", "machine topology", "standalone viewer", and related terms found no existing bead for this outcome.

## Recommended Action

Add one "Copy Mermaid" control to the selected machine's Static Machines detail header. On activation, pass the selected definition directly to `mermaid/emit` and copy that exact fenced string through a small, testable clipboard effect. Do not make the renderer rediscover registry state and do not require a rendered chart DOM node.

Make the gesture immediate: no confirmation modal and no format chooser. Give it a clear accessible name and a minimal non-modal success/failure status so a rejected or unavailable clipboard does not look successful. Omit or disable the action when no valid definition is available.

Use an existing representative Static Machines/panel-gallery fixture for the integration proof. Assert the clipboard payload equals `(mermaid/emit definition)`; the emitter's existing corpus remains the authority for diagram semantics.

Update the Machines-Viz and Xray documentation just enough to name this as the normal path for copying a registered topology into Markdown or an AI conversation, and replace the stale "Not built" statement for Mermaid only.

## Evidence

- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/mermaid.cljc:946` defines the pure `emit` API and its fenced Markdown contract.
- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/export.cljs:561-589` defines the chart-element wrapper and clipboard helper.
- `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:2078-2099` says Mermaid output is for GitHub, PRs, Notion, and other Mermaid-aware consumers and identifies `mermaid/emit` as the load-bearing pure function.
- `tools/machines-viz/spec/000-Vision.md:284-300` explicitly names README and AI-pair chat replies as the static Mermaid surface.
- A repository-wide source search finds no production use of `mermaid/emit`, `chart-as-mermaid`, or `copy-mermaid-to-clipboard!` outside Machines-Viz; references elsewhere are documentation only.
- `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:1829-1842` explicitly marks the copy-as formats "Not built".
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/definition_detail.cljs:52-90` is the existing selected-machine header, and lines 209-254 already hold the selected definition in the host view.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/panel.cljs:110-161` composes registered ids, definitions, snapshots, and selection for that surface; no new registry query is needed.
- `tools/machines-viz/README.md:95-160` documents that the viewer must be built and hosted by the consumer and that `:host` is required for a share URL.
- `tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/mermaid_cljs_test.cljc` is a 943-line semantic corpus, while Xray already has focused Static Machines panel tests and panel-gallery machine fixtures; the missing test is the one host-to-export gesture.
- Git history: d737346b4b (rf2-deo2i), ab4d4597d9 (rf2-sqhqu), 9644e0b4d8 (rf2-8d7w1), 2107f8096d (rf2-nugvv), and ee9ba1bed0 / a06227b68c / 8cef711d18 (rf2-8m344) establish the producer, ownership, removed modal, and self-host-only viewer posture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a valid selected definition in Xray Static -> Machines, one obvious "Copy Mermaid" gesture writes exactly `(mermaid/emit definition)` to the clipboard as a fenced Markdown block.
- The action uses the definition already owned by the Static Machines host. `MachineChart` gains no registry subscription, new data prop, global state, or built-in toolbar.
- The copied text is static topology only: it does not depend on the current live snapshot or trace history and does not include runtime or definition `:data` values. Existing emitter caveats for lossy runtime semantics remain intact.
- No selected/valid definition means no actionable copy control; the empty and malformed-definition paths remain stable.
- Success and clipboard rejection/unavailability produce small, accessible, non-modal status feedback. A failed write is never reported as copied.
- A focused CLJS integration test stubs the clipboard boundary, activates the real control, and asserts the exact emitter output and one write. It also covers the unavailable/rejected clipboard path and the no-definition gate.
- An existing Static Machines panel-gallery fixture exposes the action for manual/browser inspection; no new testbed application or launch mode is introduced.
- Machines-Viz README/API text and Xray's machine-inspector spec identify the Static Machines action as the normal Mermaid workflow and no longer claim the Mermaid copy path is unbuilt.
- Focused Machines-Viz Mermaid tests and Xray Static Machines tests pass, with the relevant changed-surface scheduling preserved.

## Non-goals

- PNG, SVG, share-URL, SCXML, or new export formats.
- Restoring rf2-nugvv's Share modal, URL/session-posture restoration, cascade export, a context-menu hierarchy, or a format picker.
- A hosted viewer, deployment workflow, saved-chart registry, paste-and-render playground, visual editor, or SaaS surface.
- A CLI, MCP tool, framework-level `machine->mermaid` compatibility shim, or duplicate emitter.
- New chart styling, layout heuristics, animation, overlays, simulator modes, or testbed applications.
- Copying raw machine EDN, runtime `:data`, traces, app-db, source coordinates, or session state.
- Compatibility scaffolding for the removed Share surface.

## Related beads

- rf2-deo2i (closed/historical) shipped the Mermaid emitter.
- rf2-sqhqu (closed/historical) made Machines-Viz the emitter's owner.
- rf2-8d7w1 (closed/historical) shipped the export, share codec, and viewer primitives.
- rf2-nugvv (closed/historical) removed Xray's Share modal and URL/cascade infrastructure; this task must not restore that surface.
- rf2-8m344 (closed/historical) corrected the nonexistent hosted viewer and established the explicit self-host posture.
- rf2-v4xjh (in progress) simplifies pure machine-transition results; it is adjacent machine-tooling work but does not expose topology or overlap this host action.
- No matching open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead for a reachable Mermaid-copy outcome was found.

title: reagent-slim: Form-3 docs misstate the lifecycle callback argv
description:
## Scope

Correct the public Form-3 lifecycle bridge in implementation/adapters/reagent-slim so the supported create-class callbacks receive the stock-Reagent/IMPL-SPEC argument shape. Scope is limited to reagent2.impl.component, focused reagent-slim lifecycle tests, and the directly contradictory reagent-slim contract/example prose.

## Correctness finding

install-lifecycle! discards React's prevState argument in both paired update lifecycles. It invokes :get-snapshot-before-update as (f this prev-argv) and :component-did-update as (f this prev-argv snapshot), while the published contract and pinned stock Reagent 2.0.1 invoke them as (f this prev-argv prev-state) and (f this prev-argv prev-state snapshot).

This is an implementation defect, not merely stale prose: reagent-slim presents create-class as the bounded Reagent-compatible Form-3 surface and its migration path promises a namespace-only rewrite for retained surfaces. The current bridge makes the documented fixed-arity callbacks fail at runtime and makes variadic callbacks observe shifted/missing lifecycle data.

## Evidence

- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:444-460 receives React prev-props, prev-state, and snapshot, names prev-state _prev-state, then drops it from both user callback calls.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/component_cljs_test.cljs:363-410 pins the incorrect reduced shape: three user args for :component-did-update and two for :get-snapshot-before-update. It never supplies a documented fixed-arity callback, so the test suite protects the bug.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:632-673 specifies getSnapshotBeforeUpdate(prevProps, prevState), componentDidUpdate(prevProps, prevState, snapshot), and explicitly shows user-fn receiving this plus all three React values.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md:21-23, 96-120, 255-318, 495-533 and implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/README.md:27-37 teach the three-/four-argument callbacks. The worked examples are copy-pasteable fixed-arity functions that the current bridge calls at the wrong arity.
- implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15 pins stock Reagent 2.0.1. Reading that jar's reagent/impl/component.cljs custom-wrapper shows :getSnapshotBeforeUpdate calling f with c, props-argv, oldstate and :componentDidUpdate calling f with c, props-argv, oldstate, snapshot.
- Focused readings used: rg over the lifecycle symbols in source/tests/docs; git blame over component.cljs:444-460 and the paired tests; in-memory inspection of the pinned Reagent jar entry. No repository files were changed.

## Failure scenario/invariant

A user follows FORM-3.md and defines:

    :get-snapshot-before-update
    (fn [this prev-props prev-state] ...)

    :component-did-update
    (fn [this prev-props prev-state snapshot] ...)

On the first React update, slim calls the first function with two arguments, causing a CLJS invalid-arity exception before the snapshot can be captured. If only :component-did-update is present, slim calls its four-argument function with three arguments and raises during the post-commit lifecycle. A variadic workaround is not semantically safe either: the snapshot currently occupies the prev-state position and the true prevState value is unrecoverable.

Invariant: every retained Form-3 callback must preserve the documented stock-Reagent argument order and cardinality; the wrapper may translate prevProps to prev-argv, but it must not discard or shift React lifecycle values.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a reagent2.core/create-class whose :get-snapshot-before-update is a fixed three-argument function and whose :component-did-update is a fixed four-argument function, exactly as FORM-3.md and README.md show.
2. Mount it, then render the same component with changed argv so React invokes getSnapshotBeforeUpdate(prevProps, prevState) and componentDidUpdate(prevProps, prevState, snapshot).
3. Observe that the slim wrapper calls the user functions with only two and three arguments respectively. CLJS raises an invalid-arity error; with a variadic probe, prevState is absent and snapshot is shifted into its slot.
4. As a source-level reproducer, call the installed prototype methods with distinct prevProps, prevState, and snapshot sentinels; the current component_cljs_test shape demonstrates the omission by accepting only the reduced arities.

## Recommended minimal fix

Thread prev-state through the two existing wrappers:

- :get-snapshot-before-update user callback receives this, prev-argv, prev-state.
- :component-did-update user callback receives this, prev-argv, prev-state, snapshot.

Update the focused tests from the reduced arities to the public contract and reconcile the local source comments. Keep the current prevProps-to-prev-argv translation, current-component binding, snapshot return/forwarding, cap, and React method installation unchanged. Align any directly contradictory README/FORM-3/IMPL-SPEC snippets only as needed so there is one executable contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused component test invokes the installed getSnapshotBeforeUpdate wrapper with distinct prev-argv and prev-state sentinels and proves a documented three-argument user callback receives this, the exact translated prev-argv, and the exact prev-state in order, then returns a non-nil snapshot sentinel.
- A focused component test invokes componentDidUpdate with distinct prev-argv, prev-state, and snapshot sentinels and proves a documented four-argument user callback receives all four values in order and under the correct current-component binding.
- Non-vacuity/control: the regression uses fixed-arity three-/four-argument CLJS callbacks and asserts callback counts plus sentinel identity. It must fail on the current implementation by invalid arity or missing sentinel, rather than passing through a variadic callback that tolerates omission.
- A mounted React update proof exercises reagent2.core/create-class through the real lifecycle path: changed argv commits, both paired callbacks fire, the snapshot reaches :component-did-update, and no invalid-arity error is reported. The proof asserts the update actually occurred so a skipped lifecycle cannot read green.
- Existing Form-1/Form-2 behavior, snapshot return semantics, lifecycle current-component binding, and the seven-key cap remain green.
- README.md, FORM-3.md, IMPL-SPEC.md, source comments, and tests agree on (this prev-argv prev-state) and (this prev-argv prev-state snapshot).

## Non-goals

- Adding any lifecycle key beyond the existing seven-key cap.
- Preserving the current pre-alpha reduced callback arities with overloads or compatibility shims.
- Exposing raw React prevProps instead of the established prev-argv translation.
- Redesigning component state, shouldComponentUpdate, error-boundary behavior, batching, or the ratom kernel.
- Broad stock-Reagent API parity work outside these two retained callbacks.

## Related/duplicate search

Searched all bead states and the exported issue/interaction corpus for reagent-slim lifecycle, component-did-update, componentDidUpdate, get-snapshot-before-update, prev-state/prevState, oldstate, and Form-3 arity. No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed issue owns this finding.

- rf2-b9l8o is the closed reagent2.core/reaction macro compatibility fix; it is a different public symbol and failure.
- rf2-iogzk is the closed FORM-3 imperative-subscription scheduling/ownership prose fix; it does not cover lifecycle arguments.
- Historical rf2-8u8tx broadly reviewed adapters and mentioned the component layer but filed only the distinct expand-seq truncation and use-subscribe acquisition issues; it neither identified nor owns this mismatch.

title: http: abort during body preparation can still issue the JVM request
description:
## Scope

The managed HTTP request lifecycle in `implementation/http`, specifically the boundary from body-thunk realization / encoding to the JVM `HttpClient.sendAsync` call. Cover the shared CLJC lifecycle only as needed to keep its cancellation semantics coherent; keep the public API unchanged.

## Correctness finding

An abort can win while `run-attempt!` is blocked in the managed request-preparation phase, deliver the canonical cancelled reply, and clear the in-flight registry, yet the same attempt proceeds to call `jvm-fetch` after preparation returns. On the real JVM adapter that call invokes `HttpClient.sendAsync`, so a side-effecting request can begin after the framework has told the app it was cancelled.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1810-1825` checks `@finalised?` only before `prepare-body!`; a body thunk may block inside that call. The successful-preparation branch then enters the host transport with no second cancellation check (`cljs-fetch` at 1827; `jvm-fetch` at 1884).
- The abort closure at `transport.cljc:1658-1718` flips `aborted?`, wins `finalised?`, clears the registry, and dispatches the aborted outcome. During preparation the JVM `cf-holder` is still nil, so it has no future to cancel.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport_jvm.cljc:285-290` calls `HttpClient.sendAsync` synchronously inside `jvm-fetch`; the returned future is not published to `cf-holder` until `transport.cljc:1911`, after the request has already been issued.
- Deterministic no-network probe at `dba7835137e7`: run `run-attempt!` on a future with a body thunk held by a promise; wait for thunk entry; call `registry/abort-in-flight!`; then release the thunk while `jvm-fetch` is redefined to increment a counter. Observed `:registered-before-abort true`, `:abort-result true`, `:fetch-calls 1`, `:registered-after false` (process exit 0). The cancellation succeeded observably, but transport issuance still followed it.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_body_prep_failure_test.clj` covers prep throws, encoding failures, and prep retry, but no abort during preparation. `http_abort_retry_race_test.clj` covers retry/backoff handoffs, not the preparation-to-send handoff.
- Spec 014 says body realization is a managed phase that respects abort precedence (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:218`) and that a cancelled request must not issue a fresh attempt (`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:491-499`). The user guide calls manual abort an explicit “stop now” (`docs/async/http.md:306-316`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a JVM `run-attempt!` context with a stable `:request-id` and a `:body` thunk that signals entry, then waits on a latch/promise.
2. Start the attempt on another thread and wait for the thunk-entry signal, proving preparation is in progress and the handle is registered.
3. Call `registry/abort-in-flight!` for that id and require it to return true; verify the registry slot is gone.
4. Release the thunk. Instrument or redefine `transport-jvm/jvm-fetch` with a call counter.
5. Current result: the counter becomes 1 even though abort completed before body preparation returned. As a non-vacuity control, omit the abort and observe the same harness call the transport once.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A JVM/SSR app lazily materializes a large upload or signed POST body in a thunk. While that work is running, the user cancels, a resource owner releases, an actor is destroyed, or the frame is torn down. The app receives cancellation (or stale suppression) and the registry reports no live work, but the POST starts afterward and may commit server-side.

Invariant: once an abort has completed before host transport issuance begins, that attempt must never subsequently call the host transport. If issuance wins first, the future must be published before the abort returns so the abort path can cancel it. Exactly one terminal outcome remains observable.

## Recommended minimal fix

Extend the existing cancellation-safe handoff through request preparation and JVM future publication. Re-check the shared `aborted?` / `finalised?` state immediately after successful preparation and skip host transport when cancellation already won. On the JVM, serialize the tiny check → `sendAsync` → `cf-holder` publication region with the abort path (or an equivalent one-cell phase CAS) so there is no residual check-to-send window: abort-before-send suppresses issuance; send-before-abort publishes the cancellable future before abort completes. Apply the shared post-prep guard to CLJS as well for a re-entrant external abort fired by body realization. Reuse the current abort closure, reply CAS, registry cleanup, and reply shapes; add no public surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A deterministic JVM regression test uses latches/promises, not timing sleeps, to hold a body thunk in preparation; an abort that returns true before release yields zero `jvm-fetch` / `sendAsync` calls, exactly one canonical `:status :cancelled` reply for manual abort (or the existing suppression outcome for lifecycle abort), and an empty registry.
- The same test fails against the pre-fix implementation by observing one host-transport call after abort.
- Non-vacuity control: the identical harness without abort invokes the host transport exactly once and completes normally, proving the test did not merely disable the send branch or fail before preparation.
- A deterministic handoff control covers the opposite ordering: when JVM issuance wins, the future is published/cancellable before abort completes; abort cancels it and still produces no double reply.
- A focused CLJS regression covers a synchronously/re-entrantly fired external signal during body-thunk realization, or the implementation demonstrates why the shared post-prep guard is host-neutral; no Fetch call occurs after that abort.
- Existing body-preparation failure/retry tests, abort-precedence tests, and abort/retry handoff tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- Interrupting or forcibly terminating arbitrary user body-thunk code already running.
- Expanding `:timeout-ms` semantics to govern body-preparation duration.
- Undoing a request after the server has already received it, stronger delivery guarantees, or transactional HTTP.
- New cancellation APIs, new failure categories, compatibility aliases, or broader transport refactoring.

## Related / duplicate search

Scanned all 1,109 current all-status beads via `bd list --all -n 0`, then searched titles, descriptions, and notes for HTTP, managed abort, body thunk, request preparation / `request-prep`, abort precedence, `jvm-fetch`, cancelled request, and fresh attempt. No bead covers this preparation-to-send cancellation hole. The only current HTTP surface-review bead, `rf2-lddbk`, concerns successful response metadata and is distinct. The sole in-progress bead, `rf2-jui1c`, is an unrelated prose sweep and remains untouched. Historical source/test references `rf2-065xo` (managed prep failures) and `rf2-6nczv9` (retry/backoff cancellation handoffs); neither current tracker record exists, and their shipped tests do not cover abort during body preparation.

title: surface-review(story-mcp): make project stories reachable on first launch
description:
## Scope

Make the published headless Story-MCP server expose a consumer project's JVM-loadable Story registry on its first MCP connection. Add one explicit launch-time namespace-loading seam, document one copyable consumer-project/MCP-host configuration, and prove the path end to end against a project-owned story. Preserve the settled boundary that live browser/CLJS stories are reached through re-frame2-pair.

## Findings

Story-MCP is a same-JVM adapter: every catalogue read, run, and write operates on the process-local Story registry. That makes loading the consumer's registration namespaces a prerequisite, not optional setup polish.

The only canonical launch is `clojure -M -m re-frame.story-mcp.server` from the tool directory. The README adds one sentence saying the launch “must preload” registry-populating JVM namespaces, but supplies no argument, alias, wrapper, MCP-host config, ordering rule, or executable example that does so. The server CLI accepts only the two gate flags and ignores every other flag; `boot!` installs canonical vocabulary and immediately enters the stdio loop. A normal launch therefore has tags/assertions but no project stories.

The integration corpus proves protocol and synthetic in-memory behavior, not the consumer workflow. `stdio-roundtrip.js` uses the bare canonical command and deliberately probes missing stories/variants. The SDK conformance harness starts the same command with `--allow-writes`, creates a synthetic variant only after connecting, and explicitly notes that a successful story read would need a registered story. No test starts the published server from a consuming project, preloads a project namespace, then discovers and runs that already-authored story.

This is the first-use bottleneck for the whole 20-tool catalogue: until a project registry is present, the documented `list-stories -> get-story/get-variant -> run/refine` workflow cannot begin. More protocol hardening or another tool would not fix it.

## Recommended Action

Add one repeatable explicit startup option, for example `--require app.stories.login`, whose values are trusted namespace names from the invoking project's classpath. In `boot!`, install Story's canonical vocabulary first, then `require` the supplied namespaces, then start the MCP loop. Let an ordinary require failure abort startup loudly; do not add namespace scanning, a custom discovery protocol, allowlists, or redundant name validation.

Document a single golden consumer path: a `deps.edn` alias that depends on `day8/re-frame2-story-mcp`, a project-root MCP-host command using that alias plus the explicit namespace option, and the write-gate flag only when the author/refine loop is wanted. State plainly that the namespace must be CLJ/CLJC-loadable in this headless JVM; a running browser's CLJS registry remains the pair's one live door.

Back the path with one consumer-shaped fixture driven through the official MCP SDK: launch from the fixture project, load its story namespace at boot, and immediately discover/read/run its pre-authored story without first calling `register-variant`.

## Evidence

- `tools/story-mcp/README.md:37-51` shows the bare tool-directory command and only the unimplemented “must preload” sentence.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:337-365` parses only `--allow-writes` and `--allow-sensitive-reads`; unknown flags are logged and ignored.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:368-384` applies gates and installs canonical vocabulary but has no consumer-namespace load step.
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:17,74-80` and `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:35-55` make registrations/runs process-local and define Story-MCP as the headless same-JVM host.
- `tools/story-mcp/test/stdio-roundtrip.js:45-51,247-281` calls the bare launch and verifies only missing-variant plus gated-write behavior.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-story.cjs:27,134,342-369` launches with `--allow-writes`, says a story hit needs a registered story, then synthesizes only a variant after connection.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md:15` documents the complementary browser path: Story-MCP cannot see a tab's registry; pair `eval-cljs` is the live door.
- History: initial commit `65c05d67c5` introduced the current bare command; `4cfdf55f61` added the preload caveat two months later, but no launch mechanism or consumer integration witness followed. There are 185 commits touching `tools/story-mcp`; the missing consumer bootstrap is not an unimplemented handler detail.
- Exact tracker searches across current and closed issues for `story-mcp`, project stories, JVM namespaces, preload namespace, empty registry, same-JVM registry, launch, setup, and bootstrap found no matching outcome bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A consuming project's documented `deps.edn` alias and MCP-host configuration start the published Story-MCP main from the project root without repository-local source paths or a user-written wrapper namespace.
- One repeatable explicit namespace option loads named CLJ/CLJC registration namespaces after canonical vocabulary installation and before the server accepts MCP requests; multiple supplied namespaces preserve command order.
- An official-SDK end-to-end fixture launches through that consumer path and, before any MCP write, proves `list-stories` finds the fixture story, `get-story` or `get-variant` reads it, and `run-variant` executes its fixture variant.
- A missing or throwing supplied namespace terminates startup with a useful stderr diagnostic/non-zero exit rather than continuing with a misleading empty project registry. The implementation relies on ordinary `require` failure; it does not invent a second validation layer.
- README/spec guidance clearly distinguishes JVM-loadable project namespaces from the running browser's CLJS registry and routes the latter to re-frame2-pair.
- Existing no-namespace launches, gate semantics, the MCP method set, tool names, tool input/output schemas, and Story's public registration API remain unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Adding nREPL, a JVM-to-browser bridge, or a second live-app transport.
- Auto-discovering namespaces by scanning source roots, classpaths, files, manifests, or naming conventions.
- Hot reload, namespace watching, runtime load/unload tools, or persistence of registrations to source files.
- Adding a new MCP tool, a new Story registration primitive, or extra env/sysprop aliases/config DSLs for the same bootstrap.
- Redesigning the 20-tool catalogue, token budgeting, privacy egress, cursor protocol, or JSON-RPC lifecycle.
- Making CLJS-only story namespaces JVM-loadable.

## Related beads

- `rf2-tgci` (closed) introduced the separate-jar Story-MCP server and its canonical bare launch.
- `rf2-3fc89f.21` (closed) made browser-only reads fail as capability-unavailable rather than false-empty; this task preserves that truthfulness.
- `rf2-3fc89f.22` (closed) ruled the pair as the one live-browser Story host; this task is only the explicit headless-JVM bootstrap.
- `rf2-s99lw4` (closed) documented the pair-side browser recipe through `eval-cljs`; it is the complementary path, not a duplicate.
- No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead matching this project-namespace bootstrap outcome was found.

title: bug(pair-skill): tail-build misses reloads that land before its first probe
description:
## Scope

Make the re-frame2-pair source-edit coordination path reliably prove that the browser is running the edited code. Cover the Pair skill instructions, the tail-build MCP contract/descriptor, its focused tests, and the smallest live or scripted workflow witness. This is specifically the race between a source edit and tail-build's first probe sample.

## Correctness finding

The published skill mandates the sequence edit source, then call tail-build, then proceed only when the probe value flips. The tool, however, establishes its comparison baseline only when tail-build begins, after the edit has already happened. If shadow-cljs reloads between the file write and tail-build's first nREPL evaluation, the first sample is already the new value. Every later sample is also the new value, so the tool returns timed-out even though the requested reload succeeded.

The invariant is that a successful reload must be recognizable whether it lands before or after the wait call obtains its first sample. The current protocol recognizes only the latter ordering. This is a user-visible false diagnostic on the required source-edit path, not merely an imprecise hint.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:116-121 says every source edit must be followed by tail-build with a probe before dispatching or tracing.
- skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md:256-277 prescribes edit first, call tail-build second, and proceed only after ok true plus a flipped probe. The same section concedes that equal initial/final values can mean the reload already landed, so its mandatory gate is knowingly ambiguous.
- skills/re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md:224-230 repeats the permanent-edit sequence and warns that continuing without proving the patch landed silently tests old code.
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/tail_build.cljs evaluates probe once into before inside tail-build-tool, then succeeds only when a later now is not equal to before. There is no argument carrying a pre-edit fingerprint or expected value.
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tail_build_test.cljs proves only 0 then 1 success and stable 42 timeout. The stable-value case is semantically ambiguous: it also exactly models an edited runtime that had already reached 42 before the call.
- The structural skill gates are green: python scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py, python scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, and bb skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj (27 tests, 154 assertions). None exercises the edit/reload ordering.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read a discriminating handler or var fingerprint F0 from the running app.
2. Edit the owning source file so the reloaded fingerprint will be F1.
3. Let shadow-cljs complete the incremental compile and browser swap before the agent's next MCP call reaches tail-build.
4. Invoke tail-build with the same probe.
5. Observe that it samples F1 as initial, continues to sample F1, and returns ok false, reason timed-out, probe-values initial F1 final F1.
6. Repeat with a slower reload that lets tail-build sample F0 first; when a later poll sees F1, the same edit returns success.

Correctness must not depend on MCP/file-watcher scheduling.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A successful reload must be recognizable whether it lands before or after tail-build's first post-edit sample. Today the fast ordering blocks dispatch/trace or sends the programmer toward compile-error/reload recovery even though the browser is already correct, while only the slower ordering passes.

## Recommended minimal fix

Establish the comparison value before the source edit and carry it into the post-edit wait. The smallest shape is a caller-supplied pre-edit baseline/fingerprint on tail-build, or an equivalent single-token mechanism: evaluate the same probe before editing, edit, then have tail-build treat its very first post-edit sample as success when it differs from that baseline and otherwise keep polling. Update the Pair instructions and recipes to capture and pass that baseline. Do not infer success from time elapsed, random probes, or an equal initial/final timeout.

Keep one waiter and one probe vocabulary; do not add a build-log service, watcher daemon, or second hot-reload tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The documented permanent-source-edit workflow captures a discriminating probe fingerprint before the edit and passes that evidence into tail-build after the edit; no current instruction presents a post-edit self-baseline as proof of reload.
2. A focused executable test drives pre-edit baseline F0 with the first and all subsequent tail-build samples already F1. It returns ok true without waiting for timeout and reports enough before/after evidence to show why.
3. A timing control drives baseline F0, first sample F0, then F1 and also returns ok true, proving the existing slower-reload ordering still works.
4. A non-vacuity control drives baseline F0 and only F0 through the deadline; it returns isError true with reason timed-out. The new path must not make every stable value a success.

title: websocket pattern trusts inbound correlation before validation
description:
## Scope

Align the canonical runnable WebSocket pattern across examples/patterns/websocket/, its external CLJS test wrapper, spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, and the WebSocket skill so the code programmers and coding agents copy is safe at both trust boundaries: credentials leaving the app and frames entering it.

Preserve the example's existing lifecycle machine, mock transport, UI, queue/correlation semantics, and the repository's test-free-examples policy. This is a focused correction to one worked pattern, not a new WebSocket facility.

## Findings

The four pattern examples are generally current and copyable: they use the public reg-event/reg-sub/reg-view and reg-machine/defmachine idioms, explicit frame roots and initial events, machine data schemas, recordable durable coeffects, and external headless wrappers. Every declared pattern build is derived by the examples compile gate, including the Nine States story build.

The WebSocket example is also unusually well covered for reconnects, stale socket epochs, queueing, correlation, timeouts, subscription replay, loss semantics, and teardown. Its two trust boundaries nevertheless contradict the newer canonical guidance:

- connection.cljs persists the raw :auth-token in the connection machine's :data, accepts it on :ws/connect and :ws/refresh-token events, dispatches it to the child, and copies it into the socket actor's machine :data. schema.cljs and README.md teach the same shape, and the wrapper tests assert the token is present in snapshots.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md now says raw bearer/cookie/refresh credentials must never enter machine :data or dispatch. Its canonical declaration carries only an opaque :cred-ref and resolves the bearer through an app-owned, client-only host seam.
- messages.cljs writes both pushes and correlated replies into app-db without an inbound message schema or :rf.schema/at-boundary. Its Message schema describes values after storage and is not a closed wire contract. The callback event :ws.app/request-reply is a second app-db-writing ingress with the same omission.
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md added the correct closed InboundMessage plus production boundary interceptor requirement, including the correlated reply path, but its main worked machine and re-authentication prose still carry raw :auth-token. The runnable example implements neither correction.

History explains the split rather than justifying it. Commit bc861c1d17 introduced the runnable WebSocket example on 2026-05-12. Commit ae12ce9b43 (historical bead rf2-x3u46) moved canonical credentials out of machine :data two days later, but changed the skill rather than the example. Commit d667871dae (historical bead rf2-096js) added the inbound-frame obligation to the spec on 2026-08-03, again without updating the runnable source or wrapper. The skill calls the runnable example ground truth, so this divergence makes the unsafe form the easiest one to copy.

## Recommended Action

Make the runnable example demonstrate the already-documented small seam:

- Carry only URL plus an opaque :cred-ref through connect, reconnect, rotation, connection :data, and spawned actor :data.
- Add the minimum app-prefixed, client-only host resolver needed by the demo. Resolve the real bearer immediately beside socket creation/authentication, retain it only in the private host closure for the necessary send, and discard it. Do not route it back through dispatch, app-db, machine snapshots, traces, or recorder data.
- Define one closed inbound wire schema for the demo's actual reply and push variants. Put that schema and :rf.schema/at-boundary on :ws/handle-message, and give the correlated reply-writing ingress an equally release-resident check. Keep locally synthesized connection-loss replies valid without presenting them as trusted server bytes.
- Update the README and companion spec to agree tersely with the runnable form. Reuse the current public APIs and current credential/inbound guidance; do not invent a generalized credential or protocol layer.
- Extend the existing external WebSocket wrapper to prove both boundaries while retaining its lifecycle coverage.

## Evidence

- examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:116-125 stores :auth-token in connection :data; lines 151-172 record and rotate it; lines 211-218 dispatch it; lines 344-351 copy it into spawned actor :data.
- examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs:253-269 stores the raw token in socket actor :data; lines 388-404 register :ws/handle-message with no schema/interceptor; lines 452-458 do the same for :ws.app/request-reply.
- examples/patterns/websocket/schema.cljs:36-39 declares :auth-token as connection data; its Message schema is a permissive stored-message shape, not a closed ingress union.
- examples/patterns/websocket/views.cljs:91-96 initiates the demo with :auth-token "demo-token".
- examples/patterns/websocket/README.md:93-102 teaches that reconnects carry the token through machine :data.
- skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md:28-36 requires opaque :cred-ref plus an app-owned client-only resolver; lines 174-181 identify raw machine credentials and skipped boundary validation as anti-patterns.
- spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md:429-458 specifies the closed inbound union, :rf.schema/at-boundary, and the second correlated-reply ingress, while lines 85-86, 121-130, 249-258, and 460-462 still teach raw token persistence.
- implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs has broad lifecycle coverage and explicit raw-token snapshot assertions, but no malformed/unknown inbound-frame rejection case.
- node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list derives examples/boot, examples/long-running-work, examples/nine-states, examples/nine-states-with-stories, and examples/websocket. examples/TESTING.md assigns behavior to the external wrappers and compilation to this derived gate.
- Fresh open/all-status title and description searches for the surface prefix, WebSocket, credentials, cred-ref, auth-token, bearer, inbound frames, and boundary validation found no duplicate. rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 are adjacent launch-command tasks only.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The connection and socket actor machine schemas/data carry an opaque :cred-ref, never a raw bearer, cookie, password, refresh token, or equivalent credential. Connect/reconnect/rotation event payloads and queued application events likewise carry only the reference.
2. A small app-prefixed, client-only host seam resolves the demo credential at the point of socket authentication. Initial connect, reconnect, and credential rotation still authenticate, while a distinctive raw credential sentinel is absent from inspectable machine snapshots and the exercised event/trace/recording surface.
3. The demo declares a closed schema for every accepted server push and correlated reply variant. :ws/handle-message applies that schema with :rf.schema/at-boundary, and the event that writes correlated server replies into app-db has the same release-resident protection.
4. External wrapper tests prove valid pushes and replies still land; malformed bodies and unknown :type values are rejected, produce the expected boundary-rejection observability, and do not change :messages or :last-reply. Locally generated connection-loss results remain supported.
5. Existing reconnect backoff, stale-epoch rejection, queue flush, subscription replay, request correlation, timeout, fail-in-flight, and teardown tests remain green.
6. The runnable source, its concise README, spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md, and skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md agree on the credential and inbound-frame contracts. No surface continues to call the raw-token form canonical.
7. npm run test:cljs and npm run test:examples-compile pass, along with the relevant documentation link/schema-policy checks for the touched files.

## Non-goals

- Shipping a managed WebSocket API, transport library, pattern framework, or compatibility layer.
- Building a general credential vault/resolver abstraction or prescribing an auth architecture.
- Cataloguing wire protocols or exhaustively documenting payload variants.
- Redesigning the connection machine topology, backoff, queue, subscription, correlation, timeout, or loss semantics.
- Adding tests under examples/ or a per-example browser matrix.
- Refactoring boot, long-running-work, or nine-states.
- Standardizing example launch commands; rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 own that adjacent outcome.

## Related beads

- rf2-iacw2 - adjacent core-example launch-command correction; no overlap with this trust-boundary outcome.
- rf2-ujdn0 - adjacent capability-example launch-command correction; no overlap with this trust-boundary outcome.
- rf2-x3u46 - historical commit bead named by ae12ce9b43, which established the opaque credential-reference guidance.
- rf2-096js - historical commit bead named by d667871dae, which established release-resident inbound-frame validation in the spec.

Surfaces include spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md (HOT, no live toucher) and implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs (confirm the rf2-k5r9t fence is src-only). DISPATCHABLE solo. Gates: test:cljs, test:examples-compile (heavy), check_doc_slugs.py, check_readme_links.py --ci.
AUDIT PR #8821 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness/completeness, inbound boundary: validation occurs after untrusted bytes have already affected connection-machine truth. socket-actor-machine forwards every non-auth body to :ws/received. connection-machine :receive-message then treats mere presence of attacker-controlled :request-id as a correlated reply, immediately dissocs that in-flight slot, and dispatches the raw body to both :ws/handle-message and the stored reply event. The two schema-bound app events can reject the body, but they cannot undo the already-cleared correlation state. Thus the new malformed-correlated-reply test leaves app-db unchanged while silently consuming the pending request; it never asserts :in-flight remains.

RequestOutcome also admits LocalRequestFailure solely by data shape. A server that saw the wire request id can send {:request-id rid :ok false :error :ws/timeout} with no :type. InboundMessage rejects it, but the same raw body is dispatched to :ws.app/request-reply, matches the closed LocalRequestFailure arm, mutates :last-reply as if locally minted, and clears :in-flight. The test deliberately uses a malformed body carrying :type :reply and comments that :type prevents it posing as local, so it misses the exact provenance hole. Minimal repair: enforce the closed inbound wire contract before any request-id branching or runtime-state mutation, and keep server ReplyMessage delivery distinct from the machine's locally minted loss/timeout event (or otherwise encode trustworthy provenance); malformed/unknown frames must leave both app-db and :in-flight untouched. Add the local-failure-shaped hostile frame and pending-timeout/loss controls.

Implementation quality, credential boundary: mock-socket-for-actor resolves bearer in its outer let and the stored :send function closes over it. That handle remains in sockets-by-actor for the socket lifetime, so the bearer is not 'read once, then gone' or discarded after the auth send as the source/spec/README claim. The sentinel test cannot inspect lexical host closures. Resolve inside the :auth branch (or clear a one-shot cell immediately after forming the wire send) so the stored socket handle retains only cred-ref, then preserve connect/reconnect/rotation and unknown-ref tests.

All-status searches for websocket malformed reply in-flight, local request failure spoof, RequestOutcome websocket, and inbound boundary correlation found no separate owner. These are direct residues of rf2-iyjae's two trust-boundary outcome.
AUDIT RESIDUE ADDRESSED — PR #8856 (2026-09-01, branch worker/ws-boundaries-iyjae, based on f15d7ff332).

All three audit findings verified at source before acting, and all three HELD.

(1) Inbound boundary. connection.cljs :receive-message branched on (:request-id body) and dissoc'd that :in-flight slot before any validation, so a hostile frame naming a pending request consumed the correlation while the ingress downstream refused the body — caller never answered, and the scheduled timeout found nothing to settle. Fixed with a :trusted-frame? guard (connection epoch AND schema/valid-inbound-frame?, one named guard per 005 §No combinator data form) on a two-candidate :ws/received; the second candidate, :refuse-frame, returns no :data and forwards to :ws/handle-message so the ingress still emits the one canonical :rf.error/schema-validation-failure. Branching now reads the vetted :type, not presence-of-:request-id.

(2) Provenance. RequestOutcome admitted LocalRequestFailure by shape. Now a closed :multi dispatching on :origin, which the machine stamps AFTER receipt (:ws/server on a wire body handed to a reply event, :ws/local on fail-in-flight and :clear-request bodies). A frame off the wire cannot reach the :ws/local arm. Also closed both wire arms ({:closed true}); an OPEN push arm was a second route to the same in-flight consumption, since it accepted a :request-id under a :type unrelated to request-reply. Closing the push arm required declaring :at (the manual push button's timestamp) and changing one test's ad-hoc {:type :push :n N} frames.

(3) Credential closure. mock-socket-for-actor resolved the bearer in its outer let and the stored :send closure retained it for the socket's lifetime, contradicting the 'read once, then gone' claim in source, README and spec. Resolution moved inside the :auth branch; the stored handle now closes over :cred-ref alone. NOTE this repair is STRUCTURAL and not observable to the sentinel sweep — a lexical closure is on no serialisable surface — which is recorded in the test comment rather than papered over, since that blind spot is why the finding survived the first pass.

Tests: the audit was right that the old malformed-correlated-reply case never asserted :in-flight survived. Added that, the local-failure-shaped hostile frame ({:request-id rid :ok false :error :ws/timeout}, no :type), the :request-id-smuggling push, and a pending-timeout control proving the surviving slot still answers its caller. Added websocket-request-reply-ingress-rejection as a separate deftest, because the machine no longer routes bad frames to :ws.app/request-reply and that ingress must still hold its own contract. Provenance controls added to the drop, timeout and correlation tests.

Two prose drifts the audit implies but does not name were also corrected: the skill and README placed credential resolution 'at actor spawn' / 'as the socket opens', which is exactly the shape that retains the bearer. The skill's canonical declaration gained :trusted-frame? and the two-candidate :ws/received so the copied form is the vetted one.

Gates, captured exits on the final base: test:cljs 0 (11122 tests / 54598 assertions / 0 failures), test:examples-compile 0 (56 builds, zero warnings), check_readme_links.py --ci 0, check_doc_slugs.py 0. Each gate shown RED first: both doc gates against a planted fault at a line this change edits, and test:cljs against a payload-blind :trusted-frame? — which failed exactly 2 assertions, both the new ones, reproducing the audit's bug precisely. Every restore verified by git blob hash.

rf2-ni0ko left untouched as fenced. Its fix is unchanged in shape by this work: :ws/fatal is still an :active transition with :action :record-error, and fail-in-flight is already the shared helper, so the one-action composition it describes still applies.

title: UIx substrate examples require an undeclared uix.dom consumer dependency
description:
## Scope

The copyable dependency contract for the three runnable UIx examples under `examples/substrates/uix/**`, plus the canonical UIx setup snippets they point readers to in `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` and `spec/Conventions.md`. Add a focused clean-consumer regression; do not change UIx runtime behavior.

## Correctness finding

Every UIx substrate example imports `uix.dom` to create and render its React root, but the public downstream dependency recipe supplies only `day8/re-frame2` and `day8/re-frame2-uix`, and names only `com.pitch/uix.core` as the view library. `day8/re-frame2-uix` intentionally does not depend on `com.pitch/uix.dom`; it is test-only in the adapter project. A programmer who follows the documented coordinate recipe and copies any worked UIx mount therefore gets a missing `uix.dom` namespace at compile time. The examples compile in this monorepo only because the top-level Shadow configuration injects `com.pitch/uix.dom`, masking the dependency omission a clean consumer sees.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a clean CLJS consumer with the documented UIx dependency pair from `spec/Conventions.md`: core plus the UIx adapter (use the corresponding local roots before publication), with no direct `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinate.
2. Copy the namespace/mount shape from `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs`, or use the guide's snippet adapted from it. It requires `[uix.dom :as uix-dom]` and calls `uix-dom/create-root` / `uix-dom/render-root`.
3. Compile that consumer on its own classpath. Compilation fails because the required namespace `uix.dom` is unavailable.
4. Add `com.pitch/uix.dom` at the same version as `com.pitch/uix.core`; the identical source compiles. Running the example through `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` does not reproduce the failure because that aggregate build injects both UIx artefacts globally.

## Evidence

- `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs` lines 22-25 and 103-112 import `uix.dom` and invoke both root functions. `uix/login/core.cljs` lines 23-31 and 121-150 and `uix/dashboard/core.cljs` lines 29-32 and 354-366 do the same.
- `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` lines 70-78 presents the coordinate table and lists only `com.pitch/uix.core` for UIx, then its copyable example-derived namespace at lines 89-94 immediately requires `uix.dom`.
- `spec/Conventions.md` lines 1821-1830 says a UIx consumer picks its substrate with only `day8/re-frame2` plus `day8/re-frame2-uix`; no DOM coordinate is shown.
- `implementation/adapters/uix/deps.edn` lines 20-30 explicitly keeps `com.pitch/uix.dom` out of shipping `:deps` and places it only under the `:test` alias. Thus aliases do not propagate it to downstream consumers.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` lines 14-16 says the aggregate build adds `com.pitch/uix.{core,dom}` so UIx examples resolve, and its top-level `:dependencies` includes both. This ambient monorepo dependency is why existing example compile coverage cannot detect the clean-consumer failure.
- The UIx project template is the positive control: `_uix/deps.edn` lines 30-31 correctly emits both `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` at version 1.4.4.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A worked example advertised as the source for a UIx app's view and mount must compile from the canonical dependency recipe on a clean consumer classpath. It must not rely on an undeclared namespace supplied only by the monorepo's aggregate build. Every namespace directly required by the copyable mount must have an explicit consumer dependency owner.

## Recommended minimal fix

Keep the adapter artefact lean: it does not itself require `uix.dom`, so do not make that library transitively mandatory. Instead, make the canonical UIx application dependency recipe include direct, version-locked `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinates, and have each UIx example README point to that complete recipe. Update the guide's coordinate table/snippet and the Conventions consumer block from the same authority. Reuse the template's existing 1.4.4 pair/lockstep convention rather than introduce a second version source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused executable test creates an isolated consumer classpath from the canonical documented UIx application dependency set, without `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` or its global `:dependencies`, and compiles a namespace that requires `uix.core`, `uix.dom`, and `re-frame.adapter.uix` and exercises the example's `create-root` / `render-root` mount surface.
- The test proves the documented dependency set contains direct `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinates at the same version, and the clean consumer compile succeeds.
- Non-vacuity/control: removing only `com.pitch/uix.dom` from the fixture makes compilation fail specifically on the missing `uix.dom` namespace; the control must not be satisfied by the monorepo aggregate classpath.
- The counter, login, and dashboard UIx READMEs link or show the complete canonical app dependency recipe, so each runnable example has a low-friction path from source to a standalone consumer.
- The how-to coordinate table and the Conventions UIx `deps.edn` block agree with the executable fixture and the generator template's UIx core/DOM version pair.
- Existing per-example compile coverage and UIx adapter tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- Adding `com.pitch/uix.dom` to the published `day8/re-frame2-uix` POM when the adapter implementation does not require it.
- Changing example events, subscriptions, views, mount behavior, or adapter APIs.
- Redesigning the monorepo aggregate Shadow dependency model.
- Expanding this issue into React/React-DOM npm installation guidance or general project scaffolding.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status beads for `uix.dom`, `UIx DOM dependency`, `missing UIx DOM`, `UIx downstream`, `UIx deps`, `UIx compile namespace`, `UIx copy recipe`, `documented UIx dependencies`, `uix mount dependency`, and `missing namespace uix.dom`, plus descriptions containing `com.pitch/uix.dom`; no matching issue exists. The open `rf2-oz7wr` concerns `rf/reg-view*` returning a component React cannot mount and is unrelated to dependency resolution.

---
## Worker verdict — 2026-09-01 12:36 AUSEST (PR #8864, branch worker/uix-deps-5x1xt)

**The finding holds in all three halves. Verified at source at trunk d2688dd381, rebased onto f15d7ff332.**

1. Examples: examples/substrates/uix/{counter,login,dashboard}/core.cljs each `:require [uix.dom :as uix-dom]` and call create-root + render-root.

AC1 as written — an isolated-classpath compile — was NOT built, deliberately. That needs a fixture project, Maven resolution and a build step, i.e. a new CI lane whose config lives in hot-zone files. The gap is stated in the PR body rather than papered over: the guard proves the invariant that broke (a required namespace with no owning consumer coordinate), not that a clean classpath resolves.
