title: mcp-conformance: project-stories execution proof is vacuous
description:
## Scope

Tighten only the consumer-project Story-MCP witness in tools/mcp-conformance/test/fixtures/project-stories/ and tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs so its run-variant phase proves that project-authored lifecycle work executed. Preserve the existing first-connect, no --allow-writes, consumer-alias launch and missing-namespace failure arms.

## Correctness finding

The new project-stories end-to-end gate claims to prove that a pre-authored project variant is runnable on first connect, but its run arm is vacuous. The fixture variant deliberately has no :setup, no :script, and no assertions. The harness accepts isError false plus :status "pass". Story's result contract intentionally assigns :pass to an empty assertion set with a clean tape, so that response is the default for doing no observable lifecycle work.

Consequently the gate proves registration, lookup, request routing, and a success-shaped result envelope, but it cannot prove the correctness claim named by phase 5: that run-variant executed the project-authored variant lifecycle.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From tools/mcp-conformance, run npm run test:story-project on the current fixture. Phase 5 reports run-variant green.
2. Read the registered variant in test/fixtures/project-stories/src/app/stories.cljc: it has no :setup, :script, or assertion.
3. Read the phase-5 check in test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs: it accepts the response after only isError false and aggregate status "pass".
4. Compare Story's production aggregation rule: an empty assertion vector with no unmet/failure evidence returns :pass. The same gate verdict is therefore available without any project-authored lifecycle action to observe.

Expected: the execution phase requires evidence produced only by running the fixture variant.
Actual: the default empty-program pass is sufficient for the phase and the overall gate to be green.

## Evidence

- tools/mcp-conformance/test/fixtures/project-stories/src/app/stories.cljc:27-29 says the fixture has no :setup and no :script and is therefore "vacuously runnable".
- tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs:193-205 calls this a "vacuous pass" and checks only runResp.isError and runStruct.status.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/result.cljc:44-49 states the production rule directly: a run with zero assertions and a clean tape is :pass.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/requirements.cljc:547-555 implements that rule: with no error, failure, or unmet record, aggregate-status falls through to :pass.
- Closed bead rf2-cfq8a and the harness header describe the delivered outcome as discovering, reading, and running the project story on first connection. The current last verb has no execution-only witness.

The focused Node unit cluster is green (105 passed, 9 platform skips), which is expected: it does not make this end-to-end arm non-vacuous.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A regression can stop executing :setup and/or :script for launch-preloaded project variants while still resolving the known variant to an empty, clean run result. list-stories, get-story, and get-variant continue to pass. Phase 5 still sees isError false and status "pass", so the advertised golden path remains green even though the project's lifecycle never ran.

Invariant: any gate that claims a variant executed must assert evidence that can exist only if that variant's lifecycle executed. A default success status over an empty program is not such evidence.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the existing fixture variant perform one deterministic JVM-headless lifecycle action and emit one distinctive passing assertion. A small fixture-local event used by :setup, followed by a :script path assertion over the seeded value, is sufficient and exercises both halves without a renderer or browser. In the SDK test, assert the returned assertion record (identity, passed verdict, and expected/actual evidence), not merely the aggregate :status.

Keep this inside the existing fixture and test. No new server option, MCP tool, transport, test job, fixture project, or general assertion framework is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The existing project fixture variant contains non-empty, deterministic JVM-headless lifecycle work whose result cannot be produced without executing the variant (for example, fixture-local setup state followed by a distinctive script assertion).
2. end-to-end-project-stories.cjs still launches through the fixture project's -M:story-mcp alias before any MCP write, but now requires the run-variant response to contain the exact execution-only assertion/evidence and a passing aggregate status.
3. The test fails if run-variant returns the current empty-assertions :pass shape; checking only :status is not sufficient.
4. Non-vacuity control: temporarily make the fixture's expected value wrong, or disable the setup action that produces it, and run npm run test:story-project from tools/mcp-conformance. The command must exit non-zero and name the missing/failed execution witness. Restore the plant and require the same command to exit zero.
5. The existing missing-namespace launch arm, first-connect discovery/read arms, no --allow-writes posture, and clean SDK teardown remain covered and green.
6. Focused Story-MCP tests relevant to the chosen lifecycle action remain green; no browser, Chromium, nREPL, or Pair-MCP runtime is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Changing Story's intentional rule that an assertion-free variant is vacuously green.
- Adding a blanket requirement that every user-authored variant contain assertions.
- Testing rendering or browser-only Reagent/UIx stories in the headless JVM server.
- Expanding the tool catalogue, wire schemas, launch flags, token budgeting, or CI job matrix.
- Refactoring the mature Story runtime or adding a second consumer fixture.

## Related / duplicate search

- rf2-cfq8a (closed) delivered the first-launch project-story path and this witness. This issue is a correctness correction to its execution proof, not a duplicate of its bootstrap outcome.
- rf2-a9l6e (open) concerns one honest command/profile for running MCP compatibility and explicitly excludes new protocol assertions. It does not own this vacuous run arm.
- rf2-k9rzr (closed) mentions an unrelated vacuous assertion in bundle-isolation tooling.
- All-status tracker searches over project stories, project-story, run-variant, vacuous, mcp-conformance, dedup envelope, and serialized issue descriptions found no issue owning a non-vacuous execution witness for end-to-end-project-stories.cjs.

## Priority rationale

P2: this is a real false-green in an authoritative SDK/CI compatibility witness for the first-use Story-MCP workflow. It can allow an execution regression to ship while the named golden path stays green. It is not P1 because no current production execution failure was observed; the defect is in the gate's ability to detect one.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing project fixture performs deterministic JVM-headless lifecycle work.
- SDK test asserts exact execution-only assertion/evidence, not only aggregate pass.
- Empty-assertions pass is rejected.
- A planted wrong expectation or disabled setup makes npm run test:story-project exit non-zero; restoration exits zero.
- First-connect/no-write and missing-namespace arms remain green; no browser or new server surface.
notes:
FENCED (mayor, 2026-09-01 12:18:46 AUSEST): collides with a LIVE worker on tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs — the rf2-cfq8a audit-residual worker (branch worker/mcp-host-cfg-cfq8a) may edit a comment in that exact file. This bead's scope is that file plus its project-stories fixtures, so two workers would conflict. DO NOT DISPATCH until worker/mcp-host-cfg-cfq8a's PR merges (or that worker reports without touching the file). Clears when: worker/mcp-host-cfg-cfq8a's PR is MERGED.
FENCE CLEARED (mayor, 2026-09-01 12:27:07 AUSEST): the tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs hold is discharged — worker/mcp-host-cfg-cfq8a's PR #8861 MERGED at cd03ceffbf, and it did NOT touch that file (its report states the witness needed no change because :120-124 already states the cwd property generically). No live worker holds the file now. DISPATCHABLE.

WORKER (2026-09-01 12:49 AUSEST, branch worker/conformance-proof-3n3dk, PR #8866): finding CONFIRMED at source and repaired.

Premise check. end-to-end-project-stories.cjs phase 5 asserted exactly two things — !runResp.isError and runStruct.status === 'pass' — over a fixture variant with no :setup and no :script. Vacuous as described.

Repair. The run arm's assertion is REPLACED, not supplemented. The fixture variant now carries renderer-free lifecycle work (:setup dispatches the fixture project's own :fixture-app/seed-article, seeding [:fixture-app/article :headline]; :script asserts it back with :rf.assert/path-equals). The witness requires the single assertion record — id, :path, :expected, the live :actual read from the frame app-db at assertion time, and :passed? true / :status "pass" — and rejects an empty :assertions vector by name, BEFORE the aggregate :status is read at all. The expected literal is written by hand on both sides rather than shared through a def: a shared constant would have made AC 4's wrong-expected-value plant a no-op.

SECOND FINDING, one level below the bead's. run-variant on the headless JVM stdio host is INERT without a reactive substrate: setup dispatches reach no adapter, the script plays nothing, and the run still answers :status "pass" over an empty app-db and zero assertions. Measured directly (clojure -M -e in the fixture project: BARE-APPDB {} / BARE-ASSERTIONS [] without rf/init!; a full passing record with it). story-mcp's server installs Story's canonical vocabulary but deliberately chooses no substrate — per spec/006 that choice is the app's, and tools/story-mcp's own JVM tests supply it in their fixture (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) which is why they see records where the server does not. So the FIXTURE PROJECT now makes the choice in the namespace its launch alias preloads, as a consuming project would. No server, transport, tool-catalogue or launch-flag change; the bead's non-goals hold.

Non-vacuity control (AC 4), all from tools/mcp-conformance, exit captured in the same shell, never piped:
  :setup []                       -> npm run test:story-project EXIT 1, names the null read at the seeded path
  :script []  (pre-fix shape)     -> EXIT 1, names 0 assertion records; its rejected payload still reads status "pass" — i.e. the OLD arm would have been green on that tree
  expected literal made wrong     -> EXIT 1, names the expectation mismatch
  restored                        -> EXIT 0, full golden path green
Each plant verified applied and each restore verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object (aa4c94e7dac3a646766c6bf8e74f813de216254c); no plant silently no-opped.

Other gates, all on the final rebased base 96c224e904: npm run test:story EXIT 0 (this witness plus the 20-tool catalogue harness); npm run test:unit EXIT 0 (119 tests, 110 pass, 0 fail, 9 platform skips). No markdown touched, so neither doc-link gate applies.

AC 5 preserved and green: missing-namespace launch arm, first-connect list-stories/get-story/get-variant arms, no --allow-writes posture, consumer-alias -M:story-mcp launch, clean SDK teardown.

Files: tools/mcp-conformance/test/fixtures/project-stories/src/app/stories.cljc, tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs. Nothing else touched.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8866 (branch worker/conformance-proof-3n3dk, head e55d6b3c63, base 96c224e904). The phase-5 run arm's assertion is REPLACED: it now requires the :rf.assert/path-equals execution witness — id, :path, :expected, the live :actual read from the frame app-db, :passed? true — and rejects an empty :assertions vector by name before the aggregate :status is read. The fixture variant carries deterministic renderer-free lifecycle work (:setup seeds [:fixture-app/article :headline], :script asserts it back). Non-vacuity control per AC 4: three plants (:setup [], :script [], wrong expected literal) each drive npm run test:story-project to EXIT 1 naming the missing witness; restored EXIT 0. The :script [] plant's rejected payload still reads status 'pass', so the old arm would have been green on it. Second finding recorded on the bead and in the fixture: run-variant is inert on the headless JVM host without a reactive substrate and still answers 'pass' over an empty app-db — the fixture project now installs plain-atom in the namespace its launch alias preloads, no server change. AC 5 arms preserved and green.

title: flows: tag output-path write failures instead of blaming :derive
description:
## Scope

The flow evaluation boundary in `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc`, plus the router's consumer-side error record and focused CLJ/CLJS tests. This is about attribution of an actual pre-install failure, not broader output-path validation.

## Correctness finding

`evaluate-flow!` catches the whole recompute/install block as though it were the application `:derive` callback. A derive function can return normally and the later `assoc-in` can throw because the pending app-db has a container incompatible with the declared output path. The runtime then emits `:rf.flow/failed` and `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` with the actionable message "a flow's :derive fn threw" and "Fix the :derive fn". That attribution is false: the framework output write failed after derive completed.

The error contract must distinguish the phase that failed. Otherwise local diagnostics and the always-on production error record send a programmer to working code and conceal the output-path/container mismatch that caused the event to abort.

## Evidence

- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:172` opens one `try` before `(apply (:derive flow) new-inputs)` at line 174.
- The same `try` covers `(assoc-in db (:output-path flow) new-output)` at line 184, the dirty-cache write, debug trace construction, and output-schema observation through line 208.
- Its catch at lines 209-236 unconditionally emits `:rf.flow/failed`, throws `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception`, says the `:derive` function threw, and tells the programmer to fix it.
- Registration validates only that `:output-path` is a non-empty vector of legal concrete segments (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:269-272,315-326`). Correctly, it cannot prove the shape of a future pending app-db container.
- The public contract describes `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` and `:rf.flow/failed` as derive-throw signals (`docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:249,271`; `spec/013-Flows.md` failure semantics). No focused flow test drives a successful derive followed by an output install throw.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a frame at `{:source 1 :items []}`.
2. Register flow `:flow/output-write` with input `[:source]`, output path `[:items :total]`, and a derive function that records its call and returns `42`.
3. Dispatch one event so the first flow pass runs.
4. Observe that derive returned, then Clojure/ClojureScript `assoc-in` attempts to associate keyword `:total` into the vector at `:items` and throws.
5. Observe that the event correctly aborts, but the emitted failure says the derive function threw and instructs the programmer to fix derive.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The declaration passes path validation because every segment is legal. Atomicity is preserved (the event does not commit), but both the dev trace and production error surface blame the completed derive callback and omit the failing output-write phase.

Invariant: every typed failure and recovery instruction must name the component/phase that actually threw. A framework output installation failure must not be represented as an application derive throw.

## Recommended minimal fix

Split the authored callback invocation from framework output installation in `evaluate-flow!`. Keep the existing derive-throw behavior, but classify/tag an `assoc-in` failure as `:output-write` (with flow id and declared output path) and give it an honest reason. Thread that structural phase through `:rf.flow/failed` and the router's always-on record. Reuse `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` if it remains the aggregate flow-evaluation category; a new public error id is not required if the phase and message are unambiguous. Preserve the existing exact-owner fence and pass-level dirty-cache/vacation rollback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused CLJ test and its CLJS counterpart install `{:source 1 :items []}`, register the `[:items :total]` flow above, and dispatch one drain. A non-vacuity counter proves derive ran exactly once and returned before failure. The committed app-db remains unchanged.
- The captured `:rf.flow/failed` trace and always-on error record identify flow `:flow/output-write`, identify phase `:output-write`, and do not claim or advise that `:derive` threw. The structural output path is available in the thrown diagnostic or dev trace.
- A negative control makes derive itself throw before output installation. It still produces the existing `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` contract with phase `:derive`, flow attribution, atomic abort, and no output-write attribution.
- A positive control uses the same derive and `[:items :total]` output path with `:items {}`. It commits `42`, advances dirty-check state, and emits no failure.
- The tests assert the always-on record, not only a debug trace, so production attribution cannot silently remain wrong; the existing flow atomicity/conformance tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- Do not reject legal output paths at registration based on the current app-db shape; that shape can change before evaluation.
- Do not change event atomicity, retry/dirty-cache behavior, path segment grammar, schema observation, or output vacation semantics.
- Do not add defensive validation for arbitrary application data or redesign the flow error catalogue.
- Do not address dynamic registration/clear settling; `rf2-kh73v` already owns that distinct lifecycle behavior.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all statuses by title and full tracker text for `flow`, `flow-eval`, `derive throw`, `assoc-in`, `output write`, and `output path`. No issue owns output-write failure attribution. `rf2-kh73v` is the open dynamic-toggle settling task and is distinct. Other matches concern unrelated schema, CI, Hicasso, or trace-catalogue work. Source history/tests cover derive throws and vector-index vacation, but not this successful-derive/output-install failure boundary.
notes:
## Implemented — PR #8863 (2026-09-01 12:40:52 AUSEST)

Premise verified at source before building: `evaluate-flow!` really did open ONE `try` before the derive call and close it after the install (line numbers had drifted ~4 from the bead's — the try is at 176, not 172 — but the structure is exactly as described). A fixed-string census for `output-write` across the tracked tree returned only the bead's own row in `.beads/issues.jsonl`, so no repair already existed at tip; the census was run once against a string known to be present as a control.

### The split
Structural, not message inspection. The authored `:derive` call sits in its own `try` returning a one-key marker map (`::output` / `::thrown`); the framework install — `assoc-in`, the `last-inputs` write, the `:rf.flow/computed` trace, schema observation — sits in a second `try`. An install failure is therefore unreachable from the derive handler. A new private `flow-eval-failure!` takes the phase as an argument and threads it to:

- `:rf.flow/failed` trace tags: `:phase` + `:path` (the declared output path; `:path` is the spelling `:rf.flow/computed` already uses)
- thrown ex-data: `:rf.flow/failed-phase`, `:rf.flow/output-path` (beside the existing `:rf.flow/failed-id` / `:cause`)
- the always-on error record: top-level `:phase`, lifted off the ex-data by the router's `emit-flow-eval-exception!`

`:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` stays the aggregate category — no new public error id. The derive-throw message is preserved verbatim; the exact-owner fence, pass-level dirty-cache rollback, path grammar, schema observation and event atomicity are untouched. Nothing was added to registration-time validation (bead non-goal).

### Acceptance criteria
All five met. New `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_output_write_attribution_cljs_test.cljc` — one `.cljc` so the JVM runner and the shadow `:node-test` build (ns-regexp `cljs-test$`) both run it, giving the CLJ test and its CLJS counterpart in one file. Three tests: the repro (derive-call counter proves derive ran once and RETURNED; app-db unchanged; `:phase :output-write` on trace, on the always-on record, on that record with `:exception` dissoc'd, and on the ex-data; message neither claims nor advises `:derive`), the derive-throw negative control (`:phase :derive`, wording preserved verbatim, no output-write attribution), and the legal-write positive control (`:items {}` commits 42 and a second value-equal drain skips, proving dirty-check state advanced).

### No test pinned the wrong attribution
Searched: none exists — every other `:rf.flow/failed` test throws from inside `:derive`, and `flows_vector_parent_vacation_test.clj` covers vector INDICES, which are a legal write. So nothing was flipped or renamed. One test was EXTENDED: `flows-trace-test/flow-eval-exception-routes-through-error-emit-substrate` pins the always-on record's exact key set tree-wide (the only such pin), which now gains `:phase`; its scenario is a genuine derive throw so it asserts `:phase :derive`.

### Gates
`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/flows`, foreground, exit captured in the same shell:
- green on the committed bytes: 244 tests / 6087 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0
- RED against the pre-repair sources (both files at merge base `d2688dd381`, tests kept): same 244/6087, 14 failures, 0 errors, exit 1 — the red is also what proves the gate read the worker worktree, since the test file exists nowhere else
- RED on a one-line revert (`:output-write` → `:derive` at the install catch's call site): 7 failures, exit 1, controls still green
- both restores verified by git BLOB hash against the committed objects, not by reading a diff
- both `.cljc` files reader-checked under `#{:clj}` and `#{:cljs}`, exit 0; the reader-check exercised once against an unclosed `#?(:cljs` form, which returned exit 1

CLJS lane reliance declared in the PR body: the `cljs-*` node-test jobs in `.github/workflows/test.yml` cover `implementation/flows/{src,test}`.

### Out of scope, filed
`spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/013-Flows.md`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md` and `docs/core/flows.md` still describe both signals as derive-throw signals. `spec/` is hot-zone and outside this bead's stated scope, so nothing there was edited — filed as **rf2-ywdvp** (P2, dispatch alone).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8863 (branch worker/flows-attrib-gpj9r, head 38b499c0a529e82fa2b61be846267921a4819ba6). evaluate-flow! now splits the authored :derive call and the framework output install into separate try forms, so an assoc-in write failure is structurally unreachable from the derive handler; the failing phase (:derive / :output-write) rides the :rf.flow/failed trace, the thrown ex-data (:rf.flow/failed-phase, :rf.flow/output-path) and the always-on error record's :phase slot. New flows_output_write_attribution_cljs_test.cljc covers the repro plus derive-throw and legal-write controls on both hosts; flows JVM suite 244 tests / 6087 assertions green (exit 0), red 14 against pre-repair sources and red 7 on a one-line revert. Spec/docs catalogue rows are hot-zone and out of this bead's scope — filed as rf2-ywdvp.

title: changed-surfaces: migration_v1_codemod arm misses implementation/core changes its :integration lane now depends on
description:
Surfaced by the rf2-8odvg/rf2-36u96 worker (PR #8857) as an out-of-scope finding it correctly declined to act on; OWNING ITEM: rf2-36u96, which created the dependency.

FINDING (worker's, unverified by the mayor — treat as a claim and check at source): the `migration_v1_codemod` classifier arm in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh fires on `migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/*` only. PR #8857 wired `clojure -M:integration` into the jvm-migration-v1-codemod job, and that integration lane reaches implementation/core through a :local/root. So a change confined to implementation/core does NOT arm the codemod job even though the job now depends on that code — the classic surface-armed gate that is skipped on the very push that breaks it (loops.md clause 2 names this shape: a gate skipped on the breaking commit while the trunk rollup reads green throughout).

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN #8857: widening the arm means touching .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh AND its pinned mirror implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs — the one-toucher-by-construction pair (CLAUDE.md 'Minimise merge conflicts when dispatching'). A change that alters what the classifier OUTPUTS must move both halves in ONE commit, because the test pins those outputs. The worker was fenced out of that pair and stopped and reported rather than crossing, which was correct.

BEFORE DISPATCHING: verify the arm's current pattern at source, and confirm the :integration lane really does reach implementation/core (read the codemod deps.edn's :integration alias). #8857's own report notes that rf2-36u96's description was ALREADY wrong about scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh's roster, so this bead's premises deserve the same scepticism.

SCOPE IF IT HOLDS: widen the arm so implementation/core changes arm the codemod job, moving script and mirror in one commit; no new job, no new gate.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-09-01 — the bead HOLDS on both halves. Fixed in PR #8867 (branch worker/classifier-arm-fk5jy, commit ea167a2b94).

PREMISE (a) VERIFIED — the arm's actual pattern. Read at source rather than taken from the bead's wording. In .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh, 'migration_v1_codemod=true' appears in exactly ONE arm — 'migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/*)' — plus mark_all(). No arm earlier in the same case statement matches an implementation/core/... path (the nearest, the per-feature list, enumerates sibling artefacts and the exact files implementation/deps.edn, shadow-cljs.edn, package.json — not implementation/core/*). The job's gate in test.yml is 'if: needs.detect_changed_surfaces.outputs.migration_v1_codemod == 0x27true0x27' with NO implementation_jvm fallback, so nothing else could have armed it.

PREMISE (b) VERIFIED — the :integration edge reaches implementation/core. migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/deps.edn declares, under the :integration alias, 'day8/re-frame2-core {:local/root "../../../implementation/core"}', and its own comment says it outright: 'only this alias pulls implementation/core'. test.yml's jvm-migration-v1-codemod runs 'clojure -M:test' AND 'clojure -M:integration' as two separate steps (the second added by rf2-36u96 / PR #8857).

MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX (classifier run on this trunk):
  implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc -> migration_v1_codemod=false, implementation_jvm=true, tools_jvm_machines_viz=true
POSITIVE CONTROL on the same instrument, same run:
  migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod.clj -> migration_v1_codemod=true, implementation_jvm=false
So the false was a real negative, not a classifier that had stopped classifying.

THE FIX. One boolean, 'migration_v1_codemod=true', added to the existing 'implementation/core/*)' arm — which already carries three reverse edges of exactly this shape under rf2-wq17m, whose own comment says every reverse edge in the file is spelled out the same way. No new job, no new gate, no workflow-file edit, no dependency-graph scheme.

SCOPE JUSTIFICATION (why core and no wider): implementation/core/deps.edn puts only ':paths ["src"]' and two mvn coordinates on its BASE classpath. Its cross-artefact :local/root edges (schemas, machines, routing, flows, http, ssr, epoch, resources, test-quiet) all sit under ALIASES, and a :local/root dependency never activates its target's aliases. Core's own tree is therefore the whole of what the :integration lane reaches.

ONE-WAY EDGE, pinned in both directions: core changes now arm the codemod lane, but a codemod-only diff still must not arm implementation_jvm (the codemod is downstream of core). Verified after the fix: the codemod's own source still classifies implementation_jvm=false.

ONE-TOUCHER PAIR honoured — .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs move in ONE commit. Derived at start-up that nobody else was live on the pair: 0 of 7 open PRs touched either file.

CONTROL (the deliverable). Pin added first, script un-widened: gate went RED, captured exit 1, naming exactly the planted assertion ('a core change arms the v1 codemod lane over the :integration edge (rf2-fk5jy)'). That red is also the proof the gate read the worker's own checkout, since the pin exists in no other tree. After widening: captured exit 0, and the pass count moved 291 -> 292 rather than collapsing.

GATE. The covering gate is CI job js-harness-self-tests -> 'npm run test:scripts' from implementation/, which is UNGATED (no needs: detect_changed_surfaces, no if:) so it runs on every PR; the mirror is picked up by that script's scripts/*.test.cjs glob and spawns the REAL classifier bytes. Full run after the fix: captured exit 0, 122 test files, 0 fail, 209s. All exit codes captured with redirect + echo on one command line in one shell, never through a pipe.

title: hicasso: frameless error boundary silently drops vector :on-error
description:
## Scope

implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs, plus the focused browser witness in implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs. Touch public complaint/catalogue prose only if the repair changes the stable complaint contract.

## Correctness finding

A frameless h/error-boundary accepts a vector-valued :on-error, but when a descendant fails it silently discards that intent. The boundary's render-time shape check admits every vector; later, report! wraps the vector arm in when-some on frame-of, so a missing frame simply returns nil. The fallback still catches and replaces the failed subtree, making the loss look like successful error handling while the declared reporting event never runs.

This contradicts the public promise that vector :on-error is dispatched through the boundary's frame and the package's own frameless rule: the boundary itself may be frameless only until an intent is present. A vector :on-error is an intent, not an optional best-effort callback.

## Evidence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:219-229 (check-props!) accepts :on-error whenever it is nil, a vector, or a function; it does not relate the vector arm to frame availability.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:232-235 (frame-of) can answer nil for the deliberately supported no-provider case.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:237-257 (report!) implements the vector arm as "(when-some [frame-kw (frame-of this)] ...)"; the nil case has no refusal or report and falls through to the function's final nil.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/boundary.cljs:309-328 re-establishes the frame only while lowering fallback/children. That makes an inline child intent loud, but the direct :on-error vector never passes through intent lowering and therefore misses that guard.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:404-449 proves that a frameless boundary with no intent is legal and an inline child intent refuses loudly. Its frameless harness uses a function-valued :on-error; there is no row for the subject boundary's own vector-valued :on-error.
- docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md:183 and docs/core/hicasso/cookbook.md:408-411 state that a vector :on-error is dispatched with the error appended through the frame the boundary is mounted under.
- implementation/hicasso/spec/invariants.md I10/I11 require intent semantics and loud stable failure rather than an accepted inert declaration.
- Review commands included targeted rg reads of the symbols/tests/docs and an all-status bead-corpus scan over on-error, componentDidCatch, report!, frameless, and no frame.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In the browser harness, mount an error boundary under adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel with :fallback markup, vector :on-error [:app/record-render-failure], and a child that throws during render.
2. Let React commit the boundary's error state.
3. Observe that the fallback is rendered, no :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary refusal is raised, and the declared event has no frame through which it can be dispatched. The only vector arm in report! returns nil when frame-of returns nil.

A source-level minimal reproduction is the direct control flow: check-props! accepts the vector; frame-of answers nil; report!'s when-some body is skipped.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A raw React root (or any tree deliberately carrying the no-provider context) renders:

    [h/error-boundary
     {:fallback [:p "That region failed"]
      :on-error [:app/record-render-failure]}
     [foreign-crasher]]

The declaration renders as valid. When foreign-crasher throws, React shows the fallback, but :app/record-render-failure is never dispatched and no Hicasso complaint is raised. The application loses its error record precisely when the error path is exercised.

Invariant: every accepted intent-bearing position either captures a live frame and routes exactly once or refuses loudly before it can become inert. Absence of a frame must never turn an accepted intent into a silent no-op.

## Recommended minimal fix

In the error boundary's own render, after resolving frame-kw and before rendering either branch, refuse a vector-valued :on-error when frame-kw is nil. Reuse :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary if its current contract fits, and carry at least the offending :intent plus :position :on-error.

Keep the check in render, not componentDidCatch: waiting until report! would replace the application's original failure only on the exceptional path and escape to the next boundary. Do not require a frame for the boundary generally. Nil and function-valued :on-error remain legal frameless because neither needs re-frame dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a focused browser row in boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs that mounts a healthy subject boundary under adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel with vector :on-error and proves first-render refusal with stable id :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary, the exact intent, and :position :on-error. A healthy child keeps the proof independent of descendant failure timing.
- Keep/load explicit positive controls:
  - a frameless boundary with no :on-error and no nested intent still renders;
  - a frameless boundary with function :on-error catches one deliberate descendant failure, invokes the function once, and renders its fallback;
  - the same vector :on-error under a live frame dispatches once with the caught error appended.
- Non-vacuity: removing the new frame/vector guard (restoring today's when-some-only behavior) makes the focused refusal row fail. Widening the guard to reject nil or a function makes the two frameless controls fail.
- Run the browser lane that executes the DOM row (npm run test:browser) and the focused Hicasso node/invariant gates used by this package. If an error id or catalogue wording changes, run the complaint-catalogue gate and update its governed rows; prefer reusing the existing intent-outside-boundary contract.
- Existing reset-key, fallback-intent, StrictMode once-per-failure, and live-frame isolation witnesses remain green.

## Non-goals

- Do not require every error boundary to live under a frame.
- Do not change function-valued :on-error, fallback lowering, reset/retry behavior, or what React error boundaries catch.
- Do not add a fallback dispatch channel, queue intents until a frame appears, or refactor generic intent lowering.
- Do not broaden this into overlay/presence frameless behavior.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all bead statuses and descriptions for on-error, componentDidCatch, report!, frameless, no frame, and boundary/frame combinations.

- rf2-czlb (closed) fixed unknown boundary props and malformed :on-error; its scope explicitly preserved the legal vector/function arms. It does not own the accepted vector's nil-frame behavior.
- rf2-4e5b (closed) addressed the analogous but separate frameless overlay :on-dismiss state.
- No open or in-progress bead owns vector :on-error being silently dropped without a frame.
notes:
## Verdict — 2026-09-01 (PR #8871)

FINDING CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, repaired, witnessed. Every file:line on this
bead re-derived at tip and confirmed EXACT: check-props!'s :on-error arm at
boundary.cljs:219-229, frame-of 232-235, report! 237-257, the render's frame
re-establishment 309-328, api-reference.md:183, cookbook.md:408-411. One
drift only, and it is trivial: the witness citation 404-449 names the
section comment three lines above frameless-root!, whose actual span is
407-449.

The 309-328 claim also holds as stated, and it is the shape of the fix: the
boundary re-establishes the frame around the codec walk of :fallback and
:children, so an intent at either is caught and named, while :on-error is
read straight off the props map by report! and passes through no lowering at
all. That was the one intent position a frameless boundary accepted and then
dropped.

### Site chosen: check-props!, in render

Not report!. A refusal from componentDidCatch would replace the
application's real error with a complaint about the declaration and escape
to the next boundary up — the namespace docstring already argues exactly
this for the existing shape check, and React runs render before it can run
componentDidCatch. A missing frame sharpens the argument: it is the case
where refusing late is not merely worse but indistinguishable from working,
because the fallback renders either way.

Within render the guard went into check-props! rather than inline, because
all three refusals are one class — a declaration the boundary wears while
nothing consults it — and belong at one site. check-props! now takes the
caller's frame-kw; render binds frame-kw first.

report!'s when-some on frame-of was REMOVED. It is provably dead once the
same render refuses the frameless case, and left in place it would still be
the silent drop, one guard later.

### Complaint contract UNCHANGED

Reuses :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary with :position :on-error
and the offending :intent. impl.overlay/dismissal-handler already refuses an
unroutable :on-dismiss under that id (the rf2-4e5b analogue), and
implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md's row — "lowered or fired an
intent with no frame-locked dispatch bound" — covers this site as written.
So complaints.md is untouched, and so is invariants.md: the repair makes the
code conform to I10/I11 rather than changing what they promise. That also
avoided the three-Chromium-lane toll a spec/ prose edit carries (rf2-7rzg).

### Control

Landed RED FIRST. Commit 1 is the witness alone against unrepaired source:
exit 1, 3 failures of 54 assertions, all three in
a-frameless-boundarys-own-on-error-vector-is-refused-at-first-render, with
"Escaped: nil" — nothing raised at all, the silent acceptance stated as a
measurement. After the repair: exit 0, same 11 tests and the SAME 54
assertions, so nothing skipped or crashed out of the lane. Re-run as an
explicit sabotage afterwards (checkout of the pre-repair blob) reproduced
exit 1 with the identical three failures; shadow-cljs reported "4 compiled",
which is the positive evidence the runtime observed the plant rather than
serving a stale compile. Restore verified by git blob hash against the
committed object.

Positive controls all green and all pre-existing except one: frameless with
no :on-error still renders (row 6); the same vector under a live frame still
dispatches (row 9's near miss); with the error appended, exactly once (row
10, StrictMode). Added: a frameless boundary with a FUNCTION :on-error
catching a real descendant failure and firing once — the near miss on the
exact axis this guard could have over-reached, and it passed against
UNREPAIRED source too, so it is a genuine control rather than a co-moving
assertion.

### Gates

Local, captured exit codes: full :browser-test lane 753 tests / 4115
assertions, exit 0; :node-test 11128 tests / 54669 assertions, exit 0;
check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, and exercised against a planted broken link which
it caught (exit 1, naming file and line), so its green is a check that ran.
CI on PR #8871: 84 checks, 47 pass / 37 skipping / 0 failures — including
the three-engine cljs-hicasso-controlled gate and MkDocs build, neither of
which was runnable locally.

### One scope addition, stated

docs/core/hicasso/17-errors.md gained ONE troubleshooting row for the new
refusal, beside the fallback-intent row that raises the same id. The
complaint contract did not change, so this is teaching prose rather than
catalogue prose; without it the chapter that teaches h/error-boundary would
be silent about a user-visible refusal at its own component. It mirrors the
existing row 13-overlays-and-focus.md:353 carries for the :on-dismiss
analogue. Table column counts checked by hand across all 9 rows.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8871 (worker/hicasso-boundary-wdvlp). check-props! now takes the render's frame-kw and refuses a vector :on-error with no frame, reusing :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary with :position :on-error and the offending :intent — the same contract impl.overlay/dismissal-handler uses for an unroutable :on-dismiss (rf2-4e5b's analogue), so no complaint catalogue or invariant prose changed. report!'s when-some on frame-of removed as provably dead. Witnessed by a new row in boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test that was landed RED first (3 failures, 'Escaped: nil') and is green after; existing frameless-no-intent, live-frame-dispatch and StrictMode-once controls all still pass. See the appended Verdict note for the line-number re-derivation and gate exit codes.

title: spec/docs: catalogue the flow-eval :phase discriminator (:derive / :output-write)
description:
Follow-up to rf2-gpj9r, which landed the runtime change (PR #8863) but could not touch `spec/` — hot-zone, and outside that bead's stated scope (`implementation/flows/**`, the router's consumer-side error record, focused tests).

`evaluate-flow!` now discriminates the failing flow-evaluation PHASE structurally: `:derive` when the authored callback threw, `:output-write` when it RETURNED and the framework's `(assoc-in db (:output-path flow) new-output)` threw. The phase rides three surfaces that the committed normative record does not yet describe:

- `:rf.flow/failed` trace tags gain `:phase` and `:path` (the declared output path; `:path` is the spelling `:rf.flow/computed` already uses).
- The thrown `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` ex-data gains `:rf.flow/failed-phase` and `:rf.flow/output-path`, beside the existing `:rf.flow/failed-id`.
- The always-on error record gains a top-level `:phase` slot, beside `:where :flow-eval` and `:flow-id`.

Pages to update (each currently describes the failure as purely a `:derive` throw):

- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — the `:rf.flow/failed` row's tag list (~line 618), the `:rf.flow/failed` summary row (~590), and the `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` catalogue row's always-on slot list (~2161).
- `spec/013-Flows.md` — Failure semantics (~233, ~312, ~346) and the trace-tag table.
- `spec/Conventions.md` — the `:rf.flow/*` reserved row (~71) enumerates the tag keys `:rf.flow/id` / `:rf.flow/failed-id`; add the two new ex-data keys. That namespace is 'fixed-and-additive by Spec change', so this IS the spec change.
- `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:249,271` and `docs/core/flows.md:286,395` — prose describing both signals as derive-throw signals.

No runtime change is wanted: the behaviour is already on main once #8863 merges. This is the normative record catching up.

title: pair-mcp: turn-observation recorder witness can pass on its baseline
description:
## Scope

Make live observation fit an ordinary programmer+AI tool turn. Retire Pair-MCP's progress-notification streaming subsystem: the public `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` tools; their server/runtime queue, polling, accounting, and launch-control machinery; and their schema, manifest, test, spec, skill, and conformance carriers. Establish the already-shipped result-returning tools as the one supported live-app observation workflow. Cover the smallest coherent cross-repo seam under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/**`, the companion `re-frame2-pair.runtime` preload and Pair skill, and the MCP conformance fixtures that pin the public catalogue.

## Findings

- The source catalogue exposes 33 tools. Four are one push-streaming subsystem, and four environment/launch controls exist only to bound that subsystem (`MAX_STREAMS`, event rate, abuse threshold, abuse window). This is a large public and configuration tax for an optional observation route.
- `subscribe` does not return observations as the tool result. It holds `tools/call` open until cancellation/cap/termination, emits useful data through `notifications/progress`, then returns only a terminal summary. Pair-MCP's own live conformance witness must keep a `subscribePromise` open and issue `dispatch` concurrently to exercise it. That is a valid custom MCP-client pattern, but not the natural sequential turn shape of a coding agent; out-of-band `unsubscribe` has the same second-concurrent-call assumption.
- Every normal pairing outcome already has a turn-shaped route: `dispatch` returns its consequence or settled epoch; `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` read bounded history; `watch-until` blocks to a data predicate and returns the sample; `record` + `read-recording` cover human/intermittent interaction; and `tail-build` waits for hot reload. The rare need for a bespoke live listener remains expressible through the default-enabled `eval-cljs` escape hatch and does not justify four permanent public tools.
- Eight dedicated Pair-MCP source/test files (`subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, `get-stream-controls`, `resource-controls`, and their three largest focused suites) already total 3,056 lines / 156,022 bytes, before `resource_controls_test.cljs`, the preload's subscription queues/listener fan-out, server/config plumbing, the long catalogue sections, skill prose, and the dedicated live conformance script are counted.
- The complexity is not passive. The stream needs dual event/byte queue caps, drop-oldest accounting, a token bucket, an abuse window, dead-connection retry/termination, cancellation and out-of-band teardown, per-tick cap/dedup/elision, and two diagnostic tools to explain the controls. History records repeated follow-on repairs for lost events, uncapped progress frames, dead drain loops, privacy projection, frame scoping, and control observability.
- The generated descriptor manifest is already 88,930 bytes for the full catalogue. Removing four host-specialized tools reduces the always-advertised surface as well as implementation weight; retaining them as aliases would preserve the cost and defeat the pre-alpha simplification.

## Recommended Action

Delete `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` from the registry and remove the streaming-only server/runtime implementation: runtime subscription queues and drain API, polling controller, progress payloads, concurrent-slot/rate/abuse controls, their flags/environment variables, diagnostics, and teardown state. Do not add a generic replacement, deprecated aliases, tombstones, or a compatibility mode.

Rewrite the Pair routing guidance around returned-result workflows:

1. Use `dispatch` consequence/settle for an action the agent initiated.
2. Use `watch-epochs` or `trace-window` for retained event/trace history.
3. Use `watch-until` for a known asynchronous condition.
4. Use `record` + `read-recording` while a human or the browser drives the app.
5. Use `tail-build` for code reload.

Keep `list-subscriptions`: it reads the app's reactive subscription cache and is unrelated to MCP progress streams. Preserve the retained tools' existing privacy projection, elision, wire caps, and explicit time bounds; do not replace deleted stream controls with another permission or resource-control layer.

## Evidence

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/registry.cljs` registers the four tools as a distinct streaming/diagnostic family.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/subscribe.cljs` is 864 lines. Its contract says the call runs until abort/unsubscribe and carries observations in `notifications/progress`; the final result is a summary. `resource_controls.cljs` adds another 479 lines.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-subscribe.cjs` explicitly starts `client.callTool(subscribe)` without awaiting it, fires `dispatch` concurrently, accumulates `onprogress` callbacks, and only later awaits the terminal subscription result. The test demonstrates the concurrency contract rather than a normal one-call/one-result agent workflow.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/package.json`, `spec/API.md`, and `spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` expose the stream configuration, progress wire shape, caps, filters, diagnostics, and five termination paths.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs` owns the streaming queue/listener fan-out (`subscribe!`, `drain-subscription!`, `unsubscribe!`, `subscription-info`) in addition to the retained history and recorder surfaces.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/tool-descriptors.edn` reports 33 tools and is 88,930 bytes; the streaming family consumes four names and their always-loaded descriptions/schemas.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/get_re_frame2_pair_instructions.cljs` already presents `watch-until`, `record`, `subscribe`, and `tail-build` as alternate waiting routes, confirming overlap at the routing layer.
- Source/commit history identifies the additive lineage and its repair tail: rf2-hq49 (push subscribe/unsubscribe), rf2-ho4ve (byte budget), rf2-uvfph (rate-limit event preservation), rf2-a0kxsb / rf2-3ijbl (controls and observability), and rf2-ajhwbm (dead drain-loop termination).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` are absent from `registry/tools`, `tools/list`, the canonical tool-name fixture, generated descriptor manifest, conformance corpus, package README/API/catalogue, Pair skill allow-list/routing, and current capability/status docs. No alias, deprecated descriptor, or unknown-tool special case preserves them.
2. Streaming-only Pair-MCP files and code paths are removed. The server has no progress-notification emitter, stream slot/token-bucket/abuse-window state, stream-specific launch flags or environment variables, or stream cleanup branch. The preload has no Pair-owned stream registry, bounded event queue, drain loop API, or stream-only listener fan-out. Shared framework trace/epoch facilities used by retained reads remain intact.
3. `list-subscriptions` remains and is documented/tested as the reactive app subscription-cache read, with no streaming terminology or dependency.
4. A live end-to-end witness proves the retained turn-shaped workflow without concurrent MCP calls: dispatch an event, observe its returned consequence and retained epoch/trace; a focused `watch-until` test returns a matching asynchronous sample; and the existing recorder path still captures and returns a browser/human-driven change. Each observation reaches the agent in a completed tool result, not a progress callback.
5. Tool annotations, schemas, `tool-descriptors.edn`, the stdio catalogue snapshot, and cross-server MCP conformance agree with the reduced surface. The Pair package tests, descriptor-drift check, stdio round trip, and relevant live fixture/conformance lanes pass non-vacuously.
6. Current docs state one observation decision tree using the five retained routes above. Historical design notes may record that push streaming once existed, but no current setup, recipe, status table, or diagnostic ladder instructs an agent to use it.
7. No new public tool, compatibility shim, permission gate, scheduler, queue, or background service is introduced to replace the deleted subsystem.

## Non-goals

- Removing or weakening `read-sub` / `list-subscriptions`, framework trace/epoch listeners, epoch retention, privacy projection, elision, or the ordinary per-response wire cap.
- Redesigning the remaining 29-tool catalogue, globally rewriting descriptor prose, or combining unrelated tools in this change.
- Changing MCP itself, adding a different streaming transport, or supporting dashboard/telemetry clients whose primary workload is continuous event consumption.
- Preserving compatibility for the four removed pre-alpha names, migration aliases, deprecation windows, or launch-flag no-ops.
- Tightening eval/write permissions or adding safety confirmations. The installed local Pair-MCP and explicit invoker remain the trust boundary.

## Related beads

No open or in-progress duplicate was found after title and full-description searches for `subscribe`, `stream`, `notifications/progress`, `push-mode`, `list-streams`, and `resource-control`.

- `rf2-wyza` (closed) removed the duplicated 33-entry onboarding catalogue in favor of routing rules after measuring the permanent tools/list context tax; this is the same pre-alpha/trust-the-agent posture applied to a redundant runtime subsystem.
- `rf2-ov144` (open) is an adjacent Pair-MCP catalogue change for replay-by-epoch-id. It is not a dependency; coordinate registry/manifest edits if both land concurrently.

title: surface-review(skill-setup): make one prompt produce one mounted SPA
description:
## Scope

Treat `skills/re-frame2-setup/**` as one installed product and make its unqualified greenfield request do one thing well: turn an empty directory into a running Reagent counter SPA in one pass. The default path owns the exact files, resolving dependency baseline, commands, verification, and handoff. Keep UIx and merge-into-an-empty-CLJS-project support only when the author explicitly asks for those routes. Align the emitted result with the reduced canonical scaffold owned by `rf2-zq34m`; do not maintain a second independent project template.

## Findings

1. The advertised six-step path is not a fast path. A brand-new Reagent run needs `SKILL.md` plus `deps-versions.md`, `shadow-cljs.md`, and `first-counter.md`: 75,697 bytes and about 9,942 words before the agent writes the project. If it follows the boot explanation pointer too, `entry-namespace.md` adds another 22,547 bytes. Four of the five reference leaves are over the family 16 KB ceiling, while `spec/design.md` says only `entry-namespace.md` is slightly over and that a typical session reads two leaves.
2. The default request is forced into an interview. `deps-versions.md` says the author must choose a pin and the skill must stop before editing if none was supplied. `SKILL.md` also forbids the skill from executing the repo's one-command generator and tells it to hand the command back to the author. Thus “Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me” cannot complete without a choice and a second actor.
3. The first-mount route carries decisions unrelated to mounting: schemas, Xray, `@xyflow/react`, `elkjs`, a right-side host column, CSP/production-hardening prose, publication-state branching, and substrate-specific devtools policy. Reagent is nominally the default, but UIx/Xray/Hicasso distinctions occupy cardinal rules, the main checklist, troubleshooting, and handoff before the default counter exists.
4. The copyable runtime code is currently sound: it uses the current `rf/init!` + explicit `frame-root` seed, frame-targeted schema attach, retained React root, and measured-correct `^:dev/after-load` mount path; the local-root compile cover exercises both Reagent and UIx. The gap is the product journey, not a need for more API explanation.
5. The strongest setup compile test does not materialise the documented dependency file. It synthesises a separate deps map with placeholder Maven versions, rewrites framework coordinates to monorepo `:local/root`, and proves only `compile app`. It neither proves that the exact default dependency command/coordinate resolves from an empty consumer project nor boots the page and clicks 0→1.
6. The 16 evals are explicitly trigger-only (`should_trigger`); none grades the response, resulting files, commands, no-question default, mounted DOM, or handoff. The 1,162-line structural suite instead locks Xray layout, CSP wording, publication branches, UIx routing, and the prohibition on executing the generator. It protects accumulated policy better than the outcome named by the skill.
7. History shows accretion. The initial skill commit shipped `SKILL.md` plus four references at 36,433 bytes and taught core + adapter as the day-one path. The current corresponding shipped corpus is 105,173 bytes after schema, Xray, UIx, CSP/release, troubleshooting, and parity rules accumulated. The useful hot-reload correction in `rf2-r0kk7` / `rf2-ms6r8` came from a real watch-and-browser measurement, demonstrating the kind of outcome proof this skill still lacks.

## Recommended Action

- Define a zero-interview default: an unqualified request in an empty directory chooses Reagent, a single reviewed resolving baseline appropriate to the current publication state, the conventional app namespace/build id/port, and the smallest runnable counter. A user-supplied pin or UIx request overrides the default; absence of either is not a reason to stop.
- Make the main skill a short executor and router. Put the entire default in one copy-complete shipped source (or an asset mechanically derived from the canonical reduced template) with exact filenames and commands. The skill should never reassemble one project from three large prose leaves or hand-maintain a second template.
- Execute the normal work under the explicit invocation: create the files, run `npm install`, run a terminating compile check, start the dev server, and report the URL. Broaden the routine command grants as needed; do not preserve the current user-run-generator prohibition as policy.
- Match `rf2-zq34m`'s small SPA contract. Keep only dependencies and source needed for the counter and selected adapter. Move schemas, Xray, Story, HTTP, production CSP/hosting, Pair, and other capabilities to a compact next-steps link instead of installing or explaining them on the default route.
- Keep explicit UIx and empty-project merge recipes as secondary leaves. They may share the substrate-neutral counter, but they must not introduce a wizard, option matrix, compatibility aliases, or questions into the default.
- Replace prose-lock emphasis with an exact-output behavioral contract: consume the same shipped source the skill uses, resolve its real deps, compile it, serve its real page, and assert the counter paints and advances 0→1. Keep small structural checks only where they prevent a false-green.
- End with a factual handoff: files created, command verified, URL, and the single next skill for application authoring. Mention optional tools only when requested.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:51-63` makes schemas/Xray and their npm dependencies day-one, carries the substrate/tool matrix, and makes the generator user-run only; lines 68-81 repeat route-specific checks and handoff text.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/deps-versions.md:65-73` requires an author-selected pin and explicitly says to stop before editing; line 77 begins a long publication-state/manual coordinate branch.
- Current measured sizes: `SKILL.md` 16,439 B; `deps-versions.md` 21,457 B; `entry-namespace.md` 22,547 B; `first-counter.md` 18,660 B; `shadow-cljs.md` 19,141 B; `shared-dataflow.md` 6,929 B. `skills/README.md` sets a 16 KB leaf ceiling.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/spec/design.md:17,46` locks “the author runs the build; the skill doesn't”; line 109 claims the smaller progressive-disclosure shape that the current file sizes and happy-path routing contradict.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/evals/evals.json:4-22` is trigger-only despite prompts explicitly asking the skill to start from nothing and mount a counter.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj:109-1153` contains 15 numbered structural locks (including Xray, CSP, publication state, and generator prohibition).
- `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj:1204-1490` synthesises setup deps, rewrites them to local roots, and stops at compile.
- Git history: initial commit `1806995740`; measured hot-reload repairs `rf2-r0kk7` and `rf2-ms6r8`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From an empty directory, the positive prompt “Scaffold a re-frame2 app for me” takes no clarification round, writes a deterministic Reagent project with no `<VERSION>`/`<SHA>` placeholders, and uses one resolving baseline stored in one source of truth.

title: bug(mcp-base): dedup aliases legitimate payload values as cache references
description:
## Scope

Fix the shared structural-dedup wire codec in `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc` and its JSON-side mirror in `tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs`. Keep Pair-MCP and Story-MCP tool names, arguments, opt-out behavior, and the `:rf.mcp/dedup-table` outer envelope unchanged. Update the focused specs/tests that define the reference representation.

## Correctness finding

Dedup references are not distinguishable from legitimate payload data. The Clojure/CLJS decoder classifies every symbol whose namespace is `de-dupe.cache` as a cache reference, without requiring the symbol to name a real entry. The JSON mirror is broader: after JSON erases the symbol/string distinction, it treats every string beginning `de-dupe.cache/` as a reference. Therefore `expand` is not the exact inverse promised by the codec for arbitrary persistent data. A payload scalar can become `nil`, another cached subtree, a thrown missing-reference error, or a cycle merely because its value occupies the codec's in-band namespace.

## Evidence

- `dedup.cljc:160-165` defines `cache-element?` as `symbol?` plus namespace equality only; `dedup.cljc:347-360` immediately routes every such value to `expand-entry` and reads `(get cache cache-id)` even when the table has no matching slot.
- `dedup-envelope.cjs:62-64,81-83` uses `startsWith('de-dupe.cache/')`; `dedup-envelope.cjs:137-141` then throws when that ordinary string has no table entry. JSON serialization makes real reference symbols and ordinary payload strings share this same representation.
- Both shipped consumers enable this codec on value-rich, programmer-owned data: Pair-MCP epoch/snapshot/subscribe payloads and Story-MCP run/preview/record payloads. An unrelated repeated subtree is enough to activate the wrapper, so the colliding scalar need not itself repeat.
- The current cross-host dedup suite proves common collection kinds and real references, but has no literal payload value in the reference namespace and no JSON string collision arm.

## Steps to Reproduce

Evaluate the real JVM codec with:

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.mcp-base.dedup :as d]
         '[re-frame.mcp-base.vocab :as v])
(let [shared  {:big [:repeat :me]}
      payload {:literal 'de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref
               :a shared
               :b shared}
      wrapped (d/dedup-value payload true)
      cache   (get wrapped v/dedup-table-key)]
  {:wrapped? (contains? wrapped v/dedup-table-key)
   :expanded (d/expand cache)
   :equal?   (= payload (d/expand cache))})
```

Current result is non-vacuously wrapped, but `:literal` expands to `nil` and `:equal?` is false. In the Node mirror, placing the ordinary JSON string `"de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref"` beside a real cache reference throws `cache reference ... has no matching entry`.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A re-frame app legitimately stores a namespaced symbol in app-db, a story emits one in rendered/diagnostic data, or a structured payload contains a string with the same spelling. The payload also contains ordinary repeated state, which is common in epoch pairs and enables dedup. The server advertises a successful dedup envelope, but the agent reconstructs data different from the server's value (or cannot reconstruct it at all). The required invariant is: for every supported payload value `x`, `expand(de-dupe-eq(x)) = x`, and the JSON projection must preserve the same semantic value; cache references must be unambiguous from user data.

## Recommended minimal fix

Retain the outer envelope and make the existing reference tokens collision-free rather than adding a compatibility layer. During the encoder's existing discovery walk, record literal payload symbols and strings that can collide with `de-dupe.cache/cache-N`, and allocate cache ids that skip those spellings. On decode, classify only an exact cache-id token that is present in the current cache, not every value sharing the namespace/prefix. Apply the same exact-entry rule in the Node mirror. This preserves the compact wire shape while making the encoder's own output unambiguous. If a smaller closed reference representation proves simpler, change it in one pre-alpha cut across the base spec, both decoders, and conformance fixtures; do not support two formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a cross-host test in `re-frame.mcp-base.dedup-test` whose payload contains (a) an ordinary `de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref` symbol, (b) an ordinary generated-looking `de-dupe.cache/cache-1` symbol, and (c) an unrelated repeated subtree. Assert the result actually contains `:rf.mcp/dedup-table` (non-vacuity/control), `expand` equals the original payload, and both literal symbols remain symbols with their exact values.
2. Add the JSON-mirror counterpart with ordinary strings `de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref` and `de-dupe.cache/cache-1` beside at least one real cache reference. Assert `decodeDedupEnvelope` reconstructs the exact strings and the real reference. As a positive control, a deliberately missing genuine reference must still fail loudly, proving reference resolution was not disabled wholesale.
3. Existing real-reference compression remains active: a repeated subtree produces more than the root cache entry and expands exactly on JVM and CLJS.
4. The reference grammar and collision rule are stated once in `tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md` and mirrored by the Node conformance decoder; no prefix-only decoder remains.
5. Focused commands pass non-vacuously: from `tools/mcp-base`, `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.mcp-base.dedup-test` and `npm run test:cljs`; from the repository root, `npm run test:dedup-envelope --prefix tools/mcp-conformance`.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning which tools are dedup-eligible, changing the default-on posture, or removing the `dedup false` escape hatch.
- Adding a general serialization framework, schema registry, compatibility alias, or dual-format decoder.
- Optimizing compression ratios or changing equality-vs-identity pooling.
- Hardening arbitrary attacker-authored cache tables beyond preserving the existing loud failure for malformed genuine references.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status tracker searches were run for `dedup`, `de-dupe`, `de-dupe.cache`, `cache reference`, `cache-ref`, `cache-N`, `cache element`, `namespaced symbol`, `symbol collision`, `payload symbol`, `unknown cache`, `dedup table`, `round-trip`, and `roundtrip`, including description and notes searches where supported. No bead describes this alias/corruption outcome. Closed `rf2-ntbd1` concerns package ownership of the epoch diff codec and explicitly leaves dedup in mcp-base; it is not a duplicate. Open dedup mentions concern recorder/stream/tool-surface design, not cache-reference representation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cross-host codec test is forced through a real dedup wrapper by an unrelated repeated subtree, then round-trips literal reserved-namespace and generated-looking symbols exactly.
- Node JSON decoder preserves same-spelling ordinary strings while resolving a real cache reference; a missing genuine reference remains a loud-failure positive control.
- Existing repeated-subtree compression remains non-vacuously active and exact on JVM and CLJS.
- Focused mcp-base JVM/CLJS and conformance dedup-envelope commands pass.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT TIP. dedup.cljc's cache-element? was symbol? + namespace
equality only, and dedup-envelope.cjs classified on startsWith('de-dupe.cache/'),
throwing on a missing entry. Both confirmed before any edit; the finding holds.

WIRE DECISION — escaping, NOT the recommended id-skipping. References are now
SPELLED: in value position `de-dupe.cache/cache-<digits>` is a reference,
`de-dupe.cache/!<rest>` is an escaped literal of `de-dupe.cache/<rest>`, and
anything else in the namespace is payload data. The encoder escapes (one leading
`!`) every payload token that would otherwise read as one of the first two forms,
so its own output is unambiguous by construction. Reversible under repetition;
applied to symbols AND same-spelled strings, type-preserving, so the JSON
projection is exact as well as the Clojure round-trip. Escape runs as a pre-pass
BEFORE the counting walk so both passes hash the same subtrees and pooling still
fires on a subtree carrying a colliding literal.

WHY NOT ID-SKIPPING (the description's "recommended minimal fix"): skipping
colliding ids forces the decoder to classify by TABLE PRESENCE, and that silently
drops the loud failure on a genuinely missing reference — which acceptance
criterion 2 requires kept. The two halves of AC2 are not jointly satisfiable under
id-skipping. Escaping satisfies both: `cache-<digits>` is a reference whether or
not the slot exists (missing => loud), while ordinary namespace-occupying values
decode verbatim. Taken as one pre-alpha cut across codec, spec and Node decoder;
no dual-format path.

--- 2026-09-01 14:12 AUSEST — AUDIT REOPEN CLOSED, PR #8879 (worker/mcp-dedup2-kjv05) ---

AUDIT PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, AND IT UNDERSTATED THE BLAST RADIUS. Reproduced the
audit's probe across the real CLJ -> Cheshire -> Node seam (real dedup-value, real
cheshire.core/generate-string, real decodeDedupEnvelope) BEFORE any edit, comparing the
decoded result against the payload's own JSON projection. 3 of 6 arms failed, exit 1:

  kw-value   {:literal :de-dupe.cache/cache-1 :a shared :b shared}  -- the audit's probe
             verbatim. `literal` decoded as {"big":["repeat","me"]}, the cached subtree.
  kw-key     the same keyword in map-KEY position. The key resolved to the subtree and the
             entry landed under its JSON.stringify -- unreachable by its own name.
             NOT NAMED BY THE AUDIT; found by the reproduction.
  kw-escaped payload :de-dupe.cache/!cache-1. Unescaped, so the decoder stripped a marker
             that was never added and returned .../cache-1. A DIFFERENT corruption from the
             aliasing one -- the escape's own reversibility-under-repetition breaking.
             NOT NAMED BY THE AUDIT.

kw-plain, sym-value and str-value passed, so #8854's symbol/string fix stands and was not
disabled. After the fix: 6 of 6, exit 0, with the Node decoder BYTE-IDENTICAL.

FIX SIDE: ENCODER, continuing #8854's direction rather than adding a reader rule. The
classifier side cannot be made to work at all here -- by the time the Node mirror sees a
token, JSON has erased symbol/keyword/string onto one string, so no reader-side grammar can
separate them. The repair is to CLOSE the set the encoder escapes rather than widen it:
`token-name` now tests `ident?` (was `symbol?`) and `string?`, and `retoken` preserves all
three types. Symbol, keyword and string are exactly the scalars a JSON encoder renders as a
bare namespaced string; no other Clojure scalar can produce a slash-bearing name in this
namespace. The set is now closed, not merely larger.

THE NODE DECODER NEEDED NO LOGIC CHANGE, and that is the result rather than a shortcut: its
grammar is type-blind, so it already decoded the wider output under the same three rules.
Only its contract comment and its fixtures moved. That property is now stated in both files
so the next widening does not go looking for a decoder edit.

WHY THIS SURVIVED A GREEN SUITE, recorded because it is the reusable lesson: `cache-element?`
tests `symbol?`, so an unescaped payload keyword is never aliased on the JVM or in CLJS and
every round-trip assertion passes. The Clojure round-trip CANNOT SEE this bug. The new
host-side tests therefore pin the WIRE SPELLING, not only the round-trip -- confirmed by the
planted-fault run below, where the round-trip test stayed green while the spelling tests went
red. A keyword is the ordinary spelling of both a value and a map key in re-frame app-db data,
so this was the likeliest of the three collisions to be hit in practice.

RESIDUAL AMBIGUITY -- one, inherent to JSON, not to this codec: the Clojure TYPE is not
recovered across the wire. A payload symbol, keyword and string in this namespace all reach a
Node consumer as the same string, as they would anywhere else in the payload; JSON has no
symbol or keyword. The restored guarantee is that the JSON PROJECTION passes through the codec
unchanged (encode-then-decode is the identity on it), alongside the exact Clojure round-trip on
the host. Stated in tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md so it is not refiled as a bug.

HOW THE MIRRORED PAIR WAS PROVED TO AGREE: primarily by the boundary probe -- one artefact
crossing the seam, the unmodified decoder fed the new encoder's real Cheshire output, 3/6 ->
6/6. Committed coverage mirrors it: the Clojure side pins the wire spelling, and the Node
fixtures are transcribed from a real Cheshire encode of the matching payloads rather than
hand-built. RECORDED HONESTLY IN THE SPEC: no committed gate runs the whole seam in one
process -- mcp-base's suites have no JSON encoder and no access to the Node decoder, and
mcp-conformance's Node unit cluster deliberately boots no JVM. Mirrored spellings plus an
out-of-band probe are the coverage. Building a committed crossing gate was considered and
rejected as out of scope and cross-artefact-coupling (mcp-base is a published library and must
not reach into mcp-conformance); if wanted it is a separate bead, not a silent addition here.

I (as mayor) got this wrong TWICE in one session, both times on a migration/ README, and both times the filename was the trigger: the name README.md pattern-matches to "the readme gate" faster than the path resolves to "a docs-gate root". (1) rf2-3lhuj — I ran a careful dependency analysis proving it was not blocked by rf2-0dcoa, and dispatched it. (2) rf2-0dcoa — I twice escalated this to the operator as a live ruling awaiting his decision. The ruling had been MADE and EXECUTED: commit 5fbfcfb20d deleted the five wrappers and is an ancestor of main; grep confirms zero defwrapper occurrences remain. I was escalating a decision nobody owed.

THE CHEAP SWEEP that finds this class in one command, worth running in the backlog-reread loop rather than per-item:
  for id in $(bd list --status open --limit 0 | grep -oE "rf2-[a-z0-9.-]+" | sort -u); do git log --oneline --since="7 days ago" --grep="$id" origin/main; done
It surfaced NINE open beads with merged commits citing them in one pass.

BUT A COMMIT-SUBJECT MATCH IS NOT A CLOSE. It is a pointer to go and read the tree. Some hits are partial work, and some are the very change the item was filed AGAINST — rf2-0o5dx has a merged commit citing it while its title says the defect STILL stands, so closing on the match would repeat the original error one level up. Confirm in the source (the symbol is gone, the text now reads correctly) before closing, exactly as rf2-0dcoa was confirmed by grepping for the deleted wrappers.

The rule already exists and is pasted into every dispatch preamble: "the cheapest guard is the TREE, not the item". It is addressed to the worker, and its audience LOOKS like the worker, which is why the mayor skips it.

MERGE-LOOP HAZARD: the draft interlock does NOT protect a fix worker. The method has workers publish as a draft and mark ready as their last act, so the merge loop cannot merge out from under a live author. A FIX worker dispatched onto an EXISTING branch inherits a PR that is already marked ready — by its original author, who has finished — so nothing in the rollup or the PR state says a second worker is currently inside that branch. The merge criterion tests the change, the change goes green, and the merge lands while the fix worker is still running.

Observed 2026-09-01: PR #8873 was merged on a clean five-clause pass while its fix worker (dispatched ~34 min earlier onto worker/routing-encoding-j3tud) was still live and had not reported done. Nothing was lost — its commits were what went green and they landed — but that was luck about timing, not a guarantee: had it been mid-way through a second commit, the merge would have taken a partial change.

THE ASYMMETRY TO REMEMBER: for an ordinary dispatch, draft/ready is a reliable liveness signal. For a fix dispatch, it is stale by construction and says nothing. The mayor holds the only live-worker knowledge (the dispatch ledger and the agent listing), so on a PR that has a fix worker assigned, check the agent is finished before merging rather than trusting the PR state. Candidate method-doc gap; raise at the next method-reread rather than acting on it here.
