title: bug(realworld-http): optimistic comment replies can settle into a different article route
description:
## Scope

Keep RealWorld HTTP comment mutations owned by the `/article/:slug` page that issued them. Scope is `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs` plus the existing production-source CLJS suite. Reuse the `:comments :slug` fact and `reply-for-current-slug?` introduced by PR #8845; no framework or mutation abstraction work.

## Correctness finding

PR #8845 correlates article/comments READ replies, but the optimistic comment WRITE callbacks in the same file remain slug-free and mutate the one shared comments/form state unconditionally.

- `:comment-form/submit` reads the current slug for the POST path, but emits `:on-success [:comment-form/submit-success temp-id]` and `:on-failure [:comment-form/submit-error temp-id]`. A reply from alpha after navigation to beta can reset beta's current draft/form on success or surface alpha's failure on beta.
- `:comment/delete` likewise sends `:on-failure [:comment/delete-rollback prior]`. If alpha's DELETE fails after beta has loaded, the rollback inserts alpha's saved comment into beta's comments vector.
- None of those terminal handlers consults the new `reply-for-current-slug?` gate. The new source commentary says every reply target carries the requested slug and every terminal handler gates its write, but that is true only of the two reads.

This is not hypothetical request-id protection: these writes carry no shared cross-route request id that would suppress a late terminal reply. The current main still has the slug-free target vectors above.

## Reproduction

Load alpha, begin either an optimistic comment submit or delete with its HTTP reply held, navigate to beta and settle beta's comments load, then deliver alpha's terminal reply. Alpha submit failure writes beta's form error; alpha delete failure inserts alpha's comment into beta's list. The beta route and `[:comments :slug]` remain beta throughout.

## Minimal fix

Carry the issuing slug in the submit success/failure and delete rollback target vectors, and gate each state-changing terminal handler with the existing comments-slice correlation predicate before touching comments or form state. The delete success handler is a no-op and needs no machinery. Keep temp-id/prior payloads for their current optimistic reconciliation jobs.

## Non-goals

No generic route-owned mutation layer, request cancellation scheme, cache, comment-form redesign, or changes to managed HTTP. Do not broaden this into unrelated article social controls without a reproduced defect.

## Duplicate search

All-status searches covered cross-slug comments, comment submit/delete rollback, late comment replies, route correlation, `comment/delete`, and the RealWorld handler names. No owner was found. `rf2-iy3d6` deliberately scoped itself to route-driven reads and explicitly listed optimistic comment behavior as a non-goal, so this is a discovered follow-up rather than a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused production-source CLJS test holds an alpha comment submit or delete reply, navigates to and loads beta, then delivers alpha's submit success/failure and delete failure; beta's comments slice and current form remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The request target vectors carry the issuing slug, and all state-changing terminal handlers refuse a slug that differs from `[:comments :slug]` via the existing correlation helper.
- Current-slug controls prove submit reconciliation and delete rollback still work normally; the gate must not swallow every reply.
- The focused RealWorld CLJS suite and examples compile gate pass. No framework API or new abstraction is added.

title: surface-review(flows): make dynamic flow toggles settle automatically
description:
## Scope

Change the runtime semantics of the existing `:rf.fx/reg-flow` and `:rf.fx/clear-flow` effects so their app-db consequences settle automatically on the dispatching frame. Keep the existing effect ids and 3-slot registration payload. This includes the flows runtime, the core fx/router integration it uses, focused tests/conformance, Spec 013, the API/core guides, and the shipped cart example.

## Verified Findings

- The reserved flow effects run after the event's flow transform. A flow registered by an event therefore has no output until another event drains; a flow cleared by an event leaves its old output in app-db until another event drains.
- The clear case is observably incoherent at the dispatch boundary: the registry row is already gone while the derived value it owned is still present.
- The documented solution makes every caller invent and dispatch a no-op event. The shipped cart defines `:cart/touch` solely for this purpose and emits it after both apply and remove. This is ceremony in the event catalogue, trace stream, tests, docs, and generated code, not application behavior.
- The current tracker contains no open, in-progress, deferred, or closed issue that owns automatic settling for flow lifecycle effects. Spec 013 itself labels synchronous re-walk as an untracked note.

## Recommended Action

After a successful `:rf.fx/reg-flow` or `:rf.fx/clear-flow`, have the runtime request one private, same-frame settling drain for the parent event. Reuse the existing run-to-completion queue and ordinary flow pass: this is the framework performing the exact follow-up drain it currently tells every application to hand-write. Keep one app-db install per individual event; do not re-run flows inline in the original fx walk. The private transport must not become an application-facing event or option.

Make this the only default. Delete the lag workaround contract instead of adding a synchronous variant, a `:settle?` flag, or compatibility behavior.

## Concrete Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:858` through `:869` calls the lag the least-obvious behavior and instructs callers to dispatch a follow-up no-op event.
- `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1148` through `:1184` proves clear removes the registry entry while leaving `[:wizard :result]` stale until `:touch`; `:1186` through `:1220` locks the registration lag and workaround.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:149` through `:191` spends a full handler plus two extra `:dispatch` pairs on `:cart/touch`, whose only purpose is to cause another flow walk.
- `docs/core/flows.md:299` through `:321`, `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:153`, `spec/013-Flows.md` under "Sequencing"/"Open questions", and `spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-toggle-via-fx.edn` all publish or pin the same lag.
- Git history shows the behavior was documented rather than removed: `256e6693aa` (rf2-1smwp) added the mid-event signpost, and `16bbd2f349` (rf2-2qd9wp) extended the lag to in-drain clear semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dispatching one event whose only lifecycle action is `:rf.fx/reg-flow` leaves the flow registered and its initial output materialized once the synchronous/run-to-completion dispatch settles, without an app-authored follow-up event.
- Dispatching one event with `:rf.fx/clear-flow` leaves the flow absent, its output path vacated, and existing dependent flows recomputed against that absence by the same settle boundary. The cart's apply/remove actions update `:cart/discount-rate` and `:cart/total` after one user dispatch.
- Automatic settling is frame-correct, uses the normal topo/dirty-check pass, and preserves the one-app-db-install-per-event invariant and existing derive-failure reporting.
- The public effect ids and payloads do not change, and no public settle event, flag, alternate effect, or new lifecycle API is added.
- Focused CLJ and CLJS tests fail under the old lag behavior and pass under the new default. The conformance fixture is flipped from "next app event" to automatic settle.
- The cart deletes `:cart/touch` and both manual settle dispatches. Spec 013, API/core docs, comments, and tests no longer teach or assert a user-authored no-op workaround.

## Non-goals

- Do not perform a second app-db install inside the original event.
- Do not add fixed-point iteration, conditional/liveness policies, a general scheduler abstraction, or a public "run flows now" command.
- Do not redesign the 3-slot `reg-flow` grammar, static boot registration, the optional-artifact boundary, tooling projections, classification, or exact-incarnation machinery in this task.
- Do not preserve the lag behind a compatibility switch; this is pre-alpha.

## Related beads

- No duplicate owner exists in the current 1,060-issue tracker corpus (all statuses searched across title, description, notes, and close reason for the effect ids, lag, no-op follow-up, dynamic toggle, and settle terms).
- Historical rf2-1smwp documented the registration lag; historical rf2-2qd9wp made in-drain clear preserve the same next-drain behavior. They explain the current contract but do not own removing the application workaround.
- Spec 013 "Synchronous re-walk after `:rf.fx/reg-flow`" is explicitly marked post-v1 and untracked. This task takes the smaller route: automate the already-supported follow-up drain rather than re-walk inline.

title: api-manifest omits the published re-frame.hicasso door on both hosts
description:
## Scope

The generic public-API manifest pipeline in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/**`, its committed `spec/api-manifest.edn` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` outputs, and the published public door `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc`.

## Correctness finding

The API-manifest gate promises drift detection for public vars, but `re-frame.hicasso` is absent from both host inventories: the JVM generator does not load it, and the CLJS analyzer probe does not enumerate it. Additions, removals, or renames in this published split-host public namespace can therefore remain invisible to the repository's generic API-contract gate.

## Evidence

- `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn` publishes `day8/re-frame2-hicasso` and declares `re-frame.hicasso` as its build main; the namespace describes itself as "HICASSO — the public door."
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/deps.edn` says its classpath contains core plus every optional feature artefact, but has no Hicasso local root.
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj` says `--check` detects a public var added, removed, or renamed, but its `jvm-namespaces` roster omits `re-frame.hicasso`.
- The CLJS probe `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/test/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_manifest_probe_cljs_test.cljs` neither requires `re-frame.hicasso` nor includes it in its live-public or fully-rowed namespace sets.
- Neither committed API-manifest file contains a `re-frame.hicasso` row, despite the namespace exporting JVM macros such as `defview`, `event`, and `defhost`, plus CLJS runtime aliases/functions.
- The former Hicasso-specific public-surface/naming census was removed with the other retired one-off policy gates under `rf2-6c12m.8`; no live complete census makes this generic omission harmless.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the API generator in check mode from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`; it passes while producing no `re-frame.hicasso` rows.
2. Run the existing CLJS manifest probe; it passes although its namespace roster does not contain `re-frame.hicasso`.
3. As a temporary control, add a harmless public CLJS function beside Hicasso's existing runtime aliases and rerun the probe. The current probe still cannot report that public because it never requires or enumerates the namespace. Restore the control.
4. The equivalent JVM control is a temporary public macro beside `defhost`: generator `--check` remains unaware because Hicasso is absent from both its classpath and namespace roster.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A maintainer adds or renames a Hicasso public runtime alias, or removes/renames a public macro, while updating ordinary call sites. The API generator check and CLJS manifest reconciliation can both stay green because neither host ever asks about that namespace. The required invariant is: every live public var exposed by the published `re-frame.hicasso` door is represented and reconciled on its applicable host, and stale rows are rejected.

## Recommended minimal fix

Use the existing generic machinery: add the Hicasso local root to the manifest tool classpath, enroll `re-frame.hicasso` in JVM generation, and enroll its runtime side in the existing CLJS analyzer probe/fully-rowed reconciliation. Model the `.cljc` host split with the existing classification-row and sidecar facilities, then regenerate the committed manifests. Do not add another bespoke checker or workflow job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The JVM generator loads `re-frame.hicasso`, and the committed manifest contains and reconciles its public JVM macros.
- The CLJS analyzer probe enumerates `re-frame.hicasso` and reconciles every live CLJS public runtime var for that namespace.
- An executable non-vacuity assertion fails when Hicasso coverage is absent or empty on either applicable host; merely running a green generic gate with zero Hicasso rows is not acceptance.
- A focused positive control temporarily introduces an unclassified Hicasso public on the CLJS side and proves the owning probe fails naming that var; a stale/missing JVM macro row likewise makes generator `--check` fail. After restoration, both focused gates pass.
- Existing manifest projections/consumers remain green against the regenerated authoritative rows.

## Non-goals

No resurrection of the retired Hicasso naming/budget census, no new CI job, no Hicasso API redesign, no runtime behavior change, and no attempt to make Hicasso an adapter discriminator.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status searches for `api manifest`, `manifest`, `hicasso manifest`, `public api`, `re-frame.hicasso`, and `api-manifest` found no open or in-progress duplicate. Closed `rf2-wf1ey` corrected documentation navigation and explicitly noted that Hicasso had zero manifest rows, but did not request enrollment. Closed `rf2-hxbhe`/`rf2-st1x5` concerned the former bespoke census, later deliberately removed by `rf2-6c12m.8`; extending the surviving generic manifest is distinct and preserves that consolidation.

title: skill-improver: detection algorithm still clears validated durable body reads
description:
## Scope

Correct the durable body-read guidance and behavioural fixture in skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md and skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json (behav-schemaless-body-read-trap, id 28). Keep the existing boundary-validation lesson, catalogue shape, and tool-agnostic eval workflow.

## Correctness finding

Eval 28 explicitly treats an inline always-on Malli validation as a complete acceptable fix for query parameters read from js/window.location.search and written into app-db. Validation closes the trust boundary, but it does not turn the live host read into a recorded fact. The same event replayed after the browser URL changes folds different filters into durable state.

This is not merely incomplete prose: the fixture's expected_output and graded expectations affirmatively pass the replay-unsafe rewrite. Because SKILL.md routes by matching leaves, an agent can follow the schemaless-events leaf, satisfy every eval assertion, and leave the critical durable-write contract broken. The leaf's own later regression callout and imperative-effects.md state the opposite rule.

## Evidence

- evals/evals.json:214-222 supplies a handler that reads js/window.location.search and writes params to [:search :filters]. Lines 215 and 222 say an inline m/validate in the handler is "equally acceptable" and needs no recordable marker, despite calling the destination durable.
- references/schemaless-events.md:105-124 says this exact class crosses two boundaries: validation closes trust, while durable app-db requires a recordable generator or event payload; inline validation alone is sufficient only when the body-read does not feed durable state.
- references/imperative-effects.md:46-57 requires every host fact used by a returned :db/runtime/resource/snapshot/ledger write to be recorded, never read ambiently at the write site.
- skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/cofx.md:58-68 and 95-125 defines ambient suppliers as replayed live reads and the recordable generator as the application-owned path for localStorage/sessionStorage/other host facts feeding durable state.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:15-24 implements that distinction: ambient suppliers are never recorded and rerun on replay; recordable values are captured and replayed verbatim. Lines 1067-1077 implement verbatim delivery or token write-back.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/cofx_cljs_test.cljc:1053-1070 is the executable control: a supplied/replayed recordable value wins and the generator does not run.
- docs/EP/EP-0010-causal-world-inputs.md:387-389 states the invariant directly: a world input affecting a durable write must come from a causal token or captured recordable coeffect, not an ambient host read.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run behavioural eval id 28 with the current skill.
2. Return a critique that correctly flags missing production validation but proposes only an unconditional validation branch around params, leaving js/window.location.search and URLSearchParams construction inside the event handler before the same assoc-in write.
3. Grade that answer against expectations 221-222. It passes: both assertions explicitly accept inline m/validate/m/coerce and require recordability only when the answer happens to choose a cofx.
4. Dispatch [:search/apply-url-filters] while the host URL contains ?q=alpha&page=1&sort=asc; record the event and resulting app-db.
5. Change the host URL to ?q=beta&page=2&sort=desc and replay the same event. The inline-only rewrite rereads the host and writes beta/2/desc, so the same causal token does not reproduce the original state.
6. Control: materialise and validate the params through a reg-cofx recordable generator (or carry the already-materialised value in the event payload), replay with the captured value, and observe alpha/1/asc both times without rereading the host.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A user asks the improver to fix a boundary handler that hydrates durable search state from the URL. The critique recommends an always-on validation branch and the eval marks it correct. The deployed app now rejects malformed values, but epoch restore, SSR hydration, and time-travel still read whichever URL is live during replay. A historical event can therefore produce a new route state and trigger different downstream subscriptions/effects.

Invariant: validation and causality are independent. An untrusted host value must be validated before use; when it affects durable state it must also be represented on the causal token as an event payload or recordable coeffect. A live inline body-read cannot satisfy the second requirement.

## Recommended minimal fix

- Revise eval 28's expected_output and expectations to reject any purported complete fix that leaves the URL read inside the durable-writing handler, even when it validates params unconditionally.
- Require the normal passing rewrite to materialise and validate the URL params through an application-owned reg-cofx recordable generator (preferably using cofx :schema for the always-on gate), or to carry a previously materialised validated fact in the event payload.
- Narrow the early body-read wording in schemaless-events.md so inline m/validate/m/coerce is described as sufficient only for non-durable destinations, matching its existing regression callout. Do not duplicate the cofx tutorial; link to the existing durable/diagnostic fork.
- Exercise the revised existing fixture rather than introducing a generic eval runner or a new catalogue leaf.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eval 28 no longer calls an inline validation-only rewrite acceptable for its durable [:search :filters] write. Its expected_output and graded assertions require either a recordable coeffect or event-payload fact, plus always-on validation.
2. The positive witness proposes a reg-cofx with :recordable? true and an always-on schema/validation gate, declares it via :rf.cofx/requires, and makes the handler fold the delivered value without reading js/window.location.search.
3. The negative control is the former inline-only response: it retains the in-handler URL read and adds a correct m/validate branch. It must fail the replay-safety expectation even though it passes the trust-boundary expectation. This proves the revised grade is non-vacuous and distinguishes the two contracts.
4. A second control response that materialises a validated value in the event payload passes without requiring a cofx, proving the criterion checks recordability rather than one preferred spelling.
5. Run the updated id-28 behavioural eval through the documented with-skill workflow for three runs and record per-expectation results. All with-skill runs reject the inline-only fix and accept a replay-safe fix.
6. The catalogue text consistently says inline validation alone is sufficient only when no durable state depends on the body-read; references/schemaless-events.md, references/imperative-effects.md, and eval 28 no longer contradict one another.
7. The existing focused cofx tests covering captured/replayed values remain green, and scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py passes for the edited fixture. Restoring the phrase that inline validation is equally acceptable for the durable prompt must make the negative control fail.

## Non-goals

- No runtime cofx, epoch, schema, or replay redesign; those contracts already exist and are tested.
- No new anti-pattern leaf, generic linter, automatic source scanner, eval platform, or compatibility layer.
- No requirement that every untrusted non-durable value use a recordable coeffect; inline always-on validation remains valid when the value does not affect durable state.
- No expansion into URL parsing policy, routing architecture, Malli schema design, or unrelated improver fixtures.
- No weakening of :rf.schema/at-boundary for genuine event-payload boundaries.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title, description, and notes searches covered improver, schemaless, body-read, recordable cofx, URLSearchParams, inline validation, durable write, replay boundary, and epoch-restore. No bead owns this fixture contradiction.

rf2-uhszv is the closed broad improver workflow review; it explicitly preserved replay-determinism and did not identify or repair eval 28's inline-validation exception. rf2-ov144 concerns a public replay-by-epoch-id gesture, not whether this skill teaches recorded inputs. rf2-6eh5h concerns falsey schema declaration presence in the runtime, not ambient body-reads or the improver eval. rf2-iyjae concerns WebSocket example trust boundaries, not this URL/replay guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Eval 28 must fail an inline-validation-only answer for its durable URL read and pass both replay-safe controls (recordable validating cofx and validated event payload); the documented three-run behavioural exercise, focused cofx tests, and check_skill_eval_docs.py must pass, with the former inline-only answer retained as the non-vacuity control.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-09-01 PR #8833 — REOPEN. The revised body-read bullet, regression example, and eval 28 correctly require both always-on validation and a recorded fact for a durable write, but the same leaf normative Detection logic still says at line 17: classify event-payload vs body-read; matching gate present means not a finding. An inline always-on m/validate is the matching body-read trust gate, so this algorithm still clears exactly the former inline-only rewrite even though it remains replay-unsafe. That directly contradicts line 12 and the revised eval expectation. Minimal fix: make the decision two-stage — require a matching trust validator, then, when the body-read feeds durable state, require a recorded fact; only clear the finding when every applicable boundary is closed. No new gate or harness. The independent rf2-uhszv sibling-routing repair holds.
TREE CHECK OWED 2026-09-01 14:15 AUSEST by the mayor. A merged commit cites this item — d3f992a034 'fix(skills/improver): eval 28 requires the durable URL read be recorded, not just validated (rf2-0o5dx)', on origin/main. That is NOT sufficient to close it and I have deliberately not done so: this item's title says the detection algorithm STILL clears validated durable body reads, and 'still' is the word that suggests the item POSTDATES a partial fix rather than being satisfied by it. Closing on a commit-subject match would be the same error as validating an item against its own text — one level up.

SO THE FIRST TASK OF WHOEVER TAKES THIS is to establish, at tip and at source, whether d3f992a034 satisfies this item, partially addresses it, or is the very change the item was filed against. A verified 'already fixed' closes it; a verified 'that commit is what I am complaining about' is equally complete. Neither is assumed here.
close_reason:
Verified DONE at the tree, not at the item text. Commit d3f992a034 is an ancestor of origin/main and touches exactly the two files this items Scope names: skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json and skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md.

Negative check with a control: the phrase this item cites at evals.json:215 and :222 -- "equally acceptable" -- now returns count 0 in that file, while the control string behav-schemaless-body-read-trap returns 1, so grep did read the file. A zero without that control would not have been a check.

Positive check, which is the half a matching commit cannot supply: the fix is not a deletion of the offending clause. The rewritten expected_output requires the complete fix to close TWO independent boundaries (TRUST via an always-on validate, REPLAY via a recorded fact), and the graded expectations now REJECT as incomplete any fix leaving the js/window.location.search read inside the durable-writing handler -- inline always-on validate explicitly included. It grades recordability rather than one spelling: an application-owned recordable reg-cofx generator OR an already-materialised params map on the event payload both pass.

Better than the item asked for: the former inline-only rewrite is RETAINED as the fixtures own non-vacuity control -- it must pass the trust-boundary expectation and fail the replay-safety one, so a future regression of this exact defect makes the fixture fail rather than silently re-passing.

The items title ("still clears validated durable body reads") is false at tip. That word "still" is what made the tree check owed.

title: surface-review(testbed-support): retire checkout-root plumbing now the endpoint resolves source files
description:
## Scope

Retire the repository-internal browser-side checkout-root pipeline from `tools/testbed-support/**` and its direct Xray, Story, example, launcher, Shadow, and documentation consumers. Make the already-wired JVM `POST /__rf-open-in-editor` endpoint the one source-file resolver for repository-owned dev testbeds, and return `re-frame.testbed.story-host` to its single job: live-app / Story-shell React-root handoff and hash routing.

Keep the generic public `:rf.story/project-root` / `:rf.xray/project-root` options and the client URI fallback available to external/non-shadow hosts. This is a removal of redundant repository testbed setup, not a redesign of the shipped open-in-editor contract.

## Findings

1. The surface carries two complete paths for the same repository dev workflow. `re-frame.testbed.config` derives an absolute source root in the browser from `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT` or `?checkout-root=`, while `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server` resolves the original relative coordinate against the live JVM classpath at request time. The endpoint is already attached to every dev-http port used by all twelve builds that seed the checkout-root define.
2. The older path makes each new testbed coordinate the same fact in several places: a literal source subdirectory in the CLJS consumer, a per-build Closure define in `shadow-cljs.edn`, the launcher environment export, and related docs/tests. Current consumers repeat seven Xray resolver/configure calls and five Story `:source-subdir` calls even though endpoint resolution needs none of them.
3. The cost is material for a private helper. `config.cljs` is 97 lines and its 41-test suite is 519 lines: 616 of `tools/testbed-support`'s 2,346 tracked lines (26%), before counting Story-host option tests, twelve Closure-define blocks, launcher/static-export checks, and prose across twenty tracked reference files.
4. No live caller was found for the query escape hatch. Repository-wide tracked searches for `checkout-root` find only the resolver, tests, configuration, and explanatory prose; no script emits a `?checkout-root=` URL and no runtime outside this internal support path reads it.
5. This is not a compatibility surface. `tools/testbed-support/deps.edn` and the README explicitly say the tool is dev-only and not published, and `spec/api-manifest.edn` / `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` contain no `re-frame.testbed.*` row. The private two-arity Story-host option can be deleted rather than shimmed.
6. History explains the overlap. Commit `3b4aed8b4e` (`rf2-5dphw`, 2026-05-31) introduced browser checkout-root plumbing to replace hardcoded personal paths; commit `bc895415b8` (`rf2-wn3bh`, 2026-06-14) later added the zero-config runtime endpoint and wired every testbed port, but did not retire the first mechanism. Five later commits still touched the config source/tests, including malformed-override repair, while endpoint behavior was unaffected.
7. The endpoint suite already owns classpath resolution, cwd fallback, query handling, launch behavior, JSON, and the loopback/method/origin boundary. The useful missing proof is consumer-shaped: real relative Story and Xray coordinates should resolve through that endpoint with both tool project-root atoms unset.

## Recommended Action

- Delete `re-frame.testbed.config` and `config_cljs_test.cljs` outright.
- Remove source-root configuration from `re-frame.testbed.story-host`; keep one `mount-with-hash-routing!` call shape taking only the live root view, and migrate all repository consumers to it without an alias or compatibility arity.
- Remove testbed-only `resolve-source-root` helpers and `xray-config/configure! {:rf.xray/project-root ...}` boot writes from the seven Xray consumers.
- Stop `implementation/scripts/dev-testbed.cjs` from deriving/exporting `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, and remove the twelve matching Closure defines plus now-vacuous static-export sentinel checks/prose. Preserve the launcher's explicit-build, de-duplication, process, and URL-printing behavior.
- Keep every affected dev-http entry wired to `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server/handler`. Add one bounded consumer-shaped witness using representative real Story and Xray relative coordinates, with launch stubbed so no editor opens.
- Rewrite the support README around the two remaining responsibilities and show the minimal new-testbed path: wire the handler, call the one-arity host when Story routing is needed, and launch the build. Do not introduce a replacement config layer.

## Evidence

- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/config.cljs`: 97-line query/define/path resolver whose only public operation is `resolve-source-root`.
- `tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/config_cljs_test.cljs`: 519 lines / 41 tests, including private parser and slash-normalisation contracts.
- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs:52-77`: optional `:source-subdir` exists only to invoke the config resolver before mounting.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:479-628`: fourteen dev-http entries already use the JVM endpoint handler; lines 1317-1958 separately repeat twelve checkout-root Closure defines for the affected builds.
- `implementation/scripts/dev-testbed.cjs:7-18,261-283`: the launcher exports the root solely for that define; its independently useful build/URL manifest does not need the value.
- `tools/xray/testbeds/{two_frame_isolation,standard_epochs,routes_epochs,machine_epochs,edn_inspector,managed_http,panel_gallery}/core.cljs`: seven identical resolver/configuration gestures.
- `tools/story/testbeds/{counter_with_stories,login_form,hicasso_counter}/core.cljs` and the login/nine-states example hosts: five literal `:source-subdir` options.
- `tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server_test.clj:17-54`: the server already proves relative classpath files resolve to real on-disk paths; the remainder covers the endpoint boundary and launch result shapes.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` open-in-editor launch modes: the endpoint is the preferred zero-config runtime resolver; project-root composition belongs to the generic URI fallback.
- `tools/testbed-support/deps.edn` plus the absent API-manifest rows: local dev/test support, not a published facade.
- Exact current/closed tracker title searches and issue-record scans for testbed-support, checkout-root, `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, `resolve-source-root`, source-root resolver, and open-in-editor endpoint found no outcome bead owning this retirement.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No tracked source, build config, script, test, or current documentation references `re-frame.testbed.config`, `RF2_TESTBED_PROJECT_ROOT`, `?checkout-root=`, or the deleted checkout-root Closure define. The config namespace and its dedicated test namespace are gone.
2. `mount-with-hash-routing!` has one repository-internal call shape and owns only listener/root handoff plus hash selection. All Story/example consumers call it without source-root options; all Xray testbeds boot without testbed-support project-root resolution.
3. `npm run dev -- <build-id>` retains explicit build forwarding, order-preserving de-duplication, URL reporting, cwd, signal, and exit semantics, but no longer computes or exports an absolute checkout path.
4. All twelve formerly seeded builds remain served by dev-http entries using `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server/handler`. With Story and Xray project-root config unset, one real relative Story coordinate and one real relative Xray coordinate reach the handler and resolve to the intended existing file; the test stubs `launch!` and proves the resolved argument without opening an editor.
5. The generic Story/Xray project-root configuration APIs, endpoint-preferred/URI-fallback client rule, endpoint path/query/method/security contract, and `launch-editor` behavior are unchanged. No public facade symbol or API-manifest row is added.

title: migration: path lowering misclassifies custom */path interceptors
description:
## Scope

Repair the v1-to-v2 event-registration migration path where the shipped M-73 scanner/codemod encounters interceptor-bearing reg-event-db or reg-event-fx calls. Scope includes migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod, its focused tests/README, the directly coupled re-frame-migration reference/eval, and one focused integration proof against the actual v2 reg-event contract.

## Correctness finding

The guide promises that M-73 composes with M-70, but the implementation performs a head/handler-only rewrite and deliberately preserves every middle slot. For the canonical path-interceptor example it emits an rf/reg-event whose metadata still contains the removed inline (rf/path ...) call; for historical positional chains it emits a reg-event with the retired vector middle slot. Both outputs are invalid v2 and hard-fail while the namespace loads. The codemod then reports the site as :rewrite/:rename rather than an unresolved M-70 finding, so its green unit suite certifies a broken migration.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md:482-505 tells users to prefer the shipped codemod and specifies the mechanical conversion from {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} to {:interceptors [[:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]]]}.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:883-903 calls the codemod first-class/tested and gives the same positional [(rf/path :counter)] to metadata-ref conversion.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod.clj:31-33 instead states that path-interceptor metadata is preserved untouched. analyse-call at 301-342 classifies every reg-event-fx as a pure rename and simple reg-event-db solely by its last handler; it never analyses middle-slot shape or entries. apply-rewrite-at at 665-688 replaces only the registrar head and db handler.
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/test/re_frame/migration/reg_event_codemod_test.clj:102-114 and 125-134 explicitly assert that {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]} survives while the call is renamed to reg-event, pinning the invalid output.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1962-1983 makes rf/path a throwing removal stub (:rf.error/path-removed). implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:71-82 and 126-165 require interceptor refs and reject inline values with :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed; 803-837 rejects a positional vector middle slot with :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the shipped codemod rewrite over this v1 source:

       (rf/reg-event-db :counter/inc
         {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}
         (fn [db _] (update db :value inc)))

2. Observe that it reports :action :rewrite and emits reg-event while preserving {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}.
3. Load/evaluate the emitted registration with the actual v2 re-frame.core namespace.
4. Observe the namespace-load hard failure :rf.error/path-removed before the handler registers. The positional-vector variant is also retained and is rejected as :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot; a custom inline value retained in metadata is rejected as :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed.

## Failure scenario / invariant

The current successful rewrite is:

    (rf/reg-event :counter/inc
      {:interceptors [(rf/path :counter)]}
      (fn [{:keys [db]} _] {:db (update db :value inc)}))

Loading it against v2 calls the removed rf/path stub before the handler can register. A positional v1 chain is likewise left as the now-illegal vector middle slot, and a custom inline value carried into metadata is rejected by reg-event.

Invariant: every site the codemod reports as mechanically rewritten must be a valid v2 registration shape, or it must remain an explicit unresolved M-70 finding. A source transform is not successful merely because it parses and no retired registrar name remains.

## Recommended minimal fix

Teach the codemod one small middle-slot normalization that composes M-70 with M-73:

1. Recognize the standard path constructor in bare, positional-vector, metadata-interceptors, and metadata-plus-vector source shapes; lower each (rf/path p...) to [:rf.interceptor/path [p...]], create or merge the metadata map, and preserve chain order/comments.
2. Preserve entries that are already v2 refs.
3. For any other inline/bare interceptor whose stable registered id cannot be derived without author intent, emit an explicit M-70 Type-B finding and do not claim the event migration complete. Do not leave an invalid inline value hidden behind a successful M-73 result.
4. Scan both retired reg-event-* forms and already rewritten reg-event forms for these invalid middle-slot/inline survivors so a rerun can recover a partially migrated tree.
5. Replace the string-only preservation assertions with exact normalization tests plus a focused registration integration test using the actual v2 core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A codemod test rewrites the canonical metadata source above to a reg-event containing exactly [:rf.interceptor/path [:counter]], with no executable rf/path call, and preserves the db-handler transformation.
- A codemod test rewrites a historical positional path vector and a metadata-plus-vector path chain into the one metadata-map :interceptors ref shape; multiple entries preserve declaration order.
- An executable integration test evaluates/registers the canonical transformed result against the actual v2 core and completes without :rf.error/path-removed, :rf.error/reg-event-bad-middle-slot, :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed, or :rf.error/unregistered-interceptor.
- Negative control: feeding the current preserved-inline output to that same integration harness deterministically throws :rf.error/path-removed (or the inline-value equivalent throws :rf.error/inline-interceptor-removed), proving the test observes registration rather than only parsing/substring shape. Restoring the old preserve-middle behavior makes the positive test red.
- A custom inline interceptor with no stable id is surfaced as an unresolved M-70 Type-B finding and is not reported as a completed :rename/:rewrite; a rerun over an already-renamed invalid reg-event finds it.
- Non-vacuity controls show interceptor-free reg-event-fx still pure-renames, interceptor-free simple reg-event-db still performs its existing db wrap, already-canonical ref chains remain valid, and running the codemod twice is stable.
- Add a focused re-frame-migration eval fixture whose v1 event contains a path interceptor; its expected result uses the standard ref and the eval fails if the removed inline call or positional vector survives.
- The codemod unit suite and the focused runtime integration test pass.

## Non-goals

- No general Clojure analyser or arbitrary macro evaluation.
- No auto-naming or semantic re-authoring of custom interceptors; those remain M-70 Type B.
- No compatibility alias restoring rf/path, inline interceptor values, or positional reg-event chains in v2.
- No unrelated migration-rule rewrite, formatting cleanup, or broad runtime hardening.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title and description searches were run for: M-73 codemod, reg-event codemod, path interceptor codemod, inline interceptor migration, rf.interceptor/path, middle slot codemod, preserved metadata interceptor, M-70, M-73, reg-event-db, and codemod. A full all-status issue export was also scanned across title/description/notes for the same vocabulary. No existing open, in-progress, blocked, deferred, or closed bead owns this codemod-output/runtime-registration mismatch. rf2-0qzh covered CI discovery/classification for the codemod, not transform correctness; reagent/hicasso codemod beads are different tools and surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Canonical metadata, positional-vector, and metadata-plus-vector path-interceptor inputs lower to metadata :interceptors entries of [:rf.interceptor/path <path-vector>] while preserving handler semantics and chain order.
2. The canonical transformed output is executed against actual v2 reg-event and registers successfully.
3. A negative-control fixture containing the old preserved inline rf/path output throws the expected hard error in that same harness; reverting the normalization makes the positive test fail.
4. Custom inline interceptors without a stable id become explicit unresolved M-70 Type-B findings rather than successful M-73 rewrites, including when found in an already-renamed reg-event.
5. Interceptor-free fx/db rewrites, already-canonical ref chains, and a second codemod run remain successful and stable.
6. A focused migration-skill eval rejects any answer/output that leaves rf/path executable or a positional interceptor vector in reg-event.
7. Focused codemod and runtime integration suites pass.

AUDIT PR #8828 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness: path-call-info identifies the standard re-frame constructor only by (= "path" (name hv)). It therefore treats every qualified custom function named path as rf/path. A deterministic probe on merged main with (app.interceptors/path :tenant) inside a real rf/reg-event-db returned :action :rewrite and emitted [:rf.interceptor/path [:tenant]], silently replacing the custom interceptor's semantics instead of producing the promised unresolved M-70 :flag :interceptors. This contradicts the PR's central boundary that only the standard constructor is mechanical and every other custom inline call stays unchanged for author intent. Existing tests cover a custom var, rf/debug, and a dynamic rf/path arg, but not a custom qualified function sharing the simple name. Minimal repair: resolve the call head to re-frame.core/path from the namespace's require/refer aliases, or conservatively flag ambiguous qualified path symbols; add a custom/path negative test while retaining the standard qualified/alias/bare fixtures and idempotence.

Implementation-quality/completeness: the new :integration alias is not invoked by .github/workflows/test.yml or scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh. PR checks ran only clojure -M:test, so the real-v2 registration proof and all four negative controls are currently manual/orphaned. Add clojure -M:integration to the existing changed-surface codemod CI job (keeping it separate from the self-contained :test classpath).

Duplicate search across all statuses for custom path interceptor, symbol named path, path alias codemod, and M-70 custom call found no separate owner. Both residues are exact acceptance/quality gaps in rf2-8odvg.
AUDIT PR #8846 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

Correctness/completeness: the new namespace resolver still treats namespace-level availability as call-site resolution. In a file that refers re-frame.core/path, a lexically shadowing `let` binding named `path` is therefore silently lowered as the framework constructor. Deterministic probe on merge b38d2e0: `(ns app.events (:require [re-frame.core :refer [reg-event-db path]])) (let [path app.interceptors/path] (reg-event-db ... {:interceptors [(path :tenant)]} ...))` returned `[:rewrite nil true]` — a successful rewrite containing `:rf.interceptor/path` — even though the call denotes the custom binding. This contradicts the implementation comment at lines 344-350 and the README guarantee that a local/custom path function flags rather than changes semantics.

Minimal repair: for bare `path`, account for lexical bindings at the interceptor call site, or conservatively refuse lowering when an enclosing scope binds `path`; add one deterministic local-shadow negative fixture plus idempotence. This does not require a general analyser. The separate orphaned integration-CI residue remains owned by rf2-36u96 and is not duplicated here.
REPAIRED 2026-09-01 12:14:32 AUSEST (worker, PR #8857, commit ae9a7d7e59). The reopen's probe was reproduced verbatim at branch base 4e27fbbe49 BEFORE any edit and returned [:rewrite nil true] — premise confirmed at source, not assumed. Root cause exactly as the note stated: path-head resolution was a per-SOURCE fact derived from the ns form (path-head-context), with no call-site half, so ns-level AVAILABILITY stood in for what a bare head DENOTES.

FIX: reused the in-file machinery rather than adding a second mechanism. The free-occurrence analysis already carried a binding-form vocabulary (binding-vector-forms, seq-binding-forms, collect-binding-names); that vocabulary is hoisted into one shared section above both consumers, and a new enclosing-scope-binds? walks OUT from the registrar call over the same table. The two analyses now ask opposite questions in opposite directions over one vocabulary. Added the defn family (defn/defn-/defmacro), whose params scope over a registration in the body and which the downward walk had no reason to know. standard-path-head? consults the new :shadowed-bare-path? for BARE heads only — a namespace-qualified symbol names a var and cannot be shadowed by a local.

Conservative refusal, as the note permitted: an enclosing binder routes the site to the existing :flag :interceptors (unresolved M-70 Type B) and leaves the source byte-for-byte unchanged. Position-insensitive inside a binding vector, and an unreadable binding vector counts as binding the name — both errors can only produce a flag where a lowering was possible, never a silent semantic swap.

PROBE A BEAD NOTES FIELD WITH bd show --json, NEVER bd show PIPED TO GREP (2026-09-01, mayor session 9a).

CLAUDE.md tells you to confirm an --append-notes landed by probing for known content from the start, middle and end. The obvious way to do that -- bd show <id> piped to grep -- IS BROKEN, and it fails in the ALARMING direction: it reports data loss that did not happen.

WHAT HAPPENED: appended a ~4KB note to rf2-m7sto. Probed three strings: the start marker matched, the middle and end both returned 0. That is precisely the signature of a truncated write, and the documented remedy for a damaged notes field is to reconstruct it from a git checkpoint -- which here would have DUPLICATED an intact note.

THE CAUSE: bd show renders the notes field into a fixed-width column and LINE-WRAPS it. Any probe string longer than the wrap width straddles an inserted newline, so grep cannot match it no matter how intact the data is. Short probes match; long ones do not. Nothing errors, and the zero is indistinguishable from a real truncation.

THE CORRECT PROBE: bd show <id> --json and read the raw notes field. On the same bead that returned two zeros through bd show, the raw field measured 10858 characters and ALL FIVE probes returned exactly 1 -- including the two that had read as lost.

TWO MECHANICS WORTH KNOWING: bd show --json returns a LIST, not an object, so index [0] before calling .get. And a length comparison is still the wrong check for a different reason CLAUDE.md already gives -- chunked appends shift lengths by a byte or two -- so probe content in the raw field, which gets both halves right.

GENERAL FORM: this is the "any instrument that can answer nothing-here gives the same answer when misused" hazard, turned on the VERIFICATION step rather than the work. A probe that reads a RENDERED view is measuring the renderer, not the data. Probe the raw field, or run the probe once against a string you know is present as a control -- a short one will match and expose the wrap.

title: surface-review(examples-core): make every documented core run command launch a real page
description:
## Scope

Make the primary examples/core learning path genuinely one-command runnable from the instructions programmers and coding agents actually encounter. Scope is the core catalogue landing copy in examples/README.md, the seven core README carriers (counter, flows, login, managed_http_counter, notebook, todomvc, and seven_guis), and the existing npm run dev:example runner/manifest tests only as needed to pin that documented contract.

The outcome is not a new runner. The repository already has the right one. The outcome is that every default core run recipe invokes it and reaches a real page with the required host assets.

## Findings

The application code is broadly coherent and current: the 12 core builds use the reg-event / reg-sub / reg-view idiom, explicit frame scope, the init! plus lazy frame-root mount shape (with the intentional pre-created-frame exception for frame-local flows), namespaced registrations, and external headless wrappers where behavior needs coverage. test:examples-compile derives every declared :examples/* build and rejects compile errors and warnings.

The first-contact run path is the material gap. examples/README.md says any example runs with shadow-cljs watch BUILD-ID, and every core README repeats a bare shadow-cljs watch examples/... command. Those commands compile to implementation/out/examples/ID but do not stage the colocated index.html, copy _shared, copy per-example assets, or serve that output on a discoverable URL. The core builds also have no matching generic :dev-http roots. Consequently:

- opening a source index.html cannot find its relative main.js;
- opening an output directory has no host page unless the user manually copies it;
- TodoMVC additionally misses base.css and index.css from node_modules;
- managed-http-counter additionally misses api/inc.json, so its headline success request becomes a 404;
- phrases such as "open the served page" and "open index.html against the watch build" describe a page the documented command did not assemble.

This is inconsistent inside the same catalogue. The UIx READMEs already teach npm run dev:example -- examples/ID, which cleans and stages the selected output, starts the watch, serves it on a free loopback port, and prints the URL.

History explains the split. Commit a4636f853f (rf2-pdo5mx) introduced serve-example.cjs, the npm entry point, manifest derivation, staging tests, and migrated the UIx docs. The later concept reorganisation at 210f812fe2 installed the raw-watch sentence in the new catalogue/core READMEs and lost the complete staging-and-serving recipe. Subsequent runner work made the canonical path stronger, not obsolete: 1d62730eb1 added the clean-stage boundary, 8365a4f32e centralised asset exceptions, and the current staging tests explicitly pin TodoMVC CSS and managed-http-counter's JSON fixture.

## Recommended Action

Bless one default command for the core family:

    npm run dev:example -- examples/BUILD-ID

Run it from implementation/. Put one concise explanation on the catalogue landing page: it watches, stages the host/assets, serves on a free port, and prints the URL. Give each core README its exact copy-paste command; the 7GUIs README can show one command and say to substitute the other listed build ids. Use the same runner for the login Story build if it is documented as a default runnable path.

Keep raw shadow-cljs watch only in one clearly labelled advanced/manual note if it still earns a place, and state the full copy/stage/serve obligation there. Do not repeat that troubleshooting ceremony in every example.

Extend the existing listStandaloneExamples staging test just enough to pin that all 12 documented core build ids resolve to a host page. Reuse the existing runner, manifest, and script-policy lane; do not add another wrapper or a per-example browser suite.

## Evidence

- examples/README.md:11 advertises raw watch for every example.
- Bare raw-watch recipes remain in examples/core/counter/README.md:115, flows/README.md:61, login/README.md:84, managed_http_counter/README.md:50, notebook/README.md:159, todomvc/README.md:71, and seven_guis/README.md:59.
- Every core host page loads relative main.js; the build outputs are separately declared under implementation/out/examples/* in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn.
- implementation/package.json already exposes dev:example.
- examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs documents and implements clean, stage, watch, serve, and URL reporting.
- examples/scripts/examples-asset-manifest.cjs records the two core-only staging obligations: TodoMVC CSS and managed-http-counter api/inc.json.
- implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs pins clean-before-stage, manifest projection, and those special assets, but its runnable-manifest assertion currently names only the three UIx examples.
- npm run dev:example -- --list currently returns all core ids: counter, flows, login, managed-http-counter, notebook, todomvc, temperature, flight-booker, timer, crud, circle-drawer, and cells.
- examples/TESTING.md confirms compile coverage is not a served-page smoke; examples remain test-free and behavior wrappers live outside the tree.
- Searches across open and closed bead titles/descriptions for serve-example, dev:example, core example run commands, and surface-review(examples-core) found no live duplicate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From implementation/, each documented core command uses npm run dev:example -- examples/ID and is copy-pasteable without an unstated copy, staging, or server step.
2. examples/README.md names that command as the default route and explains it once, tersely. Each core README points to the exact build id; all six non-counter 7GUIs ids are discoverable from its README.
3. No bare shadow-cljs watch examples/... remains in the scoped core docs as the default run recipe. Any retained raw-watch form is explicitly advanced/manual and names the missing staging and serving work.
4. The existing staging/runner test suite asserts that all 12 documented core builds appear in listStandaloneExamples() with an existing host page. The assertion has a non-vacuous failure if one core build falls out of the runner.
5. A clean run of the documented counter command serves the current page and main.js on the printed URL; minus and plus update the displayed count.
6. Existing staging tests prove TodoMVC's two CSS assets and managed-http-counter's api/inc.json land under their clean output roots. npm run test:script-policy, the relevant docs link/slug gates, and npm run dev:example -- --list pass.
7. The final change stays documentation-and-existing-runner focused; it does not introduce a second launcher or per-example browser matrix.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting the example applications, their API idioms, or their tutorial narratives.
- Adding a browser smoke for every core example or reversing the test-free-examples policy.
- Turning gallery examples into independent greenfield project templates; tools/template remains that path.
- Abstracting the intentionally visible mount code into a shared helper.
- Sweeping the individual READMEs under capabilities, patterns, real-apps, or substrates in this task, beyond correcting the shared catalogue entry.

## Related beads

- rf2-pdo5mx - introduced the one-command example runner and migrated the UIx learning path.
- rf2-rg2tze - made the runner clean the selected output before staging.
- rf2-cq6va5 / rf2-phpbo8 - pinned and centralised per-example runtime assets.
- rf2-8cevm - established the test-free examples policy; this task preserves it.
- rf2-0vav5.1 - introduced derived compile coverage for declared example builds; compile coverage remains complementary to, not a replacement for, a runnable documented page.

title: surface-review(examples-capabilities): make every capability README launch the real one-command app
description:
## Scope

Make the capabilities catalogue and all eight examples/capabilities/** README launch recipes copyable from a clean checkout. Cover machines/state_machine_walkthrough, routing/routing, resources/{resources,infinite_feed,linearlite}, ssr/{ssr,resources_ssr,ssr_streaming}, and the capabilities entry point in examples/README.md. Keep the existing examples and the existing runner; this is an executable-documentation correction, not a new example framework.

## Findings

- Every capability README still leads with raw "shadow-cljs watch examples/<id>" and then asks the reader to serve or open some combination of source and build output. The root catalogue makes the same blanket claim for every example.
- That is not a complete runnable recipe. Each source index.html references both main.js and _shared assets, while the browser builds emit main.js under implementation/out/examples/<id>. Seven of these examples have no dedicated dev-http root that composes those trees. Linearlite is the lone special case with a hard-coded 8044 dev-http entry, so its README works differently from every sibling.
- The repository already has the canonical solution: "npm run dev:example -- examples/<id>". The runner cleans the selected output, stages that example's real index.html and shared assets, starts watch/compile, serves loopback on a free port, and prints the exact URL.
- The runner derives its standalone-build list from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn. Its current --list output includes all eight capability build ids, and the independent compile gate derives and sweeps the same eight builds.
- History explains the drift. Commit a4636f853f (rf2-pdo5mx, 2026-06-09) introduced the one-command runner and migrated the then-UIx READMEs only. The concept-layout move in 210f812fe2 (2026-06-28) and later capability README rewrites retained the older recipes. The runtime code, mount idioms, and build declarations are already consistent; the learning front door is the stale part.

## Recommended Action

Replace each capability README's primary How to run recipe with the exact npm dev:example command for its declared build id, run from implementation/. Say that the command stages the page, watches it, selects a free local port, and prints the URL; for the three SSR examples, make explicit that the runner stages the checked-in baked SSR index rather than requiring the reader to manually combine it with the bundle. Remove the hard-coded Linearlite-only 8044 path from the primary flow.

Update examples/README.md so its generic launch instruction names the same runner. Raw shadow-cljs watch may remain only as an explicitly advanced compiler-only path that does not pretend to stage or serve a page. Reuse the runner and its manifest derivation as-is unless an actual failing capability build proves a small runner defect.

## Evidence

- examples/README.md:13 currently says any example runs with raw shadow-cljs watch.
- The eight stale commands are at state_machine_walkthrough/README.md:126, routing/README.md:89, resources/README.md:157, infinite_feed/README.md:161, linearlite/README.md:148, ssr/README.md:190, resources_ssr/README.md:171, and ssr_streaming/README.md:167.
- All eight index.html files reference main.js and _shared/css/style.css plus _shared/img/favicon.svg.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1557-1784 declares all eight builds and emits each to implementation/out/examples/<id>; only the top-level dev-http map at lines 603-611 gives Linearlite a composed source/output server.
- implementation/package.json:53 exposes dev:example.
- examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs:151 resolves the manifest, lines 202-224 clean and stage the selected app, and line 289 prints its live URL.
- examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs:222-347 derives build id, output directory, init namespace, source folder, index page, and staged assets from shadow-cljs.edn.
- "node ../examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs --list" currently lists examples/state-machine-walkthrough, examples/routing, examples/resources, examples/infinite-feed, examples/linearlite, examples/ssr, examples/resources-ssr, and examples/ssr-streaming.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the eight capability README files has one primary, copy-paste command of the form "npm run dev:example -- examples/<correct-build-id>" from implementation/.
- Each recipe tells the reader to open the URL printed by the runner; none leaves them to infer how to combine source index.html, output main.js, and _shared assets, and Linearlite no longer needs special knowledge of port 8044.

title: surface-review(core): make destroy-frame! release generation-pool provenance
description:
## Scope

Correct the lifecycle ownership of generation provenance in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc` and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc`, with focused cross-host tests in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/**`. Update the nearby lifecycle/provenance commentary or `spec/002-Frames.md` only where needed to keep the teardown contract accurate. The public API stays `make-frame` + `destroy-frame!`.

## Correctness finding

Every successful public `rf/make-frame` writes an entry to the process-global `frame-generation-pool`, including ordinary one-arity frames whose value is `nil` (meaning the live source store). `destroy-frame!` removes the live frame and releases many other frame-keyed side tables, but never removes this entry. Destroying N never-reused frame ids therefore leaves N permanent keys; the two-arity constructor can additionally keep the caller's explicit descriptor pool reachable.

This violates the documented invariant that transient frame-scoped state is released at the single normative teardown boundary. The source comment classifies the residue as harmless "dev-process memory", but the write is unconditional in the public constructor and is exercised by server request lifecycles.

## Steps to Reproduce

From `implementation/core`, run:

```clojure
clojure -M -e "(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.frame :as frame] '[re-frame.live-frame :as lf] '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as pa]) (rf/init! pa/adapter) (let [pool (var-get (ns-resolve 're-frame.live-frame 'frame-generation-pool)) baseline (count @pool) fs (vec (repeatedly 100 #(rf/make-frame {}))) after-create (count @pool)] (doseq [f fs] (rf/destroy-frame! f)) (println {:baseline baseline :after-create after-create :after-destroy (count @pool) :registered-frames (count (frame/frame-ids))}))"
```

Current-main exit 0 output is:

```clojure
{:baseline 0, :after-create 100, :after-destroy 100, :registered-frames 0}
```

The control proves the table acquired 100 rows; the terminal state proves all 100 frame records were destroyed while all 100 provenance rows remained.

## Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:592-603` explicitly accepts a residual entry for every destroyed-and-never-reused id and calls it dev-process memory.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:680-706` defines `frame-generation-pool` and records `runnable-id -> descriptors`; `nil` is a real recorded value for the normal live-store path.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:989-998` performs that write for every successful `make-frame` before the frame engine commit, while preserving failure rollback.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/live_frame.cljc:1201-1219` reads the row during reprojection, establishing that the row is needed only while that frame is live.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:4267-4307` documents the destroy cleanup hooks; the corresponding calls at lines 4522-4619 precede `dissoc-frame!` at line 4668, but there is no live-frame provenance cleanup.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:603-608` says transient frame-scoped state is torn down on `destroy-frame!`; lines 705-711 make it the single teardown path and require every feature's frame-scoped state to hang cleanup there.
- `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:269-275,278-290,353-358` documents that teardown prevents a leak per request, creates a fresh gensym frame id, calls `rf/make-frame`, and destroys it in `finally`. `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:245-250,271-276,352-353` has the same lifecycle.
- `rg -n "frame-generation-pool" implementation/core/src implementation/core/test` finds the production table only in `live_frame.cljc`; existing tests cover provenance selection, failure rollback, and construction contention, not successful destroy cleanup.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A long-lived JVM SSR service follows the documented per-request recipe: mint a unique id, construct a frame, render, and destroy in `finally`. The live frame registry returns to baseline after each request, but `frame-generation-pool` grows linearly with total requests served. The common path retains at least one unique keyword/map row per request; callers using distinct explicit descriptor snapshots can keep those larger object graphs reachable too. Tests, stories, and `with-new-frame` churn have the same process-lifetime accumulation.

Invariant: after a successful destruction, no frame-scoped generation-provenance row for that exact dead incarnation remains. An exact-value stale destroy must still be a no-op against a same-id successor and must not remove the successor's provenance.

## Recommended minimal fix

Keep provenance in its current private side table and add the missing symmetric teardown:

1. In `live_frame.cljc`, define a private idempotent cleanup function that `dissoc`s the destroyed frame id from `frame-generation-pool`, and publish it through `re-frame.late-bind` (for example `:live-frame/on-frame-destroyed!`).
2. In `frame/destroy-frame!`, invoke that hook through the existing `safe-call-hook!` cleanup path before `dissoc-frame!`.
3. Update the destroy recipe/comment and replace the accepted-residue claim with the lifecycle invariant.

No incarnation token is required at that point: destruction still holds the per-id reservation, and a same-id successor cannot be seated until the later registry dissoc. A stale exact-value destroy that does not own the live incarnation already exits before the cleanup walk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused CLJC lifecycle test captures the private provenance table baseline, creates a uniquely named ordinary one-arity frame, proves its id is present while live (non-vacuity), destroys it through the public API, and proves both the frame record and provenance row are absent.
- A two-arity control uses distinct explicit descriptor-pool objects for same-id incarnations A and B: A's live row is its exact pool; destroying A removes it; constructing B installs B's pool; a later stale `destroy-frame! A` leaves B live and B's row intact; destroying B removes the row.
- A churn test creates at least 100 fresh anonymous/public frames before destroying them, proves the table grew by exactly that live set, destroys every returned frame value, and proves the table equals its captured baseline rather than merely checking a selected key.
- The focused tests execute on both the JVM and Node/CLJS lanes that exercise `live_frame.cljc` / frame teardown.
- Existing generation-provenance controls remain green: failed first construction leaves no row, failed re-construction restores the prior row, explicit-pool reprojection uses the original pool, and same-id construction contention cannot clobber a winner.
- The destroy recipe names the new cleanup and no source comment describes destroyed-frame provenance residue as harmless or dev-only.
- Negative control: disabling the new hook (or its registration/call site) makes the ordinary-row, explicit-pool, and churn assertions fail while their pre-destroy presence controls still pass.

## Non-goals

- No weak references, TTL/reaper, periodic sweep, global reset API, or SSR-specific cleanup call.
- No public provenance accessor and no new public lifecycle verb.
- No change to image selection, generation sealing, hot-reload/reprojection semantics, construction reservations, or failed-construction rollback.
- No redesign that moves provenance into the sealed generation/frame schema unless the minimal late-bound teardown proves impossible.
- No changes to per-request id policy, SSR payloads, Hicasso state, routing/resources/HTTP teardown, or unrelated process-global caches.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched the full bead corpus, including closed issues, with `bd search` for "generation pool", "generation", "descriptor pool", "make-frame", "destroy frame", "SSR leak", and "provenance"; and `bd list --all --desc-contains` / `--notes-contains` for "frame-generation-pool", "generation pool", "generation provenance", "residual entry", "no destroy-time cleanup", "explicit descriptor pool", "per-request frame", "destroy-frame!", and "live-frame". No issue owns this core table or invariant. The only related material issue is closed `rf2-uejlj`, which fixed the analogous Hicasso `!frame-ops` per-request retention by adding its own destroy hook; it neither mentions nor clears `frame-generation-pool`. The sole in-progress bead at filing time, `rf2-jui1c`, is an unrelated P3 prose sweep and remains locked.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-cq0yi) — PR #8887, head 14e649a7ca8b23e9a8643aba28695f16d581e3f4, ready for review.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE. The bead reproduction runs verbatim on trunk 24b33a618a at exit 0 and prints exactly the recorded output: {:baseline 0, :after-create 100, :after-destroy 100, :registered-frames 0}. Line deltas are negligible: the live_frame.cljc residue comment cited 592-603, actual 594-603; the defonce cited 680-706, actual starts 677 (record fn 698-706); write site 989-998 exact; reader 1201-1219 exact; frame.cljc 4267-4307 hook doc exact, 4522-4619 hook calls and dissoc-frame! 4668 all exact; spec/002-Frames.md 603-608 and 705-711 exact.

WHO READS THE POOL. One production reader: live-frame/reproject-live-frame!, which reads the row only inside (when-let [old-generation (frame/frame-generation frame-id)]) — a destroyed frame carries no generation, so the read never happens for one. Nothing consults the table for a destroyed frame. Repo-wide grep finds the production table only in live_frame.cljc; every other hit is a test. So no reader needs post-teardown access, and a plain keyed dissoc at teardown is the right shape rather than a compromise.

ARE THE NIL-VALUED ONE-ARITY ENTRIES A DISTINCT CASE. Informationally yes, mechanically no. To the only READER they are identical to absence: (get pool id) returns nil for a live ordinary frame and for a frame that never existed, so releasing them changes no reader answer — that is the safety argument for the release, and it applies to the explicit-pool rows too, since a destroyed frame is never reprojected either way. But they are NOT identical to record-frame-generation-pool!, which distinguishes had-row? from absent so restore-frame-generation-pool! can undo exactly (its docstring says so: nil is a legitimate recorded pool, so an absent row cannot be spelled by assoc-ing nil). The one place that distinction could have become observable post-release is a failed re-construction on a previously-destroyed id: pre-fix the rollback restored a present nil row, post-fix it dissocs. Both leave every reader seeing nil, so behaviour is unchanged. Conclusion: they did not warrant a narrower first cut — one unconditional release covers both cases with no asymmetry to explain.

THE REPAIR. live-frame/release-frame-generation-pool! (private, idempotent dissoc), published as :live-frame/on-frame-destroyed! from install-reprojection! — the same make-frame-rooted once-body that installs the other two :live-frame/* keys — and invoked from the destroy-frame! step-6 auxiliary-cleanup pass, after :hicasso/on-frame-destroyed!. Late-bind because live-frame requires frame (a back-require would invert the load order). Publishing from that once-body is what makes the timing airtight: make-frame calls ensure-reprojection-installed! at line 852 and writes its first row at 993, so the hook is bound before any row can exist, and a bundle that never constructs a frame roots neither (the elision DCE contract is preserved). Keyed and unconditional, no incarnation token: destroy still owns the id reservation at hook time and a same-id successor is seatable only after the step-9 dissoc, so every row standing there is the dying incarnation. A stale exact-value destroy fails claim-frame-destroy! before the cleanup walk. Plus a late_bind/directory.cljc entry, the accepted-residue comment replaced with the lifecycle invariant (its CORRECTNESS reasoning still holds and is kept; what it got wrong was retention), and the install-reprojection! arity prose brought in step.

SPEC/002-FRAMES.MD: TAKEN, and declared in the PR body. One clause in the normative Destroy step-6 ordered list, which carries "The ordering is pattern contract — a conformant port MUST mirror it", so adding a hook to that pass without listing it leaves the spec understating the recipe. Everything else fits in-tree and was written there instead. It serialises the fleet against that file while #8887 is open.

CONTROL, AND WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS. New cross-host implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_destroy_generation_provenance_cljs_test.cljc (.cljc ending -cljs-test, so it rides clojure -M:test via -test$ AND npm run test:cljs via cljs-test$). Every case asserts PRESENCE before absence: the ordinary case proves the row was written while the frame was live, the explicit-pool case proves A row is A exact pool by identical? and B row is B exact pool, and the churn case pins the table cardinality in BOTH directions (grew by exactly 100, returned to exactly the captured baseline) rather than probing a selected key. contains? is the presence probe throughout, never get — load-bearing, because an ordinary frame recorded pool IS nil, so get cannot separate a live ordinary row from no row at all. A fourth case pins that the hook is published at all, so a never-registered release cannot present as a broken one.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, RUN ON BOTH ARMS FROM THE SAME PLANT (call site commented out; match count checked as 1 before running; blob hash 296c1893 -> e1673701 on the JVM plant and -> a4ceb908 on the CLJS one, so neither plant no-opped). JVM captured exit 1: 4 tests, 18 assertions, 4 failures. CLJS captured exit 1: 4 failures, all in this file. The same four source lines on both arms — 135, 160, 174, 198 — with the other 14 assertions still green, so the reds are a missing release and not a make-frame that stopped recording. Test and assertion totals identical to the green runs, so no namespace was skipped. The CLJS red is also the positive evidence that the .cljc really executes on the node lane and that its white-box read of the private table compiles there. Restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object each time, never by reading a diff.

FINDING NOT ASKED FOR, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE. make_frame_generation_pool_window_jvm_test (rf2-rt4jz) used the leak as a SETUP STEP: it asserted as a control that a destroyed id row still names pool V1, and the fix made that false. The first repair restated that control to pin the release instead, arguing that an ABSENT row would redden the reproduction just as hard (nil reads as the live source store, which zero-matches that frame explicit include-ns composition). That argument is WRONG, and only a sabotage run found it: reverting the rf2-rt4jz ordering left the case at 0 failures, because the zero-match is swallowed by the RESILIENT flush, so the constructor generation survives and the pin goes silent exactly where it exists to shout. A restatement that reads perfectly had removed a regression pin teeth. The other candidate was measured and also fails to reproduce: a same-id RE-construction over a LIVE frame does leave a genuine previous-pool row, but :initial-events fires only on FIRST construction, so nothing resolves inside upsert-frame! and the window never opens (app-db stays empty). So the pairing the reproduction needs — a destroyed id, making the next construction a first one that runs the setup cascade, CARRYING a previous incarnation row — no longer arises on its own, and the row is now planted explicitly, in a namespace that is white-box by construction (it already reads the private provenance table and the private dirty flag directly) and says so. Verified in both directions with the same plant (a1f1c342 -> 0655bab5): 2 failures under the pre-rf2-rt4jz ordering, the constructor returning a frame running V1, which is the original defect; and 0 with the ordering as shipped. THE GENERAL LESSON: a test that consumes a leak as a precondition goes QUIET rather than red when the leak is fixed, and restating its control by reasoning about the new state is not enough — the restatement has to be re-sabotaged.
