A TEST THAT CONSUMES A LEAK AS A PRECONDITION GOES QUIET, NOT RED, WHEN THE LEAK IS FIXED (2026-09-01, found by the genpool worker on rf2-cq0yi, PR #8887).

THE SHAPE: make_frame_generation_pool_window_jvm_test (rf2-rt4jz) used a generation-pool leak as a SETUP STEP -- it asserted as a control that a destroyed frames row still named pool V1. Fixing the leak (releasing the row at destroy-frame!) removed that precondition. The test did not fail. It kept passing while no longer pinning anything.

WHY THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS NOT ENOUGH: the worker restated the control to pin the RELEASE instead, reasoning that an absent row would redden the reproduction just as hard, since nil reads as the live source store and zero-matches that frames explicit include-ns composition. That argument is well-formed and WRONG. Re-sabotaging showed 0 failures: the zero-match is swallowed by the resilient flush, so the constructors generation survives and the pin stays quiet exactly where it exists to shout.

THE RULE: when a fix removes a state some test consumed, restating that tests control by REASONING about the new state is not enough. The restatement has to be RE-SABOTAGED -- revert the original defect and confirm the restated test goes red. Only a fresh red proves the pin still has teeth.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS: nothing signals it. The suite stays green through the fix, through the restatement, and through the regression the pin was meant to catch. A restatement that reads perfectly can have removed a regression pins teeth entirely, and code review cannot see it because the test still looks like it asserts something.

CONFIRMING MEASUREMENT FROM THE SAME WORK: after planting the precondition explicitly instead, the same test read 2 failures under the pre-rf2-rt4jz ordering (the original defect reproduced) and 0 with the ordering as shipped -- verified in BOTH directions, which is what a restored pin looks like.

GENERALISATION WORTH CARRYING: this is the sabotage discipline applied to a case people do not think of as sabotage. The gate-mechanics block already says a green sabotage run is a reason to stop rather than proceed. The uncovered case is that FIXING A BUG can silently convert a live pin into a vacuous one, so any test whose setup depended on the buggy behaviour needs its control re-proven, not re-argued.

title: surface-review(routing): make url-decode fail closed on invalid UTF-8 on both hosts
description:
## Owning item

Found while implementing rf2-j3tud (component URL ENCODING host-parity, PR #8873), which asked whether the reverse direction carried a matching asymmetry. It does not — this is a SECOND, different defect, so it is filed separately rather than folded in. rf2-j3tud's non-goals explicitly keep decoding out of scope ("No change to ... decoding", "Keep decode behavior and the literal-+ rule intact").

## Correctness finding

`re-frame.routing.url/url-decode` documents itself as HOST-SYMMETRIC and claims the JVM path "reproduces `decodeURIComponent` exactly". It does so for the `+` rule (rf2-9a9ix) and for structurally malformed input (`%`, `%a`, `%zz` are nil on both hosts). It does NOT for INVALID UTF-8 BYTE SEQUENCES.

`java.net.URLDecoder/decode` decodes with a REPLACE malformed-input action, substituting U+FFFD and returning a string. `js/decodeURIComponent` throws URIError, which `safe-url-decode` converts to the nil fail-closed sentinel.

## Evidence (production code, both hosts)

| input | JVM `safe-url-decode` | CLJS `safe-url-decode` |
|---|---|---|
| `%C0%80` (overlong NUL) | 2x U+FFFD, NON-NIL | nil |
| `%ED%A0%80` (lone surrogate) | 1x U+FFFD, NON-NIL | nil |
| `%FF` (invalid lead byte) | 1x U+FFFD, NON-NIL | nil |
| `%E0%80%80` (overlong) | 3x U+FFFD, NON-NIL | nil |
| `%C3%A9` (valid) | "e-acute" | "e-acute" (agree) |
| `%`, `%a`, `%zz` | nil | nil (agree) |

Measured consequence at the public predicate:

    (url/malformed-url? "/p/%FF")  ; JVM => false ; CLJS => true

## Why it matters

`malformed-url?` is the discriminator `:rf.route/transitioned` / `:rf.route/handle-url-change` use to separate a bare route-miss (`{:url url}`) from the fail-closed malformed case (`{:url url :reason :malformed-url}`). So for a URL carrying an invalid UTF-8 escape:

- CLJS (browser): fails closed, route-miss with `:reason :malformed-url`.
- JVM (SSR): decodes to a param containing U+FFFD replacement characters and MATCHES the route.

Two consequences, both in classes this repo already treats as defects:

1. **Host divergence on a security-adjacent sink.** `safe-url-decode`'s own docstring names the motivation as "hostile URLs, partner integrations with broken escaping". The fail-closed posture the JVM arm was written to have is not the one it has.
2. **Spec 011 hydration mismatch.** The server renders the matched route's tree; the hydrating client renders not-found for the same URL. That is a whole-tree disagreement, strictly worse than the attribute-level one rf2-j3tud fixed.

## Recommended direction (not a ruling)

Make the JVM arm fail closed on malformed UTF-8, matching `decodeURIComponent` — the same direction rf2-9a9ix took for `+` and rf2-j3tud took for the encoder, i.e. CLJS normative. Mechanically this means decoding percent-escapes to bytes and running them through a UTF-8 decoder with REPORT (not REPLACE) malformed-input action, so invalid sequences throw and `safe-url-decode` returns its existing nil sentinel. No caller changes: every consumer already propagates that sentinel.

Worth deciding explicitly: whether a legitimately-encoded U+FFFD (`%EF%BF%BD`) must still decode successfully. It should — it is valid UTF-8 — and any fix must not conflate it with the substituted one, which is exactly the bug a naive "does the output contain U+FFFD?" check would introduce.

## Acceptance criteria

- A shared CLJC test asserts `safe-url-decode` returns nil on JVM and CLJS alike for a table of invalid UTF-8 escapes (overlong, lone surrogate, invalid lead byte), with valid multi-byte input (`%C3%A9`) and legitimately-encoded U+FFFD (`%EF%BF%BD`) as controls that must still decode.
- `malformed-url?` agrees across hosts for a URL carrying such an escape in a path segment, a query key, a query value and a fragment.
- Reverting the JVM decoder makes the JVM half red while the valid-input controls stay green.
- Focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.

## Non-goals

- No change to the `+`-literal rule, to encoding, to route patterns/matching/ranking, or to the nil-sentinel propagation contract.
- No inbound URL normalisation or sanitisation beyond the decode-failure classification.
acceptance_criteria: safe-url-decode returns nil on BOTH hosts for invalid UTF-8 escapes (overlong, lone surrogate, invalid lead byte), with %C3%A9 and %EF%BF%BD as controls that must still decode; malformed-url? agrees across hosts for such an escape in path segment, query key, query value and fragment; reverting the JVM decoder reds the JVM half while the valid-input controls stay green; focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.

FENCED 2026-09-01 14:01 AUSEST by the mayor: implementation/routing/** is held by a LIVE fix worker on branch worker/routing-encoding-j3tud (PR #8873), which is repairing a cross-artefact break the url-ENCODE change caused in implementation/http. This item is the url-DECODE counterpart and touches the same namespace, so it waits for #8873 to merge — not merely for that worker to finish. Two things to carry into the dispatch when it comes, both from the worker that filed this: the defect is that java.net.URLDecoder substitutes U+FFFD where decodeURIComponent throws, so malformed-url? reads false on JVM and true on CLJS and a hostile URL matches under SSR while failing closed in the browser; and a legitimately-encoded U+FFFD (%EF%BF%BD) is valid UTF-8 that MUST still decode, so a naive 'output contains U+FFFD' check would introduce a new bug.

---

VERDICT 2026-09-01 (worker, PR #8882, branch worker/urldecode-k2d2t)

FINDING CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, not taken on faith. The five-input probe was
reproduced against production code on both hosts before any edit. JVM
safe-url-decode returned non-nil for %C0%80 (2x U+FFFD), %ED%A0%80 (1x),
%FF (1x) and %E0%80%80 (3x) — codepoints read as 65533, so these were
genuine substitutions, not an artefact of console encoding — while
decodeURIComponent threw for all four. (malformed-url? "/p/%FF") read
false on JVM and true on CLJS. Every claim on this bead held exactly.

FIX. url-decode's JVM arm now decodes in three stages: pre-escape (bare
`+`, then every literal non-ASCII character), URLDecoder under
ISO-8859-1 — the 1:1 byte<->char charset, which performs the SAME
structural validation as before (%, %a, %zz still throw
IllegalArgumentException) while substituting nothing — and finally a
strict UTF-8 decode of the recovered bytes through a CharsetDecoder set
to CodingErrorAction/REPORT. safe-url-decode's existing nil sentinel
carries the result; no caller changed.

HOW THE NEAR-MISS IS DISTINGUISHED — the trap this bead warned about.
The check is made at the BYTE level, under the UTF-8 decoder's own
validity rules, and the decoded OUTPUT is never inspected for U+FFFD.
%EF%BF%BD is a legal three-byte sequence, so it decodes to U+FFFD; %FF
is not, so it throws. An output-inspecting check cannot separate the two
— the substituted character and the legitimate one are identical — which
is exactly why that approach was refused. %EF%BF%BD is pinned as a
positive case and stayed green throughout, including under sabotage.

LITERAL NON-ASCII, which the recommended direction did not mention and
which a naive strict-decoder fix silently regresses. Both hosts pass an
unescaped non-ASCII character through today (decodeURIComponent("cafe"
with an acute e) returns it unchanged), and a strict decoder reached via
a bare latin-1 round trip would newly reject it — re-introducing the
very divergence class this bead is about. Hence the pre-escape stage.
Folding a literal into an ADJACENT escape run cannot change the verdict
either way: a literal's UTF-8 always begins with a lead byte (C2-F4),
never a continuation byte, so it can neither complete a truncated run
nor spoil a valid one. Verified against node in both directions.

TWO LATENT DIVERGENCES FOUND THAT THIS BEAD DID NOT NAME. "%C3" followed
by a literal non-ASCII character, and "%E2%82" likewise, threw on CLJS
and returned a U+FFFD-bearing string on the JVM. Both now fail closed on
both hosts and are pinned in the suite.

NO SPEC EDIT OWED — checked rather than assumed. Spec 012 §`+` is a
literal ¶1 already names decodeURIComponent as the de-facto reference
and states the browser is the canonical host "so the JVM matches it",
and the paragraph above it names a host-divergent decoder as the Spec
011 hydration-mismatch class; §Route-miss ¶5 already requires malformed
percent-encoding to fail the whole match closed. So this is a
conformance repair to standing normative text, the same conclusion
rf2-j3tud reached for the encode half. spec/011-SSR.md and
spec/012-Routing.md are untouched, and neither needed touching.

TESTS. New implementation/routing/test/re_frame/
routing_url_decoding_parity_cljs_test.cljc — one .cljc table asserted
identically on both hosts against literal expected values, extending the
mechanism rf2-j3tud built rather than inventing a second one. Pins the
invalid-UTF-8 set, the valid-decode controls (%EF%BF%BD, an astral code
point, %2B, +-literal) so it cannot pass by nil-ing everything, the
literal-non-ASCII passthrough, malformed-url? across path segment /
query key / query value / fragment with valid-escape controls in the
same four positions, the production match-url prism, and the route-url
-> match-url round trip over a value containing a real U+FFFD.

GATES, exit codes captured on one command line and quoted from the
captured .exit file (not from harness-reported status), re-run on the
final base after rebasing onto 77d6ecbbaa:
  JVM focused                  exit 0 — 6 tests, 60 assertions
  JVM full routing artefact    exit 0 — 542 tests, 3279 assertions
  CLJS focused                 exit 0 — 6 tests, 60 assertions
  CLJS full node-test          exit 0 — 11143 tests, 54841 assertions
The focused counts are identical on both hosts (6/60), which is the
host-symmetry the suite exists to assert.

CONTROL. Single-line plant (CodingErrorAction/REPORT -> REPLACE on
.onMalformedInput), anchor match count checked as 1 before running so
the plant could not silently no-op. Sabotaged JVM run: exit 1, 19
failures over the same 6 tests / 60 assertions, so nothing crashed and
no assertions were lost. All 19 are fail-closed assertions. ZERO
failures mention %EF%BF%BD — every valid-decode control stayed green
under sabotage, which is what proves the fix does not over-reject.
Restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object (line
endings are translated in this checkout, so a byte digest of the working
file would not have been sound), then re-run green (exit 0, 6/60).

title: machines: restored mixed-prefix actors violate reverse-creation teardown
description:
## Scope

Correct restored/hydrated spawned-actor disposal ordering in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/frame_destroy.cljc` and the spawn/teardown bookkeeping it consumes. Add focused coverage in `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/frame_destroy_cascade_test.clj` and update the machine runtime-db schema/spec commentary needed for any new durable ordering fact.

## Correctness finding

`teardown-on-frame-destroy!` promises reverse creation order even after epoch restore or SSR hydration has repopulated durable snapshots without the process-side `spawn-order` atom. Its fallback sorts actor IDs by the trailing `#<n>` parsed by `creation-rank`. That suffix is only a per-`id-prefix` sequence, not a frame-global creation sequence. It therefore cannot order actors created under different machine types/prefixes, and IDs supplied through `:fixed-actor-id` carry no rank at all. The implementation is attempting to reconstruct information that the durable state does not contain.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From `implementation/machines`, use the existing plain-atom/reset-runtime fixture, create one frame, and register two child machine types `:probe/a` and `:probe/b`; each child appends its stamped `:rf/self-id` to an atom from its active state's `:exit` action.
2. Register a boot machine whose action emits three `:rf.machine/spawn` effects in order: A, A, B. Dispatch it and verify `spawn-order/frame-order` is `[:probe/a#1 :probe/a#2 :probe/b#1]`.
3. Call `spawn-order/reset-all!` while leaving runtime-db snapshots intact. This is the existing test suite's model of epoch restore/SSR hydration, where durable state survives and the process-side atom does not.
4. Call `rf/destroy-frame!` and inspect the exit log. Current main produces `[:probe/a#2 :probe/a#1 :probe/b#1]`; exact reverse creation order is `[:probe/b#1 :probe/a#2 :probe/a#1]`.

## Evidence

- `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md:34-40` pins frame disposal to leaf-to-root exit cascades in reverse creation order, with the most recently spawned instance disposing first.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/frame_destroy.cljc:91-113` parses only the numeric suffix; lines 168-177 and 209-220 claim that descending suffix order reconstructs the durable creation order.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:60-75` increments `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawn-counter <machine-id>]`; lines 909-914 select `(or :id-prefix :machine-id)` as that counter key. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:2711-2718,4471` likewise defines the allocator as per-prefix.
- The existing restore regression at `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/frame_destroy_cascade_test.clj:321-366` creates three actors of the same `:rs/child` prefix, so suffix rank happens to be a valid total order and the mixed-prefix defect is invisible.
- The JVM public-surface probe above exited 0 with:

```clojure
{:recorded   [:probe/a#1 :probe/a#2 :probe/b#1]
 :exit-order [:probe/a#2 :probe/a#1 :probe/b#1]
 :expected   [:probe/b#1 :probe/a#2 :probe/a#1]}
```

The wrong first exit is forced, not a map-order flake: rank 2 sorts ahead of rank 1 even though `:probe/b#1` was created last.

## Failure scenario / invariant

An SSR-hydrated or epoch-restored frame contains actors of two worker types. The application created `a#1`, then `a#2`, then `b#1`; their exit actions release dependent resources or emit ordered cleanup effects. The transient atom is absent after the round trip. `destroy-frame!` exits `a#2` before the newer `b#1`, and may place the equal-rank `a#1` before `b#1` as well. This violates the pinned stack-discipline invariant and exposes cleanup effects in an order the application did not create.

Invariant: every supported frame-state round trip must preserve one total oldest-to-newest order for live spawned actors, independent of actor-id spelling, type, prefix, or fixed-id allocation. Frame destruction consumes its exact reverse.

## Recommended minimal fix

Persist the total live-spawn order in the durable machine runtime-db instead of deriving it from actor IDs. The smallest shape is an oldest-to-newest vector sibling under `:rf.runtime/machines` (for example `:spawn-order`): append exactly once in the same exact-owner write that successfully installs a spawned snapshot, remove the actor in every successful teardown projection, and have frame destruction read that durable vector. Epoch restore already replaces runtime-db wholesale, and the SSR projector already carries machine bookkeeping siblings verbatim, so the same fact then survives both paths without a restore callback.

The current process-side atom may be removed or retained only as a derived cache; it must not remain the source of truth after a round trip. Remove or explicitly demote the suffix parser: per-prefix ranks can be a deterministic last-resort walk for malformed/fixture-only state, but cannot satisfy or be described as satisfying reverse creation order. Keep the public actor-id format and per-prefix counters unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a red-first focused test that spawns at least `a#1`, `a#2`, then `b#1` through the public machine/fx path. Before simulating the round trip, it asserts the exact live order `[:a#1 :a#2 :b#1]` and that all three spawned snapshots exist; these are non-vacuity controls.
- Simulate the real loss boundary (wipe only transient bookkeeping or round-trip/replace the frame runtime-db) while retaining the new durable order. Then `rf/destroy-frame!` must run child exit actions exactly `[:b#1 :a#2 :a#1]`, once each. The test must fail on current main with the measured `a#2`-first result.
- The durable ordering fact round-trips through EDN and the SSR machine-runtime projection unchanged; no function, atom, host handle, or process-local token enters runtime-db.
- Successful explicit destroy/finalization removes the actor from the durable live order; a later frame destroy neither exits it twice nor leaves an unbounded stale entry. Existing system-id release, snapshot cleanup, and silent-idempotent destroy assertions remain green.
- The existing same-prefix restore control (`child#3`, `child#2`, `child#1`) remains green, demonstrating that the fix preserves the ordinary path while the new mixed-prefix case is the discriminator.
- Schema/spec/source prose names the durable total-order authority and no longer claims that a per-prefix `#<n>` suffix reconstructs global creation order.
- Negative control: removing/bypassing the new durable-order append or reverting frame destroy to suffix sorting makes the mixed-prefix assertion red while its pre-destroy liveness/order controls still pass.

## Non-goals

- No change to public actor IDs, the per-prefix spawn counters, `:system-id`, join semantics, or callback APIs.
- No compatibility layer for historical pre-alpha payloads, global wall-clock timestamp, UUID ordering, or process-wide actor registry.
- No redesign of singleton teardown, frame incarnation fencing, timer cancellation, HTTP abort, classification, or general SSR/epoch machinery.
- No claim that arbitrary hand-edited runtime-db lacking the new durable fact can reveal an order it never recorded.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all bead statuses with title and description terms `reverse-creation`, `reverse creation`, `spawn-order`, `spawn order`, `frame destroy`, `frame-destroy`, `restored spawned`, `restored actor`, `creation-rank`, `newest-first`, `newest first`, `straggler`, `disposal order`, `mixed-prefix`, and `per-prefix`; no issue owns this invariant. Open `rf2-cq0yi` concerns core's unrelated `frame-generation-pool` teardown leak, not machine actor ordering. The sole in-progress bead at filing time, `rf2-jui1c`, is an unrelated prose sweep and was left untouched.
acceptance_criteria: A focused mixed-prefix restore/hydration test proves the pre-round-trip live order, preserves a durable total order through the round trip, and observes exact reverse creation order on frame destroy; disabling the durable-order path makes that test fail while the existing same-prefix control stays green. Destroy/finalize pruning, EDN/SSR transport, schema/spec truth, and existing teardown cleanup remain covered.

AUDIT PR #8870 (2026-09-01): REOPENED. The durable order repair is sound for a fresh-process hydration, but its restore model is not faithful to the in-process APIs it explicitly claims. The new tests call `spawn-order/reset-all!` by hand and assert that this is exactly the post-`restore-epoch!` / `replace-frame-state!` state. Actual epoch restore fires `:machines/on-frame-restored!`, whose implementation only cancels timers; no production restore/replacement path clears the frame's transient spawn-order cache.

Concrete regression: spawn A, capture an epoch, spawn newer B, then restore the A-only epoch. Durable state correctly becomes snapshots/order [A], while the transient cache remains [A B]. `teardown-on-frame-destroy!` now destroys the durable segment first (A) and then treats cache-only B as an unsequenced live actor, so it emits/tears down a discarded actor after the older restored actor. Before this PR the cache walk happened B,A; #8870's new segment ordering makes the stale cache violate the reverse-creation teardown it was meant to fix. The same stale entry also keeps `destroy/actor-live?` true after B was reverted out of durable state.

Minimal completion: make every supported in-process whole/partial runtime-state install reconcile or clear this frame's transient cache (not other frames), or otherwise prove cache-only discarded actors cannot be treated as live; add a public `restore-epoch!` / runtime replacement regression without manually resetting internals. Preserve the durable vector as ordering authority and avoid a new compatibility layer.

title: mayor/fleet: three subagents register as running while idle for 1h+, stranding two green PRs behind an unset draft flag
description:
OPERATIONAL, filed by the mayor 2026-09-01 15:10 AUSEST for Mike's call. Not a code defect.

SYMPTOM. Three background workers report 'running' in the agent listing while every independent signal says they are idle:
  - a95b2faa (rf2-ni0ko, PR #8872): last commit 2h ago, worktree clean, local tip == remote tip, no reply to a direct message sent ~30 min ago.
  - a458d57b (rf2-g1m2q, PR #8876): last commit 79 min ago, no file write since 13:51, worktree clean, tip == remote, no reply to a direct message.
  - abed3ebfd (rf2-j3tud fix worker): its PR MERGED two hours ago and its remote branch was deleted; zero unmerged patches; no write for 80+ min; no reply to a stop-and-report sent ~50 min ago.

COST, and it is not just slots. PR #8876 reads 85 checks / 0 non-terminal / 0 failing — the current band exactly. It clears every clause of the merge criterion EXCEPT the draft flag, which only its author can flip. PR #8872 is complete too but computed against the pre-#8868 matrix (84), so it needs a rebase as well as a ready mark. So two finished changes are stranded behind an interlock whose protected party may no longer exist, and the effective fleet is 3 of 6.

WHY THE MAYOR HAS NOT ACTED. Three candidate remedies, each reserved:
  (a) Flip the draft flag myself. The interlock exists so the merge loop cannot land a change out from under a live worker; overriding it on an INFERENCE that the worker is dead is exactly the proxy the reaping rules exist to forbid, one surface over.
  (b) Stop the agents (TaskStop), which would establish they are not live and discharge (a) honestly — but destroys any unwritten report, and the reports are the outstanding deliverable.
  (c) Dispatch around them to keep 6 ACTIVE. Done once already this session and it worked, but it grows the registered-agent count without bound if agents keep going quiet, and it is the wrong move if the cause is machine contention.

DIAGNOSIS IS UNRESOLVED and that is why this is filed rather than fixed. The competing explanation is loops.md section 2's wedge: a heavyweight gate that stalls with no progress, no exit file and no error, which would also explain why messages are not drained (they land at the receiver's next tool round, and a wedged tool call never reaches one). Machine reads 58 chrome and 11 node processes against 1 java — real browser-lane activity, but attributable to the three ACTIVE workers, so it neither confirms nor refutes the wedge.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: whether the harness's 'running' state distinguishes a live turn from an agent stuck in a hung tool call, and whether there is a liveness probe cheaper than a message that a wedged agent cannot answer.

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE IN MY PRACTICE: a long-running worker is the DEFAULT explanation for a still tree,
not the exotic one. Before reporting an agent dormant, state how long its brief plausibly takes and

title: template: after-load hooks leave the app schema stale after edits
description:
## Scope

The generated browser entry points and schema guidance under `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template`: the default Reagent scaffold, UIx scaffold, Reagent Story scaffold, and Reagent SSR client's hot-reload path. Add focused generator/emitted-project regression coverage; no framework API redesign.

## Correctness finding

Every emitted app registers its app-db schema only from the module `init`, while Shadow CLJS calls that init function once and invokes only `^:dev/after-load` hooks after a save. Those hooks rerender the retained app but never re-register the newly loaded schema value. Consequently the framework continues validating the live frame with the boot-time schema after `schema.cljs` changes, even though the generated UI and event code hot-reload. The scaffold's advertised hot-reload loop is therefore internally inconsistent and can reject a source-valid write (or accept a write forbidden by a tightened schema) until a full page refresh.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Generate a default app, run `npm install` and `npx shadow-cljs watch app`, and open the counter page.
2. Increment the counter so preserving live state across reload is observable.
3. In `schema.cljs`, extend the closed `CounterDb` map with an optional string key such as `[:counter/label {:optional true} :string]`.
4. Change an event handler to associate `:counter/label` with a string, then save both files and let Shadow CLJS run the emitted `^:dev/after-load` hook.
5. Dispatch that event without refreshing the page. The write is validated against the original closed map, emits `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure`, and rolls back. Refreshing the page runs `init` again and makes the same write succeed.

The inverse is also incorrect: tightening a schema during the same session leaves the former permissive schema active until refresh.

## Evidence

- `_shared/schema.cljs` defines `register-schema!` with the instruction "Call once at boot (see core/init)" and passes the current `CounterDb` value to `rf/reg-app-schema`.
- `_reagent/core.cljs` lines 41-49 and `_uix/core.cljs` lines 36-45 tag `mount!` as `^:dev/after-load`, but it only retains/creates the React root and renders. Their `init` functions call `schema/register-schema!` only at lines 71 and 67 respectively.
- `_reagent/core_with_stories.cljs` lines 95-97 make `reload!` reinstall routing and render, while schema registration exists only in `init` at line 111.
- `_reagent/core_with_ssr.cljc` lines 156-164 make `render!` rerender the retained root, while the client schema is registered only in `init` at line 178.
- The emitted `root/README.md` lines 25-35 correctly says Shadow invokes `init` once and then calls after-load hooks, but lines 419-435 teach schema registration only once at boot.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc` lines 567-572 stores the schema value in `schemas-by-frame`; it does not retain a Var that follows a redefinition. Lines 698-704 explicitly define hot-reload semantics as re-registering the `(frame-id, path)` so the new value replaces the prior validation-cache entry.
- Existing HMR emission tests exercise retained-root rerendering for Reagent, UIx, Story, and SSR, but do not assert schema replacement after a reload. Initial browser smoke tests cannot expose this post-save failure.

## Failure scenario / invariant

After any successful generated-app hot reload, validation and tooling must observe the schema definitions in the just-loaded source while preserving the existing frame, app-db, React root, and routing/hydration state. A source-valid event write must not fail solely because a stale boot-time schema remains cached, and a newly invalid write must not pass for the same reason.

## Recommended minimal fix

Have each emitted `^:dev/after-load` path re-register the current app schema for its existing frame before rerendering. Preserve the current boot ordering so initial events are still validated, and do not recreate/reseed the frame. In the SSR client, re-register against `app-frame` but do not repeat hydration. Update the generated schema comments/README to describe registration at boot and after load. The runtime already makes same-frame/path re-registration atomic and hot-reload-safe, so no framework change is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused executable CLJS regression drives the actual generated after-load path (or a small extracted reload seam used by that path): it boots with the original closed schema, retains non-default counter state, substitutes a schema that admits optional `:counter/label`, invokes reload without recreating the frame, and asserts `rf/app-schema-at [] {:frame :rf/default}` returns the new schema.
- The same test dispatches an ordinary generated event that writes `:counter/label` and proves the write commits while the pre-reload counter value remains intact.
- Coverage pins schema re-registration for all four emitted browser entry variants: default Reagent, UIx, Story, and the SSR client. SSR coverage additionally proves reload does not call `ssr/hydrate!` or replay seed events.
- The proof is non-vacuous: before the production fix, the fixture observes the old schema and the new-key write is rejected/rolled back; equivalently, a mutation/control that removes the after-load registration makes the regression fail.
- Existing emitted-project compile tests, initial browser smoke tests, and retained-root HMR tests remain green.
- Generated comments and README no longer claim that registration happens only once at boot; they explain that after-load re-registration updates validation while retaining app state.

## Non-goals

- Re-running module init, initial events, frame creation, hydration, or routing setup beyond what each current reload hook already requires.
- Changing runtime schema storage, validation policy, production elision, or public schema APIs.
- Adding watcher/process orchestration when a deterministic generated-code CLJS test can prove the reload invariant.
- Compatibility machinery for older generated projects.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status beads for `stale schema`, `after-load schema`, `schema hot reload`, `schema re-registration`, `register-schema hot reload`, `CounterDb reload`, `schema.cljs after-load`, and `template HMR`; no matching issue exists. Closed `rf2-r0kk7` fixed the distinct absence of generated after-load rerender hooks and deliberately kept one-time boot ceremony in `init`; it did not refresh the schema registry and is not a duplicate.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8897, confined to tools/template/**.

DEFECT CONFIRMED AT SOURCE in all four emitted entry points. reg-app-schema is frame-local, so the scaffold cannot call it at namespace load (a load-time call raises :rf.error/no-frame-context); it lives inside schema/register-schema!. A hot reload therefore re-evaluates the CounterDb def and re-registers nothing on its own, and every entry point called register-schema! from init alone -- which shadow runs once, at bundle load.

FIX: each ^:dev/after-load hook re-attaches the schema, BEFORE its render work. Reagent and UIx fold the call into mount!, which init already delegates to, so boot and reload traverse one path; Story (reload!) and the SSR client (render!) keep their one-time boot ceremony in init and re-attach from the hook. The SSR hook does not re-hydrate or replay seed events. Ordering matters as much as presence: the boot call still lands before frame-root creates the frame, so the :initial-events seed is validated from the first write, and a DOM-free host that skips the render still registers.

QUESTION 1 -- is hook-side re-registration correct, or does it paper over a framework gap? CORRECT; no framework change and no follow-up bead. Spec 010 Multiple-schemas-at-the-same-path makes re-registration last-write-wins and calls a hot-reload re-register benign; Spec 010 Schema-migration-on-hot-reload defines the tightened-schema case (a :rf.schema/violation warning, app-db not cleared or rewound); storage.cljc's hot-reload-semantics block makes it an atomic swap! into the map that IS the validation cache; and executable framework coverage already exists (schemas_storage_test meta-at-reflects-hot-reload-replacement, schemas_reg_side_effects_test, a hot-reload race stress test).

QUESTION 2 -- one shared helper or four parallel edits? FOUR PARALLEL EDITS. A helper would still have to be called from each hook, so it saves nothing at the call site; it could not cover all four anyway, since the SSR scaffold has no schema.cljs and its register-schema! is inline in core.cljc with a different arity; the emitted files are user-facing source, so the reader must see in the hook what a reload re-does; and fixing at the defect site leaves rf2-zq34m unprejudiced.

COVERAGE. title: bug(skill-setup): generator resolves tools/template from the fresh target
description:
## Scope

Fix the explicitly requested generator route in `skills/re-frame2-setup/**`: how the installed skill locates the pre-publish `tools/template` checkout, chooses the generator command's working/target directory, and evaluates that workflow. The default manual scaffold remains unchanged. This task may add a focused command-level fixture that invokes the actual documented route, but does not redesign `tools/template` output.

## Correctness finding

The skill promises to execute the generator itself for a user standing in a fresh project directory, but its only working pre-publish command passes `{:local/root "tools/template"}`. A Clojure local root is resolved against the command's current working directory, so from the directory being scaffolded it means `<target>/tools/template`, which does not exist. The command fails before deps-new loads the template. Running the literal command from the monorepo root makes the dependency resolve, but changes the output base to the monorepo rather than the user's requested location. The advertised executor route therefore has no specified command that both finds the template and writes into the intended target.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:57` calls the generator a complete alternative that the skill runs itself when requested, and says the pre-publish working form is the local-root invocation against a checkout.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:23-24` grants the corresponding `clojure -Tnew create` and `clojure -Sdeps ... -Tnew create` commands.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:24-31` presents the pre-publish command with literal `{:local/root "tools/template"}`; unlike the template's own README, it does not bind that relative path to an execution cwd or derive the installed checkout path.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:37` reiterates that the skill executes the command, while the product is advertised as scaffolding from an empty directory at lines 5 and 41.
- `tools/template/README.md:50-58` says its relative-local-root form must run from the repository root. That premise is incompatible with treating the user's fresh target as the command cwd unless output placement is made explicit.
- `tools/template/deps.edn:19-25` already records the correct clean-directory form for in-repo smoke testing: use an absolute `<abs-path>/tools/template` local root when the command runs from an empty directory.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/evals/evals.json:26` mentions the generator as a complete UIx alternative but has no executable expectation proving path resolution or output placement from a directory outside the monorepo.
- Command witness: from a newly created empty temporary directory outside the checkout, the exact advertised `clojure -Sdeps ... {:local/root "tools/template"} ... -Tnew create` form exited 1 with `Local lib day8/re-frame2-template not found: <clean-target>/tools/template`; it emitted no project files. The temporary directory was removed after the witness.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install/link `re-frame2-setup` from a reviewed checkout, then create and enter a separate empty directory where the new app should be generated.
2. Ask the skill to use the generator route, or run the pre-publish command printed in `skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:30-31` unchanged.
3. Observe exit 1 before template hooks run: tools.deps resolves the relative local root beneath the empty target and reports that `day8/re-frame2-template` is not found.
4. Change cwd to the monorepo root and retry the same literal command. The local root now resolves, but deps-new's relative output base is the monorepo cwd rather than the original empty target unless a separate target path is supplied.

## Failure scenario / invariant

An explicitly requested generator run must satisfy both coordinates at once: its template dependency resolves from the reviewed installed checkout, and its generated files land in the user's requested project location. Neither coordinate may be inferred from one shared cwd. Today the skill conflates them, so the only documented pre-publish command is wrong in the normal fresh-target execution context.

## Recommended minimal fix

At runtime, resolve the template directory from the installed skill/repository location and pass that reviewed directory as an absolute, EDN-safe `:local/root`. Keep command execution/output targeting anchored to the user's requested project directory (or its parent using deps-new's normal target option), and state that relationship once in the generator route. Reuse the existing deps-new template and command; do not add a wrapper generator, copy template resources, or introduce an interactive path prompt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused integration fixture creates a clean target directory outside the re-frame2 checkout, invokes the same generator-command construction the skill teaches with the resolved template checkout path, and asserts exit 0 plus representative emitted files (`deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, `package.json`, and the selected substrate's entry namespace) under the requested target.
- The fixture asserts the resolved local root is the reviewed `tools/template` directory associated with the installed skill, not a `tools/template` child of the target cwd; path rendering works on Windows and POSIX without hand-authored escaping.
- Non-vacuity: the same fixture substitutes the current literal relative local root while remaining in the clean target and must fail before emission with the missing local library resolved under that target. Removing the path-resolution fix therefore makes the positive arm red.
- Control: the generator still receives `day8/re-frame2-template`, the requested project name and substrate, and no generated project directory or manifest is written into the re-frame2 checkout.
- Add an outcome-graded eval for an explicit request such as “Use the generator to scaffold a UIx app in this empty directory.” It must require the skill to execute successfully in that target, not merely print the command or assume the target is the monorepo root.
- The existing setup structural/eval checks and generator tests remain green. The fixture reports its own generator exit code and verifies a non-empty emitted manifest so a skipped command cannot pass.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the default manual scaffold, substrate API, generated application design, or template feature matrix.
- Do not publish/split the template repository, rename Maven coordinates, or solve Clojars availability; those have separate owners.
- Do not add a setup wizard, path questionnaire, copied template snapshot, compatibility command, or second generator implementation.
- Do not broaden into schema hot reload (`rf2-a0442`) or the template-minimisation program (`rf2-zq34m`).

## Related / duplicate search

Searched every tracker status across titles, descriptions, notes, acceptance criteria, and close reasons for `tools/template` with cwd/current-directory/local-root/target terms, generator with cwd/empty-directory/path terms, and setup-generator path terms. No bead owns resolution of the skill's pre-publish generator local root from a fresh target. Open `rf2-rc0yh` established the executor posture and still owns later default-manual simplification; it does not specify or test generator cwd/path resolution. Open `rf2-zq34m` owns the generated product shape, not how this installed skill locates that generator. Deferred `rf2-uelji` and `rf2-fo4ng` own publication/group coordinates and are explicitly outside this local invocation fix.

title: surface-review(routing): make component URL encoding host-identical
description:
## Scope

Correct component emission in `implementation/routing` so the pure `route-url` prism and every consumer of it produce one canonical URL on JVM and CLJS. Cover the encoder plus focused cross-host route/link tests; keep routing grammar and URL strategies unchanged.

## Correctness finding

`re-frame.routing.url/url-encode` promises `encodeURIComponent` semantics on both hosts, but its JVM implementation is `java.net.URLEncoder` with only the space-to-`%20` difference repaired. `URLEncoder` also escapes `!`, apostrophe, `(`, `)`, and `~`; JavaScript `encodeURIComponent` leaves those characters literal. Thus identical valid route data produces different URL bytes on server and browser.

## Steps to Reproduce

From `implementation/routing`, evaluate production `url-encode` on the JVM for character codes 33, 39, 40, 41, and 126; it returns `%21 %27 %28 %29 %7E`. Evaluate JavaScript `encodeURIComponent` for those same characters (the exact function called by the CLJS arm); it returns the literal characters. Then register `:probe` at `/p/:slug` and call production `route-url` with `{:to :probe :params {:slug "~"} :query {"!" "()"} :fragment "~!"}`: JVM returns `/p/%7E?%21=%28%29#%7E%21`, while the CLJS implementation emits `/p/~?!=()#~!`.

## Evidence

- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url.cljc:36-43` documents `encodeURIComponent` semantics, then uses `URLEncoder` plus only `+` -> `%20` on CLJ and native `encodeURIComponent` on CLJS.
- The executable probes above exercise production code, not a reimplementation.
- `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1477-1480,2240-2245,2251-2271` routes ordinary path captures, query keys/values, and fragments through this encoder. `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:142,511-513` makes both route-link doors consume that `route-url` result.
- `spec/012-Routing.md:724-725` requires component-wise `encodeURIComponent` emission and a pure host-symmetric route prism. `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_ssr_parity_cljs_test.cljc:66-88` uses only `x` and `comments`, so its shared JVM/CLJS table does not exercise the divergent boundary characters.
- `docs/ssr/head.md:26` shows `route-url` as the canonical-link source, making the host-dependent bytes visible beyond click handling.

## Failure scenario / invariant

For a legitimate article slug such as `draft~1`, SSR emits `/articles/draft%7E1` while the hydrated client emits `/articles/draft~1`. Route-link's `:href`, canonical head links, copied URLs, cache keys, and snapshots therefore depend on the rendering host; the first client tree can also disagree with the server tree at the href attribute. Both spellings may decode to the same route, but that does not satisfy the stronger promised invariant: identical route data has one host-independent canonical URL byte string.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the CLJ arm implement the exact unescaped character set of `encodeURIComponent`. A small normalization of the five additional `URLEncoder` escapes (`%21`, `%27`, `%28`, `%29`, `%7E`) is sufficient; `*`, `-`, `.`, and `_` already agree. Pin the boundary with one shared CLJC character table and extend the existing production route-link parity table with a punctuation-bearing address. Keep decode behavior and the literal-`+` rule intact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A shared CLJC test asserts identical literal outputs for the complete `encodeURIComponent` unescaped boundary, including `! * apostrophe ( ) - . _ ~`, on JVM and CLJS.
- The same test includes controls that must remain escaped: space as `%20`, `/` as `%2F`, and `%` as `%25`; it cannot pass by disabling encoding.
- A production `route-url` case exercises punctuation in an ordinary path param, query key, query value, and fragment and asserts the same literal expected URL on both hosts, plus exact `match-url(route-url(address))` recovery.
- The existing cross-host route-link parity suite includes a punctuation-bearing address and proves the JVM SSR render and first CLJS render emit the same `:href` under the default strategy.
- Reverting the CLJ encoder to `URLEncoder` plus only the `+`/`%20` swap makes at least the JVM boundary case and production URL/link parity case red while the escaped-character controls remain meaningful.
- Focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.

## Non-goals

- No change to route patterns, matching/ranking, schemas/coercion, URL-strategy composition, history effects, or decoding.
- No dual canonical spelling, compatibility mode, new public API, general URI abstraction, or broad encoder dependency.
- No speculative normalization of inbound URLs; this fixes deterministic emission only.

## Related/duplicate search

Searched all tracker statuses for `encodeURIComponent`, `URLEncoder`, `percent encoding`, `percent-encoding`, `host parity`, `hydration href`, `canonical URL`, `punctuation`, and `url-encode`; no matching open or in-progress issue exists. The sole in-progress bead is unrelated. Closed `rf2-skr1c` fixed whether server link rendering consults a frame's pure URL-strategy encoder and explicitly left `route-url` unchanged; this finding is the lower-level component encoder and reproduces under the default strategy, so it is not a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: A shared CLJC boundary table pins the exact encodeURIComponent literal set on JVM and CLJS with escaped slash/percent/space controls; production route-url and route-link parity cases cover punctuation across path, query, fragment, SSR and first client render; match-url recovers the address; reverting to the current JVM URLEncoder-plus-space implementation makes the focused tests red; focused JVM and CLJS routing suites pass.

  42 * -> * | 45 - -> - | 46 . -> . | 95 _ -> _   (already agreed)
  32 space -> %20 | 47 / -> %2F | 37 % -> %25     (already agreed)
JS `encodeURIComponent` for the same five: `!` `'` `(` `)` `~`, all literal.

Production prism, the item's own reproduction, reproduced verbatim:
  route-url {:to :probe :params {:slug "~"} :query {"!" "()"} :fragment "~!"}
    JVM before /p/%7E?%21=%28%29#%7E%21   after /p/~?!=()#~!  (== CLJS)
  route-url {:to :probe :params {:slug "draft~1"}}
    JVM before /p/draft%7E1               after /p/draft~1

LINE-NUMBER DELTA: nil. Every citation on this bead still resolves at tip —
url.cljc:36-43, registry.cljc:1477-1480 / 2240-2245 / 2251-2271, link.cljc:142
and 511-513, route_link_ssr_parity_cljs_test.cljc:66-88. Only

`encodeURIComponent` — a specific JavaScript function — as the emission
semantics, the CLJS arm IS that function, and the JVM arm is explicitly
labelled the emulation ("emulates it on JVM"). An incomplete emulation is a
conformance bug in the emulator, not a disagreement between peers. Same
direction rf2-9a9ix already took for `+` in url-decode. So the hot-zone
spec/*.md fence was never approached.

unescapes are unambiguous — every %XX in URLEncoder output is one it generated,
a literal `%` is already `%25`, and no `%25`-prefixed run spells one of these
escapes. No knob, no escaping abstraction, no grammar or strategy change.
`url-encode-splat` composes `url-encode` per chunk so it inherits the fix
(pinned, not assumed).

TESTS, one .cljc table per host:
- NEW routing_url_encoding_parity_cljs_test.cljc — all nine unescaped marks one
  assertion each; escaped controls (space `/` `%` `&` `=` `?` `#` `+`, plus
  non-ASCII -> %C3%A9) so it cannot pass by weakening toward identity; splat
  per-chunk; the production route-url prism over path param + query key + query
  value + fragment, with a controls case in the same three positions; and exact
  match-url(route-url(address)) recovery.
- route_link_ssr_parity_cljs_test.cljc gains a :punct column across all four
  strategy shapes and BOTH link doors. Its existing x/comments rows could not
  see the defect: neither string carries a divergent character.

GATES (runner's own captured exit codes, re-run after rebase, final base):
  JVM   `clojure -M:test` in implementation/routing        exit 0  536/3219
  CLJS  compile-node-test.cjs node-test                    exit 0  1867 files, 0 warnings
  CLJS  node out/node-test.js                              exit 0  11135/54757
Focused CLJS run over the two namespaces: exit 0, 8 tests / 80 assertions —
proving the .cljc table really executes on the CLJS host (routing/test is on
:source-paths; the :node-test build's :ns-regexp "cljs-test$" matches both).

CONTROL: reverting the JVM arm to URLEncoder + `+`->`%20` only (plant confirmed
by git blob hash e39ad7bd... -> f87f5413...) gave JVM captured exit 1, 20
failures — all five characters named individually, plus the whole-mark-set
case, the ~-bearing slug, splat per-chunk, three production route-url cases,
the match-url round-trip, and 8 in the route-link parity suite (4 strategy
shapes x 2 doors). The escaped-character controls stayed GREEN, so they are
meaningful rather than what carries the suite. Test/assertion counts were
536/3219 in BOTH the green and the sabotage run, so the plant crashed no
namespace and truncated no lane. Restore verified by git blob hash back to
e39ad7bd..., identical to the committed object.

DECODING — CHECKED, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT, NOT THIS ONE.
The five characters at issue here decode identically on both hosts (%21->!
through %7E->~), so this defect has no decode counterpart and url-decode
correctly stays untouched. But the probe did surface a separate divergence on
INVALID UTF-8: java.net.URLDecoder substitutes U+FFFD and returns a string
where decodeURIComponent throws, so safe-url-decode is non-nil on JVM and nil
on CLJS for %C0%80, %ED%A0%80, %FF and %E0%80%80 — and
`(url/malformed-url? "/p/%FF")` is FALSE on JVM, TRUE on CLJS. A hostile URL is

description:
## Scope

Align the three remaining Story-MCP documentation statements for unreachable browser-only capabilities with the shipped `capability-unavailable` error contract. Documentation only: `tools/story-mcp/README.md`, `tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md`, and `tools/story/spec/Principles.md`. No runtime, schema, tool, or transport change.

## Correctness finding

PR #8865 correctly rewrote `docs/story/api/mcp-surface.md` to say that the headless JVM cannot inspect the CLJS substrate registry or a11y-panel atom and therefore returns `isError true` / `:rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable`, never a false-empty success. Three committed authorities still state the retired opposite:

- `tools/story-mcp/README.md:18-20`: browser-only surfaces return an explicit empty result.
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:462-463`: `read-a11y-violations` returns an empty list plus a hint.
- `tools/story/spec/Principles.md:168-170`: substrates/a11y violations return empty plus a hint.

The implementation, tool descriptors, focused tests, `tools/story-mcp/spec/API.md`, and the opening host-boundary section of `002-Tool-Registry.md` all enforce the error. The stale prose is operationally material: an empty violations vector means a reached provider observed no findings, while capability absence means the host could not look.

## Deduplication

All-status searches over `read-a11y-violations`, `capability-unavailable`, `false-empty`, `empty list`, and the exact sentences found no issue owning these residual pages. rf2-udumn / PR #8865 owns the public chapter and retired `record-as-variant` residue; its enumerated scope is complete and closed, so this narrowly owns the separate capability-result contradiction.

## Recommended minimal fix

Replace the three stale clauses with one consistent rule: unreachable provider -> machine-readable capability error; empty collection -> a reached provider genuinely reported none. Keep the canonical links rather than adding another catalogue.

description:
## Scope

Make Story-MCP's headless `run-variant` / `preview-variant` path fail clearly when the consumer JVM has not installed a re-frame adapter, and teach the existing consumer-project launch recipe to install the renderer-free `plain-atom` adapter when variants are meant to run. ## Correctness finding

PR #8866 made the project-stories conformance witness non-vacuous and discovered the prerequisite needed to make that witness execute: without `(rf/init! plain-atom/adapter)`, the headless server's setup dispatch reaches no adapter, the script produces no assertion, yet `run-variant` returns the ordinary `:status :pass` envelope over `{}` and `[]`. The PR correctly installs `plain-atom` in its fixture, but the published `tools/story-mcp/README.md` golden-path alias only requires the project's story namespace and lists JVM-loadability/stdout as the two namespace rules. A real consumer following it can therefore receive a success-shaped non-run.

The no-adapter state is directly detectable through the existing `rf/current-adapter-spec` surface, and core already names it `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed`. Preserve Story's intentional rule that an actually executed assertion-free variant is vacuously green; the defect is reporting that verdict when frame allocation never obtained the mandatory state substrate.

## Evidence and deduplication

- PR #8866 / rf2-3n3dk's worker note measured `BARE-APPDB {}` / `BARE-ASSERTIONS []` without `rf/init!`, versus the exact passing assertion after installing plain-atom.

At the shared run lifecycle boundary, reject an absent core adapter before allocating/running and return the normal machine-readable MCP error envelope with a concise recovery hint. Update the existing consumer alias example/rules to require `re-frame.substrate.plain-atom` and call `rf/init!` in the preloaded JVM namespace when headless execution is wanted. Pin both failure and recovery in the existing focused tests.

## Non-goals

No automatic substrate choice, browser bridge, adapter registry, blanket assertion requirement, new MCP option/tool, or redesign of Story's vacuous-pass rule.

title: story: variant-share-url appends stale query values instead of replacing them
description:
## Scope

Correct the public tools/story share-URL builder at tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc and add focused coverage at the builder/browser-consumer seam. The issue is limited to merging Story-owned query keys when variant-share-url receives a base-url that already has a query string.

## Correctness finding

variant-share-url appends its generated query fragments after every existing query fragment. It does not replace an existing value for a key it owns. The browser hydrator reads each key with URLSearchParams.get, whose first-value semantics select the old value. A URL requested for one variant can therefore open a different, stale variant.

This violates the explicit share invariant that a pasted URL lands on the exact same cell. It is a current public-API failure, not malformed-input hardening: variant-share-url publicly accepts base-url, and existing-query merging already has a named test.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call variant-share-url for :story.new/b with base-url https://example.test/?variant=story.old%2Fa&from=index#/stories.
2. Observe that the returned search string contains variant=story.old%2Fa followed by variant=story.new%2Fb.
3. Construct URLSearchParams from that search string and call get("variant"), exactly as the Story browser hydrator does.
4. Observe story.old/a; share/parse-params therefore restores the old variant, not :story.new/b.

## Evidence

- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc:357-370 splits off the hash, detects any question mark, selects ampersand, and concatenates the generated params. It never examines or replaces existing keys.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc:486-505 exposes that behavior through variant-share-url and always emits the requested variant.
- For base https://example.test/?variant=story.old%2Fa&from=index#/stories and requested variant :story.new/b, the current algorithm produces two variant entries in old-then-new order.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/url_state.cljc:358-384 constructs URLSearchParams and calls .get for variant before share/parse-params. An executable Node URLSearchParams control over the resulting order returns getAll = [story.old/a, story.new/b] but get = story.old/a.
- tools/story/test/re_frame/story_share_test.clj:84-90 covers only an unrelated from=index query and asserts the separator. It has no same-key collision or end-to-end parse assertion.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc:5-12 and 41-44, tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/url_state.cljc:14-15, and tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:203-222 state the invariant: paste/open reproduces the exact cell.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A programmer starts with a URL that already names story.old/a, calls the documented public builder to make a link for story.new/b, and shares the result. The recipient's browser reads the first variant value and hydrates story.old/a. The visible selection is not the requested selection, even though the generated URL also contains story.new/b.

Invariant: for every query key emitted by a variant-share-url call, the returned URL contains one effective value and the real browser parser observes the value generated by that call. Unrelated base query params and the hash route remain intact.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make append-query-params perform a small key-aware merge: before appending generated fragments, remove every existing occurrence of each key emitted by this call, then append one generated value in the current deterministic order. Preserve unrelated query entries, their values, and the fragment. Keep the codec and public signature unchanged; no compatibility layer or forgiving first/last-value parser is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a focused executable share-builder test whose base contains stale variant and modes values, unrelated from=index and embed=1 values, and #/stories; request a different variant and mode through the real public builder.
- Assert variant and modes each occur exactly once, URLSearchParams.get (or an equivalent standards-faithful browser assertion) returns the newly requested values, and share/parse-params reconstructs those values.
- Assert from=index, embed=1, and #/stories survive unchanged. Retain the existing no-collision existing-query case as the control.
- Demonstrate non-vacuity: the new collision fixture fails against the current append-only implementation because the browser-observed variant is story.old/a; include that red result or an equivalent mutation control in the implementation evidence.
- Run the focused JVM share tests and focused CLJS URL-state/share tests successfully.

## Non-goals

- No URL vocabulary redesign, route redesign, new state slots, parser precedence workaround, compatibility aliases, or broad query-library abstraction.
- No changes to unrelated URL-state hydration/default semantics.
- No normalization of unrelated third-party query parameters.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status bead titles and descriptions for share, URL, variant-share-url, URLSearchParams, duplicate query, stale variant, base-url, existing query, and append-query-params. No issue owns this collision. The returned share-related hits concern shared files/scratchpads/native-share and are unrelated.
acceptance_criteria: A focused test builds from a base containing stale variant/modes plus unrelated from/embed params and a hash route; the result has exactly one value for each emitted Story key, browser first-value parsing and share/parse-params recover the newly requested state, and unrelated params/hash survive. The fixture is shown red against the current append-only implementation (or by an equivalent mutation control), the pre-existing no-collision merge case remains green, and focused JVM plus CLJS share/url-state tests pass.

title: [uix] rf/reg-view* returns a MetaFn that React cannot mount
description:
## Scope

The registry-keyed UIx view path spanning `implementation/adapters/uix/**`, the adapter seam consumed by `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs`, its React-hook shared tests, and the public UIx registry-addressing contract. This is specifically the value registered by `rf/reg-view*` and returned by `rf/view` when the UIx adapter is active.

## Correctness finding

The documented UIx registry-keyed path does not return a component head that UIx/React can mount. `build-frame-aware-view` unconditionally attaches `{:contextType frame-context}` with CLJS metadata, so `(rf/view id)` is a `MetaFn` object rather than a JavaScript function component. Passing that advertised value directly to UIx `$` / React `createElement` fails React's element-type validation before the registered view renders.

The obvious partial repair—only removing the metadata—is also incorrect for UIx. UIx sends lossless CLJS props through its `argv` channel only for a native/marked UIx component head; a generic React function goes through JS-prop conversion. The registered outer wrapper therefore needs to be both genuinely mountable and on UIx's native prop-marshalling path. It must also preserve a real React component boundary for hooks rather than requiring callers to invoke the registered function inside an ad-hoc host component.

## Evidence

- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:16` tells users to use `rf/reg-view*` for registry-keyed view addressing; `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:109` and `:253-262` repeat that UIx contract.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:496-612` (`build-frame-aware-view`) creates the registered head with `(with-meta (fn frame-aware-view ...) {:contextType frame-context})`. `reg-view*` stores and returns that value at `:614-650`.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:6610-6625` explicitly records the current defect: `(rf/view id)` is a CLJS `MetaFn`, React cannot use it as a component type directly, so the test mounts a plain JS `host` that manually invokes `render-fn`. The void-root test repeats this bypass at `:6670-6678`. Those tests therefore prove teardown below the workaround, not the advertised registry-head mount.
- `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:93-106` and `:131-138` require native `defui` shells specifically because UIx reconstructs lossless CLJS props there. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1627-1650` documents the prior failure when a plain function sat below `$`: namespaced keyword values were mangled and frame selection silently changed.
- Reading the pinned `com.pitch/uix.core` 1.4.4 sources (`uix/core.clj`, `uix/compiler/alpha.cljs`) confirms `defui` stamps a JS function as a UIx component and UIx's compiler uses that marker to carry original CLJS props in `argv`; the generic React-component branch converts props instead.
- Repository search found no UIx test that mounts `(rf/view id)` directly as the `$` component head. Existing UIx DOM coverage either mounts `wrap-view` itself or uses the manual-invocation host above.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install `uix-adapter/adapter`, define a UIx `defui` component that receives a CLJS prop and calls `uix-adapter/use-subscribe`, then register it with `(rf/reg-view* ::row row)`.
2. Under the normal UIx frame boundary, render `($ (rf/view ::row) {:payload {:tenant/id :tenant/admin}})` without an intermediate function that invokes the returned value.
3. Observe that React rejects the `MetaFn` as an invalid element type before the registered view renders. The existing shared browser test avoids this result only by mounting a plain JS host component that manually invokes `(rf/view id)`.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A registry-keyed UIx component cannot be used through the component syntax the public docs advertise. If a caller copies the test workaround, hooks and instance lifetime belong to that host and the UIx component's `argv` prop contract is bypassed.

Invariant: every public value advertised as a UIx component head must be directly mountable through `$`, receive the original CLJS props/children losslessly, own a real React hook boundary, and retain the registration wrapper's frame, tracing, source-coordinate, display-name, and unmount behavior.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the UIx adapter's registered-view result an outer, stable, native/marked UIx component shell after the shared frame-aware/instrumentation wrapper has been composed. That shell should receive props through UIx's `argv` path and delegate them without JS round-tripping while retaining a genuine React component boundary. Adjust the shared registration seam only as much as needed to let a React-hook adapter own that outer componentization; do not merely strip `with-meta`, and do not document the manual-invocation host as the solution.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a focused browser test under `implementation/adapters/uix/test/` that installs the UIx adapter, registers a hook-using `defui` via `rf/reg-view*`, and mounts `($ (rf/view id) props)` directly under the normal UIx frame boundary. The test must contain no host function that calls the registered value manually.
2. Pass a nested CLJS prop containing a namespaced keyword/value through that direct mount and assert exact equality inside the registered component; include children if the chosen public form supports them.
3. Have the registered component call `uix-adapter/use-subscribe` (and/or `use-frame`), assert its initial DOM, dispatch an update, and assert the DOM rerenders. Capture browser page errors plus `console.error` and assert there is no invalid-element-type or hook-boundary failure.
4. Retain executable coverage for registered-view render traces/source coordinates, stable instance identity, and exactly-once unmount emission; remove the shared suite's manual-host rationale/bypass where the direct UIx mount now covers it.
5. Non-vacuity/control: in the same harness, directly mount an unregistered native `defui` with the same prop/hook probe and show the harness passes independently of the registry path. During implementation, temporarily restore the current metadata-wrapped returned head (or remove the new UIx componentization seam) and record that the new registry row fails while the native control remains green.
6. `npm run test:browser` from `implementation/` passes with the new direct-mount witness and the existing UIx adapter browser coverage.

## Non-goals

- No new registry API or mandatory host/wrapper ceremony for callers.
- No Reagent registration rewrite.
- No broad React interop compatibility layer or support for arbitrary non-UIx prop conventions.
- No unrelated refactor of the shared spine, tracing schema, or UIx hooks.
- No docs-only workaround.

## Related/duplicate search

Searched the full bead corpus by title and description with `bd search "UIx" --status all`, `bd search` for `MetaFn`, `reg-view*`, `registry-keyed view`, `rf/view UIx`, and `invalid element type`, plus `bd list --all --desc-contains` for `MetaFn`, `reg-view*`, `(rf/view`, and `uix-component?`. Repeated the material terms against `--status open,in_progress`; there were no matches. Closed `rf2-9hcyf` concerns a copy-pasteable UIx component test recipe, and closed `rf2-3afns` concerns Story selecting the wrong substrate; neither owns direct mountability of a registered UIx view.
notes:
---
## Verdict (2026-09-01, PR #8874)

CONFIRMED and FIXED. Both premise checks the bead asked for hold.

**Premise (a) — line numbers.** Essentially zero drift. `build-frame-aware-view` is at views.cljs:496 exactly as cited (its body ends 612; `with-meta` closes at 578). `reg-view*` is at :614 as cited. The shared-suite citations are within ~2 lines: the manual-host rationale sits at 6610-6621 (cited 6610-6625) and the void-root repeat at 6667-6672 (cited 6670-6678).

**Premise (b) — the bypass.** Still present and still read exactly as described: both rows mounted `(fn host-cmp [_props] (render-fn))` and the comment named the MetaFn as the reason. Removed in this PR; both rows now mount `(rf/view id)` directly.

**Mechanism, verified at source rather than from the bead's summary.** `uix.compiler.alpha/component-element` (uix.core 1.4.4, read from the pinned jar) branches on `(.-uix-component? component-type)`: marked heads take `uix-component-element`, which stashes the ORIGINAL CLJS props map on `argv`; everything else takes `react-component-element` -> `interpret-attrs`, which converts props and drops keyword namespaces. A MetaFn has no marker, so it fell to the React branch and `createElement` rejected the object.

**Repair.** New OPTIONAL `:adapter/componentize-view` late-bind hook, consulted last in `reg-view*` (after the substrate wrap and the frame-aware wrapper compose, so the shell is outermost and every existing wrapper keeps its frame/tracing/source-coord/unmount behaviour). Seam split follows rf2-z7hfp's frame-provider precedent: `spine/make-componentize-view` builds the substrate-agnostic forwarding shell; the UIx adapter stamps `uix-component?` on it. The marker -- not the meta-stripping -- is what makes the mount correct. The shell is a marked FORWARDER, not a `defui`: `defui` glues `argv` for its own body, so the shell must pass the props object down untouched for the registered component (typically itself a `defui`) to read in its own idiom -- which is what keeps `(rf/reg-view* ::row row)` ceremony-free, per the bead's Non-goals. Reagent publishes no hook and is unaffected.

The head remains the callable render fn Spec 001 describes. The shell separates React's `Component(props, secondArg)` call from direct positional invocation; react-dom 19.2.0's `updateFunctionComponent` passes `void 0` as `secondArg` (read from source), so without that split a stray undefined would reach the user fn and the rf2-rpgq8 render-args capture.

**No spec change was needed, and this was checked rather than assumed.** Spec 001 s`(re-frame.core/view id)` says "the registered render fn (whatever shape)" -- the change is a strict superset. `spec/Conventions.md:1762` is a generic `:adapter/<surface>` pattern row with examples, not an enumeration, so the HOT-ZONE file stayed untouched. No new public adapter Var, so `spec/API.md` needs no row either.

**Acceptance criteria.** AC1-AC3 met by the new browser row `direct-mount-of-registered-view-head` in `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (no manual host anywhere in the file; nested namespaced-keyword prop asserted for exact equality inside the component; trailing `$` child; `use-subscribe` + `use-frame`; console.error AND window-error capture asserted clean of invalid-element-type and hook-boundary diagnostics). AC4 met: both shared-suite rows now mount the head directly, plus a third row pinning stable instance identity and continued headless callability. AC5 met (control below). AC6 met.

**Gates (captured exit codes, all on the final rebased base fd0113d5bf).** browser compile 0; browser run 0 (755 tests / 4130 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors); node lane `test:cljs` 0 (11133 / 54718, 0 failures); late-bind drift JVM 0; `:advanced` prod-elision release build 0 and its browser run 0 (91 / 289) -- run deliberately because the shell exists in production builds and `uix-component?` is a property name under a release compile.

**Control (AC5) -- the gate bites.** Restoring the metadata-wrapped head (hook key pointed at a non-existent key; source change proved by blob hash, 313 files recompiled so the runtime saw it) turned the browser run RED, exit 1: `direct-mount-of-registered-view-head` failed 9 assertions, the first reading verbatim "Element type is invalid: expected a string ... but got: object", while `native-defui-control-mounts-independently-of-the-registry` -- the same probe body and the same assertion block, mounted as an unregistered native defui -- stayed GREEN. The two de-bypassed shared-suite rows also errored, which shows the bypass removal was load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object (35f57741a4467ede665e33b162a1523e5779f426, both sides). A second control confirmed the late-bind drift gate is non-vacuous: removing the directory row reds it in both directions.

**Found beyond the brief.** `make-react-adapter` initially routed the new hook unconditionally, so every React-shaped caller supplying no factory published a NIL impl -- and `route-hook!` stores what it is handed and calls it once its adapter is installed, so the first `reg-view*` under that adapter THREW instead of declining. The browser lane could not see this; the node lane caught it as 16 errors, all on `re-frame.hicasso.substrate`, which owns its own view path (the spine's bench/test adapters are in the same position). Fixed by guarding the routing on the factory being present. Worth remembering as a general hazard of `route-hook!`: an optional routed hook must not be published at all when its impl is absent, because a routed nil is indistinguishable from a published handler until it is called.
AUDIT PR #8874 (2026-09-01): REOPENED. The new componentization is decided at registration time through a routed hook, so it still misses the repository's canonical boot order. `boot-and-mount-an-app.md` requires registration namespaces (including views) at namespace load, before `run` calls `rf/init!`. In that sequence `:adapter/componentize-view` sees no installed adapter, `route-hook!` returns nil, `apply-adapter-componentize-view` keeps the MetaFn, and `init!` only seats the adapter—it never revisits existing `:view` entries. `(rf/view id)` therefore remains a non-JS-function and the advertised direct UIx `$` mount still fails. The new browser fixture installs UIx before every `reg-view*`, so it cannot see this normal path. Minimal repair: add a register-before-init → init-UIx → direct-mount witness and make existing view registrations acquire the UIx head without requiring application authors to move top-level registrations into `run`; retain post-init registration, inactive-adapter routing, and stable lookup identity. No broad adapter redesign.
